articles.title: Former Kentucky track star Masai Russell sets World Record in 100m Hurdles
articles.summary: Kentucky track and field star Masai Russell just achieved another milestone in her burgeoning career, setting a new world record in the 100-meter hurdles.
articles._body: We’ve got some more bragging rights in Hurdle U. Former Kentucky track and field star Masai Russell just achieved another milestone in her burgeoning career, setting a new world record in the 100-meter hurdles at the Diamond League meet in Zurich. Russell, the reigning Olympic gold medalist and American record holder in the 100mH, finished in 12.09 seconds, beating the previous world record of 12.12 seconds, set by Nigeria’s Tobi Amusan at the Eugene World Championships in 2022. Amusan finished second to Russell’s in today’s race, with a time of 12.23 seconds. European champion Nadine Visser finished third in 12.34 seconds. Russell’s world record is five one-hundredths faster than her previous career-best of 12.14 seconds from May 2026, which broke her own American record of 12.17 seconds, set in May 2025. She won gold in Paris in 2024 with a time of 12.33 seconds, her Olympic debut, beating out the silver medalist by 0.01 seconds. Russell, now 26, competed for Kentucky from 2018-23 under head coach Lonnie Greene, setting the NCAA record in the 100m hurdles at the Texas Relays in April 2023 with a time of 12.36 seconds. According to Olympics.com , Russell is the first woman to simultaneously hold the world record and Olympic title in the 100m hurdles since Bulgaria’s Yordanka Donkova, who won Olympic gold in 1988 and held the world record until Keni Harrison broke it in 2016. Russell and Harrison are the only U.S. women to have held the mark. Harrison is also a Kentucky track alumna. Of course, Kentucky has another world record holder, Sydney McLaughlin-Levrone, the reigning gold medalist in the 400m hurdles. Lots to brag about as a Wildcat. We’ve still got a few years until the LA Olympics in 2028, but as of now, Russell is the one to beat. articles.title: How Each Music Listening Platform Is Treating AI Music (Updating)
articles.summary: From BandCamp's outright ban of AI music to Spotify's "AI Personas" approach, here's how all the online music platforms are dealing with the fast-growing flood of AI-generated content.
articles._body: One of the most pressing questions in the music industry right now is how streaming services should be treating the deluge of AI-generated music on their platforms. Should AI music be demonetized, or even removed from platforms? Should it be labeled or flagged so that users know what they are listening to? Or, for those optimistic about AI’s creative possibilities, should it all just be left alone? It’s hard to know the exact scale of AI music on streaming services today, but what is clear is that there’s a lot of it — and the amount of it is growing fast. Deezer reports the count of daily AI track uploads at over 50% at “peak level” in June 2026, and Apple Music told Billboard in April that “more than a third” of monthly uploads were 100% AI-generated. Qobuz also noted in January that 34% of new uploads each day are AI-generated. These metrics, however, may still represent an undercount of all the material that uses AI in some part of the creative process, given partially AI generated music is much more challenging to detect. Plus, it’s impossible to determine when AI is used to write lyrics or melodies that are then recorded by human musicians, unless a user offered up their prompting history.  Related The Recorded Music Industry Wants Labels on AI Music. How Could That Work? (FAQ) Kristin Robinson When considering the challenges of actually implementing regulations on streaming services, the question of what to do about AI music becomes incredibly complex. There’s a risk of false positives with AI detection tools, but requiring self-disclosure from rights holders will likely lead to outright deception at worst, or innocent omission at best, given how prevalent AI elements can be at any point in the recording process.  Still, lines are being drawn, and until some sort of consensus emerges, those lines are different at different digital service providers. To learn more about what each music listening platform is doing about AI-generated music, Billboard has compiled an updating list of each services’ policies as they articulate them.

articles.title: Rui Hachimura’s huge FIBA World Cup performance will catch Clippers fans’ attention
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Clippers were one of the busier teams during the offseason, as they’ve turned the page on the Kawhi Leonard era and gone to a younger version of themselves. They still went out and added some veterans, and one of them was Rui Hachimura, who proved to be a consistent player f
articles._body: The Los Angeles Clippers were one of the busier teams during the offseason, as they’ve turned the page on the Kawhi Leonard era and gone to a younger version of themselves. They still went out and added some veterans, and one of them was Rui Hachimura, who proved to be a consistent player for the Los Angeles Lakers over the past few years. The Clippers are now hoping they can get that level of play from him, and after his recent performance in the FIBA World Cup qualifiers with Japan, there should be no doubt. Hachimura finished the game against Saudi Arabia with 29 points, four rebounds and two steals. He shot 11-of-14 from the field and 3-of-4 from the 3-point line. The Clippers may not get those kind of stats from Hachimura every night, but they know he’ll be competing at a high level. The best thing about it is that he actually wanted to join the Clippers , and shortly after signing with the team, he shared why. “I’m just so happy,” Hachimura said. “The Clippers are an amazing organization. Even when talking to other NBA players, they always rave about how great the Clippers organization is. It’s truly a player-first team, you know. They take care of their players while having that winning mentality. The Clippers are a young team. A year ago, they were called the oldest team in the league, but they’ve transitioned to a younger generation especially with Kawhi Leonard getting traded. Joining them right as they build this next generation is huge for me, and I’m incredibly excited.” The Clippers should be a good fit for Hachimura as they try to rebuild their forward depth. They’ll have Brandon Ingram to carry most of that scoring load at the position, and other key pieces around the team to support him. articles.summary: As there have been multiple St. Louis Cardinals players sent to the injured list (IL) recently, like shortstop Masyn Winn and pitcher Hunter Dobbins, fans are hoping that Blake Jordan doesn’t join them after sustaining an injury on Thursday. With Cardinals fans looking for injury updates, i
articles._body: As there have been multiple St. Louis Cardinals players sent to the injured list (IL) recently , like shortstop Masyn Winn and pitcher Hunter Dobbins, fans are hoping that Blake Jordan doesn’t join them after sustaining an injury on Thursday. With Cardinals fans looking for injury updates , it all started with St. Louis’ contest against the Baltimore Orioles on Thursday. According to Derrick Goold, Jordan had to be helped off the field by manager Oliver Marmol and an athletic trainer, as he couldn’t put weight on his “left foot.” “Blaze Jordan is being helped off the field by Oli Marmol and an athletic trainer. He is not putting much weight on his left foot as he gets assistance down the stairs and into the dugout,” Goold wrote on X, formerly Twitter. The injury was sustained in the top of the eighth inning, coming on defense where he would tag a runner awkwardly while in motion, leading to immediate pain. The injury is speculated to also be an ankle issue, rather than a foot injury, though full details haven’t been revealed just yet, as Nolan Gorman took over at third base after Jordan’s exit. articles._body: At long last, college football is making its return this weekend. A handful of games will take place on Saturday as part of Week 0, including a standalone matchup in Ireland to kick off the 2026 season. North Carolina will take on TCU in Dublin as the first FBS game of the 2026 college football season. From there, two more games will take place in the late-afternoon window, including NC State vs. Virginia in an early ACC showdown. Saturday will also mark Brian Kelly’s debut in the CBS Sports Network booth. $19.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage Week 0 will also be the first chance for fans to see some of ESPN’s new-look college football booths, including the crew heading to Dublin. Here is the full announcer schedule for the first Saturday of college football. North Carolina vs. TCU (in Dublin) Date/Time: Aug. 29, Noon ET Channel: ESPN Streaming: ESPN App, Disney+ Broadcasters: Mike Monaco, Jordan Rodgers, Dana Boyle ESPN’s new Friday night college football crew will make its official debut for the Week 0 opener. Mike Monaco and Jordan Rodgers make up a fresh booth this year, with Dana Boyle joining as sideline reporter. North Carolina is coming off a rocky first season under Bill Belichick , finishing with a 4-8 record. The Tar Heels will also have a new quarterback under center in Billy Edwards as they take on TCU, fresh off a 9-4 record in 2025 and with Harvard transfer Jaden Craig now at QB. San Jose State vs. USC Date/Time: Aug. 29, 3 p.m. ET Channel: NBC Streaming: Peacock Broadcasters: Noah Eagle, Todd Blackledge, Kathryn Tappen The early afternoon window features a West Coast showdown in Los Angeles. NBC’s primetime team will have the call with Noah Eagle and Todd Blackledge in the booth and Kathryn Tappen serving as the sideline reporter. USC enters 2026 with high expectations after landing a top-ranked recruiting class and retaining quarterback Jayden Maiava . The Trojans will get things started at The Coliseum against San Jose State in what will be NBC’s first college football broadcast of the season. NC State vs. Virginia Date/Time: Aug. 29, 3:30 p.m. ET Channel: ESPN Streaming: ESPN App Broadcasters: Wes Durham, Max Browne, Madison Fitzpatrick An intriguing ACC matchup is one of the headliners in Week 0. NC State will take on Virginia with a new announcer pairing in the booth. Wes Durham and Max Browne will make up ACC Network’s primetime booth with Madison Fitzpatrick serving as sideline reporter this year. Virginia is coming off an ACC Championship appearance last season as part of a breakout year under head coach Tony Elliott , and Beau Pribula will now take over as the Hoos’ starting quarterback. On the other side, NC State retained quarterback CJ Bailey after an 8-5 record last year, including a 4-4 mark in ACC play. Jacksonville State vs. North Dakota State Date/Time: Aug. 29, 5:30 p.m. ET Channel: CBS Sports Network Broadcasters: Rich Waltz, Adam Breneman, Brian Kelly, Jordan Giorgio For the first time, former Notre Dame and LSU coach Brian Kelly will serve as a color analyst for CBS Sports. He will be in the booth alongside Rich Waltz and Adam Breneman , with Jordan Giorgio as sideline reporter, for Jacksonville State vs. North Dakota State on Saturday. The matchup will mark North Dakota State’s first game as an FBS member after making the leap from the FCS Missouri Valley Football Conference to the Mountain West this offseason. NDSU will take on Jacksonville State for the first time since 2015 – a 37-10 Bison victory. New Mexico State vs. Florida State Date/Time: Aug. 29, 7 p.m. ET Channel: The CW Streaming: ESPN App Broadcasters: Thom Brennaman, Jason Cabinda A big year for Mike Norvell and Florida State kicks off in primetime in Week 0. The Seminoles will get things started against New Mexico State on Saturday with The CW’s lead booth of Thom Brennaman and Jason Cabinda on the call. FSU is coming off back-to-back rocky seasons and will look to bounce back in 2026. Norvell overhauled the coaching staff this offseason and has a new quarterback taking over in Ashton Daniels . Florida State went 5-7 last year after going 1-11 in 2024. Hawaii vs. Stanford Date/Time: Aug. 29, 7 p.m. ET Channel: ACC Network Streaming: ESPN App Broadcasters: Jorge Sedano, Rodney McLeod, Kendra Douglas The Tavita Pritchard Era will get underway in ACC Network’s primetime slot as Stanford welcomes Hawaii in Week 0. Another new broadcast team will be on the call with Jorge Sedano , Rodney McLeod and sideline reporter Kendra Douglas in attendance. Pritchard is taking over at his alma mater after Frank Reich was the interim head coach for last year’s 3-9 campaign. Stanford will welcome a Hawaii team that went 9-4 a year ago and has quarterback Micah Alejado back in the fold for this season. Memphis vs. UNLV Date/Time: Aug. 29, 10 p.m. ET Channel: FOX Streaming: FOX One Broadcasters: Tim Brando, Devin Gardner FOX will have a late window to round out the slate of FBS games in college football during Week 0. UNLV will welcome Memphis to Allegiant Stadium with Tim Brando and Devin Gardner on the call for the matchup. The Rebels won 10 games in Year 1 under Dan Mullen in 2025, though he said the quarterback situation is still undecided entering the season opener. Meanwhile, Memphis is starting a new era as Charles Huff takes over following last year’s 8-5 record. articles.title: Ye Supports Lil Durk at Chicago Rapper’s Murder-for-Hire Trial, Posing With ‘Free Durk’ Shirt
articles.summary: Footage of West draped in all-black strolling into the downtown Los Angeles federal courthouse emerged in the afternoon.
articles._body: Ye (formerly Kanye West ) was in attendance supporting Lil Durk at the Chicago rapper’s murder-for-hire trial in Los Angeles on Thursday (Aug. 27). Footage of West draped in all-black strolling into the downtown Los Angeles federal courthouse emerged in the afternoon. Ye also posed for a photo with Durk Affiliate Doodie Lo while holding up a “Free Durk” T-shirt, which has made the rounds on social media. Related Lil Durk Put a Bounty on Quando Rondo for ‘Revenge,’ Jury Told as Murder-for-Hire Trial Opens Lil Durk Is Going to Trial on Murder-for-Hire Charges. Here’s What to Know About the Case Lil Durk Murder-For-Hire Case: Feds Add New Racketeering Charge Alleging OTF Gang Violence As a fellow Chicago native, Yeezy has long been a supporter of Durk’s, as the duo linked up on tracks like Donda ‘s “Jonah” (No. 27 Billboard Hot 100 peak), the Vultures title track, and Cardi B’s “Hot Shit” (No. 13 Hot 100 peak) in 2022. West isn’t the only rap star to pull up to support Durk: mgk made an appearance at the courthouse on Monday when the trial kicked off. “This been my bro for a decade when he called and asked if id pull up and support im there no question free durk,” the Cleveland native wrote on X. Meek Mill joined in to call for Durk’s freedom in a post to X on Thursday as well. Free lil Durk! — MeekMill (@MeekMill) August 27, 2026 Federal prosecutors are alleging that Lil Durk became “consumed with revenge” and put a hit out on rapper Quando Rondo in response to the murder of King Von, a close Durk affiliate, in 2020. Rondo was targeted in a 2022 shooting at a Los Angeles gas station, but his friend, Lul Pab, was ultimately killed in the crossfire. The “All My Life” rapper was arrested in October 2024 near Miami International Airport. In addition to murder-for-hire, Durk faces charges of conspiracy and stalking. Durk has maintained his innocence since being apprehended and he can be sentenced up to life in prison if convicted. The Los Angeles trial is expected to last several weeks. As for Ye, West will be traveling to New Orleans for a show at the Caesars Superdome on Friday (Aug. 28), before heading home to Chicago for a pair of Soldier Field concerts on Sept. 3 and Sept. 4. Billboard has reached out to Ye’s reps for comment.

articles._body: KATSEYE is no longer performing at Olivia Rodrigo ‘s fast-approaching Daisy Chain Fields, with the girl group members announcing two days prior to the festival that they had to pull out after member Megan sprained her ankle. In a note posted to KATSEYE’s Instagram Story, the band began by writing, “We’re so incredibly sorry to share that we are unable to perform at Daisy Chain Fields this Saturday.” “Megan sprained her ankle yesterday during tour rehearsal and after being evaluated by doctors, she has been advised to stay off it and allow it to properly heal so we can be ready for our upcoming tour,” the message continued. “We know how much our fans were looking forward to seeing us, and it breaks our hearts to disappoint anyone who made plans to be there.” Taking place Saturday in Irvine, California, the inaugural Daisy Chain Fields will feature Rodrigo headlining a self-curated, all-women lineup that also includes Chappell Roan, Doechii, Rachel Chinouriri, The Breeders, Garbage and “special guests” Stevie Nicks, Karen O and Sarah McLachlan. All of the proceeds will benefit charities supporting women and girls, including Planned Parenthood and Center for Reproductive Rights. “We were especially excited for Daisy Chain Fields because it’s not just about music, but the greater mission of joy and community,” KATSEYE’s statement continued. “We’re sending all our love to Olivia and to all of the incredible artists, non-profit organizations and volunteers who have given their time to make this day so special.” “It’s going to be such an amazing day,” it concluded, “and we can’t wait to see everyone out on tour.” The news marks the latest bump in the road in an already-challenging year for KATSEYE. In February, HYBE announced that Manon would be taking a hiatus from the group to focus on her mental health. Earlier in August, Sophia revealed that she, too, was stepping back from band duties to prioritize her mental well-being, bringing KATSEYE’s member count down to four: Lara, Daniela, Yoonchae and Megan. In place of KATSEYE, alt-pop singer/songwriter Devon Again will perform at Daisy Chain Fields. The festival’s official Instagram account posted an updated lineup shortly after the girl group’s announcement, writing: “Megan is recovering from a sprained ankle, and the group will no longer be able to perform this weekend. We are wishing Megan a smooth and speedy recovery!” See the updated lineup below. View this post on Instagram

articles.title: South Carolina opens 2026 on Sept. 5; How to watch two Gamecock opponents who play before then
articles.summary: Two South Carolina football opponents will take the field before Sept. 5, the day of the Gamecocks' first game.
articles._body: Rejoice, college football fans: the season is here. Shane Beamer’s South Carolina football team opens the season on Sept. 5. Week 0, though, begins Thursday night and extends into the weekend. In preparation for the 2026 slate, Gamecock fans can check out a pair of USC opponents before their favorite team takes the field for the first time. Both the Towson Tigers and Oklahoma Sooners will play their first games before Sept. 5. Because of that, there will be opportunities to watch them play before the first Sandstorm at Williams-Brice Stadium. Have a question for the GamecockCentral staff? Ask it now on The Insiders Forum. In fact, Towson opens the 2026 campaign on Thursday night. The Tigers will take on the Maine Black Bears at 6 p.m. in one of the first Division I matchups of the year. The game will be broadcast on the Monumental Sports Network and stream on FloSports (also available on Amazon Prime). South Carolina, of course, will take on Towson in week two on Saturday, Sept. 12. The Tigers and Gamecocks will face off at Williams-Brice Stadium under the lights at 7 p.m. The non-conference matchup will stream on SEC Network+ on the ESPN app. No other Gamecock opponents will join Towson in playing during week zero this weekend. However, the Oklahoma Sooners will get a head start on week one. Brent Venables’ team will open their 2026 season on Friday, Sept. 4 against the UTEP Miners. SEC Network+ will stream the showdown. Kickoff is set for 8 p.m. (Eastern). South Carolina will then play Oklahoma in each team’s eighth game of the season. Exact times and networks have not yet been announced. Considered a “flex” game, the Gamecocks and Sooners will meet in either the afternoon or night window. Have a question for the GamecockCentral staff? Ask it on The Insiders Forum.

articles.summary: Connor Hellebucyk of Winnipeg Jets expressed his desire to be traded away from the Winnipeg Jets months ago. articles._body: Connor Hellebucyk of Winnipeg Jets expressed his desire to be traded away from the Winnipeg Jets months ago. With NHL training camps weeks away from opening up in mid-September and no movement since he made his request, Hellebuyck came out with a statement confirming that he still wants to go to a new team this year. Statement in response to Connor Hellebuyck’s request for a trade. pic.twitter.com/plv5xH92M4 — Winnipeg Jets (@NHLJets) August 27, 2026 His statement was posted on X by NHL insider Frank Servalli. The statement started off with a warm tone, thanking the Jets for drafting him in 2012 and taking a chance on an American-born goalie from Odessa, Texas. However, the statement turned all business after that, as he said he “politely” requested a trade and has been waiting for the Jets to move him to another team. He said a trade is the best thing for him and his family. Jets follow up with explanation The Jets issued a statement through executive vice president and general manager Kevin Chevedayoff saying they would continue “to work through the situation” but there was no update to report. Hellebuyck has been recognized as one of the best goalies in the NHL, and while he has struggled to perform at a high level when the Jets have had postseason opportunities, he was the gold-medal-winning goaltender for the United States in the 2026 Winter Olympics. The goaltender has not said if his trade request would be to send him to an NHL team based in the United States, but it seems quite likely that would be his desire. Hellebuyck is a four-time NHL All-Star and he has been the league’s Vezina Trophy winner as the top goalie three times. He also won the Hart Trophy as the NHL’s Most Valuable Player in in the 2024-25 season. Hellebuyck had a 23-23-11 record last season along with a 2.86 goals-against average and an .895 save percentage. articles._body: Jason Klotz , a former Texas Longhorns basketball player, died this week, according to the Houston Chronicle . He was 44 years old. Former Houston Rockets player PJ Tucker, who played with Klotz at Texas, shared the news on Wednesday night. “Damn dawg. This one hurts,” Tucker wrote on social media. “1 of 1! (If you know, you know) When I first got to Austin, you (were) one of few that looked out for me. Too many memories. Love you, brother, forever.” [ $19.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage ] Officials confirmed Jason Klotz’s death to the Houston Chronicle on Thursday, but the official cause of death has not been revealed. According to his LinkedIn bio, Klotz was a sales manager in the oil and gas industry and was living in the Houston area. Klotz played for the Longhorns from 2000 to 2005. During his freshman season in 2000-01, Klotz played in three games and saw six minutes of action before suffering a sprained right ankle. The NCAA granted him a medical redshirt after the season. Jason Klotz became a captain and MVP at Texas In 2001-02, Klotz was named Texas’ Most Improved Player after playing in all 34 games with three starts and averaging 3.5 points and 3.2 rebounds per contest. The following year, Klotz played in 32 of the 33 games with one start and ranked third on the team in blocks (21) and field goal percentage (.500). During the 2003-04 season, Klotz earned an All-Big 12 Honorable Mention and also earned a spot on the five-person Big 12 All-Improved Team. He played in 32 of the team’s 33 games with seven starts and averaged seven points and 3.9 rebounds with 27 blocks. During his senior season, Klotz was named a team captain and co-MVP. He played in 30 of 31 games with 16 starts and ranked fourth on the team in scoring (11.2 points per game), fourth in rebounding (5.8), and second in blocked shots (33). After college, Klotz played on the Orlando Magic Summer League team but never saw action in the NBA. He did play professionally overseas, spending time in China, Spain, Japan, Turkey, Uruguay, and Holland.

Tampa owns a current 79-54 overall record, while NYY remains 3.5 games behind the leader before first pitch of the Astros game. The rival Boston Red Sox aren’t far behind from the Yankees either, standing at 73-60 and sitting in third place in the division race. articles.title: J.Crew’s ’80s Rollneck Gets a New-Gen Remix, Courtesy of Emma Chamberlain
articles.summary: The Gen Z star fronts the retailer’s latest campaign for its new cropped, fitted take on the classic (and affordable) fall sweater.
articles._body: All products and services featured are independently chosen by editors. Emma Chamberlain knows a thing or two about setting the tone, whether she’s talking fashion, sharing a playlist or documenting her latest festival experience. Now, she’s bringing that same Gen Z energy to one of J.Crew’s most recognizable classics. The retailer has named Chamberlain the face of its new Tiny Rollneck campaign , putting a fresh take on the sweater J.Crew first introduced in 1988. The new version launched Aug. 26 on J.Crew, bringing the heritage knit into a tailored and chic silhouette. Shop Emma Chamberlain x J. Crew The Tiny Rollneck keeps the details that made the original a J.Crew staple, including its heavyweight cotton construction, rolled neckline and raglan sleeves. But this time, the proportions are smaller, with a slightly cropped length and closer fit, plus bright, graphic colors that give the classic a more playful feel. For the campaign, Chamberlain appears in a candy-colored, retro-futuristic setting inspired by early-2000s fashion imagery and video game character-selection screens. The launch follows several recent attempts by J.Crew to reintroduce the Rollneck to a new generation. The brand’s “New Rollneck Generation” campaign last fall featured a cast including Maggie Rogers , Molly Gordon , Dominic Sessa and Benito Skinner . Earlier this year, its “Rollneck Remix” project brought in five independent designers — Buci, Collina Strada, Eckhaus Latta, Patrick Taylor and Tanner Fletcher — to reinterpret the sweater with details including lace, color blocking and nautical-inspired elements. POP OF COLOR Tiny Rollneck in Stripe $118 Buy Now at J.Crew Every fall wardrobe needs a good stripe, and this bold red-and-black colorway is an easy pick. Sport this sweater with low-rise jeans for an easy, laid-back look. It’s easy to see why the Rollneck has remained at the center of J.Crew’s fall staples for decades. Its heavyweight cotton, signature rolled neckline and instantly recognizable shape make it the kind of sweater that can be worn year after year without feeling dated. Now, Chamberlain’s take gives the classic the slight shift it needed to connect with a new generation. That same new-gen perspective makes Chamberlain a natural fit for J.Crew’s approach. Beyond her fashion influence, she has built a strong connection to music through her Spotify playlists, festival appearances and Anything Goes podcast. She has documented trips to Coachella and shared her enthusiasm for discovering new music, making her a familiar face to a generation that moves fluidly between fashion, music and internet culture.

articles.title: Texas A&M basketball guard Bryson Warren enters transfer portal, still looking to be eligible for 2026-27 season
articles.summary: Texas A&M guard Bryson Warren is entering transfer portal following recent SEC and NCAA rulings according to reports. AggieYell has the latest..
articles._body: Texas A&M basketball guard Bryson Warren entered the transfer portal Thursday, a source with knowledge of the situation confirmed to AggieYell following a report from Matt Zenitz of CBS Sports. The former G League guard received a temporary restraining order Wednesday after the NCAA recently ruled him ineligible. He has a court hearing set for Sept. 4 that could lead to him receiving court-ordered eligibility for the upcoming season. Warren returning to A&M remains possible, according to a source. Warren, 21, had been in the G League since the 2023-24 season and most recently played for the New York Knicks’ affiliate, the Westchester Knicks. He appeared in 21 games with 17 starts last season, averaging 19.8 points, 5.0 assists, 3.1 rebounds and 1.2 steals per game while shooting 42.4% from the floor, 38.6% from 3-point range and 80.6% from the free-throw line. He spent the previous two seasons with the Miami Heat’s G League affiliate, the Sioux Falls Skyforce. He also joined the Heat on an Exhibit-10 contract in September 2024 before being waived the following day. Before joining the G League, Warren played for Little Rock Central (Ark.) and spent time in the Overtime Elite basketball league with Team OTE in 2021-22 and YNG Dreamerz in 2022-23. He claimed the OTE title in 2022 and received second-team All-OTE recognition in 2023. He went unselected in the 2024 NBA Draft following his first season with Sioux Falls and remained in the G League. Without Warren in the mix, the Aggies have one scholarship spot remaining on their roster. They’re still evaluating their options ahead of the second season under coach Bucky McMillan and looking to maintain flexibility with their final roster spot.

articles.title: In Rapsody’s World, God Looks a Lot Like You: ‘There’s a Power Within Us That We Haven’t Tapped All the Way Into’
articles.summary: The Grammy-winning MC talks her new God Gotta Afro & Gold Hoops album, sampling D'Angelo and honoring Nolan Wells.
articles._body: Fierce public discourse about the value and necessity of media representation — particularly for those belonging to oft-overlooked social spheres — inundated most of the 2010s. On her masterful fifth studio album God Gotta Afro & Gold Hoops , Grammy-winning rapper Rapsody is interested in a different kind of representation: If we’re to believe that we were all created in God’s image, then what are we to do with depictions of Him that are completely devoid of Blackness in an effort to uphold white Christianity and, by extension, white supremacy? Related Yung Miami Is Ready for Her Solo Debut Thanks to ‘Spend Dat’: ‘People Are About to Eat Their Words’ D’Angelo’s 10 Best Songs: Staff Picks Leon Thomas & Kehlani Talk R&B’s Future, Wellness & Friendship | Billboard Cover Interview “It’s about reshaping the narrative and rewriting the truth,” she tells Billboard mere hours before her new LP hits streaming on Aug. 21. “We’ve been miseducated so much — shout out to Lauryn Hill — and now we need to do the knowledge and re-educate ourselves. And we have to start with God and our spiritual connection with the Divine. We know that we are all made in the image of God, so when you look in the mirror, do not allow this world to erase you from it. Look in the mirror and see God in yourself.” Released via We Each Other and Roc Nation, God Gotta Afro & Gold Hoops landed at a particularly precarious time for hip-hop. To put it plainly, the genre has been in a wacky, and ultimately transitional, period this year. Drake’s “Janice STFU” ended a year-long drought for rap songs at the top of the Billboard Hot 100; and, according to Luminate’s 2026 midyear report, R&B/hip-hop’s market share fell by 1.6% versus midyear 2025, despite remaining the most-consumed genre of music in the U.S. As some members of the culture lamented the genre’s future on podcast couches, Rapsody took herself all the way back to its beginning — and found herself on a trip across multiple African nations. Rapsody first visited South Africa in 2013 — “I didn’t come back the same person,” she gushes — but her most recent trip in 2025 provided the foundation for her latest LP. After an edifying, restorative stint in Ghana, Rapsody made her way to Johannesburg, where she “visited the Ashanti people and all that was playing on the radio was this Westernized, white form of gospel music.” That sonic friction sparked thoughts of “how much of the religion has been co-opted [by] Western ideas of spirituality and God,” which later turned into inner musings on both her father’s love of [the Emmy-winning 1977 historical drama miniseries] Roots and her favorite book, activist Sister Souljah’s No Disrespect . By the time Denaun Porter, Rapsody’s collaborator of more than a decade who accompanied her on her trip to Africa, played her his first beat for the project, the very first thing out of Rapsody’s mouth was the refrain for the album’s title track: “God gotta Afro.” “I wanted to return to a familiarity, a feeling, an energy, a sound, a frequency to keep that bridge open between Black [American] and African men and women,” Rapsody tells Billboard . “Pan-Africanism and Afrofuturism are the connection back to the Motherland.” As Rapsody tells it, “Africa was the breath and heart of the album, and in Detroit, we added arms, legs and a head,” making God Gotta Afro & Gold Hoops a genuine bridge between two Black music meccas. “Free Your Mind,” the first full-length track on the album, was the first song she recorded to Porter’s first batch of beats, and “You,” a street-ready, DJ Whoo Kid-assisted banger, was the last song recorded for the LP. “Denaun’s genius is that he understands how to reach people in a different way than I do as a writer,” Rapsody says. “He made me feel like it’s 2005 again, and I’m in college making music because I love it and there’s nothing else attached.” At 16 tracks, God Gotta Afro & Gold Hoops traverses the blues, jazz, traditional hip-hop, soul and funk, bringing along a bevy of special guests, including Malice, George Clinton and Amanda Reifer. And there are also “three or four other ideas” she’s considering including on a potential deluxe album. Rapsody remembers Porter telling her, “You don’t have to shoot in the gym anymore. We’re not recording 80 songs because we don’t have to. We can pick our spots on the floor and decide if we want to go for a lay-up or shoot long range from the three.” And that kind of intentionality grounded her decision to recruit Soweto’s Karabo yaMorena children’s gospel choir, Ghanaian artist Jojo Abot and South Africa’s Nomisupasta (also known as Nomsa Mazwai), who Rapsody first linked up with on her 2013 She Got Game mixtape. “There’s a certain vibration in songs and sounds and voices from Africa,” she says. “We have our own in gospel and the soul of Black people. I wanted to build that bridge between Black America and Africa, [which] comes from going to Ghana and learning about W.E.B. Du Bois, Dr. Kwame Nkrumah and how intentional they were about maintaining that connection.” The greatest guest star on God Gotta Afro , however, blessed the album from the ancestral realm. “Apple Juice,” a sweet, melodic tune about the innocence of burgeoning crushes, initially arrived as a pre-release single, complete with a music video starring three-time Olympic medalist and track and field star Will Claye. The track finds Rapsody fully stepping into her singing bag with courage sourced from the sample that gives the track its sonic backbone: the late D’Angelo’s Voodoo highlight “One Mo’Gin.” “The purpose is always to carry our ancestors through and that they continue to guide us,” Rapsody says of “Apple Juice,” which she recorded about three and a half months before D’Angelo’s passing. “Now, I have a connection with [D’Angelo’s children] Imani and Michael and all the kids; I think that’s beautiful.

articles.summary: MLBPA interim executive director Bruce Meyer pushed back strongly Thursday against MLB’s latest collective-bargaining proposal, taking particular issue with the league tying proposed offseason changes to a salary-cap system. The dispute comes with the current collective bargaining agreement set t
articles._body: MLBPA interim executive director Bruce Meyer pushed back strongly Thursday against MLB’s latest collective-bargaining proposal, taking particular issue with the league tying proposed offseason changes to a salary-cap system. The dispute comes with the current collective bargaining agreement set to expire December 1 and the sides still divided over key economic issues. ESPN’s Jeff Passan shared Meyer’s response on X, formerly Twitter, as the union challenged the premise behind MLB’s proposal. “The suggestion that the only way to limit roster churn, or incentivize earlier Free Agent signings is with a salary cap is entirely unserious.” MLB’s proposal would reshape the offseason by concentrating most free-agent activity into a shorter window through December 21, followed by a transaction freeze lasting until the first Monday in February. The league also proposed weekly 26-man rosters, four in-season minor-league options instead of five, and allowing clubs to carry 14 pitchers. However, MLB conditioned those changes on players accepting the salary-cap-and-floor structure owners proposed in May. That economic model features a $245.3 million cap, a $171.2 million floor, and a 50-50 revenue split with escrow. Meyer argued that such a system would reduce overall player compensation, weaken guaranteed contracts, and diminish players’ leverage in free agency. He also said the union has proposed alternatives designed to address roster churn and encourage earlier signings without implementing a salary cap. The disagreement underscores the significant economic divide between the league and union, with roughly three months remaining under the current CBA. No agreement on a salary cap or the proposed offseason changes had been reached as of Thursday. articles.title: Former G League guard Bryson Warren enters NCAA transfer portal
articles.summary: Former NBA G League guard Bryson Warren has entered the NCAA transfer portal, according to a report from On3’s Pete Nakos. Warren had committed to Texas A&M earlier this year, before the SEC passed a rule preventing players from professional leagues from suiting up for member schools. The
articles._body: Former NBA G League guard Bryson Warren has entered the NCAA transfer portal , according to a report from On3’s Pete Nakos . Warren had committed to Texas A&M earlier this year, before the SEC passed a rule preventing players from professional leagues from suiting up for member schools. The SEC’s new professional sports rule carries heavy penalties for teams who roster former professional players, making it untenable for Texas A&M to have Warren on the team this fall. So what are the new rules, exactly? [ $19.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage ] Violating the new SEC-pro sports rule will result in a coach suspension of 50% of contests and a hefty fine, On3’s Wilson Alexander confirmed and the league later announced. The fine will amount to 50% of that sport’s annual operating budget, and the head coach’s suspension will include all coaching, recruiting and administrative duties. The punishment is similar to the one the NCAA has in place for “ghost transfers,” or players who leave one school for another without entering the transfer portal. As for Bryson Warren, he’s a 21-year-old prospect who averaged 19.9 points, 5.0 assists, 3.0 rebounds, and 1.1 steals per game in 21 games, including 17 starts, with the Westchester Knights this past season. From 2023-2025, Warren averaged 11.8 points across 51 combined games with the Sioux Falls Skyforce. Before joining the G League, Warren was a product of Overtime Elite where he played for both Team OTE and the YNG Dreamerz. He won the OTE title in 2022 and was named second-team All-OTE in 2023. The 6-foot-3, 191-pound Warren entered the 2024 NBA Draft but ultimately went undrafted. Bryson Warren isn’t the only former professional player who has looked to enter the NCAA ranks this offseason. A handful of prominent court cases have granted eligibility to a certain subset of players, paving the way for a return. Warren was one of several who sought to take advantage. He will still likely be able to, but he’ll have to find a welcoming home. Multiple leagues, including the Big 12, Big Ten and ACC have passed similar rules as the SEC in recent days preventing professional players from joining their leagues. On3’s Alex Byington also contributed to this report.

articles._body: The Washington Commanders have issues to clean up before Week 1. But first, they must solve the 53-man roster dilemma . And here is the Commanders player on the roster bubble with the most at stake in the 2026 NFL preseason finale. The Commanders will battle the Ravens on Friday at 6 p.m. It will be a chance for quarterback Athan Kaliakmanis to prove he deserves a chance to stick around in 2026. A seventh-round pick in this year’s NFL Draft, Kaliakmanis has shown good signs during the preseason. But has it been enough for Dan Quinn and the Commanders to keep him around? Does Commanders QB Athan Kaliakmanis have what it takes? The battle is for the QB3 spot on the Commanders’ roster. In Kaliakmanis’ way is Sam Hartman. It’s a spot Kaliakmanis should be able to grab, thanks in part to a passer rating of 104.3 in his two preseason games. The rookie said he’s trying to state his case , according to commanders.com. “Just constantly getting better, striving towards perfection, even though it’s not attainable,” Kaliakmanis said. “I think it just goes into your preparation. Having confidence in your preparation, knowing that I don’t need to be a superhero today. I just need to trust the game plan. I need to trust my teammates and go out there and execute.” Against the Lions, completed 11 of his 14 passes for 162 yards and didn’t take a sack. Commanders head coach Dan Quinn said Kaliakmanis has looked good under pressure. “I was pleased to see him in the chaos,” Quinn said after the Dolphins game, where Kaliakmanis went 6 of 10 for 87 yards and got sacked twice. “He felt calm in the space tonight. I’ll be looking forward to watching him. I thought you’d see his arm strength come out a little bit, and it did, on some of the play-action passes.” Kaliakmanis said he’s already growing a connection with the receivers. “I just trust my receivers,” Kaliakmanis said. “I’ve always been that type of player. I’ve been the type of player to throw it up and give my guys a shot. So, that’s what I did, and he made an incredible play. Great play by Nash, and I appreciate him for that.” However, despite the positives from Kaliakmanis and the negatives from Hartman — notably lack of arm strength — the battle for the third spot hasn’t been decided. “They’re battling for it,” Quinn said. “There will be a bunch of things we’re gonna want to look at to keep digging in. The other game coming up is so important for them. Managing the clock, working it all, being in tough scenarios, feeling the rush that they don’t do that in practice. So, the next practice, the next game, will be super valuable for the both of them.” However, there’s information working against Hartman. Included is his potential lack of fit with offensive coordinator David Blough’s scheme, according to roundtable.io. “David Blough’s offense is built on play-action, RPOs, and rollouts that require a quarterback who can plant and drive the ball downfield from unconventional platforms,” Roundtable wrote. “Kaliakmanis looks more comfortable after two preseason games than Hartman has in three years of being in the building. “ Certainly, Kaliakmanis wants the opportunity to stick with the Commanders, according to wjla.com. “Oh my gosh, it would mean everything,” Kaliakmanis said. “That’s what you dream about as a kid, but right now it’s not thinking about the future. It’s staying right where my feet are, being present in the moment and just doing everything I possibly can to incrementally grow.” The post Commanders player on roster bubble with most at stake in 2026 NFL preseason finale appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles.title: College Basketball In Crosshairs of Pro-Athlete NCAA Eligibility Chaos
articles.summary: Petre Thomas-Imagn Images
articles._body: For the first time in college sports, top conferences have now implemented different rules about which athletes are eligible to play on their teams. Following a bombshell ruling allowing several players who signed NFL contracts to return to college, the Big Ten adopted bans on professional football players returning to college. The Big SEC and ACC chose to put in place a similar ban for football—but also added basketball to the list. The Big 12 implemented a policy for all sports. Even more than football, basketball will feel the biggest impact of these new policies. In some cases, they ban players who may have gotten eligibility under NCAA rules. In others, they’ve caused confusion about the complex international professional basketball rules less relevant in football. And looming over it all is the flood of lawsuits and court decisions. “I think everyone believes things have got to change,” one power conference administrator told Front Office Sports. “But I think until things do change, everyone goes week by week with this. Like, ‘What’s gonna happen this week?’” Pro Eligibility Yo-Yo In men’s college basketball, the eligibility landscape has already been marred with confusion for the past two years, from the NCAA allowing some players to return from the G League but banning others who have signed NBA contracts, including two-way deals. The NCAA has faced challenges to those rules, however, as in the case of Charles Bediako , who sued to return to Alabama after a stint in the G League that included an NBA two-way contract. It was able to fight off that particular challenge. The chaos was only amplified this summer in the wake of the NCAA’s “age-based” eligibility policy , granting athletes five years to play five seasons, up from four. Players nationwide who started college in 2022 but exhausted four seasons of eligibility filed lawsuits to force the NCAA to include them in that policy. (One of those cases included NFL players—two of whom, Dae’Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris, signed deals to return to LSU .) Now, for Big 12, ACC, and SEC players, conference-level restrictions add to the sport’s murky eligibility landscape. As of Thursday afternoon, these were the only conferences that have publicly announced policies applying to basketball professional experience. First, the leagues ban players who entered the NBA or WNBA drafts but did not properly withdraw. In men’s basketball, underclassmen can declare for the draft, but must decide to opt out if they want to return to school. Players are automatically entered once they exhausted their college eligibility, however; the SEC policy allows players from the 2022 freshman class whose names were automatically entered into the draft, and who have now won an injunction for a fifth year, to return. (For women’s basketball, players must be four years removed from high school graduation or 22 years old—meaning most won’t enter the draft before exhausting their college eligibility anyway.) They also bar the return of players who have signed NBA and WNBA contracts, or who have appeared on these rosters. But they take a stricter stance than NCAA rules: Men’s players can’t have participated in the G League, either. The Big 12 bans players who signed any “professional league” contract, while the SEC specifically stipulates G League and NBA contracts. The ACC’s policy notes that NBA Summer League contracts mean Exhibit 10, two-way, or “any agreement providing for compensation beyond expenses and per diem.” And then there’s the question of international players—teams are increasingly more likely to recruit athletes who played professionally overseas. The Big 12 has barred all professional leagues—but will make an exception for international athletes who played in the pros overseas before coming to college in the first place. Players can’t, however, leave college and go pro overseas and then come back. What’s more, the patchwork of conference rules has created an uneven set of rules. For example, players who left college and signed G League contracts can’t return to play men’s college basketball in the SEC, Big 12, and ACC; but they could return to other leagues that haven’t yet passed a similar rule. However, other leagues are rushing to follow the lead of these conferences: The Big East was set to meet Thursday to discuss basketball options, FOS confirmed. “Optimism” and Uncertainty Multiple sources across conferences said they supported the decision for leagues to levy specific rules preventing professional participation. One source associated with a power conference school described it as a feeling of “relief;” the administrator said it provided a sense of “optimism.” But that doesn’t mean there won’t be complications with enforcement. For example, it could be hard to police the question about whether players have signed contracts, given that it’s often difficult to determine whether players have actually put pen to paper on G League, Exhibit 10, or other deals versus agreeing to them verbally. Then, there’s also whether the league-wide rules will hold up in court. The problem: If courts prohibit the NCAA from enforcing specific eligibility rules, could these rulings also, by proxy, apply to conferences? That’s the argument being made in multiple cases right now, including that of Kentucky transfer Mark Mitchell, whose attorneys filed an amended complaint Thursday arguing the SEC can’t enforce eligibility rules enjoined by a court order stopping the NCAA. Sources say they are all waiting to see how the league will respond to LSU rostering its football players as well as monitoring the case of former St. John’s standout RJ Luis Jr., who won an injunction to play at LSU this season despite going through the NBA Draft process and signing with multiple NBA teams. In addition to asking the court to clarify that the injunction applies to the SEC as well as the NCAA, LSU itself could sue the SEC once it receives a penalty. Or, the SEC could sue LSU in adv

articles.title: Genius Group Sets $2B Dual Treasury Target Months After Liquidating Bitcoin Holdings
articles.summary: Bitcoin Magazine
articles._body: Bitcoin Magazine Genius Group Sets $2B Dual Treasury Target Months After Liquidating Bitcoin Holdings Genius Group has announced a new plan to buy bitcoin — just months after selling its entire stash.  The NYSE-listed AI-powered education company said in a Thursday statement that it was aiming to build parallel AI and bitcoin treasuries worth a combined $1.6 billion, with total company assets targeted at $2 billion by fiscal year 2031.  Just in April, Genius Group sold its entire bitcoin reserves to repay $8.5 million in debt. The sale came as a number of digital asset treasuries were struggling due to a drop in crypto prices.  “Every dollar of preferred capital deployed into our bitcoin and AI Treasury that generates returns above the preferred dividend rate flows directly to our ordinary shareholders’ net asset value,” Genius Group CEO Roger James Hamilton said.  Genius Group first adopted a “Bitcoin first” strategy in late 2024, building a position that grew to 440 BTC by February 2025.  That effort was disrupted when a court order blocked the company from raising funds or issuing shares, forcing a series of sales that reduced its holdings — including roughly 86 BTC sold in a single month, leaving about 84 BTC by February 2026.  The company has now sold its remaining bitcoin entirely, using the proceeds to eliminate $8.5 million in debt. The liquidation reportedly came at a loss, leaving Genius Group with no crypto reserves. Against that backdrop, the company is now proposing to rebuild a bitcoin treasury — this time alongside a similarly sized AI treasury — funded not through equity sales but through a new preferred stock offering. Genius Group intends to draw on its $1.2 billion SEC-cleared shelf registration to issue Perpetual Preferred Securities, targeting an initial $12.5 million raise. Proceeds would be split between the AI treasury, the bitcoin treasury and a cash reserve covering about 18 months of dividend payments.  The plan mirrors moves by the biggest corporate holder of bitcoin, Strategy . The company has raised over $16 billion via perpetual preferred stock for its bitcoin holdings. Nasdaq-listed Strive Asset Management has raised more than $150 million similarly.  Genius Group says preferred capital will become its primary funding tool going forward, reducing reliance on its ordinary share ATM program. This post Genius Group Sets $2B Dual Treasury Target Months After Liquidating Bitcoin Holdings first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Mathew Di Salvo .

articles._body: After Golden State Warriors veteran Draymond Green survived last season’s trade deadline, are his days numbered entering the 2026-27 season? Green’s long-term future with the Warriors hangs in the balance as the Warriors attempts to remain relevant in a competitive Western Conference. Prediciting the potential of the aging Warriors’ core is difficult to gauge ahead of next season. However, if the Warriors struggle, Green is a name that could be tossed around again before the NBA trade deadline, according to ESPN’s Ben Golliver. “The NBA’s two longest-tenured players with one team are Curry, who is entering his 18th season with the Warriors, and Green, who signed a one-year, $27.7 million deal to return for his 15th campaign. While their illustrious partnership won’t last forever, Green’s willingness to opt out this summer to aid Golden State’s free agency pursuits suggests a close alignment still exists between team and player,” Golliver reported. “Green remains a high-level defender at age 36, but it’s unclear whether trade suitors still view him as a player capable of putting a championship hopeful over the top. His shaky outside shooting has long required surrounding him with the right personnel, and his scoring efficiency has dipped dramatically over the last two seasons.” If the Warriors find a potential suitor, Draymond Green could be entering his final season with the only team he’s ever played for. “Green’s value to Golden State as an icon and mainstay likely exceeds what the team could acquire by trading him, in part because a player with his skill set and salary only makes sense for aspiring contenders,” Golliver added. “However, that dynamic could theoretically change if the Warriors stumble out of the gate while waiting for Butler’s return from an ACL injury.” How the Warriors fare in the beginning of the regular season could determine Green’s future. articles.title: Patriots player on roster bubble with most at stake in 2026 NFL preseason finale
articles.summary: The New England Patriots enter Thursday night’s preseason finale vs. the Cleveland Browns with several unsettled depth-chart decisions. No player better represents the uncertainty surrounding the back of the roster than linebacker Chad Muma. Muma appeared positioned to claim the third linebacker
articles._body: The New England Patriots enter Thursday night’s preseason finale vs. the Cleveland Browns with several unsettled depth-chart decisions. No player better represents the uncertainty surrounding the back of the roster than linebacker Chad Muma. Muma appeared positioned to claim the third linebacker role earlier this summer. He wore the green-dot helmet, communicated the defensive calls, and brought more NFL experience than most of his competition. Two uneven preseason performances have since weakened that advantage while K.J. Britt, Khalil Jacobs, and Namdi Obiazor have strengthened their cases. That reversal makes Muma the Patriots player on the roster bubble with the most on the line vs. the Browns. His roster fate will not depend exclusively on one exhibition game. Still, the finale represents his last opportunity to replace recent mistakes with evidence that New England can trust him on defense and special teams. The pressure leaves almost no room for another setback. Chad Muma’s uneven preseason has altered Patriots linebacker competition Muma entered the NFL as a third-round selection by the Jacksonville Jaguars in 2022. He spent three seasons with Jacksonville before the Jaguars released him during final reductions in 2025. The Indianapolis Colts claimed him, later moved him to their practice squad, and lost him when New England signed him to its active roster in December. The 27-year-old has appeared in 58 regular-season games with seven starts. He played three games for the Patriots last season, primarily on special teams, and dressed for all four postseason contests. That background gave Muma a logical edge over younger players competing to support starters Robert Spillane and Christian Elliss. His early work reinforced that belief. New England trusted the linebacker to relay calls during offseason practices, and he carried that responsibility into the preseason. However, the games exposed problems that a veteran reserve cannot afford. Muma missed four tackles across matchups with the Indianapolis Colts and Philadelphia Eagles. His extended fourth-quarter workload against Philadelphia also showed that the coaching staff still needed more information. The Eagles game illustrated the concern. Muma missed two tackles that produced 30 combined yards and struggled to separate from blocks on runs, gaining 18, 7, and 6 yards. Philadelphia also completed all three passes thrown into his coverage, gaining 50 yards. He diagnosed a screen for a third-down stop and added a run stuff, but those positive snaps did not erase the larger inconsistency. Meanwhile, Britt improved his standing with an impactful opener against Indianapolis. Jacobs earned second-team opportunities before suffering an injury against Philadelphia. Obiazor has handled core special-teams responsibilities and recorded an end-zone pass breakup against the Eagles. None has completely secured a backup job, which keeps the Patriots linebacker competition open entering the finale. Muma still owns a meaningful counterargument. He has accumulated 18 regular-season tackles on special teams throughout his career and understands how to contribute without playing regular defensive snaps. That experience is relevant for a reserve linebacker, especially for a special-teams unit that ranked 20th in DVOA last season. Patriots need Chad Muma to provide a strong finish Muma’s assignment against Cleveland is straightforward even if his roster outlook is complex. He must tackle cleanly, maintain proper leverage against the run, and avoid surrendering easy yards in coverage. He also needs to show urgency across the kick-coverage and protection units, where the Patriots will make several final roster decisions. His health adds another consideration. Muma exited the Philadelphia game late after appearing to play through an injury. That context could explain part of his uneven performance. It also makes Thursday’s workload worth monitoring because his availability will influence the team’s ability to evaluate his response. The decision extends beyond Muma against one direct rival. New England must determine whether to keep four or five off-ball linebackers and whether its current depth is sufficient. The Patriots have received inconsistent play behind Spillane and Elliss, leaving open the possibility of adding a player released by another team after final roster reductions. A strong showing would remind the coaching staff why Muma once appeared to lead the competition. Another uneven performance would give Britt and the rookies more leverage. Neither result alone guarantees the final outcome because practices, injuries, special teams, and outside additions remain part of the equation. That uncertainty is precisely why Muma has the most at stake in the Patriots’ preseason finale. He began the summer with a clear route to a defensive role but now enters Cleveland needing to reestablish his reliability. Thursday offers one final chance to show that his experience still separates him in a crowded competition. articles.summary: The Tennessee Titans and Chicago Bears practiced together Thursday, and the event turned controversial in the blink of an eye, as so many joint practices do. .@Titans QB Cam Ward discusses today’s practice with Bears — and he said it was his fault for putting Wan’Dale Robinson in a position to ta
articles._body: The Tennessee Titans and Chicago Bears practiced together Thursday, and the event turned controversial in the blink of an eye, as so many joint practices do. . @Titans QB Cam Ward discusses today’s practice with Bears — and he said it was his fault for putting Wan’Dale Robinson in a position to take a big hit across the middle. Ward said Robinson is OK. pic.twitter.com/xiRaEEXPHR — Jim Wyatt (@jwyattsports) August 27, 2026 Tennessee wide receiver Wan’Dale Robinson was going over the middle on a a pass pattern, and when Titans quarterback Cam Ward was somewhat late in delivering his throw, the receiver was in a vulnerable position. As a result, Bears safety Xavier Woods delivered a huge hit on Robinson and the receiver hit the ground hard. Robinson was able to walk off the field without assistance a few moments later, but Tennessee head coach Robert Saleh called the hit “cheap” and was frustrated by the force of the blow. Ward met the media after practice and he said that he thought Robinson was fine after the hit and that the Titans wide out would not have to miss time. He also took the blame for the big hit, admitting he did not give Robinson a good throw. “I have to put him in a better situation,” Ward said . “So that’s really more about me than it is about him. But he’s tough. He got up and he’s good. I have to make sure I don’t put him in that kind of position again.” Robinson has played four seasons in the NFL, all with the New York Giants. The 5-foot-8, 185-pound pass catcher signed a free-agent contract with the Titans in the offseason and he is expected to become one of Ward’s go-to receivers. Robinson is coming off back-to-back solid seasons with the Giants. He caught 92 passes for 1,014 yards and 4 touchdowns last season.   The post Titans’ Cam Ward apologizes for getting Wan’Dale Robinson killed by Bears, but there’s a silver lining appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles.title: 20 Businesses Dolly Parton Launched Over Her Career
articles.summary: From a publishing company to a truck stop, Billboard runs through some of Parton's many business ventures.
articles._body: When one says the name Dolly Parton , for most the immediate image that comes to mind is a globally beloved superstar and Country Music Hall of Famer known for her enduring songs, her charismatic personality, larger-than-life style, rags-to-riches story of grit and dedication, as well as her charitable efforts such as her Imagination Library. But longtime Parton fans have also watched over the decades as the East Tennessee native has steadily built a multifaceted business empire that has made her one of the world’s most recognizable, and enduring, stars. Related Dolly Parton’s Manager Details the Business Ventures ‘She Had Yet to Fulfill’ Jessica Nicholson Her songs including “9 to 5,” “Coat of Many Colors” and “I Will Always Love You” established her as a songwriting powerhouse, while her performances, recordings and collaborations helped make her an entertainment legend. In the process, Parton’s business acumen was apparent early on, as she retained ownership of many of the songs she wrote, including famously turning down Elvis Presley ‘s offer to record the Parton-written “I Will Always Love You” because Presley’s manager, Col. Tom Parker , insisted that Parton give up half of her publishing royalties on the song in the process. In a 2020 Billboard cover story , Parton said, “That was one of the hardest things I ever had to do, because I loved Elvis.” Creatively, she proved herself to be adept in multiple lanes, from music to books to movies. Parton has also used her musical success as a foundation for an increasingly diverse portfolio of business ventures, ranging from her famed Dollywood theme park in Sevier County, Tenn., to her soon-to-be opened SongTeller Hotel in Nashville. Beyond music and entertainment, Parton — who died on Aug. 25 at the age of 80 — worked hard to build her name, image and music into a powerful, versatile global brand. That brand has spanned across an array of business and licensing categories ranging from beauty and food to hospitality and pet products. Below, Billboard highlights some of Parton’s abundant business endeavors, partnerships and/or licensing deals that she has launched through the decades, and how she’s turned her songs into an enduring business enterprise. While this list is by no means comprehensive, it helps to highlight the breadth and diversity of the Parton business acumen.

articles._body: The Green Bay Packers had to deal with Josh Jacobs’ arrest earlier this year. And they have a backup plan if he faces a suspension. However, Jacobs is facing reduced charges after his May arrest, according to a post on X by Tom Pelissero. “The Brown County District Attorney has formally charged Packers RB Josh Jacobs with two misdemeanors related to his May arrest. Originally booked on five charges, including felony strangulation, Jacobs now faces reduced charges of misdemeanor battery and criminal damage to property. The NFL has been monitoring all developments in the matter, which remains under review.” Jacobs is a 28-year-old, seven-year veteran. He came over to the Packers from the Raiders back in 2024. In his first season in Green Bay, he rushed for 1,329 yards with 15 touchdowns. Last year, he totaled 929 yards rushing with 13 scores. Packers RB Josh Jacobs could still miss games Jacobs has been available to practice and play since the arrest. But, of course, he could face discipline under the league’s Personal Conduct Policy. Packers general manager Brian Gutekunst said earlier this week that the Packers have made plans if Jacobs faces NFL discipline, according to a post on X by Jason B. Hirschhorn. Packers GM Brian Gutekunst on plans for if/when Josh Jacobs is suspended: ‘We’ve obviously been preparing for that in case that happens. But at the same time, I feel really good about the guys we have in that room.’ ” Some suspension is expected, according to Adam Schefter via NBC Sports. “ESPN’s Adam Schefter said in August that the league would likely suspend Jacobs, though the length of the suspension had yet to be determined,” Denny Carter wrote. “MarShawn Lloyd would likely function as Green Bay’s lead back if Jacobs — who’s dealing with a lingering groin issue — misses regular season games. The oft-injured Lloyd has stayed healthy this offseason and has reportedly run well in training camp and joint practices.” Lloyd played the majority of snaps with the first-team offense in the Packers’ recent preseason game against the Broncos. articles.title: GOP heads to Supreme Court after losing case over TV election ad prices
articles.summary: GOP campaign committees want quick ruling before election ads ramp up next week.
articles._body: Republican campaign committees want the Supreme Court to mandate lower prices for election commercials on broadcast TV stations. If the court agrees, broadcasters would be forced to offer their lowest ad prices to political parties and joint fundraising committees. For a more thorough description of the legal issues in the dispute, see this article that Ars published yesterday. In short, US law requires broadcasters to offer individual candidates the “lowest unit charge,” or LUC, during the 60 days before an election. The law helps level the playing field somewhat by letting candidates make their cases to voters who watch broadcast TV without needing to raise exorbitant sums of money. The Trump administration, acting through the Federal Communications Commission, ordered broadcast TV stations to also give these discounts to political parties and joint fundraising committees, which face fewer limits on how much money they can raise and spend. Four Democratic candidates appealed, and a judges’ panel at the US Court of Appeals for the 4th Circuit ruled that the FCC order cannot be enforced because it contradicts the plain language of US law. articles.summary: The Toronto Blue Jays’ pitching experience has been a roller coaster of a ride this season. After making it to Game 7 of the World Series, the team added Dylan Cease to their starting rotation. The ex-San Diego Padres star is one of the best starters in baseball. Cease was joined by Kevin G
articles._body: The Toronto Blue Jays’ pitching experience has been a roller coaster of a ride this season. After making it to Game 7 of the World Series, the team added Dylan Cease to their starting rotation. The ex-San Diego Padres star is one of the best starters in baseball. Cease was joined by Kevin Gausman, Trey Yesavage, Shane Bieber, and Max Scherzer for much of the season in one of the most star-studded rotations in MLB, but the unit never quite lived up to its potential. In fact, the Blue Jays made some sellers moves at the trade deadline, which included trading away Gausman , a two-time former All-Star. Toronto didn’t completly blow up the ship, and they added some key pieces, too. One highly-praised move was the trade for Jose Soriano, a young and controllable arm who could still help the team push for the playoffs in a tightly contested American League race, despite the fact that Toronto is currently in last place in the division. Toronto just made another move for an arm, too. According to Shi Davidi, the Blue Jays signed Michael Lorenzen, an All-Star as recently as 2023. The Blue Jays will be the eighth major league team that Lorenzen has played for. He was designated for assignment by the Colorado Rockies and then released on Aug. 19. Lorenzen gets a pro-rated portion of the league minimum, and the Rockies are responsible for the remaining $8 million of his salary. The righty hasn’t been great this season, as he has just a 3-11 record and a 7.08 ERA. Some of that can be blamed on pitching a mile above sea level on a really bad team, though, and the Blue Jays will hope he can rediscover his old self as the team tries to make a run. There is a lot of pitching talent in Toronto, so perhaps they can shock the world, just as they did last year. articles.title: Somebody at ESPN thinks this will be Luka Doncic’s final season with Lakers
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Lakers are trying to keep their attention on the basketball court as the ownership drama surrounding the organization continues. The Lakers made some interesting moves this summer after catching wind that LeBron James would be bolting town, trying to give Luka Doncic the best supp
articles._body: The Los Angeles Lakers are trying to keep their attention on the basketball court as the ownership drama surrounding the organization continues. The Lakers made some interesting moves this summer after catching wind that LeBron James would be bolting town, trying to give Luka Doncic the best supporting cast they could put together. However, not everyone is convinced that Doncic will be around for the long haul in LA, as recently, at least one ESPN NBA insider voted that 2026-27 will be Doncic’s l ast season in a Lakers uniform in a poll of experts. Of course, the majority of the panel voted that Doncic will stick around beyond this year, but it was still a jarring sight. “Even with the Lakers’ ownership about to change hands from Mark Walter to Josh Kushner and Bob Iger, it’s hard to imagine the organization suddenly changing directions and not continuing to build with Doncic as the center of its universe. It’s similarly unfathomable to believe that Doncic, who just footed a six-figure bill to host all of his teammates for a minicamp and camaraderie-growing retreat in Slovenia, would suddenly decide that he is done with the Lakers next summer,” noted Dave McMenamin. Still, it’s not hard to imagine Doncic turning the pressure up on the organization if they aren’t very competitive this year, which some fans expect will be the case after the team’s underwhelming free agent “frenzy.” Doncic is squarely in the prime of his career, and with his history of conditioning issues, it’s not exactly a safe bet that his peak years will last long into his 30s. Still, the prospect of him joining a third team in four years is quite difficult to wrap one’s mind around. articles.title: Dolly Parton Had the Second-Most Streams of Any Artist on the Day of Her Death
articles.summary: On this week's Trending Up, we look at listeners flocking to the timeless catalog of the late legend, as well as a resuscitated Dua Lipa hit and another new Tove Lo-spun-off rap hit.
articles._body: Welcome to Billboard Pro’s Trending Up newsletter, where we take a closer look at the songs, artists, curiosities and trends that have caught the music industry’s attention. Some have come out of nowhere, others have taken months to catch on, and all of them could become ubiquitous in the blink of a TikTok clip. Related Fearless, Fabulous Dolly Parton and What We Can All Learn From Her: A Remembrance Dolly Parton’s Top Billboard Hot Country Songs Hits Dolly Parton’s Half-Century Hot 100 Legacy: ‘9 to 5,’ ‘Islands in the Stream’ & More This week: The legendary late Dolly Parton’s catalog experiences a truly jaw-dropping spike from a nation in mourning, while “Training Season” may be both ending and beginning for Dua Lipa and another rapper capitalizes on a perpetually viral Tove Lo hit. Dolly Parton’s Streams Skyrocket by 2,056% on the Day of Her Death It’s been two days, and the music world is still just beginning to process the death of country music and pop culture icon Dolly Parton , who passed away on Tuesday (Aug. 25) at the age of 80. Parton’s death inspired tributes and homages from all across the entertainment realm — and of course from both pop peers and followers too numerous to count — and inspired an explosion of appreciation of her songs, both in the words of those trying to capture her musical impact, and in the streams of those simply hoping to relive it (or experience it new). Consequently, Parton’s catalog experienced an absolutely gigantic surge on Tuesday following the news of her passing. After drawing a little over 1.2 million official on-demand U.S. streams the previous Tuesday (Aug. 18), her streaming totals were all the way up to 26.3 million on the 25th, according to early data provided by Luminate — an eye-popping gain of 2,056%. Leading the way in her catalog were the classics “Jolene” (2.7 million streams), “9 to 5” (2.3 million) and the Kenny Rogers duet “Islands in the Stream” (1.8 million) — all three of which appeared on the Billboard staff’s list of the 100 Best Country Songs of All Time (with “Jolene” topping the entire ranking). To put that 26.3 million number in perspective, that’s the second-highest daily official on-demand U.S. streaming count registered in Luminate of any artist for the date of Aug. 25 — higher even than modern-day streaming super-duperstars like Morgan Wallen (24.2 million), Taylor Swift (22.9 million) and Bad Bunny (14.5 million). The only artist to outpace Parton in streams on Tuesday was Drake, he of the three new albums from a couple months back, with 36.6 million. (Drake’s most-streamed song on the day, however — the former Billboard Hot 100 No. 1 “Janice STFU,” with 1.3 million — would have only ranked as Dolly’s fifth-most.) And the really crazy thing: Those numbers were all with her news of Parton’s death spreading more than halfway into the tracking day — meaning those numbers could be much, much bigger for Wednesday with a full day’s impact, and that Parton may very likely posthumously become the most-listened-to artist in all of America. —  ANDREW UNTERBERGER   Dua Lipa’s ‘Training Season’ Makes a Streaming Comeback Thanks to Marriage-Inspired Manifestation Trend   In online pop conversations, Dua Lipa’s 2024 Radical Optimism LP — which peaked at No. 2 on the Billboard 200 — is often derided for its lack of smashes on the level of the ones that made 2020’s Future Nostalgia a pandemic era-defining, Grammy-winning opus. Now, it looks like the pop star may be getting the last laugh.  According to Luminate, “Training Season,” a Radical Optimism single that stalled at No. 27 on the Billboard Hot 100 during its initial chart run, has risen nearly 50% in streams over the past two weeks. During the week-long period of Aug. 5-11, “Training” collected 1.87 million official on-demand U.S. streams, jumping 9.7% to over 2.05 million stream the following seven-day period (Aug. 12-18). By Aug. 19-25, “Training” streams jumped a further 35% to over 2.79 million official streams.  The recent resurgence is due to a larger manifestation trend that has taken over social media. Back in 2024 during an appearance on The Drew Barrymore Show , Lipa said: “Then we have ‘Training Season,’ which was almost like a manifestation because I believe that… I have to be careful [with] what I write, because sometimes I feel like they can come true, because they become a mantra, then I say them over and over.”  Adding fuel to the fire, “Training Season” dropped on Feb. 15, which happens to be the birthday of actor Callum Turner, who Lipa married earlier this year (May 31). The pair reportedly met around the time the song dropped, giving the manifestation trend even more legs. Edits soundtracked by Lipa’s Royal Albert Hall rendition of “Training Season” started popping up in June, collecting millions of views and hundreds of thousands of likes . By July 3, user @/zoevlachou shared a TikTok of herself posing with prayer hands captioned, “How you’ll find me every night cause Dua Lipa said she manifested Callum with this song.” That clip now boasts over 6.9 million views and 1.3 million likes, giving way to a similar post from user @/mia.perezzzzzzz on July 27, which garnered over 7.7 million views and 1.7 million likes. On Aug. 16, Dua herself hopped on the trend with a post via her @/teamdua.hq account , which 430,000 views.  The official TikTok sound for the live version of “Training Season” currently plays in over 1.3 million posts, while the official TikTok sound for the studio version plays in over 766,000. Additionally, the live version can be heard in 123,000 Instagram Reels, while the studio version appears in a further 246,000.  Dua’s personal “Training Season” may
