articles.title: Good Good Golf Pulls Out of PGA Tour Sponsorship
articles.summary: REUTERS/Nick Lachance
articles._body: Good Good Golf will no longer be the title sponsor for a PGA Tour event in Austin in November, a source familiar with the matter told Front Office Sports . The media and apparel company was set to pay the Tour at least $6 million annually in a multiyear deal before the fallout from an ad for a co-branded driver that depicted one of its founders striking a woman. The Tour confirmed the move in a statement Thursday. “The PGA Tour has been informed of Good Good Golf’s decision to step away as sponsor of the event in Austin, Texas, this fall,” the statement read. “We agree with their decision to use this time to focus on their organization and the work ahead. The PGA Tour believes in golf’s ability to bring people together and create a welcoming environment for all.” The Tour added that the tournament will continue on as scheduled Nov. 12–15, noting an update on sponsorship plans will come at a later date. In a statement of its own, Good Good said it had decided to step away as sponsor of the event “after thoughtful discussions with the PGA Tour and careful reflection. “We recognize that we have work to do as an organization, and our focus right now is on our team, our culture and ensuring we learn from this situation,” the statement continued. “We are grateful for our relationship with the PGA Tour and appreciate their partnership over the years. We remain committed to earning back trust, and we hope to work together again in the future.” Callaway dropped Good Good in the middle of the first round of the Tour Championship, and the controversy has taken over all the buzz at the PGA Tour's $40 million season finale in Atlanta. This is how we got here pic.twitter.com/Y8I3SdjAyD — David Rumsey (@_DavidRumsey) August 27, 2026 The Austin event was set to be titled the Good Good Championship. The event is now merely listed as the “Austin Championship” on the PGA website. Earlier Thursday, Callaway severed its deals with Good Good “effective immediately.” The post Good Good Golf Pulls Out of PGA Tour Sponsorship appeared first on Front Office Sports .

Known as the most prestigious and longest-running awards in Latin music, the Billboard Latin Music Awards ceremony will take place on Thursday, Oct. 22, at the James L. Knight Center in Miami and will be broadcast live on Telemundo and Peacock. The Billboard Latin Music Awards honor the top artists, albums and songs of the year, determined by actual sales, streaming, radio airplay and social data that inform Billboard ‘s weekly charts over a one-year period. As is tradition, the awards will coincide with the 2026 Billboard Latin Music Week, which will return to the Faena Forum in Miami Beach Oct. 19-22. Now in its 37th edition, the weeklong even — recognized as the highest profile and most influential gathering in the Latin music industry — will include exclusive artist conversations, business panels with key executives, its celebrated Billboard En Vivo showcases and countless networking opportunities.  Last year, Bad Bunny was the big winner at the Billboard Latin Music Awards, taking home 11 trophies, including artist of the year. He was closely followed by Karol G and Fuerza Regida, who won six and five awards, respectively. articles.title: The $40 trillion national debt is growing while Social Security goes broke—because wealthy Boomers are collecting over $100k in benefits per year
articles.summary: Boomers are getting 265% returns from Social Security—and the “great wealth transfer” won’t save Gen Z.
articles._body: The United States is entering the most expensive phase of retirement. Some of America’s oldest are eligible for more than $100,000 a year in combined Social Security benefits, while remaining as one of the wealthiest generations in the country. The national debt is rising—just passing $40 trillion this month—and Social Security is set to enter insolvency by 2032, meaning it may already be too late for the generations left behind. The Congressional Budget Office projected in 2023 federal spending on Social Security and medicare will account for 81% of the increase in mandatory spending between 2023 and 2033. In 2026 alone, increases in Social Security and Medicare spending account for nearly half the projected $362 billion increase in mandatory outlays. Interest on the debt is adding even another layer on the stack of debt pancakes. CBO projects net federal interest costs will exceed $1 trillion in 2026 and rise to $2.1 trillion by 2036. That means the government is spending money to simply service the debt accumulated from previous deficits, even as entitlement programs continue growing. The state of Social Security appears to have contributed to drastically different generational outlooks on the benefit. A December 2025 survey by the Cato Institute found that only 34% of Gen Z respondents expected Social Security to exist when they reached retirement. Cato’s June 2026 analysis also found that 79% of younger respondents expected some type of cut to their own future benefits. “The survey revealed that young Americans are the least likely to expect Social Security will exist for them,” the study noted, “the most open to reforms, and the least likely to understand how the program works.” Social Security is a pay-as-you-go program , meaning most payroll taxes collected from today’s workers are used to pay benefits to today’s beneficiaries. In simpler terms, a part of your paycheck subsidizes a boomer’s benefits—and according to the Cato Institute’s 2025 polling, only 45% of Americans correctly understand how the program works. Under current law, employees and employers each pay 6.2% of wages into Social Security up to an annual taxable maximum, which is $184,500 in 2026. Self-employed workers pay the combined 12.4% rate. That structure worked far smoother when there were many workers for every retiree. But the demographic math changed—baby boomers are now moving through retirement while younger generations deal with record job market difficulty. And it doesn’t help that Social Security beneficiaries are getting over double their investment into the program back. A median-wage worker retiring in 2027 is expected to receive roughly $730,000 in lifetime Social Security benefits compared with less than $200,000 in combined contributions from the worker and employer. When the employer contribution is excluded, the lifetime benefits amount to roughly 265% of what the worker personally paid into Social Security. The current system is effectively relying on the workers of today—which include millennials and the younger end of Gen X—to finance retirees. What the government is going to do about it The federal government has reached a point where arithmetic becomes unavoidable. The 2026 Social Security trustees report projects that the Old-Age and Survivors Insurance trust fund will be depleted in the fourth quarter of 2032. At that point, continuing program income would cover only 78% of scheduled retirement benefits. The theoretically combined Social Security trust funds are projected to be depleted in 2034, when incoming revenue would cover 83% of scheduled benefits. Without congressional action, that would mean an automatic reduction in benefits. The Committee for a Responsible Federal Budget estimates the retirement program would face an approximately 22% across-the-board reduction when the retirement trust fund is exhausted. The committee has proposed one way to address the issue—putting a ceiling on the benefits paid to its wealthiest retirees. Dubbed the “Six Figure Limit,” the proposal would cap Social Security benefits at $100,000 annually for a married couple retiring at the normal retirement age, with the limit adjusted for marital status and claiming age. A single retiree’s comparable limit would be $50,000.  The proposal is aimed at an extremely small group. CRFB estimates the cap would only really affect the top 0.05% of couples in its early years, households with average annual retirement income above $2.5 million and average net worth above $65 million. The organization says the cap would become more consequential over time as Social Security’s maximum benefits continue to rise. CBS News reported in March that roughly one million individual Social Security beneficiaries receive at least $50,000 a year, meaning a married couple with two such beneficiaries could receive more than six-figures. The Social Security Administration did not immediately respond to a request for comment from Fortune . Boomers are rich—but no one else will get their wealth Baby boomers collectively hold roughly $93 trillion in wealth, according to Visa Business and Economic Insights, but only about $36 trillion is expected to pass to millennials and Gen X over the next two decades. The difference is reflected in taxes, debt, spending during retirement and the concentration of wealth among the richest boomers. After the dedication in liabilities, about $88 trillion remain—and the top 1% holds about one-third of that wealth. Boomers are also expected to spend approximately $16 trillion during retirement on housing, food, healthcare, prescriptions and other expenses. That means the “Great Wealth Transfer” will not move a $93 trillion pile of assets from retirees to younger Americans. A substantial portion of it will never be inherited, and much of what is transferred will be concentrated among the affluent households. But the Social Security program was created as social insurance, not as a means-tested w

articles.title: Report: Nvidia to acquire AI model repository Hugging Face for $13 billion
articles.summary: Nvidia is nabbing critical infrastructure for open models as interest grows.
articles._body: Nvidia is reportedly moving forward to acquire Hugging Face for $12.9 billion. The acquisition could help the hardware giant expand and fortify its deep integration with the wider AI industry. Among other things, Hugging Face is a cloud repository for AI models, similar in some respects to what GitHub is for conventional computer software. Developers and researchers search for models that meet certain criteria, download and run them, and fine-tune them into different variants that then get uploaded back up to Hugging Face. The deal is not finalized, so it could still run into trouble ahead, but both parties appear to be actively pursuing it, according to a report from The Information, which cites one person with knowledge of the matter. Another source confirmed to CNBC that talks are underway. Hugging Face reportedly had other companies trying to buy it, too, including Salesforce. Nvidia had invested in Hugging Face in the past, but it wasn’t the only one—Google and Microsoft had also invested. The company was founded in 2016. Nvidia and several other tech companies have publicly supported the role of open-weight models as alternatives to the proprietary closed-frontier models trained by companies like OpenAI and Anthropic. Nvidia has even released its own family of open models, called Nemotron.

articles.title: Nas Crowned Icon, Kendrick Lamar Honored as Top Songwriter at 2026 BMI R&B/Hip-Hop Awards
articles.summary: "Luther," producer O Lil Angel and Sony Music Publishing also earn prestigious honors.
articles._body: “Never in a million years did I think I would be partners with BMI. It just shows you that the things you dream about could really happen.” That’s how newly crowned BMI Icon Nas began his remarks after joining presenter Kenneth “Babyface” Edmonds onstage at BMI’s annual R&B/Hip-Hop Awards (Aug. 26). The presentation followed a rollicking performance by R&B/disco diva Evelyn “Champagne” King, who had the entire ballroom audience inside Beverly Hills’ Fairmont Century Plaza dancing and singing along — including a smiling Nas. King performed two of her Billboard Hot 100 hits from the ’80s: “I’m In Love” and “Love Come Down.” The latter song was sampled on the 1997 track “Calm Down” by Capone-N-Noreaga featuring Nas. The evening’s lineup also featured spirited performances from openers Belly Gang Kushington and YKNiece followed by Real Boston Richey, Miles Caton, Tone Stith and Tiana Major9. Large Professor closed the ceremony with a DJ mix of Nas’ biggest hits. In presenting the award to Nas, Babyface — a prior icon honoree — noted, “He’s not an ordinary rapper. He’s a poet and a philosopher.” After thanking both Babyface and King for being important inspirations, Nas said, in part, “Every one of the artists who were appreciated tonight, I appreciate you more. I’m going to stream you more because your genius inspires me, and your genius inspires the whole globe.” Prior to the icon presentation, BMI’s CEO Mike O’Neill, executive vp & chief revenue & creative officer Mike Steinberg and vp, creative/Atlanta Catherine Brewton welcomed the evening’s additional award winners to the stage. Kicking off that drumroll was the rights organization’s recognition of the top producers and songwriters of the previous year’s 35 most-performed R&B/hip-hop songs in the U.S. — which included 63 first-time winners. From there, BMI revealed the winners of its other prestigious awards. Kendrick Lamar was named R&B/hip-hop songwriter of the year for co-writing six of 2025’s most-performed songs including “30 for 30,” “Squabble Up” and “Luther.” The latter, which spent 23 weeks atop Billboard’s Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs tally, was also recognized as BMI’s R&B/hip-hop song of the year. Producer O Lil Angel was named R&B/hip-hop producer of the year. The honor stems from his collaborations with Drake and PARTYNEXTDOOR (“Spider-Man Superman,” “Somebody Loves Me”) plus production credits on the Drake albums Habibti , Made of Honour and Iceman as well as the hits “What Did I Miss,” “Which One” and “Janice STFU.” Named as top producers were D’Mile, Michael “Finatik” Mulé and Isaac “Zac” De Boni of FNZ and Jahaan Sweet. During a special moment, the late songwriter/producer Tay Keith was remembered. His sister and uncle were on hand to accept Keith’s 2025 BMI R&B/hip-hop songwriter of the year award, which was announced at last year’s ceremony. Sony Music Publishing rounded out the winners’ circle with its award for R&B/hip-hop publisher of the year. The company represents 27 of last year’s most-performed songs. Among them: “Luther,” “ Timeless,” “Like Him,” “Yukon” and “25.” Ahead of the awards, the inaugural BMI Foundation Babyface Award was given to songwriter and producer Rijah Banerjee. This competitive grant and mentorship program focuses on emerging songwriters and composers of R&B, hip-hop, soul and other music of the African diaspora. For the complete list of winners for the 2026 BMI R&B/Hip-Hop Awards, visit the organization’s site .

articles._body: The Las Vegas Aces have been dealt a tough injury blow as the playoffs start in a few weeks. Aces forward NaLyssa Smith is set to miss the rest of the season following a leg injury she suffered on Sunday in the team’s victory over the Toronto Tempo. Smith suffered a non-contact leg injury, per Alexa Philippou. “Aces forward NaLyssa Smith will miss the remainder of the 2026 season after suffering a non-contact leg injury on Sunday, the Aces announce. The exact injury and whether surgery is required were not released,” Philippou posted on her X account. The Las Vegas Aces released a statement about the injury on Thursday afternoon. “Las Vegas Aces forward NaLyssa Smith suffered a non-contact, left leg injury at the 3:15 mark of the third quarter of the August 23 game against the Toronto Tempo and will be sidelined for the remainder of the 2026 season.” NaLyssa Smith was having a stellar season for the Aces, who are looking to win their second straight WNBA championship. She started all 38 games that she played for the team this season and averaged 11.7 points and 6.4 rebounds while shooting 63.8% from the field. Before her injury on Sunday, she accumulated eight points, eight rebounds, one assist, two steals, and one block while shooting 4-4 from the field in 19 minutes of play. The Aces currently sit as the third-best team in the WNBA with a record of 26-13. They’re one game ahead in the win column of the Atlanta Dream and have clinched a berth in the 2026 WNBA Playoffs. articles._body: The Miami Heat had a big offseason acquiring Giannis Antetokounmpo, but they also made other moves to help complement him and the rest of the team. The latest move seemed inevitable after rumors over the past few weeks, as Nick Richards is set to join the team, according to ESPN’s Shams Charania. “Free agent center Nick Richards has agreed to a one-year deal with the Miami Heat, sources tell ESPN. After signing Klay Thompson, the Heat fill roster slot No. 14 with a reserve big man,” Charania wrote on X, formerly Twitter. Richards had been practicing at the Kaseya Center for some weeks with other Heat players, so it only made sense that they officially added him to the team. This is a nice move for the Heat, who were in need of center depth after trading Kel’el Ware to the Milwaukee Bucks as part of the Antetokounmpo deal. Last season for the Phoenix Suns and Chicago Bulls, Richards averaged 5.8 points, 5.1 rebounds and 14.6 minutes in 48 games. After signing Richards, the Heat were not done, and they agreed to a two-year deal with Keshad Johnson, according to Michael Scotto of Hoopshype. Johnson had been with the Heat for the past few seasons. It feels like the Heat’s roster is starting to take shape, and they should be ready to go when training camp starts in almost a month. It wouldn’t be a surprise if they added a player here or there before then, but for now, this is a good roster they can go into the season with. Thompson was a key addition for them, and should be competing with Tim Hardaway Jr. for the starting 2 spot on the team. Of course, Thompson is still one of the better shooters in the league, and he should get a lot of open opportunities with Antetokounmpo on the floor. articles.title: Barret Zoph, the Thinking Machines co-founder ousted before joining OpenAI, is now at Google
articles.summary: Zoph, who co-founded Thinking Machines Lab alongside Mira Murati and also served as the startup's CTO, led a brief stint at OpenAI and is now at Google.
articles._body: The game of musical chairs for AI executives continues. Barret Zoph, a co-founder of the AI startup Thinking Machines who left the company earlier this year to rejoin OpenAI, has found yet another job. Zoph spent two years at OpenAI and left in October 2024 to co-found Thinking Machines with Mira Murati, who had left the AI lab the month prior. In January, Zoph and another Thinking Machines co-founder, Luke Metz, quite dramatically departed from the startup to return to OpenAI. It was later revealed that Zoph had been fired. His return didn’t quite stick. Zoph spent only five months at OpenAI, where he was tasked with heading AI enterprise sales. He left the company in June. And now we know where he landed. Zoph has taken a position as vice president of research at Google (which happens to be another company where he previously worked). “We look forward to Barret returning to Google and bringing his RL and post-training expertise to Gemini,” a Google spokesperson told the Wall Street Journal. TechCrunch reached out to OpenAI and Google for more information. It’s not always easy to divine why tech executives seem to be spending less time in their roles. The turnover rate in the AI industry is high, and it’s been especially high at OpenAI — a company that, despite readying itself for an IPO and being one of the most powerful presences in the tech world, has lost a lot of critical staff over the last eight months. The turnover of high-level executives — from the departure of its COO to the recent loss of one of its top data center execs — has left onlookers scratching their heads. This story has been updated to include the fact that Zoph was fired from Thinking Machines.

articles.title: A startup claims it’s found a drug to make your blood young
articles.summary: I knew I’d officially become a ‘longevity influencer’ this month when a company called Generation Lab reached out to offer me the chance to write about—and even receive—their new rejuvenation treatment, an injectable combination of two existing drugs which they call 1 Generation. This wasn’t just an
articles._body: I knew I’d officially become a ‘longevity influencer’ this month when a company called Generation Lab reached out to offer me the chance to write about—and even receive—their new rejuvenation treatment, an injectable combination of two existing drugs which they call 1 Generation. This wasn’t just any antiaging treatment, either. A company fact sheet says that it “blocks the systemic spread of aging in the bloodstream, reawakens the body’s own repair mechanism and restores health and youth to multiple tissues.” The exclusive offer to join a “private cohort” receiving access to the treatment was being “extended to a limited number of people whose judgment on the science we trust, under close physician supervision.” “There’s a long wait list including a lot of celebrities, well-known people, people who you have heard of,” Generation Lab’s CEO Alina Su told me in a conference call. “So we’re super excited to, like, create this drug and [are] letting you know that this first longevity therapeutic in [the] human body is here and it’s actually working.” This was all clearly a marketing campaign and, like most other claims in the world of longevity medicine, probably too good to be true. What’s more, Generation Lab wouldn’t tell me what the two drugs are, making the proposition hard to take seriously. Yet this pitch got my interest. The reason? I am a longtime follower of Generation Lab’s irascible scientific founder, Irina Conboy, a take-no-guff specialist in the bizarre, but scientifically fruitful, practice of joining together the circulatory systems of old and young lab animals. The procedure, called parabiosis, or heterochronic blood exchange, is one of the few things actually proven to make an old animal act younger.   But you can’t go through life attached by the veins to a younger person. So the quest has been to find practical ways to mimic those benefits.  And that is something Conboy says she’s now achieved by hitting on a combination of two existing drugs that produce youthful effects—but without the need for any bodily fluid exchange.  Over the last two months, Conboy has been taking the drug combination and feeling quite a bit better and more energetic, she says. So have a handful of other insiders, including Su, the company’s 26-year-old CEO, as well as Conboy’s husband and scientific collaborator Michael Conboy. The company’s public relations staffer sent me a spreadsheet of the supposed benefits experienced by the participants, including improved vision in a 64-year-old female, longer landscaping sessions for a 59-year-old man, longer badminton games, improved hand grip, better erections than with Viagra, as well as “increased bowel movements.” Obviously, any age-reversal drug that works would be the best-selling product of all time. The problem is that none have ever been shown to do that. And Generation’s approach to evidence raises several red flags. For instance, Su says the company now plans to launch a larger study, involving a hundred or more people. However, these subjects will be asked to pay for their enrollment. Such “pay-to-play” clinical trials are often seen as a sales channel, rather than a scientific pursuit. In addition, the trial will be led by longevity doctors who practice alternative medicine. These include Matt Cook, founder of a network of clinics called BioReset Medical. Cook’s clinics offer what I would characterize as unproven treatments, such as stem-cell injections. A 2021 article reported he’d recommended covid-19 treatments designated as “fraudulent” by the FDA. Those included inhaling amniotic fluid from a nebulizer. In a phone call, Cook says he initially agreed to prescribe the combination to Conboy and a few other insiders. (Everyone involved, he says, is a member of the same “happening” Silicon Valley scene around life extension.) “My confidence this was going to work was a zero. Like, I did not believe it was actually going to work,” says Cook. That is because “it’s two safe, generic drugs that are not even longevity drugs. ” But Cook, who also took the combination, says there was an effect. “And I have to tell you, it was the most surprising thing that ever happened to me,” he says. After taking the weekly injections, he experienced a sense of mental clarity that lasted for a day, and then several days. The other subjects, he says, reported a sense of well-being, as well as old aches and pains that evaporated.  “There was a fairly significant broad set of symptoms that doesn’t really match what either of the drugs do,” he says. “So it’s interesting. [But] I have many more questions than I have answers … I still feel like I don’t understand exactly what the mechanism is.” Prior to joining Generation Lab full time in 2025, Irina Conboy had a long career at the University of California, Berkeley, where she made her name via a widely cited series of experiments aimed at learning   whether the characteristics of age, or youth, could be transferred between animals via the bloodstream. In 2005, for instance, she surgically connected two-month-old mice to very aged ones, finding that the old animals’ ability to heal from injury dramatically improved. This suggested that young blood must contain specific, powerful molecular signals capable of restoring the regenerative capacity of an old animal. As researchers zeroed in on candidate signals, several startups, including Elevian , a Harvard spinout, and Alkahest , tied to Stanford University scientists, were able to raise millions to pursue treatments for stroke or Alzheimer’s. However, those efforts still have not hit commercial paydirt. Although it’s clear that young blood is good for old mice, scientists also know the reverse is true: Even a single exchange of plasma from an aged mouse has powerful, negative effects on a younger animal. That means that in the battle of age versus youth, says Conboy, “old blood dominates.”   Conboy next tried a new approach. Instead

articles.title: Show HN: go-binsync – Go binary patches up to 67× smaller than bsdiff
articles.summary:
This project is a little performance-optimization experiment focused on reducing the size of Go binary patches, which can be useful for quick incremental updates of live services.

When a Go program grows by a few bytes through an incremental change, a bunch of related references and offsets thr
articles._body: This project is a little performance-optimization experiment focused on reducing the size of Go binary patches, which can be useful for quick incremental updates of live services. When a Go program grows by a few bytes through an incremental change, a bunch of related references and offsets throughout the compiled binary end up changing that makes general-purpose binary-diff encoders inefficient: `zstd --patch-from` produces a 530kb patch for a one-line change in a 30MB binary. bsdiff improves upon this (150KB patch) thanks to a delta compression algorithm that can handle relative offsets. go-binsync goes a step further for Go binaries by borrowing an idea from Courgette, the technique Google uses to ship Chrome updates: read the structure the compiler left behind, predict the expected results from that structure, and send only the correction. Courgette gets that structure by disassembling; go-binsync gets more detailed Go-specific structure from additional metadata embedded in every compiled Go binary. The end result is a 2,262-byte patch for the one-line change, or a 67× improvement over the bsdiff result. (For a less synthetic result, a Prometheus 3.13.1 - 3.13.2 patch is still 28× smaller.) Still just a proof of concept (no CGO, no debug symbols, amd64 only) but I thought others might find the initial results interesting. I think this predictive-encoding approach could be generalized beyond Go binaries to efficient compression in other domains where some kind of specialized predictive structure is available. articles.title: Japanese Bitcoin Industry Unveils ‘Aurora’ to Let Global Anime Fans Support $2 Trillion Yen Space
articles.summary: Bitcoin Magazine
articles._body: Bitcoin Magazine Japanese Bitcoin Industry Unveils ‘Aurora’ to Let Global Anime Fans Support $2 Trillion Yen Space Japan Bitcoin Industry Co., Ltd. has debuted a self-custodial Bitcoin payments platform designed to help Japanese companies sell to international fans who are often shut out by traditional payment systems. Using this week’s Bitcoin Asia conference in Hong Kong to introduce the product, JPI dropped Aurora — aiming to reach an audience that could not be serviced before.  The pitch is simple: anime, manga, games, and other Japanese content have a massive global following, but the payment rails supporting that content haven’t kept pace.  香港で開催中のbitcoinasiaに当社取締役の加藤( @btc_dakara ) が登壇します。ビットコインとステーブルコインの関係について登壇者の方々とお話しいたします。 https://t.co/8e1aKAvjgv — 日本ビットコイン産業株式会社 (@JBIinc_bitcoin) August 27, 2026 Aurora aims to close that gap by letting international customers pay in Bitcoin over the Lightning Network , while giving Japanese merchants a simple point-of-sale and API layer to manage invoicing, payment tracking, and integrations. According to JBI, the market for Japanese anime content outside Japan reached ¥2.17 trillion in 2024, up 26% year-over-year — yet many overseas fans still struggle to pay for streaming subscriptions, digital merchandise and limited-access drops due to geographic payment restrictions. The platform’s core design principle is that JBI never touches the money. Each merchant runs its own self-custodial Lightning node, receiving Bitcoin directly from customers.  JBI says this setup gives businesses cleaner regulatory footing, since the company isn’t acting as a custodian, while still handling the harder operational lift — node uptime, liquidity, accounting and auditing, and conversion to fiat — that has historically kept enterprises from adopting Bitcoin payments on their own. JBI says aurora draws on lessons from its existing consumer business, UseBitcoin.jp, which has let customers buy digital gift cards — including au PAY, V-Preca and Kyash cards — using Lightning payments for the past two years. The company is inviting media, prospective merchants and wallet providers to connect with the team at Bitcoin Asia 2026 in Hong Kong. The two-time NBA has often been seen trolling and responding to fans online, especially when they have something to say about him, or his teams. And well, Durant has now sent another
articles._body: There are not many NBA players known for their social media presence more than the Houston Rockets’ Kevin Durant . The two-time NBA has often been seen trolling and responding to fans online, especially when they have something to say about him, or his teams. And well, Durant has now sent another warning to rage baiters who decide to ‘say something’ to him. During his appearance on the Boardroom podcast, the Rockets ace went into detail about the kind of ‘rage-baiters’ he responds to on the internet. "People know if they say something to me, Imma say something back. You're going to leave this interaction feeling f*cked up. Imma hit you in the soul." Kevin Durant on fans who try to rage bait him (via @boardroom ) pic.twitter.com/O7P1yfR9JG — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) August 27, 2026 “People know if they say something to me, Imma say something back. You’re going to leave this interaction feeling f*cked up. Imma hit you in the soul,” he explained. The Slim Reaper was then told that he might be the most ‘rage-baitable’ player in the NBA. However, Durant was quick to respond, claiming that he only responded to people when they talked about personal stuff. The Rockets star then explained that it was a part of him that people wanted to see. “It’s just way personal s**t like, I am way better than you at life, I have accomplished what you wanted to do in life, this type of stuff..You can cheer for me and react to a player but you want to see this part inside of me. So why not?” he said. KD explained that it was the same approach that he took towards basketball, claiming that he was happy he could provide his trollers one of their ‘core moments’ of their life. Needless to say, Durant not only has no intention of stopping his social media antics anytime soon, he also believes fans want to see him respond to their comments on the internet. Hence, fans can expect the ‘rage-baiting’ to continue, with Durant revealing that he tends to think of his replies ‘on the fly.’ The post Rockets’ Kevin Durant sends ‘f****d up’ warning to rage baiters who dare challenge him appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles.title: Pelicans rumors: Did Bennedict Mathurin just leak another new jersey?
articles.summary: Celebrating a cheap free agent signing this late in the offseason is usually not a needle mover unless it’s LeBron James. However, with the ink still drying on Bennedict Mathurin’s deal with the New Orleans Pelicans, the former lottery pick may have already given fans two reasons to s
articles._body: Celebrating a cheap free agent signing this late in the offseason is usually not a needle mover unless it’s LeBron James. However, with the ink still drying on Bennedict Mathurin’s deal with the New Orleans Pelicans , the former lottery pick may have already given fans two reasons to start shopping for new gear. The first is fairly straightforward. Mathurin appears set to reclaim No. 9 after agreeing to a two-year, roughly $16 million contract. The second is far more intriguing than a Skelican in September. Mathurin updated his Instagram profile picture after news of the Pelicans deal broke, using an image of a previously unseen New Orleans uniform. That would normally qualify as harmless introductory artwork for a new signing, and it is, even though the design looks clean. Before fans get too excited for this particular look, it has been confirmed this is just an AI image. The timing makes this one worth a closer look, though. It’s the league’s dead period without much to drum up interest in the new season. Much like the annual trade deadline, the NBA world is expecting something to drop soon. The Pelicans joined the rest of the NBA in a Nike-backed social media campaign teasing something new for September 15. Posts told fans to “Prepare to be obsessed,” accompanied by the date and Nike branding. The campaign has appeared across the league rather than being limited to New Orleans, strongly suggesting a new uniform collection is on the way. But those blues and reds need a refresh, with at least one uniform saying ‘Pelicans’ again, right? That is where Mathurin’s new profile picture becomes interesting. This new profile pic feeds a persistent rumor that Pelicans fans have been trying to will into existence for years. New Orleans could debut two new uniforms this season rather than the more typical single addition or refresh. NBA teams generally rotate through Association, Icon, Statement, and City editions, with special sets for events like the NBA Cup sometimes layered on top. Nike has experimented plenty with its alternate looks while leaving the basic structure of the Pelicans’ primary uniforms largely untouched. Current Pelicans merchandise still features the familiar white Association Edition and navy Icon Edition designs, while the team’s red Crescent City Statement jersey received a more substantial refresh before the 2023-24 season. The annual City Edition program has provided most of the creativity. Perhaps now, if the Skelican rebrand ever becomes official, this Mathurin look becomes more of a callback. And no city does call-and-response better than New Orleans. The biggest question is how fans will respond to the actual, official uniforms being released soon. articles.title: Broncos’ most agonizing roster decision looming on 2026 cutdown day
articles.summary: George Paton has a tough task ahead of himself. The Denver Broncos general manager has to trim the team’s roster down to 53 players on Aug. 30, also known as cut-down day. That won’t be an easy task for Paton because Denver’s roster is loaded with talent. The GM will have to cho
articles._body: George Paton has a tough task ahead of himself. The Denver Broncos general manager has to trim the team’s roster down to 53 players on Aug. 30, also known as cut-down day. That won’t be an easy task for Paton because Denver’s roster is loaded with talent. The GM will have to choose whether or not to keep three quarterbacks on the active roster. Bo Nix is the team’s leader, and he is backed up by Jarrett Stidham, but trying to risk squeezing Sam Ehlinger onto the practice squad could lead to another team scooping him up. Paton also has to manage the off-ball linebacker and edge rusher spots. Inside linebacker is arguably the weakest position group on the team, and a number of players are fighting to earn a spot at LB. The edge rusher position is different. After a 68-sack season, the Broncos are loaded with pass rushers. That will lead to some really good players being cut, though, and there is still uncertainty regarding a potential Jonathon Cooper suspension. No decisions regarding those position groups are what Paton has to dread most, though. So, what is the Broncos’ most agonizing roster decision for cut-down day? The Broncos will have tough decisions to make at running back Brett Davis-Imagn Images The Broncos will have to make many tough cut-down decisions, but what they will do at running back is the biggest question. The team has what appears to be a potentially great three-headed monster. J.K. Dobbins has always been great when he’s been on the field, as was the case during his first season in Denver last year. However, injuries have proven to be an inevitability with Dobbins, and the Broncos need to prepare for situations where he can’t play. Dobbins is backed up by two young ball carriers with loads of potential. RJ Harvey was with the team last year, and his big-play ability was evident right. Harvey wasn’t always efficient during his rookie season, though. The team then drafted Jonah Coleman in the fourth round of the 2026 NFL Draft. The Washington product was considered a perfect fit and a draft day steal by many, and he has reportedly been one of the biggest standouts of training camp. Coleman is also unproven and will surely have some rookie struggles in year one. Regardless, those three players will all be big parts of Sean Payton’s offense. While there is talent and potential in this backfield, there is also inexperience and injury concerns. Rostering more than three running backs seems like a must, especially because it is unclear how much any of Dobbins, Harvey, and Coleman will play on special teams. Jaleel McLaughlin and Tyler Badie are in a battle to earn the fourth the RB4 spot. McLaughlin is a speed threat who has become a fan favorite. He thrives as a pass catcher out of the backfield and as an outside-the-tackles speed back. Badie isn’t as flashy, but he has Payton’s trust. Badie is a versatile player who the Broncos have used in a number of ways, including in pass protection situations. He also has an edge when it comes to special teams talent, too. However, reports suggest that Cody Schrader has outplayed the both of them during training camp, so he has to be considered for a roster spot, too. For peace of mind, Paton will hope that one ball carrier outshines the others during Denver’s final preseason game, but if that doesn’t happen, he will have a super hard choice in choosing who the final running back on the 53-man roster will be. We had to trade a guy who’d won three championships with the t
articles._body: In a recent interview on The Cousins , hosted by Tracy McGrady and Vince Carter, former Warriors president of basketball operations Bob Myers opened up about one of the most difficult decisions of his career. “Trading [Andre] Iguodala. We had to trade a guy who’d won three championships with the team, to sign D’Angelo Russell… As far as a player handling a tough thing, I’ve never seen one do it as well as he did.” Bob Myers on the hardest basketball decision he’s had to make … — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) August 27, 2026 Myers served with the Golden State Warriors in several capacities from 2011 to 2013, eventually being elevated to president of basketball operations. Even with four NBA championships in his tenure, he still identifies trading Andre Iguodala as one of the most difficult decisions of his tenure with the team. “We had to trade Iguodala, who had won three championships with the team, to sign D’Angelo Russell.” Despite the difficult decision, he praised how Iguodala handled the news. “The way he took it, the professionalism… as far as a player handling a tough thing, I’d never seen one do it as well as he did in that moment…Andre looked at me and said, ‘I understand. You gotta do what you gotta do.’ It wasn’t bitter. I’m sure he felt a certain way, but it wasn’t like that.” He noted how Iguodala’s career continued to flourish after the trade. “He ended up going to the Heat and going to the Finals again after that. Going five years in a row with the Warriors, he went six with Miami.” But Myers reflected on the fairness of the situation, specifically for a player like Iguodala, who meant a lot to the Warriors dynasty. “It wasn’t fair. It wasn’t right. When a player does so much for you and your organization, and you make a decision like that, he deserved better. articles.title: In border states, even Trump’s own party wants the Canada fight to be over
articles.summary: Governors, senators, and automakers in Maine, Vermont, and Michigan have spent 18 months warning the White House a trade war with Canada would bite.
articles._body: When U.S.-Canada trade talks collapsed for good last Friday night , the recriminations broke out almost instantly, and not just between Washington and Ottawa. In Maine, Vermont and Michigan—three states with outsized economic exposure to Canada—elected officials from both parties and the executives who run the region’s largest employers have spent the past week saying, in various ways, the same thing: enough. The latest escalation came Monday, when U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer told CNBC’s Squawk Box Canada was to blame for the breakdown, saying negotiators had reached the outline of a deal by Tuesday night only for Ottawa to add last-minute demands. “In the last hours, I think there were things that the Canadians just—you know, they wanted more,” Greer said. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney has offered the mirror-image account , saying the U.S. side introduced “last-minute changes” to proposed terms that were “unfair, uneconomic, and called into question the reliability of any deal.” Politico ‘s reporting on the 72 hours before the deal cratered found the dispute came down to a central sticking point: U.S. tariff rates on heavy-duty trucks, which Canadian negotiators pushed to lower late in the process, though U.S. officials also cited internal turf wars and Carney pointed to American refusal to extend auto-tariff relief to medium- and heavy-duty trucks. The practical result was the same regardless of which account is right: 50% U.S. tariffs on roughly $20 billion of Canadian goods took effect at 12:01 a.m. Aug. 22, and Canada’s retaliatory tariffs on steel, dairy, appliances, agricultural equipment, pulp and paper and electronics are set to hit Sept. 8. Maine’s senators, from opposite parties, agree Maine’s congressional delegation has been unusually unified for a state represented by one Republican and one independent who caucuses with Democrats. Sen. Susan Collins, a Republican facing a competitive reelection race this fall, called the tariffs “a mistake” in an interview with News Center Maine , adding she’d recently met with Canada’s ambassador to press on dairy trade barriers and still wants “the very friendly, economically beneficial relationship” restored. On social media, Collins urged “both sides to return to the negotiating table,” writing on X the on-again/off-again trade talks between the U.S. and Canada lead to “higher costs, risk, and uncertainty for Maine businesses.” Sen. Angus King, the state’s independent senator who caucuses with Democrats, has focused on the lobster industry specifically, warning Canada’s coming 25% tariff on lobster—which takes effect alongside the broader Sept. 8 retaliation—could be compounded if Trump imposes a reciprocal charge on the processed product when it re-enters the U.S. “If the president’s misguided trade war further escalates, the processed lobsters could be taxed again when they are shipped back from Canada to the United States,” King said , noting almost half of Maine’s fall lobster catch goes to Canada for processing. Collins raised the same underlying vulnerability months earlier in a Senate Appropriations Committee hearing , telling Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick Maine’s meat, blueberries, potatoes, lobster, and lumber are largely processed across the border—testimony Lutnick answered by pointing to USMCA rules governing which goods qualify for tariff-free treatment. Vermont’s governor: consistent from the start Vermont Gov. Phil Scott, a Republican, has been arguably Trump’s most consistent GOP critic on this specific issue, repeating a version of the same warning through every phase of the standoff. In July, Scott said flatly : “My feelings on punitive tariffs imposed on Canada have not changed over the last two years and are simply a bad idea that will lead to increased costs on Vermonters.” When the administration briefly paused the tariffs in mid-August, Scott called it a hopeful sign , while noting Vermont still had “a long ways to go to rebuild this relationship with our friends in the north.” When the pause lapsed and the tariffs took effect anyway, Scott’s tone hardened further: “The Trump tariffs are basically taxes—they raise costs for families, farmers and employers on both sides of the border and strain a relationship that has made both countries stronger and more secure,” he said in a statement in late August . Vermont’s exposure explains the persistence: Canada is Vermont’s largest export market by a wide margin, accounting for 31% of the state’s total goods exports in 2025—more than double its next-largest market, according to the U.S. Trade Representative . Michigan’s governor and the Big Three close ranks No governor has been louder than Michigan’s Gretchen Whitmer, a Democrat who has criticized the tariffs since shortly after they were first imposed in February 2025 and escalated her rhetoric as the fight dragged on for roughly a year and a half. “It is a blunt tool. You can’t just pull out the tariff hammer to swing at every problem without a clear defined end-goal,” Whitmer said in an April 2025 speech , warning tariffs risked economic “paralysis.” In an October 2025 keynote address delivered in Canada, Whitmer said tariffs put 1.2 million Michigan jobs at risk, citing the additional 25% tariff already in place on foreign-made auto parts. Whitmer renewed the attack this week after talks collapsed, posting on X. on Aug. 22 Michigan residents were “uniquely impacted by DC Republicans’ ongoing, chaotic tariff wars with Canada,” and that the tariffs amounted to “a tax hike on Michigan families and businesses by raising prices at the grocery store and the gas pump.” Detroit’s auto

articles.title: Bitcoin Again Flirts With $81,000 Ahead of Fed’s Jackson Hole Meeting
articles.summary: Bitcoin Magazine
articles._body: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Again Flirts With $81,000 Ahead of Fed’s Jackson Hole Meeting Bitcoin again closed in on the $81,000 mark on Thursday before dropping again as its stellar week continued.  The leading cryptocurrency was recently trading for $80,236 after notching as high as $80,793 earlier in the day in New York.  Bitcoin is now up more than 2% over the past day after gaining 10% in a week. The coin’s rise comes ahead of Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh’s keynote on Friday where he is expected to talk about digital payments — including crypto.  JUST IN: The Bitcoin Fear & Greed Index is now up to 71, "Greed" Bullish pic.twitter.com/FM05AzGYWt — Bitcoin Magazine (@BitcoinMagazine) August 27, 2026 The Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City will hold the annual event at Jackson Hole, Wyoming, where central bankers, Federal Reserve officials, policymakers and academics will gather to discuss “Financial Innovation: Implications for Payments and Policy.” According to the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City website, this year’s event will touch on how “recent years have seen a dramatic increase in innovation in financial intermediation and payments,” including new technologies such as “cryptocurrencies and stablecoins.”  It will be Warsh’s first major speech as chairman of the Federal Reserve. Warsh, who has made pro-Bitcoin statements in the past, has been reluctant to lower interest rates; President Donald Trump, who nominated Warsh, has since last year pushed for borrowing costs to come down.  Bitcoin in the past has done well in a low interest rate environment.  Bitcoin’s run started last week when it sustained its biggest run in years following positive regulatory news and an announcement from the U.S. Treasury.  But recent positive regulatory news has helped the coin. While a vote on the long-awaited crypto Clarity Act has been delayed until September, President Donald Trump last week said that the bill was a “very, very powerful” piece of legislation, and urged lawmakers to get it over the line.  The proposed law will establish a framework for distinguishing between digital assets that are securities, commodities or payment stablecoins — legislation that the crypto industry has long called for.  And U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent also last week announced the department would double the size of its long-dated bond buybacks.  The news sent yields down lower; lower long-term yields reduces the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding assets like bitcoin and gold, and generally supports risk-on sentiment.  This post Bitcoin Again Flirts With $81,000 Ahead of Fed’s Jackson Hole Meeting first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Mathew Di Salvo .

articles.title: A consultant who once railed against ‘the billionaire boys club’ is now leading opposition to California’s wealth tax
articles.summary: Ned Wigglesworth once blasted big donors for buying influence. Today, he’s helping lead a nine-figure campaign against Prop. 40
articles._body: The consultant who once warned that California’s richest poured millions into politics because they had something to gain is now helping billionaires fight a tax on their fortunes. Ned Wigglesworth , who decried the “billionaire boys’ club of politics” as a campaign finance reformer decades ago, is a key strategist behind Building a Better California, the political organization opposing Proposition 40, the November ballot measure that would impose a one-time 5% tax on Californians worth at least $1 billion. The campaign has already pulled big Silicon Valley money—Google cofounder Sergey Brin alone contributed over $100 million to the group , with venture capitalist John Doerr and crypto billionaire Chris Larsen also putting money into committees fighting the tax. Building a Better California has also reserved $87 million worth of advertising ahead of the vote. It’s unclear what led Wigglesworth from opposing the political influence of California’s wealthy to helping them defeat a tax targeting their wealth. The San Francisco Standard called him a “billionaire whisperer” while citing several interviews with anonymous colleagues of his who described him as a creature of Sacramento lobbying. His LinkedIn profile shows him at several communications firms: founding partner and CEO of Spectrum Campaigns for the past 10-plus years, and previously a partner at Redwood Pacific Public Affairs, Vice President at Goddard Claussen/West and Vice President at the California Medical Association. Presumably, Wigglesworth’s clients have migrated from less to more billionaire-friendly over time; he did not respond to Fortune ‘s requests for comment. But the arc of Wigglesworth’s career reflects a tension that has long percolated through California politics: the Golden State state has produced extraordinary concentrations of wealth and a political appetite for taxing it while relying on the wealthy people and companies behind that prosperity. Gov. Gavin Newsom has been caught in this bind, both an opponent of the billionaire tax and yet an advocate for reducing inequality as it’s become a potent issue for Democrats. Newsom has proposed higher taxes on the ultrawealthy at the federal level and argued that California needs to “democratize our economy” amid the rhetoric of AI-related job loss. As a campaign finance watchdog two decades before the billionaire tax proposition, Wigglesworth warned Californians about what happened when wealthy donors flooded politics with cash. “There’s some very wealthy and powerful special interests who have enough at stake to spend 150 million bucks ,to either defend their turf or improve their bottom line,” Wigglesworth said in 2005 . “These people aren’t spending money out of some benevolent sense of improving societal good, improving the public good. This is about people fighting for their piece of the pie.” “In other words,” Wigglesworth wrote in a 2007 Capitol Weekly column , “they give because they get.” California’s wealth tax battle offers an especially vivid test of Wigglesworth’s (onetime) thesis. Prop. 40 would hit roughly 200 billionaires who lived in California as of Jan. 1 with a one-time levy equal to 5% of their wealth. Supporters say the measure could generate around $100 billion , with most of the proceeds earmarked for health care after federal Medicaid cuts. But for the billionaires affected, the potential bills are enormous, with Brin reportedly owing $13 billion if the measure passes. He and fellow Google cofounder Larry Page moved out of California before the Jan. 1 cutoff and have since amassed roughly $225 million in Miami real estate.  The tax has also sparked public sparring over whether California risks driving away the people who pay an outsized chunk of its bills, with nearly half of the state’s personal income tax revenue coming from the top 1% . Gov. Gavin Newsom opposed the measure on those grounds. Venture capitalist Vinod Khosla said he has no plans to leave California , but has warned the state could permanently damage its tax base if wealthy residents flee.  The sums involved today dwarf even the spending Wigglesworth was warning about more than 20 years ago. California’s 15 richest billionaires had poured more than $336 million into state and federal elections this year , with Brin, Marc Andreessen, Ben Horowitz and Larsen accounting for $331 million of the total. This story was originally featured on Fortune.com

articles.title: Freshman Luke Ertel’s background, composition set him up for success at Purdue
articles.summary: Luke Ertel's background and basketball wiring should make him an ideal fit for Matt Painter and Purdue.
articles._body: FORTVILLE — Luke Ertel ’s now-storied story at Mount Vernon High School started adorably. He was that kid every Indiana high school gym seems to have, the one who’d run out on the floor during every stoppage to shoot baskets, the then-roughly-2-year-old hoisting a ball he was barely big enough to get his arms around toward the rim, too small for the referees to shoo away. He was there with his family watching older brother Michael Ertel star at the school. Most of those shots — if you can call them that — went in. “People would come up to him and video him as he was out in the middle of Michael’s games,” mother Amy Ertel said. “They’d be like, ‘Oh my gosh, this kid .’ That’s how little he was.” Little was it known at that time that those moments on that court and the responses from onlookers then were the first of many, many more to come during the next decade-and-a-half. After Luke Ertel played his last formal game in his home gym, an Indiana All-Star event back in June, he did so wearing the No. 1 jersey reserved for the state’s Mr. Basketball and being looked down upon by the state championship banner he stood tall in hanging over the gym’s northwest entryway. The banner joined three others in Mount Vernon history: Softball’s 2000 title, girl’s basketball’s 2013 Class 3A championship and football’s 4A crown in 2021. Mount Vernon winning both football and basketball titles lately is suggestive of it becoming another high-level high school program born from Indianapolis’ northeast sprawl. It’s no coincidence its ascent occurred in lockstep with Ertel and his family passing through. “We’re still not the size of a (Hamilton) Southeastern, Noblesville or Fishers, or schools of those sizes in 4A,” boy’s basketball coach Joe Bradburn said of his team becoming the state’s first-ever boy’s basketball champion from Hancock County. “We’ve had some success in the lower classifications and things like that, but to come onto the scene and do what we did at the 4A level was phenomenal.” In that sense, Ertel was a transformative figure at his school and by extension in his community, one that has meant a great deal to Ertel, the fifth of five kids to come through the school. En route to Gainbridge Fieldhouse for that state title game, Ertel stopped by the home of Brian Burhenn to deliver T-shirts to commemorate the occasion. Brian Burhenn is the father of current Purdue football player George Burhenn , Ertel’s one-time football teammate, and long a friend and influential figure in the Ertels’ life. As important as that community has been to Ertel, it’s very much gone both ways. Mount Vernon’s black-and-gold filled Gainbridge Fieldhouse for that Crown Point game, very likely the sort of experience Luke Ertel will see again during his college years. In the spring, when Ertel took part in a three-point shootout at Hinkle Fieldhouse during Final Four weekend, he was swarmed by children and adults alike seeking autographs and selfies, not just because he’s moving on to Purdue, but because his reputation in the Indianapolis area following that Mount Vernon state title merited a level of attention few experience. “Luke just loves this place,” Amy Ertel said of Mount Vernon, sitting in the stands before that Indiana All-Stars event back in June. “ Loves it.” Luke Ertel’s response: Gratitude. “Appreciation is our family is really big,” father Mike Ertel said. “We’ll do anything we can to support our kids, but we want appreciation. If you’re passionate about something, we’ll support it. We had a dancer. She loved dance, so we supported that. Both of my other daughters loved volleyball, so we supported that. “But a lack of appreciation will get you. He has that balance of confidence and humility. I don’t know that we did that. Some of it was probably just born into him.” It’s not all that common for players of Ertel’s achievement to not just feel gratitude, but for it to emanate from them. His approach is to take nothing for granted, exhibiting the sort of substance Matt Painter is particularly drawn to. “I’m living out my dream,” Ertel said before enrolling at Purdue. “Mr. Basketball, I get go to Purdue. I’m getting paid to go to college and play basketball. It’s pretty cool.” Purdue’s Luke Ertel (Chad Krockover) ORIGIN STORY He was conditioned for humility, not just by his parents, but by the sometimes-trying existence of any fifth kid in a family full of competitors. “I was kind of a late bloomer growing up, and then I got to where I was, and I just kept that same edge,” Ertel said. “If you have that same edge and you’re skilled, you can dominate high school games, which is what I did throughout my senior year. “I think the biggest thing that shaped me was just believing in myself. My brother and my dad always told me, ‘Who’s going to believe in you if you don’t?’ The biggest thing is having self-belief, and having belief in God. Those things shaped me.” Luke Ertel, today, isn’t necessarily small, but he’s never been particularly big. Size shapes players. Ertel’s has. The lefty guard’s craftiness and keen understanding of angles and leverage are probably the product of a childhood spent playing driveway ball with older brother Michael and neighbor and future college football player Sampson Levingston. “I think it made him tougher, especially basketball-wise,” said Michael Ertel, who scored more than 2,1000 points during stints at Louisiana-Monroe and UAB in college and has played professionally overseas since. “I was a lot older, so I would just destroy him. I was eight years older than him, so he grew up with me pretty much bullying him. I think it helped with his toughne

articles._body: Hi HN, I’m Theo. I built AgentCloud because at Fiber we use Cursor Cloud a lot but cannot test our ios app on it. articles.title: Rams reunite with Tutu Atwell in trade with Dolphins
articles.summary: Some would say the Los Angeles Rams are trying to build the NFL’s super team after adding Myles Garrett and trying to get Aaron Donald out of retirement. They’re also bringing back one of their wide receivers, as they made a trade with the Miami Dolphins to acquire Tutu Atwell, accord
articles._body: Some would say the Los Angeles Rams are trying to build the NFL’s super team after adding Myles Garrett and trying to get Aaron Donald out of retirement . They’re also bringing back one of their wide receivers, as they made a trade with the Miami Dolphins to acquire Tutu Atwell, according to ESPN’s Adam Schefter. “Trade: Dolphins traded WR Tutu Atwell back to the Los Angeles Rams in exchange for RB Jarquez Hunter, sources tell ESPN,” Schefter wrote on X, formerly Twitter. Before signing with the Dolphins this offseason, Atwell spent his first five seasons in the league with the Rams. In those five seasons, he’s caught 105 passes for 1,535 yards and five touchdowns. The Rams’ wide receiver room is loaded with talent that starts with Puka Nacua and Davante Adams, but with Atwell’s familiarity with the team, he could make a case to be the WR3 on the team. He’ll have to work for that spot, and it’ll be interesting to see if he plays in their preseason finale. It was going to be hard for Hunter to get playing time with the Rams, with their running back room already solidified. He can now carve out a real role for himself on the Dolphins as they look to build depth around De’Vone Achane. The Rams continue to add the talent to their team needed to compete for a championship, and they’re one of the favorites to go all the way this season. It won’t be that easy, as they’re in one of the toughest divisions in the league, and the reigning Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks will have something to say about that. articles._body: Can 10-time All-Star Anthony Davis and Trae Young lead the Washington Wizards to snap a six-year playoff drought? The Wizards should have a better idea two months into the 2026-27 regular season. If not, Davis could once again be on the move, according to one ESPN NBA insider. Amid his third team in two seasons, Davis is entering his first full season with the Wizards, which could end up being his last , as ESPN’s Tim MacMahon noted. “Davis and the Wizards are essentially opening the season on a trial period. That’s quite a stark contrast to the franchise’s partnership with Trae Young, the other former All-Star that Washington acquired before last season’s trade deadline — and signed to a four-year, $213 million extension this summer that raised eyebrows around the league,” ESPN insiders reported. “Davis and his agent, Klutch Sports CEO Rich Paul, haven’t been coy about their desire for a maximum (or close to it) contract extension. That was a driving factor in Dallas’ decision to trade Davis a year after he was the headliner in the return of the Luka Doncic deal, and it made finding a market for him difficult.” If the Wizards, who inked Trae Young to a $212 million extension after his mid-season trade from the Atlanta Hawks, aren’t willing to pay Anthony Davis what he wants, trading him ahead of next season’s deadline makes the most sense for Washington. However, winning helps. If the Wizards are to emerge as a playoff team with potential to make a deep run, things could change for Davis’ future beyond the upcoming season. articles.title: Every Role Cast in the Snoop Dogg Biopic So Far, From Dr. Dre & 2Pac to Snoop Himself
articles.summary: 'Snoop' hits U.S. theaters on Aug. 6, 2027.
articles._body: Snoop Dogg is the latest rapper to bring his life story to Hollywood. The hip-hop legend broke the news that production was already in motion in April on a biopic simply titled Snoop while speaking at CinemaCon in Las Vegas, and the Universal Pictures film is slated to hit theaters across the U.S. on Aug. 6, 2027. The biopic will be directed by Hustle & Flow ‘s Craig Brewer, while 8 Mile producer Brian Grazer is set to produce the film alongside the West Coast rap legend. “After my brothers told their story in Straight Outta Compton , it’s my turn,” Snoop said at CinemaCon in reference to N.W.A’s 2015 biopic. “[Brewer] just showed us how hard it is out here for a pimp from Hustle & Flow . And then last year, he got us all singing ‘Sweet Caroline,'” he added of Brewer’s 2025 film Song Sung Blue . Fellow rap deities like 2Pac, The Notorious B.I.G ., Eminem, N.W.A and 50 Cent have all had movies made at least loosely about their life stories, and now it’s Snoop’s turn to hit the silver screen. Snoop is still releasing new music more than 30 years into his career and he’s completed unfamothable side missions, like being a correspondent for the Olympics and co-hosting a cooking show with Martha Stewart. The Snoop movie has already started to make casting announcements, with roles carved out for 2Pac, Dr. Dre, Suge Knight and Warren G, all of whom played a significant role in Snoop’s music career, as well as Snoop himself. Find the entire cast for Snoop (so far) below. ( This list will be updated.)

articles.title: South Carolina women’s basketball: Gamecocks will host Thanksgiving tournament
articles.summary: South Carolina will host three HBCUs for the PowHER Player Classic on Thanksgiving weekend. The event is organized by Rae Rose Media.
articles._body: South Carolina will host three HBCUs for the PowHER Player Classic on Thanksgiving weekend. The event is organized by Rae Rose Media.  The HBCUs participating in the event are Tennessee State, NC Central, and Alabama A&M. Tennessee State and NC Central have ties to the Gamecocks. Tennessee State is coached by Candice Dupree, a WNBA great who played for Dawn Staley at Temple. NC Central is coached by former Gamecock Olivia Gaines. The event begins on Thursday (Thanksgiving) with a holiday-based community service event. Friday will focus on an NIL Marketplace. The pre-tournament events will include sponsor activations for all four participating teams as well as educational and networking sessions for potential future partnerships. Friday’s events will include a Culture Night Kickoff Dinner hosted by Rae Rose. What does this mean for the Gamecocks? Chris Wellbaum and fellow subscribers are discussing it now on the Women’s Basketball forum. The first round of games is on Saturday, November 28. NC Central and Alabama A&M face off first, followed by Tennessee State and South Carolina. On Sunday, the winners of the first two games will match up, as will the losers. Game times will be announced later. “To me, basketball has always been a vehicle for access and opportunities, and our game has grown to where those go well beyond just what happens on the court,” Dawn Staley said in a statement. “I am passionate about making sure no young women who pour into our game get left behind in those expanding prospects, regardless of where they play. That was the inspiration for this event, and I’m so proud to work with Rae Rose Media to bring it to life this season.” Rae Rose Media first teased the event back on July 21 with a graphic featuring four blurred-out logos. Rae Rose is the marketing agency that has worked with South Carolina in the past on NIL projects such as the NCAA selection watch party. South Carolina has played an HBCU in 15 of Staley’s 18 seasons. With the announcement of the PowHER Player Classic, South Carolina’s non-conference schedule is nearly complete. Teams can play up to 32 games this season, plus three exhibitions, and with 16 SEC games, that leaves up to 16 non-conference games. South Carolina also has two more exhibitions to announce. South Carolina does not have to schedule all 16. The last time the Gamecocks played in Paris, they scheduled one less non-conference game to accommodate the travel. South Carolina currently has 12 officially confirmed games. There are two more at the Players Era Championship, which have not been officially confirmed by the organizers but have already leaked.  That means South Carolina could still schedule two more games. The current non-conference schedule: September 27 vs College of Charleston (Exhibition) (at Credit One Stadium, Charleston) November 2 vs Maryland in Paris (OuiPlay) November 8 vs North Carolina in Charlotte (Ally Tipoff) November 12 at Clemson November 15 vs Southern Cal in Greenville, SC (Real SC) November 21 at Providence November 24 vs UConn in Uncasville, CT (Hall of Fame Showcase) November 28 vs Tennessee State (PowHER Player Classic) November 29 vs Alabama A&M or NC Central (PowHER Player Classic) December 3 at Duke (ACC/SEC Challenge) December 6 vs Oklahoma State December 16 vs UAlbany December 19 vs UCLA in Las Vegas (Players Era Championship) December 20 vs Notre Dame in Las Vegas (Players Era Championship) December 28 vs Gardner-Webb What do you think? Join the discussion on the Women’s Basketball forum.

articles.title: Show HN: Telem – Route agent web search across providers and inspect the traces
articles.summary:
TL;DR: Web search open router that routes agent web search across providers (Exa, Parallel, Tavily, Brave, SerpAPI etc.), and traces web search results with quality metrics, so you can visualize whether a bad agent run is a web search problem or a reasoning problem.

I work in venture capital, a
articles._body: TL;DR: Web search open router that routes agent web search across providers (Exa, Parallel, Tavily, Brave, SerpAPI etc.), and traces web search results with quality metrics, so you can visualize whether a bad agent run is a web search problem or a reasoning problem. I work in venture capital, and before that I worked in information retrieval. When agents went viral, I built a due diligence agent for my day job. I vibe-coded the first version. It was pretty bad. My first reaction is to blame the model. I tried to change backend models, maybe because Fable doesn't want to help me do people search? Maybe because GPT 5.5 overthinks things? I tried DeepSeek, Kimi, Qwen; I changed prompts again and again, no good. Then I stopped just simply checking the final answer and started reading the actual trajectories: what did the agent search for? What came back? What pages did it read? At what point agents were off the rail? Pretty interesting: Sometimes the agent is stuck and confused because the information provided is irrelevant or even wrong; Sometimes the agent keeps iterate the same query, like "XXX lab UCB CS PhD founder 2026" "2026 XXX lab machine learning systems students startup" because the web search provider is not up-to-date; Sometimes sub-agents give up too early because the agent's intelligence is not enough or too "guardrailed"; Sometimes everything is just slow. A run jeopardized at minute 1 but still ran for another 10 before returning nonsense. That's because of bad searches, but nothing reveals it. So I built two things: 1. Web Search/Fetch router: One gateway for Exa, Parallel, Tavily, Brave, Ceramic, Linkup, Seltz, You, SerpAPI, etc. You or your agent can pick one or query several concurrently, and the responses come back in a homogeneous format. 2. Web Search Observability: Trace every search your agent (and its sub-agents) makes with an evaluator scoring relevance, diversity, and a few other things. Point is to answer one question: is your pipeline broken because the web search is bad? If so, where? Everything is agent-operated. All u need to do is to run this shell script: https://docs.telem.ai/alpha_install.sh | sh> Please give it a try, any feedback/suggestion would be great! Especially I’d like to ask: how are you debugging search/retrieval failures nowadays? Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49469804 Points: 8 # Comments: 2

C heck out our UFC Shanghai odds series for our Nurmagomedov-Song prediction and pick. Now the surging contender looks to keep climbing the bantamweight ladder as he comes into this fight this weekend against Song Yadong. Song Yadong (23-9, 1 NC) rebounded from a decision loss to Sean O’Malley at UFC 324 by submitting Deiveson Figueiredo via second-round guillotine choke at UFC Fight Night in Macau this past May, earning Performance of the Night. Fighting on home soil in China, the surging contender now looks to build on that momentum as he comes into this fight this weekend against Umar Nurmagomedov. Song Yadong, meanwhile, dropped a decision to Sean O’Malley at UFC 324 before rebounding with a submission finish over Figueiredo, but that O’Malley loss revealed he can struggle against elite competition when his striking gets neutralized. Umar’s wrestling pedigree, part of the famed Dagestani lineage that includes his cousin Khabib Nurmagomedov, gives him a dimension Song has rarely had to solve throughout his career. Seven of Umar’s twenty career wins have come by submission, showing real finishing ability once he secures top position. That grappling threat should force Song to fight cautiously and give up the center of the cage, playing directly into Umar’s methodical, control-heavy approach. Fighting on the road in Song’s home country of China adds pressure, but Umar has proven he can execute a fight-long strategy regardless of hostile atmosphere, as shown in his composed performance against Figueiredo. Expect Umar to mix in timely takedowns, control Song against the fence for long stretches, and grind out a clear decision win that reestablishes him as the top contender in the bantamweight title picture. Why Song Yadong Will Win Song Yadong enters this fight with real momentum, having just submitted Deiveson Figueiredo via second-round guillotine choke in May and earning Performance of the Night for the effort. Fighting in front of a Chinese crowd gives Song a genuine home-field advantage that Umar Nurmagomedov, competing on foreign soil, simply won’t have access to in this fight. That environment could prove decisive in close, competitive rounds. Song’s diverse skill set, with nine knockout wins mixed into his career total, shows he can end fights standing or on the mat, unlike a more one-dimensional grappling approach. His recent submission win over Figueiredo also proves his ground game has improved significantly. Umar’s only loss came against Merab Dvalishvili, and while he bounced back with decisions over Bautista and Figueiredo, none of those performances showed explosive finishing ability, suggesting he may lack the firepower to keep Song off balance. Song’s veteran championship experience, including a competitive decision loss to Sean O’Malley, means he’s already tested himself against elite bantamweight talent and adjusted accordingly heading into this matchup. Expect Song to use his home crowd energy, mix his striking with underrated grappling defense, and either find a finish late or edge out a competitive decision to hand Umar his second career loss. Final Umar Nurmagomedov-Song Yadong Prediction & Pick Umar Nurmagomedov enters this bantamweight showdown looking to build on his bounce-back stretch, having outpointed Mario Bautista and Deiveson Figueiredo since his lone career loss to champion Merab Dvalishvili. Song Yadong brings real momentum of his own after submitting Figueiredo in May, but that O’Malley loss at UFC 324 exposed vulnerabilities against elite, high-IQ competition that Umar can exploit. Umar’s Dagestani wrestling pedigree gives him a clear path to neutralize Song’s power, and with seven submission wins on his résumé, he has the tools to threaten finishes once he secures top position against the fence. Fighting on the road in Song’s home country adds pressure, but Umar has shown the composure to execute his game plan regardless of hostile crowd energy. Expect Umar to time his entries, control extended stretches on the mat, and grind out a clear, workmanlike decision that reestablishes him as the division’s top contender heading into a potential title shot. Why Denise Gomes Will Win Denise Gomes arrives in Shanghai riding a four-fight win streak, including a Performance of the Night finish over Elise Reed in just 30 seconds of the second round, showing the kind of finishing power that has separated her from the rest of the strawweight pack. Yan Xiaonan, meanwhile, is coming off a decision loss to Virna Jandiroba and has dropped two of her last four outings, suggesting her championship window may be closing as younger, more explosive fighters emerge . Gomes’ striking numbers are elite, landing at a high volume with real knockout power in her hands, seven of her wins by knockout compared to Yan’s slower, more decision-reliant style built around veteran craft rather than fight-ending power . Final Yan Xiaonan-Denis Gomes Prediction & Pick Yan Xiaonan looks to defend home turf in Shanghai against a red-hot Denise Gomes, who arrives on a four-fight win streak highlighted by a 30-second knockout of Elise Reed. Expect an early feel-out period where Yan tries to establish range and counter, but Gomes’ volume and power should eventually take over.
