articles.title: Texas women’s basketball schedules games against Ohio State, TCU in Fort Worth
articles.summary: Texas women's basketball is returning to the site where the Longhorns punched their ticket to the 2026 Final Four. Here's more on that.
articles._body: Texas women’s basketball has not shied away from tough competition during the Vic Schaefer era. The 2026-27 schedule will be no different. The Longhorns are officially playing Ohio State and TCU at Dickies Arena in Fort Worth this season, the university announced Thursday. The matchup against the Buckeyes takes place on Nov. 22. Then the Horns go back to the site of their Elite Eight triumph that sent them to the Final Four in March to take on the hometown Horned Frogs on Dec. 6. These are the first two non-conference regular season games Texas has announced. The games are a part of what is being dubbed the “Lone Star Series” sponsored by Wild Horse Sports Management. “In creating our schedule for this season Wild Horse Sports provided us two tremendous opportunities to compete in the state of Texas in the Fort Worth area,” Texas Head Coach Vic Schaefer said in a statement. “Some of our fans don’t have the opportunity to get to Austin very often, so it was really an easy decision, especially with the chance to play two great opponents in Ohio State and TCU.  Two well coached teams always in the Top 25, always in the NCAA tournament. Adding these two games along with our existing elite games, it’s another very difficult non-conference schedule.” *** Join InsideTexas.com for 75% off an annual subscription today *** Texas will play UConn in an exhibition in Connecticut on Oct. 19 and UCLA in another exhibition at the H-E-B Center on Oct. 25. The Longhorns are expected to announce late December regular season games against Duke and UCLA in Las Vegas soon as well, getting at Schaefer’s point about “existing elite games.” The Buckeyes went 27-8 last season and lost as a No. 3 seed in the second round of the NCAA Tournament to No. 6 seed Notre Dame. The Horned Frogs were a No. 2 seed and made it all the way to the Elite Eight before falling to No. 1 seed South Carolina. Kevin McGuff has been the head coach at Ohio State since the 2013-14 season. His teams have been to the NCAA Tournament nine times in that span, including each of the last five seasons. OSU has lost in the second round of the tourney three years in a row now, however. Mark Campbell will be going into his fourth season at TCU. The Horned Frogs have been to the Elite Eight in each of the last two seasons. They need to replace superstar point guard Olivia Miles , though, who is tearing up the WNBA in her rookie season. Texas, of course, has to replace a lot from last year’s team as well. The Longhorns have done their best on that front with five of the most talented freshmen in the country coming in this year as well as two transfers and a late addition in the form of 21-year-old Australian Jayda Clark this week. Texas will figure out a lot about how the new faces work together against Ohio State and TCU early in the year.

Why Aoriqileng Will Win Aoriqileng brings serious knockout ability into this matchup, having finished Cody Gibson in a lightning-fast 21 seconds and racked up an extensive 26-13 professional record built on aggressive, high-volume striking. That kind of finishing instinct and sheer experience edge, with 39 total professional fights, gives him a wealth of tools to draw from against Kai Asakura. Asakura, despite his own knockout power, started his UFC tenure 0-2, including a submission loss to Tim Elliott, showing real vulnerability once he’s taken off his feet or forced to defend on the mat. Aoriqileng’s aggressive forward pressure could similarly expose gaps in Asakura’s defensive grappling if he chooses to change levels. Fighting on Chinese soil at UFC Shanghai, Aoriqileng also benefits from a supportive home crowd, an environment that has historically fueled strong performances from Chinese fighters on these cards. That energy could help him push through any early adversity against a striker of Asakura’s caliber. Aoriqileng’s recent TKO loss to Cody Haddon came via strikes rather than exposing any grappling deficiency, meaning his durability concerns are stylistic rather than fundamental. If he can control range, mix in takedown threats, and press his superior volume, his well-rounded attack and home-crowd momentum should be enough to hand Asakura another setback. Final Kai Asakura-Aoriqileng Prediction & Pick Kai Asakura enters this bout with genuine confidence for the first time in his UFC career, having snapped a rocky 0-2 start with a first-round knockout of Cameron Smotherman this past May. That left-hook finish earned him Performance of the Night and proved his power translates against legitimate UFC competition. Aoriqileng, by contrast, is coming off a second-round TKO loss to Cody Haddon, a fresh setback that snapped his own momentum after a blistering 21-second knockout of Cody Gibson. That recent finish loss raises real questions about his durability heading into another dangerous striking matchup. Asakura’s RIZIN pedigree gives him elite composure under bright lights, and his improved adjustments since that early UFC skid suggest a fighter finding his rhythm at the perfect time. Expect Asakura to use sharp footwork to draw Aoriqileng into exchanges, land his signature left hook clean, and capitalize on the same durability issues Cody Haddon exposed. Look for Asakura to close the show with another first or second-round knockout, extending his UFC winning streak with a statement performance in Shanghai. articles.summary: Utah WR coach Chad Bumphis shares some key updates about his group ahead of the start of the season.
articles._body: Versatility has become the word of the year for Utah football with one week to go until the start of the season. Utah wide receivers coach Chad Bumphis not only has an extremely deep room this season, but it’s also versatile. For a program like Utah that doesn’t have a long history of great wide receiver rooms, this is a refreshing situation to be in. At this point this offseason, this room looked to be six deep. But now this room could go nine deep due to how fall went. That number of viable players keeps everyone on their toes, according to Bumphis. “The guy behind you can do just as much as you can. It’s a good thing. It’s a competitive room, and they push each other. It’s one of the closest rooms I’ve ever been a part of, and they just love each other. But there is real depth. I think we have everything we need. And again, we’re not there yet. We have to keep climbing, keep making those plays, and continue to sharpen what we have. But we’re really close,” Bumphis said. Braden Pegan is picking up steam: The Utah State transfer has been praised countless times since stepping on campus for not only his leadership but his play. Bumphis says that Pegan has gotten even more comfortable with his new surroundings in Salt Lake City. Pegan was named to the leadership council earlier this week, showing why Bumphis called him ‘a true leader in every sense of the word.’ Pegan’s play has also taken a major step forward just days before the season kicks off. “You’ve seen him toward the back half of camp make some of those plays that he wasn’t making early on, so it’s been good. And then again, as you see his level of play raised, the rest of the room’s doing the same. So it’s good to have him here. He feels good about the system, and he’s happy here. So it’s been really good.” Don’t sleep on these two pass catchers: Both Mana Carvalho and Tobias Merriweather weren’t available back in the spring as they recovered from injury, but the pair have really shown out on the field during camp. Merriweather has been an extremely strong leader for this WR room even when he was injured. He was also named to the leadership council this fall. According to Bumphis, the final scrimmage of camp was one of Merriweather’s best days. “He’s another one just getting more comfortable. Obviously, a new system, but again, as you see yourself start to make those plays, it just continues to go. And I tell them all the time, it’s contagious. So when you see one guy make one, then it just spreads throughout the room. So it’s been huge for him,” Bumphis said. Carvalho broke onto the scene last year as a punt returner, but he is on the path to carving out a role for himself in this offense as well. “He’s a real ball in hand guy. And now that he’s healthy, he’s made a bunch of plays for us. So feel good about him. He’s an ideal slot receiver. You can just put the ball in his hands and let him go. He runs really good routes and has great hands. So really excited about Mana,” Bumphis said. Later, Bumphis said that Carvalho and Creed Whittemore are the top two true slot receivers on this year’s squad. articles.title: Lincoln Riley on DC Gary Patterson at USC: ‘I can’t wait to be on the same sideline’
articles.summary: Lincoln Riley knew his defense needed a boost this offseason, so he went out and got former TCU head coach Gary Patterson. He’s raved about Patterson all offseason long and the newly minted College Football Hall of Famer will be on the USC sidelines as the Trojans’ new defensive coordinator. Going u
articles._body: Lincoln Riley knew his defense needed a boost this offseason, so he went out and got former TCU head coach Gary Patterson . He’s raved about Patterson all offseason long and the newly minted College Football Hall of Famer will be on the USC sidelines as the Trojans’ new defensive coordinator. Going up against a defense like that every day in practice is only good for the USC offense. And Riley is surely glad Patterson is on the same sideline as him this year, considering the two had battles when they were at Oklahoma and TCU, respectively. $19.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage “Well, it’s huge. It’s huge,” Riley told Big Ten Network . “You, it’s hard to explain to people what it’s like sitting in that chair as a head coach, unless that person’s done that. And Gary’s obviously not only done it, but done it at an all-time level. So, having his expertise and being able to to talk with him about all the different things that come at the head coach has been has been great for myself for our program, and then certainly, I’d say, standard defensively that he brings into the building with the track record to prove it.  “His leadership that way I think has been invaluable, and you feel his burning desire to be to be elite defensively and to play the way that he expects to play … Our players feel it, our coaches feel it, and I think that that permeates the entire program. It’s been a lot of fun being on this side and not competing against him and having him with us. And I can’t wait to be on the same sideline with him.” Gary Patterson motivated by opportunity at USC Patterson last coached TCU from 2000-21 as their head coach, going 181-79 and won six conference championships in a variety of leagues. He was then a special assistant to head coach Steve Sarkisian at Texas in 2022 and then a consultant for Baylor in 2024, but this is his first big return to the sidelines. Being out of coaching for five years in this type of capacity could lead to questions on how Patterson’s adapted. But Riley sees a competitive fire that is needed at USC. “So he’s incredibly motivated,” Riley said. “He wouldn’t have done this without it, and I think he senses the opportunity to even for a guy that’s accomplished just about everything you can in this game, there’s a few other things left out there, and he knows that he can do that here.  “And so it’s been awesome working with him. I can’t wait to get into the season with him and go. But he and our entire staff are, you know, I think bring a lot of advantages to our program.”

articles.title: John Cena makes ‘fall’ promise for future WWE appearances
articles.summary: It is known that John Cena has wrestled his last match, but don’t expect him to ever get physical again and take a bump, even as a WWE ambassador. Speaking to Conan O’Brien (via Fightful), Cena said that he will never be seen “falling down” again in the ring. He will appea
articles._body: It is known that John Cena has wrestled his last match , but don’t expect him to ever get physical again and take a bump, even as a WWE ambassador . Speaking to Conan O’Brien (via Fightful), Cena said that he will never be seen “falling down” again in the ring. He will appear in non-physical capacities only. “After 23 years of tenure there, and now I need to let the audience know, I don’t want to confuse the audience of ‘he’s going to do something physical.’ I’ve said, ‘I’m not going back to falling down.’ I’m just not,” he said. “It’s not conducive to the goals I’ve set for myself. I’m still curating what the personality is. It’s over when you walk away from it. “As long as I’m still involved, WWE is my family and I’ll never leave until they throw me out. I have to continue to evolve. In doing that, my first rule is ‘don’t confuse the consumer.’ Show up in a different outfit so they know you’re not getting your hands dirty. I’m far more of a promoter and salesperson,” Cena continued. Don’t expect John Cena to take bumps in post-WWE retirement appearances Joe Camporeale-Imagn Images. Cena is leaving his days of physicality behind in retirement. It’s understandable, as he had a long career in WWE and is now 49 years old. Over the last decade, Cena has become a full-time actor. He can do more without as much physicality in Hollywood. Cena probably wants to keep it that way. Plus, he gave WWE fans a full year to see him take bumps for the last time. His retirement tour went for the entirety of 2025, bringing him around the world for audiences everywhere. The tour culminated with a match at Saturday Night’s Main Event on Dec. 13 against Gunther. Cena lost by tapping out for the first time in years. The post John Cena makes ‘fall’ promise for future WWE appearances appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles.title: Kentucky WBB finalizes 2026-27 non-conference schedule
articles.summary: Kentucky women's basketball's 2026-27 schedule has been finalized after a few new opponents were revealed on Thursday.
articles._body: Kentucky women’s basketball’s 2026-27 schedule has been finalized. UK announced the completed non-conference schedule on Thursday , revealing a few new games that we didn’t already know about in the process . We now know the dates for all 30 regular-season games (plus Big Blue Madness and the SEC Tournament) this coming season, with most of the start times and TV assignments set to be announced at a later date. There will be no preseason exhibitions this season, either. As for the newly unveiled games, Kentucky is set to play in the Daytona Beach Classic in the days after Thanksgiving. The Wildcats will face Maine on Friday, Nov. 27 (3:30 p.m. ET) and then South Dakota State on Saturday, Nov. 8 (3:30 p.m. ET) at the Ocean Center in Daytona Beach, FL. The other previously unknown game will come against Le Moyne on Sunday, Dec. 13 (12:00 p.m. ET). It will be a road matchup for Kentucky, taking place at Donald J. Savage ’51 Basketball Arena in Syracuse, NY — the only true road game on the non-conference slate. Why this opponent and why this venue? It’s more so a homecoming game for a trio of UK players who are familiar with that area: Clara Strack , Emily McDonald , and Savvy Swords . Le Moyne was bumped up from Division II to Division I in 2023 and is now part of the Northeast Conference. Five 2026 NCAA Tournament teams. One WNIT champion. Two national TV showcases. The 2026-27 nonconference schedule is set! : https://t.co/pudZWykvwX pic.twitter.com/Q2OyMtJHZH — Kentucky Women’s Basketball (@KentuckyWBB) August 27, 2026 As for some other non-conference scheduling notes, Kentucky will face five teams that made the 2026 NCAA Tournament: NC State, South Dakota State, Clemson, Louisville, and Virginia. The latter two made it to the Sweet 16. South Dakota State made it to the NCAA Tournament after winning the Summit League Tournament. Meanwhile, Marshall is coming off a WNIT championship victory. There will also be four in-state opponents on the docket (Morehead State, Northern Kentucky, Bellarmine, and Louisville), along with a pair of home games at Rupp Arena against Louisville and Clemson. articles.title: Sydney Colson says Aces’ A’ja Wilson should win MVP, calls out ‘greatness fatigue’
articles.summary: As with many giving Las Vegas Aces center A’ja Wilson “GOAT” status, standing for Greatest of All Time, the star could be well on her way to capturing a fifth Most Valuable Player (MVP) award. With Wilson cementing herself as a WNBA legend with the Aces, this former player would
articles._body: As with many giving Las Vegas Aces center A’ja Wilson “GOAT” status , standing for Greatest of All Time, the star could be well on her way to capturing a fifth Most Valuable Player (MVP) award. With Wilson cementing herself as a WNBA legend with the Aces , this former player would give an insightful take on the type of fatigue that is out there if others feel anybody else should win MVP. Former player Sydney Colson would speak on Yahoo Sports and was asked who their MVP is, as she mentioned Wilson, expressing that there is a “greatness fatigue” in the WNBA, as she has already won four MVPs. “My MVP? Probably A’ja. I think people, a lot of time, have like…greatness fatigue, but for some reason with the WNBA, they do, and I just think that that’s gonna be something that’s not seen for a long time. Like, we’ve had the like 6’3″, 6’4″ point centers and other people who have, you know, like the Stewies, but Candace Parker in the past, A’ja, they’re kind of a mold that isn’t around anymore,” Colson said. . @SydJColson says A'ja Wilson is her pick for 2026 WNBA MV'P "People a lot of time have greatness fatigue … that's gonna be something that's not seen for a long time." (via Yahoo Sports Daily) pic.twitter.com/XHVhE52NAp — Yahoo Sports (@YahooSports) August 27, 2026 The other stars in the WNBA MVP race aside from Aces’ A’ja Wilson So far this season with the Aces, Wilson is averaging 26 points, 9.5 rebounds, 3.2 assists, and two blocks per game while shooting 52.1 percent from the field and 40.7 percent from beyond the arc. The other two stars in the race are Minnesota Lynx’s Olivia Miles and Indiana Fever sensation Caitlin Clark, and while Colson shouts them out, it doesn’t mean that Wilson’s extraordinary play is undermined. “Fortunately, we have a lot of talented guards that are in the running that are gonna be in the league for several years,” Colson said. “Whether it’s Kelsey [Mitchell], CC [Clark], probably Olivia Miles is gonna get one soon. Like, there are a lot of other guards who are gonna get it for several years as well. But I don’t think that means A’ja should be counted out because she’s still doing it right now.” It remains to be seen if Wilson wins her fifth MVP or another star gets the honor. articles.title: Titans’ Robert Saleh calls out Bears player for ‘cheap’ hit after Wan’Dale Robinson injury
articles.summary: The Tennessee Titans are taking part in joint practice with the Chicago Bears, and Wan’Dale Robinson had to leave practice due to an injury, according to head coach Robert Saleh. It must not have sat well with Saleh, as he used a specific word to describe the hit that Robinson took from the
articles._body: The Tennessee Titans are taking part in joint practice with the Chicago Bears, and Wan’Dale Robinson had to leave practice due to an injury, according to head coach Robert Saleh. It must not have sat well with Saleh, as he used a specific word to describe the hit that Robinson took from the Bears. “Titans HC Robert Saleh said WR Wan’Dale Robinson left practice to be evaluated for a concussion and called the hit he took from a Bears player ‘cheap'” Ari Meirov of The33rdTeamFB wrote on X, formerly Twitter. #Titans HC Robert Saleh said WR Wan’Dale Robinson left practice to be evaluated for a concussion and called the hit he took from a #Bears player “cheap.” https://t.co/FfVKRAHPfs pic.twitter.com/jjIIuhCFq4 — Ari Meirov (@MySportsUpdate) August 27, 2026 Injuries are a part of the game, but it’s also good to note that players shouldn’t be going too hard in practice. There have been several instances during the past few weeks where teams involved in joint practices have gotten into scuffles, but no players were hurt in the process. It doesn’t sound like the Titans and Bears were in a scuffle during Robinson’s injury, and it just happened to be during a play. Hopefully, Robinson is able to recover quickly and doesn’t have to miss substantial time, especially with the season starting in a few weeks. The Titans are looking to have a better season than they did last season, and with Saleh in place, their culture should already be set in place for them to be competitive. It will start with Cam Ward and the offense, and the hope is that the quarterback takes a Year 2 leap. With Saleh being a defensive guy , that side of the ball should be much improved as well, and it’ll be interesting to see how they perform.   The post Titans’ Robert Saleh calls out Bears player for ‘cheap’ hit after Wan’Dale Robinson injury appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles.title: AI industry says Trump plans to tax chips in the “single dumbest way imaginable”
articles.summary: Tech industry is perplexed by Trump’s plan to win AI race by taxing data centers.
articles._body: Donald Trump may be preparing to announce sweeping new semiconductor tariffs at the absolute worst time, the tech industry fears. On Thursday, Politico reported that a wide range of new semiconductor tariffs, which the tech industry expects will “doom” artificial intelligence innovation in the US, could be imposed in the coming “weeks or months.” About eight people familiar with the Trump administration’s plans were granted anonymity to discuss how the tariffs might work. They suggested that the framework for tariffs may change as it becomes finalized, but one approach under consideration could “dramatically expand the number of tech products subject to the duties, hitting not just chips but potentially many of the goods made with them, such as gaming consoles or the servers that fill data centers.” Read full article Comments

articles.title: Dave Dombrowski announces 4 front office moves ahead of playoffs
articles.summary: The Philadelphia Phillies are making a push for the playoffs. They are 74-60 and trail the Atlanta Braves by 4.5 games in the National League East. Plus, they trail the Chicago Cubs by two games in the National League Wild Card standings. Meanwhile, the front office is making some upgrades before
articles._body: The Philadelphia Phillies are making a push for the playoffs . They are 74-60 and trail the Atlanta Braves by 4.5 games in the National League East. Plus, they trail the Chicago Cubs by two games in the National League Wild Card standings. Meanwhile, the front office is making some upgrades before October rolls around. On Thursday, President of Baseball Operations Dave Dombrowski officially released the names of front-office personnel who received promotions. Dan Aucoin was promoted to Assistant General Manager, Research, and Information. Furthermore, Luke Murton was promoted to Assistant General Manager, Hitting. Plus, Ray Robies was promoted to Director, Minor League and International Operations. Finally, Edwin Soto was promoted to Manager, Baseball Administration. Murton and Soto received newly created positions. The Phillies today made several personnel moves in baseball operations. pic.twitter.com/Zt9WVySx7D — Philadelphia Phillies (@Phillies) August 27, 2026 The latest changes are part and parcel of a changing structure within the organization all year long. After a 9-19 start in April, the Phillies fired manager Rob Thomson and brought on Don Mattingly. Afterward, the Phillies went on a tear and compiled a 64-41 record under Mattingly. Now they are within reach of possibly securing a postseason spot in some way, shape, or form. In Dec. 2020, the Phillies announced Dombrowski as the first-ever President of Baseball Operations in franchise history. Under his tenure, the organization has made advances in winning division titles, bolstering the roster, and being a consistent postseason presence. In 2022, he oversaw the Phillies reaching the World Series for the first time since 2009. Later that year, Dombrowski signed a three-year contract extension through 2027. He is expected to receive another contract extension this winter. The post Dave Dombrowski announces 4 front office moves ahead of playoffs appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles.title: Bitcoin is having a great month—but Solana is doing even better as coin soars above $100
articles.summary: Investors have found fresh reasons to buy Solana beyond Bitcoin’s comeback.
articles._body: Bitcoin may have broken $80,000 , but Solana is stealing the spotlight. SOL, the blockchain’s native token, climbed more than 23% over the past week, with much of that gain coming in the past 24 hours. The token recently crossed $100 for the first time since February and now trades at $107, according to crypto analytics platform CoinGecko. Solana’s price surge coincided with record-breaking trading volume in Solana exchange-traded funds. On Tuesday, Solana reported that its ETF cumulative inflows hit a record $1.2 billion, with nearly $34 million coming in on Monday alone. It marked the biggest single day so far this year, capping five straight days of inflows.  The total stablecoin value on Solana approached $16 billion on Thursday, according to data aggregator DefiLlama, giving investors more readily available dollar-backed liquidity on the network. These gains have come during a more favorable stretch for crypto markets. Last week, the Treasury Department announced a series of bond buybacks, which investors interpreted as a sign that more cash could circulate through financial markets. The rebound marked a sharp reversal from the crypto downturn that began last October. When investors anticipate more liquidity, they tend to take on more risk by investing in speculative assets like crypto.  Bitcoin rose first and lifted the broader market, but Solana has outperformed many other altcoins, a catchall term for tokens other than Bitcoin. “$SOL is moving upwards here, but as you can see, the bear market lasted for a year and we’ve not even gained 20% of that back. Great period upon us,” wrote crypto analyst Michael van de Poppe.  Alongside its price, Solana has benefited from signs of growing network activity. Bitcoin’s appeal rests largely on its fixed supply and store-of-value narrative, while Solana’s case depends more on its ability to support fast, low-cost trading and other decentralized finance applications. According to DefiLlama, Solana’s decentralized exchanges handled nearly $56 billion in trades over the past 30 days and have processed more than $10 billion so far this week. Some of that activity came from memecoin trading , which has increased sharply in recent weeks. Solana’s low transaction costs and Pump.fun, a popular token-launch platform, have made it a popular venue for traders to quickly buy and sell such highly speculative tokens. But the volume can disappear as fast as it arrives and does not necessarily signal lasting demand. Still, the numbers do not show that investors are broadly abandoning Bitcoin for Solana. U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs drew more than $232 million in net inflows on Thursday and recorded daily trading volume of $8 billion, according to crypto analytics platform CoinGlass. This story was originally featured on Fortune.com

articles.title: No Fork Required: Bitcoin’s First Quantum-Safe Transaction Just Happened
articles.summary: Bitcoin Magazine
articles._body: Bitcoin Magazine No Fork Required: Bitcoin’s First Quantum-Safe Transaction Just Happened Should fund managers dealing in Bitcoin be worried about the threat of quantum computing ?  The short answer is yes — but there’s time to prepare and solutions are already being found. One of them? Post-quantum Bitcoin transactions on the mainnet. And the first one happened this week thanks to the Starknet Foundation.  JUST IN: The first post-quantum resistant Bitcoin transaction was mined today. "It required no soft forks. It required no hard forks. It required no core protocol upgrades. And it's live today." pic.twitter.com/YyZbHhm8HI — Bitcoin Magazine (@BitcoinMagazine) August 27, 2026 Speaking at Bitcoin Asia in Hong Kong on Thursday, Damian Chen, VP of growth at the Starknet Foundation, demonstrated how funds vulnerable to future quantum attacks can be secured without requiring a network-wide fork, thanks to the company’s latest solution.  “This is a monumental moment,” Chen said. “This is the first post-quantum-resistant Bitcoin transaction on bitcoin mainnet today. It required no soft forks; it required no hard forks; it required no core protocol upgrades, and it’s live today.” The transaction happened using a method created by StarkWare researcher Avihu Levy. It works like this: Bitcoin transactions sit briefly in a public queue before confirmation. During that window, they expose cryptographic material that a sufficiently powerful quantum computer could use to forge a signature and steal the funds before the transaction is confirmed. But rather than accepting the first valid signature, his method generates millions of signature candidates until it finds one with a specific structural property that doesn’t expose that vulnerable material while waiting in the mempool.  This “signature grinding” is deliberately computationally expensive — a single transaction takes hours to produce — but that cost is what makes it resistant to quantum shortcuts. Touting Quantum safe Bitcoin transactions — dubbed “QSB” — to institutions, Chen said that even if attackers have a fund’s private keys, they couldn’t make a fraudulent transfer.  “QSB introduces a new hash authorization, and so an attacker with a sufficiently capable computer, even if they have your exposed public key, even if they derive your private key from your public key, even if they try to use that to authorize a spend to move your coins out of your wallet, those things are not enough for them to do so,” he said.  It’s worth noting that ordinary Bitcoin nodes currently don’t recognize this non-standard transaction format, so it couldn’t go into the public mempool and instead had to be handed straight to a miner willing to accept it — with mining company MARA’s Slipstream service being the one that mined the QSB transaction.  Quantum researchers have warned that a time will come when Bitcoin’s software — which underpins the biggest and strongest computer network in the world — will need to be upgraded to deal with quantum computing.  While some crypto VC firms have urged action, top Bitcoin developers have argued that many of today’s quantum computers have limited capabilities, and have only demonstrated trivial computations.  Still, they have noted that their development could arrive unexpectedly — just like advances with artificial intelligence — and have started developing some solutions.  Chen added: “The question to me has never been when will quantum arrive. We all know quantum will arrive at one stage, but the question to me has always been, how long will it take for you to be ready when quantum does arrive?” This post No Fork Required: Bitcoin’s First Quantum-Safe Transaction Just Happened first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Mathew Di Salvo .

articles.title: ESPN experts hit Lakers with ultimate diss in ‘biggest tumble’ poll
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Lakers have had an eventful offseason, headlined by the loss of LeBron James in free agency and the sign and trade for Walker Kessler, among other moves. The Lakers are currently trying to keep their focus on the court as their ownership drama continues, with no end in sight. Rece
articles._body: The Los Angeles Lakers have had an eventful offseason, headlined by the loss of LeBron James in free agency and the sign and trade for Walker Kessler, among other moves. The Lakers are currently trying to keep their focus on the court as their ownership drama continues , with no end in sight. Recently, ESPN conducted a poll of its analysts, and one of the questions asked was which team will be the most disappointing this season, or take the biggest tumble from last year. The Lakers ended up getting the most votes of any team in the league. “If L.A. can’t build on its last two 50-win seasons, the team’s handling of LeBron James’ exit will be called into question all over again,” noted Dave McMenamin of ESPN. It’s unclear what expectations the publication is projecting the Lakers to disappoint relative to outside of just last year’s record. Few if any pundits consider the Lakers to be legit title contenders this season, not as long as the Oklahoma City Thunder and San Antonio Spurs are in the Western Conference. Beyond them, teams like the Minnesota Timberwolves, Houston Rockets, and Denver Nuggets are also widely expected to be better than Los Angeles this season, so the team having an early playoff exit or not securing home-court advantage in the first round wouldn’t exactly be a shock. Still, Luka Doncic isn’t getting any younger, and the clock is starting to tick on Rob Pelinka and company to put a competitive team around him. It’s unclear whether the Lakers’ free agency signings of Quentin Grimes and others will be enough to give Doncic a legit supporting cast, alongside newly re-signed Austin Reaves. The Lakers are set to kick off their new season on October 21 against the Golden State Warriors. articles.title: Ken Rosenthal reveals new information about Diamondbacks’ Ketel Marte drama
articles.summary: The Arizona Diamondbacks are likely to have infielder Ketel Marte back on the active roster Monday when he is eligible to come off the injured list. Shortly before he disappeared, Ketel Marte told some teammates that he felt like he wasn't needed, @Ken_Rosenthal was told. "He seems to be someone
articles._body: The Arizona Diamondbacks are likely to have infielder Ketel Marte back on the active roster Monday when he is eligible to come off the injured list. Shortly before he disappeared, Ketel Marte told some teammates that he felt like he wasn't needed, @Ken_Rosenthal was told. "He seems to be someone who needs positive reinforcement." pic.twitter.com/C1q8YF2wzg — Foul Territory (@FoulTerritoryTV) August 27, 2026 Marte left the Diamondbacks earlier in August when the team started a series in Boston against the Red Sox. The Diamondbacks placed him on the Restricted List when he was a no-show Aug. 17 at Fenway Park. Manager Torey Lovullo has been a big supporter of Marte, but he was clearly disappointed when the three-time All-Star didn’t show up and he couldn’t put his name in the lineup. That apparently will change Aug. 31 when the Diamondbacks host the Phillies. MLB insider Ken Rosenthal explained that the player’s absence was keyed by Marte’s feeling that the team did not need him while he was recovering — and still playing — from a knee injury. Rosenthal explained that Marte will feel somewhat down about his play as a season is progressing and that led to his absence. He has since spoken with Lovullo and general manager Mike Hazen and both apologized and tried to explain his actions. The Diamondbacks responded by moving him from the Restricted List to the Injured List. Marte is one of the best second baseman in Major League Baseball and an elite player on the Diamondbacks. He will make their lineup better and more effective as the team fights for a National League Wild Card playoff spot in the final weeks of the season. Marte is slashing .249/.314/.446 this season, and while those numbers are down compared to the last three seasons, he has hit 21 home runs and driven in 67 runs. articles.title: Bills GM Brandon Beane reveals what really happened with failed in-division trade deadline deal
articles.summary: Buffalo Bills general manager Brandon Beane addressed the circumstances surrounding an unnamed in-division trade that failed to materialize before the 2025 NFL deadline. WGR 550’s Sal Capaccio asked Beane during an interview Wednesday how far the negotiations had progressed. Capaccio also asked w
articles._body: Buffalo Bills general manager Brandon Beane addressed the circumstances surrounding an unnamed in-division trade that failed to materialize before the 2025 NFL deadline . WGR 550’s Sal Capaccio asked Beane during an interview Wednesday how far the negotiations had progressed. Capaccio also asked whether the Bills had a deal in place that the other team pulled away, or whether talks ever reached that point. Capaccio posted Beane’s response on X, formerly Twitter. “In that context of last year, it was what was said to be what it would cost. Okay, it was a moving target, and ultimately, they were not willing to trade in division.” So what exactly happened at the trade deadline last year? Did the Bills have a deal in place that was pulled away from them? Did it ever get that far in the first place? I asked GM Brandon Beane during our lengthy interview today. Here’s what he said: pic.twitter.com/SbeqSNfEOe — Sal Capaccio (@SalSports) August 26, 2026 Beane pointed to two problems: the stated price moved, and the other club would not complete a trade within the division. That account explains why the pursuit ended from Buffalo’s side. It does not resolve the proposed compensation or how close the sides came to an agreement. Beane did not name the opposing team or the player. He also did not say the Bills had completed an agreement that the other team later withdrew. His wording shows Buffalo worked from a stated price, then watched that price move as talks continued. Beane’s distinction matters when assessing Buffalo’s unsuccessful deadline pursuit. A changing asking price does not necessarily mean both teams had accepted the same terms. Likewise, discussions that advanced significantly would not constitute a completed trade without final approval from both organizations. Beane did not name the other party, so the exchange remains an unidentified divisional negotiation. Reporters would need evidence beyond Capaccio’s post to connect his answer to a specific team or player because Beane’s remarks do not establish either identity. The comments nevertheless provide a direct account of the breakdown from Buffalo’s top football executive. The Bills worked from a stated cost, that cost moved, and the other club would not complete an in-division trade. The post Bills GM Brandon Beane reveals what really happened with failed in-division trade deadline deal appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles.title: Steelers rumors: Adam Schefter provides Joey Porter Jr. update
articles.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers and Joey Porter Jr. have still not come together on a new deal, and the cornerback will continue to sit on the sidelines until something is done. The latest update from ESPN’s Adam Schefter is that both sides are not close on a number, which means this could get drag
articles._body: The Pittsburgh Steelers and Joey Porter Jr. have still not come together on a new deal, and the cornerback will continue to sit on the sidelines until something is done. The latest update from ESPN’s Adam Schefter is that both sides are not close on a number, which means this could get dragged out for some time. “They haven’t appeared to be close either to a deal, and they’ve never gotten close, and he’s still not practicing, Schefter said on the Pat McAfee Show. “He’s on PUP with a back injury, and backs are often confused with contractitis. They’re waiting on him, and he’s waiting on them, and that doesn’t seem to be going anywhere. I want to point out, we’re headed into what is always a very interesting weekend, where teams go from 90 to 53, and there are trades made, a lot of trades of people rounding out their roster. "The Steelers and Joey Porter Jr have never gotten close to a deal.. Could the Steelers get an offer that would be enough to make them think about trading Joey Porter Jr" ~ @AdamSchefter #PMSLive pic.twitter.com/rucdUcTDzI — Pat McAfee (@PatMcAfeeShow) August 27, 2026 “Could the Steelers get an offer that would be enough to make them think about trading Joey Porter Jr., and who would that be? Who would be willing to give up what it takes to get the player and pay the player? T here aren’t a lot of people that could do that this time of the year.” Porter has been in trade rumors over the past few weeks, but someone has to want him. What makes it even more difficult is that someone has to pay him the money he wants, and as Schefter said, most teams’ resources are cut short during this period. That leaves the Steelers in a position where they may just need to find common ground with Porter. He’s their best corner, and his stats prove that he deserves to get paid, but it looks like the Steelers are offering less than what he desires. The post Steelers rumors: Adam Schefter provides Joey Porter Jr. update appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles.title: Eugenio Suarez, TJ Friedl clear waivers after Reds’ roster decision
articles.summary: With the Cincinnati Reds featuring young stars Sal Stewart and Elly De La Cruz, the team has been having a relatively disappointing year, leading the team to make some key moves. As the Reds put Eugenio Suárez and TJ Friedl on waivers, the next step of the process has been revealed, as they have
articles._body: With the Cincinnati Reds featuring young stars Sal Stewart and Elly De La Cruz, the team has been having a relatively disappointing year, leading the team to make some key moves. As the Reds put Eugenio Suárez and TJ Friedl on waivers , the next step of the process has been revealed, as they have cleared waivers. According to Cincinnati beat reporter C. Trent Rosencrans of The Athletic, Suárez and Friedl cleared waivers, as both players will be with the Reds for the start of the series against the Chicago Cubs on Friday, according to C. Trent Rosencrans of The Athletic. How the times have changed as Cincinnati signed Suárez to a one-year, $15 million contract back in February, viewing him as a potential piece that could help bring the club back to the postseason, which would be the team’s second straight time. When the Cincinnati Reds signed free agent Eugenio Suárez to a one-year, $15 million contract in early February, they viewed him as a slugger who could help them to a second straight postseason appearance. Fast forward to the present, and with them last in the NL Central, the team chose to put Suárez and Friedl on waivers, per Ken Rosenthal. Instead, in the latest indication of a season that has gone awry, the Reds have placed Suárez and outfielder TJ Friedl on outright waivers, according to people briefed on the process. The Reds attempted to save money So far this season with the Reds, Suárez recorded a .208 batting average with 19 home runs and 57 RBIs, while Friedl has hit a .158 batting average with three home runs and 11 RBIs in 76 games. Rosenthal would say that the attempt to put the two on waivers was for the team to “save money,” though he predicted both would remain with the club, “unless the Reds move to cut ties by designating one or both for assignment.” “Suárez, 35, is owed slightly less than $3 million for the rest of the season; Friedl, 31, slightly more than $700,000,” Rosenthal wrote. “Neither is expected back next season.” It remains to be seen what the future of Suárez and Friedl looks like. The post Eugenio Suarez, TJ Friedl clear waivers after Reds’ roster decision appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles._body: UFC Shanghai: Umar Nurmagomedov vs Song Yadong continues on the main card with a fight between Alex Perez and Sumudaerji in the flyweight division. C heck out our UFC Shanghai odds series for our Perez-Sumudaerji prediction and pick. Alex Perez (26-10, 1 NC) is set for a rematch after his last meeting with Su Mudaerji ended in a no contest due to an accidental groin kick in May 2026, a bout that followed a first-round TKO win over Charles Johnson at UFC 324 that January, as she comes into this fight this weekend against Sumudaerji. Sumudaerji (19-7, 1 NC) is set for a rematch against Alex Perez after their May 2026 bout ended in a no contest due to an accidental groin kick that left Perez unable to continue, a result that followed a clean unanimous decision win over Jesús Santos Aguilar in March 2026 to extend his winning stretch, as she comes into this fight this weekend against Alex Perez . UFC Shanghai Odds, courtesy of DraftKings . UFC Shanghai Odds: Alex Perez-Sumudaerji Orolbai Odds Alex Perez: +180 Sumudaerji: -218 Over 2.5 rounds: +100 Under 2.5 rounds: -130 Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Why Alex Perez Will Win Alex Perez enters this rematch with a massive experience advantage, having compiled 37 professional fights against some of the flyweight division’s toughest names. That kind of championship-rounds pedigree gives him a deep well of tools to draw from against Sumudaerji, who has built most of his success against comparatively less battle-tested competition. Perez also carries a unique scouting advantage into this fight, having already shared the cage with Sumudaerji once before their May 2026 meeting ended prematurely due to an accidental groin kick. That firsthand look at range, timing, and tendencies gives Perez a head start no other Sumudaerji opponent has had . Perez’s finishing arsenal is genuinely diverse, with seven knockouts and seven submissions among his 26 career wins, showing he can win in multiple ways. Sumudaerji, despite his power, has only one submission in 19 career victories, suggesting his path to victory is far more one-dimensional if the fight goes to the mat . Perez also enters off a sharp first-round TKO finish of Charles Johnson at UFC 324, proving his power and finishing instincts remain sharp even against live UFC-level competition. Given his superior well-roundedness, unmatched experience, and unique tactical insight from their aborted first encounter, expect Perez to exploit any grappling opportunities and control the pace to a clear decision win. Why Sumudaerji Will Win Sumudaerji brings home-cage advantage into this rematch, fighting in front of a supportive Chinese crowd in Shanghai, an environment that has historically fueled Chinese fighters performing above expectations on these cards. That kind of crowd energy could push him through any early adversity against Alex Perez . His power is legitimate, with 13 knockouts among his 19 career wins, an 68% finishing rate on the feet that makes him dangerous in every exchange. Perez, despite his own finishing ability, was submitted by Asu Almabayev as recently as November 2025, exposing real vulnerability on the mat that Sumudaerji’s power could exploit if he can keep the fight standing. Perez’s 37-fight professional career, while impressive for its depth, also means significant accumulated damage over more than a decade of competition. Sumudaerji, comparatively fresher and younger, could benefit from that wear as the fight extends into the later rounds . Sumudaerji’s recent unanimous decision win over Jesús Santos Aguilar showed he can also grind out rounds when needed, adding a dimension beyond his obvious knockout power. If Sumudaerji can use his home-crowd momentum and heavy hands to press forward early, his power and freshness could be enough to finally finish what their first meeting left unresolved, securing a statement knockout win. Final Alex Perez-Sumudaerji Prediction & Pick Sumudaerji looks to settle unfinished business with Alex Perez at UFC Shanghai, running back their May 2026 bout that ended in a no contest after an accidental groin kick left Perez unable to continue in round two. Fighting in front of his home crowd, Sumudaerji brings elite knockout power into this rematch, with 13 of his 19 career wins coming by knockout and 11 finished in the first round, a finishing rate that should worry Perez heading into the cage . Sumudaerji enters as the betting favorite at -160 to -235 across sportsbooks, reflecting real confidence in his power and home-field advantage translating into a cleaner outcome this time around. Expect Sumudaerji to pick up where the interrupted fight left off, pressing forward behind heavy hands and looking to close the show early. Look for him to find the finish in the opening two rounds, avenging the no contest with a clean knockout win in front of an electric Shanghai crowd. Final Alex Perez-Sumudaerji Prediction & Pick: Sumudaerji (-218); UNDER 2.5 Rounds (-130) The post Alex Perez vs. Sumudaerji prediction, odds, pick for UFC Shanghai appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles.title: Dolly Parton Wanted Her Doctors to ‘Try Experimental Drugs’ on Her ‘in the Hope of Helping Others,’ Sister Says
articles.summary: "She left the world a better place by being in it, so let's follow her example," Stella wrote.
articles._body: Dolly Parton ‘s sister Stella Parton has spoken out following the legendary musician’s death, sharing an emotional statement that highlights how Dolly was a beacon of generosity until the very end. Related Miley Cyrus Mourns Her Godmother Dolly Parton: ‘I Have an Angel by My Side’ Dolly Parton Remembered by Reba McEntire, Paul McCartney, George Strait & More: ‘We Will Always Love You’ Dolly Parton’s Imagination Library Program Honored by Library of Congress: ‘Titan of Children’s Literacy’ “My big sister Dolly got her wings this past Tuesday,” Stella began in a Thursday (Aug. 27) post on Instagram. “If anyone gets to heaven I’m sure she made it right on time. I know she’s showing out big time, in all her sparkles and shine. That was my sister’s way.” Stella — who is one of Dolly’s 11 siblings — went on to share a ritual that she and her older sister had of waking up early and drinking coffee while on the phone with each other every Tuesday. “Being little farm girls we’ve continued to be early risers,” she noted. “My sister was one of the most generous, thoughtful and kind people I’ve ever known,” Stella continued. “What the world saw is exactly who she was, so much so, she told me recently that if there was no hope for her, she would still allow her medical team to try experimental drugs in the hope of helping others in the future.” The younger Parton also thanked fans “for the outpouring of love and respect” they’ve shown her family since Dolly’s passing. She encouraged people interested in honoring her legacy to “show more kindness, lift others up and give more of your time and resources, as she continued to do to the very end.” “My Tuesday morning coffee time will never be the same, but her love, respect and goodness will remain,” Stella added. “She left the world a better place by being in it, so let’s follow her example.” Dolly died at the age of 80 on Tuesday (Aug. 25) after a brief cancer battle, less than a year and a half after the death of her husband of nearly six decades, Carl Dean. The news was shared in a video statement delivered by Bryan Seaver, Dolly’s nephew and head of security for 20 years. “Sadness lies with us, not Dolly,” he said in the announcement. “Dolly has lived in the light and is in the arms of Jesus, surely met by Carl, her parents and countless others who had watched her and longed for her to meet them in the heavens. She never saw a door she couldn’t open and the doors she opened made and changed history.” Since then, countless stars have spoken out to mourn the Queen of Country, with Taylor Swift, Beyoncé, Paul McCartney, Elton John, Mick Jagger and dozens more all releasing statements paying tribute. Miley Cyrus also honored her godmother in a post reading: “What I KNOW is Dolly would want me to feel [the loss], write a song about it, and then continue on and be strong. I have an angel by my side. I always have.” Dolly and Stella were, respectively, the fourth- and sixth-oldest of the Parton siblings, a clan also comprised of Willadeene, David, Coy, Bobby, Cassie, Randy, Larry, Floyd and twin sisters Freida and Rachel. Larry died in 1955 shortly after birth, while Floyd passed away in 2018. Randy died in 2021 and David in 2024, and Coy died this past July. The family was raised in a small, one-bedroom cabin in the Smoky Mountains, a heritage that Dolly was deeply proud of. She spent her life giving back to the region in which she was raised, fueling the economy with the opening of her Dollywood amusement park and choosing Sevier County, Tenn., as the starting point for her now-global Imagination Library program. “As the Scripture says, ‘To whom much is given, much is required,'” Parton told Billboard in her 2020 cover story. “If I can be an inspiration, then I want to be that. articles._body: UFC Shanghai: Umar Nurmagomedov vs Song Yadong continues on the main card with a fight between Levi Rodrigues and Liu Ce in the light heavyweight division. C heck out our UFC Shanghai odds series for our Rodrigues-Ce prediction and pick. Levi Rodrigues Jr. (5-1) suffered his UFC debut loss via second-round TKO to Felipe Franco in July 2026, snapping momentum built by a first-round KO of Alan Ribeiro that September and a no-contest outcome against Freddy Vidal on Contender Series in October 2025, as she comes into this fight this weekend against Liu Ce. Liu Ce (3-1 MMA) makes his UFC debut fresh off a first-round TKO of Igor Barabanov via punches this past May, avenging a lone career setback, a second-round TKO loss to Ivan Gnizditskiy in October 2024, and arrives boasting an 18-3 kickboxing pedigree as a former K-1 cruiserweight champion, as she comes into this fight this weekend against Levi Rodrigues. UFC Shanghai Odds, courtesy of DraftKings . UFC Shanghai Odds: Levi Rodrigues-Liu Ce Odds Levi Rodrigues: +160 Liu Ce: -192 Over 1.5 rounds: +160 Under 1.5 rounds: -210 Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Why Levi Rodrigues Will Win Levi Rodrigues brings genuine mixed martial arts pedigree into this fight, having already tested himself under UFC lights against Felipe Franco. Liu Ce, by contrast, is transitioning from a pure kickboxing background, and that stylistic gap in grappling and cage awareness often proves costly for combat-sport crossovers making their MMA debut. Rodrigues has shown real finishing power of his own, with five knockouts among his six professional bouts, meaning he isn’t simply a defensive grappler hoping to survive. He can match Liu Ce’s kickboxing pedigree with legitimate hands while also threatening to change levels if the striking exchanges get competitive. Liu Ce’s 3-1 MMA record was built almost entirely against regional Chinese competition, a considerable step down from the level Rodrigues has already tested himself against inside the UFC Octagon. That disparity in competition quality matters significantly once the cage door closes. Even Liu Ce’s own promotional material leans heavily on his kickboxing accolades rather than his still-developing grappling and ground game, a clear signal of where his vulnerabilities lie . If Rodrigues can use his superior MMA-specific instincts to close distance, mix in a takedown threat, and force Liu Ce to fight outside his comfort zone, his overall well-roundedness should be enough to secure the win. Why Liu Ce Will Win Liu Ce enters this fight with a genuinely elite striking background, having won the K-1 Cruiserweight championship and an Openweight Grand Prix across an 18-3 kickboxing career with 14 knockouts. That level of world-class striking experience simply dwarfs anything Levi Rodrigues has faced in his relatively short MMA career. Rodrigues is also coming off a fresh setback, having been finished via second-round TKO in his UFC debut against Felipe Franco. That kind of finish loss can expose durability concerns, and Liu Ce’s granite kickboxing pedigree gives him every tool needed to test that same weakness again . Liu Ce’s own MMA transition has been seamless so far, avenging his lone career loss with a first-round TKO of Igor Barabanov, showing he can translate his world-class hands into finishes inside the cage as well as the kickboxing ring . Rodrigues’ power is real, but facing a former world champion kickboxer means every exchange carries outsized risk, and few pure MMA strikers can match the technical precision Liu Ce brings from years at the sport’s highest levels. If Liu Ce can keep the fight standing and in his kickboxing wheelhouse, his elite hands and vastly superior striking pedigree give him a clear path to a devastating knockout finish over Rodrigues. Final Levi Rodrigues-Liu Ce Prediction & Pick Liu enters at 3-1, while Rodrigues is 5-1 with one no contest, but the Brazilian was stopped by Felipe Franco in the second round just six weeks before this booking. He also accepted the matchup on five days’ notice after Junior Tafa withdrew, leaving little time for a full camp or tailored preparation. Rodrigues owns genuine finishing ability, with his pro wins largely coming by knockout or TKO, so Liu cannot be careless in the pocket. Still, Liu carries a considerable height advantage—6-foot-5 to Rodrigues’ 6-foot—and brings a K-1 Openweight Grand Prix background into his UFC debut. The key is whether Rodrigues can pressure the newcomer before Liu establishes kicking range and forces a slower fight. Given the quick turnaround and Liu’s physical tools, that is a hard formula for Rodrigues to execute consistently. Expect Liu to manage distance early, punish entries with straight shots and kicks, then take over as Rodrigues’ pace fades. Final Levi Rodrigues-Liu Ce Prediction & Pick: Liu Ce (-192); UNDER 1.5 Rounds (-210) The post Levi Rodrigues vs. Liu Ce prediction, odds, pick for UFC Shanghai appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles.title: Dance Up-And-Comer of the Month Riordon Parlayed a Job in Influencer Marketing Into a Fast-Rising DJ Career
articles.summary: This weekend, the producer releases a new track and plays gigs at DC10 in Ibiza and Reading Festival and Creamfields in his native U.K.
articles._body: Riordon knew he was on to something when he was first asked to play Coachella 2023. But the request didn’t come through an agent or manager, and the performance wasn’t actually at the festival. “I had this millionaire reach out to me on TikTok” Riordon says. “He was like, ‘Yo, I throw the craziest Coachella afters every year. I’ll fly you out if you want to come be the resident DJ for the weekend.” It was the U.K. producer’s first big gig. “I hadn’t even put out any like full sets at that point,” he recalls. “He just told me that he likes seeing young people grinding, and he could see I was trying to make something of myself, and he saw some potential.” For the then 19-year-old artist, the offer was a clear sign that the efforts he’d been making — producing and posting tracks, along with remixes, photos, videos and other assorted social content — were breaking through. While “you can imagine how my mum felt when I told her this random guy with an NFT as his profile picture was gonna fly me out to America,” says Riordon, he accepted the gig. Out in the SoCal desert, he spent the weekend playing for a crowd that included Wiz Khalifa and Logan Paul. Two years later, Riordon returned to Coachella as part of the actual lineup, playing the festival’s beloved Do Lab stage in April of 2025. This past April, he returned to play its Yuma Tent club space. This year he even secured one of the famous billboards located on the side of the interstate near the fest, with his jokingly proclaiming “Pronounced Riordon, Not Riordon.” (The proper pronunciation of his name rhymes with “Jordan.”) These shows are among the many highlights of Riordon’s current rise, which also includes getting signed to Darkroom Records, home to artists including Billie Eilish and John Summit , a series of highly streamed releases including a Beatport No. 1, an upcoming Boiler Room set and tomorrow’s release of his latest track “Friction,” a house/UKG collab with London producer Locky. Riordon’s Boiler Room set in London Sandra Nagel Riordon grew up on the South Coast of England, with performance always part of his life. As a kid he had roles in traveling productions of shows including Oliver! and planned to attend drama school with the goal of working in film and television. But when the pandemic hit and schools went virtual, his plans shifted too. Recalling a glorious party moment when he’d grabbed the aux cord, played MK’s 1993 track “Burning” and watched the room go crazy, he was interested in making dance music. As the world shut down during COVID, “I ended up going all-in,” he says. “With acting, it’s hard to sit at home during COVID and take career steps, whereas with music I could actually make something happen for myself just from being at home and making tunes.” He was simultaneously working at an influencer marketing company that works with musicians and record labels to get their music on TikTok. The gig was serendipitous, “Because I was essentially studying TikTok for my job every day,” he says. “I would search for musicians that we could try and get on the platform, and I saw how influencers were using music and going viral. Understanding social media was so crucial for my growth early on.” Still living with his parents, he did this job by day and taught himself to DJ and produce at night. In February of 2022, he quit the job to fully focus on music. His mom was supportive, his dad was less enthusiastic, but both could see that he treated his goal like a real career, living off his savings and working 9-to-5 and into the evenings to make something happen. Up until that point, Riordon had been releasing a lot of Latin house songs, finding them “easy to make.” While these tracks were streaming fairly well, “it wasn’t the sound I wanted to be pursuing.” His life during this period “was basically rinse and repeat,” he says, “making music, promoting it on TikTok and on socials, putting it out and trying to grow each record from the next.” Then, the person who’d become his manager reached out via TikTok, and they made an inspiring trip to Miami Music Week 2023. Then came the Coachella afterparty gig. A voyage to Chicago’s ARC Music Festival in September of 2023 confirmed that he wanted to pursue house and tech house, an instinct that proved correct when his November 2023 track “Needle on the Record” got signed to Gorgon City’s Realm Records, got rinsed by “DJs I looked up to,” and hit No. 1 on Beatport’s overall chart. “I remember going out for a walk and calling my mom and my dad,” he says of getting the news of this Beatport No. 1. “That was the day when I felt like, ‘I think I can actually do this for a career.'” Why Riordon Is an Up-and-Coming Dance Artist From here, the momentum ramped up significantly. In November of 2024, Riordon appeared with Gorgon City during their set at the U.K.’s hallowed Drumsheds to play “Needle on the Record,” toured and released music consistently during 2025 and continued putting numbers on the board this year. He says his February Raw Cuts performance with Silva Bumpa in New York felt particularly massive — and last month, he sold out the city’s Knockdown Center. “I love the New York crowd,” he says. With a few Coachella sets already under belt, his goal now is to secure “a big spot in the Sahara tent, hopefully maybe in a year or two.” In the meantime, he plays the fashionable Solid Grooves party at DC10 in Ibiza tonight (Aug. 27) ,the U.K.’s Reading Festival (where he had one of his early formative raving experiences as a teenager) tomorrow and the esteemed Cre

If you’re a live music lover, and staycation enthusiast, then there’s no place to explore the robust live music scene and rich music history than Nashville, Tennessee. The city offers a wonderful blend of Southern charm and hospitality with a modern urban lifestyle with countless live music venues and concert halls. It’s no wonder why Nashville has the perfect nickname of “Music City.” In addition, the city offers a wide selection of world-class museums, notable restaurants and all sorts of fun bars and cocktail lounges from low-key dive bars to upscale and swanky cocktail lounges. It’s really the place to be for music lovers. Hilton’s downtown Nashville portfolio offers several distinct ways to experience Music City, whether you want an art-forward boutique stay, flexible accommodations for a group or a rooftop setting with live local music. Here are four Hilton hotels to consider for your next Nashville staycation. The Untitled Nashville Hotel, Tapestry Collection by Hilton Book Now Online Located at 221 2nd Avenue North, The Untitled Nashville Hotel, Tapestry Collection by Hilton (formerly known as Bankers Alley Hotel) is central to beloved honky-tonks and live music on Broadway — adjacent to Bankers Alley. In fact, the hotel is just mere steps away from the action in the city and less than a mile away from Nissan Stadium, Bridgestone Arena and Ryman Auditorium. But what makes The Untitled Nashville Hotel unique is its art-filled corridors and lobbies with thoughtfully crafted dining at Gray & Dudley, which features seasonal ingredients and handcrafted cocktails. It features a well-equipped fitness center, multiple art galleries that highlight regional artists and a terrace. Motto by Hilton Nashville Downtown Book Now Online Motto by Hilton Nashville Downtown at 311 3rd Avenue South is located near iconic attractions, including Country Music Hall of Fame, Ascend Amphitheater, Music City Center, Bridgestone Arena, Ryman Auditorium, The Grand Ole Opry and other must-see music stops. Its signature restaurant is Junie’s, which serves elevated Southern dishes, craft cocktails and offers live music nightly. There’s even a cute café that serves morning specialty coffee and treats. The property is ideal for large groups with accommodations for groups up to 15 people in connected rooms, while it’s also walkable to the downtown base. The Printing House Hotel Nashville Downtown, Tapestry by Hilton Book Now Online Opened in September 2025, The Printing House Hotel Nashville Downtown, Tapestry by Hilton at 501 3rd Avenue South offers mid-century influences, historical details and Nashville’s printing heritage for an overall unique experience for music lovers and travelers, alike. It’s located near the legendary Honky Tonk Highway (Lower Broadway), Printer’s Alley and Ryman Auditorium, and works as a great starting point when visiting and discovering Music City. The property features The Letterpress Lounge & Terrace, which offers guests live music, quick bites and crafted signature cocktails on its rooftop that offers indoor-outdoor seating and skyline views. It’s definitely a great place for a design-forward staycation with rooftop views and live local music and to connect with Nashville’s art and music scene. articles.title: How Dolly Parton’s Music Gave Whitney Houston & Beyoncé Milestone Chart Moments
articles.summary: “I Will Always Love You” became a record-setting No. 1, while “Jolene” was reinterpreted 50 years after the original reigned at country.
articles._body: Of the many roles that Dolly Parton held — including singer, actress, philanthropist, author and humanitarian — perhaps the chief legacy of the late icon, who died Tuesday (Aug. 25) at age 80, is as a songwriter. Related Dolly Parton’s Top Billboard Hot Country Songs Hits Forever No. 1: Dolly Parton, ‘9 to 5’ Dolly Parton Hit Billboard’s Dance Charts, Too, And Even Earned a No. 1 Hit Gifted with a unique talent to distill the most universal feelings into sage reflections, catchy quip-filled charm or tear-jerking sentiments, Parton created a catalog that stretched across genres and generations. Beyond establishing the foundation of her own career, the works assisted in milestone moments for fellow iconic superstars — including a pair of significant Billboard Hot 100 top 10 hits — in markedly different renditions from the originals. The most obvious case occurred in 1992 when Whitney Houston covered one of Parton’s signature tunes, “I Will Always Love You,” for the soundtrack to her feature film debut, The Bodyguard . Given the song’s placement, where characters played by Houston and her co-star Kevin Costner finally drop their guard and share an extended kiss, and its segue into the closing credits, the song selection was a pivotal moment — and the iconic result nearly never happened. Houston was initially set to record a cover of Jimmy Ruffin’s “What Becomes of the Brokenhearted,” but two conflicts prevented its final approval. The first, as Bodyguard music supervisor Maureen Crowe told the New York Post in 2022, “when you slow that song down, it’s like a dirge.” And worse, during production, singer Paul Young covered the song for 1991’s Fried Green Tomatoes and it climbed to a No. 22 Hot 100 peak. “We couldn’t use that song because it would just seem like we ripped it off.” Parton’s song was then suggested, a pitch that satisfied Houston, Costner and Arista Records head Clive Davis. Several adjustments make it plenty different from Parton’s — an a cappella opening, a slower tempo and the return of an oft-skipped third verse — but the core DNA of an agonizing, tearful heartbreak remains. Unlike the fictional Bodyguard scenario, Parton’s inspiration was autobiographical, stemming from a decision to exit The Porter Wagoner Show after a multi-year run with the host, with whom she recorded many duets in the 1960s and ‘70s. In both scenarios, the song became a hit. Parton’s original topped the Hot Country Songs chart in 1974, while a re-recorded rendition ruled again in 1982. Houston’s version, meanwhile, became a pop-culture juggernaut, setting a then-record 14-week stay at No. 1 on the Hot 100, and winning Grammy Awards for record of the year and best pop vocal performance, female. Parton co-presented the latter, and Houston began her acceptance speech with the appreciation, “Dolly, of course, coming from you, this is truly an honor. Thank you for writing a beautiful song. Thank you so much for writing beautiful songs.” Another Parton signature, “Jolene,” received an overhaul to top 10 success when Beyoncé restyled the track for 2024’s Cowboy Carter , her first full-length album to explore country music and adjacent sounds. Recasting the plea as a warning — flipping “I’m begging of you, please don’t take my man” to “I’m warnin’ you, don’t come for my man,” for example — the heavier drum-backed, cautionary tale marked one of the album’s most anticipated listens. Upon Cowboy Carter ’s chart debut, “Jolene” debuted at No. 7 on the Hot 100, the third highest of the album’s 23 placements on that week’s chart, behind lead single “Texas Hold ‘Em” and the “II Most Wanted” duet with Miley Cyrus — Parton’s goddaughter. While the twist caught Parton off-guard, she appreciated the reworked take. “When they said she was going to do ‘Jolene,’ I expected it to be the regular one, but it wasn’t,” Parton told E! News in 2024. “I loved what she did to it. As a songwriter, you love the fact that people do your song, no matter how they do them. She wasn’t about to beg some woman like I did.” Through Beyoncé, “Jolene” reached No. 3 on the Hot Country Songs chart in April 2024, its highest rank since Parton’s original, a No. 1, in February 1974 — just over 50 years apart. The two shared another Cowboy Carter connection thanks to Parton’s feature on “Tyrant,” on which she provided a spoken introduction. Just as Parton’s classic helped Beyoncé make inroads into the country lane, “Tyrant” aided the reverse of their traditional home bases by giving Parton her first entry on the Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs chart, peaking at No. 18. “Dolly, you were the barometer. The North Star. Bold and brilliant. Talented and tenacious,” Beyoncé wrote in part upon Parton’s death. “I’m honored that I had the privilege to work with you. I will treasure that forever. Thank you for your profound impact on the world. You are truly one of one. Rest peacefully.”

articles._body: Olivia Rodrigo is loving Ariana Grande ‘s recent album petal so much, you might just hear her cover one of the songs from the project someday. Related Olivia Rodrigo to Guest Host on iHeartRadio One Day Before Her Inaugural Daisy Chain Fields Festival Olivia Rodrigo’s ‘Handmaid’s Tale’-Inspired Song ‘Serena Joy’ Is Now on Streaming After Record Store Release Ariana Grande Slams Trump Administration for Using ‘We Can’t Be Friends’ in TikTok Video: ‘Your Truth Is False’ In a Wonderland interview published Tuesday (Aug. 25) ahead of her Daisy Chain Fields festival, Rodrigo gushed about Sienna Spiro and Role Model’s recent covers of her music before answering a question about whether there was a song by another artist she’d like to put her own spin on soon. “I’ve been listening to Ariana’s album a lot, so maybe something from Ariana’s album,” the former Disney star said. “It’s so exciting to have people cover your songs,” Rodrigo also told the publication. “It’s like the coolest thing ever. Role Model covered ‘maggots for brains,’ and Sienna Spiro covered my song ‘less’ the other day. It was just so much fun, and it’s so flattering because I think both of them are incredible artists, and to get to see their take on the song is really special.” Both Spiro and Role Model shared their takes on Rodrigo songs for the BBC Radio 1 Live Lounge, where Rodrigo herself has previously delivered covers of Noah Kahan’s “Stick Season” and CMAT’s “When a Good Man Cries.” Grande’s music has made for some memorable Live Lounge performances over the years, from Hozier performing “Problem” in 2015 to The 1975 covering “Thank U, Next” in 2018 and Gracie Abrams singing “We Can’t Be Friends” earlier this year. It’s only been about a month since petal dropped in late July, debuting at No. 1 on the Billboard 200 after landing a Billboard Hot 100 -topping single with “Hate That I Made You Love Me.” Rodrigo is also fresh off the release of a new album, with you seem pretty sad for a girl so in love also entering the U.S. albums chart at No. 1 and hosting a No. 1 Hot 100 hit with “Drop Dead.” The two pop stars have previously nodded to their fandom of each other, with Rodrigo dancing to “The Boy Is Mine” in a TikTok that Grande reposted on her Instagram Story a couple of years ago. When the Wicked star was a coach on The Voice , she at one point praised Rodrigo’s breakout hit after a contestant auditioned with “Drivers License.” “Covering a song that is as big and as good as drivers license is a tall order,” Grande said at the time. Rodrigo is currently gearing up to host the inaugural Daisy Chain Fields, a festival she created to raise money for causes supporting women and girls. She also personally curated the event’s all-women lineup, which includes Chappell Roan, Doechii, KATSEYE, Stevie Nicks and more. “I feel like Daisy Chain Fields is going to be such a magical day,” Rodrigo told Wonderland . “I literally can’t wait … There are so many of my friends and my heroes [on the lineup], and I can’t wait to watch all of the sets, and I just think they’re incredible human beings also because they are donating their time and doing this completely for free and for charity. Everything about it is just incredible and very special.”

articles.title: Alex Warren on Honoring His Parents on ‘WILDCHILD’ & His Wife’s Reaction to Another Love Song: ‘She’s Like, ‘I Get It, You Like Me”
articles.summary: The "Ordinary" singer stops by the Billboard News studio to talk inspiration & pending fatherhood.
articles._body: When making his new album WILDCHILD, out Friday (Aug. 28), Alex Warren had a very specific road map. “This album was heavily inspired by my live shows,” he says in a new Billboard News interview. “Funny enough, whenever I play a show, it’s very fun and people dance, and then, all of a sudden, they cry and then they laugh. And for me, I loved that whiplash of emotions every few minutes.” Related Songs With the Most Weeks Atop All of Billboard’s Airplay Charts Combined: Alex Warren’s ‘Ordinary’ & More Bruce Springsteen & Alex Warren to Play Stand Up for Heroes on 20th Anniversary of Veterans Benefit Show Alex Warren Joins UTA Roster Following Hot 100-Topping ‘Ordinary’ and Grammy Nomination Yet, there is still a sense of cohesion on the new Atlantic set. “You’re going to listen to the first song, the second song, and they’re going to be sonically so different, and they’re going to be so different what I’m talking about,” he continues. “But you’re going to feel like it’s still a story that you can pay attention to.” And that story is influenced by Warren’s relationship with his parents. His father, who called him “wild child,” died when Warren was 9, but his dad comes back to life on WILDCHILD through audio snippets incorporated into the album from videos he made for Warren. Now, Warren finds himself doing the same thing for his future children. In fact, he’d made a new video the day of the Billboard News interview. “I made a video for my kids this morning, and I don’t know why I like making videos for my kids, my future self. I just start filming them,” he says. In part, he wants to capture this time. “I was really just happy with where I am in my life right now, which is like weird to say out loud,” he says. “I just made a whole video where I was like, ‘I hope I’m a cool dad.’ It was fun.” Warren wrote the album with the same core collaborators, Adam Yaron, Cal Shapiro and Mags Duval, who worked on You’ll Be Alright, Kid. That album, of course, included “Ordinary,” which spent 10 weeks at No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 last year and was crowned Billboard ’s 2025 Song of the Summer . He knows almost everything he does will live in that song’s shadow, given its enormous success and he’s more than OK with that. “I will never have a record as big as ‘Ordinary.’ Statistically, it’s impossible,” he says. Several songs on the album reflect his love story with his wife, Kouvr Annon, including “Fine Place to Die” and “Rescuer,” but Warren jokes she’s grown tired of hearing about his devotion. “It’s so funny, because my wife isn’t very expressive when it comes down to these songs,” he says. “You have to think how many love songs I’ve written about this girl. Like at a certain point, she’s like, ‘All right, dude, I get it. You like me.’” Watch the full video above.
