articles.title: See the Best Dolly Parton Musical Tributes, From Harry Styles, Katy Perry, John Mayer, Jack White & More
articles.summary: Even Vin Diesel got in on the outpouring of love for the late country icon, who died Aug. 25 at age 80.
articles._body: It’s hard to think of an artist whose death has elicited the kind of unadulterated love, grief and heart-swelling emotion as Dolly Parton , who died Tuesday (Aug. 25) at age 80. The beloved Queen of Country charmed the world over a six-decade career with her 50 charted albums on the Billboard 200 chart, featuring such indelible hits as “Jolene” and “I Will Always Love You,” and brought joy to millions of children around the world with her Imagination Library, which has distributed more than 200 million books over the past 30 years. And while everyone from President Trump to the Library of Congress and Nashville politicians lined up to pay homage by ordering flags at half-staff , honor her good works and push to have the Nashville International Airport renamed in her honor , many of Parton’s peers and musical admirers paid tribute in the most fitting way: by playing her songs . Since it was announced that Parton had died following a brief battle with cancer after several years of health issues, everyone from Harry Styles and Chris Stapleton to Jack White, John Mayer, Kesha, Jon Batiste, Orville Peck and even Vin Diesel have poured their hearts into covers of some of Parton’s biggest, most beloved hits, with the majority of them focusing on the song that will forever be in our hearts: “I Will Always Love You.” The 1974 song written by Parton to mark her split with her musical mentor and duet partner Porter Wagoner topped the Hot Country Songs chart in 1974 and then again in 1982, but it is perhaps best known for Whitney Houston’s soaring The Bodyguard cover, which topped the Billboard Hot 100 for 14 weeks in 1992-93. Check out some of the best covers of Parton songs and live tributes to the Queen of Country since her death.

articles.title: Anthropic makes first move into physical AI with new way for scientists, manufacturers to bring equipment to life
articles.summary: The Model Hardware Standard (MHS) works with any AI model, not just Claude, but for now only a handful of companies can access the research preview.
articles._body: Imagine a factory where all the equipment is powered by AI, where robotic arms and assembly lines can “communicate” with their own shared language. Or picture a science lab, where microscopes can autonomously search for a certain type of molecule—all hours of the day, no humans necessary. That’s the idea behind Anthropic new Model Hardware Standard (MHS), which the company released as a research preview on Thursday. MHS, which marks Anthropic’s first foray into so-called physical AI, is essentially a framework for connecting advanced large language models (LLMs) like Anthropic’s Claude with physical objects, from manufacturing equipment to microscopes. With MHS, companies can integrate AI into their equipment in “hours or minutes,” Anthropic said. Typically, this process would take “weeks, if not months,” and require specialists to do a custom build. Expanded access to advanced AI tools will pave the way for “autonomous, round-the-clock experiments and workflows,” the company said. Scientific research and advanced manufacturing applications are among the primary uses. The MHS can also help connect multiple devices to one another, enabling them to communicate through a set of commands, such as “read.” Any hardware device can understand these commands and act on them. MHS is model-agnostic, meaning it works with any LLM—not just Claude—including models built by other companies such as OpenAI or open-source models. It’s built on the Model Context Protocol (MCP), a universal, open standard for connecting data sources that Anthropic debuted in 2024. The MCP is “kind of like the USB for AI to software connection,” Alek Kemeny, a member of the technical staff at Anthropic, tells Fortune . Not all existing equipment can connect to MHS out of the box, as not all have a programming interface, Kemeny said. As part of this project, Anthropic is working with “a lot of device manufacturers” to build new products with the necessary interface, and are pre-loaded with the MHS. The company is also helping manufacturers to add MHS connections to existing products. “That’s the future we imagine and are moving into,” Kemeny said. “In the future, scientists can buy these devices and out of the box it works. That’s just the process of adopting a standard.” Jonah Cool, head of partnerships and deployment of science at Anthropic, added that often scientific equipment “suffers from proprietary solutions that are very brittle and often don’t meet the need of scientists.” MHS offers a standardized, easily programmable interface that aims to help them connect any model to their equipment. “We want to avoid vendor lock-in for scientists,” Cool said. The MHS research preview comes amid increasing interest in the potential of combining AI and robotics. Hugging Face also debuted its first physical AI product today, a robotic duck , although it is not powered by MHS, Anthropic said. Nvidia , which is set to purchase Hugging Face for $13 billion, has also long championed physical AI. In March, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang predicted that in the future “every industrial company will become a robotics company.” Anthropic developed MHS in partnership with the HHMI Janelia Research Campus, a biomedical research center in Virginia. A “handful” of labs and hardware manufacturers received early access during development, in fields such as biotech, robotics, and quantum computing. Some partners include Genentech, Carnegie Mellon university, quantum computing company QuEra, Universal Robots, Amazon Web Services, Doosan Robotics, Danaher , and Hugging Face. This story was originally featured on Fortune.com

articles.title: Rock al Parque Unveils Full 2026 Lineup Featuring Ministry, Editors, Mon Laferte and More
articles.summary: The free festival will celebrate three decades at Bogotá's Parque Simón Bolívar with more than 60 performers.
articles._body: Rock al Parque has finalized the lineup for its historic 30th anniversary edition. The free Colombian festival will return to Bogotá’s Parque Simón Bolívar from Oct. 10-12 with a program featuring international acts such as Los Bunkers (Chile), Editors (England), Mon Laferte (Chile/Mexico), Ministry (USA), Apocalyptica (Finland), Rata Blanca (Argentina) and Porter (Mexico). Related The 50 Best Latin Rock Bands of All Time: Staff Picks Nicole Kidman Says She's Planning to See Adéla Live in Nashville & The 'Nicole Kidman' Singer Is Freaking Out Jay Wheeler's 'De Lejitos' Gets Up Close With No. 1 on Latin Airplay: 'Fills Me With Great Pride' The announcement, made on Wednesday (Aug. 26) by the Instituto Distrital de las Artes (Idartes ), comes just over a week after the event unveiled its 26 local artists . The new wave of acts confirms the international scope of the celebration, with alternative rock, metal, punk, ska, reggae and other related sounds spread across four stages. The lineup also includes the iconic power metal band Stratovarius (Finland), alongside Between the Buried and Me, Algiers and Darkest Hour from the U.S.; Grave and Hellbutcher from Sweden; as well as Burning Witches and Triptykon with Hellhammer and Celtic Frost from Switzerland. Also featured are Japan’s Tokyo Ska Paradise Orchestra, Venezuelan group Desorden Público, Chile’s Gondwana and Spain’s Green Valley and Iseo & Dodosound. Plus, Argentina’s Bandalos Chinos, Ratones Paranoicos and Serú Girán; Mexico’s División Minúscula and Las Fokin Biches; Chile’s Los Tetas, Claudio Narea and Decessus; as well as Uruguay’s Trotsky Vengarán. Representing Colombia, Esteman, I.R.A. and Nadie, among others, will also be present. Founded in 1995, Rock al Parque has established itself as one of the largest free open-air festivals in Latin America. For its 2026 edition, the event will celebrate three decades of history with a mix of international icons, Latin American artists and a broad showcase of Bogotá’s local scene. articles.title: OpenAI bans pro-Russia ChatGPT accounts used to spread pro-Kremlin content including an Israel-based think tank using real researchers’ names
articles.summary: OpenAI claims Russian users hid behind VPNs to push a think tank tied to an influence operation and spread pro-Russia content online.
articles._body: OpenAI banned a “cluster” of ChatGPT accounts that it claims were part of a pro-Russia operation aimed at bashing Western countries and promoting a think tank with misattributed academic research.  The company said in a blog post this week that the banned ChatGPT users used VPNs to get around its restriction on Russian users and then used its tech to create social posts promoting the International Burke Institute, a think tank that describes itself as an “expert community” based in Israel, but which OpenAI says is the “core” of a Russian influence operation.  According to OpenAI, the think tank, the website of which is still online, claims to include among its contributors notable figures like American linguist and intellectual Noam Chomsky as well as American political scientist and author Francis Fukuyama. Neither Fukuyama nor Chomsky responded immediately to requests for comment from Fortune . One such author who was listed on the site didn’t know the website was using her name until Fortune reached out for comment. Other listings include experts who passed away before the IBI was founded, such as Shlomo Avineri and Jiang Ping. OpenAI said the website, which was registered in February 2025, also included a “sovereignty index” that favored Russia as well as dozens of articles with misattributed authors. A scan by Fortune of the Burke Institute’s website on the Wayback Machine reveals that while it existed as of February last year, nothing was published on the page prior to October 2025.  The institute, in response to reporting by French outlet Le Monde on OpenAI’s claims, doubled down with a statement that said it rejected the idea it was not a legitimate think tank. “The fact that third parties use or cite an IBI publication, the Institute’s name, or findings from the Sovereignty Index does not, in itself, constitute evidence of cooperation, coordination, funding, or a common underlying purpose.” The Burke Institute did not immediately respond to a request for comment from Fortune sent to the email listed publicly on its website. OpenAI said that according to its research, a handful of individuals in Israel represented the Burke Institute in interviews and at conferences. Using real researchers’ names The AI company’s review of the Burke Institute’s articles found 34 of 36 were real academic articles misattributed to other authors. A screenshot published by OpenAI showed a legitimate article on the Burke Institute’s website on migration governance that was taken from the Migration Policy Institute but misattributed to Kate Howell, a professor of food science at the University of Melbourne, with a headshot taken from the internet. Since OpenAI published its blog post, the website changed the article’s attribution to one of the real authors, Kate Hooper, a senior policy analyst at the Migration Policy Institute. Hooper did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Another professor listed as an expert on the Burke Institute’s website was Susan Ariel Aaronson, a professor of international affairs at George Washington University. A legitimate article she authored for the Centre for International Governance Innovation was posted on the website with a link to download. Yet, Aaronson, who is also a co-principal investigator for the NSF-NIST Institute for Trustworthy AI in Law & Society (TRAILS), told Fortune she was not associated in any way with the Burke Institute. Reached by phone, she said the situation was disturbing.  “Trust is really important in the governance of AI, and here you have this really weird, you know, situation causing substantial distrust, and so it’s just really disturbing,” she said.  She also lamented that there is little regulation at the federal level to deal with such instances, and that it needs to be handled from the top.  “The Trump administration is doing nothing to effectively govern it, and is governing AI in an opaque manner. That is opacity does not build trust,” she added. Other articles on the Burke Institute’s website appear to be translated into English from a Slavic language, based on clues like the use of the word “svetofor,” which means traffic light in several Slavic languages, including Russian, according to OpenAI. The AI company claims the ChatGPT users created numerous social posts to promote the institute, some of which came from accounts with the International Burke Institute name and branding. Other posts came from made-up individuals that promoted the institute on Facebook, LinkedIn, and X as well as Substack and Telegram. OpenAI said posts from individual accounts “only received low numbers of views”  and the official accounts for the institute had “low subscriber numbers.” Still, on the instant messaging platform Telegram, the users were able to attract a larger audience of between 10,000 and 20,000 followers per channel.  Despite what OpenAI claims is a small following, the company’s findings show how Russia-linked actors have reportedly used AI to step up their propaganda campaigns.   Earlier this year, OpenAI said it disrupted another operation it said originated in Russia, that used ChatGPT to generate German-language political content ahead of Germany’s federal election. The campaign criticized the U.S. and NATO and distributed content through Telegram and X and created AI-generated material supporting Germany’s far-right Alternative für Deutschland party.  Russian-speaking cybercriminals also used SpaceX’s AI coding assistant Cursor to hack into a Belgian chemical company along with six other companies this year alone, according to a report by Reuters citing data from cybersecurity company Gambit Security. articles._body: Hey there, I’m Brian. I've been shipping conversational models over here at Tavus for the past two years. I want to tell you about our new audio-understanding model: Sparrow-2! It’s a new category of model and a unique new approach to conversational audio. Earlier this year we launched Sparrow-1, (at the time) our SoTA turn taking model. Since our Sparrow-1 launch, I’ve spent a lot of time listening to humans talking and trying to really understand how people know when to talk, when to listen, and when to wait. I’ve also been hunting down failure modes of the current SoTA models. And while Sparrow-1 is great, there are some failure patterns I see. We tried solving the problems with existing approaches, but solving one problem only created another. Sparrow-1 and a lot of the existing turn taking models require noise cancellation to isolate the speaker’s audio from background noise. After removing the “noise” these models rely on simple prosodic and phonetic cues from spoken words to decide when a turn has ended. They throw out information and then pay attention to a small set of verbal and prosodic cues. This approach ignores a ton of important information. Non-verbal cues, sounds, and environmental noise impact turn taking. Noise cancellation models assume everything non-transcribable is noise, but that’s wrong. Humans use breath, sighs, and other sounds to hold the conversational floor or bid for a turn. There are constant micro-interruptions, affirmations, quiet human and environmental sounds that add to the conversational scenario. That sound is part of what we use to understand the nuanced space of the conversational floor! Cancelling out the “noise” has the ruinous side-effect of cancelling out the flow. Now, with Sparrow-2, instead of modelling just the primary speaker’s transcribable audio, we’ve been training a model on all the sounds and letting it decide what matters and what does not when it comes to conversational flow. Our new model continuously streams in audio and is able to understand semantics, prosody, timing, speaker identity, sighs, breaths, backchannels, interruptions, background speech, and unintelligible audio with the goal of understanding what the agent should do given the state of the audio. Sparrow-2 fits into our larger model family and unlocks new conversational behavior, not seen before in production-ready conversational pipelines. It can pass signals to different parts of the conversation. For example if the user is in a room that’s too noisy, the bot will ask the user to move to a quieter space. Also, Sparrow-2 is semi-duplex: it considers the timing of sound in relation to the AI speech as well as the user’s. Our main objective with Sparrow-2 is to finally crack the Cocktail Party Problem: how can we have a human-like conversation 1:1 with a user in noisy environments. I wrote up some technical details about the model architecture here: https://www.tavus.io/blog/sparrow-2 I’d love for you guys to give it a try and let me know what you think and feel. articles.title: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and 100 other companies call for action to defend against rogue AI
articles.summary: Some of the world's largest tech companies and AI startups have come together to decry the current state of cybersecurity and to advertise a new solution that they say can ward off a new generation of cyber threats.
articles._body: Over a hundred tech companies — including OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and Microsoft — have signed an open letter urging both the private and public sectors to work together to defend themselves from AI-related cyber threats. The letter — which was also signed by prominent cyber firms like CrowdStrike, Okta, and Fortinet, as well as prominent financial institutions and internet infrastructure firms — calls for the adoption of new forms of cyber defense, while also encouraging governments at the “local, national, and international levels” to collaborate on security. “In the coming months, AI-enabled cyber attacks will become far more widespread and sophisticated as models around the world become increasingly capable,” the letter states. “The companies and public services our communities depend on — from hospitals to water treatment plants to the infrastructure that powers the internet — are at risk.” The problem AI poses to traditional cybersecurity defenses has been thrust into the spotlight lately by a string of bizarre incidents in which AI agents have attacked companies. The Hugging Face incident — in which one of OpenAI’s agents autonomously broke out of its sandboxed environment and attacked the tech company — has been followed by a trail of other reported break-ins involving agents developed by other AI companies, including Anthropic and Meta. These incidents have bolstered the argument that the field of cybersecurity has been fundamentally altered and that bold new commercial solutions are necessary to mitigate them. The letter further suggests the mobilization of a “collective response,” one in which “new partnerships” are formed “to raise security standards and find new solutions to emerging cyber threats.” Several of the AI companies that have signed the letter are still actively developing ever more advanced AI models, highlighting their conflicted position. At the same time, they are also offering programs to use frontier AI models for defensive purposes, including OpenAI’s Daybreak program, Anthropic’s Mythos, and Microsoft’s new cyber platform Perception.

articles.title: Callaway Drops Good Good Golf After Ad Fallout
articles.summary: Aaron Doster-Imagn Images
articles._body: ATLANTA — Callaway is dropping Good Good Golf in the wake of the controversy surrounding the YouTube group’s controversial driver ad . The golf equipment manufacturer first partnered with Good Good in 2023, in a wide-ranging deal that included collaborations on content, products, and other brand campaigns. Callaway informed Good Good of its decision to part ways Thursday morning, a source with knowledge of the situation told Front Office Sports . “Over the last several days, we have listened and reflected deeply on the hurt and disappointment caused by the video we reposted,” a Thursday statement from Callaway read. “We heard from individuals who shared personal experiences related to violence against women, and their stories were powerful reminders that this issue touches the lives of far too many people. Unequivocally, violence against women is unacceptable and should never be trivialized, normalized, or used as entertainment. “Callaway has ended its relationship with Good Good, effective immediately.” The news broke in the middle of the first round of the season-ending Tour Championship, which is playing out at East Lake Golf Club in Atlanta, where $40 million of prize money and a $10 million FedExCup champion will be crowned this weekend. Good Good’s uncertain future had already been the hottest topic early in the week at the PGA Tour’s playoff finale. Callaway said it was “committing” $1 million to “support organizations working to prevent violence against women.” It was not immediately clear which organizations would receive that money over what time frame. Callaway blamed its own poor internal review processes for the ad , which depicted Good Good cofounder Garrett Clark shoving a woman to the ground as she approached his Good Good/Callaway co-branded driver. “We sincerely apologize to everyone who was hurt, disappointed, or offended by this incident,” Thursday’s Callaway statement read. After the ad debuted Aug. 21 and negative feedback poured in that night before the ad was pulled the next day, there was disagreement between Good Good and Callaway over who would take the bulk of the responsibility for the ad’s production and release, multiple sources with knowledge of the companies’ thinking told FOS . The fallout escalated rapidly Wednesday, when several major retailers including Dick’s Sporting Goods, Golf Galaxy, PGA Tour Superstore, and Target pulled Good Good merchandise from their in-store and online shelves. More Dominoes Late Thursday afternoon, Good Good dropped its title sponsorship of the inaugural Good Good Championship, a new PGA Tour event scheduled for Nov. 12–15 at Omni Barton Creek in Austin. Last year, Good Good signed a multiyear contract, agreeing to pay at least $6 million annually to back the event. “We agree with their decision to use this time to focus on their organization and the work ahead,” the PGA Tour said in a statement. Now, attention shifts to Golf Channel. Golf Channel postponed the premiere of Big Break x Good Good —a revamp of its reality competition series that was popular in the 2000s—from Tuesday to Sept. 1, due to the show’s presenting sponsor, Golf Galaxy, dropping out. The show was filmed earlier this year at Omni Barton Creek in Austin, so canceling it would be a major financial blow for Golf Channel, given the production and marketing costs the network has already spent. Golf Channel did not immediately comment on the status of its relationship with Good Good after Callaway’s move Thursday. Good Good’s Response Good Good Golf cofounder Garrett Clark—who starred in the ad that depicted him shoving fellow Good Good creator Alexis Miestowski to the ground—shared a lengthy video to his personal social media accounts late Wednesday addressing the controversy . “I want to personally apologize for playing a role in the skit in this ad at the magnitude that I did,” Clark said in the video. “And on Good Good’s behalf, on Good Good marketing’s behalf, I want to apologize as well because how this ad was received is not at all what we stand for. Also, I do not support [domestic violence], abuse, or any of that of any kind.” FOS obtained a copy of a memo CEO Matt Kendrick sent to all Good Good staff Monday. In the email subject-lined “Owning Our Mistake,” he said the company plans to donate all proceeds of the driver campaign to an “organization supporting women in [its] local community” of Frisco, Texas. Good Good and Callaway did not immediately answer questions about how the breakup would play out. The post Callaway Drops Good Good Golf After Ad Fallout appeared first on Front Office Sports .

articles.title: High School Football: How to Watch DeSoto (Texas) vs St. Thomas Aquinas (Fla.)
articles.summary: The Texas high school football season gets underway this week; however, first, the number one team in Texas, DeSoto (Texas) travels out of the state to take on one of the top teams in the nation, Ft. Lauderdale St. Thomas Aquinas (Fla.), on Saturday, August 29, 2026.
articles._body: The Texas high school football season gets underway this week; however, first, the number one team in Texas, DeSoto (Texas) travels out of the state to take on one of the top teams in the nation, Ft. Lauderdale St. Thomas Aquinas (Fla.), on Saturday, August 29, 2026. Going into the Texas high school football season, with their reclassification to 5A, DeSoto enters the year as the number one team in the state according to Massey Ratings. During the 2025 high school football season, the Eagles finished with a 13-3 record, capturing the 6A Division II state championship. However, ahead of the upcoming season, DeSoto will be unable to defend its 6A state championship after UIL district realignment forced them to move down to 5A. In a report from the DeSoto ISD, the specific terms of the Eagles’ realignment were revealed. “Beginning in the 2026–27 school year, DeSoto ISD will transition to UIL Class 5A competition, with this alignment remaining in place through 2028. This change is based on enrollment data, team roster sizes, and input from coaches, and is designed to support student safety, equity, and meaningful participation.” Despite its realignment, the Eagles still boast one of the most dominant rosters in all of Texas high school football. Included in that is four-star running back prospect SaRod Baker . Committed to Texas Tech , Baker is one of the top running backs in the state, returning for his senior year. Last year, through just a five-game period, Baker rushed for 1,503 yards on 135 carries, with nine scores in the playoffs, finishing the season with 3,206 yards on 345 carries and 45 touchdowns. The Aggies’ commit ranks No. 5 at his position and No. 82 nationally. On top of having one of the top running backs in the country, DeSoto also boasts a top defense, headlined by four-star defensive line prospect K’Adrian Redmond . The defense is also backed by a number of ranked prospects, including three-star corner Dhillon McGee and three-star edge rusher D.J Rumph . Meanwhile, their opponent, St. Thomas Aquinas, also boasts one of the top rosters in Florida high school football. Predicted by Rivals’ Andy Villamarzo to hoist the first-ever Florida Open Division title this year, the Florida schools boast one of the top rosters in the nation, with five-star offensive lineman Mark Matthews . “High-upside offensive tackle prospect with top-notch physical and athletic tools for the position. Measured in at 6-foot-5.5 and around 285 pounds with plus length before his senior season. Added nearly 15 pounds to his frame early on in the offseason before his junior year.” “Has an ideal build for an offensive lineman with little bad weight and considerable mass in his lower body, helping to create a strong base. Tests as an athlete in the combine setting, with a 4.98 second 40-yard dash and 4.69 short shuttle at the Miami Rivals Camp after his junior season.” Rivals’ Charles Power wrote in his scouting report on the player. Across the board, on both sides of the ball, the Raiders also boast a number of four-star talents, including edge rusher Wyatt Smith , wide receiver Julius Jones , and safety Zayden Gamble . They also return a significant number of ranked three-star prospects, one of the most stacked rosters in the nation. Two of the top teams in the nation: here is everything you need to know about watching one of the biggest clashes of the year. How to Watch St. Thomas Aquinas and DeSoto Eagles High School Football Matchup Date: Saturday, August 29, 2026 Time: 6:00 p.m. (Local.) Location: Ft. Lauderdale, Florida Livestream: ESPN2

articles._body: While there may be unrest at the top for the Dallas Cowboys , there are high hopes for the 2026 season . Still, a Cowboys insider has one big question about Von Miller helping the defense get out of the gutter. “If Von Miller gets 10-15 snaps a game (is) that enough for an impact? Miller looks in great shape, thought he would practice a little more in teams.” The Cowboys recently signed the veteran edge rusher. They hope he will be a difference-maker with the team’s pass rush this season, despite his age (37). Will edge rusher Von Miller stand out for the Cowboys? One thing the Cowboys would like to see from Miller is quality mentoring of younger players. And one of those guys already expressed the importance of having a guy like Miller in the locker room, according to dallascowboys.com. “Having a guy like that, he’s like another coach in the room,” edge Marist Liufau said. “So it’s such a blessing to have him. Since the first day he came, he’s been pouring into us and helping us, and just giving us his insight on every single thing that he can in the meeting room. He’s nonstop talking and helping us out on the field, before practice, getting ready to practice, and working on different things. He’s been super helpful to us.” Expectations are super high for the Cowboys in 2026. They have a better overall roster, a potential strong defense, and still have one of the NFL’s best offenses. It’s looking positive, and Miller is part of it , according to The Athletic. “He can still get after the passer,” said Will McClay, the vice president of player personnel. “When you have a bunch of rushers, the offense has to figure out what you’re doing, how you’re doing it. I think (new defensive coordinator Christian Parker) will use that very well. But also the leadership. We have young players that they’re learning from coaching, but they also learn better from guys that have done it at a high level. They’re probably more willing to listen to that. And he’s the right kind of guy to pour into a guy like Malachi (Lawrence) and some of the young guys we have.” The post Cowboys insider has 1 big question about Von Miller helping get defense out of gutter appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles.title: Josh Allen’s gruesome depiction of turf burns makes Bills star’s grass stance easy to understand
articles.summary: The Buffalo Bills have been participating in practice this week as they gear up for their final preseason game against the Pittsburgh Steelers. The Bills will be playing their home games this year in Highmark Stadium, which has real grass on the field instead of the increasingly used artificial t
articles._body: The Buffalo Bills have been participating in practice this week as they gear up for their final preseason game against the Pittsburgh Steelers. The Bills will be playing their home games this year in Highmark Stadium, which has real grass on the field instead of the increasingly used artificial turf , which has drawn numerous complaints from players around the league. Recently, Bills star quarterback and former league MVP Josh Allen broke down why he is a fan of real grass instead of turf. “I’ve gotten numerous burns on my legs from artificial turf, like to the point where I can’t sleep at night because it’s bubbling over,” he said, per Skyler Caruso of PEOPLE. “It’s very painful, so I’m excited to not have to deal with that at home at least. I know we’ll probably still play games on the road that are turf.” “But if I can snap my fingers and make every field grass, that’s what I would do for sure,” he added. Allen is far from the only player who has expressed dismay that the NFL is still implementing artificial turf despite the increasing documentation of its injury risk to players. Many players voiced their displeasure when NFL stadiums that usually use turf switched to real grass for the FIFA World Cup this summer, only to revert back to turf ahead of the upcoming football season. Allen indicated that he believes real grass can help the league out in its quest for “injury prevention.” Meanwhile, on the field, the Bills will be looking to bounce back after a tough playoff exit vs the Denver Broncos last year. Buffalo will kick off its season on September 13 vs the Houston Texans on the road. articles.title: College fantasy football: Top 10 running backs in 2026
articles.summary: Week 0 of the college football season kicks off on Saturday. Last year, 12 different running backs ran for over 1,300 yards while another 12 had 15 or more touchdowns. Many of the top offensive units in college fantasy football have star quarterbacks leading the charge. Regardless, in a day of hi
articles._body: Week 0 of the college football season kicks off on Saturday. Last year, 12 different running backs ran for over 1,300 yards while another 12 had 15 or more touchdowns. Many of the top offensive units in college fantasy football have star quarterbacks leading the charge . Regardless, in a day of high-flying offenses led by quarterbacks who can sling the ball all over the field, some teams still have solid running games. Many of the top running backs are returning from 2025, including Kewan Lacy and Ahmad Hardy. Meanwhile, Caleb Hawkins and Cam Cook are in new places. Still, some spots in the top ten are open from players moving on, such as Jeremiyah Love and Emmett Johnson, who are now in the NFL. With some backs in new places, some working with new offensive coordinators, and others returning to great spots, these are the top ten college fantasy running backs in 2026. 1. Kewan Lacy | Ole Miss Kewan Lacy was one of the top running backs in the nation last year. He led the nation with 306 carries and racked up 1,567 yards to go with 24 touchdowns. Lacy’s value is all about volume, especially since he does not factor into the passing game on a regular basis. He had 18 or more carries ten times last year, seven 100-yard games, and a 200-yard outing. He also failed to find the end zone just once last season, giving him more three-touchdown games than zero. Having Trinidad Chambliss also helps. His ability keeps the defense honest and allows big runs, which Lacy capitalized on. If Ole Miss can continue to put up major points like that year, Lacy will find the end zone a ton and be the top back this year. 2. Caleb Hawkins | Oklahoma State Credit: Danny Wild-Imagn Images Caleb Hawkins finished last year as the top fantasy running back. He led the nation in rushing touchdowns with 25, while also sitting 12th in carries at 231 and racking up 1,434 yards. Unlike Lacy, Hawkins is a part of the passing game with Drew Mestemaker. He brought in 32 receptions for 370 yards and four touchdowns last year. Hawkins had some boom-or-bust tendencies last year. Of his 25 touchdowns, 17 of them came in just four games. He was also much less valuable than Lacy when his team was behind. Considering Hawkins is making the move from North Texas to Oklahoma State, but in a similar offense, the chances for those games increase. 3. LJ Martin | BYU LJ Martin was the 2025 Big-12 Offensive Player of the Year for BYU. He finished with 1,305 yards and 12 touchdowns last season, but did not have a receiving score. The BYU offense under Kalani Sitake has been historically run-heavy, which should give Martin the carries needed to put up a huge season. Further, BYU played a lot of tight games last year, but often had the lead late in the game. This should be similar this season, which will give Martin more carries. As long as Martin keeps his volume up, he will be over 1,200 yards again, and if he can find the end zone more, he has the ability to be the top running back in fantasy. 4. Cam Cook | West Virginia No one is benefiting from a transfer more than Cam Cook. Cook was a stud for Jacksonville State last year. He ran for 1,659 yards on 295 carries and found the end zone 16 times. It was his only season at Jacksonville State, meaning he never overlapped with Rich Rodriguez, his new coach at West Virginia. Still, the offense last year ran many similar components to the offense Cook will be moving into. With his speed, the former Jacksonville State running back is a perfect fit for the spread speed option attack that West Virginia will be running, which is going to set Cook up for a huge year. 5. Jadan Baugh | Florida Bob Kupbens-Imagn Images Jadan Baugh is set to be the primary back for Florida this season. Baugh ran for 1,170 yards and eight scores last year. The new offense should help Baugh out as well. Jon Sumrall runs an aggressive style of offense that has spread and pro set aspects. It relies heavily on a strong ground game, which will be led by Baugh. Further, Sumrall offenses typically run more down near the goal line than Billy Napier did, which should result in his touchdown numbers going up. Baugh will also be more involved in the passing game, which only increases his value. 6. Mark Fletcher | Miami (FL) Mark Fletcher returns to Miami (FL) in 2026 looking for vengeance . Fletcher was RB17 in 2025 after running for 1,192 yards and 12 touchdowns last year. With a new quarterback coming in for Miami, Fletcher may be seeing more carries as well. He was phenomenal in the College Football Playoffs for the Hurricanes as well. He ran for over 100 yards in three of the four games, and ran for 90 yards against Ohio State. Further, he scored three times in the playoffs, twice on the ground and once on a reception. The key for Fletcher will not be volume, but making the most of his carries. He had four games last year in which he averaged 3.5 yards per carry or worse. 7. Justice Haynes | Georgia Tech Justice Haynes decided to transfer from Michigan to Georgia Tech in the offseason. Haynes was solid in 2025, running for 857 yards and ten touchdowns. He did all of that in just seven games. Haynes ran for over 110 yards in six of the seven games, while scoring a touchdown in six of the seven games as well. He also was not a part of the passing game, and he also split carries with Jordan Marshall. Now, Haynes will be the lead back and not be splitting nearly as many reps. Marshall will take his first reps in the new role in Kansas’ season opener against LIU, at 8 pm ET, Sept
articles._body: The Kansas Jayhawks have named redshirt sophomore Isaiah Marshall as the team’s starting quarterback to kick off the 2026 college football season, according to On3’s Pete Nakos . Marshall will take his first reps in the new role in Kansas’ season opener against LIU, at 8 pm ET, Sept. 4 on ESPNU. [ $19.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage ] Marshall beat out Cole Ballard and Chase Jenkins for the starting QB job, replacing Jalon Daniels as the Jayhawks’ QB1 over the last two years. The Southfield (Mich.) native is entering his third season at Kansas. He played in nine games for the Jayhawks last year and completed three passes for 28 yards, while rushing for 160 yards on 15 carries. In 2025, Ballard played in eight games and completed 10 of 22 passes for 108 yards, one touchdown, and one interception, while also rushing for 92 yards on 15 carries. The two duked it out during the spring and through the early stages of fall camp, with Marshall ultimately getting the nod. Ballard is likely to see action in the opener against LIU, with the Jayhawks considered to be 40-point favorites over the visitors. Ballard, Marshall have developed strong friendship in QB battle Despite both pushing for the starting job, Marshall and Ballard have become friends who are genuinely happy for the other’s success. “They’re [in] a great competition, and they’ve become really close friendship-wise, which is kind of cool in that deal,” offensive coordinator Jim Zebrowski told JayhawkSlant earlier this month. “Pushing each other. They’re making each other better.” The two spend plenty of time together on the field and in the locker room, but have also found common interests off of it. “We had talked about it, and then he came into the locker room after a lift and said, ‘Hey, when are you golfing?’ I said, ‘I’m golfing tomorrow. You want to come?’ He said, ‘Yeah,’” Ballard said. “Our goal is to go play with LeBron one day. Since LeBron got into golfing, if we can ever do that, it’d be awesome.” Both will be looking to be part of a successful rebound in 2026 after the Jayhawks finished 5-7 last season. Following the opener against LIU, Kansas will welcome arch rival No. 25 Missouri into Lawrence for a Friday night showdown on Fox on Sept. 11.

articles.title: The AI Odyssey: How a primal fear from the Ancient Greek world has been awakened by new technology
articles.summary: Long before chatbots, the Greeks built an entire philosophy around the anxiety that rules 2026. We are all Odysseus, sailing through the the sirens' call.
articles._body: The myth of the sirens’ call has been with us for thousands of years, most recently brought to life in Christopher Nolan’s blockbuster The Odyssey . They’re a supernatural creature whose call is so enticing that it sends men to their doom—but the phrase has become a stand-in for that thing you know you shouldn’t do, but you simply can’t resist. Odysseus ended up lashing himself to the mast and ordering his crew to plug their ears with wax. When he heard the sirens’ call, though, he screamed to be released and begged his men to let him go. The man who’d spent 10 years outwitting gods didn’t trust himself for 30 seconds within earshot of a sound he knew would destroy him. That specific kind of dread—the fear of what you might do if the temptation were real—is older than the internet, older than AI, older than any technology that has ever been accused of making us weaker. It was a key plot line in the Iliad and The Odyssey, and centuries later, became the central problem of Greek philosophy, the thing the Stoics spent their lives trying to solve. And it is the same thing a large and quietly growing number of people feel every time they open a chatbot; why they hate the technology without using it, and want to bring to a screeching halt the data centers driving the biggest economic boom in at least a century. It’s the fear about how you can’t help yourself, that you’re not good enough or smart enough; that when an easy, even potentially destructive solution lies in front of you, you won’t be strong enough to resist the call of the sirens. Socrates had the same fear about the act of writing, scribes had the same fear about Gutenberg’s printing press, and John Saxon had the same fear about the calculator. But AI concentrates all of these fears in a place beyond the act of writing, printing or calculating to the very act of thinking itself. Seen in this light, The Odyssey ‘s billion-dollar success isn’t an accident for times like these. The fear underneath the data People who secretly use AI at work and describe it as “cheating” aren’t worried about their boss finding out. The word surfaces because some part of them is already asking a different question: if this were taken away tomorrow, would I still be good at my job? Would I still be smart? Everyone knows the name for this: impostor syndrome, the persistent, private fear of being exposed as less capable than everyone believes. With AI, there’s now a tool sitting by your side, silently keeping score—and exposing every hallucination that you’re not qualified enough to catch. The second fear is about character, not competence: what if I don’t actually have any self-control? What if I accept the first output from the chatbot without thinking of a way to genuinely improve it? What if I get roasted for putting more AI slop into the world? The psychological literature calls this “cognitive offloading”—using external tools to reduce the internal demands of a task. Humans have done this since the days of the ancient Greeks, with Socrates one of the earliest recorded voices in history to worry about how humans let themselves off the hook of heavy intellectual lifting. Generative AI offloads reasoning, synthesis, and creative judgment—the cognitive work through which expertise is actually built, not just retrieved. Social psychologists have documented for decades how people are “ cognitive misers ,” a term coined by Susan Fiske and Shelley Taylor in their foundational work on social cognition, meaning we find effortful deliberate thought aversive and default to shortcuts whenever available. This may be the real controversy over AI that is roiling the workplace and society, as noted in The AI Shift , the Financial Times ‘ weekly newsletter on how AI is reshaping work by columnist John Burn-Murdoch , who drew on research from economists José Azar, Mireia Giné and Javier Sanz-Espín to show that the most AI-exposed occupations aren’t shedding workers—employment, on paper, looks fine. But wages in those roles are down sharply relative to less-exposed work, and workers in them have become far less likely to switch jobs at all. Workers aren’t getting fired as a result of AI, but they seem to be getting quietly worth less, and quietly stuck. The real fault line, Burn-Murdoch argues, isn’t between occupations, but between execution and evaluation. Burn-Murdoch’s name for what separates these two groups is conscientiousness—and he notes that large numbers of workers who use AI on the job do so secretly, describing it as “cheating.” But in the summer of Odysseus, workers in an AI-addled word seem to fear something more primal and ancient: that they can’t resist the sirens’ call. Every technology that saves you effort has done this before Back to Socrates, for a second: the great Greek philosopher made eerily familiar arguments in opposition to the creation of the technology of writing, around 370 BCE. He argued that writing would “ implant forgetfulness ,” producing students with the mere appearance of wisdom—people who can recite but can no longer actually think. Scrolls would turn humans into stochastic parrots, he said, to paraphrase a modern critique of AI. The same fear resurfaced, smaller and less remembered, when the printing press began moving knowledge out of memory and onto the page. A German Benedictine abbot named Johannes Trithemius wrote a treatise called De Laude Scriptorum (“In Praise of Scribes”) arguing that printed books would never be the equal of handwritten manuscripts. “Printed books will never be the equivalent of handwritten codices, especially since printed books are often deficient in spelling and appearance.” The fear resurfaced again, with real data behind it this time, when calculators entered Ame

articles.title: ‘Clearly, people hate data centers’: Sam Altman admits Americans hate what he’s wrought as his own data centers head quits
articles.summary: Seven in 10 Americans oppose an AI data center near them, even as OpenAI adds multi-gigawatt projects across the U.S
articles._body: OpenAI’s infrastructure ambitions are colliding with a less technical problem: public backlash. CEO Sam Altman is conceding that Americans are openly hostile to the facilities powering the AI boom, awkward timing for a company both planning to spend $50 billion this year on compute. “Clearly, people hate data centers—right now, at least,” Altman told Time in an interview. “People are pretty negative on AI.” The week before Altman sat for Time, OpenAI’s head of data centers Chris Malone left the company , the Wall Street Journal reported, as confirmed by CNBC, which obtained a statement from OpenAI saying that he had “recently reorganized” the infrastructure team. OpenAI spent the past year dramatically expanding Stargate , the infrastructure project it launched with SoftBank early last year with plans to invest as much as $500 billion in the U.S. AI infrastructure. By September 2025, OpenAI had announced six U.S. Stargate sites , and said those facilities—along with its Abilene flagship and ongoing CoreWeave projects—would bring Stargate to nearly 7 gigawatts of planned capacity. It has since added a more-than-1-GW Michigan campus , a Georgia project contracted for 3.2 GW of power, and, this month, an agreement to secure approximately 8 GW of IT capacity in southern Ohio . OpenAI said it is already planning beyond Stargate’s original 10-gigawatt target , and claims it still does not have enough computing power.  “If anything, we should have bought a lot more,” Sachin Katti, the OpenAI executive overseeing its compute efforts, told Time. Americans increasingly don’t want data centers next door Altman’s assessment of the public mood isn’t far off.  Seven in 10 Americans oppose building data centers in their area, according to a Gallup poll released in May, including 48% who strongly oppose one. Data centers can consume enormous amounts of electricity, and residents in communities targeted for development worry about higher power bills , water usage, noise and the strain on local infrastructure. Some estimates peg the electricity cost of data centers to $23 billion . The opposition is already having financial consequences for hyperscalers. At least 48 data center projects representing $156 billion in investment were blocked or stalled by local resistance. Even though only 8% of Americans who oppose data centers live near one, the outrage has gone national .   A Pew Research Center survey released earlier this year found Americans were much more likely to say data centers were bad than good for home energy costs, the environment and nearby quality of life. Among people who said they had heard a lot about data centers, 67% said they believed the facilities were mostly bad for household energy costs. Those concerns are colliding with a surge in electricity demand. U.S. power consumption grew about 1.7% a year from 2020 through 2025 after barely growing over the previous 15 years, according to the Energy Information Administration . The agency said data centers are helping drive the increase. The backlash is starting to shape policy–and the midterms State governments are now responding to frustrated constituents with potential ramifications for OpenAI and other hyperscalers. Local officials proposed more than 120 moratoriums on data center development in 38 states as of July. Texas Gov. Greg Abbott ordered regulators to scrutinize data centers seeking to connect to the state’s power grid before allowing projects to move forward earlier this month. ERCOT, which manages most of the Texas grid, was facing roughly 474 gigawatts of requests for new connections— more than five times the state’s record peak electricity demand. That matters for OpenAI because Texas is central to Stargate, with its flagship site in Abilene, and additional pending projects in the state. Pennsylvania Gov. Josh Shapiro took his own steps on Aug. 18, signing an executive order that imposed new energy-affordability, environmental and community requirements on data centers and removed AI data centers from a fast-track permitting program. Data center backlash is also uniting people from across the political spectrum ahead of the midterm elections. While President Donald Trump champions them, most registered voters oppose data centers, including 60% of Republicans and 53% of MAGA, according to a Fox News poll .  This story was originally featured on Fortune.com

Looks like he hurt his right arm on a run play in 11 on 11s. He’s being evaluated on the sideline,” reported Nicholas Moreano of Bears Roundtable on X, formerly Twitter. Moreano did note that “Maybe a positive, but Jaylon Johnson is still out here, standing next to Al Harris.” It’s unclear exactly what occurred on the run play that caused Johnson to go down with the injury, and just how serious the ailment might be. The incident occurred during a joint practice with the Tennessee Titans as the two teams prepare for their upcoming preseason game against one another this weekend. Losing Johnson for any significant amount of time for a second straight year, after he missed several games with an adductor tear last season, would certainly be a tough blow for the Bears to stomach as they look to build off the success of last season. articles.title: Packers player on roster bubble with most at stake in 2026 NFL preseason finale
articles.summary: The Green Bay Packers enter their preseason finale with several difficult decisions remaining before Sunday’s roster deadline. No decision captures the tension between potential and practicality better than Isaiah Neyor’s bid for a place in a crowded Packers receiving room. Neyor has produced eno
articles._body: The Green Bay Packers enter their preseason finale with several difficult decisions remaining before Sunday’s roster deadline. No decision captures the tension between potential and practicality better than Isaiah Neyor’s bid for a place in a crowded Packers receiving room. Neyor has produced enough to remain in the conversation. He also has not separated himself enough to make the choice easy. Christian Watson, Matthew Golden, Jayden Reed, Savion Williams, Bo Melton, and Skyy Moore appear positioned to claim six receiver spots. Green Bay must decide whether a seventh wideout provides more value than extra depth elsewhere. That makes Neyor the clearest player on the Packers’ roster bubble with the most at stake Friday vs. the Arizona Cardinals. Will Sheppard has offered steadier production and punt-return experience. J. Michael Sturdivant has also received meaningful work on special teams. Neyor owns an intriguing combination of size and speed, but he must prove that upside can help the Packers on more than occasional passing downs. Isaiah Neyor has flashed without securing a Packers roster spot The former Nebraska receiver’s path makes this opportunity especially significant. The 6-foot-4, 218-pound wideout signed with the San Francisco 49ers as an undrafted free agent in 2025 before being released. The Packers signed him during training camp, kept him on the practice squad throughout his rookie season, and elevated him for their NFC Wild Card playoff game. He returned on a reserve/future contract and spent a full offseason learning the offense. The progress has appeared throughout camp and the preseason. Neyor caught all four of his targets for 34 yards during Green Bay’s opener against the Pittsburgh Steelers. He followed with three receptions for 47 yards in a 33-13 victory over the Denver Broncos. His 27-yard reception from Kyle McCord displayed the downfield ability that makes him different from many reserve receivers. Through two games, Neyor and Sheppard share the team lead with seven receptions. However, the numbers do not tell the entire story. Neyor caught only three of six targets against Denver and also had a drop and penalties that he cannot repeat in the Packers’ preseason finale . Sheppard caught six passes for 47 yards and a touchdown in the same game, turning his best week of practice into the strongest performance among the bubble receivers. The Packers’ wide receiver competition also extends beyond offensive production. Sheppard has worked as a punt returner, while Sturdivant logged 15 special-teams snaps through two preseason games despite leaving the Denver contest with a concussion. Sturdivant returned to team work during Wednesday’s joint practice with the Cardinals, preventing Neyor from gaining an uncontested path to the final spot. Neyor may offer the highest receiving ceiling of the three. Still, the seventh receiver is unlikely to earn regular targets ahead of Green Bay’s established options. That player must cover kicks, block, handle an emergency return assignment, or fill another weekly role. Athletic promise alone does not settle the roster math. Packers need a complete performance from Isaiah Neyor Friday’s game at Lambeau Field is not simply another opportunity for Neyor to make one impressive catch. It is his last chance to present a complete case before the Packers’ 53-man roster takes shape . He needs clean routes, dependable hands, disciplined blocking, and error-free work wherever the coaching staff deploys him. A splash play would help because explosive receiving ability is Neyor’s strongest argument. At the same time, one deep completion cannot outweigh a missed assignment, a costly penalty, or an unwillingness to contribute on special teams. Coaches have evaluated every practice rep since July, and the finale will matter most if it confirms the growth they have already seen. The larger roster construction makes the challenge even harder for the second-year wide receiver. Green Bay could use an additional spot at tight end, offensive line, defensive tackle, or safety. Keeping seven receivers would require general manager Brian Gutekunst to believe the final wideout offers more immediate value than a player at one of those positions. Neyor, therefore, is competing against Sheppard and Sturdivant but also against every bubble player elsewhere on the roster. Neyor has done enough to deserve serious consideration, so portraying Friday as a simple make-or-break referendum would overstate one exhibition game. A strong finale would not guarantee his place. A quiet or mistake-filled night, however, would leave little reason for the Packers to depart from the more conventional six-receiver approach. That is why Neyor has more to prove than any other Green Bay player in the finale . His physical talent has kept the door open, and his preseason production has placed him within reach of the roster. Now he must show the reliability and versatility required to walk through it. articles.title: NC State coach Dave Doeren opens up on new mindset about transfer portal departures
articles.summary: NC State coach Dave Doeren used to grow frustrated at the revolving door of talent his program has become with the popularity of the transfer portal. At times, players that he and his staff identified and developed has darted to other Power Conference programs after two or three years in Raleigh. Bu
articles._body: NC State coach Dave Doeren used to grow frustrated at the revolving door of talent his program has become with the popularity of the transfer portal. At times, players that he and his staff identified and developed has darted to other Power Conference programs after two or three years in Raleigh. But shortly after the Wolfpack lost three defensive backs in the final hours of the portal being open on Jan. 2, 2025, Doeren changed his thinking on the process. He was disappointed in the moment, even going as far as calling it a “below the waist blow,” but once he reflected on it in the following days, the veteran coach emerged with a new mindset. “I [asked myself], ‘Why do you do this?’’ Doeren said on his weekly radio show Wednesday night. “You go back to what you love. You love helping these guys, you love competing, you love the game, you love the staff chemistry. None of that’s changed. Let’s just figure out how to handle this other piece that has changed. Sometimes you need a little break from it all to marinate on what’s really important.” Instead of being the type of coach to grow angry at what has become the norm in college football, Doeren took the opposite approach. He self-assessed himself and the program before coming up with a plan of how to move on from these situations in a positive manner.  After all, sulking or feeling sorry for himself wouldn’t solve the problem that sat in front of him: Who would replace the holes on his roster? That’s where he found peace, even believing that the team could grow stronger through adding new blood to the roster when others depart for what they believe are greener pastures. Soon enough, Doeren took his new mentality into the Murphy Center where he shared it with the rest of his coaching staff. In the blink of an eye, the whole program’s mindset changed and followed the now 14th-year coach into the new era of college athletics. “I just kind of got sick of hearing, ‘That’s not what I signed up for’ from people in our business. It was kind of like, ‘OK, well then get out of the business,’” Doeren said. “If you’re going to be in it, find a way to be successful in it, find a way to be happy in it. I had to look in the mirror. You have to be a part of the solution.  “That’s why I told my staff, ‘We’re going to figure this out, do the best we can in this space. Don’t bring your negative thoughts about it to the building anymore.’” Doeren and his staff came up with a “solution-based planning” approach to work through this process. He made it clear that there can still be disappointment from losing a player that the team wanted to keep to the transfer portal, one that the staff would have liked to watch develop and grow in an NC State uniform. But at the same time, that can’t affect what happens next. “At some point, if they want to leave, you know there’s a great place for someone else to come,” Doeren said. “We’ve been successful in the portal, so it’s not like the end of the world. We’ll go find another guy that wants to play here, just like when a coach leaves, I’ll find one that can make us better.” Doeren has been successful on both ends of his comparison. Take this past offseason, for example, NC State lost starting left tackle Jacarrius Peak to the portal (and eventually South Carolina), but signed ECU’s Jimarion McCrimon to fill the void in what some around the building believe is a long-term upgrade at the position. At the same time, Doeren replaced Charley Wiles (who moved to director of high school relations) with defensive tackles coach Elisha Shaw , a former four-star defensive lineman that has turned into a rising star in the coaching profession. That’s just one example, but NC State has worked to make the most of the new era of athletics. Yes, that early-January night when Brandon Cisse , Bishop Fitzgerald and Tamarcus Cooley all entered the transfer portal with just hours remaining before the deadline after initially making their intentions to return known hurt, but at the same time, it led to a positive growing point for Doeren and the program. It might have come from one of Doeren’s lower points of his tenure in Raleigh, but his new opinion of the transfer portal’s ripple effects has seemed to extend his desire to coach as he continues to adapt heading into his 14th season leading the Wolfpack. Other notes from Doeren’s radio show – Offensive line coach Garett Tujague made a brief appearance on the show. He noted that he has eight players that he’s comfortable playing on the offensive line this season: tackles Teague Andersen , McCrimon and Trent Mitchell , and interior players Spike Sowells , Kamen Smith , Yousef Mugharbil , Rico Jackson and Daniel Cruz . – Tujague stressed that Jackson will play significantly as a rotational player. The goal is to take snaps off some of the others on the unit. Jackson can play both guard and tackle and could be featured at both spots throughout the season. – Doeren shared a positive review of junior wide receiver Keenan Jackson . He said the third-year player has “practiced really well,” while also displaying his “good chemistry” with junior quarterback CJ Bailey over the last month.  – NC State’s running back room depth seemed to excite Doeren. articles.title: A List of All the Guests in Rosalía’s Confessional on Her ‘LUX’ Tour
articles.summary: The singer has invited celebrities ranging from Aitana and Marcello Hernández to Yeri Mua and Chappell Roan to share secrets about their love lives onstage.
articles._body: Why go to church when you can go see a show at Rosalía ’s LUX Tour? The Spanish artist, who is currently on the Latin American leg of her LUX Tour, has delivered a deeply conceptual, carefully curated performance. Each concert includes ballet and intricately choreographed routines, as well as an art exhibition — with the dancers and singer as the main characters — filled with nods to some of history’s most iconic works of art, religious iconography and representations of Catholic and Christian symbols and emblems. One of the Catholic Church’s best-known practices is confession, in which people reveal their sins to a priest bound by a vow of silence. Every night on Rosalía’s tour, she also has a confessional. Right before performing “La Perla,” one of the biggest hits from  LUX , she invites a famous figure from the entertainment world to enter her confessional, set up onstage and in full view of the audience, to share intimate stories about their love life. According to Rosalía’s song, a “perla” is a problematic or dishonest person who cannot be trusted. Rosalía released  LUX , her fourth studio album, in November 2025, making history on the Billboard charts as the first artist to simultaneously score No. 1 debuts across five album charts:  Top Latin Albums , Top Latin Pop Albums , Classical Albums , Classical Crossover Albums and World Albums.  The artist kicked off her tour in Lyon, France, on March 16. During stops in Paris, London, Madrid and Barcelona, she welcomed famous faces — including Lola Young, Aitana and Cara Delevingne — into her confessional. All of the other concerts have featured celebrities and friends who have joined her in the confessional. After rescheduling the Florida concert dates of the U.S. leg of the tour, which was set to begin in Miami, the “Motomami” singer gave her first performance in Boston on June 11. She has completed 10 of the 13 planned stops in North America, where several artists have joined her and made controversial revelations. Here’s a list of all the guests who have joined the LUX tour confessional so far.

articles.title: Browns rumors: Shedeur Sanders dirt comes out with trade, Dillon Gabriel revelations
articles.summary: The Cleveland Browns are still recovering from the aftershocks of naming Deshaun Watson their starting quarterback this year ahead of Shedeur Sanders. Todd Monken’s decision was met with plenty of backlash from fans who were hoping to see the Sanders get more opportunities to refine his gam
articles._body: Th e Cleveland Browns are still recovering from the aftershocks of naming Deshaun Watson their starting quarterback this year ahead of Shedeur Sanders. Todd Monken’s decision was met with plenty of backlash from fans who were hoping to see the Sanders get more opportunities to refine his game this year. Perhaps unsurprisingly, reports are now coming out that seem to help justify the Browns’ decision to hand the reins to Watson. “There are also even questions about Sanders’ fit as a backup, including — fair or not — because of the celebrity and distraction components that come along with him being such a high-profile and polarizing figure,” reported Matt Zenitz of CBS Sports. “Do you really want to deal with that (especially with someone who’s not your starting quarterback)?” said one front office staff member. Sanders slipped to the fifth round in last year’s NFL Draft despite having a strong college football career at Colorado under his father, Deion Sanders. While there were questions about his attitude and perceived overconfidence, there are also plenty of concerns about his viability as a true starting-level talent in the NFL, without many pro tools that seem to have translated thus far. This, combined with the perceived distraction of his media attention, might make the juice not worth the squeeze in the eyes of some teams. Zenitz also reported that “there are even some around the NFL who even wonder if Gabriel would be a better fit as Cleveland’s backup, referencing things such as his work ethic and the ability to function on short notice.” In any case, the Browns are slated to get their new season underway on September 13 with a road game against the Jacksonville Jaguars. articles.title: Sooners Have Youngsters Way Ahead of Schedule, How’s That Happening?
articles.summary: With Oklahoma football a little over a week from kicking off their 2026 season Sooners fans are taking some deep dives into the roster. We take a look at just how Oklahoma football has gotten to where they are with some young players way ahead of schedule.
articles._body: With the Sooners kickoff just eight days away the season is nearly upon us. And with that in mind we’re looking at all that is happening around Oklahoma football. From an intriguing situation that is emerging along the offensive line to how the simple realities of team 132 are impacting Oklahoma’s recruiting plans and message. Sooners fans had plenty to ask and talk about and here are just a few examples of this week’s Board Chat . Has Spring and now August camp, changed your viewpoint on OU’s 2027 fall high school needs? – Severus No, not really. I do think you feel better with what the Sooners are adding/where they are adding. I mean you think about the young OL that should return next year and you add pieces like Cooper Hackett , Kaeden Penny , Isaac Coughran , etc. There’s a lot that makes sense there. Adding Cooper Witten and Taven Epps to James Nesta / Cole Sullivan / Marcus James /etc. Again, more than I’ve thought this since maybe…2000s Bob Stoops era, there’s such a clear plan to what they are doing. Now does it all go the way they hope? We’ll see but I can see what they are thinking. Obviously it appears Noah Best was underrated at least by Rivals. Why do you think everyone missed this evaluation? Or do you? Will he get a lot of playing time even if the Sooners O-line is injury free? – Willie T the Neon Sooner He’s going to play and a lot. I’m not sure when Jake Maikkula comes back if he isn’t the starting RG. They are very high on him. As far as his evaluation, I liked him and so did most – but I think he’s a better athlete than any of us recognized. He’s also a guy that very much understands the job. This is a kid that I watched fight Jalen Brewster to a near stalemate. He moves well and he’s tremendously strong. There’s some Ben Powers in his game if you’re looking for an Oklahoma football name to file away. People have talked about Ryan Fodje having one of the best fall camps, but now we’re talking about Best battling Fodje for the RG spot. Does Fodje not have a starting spot somewhere locked down? – SoonerAlex OU offensive lineman Ryan Fodje at spring practice March 30, 2026. Photo by Carey Murdock/SoonerScoop I think that’s one of the real questions. I think he’ll get a ton of reps no matter what – they want him to know how much they value him and see him as a future NFL guy. BUUUUT if their best five has Best at RG…they don’t have a lot of options. What I’d expect, in that scenario is that you’d get a lot of Fodje rotating. Maybe with Harris at right tackle and Best at right guard, just as examples and possibilities. Just to make sure he’s staying up with reps and preparing him for the reality that he’s either the starting RG or RT next year. I don’t think there’s much question he’s one of OU’s 5 best offensive linemen right now but he’s also such a unique talent in his ability to swing from position to position. He gives OU cover at a number of spots. He is either Oklahoma football’s No. or No. 2 at LT/C/RG/RT. That’s just crazy to think about. Can you speak to how well so many true are showing out in Sooners camp and how that reflects on Jim Nagy and company? – BobStoopsBrokenPinky I think it shows you that not only are they identifying good talent early on but are identifying guys that are good fits for their coaches/playstyle. The last two years OU has had 3 young OL who immediately made an impression – Michael Fasusi and Fodje…those were guys that predated Nagy’s involvement but now you look at a guy like Best? I went back and looked at TRUE freshman who were at least very buzzy like those 3 were almost from the jump. Since 2017? There’d been two. Creed Humphrey and Cayden Green . Now other players emerged, Andrew Raym , Anton Harrison , etc. but for guys to hit the ground running it’s about more than just physical talent. There has to be a mindset and again that’s just OL I’m talking about in this example. Courtland Guillory , Tank Carrington , Jake Kreul , Jacob Curry (he was on that path before injury IMO), Markel Ford , that’s a lot of guys in a few years who were ready to not just compete but to have a role as freshmen.

articles.title: Lauren Alaina Breaks Down 5 Essential Tracks From Her New Album ‘Stages’: ‘I Am in the Best Stage of My Life, Ever’
articles.summary: The country hitmaker reflects on the album that looks at life's highs and lows.
articles._body: Lauren Alaina has gone through many chapters in her life, and she relives many of them on her new album Stages , out Friday (Aug. 28). But happily, for Alaina, she is in a great stage right now, to say the least. “I am in the best stage of my life ever,” she tells Billboard during a recent visit to Los Angeles.  “I’ve still lived some heartache in this stage, losing my dad [in July 2024], but I genuinely feel like I am living the life that I’ve always dreamed of.” The former 2011 American Idol runner up (she came in second behind Scotty McCreery ) says she’s finally found the balance between career and family she dreamed of for years. “I remember for so long thinking I would never have a husband and a family, because I worked so much, and I was like, “Where am I going to meet a husband?’ Now I look at my daughter, and she is everything to me,” she says. “I can’t believe it’s my life. I think a lot of women fear that if you have a family and a marriage, your career will take a back seat, and I think that is probably true for some people. But I’m so grateful that I found a way to navigate both.” Alaina, 31, married Cam Arnold in February 2024, and their daughter, Beni Doll Arnold, was born in June 2025. This stage has also brought Alaina to a new label, Big Loud — after more than 10 years on Mercury Nashville — and to the release of her first full-length album in five years. “I’m so thankful for everything I did [on the previous label]. But it was time to move on and do something new,” she says. “That was really scary for me to make that step, because I was like, ‘What if I’m wrong?’ It took some time at my new label to get things established and make the new music.” Fans clearly missed Alaina, given the reaction to “All My Exes,” a lighthearted duet with Chase Matthew that is bulleted at No. 14 on Billboard ’s Country Airplay chart dated Aug. 29. Alaina worked with producers Joey Moi and Ben Johnson on the 16-track set, and co-wrote most of the songs. She also reunited with her childhood friend, Kane Brown , on “Never Been in Love,” their first duet together since “What Ifs,” their 2017 hit that topped both the Country Airplay and Country Songs chart. Alaina, who acted in the Hallmark movie Roadhouse Romance in 2021, still wants to pursue more acting roles. “I just had an audition sent to me two weeks ago, and I couldn’t read for it because my tour dates,” she says. Her dream costars are Matthew McConaughey and Reese Witherspoon. “It’s probably not going to happen, but you never know,” she says. “I mean, everything that I’ve had so far in my career, people would have said probably was not going to happen, and it has.” Below, Alaina breaks down five essential tracks from Stages for Billboard .

articles.title: Notre Dame national championship buzz shoots to stratosphere with expert picks

After missing the College Football Playoffs in 2025, the team is set for a run in 2026. Now, more experts are also selecting Notre Dame
articles._body: Expectations are through the roof for Notre Dame football in 2026. Rece Davis recently declared that Notre Dame is the favorite to win the national championship. After missing the College Football Playoffs in 2025, the team is set for a run in 2026. Now, more experts are also selecting Notre Dame to win it all, per Nicole Auerbach and Joshua Perry of NBC Sports. “My bracket reflects my overall philosophy heading into this college football season: I trust the Big Ten’s big three, and I trust Notre Dame,” Auerbach wrote. She has the Irish getting the top overall seed in the tournament, knocking out Ohio State and Oregon on the way to the national championship game. There, they will face defending champion Indiana, but get the win. “But, overall, I like Notre Dame best. The Irish have the best defensive player in the country in cornerback Leonard Moore. They have what could be the best quarterback in the country in CJ Carr. They feel good about every level of their defense and are confident that they can have a productive run game, even after losing the special Jeremiyah Love-Jadarian Price duo,” Auerbach continued. Auerbach was not the only one to pick Notre Dame, as Joshua Perry also has them winning it all. He has Notre Dame as the two seed, beating Miami and Ohio State before taking out Georgia in the national championship. “My game picks were pretty much chalk, mostly because I’m not going to pick against myself right now. I’m really high on Notre Dame, and that’s my championship pick. Marcus Freeman has built a strong program, and when you combine that with a schedule that virtually guarantees them a playoff bid and all of his roster talent, the Irish will be in position to be the last team standing,” Perry wrote. Notre Dame opens the season against Wisconsin at Lambeau Field on September 6. articles._body: With the Kansas City Chiefs preparing for the 2026 NFL season , the team is looking to get fully healthy, especially when it comes to star quarterback Patrick Mahomes after a frustrating 2025. As Mahomes makes his injury recovery with the Chiefs , he’ll need his offensive line to be healthy, with the latest update on Josh Simmons coming from an NFL insider that fans definitely want to hear. According to Nate Taylor at ESPN, he said on “Chiefs on KCSN” that Simmons is seen as “day-to-day” with a lower back injury, and it isn’t serious. He would even go as far as to say that if this week had a game on Sunday, he would be out there playing. “According to someone with knowledge of the situation, Josh Simmons is day-to-day with a lower back injury. I’m here to tell you he’s fine. If it was a game week, he’d be out there,” Taylor said. “Day-to-day is what was told to me.” “He’s fine. Okay, he’s fine. Josh Simmons’ back is fine,” Taylor continued. Josh Simmons is “day-to-day” But there’s reason for optimism pic.twitter.com/38JwExC2sb — Chiefs on KCSN (@chiefs_kcsn) August 27, 2026 Chiefs’ Andy Reid on Josh Simmons’ injury Simmons is looking to vastly improve in his sophomore season with the Chiefs after being selected with the 32nd overall pick in the 2025 NFL Draft, where he only appeared in eight games as a rookie. Having dealt with a family matter and a wrist injury impacting his availability last season, he’s looking to log a full season with Kansas City, though it remains to be seen if this back injury will be a nagging one. Chiefs head coach Andy Reid would even speak on Wednesday about Simmon’s status, according to Sports Illustrated. “Just getting his back checked out,” Reid said. “That’s the main thing. Like any other injury, we’ve got to make sure and see if it’s right or what’s wrong with it.” It remains to be seen when Simmons returns to practice for Kansas City and whether he will be ready to go for the regular-season opener on Week 1 on Sint. 14 against the Denver Broncos.
