articles._body: The Los Angeles Dodgers are closing in on their shot to go for three straight World Series titles. Shohei Ohtani being in the lineup is a given. However, Ohtani is looking to get back to the mound . He’s been off the pitching rotation due to soreness in his left knee. However, Dodgers GM Brandon Gomes gave a glimpse of behind-closed-doors meetings with Ohtani about a return for October, per MLB Now. Gomes told Brian Kenny that his communication with Ohtani is ongoing. “We have to talk to him and continue to communicate because there is no one else doing what he’s doing,” Gomes said. Dodgers GM Brandon Gomes shares insight into Shohei Ohtani's road back to the mound: "We have to talk to him and continue to communicate because there is no one else doing what he's doing." MLB Network + @SageUSAmerica pic.twitter.com/HvPhTCE67L — MLB Now (@MLBNow) August 27, 2026 Ohtani’s last appearance on the mound was July 3. He pitched 6 innings and recorded 9 strikeouts in a 4-3 win over the San Diego Padres. Afterward, Ohtani was taken off the rotation indefinitely . He is batting .288 with 137 hits, 30 home runs, and 80 RBIs. However, his inability to pitch has drastically limited his chances of winning the NL MVP Award. Lately, Ohtani has been competing with Pete Crow-Armstrong of the Chicago Cubs for the NL MVP. Ohtani is coming off winning three straight MVP Awards. In 2023, he won with the Los Angeles Angels in the American League. He won the last two with the Dodgers. Meanwhile, the Dodgers are looking to bounce back from two straight losses to the Atlanta Braves in a three-game series. The third game is scheduled for Thursday at Truist Park in Atlanta. Ohtani is expected to take a bullpen session on Friday, per Sonja Chen of MLB.com. He could make his return to the mound on Sunday against the Detroit Tigers. articles.title: John Fanta Discusses Vision For His New NBC Sports Show
articles.summary: Eric Canha-Imagn Images
articles._body: John Fanta’s new show, Fanta in 60 , debuts Monday night at 6 p.m. ET on Peacock and the NBC Sports NOW FAST channel. Ahead of the show’s launch, he spoke to Front Office Sports about what he’s striving for with the talk show, his hottest takes, a surreal interaction with a broadcasting icon, and his revelation that he’ll be a part of NBC’s Summer Olympics coverage in Los Angeles in 2028. Front Office Sports : You’re starting this new talk show. A lot of your work with NBC and just professionally in general has been related to the games, whether that’s doing play-by-play or sidelines or studio. Do you see yourself ever wanting to have a daily national talk platform, kind of like Dan Patrick’s show or The Herd ? John Fanta: Well, look, I love all sports. And for me, I idolize those guys. They speak up about what they’ve done every day. And I think I don’t look at myself as just a play-by-play guy or just a host or just a reporter.’ I think a lot of people looked at my career up until this time last year and said, “Well, you know, he’s been a college basketball person.” And the biggest reason why I joined NBC was to show I could expand beyond that. And so for me, the same can be said of the medium that I’m doing it in that I love the idea of bringing this show into people’s living rooms. And we’re going to start by doing it one day a week. And, it’s my goal for us to grow a product that people enjoy. We’ll take it where we go. I wouldn’t say that I want 12 to 3 or 6 to 9 or, in this case, 6 to 7 every single day to trump the responsibilities I have elsewhere for the company. I think that everything can go hand in hand. Because I like what I do in the play-by-play world and the reporting world, and I’m hopeful that I can continue to do all of these types of things. FOS : When you do Big East “Spaces,” I love it when you spar with some of these fans and get really animated. Are there any plans to have that type of audience interaction on your NBC show? JF: We’re going to be animated—why wouldn’t we be? TV is emotion and sports is emotion. And to bring that energy that you get that people have heard on Spaces, we’re going to have a voicemail box. That phone number will go live later this week. My goal is that we take people’s voicemails whether they are on the Browns quarterback saga that’s going down currently, or whether they’re on how LeBron fits in in Philadelphia, or whether they’re on someone’s movie review of what they saw over the weekend, or when somebody calls me and says, what’s your favorite Jersey Shore bar? I want to be interactive with fans. I don’t just want to come on the air and say, “You know, this is what I think and that’s what I think.” I want to blend comments from X, other social media, and YouTube with linear TV. I want it to sort of morph into those communities because I have social media to thank for my ride. I’ve been able to get more linear opportunities because I do think growing a social presence and audience has been important in that development. So I want to engage with people. I want them to be the pulse of the show. And I want us to answer as many voicemails live on our show that we can. And the voicemails that we don’t get to, we’ll probably be taping segments that will go on YouTube and on my X page so that we become that “Dear Abby” hotline. I want to be that. FOS : You’re obsessed with all these sports, regional and national. How do you keep up with them on the road when you’re working events, flying, and the hotels don’t have half the games you need? How are you just keeping up on all of this when you’re all over the place? JF: I read, and I will watch games back. I’ll watch tape. I read religiously. We have a research department in Stamford. They send a daily briefing for basically every sport. Without that daily briefing, I can’t do my job. I want to see what’s happening. Take NFL preseason takeaways from the weekend. I don’t think many people were able to watch every single preseason game in its entirety. But I opened up that briefing and I saw Jayden Daniels had limited action. So then I take a look for the Commanders and I take a deeper look there for the Cowboys trying to figure out their backup quarterback situation. Without that team of people behind the scenes, I don’t think any one human can consume every single thing that’s happening in this crazy world of sports. But I am a sports fan like our viewers and like you. When I put my son down to bed and I’m with my wife at night, she’ll sometimes fall asleep at 8:30 or 9. And I can tell you right now from about 9 to 10:30 or 11, I’m watching a mix of what’s happening live. And then I’ve got my laptop open and I am in bed and I’m reading and I’m looking at what’s happening. What are the headlines? What’s going on? Because to me, the preparation’s ongoing. My mind is spinning. And I think that that’s what you have to do if you’re going to be in the sports content game. You’ve got to be following what’s happening in real-time reacting to it in real-time. And for us, that’s why this show was a fun concept that’s now going to come to life because Monday, especially during football season, which is when this is launching, it’s the day. Everything’s happened over the weekend. We’re going to react to that, and then we’re going to look ahead. Here’s what’s coming your way. Here’s what we should be on the lookout for. And at NBC, we’ve got all these different properties. So it’ll be fun to get guests who are sometimes checking in to us from an NBA game or checking in ahead of a big Big Ten football game that week, or whatever Sunday night game [NFL, NBA, or MLB] there is. I’m constantly reading, and I talk to people. I live in New Jersey. I can tell you right now that my hour, 15-minute drive to Stamford, I get three to six phone calls in. articles.title: Vikings’ Kevin O’Connell teases cryptic Harrison Smith conversations
articles.summary: The Minnesota Vikings have just over two weeks to go until they are set to kick off the new 2026 NFL season. The Vikings recently got some tough news when it was announced that linebacker Jamal Adams would miss the entire upcoming season due to an injury sustained during training camp. Some have
articles._body: The Minnesota Vikings have just over two weeks to go until they are set to kick off the new 2026 NFL season. The Vikings recently got some tough news when it was announced that linebacker Jamal Adams would miss the entire upcoming season due to an injury sustained during training camp. Some have speculated that the move could open up a return for veteran defensive back Harrison Smith, who has yet to sign a new deal with the Vikings after playing out the end of his contract last season. Now, Kevin Seifert of ESPN has reported that Vikings head coach Kevin O’Connell “said he spoke with veteran safety Harrison Smith as recently as this week. The Vikings are clearly leaving open the possibility that Smith could play in 2026 rather than retire.” “I have had some conversations about where he’s at, what he’s thinking,” O’Connell said, “and we’ll keep you guys updated if there is an update on that.” Vikings fans certainly wouldn’t mind seeing Smith back in uniform this year, especially with the tough update regarding Adams. While he’s no longer the same explosive player that he was in his prime, Smith is still an elite defender with a high football IQ and physical tools to wreak havoc on opposing offenses. The Vikings had a strong defense once again in 2025, but fell short largely thanks to the quarterback position. This year, Minnesota will be starting veteran Kyler Murray ahead of JJ McCarthy, who had a rough first full season at the helm last year. The hope is that the Vikings’ offense will be able to match the production of its defense under Murray’s leadership. The Vikings will kick off their season on September 13 vs the Green Bay Packers. articles.title: Jahron Manning begins search for new team
articles.summary: Former Mississippi State safety Jahron Manning had hoped to return to the Bulldogs, but he does not qualify under new conference rules.
articles._body: Former Mississippi State safety Jahron Manning is in search of a new program. The player announced the decision on social media on Thursday after briefly exploring a return to the Bulldogs. Manning and fellow former Bulldog Malick Syalla had tried to gain eligibility together, and were practicing with the Bulldogs for the past two weeks as they continued the process. Manning posted his stats and highlights on Twitter on Thursday. Both players transferred to Mississippi State in 2025 and became key players on the defense. Sylla led the team in tackles for loss while Manning led the team with 91 total tackles. Manning was undrafted in the 2026 NFL Draft but signed briefly with the Atlanta Falcons in offseason spring workouts as a free agent. He was released from the team and did not make another NFL roster for the preseason when teams resumed operations in July and August. Manning had reportedly filed a suit against the NCAA along with Sylla in Oktibbeha County Chancery Court. Given his brief time spent with an NFL team in offseason workouts, he does not qualify under new conference rules set by the SEC, Big 10 and Big 12 disqualifying players returning to college from the professional ranks.

articles.title: Browns make shocking QB pick in ClutchPoints’ 2027 NFL Mock Draft
articles.summary: The Cleveland Browns recently made headlines when head coach Todd Monken announced that Shedeur Sanders would be benched this season in favor of Deshaun Watson, who will assume the starting quarterback position. The move angered fans, who were hoping that the younger Sanders would get another sho
articles._body: The Cleveland Browns recently made headlines when head coach Todd Monken announced that Shedeur Sanders would be benched this season in favor of Deshaun Watson , who will assume the starting quarterback position. The move angered fans, who were hoping that the younger Sanders would get another shot to prove himself, despite his struggles this past season. The Browns aren’t expected to be very competitive this year, and with this being the case, they could very well be looking at another premium draft pick in 2027, where selecting a quarterback will certainly be an option. Recently, Tim Crean of ClutchPoints projected the Browns to select quarterback Drew Mestemaker out of Oklahoma State with the number four pick next year in a mock draft. “After a massive year at North Texas, Drew Mestemaker is taking his talents to the big leagues in college football. And if he has another season where he slings it all over the yard, but this time does it in the Big 12, the NFL will come calling next. So, putting him here at N. 4 to Cleveland is a prediction that a big season is coming,” noted Crean. Not any pundits have Mestemaker going this high in their mock drafts, so it would certainly be a big swing for Cleveland at this spot, unless Mestemaker follows through and indeed has a huge season with Oklahoma State this year. The Browns are currently in somewhat of a quarterback jail, with Watson having seemingly stalled out after his promising first few years with the Houston Texans, and Sanders not having many pro-level tools at his disposal to be excited about. If the Browns do indeed end up with a top pick next year, it will be crucial for them to finally nail the choice and bring in a true building block. articles.title: LOCASH’s ‘Three Minutes of Positivity’ New Single Has The Duo ‘Talkin Bout’ Its Next Radio Run. Period.
articles.summary: Billboard's Makin' Tracks column looks at the writing and recording behind LOCASH's "Talkin Bout."
articles._body: “I hate punctuation.” LOCASH co-founder Preston Brust, should he read this story, will probably dislike the previous sentence — since periods and quotation marks are not his thing. “I will go back and erase punctuation out of my texts a lot, just kind of leaving a fingerprint of how I talk,” he says. Brust’s unusual take on commas and colons is behind the clean title presentation of the duo’s latest single, “Talkin Bout,” which took a bit of work to create. One of their Galaxy Label Group employees originally typed it as “Talking About,” then – after he corrected her – put apostrophes in place of the “g” and second “a.” He had her remove those, too. “She must’ve hit me up five times,” Brust notes. “I was really kind about it. I wrote back, ‘Talkin Bout.’ If it was up to me, the ‘T’ wouldn’t be capitalized and the ‘B’ wouldn’t be either.” “Talkin Bout,” released to country radio via PlayMPE on July 29, is two minutes and 37 seconds of sweet midtempo affirmation, supported by a burning production and hooky guitar riff. “Talkin” has sat in LOCASH’s possession for nearly three years since they created it, with the duo’s Chris Lucas checking in via Zoom on Oct. 6, 2023, as Brust and songwriter Nate Kenyon (“Dear Big City,” “Life With You”) met up to write at the home studio of Combustion Music writer-producer Blake Bollinger (“This Heart,” “Caught Up in the Country”). Kenyon started running through about a half-dozen song ideas, but they stopped him when he brought up “Talkin Bout” – or, as he was probably spelling it, “Talkin’ ‘Bout” – for a deep dive on the idea. “I saw the blueprint for it pretty easily,” Kenyon recalls. It felt “like a radio-hit kind of deal, like, ‘If I’m talking about this, it’s this.’ ‘This is this.’ ‘But if I’m talkin’ ‘bout a girl, I’m talkin’ ‘bout you.’ They loved it.” Bollinger brought up a percussive track he’d previously sketched out, and they launched into the process, which evolved rather quickly. The early ‘Talkin Bout’ images addressed baseball and George Strait, and the song’s first seven examples – including cold beer, dirt roads and blue-collar – all pointed to an unpretentious, small-town lifestyle. “Talkin’ ‘bout” started nearly every one of the first eight lines, and they kept that pattern going during the chorus. Even though it wasn’t all that different from the verse, they managed to telegraph to the listener that the sing-along part had arrived by spelling it out. “When that Y-O-U hits, even though it’s Y-O-U, it feels more like 3-2-1, like it’s a countdown,” Kenyon notes. “That’s when that chorus hits. You do feel it.” They raised the Y-O-U to another level at the chorus’ E-N-D: “If I’m talkin’ ‘bout a girl, I’m talkin’ ‘bout you.” “All I want to talk about is you – that’s how it pays off at the chorus,” Lucas says. “It really is just a quick love song.” As they rolled out of that chorus into the second verse, they dropped the small-town talkin’-‘bout topics and leaned into kisses and irresistibility. “Once she’s brought into the subject in the chorus, I think it’s like, ‘Okay, now let’s just stay there,’” Brust says. “Let’s keep it all about her. That’s what she’s gonna want to hear. That’s what we want to talk about.” The only spot where the “talkin’ ‘bout” if-then pattern shifted into a more subtle treatment came during the bridge, where the lyrics turn to future possibilities. “It’s talking about the serious stuff at that point: ‘Talkin’ ‘bout you, me,’ ‘talkin’ ‘bout maybe have a couple babies’ with a wraparound porch and a swing,” Lucas notes. “That’s the dream, you know – everybody’s dream when they find their girl.” Bollinger finished out the demo, putting a staccato guitar riff on the track, but it didn’t go anywhere for a year or two. After they wrote more songs on the LOCASH tour bus during a later concert run, Bollinger sent the duo those demos on Dropbox and tucked in a few older demos he still liked, including “Talkin Bout.” Both singers thought it was a standout, and they hired Bollinger and Sam Bergeson (Graham Barham, Teddy Swims) to produce it among four songs. The original demo had been recorded in B-flat, but since several LOCASH hits were in C, the duo had them record in the higher key. Bergeson and Bollinger focused on making it sound like a hit. “We kind of knew that that one had a shot,” Bergeson says. “We really just tried to make it as ‘country radio’ … as we could. We just tried to pull out all the stops and make sure that you could press ‘play’ at any point and be fun and high-energy.” Bollinger played some of the keyboard parts and provided some of the programming, but also served as a sounding board as Bergeson played everything else. That included a revision of the guitar riff that required interlocking parts. “He adds all kinds of layers that are just very subtly mixed in to add twang and thickness,” Bollinger says. “He’s a bit of a savant at his craft, and we came up with all the ideas together.” The bulk of the drums were programmed, though Bergeson enlisted his cousin, engineer Nathan Krauss, to record real hi-hats and cymbals to fill the higher frequencies. As it came together, Lucas had second thoughts about the pitch. After all that work in the key of C, he decided they should bring it back to B-flat, which would cost more money. That caught the producers off guard. “I think they thought I was punking them,” Brust recalls. “You can’t just push a button, but I said, ‘Man, let’s do it. Let’s start over again and get it.’” Lucas’ voice worked in C from the producers’ perspective, but they agreed that the lower key made more sense. “They did pull it off,” Bollinger says. “It just sort of felt like the magic was going back to the original B-flat.” Some of the sounds – particular the percussion – didn’t need to be re-recorded, but they re-cut the parts that couldn’t be re-pitched digitally, an

articles.title: The Kentucky Football Team is Ready to Kick Some Ass
articles.summary: The end of fall camp is on the horizon. The Kentucky football team can't wait to finally play a game at Kroger Field.
articles._body: Labor Day in 2026 is on Sept. 7. That should be illegal. It’s making the agonizing wait for football season feel even longer. If you think the wait is hard on you, just ask the Kentucky football players. Fall camp has been underway for three weeks. Fall semester classes at Kentucky began on Monday, yet Will Stein ‘s team still has about 10 more days of practice in 90-degree weather before they can suit up for a game at Kroger Field. “Fall Camp has been very long,” said wide receiver Shane Carr . “I feel like we’re all ready to go out and kick some ass.” Even though fall camp is a grind, Stein is doing everything he can to keep his team engaged throughout the dog days of summer. As Jeremy Jarmon explained , he’s gamifying the game within practice by transforming portions of practice into competitions. “Coach asked after practice, ‘Who had fun today?’ I raised my hand really high. The whole team did. We had a lot of fun out there today,” special teams coach Parker Fleming said on Thurrday. “You can say it’s a grind, but that’s just what we do. You say it’s been three weeks, but summer, spring, it’s just kind of what we do now. The guys love it. They’ve had great energy throughout fall camp. School started on Monday. Now we have a new element. Guys come out with energy. I don’t feel it at all, in terms of the grind getting to them. We’re having fun.” Even though practice may be more fun than normal, it’s still practice. It can’t compare to that first kickoff of the season. There are only nine days until Kentucky hosts Youngstown State, but who’s counting? More Kentucky News and Views on the KSR YouTube Channel Fleming, Carr, and punter Thomas O’Hara spoke with the media on Thursday. We’ll hear from safeties coach Josh Christian-Young on Friday morning before the Wildcats’ “ mock game ” on Saturday. The game week schedule begins with Stein’s first weekly press conference next Tuesday at noon. Kentucky Sports Radio has expanded its coverage of the Wildcats in the most ridiculous manner possible on our YouTube Channel. Here you will be able to find interviews with coaches and players, as well as commentary from the KSR crew. From Rapid Reactions following big events to our lengthy lineup of live shows, subscribe to the KSR YouTube Channel to stay up to date on everything happening around the Big Blue Nation.

articles.title: How Billboard’s Up-And-Coming Country Artist Blake Whiten Went From Viral Covers to Opening Stadium Tours & Scoring His Own Hot 100 Hit
articles.summary: The South Carolina native just earned his Billboard Hot 100 debut with “Bet on That.”
articles._body: In June 2024, Blake Whiten’s stripped-down cover of Morgan Wallen’s “I’m The Problem” went viral on social media.  Fast forward two years and Whiten opened shows for Wallen in Pennsylvania and Michigan this summer on the country superstar’s Still The Problem stadium tour, joining Wallen on stage for his 2017 hit “Up Down.” “That was the first time I’ve ever gotten a little bit emotional at a show,” Whiten tells Billboard of the first time he sang with Wallen. “I think it clicked for me when I was onstage for that last time [singing] ‘Up Down.’ It kind of just hit me, like, ‘OK, we are moving in the right direction.’” It’s been a whirlwind couple of months for Whiten, who released his Enchntmnt/Warner Records debut album Something to Say in July, sent his first single, “Bet on That,” to country radio, and is now seeing “Bet on That” become his first entry on the Billboard Hot 100, debuting at No. 98. “To finally be able to say that I’m actually pushing a song on the radio, it’s a pretty huge achievement in my mind. And I’m just happy that I finally got to do it,” he says. The son of a former preacher, the South Carolina native grew up around music. He soaked in the sounds of country artists like Wallen and HARDY, but also AC/DC, Poison and Tesla. Still, it wasn’t until his late teen years that he realized, “I have this crazy love for music. I could put a song on and it could change my entire day.” Since he was 16, Whiten, now 22, had been working in construction, but within 48 hours of his version of “I’m the Problem” gaining traction on social media, he packed his bags and booked his first ever flight, headed for Nashville. On Something to Say , Whiten worked with producer Austin Shawn, known for his work with Bailey Zimmerman (Whiten also co-wrote Zimmerman’s “Holding On,” which reached the top 40 on the Hot Country Songs chart.) As he sees a chart breakthrough with “Bet on That,” he’s bringing his new music on the road on his headlining Something To Say Tour, which launched Aug. 20. “I feel like I have a dream, but I feel like I have a pretty good shot at this dream — at least, I hope I do,” Whiten says. “And just working on all these songs over the last two and a half years, getting them written was a crazy experience, meeting all the people and all the songwriters. And then going into the studio and recording these songs, it was an amazing experience and I cannot wait till we get to the next album.” Whiten, Billboard ’s Up-and-Coming Artist of the Month for August, talked to Billboard about the release of his debut album, what he’s learned being on the road with stars like Wallen and Zimmerman, and what he’s passionate about beyond music. You celebrated your album’s release with a party and concert in your hometown of Six Mile, South Carolina, at a local convenience mart. What did it mean to you to be able to celebrate there? I’ve always wanted to somehow go back. I wanted to also give back to the community that got me through a lot of the years of my life. We bought gas and food for everybody for a little while, right before the show. I was pumping people’s gas and serving people food at the desk. I was really glad that I could go back and finally give back to the people and all the faces and all the characters that really built me as a person. When you opened for Morgan’s stadium shows, did you get any advice? I gathered up with [fellow show opener] Hudson Westbrook before the first time going out there, and was like, “Dude, is there something I should do or something I shouldn’t do?” He was like, “Just don’t get burned by the pyro and you’ll be fine.” What lessons have you learned from opening for artists like Morgan and Bailey that you’ve applied to your own live shows? You take something from every artist you watch. Bailey is insane on stage, bouncing around the whole time. Morgan has a lot of energy, but he’s also super chill about it — the dude don’t even break a sweat onstage. I was sweating before I ever got [onstage] for ‘Up Down,’ and you go out and shake his hand and his hand’s completely dry. But you want to get everybody hyped up, make the audience happy, make them cry. I’ve just mainly learned to live in the moment. It’s going to blow right past you, so make sure you live that moment up to its fullest and try to have the best time while you’re up there. Of the artists you’ve opened for, who had the best catering? The Morgan tour, they had a ton of options. On Bailey’s tour, they had a different theme every night, and [the theme] Taco Tuesday always came around, so that was probably my favorite. What is the first album you were obsessed with? Morgan’s [2018 album] If I Know Me . That’s the first album I actually listened to religiously for a couple of months. Who is an artist fans maybe wouldn’t guess you are a fan of? YUNGBLUD.  What is a hobby or subject that fans might not realize you are into? I don’t do it a lot, but I actually love cooking, and I’m a huge golfer. What is the best course you’ve played? There’s a course in Nashville called Nashboro. I love that course, but it’d be really cool to one day get the chance to go out and play one of the PGA Tour courses…Pebble Beach or Augusta would be sick, but the likeliness of actually getting on that is slim to none. What is one song you wish you had written? “A Rock” by HARDY — just how he based the entire song off of skipping a rock and then putting a rock on someone’s hand and then putting your name on a rock when you die. It’s so simple, but the thought that goes into it is just so fascinating to me.

articles.title: Hoomanely’s building a smart feeding bowl and an AI platform to help owners spot when their pup is sick
articles.summary: Hoomanely has developed a smart bowl to measure and record dogs' feeding data, then tells owners if behaviors change.
articles._body: Dogs are amazing. But as many pet parents will tell you, they can be remarkably good at hiding when something is wrong. My Labrador-Great Dane mix, for example, contracted tick fever several times over his 14 long years, and it was always at least a couple of weeks before I suspected something was off. It nearly gave me anxiety ulcers a few times. Hoomanely, a new startup out of Palo Alto, thinks it can help people like me spot health problems in their dogs much sooner with an AI platform that gathers data using a sensor-laden feeding station. Dubbed the EverBowl, the station measures dogs’ food and water consumption and eating speeds, and records chewing and swallowing sounds, facial thermals, oral motions, and a few other signals. The company’s AI platform analyzes that data to establish a baseline and then builds a health record. Any subsequent and prolonged departures from that baseline are shown to the pet owner via an app and in long-term reports, which the company says can provide more useful data to veterinarians if and when they get involved. The app also accepts information from the user, so the baseline can be kept updated with information outside the sensors’ scope. “Practically, the bowl is the best capture environment in a pet’s life: same place, same posture, same routine, twice a day, for years,” Sai Supriya Sharath, co-founder and CEO of Hoomanely (pictured above, in the middle), told TechCrunch. She added that appetite, hydration, and oral comfort are among the first things to be disrupted by pain, dental disease, tummy issues, endocrine changes, and illness. “Dogs are evolved to mask lethargy and limping. They are far less able to mask how they eat and drink … reduced or altered intake and changed drinking are presenting signs across a wide range of conditions.” Hoomanely says its platform was built after an 18-month beta-testing phase during which the company gathered about 5 million data points across more than 80 dogs. During testing, the platform detected changes in one dog’s eating patterns, which were eventually tied to a chipped tooth that was starting to become infected. In another case, the company’s app showed a sustained change from the dog’s regular eating and temperature baselines, which prompted the owner to take their dog to the vet and get a diagnosis for tick fever. While this sounds useful, there are some caveats. The cohort for this beta was quite small, and the company seems to have shipped only about 50 devices so far. It currently offers the EverBowl and the app reports through a $29-per-month subscription service. Sharath also said the company does not yet have independent sensitivity, specificity, or false-positive rates for clinical events, as that would require a study comparing the system’s alerts against actual diagnoses. Hoomanely admits that its platform is not a replacement for a veterinary diagnosis but is instead meant to help owners and vets to identify potential issues faster. The company is using its data for formal veterinary studies to find out whether its system works across a larger group of dogs. “The veterinary studies being designed will measure sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value, and false positives for each alert category, and we intend to report results by use case rather than as one headline number,” Sharath said. Along with those studies, Hoomanely plans to build more devices to gather data. EverSense is planned to be a wearable that will measure movement and rest information, and EverHub will be able to accept inputs from third-party devices such as smart collars, feeders, or home devices to record environmental data. Sharath said the long-term plan for Hoomanely is to eventually become an animal health data company by using the data gathered from its devices to support research and serve nutrition and insurance companies. Because the data capture system isn’t specifically designed for dogs, she said it may eventually expand to other animals, such as cats, livestock, or horses. The startup has raised $1.8 million in pre-seed funding so far and says it’s starting conversations for a seed round.

articles.title: ESPN ranks Bears a clear No. 1, but these aren’t your usual power rankings
articles.summary: Some analysts believe the Chicago Bears will regress this season. But Chicago has also been named No. 1 in a special ESPN NFL Power Rankings. But there is a catch, as these rankings are unique in how they rate each team, according to Ben Solak of ESPN. If you watched every Bears game last season,
articles._body: Some analysts believe the Chicago Bears will regress this season . But Chicago has also been named No. 1 in a special ESPN NFL Power Rankings. But there is a catch, as these rankings are unique in how they rate each team , according to Ben Solak of ESPN. If you watched every Bears game last season, you saw an NFL-leading six comeback wins by quarterback Caleb Williams and Chicago’s ludicrously explosive offense. Such games included a 58-yard Colston Loveland catch-and-run touchdown in a 47-42 barn burner against the Bengals, a 56-yard kickoff return with less than 50 seconds left to set up a last-second field goal winner against the Vikings, and the fourth-and-goal fadeaway touchdown to Jahdae Walker to set up the 50-yard DJ Moore lightning bolt against the Packers,” Solak wrote. The Bears were not short of drama. Their comeback to stun the Green Bay Packers was historic. Then, Williams completed a miraculous touchdown pass that nearly stunned the Los Angeles Rams. This was an exciting team to watch, and they left no room for breathing when it came to the teams they chased. Their offense needed to be exciting because their defense was not. With the Bears’ pass rush facing injury woes, that could be the story again in 2026. Williams is in his third season in the NFL and will look to reach new heights. A defense that struggles will give Williams more chances to lead comebacks. The only question now is whether that will result in more victories or if, this time, Chicago falls short. articles.title: How Did Nelly Furtado Rebound for Her Greatest Pop Star Year Ever in 2006 — And Why’d She Vanish From Top 40 Right After? Greatest Pop Stars Podcast
articles.summary: This Vintage Pop Stardom episode of 'Greatest Pop Stars' looks at Furtado's year of Billboard chart domination, an '00s nostalgia bomb the likes of which we don't get anymore.
articles._body: In 2006, few would have tabbed Nelly Furtado to end up being one of the year’s defining pop stars. The singer/songwriter had scored a pair of top 10 Billboard Hot 100 hits and won a Grammy a half-decade earlier with her debut album Whoa Nelly! , but 2003’s Folklore follow-up failed to make any mainstream impact, and her top 40 days seemed like they were over. But a partnership with hip-hop superproducer Timbaland — on a bit of a cold streak himself — ended up enormously beneficial for both artists, bringing them to the mainstream’s center in a totally new way for each, and in a way that neither was able to replicate any year after. On this week’s extended  Vintage Pop Stardom episode  of the  Greatest Pop Stars podcast , host Andrew Unterberger is joined by  YouTube star  and  Song vs. Song podcast  co-host Todd in the Shadows to remember the peak year of Nelly Furtado. We try to remember the unusual circumstances that made her a mid-’00s pop star in the first place, and catch up with what exactly has gone on with her in the 20 years since. Along the way, we answer all the most pressing questions about 2006 Nelly Furtado: What was going on in her professional and personal life that motivated her to make such a massive mid-decade pivot? What made her and Timbaland such an immediately great match? Do we believe that “Maneater” really exploded the first speaker it was played on? How much does the goofiness of the “Promiscuous” lyrics (or the free-associativeness of the “Say It Right” lyrics) bother us? How much credibility did (or do) we give her supposed feud with Fergie at the time? Would Dirk Nowitzki have worked as well as Steve Nash as the NBA star dropped in the “Promiscuous” lyrics? And perhaps most importantly: How did Nelly Furtado go from scoring three No. 1s in eight months to barely ever scraping the Hot 100 again? Check it out above, along with a YouTube playlist of Nelly Furtado’s biggest 2006 moments — all of which are discussed in the episode — and subscribe to the  Greatest Pop Stars  podcast  on  Apple Music  or  Spotify  (or wherever you get your  podcasts ) for weekly discussions every Thursday about all things related to pop stardom! And as we say in every one of these GPS podcast posts — if you have the time and money to spare, please consider donating to any of these causes in the fight for trans rights: Transgender Law Center Trans Lifeline Destination Tomorrow Gender-Affirming Care Fundraising on GoFundMe Human Rights Campaign – In Your Area

articles.title: Roger Goodell tips hand with new Bears stadium desire vs. move to Indiana
articles.summary: The Chicago Bears are looking for a new home. They are currently debating fiercely over funding for a new stadium, while also considering a move to Hammond, Indiana. On Thursday, NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell met with Illinois lawmakers to discuss the matter. Afterward, Goodell gave both locatio
articles._body: The Chicago Bears are looking for a new home . They are currently debating fiercely over funding for a new stadium, while also considering a move to Hammond, Indiana. On Thursday, NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell met with Illinois lawmakers to discuss the matter. Afterward, Goodell gave both locations a chance to make their case for a new stadium, per Jarrett Bell of USA Today. “There’s no specific timetable from my standpoint, other than we know that they are looking at the alternate groups, Indiana or Arlington Heights,” Goodell told reporters after team owners met at an airport hotel. “We want to make sure that Arlington Heights and Illinois have an opportunity, as well as Indiana, to put their best foot forward.” Goodell also explained his role as commissioner in stadium location. “I’m involved in a lot of stadium efforts,” he said. “It’s not unusual for me to be involved in conversations with either public officials or others. Or our staff. There are important decisions, not just for the communities but for teams and the NFL. So these are important things for us.” The Bears have played in Soldier Field for 54 years. Lately, the Illinois state legislature has been at a stalemate over stadium funding. Governor J.B. Pritzker and Chicago Mayor Brandon Johnson have been at odds over the Bears possibly leaving . While a move to Hammond, Indiana, is likely, the team has not secured an official stadium deal. Meanwhile, the Bears are in the midst of training camp/preseason. Their first game of the 2026-27 NFL season is scheduled for Sept. 13 against the Carolina Panthers on the road. articles.title: Run-D.M.C.’s ‘Raising Hell’ at 40: How Billboard Tracked the Rise of Rap’s First Blockbuster Album
articles.summary: “It doesn’t get any hotter than this.”
articles._body: Forty years ago, a trio from Queens catapulted hip-hop into the mainstream with Run-D.M.C.’s third album,  Raising Hell . Rap had been raising a ruckus across the five boroughs starting in 1973, but the New York-born genre didn’t become a pop culture force until September 1986, when  Raising Hell  and its second single, “Walk This Way,” put hip-hop into the top five of the Billboard 200 and the Billboard Hot 100, respectively, for the first time. Related Run-D.M.C. Celebrates 40 Years of Seminal ‘Raising Hell’ Album: ‘It’s the <em>Sgt. Pepper’s</em> of Hip-Hop’ Nicole Kidman Says She's Planning to See Adéla Live in Nashville & The 'Nicole Kidman' Singer Is Freaking Out Jay Wheeler's 'De Lejitos' Gets Up Close With No. 1 on Latin Airplay: 'Fills Me With Great Pride' ‘Adidas’ Is a Shoo-In “Run-D.M.C. previews the  Raising Hell  album with the go-go rap ‘My Adidas’ (Profile), and the flip, ‘Peter Piper,’ which confirms that their style is getting faster and more showy,” reported the May 17, 1986, issue of  Billboard , calling the “fast-moving” single a “singular tribute to sneakers” when it debuted on Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs. “Profile is breaking initial sales records with the new Run-D.M.C. album,” reported the May 31, 1986, issue. “According to label chief Cory Robbins, the album’s preorders exceeded 500,000 units.” Raved the June 7, 1986,  Billboard : “It doesn’t get any hotter than this.” Raising Hellions Based on data from retail and Run-D.M.C.’s  Raising Hell  tour, the June 21, 1986,  Billboard  reported the group’s audience “was 2-1 male. This is similar to the gender ratio one would see at a metal concert. The age of the audience is young, starting with fans under 15 and going up to 23.” A column in the July 26, 1986, issue, opined that while  Raising Hell  was “helped by having [the ‘Walk This Way’] video on MTV with Aerosmith,” it was still “one of the most hardcore hip-hop albums ever made… The reason that people like Run-D.M.C. and Prince seem so radical is because everyone else sounds so tame.” ‘Walk’ of Fame By the Aug. 2, 1986,  Billboard , “Walk This Way” was sprinting up the Hot 100: “Much to everyone’s surprise, the rap record is receiving substantial airplay on top 40 radio.” The next week,  Raising Hell  became “the first rap album to crack the top 10” on the Billboard 200. “Thanks to the unprecedented 2 million-plus sales of Run-D.M.C.’s  Raising Hell  LP, the 5-year-old independent Profile label is the toast of the indies,”  Billboard  declared on Sept. 27, 1986, the week after the album hit No. 3. “You can beg or use all the gimmicks you want, but programmers play what they like,” Robbins told  Billboard . “When people hear something good, they buy it.” Licensed to Illin’ Three weeks after third single “You Be Illin’ ” went top 30 on the Hot 100, the Jan. 10, 1987, issue hailed Run-D.M.C. for helping “to create a new fusion sound in which rap/street music meets heavy metal rock — the teen music of the inner city meeting the teen music of the suburbs — to the delight of everyone young.” A piece on the ascendant Beastie Boys in the next issue noted the “invaluable exposure” they got opening the  Raising Hell  tour. “Run-D.M.C. helped us out a lot,” Ad-Rock said in the Jan. 17, 1987,  Billboard . “When ‘Walk This Way’ got on AOR, it made it that much easier.” This story appears in the Aug. 22, 2026, issue of  Billboard.

articles.title: Rockets’ Kevin Durant reveals intitial ‘what the f**k’ reaction to Russell Westbrook retiring
articles.summary: Recently, future Hall of Famer Russell Westbrook shook up the NBA world when he announced that he would be retiring from the game after 18 seasons. Among the many stars who shouted out Westbrook in the wake of the news was Houston Rockets wing Kevin Durant, who was Westbrook’s season for ne
articles._body: Recently, future Hall of Famer Russell Westbrook shook up the NBA world when he announced that he would be retiring from the game after 18 seasons. Among the many stars who shouted out Westbrook in the wake of the news was Houston Rockets wing Kevin Durant , who was Westbrook’s season for nearly a decade with the Oklahoma City Thunder. Now, Durant has spoken on his initial reaction when he found out Westbrook was hanging up the sneakers. “I’m like, ‘what the f***?’ I looked at Shams (Charania’s) tweets, you’ve always got to go to Shams’ tweets. It was shocking,” he said, per Boardroom on X, formerly Twitter. “It just hit me, man, because it’s just like that’s one of the first dudes you come in with and you was around every day to finally step out of this sh*t… It surprised me,” he continued. Westbrook and Durant produced plenty of highlights during their tenure with the Thunder in the late 2000s and early 2010s. Although they didn’t seem to be on the best of terms when Durant took his talents to the Golden State Warriors in 2016, the two have since appeared to mostly mend their relationship, and have always had a clear mutual respect for one another. Westbrook was lauded by fans for his intensity and fearlessness on the court, and although he didn’t reach his ultimate goal of winning a championship, he still made an impact on every team he played for, including the Rockets. In the present day, Durant will look to lead Houston into legit championship contender status after a frustrating playoff exit in the first round this past season. articles.title: Juicy J Shares What Dolly Parton Told Three 6 Mafia After They Beat Her for an Oscar in 2006
articles.summary: "I'm glad somebody from Tennessee won the Oscar," Parton wrote.
articles._body: Dolly Parton had a heart of gold, and many stories surrounding the music icon have resurfaced following her passing on Tuesday (Aug. 25). Juicy J added to the discourse on Wednesday (Aug. 26) during an appearance with his brother Project Pat on Jimmy Kimmel Live! , which is being guest hosted by Jelly Roll . He recalled Dolly Parton graciously writing Three 6 Mafia a letter after the Memphis rap group beat her for an Oscar in 2006. “The only person almost excited as y’all were was Dolly Parton,” Jelly Roll quipped after they replayed the 2006 Oscars clip, which showed Parton cheering on Three 6 even in defeat. “She sent us a letter and signed it and said, ‘Congratulations and I’m glad somebody from Tennessee won the Oscar,'” Juicy J shared of Parton’s kind gesture. Juicy said he met Dolly before they went on stage and then headed to the “longest Oscar party in the world” to celebrate the group’s victory. Three 6 Mafia made history at the 2006 Oscars when “It’s Hard Out Here for a Pimp” ( Hustle & Flow ) won best original song over Dolly Parton’s “Travelin’ Thru” ( Transamerica ) and Kathleen York’s “In the Deep” ( Crash ). With the win, Three 6 became the first hip-hop group to win an Oscar; they were also the first rap act to perform at the ceremony. Dolly Parton died in Nashville on Tuesday (Aug. 25) following a brief battle with cancer, according to a statement shared by the “9 to 5” singer’s team. The 10-time Grammy winner and influential songwriter was 80. As for Juicy J and Project Pat, they performed “Yes Lord” on Kimmel from the brothers’ Dem Goats album, which arrived in July. Watch the clip of Juicy J recalling his Oscars moment with Dolly Parton and the duo’s performance below.

articles.summary: Fans will always go to bat for their favorite professional wrestling promotion, but MJF has defended WWE despite being a three-time AEW World Champion and one of the company’s top home-grown talents. During an interview with Richard Deitsch on the Sports Media podcast (via Fightful), MJF ex
articles._body: Fans will always go to bat for their favorite professional wrestling promotion, but MJF has defended WWE despite being a three-time AEW World Champion and one of the company’s top home-grown talents. During an interview with Richard Deitsch on the Sports Media podcast (via Fightful), MJF explained that fans should be able to enjoy whatever product they enjoy without tearing the competition apart . Instead, they should “just put your side over.” “If you like AEW more than WWE, and there are a lot of people that feel that way, that doesn’t mean you have to s**t on WWE,” he said. “You don’t need to make think pieces online about why WWE sucks. Make think pieces about why AEW is better. Whatever those logical reasons are — whether it’s because you get more bang for buck on pay-per-views or because our matches are better or because our rivalries are better or because MJF is better looking than any top guy in any promotion. “There are so many different things, but that doesn’t mean you have to attack the other side. Just put your side over,” the three-time champion added. Will AEW’s MJF ever jump ship to WWE? Joe Camporeale-Imagn Images. As of the time of this writing, MJF is still part of AEW’s roster. For years, there have been rumors about him jumping ship to WWE, but that has yet to happen. During an interview with Ross Tucker, he revealed that he turned down a contract from WWE before signing with AEW. He bet on himself, and that bet paid off. MJF is one of the biggest stars in AEW. He is a three-time World Champion, and he has also held the International Championship once. His other accolades include winning the 2022 Casino Ladder Match. In addition to his wrestling career, he has started acting in other projects. He was in The Iron Claw and also starred in Happy Gilmore 2 and will appear in Violent Night 2 later this year. articles._body: The Detroit Lions are dealing with some injuries on both sides of the ball, but Isiah Pacheco is dealing with two at the moment. The good news is that one of them isn’t too much to be worried about, according to head coach Dan Campbell. “Dan Campbell on Lions RB Isiah Pacheco’s status for Week 1: ‘I can’t give you anything definitive.’ Says Pacheco picked up a back injury in addition to his MCL sprain. With David Montgomery getting traded to the Houston Texans, the Lions needed an RB2, and Pacheco was the perfect signing. Throughout his years with the Kansas City Chiefs, Pacheco showed his speed and physicality coming out of the backfield, and that’s what the Lions are looking for to pair along with Gibbs. Both players are working back from injuries they suffered last season, and the hope is that they get on the field sooner rather than later. There was some concern about Sam LaPorta’s status after dealing with a hip injury , but he’s come back and looks like he’ll be ready for Week 1 against the New Orleans Saints. It’ll be interesting to see if the other players who have injuries will be able to make a return soon. articles.title: RFK Jr. goes full anti-vaccine bananas over two measles deaths—one was a newborn
articles.summary: Kennedy and his allies have a history of downplaying vaccine-preventable deaths.
articles._body: In the wake of news on Tuesday that two people in Pennsylvania died from measles , Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. has been posting a slew of anti-vaccine rhetoric and misinformation on social media—marking a resurgence of his old ways as a fervent opponent of lifesaving immunizations. The deaths are the first measles-linked fatalities in Pennsylvania in 35 years and are the first US measles deaths reported in 2026. They occurred amid an explosive outbreak in the state that has reached nearly 400 confirmed cases, as well as an ongoing nationwide surge for the vaccine-preventable disease. The US has tallied nearly 2,800 cases so far this year, the highest total since 1991. Pennsylvania health officials initially declined to provide details about the deaths, only reporting that they were in unvaccinated people from Lancaster County. However, news broke Wednesday that one of the deaths occurred in a newborn baby. That heart-wrenching news was swiftly entangled in the anti-vaccine misinformation Kennedy was spewing online. However, ankle surgery in March has had Pierce sidelined during training camp. The Colts
articles._body: Alec Pierce got paid handsomely in the offseason. The Indianapolis Colts gave their receiver a four-year, $114 million deal, making him the 13th highest-paid receiver in the NFL based on total contract value. However, ankle surgery in March has had Pierce sidelined during training camp. The Colts just activated their prized possession from the PUP , and Aug. 27 was his first practice back. Of course, though, Pierce needs time to ramp up after being out for so long. James Boyd confirmed that the Cincinnati product didn’t partake in team drills during his first practice and instead did individual work off to the side. As of now, signs point toward Pierce being ready to go for Week 1 of the regular season. The Colts will have three practices next week, a long Labor Day weekend to follow, and then a standard week leading up to the opener against the Baltimore Ravens. Pierce was seen making plays during the warm-up stage of his first practice back. #Colts WR Alec Pierce’s first catch in practice. pic.twitter.com/4xwGiQLq0C — James Boyd (@RomeovilleKid) August 27, 2026 Indianapolis traded Michael Pittman to the Pittsburgh Steelers in the offseason, so Pierce will be asked to take on a bigger role this season. In the past, he has predominantly been used as a deep threat. While his back-to-back seasons leading the league in yards per reception illustrate that he thrives there, the Colts will need Pierce to be more of a high-volume receiver going forward, especially since they gave him a contract that many believe was an overpay. Kim has had a difficult season between injuries and underperformance, but he displayed why the Braves have continued to tru
articles._body: The Atlanta Braves earned a 6-5 victory over the Los Angeles Dodgers on Wednesday after Ha-Seong Kim came through with a clutch walk-off hit in the bottom of the 9th inning. Kim has had a difficult season between injuries and underperformance, but he displayed why the Braves have continued to trust him on Wednesday night. “In a baseball season, there will be lows. This year has shown that for me,” Kim said after the win , via Grant McAuley of 92.9 The Game. “But I feel like if I continue to put the work in, baseball continues and I’ll find my ups again.” Kim is hitting just .078/.174/.078 across 32 games played. Finding consistency while missing time due to injury is difficult, so perhaps that has played a role in Kim’s struggles. Kim was expected to be the everyday shortstop for the Braves this season. However, his playing time has been limited in recent action as he has continued to struggle overall. Perhaps his walk-off hit will give him the momentum boost he needs to get back on track. Kim is ready to play whenever the Braves need him. “It’s been a rough season personally, but the team’s doing great,” Kim added, via McAuley. “So, I’m always trying to think, ‘How can I help the team?’ I feel like I was preparing myself and all that hard work and preparation paid off in this moment.” The Braves will look to earn another victory on Thursday night and sweep the Dodgers in their three-game series. articles.summary: In this week's Deal's roundup, Merlin and Jamen complete their acquisition of Curve Royalty Systems and more.
articles._body: Global investment firm KKR has invested in one of India’s largest entertainment companies, BookMyShow . Under the new agreement, funds managed by KKR have acquired a minority stake in BookMyShow, providing support for the live entertainment company’s next phase of growth as it scales and deepens its offerings in India. Over the past few years, BookMyShow Live , the live entertainment experiential division of BookMyShow, has brought Lollapalooza India, U2’s The Joshua Tree Tour, Coldplay, Ed Sheeran, Travis Scott, Linkin’ Park, John Mayer, Guns N’ Roses, Post Malone, Def Leppard and Justin Bieber to the Indian market.  “BookMyShow has been a pioneer in delivering high-quality entertainment experiences in India. We are pleased to support BookMyShow as it continues to lead the next phase of growth in India’s out-of-home entertainment sector,” said KKR partner and head of India private equity Akshay Tanna in a release. “We believe BookMyShow will play an important role in advancing India’s ambition to become a global entertainment hub and a premier destination for leading artists and acts from around the world.” KKR’s “global perspective, deep expertise and strong understanding of consumer businesses will be invaluable as we enter the next phase of our journey,” said BookMyShow founder and CEO Ashish Hemrajani in a release. “The timing of this investment is particularly exciting, as we have significantly expanded our presence across the live entertainment landscape and are seeing the opportunity for India’s entertainment economy grow like never before.” BookMyShow adds to KKR’s global portfolio of media and entertainment investments, including Internet Brands, ByteDance, Chord Music Partners, Epic Games, PlayOnSports, OverDrive, Superstruct and Simon & Schuster. BookMyShows also counts Network18 (part of Reliance Industries Limited), Accel Partners, Elevation Capital, Stripes Group, and TPG as longstanding investors. — Taylor Mims See more deals below.

articles.title: Bitcoin Asia: Binance’s CZ Says $1M Bitcoin Is Coming — and Gold Won’t Keep Up
articles.summary: Bitcoin Magazine
articles._body: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Asia: Binance’s CZ Says $1M Bitcoin Is Coming — and Gold Won’t Keep Up Binance founder Changpeng “CZ” Zhao has said that Bitcoin will hit $1 million dollars per coin sooner than we think — and eventually surpass gold’s market value.  Speaking at this year’s Bitcoin Asia on Thursday, the crypto entrepreneur also said that Bitcoin is “dangerous” for countries that don’t use it. Bitcoin Asia kicked off on Thursday in Hong Kong, bringing the biggest names in the space to Hong Kong to talk about everything from treasury companies to building apps from scratch.  JUST IN: Former Binance CEO CZ says "I think for Bitcoin to hit $1,000,000 would be a good thing. And it'll happen." "I don't think we need 25 years. I think it's gonna happen much quicker." pic.twitter.com/Qo4VRNoTso — Bitcoin Magazine (@BitcoinMagazine) August 27, 2026 “I think for Bitcoin hitting a million dollars would be a good thing — it will happen,” CZ said. “You think we need 25 years for that to happen? No, I actually don’t think we need 25 years, I think it’s going to happen much quicker.” CZ continued: “Bitcoin will, for sure, become more important than gold,” adding that large counties would over the years realize that the leading cryptocurrency is a “much better asset.”  Bitcoin’s price started surging last week on news that the U.S. Treasury would at least double the size of its liquidity-support buyback operations. The announcement last week hurt the dollar but non-yielding assets like Bitcoin and gold have benefited. The price of Bitcoin has jumped nearly 12% over the past seven days, touching as high as $81,160 this week before dropping again to its current price of $80,520.  Bitcoin’s $1.6 trillion market cap is still well below gold’s $32.2 trillion value.  Regarding nation state adoption, CZ said that countries that don’t end up adopting Bitcoin will lose out — just like with other emerging technologies, such as AI.  “If you think about AI, which country doesn’t want to hold the AI technology itself? Not investing in AI technology, not promoting the AI industry in your country, is dangerous for you,” he said.  “Many countries view Bitcoin as this dangerous thing — it’s not. Bitcoin is much more dangerous if you don’t use it: you’re missing out.” He added that countries making the move to shift into Bitcoin would take time but would eventually happen.  This post Bitcoin Asia: Binance’s CZ Says $1M Bitcoin Is Coming — and Gold Won’t Keep Up first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Mathew Di Salvo .

articles.title: Chart Rewind: In 2016, Jon Pardi’s ‘Boots’ Stepped to No. 1 on Country Airplay
articles.summary: The traditional country singer scored his first leader.
articles._body: At a time when bro-country dominated the sound of country music playlists, Jon Pardi offered a palate-cleansing throwback feel with his 2015 single “Head Over Boots.” Related Jon Pardi On Touring With Alan Jackson, Fatherhood, New Music & More | CMA Awards 2022 Chart Rewind: In 1996, Deana Carter’s ‘Strawberry’ Jammed Its Way Onto the Country Chart Dolly Parton’s Top Billboard Hot Country Songs Hits The song used a hint of Western swing to make it ideal for two-stepping across the hardwood, slipping old-school country into the format in the same way that Randy Travis’ “Forever and Ever, Amen” or Ricky Van Shelton’s “From a Jack to a King” flavored radio rotations three decades earlier. “Head Over Boots” stepped 3-1 on Billboard ’s Country Airplay list dated Aug. 27 in its 46th charted week, putting Pardi’s name at the summit for the first time in his career. Produced by Bart Butler (Midland, Randall King), “Boots” was co-written by Pardi and Luke Laird (Eric Church’s “Drink in My Hand,” Megan Moroney’s “Am I Okay?”), inspired by the atmosphere of a dancehall that Pardi visited during a 2013 trip to his father’s place in central Texas. Born and raised in Northern California, Pardi moved to Nashville in 2008 and set himself up with his energetic 2014 debut album, Write You a Song . “Boots” was released as the lead single from his sophomore project, California Sunrise , which debuted at No. 1 on Top Country Albums in July 2016. The song became the first of five Pardi singles to top Country Airplay, the most recent coming with 2022’s “Last Night Lonely.” “Boots” has since been certified seven-times Platinum by the RIAA, tying it with follow-up “Dirt on My Boots” as the top title among his 17 certified singles. A 10th-anniversary edition of California Sunrise , certified triple-platinum, was released June 12.

articles.title: Chinese open-source AI is starting to win over U.S. businesses
articles.summary: New spending data suggests companies are increasingly turning to cheaper, customizable open models—including fast-improving systems from China.
articles._body: Welcome to Eye on AI. Beatrice Nolan here. In today’s issue: Google DeepMind is losing its grip on elite AI talent, new data shows . DeepSeek seeks $7.4 billion at a $74 billion valuation. OpenAI data-center head leaves amid broader exodus. And OpenAI releases more details on the Hugging Face hack. Enterprises are starting to look beyond America for their AI needs.  As Chinese open-weight AI models increasingly close the gap with their closed-source U.S. counterparts, more enterprises are warming to the idea of using Chinese alternatives. It’s easy to see why: Open-weight models offer companies more opportunities to fine-tune AI models, are much cheaper, and generally give enterprises more control, including more assurance that their data isn’t being used to train potentially competing products. While Anthropic and OpenAI still dominate how American businesses buy AI, new spending data suggests that at least a minor shift is underway. According to Ramp’s latest AI Index —which tracks token and subscription spend across its customer base—the share of businesses paying for model serving platforms, which give companies access to open-source and Chinese-developed models, rose to 6.1% of total AI-spending businesses in July, up from 4.5% in January 2026. The shift may show increased enterprise interest in open-weight models such as Moonshot’s Kimi K3, which made waves on its release for being both an unusually large open-weight model but also one that showed coding and agentic performance close to leading proprietary systems. Z.AI, another Chinese AI lab, this week confirmed that it built Ox Alpha, a previously anonymous model that had been performing well on AI benchmarks and gained enthusiastic reviews from AI developers over the weekend. The company has renamed it GLM-5.3-Flash and said it will charge $0.15 per million input tokens and $0.50 per million output tokens—another aggressively priced Chinese offering in a market where DeepSeek and Moonshot have already put pressure on rivals’ pricing. Z.ai is also thought to be close to releasing a larger version of GLM-5.3 that many believe will rival some of the best models from Anthropic and OpenAI in cyber capabilities, potentially a watershed event that many fear will usher in a new era of AI-powered cyber attacks for which industry is woefully unprepared. China is now clearly ahead in the open-model race. For example, Hugging Face found that, in almost every month of 2026, the largest and most capable open model came from a Chinese lab, while the U.S.’s most notable recent challengers have come from Thinking Machines Lab, and, more recently, Meta. But those American releases have generally not matched Kimi K3’s scale or developer pull. Alex Brunicki, a partner at Backed VC, told me he’s already seeing a shift in how enterprises are approaching open-source models. “We’ve seen a lot of companies…developing industry‑specific foundation models using open-source models that are then fine tuned on very particular data sets,” he said. “They’re not necessarily using the frontier models for all of the work that they’re doing. They’re actually using these open-source models which are free to use.” At least two established organizations have recently publicly switched to open-source for some areas of their business. Thomson Reuters said this week it has built an in-house model, called Thomson-1, based on Snowdon, a system the company developed by adapting Alibaba’s open-source Qwen model. The model will handle document-review tasks that previously ran on Claude. As part of the announcement, CTO Joel Hron said companies do not need ever-larger, more expensive models to get useful results, and that starting from a strong open foundation and specializing it deeply can produce capable AI at lower cost. Harvey, the legal tech firm backed by OpenAI, Sequoia, and Andreessen Horowitz, also recently announced that its new model, Harvey Tenet, was post-trained on top of Moonshot AI’s open-weight Kimi K3 and that it outperformed both its base model and U.S. frontier systems, including Fable 5 and GPT-5.6 Sol, on complex legal agentic tasks. Harvey had previously built its product by customizing closed models from Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google. Ramp’s lead economist, Ara Kharazian, wrote that recent growth of open-source has not yet dented spending on OpenAI or Anthropic directly. New AI buyers are still choosing the established American labs; for example, Anthropic gained the most ground among businesses in July, rising 1.1 percentage points to 43.5% market share, and OpenAI climbed just 0.23 points to 39.7%. However, Anthropic’s Fable 5, thought to be the most advanced model on the market—so much so that the U.S. government briefly suspended foreign access to it for national security purposes—accounted for just 6% of tokens businesses purchase from Anthropic and 11.4% of dollars spent on Anthropic models overall, despite being priced at roughly $10 per million tokens, twice the cost of OpenAI’s GPT-5.6 Sol.  That model, by comparison, makes up 25% of OpenAI’s tokens and 23% of its spend. Kharazian argues Fable 5 has effectively found the market’s ceiling, and businesses are not willing to pay a premium for the best model on the market when a cheaper one is good enough. Taken together, all this may suggest American frontier labs have found the limit on what customers will pay for the newest, most expensive model, and open-source may just be stepping in to fill that gap. With that, here’s more AI news. Beatrice Nolan beatrice.nolan@fortune.com @beafreyanolan This story was originally featured on Fortune.com

articles.title: NFL Won’t Reach Prediction-Market Deals Before Start of Season
articles.summary: Stephen Lew-Imagn Images
articles._body: The NFL announced three sports-betting partners on Thursday, but you won’t see any prediction-market deals when the regular season kicks off in two weeks. For months behind the scenes, the league has been holding talks with companies including Kalshi and Polymarket, as well as the CFTC. But it remains unready to get into business with prediction-market platforms, and there will be no deals in place when the regular season begins, sources tell Front Office Sports . “I don’t see a scenario where the NFL is ready by the start of the season,” one prediction-market industry source tells FOS . “I would be incredibly shocked if anything at all happens this season.” “Nothing has changed in regard to prediction-market partnerships,” says a source familiar with the NFL’s thinking. The league has been lobbying the CFTC to “adopt regulations that mirror game integrity and consumer protections in legalized sports betting,” the source says. In July, the NFL said the CFTC’s prediction-market rule proposal falls “ significantly short ” in addressing risks around integrity, consumer protection, and market manipulation. The NFL is “alarmed” about markets “related to injuries” that are being offered by some platforms, the source familiar with the league’s thinking tells FOS . Kalshi is not offering markets explicitly tied to injuries, but it does have markets on when a given player will compete (for example, users can put money on whether Patrick Mahomes, who suffered a torn ACL in December, will play in week one). Polymarket recently filed with the CFTC to list markets on player participation, but has since pulled them . Such markets are “easily manipulable and offensive” to players, which is “why they are included in the league’s prohibited bet categories,” the source familiar with the NFL’s thinking says. The NFL on Thursday announced DraftKings, FanDuel, and Fanatics as its official sports-betting partners, with all three having signed multi-year deals. DraftKings and FanDuel have been NFL partners in sports betting since 2021, while the Fanatics relationship is new. Although all three also have prediction-market platforms, the data and intellectual-property rights from the sports-betting deals do not carry over to their prediction markets. “That’s not a space that we’re considering right now commercially,” NFL EVP and chief revenue officer Renie Anderson told ESPN . NFL EVP Jeff Miller told FOS in February ahead of Super Bowl LX in San Francisco that while the league was still skeptical about prediction markets—it didn’t allow any prediction-market commercials to air during the Super Bowl—it wouldn’t rule out the possibility of eventually doing business with the industry if regulatory issues it has concerns about are resolved. Although it appears any formal relationship between the league and prediction-market platforms remains far off, individual teams have interest in commercial partnerships with platforms, sources tell FOS . “NFL teams have certainly inquired,” says a source who works for a well-known prediction-market company. “Everybody wants a partner in this space. People see the dollar signs and want to do something.” But currently, no team-level deals would be allowed, a source familiar with the matter tells FOS . The NFL was the last of the big-four North American pro sports leagues to embrace sports betting, and sources say the same pattern is likely with prediction markets. The NHL last October partnered with both Kalshi and Polymarket; subsequently Kalshi signed an agreement with the Blackhawks and Polymarket signed a deal with the Rangers . MLB in March reached a deal with Polymarket, and now nearly one-quarter of teams in the league have individual deals of their own (the Mets with Novig , Polymarket with the Yankees , and Kalshi with the Giants, Braves, Padres, Red Sox, and Dodgers). The NBA has yet to come around, although it has been in talks with platforms for months and sources expect it will reach deals before the NFL. The post NFL Won’t Reach Prediction-Market Deals Before Start of Season appeared first on Front Office Sports .

articles.title: Dude Perfect, Weird Al & More on Monthly Comedy Boxscore Recap: By the Numbers
articles.summary: A detailed breakdown of the biggest touring comedians of the month.
articles._body: Earlier today (Aug. 27), Billboard published the July Boxscore report with The Weeknd on top for the first time, leading a record-breaking month that include sold-out shows by BTS, Ariana Grande and Luke Combs. But while the biggest stars of R&B, K-pop, country and more packed stadiums, comedians were road warrior-ing their way to sold-out theaters and arenas. Here, we’re looking at the five biggest comedy tours of July 2026. Last year, Billboard launched its comedy hub with rundowns of the biggest touring comedians of the midyear Boxscore period and of the months that followed. Sebastian Maniscalco, Matt Rife, and John Mulaney topped some of those lists, but while this month’s top five includes some familiar faces, a new act is No. 1, ending — for now — a dominant reign by Nate Bargatze. While Tyler Toney, Coby and Corry Cotton, Garrett Hilbert and Cody Jones have appeared on the monthly comedy rundown before, July marks Dude Perfect’s first month at No. 1. According to figures reported to Billboard Boxscore, the comedy group brought in $8.5 million and sold 135,000 tickets over 16 shows during the month. Dude Perfect’s Squad Games Tour swept through July with kickoff shows in June and two final shows at the beginning of August. Altogether, the trek grossed $11.4 million and sold 180,000 tickets. The biggest show was at Thompson-Boling Arena in Knoxville, Tenn., which earned $827,000 from 13,200 tickets on July 18. Four of the group’s members met at Texas A&M University, leading to three statewide shows in Austin, Dallas, and Fort Worth. Hi HN! We built Meridian because we kept seeing the same thing: developers get estimates for planned work, and then spend a huge chunk of their time doing everything that wasn't planned.
