articles._body: Hi HN! We built Meridian because we kept seeing the same thing: developers get estimates for planned work, and then spend a huge chunk of their time doing everything that wasn't planned. Debugging something weird, helping a teammate, reviewing PRs, jumping on an incident, fixing a flaky test, answering questions, etc. All useful work, but a lot of it never makes it back into the estimate. So when the sprint slips, it can look like the estimate was wrong, when really, a bunch of other work happened in between. Meridian is our attempt to make that work visible and better account for it. We’re building it in the open and open sourcing it because we’d much rather have developers tell us where we're getting this wrong than build another productivity dashboard in a vacuum. We launched last week and ended up #1 on Product Hunt, which was pretty wild. Now we're looking for feedback from the core dev community. Curious how you deal with unplanned work today, and whether this is actually a problem worth solving today. Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49466731 Points: 5 # Comments: 0

articles.title: Launch HN: Salem Robotics (YC S26) – Software for industrial inspection robots
articles.summary:
Hi HN, we're the founders of Salem Robotics (https://salemroboticsinc.com). We give existing mobile robots the task-specific intelligence to carry out surveys and physically interactive inspections in hazardous industrial facilities.

Here's a video of
articles._body: Hi HN, we're the founders of Salem Robotics ( https://salemroboticsinc.com ). We give existing mobile robots the task-specific intelligence to carry out surveys and physically interactive inspections in hazardous industrial facilities. Here's a video of it running on real robot hardware with a few words from us: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=U_228h3NE7c We came to Salem through robotics research at UT Austin and a combined 15 years working in nuclear, including about 10 years developing and deploying autonomous robots at Los Alamos National Laboratory. Over the last five years, we kept running into the same gap: robot hardware had become very capable, but making a robot carry out a complete industrial procedure still required a surprising amount of robotics work and manual intervention. The part that interested us most was manipulation. A nuclear contamination survey, for example, can require taking a "smear": wiping a defined area of a surface so it can be checked for removable radioactive contamination. In an oil, gas, or chemical facility, an LDAR (leak detection and repair) inspection can require moving a detector around a particular valve, flange, or connection. Other inspections require positioning an instrument at a precise location and orientation relative to a pipe or piece of equipment. These are easy tasks to compress into verbs like "wipe", "measure", or "inspect", but considerably harder to make a robot do reliably. A probe might need to remain normal to a surface throughout a path, stay within a narrow offset from a pipe, or trace a region while maintaining a particular end-effector orientation. The planner has to find a feasible motion while respecting the task geometry, manipulator kinematics, joint limits, collisions, and the environment around it. We work down to joint-level control for those interactions. One problem we've spent a lot of time on is generating constrained manipulation plans quickly enough that they can be based on the geometry the robot actually observes instead of requiring someone to carefully author a trajectory for every individual surface, valve, or flange. The physical world makes this annoying. A few centimeters of error may not matter much when navigating down a hallway, but it matters if a sensor is supposed to remain normal to a curved surface. And successfully executing a trajectory doesn't necessarily mean the inspection worked. The detector could be misaligned, contact could be wrong, the geometry could differ from the model, or the measurement itself could be invalid. We care about closing that loop around the inspection result, not just whether the arm reached the commanded pose. Our approach is a combination of AI and classical robotics. A lot of robotics research and industry attention right now is going toward increasingly end-to-end learned systems, particularly around humanoids. Working in safety-critical environments has made us appreciate how relevant classical approaches still are when you want explicit constraints, predictable behavior, and theoretical guarantees about what a robot can and cannot do. We use AI where semantic understanding and flexibility are useful, such as interpreting less structured information or understanding what in an unfamiliar scene is relevant to a procedure. Once the system knows what physical interaction it needs to perform, we prefer explicit geometry, planning, optimization, and control where possible. We're interested in the marriage between the two rather than trying to make every part of the robotics stack learned. The other idea behind Salem is that we don't think every useful robot application should require building a new robot. Companies like Boston Dynamics are getting very good at building increasingly capable hardware platforms. We think there is room for a domain-specific application layer on top of that hardware. The same underlying robot might perform nuclear radiological surveys in one facility and LDAR inspections in another, but the procedures, sensors, manipulation constraints, success conditions, and outputs are different. That's also why we're hardware agnostic. We don't expect one robot to be the best platform forever, and facilities already own different hardware. We'd rather describe an inspection in terms of what needs to happen and then map that onto the capabilities of the right robot for the job. One thing that surprised us after spending more time with facilities is how manual many inspection workflows still are. In sophisticated nuclear and industrial sites, people still physically walk survey routes, take measurements one at a time, visually inspect equipment, record results manually, and sometimes make judgments based on things like how a component sounds. Some of the basic workflows would be recognizable to someone doing the job decades ago, even though the sensors, computation, and robots available today are radically different. We're starting with radiological inspection in nuclear because it's the industry we know best, and we're also working on manipulation-heavy inspection problems in oil, gas, and hazardous chemical facilities. The technicians and inspectors still define the procedure, interpret results, and make the consequential judgments. We're trying to automate more of the repetitive physical execution that currently requires someone to enter the environment or manually operate a robot. We sell directly to industrial facilities, usually starting with a paid technical validation and then moving to an ongoing deployment. Pricing varies substantially with the workflow: validations range from tens of thousands to over $100k, and larger deployments can range from the low hundreds of thousands to roughly $500k per robot. One thing we're especially curious to hear HN's thoughts on is where the abstraction boundary in robotics should sit. articles.title: Good Good Golf Co-Founder in Ad Apologizes, Says He Hopes People ‘Move On’
articles.summary: Screenshot
articles._body: Good Good Golf co-founder Garrett Clark shared a lengthy video to his personal social media accounts late Wednesday addressing the controversy that has swirled around the company since it posted (and quickly deleted) an ad for its new co-branded driver with Callaway last Friday. The promotion depicted Clark running and shoving fellow Good Good talent Alexis Miestowski to the ground as she reached for the club out of his bag. Standing above Miestowski as she lay on her back, Clark threateningly says, “Do not touch my new driver.” Online backlash ensued immediately, with many describing the ad as confusing , scary , and endorsing violence against women. The condemnation reached the highest levels of golf, with even PGA Tour CEOBrian Rolapp criticizing the ad and the company’s slow-footed response. “I want to personally apologize for playing a role in the skit in this ad at the magnitude that I did,” Clark said in the video post Wednesday night. “And on Good Good’s behalf, on Good Good marketing’s behalf, I want to apologize as well because how this ad was received is not at all what we stand for. Also, I do not support [domestic violence], abuse, or any of that of any kind.” pic.twitter.com/mpFFRvUedE — Garrett Clark (@gm__golf) August 26, 2026 In recent days, the fallout has rapidly escalated. On Tuesday, Golf Channel postponed the premiere of a new show with the YouTube-native brand—set to be called Big Break x Good Good —by a week after a sponsor dropped out, and Callaway announced it was investigating how the ad was approved by its team. On Wednesday, several major retailers including Dick’s Sporting Goods, Golf Galaxy, PGA Tour Superstore, and Target pulled Good Good merchandise from their in-store and online shelves. Calls for the Tour to drop Good Good as the title sponsor of its Fall Series event taking place Nov. 12–15 in Austin, Texas, have also been mounting. Asked about this at the Tour Championship earlier this week, Rolapp indicated that a change wasn’t off the table, noting the organization will “continue to monitor the situation and see how it develops.” After apologizing, Clark walked through how the ad was made, splicing in behind-the-scenes footage that showed the tackle of Miestowski was staged and that he didn’t strike her. He also reiterated what Good Good CEO Matt Kendrick told the Wall Street Journal on Monday: The ad was supposed to be a spoof of “Obsession,” a horror movie released earlier this summer, but missed the mark. “Looking back, super dumb ad concept, terrible ad in general, not the greatest idea in general,” he reflected. “Minutes after it got posted, I was cringing. I thought it was the worst ad known to man.” He then called attention to the online criticism and abuse that Miestowski and her fellow “Good Good Girls” have been targeted with amid the backlash. (Good Good launched Good Good Girls, a women-focused YouTube channel featuring four ex-college golfers, in late 2025. Miestowski, a former varsity golfer at Indiana, has not commented publicly since the furor began.) Clark showed screenshots of recent comments on Miestowski’s Instagram posts and direct messages she has received. “Hope someone beats you after your round,” read one; “Get the fuck off the planet now you little fucking loser bitch,” said another. “There are hundreds of these comments and messages circulating about her,” Clark said. Beyond Clark’s video and Kendrick’s comments to the WSJ , Good Good hasn’t put out any formal communications since a tweet last Saturday. “We posted a video to our channels that ultimately depicted actions that are not aligned with our values as a brand,” the statement said. “We have since taken that content down, and sincerely apologize. Good Good has always stood for making the game of golf more inclusive to all, and we will continue to ensure that is our mission moving forward.” Clark ended his eight-minute message with a forward-looking plea. “Good Good messed up by promoting a very poor-taste ad, but hopefully you guys can forgive Good Good as well as myself for being a part of it,” he said. “Hopefully we can move on and grow the women’s side of golf, because that is one of our huge, huge goals.” The post Good Good Golf Co-Founder in Ad Apologizes, Says He Hopes People ‘Move On’ appeared first on Front Office Sports .

articles._body: A few months ago, I created the WARP engine (formerly WASTE) to run Kimi K3, the complete 2.78-trillion-parameter model, on macOS. articles.title: Why did 1,000 world citizens bury their underpants?
articles.summary: Study: Land use is the biggest factor in determining decomposition rates of organic cotton underpants.
articles._body: A thousand people voluntarily buried their cotton underpants for two months—not to keep the Underpants Gnomes from stealing them, but as part of a citizen science project to map out soil health in 25 countries around the world. The results of this unique experiment were reported in a new paper published in the journal Plants People Planet. “Our results show that how soil is managed can significantly affect both soil life and soil quality,” said co-author Marcel van der Heijden , an agroecologist at the University of Zurich. “Healthy, biologically active soil is crucial for fertility, nutrient cycling and many other ecosystem services.” Soil health is critical for agriculture and, by extension, food security, not to mention a healthy global ecosystem, but it has been declining worldwide, per the authors. One key indicator of soil health is decomposition rates of complex organic matter, breaking down stuff like leaves, wood, even cadavers into simpler organic and inorganic compounds, releasing C0 2 and nutrients in the process. There have been relatively few large-scale national decomposition studies involving different land use types, although smaller studies have shown that how humans use a site can significantly affect the soil's biological diversity. FAYETTEVILLE — Arkansas safeties Caleb Wooden and Sean Williams were granted a temporary restraining order by a judge in Washington County, making them eligible for the 2026 season. The lawsuit, which was filed in Washington County on Wednesday evening, was entered by attorneys Marshall Ney and Kael Bowling of law firm Friday, Eldredge and Clark, LLP. The motion was granted by Judge Doug Martin. “After review of that complaint and the materials submitted in support of the motion, the Court finds that temporary relief is warranted as set forth herein,” The court filing reads. Both Wooden and Williams had initially been made eligible for another season of college football because of the court case in Colorado. The NCAA was granted a stay in that case, making them ineligible unless they filed their own lawsuits, which they did jointly on Wednesday. Wooden went through drills without pads on and Williams was in street clothes watching from the sidelines during practice last week. Woodenis coming off of his worst season after posting an overall grade of 56.7, according to Pro Football Focus, but did have his most successful collegiate campaign under Roberts’ tutelage at Auburn in 2023 when he posted a 76.6 grade with the Tigers. Williams is a Dartmouth transfer and was an All-Ivy League defensive back a year ago. He started 37 of the 38 games he played in from 2022-2025. Last season, Williams logged 31 total tackles – 16 solo and 2.5 for loss – 8 pass deflections and 4 interceptions. He has 11 career interceptions and returned one for a score. Per Pro Football Focus, he posted a 71.5 grade in 570 snaps.

articles.title: The Weeknd Leads Record-Breaking Monthly Boxscore Report
articles.summary: The After Hours til Dawn Tour grossed more than $120 million and sold nearly 900,000 tickets in July.
articles._body: July 2026 marks The Weeknd ’s 15th appearance on Billboard ’s monthly Top Tours chart, all since the kickoff of his ongoing After Hours til Dawn Tour (2022-present). It’s his 13th time in the top 10, ninth in the top five, and seventh in the top three. But this is his very first time at No. 1 with the highest-grossing and best-selling tour of the month. Plus, stadium season heats up with best-ever overall figures for the month’s top 30 tours. According to figures reported to Billboard Boxscore, The Weeknd grossed $124.4 million and sold 892,000 tickets across 16 shows during July. More than four years deep on his stadium world tour, it’s his biggest monthly take yet. Less than 1% ahead of Bad Bunny ’s $123.7 million from September 2022, it’s the biggest one-month gross by a solo male act since the Top Tours chart’s 2019 launch. Among all acts, it ranks seventh. By tickets sold, it’s higher on the all-time leaderboard. The Weeknd’s 892,000 is the second biggest one-month attendance figure, beating his own 891,000 from July 2023 by less than one tenth of a percentage point. Harry Styles has the lead with 967,000 tickets sold in June 2023. Both of The Weeknd’s 800k+ months were spent in European stadiums. The same goes for Styles’ record-holder, as well as the fourth, fifth, and sixth biggest monthly attendance counts in the chart’s history. Stadium capacities are generally bigger abroad than in the United States, with The Weeknd averaging more than 55,000 tickets per show. By contrast, the six biggest months ranked by revenue each included shows in North America. The highlight of The Weeknd’s July was a four-show run at Paris’ Stade de France (July 8-9 and 11-12). Those shows brought in $44.2 million from 300,000 tickets sold, easily reigning as the month’s highest-grossing and best-selling concert engagement (No. 1 on Top Boxscores). Combined with his two shows at the same venue on July 29-30, 2023, the After Hours til Dawn Tour now counts a record six sold out shows at the stadium with more than $60 million and 450,000 tickets. Elsewhere, The Weeknd played multiple nights in Lille and Nice (both in France), Amsterdam, Milan, and Frankfurt. All six stops appear on Top Boxscores, bookending his Paris shows at No. 1 with two nights at Nice’s Allianz Riviera (July 21-22) at No. 30. Since launching in 2022, the After Hours til Dawn Tour played 141 shows through Aug. 1. Those dates have collectively grossed $910.1 million and sold 7.1 million tickets, making it the fourth-highest grossing tour of all time behind treks by Taylor Swift , Coldplay , and Elton John . According to Tesfaye’s team, another dozen shows that have played since and almost two dozen more on the books will make it the third tour to gross more than $1 billion . In terms of gross and attendance, it is the biggest tour by an R&B artist and biggest tour by a Black artist in Boxscore history. The Weeknd is the first R&B artist to lead the Top Tours chart in 2026 and is only the third to do so in the ranking’s seven-year history. He follows Beyoncé , who did it seven times between 2023-25, and Chris Brown , who led a three-peat last year. Speaking of Brown and R&B chart-toppers, his and Usher ’s co-headline The R&B Tour is No. 3 in July with $98.4 million and 538,000 tickets sold. Including the tour’s opening shows in June, plus an Aug. 1 show in Syracuse, N.Y., it earned $115.9 million in its first 16 shows with more than 40 left to report. Sandwiched between these R&B juggernauts is BTS , at No. 2 with $102.5 million and 582,000 tickets. The group’s four stops in July – Brussels, London, Munich and Paris – land at Nos. 3 and 5-7 on Top Boxscores. As with The Weeknd’s tour, Paris was the biggest, generating $30.6 million from 185,000 tickets. BTS previously crowned the Top Tours chart in April and May, in addition to two prior wins on earlier tours. After sliding to No. 6 in June with a lighter schedule of shows, a bulked-up run of eight dates (still light compared to The Weeknd’s 14) brings them back toward the top of the list. One month after Bad Bunny joined the club, BTS becomes the third act to gross a reported $100 million in multiple months, in addition to Beyoncé. This also marks the second time that two tours have grossed more than $100 million in the same month, after the one-two of Beyonce and Kendrick Lamar & SZA in May 2025, both over $150 million. Since kicking off in April, BTS’ Arirang World Tour has earned $433.2 million and sold 2.3 million tickets over 38 shows through Aug. 11. It is already, by far, the biggest tour of the group’s career and is scheduled to continue through March 2027. Altogether, the month’s top 30 tours grossed a reported $1.155 billion and sold 8.189 million tickets, marking record highs since Top Tours’ 2019 launch. Beyond the chart’s publication, it’s the highest-grossing calendar month in the history of the touring industry, by reported grosses. Even accounting for unreported figures for Swift’s gargantuan The Eras Tour, it’s highly unlikely that any month in 2023-24 could have caught up. The previous best was in June 2025, with $1.029 billion and 7.534 million tickets. This month’s figures exceeded the old records by 12% and 9%, respectively.

Now, the team has given an update about his recovery, according to MLB.com. “Began rehab assignment on Aug. 25 with Triple-A Oklahoma City. Expecte
articles._body: The Los Angeles Dodgers took a big hit last month when they placed Will Smith on the 60-day IL after he continued to suffer from a neck injury. Now, the team has given an update about his recovery , according to MLB.com. “Began rehab assignment on Aug. 25 with Triple-A Oklahoma City. Expected to catch seven innings on Aug. 27 with the Comets,” MLB.com wrote. This is good news for the Dodgers, as they will potentially get their starting catcher back for the playoff run. Smith has demonstrated some power in his rehab assignment and has gained some strength. Ultimately, the goal is to build himself back up. Smith has reported no pain, but still needs the reps before he is fully ready to return. Before his injury, Smith was hitting .249 with six home runs, 23 RBIs, and 23 runs in 52 games. Dalton Rushing has also been injured, causing a depth issue at the position. This has forced the Dodgers to use Hunter Feduccia, and he has been inconsistent at best. While the Dodgers are still likely to make a playoff run, they need their catcher. Smith has been at the helm for both of the Dodgers’ last two titles. Therefore, the team needs him to be fully healthy for this run. Although he was not able to play through his pain earlier this season, his not having any right now is a good sign. If Smith can clear his rehab, he will give the Dodgers a valuable weapon in October, as they attempt to win the World Series for the third consecutive season. articles._body: The Cincinnati Reds recently placed Eugenio Suarez and TJ Friedl on outright waivers . According to Ken Rosenthal of The Athletic, teams have 48 hours to place a claim on either player. While it remains to be seen if either player will be claimed, Jon Morosi of MLB Network believes the Seattle Mariners should consider a reunion with Suarez. “The Mariners are in prime position, if they are interested in an Act III with Suárez. Waiver claims are awarded in reverse standings order; Seattle has one of the worst records of any viable contender,” Morosi wrote on X, formerly Twitter. Suarez was mentioned as a trade candidate before the deadline in early August but a deal never came to fruition. The veteran slugger has hit just .208 this year to go along with a .705 OPS. He does have 19 home runs, so he could help a number of lineups out. The San Diego Padres and Cleveland Guardians are other contenders that would benefit from an offensive boost. However, the Mariners certainly make sense. Their lineup has question marks and they also have history with Suarez. Suarez played in Seattle from 2022-2023 before being traded to the Mariners in 2025 as well. So, should the Mariners consider an “Act III” with Suarez as Morosi mentioned? Suarez can play third base or designated hitter. At the very least, he could be a bench bat who offers serious right-handed power. Claiming Suarez makes sense for Seattle, as the Mariners attempt to save their playoff hopes. Seattle is currently 64-70 and 2.5 games back of first place in the American League West standings. The ball club is also four games back of an AL Wild Card spot. The post Insider calls for Mariners-Eugenio Suarez reunion to save playoff hopes appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles.title: Calling my shot: Five bold predictions for the 2026 college football season
articles.summary: If new Alabama starter Keelon Russell or new Tennessee starter Faizon Brandon or new Florida starter Aaron Philo leads a team to the CFP, there is a good chance that QB will finish high in Heisman voting.
articles._body: When I unveiled my Bold Predictions this time last year, I called the 2025 season the most unpredictable in years. I was correct because only four of those 10 predictions came true. That’s OK. Batting .400 gets you into the Hall of Fame in some sports. This year feels even more unpredictable, and we probably should get used to that in the transfer portal/NIL era. Teams change drastically every offseason, and we may not know until October how to accurately gauge their prospects. But that won’t stop me from trying to predict the future before a single game is played. Here are five Bold Predictions for a season that blessedly begins with week zero games on Saturday… 1. The SEC will break its national championship drought. The national title race is more wide open than ever. The Big Ten has at least three teams at the top ( Indiana , Ohio State , Oregon ) that are definitely capable of winning a title. The league has even more candidates that — if things break correctly — are capable of making a deep College Football Playoff run that could turn into a title ( USC , Michigan , Penn State ). The ACC’s Miami is as talented as any team in the country. Ditto for independent Notre Dame . If anything, it should be even more difficult for the league that dominated the sport from 2006 to 2022 to have one of its teams hoist the trophy. But SEC teams have had time to recalibrate. Georgia and Alabama realize they can’t stockpile talent the way they used to and have adjusted. LSU has spent millions on its roster and swiped Lane Kiffin from Ole Miss . The Rebels still have the most exciting quarterback in college football in Trinidad Chambliss . Oklahoma brings back a nasty defense and an improved offense. Meanwhile, Texas spent lavishly (but wisely) in the portal to plug the weaknesses that led to the Longhorns’ 9-3 record last year. If the SEC keeps throwing enough good teams on the field, it eventually will break through again. This feels like as good a year as any. 2. Penn State’s Whiteout game against USC will determine a College Football Playoff berth. USC also has Oregon, Washington , Ohio State and Indiana on its Big Ten schedule. As difficult as it will be to go to Happy Valley and beat Matt Campbell ’s team in front of 107,000 screaming fans — many of whom will be making Pablo Pledgescobar jokes on their white shirts — the Trojans probably need to win this one to make the CFP. They’ll have to win some of the others too. But if they can’t beat this Penn State team, they probably aren’t beating either Indiana or Ohio State later.  Meanwhile, Penn State got the opposite of USC’s Big Ten schedule draw. The most difficult games on paper are the visit from USC on Oct. 10 and a trip to Ann Arbor to play Michigan the following week. If the Nittany Lions can beat the Trojans, it means they’re probably beating just about everyone else. An 11-1 regular season (or maybe 12-0) certainly would seem possible.  3. The Heisman Trophy winner will be a quarterback who wasn’t a full-time Power 4 starter* last year. This isn’t nearly as implausible as it sounds. In fact, this describes six of the past 20 Heisman Trophy winners. Tim Tebow , Cam Newton , Johnny Manziel , Jameis Winston , Kyler Murray and Bryce Young all were backups, redshirts or — in Newton’s case — playing JUCO ball the year before they won the Heisman.  *For the purposes of this exercise, we’ll crib from the old redshirt rule and say that to qualify, the player had to start four or fewer games at QB for a Power 4 team in 2025. If new Alabama starter Keelon Russell or new Tennessee starter Faizon Brandon or new Florida starter Aaron Philo leads a team to the CFP, there is a good chance that QB will finish high in Heisman voting. Also, note that I only eliminated returning Power 4 starting QBs. If Drew Mestemaker lights up the Big 12 after transferring from North Texas to Oklahoma State or USF -to- Auburn transfer Byrum Brown puts up the kind of numbers in the SEC that he did in the American, they could land on a lot of ballots. Or maybe it’s Old Dominion transfer Colton Joseph playing for this next guy… 4. Wisconsin coach Luke Fickell will save his job this season. Luke Fickell ’ s first three seasons in Madison were objectively awful. He’s 17-21 overall and 10-17 in Big Ten play after taking over for Paul Chryst , who went 67-26 overall and 43-18 in Big Ten play while leading the Badgers.  But former Wisconsin athletic director Chris McIntosh admitted last year — when announcing Fickell would get another year — that Wisconsin’s administration had failed to provide Fickell with the appropriate resources to stock the roster. That changed this offseason. The Badgers had more money to spend than any previous point in Fickell’s tenure. Fickell also starts year two with offensive coordinator Jeff Grimes , whose scheme should fit a more traditional Wisconsin talent profile. Grimes replaced Phil Longo , whose Air Raid scheme simply didn’t fit in America’s Dairyland. It wasn’t an accident that after the administration said Fickell was staying last season, the Badgers shocked Washington and Illinois . He hasn’t lost the team, and now he has more to work with. The aforementioned Joseph joins the Badgers from Old Dominion, and he should add a QB run threat Fickell’s Wisconsin teams haven’t had. Hopefully Joseph can stay healthy. The last two QBs Fickell plucked from the portal ( Tyler Van Dyke and Billy Edwards Jr. ) got hurt early and their injuries helped derail the 2024 and 2025 seasons. 5. North Dakota State will play for the Mountain West title. When James Madison moved from the FCS to the FBS, the Dukes were hamstrung by a silly NCAA rule that barred teams moving up from playing in the postseason for their first two years in the FBS. That rule has been waived for North Dakota State , which enters the Mountain West this season after winning 10 FCS national titles since 2011. If North Dakota State were entering the Mountain

articles.title: Jonathan Kuminga will rue day he spurned Lakers for less money from Timberwolves
articles.summary: The Jonathan Kuminga saga finally concluded after it emerged that the former Golden State Warriors man has agreed to sign a 2-year, $12 million deal with the Minnesota Timberwolves. And while the intention was to ensure a starting role, Kuminga has turned his back on some major money with his lat
articles._body: The Jonathan Kuminga saga finally concluded after it emerged that the former Golden State Warriors man has agreed to sign a 2-year, $12 million deal with the Minnesota Timberwolves. And while the intention was to ensure a starting role, Kuminga has turned his back on some major money with his latest decision. The Timberwolves used their taxpayer mid-level exception, worth roughly $6.06 million in year one, to get the deal done. Kuminga ended up walking away from a sign-and-trade offer from the Lakers reportedly worth more than $36 million over three years, north of $12 million annually. Kuminga chose Minnesota’s shorter, cheaper deal instead, prioritizing what sources described to ESPN as “an ability to have more control of his future” over guaranteed money and Los Angeles’ market. Chicago and Portland also made offers that were passed over. So Kuminga lost his Bird Rights, turned down LAL’s $36+M deal ($12m/yr) to sign a $6M Bet on Myself deal- To chase, at best – the $16M NTMLE next summer? And if he manages to get that deal- In Two years, he’d still have made $2M LESS than if he’d just signed w/ LA at $12/yr?? pic.twitter.com/p9wu2M8W5W — Lakers Legacy (@LakersLegacyPod) August 26, 2026 This is the second consecutive offseason Kuminga has bet against a bigger guarantee. Last September, after the Warriors offered a three-year, $75.2 million deal, Kuminga’s camp rejected it specifically because of the team option in the third year. He also turned down a three-year, $54 million offer without options and a two-year, $45 million offer with a team option. Correction: Kuminga turned down a 3 year $75 million deal last summer for a 2 year $48 million deal. Now, he rejects a 3 year $36 million deal in favor of a 2 year $12 million one, favoring flexibility both times. Again, still not sure who else has kept betting on themselves like… — jeffonsports (@jeff_on_sports) August 26, 2026 Kuminga eventually settled for two years and $48.5 million with Golden State, a deal built around retaining control rather than maximizing his payday. After he was traded to Atlanta, the Hawks subsequently declined his $24.3 million team option for 2026-27 in late June, pushing him back into unrestricted free agency. Statistically, Kuminga’s case for a bigger payday is mixed. He averaged 12.3 points and 5.3 rebounds across 16 games with Atlanta after the trade, and has never held a full-time starting role over a full NBA season. Regardless, Kuminga has now twice declined the higher guaranteed number in favor of shorter-term flexibility. He first rejected a $75.2 million, three-year offer for a $48.5 million, two-year deal, and is now bypassing a $36 million, three-year offer for roughly $12 million in a two-year deal. And while much will depend on how his Minnesota tenure goes, it remains to be seen whether the 23-year-old will come to rue his decision.   The post Jonathan Kuminga will rue day he spurned Lakers for less money from Timberwolves appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles.title: Forever No. 1: Dolly Parton, ‘9 to 5’
articles.summary: Good as Parton was playing Doralee in her breakout film role, her biggest contribution to the '9 to 5' movie may have been writing and performing its letter-perfect title song.
articles._body: Forever No. 1 is a Billboard series that pays special tribute to the recently deceased artists who achieved the highest honor our charts have to offer — a Billboard Hot 100 No. 1 single — by taking an extended look back at the chart-topping songs that made them part of this exclusive club. Here, we honor the late, great Dolly Parton, whose workers anthem “9 to 5” reached No. 1 in February 1981. Related Dolly Parton, One of Country Music’s Biggest & Brightest Icons, Dies at 80 Dolly Parton’s 25 Best Songs: Critics’ Picks Dolly Parton’s Half-Century Hot 100 Legacy: ‘9 to 5,’ ‘Islands in the Stream’ & More Dolly Parton was well on her way to becoming a crossover superstar when the movie 9 to 5 was released in December 1980. She had reached No. 3 on the Billboard Hot 100 in January 1978 with “Here You Come Again,” a winsome pop song written by the great team of Barry Mann and Cynthia Weil . But 9 to 5 took her to another level. She more than held her own with two superstars, Jane Fonda and Lily Tomlin . She was great in her role as Doralee Rhodes, a secretary who is perennially harassed by her boss from hell, Frank Hart (played by Dabney Coleman ). But her biggest contribution to the film may have been writing and performing its letter-perfect title song. It was one of the biggest and best hits that Parton, who died on Tuesday (Aug. 26) at age 80, ever had. The song suits the film perfectly – it’s uptempo, which is ideal for a comedy. It distills and advances the film’s central theme – how workers are often taken advantage of in the workplace. (Both the film and the song owe their titles to 9to5, an organization founded in 1973 to bring about fair pay and equal treatment for women in the workplace.) But the song is more nuanced than, say, Johnny Paycheck’s recording of David Allan Coe’s “Take This Job and Shove It,” another country crossover hit that reached No. 1 on Hot Country Songs in January 1978. Parton wisely opened the song with a verse that is completely universal about worklife, saving more specific complaints for later. She opens with clever rhymes and witty wordplay: “Tumble out of bed and I stumble to the kitchen/ Pour myself a cup of ambition/ And yawn and stretch and try to come to life.” In the chorus, she begins the litany of complaints: “Working 9 to 5, what a way to make a livin’/ Barely getting by, it’s all takin’ and no givin’/ They just use your mind and they never give you credit…” But the very next line contains a glimmer of hope: “It’s enough to drive you crazy if you let it.” The clear implication: don’t let it. (Parton also lays in hopeful messages in the second verse: “But you’ve got dreams he’ll never take away/ In the same boat with a lot of your friends/ Waitin’ for the day your ship’ll come in/ And the tide’s gonna turn an’ it’s all gonna roll your way.”) The song mixes blunt talk that almost makes Parton sound like a union organizer (“It’s a rich man’s game no matter what they call it/ And you spend your life puttin’ money in his wallet”) with glimmers of the hope and optimism that were at the core of who Parton was as a person. On paper, the lyrics read as borderline-angry in spots, but Parton doesn’t sing it that way. Her charm and warmth, her audible smile, all soften the impact of her words. It was Fonda’s idea to cast Parton in the film, and the role was written with her in mind. Parton wrote the song on the set of the film. She has often explained that she devised the clacking typewriter rhythm by running her acrylic fingernails back and forth against each other. In the 2019 BBC documentary Dolly Parton: Here I Am, Fonda explained how the casting came together in early 1978. “I was driving home from having just seen Lily Tomlin for the first time in her one-woman show called Appearing Nitely , and I was totally smitten by Lily. … I turn on the radio. [Parton’s] ‘Two Doors Down’ is playing, and I suddenly get an image of Dolly Parton sitting at a typewriter, and I thought that would be something – Dolly Parton in her first movie playing a secretary in a movie that, among many other things, is going to touch upon sexual harassment. She’s perfect.” In that doc, Parton said that she pushed to write the title song. “When Jane came to me with it, I said, ‘Well, this is a good opportunity, but I will only do it if I can write the theme song.’ So they said, ‘Okay.’” Fonda and Tomlin knew the song was a home run the moment they heard it. Fonda remembered “the morning that Dolly came to work and motioned us over, and just outside the set, she said, ‘I’ve just written the song, and she used her long nails as a washboard, and she sang ‘9 to 5.’ And Lily and I looked at each other, and we had goosebumps.” Tomlin added: “[We] were just flabbergasted. We thought it was so great. I said to Jane, ‘This will make the movie a hit, if nothing else.’ And we knew this is not just a movie song. This is an anthem.” Gregg Perry, Parton’s long-time musical director and occasional producer, produced Parton’s single. The track featured such pros as guitarist Jeff Baxter, pianist Larry Knechtel and trumpeter Jerry Hey. Joey Scarbury, who would land a No. 2 Hot 100 hit in August 1981 with “Theme From Greatest American Hero (Believe It or Not),” was among the backup singers. The song entered the Hot 100 at No. 73 in the week ending Nov. 29, 1980. It was the week’s second-highest debut, behind Steely Dan ’s “Hey Nineteen.” In the week ending Feb. 14, 1981, the song jumped from No. 4 to No. 2, becoming Parton’s highest-charting hit to that point. The following week, it hit No. 1, bumping off Kool & the Gang ’s “Celebration.”  After one week on top, it was in turn displaced by Eddie Rabbitt ’s “I Love a Rainy Night.” Rabbitt’s song was No. 1 for two weeks, before “9 to 5” regained the top spot in the week ending March 14, 1981. articles._body: I thought this was something the Hacker News audience would appreciate; it's an aggregator of computer and security news. We initially built it for ourselves (we have a monthly newsletter, for 12+ years), but realised that others might like it as well. Although we collect a wide range of news, we currently promote to the front page what's on-topic for our audience, which is (currently) Web PKI, TLS, post-quantum cryptography, some cryptography, some security, and some privacy. We generally don't do vulnerabilities at all (although those will inevitably be picked for in the "all news" section). I've made an attempt to amplify the original voices in the security space, rather than just collecting what's already news. There's more work to be done in that direction. articles.title: Good Good Golf Fallout Is Talk of Tour Championship
articles.summary: Brett Davis-Imagn Images
articles._body: ATLANTA — As the Tour Championship begins Thursday, the hottest topic of discussion this week at East Lake Golf Club has been the Good Good Golf driver ad controversy . With fallout from the situation continuing, Good Good’s three biggest partners impacted most—Callaway, the PGA Tour, and Golf Channel—have added damage control to their list of duties at the $40 million FedExCup playoffs finale. Good Good cofounder Garrett Clark; the content creator group’s CEO, Matt Kendrick; and Callaway president and CEO Chip Brewer have all issued various statements and apologies following initial dispatches from the brands Saturday that many people perceived as lacking accountability. As the negative feedback poured in Friday night and Saturday, there was disagreement between Good Good and Callaway over who would take responsibility for the ad, multiple sources with knowledge of the companies’ thinking told Front Office Sports . Now, major questions still remain for Good Good, its Callaway partnership, and its upcoming Golf Channel show and PGA Tour event. Callaway Amid ongoing efforts to put out the Good Good fire since the ad was removed Saturday, Callaway has a strong contingent of equipment endorsers teeing it up at the 30-player Tour Championship: Xander Schauffele, Sam Burns, Akshay Bhatia, Min Woo Lee, and Si Woo Kim. Top Callaway executives are not on-site this week in Atlanta, but the brand has a strong presence, like it does at all tour events, with various equipment reps supporting its players. Callaway is conducting internal and external investigations into the ad creation and approval process, Brewer said Tuesday. Callaway began its official partnership with Good Good in 2023, working together on content, products, and brand campaigns throughout the past three and a half years. Severing ties with Good Good would be a major blow for Callaway’s bottom line, but at this point is not out of the question, some golf industry sources believe. Good Good products are being removed from major retailers including Golf Galaxy, Dick’s Sporting Goods, PGA Tour Superstore, and Target—but standalone Callaway products are remaining. Callaway is a publicly traded company; its stock price has remained relatively flat since closing at $15.78 on Aug. 21, before the ad controversy hit over the last weekend. Callaway opened at $15.68 on Thursday. PGA Tour The inaugural Good Good Championship is scheduled for Nov. 12–15 at Omni Barton Creek in Austin. Good Good signed a multiyear contract with the PGA Tour to launch and sponsor the new tournament, agreeing to pay at least $6 million annually to back the event. But now the event’s status is in question, with many golf industry sources believing it’s not viable to play the tournament as planned this fall. “It’s a bit of a fluid situation,” PGA Tour CEO Brian Rolapp said Tuesday when asked about the Good Good Championship at his pre-tournament press conference . “We were disappointed at first. It sounds like in the last 24 hours they’ve made some progress. We’ll continue to monitor the situation and see how it develops.” The PGA Tour could fund the event without a primary sponsor if it were to remove Good Good, or not play the tournament at all. Adding Good Good to its tournament lineup was likely to bring in swells of younger fans that would not typically be interested in fall PGA Tour golf. Golf Channel As Golf Channel carries coverage of the Tour Championship during all four rounds this weekend, the network postponed the premiere of Big Break x Good Good —a revamp of its reality competition series that was popular in the 2000s—from Tuesday to Sept. 1, due to the show’s presenting sponsor Golf Galaxy dropping out. Like the Good Good Championship, the status of Big Break x Good Good is also uncertain. The show was filmed earlier this year at Omni Barton Creek, so canceling it would be a major financial blow for Golf Channel. The show’s eventual winner is set to earn a spot in November’s Good Good Championship. Good Good members Brad Dalke and Sean Walsh are two of the show’s twelve competitors, while Clark and fellow member Bubbie Broders are non-playing team captains. articles.title: Utah QBs Making Strides Under Ryan Gunderson
articles.summary: Utah QB Coach Ryan Gunderson says Devon Dampier is making strides this fall and shares how he coaches Byrd Ficklin up as well.
articles._body: Bringing in a true quarterbacks coach quickly became one of the more unique, under-the-radar things Morgan Scalley did at Utah this offseason. But Ryan Gunderson slid into his new role quickly with one goal in mind: make the Utah QBs better than they already are. During the previous years, Devon Dampier didn’t have a true QB coach. His offensive coordinator had coached him. Things changed a lot internally but Dampier has taken everything in stride knowing he needs to improve for the Utes to be successful and for him to possible play at the next level. “We’ve asked him to try some new stuff, and he’s liked it or not liked it. I think just the relationship between him, I, and and Coach McGiven of being able to have conversations, and I don’t want him to be afraid that he’s going to hurt anybody’s feelings with saying I don’t like that or I’m not so confident in that,” Gunderson said. “But he also does a good job of, hey, I don’t have enough reps of this. I want to get some more.”   With the season a week away, Gunderson says Dampier has made strides, but he needs to do more to become truly elite. “Feel really good about where he’s at. I’m also not the type to say like, oh yeah, he’s good. Like we’ve got work to do. We’ve got work to do today, tomorrow, the next day. It’s a long road, the road of improvement. There are no stop signs. There’s no finish line. We’ve got a long way to go on this thing. But I’m very happy with where he is right now,” Gunderson said. Now that the pair have been working together for a little over eight months, Gunderson can fully admit what Dampier’s strengths are as a passer. “Devon throws a really nice ball. He’s got good arm strength. Devon’s biggest strength is vision. Did you ever play Madden when they had the quarterback vision, and you know it opened up or closed? Devon’s got really wide vision,” Gunderson said. “And then I think the obvious thing that you guys have seen more than I have is his ability to extend plays, and he’s fantastic throwing the ball outside the pocket. That’s one of the things we’ve worked a bunch on is throwing it from the pocket, and he’s gotten way better at it.” While Gunderson works on getting Dampier ready for the next level, he is also making sure Byrd Ficklin gets the time and reps needed to continue his development. “We are spending a lot of time with him, talking to him about stuff that I don’t have to talk to Devon about. Just Devon’s got some time on him and experience on him, but I’m really happy with where Byrd is at. But we’ve got to keep continuing to push him further and further. And then there’s some technique stuff that we’ve got to hone in on. This is going to be different than the stuff that we’re working on with Devon,” Gunderson said. Gunderson said that everyone in his room can learn something even if the conversation isn’t directed at them. “You’re talking to everybody in the room. But sometimes things are a little more directed at one person than the other. And then you hope that you have the maturity in the room,” Gunderson said. articles.summary:
Hi everyone,

I am a professor in AI, and I often build AI apps as a hobby and for academic projects. I felt that I was wasting too much time setting up backends, DB, and secrets for each app, and testing the prompts, updating them, and redeploying seemed tedious. So I built Backprompter to do a
articles._body: Hi everyone, I am a professor in AI, and I often build AI apps as a hobby and for academic projects. I felt that I was wasting too much time setting up backends, DB, and secrets for each app, and testing the prompts, updating them, and redeploying seemed tedious. So I built Backprompter to do all this without any setup. You can create agents, track different versions, test them, create mock users, simulate conversations, and track your evaluations. It supports usual agent setups - model selection, prompts, RAG, and tools (currently, HTTP API calls). Agents can also be combined by simply tagging them and describing the orchestration in natural language. For production, there is a single-click deployment of a chatbot interface, no setup needed. Also, developers can integrate the agents with their own frontend (Backprompter handles authentication and data management), or with their own backend if they want more control over authentication and data management. With one click, you can deploy your edited agent to production. I think there are broad applications for hobbyists, small teams, and organizations who want to integrate AI but don't have the time or expertise to set up backend, secrets, databases, and evaluation workflows. I started building this about 9 months ago. This is a solo project, so I would love some feedback. It's free to start, but with some limits. If you want to test more, I am happy to provide more credits for free. Also, looking for advice on what features to add next: Would the ability to deploy your agent to Slack or ChatGPT (as a custom GPT) be an important feature? https://backprompter.com/ I also built a version that can be self-hosted for complete privacy and for deploying apps within the network. The early merch stand at Madison Square Garden (via @HonkLaurennn ) pic.twitter.com/D5jWR3ynn0 — HSD Together On Tour (@hsdtogethertour) August 26, 2026 The jersey is an exclusive item for Styles’ 30-night Madison Square Garden residency, which runs from Aug. 26 to Oct. 31. Harry Styles’ 30-night stay at the Knicks’ Madison Square Garden Robert Hanashiro-USA TODAY. For the next couple of months, Styles will be playing shows at the Garden. His Together, Together Tour — which has previously visited Amsterdam, Netherlands; London, England; São Paulo, Brazil; and Mexico City, Mexico — will stay at MSG for 30 nights. These are the only shows that Styles is performing in the United States in 2026. The tour will conclude with six shows in Australia across Melbourne and Sydney later in the year. The Madison Square Garden residency concludes on Halloween. This is his second tour in a row to feature a show at the Garden on Oct. 31. Styles shook things up during the first MSG show . “Dance No More” made its debut as the opener, and songs like “Carolina,” “Cinema,” “Satellite, and “Kiwi” made their first appearances during the tour. Together, Together marks Styles’ first tour since Love on Tour ended in July 2023. It is in support of his fourth album, Kiss All the Time. Disco, Occasionally. articles.title: Show HN: ThunderPhone v2 – a new architecture for voice AI
articles.summary:
Hi folks, Alex here from ThunderPhone. Today we're launching v2.

Voice AI has been a hot topic for the past year or two, both for automating phone calls and for adding voice features to apps.

Most of the voice agents deployed have been using a "3 step pipeline": a transcription model to turn
articles._body: Hi folks, Alex here from ThunderPhone. Today we're launching v2. Voice AI has been a hot topic for the past year or two, both for automating phone calls and for adding voice features to apps. Most of the voice agents deployed have been using a "3 step pipeline": a transcription model to turn user speech into text, an LLM to generate a response in text, and a TTS model to turn the response text into audio. But the performance of these 3-step voice agents has often been so-so, largely for 3 reasons: 1) Voice agents have to be fast, usually requiring non-thinking LLMs to handle the conversation. Non-thinking LLMs make mistakes, leading to dumb behavior that derails conversations. 2) Today's voice AI stacks typically rely on a single transcription model to turn what the user says into text. This step loses a ton of information from the audio, and if the transcription model makes a mistake, the LLM often has no way to recover. This also leads to a lot of dumb behavior that breaks calls. 3) Natural conversation handling is a hard problem - filtering out noise like background voices, knowing when to allow the AI to be interrupted by a "uh, wait" but not by an "uh-huh", etc. - this also leads to awkward conversations. The "bitter lesson-pilled" solution to all of these is most likely going to be a "full duplex" model that receives and emits audio at all times, allowing for fluid back-and-forth, while also calling a smarter model behind the scenes. OpenAI appears to have been the first to make real progress towards this architecture with their latest GPT-Live release, but that tech is not yet ready to plug into phone calls. In the meantime, we've stitched together a stack that improves the performance of phone calls far beyond what's possible with a 3-step pipeline. The ThunderPhone stack combines a few insights: 1) Grabbing signal from audio in more than one way, including running multiple transcription models at once, and piping audio directly into LLMs. This hugely reduces mistake rates, especially on challenging problems like data entry, multilingual calls, etc. 2) Combining thinking and non-thinking LLMs: in a conversation, it's natural to respond to some things more quickly than others, and sometimes even say things like "oh, let me think about that" - to indicate that it'll take longer to get back to someone with a final answer. ThunderPhone does the same thing. 3) This is less unique to us but we've stitched together a very big swarm of small (and in a few cases large) models to help make conversation handling more natural, even in hard environments like loud places, speakerphone, etc. We've made the ThunderPhone stack available at 3 price points - 2c/min, 5c/min, and 9c/min, each with their own level of capability. The 2c/min model ("Spark") is the cheapest on the market to our knowledge, and is smart enough to handle simple transactional calls. Bolt at 5c/min is a middle ground, and the fastest model we offer. Storm at 9c/min (+3c/min for extra intelligence) is our flagship model, able to handle even quite complex calls with very few mistakes. With extra intelligence turned on, it sets the record on the Big Bench Audio benchmark at 99.4% accuracy. ThunderPhone is mostly aimed at B2B applications, but is also useful if you want to do something like setting up a smart voicemail for yourself, or calling around restaurants to make a reservation, calling around pharmacies to find a prescription, etc. for personal use. Let me know if you have questions - happy to answer anything about ThunderPhone except a few "trade secret" specifics, and about the voice AI space more broadly, including where we think the tech is going. And comment here or email me at alex@thunderphone.com if you want to get set up with some credits to try it out. articles.title: We laid him off. Then we hired him back
articles.summary: When we rehired Jonathan at Syndio, he logged back in and found our cold, corporate restructuring announcement still sitting in his inbox. Gut punch.
articles._body: In May, we eliminated a number of roles at Syndio as part of a company redesign. One of the people we let go was Jonathan Vidales, a labor economist who had been with us for five years. Around the same time, we redefined other jobs and asked those employees to take on more responsibility and a quota. We assumed they wouldn’t blink. These were leaner times. Jobs were harder to come by and the pendulum had shifted back toward employers. For those employees, we assumed, staying in a beefed-up role with a higher earning potential would be a no-brainer. Right? Wrong. Within a few months, several of the people I had expected to keep resigned. Suddenly, in our push to be more efficient in the age of AI, we lost some of the very talent we needed. The good news: Jonathan came back. In August, he applied for one of our newly-opened roles, and we rehired him. On a Zoom call, he told me sheepishly that coming back felt like “sneaking back in the house after I got kicked out.” That was a gut punch. But the next part was worse: When we reactivated his account, he said, he found our cold, corporate restructuring announcement still sitting in his inbox. What struck him was how impersonal it felt. In my mind, we were announcing a restructuring. In his, people he knew and worked alongside had just lost their jobs. Why couldn’t we have simply acknowledged them—and said something kind about the people who were leaving? Cringe. I won’t have to learn that lesson twice. At a time when every CEO feels they have to move faster, get leaner and reorganize completely around AI, it’s easy to undervalue the people you already have. AI-attributed cuts peaked in May, when  US employers announced 97,000 job cuts  and blamed 40% of them on AI.  Zillow cut more than 500 people  earlier this month, announced the day before earnings, according to executive coaching firm Challenger, Gray & Christmas. The AI excuse is getting old. Former Lululemon executive Julie Averill wrote a  piece in the New York Times  earlier this month saying you either see leaders believing they can fix a problem by waving AI at it (“AI wishing”) or blaming AI on job cuts (“AI washing”) credited to efficiency that doesn’t exist yet. Companies are imagining what AI might make possible, and making moves before fully understanding how to get there. Three in 10 employers eliminated positions after implementing AI, only to later add those roles back, according to an  April 2026 study  by global staffing firm Robert Half . I’m not saying companies shouldn’t change. That’s not the lesson.  We  had to change, when we shifted from being more of a pure software consultancy to becoming an AI-centric technology company. Advisory work remains an important part of what we do, but the center of gravity shifted. New priorities required new roles, and inevitably, some restructuring. But I did learn something about the danger of chasing the Next Big Business Model before fully understanding whether the skills, experience, and institutional knowledge you already have can evolve with you. There’s a refrain in the market along the lines of ‘knowledge work is becoming irrelevant in the age of AI.’ I’ve come to believe almost the opposite: AI can make experienced people even more valuable, if you give them the right tools to adapt. Roles can evolve. Skills can be rebuilt. But that requires leaders to invest in training and creating a path for people to make that transition. And as leaders, that’s on us. The bottom line is: People aren’t interchangeable parts. Institutional knowledge, trust, relationships, expertise–all those things take time to build and sometimes you don’t fully understand their value until they are gone. In the end, I share this small yarn about Jonathan because it is ultimately a story of second chances–both for an employee taking another chance on a company, and of a company taking another look at what it values. It’s also about reinvention. As leaders, we spend so much time looking forward that we forget the value of also looking back, and questioning the decisions we made along the way. It’s okay to change your mind. To reinvent yourself. Reinvent your company. Reinvent your team. Reinvent your leadership style. Sometimes moving forward means admitting you got something wrong–and getting a second chance to make it right. articles.title: Taylor Swift’s ‘Toy Story 5’ Tune Remains Triumphant on Top Movie Songs Chart
articles.summary: “I Knew It, I Knew You” leads for a second month in a row.
articles._body: For the second month in a row, Taylor Swift ’s Toy Story 5 contribution “I Knew It, I Knew You” is No. 1 on Billboard ’s Top Movie Songs chart, powered by Tunefind . Rankings for the Top Movie Songs chart are based on song and film data provided by Tunefind and ranked using a formula blending that data with sales and streaming information tracked by Luminate during the corresponding period of July 2026. The ranking generally includes newly released films from the preceding three months, with exceptions given to movies whose music is still experiencing a high volume of public interest. “I Knew It, I Knew You” crowns the July 2026 chart following the song’s first full month of release. It was originally released on June 5, preceding the premiere of its parent film by two weeks (June 19). The song earned 82.5 million official streams and sold 16,000 downloads in the United States in July 2026, according to Luminate. After leading the weekly Billboard Hot 100 for two weeks upon its release in June, the song appeared at No. 2 for the entirety of July (it ranks at No. 3 on the latest survey, dated Aug. 29). “I Knew It, I Knew You” leads a slew of new entries to Top Movie Songs for July 2026 following the departure of music featured in the Michael Jackson biopic Michael after three months of the film’s release. After Swift comes a pair of tracks from Netflix’s Voicemails for Isabelle in Benson Boone ’s “Beautiful Things” and Robyn ’s “Dancing on My Own” at Nos. 2 and 3, respectively. Boone ranks at No. 2 on the strength of 52.6 million streams and 4,000 downloads; the song peaked at No. 2 on the Hot 100 in 2024. Robyn, meanwhile, racked up 16.1 million streams and 10,000 downloads, scoring appearances on multiple weekly charts after its Voicemails for Isabelle synch, including a debut on the Billboard Global 200, peaking at No. 176. articles.title: Yankees’ Aaron Boone’s ‘dangerous game’ brings even more playoff concerns
articles.summary: Earlier this week, the New York Yankees lost Fernando Cruz for the season, depleting another arm from their bullpen. Because of this, Aaron Boone has had to take special measures with his use of the bullpen. Even though the Yankees’ playoff odds are good, their World Series chances are in d
articles._body: Earlier this week, the New York Yankees lost Fernando Cruz for the season , depleting another arm from their bullpen. Because of this, Aaron Boone has had to take special measures with his use of the bullpen. Even though the Yankees’ playoff odds are good, their World Series chances are in danger as they attempt to navigate the bullpen , according to Brendan Kuty of The Athletic. “The team’s decision not to trade for a reliever at the Aug. 3 deadline had already seemed like a gamble. At the time, the Yankees were leaning heavily on Cruz, left-hander Brent Headrick, righty Paul Blackburn and closer David Bednar,” Kuty wrote. For context, the Yanks recently used newly acquired reliever Brad Fullmer. But they haven’t acquired much else. New York is currently second in bullpen ERA , according to MLB.com. For the most part, they have been excellent all season. But a recent game against the Houston Astros exposed some weak points. In that game, Headrick allowed three earned runs to take the loss. Over the weekend, both Yerry de Los Santos and Bradley Hanner allowed a run in the same game. With Cruz on the IL, the Yankees have not found someone they trust completely. The Yankees can still surpass the Tampa Bay Rays , but the injuries are piling up for this bullpen. If the offense cannot score more than four runs and the starting pitchers cannot go deep, there might be some issues in the playoffs. With multiple relievers on the IL, the stretch will be interesting for the Yankees. If the playoffs were to begin today, they would be facing the Boston Red Sox in a best-of-3 wildcard round. The only question that remains is whether their bullpen could survive a long series. articles.title: Bush’s Gavin Rossdale & His Shelter Dog Kaya Help Spread the ‘Rescue Effect’ With ASPCA: ‘It’s Mesmerizing What Animals Can Do for You’
articles.summary: The ASPCA is providing $2 million in grants to support fee-waived adoption events through its new campaign.
articles._body: For Gavin Rossdale , adopting a dog was supposed to be a simple act of compassion, but it ultimately turned his life right-side up. The Bush frontman first met Kaya at Los Angeles Animal Services’ East Valley Animal Shelter , where the dog had already experienced a traumatic past. Kaya had been hit by a car, suffered a dislocated shoulder and had smashed teeth. Yet when Rossdale saw him sitting in the shelter, he remembers a dog who seemed completely undeterred by everything he had been through. Related Gavin Rossdale Recalls Time He Took a Backyard Dip With His Mega-Pop Star Neighbor: ‘She’s a Great Swimmer’ Bush Announce Dates For 2026 Land of Milk and Honey U.S. Tour Gavin Rossdale Says Making a Living in Music Is ‘Terrifying’ for New Artists “He owned nothing,” Rossdale tells Billboard , “and there he was, sitting in the shelter, looking like he owned the world.” Now, Kaya travels with Rossdale on the road, spends his days getting plenty of exercise and attention, and has become the catalyst for the rock star’s increasingly vocal advocacy for shelter animals. The pair are now joining the ASPCA’s annual Rescue Effect campaign, which encourages people to adopt or foster animals and highlights how one adoption can create space and resources for other animals in need. The ASPCA launched the third annual Rescue Effect campaign Aug. 1, with more than 450 shelters and rescues participating nationwide. The organization is providing $2 million in grants to support fee-waived adoption events through the campaign, which runs through Adopt a Shelter Dog Month in October. According to the ASPCA, nearly 6 million dogs and cats entered shelters and rescues across the U.S. in 2025, with animals — particularly dogs — often spending longer periods waiting to be adopted. For Rossdale, the campaign sits very close to his heart. “I love animals, I love dogs,” he says. “It’s mesmerizing what animals can do for you.” Below, watch the new campaign video — soundtracked by “Glycerine,” Bush’s highest-charting song ever on the Billboard Hot 100 , peaking at No. 28 in 1996 and topping the Alternative Airplay chart. View this post on Instagram Rossdale initially went to East Valley after his son chose Kaya from a photograph. He admits he was nervous about adopting another dog after the family had lost their previous pet roughly nine months earlier. But his son went to meet Kaya, and the connection was almost instantaneous. “These dogs know that their chance is there,” Rossdale says. “And they take it in all four paws.” Rossdale ultimately went to the shelter with his son, and the pair brought Kaya home. What followed, he says, was an “incredible learning curve” that transformed him into something of a self-described “dog handler.” The responsibility has single-handedly become one of the most meaningful parts of his life. “He’s made me really responsible,” Rossdale says, noting that Kaya needs his time and attention “dark or light, rain or shine.” Caring for the dog has also forced him to look outside of himself, he says, instead of solely spending his time focused on his own needs. That commitment has followed Rossdale onto the road with Bush. Instead of simply finding the nearest tennis court or fitting Kaya into his existing routine, Rossdale says touring now involves looking for open spaces and parks where the dog can run and spend time outside. And Kaya, apparently, has adapted to the rock-star lifestyle just fine. “He’s always moved like a celebrity,” Rossdale says. “He’s got a very regal way of carrying himself.” That majestic attitude is even more remarkable given Kaya’s beginnings. Rossdale says the dog had been homeless and injured before arriving at the shelter, making his transformation all the more extraordinary and heartwarming. Lucas Pool/ASPCA Rossdale has increasingly used his platform to advocate for shelter animals. In November 2025, he returned to East Valley Animal Shelter for a PETA campaign encouraging adoption, and he has also worked with Best Friends Animal Society on efforts highlighting adoptable dogs. His ASPCA partnership continues that work, but Rossdale says he particularly likes the opportunity to do something that isn’t directly connected to his career. “Everything that generally I do is just to further my career,” he tells Billboard . “So it’s quite nice to do something where you do something else.” And he hopes that putting Kaya front and center will make someone else take the next step. “I’d like to be sort of everywhere with pictures of Kaya,” Rossdale says. “If anyone has a half an inkling of adopting,” he hopes the dog can provide the inspiration to follow through. That, he says, is ultimately what the campaign is about: encouraging people to take action. “Any kind of inspiration for people to follow through and help these animals is the only thing it’s about,” he says. Rossdale knows that adopting one dog doesn’t solve the shelter crisis. But he also sees the power in what he calls the “rescue effect”: One animal leaving a shelter means another animal can potentially take its place. “By getting one dog, I mean, it’s only 6 million minus one,” he says. “It’s not like I’m doing the greatest thing. But imagine if everybody did that.” Meanwhile, Kaya has taken somewhat of an interest in the musician’s career. When asked whether his dog has a favorite Bush song, Rossdale laughs before providing a humorous answer. “It’s probably the one that buys them the most steak,” he says, suggesting the band’s most successful, most-played songs are Kaya’s favorites. Rossdale adopted Kaya for $72, he adds, “But his tab has really been expanded since then.” It’s a fitting ending to Kaya’s unlikely journey: From an injured shelter dog with little to his name to a touring companion who now gets to live the rock-star life — and, potentially, help other shelter animals get their own second act. articles.title: Browns’ 2026 draft forces out 2023 3rd-round pick
articles.summary: The Cleveland Browns’ receiving corps was a weak point last season. The AFC North team recognized that and made adding pass catchers a priority in the 2026 offseason. Two of the team’s first three picks in the 2026 NFL Draft were used on receivers. The Browns took KC Concepcion 24th o
articles._body: The Cleveland Browns’ receiving corps was a weak point last season. The AFC North team recognized that and made adding pass catchers a priority in the 2026 offseason. Two of the team’s first three picks in the 2026 NFL Draft were used on receivers. The Browns took KC Concepcion 24th overall, and Denzel Boston was selected not long after with the 39th pick. The moves significantly improve the outlook for Cleveland’s passing attack, which, for now, will be led with the recently crowned-as-starter Deshaun Watson . The quarterback beat out Shedeur Sanders, but it wouldn’t be a surprise if the Colorado product was promoted at some point this season. Regardless of who is under center, Cleveland passers have to be happy about the added receiving depth. Concepcion and Boston’s presence meant there wasn’t room for Cedric Tillman, though. Adam Schefter reported that the Browns are releasing the receiver who was a third-round pick in 2023. Tillman flashed potential through three seasons, but he struggled with consistency and injury problems. He racked up 132 catches for 833 yards before the rookie additions buried him down the depth chart. In addition to Concepcion and Boston, the Browns still have Jerry Jeudy, Isaiah Bond, and Harold Fannin Jr. Jeudy is one of the best route runners in the NFL, and Bond went undrafted last year because of sexual assault accusations. However, he was expected to be drafted on Day 2, and he proved his talent with the Browns after the charges were dropped. Fannin is a tight end who broke out as a potential star last year. While he is listed at tight end, he often lines up in the slot, where he can use his big body and elite athleticism to create matchup nightmares for opposing defenses. Tillman will surely be one of the top free agent targets of the victims of the cut-down period. The post Browns’ 2026 draft forces out 2023 3rd-round pick appeared first on ClutchPoints .

The 92,000-capacity stadium was previously utilised in the 2025 season, in a UIL 5A state semifinal clash between South Oak Cliff (Texas) and Meliss
articles._body: Texas high school football is officially set to get underway tonight, in one of the most exciting years for the state’s high school football action. However, ahead of that, one of the best teams in the Lone Star State, Southlake Carroll (Texas), is in out-of-state action. In one of the most high-profile interstate matchups of the year, the Dragons take on Jenks (Okla.) in the latest inauguration of the Oklahoma-Texas rivalry in the iconic Cotton Bowl. In one of the most high-profile matchups of the year, both sides have championship hopes. READ MORE: Southlake Carroll (TX) 2026 Preview: State title odds, game-by-game predictions In the high school football renewal of the Red River Rivalry, tonight’s matchup is held at a venue that needs almost no introduction for football fans. The 92,000-capacity stadium was previously utilised in the 2025 season, in a UIL 5A state semifinal clash between South Oak Cliff (Texas) and Melissa (Texas). “It’ll be a great experience for our kids. So, we got to tell our kids, and first of all, they were really excited about playing Southlake Carroll; they were really excited. And then to tell them we’re going to get to play in the Cotton Bowl, everyone’s really excited and looking forward to that.” Jenks’ head coach, Adam Gaylor , stated on Oklahoma’s Own Sports in February. Entering the upcoming season, Southlake Carroll has remained in 6A play following the Texas high school football district realignment. One of the top teams in the state and a state title contender, the Dragons enter the upcoming season under a new coaching staff. During the offseason, the Dragons promoted defensive coordinator Lee Munn to the position of head football coach. With the program for over eight years, the former defensive coordinator takes over for long-time head coach Riley Dodge, who took a coaching job at SMU. Meanwhile, the Jenks Trojans are coming off a deep playoff run in 2025. Reaching the 6A semifinals, the No. 3 team in the state ultimately fell to a perennial state contender in Owasso (Okla.), in a game that could have been decided on the flip of a coin. Behind the offensive line, both sides have lost significant offensive weapons. With Landon Kizzar set to start at quarterback for Jenks, the Trojans will have to replace a significant amount of rushing offense with Oklahoma State running back Kaydin Jones gone. For Southlake Carroll, the Dragons will have to replace one of Texas high school football’s top quarterbacks. During the 2025 season, three-star senior Angelo Renda threw for over 4000 yards, finishing the year with 4,266 yards and 46 touchdowns. With Renda enrolled at Pittsburgh , three-star junior Hudson Tomcheck is set to take the reins at quarterback. However, he will have one of Texas high school football’s top pass catchers to throw to, with three-star receiver Blake Gunter . Gunter hauled in 68 passes for 1,224 yards last year. With both sides having massive questions to answer tonight in their opening game of the season, Rivals has everything needed to catch this week’s Cotton Bowl matchup. articles.title: This Kentucky WR is viewed as a potential breakout player in 2026
articles.summary: After a promising end to his true freshman season, Kentucky's DJ Miller is poised for a breakout campaign in 2026.
articles._body: Kentucky’s wide receiver group is viewed as one of the biggest question marks going into Will Stein ‘s first season as head coach. But there is an up-and-coming player in that room who many think is on the verge of a breakout year. Sophomore pass-catcher DJ Miller has been drawing praise throughout the offseason. A big target at 6-foot-3, 210 pounds, the St. Louis native is coming off a promising true freshman campaign in 2025. Most of Miller’s production came against the second half of the schedule, but he still posted 13 receptions for 175 yards with a pair of touchdowns across seven games played. Now in a new system at Kentucky under Stein and offensive coordinator Joe Sloan , led by Notre Dame transfer quarterback Kenny Minchey , there are high hopes of a productive 2026 for Miller. ESPN’s Adam Rittenberg sees that, too. He dropped an article on Thursday morning outlining 51 breakout candidates for the upcoming season. Miller made the cut. “Miller is among the holdovers on offense from the previous coaching staff, and he has a chance to see his production grow under new boss Will Stein,” Rittenberg wrote. “Miller had at least one catch in six of his seven games as a true freshman last fall, and had a breakout performance against Tennessee with five receptions for 120 yards and two touchdowns, which tied the team single-game freshman record. Miller started three games against SEC opponents and had all but one of his receptions against conference foes.” Minchey is going to need some studs to pass to this fall. Miller, a former four-star high school recruit, is one of the wideouts expected to fill that role. Stein has been open about his desire for Miller to take a significant leap as a sophomore. Sloan views him as a deep-ball vertical threat in the passing game. A productive season from Miller will go a long way in helping Kentucky’s offense compete with the SEC’s best. Kickoff is right around the corner…
