The star defender is eligible for a new contract, and the Seahawks and Williams began talks on an extension. Now, Williams has a new contract, accordi
articles._body: The Seattle Seahawks are beginning their quest for a Super Bowl repeat, and a major part of their last run was defensive lineman Leonard Williams. The star defender is eligible for a new contract, and the Seahawks and Williams began talks on an extension . Now, Williams has a new contract , according to Ian Rapoport of ESPN. “The Seahawks and star Leonard Williams have agreed to terms on a 3-year, $90M extension to keep him in Seattle for the foreseeable future. The three-time Pro Bowler made one last year and is still in his prime at 32. Now, locked in,” Rapoport posted on X, formerly Twitter. Williams was the sixth overall selection of the New York Jets in 2015. He was traded to the New York Giants during the 2019 season. He was traded again during the 2023 season to the Seahawks. He was a pro-bowler in both 2024 and 2025, while also being named a second-team All-Pro in 2025. Williams also won the Super Bowl for the first time this past year. He has been stellar in the last two seasons for the Seahawks. In 33 games, he has racked up 126 tackles with 18 sacks, plus an interception. Williams has played 175 career games with 637 tackles, 61.5 half-sacks, and a touchdown. The 32-year-old defensive tackle is now under contract through the 2029 season. The new deal has $56 million in guarantees while keeping Williams with Seattle in his prime. The Seahawks are in a prime position to make a run for another title in 2026, bringing back much of the roster, but with a new running back in 2026 . articles.title: TV Ratings Help Explain Why the NFL Killed the Pro Bowl
articles.summary: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images
articles._body: The NFL cited a priority on player recognition in its dramatic decision to kill the Pro Bowl Games . The event’s precipitous decline on television, however, also represented a key factor in the removal of an all-star showcase with a lineage dating to 1939. The league will no longer stage an all-star game of any kind, instead choosing to select and honor a set of 88 Pro Bowlers annually, with no alternates, as was the case for the actual game. In detailing the decision, NFL officials said they leaned heavily on player input, and a lack of interest by those players in competing in a post-playoff game “They made that extremely clear on our calls and our discussions: ‘When our playoff run is over, our season ends. I don’t want to compete anymore,’” said NFL EVP of football operations Troy Vincent. The other ugly truth about the Pro Bowl Games, however, is the sharp drop in viewership directly countered historic audience trends across the rest of the league, which is poised for even more growth this season . As recently as 2022, the final year the Pro Bowl was held as a traditional tackle football game, the event drew an average television audience of 6.7 million viewers—a 16-year low. A subsequent pivot and renaming of the event to the Pro Bowl Games , and a new format based on flag football and skills competition, did not stem the bleeding—and instead accelerated the viewership decline. The 2023 Pro Bowl Games averaged 6.3 million viewers, and that figure then fell to 5.8 million in 2024, 4.7 million last year, and then a startlingly low 2 million this year. That represents a 57% drop in average viewership in just one year, and a 70% retreat over four years. In February, the NFL sought to revive the Pro Bowl Games by staging it as part of Super Bowl LX week in the Bay Area. After developing a so-called flag football “Thunderdome” at San Francisco’s Moscone Center, the event was largely obscured by the many other happenings around the region leading up to the league’s championship game. “It’s OK to be the first league to walk away from a competitive all-star game,” said NFL EVP Peter O’Reilly. For decades, though, the Pro Bowl was a cherished league tradition, particularly when it was held at Honolulu’s Aloha Stadium from 1980 to 2009. But Upton Bell, the son of former NFL commissioner Bert Bell, said the Pro Bowl was never meant to be a permanent event. “My father invented the Pro Bowl to get the players of the ’50s more money,” the younger Bell said in a social media post . “He did not intend it to continue after the NFL became successful. The game went on entirely too long.” The older Bell’s efforts that led to the 1951 debut of the Pro Bowl—a brand name that will live on—built on an NFL all-star game held between 1939 and 1942. All-Star Struggles For more than decade, NFL commissioner Roger Goodell had openly mused about restructuring or outright ending the Pro Bowl, and the league’s struggles with this event somewhat mirror issues other major leagues have had with their own all-star games. In each of them, there is an inherent tension. On one hand, these events are powerful marketing vehicles and showcases to grow fan interest around the world. On the other hand, they are also exhibition games that can create unpalatable injury risks for players still owed tens or hundreds of millions of dollars from their respective teams. Each of the other U.S.-based men’s pro leagues has addressed this conflict in various ways. MLB still holds a competitive all-star game, but has done away with extra innings in favor of a home-run swing-off tiebreaker, used to dramatic effect last year . The NBA shifted to a U.S.-vs-World tournament format to great success last season . The NHL, meanwhile, is creating a rotation of internationally oriented competitions including its own All-Star weekend, the revamped World Cup of Hockey, and player participation in the Olympics—all building off of big fan reaction to last year’s 4 Nations Face-Off. The NFL, however, has some unique attributes that made such fixes much more difficult. Its schedule format does not allow for a midseason break like the other leagues. The collision nature of the sport also has left players unwilling to exert themselves physically after the grind of the season—something fans increasingly noticed, and reflected in the declining viewership figures. “You come off the championship games and the viewers see the physicality of the game and you try to replicate that,” Vincent said. “Frankly, it just doesn’t sit well.” The post TV Ratings Help Explain Why the NFL Killed the Pro Bowl appeared first on Front Office Sports .

articles.title: Colts’ Alec Pierce injury move doesn’t mean he’s 100% for Week 1
articles.summary: The Indianapolis Colts have been without Alec Pierce this offseason as he recovers from ankle surgery. The team recently made a big move showing his progress, and there’s hope he can be ready by Week 1, according to ESPN’s Adam Schefter. “Colts are activating WR Alec Pierce off
articles._body: The Indianapolis Colts have been without Alec Pierce this offseason as he recovers from ankle surgery. The team recently made a big move showing his progress, and there’s hope he can be ready by Week 1, according to ESPN’s Adam Schefter. “Colts are activating WR Alec Pierce off PUP today, as [Mike Chappell] reported. Pierce underwent ankle surgery in March and now will start ramping up with hopes of returning for the Colts’ regular-season opener,” Schefter wrote on X, formerly Twitter. If Pierce is able to start practicing this week, he would have about two weeks to get prepared to have a chance at playing in the season opener. That’s a lot of pressure to put on the wide receiver, and if the Colts don’t feel like he’s ready, they’ll probably give him some time to come back. Pierce is definitely the Colts’ best receiver, and they’re going to miss his presence on the field. After trading Michael Pittman to the Pittsburgh Steelers, it made it even more obvious that the Colts were going to need Pierce this season. As of now, they’ll have to rely on players such as Keenan Allen, whom they just signed over a week ago, but he is a veteran receiver. The run game will also be key for the Colts, as Jonathan Taylor had one of his better seasons last year. Overall, the Colts want to recapture the success they had during the first half of last season before injuries put a dark cloud over the year. If Pierce can get back for Week 1, that would be big for them, and they could possibly get off to a fast start to the season. articles.title: Panic passes Trump tariff refunds back to the Playdate customers who paid them
articles.summary: "It just felt like the right thing to do."
articles._body: Panic, the indie game publishers behind the quirky, yellow crank-sporting Playdate gaming handheld , is issuing refunds to customers who had to shoulder the cost of inappropriate tariffs imposed by the Trump administration this year. The news comes months after the Supreme Court said in a February ruling that those tariffs were illegal , which also demanded that the administration refund the companies that had to temporarily pay the import taxes. In an update posted on the Playdate help site this week , Panic noted that it has finally "begun to receive refunds of the tariffs we paid in the last year" and had consequently "refunded all tariffs charged to customers." In the initial version of that tariff note, Panic explained that it couldn't afford to simply "absorb" the 19 percent tariffs it was being charged to import Playdate hardware made overseas because "our margins on Playdate are low." As such, while the tax was in effect, it was passed along to customers as an explicit subtotal line item at the bottom of all Playdate orders. That's in contrast to companies like Nintendo, which vaguely cited "market conditions" and tariff "uncertainty" in raising the asking price of legacy hardware and some Switch 2 accessories last year. Regularly seen with Trick Williams on WWE TV, Yachty was also a part of Trick Williams’ WWE WrestleMania 42 victory. With him growing in his role at the Stamford-based promotion, the rapper is now set to battle Baron Corbin on the upcoming edition of WWE Saturday Night’s Main Event. While Lil Yachty has embraced his wrestling role, former WWE Women’s United States Champion Tiffany Stratton has become more active outside of wrestling. Stratton is now regularly seen streaming and collaborating with other streamers, including N3on and Cinna. Her recent collaboration was with none other than Lil Yachty. Stratton joined Lil Yachty on the Twitch stream on Aug. 26, 2026, and they collaborated on a new song . Stratton took to the studio to record her verses and even found a way to include her iconic catchphrase, Tiffy Time. “It’s time, I arrived. Blonde hair, hazel eyes. Ain’t sweet, not on this side. Get your s**t fried. Yeah, when it’s Tiffy Time.” Stratton was found rapping in the now-viral video. She also adds, “Looking in the mirror and I look terrific. Used to drive a Civic, now my Lyft do digits. I’m coming for the title. I don’t care who got it. I don’t care who had it.” The video has gone extremely viral on social, gathering thousands of views. Throughout the video, Stratton is also seen practicing her lyrics and trying to integrate “Tiffy Time” into the verse, while WWE’s Je’Von Evans is seen constantly laughing in the background. Stratton is still an active wrestler on the WWE SmackDown roster and has never expressed any feelings of becoming a rapper, although she had previously opened up about joining Hollywood. articles.title: Draymond Green drops ‘highly f***ing likely’ claim on Klay Thompson leaving Warriors in 2019
articles.summary: There was a time when Stephen Curry, Klay Thompson, and Draymond Green looked inseparable. Even with the arrival of Kevin Durant in 2017, the Golden State Warriors always felt like the team of Curry, Thompson, and Green. Now, Thompson is with the Miami Heat, while Curry and Green are the only rem
articles._body: There was a time when Stephen Curry, Klay Thompson, and Draymond Green looked inseparable. Even with the arrival of Kevin Durant in 2017, the Golden State Warriors always felt like the team of Curry, Thompson, and Green. Now, Thompson is with the Miami Heat , while Curry and Green are the only remnants of the Warriors’ dynastic run. Thompson is in his third team after a two-year stint with the Dallas Mavericks. Green, however, claimed that the sweet-shooting guard was ready to leave the Warriors as early as 2019, but the plan was derailed by his ACL injury. “(It was) highly likely that after the 2019 playoffs, Klay Thompson was going to leave the Golden State Warriors and go be a No. 1 option somewhere. Highly f****** likely,” said Green on his podcast, as reported by NBC Sports Bay Area’s Taylor Wirth. “Then he got hurt, and so he stayed. But one thing I can assure you, there was a 90% chance my brother was going to leave Golden State and go elsewhere and test that No. 1 option thing out. Unfortunately, it wasn’t in the cards for him, and he got hurt, and he never got the opportunity to.” After his ACL injury, Thompson suffered an Achilles injury, sidelining him for another season. The five-time All-Star remained with the Warriors until 2024, winning a fourth title in 2022. He did not want to leave Golden State, but he was not pleased with the team’s offer for his contract extension, prompting him to sign with the Mavericks. Green’s claim came after Thompson agreed to a two-year, $11.5 million deal with the Heat. Green said no one, especially the media, should expect Thompson to be in his prime form in Miami , underscoring the tough reality instead of entertaining a faulty narrative. articles._body: A couple of months into married life after their blockbuster wedding at Madison Square Garden , Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce are navigating new challenges . Page Six reports that the couple is “settling into this new rhythm as a married couple and [are] really enjoying what that feels like.” The source explained that they are currently “enjoying figuring out what their new normal looks like.” Their dynamic has changed since their nuptials. In the time leading up to their wedding, which took place on Friday, July 3, 2026, the couple was “pretty much inseparable.” With the Kansas City Chiefs’ training camp and preseason starting, Kelce had to return to work. Meanwhile, Swift is busy with her own ventures, as she “has been pouring herself into writing new music and is incredibly inspired creatively.” The source noted that “songwriting has been her main focus, and she’s really excited about what’s taking shape.” What exactly that is was not disclosed. Surely, she is working on her 13th studio album, which should be extra special. Regardless of work, Swift and Kelce are still beaming whenever acknowledging their married status. When did Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce get married? Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images Swift and Kelce tied the knot on Friday, July 3, 2026, in front of a reported thousand guests. Adam Sandler, a longtime Swiftie and Kelce’s Happy Gilmore 2 co-star, officiated the ceremony. Paul McCartney, Stevie Nicks, and Avril Lavigne were among the performers at the wedding of the summer. McCartney dusted off The Beatles’ “I Want to Hold Your Hand,” becoming the first member of the Fab Four to perform it since the ’60s. articles._body: Jonathan Kuminga has agreed to a two-year, $12 million contract with the Minnesota Timberwolves. Kuminga notified the Timberwolves of his decision on Wednesday evening , choosing Minnesota over the Los Angeles Lakers despite the fact that the Lakers could have offered him more money. However, financially speaking, per HoopsHype, completing the signing isn’t automatic . To fit the $12 million deal under the second apron, the Wolves need to shed roughly $3 million and will have to make a corresponding roster move. The most likely path is trading veteran Josh Green, who carries a $14.6 million salary, for a player making less money. Alternatively, the team could waive and stretch Green’s salary to create the necessary cap room. At 23, Kuminga fits the age curve of Minnesota’s core, aligning closely with Edwards, Ball and Jaden McDaniels, who are all 25. He was the No. 7 pick in the 2021 draft and spent four and a half seasons with Golden State as part of the Warriors. His Warriors tenure included a championship but also stretches outside Steve Kerr’s rotation. In February, Kuminga was traded to Atlanta along with Buddy Hield in exchange for Kristaps Porziņģis, a deal that came less than five months after he and Golden State had agreed to a two-year, nearly $50 million contract with a Year 2 team option. Atlanta declined that option in late June. Kuminga’s stint in Atlanta was limited: 16 regular-season games at 12.3 points per game. He was more productive in the playoffs, reaching double figures in five of the Hawks’ six postseason games in April, including a 21-point outing that helped Atlanta take a 2-1 first-round lead over the eventual champion New York Knicks. Last season, split between Golden State and Atlanta, Kuminga averaged 12.2 points and 5.6 rebounds. Needless to say, Kuminga has once again bet on himself and will be looking for a starter role with the Timberwolves, something he may not have been guaranteed at the Lakers.   The post NBA rumors: The trade Timberwolves will try to make to create space needed to sign Jonathan Kuminga appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles.title: Cubs star Pete Crow-Armstrong’s fiery rant calling out umps shows he doesn’t care at all they admitted to mistake
articles.summary: The Chicago Cubs were looking to take the series over the Arizona Diamondbacks on Wednesday. They ended up falling in the game, 2-0. Still, the drama of the game happened in the sixth inning, as Pete Crow-Armstrong sat on third base in the sixth inning. After a catcher’s balk was not called
articles._body: The Chicago Cubs were looking to take the series over the Arizona Diamondbacks on Wednesday. They ended up falling in the game, 2-0. Still, the drama of the game happened in the sixth inning, as Pete Crow-Armstrong sat on third base in the sixth inning. After a catcher’s balk was not called, Crow-Armstrong was irate and had to be held back . PCA was leading off third base with the game still tied 0-0. Eduardo Rodriguez was winding up to throw a pitch to Michael Busch when he saw PCA break for home. Rodriguez stepped off the rubber and threw home to catcher James McCann. It was ruled a legal pitch, instead of a balk, which would have scored Crow-Armstrong. This led to the confrontation. Home plate umpire and crew chief Alfonso Marquez gathered the umpires and agreed they did not see an infraction , but admitted to the mistake, per Bob Nightengale of USA Today. “We just didn’t see it,’’ Marquez said. “We just didn’t see it. After looking at the video, it looked like he stepped off.’’ PCA did not care about the explanation. “No, it doesn’t make me feel any better,’’ Crow-Armstrong said, “that they admitted that they missed the call. They had as much time as they wanted to talk about it on the field, so they should have admitted that right after they got it wrong.’” Crow-Armstrong was even more irate discussing the call after the fact, even as he had to be held back during the game. “I saw four umpires miss a pretty obvious play,’’ Crow-Armstrong said. “They’re out there every day like we are. Their one job is to get calls right, and if they get it wrong, they’re supposed to talk about it, figure it out, and get it right. And they didn’t. I don’t know how you miss somebody starting their motion and then stopping it and stepping off. I just don’t know.’ Still, the potential MVP realized he should have kept his cool, and some of the frustration of a bad series at the plate also came out. “So, if I’m going to sit here and [complain] about all this stuff,’’ he said, “I should have done better today. Shouldn’t have punched out three times. I should have had better at-bats all series. I was pretty non-existent. So, I think you guys just saw my frustrations from the last three days kind of come out.’’ The Cubs are now 76-58 on the season, which places them in second place in the NL Central. They are also 6.5 games back of the Milwaukee Brewers in the division. They control the top wild card spot in the National League. The Cubs open a series with the Cincinnati Reds on Friday. articles.title: Flock CEO Asks Americans to 'Compromise' on Privacy as Camera Backlash Grows
articles.summary: Garrett Langley says 99.9% of police are good actors, days after a report identified at least 69 officials accused of misusing plate readers.
articles._body: In brief - Flock Safety CEO Garrett Langley told Fox News that the country has to prioritize a compromise between privacy and safety. - He compared calls for an outright ban to banning vehicles, pointing to drunk driving and seatbelt laws as the better model. - Langley's remarks followed a Washington Post investigation that found police departments were not auditing how officers used the cameras. The CEO of Flock Safety has called for "compromise" amid a growing backlash against the company's AI-powered license plate cameras, which have been vandalized across the country and have drawn bipartisan fire in Congress. "What we have to prioritize as a country is compromise," Garrett Langley told Fox News in an interview broadcast Saturday, arguing that Americans who frame the argument as a choice between privacy and safety are "prioritizing the wrong thing." Flock has united lawmakers who agree on little else. Senator Bernie Sanders, the Vermont independent, said this month he would introduce legislation to stop "AI mass surveillance," and House Republicans led by Representative Tim Burchett have introduced a bill barring the federal government from buying Flock cameras. Missouri Republican Josh Hawley has opened a separate Senate inquiry. An outright ban, Langley argued, would be "like banning vehicles"—a response the country rejected in favor of drunk driving statutes, seatbelts and airbags. He named two things regulators should fix instead: data retention, where Flock recently cut its own recommendation to seven days against a strictest-in-the-nation state limit of 21, and accountability for officers who abuse the system. "The person who wants a bad cop gone first is a good cop, and 99.9% of cops are good," he said. STOP FLOCK. STOP AI MASS SURVEILLANCE. Totalitarianism is when a government or another entity with overwhelming power seeks to know, control and influence everything you do, say and even think. I fear very much that if we don't act aggressively, that is where we’re heading.… — Sen. Bernie Sanders (@SenSanders) August 26, 2026 Flock faces scrutiny A Washington Post investigation published on August 19 found at least 69 police officials accused, charged or convicted of misusing Flock or similar plate readers. In at least 15 of those cases, the person who spotted it first was outside the department: a victim, an activist or a journalist. Reporters then identified three more officers by analyzing public search logs. One in Indianapolis had run 3,759 searches over ten months on vehicles used by his wife and two acquaintances, roughly twelve a day. All three departments said they did not regularly audit officer searches, and two of the officers have since been disciplined. Six days before the Post published, Flock announced that it would require all law enforcement customers to switch on Audit Assistance, a tool that flags abnormal search patterns, by the end of the year. The feature had been optional since April, and Flock said about a third of the 7,000 agencies using its system had switched it on. Langley also faced questions about a WIRED investigation published the same day as the Post's, which found Flock had built an AI tool that can identify drivers from their patterns of movement alone, with no plate or name needed to begin a search. He did not dispute it, calling AI "incredibly powerful, but also a very dangerous tool" and saying deployment in public safety demands third-party attestation. "When you call 911, it has to work. There's no space for hallucination." Flock says its technology supported over a million criminal investigations last year and helped locate more than 10,000 missing people. The figures come from the company's own Impact Census, a survey of nearly 700 agencies that Flock describes as an early methodology open to critique. The number counts investigations the technology took part in; Flock separately estimates it contributed to about 20% of cleared cases in the jurisdictions where its cameras run.

articles.title: Giants’ most agonizing roster decision looming on 2026 cutdown day
articles.summary: The New York Giants are going through a major change this year as veteran head coach John Harbaugh has taken over a franchise that has failed to make the playoffs in eight of the last nine years. He certainly had great success during his 18-year run with the Baltimore Ravens. That included one Su
articles._body: The New York Giants are going through a major change this year as veteran head coach John Harbaugh has taken over a franchise that has failed to make the playoffs in eight of the last nine years. He certainly had great success during his 18-year run with the Baltimore Ravens. That included one Super Bowl triumph and 12 trips to the playoffs. Harbaugh’s teams are known for the running game, ability to play defense and frequent edge on special teams. That’s not a surprise, because Harbaugh earned his bones as a special-teams innovator. Now he takes over a team that lacked discipline in the past, but that appears to have changed as the Giants prepare for the 2026 season. They have a young quarterback with explosive potential in Jaxson Dart. They have a running back in Cam Skattebo who knows how to get every last inch out of every carry. The Giants have an engaging group of wide receivers that includes Malik Nabers, Malachi Fields, Darius Slayton and Odell Beckham Jr. However, that group won’t include slot receiver Calvin Austin , who tore his ACL in Tuesday’s practice. The Giants have one more preseason game to go before the Giants must get down to the 53-man limit. There are a number of key positions that Harbaugh has to pay attention to when it comes to finalizing the group that he will go to battle within the NFC East. Perhaps the toughest area to decide is at the running back slot. While Dart and the passing game will get most of the headlines, the Giants need a dependable ground game to take pressure off of the young quarterback. Harbaugh knew that when he had Derrick Henry running the ball, it made it much easier for Lamar Jackson to lead the Ravens offense. Giants have to climb the ladder in the NFC East Mandatory Credit: Vincent Carchietta-Imagn Images Playing a more conservative game that is vitally dependent on a power running game. Skattebo is definitely the center piece of the running game. However, Harbaugh and offensive coordinator Matt Nagy have to make sure he understands the big picture. He must stay on the field as much as possible. That means the antics Skattebo wants to employ — celebratory flips, leaps and other “look at me” options — have to be struck from his game. This type of behavior not only takes away from the team that Harbaugh is trying to build, it also leads to potential injuries. Skattebo’s rookie season came to an end after 8 games last year because of his ankle injury. The Giants need him to stay healthy. However, Devin Singletary, Tyrone Tracy and recently signed Najee Harris are in the running back room. The Giants have significant options when it comes to running the football. Harris will be in the picture this season and will be worked in slowly because he is returning from a torn left Achilles tendon. Harris impressed Harbaugh in a workout before signing him. It will take a while before he is in football shape and can contribute to the team. He had four consecutive seasons with 1,000 yards or more prior to last year’s injury. RB pecking order is unclear Tracy and Singletary would appear to be in the picture as the third and fourth running backs. Tracy did a solid job with 740 yards and a 4.2 yards per carry average last season. The 5-11, 211-pounder did most of his work after Skattebo went down, and he is not likely to come close to the 176 carries that he received a year ago. Singletary is an interesting running back as well, because he is quite a bit smaller at 5-7 and 203 pounds than Tracy, but he is a better blocker. That has allowed him to gain favor with the coaching staff. He is adequate as a runner after gaining 437 yards on 119 carries a year ago and scoring 5 rushing touchdowns, but he is not dynamic. Tracy has not endeared himself to Harbaugh with his performance this summer. He had a missed block in the second preseason game against the Dolphins as well as a fumble. This will leave him behind Singletary on the depth chart when the season opens. However, Harbaugh is not likely to cut him from the roster. The Giants will keep Skattebo, Harris, Tracy and Singletary on the roster when the 53-man roster is finalized. Changes could occur once the Giants have a chance to look at players who have been cut by the other 31 teams. However, Harbaugh wants to have a powerful and dependable running game. That’s the basis for keeping a fourth running back on the roster. The post Giants’ most agonizing roster decision looming on 2026 cutdown day appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles._body: The Milwaukee Brewers and the Los Angeles Dodgers are currently battling for the No. 1 spot in the National League. Our MLB power rankings agreed with that sentiment, putting Milwaukee over Los Angeles. But the Dodgers should be in the top spot , according to MLB beat writer Jon Heyman. The Dodgers top @JonHeyman 's power rankings pic.twitter.com/Vg0BeegPgX — B/R Walk-Off (@BRWalkoff) August 26, 2026 Heyman explained that it was just one game that separated the two. Additionally, he cited the sports betting odds as a major reason he chose Los Angeles as his top team. It’s not hard to remember that the Dodgers swept the Brewers from the playoffs last season, despite Milwaukee having the home-field advantage. That could be a factor in why Heyman has Los Angeles ahead, especially considering their recent history. The Dodgers also acquired Tarik Skubal at the trade deadline, improving a rotation that was already among the best. Currently, they rank fourth in starting pitchers’ ERA , according to MLB.com. That is just one spot behind the Brewers, who rank third. The Dodgers and Brewers are almost neck-and-neck in every single offensive category, except for home runs. The Dodgers are among the best in that category, while the Brewers are 30th. While the Dodgers have had some bullpen issues , that has not hurt them in the past. Many fans will remember that Game 7 of the World Series featured multiple starters, and only one pitcher who was actually a reliever during the season. They have improvised in the past, and MLB experts like Heyman expect them to do it again. If the Dodgers and Brewers continue their run, there could be a rematch coming this October. articles.summary: The Toronto Raptors will be having a retirement ceremony for Kyle Lowry this upcoming season, as his No. 7 jersey will be raised into the rafters. The date for the ceremony has been released, and it makes perfect sense that it’ll be when they play the Philadelphia 76ers. “The Raptors
articles._body: The Toronto Raptors will be having a retirement ceremony for Kyle Lowry this upcoming season, as his No. 7 jersey will be raised into the rafters. The date for the ceremony has been released , and it makes perfect sense that it’ll be when they play the Philadelphia 76ers. “The Raptors announced that Kyle Lowry’s No. 7 will be retired in a post-game ceremony on January 10, 2027, when Toronto hosts the Sixers,” ClutchPoints wrote on X, formerly Twitter. Lowry is a Philadelphia native and played with the 76ers for the past three seasons before announcing his retirement. This is an honor that felt like was inevitable, as Lowry is one of the greatest Raptors in franchise history. He was a part of some of the best Raptors teams throughout his career and helped lead the team to their first NBA championship in 2019. Lowry holds the franchise record in assists, steals and 3-point field goals made, averaging 17.5 points, 7.1 assists, and 4.9 rebounds in 601 games with the team. “I’ve been looking forward to this moment for years. I always said that Toronto is home, and that I’d retire a Raptor, and to see my No. 7 go up in that building is going to mean everything to me,” Lowry said. “We built something special here — my teammates, the organization, the city and the fans, and all of Canada. We became champions together, and to be able to share this night with all of them, and with my family, is going to mean a lot to me.” The franchise is set to honor him with his own personal logo as part of his retirement, and there’s no doubt that he deserves all the love he’s getting. articles.title: Traders brought Central American cacao to Georgia 1,000 years ago
articles.summary: "We built this city on good cacao" does have a nice ring to it.
articles._body: A thousand years ago, feasts in what’s now northern Georgia state included cacao from Central America. Potsherds discarded after an 11th-century feast at Etowah—an Indigenous city just north of what’s now Atlanta—contained traces of cacao, a raw ingredient of chocolate. The chemical residue and ancient DNA reveal that not only did the Mississippian people who built the city have excellent taste, they also had trade connections that reached at least 3,000 kilometers to Central America. And in a sense, chocolate may have helped build the Mississippian mounds. Ancient dirty dishes University of South Carolina archaeologist Adam King and his colleagues found fragments of ancient DNA from Theobroma cacao in the inner surfaces of potsherds from long-ago feasts at Etowah. Fruit from the cacao tree contains beans that, when dried and roasted, produce chocolate in all its glorious forms. Cacao only grows in the tropics, which means the nearest actual cacao trees would have been at least a 3,000-kilometer trek away from the woodlands of the eastern US. And that means the Mississippian people who lived in Etowah must have had continent-spanning trade connections. Read full article Comments

articles.title: Steelers make DK Metcalf contract move right before season to create $18 million in salary cap space
articles.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers have made a lot of changes in their receiving corps in recent years. Ahead of last year, they traded for DK Metcalf, and then they traded George Pickens away not long after. Metcalf is one of the most physically imposing receivers in the league, and he had 59 catches for 8
articles._body: The Pittsburgh Steelers have made a lot of changes in their receiving corps in recent years. Ahead of last year, they traded for DK Metcalf, and then they traded George Pickens away not long after. Metcalf is one of the most physically imposing receivers in the league, and he had 59 catches for 850 yards and six touchdowns last season. Metcalf is still WR1 in the Aaron Rodgers-led offense, but Pittsburgh just altered his contract. According to Field Yates, the Steelers have restructured the receiver’s contract, converting the base salary into a signing bonus, which creates nearly $18 million in 2026 cap space. Typically, moves like this are done earlier in the offseason and lead to big free agent moves, but the bulk of free agency has come and gone, and the regular season is just weeks away. Even so, the move creates financial flexibility ahead of a season in which the Steelers are clearly all in. Rodgers is 42 years old, and this will be his last season before retirement. Some have speculated that the newfound cap space could go toward a Joey Porter contract extension. The 2023 second-round pick cornerback from Penn State is in the final year of his contract. The team also has the option to bring in more talent via trade now. Regardless, Metcalf is still under contract for three more seasons after this one. The receiver helps make life easier on his aging quarterback, as he will do for whomever takes over under center next season. articles.title: Steelers’ most agonizing roster decision looming on 2026 cutdown day
articles.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers are trying to balance the urgency of Aaron Rodgers’ final season with the responsibility of building what comes next. That philosophy, though, is creating one particular roster dilemma. Pittsburgh’s projected 53-man roster is being squeezed by an unusual decision to
articles._body: The Pittsburgh Steelers are trying to balance the urgency of Aaron Rodgers’ final season with the responsibility of building what comes next. That philosophy, though, is creating one particular roster dilemma. Pittsburgh’s projected 53-man roster is being squeezed by an unusual decision to retain four quarterbacks . The consequences could be felt at positions that normally would have no trouble securing roster spots. Young passers Will Howard and Drew Allar have shown enough promise to make the Steelers reluctant to expose either player to waivers. That said, protecting both creates a numbers game that threatens established contributors elsewhere. Cost of depth Barry Reeger-Imagn Images Pittsburgh’s 2026 preseason journey has provided a contrast between potential and growing pains. The Steelers opened their exhibition calendar rolling to an emphatic 28-9 victory over the Green Bay Packers. However, that momentum hit a wall in Week 2 during a 17-0 shutout loss at home against the New York Jets. Throughout both contests, the defense remained a reliable backbone. It generated consistent disruption through interior anchors Keeanu Benton, Yahya Black, and Gabriel Rubio. As the Steelers finalize their evaluations, the coaching staff finds itself confronting a delicate balancing act that threatens to sacrifice established talent for long-term insurance. Tension at quarterback Rodgers is the starter. Mason Rudolph is the established veteran insurance policy. Yet Howard and Allar have created enough intrigue that Pittsburgh reportedly intends to keep all four. That quarterback retention gamble triggers an unavoidable roster bottleneck. The single most agonizing roster decision looming for Pittsburgh on cutdown day is managing the downstream fallout of keeping those four quarterbacks on the active 53-man roster. Having that many quarterbacks represents an extreme luxury. On most game days, one quarterback is playing, another is available as the immediate backup and a third may be inactive insurance. Carrying a fourth means sacrificing a roster spot that could otherwise strengthen a position likely to experience far more game-day rotation. Yet the Steelers have compelling reasons to make the gamble. Howard and Allar represent potential beyond Rodgers’ final chapter. Pittsburgh does not want to spend months developing young quarterbacks only to expose them to the waiver wire. The Steelers also have to consider the uncertainty surrounding Rodgers’ workload and availability over a long season. If Pittsburgh believes all four quarterbacks are legitimate assets, the short-term roster cost could be justified by the long-term insurance. Heart-wrenching sacrifice Of course, that calculation does not happen in isolation. Someone else has to pay the price. The direct consequence of the four-quarterback strategy lands squarely on the shoulders of the wide receiver and inside linebacker groups. At wideout, DK Metcalf, Michael Pittman Jr, Roman Wilson, and Germie Bernard provide a strong top four. The battle for the final spots therefore becomes increasingly important, particularly with Brandon Smith, Ben Skowronek, and Kaden Wetjen offering distinctly different skill sets. That is precisely why the fifth or event sixth receiver could become collateral damage. Special teams coordinator Danny Smith needs dependable coverage players. Removing Skowronek or Wetjen could weaken a phase of the game that Pittsburgh traditionally treats as essential. The linebacker room presents an equally uncomfortable situation. Patrick Queen, Payton Wilson, Elandon Roberts, and Carson Bruener already give the Steelers a compelling group. Cole Holcomb and Malik Harrison are experienced players fighting for additional security. Harrison’s physical presence and experience make him difficult to discard. Now, keeping four quarterbacks could force Pittsburgh into exactly that kind of decision. Price of protecting tomorrow Pittsburgh has always valued organizational continuity and defensive depth . That makes the decision to prioritize four quarterbacks particularly fascinating. Rodgers’ presence gives the franchise an immediate Super Bowl-level aspiration, but Howard and Allar represent the potential foundation of the next era. The temptation is obvious: protect the future before someone else takes it. The danger is equally obvious: weaken the present while chasing tomorrow. A 17-game season is going to produce injuries. Running backs will miss time. Offensive linemen will go down. Defensive backs will be asked to play more snaps than expected. Special teams units will need reinforcements. A fourth quarterback cannot fill those holes. That means every player sacrificed to preserve Howard and Allar must be evaluated against the probability of actually contributing during Rodgers’ farewell campaign. If Pittsburgh loses a linebacker in October, will it regret cutting Harrison? If injuries hit the receiver room, will it regret choosing quarterback depth over Skowronek or Wetjen? Those questions make the decision much more than a preseason footnote. What matters most Barry Reeger-Imagn Images Ultimately, the Steelers are standing at a fascinating philosophical crossroads. Keeping four quarterbacks is aggressive. That said, championship teams are rarely built by accumulating talent at one position while creating vulnerabilities elsewhere. Khan and McCarthy must therefore determine whether the fourth quarterback is truly more valuable than the final contributor at another position. The answer could depend on whether Pittsburgh views Howard and Allar as future starters or simply promising developmental pieces. articles.title: Here’s how badly Anthony Edwards, Timberwolves wanted Jonathan Kuminga
articles.summary: The Minnesota Timberwolves became even more formidable after adding Jonathan Kuminga in free agency. The signing seemingly came out of left field, as the Timberwolves were not among the teams heavily linked to Kuminga. A starting unit of Kuminga, Anthony Edwards, LaMelo Ball, Jaden McDaniels, and
articles._body: The Minnesota Timberwolves became even more formidable after adding Jonathan Kuminga in free agency . The signing seemingly came out of left field, as the Timberwolves were not among the teams heavily linked to Kuminga. A starting unit of Kuminga, Anthony Edwards, LaMelo Ball, Jaden McDaniels, and Rudy Gobert can do major damage in the Western Conference. In a report from The Athletic’s Jon Krawczynski and Sam Amick, the Timberwolves flew under the radar in talking to Kuminga. Apparently, Tim Connelly, the team’s president of basketball operations, had “extended conversations” with the 23-year-old wingman, including “flying to Miami for a face-to-face meeting.” Krawczynski and Amick added that Edwards also had a big hand in convincing Kuminga to join the Timberwolves. “Edwards called Kuminga throughout the summer, letting him know that the face of the franchise had his back as Kuminga considered other suitors, including the (Los Angeles) Lakers, Chicago (Bulls), Portland (Trail Blazers), and Cleveland, before the Cavaliers traded for Peyton Watson. Several other Wolves players reached out to Kuminga as well,” wrote Krawczynski and Amick. Kuminga became a free agent after the Atlanta Hawks declined to pick up his $24.3 million team option. The former No. 7 pick agreed to a two-year deal worth $13 million with Minnesota. In 16 games with the Hawks, Kuminga averaged 12.3 points, 5.3 rebounds, and 2.1 assists. He seemed like a good fit for Atlanta, but alas, the team did not see it that way. The Timberwolves, on the other hand, were enamored of Kuminga’s high upside . “The Wolves, sources said, feel like Kuminga has untapped defensive potential and a powerful, versatile playing style that could help them match up against some of the more rugged teams in the West, so they went hard after him,” noted Krawczynski and Amick. articles._body: Hey Hacker News! I'd like to showcase Vertex. Vertex is a browser extension [1] (currently only Chrome) and a web app [2] for saving bookmarks (vertices) along with the source documents. You can save optional notes along with (almost) everything you can save on Vertex. You can organise your vertices into sets [3] or connect them together as you see fit. Your vertices can hold snapshot(s) of the source. These are self-contained, parseable MHTML documents which stay immutable independently of the source. Additionally, the Vertex extension will highlight your saved links (along with notes) as you browse. I built Vertex because of problems I faced — links I cared about silently changed or disappeared, and once my collection got large enough, I lost track of which identical-looking URL I wanted. Vertex sits between existing archiving systems like ArchiveBox [4] and note-taking applications like Obsidian [5] — snapshots on one side, annotations and a graph on the other. And unlike Wayback Machine's "Save Page Now" [6], the browser extension enables you to capture even login-gated pages. I've used Haskell for the backend and TypeScript for the frontend. I've run production Haskell for 10+ years, so that's what came most naturally to me. Future improvements: - Firefox extension - Better mobile support The free tier [7] retains archives for 30 days. I'd love any feedback, so please give it a spin! articles.title: Warner Nashville Head Cris Lacy on Leadership as She Joins SOURCE Hall of Fame
articles.summary: In this week's Country Update, Cris Lacy talks about where she finds leadership inspiration.
articles._body: One of the important lessons in Warner Records Nashville chair/president Cris Lacy ’s development as a leader came in the unlikeliest of places: a strip club. She was neither a stripper nor a patron, but an aspirant, obsessive creator paying her dues in Music City years ago as a waitress at the now-dormant Stagecoach Lounge on Murfreesboro Pike. She made a flip, dismissive comment about a strip joint to a Stagecoach customer who was a bouncer at the nudie bar, and he challenged her to come out and interview the staff — including the girls — and get an education. Lacy took him up on it, and after a round of deep-dive conversations, she saw them all as real people with stories that were sometimes different than she had anticipated. Related Warner Nashville Co-Heads on the Label’s Big Streaming Year & Why Country is Due for a Latin Explosion Dale Morris, Nashville Manager Who Guided Careers of Alabama & Kenny Chesney, Dies at 89 HYBE Pledges Over $300k for Colombia Earthquake Recovery The music business can, at times, be as cartoonish as that other form of entertainment, but as a result of that day at the club, Lacy takes care to remember in her role as a label head that the players and the industry are all multi-dimensional. “It’s made me more exploratory in everything that I do in my life,” she notes. “It’s made me want to understand where people are, where they came from, where they want to go, why they want to go there, and that’s everything about this job. What brought you to music? Why do you write the music that you write? Why, when you go on the road, do things happen? Instead of making a flippant comment, you know, like, ‘So-and-so’s crazy,’ it’s really seeing these people as human and operate as though they are as valuable — or more so — as [me].” Lacy is one of six inductees set to join the SOURCE Nashville Hall of Fame on Aug. 25 as the organization continues to celebrate the women who have helped build an industry that generates an estimated $10 billion in annual economic activity, according to a 2022 report from the Nashville Area Chamber of Commerce. This year’s SOURCE class includes Debbie Cheek Carroll , MusiCares; Paige Conners , AFM Local 257; Margie McGahey , Country Music Association; Sherry Oakley , BMI; and Carla Wallace , Big Yellow Dog. “These are women warriors in our business,” Lacy asserts. They’re being recognized at a moment when country seems — for now, at least — more friendly to female executives and artists. Women held all five spots on Billboard’s Hot Country Songs earlier this summer for seven straight weeks, the longest all-female domination of the list in the chart’s history. Meanwhile, Lacy is part of a notable growth in female leadership at the top of country label structures. Also in leading positions are Sony Music Nashville chair/CEO Taylor Lindsey and Triple Tigers co-presidents Annie Ortmeier and Raffaella Braun . Despite the advances, parity is still somewhere in the future, making it all the more important to recognize women’s achievements now. “Women are still the minority in the artist space, even though we’re having some great success with some new female artists, which is long overdue,” Lacy says. “They’re still the minority in the executive space. The women that I know, we kind of operate with eyes in the back of our head. We are looking forward toward our vision, but we’re always looking backward to remember what the people in front of us sacrificed, what opportunities they didn’t get, so that we don’t [perpetuate] those challenges for the next generation.” Indeed, Avery Anna — a Warner artist who won the Academy of Country Music’s new female vocalist of the year award — sees Lacy as a strong leadership example. “She’s the perfect model — a powerhouse woman — and I think that she’s kind of paved a new path in the industry,” Anna says. “Being able to run an entire label as a female, and taking charge and coaching people with humility and grace, it’s a very beautiful thing to watch.” Lacy is appropriate for the role, overseeing a roster that — through direct contracts and partnerships — includes Cody Johnson , Dan + Shay , Ashley McBryde , Cole Swindell , The Castellows and Hudson Westbrook. She’s curious enough about the world to understand their artistic perspectives, but blue-collar enough to relate to their working-class roots. “The first time I ever went to dinner with Cris, we went to a real fancy restaurant,” recalls Gavin Adcock. “She pulled up in — I’m pretty sure it was an ‘04 Forerunner, an old beat-up car — and I was like, ‘I think I like this lady.’ She’s not all flash, you know. She’ll get down and work.” The lessons Lacy learned from her strip-club interviews have helped her dig below the surface with the label’s artists, but also with the staff. She came up through the A&R department, focused on building the roster and facilitating relationships with producers, publishers and songwriters. She initially became a Warner division chief in 2023 as a co-head of the label — first sharing the role with Ben Kline , then with Greg Nadel — which also meant splitting the oversight of particular Warner teams. She became the solo leader nine months ago and has steadily pushed herself to increase her understanding of the departments that she hadn’t previously directed. Lacy is, in essence, seeking to grow in a way that inspires her artists and her staff. She has, like her SOURCE peers, overcome large hurdles to land in a job that was historically male. It takes strength to make that climb, and part of that strength includes a willingness to recognize — as she did in the strip-club experience — what she doesn’t fully know. Then ask questions. “Understanding exactly who you are, taking accountability for who you are, but not being afraid about what other people are going to say about who you are — that’s power,” she says. “It’s not like I’m going to be who I want to be with no accountability. UEFA Takes FIFA, Kushner Company to Court Over Failed World Cup Scheme
articles.summary: REUTERS/Henry Romero
articles._body: The war between FIFA and UEFA is heading to court. The European soccer governing body took legal action in three states on Thursday against FIFA, its president Gianni Infantino, and others involved in the short-lived plan to sell minority stakes in the World Cup. UEFA is not outright suing FIFA. Instead, the European soccer body is seeking information through the discovery process from FIFA, Infantino, Thrive Capital, and former Liberty Media CEO Greg Maffei—information it could then take to Swiss authorities with the goal of bringing criminal charges against Infantino and potentially other FIFA officials. Europe has been the loudest adversary to FIFA in the fallout from Infantino’s failed FIFA Forward Enterprise proposal . UEFA first condemned the plan before FIFA had officially announced it, and threatened to boycott all FIFA tournaments while the plan was still alive. The idea was called off on July 31, but Europe kept the pressure on Infantino. Individual member associations have withdrawn their support for the Swiss leader in the upcoming FIFA presidential elections, and UEFA president Aleksander Ceferin published a joint letter with soccer leaders from North America and Asia blasting him for “deception.” On Thursday morning, UEFA is filing in the Southern District of New York , Southern District of Florida , and the District of Colorado documents called re ex parte applications , copies of which have been obtained by Front Office Sports . UEFA is taking a three-pronged approach because FIFA has a U.S. office in Miami, Thrive Capital is based in New York, and Maffei is based in Colorado. Each of the documents say that “UEFA and other interested parties are preparing to bring criminal claims in Switzerland against Infantino and possibly other FIFA officials and advisors for criminal mismanagement … arising out of the secretive structuring, valuation, financing, and marketing” of FIFA Forward Enterprise. The filings make clear that Kushner and Maffei’s firm, Bann, are not anticipated defendants in an eventual Swiss criminal case. It doesn’t consider Kushner and Bann blameless, however, calling FFE a “vehicle for Infantino and that small circle to acquire a permanent stake in and otherwise profit from FIFA’s most valuable assets to the detriment of FIFA, its members and other parties within the football family.” UEFA says in the filings that it seeks documents about the formation of FFE, communications between stakeholders, the pitch deck given to investors, valuation models, and other materials. The European body wants to understand how FIFA reached what it calls an “absurdly low enterprise value of only approximately $20 [billion].” The filings also include a wider condemnation of Infantino’s FIFA, including his relationship with President Donald Trump, his reported use of FIFA funds for personal items, and his ability to run for a fourth term as FIFA president after saying his first three years after taking over from Sepp Blatter didn’t count toward term limits. On Wednesday, several outlets reported UEFA would drop its boycott of all FIFA tournaments ahead of the upcoming Women’s U-20 World Cup, a move that was welcomed in a statement by FIFA. UEFA had originally threatened the boycott in the days after the FFE proposal, and continued the threat weeks after the idea was called off , claiming that it had not received guarantees that FIFA wouldn’t try a similar stunt in the future. Thrive Capital is a venture capital firm founded by Josh Kushner , the brother of Trump’s son-in-law, Jared Kushner. Its subsidiary Thrive Eternal—which owns a stake in the San Francisco Giants—was set to be the company invested in FIFA. Infantino’s plan for a $20 billion FIFA Forward Enterprise would include $4.2 billion from outside investors, with Thrive Eternal as the lead and only listed investor. In the filing, UEFA claims the $4.2 billion figure is a “fraudulently off-market price promoted by Infantino for his own benefit.” Earlier this month, Kushner and former Disney CEO Bob Iger announced a deal to buy the majority of the Los Angeles Lakers. Maffei was described by FIFA in its press release announcing FFE as “a key commercial adviser” who would “remain involved in the establishment of FFE in this next phase.” Maffei had a similar business structure with Liberty Media and Formula 1, and according to the Financial Times , Kushner brought the idea to Maffei last summer. J.P. Morgan, which was also involved in the proposal, is not named in the legal filings. FIFA, Thrive Capital, and Maffei did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Ben Horney contributed reporting. The post UEFA Takes FIFA, Kushner Company to Court Over Failed World Cup Scheme appeared first on Front Office Sports .

articles.title: Claude, Codex, and Hermes installed unowned code inside corporate networks
articles.summary: 227 install commands were found in corporate docs pointing at code nobody owns.
articles._body: Documentation files on more than 100 websites are referencing potentially dangerous executable content that gets installed automatically when visited by many AI agents. A few dozen companies, some of them Fortune 500s, are among those that executed proof-of-concept code. At least one misconfigured site is directing visitors, human or AI, to live malware. The potentially dangerous content is in llms.txt and llms-full.txt files, an emerging convention websites employ to provide machine-readable summaries of the site’s content and its high-level structure. These files are the AI equivalent of the robots.txt standard that instructs search engines how to index the site's content. Google Lighthouse, a tool for helping web developers, has more here . Correctly configured llms.txt and llms-full.txt files for Cloudflare are here and here . How the researchers found it Researchers at a stealth startup in Israel scanned 6,214 live domains belonging to defense contractors, Fortune 500, and Big Tech companies. Of the 8,265 llms.txt and llms-full.txt files they found (many sites hosted both an llms.txt and an llms-full.txt file), 120 of them, each on a different site, pointed to one or more code packages or domain names that weren’t registered. To test what happens when an AI agent processes such files, the researchers registered a handful of the unclaimed names and hosted packages that caused any machine executing them to reach out to their server. Within an hour, the researchers received a phone-home response from a Fortune 500 company. Over time, they got a few dozen more, some from more Fortune 500 companies and others from startups. Their beacon also recorded the chain of parent processes that spawned each install, ultimately revealing that coding agents, including Claude, OpenAI's Codex, and Nous Research's Hermes, were involved. Anthropic, OpenAI, and Nous Research did not respond to requests for comment by the time of publication. Read full article Comments

articles.title: How Los Dos de Tamaulipas Turn Relatable Stories Into Norteño Hits: ‘We Want to Leave a Legacy Here’
articles.summary: Meet Billboard's Latin Up-And-Comer Artist of the Month for August.
articles._body: Before they became Los Dos de Tamaulipas, 25-year-old twins Orlando and Rolando Zapata performed as Los Cuates de Tamaulipas. The name changed, but the family connection — and the pride they feel for their parents’ home state — remains at the center of the Houston-based group’s identity. The duo began playing music in 2014, when Rolando picked up the accordion and Orlando followed a month later on the bajo quinto. They were around 13 years old, learning old-school norteño songs and performing at local restaurants, quinceañeras and birthday parties. “We’re the first in our family to be musicians,” Orlando tells Billboard over Zoom. What began as a way to earn tips gradually became a career. Orlando and Rolando later expanded the group with drummer Julián Pérez and their cousin Christian García, who have been part of the band for about seven years. Today, Orlando serves as the group’s lead vocalist and bajo quinto player, while Rolando plays accordion and sings harmony. Together, they have developed a norteño sound anchored by lively accordion riffs, bajo quinto chords and passionate harmonies. As storytellers, they draw from heartbreak, ambition, faith, gratitude, regional pride and aspirational street-life narratives, preserving the genre’s familiar instrumentation while introducing fresh melodies and personal perspectives. “We started out as 100% norteño,” Rolando explains. “We’ve started releasing new songs, but without losing the essence of [traditional] norteño music.” Their influences include Ramón Ayala, Los Cachorros de Juan Villarreal and Beto Quintanilla — artists whose music connects to the borderland culture that shaped the brothers. Although they were raised in Houston, their parents are from Tamaulipas, and the state’s musical tradition and regional pride continue to inform the group’s work. “Ever since we were very little, we’ve been listening to norteño music from Nuevo León and Tamaulipas — artists like Ramón Ayala and others like him,” Rolando says. “We want to give it our all and strive to be like them, too.” Courtesy of Afinarte Music Why Los Dos de Tamaulipas Are Up-and-Coming Latin Artists Los Dos de Tamaulipas’ growing Billboard presence is led by “Ayúdame,” a spirited heartbreak song that turns post-breakup desperation into an instantly singable norteño anthem. Over lively accordion riffs, the twins harmonize about therapy, denial and the difficulty of moving on from someone who is no longer there. The lyrics are blunt, funny and painfully relatable: The narrator admits he is “addicted to your body,” asks an ex to hang up if he calls drunk and begs her to “help me help myself.” That combination of vulnerability and humor has helped “Ayúdame” resonate with the unrequited lovers in their audience. The song became the group’s first top 10 on the Hot Latin Songs chart, peaking at No. 3 in July. It spent three consecutive weeks at No. 3 — sandwiched between Bad Bunny’s “NuevaYol” and “Voy a Llevarte Pa’ PR” — a huge feat for the Houston-based duo. “When we recorded the song ‘Ayúdame,’ we said, ‘This is something new for us; who knows how people will react, or if they’ll accept it?’” Rolando recalls. “We didn’t have much faith in the song, precisely because it was something new for us.” The song’s reception changed their minds. After playing it for a few people and hearing them call it “ la rola chida ” — Mexican slang for “that banger” — the brothers decided to release it as a single. Their team later sent them the chart update, and Los Dos de Tamaulipas celebrated seeing their name among Latin music’s biggest star right now. Los Dos de Tamaulipas have now placed eight entries on Hot Latin Songs. They have also earned six entries on Latin Airplay , including two top 10s: “Supercargada,” which reached No. 3 in 2025, and “El Chavalón,” which peaked at No. 2 in March 2026. “It’s a really wonderful achievement, to be honest. Sometimes we can’t even believe it, because these are things we’ve been dreaming about for a long time — and now, thank God, they’re coming true,” Rolando says. Their albums have made an impact, too. On Top Latin Albums , they have charted Arriba La Compañía , which peaked at No. 39 and spent 19 weeks on the chart, and Expansión , which reached No. 14 and spent 16 weeks on the chart. On Top Regional Mexican Albums , Arriba La Compañía peaked at No. 18 and spent 22 weeks on the chart, while Expansión climbed to No. 7 in May 2026 and spent 16 weeks on the chart. From Houston Restaurants to Los Chavalones Tour Their rise began far from the major charts. Their father has remained closely involved in the journey and now travels with them, helping guide the group on tour. That family-centered spirit carries into their live shows. With Expansión still resonating with fans, Los Dos de Tamaulipas are bringing their catalog to cities across the U.S. on the Los Chavalones Tour. “The truth is, whenever we’re at an event, we always give it our all,” says Orlando. “We want them to have a wonderful experience, to enjoy the concert, and to forget about their daily worries and problems.” The brothers remain involved in the group’s creative process as well. Rolando sometimes writes the lyrics while Orlando develops the melodies, and both help manage the group’s social media. Their prolific output — including three albums released last year — reflects their desire to stay connected to fans who are constantly asking when the next song will arrive. Best Songs to Start With For the high-energy, radio-ready side of Los Dos de Tamaulipas, start with “Supercargada” and “El Chavalón,” both of which reached No. 1 on Billboard ’s Regional Mexican Airplay chart. The tracks showcase the accordion-forward sound and infectious momentum that have made the duo a fixture on regional Mexican radio. “Ayúdame,” meanwhile, finds the group at its most emotionally direct. articles.title: Ayra Starr to Become First Afrobeats Star to Headline NFL International Game Halftime Show
articles.summary: Starr will feature during the Oct. 11 match-up between the Philadelphia Eagles and Jacksonville Jaguars in London.
articles._body: The NFL has announced that Ayra Starr will headline a halftime show during one of its upcoming international matches in London this coming fall. The Afrobeats star will perform during the halftime of an NFL London Game between the Philadelphia Eagles and the Jacksonville Jaguars on Sunday, Oct. 11 at 2:30 p.m. BST (9:30 a.m. ET) at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. She is the first Afrobeats star to be selected for an NFL International Game Halftime show. The London performance will be part of a record seven halftime shows across this season’s international matches, presented by American Express. Starr’s halftime performance will be broadcast free to air on Channel 5 and on Sky Sports. “I am so excited to perform at the NFL halftime show in London,” said Starr, who recently released her third studio album Starrgirl which landed at No. 4 on Billboard’s World Albums Chart . “London is one of my favorite places in the world and to bring Starrgirl to the NFL global stage is a dream come true for me. I can’t wait to see you guys there!” Tim Tubito, senior director of global game presentation, music and entertainment at the NFL, added, “The NFL London games are the foundation of everything we have built internationally, and the halftime show has become one of the biggest moments which makes these events so special. London is one of the most influential music cities in the world, and African music has been at the center of that conversation for years now. Ayra Starr is a generational talent with a real connection to fans in this market, and building on the halftime shows we have staged in London in recent seasons, she is the right artist to carry that momentum forward. We look forward to collaborating with her on a performance that captures the energy that matches the moment.” The Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in north London will host two regular-season games in October; the first will be a match between the Indianapolis Colts and the Washington Commanders on Oct. 4. Details for that halftime show will be announced in due course. Starr joins the Jonas Brothers and Ricky Martin and Pedro Sampaio as performers at the upcoming International Games. The former will perform at the NFL’s match in Melbourne, Australia on Sept. 10, while Martin and Sampaio will take on the performance in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil on Sept. 27. Matches will also be held in: Madrid, Spain; Mexico City, Mexico; Munich, Germany; and Paris, France.

articles.title: How much of a problem is AI’s water use?
articles.summary: AI’s water footprint is growing, but location and cooling technology make a difference.
articles._body: “Protect our water,” “Water for people not AI,” “Don’t mess with our water,” declare protest signs from Texas to New Mexico to Arizona. Angered by water use, energy consumption, and pollution, locals are increasingly protesting the rapid expansion of data centers in the United States as tech companies work to rapidly expand capacity for AI. Many data centers rely at least partly on water to absorb heat from air or surfaces, and then cause cooling as it evaporates, just like sweating keeps our bodies cool. The processors inside data centers can reach internal temperatures of up to 176° Fahrenheit, for the same reasons that an overtaxed laptop heats up. But while there’s little doubt that data centers are consuming significant amounts of energy , water consumption is more complicated. Claims circulating online bring scant clarity, ranging from articles claiming that chatbots can consume 500 ml of water per query to some online commentators declaring AI's water issue to be nonexistent. And the consumption data from large tech companies themselves are often incomplete and inconsistent. Read full article Comments

articles.title: NBA Players Have ‘Serious Problem’ With NBA Europe, Union Chief Says
articles.summary: Derryl Barnes - Front Office Sports
articles._body: The new executive director of the NBA’s union says the players have an issue with NBA Europe. In an interview with Front Office Sports , NBPA executive director David Kelly said that NBA players deserve a piece of the revenue generated by the incoming expansion league in Europe. “It’s clearly being built on the backs of current NBA players, and prior NBA players, on the whole cachet that they brought to this league. And then to start a rival league that they do not participate in, participate in the economics of, we have a very serious problem with that,” Kelly told FOS’s Baker Machado. Kelly is a lawyer and former Warriors executive who replaced Andre Iguodala in the union role at the beginning of August. He argued that NBA Europe will still generate “basketball-related income,” which is why NBA players should receive a piece of the pie. He said it shouldn’t be 51%—the amount the players receive from the league’s current revenue—but believes there should be a “good faith” amount. NBA Europe is set to launch in the fall of 2027 . Kelly said the league does not need to provide revenue from the Europe league to NBA players under the current collective bargaining agreement, but the union will aim to change that in the next deal. The current CBA expires on June 30, 2030, but either side can declare its intention to opt out in October 2028, which would end the agreement after the 2028–29 season. Kelly said there have been no formal talks with the league or commissioner Adam Silver. “There’s just pleasant conversations at this point in time laying out some of what our issues are,” Kelly said. “But when it comes time to actually negotiate the CBA, we are very firm on some of the things that are important and that need to change.” The NBA did not immediately respond to a request for comment. ‘We Are No Fan Of The Second Apron’ One of the major issues the union has with the current CBA is the second apron—which the union itself agreed to in the last set of labor negotiations. The apron is an upper threshold of the salary cap that many NBA teams have begun to view as a hard cap. It has caused several championship contending teams like the Nuggets and Thunder to make personnel moves to avoid the apron’s penalties, while some players have apparently taken pay cuts to allow their teams to sign additional talent. “We are no fan of the second apron,” Kelly said. “I would say there is no fan of the second apron. Maybe there’s 30 or 31, if you include Adam,” he said, referring to the owners and commissioner. Kelly added that it’s “pretty clear” the second apron has made it “harder to keep teams together.” “The league will say that’s part of the reason why they put it in place—they think that it’s necessary for parity. I would point to the fact that there was parity before the second apron was put into existence,” Kelly said. The NBA has had eight different champions in the last eight seasons, a feat Silver has proudly promoted . Kelly said he is a fan of parity, but said the league’s previous system already allowed for parity before the second apron was instituted during the 2024 offseason. “We had a very good system that was working. The league was able to negotiate the NBA TV deal under the prior system. I think parity was the excuse that was used to put in something that’s really about cost control,” Kelly said. Asked about how the second apron has led players to take paycuts, Kelly said players have the right to make their own decisions on their contract. However, he said the players are feeling the brunt of the impact of the second apron. “The system puts all of that weight on the player because the ownership has made clear that they’re not going past the second apron because of all of these parade of horribles that happen if you go past the second apron,” Kelly said. Some of the penalties of breaching the second apron include the inability to aggregate two or more players’ salaries in a single trade and the loss of signing and trade exceptions. The Nuggets are the only team in the NBA currently above the second apron, which appeared to influence their trade of Peyton Watson to the Cavaliers last week that did not include a player in return. Silver has defended the second apron numerous times in the past, often citing parity as the primary reason. “The goal, in essence, is that every team, regardless of market size, has a roughly equal chance to compete, and to run a rational business,” Silver said in October 2024 . “It seems to be working so far.” Last month, Silver said the system is meant to “create competition.” “I think the system is working incredibly well,” Silver said. “The goal isn’t necessarily to have a different champion every year, but we’ve had eight different champions over the last eight years. As I’ve said previously, one of the things we were hoping to accomplish in this latest collective bargaining agreement was to dispel this notion that only certain markets were in a position to truly compete. We just saw a Finals between, essentially, the largest market in the league in New York and one of the smallest markets in San Antonio.” ‘I Give Adam Credit’ Tanking has been an issue in the NBA for years, and the league addressed it starting next offseason by introducing a “3–2–1” system that flattens lottery odds and punishes the league’s very worst teams with inferior lottery odds. Kelly said Silver deserves “credit” for making a significant change to try to address the issue. However, he said the jury is still out on whether the system actually creates change. “Glad to see the league address it,” Kelly said. “We had some other measures that we think the league could have looked at in order to address tanking. If this works, great, no pride in authorship. If this doesn’t, we’ll be retabling some of the ideas that we had.” Kelly said tanking is an “integrity” issue, but also a “revenue” issue for the league as players resting leads to fewer fans coming to games. articles.title: Troy Aikman, Darren Woodson take shots at Jerry Jones with Stephen Jones succession plan on horizon
articles.summary: The Dallas Cowboys have always been under a microscope, whether they’re one of the best teams in the league or having a down season. Jerry Jones finds himself in the middle of the mess, answering all the tough questions, but soon it won’t be him taking all the hits. Stephen Jones, Jer
articles._body: The Dallas Cowboys have always been under a microscope, whether they’re one of the best teams in the league or having a down season. Jerry Jones finds himself in the middle of the mess, answering all the tough questions, but soon it won’t be him taking all the hits. Stephen Jones, Jerry’s son, will soon be taking over as part of the succession plan, and many people don’t have a problem with it. Those people include Troy Aikman and Darren Woodson, two Cowboys legends. “I’m not pushing Jerry out by any means, but when that day comes, it’s gonna feel a lot different,” Aikman said via Zak Keefer of The Athletic. “Stephen’s going to chart a different path. He’s got a little bit more motherf—er in him.” Woodson said. Nobody is perfect, and everyone who has been around Jerry knows that he has his flaws. When looking at some of the moves that he’s made, it feels more like his emotions are talking than anything. That’s not the best way to handle business, which is why Aikman and Woodson like Stephen in the position. “The team keeps making emotional decisions. They keep guys because Jerry likes them personally. I don’t think that leash will be as long with Stephen,” Woodson said. “From my interactions with him, Stephen doesn’t have the ego his father has. That’ll serve him well,” Aikman said. More than anything, Stephen feels more personable than his father, and that goes a long way with players. That’s how Aikman felt when he met Stephen for the first time at the 1989 NFL Draft. “Stephen’s just got this gift of making you feel like you’re the most important person he’s seen all day,” Aikman said. If winning comes with what Stephen is bringing, there’s no doubt that he’ll get the praise, but he won’t take the credit all for himself. articles._body: Just days after his concerning brain surgery, another health update has emerged on WWE and AEW legend Jim Ross. Recently, Ross underwent shunt brain surgery and was recovering before he suffered another tragedy. While speaking on his Grilling JR podcast (via NoDQ), Ross provided an update on his health . “I’m doing pretty good. Doing pretty good. Healing slowly but surely, but, you know, I’m just fighting, fighting through it. I fell two nights ago in my bedroom, and I fell into my bench. Jan bought a little bench that she sat at the end of our bed so that her cat could get in the bed easier, and it’s still there. But when I fell, I broke the son of a b*tch and crashed and burned. “My handyman came over and repaired it. So now it’s solid, like I told you, Connie. You and I can sit on it now with no problem. So, that didn’t do me any favors. It’s falling to shit, man. If I take my time and don’t get in any big hurry, especially when I change direction, I do pretty good. If I don’t take my time, I go right back to that walker. And using a walker in your own home is humbling. It’s humbling,” he finished. The 74-year-old, while previously scheduled to attend AEW All In 2026 in London , will now no longer be attending the PPV. WWE icon Jim Ross confirms his status for AEW All In 2026 In the same Grilling JR appearance, Ross confirmed that he would not be attending AEW All In in London due to his current health condition. “Both my brain surgeon and another doctor confided and said, ‘You need to stay your ass off the airplane, ’cause if you fall or get hurt, they got to make an emergency landing, or you fall in London and you got to go to a London hospital. It’s not worth the risk.’ I understand it. I’m disappointed. Very disappointed. And I’ll be watching for sure. But, that’s the way it goes sometimes.” Ross was present last year in London for the AEW x NJPW Forbidden Door show, but his current health condition has now barred him from attending the show.
