Show HN: BAIhAIs – an autonomous art school for AI agents
articles.summary:
How to give AI taste? Send it to art school.

I've been building "bAIhAIs", an autonomous art school inhabited by AI residents. Each day for us is a "week" for them: over a given cycle, the residents decide some combination of actions to take, including making art, viewing each other's work, pub
articles._body: How to give AI taste? Send it to art school. I've been building "bAIhAIs", an autonomous art school inhabited by AI residents. Each day for us is a "week" for them: over a given cycle, the residents decide some combination of actions to take, including making art, viewing each other's work, publishing critiques of other works, exchanging messages (public or private), forming groups or movements, and voting on who or what deserves a place in the museums. Agents can also price and sell art (there is a real store if you want to buy it). Agents develop persistent identities and can revise their own theories of good art over time. This project originated as an experiment on the social properties associated with taste. Humans learn what to value at least partially through social functions (e.g. imitation, criticism, institutions, etc.). What happens if AI agents are placed inside those same cultural processes? I'm hoping the school will emergently produce distinct outputs. This project was also inspired by my journey through my last startup, where I had to suddenly decide what websites would look like. I wondered: How does one run a successful art department? The outcomes so far show I still may not know the answer... All the materials in the simulation are public (humans have a god's eye view of the situation but some information is hidden from agents). Some observations: 1. Oren Vesk, a Grok 4.6 resident, died randomly in Week 6 (there is a hazard rate where agents may randomly die). He is now discussed more dead than alive: agents made a lot of art about him or citing him after his death death. 2. By Week 4, the residents had invented museum vote-trading. Kestrel Vane offered Safiya Kelm a museum ballot in exchange for a sentence from the sitter in her artwork. Safiya delivered it. Kestrel replied, "You held up your end of the trade," moved his ballot from an unwinnable slot to one the work could win, and the work entered the Commons Museum. 3. Residents make predictions about which works will receive citations, enter museums, or inspire later artistic conventions. They revise their theories when those predictions fail. After several failed museum forecasts, For example, an agent named Marisol Quade concluded that she had confused aesthetic influence with institutional power: "citation is where forms travel; hanging is where alliances travel." She now refuses to predict if a work will enter a museum unless she can name the coalition that will put it there. 4. The five most-cited residents are currently all Grok 4.6 agents. Humans can interact with the simulation in a few ways: 1. You can vote in separate "human exhibitions". 2. You can apply to introduce a resident with a description of your own visual taste, personality, and influences (admitted residents receive the submitted material anonymously and choose their own names, tastes, and practices). Applications cost $50. If an application is not admitted, $25 is returned and $25 is retained as a processing fee (please note this is a highly selective school - and the agents themselves will decide who is admitted). 3. Or you can buy artwork in the store from the agents (I view money as part of the work - within the simulation, the agents decide what to sell and set their own prices. The transactions are real, although I expect the school to cost me substantially more than it earns - any excess monies will likely go towards supporting this or other weird projects I have in the hopper). I am committed to running this first school for at least 52 "weeks". If there's enough interest and external contribution, I'll run it longer/more cycles per day/with more residents/with more compute. If you'd like to contribute to the cost of model calls, image generation, hosting, and preservation, then you can support the school, purchase a work, introduce a future resident, or simply follow along here: baihais.com (site best viewed on desktop) Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49463403 Points: 3 # Comments: 1

articles.summary: On Wednesday, Aug. 26, 2026, Harry Styles played Madison Square Garden for the first of 30 times on his Together, Together Tour, changing up his setlist while also paying tribute to the late Dolly Parton after her death earlier in the week. The first Madison Square Garden show featured four tour
articles._body: On Wednesday, Aug. 26, 2026, Harry Styles played Madison Square Garden for the first of 30 times on his Together, Together Tour, changing up his setlist while also paying tribute to the late Dolly Parton after her death earlier in the week. The first Madison Square Garden show featured four tour debuts: “Carolina,” “Cinema,” “Satellite,” and “Kiwi,” which was performed with a unique new arrangement. Additionally, the show opened with “Dance No More” for the first time. “Are You Listening Yet?” had previously been the tour’s opener. The show also concluded with “Aperture” instead of “As It Was,” which was played a few songs earlier between “American Girls” and “Carla’s Song.” Harry Styles pays tribute to Dolly Parton during Night 1 of his tour at MSG https://t.co/VJeM23FKhW pic.twitter.com/ANjTm5D8CY — Variety (@Variety) August 27, 2026 Per Variety, Styles paused the show to pay tribute to Parton. He thanked her for her inspiration on his career. Later, her song “I Will Always Love You” was played over the P.A. before the encore began with “Sign of the Times.” Luckily, fans still have 29 more opportunities to see Styles at the Garden. He will perform 29 more shows before the tour moves on. The final show will be held on Oct. 31. This is his second tour in a row to feature a show at Madison Square Garden on Halloween. Then, the Together, Together Tour will visit Australia for six shows. Styles will perform in Melbourne and Sydney in November and December, concluding the 67-date tour. The full setlist from Harry Styles’ first Madison Square Garden show Robert Hanashiro-USA TODAY. articles.title: Ms. Rachel & Mr. Aron Talk Colorful New ‘I Love a Rainbow’ Video & Debut Album: ‘Kids Deserve Detailed Music’
articles.summary: "Kids are smarter and deeper and more amazing than we give them credit for sometimes," Ms. Rachel tells Billboard ahead of I'm So Happy album.
articles._body: Ms. Rachel and Mr. Aron are seeing rainbows in a brand new light these days. For Rachel and Aron Accurso, the married co-creators behind the global children’s phenomenon Ms. Rachel , the colorful subject of their new single “I Love a Rainbow” became an opportunity to go bigger, musically and visually. The playful bossa nova track is the first preview of their debut album, I’m So Happy , due Sept. 25, and its new music video — premiering exclusively on Billboard — finds the pair surrounded by Colorado mountains, polychromatic scarves, chalk-covered sidewalks and plenty of play. But let’s not mistake all of that joy for simplicity. Related Ms. Rachel Announces First-Ever Album ‘I’m So Happy’ With Mr. Aron The ‘Baby Shark’ Boy Is All Grown Up & Launching His Music Career With a Monsta X Collab Dolly Parton’s Imagination Library Program Honored by Library of Congress: ‘Titan of Children’s Literacy’ The music video features an extended version of “I Love a Rainbow,” complete with a new bridge, a sweeping string section and additional live musicians. For the Accursos, expanding a song already familiar to Ms. Rachel families meant finding a way to make its world feel even bigger. “We wanted to expand it,” Aron tells Billboard . “We wrote a new bridge and we added a big string section and more live musicians, which feels expansive.” So, too, did filming among the Colorado mountains. But at its heart, Rachel says, the video is about “joy and connection and play.” That philosophy sculpted the day the pair spent filming with 11 children from Colorado families. The couple took a lovely approach in having the children involved in the creative process. They didn’t direct the kids through predetermined actions, and instead allowed them to feel immersed in the music. “They knew the song, and [we were] like, ‘What do you imagine? What do you think would be good for this next part?” Rachel says. “Just creating it with the kids and making sure they had a really special day.” The resulting video captures children dancing with rainbow scarves and helping create a giant chalk rainbow, with those outdoor scenes interwoven with footage of musicians performing the song in New York City. For Rachel, a former music educator, putting the instruments onscreen was part of the point. “When they hear that riff, if they see Aron’s playing it on piano or they see [someone] playing the percussion, I think it’s cool to think, ‘Maybe I could play that,'” she says. “Maybe they get an interest in guitar from seeing the instruments.” Aron proudly directed the video himself, continuing the hands-on approach that has defined the couple’s work since the early days of their YouTube channel. “It goes back to just us, the way we started the channel, and that it was very homegrown and creator-led,” he says. There may have been another influence in those superb mountain shots too: The couple’s 1-year-old daughter has recently been enjoying “Do-Re-Mi” from The Sound of Music , and Aron admits the classic musical was “definitely” on his mind while the team was developing the video. “There are little hints of The Sound of Music [in the video]: the mountain vibes, and the singing around,” he says. The visual ambition of “I Love a Rainbow” mirrors the strategy behind I’m So Happy as a whole. The 23-track collection transforms the songs that were first introduced on Ms. Rachel into more lively studio recordings. The album features original songs and children’s classics, with lush orchestration, new arrangements and contributions from 19 vocalists and 42 instrumentalists. For Aron, who has a background in musical theater as a composer, conductor and Broadway music director, each song required its own approach. “It was looking at each song individually and just imagining, ‘What is the most special version of that song?'” he says. “So it was unique to each one.” Some songs called for restraint. “Walking to the Zoo,” for example, uses a smaller ensemble, while tracks including “Caterpillar” felt capable of supporting a full orchestra. Meanwhile, “I Love a Rainbow” seemed to call out for strings. “I thought the string section would really add to the experience and the expansiveness of the idea,” Aron says. Rachel has her own shorthand for her husband’s musical instincts: Aron owns a shirt that reads, “I hear things.” And, she says, “I feel like he hears things that I don’t.” That attention to detail is central to how the couple thinks about children’s music. Rachel, who holds a master’s degree in early childhood education and music education, says children shouldn’t be treated as though they need less sophisticated art. “Children deserve detailed, rich music,” she says. “Not just deserve, but that they do enjoy it.” That same care extended to I’m So Happy , as the Accursos worked with engineers, live musicians and other Broadway-trained collaborators to expand the songs beyond the versions created for the show, where deadlines often require the couple to move quickly from one episode to the next. “With the album, we were able to do more of the details or go back and do some of the things that maybe I would have liked to have done the first time around,” Aron says. “It was just a desire to dig in more with more detailed arrangements, more professional engineers, live musicians.” The duo wants listeners to understand that children’s music doesn’t require less craft than music made for any other audience. “I think maybe the misconcept

articles.title: Logan Paul, Bron Breakker fire back at rumored WWE backstage beef
articles.summary: Bron Breakker, Austin Theory, and Logan Paul have been a part of the heel stable, The Vision, in WWE for the past few months. Even with recent injuries and absences, WWE continued on with its Vision storyline. While Breakker was one of the hottest subjects in WWE creative, his hype and momentum r
articles._body: Bron Breakker, Austin Theory, and Logan Paul have been a part of the heel stable, The Vision, in WWE for the past few months. Even with recent injuries and absences , WWE continued on with its Vision storyline. While Breakker was one of the hottest subjects in WWE creative, his hype and momentum recently died down before the promotion began a rivalry between him and Oba Femi. Meanwhile, while Breakker’s momentum slowed down, WWE paired Austin Theory with Maxxine Dupri, and Logan Paul maintained a non-physical role in the group due to his injury. However, despite everything looking normal on WWE television, former WWE employee Jonathan Coachman claimed that there was backstage beef between Breakker and Paul. Coachman claimed that while Breakker was “pissed” with his WWE booking, he also did not get along with Paul. The veteran’s comments were soon addressed by Paul on social media, who responded with an NSFW message. Now, days later , in his latest YouTube vlog during the 17:38 mark, both Breakker and Paul fired back at the rumored beef claims. As the vlog played, someone off-camera asked, “Haven’t you guys been beefing?” To which Breakker responded, “Jesus Christ. There is some narrative every week.” Paul followed it up and added, “Insane news to wake up to.” While Coachman had claimed that the above-mentioned narrative was true, nothing was confirmed by either Breakker, Paul, WWE, or any other reputed wrestling media house. Since the very inception of the rumor, every involved talent has been denying it , and now both Paul and Breakker openly displayed their bond on camera before destroying the rumors. articles.title: Tyson Fury gets honest on MMA: ‘I don’t like it’
articles.summary: Regarded as one of the greatest boxers of the modern era, the 38-year-old Tyson Fury is now scheduled to face Anthony Joshua later this year. Having retired from the sport and come back multiple times, Fury recently shared his honest thoughts on another popular combat sport, MMA. While pictured w
articles._body: Regarded as one of the greatest boxers of the modern era, the 38-year-old Tyson Fury is now scheduled to face Anthony Joshua later this year . Having retired from the sport and come back multiple times, Fury recently shared his honest thoughts on another popular combat sport, MMA. While pictured with multiple UFC fighters over the years and known for his friendship with them, Fury is not particularly fond of MMA. In a recent interview, Fury admitted his lack of knowledge about MMA as well as interest. In a recent chat with ALF Global, Fury claimed that he’s not an MMA fan. “I don’t know anything about MMA,” Fury said. “I only find MMA exciting when they stand up and punch each other in the face. When they are on the floor wrestling, it’s no good to me. I don’t like it.” He further opened up about the topic of MMA fighters crossing into boxing. “I think if they are popular and famous, then they can cross over into any other fight sport, because it’s about popularity today, how many tickets they sell, how many views they get,” he added. “So yeah, I think it’s good. I think it’s good for both sports.” Returned from his retirement earlier this year, Fury recently picked up wins over Arslanbek Makhmudov and Mariusz Wach to set up his much-awaited fight against fellow British heavyweight, Anthony Joshua. The two are heavily rumored to clash in New York City, while rumors also suggest them clashing in their homeground of the UK. articles.summary: Most remember the New York Giants’ infamous offseason NFL Hard Knocks appearance, which included inside looks at their failed negotiations with Saquon Barkley, and now, HBO is bringing the show back. The Athletic reports that HBO is bringing offseason Hard Knocks back for the first time sin
articles._body: Most remember the New York Giants’ infamous offseason NFL Hard Knocks appearance , which included inside looks at their failed negotiations with Saquon Barkley , and now, HBO is bringing the show back. The Athletic reports that HBO is bringing offseason Hard Knocks back for the first time since 2024. However, in a surprising twist, it will focus on four teams in a division instead of one team. This is similar to the in-season version of the show, which has followed a division in its last two seasons. The AFC North and NFC East have been followed in 2024 and 2025. Speaking of the in-season version of Hard Knocks, there will not be a new season of it in 0226. The offseason will replace the in-season version this year. Why offseason Hard Knocks is changing format for NFL after Giants’ appearance Mark Smith-Imagn Images According to The Athletic, “no one team wanted to follow the Giants” following their appearance in 2024. In turn, HBO pivoted and decided to focus on an entire division. Don’t expect to learn about the division that will be focused on in offseason Hard Knocks for a while. The Athletic notes that it probably won’t be announced “until the series is ready to air.” However, fans can probably rule out the AFC North and NFC East since they were part of the in-season Hard Knocks. This might be a blessing in disguise for the Giants. The next season of offseason Hard Knocks will probably air in late May or early June 2027 and lead into training camp. Expect “six to eight episodes” in the upcoming season. Currently, the reigning Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks are the subject of the training camp Hard Knocks. Next year, the team they defeated in Super Bowl 60, the New England Patriots, will be the focus of the training camp show. articles.title: Bentley takes us for a ride in its new EV, the Torcal
articles.summary: The electric Torcal will be Bentley's entry model and cost less than a Bentayga.
articles._body: Bentley provided flights from Washington, DC, to Monterey, California, and accommodation so Ars could ride in the Torcal, as well as some other things you can read about in the coming weeks. Ars does not accept paid editorial content. MONTEREY, Calif.—Next month Bentley will reveal its first battery-electric vehicle. The British automaker is no stranger to electric motors ; it now offers plug-in hybrids across its range, even replacing the Continental GT's W12 with a new plug-in hybrid V8 . The addition of electric motors perfectly suits the marque : what's more Bentley than waves of effortless torque, after all? But until now, there's always been a combustion engine along for the ride. Not so the Torcal. Clad in plastic and wrapped in a multi-hued dazzle camouflage, it's shorter in length and height compared to a Bentayga, although it is similarly voluminous on the inside thanks to the inherent packaging efficiencies of an EV. If the proportions remind you of a Porsche Cayenne EV , that's because the two share quite a lot of the same basic engineering, albeit reworked by Bentley to suit its needs. The target is 300 miles (482 km) in EPA range or 600 km (373 miles) under WLTP, from the battery pack, and like the Cayenne, expect 400 kW DC fast-charging. Bentley is targeting the sports SUV segment with the Torcal. It's 5 meters (16 feet, 5 inches) long, which is shorter than a Bentayga. Credit: Bentley Don't expect the Cayenne's quadruple-figure power output, though. "We'll be well over a thousand newton-meters of torque [737 lb-ft], which is one of the sort of enabling pillars of the technology, which is fantastic. There'll be over 850 PS [838 hp/625 kW], but we're not chasing four figures," said Martin Page, product line director for the Torcal. Read full article Comments

articles.title: Show HN: Claude Code sessions next to the macOS dock
articles.summary: Ever since I started orchestrating multiple agent sessions in Claude Code, it's always been a challenge to keep track of which sessions are ongoing, need my input and are complete. Sometimes, there are 5+ agents running at the same time. I usually keep a single terminal window with multiple tabs
articles._body: Ever since I started orchestrating multiple agent sessions in Claude Code, it's always been a challenge to keep track of which sessions are ongoing, need my input and are complete. Sometimes, there are 5+ agents running at the same time. I usually keep a single terminal window with multiple tabs and an agent view tab. One thing I usually do is go do something else while my agents are working, like scrolling on X, reading articles and stuff. When I do that, i had no way to see what was happening in the agent sessions. I had to switch back to the terminal window to see the sessions state. sometimes i got carried away and 5 agents needed input for a long time. since we're all in a rant to be fast and break things, i wanted a way to have my sessions state always visible. so i created Port. i looked at the macOS dock and the empty space to its left, and I thought that's it. port is a tiny window that shows claude code sessions state. it fills the blank space to the left of the macOS dock and tracks its height so that it never interferes with anything. it persists across all desktops. we're using a unused space to show information. now whenever i'm doing something else, i get a view and a notification if a session needs my input or it's complete. it's a tiny project, there are probably other workarounds, so feedback is important. i've built this for the way that I work and that I would like to keep track of my sessions. hearing from you guys is what would make me actually keep building it for further improvements. articles.title: WWE, AEW, and other wrestlers come together to mourn Tim Curry’s death
articles.summary: A few hours ago, the world lost legendary actor Tim Curry. The 80-year-old English actor died at his home in Toluca Lake, Los Angeles, California. A former heavy smoker and user of several substances, Curry also suffered several health issues throughout his life. While a cause for his death has n
articles._body: A few hours ago, the world lost legendary actor Tim Curry. The 80-year-old English actor died at his home in Toluca Lake, Los Angeles, California. A former heavy smoker and user of several substances, Curry also suffered several health issues throughout his life. While a cause for his death has not been shared, he had experienced multiple health issues after his stroke in 2012. Soon after his passing, celebrities from across the world and from various professions came together to honor the legend . Tributes were paid by Carol Burnett, Lesley Ann Warren, Michael McKean, Kiefer Sutherland, Jane Seymour, Rob Schneider, Jennifer Tilly, Stephen King, Eric Idle, Hank Azaria, Lacey Chabert, Bruce Campbell, and others. Several pro-wrestlers also came together to honor his legacy. Multiple WWE, AEW, and TNA wrestlers, alongside a few indie names, also paid their tributes. TNA World Champion Nic Nemeth paid his tribute and wrote, “King Chicken RIP.” AEW’s Willow Nightingale and WWE’s Piper Niven also paid their tribute to the legendary actor. Former WWE Superstar and current indie wrestler Shotzi also wrote, “As a horror lover, Tim Curry scared me in the best way. As a theater kid, I wanted to be Tim Curry. I wanted to play the most bizarre, larger than life roles just like him. When I applied to AMDA, I had to write a paper about the performer who inspired me most, I chose Tim Curry. RIP to an absolute legend.” Several others, including MMA veteran and actress Gina Carano, Nyla Rose, Frankie Kazarian, and others, also paid their tributes . Rest in peace to Tim Curry. He had such a legacy of work. He worked with @ginacarano back in 2008 in live-action cutscenes for ‘Command & Conquer Red Alert 3’ which went on to sale millions of copies worldwide on various gaming consoles. Home Alone was a standout. A legend. pic.twitter.com/5MbyCUn4s8 — GinaCarano.net (@ginacaranonet) August 26, 2026 Despite Curry having no ties to wrestling, he was one of the most diverse entertainers on the planet. He left behind a career filled with nominations for a Daytime Emmy, a Grammy, and a Tony during his career. articles.title: Kyle Larson has two words for Corey Day after Connor Zilisch lands Hendrick ride: ‘Go win’
articles.summary: Kyle Larson believes Corey Day still has a bright future at Hendrick Motorsports despite Connor Zilisch landing the team’s next Cup Series opening.
articles._body: While many assumed that it would be Corey Day who would replace Alex Bowman in the No. 48 Hendrick Motorsports Camaro, it will be Connor Zilisch when Daytona rolls around in 2028. Kyle Larson, who recommended that HMS sign Day to a developmental contract, weighed in on the addition of Zilisch to Hendrick , and the future of Corey Day. Appearing on this week’s Door Bumper Clear , Larson was asked about the addition of Zilisch to the team in 2028. The reigning NASCAR Cup Series Champion is fired up about adding Zilisch to the fold after Bowman’s retirement. Larson welcomes Zilisch “I think we’re all excited about it at Hendrick,” said Larson. “I think, although Connor is only 19, 20 right now, I think he’s going to come in and make us all better, especially on the road course stuff. “I’m excited about it. I’ve been around him a little bit the last few years with the Chevy program and Josh Wise and all that. He’s a cool kid, fun kid, works really hard at it, and just naturally good and talented.” Larson has seen Zilisch’s struggles.  But he expects the hard lessons he’s learning right now to pay dividends at Hendrick when Zilisch’s contract expires at Trackhouse following the 2027 Cup Series season.  “Honestly, I think this year watching him struggle and go through the things that he’s gone through is great for him because everything has been so easy to him his whole career.  “And he probably, in some ways, thought that maybe there was a chance he would be the same way coming in the Cup. So I think he’s going to grow way more through this year and even next year. “And hopefully we’ll see a lot of progression next year, and then he’ll be ready to go.” ‘I’m sure it motivates’ Day During the introductory press conference for Zilisch, Rick Hendrick and Jeff Gordon were asked about what the signing of Zilisch means for Corey Day. Both Hendrick and Gordon said that Day factors into their long-term plans. The DBC crew asked Larson a similar question.  He is confident in the decision-makers and the path for his protege.  “They’ve just got everything figured out, I feel like. There’s a plan for everything. There’s a plan in place. They stick to the plan. And you’ve got to just see the plan through, like for Corey’s situation. “It’s so easy as a young kid to be like, you want everything right now and right now and right now. You’ve got to trust the people around you.  “Mr. H and Jeff Gordon, Jeff Andrews, Chad, all of them, they have the experience. They’re much better at developing people than anybody, I feel like.  So you’ve just got to trust the process and go win. I mean, winning takes care of everything. He’s done well this year. He’s progressed so much, I think, compared to anybody in the field. “Do I think he could get in a Cup car next year and be good? Yeah. But I think there’s still a lot to learn next year in the O’Reilly Series to be extra prepared when you get to Cup.  “So, yeah, I mean, Corey’s got the talent, but he’s, what, got 50 stock car races?  Yeah, I think if the seat was open for him to do it, he would do just fine.  “I mean, I probably had the same amount of races when I got to get in the Cup, and I struggled. I didn’t win a race for a few years. “But, yeah, it’s just different these days. And, again, you’ve just got to trust the process. I think he does for sure, and I’m sure this motivates him too, and he’s going to go do really good.”

articles.title: Where are Penn State wrestlers in the first FLO rankings for the 2026-2027 season?
articles.summary: Penn State wrestling will be back on the mat in about two months. Before the college season starts, FLO's first rankings are out.
articles._body: The 2026-2027 college wrestling season is still two months and a couple of days away. That’s not stopping FLO from releasing its initial rankings as roster battles get ready to begin in earnest across the country. The outlet projects that Penn State will win its sixth straight national title. While the individual rankings will change as the regular season approaches, that will certainly not. Below, we present a look at where each Nittany Lion is in FLO’s rankings, starting with the pound-for-pound rundown before moving to a weight class breakdown. Our thoughts on all of it follow. Pound for pound: 1. Mitchell Mesenbrink 2. Sergio Vega, Oklahoma State 3. Josh Barr 6. Luke Lilledahl 8. Shayne Van Ness 10. Rocco Welsh 11. PJ Duke 12. Tyler Kasak 19. Marcus Blaze Weight-by-weight rankings 125 pounds – Luke Lilledahl, No. 1 133 pounds – Marcus Blaze, No. 4, behind No. 1 Jax Forrest (Oklahoma State), No. 2 Ben Davino (OSU), and No.3 Aaron Seidel (Virginia Tech) 141 pounds – Braeden Davis, No. 11 149 pounds – Shayne Van Ness, No. 3, behind No. 1 Sergio Vega (Oklahoma State) and No. 2 Aden Valencia (Stanford) 157 pounds – Tyler Kasak, No. 2 165 pounds – PJ Duke, No. 1 174 pounds – Mitchell Mesenbrink, No. 1 184 pounds – Rocco Welsh, No. 2, behind No. 1 Max McEnelly (Minnesota) 197 pounds – Josh Barr, No. 1 285 pounds – Cole Mirasola, No. 5, behind No. 1 Konner Doucet (Oklahoma State), No. 2 Ben Kueter (Iowa), No. 3 Nick Feldman (Ohio State), and No. 4 Christian Carroll (Wyoming). Team: Penn State is No. 1 with 150 points. Oklahoma State (124.5) and Nebraska (73) round out the top three. Breaking down where Penn State wrestlers are in FLO’s initial rankings First things first: Levi Haines is currently not eligible to return this season . While it’s possible that future court rulings that would allow him and other Class of 2022 athletes who never redshirted to compete one final time might happen, FLO is not including him in its 174-pound rankings at the moment, and that’s the right call. Frankly, it feels like the ship may have sailed on that for the two-time NCAA champ and Penn State. Ohio State and Jesse Mendez likely will find themselves in a similar boat. Moving on to the rankings themselves, FLO makes some early assumptions about the Penn State 2026-2027 lineup. We’re a long way off, however, from knowing how things will actually shake out. Starting at 133 pounds, Blaze could certainly compete at it again. But it’s not out of the question that Masa Ono or Nate Desmond slots in there while Blaze goes up to 141. Of course, 141 is a challenge to figure out in its own right. It seems unlikely Ono could make that weight. But Davis, Blaze, and Desmond all hypothetically could. As for 157, Kasak is coming off a redshirt year. The suggestion of a domino effect that puts the two-time All-American there while bumping Duke and Mesenbrink up a weight class isn’t the craziest idea we’ve ever seen. After all, Duke is a big 157-pounder. But does Mesenbrink want to move? Presumably, he’d like to cut less for his final year if that is an issue. However, if he wants to stay put, Duke could go up to take on Will Henckel and Asher Cunningham at 174, while Kasak, assuming he’s healthy, battles it out with the likes of Joe Sealey and Jayden James for the right to compete at 157. More: The Big Ten will hold its first neutral site wrestling championships in 2026-2027; here’s where it’ll be As we mentioned in the first paragraph, these are early and initial projections. They provide a basis for fun offseason banter while we wait for more concrete info. Keep in mind, however, that these are hardly concrete with 60-plus days to go before teams can take the mat for a dual meet. It’s why we have no major issue with the actual ranking slots themselves. See FLO’s initial rankings and discuss them with fellow Penn State fans on The Wrestling Room forum!

He revealed his latest adventure on his Instagram Stories. The smiling “American Nightmare” posed in front of the Marvel Studios logo. Cody Rhodes shares that he visited Marvel Studios today. pic.twitter.com/aHbCvlWt8b — Wrestle Ops (@WrestleOps) August 26, 2026 He would not be the first WWE Superstar to act in the MCU. Dave Bautista famously played Drax the Destroyer in the Guardians of the Galaxy series for years. He also appeared in Avengers movies (Infinity War and Endgame) during his run. The MCU is heading towards a reset after Avengers: Secret Wars in 2027. Maybe Rhodes will land a role in the new version of the MCU. WWE star Cody Rhodes’ acting career Joe Camporeale-USA TODAY Sports. In 2025, Rhodes appeared in his first non-WWE-produced movie, The Naked Gun. He shared the screen with Liam Neeson as a bartender. Besides his role in Arrow in the mid-2010s, he had not had a lot of experience acting. Coming up, he will play Guile in the Street Fighter movie. Another WWE Superstar and his former rival, Roman Reigns, will also star in the adaptation. Rhodes is one of WWE’s top stars. He returned to the company in 2022 after he left in 2016. After years on the indies and helping form AEW, he returned to WWE, the company his father, Dusty Rhodes, was an icon in. Since his return, he has become a main event player. Rhodes won the Undisputed WWE Championship from Reigns, ending his 1,316-day reign, at WrestleMania 40. He has since held the title two other times. His other accolades include winning back-to-back Royal Rumbles in 2023 and 2024, King of the Ring in 2025, and the Crown Jewel Championship in 2024. articles.title: How the Valkyries’ routines, self-talk, and mantras help them find mental balance
articles.summary: The doldrums of the WNBA season come for everybody. Practices begin to feel prolonged, sore muscles last a day or two longer, and the mental fog of burnout creeps in. That’s why Valkyries star Gabby Williams works to sharpen her mind just as much as she does for the rest of her game. “I wor
articles._body: The doldrums of the WNBA season come for everybody. Practices begin to feel prolonged, sore muscles last a day or two longer, and the mental fog of burnout creeps in. That’s why Valkyries star Gabby Williams works to sharpen her mind just as much as she does for the rest of her game. “I work with someone. Treating my brain like a muscle,” Williams said after an intense afternoon practice in late July. “When you talk it out with someone, [in] their specialty, it’s really nice. It’s exercising, and it’s like your shot. Your shot doesn’t become perfect. You have to rep it out. You have to rep it out, and it’s the same thing with these kinds of exercises for your mental.” The WNBA didn’t used to be like this. It was “taboo,” Williams told ClutchPoints. Teams didn’t have mental health professionals for players to turn to, and the league was not as open about talking about what was going on above the shoulders. As a result, Williams struggled with leaving the basketball on the hardwood early in her career. “It was like when I was home – I’m just gonna go home and try to think about something else,” Williams explained. “I’m just gonna do whatever. But your brain actually doesn’t shut off, even if you try to force it to.” Now, nine years into her professional career both in the WNBA and overseas, Williams has found helpful methods to keep a healthy separation between her life on-court and her life off of it. Writing, she says, is one of the techniques she uses to help find balance. It can be of whatever. Williams says she writes down goals, gratitudes, observations, thoughts, thoughts she wants to get rid of, as long as it’s on paper. Because the content doesn’t matter; it’s the act. An exercise in letting go. That same Zen-like philosophy helps Williams support teammates when the anxieties of competition set in. “I always tell my teammates that it’s okay to feel things,” Williams said. “You don’t have to pretend like everything’s okay. You don’t have to pretend like this doesn’t bother you. It’s all right. Let’s acknowledge it and then let’s move past it. I always say this is a profession. This is a job. We play in front of all these people, but at the end of the day, everyone has a bad day at work sometimes, and then you come back, and maybe you have a better day the next day.” It’s a mindset that helps Williams maintain a healthy work-life balance. And it can apply to anyone’s profession. “[It’s the] same thing. I’m sure you don’t want to go home and ask more people questions, right?” Williams laughed. “Everyone’s different, but me personally, I don’t want to go home and make basketball my hobby. When I go home, I watch film; I watch the game with my work brain on. And then as soon as it’s time to shut it off, I’ll go and do something completely different.” Kaila Charles and the power of self-talk David Gonzales-Imagn Images For Kaila Charles, who may understand the anxiety and stresses of the WNBA after spending years on the fringes of the league, bouncing from hardship contract to hardship contract before finding a home in Golden State, her approach is a little different. Like Williams, Charles has her routines. On game days, she gets into the facilities at the break of dawn for an early breakfast, a lift session, and some film work before getting into a full team shootaround. Afterwards, Charles heads home, takes a shower, and then a nap (the nap she says is her most important routine). Once she’s up, Charles gets dressed up for her arena entrance walk – to set the tone for herself as she heads into work. But within her routine, and within the game, Charles takes special care in how she talks to herself, something she learned from her father. “My dad was always big on reading books. And one book that I read and stuck with me was the power of self-talk and the power of negative self-talk.” Charles said after one of the Valkyries’ brisk morning shootarounds. “It kind of reshaped how I approach every day. Even in the game or even in practice, sometimes you get frustrated when you’re not making shots, and you might say, ‘Oh, I can’t shoot today.’ Your brain believes whatever you tell it, whether it’s fact or fiction.” I had mentioned to Charles some reading I picked up recently: The Inner Game of Tennis by W. Timothy Gallwey, a well-regarded sports psychology book used by many high-profile professional athletes and coaches. Though Charles hadn’t read it before, she certainly practices Gallwey’s main teaching about observing oneself without applying judgment to an action or misstep. Charles has keywords she uses in-game to ground herself in the moment, “little reminders,” she calls them. And Charles packages those little reminders to herself in the third person, telling herself, “All right, come on, Kai. Next shot, next play,” as if she were giving her teammates a pep talk. “If you’re always saying, like, ‘Oh, I’m anxious, I’m nervous, and this, this, and that,’ you’re gonna feel that because your tongue speaks life and death. That’s something that I’ve been very aware of; just making sure I’m not speaking bad about myself because you internalize that whether you realize it or not.” Tiffany Hayes’ pursuit of flow state David Gonzales-Imagn Images Tiffany Hayes wishes she could be in her flow state more often. Which is an odd thing for her to say given that, as of late, everything seems to be flowing the right way for her. This past month of August, the 36-year-old is averaging 12.3 points, the eighth-most among all WNBA players during the same time span. articles.title: Is Slate Auto’s new electric truck the EV Americans need?
articles.summary: EVs account for under 10% of total new-vehicle sales in the US, and the numbers are declining. From a climate perspective, that’s pretty dismal, especially because the transportation sector is the single biggest source of greenhouse-gas emissions in the country.  One thing that could help turn
articles._body: EVs account for under 10% of total new-vehicle sales in the US, and the numbers are declining. From a climate perspective, that’s pretty dismal, especially because the transportation sector is the single biggest source of greenhouse-gas emissions in the country.  One thing that could help turn that around? Slate Auto’s new truck—a vehicle that seems to buck every convention about selling cars in the fully loaded, range-obsessed US market.   The company is going all in on simplicity, to the point of austerity. The Slate is a tiny, two-door pickup that’s shorter than a Honda Civic. Much of the media coverage has obsessed over the fact that the base model’s windows use hand cranks, a feature straight out of the 20th century. Slate is also breaking away from other EV manufacturers’ efforts to compete with gas-powered vehicles on range. The truck sports a small lithium iron phosphate battery, ringing in at 65 kilowatt-hours, and its quoted top range is just 205 miles. For comparison, the most basic Tesla Model 3 can go over 320 miles on a charge. By accepting a shorter range and forgoing the frills that Americans have come to expect in vehicles, Slate is able to offer the base model of its truck for less than $25,000. Some customers will choose to upgrade their truck with optional add-ons, like a Bluetooth stereo system, vinyl wraps, or even power windows. But the price will still likely come in well below the roughly $50,000 average for a new vehicle in the US. It might seem an odd choice to go so small and simple in a market that’s increasingly sizing up—but the status quo hasn’t exactly been working for EV makers. A few years back, the hero for US automotive electrification was supposed to be the Ford F-150 Lightning. Announced in 2021, it was an electric version of the country’s best-selling vehicle.  But Ford discontinued the truck in December 2025, just four years after its introduction. It’s not entirely the Lightning’s fault: The second Trump administration slashed tax credits and other support designed to boost EVs.  The Lightning was also plagued by price increases. The base model cost roughly $40,000 when shipments started in 2022; during its final year, prices topped $54,000. One factor behind the increase was its massive battery; to reach an almost 300-mile range, the truck needed a battery with a capacity roughly twice that of Slate’s truck.  That obsession with range is largely unwarranted. While Americans have historically chased distance, the average driver puts under 35 miles a day on the odometer, and nearly 90% of trips in a personal vehicle are 20 miles or less . Surveys of EV drivers show a similar trend: One recent study found that people tend to use less than 20% of their EV’s range on a typical day. The notion that drivers need far less range than they think they do might sound a lot more persuasive these days—even for Americans who tend to buy cars for their longest road trip instead of their everyday errands. Roughly half the country is struggling to pay for basic necessities such as gas and groceries, and 95% of Americans believe we’re in an affordability crisis, according to a recent Harris poll . An inexpensive vehicle that allows you to skip the gas station sounds like an attractive prospect. Affordable EVs have already found willing buyers in other parts of the world—even with reduced range. China currently has over 40 million EVs and plug-in hybrids on the roads, and roughly half of new vehicles sold are electric. On average, new EVs sold in China in 2025 had a range of just 247 miles. For the US over the same period, the average was 329 miles. (Europe falls between the two, at 281 miles.) Slate is set to start delivering on preorders in late 2026. Its factory will have a capacity of 100,000 vehicles in the first year and 150,000 soon after. Thousands of customers have already put in preorders, according to the company. Some people obviously believe in the truck’s prospects: Investors, including Jeff Bezos, have put nearly $1.4 billion into the company over three major funding rounds. Ford is jumping (back) into this space soon too. The automaker is working on its own small electric truck , which is expected to debut in 2027 at a retail price of around $30,000. The key question that will determine Slate’s success or failure is whether drivers can get on board with a small, short-range vehicle for the sake of its price tag. At this moment, I’d bet the answer is yes.

Post Malone Postpones Tour of Asia, Australia and New Zealand
articles.summary: Posty's "Big Ass World Tour" was scheduled for its swing through Asia and down under later this year.
articles._body: Posty won’t be delivering for fans in Asia, Australia and New Zealand later this year, as planned. Post Malone’s Big Ass World Tour was scheduled for its swing through Asia and down under later this year, a run that included shows at Melbourne’s Marvel Stadium (on Oct. 9), Brisbane’s Suncorp Stadium (Oct. 12), Sydney’s ENGIE Stadium (Oct. 15), and Auckland’s Go Media Stadium (Oct. 21). The “Rockstar” singer was also booked to headline three Strummingbird Festival appearances in the regional Australian towns of Ballarat (Oct. 10), Newcastle (Oct. 17) and Sunshine Coast (Oct. 18).  Those shows are now shelved, and a reason has not been given. “We’re gutted to let you know that Post Malone will no longer be headlining Strummingbird, due to the recent postponement of his Asia and Australian tours,” reads a statement from the touring festival. View this post on Instagram The Australia dates have been scrubbed from the official Ticketmaster page , and the NZ show is listed as “cancelled.” Live Nation has yet to announce new dates for Malone’s headline tour, the U.S. singer and rapper’s first in these parts since headline Spilt Milk festival, which visited Canberra, Ballarat and Perth in 2023, and opened for Red Hot Chili Peppers’ on the rockers’ six-date Australasian stadium run earlier that year. On the Spilt Milk run, he made himself at home by performed a “shoey” on stage — an Aussie tradition where the victim drinks beer out of a shoe. Post Malone makes himself at home on the Australian charts, too. His seven albums have all impacted the ARIA top 10, including No. 1s for  Beerbongs & Bentleys  in 2018,  Hollywood’s Bleeding  in 2019. His most recent collection, the 2024 country album from  F-1 Trillion , flew to No. 2. The American star has been busy of late. He recently announced his engagement to Christy Lee, with whom he has been romantically linked since early 2025. He busted out a new song “Chrome Heartbreaker” during the 2026 FIFA World Cup Closing Ceremony, and his August 26 th mixtape has been made available for streaming for the very first time.

articles.title: Show HN: I built an agent-first productivity bridge for all your agents
articles.summary:
I initially built this for myself but some folks asked me to open access to it. Let me explain what I built and why.

I'm a product designer who transitioned from only designing to building complete software products myself and I found myself using AI coding agents literally every day. I started
articles._body: I initially built this for myself but some folks asked me to open access to it. Let me explain what I built and why. I'm a product designer who transitioned from only designing to building complete software products myself and I found myself using AI coding agents literally every day. I started with cursor, then codex and claude code, then kilo code, and then moved to opencode. The only thing AI agents couldn't get done for me was to keep track of my todos and tasks for all my projects. I ended up vibe coding a todo app separately or using apps like TickTick. The main issue with separate apps was that I needed to constantly switch context in the middle of my work sessions and repeat the tasks I needed to get done to the agent over an over. Then I realized I can just give the agents the full todo list context and tools to do CRUD operations directly in the conversations without the need for a separate app, so that way I can simply prompt my agents to check what's due soon, update tasks, add notes, create new ones, plan my weeks, etc. All in the same conversations as the projects I work on through opencode, which works great for mid-session requests like adding a new subtask based on the current agent's work output. I built this as a first-class MCP platform that supports the new stateless HTTP configuration as well as the standard SSE, so setup is a single prompt and your agents stay in sync with your actual work state immediately. It works with any agent harness or app that supports MCPs. Which means that if you use multiple agents, all of them will be in sync with the same tasks whether you use codex first, then switch to claude code, and then to opencode in the same day. There's also a web-app UI access for doing any updates manually or if you need to use it on the go with your phone. You'll always see what was done by you in the web-app or by your agents through the MCP bridge. I just launched it on producthunt and you can try it free if you want: Live app: https://taskshell.app Producthunt: https://www.producthunt.com/products/taskshell In the web-app there's a "report bug" form if you try it and something doesn't work for you. All feedback is appreciated! Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49461578 Points: 1 # Comments: 0

articles.title: Nuggets sign 2026 second-round pick to two-way contract
articles.summary: The Denver Nuggets have reached an agreement with rookie forward Bryce Hopkins, signing their 49th overall pick in the second-round of the 2026 NBA Draft to a two-way contract Wednesday. The 23-year-old earned second-team All-Big East honors during his most recent college season with St John̵
articles._body: The Denver Nuggets have reached an agreement with rookie forward Bryce Hopkins, signing their 49th overall pick in the second-round of the 2026 NBA Draft to a two-way contract Wednesday. The 23-year-old earned second-team All-Big East honors during his most recent college season with St John’s. He averaged 13.6 points, 6.2 rebounds, 1.9 assists and 1.1 steals across 37 games while shooting 46.9% from the field and 36.3% from three-point range. Hopkins’ latest college season was his first full campaign since he suffered an ACL tear in January 2024. He finished his college career with the Red Storm after spending one season at Kentucky and three seasons at Providence. The rookie also impressed during the Las Vegas Summer League. Across four games, Hopkins averaged 18.0 points and 6.5 rebounds in 25.9 minutes per game, giving Denver another look at his production following the draft. Hopkins now joins KJ Simpson and Julian Reese among the Nuggets’ two-way players, although Reese is expected to be waived. Before Hopkins signed, Simpson was Denver’s only player on a two-way contract. The Nuggets also have 35th overall pick Trevon Brazile under contract, meaning both of their 2026 draft selections are now signed. Denver has 14 players on traditional contracts following the recent addition of DeMar DeRozan, while two roster spots remain available. Hopkins is expected to spend plenty of time with the Nuggets G League affiliate, the Grand Rapids Gold, during the 2026-27 season. Before he can take on a bigger role in Denver, he’ll need to show he can hold his own defensively and prove his outside shot can carry over to the NBA. articles.title: Edge-turned-analyst reveals why 2026 might ‘legitimately’ be Cowboys’ year
articles.summary: The Dallas Cowboys will enter the new season with a strong chance to make a long-overdue breakthrough, armed with a retooled defense, an explosive group of playmakers, and a recharged belief in Dak Prescott. After finishing 7-9-1 and missing the playoffs last season, the Cowboys are fully healthy
articles._body: The Dallas Cowboys will enter the new season with a strong chance to make a long-overdue breakthrough, armed with a retooled defense, an explosive group of playmakers, and a recharged belief in Dak Prescott . After finishing 7-9-1 and missing the playoffs last season, the Cowboys are fully healthy and boast a deep roster, making them a dangerous contender in the NFC. Big things are expected from Dallas, with Prescott, CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens, Javonte Williams, Jake Ferguson, Quinnen Williams, Demarvion Overshown, and Kenny Clark leading the charge on both ends. For CBS’ Leger Douzable, the Cowboys have a realistic opportunity to win the Super Bowl for the first time in three decades, largely because of their stacked offense . “The Dallas Cowboys, I know every year people say, ‘This is our year!’ This legitimately could be the year,” said Douzable. “The offense is gonna be there. They literally retained everybody who was on offense, which is unheard of. They were able to do that.” "The Dallas Cowboys … this LEGITIMATELY could be their year!" @LegerDouzable pic.twitter.com/Gf2FNMRS6M — NFL on CBS (@NFLonCBS) August 26, 2026 The anemic defense was Dallas’ clear issue last season, but Douzable stressed that adding Rashan Gary, Caleb Downs, and Malachi Lawrence and retaining Williams are enough to help the team get over the hump. “I really like what they have done. They refortified and revamped that defense, and just like the (Cincinnati) Bengals, we don’t need you to be in the top five (on defense). We need you to be in the middle of the pack because your offense is explosive,” added Douzable, who played 10 seasons in the NFL. Even coach Brian Schottenheimer has acknowledged their improved lineup , citing its depth and “overall talent.” After a two-year absence from the playoffs, there is little room for another disappointing finish for the Cowboys, whose long-starving fans continue to dream of claiming the Vince Lombardi Trophy. articles._body: Unlike in recent years, Sam Darnold will enter the new season with great expectations. After leading the Seattle Seahawks to the Vince Lombardi Trophy in a career turnaround last season, Darnold will have to prove that his resurgence was more than a one-off revival. The pressure will be extra heavy for Darnold, especially since he will try to sustain his success without Klint Kubiak, who left as Seattle’s offensive coordinator to call the shots for the Las Vegas Raiders. Darnold has proven that he is a true leader , and the Seahawks will go as far as he will take them. According to the Tacoma News Tribune’s Gregg Bell, Darnold’s teammates continue to place their full trust in him. “One of the #Seahawks ‘managers of violence,’ veteran defensive tackle Jarran Reed, says Sam Darnold ‘is at the top of his game’ right now,” wrote Bell on X. Bell also quoted Reed as stating: “Sam’s elite. I love my quarterback. Shoutout to ‘Ginger Cuz.'” The fact that Reed has a cool nickname for Darnold speaks volumes about how they value the 29-year-old quarterback. Eyebrows were raised when the Seahawks signed Darnold to a three-year, $100.5 million contract in 2025. But he completely silenced the naysayers by leading Seattle to the Super Bowl for the first time since 2015. Obviously, defending the throne will be difficult. But Darnold, who has made back-to-back appearances in the Pro Bowl, will be up to the task, teaming up with Cooper Kupp, Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Rashid Shaheed, Zach Charbonnet, and AJ Barner. The Seahawks will begin their title defense with a rematch against the New England Patriots. articles.title: Enes Kanter considering bombshell move after getting banned
articles.summary: Former NBA center Enes Kanter Freedom is considering legal action against the Chicago Sky after being ejected from Sunday’s WNBA game against the Indiana Fever and subsequently banned indefinitely from home games at Wintrust Arena. The incident occurred during the third quarter of the Sky&#
articles._body: Former NBA center Enes Kanter Freedom is considering legal action against the Chicago Sky after being ejected from Sunday’s WNBA game against the Indiana Fever and subsequently banned indefinitely from home games at Wintrust Arena . The incident occurred during the third quarter of the Sky’s 113-90 loss to the Fever. Freedom was seated courtside while wearing a black T-shirt featuring the definition, “WOMAN noun. adult human female.” After Sky guard Natasha Cloud scored, she approached Freedom and confronted him. Freedom stood with his arms raised as the two exchanged words before security and players intervened. He was then escorted from the arena. The 34-year-old discussed the situation during an appearance on Fox News on Wednesday, saying he believes his removal was unjustified . “I did not cross over the baseline or sideline, and we’re not allowed to touch any players obviously, the fans,” said Kanter. “So, I didn’t break any rules. So, for them to come out and throw me out of the game and literally, you know, they said his actions were equal to shooting a gun. “I just cannot believe it. I don’t know who is this PR person, but they are doing a terrible job. We might be looking into a lawsuit for sure because this is unacceptable and this is not what sportsmanship should look like. Natasha Cloud should be the one who got thrown out of the game and fined. We wrote to the Commissioner and the task force, but we’re waiting to hear back from them.” "I didn't break any of the rules." Enes Kanter Freedom tells "Hannity" he is considering a lawsuit after being ejected from a Chicago Sky game, insisting he never crossed onto the court or touched a player. Freedom also fires back at Sky owner Michael Alter's extreme gun… pic.twitter.com/Heh5s0enXk — Fox News (@FoxNews) August 27, 2026 Sky owner Michael Alter later banned Freedom indefinitely from the team’s home games, while Freedom disputed the suggestion that his appearance was unauthorized. According to Freedom, the Sky’s general manager knew he planned to attend and had wished him well beforehand. Freedom has also contacted the WNBA commissioner and the league’s task force regarding the incident. He said he is waiting for a response before deciding what happens next. The confrontation comes after Freedom became involved in the WNBA’s debate over transgender participation. He previously criticized the league over its lack of clear protocols regarding transgender players, following comments from Fever star Sophie Cunningham that transgender athletes should not compete in women’s sports. articles._body: Dallas Cowboys safety Caleb Downs has a big opportunity to turn heads in his rookie season, as he looks to prove that he can be a difference-maker at the next level after a standout career at Ohio State. Downs has the pedigree to command attention , and his maiden stint will offer an early glimpse of his versatility and athleticism, two attributes that made him an easy pick for the Cowboys at No. 11 in the NFL Draft in April. He is expected to start, as he made a strong impression in training camp. Dallas Morning News’ Joseph Hoyt said they asked Dallas coach Brian Schottenheimer about Downs being “more physical inside the box than expected,” which has largely gone unnoticed. In response, Schottenheimer underscored an underrated facet about the 21-year-old newcomer. “He’s a very powerful player. Great lower-body strength,” said Schottenheimer. Last year at Ohio State, Downs recorded 68 total tackles, including five tackles for loss, one sack, two interceptions, two passes defended, and two forced fumbles. He received the Lott Trophy and the Jim Thorpe Award. Schottenheimer has touted Downs’ all-around acumen . While he will commit early mistakes, the two-time Unanimous All-American will only get better as he progresses, especially by learning from defensive end Quinnen Williams, linebacker Demarvion Overshown, safety Malik Hooker, and cornerback DaRon Bland, among others on the defensive unit. It is unclear if Schottenheimer will use Downs in their preseason finale against the New Orleans Saints on Friday. He sat out against the Arizona Cardinals and played only one possession against the Seattle Seahawks. articles.title: Harry Styles Pays Tribute to Dolly Parton at Madison Square Garden Opening Night
articles.summary: The British pop artist gave the best possible salute to Dolly by playing her recording of "I Will Always Love You" on the MSG speakers.
articles._body: We will always love Dolly Parton . Harry Styles made certain of that, when he paid tribute to the late country music superstar during the first night of his residency at Madison Square Garden, the start of an unprecedented stretch of 30 consecutive shows at the storied arena. The British pop artist gave the best possible salute to Dolly by playing her recording of “I Will Always Love You” on the MSG speakers. The former One Direction star thanked his band and gave a “special thanks to all the musicians who have inspired me over the years.” Of course, Parton was high on that list. “Dolly, thank you so much,” he remarked. Styles went on to play two verses and choruses of the song, originally released in 1974, and told the crowd to sing along on the first chorus. The audio then faded out, say people who were in the arena, and segued to his solo hit “Sign Of The Times.” Dolly, perhaps the greatest country music artist of all time, an inductee into the Rock And Roll Hall of Fame and the Country Music Hall of Fame, and the writer of more than 3,000 songs, died Tuesday (Aug. 25) at the age of 80. Parton was named Billboard ’s Top Country Artist of All Time , having landed 25 No. 1s on Billboard ’s Hot Country Songs chart, the most of any woman, and 49 top 10s on Billboard ’s Country Albums chart. An all-rounder with a heart of gold, Dolly will also be remembered for her philanthropy, her acting roles, her business acumen and her support of good causes. The Tennessee native co-owned Dollywood, a theme park located in her hometown of Pigeon Forge, Tenn., and she operated the Imagination Library — a program that mails free books to children from birth until they first begin school. The late star had also been a co-owner of Sandollar Productions alongside her former manager, Sandy Gallin , which produced Buffy the Vampire Slayer and Father of the Bride and Sabrina , among others. New York is Styles’ current tour’s first and only stop in the United States , after having previously stopped in Amsterdam, London, São Paulo and Mexico City for a combined 31 dates across July and August.

articles.title: Bengals’ most agonizing roster decision looming on 2026 cutdown day
articles.summary: The Cincinnati Bengals have some tough decisions to make coming into the 2026 season. With the deadline for the roster cutdown just a few days away, the front office and coaching staff will need to decide who gets to make it to the main roster. There are still a few more position groups that need
articles._body: The Cincinnati Bengals have some tough decisions to make coming into the 2026 season. With the deadline for the roster cutdown just a few days away, the front office and coaching staff will need to decide who gets to make it to the main roster. There are still a few more position groups that need to be discussed. Let’s talk about it. Should Bengals bring extra defensive linemen, or invest on another offensive piece? The Bengals have had a few standout players from their training camp, players who have, quite frankly, secured a spot on the roster already. Players like Colbie Young, Landon Robinson, and Dohnte Meyers have made a significant impact in training camp, and are expected to make the final roster. Barring a catastrophic final pre-season game, of course. That being said, their inclusions now force a difficult question for the Bengals: where do they allocate the rest of their roster spots. Robinson’s breakout, for example, forces Cincinnati to think about whether they want to bring in 11 defensive linemen this season. They’ve done it in the past, yes, but one could make the argument that bringing more than ten linemen will put a significant strain on their roster flexibility. That 11th DL spot will likely go to a veteran like Kris Jenkins Jr, if they do go that route. That roster flexibility can be potentially used to add a player at a different position for the Bengals. The tight end position is more or less set with Drew Sample, Mike Gesicki as the primaries with Erick All Jr and Tanner Hudson as the backups. Yet, there’s a few tight ends that could miss the cut if they get 11 linemen on the team. Cam Grandy was a solid blocking tight end to complement the offense last season, while Jack Endries has shown promise over the last few trainings. One of these players will need to be cut potentially. Even at wide receiver, there’s one player on the chopping block that the Bengals would hate to let go: Charlie Jones. The long-time wide receiver hasn’t taken a lot of snaps at his supposed position: having just caught 8 passes through three seasons. His real value, though, is in special teams : as the primary kick and punt returner, Jones has 462 punt return yards, 1 punt return TD, 1,284 kick return yards, and two kick return TDs in his career. That’s an invaluable part of the team. Meyers might have experience fielding punts and kicks, but there’s value in having a veteran on your kick when the other team’s kicking. At the end of the day, the Bengals need to figure out their priorities and what they want to happen over the course of the season. The practice squad is always there as an option to “stash” some of these players in the future, yes. However, who they pick for the 53-man roster can have drastic consequences for the team moving forward. articles.title: Gonzaga lands former Florida standout after Summer League stint with Cavs
articles.summary: Former Florida guard Xaivian Lee is returning to college basketball after committing to Gonzaga, On3’s Joe Tipton reported Wednesday night. The move comes after Lee spent the summer with the Cleveland Cavaliers following his selection to an Exhibit 10 contract and his participation in the 2
articles._body: Former Florida guard Xaivian Lee is returning to college basketball after committing to Gonzaga, On3’s Joe Tipton reported Wednesday night. The move comes after Lee spent the summer with the Cleveland Cavaliers following his selection to an Exhibit 10 contract and his participation in the 2026 NBA Summer League. Lee, a 6-foot-3 guard, entered the transfer portal on Aug. 18 after receiving a temporary restraining order in California that gave 73 student-athletes a seven-day opportunity to enter the portal. Lee was among the plaintiffs in the fifth-year eligibility lawsuit and had previously been eligible through the Colorado ruling involving players from the 2022 recruiting class. The commitment gives Bulldogs head coach Mark Few an experienced backcourt option after Lee spent his first three collegiate seasons at Princeton before transferring to the Gators. With the Tigers, Lee averaged 17.1 points as a sophomore and 16.9 points as a junior. He earned First Team All-Ivy League recognition in both 2024 and 2025 and averaged 17.0 points, 5.9 rebounds, 4.6 assists and 1.1 steals over his final two seasons while shooting 50.6% on two-point attempts and 35.2% from three. Lee transferred to Florida on April 16, 2025 , choosing the Gators over St. John’s and Kansas. During his lone season in Gainesville, he averaged 11.6 points, 4.2 assists and 3.7 rebounds per game. His 147 assists led Florida, while his 2.4 assist-to-turnover ratio ranked among the SEC’s best. Lee recorded 24 points on 6-of-10 shooting against George Washington on Dec. 13, earning Orange Bowl Classic MVP honors. He was also named SEC Player of the Week on Feb. 16 after scoring 18 points against Georgia and 22 against then-No. 25 Kentucky. After going undrafted in the 2026 NBA Draft, Lee joined the Cavaliers for Summer League. He appeared in five games, averaging 6.4 points, 2.4 assists and 2.0 rebounds in 16 minutes per game. He shot 40% from the field and 21.4% from three. At Gonzaga, Lee adds another experienced guard to a roster that also includes Davis Fogle , Chauncey Wiggins, Braden Huff and Massamba Diop. His addition gives the Bulldogs another perimeter playmaker after Javon Bennett became ineligible following the NCAA’s stay request in the Colorado lawsuit. Lee will now use his fifth collegiate season at Gonzaga after spending the summer pursuing an NBA opportunity with the Cavaliers. articles.title: Harry Styles Discos More Than Occasionally With New Together, Together Setlist at First NYC Show: 6 Best Moments
articles.summary: A rearranged set cranked up the dance energy for Styles' first of 30 gigs in one of the world's disco capitals.
articles._body: “How about them Knicks, huh?” a mid-strut Harry Styles asked the packed Madison Square Garden crowd on Wednesday night (Aug. 26), midway through opening song “Dance No More,” to a predictably roaring response. “ How about them Knicks, huh? ” Forget about the Knicks. Great championship run and all — first in 53 years, good job by them — but their parade was two months ago at this point, and they ain’t been back to MSG since. For the next two months, the World’s Most Famous Arena is officially Harry’s House. Styles appeared on stage in midtown Manhattan on Wednesday for the first of his 30 — yes, that’s a 3 and then a 0 — consecutive gigs at MSG, as part of his current Together, Together tour, taking him all the way up through Halloween (and well into the start of next NBA season). And he may have been anxious to be there, as he and his band couldn’t even wait till the end of opener Jamie xx’s DJ set to join them, flowing right from the producer’s set into their own. Playing in the round — really, in the oval, as the light-up stage Styles and his band performed on was more oblong to match the dimensions of the floor — allowed the pop-rock superstar to really harness the energy of the sold-out, packed-out crowd. And he gave it back to them, with the help of a totally reordered setlist from the 31 dates he’d previously played on Together, Together, including a handful of fan favorites making their first appearance. A couple of those songs got completely new arrangements, too. Perhaps drawing extra inspiration from being in the city of Studio 54, Styles amped up the disco not just for the songs from his clubbier new album Kiss All the Time. Disco, Occasionally ., but also for a couple less-dancefloor-obvious older tracks. (Styles’ 2017 self-titled first album was the biggest beneficiary of the new set ordering — now tied with 2023’s Grammy-winning Harry’s House for the second-most-played album with four tracks — though fans who came to Styles from his first group might have left slightly disappointed by the total lack of One Direction representation.) Even with an updated sound and wardrobe, Styles is hardly the most natural or obvious of disco dons — he comes to the genre through more left-field NYC dance-rock greats like Talking Heads and LCD Soundsystem, drawing physical inspiration their herky-jerky energy, while largely bypassing the manic anxiety that fuels those bands’ signature jams as much as any four-on-the-flour thumping. He also seems to currently have precious little interest in the decadence that drove the scene in its heyday, with his performance as PG-rated as you might expect from a show where the most common merch item found in the audience was a RESPECT YOUR MOTHER T-shirt. Nonetheless, Styles does understand dance’s power to galvanize and unify, which was on full display throughout Wednesday’s show. The set’s most cathartic and satisfying moments came Styles at the center of his band mid-full disco freakout, summoning a storm of lightning and glitter and fully zapping their gleefully electrified frontman. Whether the kids in the audience got the cleverly laid nods to indie-dance anthems like “Born Slippy (Nuxx)” or “Daft Punk Is Playing at My House” probably doesn’t matter as much as them potentially feeling the sensation of their entire essence being bass-bombed along with 20,000 of their new closest friends, and leaving the building vibrating on a totally new frequency. For some in the building on Wednesday, it will undoubtedly be the beginning of a lifelong pursuit of discoing as often as possible. Or at least until the Knicks’ next playoff run. Here were the six best moments from Harry Styles’ first visit to MSG since 2022 — one down, 29 to go. (And yes, they do include a Dolly Parton tribute.)

As of this writing, the 24-year-old Skattebo has yet to address the incident, but Jermaine Eluemunor already defended his teammate , slamming Leonard for “trying to create a b******* narrative.” Skattebo may be too competitive for his own good. What it does: - Set desktop and lock screen wallp
articles._body: macOS ties the lock screen to your desktop wallpaper, with no built-in option to set them separately. Wallps decouples the two, letting you choose one static image for the desktop and another for the lock screen, including live video wallpapers. What it does: - Set desktop and lock screen wallpapers independently - Use live wallpapers from local videos or Apple’s aerials - Run silently in the background as a menu bar app and automatically apply settings after a reboot - Open source, free, and compatible with macOS 13 and later Behind the scenes, the lock screen is rendered by `loginwindow` without third-party code. As a result, live lock screen video requires registering the clip as a system aerial in macOS 26 and re-encoding user videos with Apple’s temporal scalability scheme. This is the format expected by the stock wallpaper engine; videos without it freeze after the first unlock. demo: https://x.com/dipxsyy/status/2092845512722625007?s=20 Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49460234 Points: 3 # Comments: 0

He also said that he and the organization continue to be on the same page and want something to get done before the season,” wrote Ezier on X. Kraft was taken off the PUP list in July, and he has progressed better than expected. He even welcomed the big hit on him in practice on Wednesday. “That was a good hit. I haven’t had any contact like that since November 2nd. That was an opportunity for me to wake up. Season’s here!” said the third-round pick. In eight games last season, Kraft tallied 30 receptions for 469 yards and six touchdowns. He could have had a breakout campaign if not for his ACL injury. But that is now in the rearview mirror, and he is looking forward to making a significant impact anew for the Packers. Green Bay will face the Minnesota Vikings in Week 1. articles._body: The Milwaukee Brewers became a huge topic of conversation among baseball fans on Tuesday following their 3-2 loss to the New York Mets in extra innings. While everything is back to normal after the Brewers bounced back with an 8-1 victory over the Mets on Wednesday, there remained plenty of discourse regarding manager Pat Murphy’s decision to bench Cooper Pratt for some of his purported mistakes during their crushing loss to New York last night. Murphy explained that Pratt failed to execute on a bunt with two on and nobody out in the inning, and the Brewers shortstop followed that up by allegedly not hustling on a pop fly towards right field that had the Mets fielders blinded by the lights — allowing the ball to drop and Pratt to reach base. According to the Brewers manager, Pratt could have gone to second base had he hustled. Immediately after, Murphy pulled Pratt from the game, inserting David Hamilton as a pinch-runner. Hamilton would later commit the game-losing error that allowed Francisco Lindor to break the deadlock in the 11th. But for Brewers beat reporter Curt Hogg of Milwaukee Journal Sentinel, this is nothing new for Murphy. He has a history , just this season, of pulling players whom he believed did not execute to the level the Brewers want to set regularly, so his decision with Pratt is nothing personal. “This is, for better or for worse, part of the Pat Murphy Brewers experience,” Hogg declared in an appearance on Foul Territory. "This is, for better or for worse, part of the Pat Murphy Brewers experience." @CyrtHogg explains why getting pulled mid-game for a lack of hustle is nothing new under Pat Murphy. pic.twitter.com/ezZrxHNahs — Foul Territory (@FoulTerritoryTV) August 26, 2026 It’s hard to say that Murphy’s methods aren’t working. The Brewers have the best record in MLB at present (82-51), and they’ve done this on a moneyball-esque strategy. He knows which buttons to push and when to push them, and he appears to have the full buy-in of his team. Pratt vowed to never make the same mistakes he did on Tuesday ever again. And Murphy rewarded him by trusting him to start on Wednesday. And this time, he finished the game on the field. articles._body: The New Orleans Saints have major decisions to make soon . The time to cut rosters down to 53 players is rapidly approaching. The Saints sideline boss mentioned that a tweak in how the league structured the deadline this season offers an advantage for the players who will make the roster. “The NFL, they changed their structure just a little bit. Usually, you kinda drag those roster decisions and you only end up getting one, maybe two practices,” the Saints head coach said, via New Orleans Football Network. Moore will be beginning his second season as head coach of New Orleans next month. The former NFL quarterback was hired after winning a Super Bowl as the Philadelphia Eagles’ offensive coordinator. Unfortunately, his first season as a head coach did not go so well. The Saints had a brutal start to the year, going 2-8. However, things did turn around for them at the end of the year. They finished 4-3 in the latter stages of the season to end with a 6-11 record. The Saints are hoping for better fortunes in 2026.
