articles.title: Heat news: Klay Thompson shares interesting story behind jersey No. 11
articles.summary: Klay Thompson recently secured a move to the Miami Heat after getting the final year of his contract with the Dallas Mavericks bought out. Thompson had been angling for a move to a team with contending aspirations, and with the Heat in dire need of floor-spacing after trading away a handful of ro
articles._body: Klay Thompson recently secured a move to the Miami Heat after getting the final year of his contract with the Dallas Mavericks bought out. Thompson had been angling for a move to a team with contending aspirations, and with the Heat in dire need of floor-spacing after trading away a handful of rotation players in their blockbuster trade for Giannis Antetokounmpo , both sides felt as though teaming up was perfect. As an added bonus, Thompson gets to wear his preferred jersey number of 11 once more. He had to don the number 31 when he signed with the Mavericks, as the no. 11 belonged to Kyrie Irving. Now, he’s back to more familiar territory. In fact, Thompson has a plethora of reasons as to why he chose to wear the no. 11 during the 12 seasons he spent with the Golden State Warriors. “I grew up on 11 Paverstone Lane in Ladera Ranch. I was 11th pick in 2011. ‘K’ is the 11th letter of the alphabet,” Thompson told head coach Erik Spoelstra in a video posted by the official Heat account on X. “I had to go with the second-best option which is 11.” Klay Thompson reveals the story behind the #11 (via @MiamiHEAT ) pic.twitter.com/tEioVXNl6m — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) August 27, 2026 Thompson did wear jersey no. 1 when was at Washington State. However, back when the Warriors drafted him, Dorell Wright, who was a member of the 2006 Heat team that won the championship, was on the team with veteran ownership of that number. In turn, Thompson had to be the one to adjust. And the rest is history. “Dorell Wright had number one. I wore number one in college. I had to go second best option,” Thompson added. Thompson has made the jersey number 11 iconic in his own right. The Warriors dynasty would not have been what it was if not for him, and even now that he’s 36 years of age, he commands so much respect on the hardwood simply by virtue of being who he is — one of the best shooters in NBA history. The Heat are excited to see what Thompson can do for a team with winning ambitions, as he spent the last two seasons of his career playing for a Mavs team that was in constant flux. articles.title: Former NBA star Russell Westbrook’s NBA 2K27 rating after retirement will grab attention
articles.summary: Russell Westbrook may have played his final NBA game, but he still has a place in the league’s most popular video game, and his new number is turning heads. Even after announcing his retirement earlier this month, Westbrook appears in NBA 2K27 as a free agent with a 79 overall rating. For a
articles._body: Russell Westbrook may have played his final NBA game, but he still has a place in the league’s most popular video game, and his new number is turning heads. Even after announcing his retirement earlier this month , Westbrook appears in NBA 2K27 as a free agent with a 79 overall rating. For a nine-time All-Star and former MVP, it is a humbling figure , and a reminder of just how far the game had shifted by the end of his 18-year career. In the game, he is listed as a 6-foot-4 point guard wearing No. 18, tagged with a Blow-By Finisher build. The rating reflects the version fans saw in his final seasons rather than the force who once bent games to his will. His card leans on the traits that always defined him, with a 87 in athleticism and an 83 in playmaking pacing the profile. His 75 outside scoring and 67 inside scoring speak to the streaky efficiency that followed him from stop to stop, while his defending and rebounding both sit in the high 50s. He carries 10 total badges, none of them gold or Hall of Fame level. It is a stark contrast to the peak, when Westbrook routinely rated in the mid-90s during his MVP prime in Oklahoma City. In 2016-17, he became the first player since Oscar Robertson in 1962 to average a triple-double across a full season , posting 31.6 points, 10.7 rebounds and 10.4 assists on his way to the award. He remains the NBA’s all-time leader in triple-doubles with 209. Westbrook closed his career with the Sacramento Kings , the seventh franchise of a well-traveled run that began when Seattle drafted him fourth overall in 2008. He announced the end on August 12 through a video narrated by actor Michael B. Jordan, choosing a quiet exit over a farewell tour despite reported interest from teams this offseason . Now his legacy lives on in pixels. A 79 will not headline anyone’s starting five, but for a generation that grew up watching Westbrook attack the rim with unmatched fury, seeing him listed among the game’s free agents is a fitting, if bittersweet, final chapter. articles.title: Reds put Eugenio Suarez on waivers after hitting grand slam
articles.summary: The Cincinnati Reds have had themselves quite an evening. They came back from six runs down in the ninth inning to take a 10-9 victory over the San Francisco Giants, with Eugenio Suarez hitting a grand slam which cut the deficit to one, 9-8. (Jose Trevino and Tyler Stephenson each drove in a run
articles._body: The Cincinnati Reds have had themselves quite an evening. They came back from six runs down in the ninth inning to take a 10-9 victory over the San Francisco Giants, with Eugenio Suarez hitting a grand slam which cut the deficit to one, 9-8. (Jose Trevino and Tyler Stephenson each drove in a run a piece to give the Reds the lead.) Suarez and the Reds were on cloud nine, justifiably so, but little did they know that these celebrations were going to be cut short by a surprising move from the franchise. As reported by Ken Rosenthal of The Athletic, the Reds placed Wednesday’s hero in Suarez on waivers along with TJ Friedl. It’s important to note the distinction between being put on waivers and being designated for assignment. Being put on waivers means that Suarez and Friedl can still play for Cincinnati for the 48 hours they spend on waivers, all while other teams are free to claim their services. Should a team claim them off waivers, they assume their remaining salary for the season, removing that from the Reds’ books. The rationale behind the Reds’ decision is simple. Suarez and Friedl are both over the age of 30 (35 and 31 years old, respectively), and they haven’t been very impactful for Cincinnati in 2026. Both of them entered their Wednesday victory over the Giants with an fWAR total in the negatives for this season. Moreover, the Reds, with a 63-71 record on the season, are unlikely to make it to the postseason. They may have snuck into the postseason last year following the New York Mets’ collapse, but Cincinnati, as things stand, is nine games back of an NL Wild Card spot with five teams ahead of them and just 28 games to play. Putting Suarez and Friedl on waivers opens up the possibility that they latch on with a contending team, all while giving the Reds some salary relief. This is a gesture of goodwill from Cincinnati, as these veterans can potentially contribute for a team with postseason aspirations. Suarez’s pop, in particular, could be of interest to a team in need of a bench bat. The post Reds put Eugenio Suarez on waivers after hitting grand slam appeared first on ClutchPoints .

He trained with Los Angeles Rams star Myles Garrett ahead of the 2026 NFL season. Anderson spoke about that traini
articles._body: Houston Texans pass rusher Will Anderson Jr. has established himself as one of the best in the NFL. This offseason, he sought an “iron sharpens iron” moment, so to speak. He trained with Los Angeles Rams star Myles Garrett ahead of the 2026 NFL season. Anderson spoke about that training session earlier in training camp. Now, recent footage emerged showing an interesting interaction between the two. Garrett commented that the Texans star has some time before he can catch him. However, Anderson warned Garrett that he’s closer to snatching the crown than the Rams star may think. “It was about this close this year. And I didn’t even hit my prime yet! That’s the scary thing about it MG! I was right behind you this year. And I didn’t even hit my prime yet!” Anderson said in a clip shared by Houston Stressans on social media. In terms of impact, there are certainly similarities. Both pass rushers led one of the best defenses in the NFL. The Texans made the playoffs in 2025 thanks to their defense. Garrett’s former team, the Cleveland Browns, was not so lucky. However, when it comes to taking down the quarterback, there is a significant gap. Anderson turned in a good season, recording 12 sacks. Garrett, meanwhile, broke the single-season sack record with 23 in 2025. Houston certainly hopes Anderson can become a player similar to Garrett. Their defense is already tough to beat, boasting a fearsome pass rush. If Anderson can somehow replicate Garrett’s production, this Texans defense would be a nightmare to face for years to come. articles.title: Mike Breen points to key difference in Knicks’ championship run
articles.summary: Legendary New York Knicks play-by-play announcer Mike Breen made a special appearance in the SNY broadcast booth alongside Gary Cohen and Keith Hernandez during a New York Mets game. While taking a break from baseball action, Breen broke down what truly propelled the Knicks through their historic
articles._body: Legendary New York Knicks play-by-play announcer Mike Breen made a special appearance in the SNY broadcast booth alongside Gary Cohen and Keith Hernandez during a New York Mets game. While taking a break from baseball action, Breen broke down what truly propelled the Knicks through their historic championship run. When asked if a single factor stood out during the team’s postseason journey, Breen didn’t point to dynamic scoring or defensive dominance. Instead, he highlighted the mental fortitude gained from past battles. “Their playoff experience was the difference in the Finals,” Breen explained in the booth. “All 5 games they were down double figures in the first quarter, they put themselves in a hole, but the playoff experience taught them it’s okay, we’re gonna fight back, we’re gonna get our run. And the other thing was, they all sacrificed, all that mattered was winning.” "Their playoff experience was the difference in the Finals." Mike Breen talks with Gary Cohen and Keith Hernandez in the SNY booth about the Knicks' championship run: pic.twitter.com/rOMBtzLmw5 — SNY Knicks (@sny_knicks) August 27, 2026 That resilience defined the series. In Game 1 of the 2026 NBA Finals, the Knicks found themselves trailing the San Antonio Spurs 27-19 after the opening period. Despite falling behind early, New York clawed back behind Jalen Brunson , who battled through injuries to drop a team-high 30 points. Karl-Anthony Towns anchored the interior with 18 points and 12 rebounds, while Josh Hart snatched 15 rebounds to fuel a 105-95 comeback win. Game 2 followed the exact same script. San Antonio rushed out to a 34-25 lead after 12 minutes, putting New York right back in a double-digit deficit. Once again, veterans like Towns (21 points, 13 rebounds) and Mikal Bridges (20 points) weathered the storm. Brunson added 20 points and five steals as the Knicks pulled out a nail-biting 105-104 victory. Breen’s insights highlight why championship pedigree matters . By trusting their experience and sacrificing individual stats, the Knicks repeatedly erased early deficits to reach the ultimate prize. articles.title: Eagles’ 53-man roster prediction for 2026 NFL season
articles.summary: Though the Philadelphia Eagles still technically have one more preseason game to play on Friday against the Cincinnati Bengals, Howie Roseman and his fellow front office members are hard at work in South Philly trying to decide how to proceed with all 91 members of their preseason roster heading
articles._body: Though the Philadelphia Eagles still technically have one more preseason game to play on Friday against the Cincinnati Bengals, Howie Roseman and his fellow front office members are hard at work in South Philly trying to decide how to proceed with all 91 members of their preseason roster heading into September. For some players, their 53-man roster spots are more or less set, as the Eagles probably have about 48 players who can sleep easy on Saturday knowing where they will be reporting for work on Monday, but for the other 43 players? Well, they could be traded, released, or even stashed on the practice squad, assuming they aren’t claimed off waivers, creating a sort of football musical chairs that adds drama to the end of the month. On paper, those last few roster spots could ultimately be decided against the Bengals on Friday, as no one expected a player like Carson Steele to be in play for a spot on the 53 before his efforts against the New England Patriots, but for now, which players look like they have an inside track to make the roster and which will be on the phone with their agent looking for the next steps on Sunday? At some positions, things have a chance to get pretty interesting. Edward Finan-Imagn Images Quarterback – Jalen Hurts, Tanner McKee, Cole Payton For seemingly the entire summer, the Eagles have been trying to make Andy Dalton work as their backup quarterback , but unfortunately, it just hasn’t happened. Initially acquired for a seventh-round pick earlier in 2026, Dalton looked like the kind of veteran who could hold things down behind Jalen Hurts if something went bad while Parks Frazier developed Cole Payton as a long-term backup on a rookie contract. Instead, the Eagles might just have to bite the bullet and keep Tanner McKee instead of trading him for a 2027 draft pick, allowing his value to become what it is over the course of his rookie contract’s final season and scoop up a pick in 2028. Why? Because at this point, Dalton simply can’t be trusted to do anything but lose as a QB2, and Payton has more long-term upside. Eric Canha-Imagn Images Running Back – Saquon Barkley, Tank Bigsby, Will Shipley, Carson Steele Speaking of Carson Steele, he really isn’t competing for a roster spot against players like Dameon Pierce but instead utility options like fullback Cameron Lomu, tight end Grant Calcaterra, and wide receiver Elijah Moore, who all may have to make their money on special teams due to limited opportunities on offense. Of that quartert, Steele might just be the most intriguing, as he did a little bit of everything against the Patriots in Preseason Week 2 and has even more upside to contribute as a gunner, on kickoff units, and even as an offensive weapon, where he could serve as depth at running back, fullback, and even wide receiver due to athleticism that earned him a spot on Bruce Feldman’s Freaks List. Could the Eagles opt to keep three running backs and hope that Steele ends up on the practice squad? Sure, but consider the (lack of) external demand for those other three players on the open market, stashing Steele makes the most sense. Bill Streicher-Imagn Images Wide Receiver – DeVonta Smith, Deontavyon Wicks, Makai Lemon, Hollywood Brown, Darius Cooper If Steele makes the 53-man roster, then this decision is one of the easiest the Eagles will have to make heading into the fall. When Johnny Wilson was still a member of the 91-man roster, this was a little more dramatic, as he did play at a high level at times in 2024, but after being waived with an injury settlement and reverting to season-ending IR, keeping DeVonta Smith, Deontavyon Wicks, Makai Lemon, Hollywood Brown, and Darius Cooper feels like the play for the Eagles at wide receiver, with Moore and Quez Watkins options to sign with the practice squad. Bill Streicher-Imagn Images Tight End – Dallas Goedert, Eli Stowers, Johnny Mundt When the Eagles drafted Eli Stowers in the second round of the 2026 NFL Draft, he looked like the future of the position in Philadelphia, but now he looks “ unplayable ,” according to The Philly Voice’s Jimmy Kempski? While Stowers has suddenly become the top player for fans to watch in the preseason finale to see if such a major assertion is correct, his spot on the 53-man roster is 100 percent secure, as are those of Dallas Goedert and Johnny Mundt, the blocking specialist Howie Roseman added in free agency. Speaking of free agency, if March is of any indication, there likely won’t be a massive market for Calcaterra or Latu to sign elsewhere after Sunday, so the Eagles could sign one or both of them to their practice squad for the first month or so of the 2026 season, giving them full-time contracts when spots on the 53-man roster open up for one reason or another and still elevating at least one for game days in September. Bill Streicher-Imagn Images Offensive Line – Jordan Mailata, Landon Dickerson, Cam Jurgens, Tyler Steen, Lane Johnson, Fred Johnson, Micah Morris, Willie Lampkin, Drew Kendall, Markel Bell Another relatively low-drama position grouping. After beginning the summer as a longshot to stick around, Willie Lampkin has basically locked up a spot on the 53-man roster as a reserve guard/center alongside Drew Kendall, with the potential to even contribute on special teams if need be. Micah Morris gets the final spot because he was drafted this year, even if he didn’t exactly dazzle over the summer, and players like Myles Hinton and Cameron Williams will hope to keep developing on the practice squad, or look for new homes elsewhere. articles.title: Celtics’ Brad Stevens weighs in on Jaylen Brown’s jersey retirement
articles.summary: The Boston Celtics were one of the biggest casualties of the presence of the second apron, as they relieved themselves of future cap troubles by trading away Jaylen Brown to the Philadelphia 76ers earlier this offseason. This trade had been in the works, but the Celtics’ decision to pull th
articles._body: The Boston Celtics were one of the biggest casualties of the presence of the second apron , as they relieved themselves of future cap troubles by trading away Jaylen Brown to the Philadelphia 76ers earlier this offseason. This trade had been in the works, but the Celtics’ decision to pull the trigger on a trade that netted them Paul George and two first-round picks was what came as a shock , as the return was deemed light considering that Brown was coming off a season in which he made the All-NBA Second Team. Brown spent the first 10 seasons of his career with the Celtics and partnered up with Jayson Tatum to form a formidable duo that competed year-in, year-out in the Eastern Conference. They even broke through in 2024 and won a championship — the 18th in franchise history. And that all came to an end on one random afternoon. Nonetheless, Brown has certainly done enough to cement himself as a Celtics legend, and president Brad Stevens, despite making the call to trade him away, agrees with this notion. After all, he said that it’s “likely” for the franchise to retire Brown’s jersey no. 7, according to the Boston Globe. The Celtics own the record for the most retired jerseys in the NBA, with 24 unique numbers hanging in the rafters. Some believe that this is too many, but Boston has simply had that many legendary players suit up for the franchise — with Brown undoubtedly being one of them. Even before Brown took on the first option role for the Celtics for the first time in his career, he had already carved a memorable legacy for the team. The end to his tenure in Beantown may be as abrupt as it can get, but that should not change his legendary status for the team. And it should help that once it’s time for Boston to retire Brown’s number, time should have already healed all wounds. Downs also dealt with a groin injury a few weeks ago. The 25-year-ol
articles._body: Indianapolis Colts wide receiver Josh Downs is down but not out. With that lame pun out of the way, Downs can focus on recovering from his calf injury, which prevented him from participating in practice on Tuesday and Wednesday. Downs also dealt with a groin injury a few weeks ago. The 25-year-old pass-catcher is in the final year of his rookie contract, and he cannot afford to sit out for an extended period if he wants to secure a bigger deal. He said he is not worried about his calf injury. “Very minor. Just precautionary stuff,’ said Downs, as quoted by The Athletic’s James Boyd. It remains unclear when he will return to action, but he will likely be ready by Week 1 against the Baltimore Ravens. He will continue to play a key role for the Colts, even with the arrival of wide receiver Keenan Allen , whom the team signed to a one-year, $3.2 million contract just a few days ago. Downs expressed confidence that coach Shane Steichen will find ample touches for him and Allen, along with Alec Pierce, tight end Tyler Warren, and running back Jonathan Taylor. “Coach’s gonna handle it how he wants to handle it. So, that’s his responsibility,” said the former North Carolina standout. Downs, who was drafted by the Colts in the third round in 2023, had a promising stint in his second year, but he saw his numbers dip last season to career-lows of 58 receptions and 566 receiving yards. He also had four touchdowns. He did not see action in their preseason meetings against the New England Patriots and the Atlanta Falcons. In fact, Darvish remains in rehab after he underwent internal brace surgery on his right elbow last October. Wednesday ma
articles._body: Yu Darvish remains under contract with the San Diego Padres and will continue to be until 2028. However, Darvish hasn’t made much of an impact for the Padres as of late. In fact, Darvish remains in rehab after he underwent internal brace surgery on his right elbow last October. Wednesday marked Darvish’s 40th birthday, and he continues to be hard at work on his journey back to the big-league mound. He posted a powerful message on his official X account, thanking the Padres for their continued support even as he goes through the ups and downs of a lengthy layoff from pitching. Darvish has even resumed throwing , so he’s on his way to an eventual return in 2027. “I turned 40 the other day. To everyone who sent me messages, thank you so much I’ve been quietly continuing my rehab from the right elbow surgery I had last year. Thanks to the Padres and team staff who support me even though I’m not traveling with the team, I’ve been able to get to the point where I can resume pitching from the mound. This is a video of my second bullpen session, and so far, things are going smoothly,” Darvish wrote. 先日40歳を迎えました。 メッセージくださった方々、本当にありがとうございました 私は昨年受けた右肘の手術からのリハビリを細々と続けています。 チームに帯同していないのにサポートしてくださるパドレス、チームスタッフのおかげでマウンドからの投球を再開出来るまで来られました。… pic.twitter.com/jHX8pwzrxP — ダルビッシュ有(Yu Darvish) (@faridyu) August 27, 2026 It’s a testament to Darvish’s drive and his love for the sport that he is still hard at work at a comeback attempt even though he’s already turned 40 years of age. It would be understandable for a pitcher of his age to decide to hang it up considering how grueling the recovery process must be, but the Padres veteran is not yet done making an impact in the big leagues. Darvish last threw for the Padres back on the 26th of September in 2025. Last year, he recorded an ERA of 5.38 across 15 appearances (72.0 innings of work). There were reports in the past stating that he had intended to retire, but his MLB story still has a few chapters left for him to write. articles.title: Why Michael Irvin likes Carson Beck even more with Cardinals than at Miami
articles.summary: Pro Football Hall of Famer Michael Irvin knows a thing or two about elite quarterback play, and he is fully buying into Arizona Cardinals rookie quarterback Carson Beck. On a recent episode of The White House, the former Miami Hurricanes legend shared why he believes Beck will actually be a bette
articles._body: Pro Football Hall of Famer Michael Irvin knows a thing or two about elite quarterback play, and he is fully buying into Arizona Cardinals rookie quarterback Carson Beck . On a recent episode of The White House , the former Miami Hurricanes legend shared why he believes Beck will actually be a better signal-caller in the pros than he was in college. “I like Carson Beck as a pro,” Irvin said. “I loved him for us at University of Miami. I like him better as a pro than a college player.” Michael Irvin believes Carson Beck might be even better suited for the NFL than he was in college. The guys break down Beck’s potential and what Arizona is building for the future on The White House, now streaming on @netflix . #NFL #Cardinals pic.twitter.com/un1vKY0eLy — The White House Pod (@dawhitehousepod) August 27, 2026 For Irvin, it all comes down to processing power and football IQ. The Playmaker believes Beck’s ability to diagnose defenses before the snap gives him a distinct advantage over quarterbacks who rely solely on reactive, post-snap play. “That first preseason game, he looked great,” Irvin noted. “And I said to people, I knew he would be a better pro than he even was in college. Coz the quarterbacks that can play the game shoulders up, pre-snap quarterbacks as opposed to post-snap quarterbacks. Carson Beck has that pre-snap ability; he sees the game.” That pre-snap intelligence showed out immediately during the NFL Hall of Fame Game against the Carolina Panthers. Drafted in the second round with the 52nd overall pick by Arizona, Beck commanded the offense with veterans’ poise. He dissected Carolina’s defense by completing 15 of 19 passes for 188 yards, zero interceptions, and a five-yard touchdown pass to wide receiver Simi Fehoko. He also uncorked a 49-yard strike to wide receiver Jalen Brooks, earning a stellar 125.4 passer rating in his exhibition debut. While Arizona currently has veteran Jacoby Brissett on the roster, Beck’s mental sharpness and impressive preseason start give fans plenty of reason for optimism . If Irvin’s instincts are right, the rookie’s sharp mind will translate to big-time success in the NFL. The system works on Windows, Linux and macOS. This is a standalone binary file with no CI server to configure, just download, run and open in browser. You can also migrate your existing pipelines from GitHub Actions, Azure DevOps and Jenkins. It would be awesome if you could check it and give me some feedback. articles.title: Deshaun Watson’s critics may not want to hear Ryan Fitzpatrick’s assessment
articles.summary: Veteran quarterback Deshaun Watson has a big opportunity to find redemption with the Cleveland Browns after coach Todd Monken chose him to start over sophomore quarterback Shedeur Sanders, ending their tight competition in training camp. Watson was sidelined last season due to an Achilles injury.
articles._body: Veteran quarterback Deshaun Watson has a big opportunity to find redemption with the Cleveland Browns after coach Todd Monken chose him to start over sophomore quarterback Shedeur Sanders, ending their tight competition in training camp. Watson was sidelined last season due to an Achilles injury. While he has a lot of catching up to do, he did enough in training camp to get the nod from Monken, who is in his first year with the Browns. Monken’s decision raised a lot of eyebrows, especially since Sanders was on his way up. Watson, on the other hand, has not played significant football since 2020 due to various injuries and off-field issues. NFL analyst Ryan Fitzpatrick, however, claimed that the 30-year-old Watson is the right guy for the Browns, noting that he is “more ready” than the 24-year-old Sanders. “He knows how to do an operation in the NFL. He knows how to get the ball out. He knows how to throw on time. He knows how to throw with anticipation. Those are all things that he does and does well,” said Fitzpatrick on his podcast. “On the flip side of it, when you watch Shedeur, there are things that certainly pop. He makes more plays downfield with some of the throws and scrambling outside the pocket. But rarely is he playing on time. I think this is probably why he lost the job to Deshaun.” “I first went back and I watched Deshaun, and then I watched Shedeur… the hard part is you put on the film and there’s things that Deshaun has really regressed at” Fitz breaks down what he sees in each of the Browns QBs and why he thinks they ended up going with Watson pic.twitter.com/2FGsfru7CZ — Fitz & Whit (@fitzandwhit) August 26, 2026 Last season, Sanders threw for 1,400 yards, seven interceptions, and 10 interceptions in eight games. Watson is in the final year of his five-year, $230 million contract he signed in 2022, which was the largest guaranteed deal in league history at that time. Now that he is back in action, he has every motivation to perform well and regain the old form that made him a three-time Pro Bowler. But perhaps most importantly, Watson should regain the trust of the fans . The Browns will open their new season against the Jacksonville Jaguars on September 13. articles.summary: On Sunday, No. 1 Stanford women’s soccer defeated UC Irvine 6-0 as six different Cardinal players found the back of the net.
articles._body: Credit: Maciek Gudrymowicz/ISI Photos On Sunday, No. 1 Stanford women’s soccer defeated UC Irvine 6-0 as six different Cardinal players found the back of the net. Stanford goalkeeper Caroline Birkel played the first 45:00 for the Cardinal before Rhiannon Stewart (26:21) and Kaiya Jota (18:39) played the second half. Stewart with the lone save for the Cardinal. Savanna Arruda played all 90:00 for the Anteaters, totaling five saves while giving up six goals. Stanford improves to 3-0-0 on the season while UC Irvine falls to 0-1-1. Stanford remains No. 1 in the nation after the win. BOX SCORE: UC Irvine at Stanford-Sunday, August 23 rd “No, I’m happy, 6-0 is a fantastic result against a really good UC Irvine team,” Stanford head coach Paul Ratcliffe said after the match. “We scored four in the first half, so really proud of how the team started and they capitalized. It’s something we’ve been talking about. We want to execute more and score more goals and be more aggressive and more relentless. And they did that. It was coming from all different players, which is really rewarding for our team.” The first goal for Stanford came at 7:40 as Bella Winn found the bottom left of the goal off the right foot thanks to an assist from Charlotte Kohler . Stanford already had corner kicks at 0:50 and 6:05, so they were putting pressure on UC Irvine from the jump. Stanford’s next goal came at 13:48 as Brooke Holden found the bottom left of the goal off her left foot, making it 2-0. UC Irvine just had a corner kick at 12:45, but obviously, it didn’t amount to anything. Stanford would then get two more corner kicks at 20:00 and 36:50. Shortly after the corner kick at 36:50, Lizzie Boamah found the top right of the goal off her left foot thanks to an assist from Y-Lan Nguyen . UC Irvine’s Hailey Clingan would soon get a yellow card at 37:33 for unsporting before Stanford found their fourth goal of the afternoon at 41:08 as Eleanor Klinger found the top left of the goal off her left foot thanks to an assist from Erica Grillione . Stanford would take that 4-0 lead into halftime. “Well, I think me and Y-Lan have really good chemistry and I usually know where she’s gonna play the ball and she does a really good job of setting it up towards the back post,” Boamah said of her goal. “So, I kinda just had to time the run and I saw the flight of the ball, like, coming to the back post, and then, I mean, it was pretty simple from there. I just like kinda tapped it in. But, I think the main props actually go to Y-Lan and she just does a really great job on serving the ball in. So yeah, it came right to me and just tapped it in.” “Oh, Lizzie has such a big personality and brings so much to our team,” Ratcliffe said of Boamah. “She’s a leader on the field, leader off the field, she just has so much enthusiasm that she really brings some excitement to our practices and to our games. So we’re gonna miss her when she’s gone with the U-20s, but she’s a phenomenal talent and I know we’ll continue to get better and grow.” In the second half, Stanford got an early corner kick at 45:55 before UC Irvine had a corner kick of their own at 56:15. Soon, at 59:55, Stanford went up 5-0 as Charlotte Kohler buried one in the back of the net as Holden and Winn got credited for the assist. Stanford would find one more goal before the match was over as Grillione found the top left of the goal off an assist from Sadie Leal-Schuman at 84:26. 6-0 would be the final score as Stanford cruised to a dominant win. “Yeah, it’s something I spoke about at halftime that I was really proud of the players that came in off the bench,” Ratcliffe said. “I thought they added a huge amount of energy and some quality chances and goals. So that’s the key to our success and in the second half is the same way. We’re able to change people around and I think the level continued to get better with players coming in off the bench.” For Stanford, this was a nice win for them. They dominated from start to finish and got a lot of players a chance to show what they can do. When you have six players scoring, that speaks to the depth that you have on your team. “Yeah, it shows we have a quality squad and so happy they’re all working hard and getting opportunities,” Ratcliffe said of six different players scoring. “And then capitalizing scoring goals is exactly what we’re doing in training.” “Yeah, I think our backline has done a really good job of coming together in these past couple games and just really having to grind out a couple wins,” Boamah said of getting the shutout. “And I think it goes to say that we have been working on our organization in the back and building out of the back also counts as well and I think when everybody’s on the same page, when we’re sliding together and shifting, it makes it really, really easy to win the ball in really good areas for us and then that creates good attacks as well. So, I think just being super organized in the back has helped us obviously keep shut outs and just being super tough as well.” Stanford’s depth will certainly get tested in the month of September as Caroline Birkel (USA), Lizzie Boamah (USA), Y-Lan Nguyen (USA), Kaiya Jota (England), Eleanor Klinger (England), and Alex Tay (Ghana) will compete in the U-20 World Cup. It will be interesting to see how the Cardinal navigate this next month of soccer with six players competing internationally. “Yeah, I think it’s going to be the next month, unfortunately, but it’s great opportunities for other players to step up,” Ratcliffe said of the U-20 World Cup. “Next player up and we do have some quality players on our squad that I think will step up and capitalize on the opportunities, but we will miss. We are wishing them the best for their respective countries and excited to watch them from afar, but we’ll be happy when they come back and we can get back together as a group.” “Yeah, I mean, it’s definitely always been my dream to go to a World Cup and especially like a U-20

articles.title: Harry Styles’ Brand New Together, Together NYC Setlist: Every Song Played at Tour’s First U.S. Show
articles.summary: Styles brought his latest tour to the States for the first time at New York's Madison Square Garden on Tuesday night (Aug. 25), with a totally rearranged setlist.
articles._body: It’s been a building he’s made his own since the 2018 North American leg of his first-ever solo tour, but never quite like this before. When Harry Styles took the stage at New York’s iconic Madison Square Garden last night, he did so for what would be the first of an unprecedented 30 consecutive shows at the storied venue, taking him all the way through to Halloween — by which point the defending-champion New York Knicks will have already played three home games as part of the 2026-27 NBA regular season. But of course, to the MSG crowd last night, Harry Styles was a star more than equal to Jalen Brunson and Karl-Anthony Towns, as the One Direction alum and solo superstar brought his best-selling Together, Together tour to New York in support of his dance-flavored February LP, Kiss All the Time. Disco, Occasionally. Support for Styles came in the form of DJ-producer Jamie xx, who set the clubby tone for the evening with a mix of solo hits, productions for other artists and classics from his beloved indie-electronic band The xx. Styles and his band joined even Jamie xx during his final song, and took over things from there. New York is the tour’s first and only stop in the U.S., after having previously stopped in Amsterdam, London, São Paulo and Mexico City for a combined 31 dates across July and August. (After New York, Styles will visit Melbourne and City before calling it a day on the trek — for the time being, at least.) Perhaps due to the unique nature of his visit — and Styles’ history with the Garden — he greeted fans with a completely new song ordering from the setlist he’s been playing on Together, Together to this point, including a handful of longtime fan favorites he’d yet to revisit on this trek, and a tribute to a fallen musical icon. Find the complete new set list for the first of Styles’ 30 NYC shows below.

articles.title: Dodgers’ Dave Roberts announces move after tough Roki Sasaki injury update
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Dodgers will be without Roki Sasaki for at least a turn through the rotation, and manager Dave Roberts has already lined up the replacement. Roberts said Sasaki is headed to the injured list because of the blister that forced him out of Wednesday’s start against the Atlanta
articles._body: The Los Angeles Dodgers will be without Roki Sasaki for at least a turn through the rotation, and manager Dave Roberts has already lined up the replacement. Roberts said Sasaki is headed to the injured list because of the blister that forced him out of Wednesday’s start against the Atlanta Braves . In his place, veteran left-hander Eric Lauer is expected to move back into the starting rotation for the next turn. The injury surfaced in the fourth inning at Truist Park. Trainers visited Sasaki on the mound before he exited with a blister on his right middle finger, leaving with the Dodgers up 3-2 and runners on second and third. He finished with four earned runs on six hits and two walks across 3.1 innings, striking out three while serving up a solo home run to Matt Olson. A blister is rarely a long-term issue, but it is a tricky one for a pitcher who relies on feel and grip, and the Dodgers opted for caution rather than pushing Sasaki through it. The move buys the right-hander time to let the finger heal without risking a setback that could linger into a pennant race. The timing stings for Los Angeles. Sasaki had been one of the team’s better stories in the second half , turning a corner after the All-Star break and settling into a dependable rotation piece. The bounce-back carried extra weight given how his injury-marred 2025 rookie year went, when a shoulder problem cost him months. Losing him, even briefly, thins a staff that the defending World Series champions have already had to juggle through injuries all season . That is where Lauer comes in. The left-hander has bounced between the rotation and the bullpen for the Dodgers this year, giving Roberts a flexible arm to plug into exactly this kind of gap. Stretching him back out to start is a natural fallback with Sasaki sidelined. For now, the Dodgers are treating the absence as a short one. A blister landing him on the IL points to caution more than alarm, and the expectation is that Sasaki returns to the rotation once the finger is fully healed. articles.title: Trey Reynolds on Being Named Utah Football Captain
articles.summary: The Utah linebacker on his leadership role, pre-snap recognition, and why Semi is a headache to deal with in practice:
articles._body: Trey Reynolds , one of Utah’s returning linebackers, was named one of the team’s captains heading into the 2026 season, and when asked about it after practice, he expressed his gratitude. “It’s a great opportunity. I’m super grateful for my teammates for voting me into this leadership position,” Reynolds said. “I pride myself on being a leader and kind of just got the title now. It means a lot to me. I love this team, and I’ve worked really hard for it.” Captaincies voted on by teammates carry a different weight than those handed down by a coaching staff. Reynolds earned this one from the guys in the room with him every day. Pre-Snap Recognition Has Been the Biggest Jump When asked where he’s improved the most from a season ago, Reynolds pointed straight to the mental side of the game. “I would say my knowledge of the game and just knowing what’s coming, my pre-snap recognition,” he said. “I think that’s been the biggest part of my improvement.” That tracks with what defensive coordinator Colton Swan has been building schematically. Reynolds elaborated on how Swan’s elevation to DC has helped him connect the dots between assignment and concept. “He’s really been opening up the reason why we’re doing things,” Reynolds said of Swan. “It’s really been helping me coach up other people and be that leader that the defense needs.” A linebacker who understands the why behind the scheme is infinitely more valuable than one just reacting to keys. Reynolds sounds like he’s operating on a different level mentally than he was a year ago. The Linebacker Room is as Competitive as It’s Been Reynolds was asked about two younger linebackers, Cyrus Polu and Elijah Elliss , who have been generating buzz through the early days of camp. His answer said everything about the room’s current environment. “There’s so much competition in the linebacker room right now,” he said. “I love those guys, and they push me every day. They work so hard, and that room has just been so competitive. It’s so awesome for all four of us.” Competition from within is exactly what a veteran captain should welcome. Reynolds is keeping his mind in the right spot. On Why Game Week Can’t Come Soon Enough The most entertaining moment of Reynolds’ availability came when he was asked about facing Utah’s Semi Taulanga , one of the more unique offensive weapons on the roster. “He’s going to be running people over, that’s for sure,” Reynolds said, laughing. “It’s a lot nicer in practice when you don’t get to actually tackle him, but taking him on blocks is a headache sometimes.” And when asked what he’s most looking forward to about the season opener? “I’m just excited to hit someone else, not my teammates and the people that I love around me. Excited to take it out on some other people.” Week one against Idaho cannot come soon enough for Trey Reynolds, and he could be in for a big season at the second level.  UteZone Take your Utah fandom to the next level by joining the ultimate community for dedicated fans at UteZone. articles.title: Lightning’s Victor Hedman makes sobering admission on 2025-26 season
articles.summary: The Tampa Bay Lightning had another successful regular season last year, which saw them return to the Stanley Cup Playoffs for the ninth straight season. Unfortunately, it was not a successful season for everyone involved. Defenseman Victor Hedman had a rough go of it in 2025-26. The veteran defe
articles._body: The Tampa Bay Lightning had another successful regular season last year, which saw them return to the Stanley Cup Playoffs for the ninth straight season. Unfortunately, it was not a successful season for everyone involved. Defenseman Victor Hedman had a rough go of it in 2025-26 . The veteran defenseman struggled with injuries throughout the year. He missed about a month from early November to early December. And then he missed another two months later in the season. He did not play past March 19, taking a leave of absence from the team. In a recent interview, the Lightning star made a rather eye-opening admission on how things went last year. “For me, it was not really feeling low, but it was performance anxiety, kind of feeling that pressure in your chest as soon as a gameday would hit,” Hedman said, via NHL.com. “It kind of locks you up. You make a mistake and in the past you’d be able to shake it off, but I couldn’t do that. And I wasn’t feeling 100 percent physically.” In the end, the veteran Lightning rearguard was limited to just 33 games. He scored one goal and 17 points in that span. He did not skate in Tampa’s first-round series loss to the Montreal Canadiens in the playoffs. The 2026-27 season is quickly approaching. And the Lightning are hoping to have their captain back healthy. As things stand, the veteran rearguard is motivated to step back onto the ice. “I’m sure it’s going to take me a few games to get back into the rhythm of playing in the League since I haven’t played in a long time, but I’m super fresh, hungry and super motivated to go out there and play my best hockey,” the Tampa captain said. The Lightning open their 2026-27 regular season on October 1 against the New York Rangers. articles.title: Roger Goodell breaks silence on former 49ers’ CEO Jed York’s arrest
articles.summary: NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell finally addressed the elephant in the room regarding San Francisco 49ers former chief executive officer and principal owner Jed York. Following York’s recent arrest in East Palestine, Ohio, during an undercover prostitution sting, the league is officially stepping i
articles._body: NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell finally addressed the elephant in the room regarding San Francisco 49ers former chief executive officer and principal owner Jed York. Following York’s recent arrest in East Palestine, Ohio, during an undercover prostitution sting, the league is officially stepping in to evaluate potential discipline. “Yes, it’s being reviewed under the personal conduct policy,” Goodell told reporters at the NFL owners’ meetings in Atlanta. “We’ll do that and when there’s something to be reported we’ll talk.” The situation escalated quickly after the Mahoning Valley Human Trafficking Task Force arrested the 46-year-old executive at a mobile home park. Police reports revealed that York used a pseudonym to text an undercover officer posing as a sex worker online, agreeing to pay $160 for an hour of service. Authorities seized his phone and $160 in cash upon arrival. York initially faced charges of engaging in prostitution and possessing criminal tools. However, prosecutors amended the prostitution charge to disorderly conduct after he entered a no-contest plea. York received credit for time served on two concurrent one-day jail terms, completed an online education course, and paid $1,150 in fines. While the San Francisco 49ers gear up for their upcoming campaign, head coach Kyle Shanahan emphasized that general manager John Lynch and the coaching staff remain completely focused on football operations. However, the shadow of potential league sanctions hangs heavily over the franchise. The NFL Personal Conduct Policy holds team executives and owners to a higher standard than roster players. While a forced sale of the franchise remains unlikely given league precedent, Goodell has suspended and fined owners in the past for off-field infractions. For now, the Bay Area faithful must play the waiting game while league officials complete their investigation into York. articles.title: Yankees pitcher Fernando Cruz’ UCL tear could require Tommy John surgery, Aaron Boone warns
articles.summary: The New York Yankees are bracing for a potentially significant loss in their bullpen after learning the severity of Fernando Cruz’s elbow injury. Manager Aaron Boone told reporters that Cruz has a partial tear of his ulnar collateral ligament (UCL), the elbow ligament repaired by Tommy John
articles._body: The New York Yankees are bracing for a potentially significant loss in their bullpen after learning the severity of Fernando Cruz’s elbow injury . Manager Aaron Boone told reporters that Cruz has a partial tear of his ulnar collateral ligament (UCL), the elbow ligament repaired by Tommy John surgery. The right-hander will seek a second opinion before determining a course of treatment, but Boone acknowledged that surgery is a real possibility. The setup man was placed on the injured list with what the team initially described as right elbow discomfort . Further testing revealed the ligament damage, turning a short-term concern into one that threatens to sideline Cruz well beyond this season. A partial UCL tear does not automatically mean an operation. Some pitchers manage the injury with rest, rehab, or a less invasive internal brace procedure , while others ultimately require a full Tommy John reconstruction. The second opinion Cruz is seeking should help clarify which path makes the most sense. Either way, the timing is difficult for both player and team. Cruz is widely expected to be shut down for the remainder of the campaign, and a full reconstruction would likely keep him out for most or all of 2027 as well. A brace procedure could offer a slightly faster runway, but any return next season would come late in the year at best. The injury is a blow to a Yankees bullpen that has already been stretched . Acquired from Cincinnati ahead of last season, Cruz built his value on a devastating splitter and elite swing-and-miss rates , giving Boone a high-leverage weapon when healthy. His 2026 season had been a struggle by his standards, and the elbow trouble adds context to that rough stretch. To help cover the loss, New York signed veteran reliever Michael Fulmer to a major league contract. Still, replacing Cruz’s strikeout ability is no simple task for a Yankees team already navigating a demanding stretch run. For now, the Yankees will wait on the second opinion before mapping out the next step. What is clear is that one of their most electric relievers, when right, faces a long road back. articles.title: Mets’ Bo Bichette gets encouraging X-ray update from Andy Green after injuring ankle
articles.summary: The New York Mets got a measure of good news on Bo Bichette after their third baseman was forced out of Wednesday’s 8-1 loss to the Milwaukee Brewers with an ankle injury. Bichette exited early after fouling a ball off his own ankle at Citi Field, with Brett Baty taking over at third base.
articles._body: The New York Mets got a measure of good news on Bo Bichette after their third baseman was forced out of Wednesday’s 8-1 loss to the Milwaukee Brewers with an ankle injury. Bichette exited early after fouling a ball off his own ankle at Citi Field, with Brett Baty taking over at third base. Interim manager Andy Green offered reassurance afterward . “He’s got a contusion on his ankle from the foul ball. X-rays were negative,” Green told reporters. Andy Green says that X-rays were negative on Bo Bichette after he was removed from the game with a contusion on his ankle pic.twitter.com/DuVwMtRRfF — SNY Mets (@SNY_Mets) August 27, 2026 Green stopped short of offering a definitive timeline, framing the situation as something that would become clearer with rest. “We’ll see where he’s at when he wakes up in the morning,” the skipper said. “You never really know how that is till the next day, but hoping he’s fine.” A negative X-ray rules out a fracture, though contusions can still leave a player sore and limited for a game or two depending on the location and swelling. For now, Bichette’s status appears to hinge on how the ankle responds overnight rather than on any structural damage. The update carries added weight given how the season has gone for Bichette. The infielder joined the Mets in January on a three-year, $126 million contract with player options, his first stop after seven seasons with the Toronto Blue Jays. Brought in to play third base, he spent much of the year at shortstop while Francisco Lindor recovered from a calf strain . The signing added a two-time All-Star on a big-money deal, but his debut campaign has been an uneven one at the plate as he adjusts to a new league and a new home. Bichette has also dealt with lower-body issues before this. Earlier in the summer, he missed time around the All-Star break with soreness in his legs and right ankle , discomfort Green traced to a stretch in which Bichette repeatedly fouled balls off his legs. This latest knock lands in the same general area, which makes the clean imaging all the more reassuring. The Mets will provide further clarity once Bichette is reevaluated. Until then, the takeaway is a positive one by injury standards. No breaks, no immediate alarm, and a manager cautiously optimistic that his infielder avoided anything serious. articles.title: Ha-Seong Kim walks off Dodgers with first hit since June
articles.summary: The Atlanta Braves took advantage of the Los Angeles Dodgers pulling Roki Sasaki Wednesday. Atlanta engaged in a back-and-forth with the defending World Series champs. Until Ha-Seong Kim walked off the Dodgers. Plus ended a personal hit-less streak that started in June.  Tied 5-5 with two runners
articles._body: The Atlanta Braves took advantage of the Los Angeles Dodgers pulling Roki Sasaki Wednesday . Atlanta engaged in a back-and-forth with the defending World Series champs. Until Ha-Seong Kim walked off the Dodgers. Plus ended a personal hit-less streak that started in June. Tied 5-5 with two runners on second and first base, Kim ripped through a Tanner Scott fastball that scored the wining run 6-5 at home. HA-SEONG KIM DELIVERS THE WALK-OFF WIN FOR THE BRAVES pic.twitter.com/z7k4EcNIcn — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) August 27, 2026 Kim watched three pitches land outside of the strike zone to put together a three-ball, zero-strike count. But Scott forced a strike looking swing on pitch No. 4 in that sequence. Kim later pounded three straight foul balls. So Kim faced a full count with the game on the line. But he powered through the 97 miles per hour fastball to clinch the victory. Kim lifted the Braves’ record at home to 44-23. Atlanta also raised its record to 78-55, which now has the National League East leader at least 2.5 games behind the Dodgers in the NL race, but remain four games behind the current NL leading Milwaukee Brewers. Manager Walt Weiss has helped put together five wins in the last five games for the Braves. Matt Olson set the tone against the right-handed Sasaki, powering through his fastball on a solo home run blast that topped at 400 feet. Sasaki needed to leave the game early because of a blister discovery on his right hand. Sean Murphy pounded one more homer for the victors, ripping through an 87 mph cutter via Dodgers relief pitcher Eric Lauer that made it 5-3. Los Angeles ultimately tied things up at 5-5 in scoring two runs during the top of the seventh. But Kim got the Braves’ dugout to clear out in euphoria before facing extra innings. articles.title: Why Eagles’ Vic Fangio isn’t worried about Jalen Hurts’ training camp interceptions
articles.summary: The Philadelphia Eagles are gearing up for their preseason finale against the Cincinnati Bengals at Lincoln Financial Field on Friday. The Eagles are looking to head into the new season on a positive note after dropping their first two preseason outings against the Baltimore Ravens and the New En
articles._body: The Philadelphia Eagles are gearing up for their preseason finale against the Cincinnati Bengals at Lincoln Financial Field on Friday. The Eagles are looking to head into the new season on a positive note after dropping their first two preseason outings against the Baltimore Ravens and the New England Patriots. Philadelphia ended its training camp on Wednesday, leaving quarterback Jalen Hurts feeling good about their offseason. While he is still adjusting to the system of new offensive coordinator Sean Mannion, Hurts should be more than ready by Week 1. There have been concerns about the frequent interceptions thrown by Hurts in training camp. He had at least five in their two-day joint practice with the Patriots last week. Defensive coordinator Vic Fangio, however, is not the least bit worried about the former Super Bowl MVP. “He’s learning a new offense. I think he’s trying things, seeing what’s available and what isn’t available. So I don’t think that’s gonna carry over,” said Fangio, as quoted by Eagles reporter Anthony DiBona. Eagles DC Vic Fangio on Jalen Hurts throwing a lot of interceptions in practice: “He’s learning a new offense. I think he’s trying things, seeing what’s available and what isn’t available. So I don’t think that’s gonna carry over.” pic.twitter.com/Bjl5uQsg6t — Anthony DiBona (@DiBonaNFL) August 26, 2026 Philadelphia hired Mannion, prying him away from the Green Bay Packers, to inject fresh ideas, strategic vision, and a modern scheme into an offense that has grown staid in recent years. Hurts, for his part, is aiming to move on after failing to defend their title last season. There will be birth pains with Mannion, but the talented signal-caller will likely figure things out sooner rather than later. ESPN’s Dan Graziano predicted a bounce-back season for Hurts and the Eagles , stating that they are “too good to flop completely.” The post Why Eagles’ Vic Fangio isn’t worried about Jalen Hurts’ training camp interceptions appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles.title: Did the Lakers dodge a Jonathan Kuminga bullet? ESPN personality weighs in
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Lakers missed out on Jonathan Kuminga this week, and at least one ESPN voice thinks that is a good thing. After Kuminga agreed to a two-year, $13 million deal with a player option to join the Minnesota Timberwolves, ESPN Los Angeles host Deondre Hawkins made the case that the Lake
articles._body: The Los Angeles Lakers missed out on Jonathan Kuminga this week, and at least one ESPN voice thinks that is a good thing. After Kuminga agreed to a two-year, $13 million deal with a player option to join the Minnesota Timberwolves , ESPN Los Angeles host Deondre Hawkins made the case that the Lakers are better off without him. “I truly believe the Lakers dodged a bullet by not signing Jonathan Kuminga,” Hawkins said, quickly clarifying that the take had nothing to do with the forward’s ability. Did the Lakers make the smart decision by not signing Kuminga? pic.twitter.com/oaoFwrrgHB — ESPN Los Angeles (@ESPNLosAngeles) August 26, 2026   The concern, instead, was fit. Kuminga is a ball-dominant, athletic scorer, and the question was how he would slot in next to Luka Doncic and Austin Reaves in an offense that already runs through those two. “The Lakers can move forward with the team that they already have constructed and continue to build that chemistry,” Hawkins said. Kuminga reached free agency after Atlanta declined his team option in June , closing a brief stint with the Hawks that followed his messy exit from Golden State. That backdrop fed a second concern, one about motivation. On his new short-term deal, Kuminga enters the season needing to prove himself and angling for a bigger long-term payday. The worry was that such a chase could work against the continuity Los Angeles built this offseason rather than add to it. For Minnesota, Hawkins saw the signing differently, calling it a smart, low-risk move for a team that stays young and adds a high-upside piece. Kuminga is expected to start alongside Anthony Edwards, LaMelo Ball, Jaden McDaniels and Rudy Gobert, giving the Timberwolves one of the more athletic starting fives in the West . That, of course, cuts both ways. Hawkins acknowledged that a Wolves team already built to contend will remain squarely in the Lakers’ path in a loaded conference, Kuminga or not. Whether Los Angeles truly dodged anything will not be settled until the games begin. Kuminga reportedly chose Minnesota’s player-friendly deal over interest from the Lakers, who by some accounts offered more, a decision that says plenty about how he views his own situation. For now, the Lakers appear content to run it back and let the chemistry do the talking. The post Did the Lakers dodge a Jonathan Kuminga bullet? ESPN personality weighs in appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles._body: Todd McShay believes there’s a chance that Arch Manning stays another year at Texas and enters the 2028 NFL Draft. During his appearance on The Ryen Russillo Show , McShay said Manning could play for the Longhorns in 2027 because his family has a history of staying for one extra season. “Let’s back off this expectation that he’s the No. 1 overall pick, and he’s the guy, and this is Texas’ year. Because I got news for you, I don’t even know that the Mannings are looking at this as the swan song at Texas,” Todd McShay said. “There’s a long history of Manning sticking around that extra year that people didn’t think they were going to stick around until they’re right and they feel like they’re ready. I won’t be surprised at all if he’s in the 2028 draft.” [ $19.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage ] Don't be shocked if Arch Manning stays at Texas after this season @DraftKings #DKPartner pic.twitter.com/XCEG8rdSUb — The Ryen Russillo Show (@TheRyenRussillo) August 27, 2026 When it comes to the Manning family, Peyton Manning and Eli Manning , quarterbacks who stayed in college for at least four years. Peyton played for Tennessee and was a starter for nearly all of his four years. Eli played at Ole Miss and redshirted his freshman season before playing the next four years. Todd McShay says the 2027 draft is ‘not a guarantee’ for Arch Manning Arch Manning is entering his fourth season at Texas, but it will be his second year as the starting QB. In 2025, the 22-year-old completed 61.4 percent of his passes for 3,163 yards, 26 touchdowns, and seven interceptions. Manning also rushed for 399 yards and 10 TDs on 92 carries. What McShay said on The Ryen Russillo show echoed what he said on the Brandon Walker College Football Show earlier this month. “I spent a lot of time with Archie, Cooper. Spent time down in Thibodaux, La., talking to the Manning family,” he said. “Like, the 2027 NFL Draft is not, by any stretch, a guarantee that Arch is going to be in it. So that’ll be an interesting storyline.” The expectations are high for Manning heading into the 2026 season. He was recently selected to the Preseason Coaches All-SEC Second Team and is one of the 30 quarterbacks named to the Davey O’Brien Award Preseason Watch List.

articles.title: UNIFIED Artist Management Signs ‘Freaked Out’ Creators Fat Papi and Prodshushy
articles.summary: The trans-Tasman pair are the first signings since UNIFIED Artist Management established its New Zealand office, led by senior artist manager Matt Harvey and announced in May.
articles._body: MELBOURNE, Australia — Breakout Aotearoa New Zealand artist Fat Papi and Perth, Australia producer prodshushy, the team behind the viral hit “Freaked Out,” are now part of the UNIFIED Artist Management roster. The trans-Tasman pair are the first signings since UNIFIED Artist Management established its New Zealand office, led by senior artist manager Matt Harvey , announced in May . “Freaked Out” blew up when it was paired with content themed around summer haircuts, giving Fat Papi his first career entry on the Billboard Hot 100 when it debuted at No. 89, lifting to No. 88. The single has reached No. 55 on the Billboard Global 200 and this week No. 2 on YouTube’s US Top Songs on Shorts. Produced by prodshushy, the track has accumulated over 7 billion views across TikTok and 9 billion views on YouTube Shorts, and propelling Fat Papi to nearly 10 million monthly listeners on Spotify. Fat Papi (real name: Baban Hussain) has been releasing music independently since 2023. The Auckland-based Kurdish rapper, singer and songwriter is behind a distinctive style that blends melodic hip-hop, synth-driven club production, and infectious hooks. “Joining UNIFIED is an exciting next step for shushy and I. Being able to work with Matt and access the backing of the wider team gives me the right mix of independence and support,” comments Fat Papi. “I’m proud to represent both my Kurdish heritage and New Zealand on the world stage, and we’re just getting started.” Prodshushy, Fat Papi, Matt Harvey, Jaddan Comerford UNIFIED Adds Harvey: “Fat Papi is a generational talent whose music has resonated internationally in a remarkably short space of time. ‘Freaked Out’ proved that world-class music originating from New Zealand can break global boundaries without compromise. “Bringing him and shushy into the UNIFIED Artist Management family as our first trans-Tasman management signing since joining forces, sets the standard for what we intend to build here: sustainable, long-term global careers for top-tier local talent.” UNFIED, reads a statement, will provide dedicated global management support for the next phase of their career. The management agreement is announced just days after Warner Chappell Music struck a worldwide publishing deal with Fat Papi and prodshushy.

They looked impressive and menacing, sending a stern warning to the rest of the NBA that the Philadelphia 76ers are raring to wreak havoc. Getting James and Brown instant
articles._body: LeBron James and Jaylen Brown recently went viral after a video of their workout with Tyrese Maxey was posted on social media. They looked impressive and menacing, sending a stern warning to the rest of the NBA that the Philadelphia 76ers are raring to wreak havoc . Getting James and Brown instantly made Philadelphia a heavy favorite in the Eastern Conference. The 76ers have experienced marginal success in the playoffs, but all signs point to a long-overdue breakthrough in the upcoming season. Brett Brown knows all about the arduous journey of the 76ers. He coached Philadelphia from 2013 to 2020, overseeing the so-called “Process Era.” While he failed to bring a title to the City of Brotherly Love, he is still supportive of the 76ers, lauding the arrival of James and Brown. “I think it’s fantastic for the city. I think it’s an endorsement to the players and Nick (Nurse) that LeBron chose them. There’s a lot of great things to be admitted with LeBron’s decision to come to Philadelphia, and Jaylen (Brown)’s trade,” said Brown in a report from Liberty Baller’s Gordie Jones. “It’s real. They’ve got a team that is as good as anybody in the league.” Brown added that he is very excited for Joel Embiid , whom he helped develop into an MVP player. Embiid is the only remaining player coached by Brown in Philadelphia. “It’s an opportunity, maybe the last, that he can do what I know down deep he wants to do, and that’s to be remembered as a champion. There’s a side of me that thinks like that as it relates to my old days with Philadelphia, and Joel especially,” said Brown. Brown tallied a 221-344 record with the 76ers, steering them to three straight appearances in the playoffs from 2018 to 2020. While Brown has returned to the San Antonio Spurs as an assistant coach and senior consultant, it is pretty clear that he will always cheer for the 76ers. articles.title: Mark Mitchell’s Intra-Conference Transfer Reportedly Under Scrutiny by SEC
articles.summary: Kentucky’s pursuit of fifth-year player Mark Mitchell has forced the Wildcats to jump through many hoops. There’s a new twist and turn almost every day. There’s a new wrinkle in this situation, and it doesn’t sound like good news for Mark Pope‘s Wildcats. Mitchell is on
articles._body: Kentucky’s pursuit of fifth-year player Mark Mitchell has forced the Wildcats to jump through many hoops. There’s a new twist and turn almost every day. There’s a new wrinkle in this situation, and it doesn’t sound like good news for Mark Pope ‘s Wildcats. Mitchell is one of numerous athletes from the class of 2022 who sought out an additional year of eligibility through the court system. The former All-SEC talent received a temporary restraining order (TRO) from a Louisville judge last Friday, giving him the green light to enter the transfer portal and find a new school. About 24 hours later, he was committed to Kentucky. In the wake of the NCAA chaos, various conferences decided to take a stand. The SEC created heavy-handed punishments for teams that are considering playing former NBA or NFL players. An SEC spokesperson confirmed that Mitchell did not fit that criteria, allowing the Cats to dodge a bullet, but another has been fired from the league office. CBS Sports’ Matt Norlander reports that Mitchell’s intra-conference transfer is under renewed scrutiny and in doubt after SEC presidents reaffirmed their conference’s policy on intra-league transfers. “From the sounds of it, the SEC is readying to treat Mitchell’s transfer in a secondary/delayed window as falling under the terms of its previously agreed-upon bylaw,” reports Norlander. Violating that rule would result in a half-season suspension for Mark Pope, among other significant financial penalties. SEC presidents reaffirmed their intraconference transfer policy prohibiting players moving within the league outside of the portal, per a copy of a Sankey memo. Violators are subject to (1) half-season suspension; (2) 50% of school’s sport budget; (3) removal of vote privileges. pic.twitter.com/kf4GaBs3Y0 — Ross Dellenger (@RossDellenger) August 27, 2026 Mitchell is not the only notable intra-conference transfer move in the SEC. A pair of former Ole Miss players, TE Dae’Quan Wright and DL Zxavian Harris , received a TRO and announced they will be following Lane Kiffin to LSU. Unlike Denzel Aberdeen , who elected to enter the portal prior to the creation of the 5-for-5 rule, Mark Mitchell did not submit his name to the transfer portal this spring. There’s a simple reason why: He thought his eligibility had expired. “UK will obviously fight for Mitchell to be on the roster and argue the option for him to enter the portal in the spring didn’t exist. Of course, the NCAA doesn’t believe the option should be there period,” Norlander wrote on Twitter . “Mitchell theoretically could be eligible back at Mizzou—or outside the SEC.” Prior to the official addition of Mitchell, there were rumblings that SEC commissioner Greg Sankey would use his power to prevent the intra-conference transfer from happening. It sounds like that process is underway. It’s not great news for Kentucky basketball fans. However, now is a good time to remember that during these silly times, the circumstances can change (for better or worse) in an instant. We’ll continue to closely monitor this developing situation.

articles.title: USC freshmen Luke Wafle, Mark Bowman named starters
articles.summary: USC football released its first depth chart of the season, which included No. 1 recruit Luke Wafle as a starter.
articles._body: No. 1 overall 2026 recruit Luke Wafle was named a starting defensive end among USC football’s initial depth chart on Wednesday evening. Wafle will start opposite of junior edge Kameryn Crawford , who led the team in sacks in 2025. Fellow five-star signee Mark Bowman was also named an outright starter at tight end. Freshman wide receivers Trent Mosley and Kayden Dixon-Wyatt also were named starters. Freshman cornerback Elbert Hill was named OR alongside Chasen Johnson as a starter as well opposite Jontez Williams . The 6-foot-5.5, 255-pound Wafle finished the 2026 cycle as the No. 1 prospect in the Rivals rankings. Wafle turned heads in spring but underwent freshman growing pains. But his work ethic and mentality helped him break through with an impressive summer and fall camp. “No matter what business you’re in, no matter what profession you’re in, you always start with the mindset,” said defensive end coach Shaun Nua in spring. “That young man’s mindset and mentality, his makeup is up there. He’s tough, intelligent and just willing to work. And the thing that you see out there, he’s always putting himself on the line in conditioning, so he’ll give you everything he’s got.” Luke Wafle On3 Scouting Report: The most ready-to-play top EDGE prospect in the 2026 cycle. Measured over 6-foot-5, 255 pounds with arms over 33 inches and big hands prior to his senior season. More physically mature than many of his highly-rated peers. Combines play strength and motor with functional athleticism. Wins at the point of attack with a powerful punch and the ability to convert speed to power. Uses quick power swipes to disengage from offensive linemen. Shows multiple pass-rush pathways and closing speed to finish behind the line of scrimmage. – Charles Power Bowman, Wafle and Mosley were all recently named to On3.com’s preseason true freshman All-American team. Wafle, Bowman were one of three five-star signees via Rivals for USC’s No. 1 ranked 2026 recruiting class. The Trojans opened the 2025 season with one true freshman starter in wide receiver Tanook Hines . Young Offensive Weapons While Luke Wafle ‘s debut as a starter is quicker than expected, Trent Mosley and Mark Bowman were heavy favorites to crack the starting lineup. Kayden Dixon-Wyatt surged in fall camp with veterans Terrell Anderson and Tanook Hines limited. Overall, the trio out of the Trinity League created a ton of buzz, particulary Mosley and Bowman in spring camp and ended high on the projected depth charts. “[Mark] did take tremendous strides. Obviously, he’s got the natural gift of being a willing blocker, plays compact, ability to unlock his hips. But just him investing the time,” said tight ends coach Chad Savage. “So just really breaking down the fundamentals and technique. Dialing in on his footwork, his steps, his hand placement. He’s a kid that’s in my office every single day asking the right questions where he can get better at. And we went over yesterday just an attack list on what we’ve got to really improve on these next few weeks, going into fall camp. He’s got the unique skill set. I think, as his body continues to mature in the weight room, he’s just going to get better and better.” Bowman, who added ten pounds over the summer, was limited in fall camp but returned during mock game week. Bowman was the No. 32 overall prospect and the No. 4 TE in the country via the Rivals Industry Ratings. Dixon-Wyatt ranked No. 56 overall, a late flip against Ohio State. Mosley ranked No. 225 overall. articles.summary: Houston Texans pass rushers Danielle Hunter and Will Anderson Jr. were the biggest reasons Carolina Panthers head coach Dave Canales described Wednesday’s joint practice as a “lopsided” day for his offense. Houston’s defensive front consistently disrupted Carolina’s first-
articles._body: Houston Texans pass rushers Danielle Hunter and Will Anderson Jr. were the biggest reasons Carolina Panthers head coach Dave Canales described Wednesday’s joint practice as a “lopsided” day for his offense. Houston’s defensive front consistently disrupted Carolina’s first-team offense, with Hunter and Anderson making life difficult for quarterback Bryce Young and the Panthers’ offensive tackles. Hunter recorded five “sacks” during the practice, while Anderson added another late in team drills. Canales singled out both players afterward, praising their level of play following a difficult session for Carolina’s offense: “Two words: Danielle Hunter & Will Anderson, I think that’s four words actually. Those guys are fantastic players. That’s exactly what we needed to see. When we dropped back today, we couldn’t really do much. The rush was phenomenal. It was pretty lopsided today, I’ll be honest. If we want to be good, we have to be able to play against teams like this.” Panthers head coach Dave Canales after joint practice vs the Texans: “Two words: Danielle Hunter & Will Anderson, I think that’s four words actually. Those guys are fantastic players. That’s exactly what we needed to see. When we dropped back today, we couldn’t really do much.… pic.twitter.com/IRqHGnDv2q — Houston Stressans (@TexansCommenter) August 26, 2026 Hunter’s production helps explain why the Panthers were unable to contain him. The veteran has garnered 114.5 sacks across 10 NFL seasons, including 15.0 last year. Anderson, meanwhile, has accumulated 30.0 sacks through three seasons, with 12.0 coming in 2025. The Texans also entered the practice with a defense that finished first in the NFL in total defense and second in points allowed last year. articles.title: ESPN analyst puts massive burden on Keelon Russell’s shoulders after QB1 nod
articles.summary: Alabama football turns the page to the Keelon Russell era behind center. Russell beat out Austin Mack for the coveted starting quarterback spot. But now ESPN analyst and one-time NFL executive Louis Riddick placed a massive burden on Russell’s shoulders. Riddick sounded off on the move Wedn
articles._body: Alabama football turns the page to the Keelon Russell era behind center. Russell beat out Austin Mack for the coveted starting quarterback spot. But now ESPN analyst and one-time NFL executive Louis Riddick placed a massive burden on Russell’s shoulders. Riddick sounded off on the move Wednesday during his appearance on First Take. “I don’t think there’s a single player who has more pressure on him in college football this year, to be quite honest with you,” Riddick boldly said. It’s understandable considering how scrutinized the QB position is in Tuscaloosa. Past Crimson Tide quarterbacks dealt with millions of watchful eyes; from Ty Simpson, to Tua Tagovailoa, all the way to even Joe Namath during the era of the legendary Paul “Bear’ Bryant. So Russell enters a room where all eyes even outside of the SEC will be on him. Except Riddick threw out one more obstacle the QB faces. “Because think about it like this: Austin Mack had a relationship with Kalen DeBoer going back to Washington and then transfers to Alabama, so that was Kalen’s guy,” Riddick explained. “That was Ryan Grubb‘s guy. Now Keelon has taken the reins now and they’ve decided this is the guy who’s going to inject a lot of energy, playmaking ability, improvisation into this offense here for 2026. That’s a lot.” Certainly Russell may have altered the relationship between Mack and his aforementioned coaches. But still, Russell has a struggling and questionable offense to ignite ahead of the 2026 season. Especially with Simpson gone.
