articles.title: Colts’ Josh Downs shrugs off Keenan Allen’s impact on his targets
articles.summary: Josh Downs is not sweating the addition of Keenan Allen to the Indianapolis Colts’ wide receiver room. Allen, who is coming off a short comeback stint with the Los Angeles Chargers, arrives in Indianapolis on a one-year, $3.32 million contract. Although his best days are already behind him,
articles._body: Josh Downs is not sweating the addition of Keenan Allen to the Indianapolis Colts’ wide receiver room . Allen, who is coming off a short comeback stint with the Los Angeles Chargers, arrives in Indianapolis on a one-year, $3.32 million contract. Although his best days are already behind him, Allen is still someone expected to draw ample looks downfield from quarterback Daniel Jones. The 34-year-old Allen’s presence could have a significant impact on Downs’ target share, but he is not worried about it . “Nah, coach gon’ handle it how he wants to handle it. So, that’s his responsibility,” the 25-year-old Downs said in front of the media on Wednesday (h/t James Boyd of The Athletic). If anything, Downs could learn a lot even from just being around Allen, who has a wealth of experience in the pros. Allen played 11 of his first 13 seasons in the NFL with the San Diego/Los Angeles Chargers franchise before playing the 2024 campaign with the Bears. He returned to the Chargers on a one-year deal for the 2025 campaign before deciding to take his talents to the AFC South to play for the Colts. So far in his NFL career, Allen has 12,051 receiving yards and 70 touchdowns on 1,055 receptions and 1,552 targets across 171 games. Even at this stage of his career, the former California Golden Bears star wideout can stretch the field and make great plays, and Indianapolis is surely expecting to see that from him in 2026. Downs, meanwhile, is entering just his fourth season in the league. He took a step back in 2025, going from 803 receiving yards in 2024 to only 566 in 2025. articles.title: Former Florida Gators guard Xaivian Lee commits to Gonzaga
articles.summary: Former Florida Gators guard Xaivian Lee, who went unselected in the 2026 NBA Draft but then participated in the NBA Summer League, has committed to Gonzaga.
articles._body: Former Florida Gators guard Xaivian Lee , who went unselected in the 2026 NBA Draft but later participated in the NBA Summer League, has committed to Gonzaga , per Joe Tipton of On3. The 6-foot-3 Lee, a native of Toronto, Canada, played one season for the Gators. He averaged 11.6 points, 4.2 assists and 3.7 rebounds as UF went 27–8, won the SEC regular season championship and was a No. 1 seed in the NCAA Tournament. Lee made 42 percent of his field goals, but only 29.2 percent from 3-point range. Previously, Lee played three seasons at Princetown. As a sophomore, he averaged 17.1 points a game, then followed that up by scoring 16.9 points a contest. Xaivian Lee recently entered the transfer portal Lee announced his plans to enters the transfer portal Aug. 18. Per Nick Kosko of On3, “Lee entered the NBA Draft process earlier this summer and went unselected during the 2026 edition. He agreed to am Exhibit 10 deal with the Cleveland Cavaliers back in June. An Exhibit 10 deal is a one-year, non-guaranteed NBA minimum-salary contract that invites a player to training camp. It is often utilized by franchises to evaluate undrafted rookies along with fringe players and allows them to retain the player’s G League rights if they are waived.” Earlier this year, Lee participated in the NBA G League Combine in Chicago. Lee was not among the  six players invited to the NBA Draft Combine  that week, but he made his mark in the two games he played and tested well in the various workouts. He led his team in assists on both scrimmages.  Lee came off the bench in the first game and recorded eight assists, three rebounds and two points in 20:40 played. He then got the start in his second game and finished with six points, five assists, two rebounds and two steals in 23 minutes. He was one of the top performers in workouts.  In February, Lee played some of his best basketball as a Gator. After a couple strong performances, he was named co-SEC Player of the Week. Lee posted 18 points and seven assists with no turnovers in Florida’s 86-66 victory at Georgia. He scored or assisted on 14 of UF’s 32 field goals in the game (44%). Three days later, Lee scored a team-high 22 points — leading five Gators in double figures — in the 92-83 win over No. 25 Kentucky on Saturday. He made his first four attempts from 3, tying his season high.

articles.title: Recap: Stanford Men’s Soccer rises to No. 1 after win over Denver
articles.summary: On Sunday, Stanford men’s soccer defeated Denver 3-1, rising from No. 9 in the nation to No. 1 as a result.
articles._body: Freshman Logan Tsopanoglou scored two goals for the Cardinal. Credit: GoStanford.com On Sunday, Stanford men’s soccer defeated Denver 3-1, rising from No. 9 in the nation to No. 1 as a result. Jack Pymm scored the first goal for the Cardinal off a penalty kick while Logan Tsopanoglou recorded the first brace of his career, scoring two goals. Bryce Willoughby scored the lone goal of the match for the Pioneers. Rowan Schnebly was the winning goalkeeper for the Cardinal, playing all 90 minutes while totaling one save in addition to giving up one goal. Alex Hohl was the losing goalkeeper for the Pioneers, playing all 90 minutes while totaling 10 saves in addition to the three goals allowed. Stanford improves to 2-0-0 while Denver falls to 0-1-1. BOX SCORE: Denver at Stanford-Sunday, August 23 rd “I must be a really bad coach because we did everything wrong in the first five minutes after my team talk,” Stanford head coach Jeremy Gunn said after the match. “So I’ll take one hundred percent credit for my players not following our instructions in the first five minutes. After that, I thought we played really really well. I thought we did an awful lot right and we were on top for massive parts of the game and so if we can get the script right at the beginning of the game, then we’ll be in good positions. “And so yeah, very frustrated with how we began the game. It was nothing like what we wanted. Just so many really poor mistakes. Really poor decisions. And then after that, I thought we were fantastic and we did everything right. We kept asking questions. Denver got a very very good team and we managed to stay on top for much longer periods than I would have expected before the game. But again, it’s another really exciting game of soccer and regardless of the shots, regardless of the different things, the game was always gonna be in the balance until we got that third insurance goal that then pretty much put us ahead, you know, kept us ahead.” Denver was the first team to strike in this match as Willoughby score at the 5:15 mark, finding the bottom left of the goal off his right foot. Up 1-0, the Pioneers were in a good spot. “Yeah, we came out, I mean, we had the game plan, like turn them around first 10 minutes, put the ball in behind. I think we failed to do that a little bit,” Tsopanoglou said. “I think we came out a little more, little on the back heel a little bit, rather than putting them behind and getting in behind. You know, their goal is a lapse of judgment. Center back played the midfielder a little sloppy pass and they’re in. So, there’s always room for improvement, especially when at the beginning of the game you need to set the tone.” From then on, Stanford would out-play Denver. At 10:28, Stanford got a corner kick before later getting a corner kick at 25:20. Soon thereafter at 32:32, Hugo Berg got a yellow card for Stanford for unsporting. At 34:41, Denver got a corner kick. However, Stanford would be the team to score next at 41:08 as Jack Pymm got fouled inside the box as Alex Hohl was called for a foul, tripping Pymm after going down himself. Pymm would capitalize on the penalty kick opportunity, absolutely burying the goal. 1-1 would remain the score going into halftime. “Oh yeah, I mean, it’s a really important goal because it puts us back on even terms,” Gunn said of Pymm’s strike. “And so, the halftime talk was ok, we’ve got 45 minutes to play with competitive intelligence. And then 45 minutes to go bury them. And so, to get back on level terms before the half was a huge thing because it just meant that we knew exactly what our task was second half.” In the second half, it was time for freshman Logan Tsopanoglou to shine for the Cardinal, but not before five yellow cards were issued combined to Denver and Stanford. To say things got chippy in the second half would be an understatement, though nothing really crossed a line, either. It was just two teams out there to prove that they belonged. “And I think, look, everybody’s energetic and everybody’s fighting for their team right now,” Gunn said of the physicality. “I didn’t see too many moments that were particularly dangerous or of concern for people’s well-being. I think it was a lot of posturing, a lot of bravado, and great college players showing that they mean business and so no concerns as far as that goes.” At 72:10, Tsopanoglou would score for the Cardinal, finding the top left of the goal off his right foot thanks to an assist from Alex Chow . That made it a 2-1 lead for the Cardinal as Human Nature by Michael Jackson filled the stadium, a song that Tsopanoglou chose as his goal-scoring song. “Yeah, it was just like the ball top of the box,” Tsopanoglou said of his first goal. “I found space out wide. Touch. Finish. You know? I mean, it’s an important goal. Especially like, beginning of the season, like, putting us ahead and getting us in a position where we can build on top of it…That was all me [choosing Human Nature]. It’s a great song. I like it.” After two more yellow cards called against Stanford ( Yujin Kikuchi and Trevor Islam ), Tsopanoglou found the back of the net for the second time at 77:47 as Jayden Fitzgerald Boes got credited with the assist. Once again, Human Nature, a song that made Thriller by accident , played in the stadium as the Cardinal now had firm command of the match with a 3-1 lead. There was no accident with the way the Cardinal were playing. They were clearly the better team. “Yeah, Jayden’s high pressing, I’m there for the rebound, he’s poking it, I’m finishing, you know?” Tsopanoglou said of his second goal. “Whoever can get the ball first, putting it in the net and it was me. So after that, 3-1. Pretty much just sealing it. Maybe 15 minutes left. Getting in, making sure, not letting them in behind. Very important. Almost had a goal to make it 4-1. Had it. articles.title: Cameron Brink reveals Nneka Ogwumike’s ‘important’ influence on her development
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Sparks have already been mathematically eliminated from playoff contention this season, but with a handful of games remaining on the schedule, the continued development of Cameron Brink is still a big storyline. The former No. 2 overall pick has battled a couple of injuries this s
articles._body: The Los Angeles Sparks have already been mathematically eliminated from playoff contention this season, but with a handful of games remaining on the schedule, the continued development of Cameron Brink is still a big storyline. The former No. 2 overall pick has battled a couple of injuries this season , but has shown flashes of being the high-impact defensive player the team believed they were getting when they drafted her. But it’s not just defense where Cameron Brink has been making an impact for the Sparks this season. Her offensive game has gotten a bit more refined, and she has continued to grow into a leadership role. The former Stanford star has formed a strong bond with teammate Nneka Ogwumike, a fellow Cardinal alum, and she’s picked up pointers as far as being able to effectively use her voice on the court. “I think Nneka has taught me that you don’t have to say much, but when you speak up, make sure it’s important and people feel included and you’re meeting people where they’re at,” Brink said following the Sparks’ loss to the Atlanta Dream on Monday. “I feel like I still have a long ways to go and I’m still building my confidence in that sense. But I do feel like the more I talk, the more together we feel as a team. So I’m just going to keep leaning on that.” The biggest area where Brink has shown leadership this season is on the defensive end. She’s the Sparks’ anchor in the middle, the rim protector who can clean up when the perimeters players get blown by. The numbers certainly reflect her impact on that end of the court as far as being a lead player. She is averaging 1.7 blocked shots per game, tied with Golden State Valkyries veteran Kiah Stokes for second in the league, and behind only Las Vegas Aces star A’ja Wilson at 2.0. She also holds the best defensive rating on the team at 108. She can be seen using her voice in quick huddles during game stoppage or communicating defensively. This is also the most number of games Brink has appeared in during a single season, at 28 and counting. While she certainly deserves plenty of credit for the work she’s put in, the humble Brink is quick to mention that it wouldn’t be possible without the guidance and mentorship she’s received from Ogwumike. “Nneka, like I said before, has been the most amazing role night and has been the perfect example of coming into practice every day early, doing her work, asking the best questions,” Brink said. “It’s just all the little things, but for me, I think it’s just experience and as time goes by, I’ll get more comfortable.” To date, Brink is averaging a career-best 9.4 points, 5.0 rebounds and 1.5 assists to go along with her blocks. She’s shooting 50 percent from the field, 33.3 percent from the 3-point line and 76 percent shooting from the free-throw line. The Sparks have only six games left in their season, and during that final stretch, all eyes will certainly be on Brink as she continues to solidify herself as one of the team’s building blocks of the future. articles.title: Australia’s CORE Talent Agency Launches With Teen Jesus, Budjerah & More
articles.summary: CORE operates as part of the broader UNIFIED Music Group ecosystem, and is led by co-general managers, Desiree Venuto and Adam Montgomery.
articles._body: MELBOURNE, Australia — A new artist booking specialist opens for business in the land down under, CORE Talent Agency. The agency is founded by Jaddan Comerford , CEO of UNIFIED Music Group, and Regan Lethbridge , co-founder of Lemon Tree Music, and emerges from Lonely Lands Agency (LLA), which Tash Sultana established with the pair back in 2019 . CORE operates as part of the broader UNIFIED Music Group ecosystem, and is led by co-general managers, Desiree Venuto and Adam Montgomery and boasts a roster that includes Teen Jesus and the Jean Teasers, The Terrys, Budjerah, Day We Ran, Emma Donovan, South Summit, Slowly Slowly, DEVAURA and others. It’s mission: to focus on established independent Australian artists, as well as some of Australia and New Zealand’s “most exciting up-and-coming talent,” reads a statement, with its artists enjoying access to UNIFIED’s experience, infrastructure and connections. Venuto joined LLA in 2019, and has been namechecked in The Music Network’s 30 Under 30 and Pollstar’s Impact International Next Gen Honorees lists, while Montgomery is an experienced professional who led boutique booking agency Four Tone Artists, representing the likes of Bec Sandridge, Didirri and Mia Dyson. CORE’s dedicated launch team includes LaBelle Jackson, Victoria Kozbanis and Jo Syme . “We are thrilled to officially unveil CORE. Having been a part of this journey since its inception, it is incredibly rewarding to step into this new role to lead the next iteration of the agency,” comments Venuto. “Artist creativity has always been our foundation, and we are stepping forward with a unified team backed by decades of shared industry expertise.” Adds Montgomery: “Partnering with Desiree to lead this next chapter is a true career highlight. CORE is built around putting the artist at the heart of every decision, and we’re excited to bring this fresh energy into each conversation. “With the support of Comerford and Lethbridge, he continues, “we’re eager to champion our incredible roster and continue to expand our community.” Visit cta.live for more.

articles.title: Harry Moore Launches Independent Australian Booking Agency Lowtide
articles.summary: At launch, the Lowtide roster includes Tones And I, Ocean Alley, Hockey Dad, The Cat Empire, Brad Cox, Boy & Bear, and others.
articles._body: MELBOURNE, Australia — Harry Moore is back in business with Lowtide, his new independent booking agency. The Australian agent previously served as general manager at Lonely Lands Agency (LLA), where he led the team to deliver over A$50 million dollars in ticket sales for local artists across 2024-25, reps say. Lowtide’s ethos is to focus on an “artist first” model, one that keeps the roster small to allow that focus and strategy on helping the artists reach grand goals, Moore explains. “I want to create a culture that positions artists and their needs at the forefront of the approach to their touring,” he tells Billboard . “There’s a difference between agents who fill dates to hit budgets and agents who move like business strategists working along side the artist and management to create long term, sustainable careers that culminate in steady growth. I want the culture at Lowtide to reflect the latter.” At launch, the Lowtide roster includes Tones And I, Ocean Alley, Hockey Dad, The Cat Empire, Brad Cox, Boy & Bear, and others. “At certain times,” Moore continues, “saying no and letting an opportunity go is the most powerful step towards growth. I also want to be known as a fair operator when it comes to my dealings with the rest of the sector. We need venues and promoters to survive and thrive so artists can do the same.”  Moore’s new business emerges from LLA, formed in 2019 by artist Tash Sultana , UNIFIED Music Group CEO Jaddan Comerford and Lemon Tree Music co-founder Regan Lethbridge . LLA is no longer an active brand, Billboard understands, with Comerford and Lethbridge this week announcing their new, separate agency, CORE. “My philosophy for Lowtide is artists first, with a quality-over- quantity approach; music is so personal, the business side of it should be too,” Moore continues. Visit lowtideagency.com for more.

articles.title: Sparks’ Cameron Brink calls out ‘stupid piece of s***’ Enes Kanter for WNBA stunts
articles.summary: Los Angeles Sparks center Cameron Brink joined the growing list of athletes and personalities calling out former NBA player Enes Kanter for his controversial stunts involving the WNBA. Kanter was recently removed from the game between the Chicago Sky and the Indiana Fever at Wintrust Arena for ha
articles._body: Los Angeles Sparks center Cameron Brink joined the growing list of athletes and personalities calling out former NBA player Enes Kanter for his controversial stunts involving the WNBA. Kanter was recently removed from the game between the Chicago Sky and the Indiana Fever at Wintrust Arena for having a heated exchange with Natasha Cloud. Kanter, who purposely wore a provocative shirt, earned more backlash following the incident. Brink did not hold back on Kanter when she was asked about the issue surrounding transgender athletes . “I don’t even know what the f*** his name is. Enes Kanter. He’s a stupid piece of s***,’ said Brink in the video posted by The Mirror US’ Jarrod Castillo. “I think a lot of people think that, and I think he’s just trying to stay relevant.”   View on Threads   Kanter first grabbed attention after making a video declaring himself eligible for next year’s WNBA Draft because he identifies as a woman. He has been banned by the Sky from going to Winstrust Arena . The 24-year-old Brink stressed her support for transgender athletes, suggesting that all the recent noise should be tuned out. “Personally, I think when it comes to the trans issues, I think it’s a non-issue, and I think it’s people trying to just come for the trans community, and I just don’t stand for that,” said the third-year center. Aside from Brink, New York Knicks forward Mikal Bridges, Milwaukee Bucks forward Kyle Kuzma, and former NFL player Torrey Smith also slammed Kanter for his questionable behavior. articles.title: NFL Owners Remain Confident About Roger Goodell Extension
articles.summary: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images
articles._body: ATLANTA — NFL team owners did not discuss commissioner Roger Goodell’s pending contract extension during their meeting Wednesday but remain confident they will complete a deal with him in the coming months. “That’s going to get done,” a source told Front Office Sports at the meeting, which was conducted at a hotel near the Atlanta airport. “I have no doubt.” An owner told FOS afterward the topic was not discussed during the meeting. “Nothing on that,” the owner said. The owners’ next scheduled meeting comes in October in New York. FOS reported last month the owners are confident they will reach an agreement with Goodell on an extension in the coming months. His current contract expires in March 2027, when he will be 68. The owners, who first elected Goodell commissioner in 2006, agreed to a three-year extension with him in October 2023. Many owners feel it is important to keep Goodell in place for the upcoming negotiations for a new collective bargaining agreement with the NFL Players Association, which could include an 18-game season and new broadcasting deals. Mahomes has been recovering from the torn knee l
articles._body: Kansas City Chiefs head coach Andy Reid made the final call Wednesday on quarterback Patrick Mahomes’ status for Friday’s preseason finale against the Seattle Seahawks at Arrowhead Stadium, with the two-time MVP set to remain sidelined . Mahomes has been recovering from the torn knee ligaments he suffered on Dec. 14, 2025. Although he has participated throughout the offseason program and training camp, Friday will be the first preseason in his entire career in which he does not appear in a game. His previous missed preseason came in 2020, when the NFL canceled all exhibition games. The Chiefs have consistently expected Mahomes to remain out during this year’s preseason, with his focus now on returning for the regular season. Kansas City opens its regular season against the Denver Broncos in a Monday night matchup on Sept. 14, which is expected to be the 30-year-old’s first game action since his injury. With Mahomes unavailable, Reid also indicated that Justin Fields is unlikely to play against the Seahawks. Instead, rookie Garrett Nussmeier is set to receive the starting assignment and could handle the entire game. Nussmeier, selected No. 249 overall in the seventh round of the 2026 NFL Draft, has taken first-team offensive reps during practice this week while Mahomes has worked with the scout team. The rookie completed 13 of 19 passes for 98 yards against the Los Angeles Rams in the preseason opener before going 9-for-17 for 74 yards against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers last week. He has yet to throw a touchdown pass, but he has also helped produce the Chiefs’ only touchdown of the preseason. Chris Oladokun remains in concussion protocol and is ruled out, removing another quarterback option for Friday. If he cannot return, Nussmeier could play all four quarters, with Fields available if an injury forces a change. Reid also did not confirmed whether wide receivers Rashee Rice and Xavier Worthy will play. Rice is returning from offseason knee surgery , while Worthy has been dealing with a shoulder injury suffered during training camp. Running back Kenneth Walker III is also unlikely to play after missing practice time because of a swollen ankle. articles.title: Florida transfer guard Xaivian Lee commits to Gonzaga
articles.summary: Former Florida guard Xaivian Lee is officially headed back to college basketball. After going undrafted in the 2026 NBA Draft and spending the summer with the Cleveland Cavaliers, Lee has committed to Gonzaga, according to On3’s Joe Tipton, giving Mark Few another experienced playmaker for the
articles._body: Former Florida guard Xaivian Lee is officially headed back to college basketball. After going undrafted in the 2026 NBA Draft and spending the summer with the Cleveland Cavaliers , Lee has committed to Gonzaga , according to On3’s Joe Tipton , giving Mark Few another experienced playmaker for the upcoming season. The veteran guard participated in the NBA Summer League in Las Vegas but will instead return to the college ranks after entering the transfer portal. His decision gives Gonzaga one of the most accomplished guards available, while providing Lee another opportunity to boost his NBA stock. $19.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage Earlier this summer, Lee signed an Exhibit 10 contract with Cleveland shortly after going undrafted in June, earning an opportunity to compete during Summer League. Across five appearances with the Cavaliers, the 6-foot-3 guard averaged 6.4 points, 2.0 rebounds and 2.4 assists in 16 minutes per game while shooting 40% from the field. However, his outside shooting never quite found a rhythm. Lee connected on just 21.4% of his 3-point attempts during Summer League while posting a minus-1 plus-minus across his five contests. Although he showed flashes as a facilitator and playmaker, the performance ultimately wasn’t enough to keep him on the NBA track for now. Instead, Lee will return to the college game after one season at Florida. He transferred to Gainesville last offseason following three standout years at Princeton , where he established himself as one of the Ivy League’s premier players.  Lee earned back-to-back First Team All-Ivy League honors and became the first player in Princeton history to record a triple-double before making the jump to the defending national champions. That’s what Gonzaga will be expecting with his addition.  While sharing the ball with a veteran Florida roster, Lee averaged 11.6 points, 4.2 assists and 3.7 rebounds per game. His 147 assists led the Gators, while his 2.4 assist-to-turnover ratio ranked among the SEC’s best as Florida captured the SEC regular-season championship and earned a No. 1 seed in the NCAA Tournament. Prior to arriving at Florida, Lee showcased his ability as a primary offensive option at Princeton. During his junior season with the Tigers, he averaged 16.9 points, 6.1 rebounds and 5.5 assists while emerging as one of the nation’s most versatile guards. NBA evaluators have praised Lee’s offensive creativity, court vision and ability to create shots off the dribble. However, questions surrounding his size, defensive consistency and outside shooting contributed to him going undrafted this summer. Now, Lee will look to answer those questions at Gonzaga. The Bulldogs have developed a reputation for preparing experienced guards for the professional ranks. With this decision, Lee will have another opportunity to showcase his offensive skill set in one of college basketball’s premier programs.  After taking his shot at the NBA, he’ll return to Spokane with hopes of leading Gonzaga on another deep postseason run while improving his draft stock for 2027. Time will tell if he’s successful in his quest.  To keep up with the latest players on the move, check out On3’s Transfer Portal wire . The On3 Transfer Portal Instagram account and X (formerly Twitter) account are excellent resources to stay up to date with the latest moves.

articles.title: Packers’ Tucker Kraft is fired up for the season after brutal practice hit
articles.summary: The future is once again bright for Green Bay Packers tight end Tucker Kraft, as he appears to be on track to play in Week 1 of the 2026 NFL season after suffering a devastating lower-body injury in the middle of the 2025 campaign. Kraft tore his ACL during a Week 9 matchup against the […]<
articles._body: The futu re is once again bright for Green Bay Packers tight end Tucker Kraft , as he appears to be on track to play in Week 1 of the 2026 NFL season after suffering a devastating lower-body injury in the middle of the 2025 campaign. Kraft tore his ACL during a Week 9 matchup against the Carolina Panthers at Lambeau Field in Green Bay last season, ending what could have been a historic year for him. No Green Bay tight end has ever recorded at least 1,000 yards in a season, and Kraft had a shot at becoming the first one to do it until he got injured. Several months later, Kraft is working out and practicing again with the Packers. He was activated off the physically unable to perform (PUP) list last July. Kraft is even already taking big hits in practice . “He got me good… I was smiling,” the former South Dakota State football star tight end told reporters about the big hit that rocked him in Wednesday’s practice (h/t Dave Schroeder of WBAY-TV). “That was a good hit. I haven’t had any contact like that since November 2nd. That was an opportunity for me to wake up. Season’s here!” Kraft, still waiting for an extension contract offer from the Packers , was taken by Green Bay in the third round of the 2023 NFL Draft. After recording 355 receiving yards and two touchdowns in his rookie campaign, he took a big step forward with 707 receiving yards and seven touchdowns in 17 games in 2024. The 2025 season was supposed to be his best yet in the league, as he racked up 489 receiving yards and six scores in eight games before the injury. articles.title: Tennessee Court of Appeals puts fifth-year eligibility for 2022 HS class on hold
articles.summary: In the latest development in a multi-layered case, the Tennessee Court of Appeals has temporarily blocked a lower-court ruling that had allowed a group of basketball players from the high school class of 2022 to return for a fifth season. This is the second legal victory for the NCAA after the Oh
articles._body: In the latest development in a multi-layered case, the Tennessee Court of Appeals has temporarily blocked a lower-court ruling that had allowed a group of basketball players from the high school class of 2022 to return for a fifth season. This is the second legal victory for the NCAA after the Ohio Court of Appeals granted a motion to stay an injunction in a similar lawsuit a few days ago. As the case proceeds through the process, the group of over 20 plaintiffs covered by the lower-court ruling is again considered ineligible unless the Tennessee Court of Appeals ultimately rules in their favor. Some of them are Tennessee’s Jalen Washington, UNLV’s AJ Storr, North Carolina’s Cameron Fens, Oklahoma’s BJ Edwards, Houston’s Chendall Weaver, and Indiana’s Sam Alexis. Sports journalist Sam Ehrlich obtained a copy of the decision of the Tennessee Court of Appeals, describing the NCAA’s motion as an “appropriate case for an extraordinary appeal.” “After considering all the relevant factors and, in particular, the NCAA’s likelihood of success on the merits based on the legal issues presented, we conclude that the trial court’s August 19, 2026 order denying a stay pending appeal constitutes an abuse of discretion,” read the ruling. “It is, therefore, ordered that the application for an extraordinary appeal is granted.” The Tennessee Court of Appeals has issued an order staying the injunction granted to the plaintiff athletes pending appeal. As with Ohio, those players are now ineligible unless and until the Court of Appeals rules in their favor. pic.twitter.com/l6LdAGCYj2 — Sam C. Ehrlich (@samcehrlich) August 26, 2026 The NCAA recently announced a five-year, age-based model, but it does not retroactively apply to the high school class of 2022, which has prompted college athletes across the country to challenge the policy through judicial means. The legal fight is part of a growing dispute over how the NCAA should handle college athletes who exhausted their traditional eligibility before its new five-year, age-based model takes effect, not to mention the increasing number of ex-professional athletes returning to college sports. articles.title: Za’Darius Smith Returns to Football After Tragic Loss
articles.summary: Za'Darius Smith abruptly retired last season to spend time with his mother before she passed. It wasn't his only loss, either.
articles._body: “I wasn’t supposed to retire,” Za’Darius Smith said on Wednesday. “I said I wasn’t going to tell the story, but I’m going to tell it.” The former Wildcat, one of Mark Stoops ‘ first star players at Kentucky, abruptly announced his retirement five games into the 2025 season with the Philadelphia Eagles. Plenty of tread was worn off the tires of the 33-year-old, but it looked like he still had some good football left to play. When you learn why Za’Darius Smith stepped away from football, it all makes sense. “I got a phone call from my mom’s doctor telling me that she don’t have much longer to be on this Earth. So I let the team know. Obviously, they wasn’t trying to let me leave, but that was the only thing I had left — to retire. So I retired.” His mother was losing her fight with cancer. He needed to spend her final days by her side. That’s when things got even worse. “Dealt with that. After losing my Mom, I lost my Grandma. Then after my Grandma, I just lost my Dad. So y’all obviously know what I’ve been through,” he said. Heartbreaking. Gut-wrenching. Unimaginable. Za’Darius Smith’s infectious smile has captivated fans since he was a Wildcat. It was hard for him to find that smile after suffering so much loss. When the Cleveland Browns called him this offseason, he decided to see if he could still bring it to the gridiron. Even though he couldn’t agree to terms with Cleveland, his former coach in Cleveland, Kevin Stefanski, was ready to see if Atlanta could be the right spot, one that could bring back his smile. “I see this as my happy place,” Smith said while holding back tears. “But yeah, this is my happy place. Come back, play football. I was in a dark place, but, you know, coming out, running out on the field, the fans — not only just the fans, man, the joy that I get from winning and just getting sacks.” Atlanta is not too far from his hometown in Montgomery. Smith is working to get a pair of Greyhound buses to bring his mother’s “church family” 2.5 hours to Atlanta for Falcons home games. “My mom — rest her soul, man — she always wanted me to be in Atlanta with the Falcons,” Smith said. It’s been a trying year, but he’s rediscovered joy ahead of his 12th NFL season. That joy will turn into jubilation when the Pro Bowler finds his way back into the backfield. “When I retired, I had 70 sacks. Now, I’m trying to reach a hundred. Any way I can get to it would be good,” he said. “But man, I’m happy to be back. This is my happy place. I’m ready to get going.” One of the most moving press conferences I've ever been a part of…. Za'Darius Smith retired in 2025 during his 11th NFL season, just five games after signing with Philadelphia, for personal reasons. Today he shared those reasons. Very emotional and said his mom always wanted… pic.twitter.com/d94v3QD3yT — Kinsey Lee (@kinseyleetv) August 26, 2026

articles.title: Dodgers’ Roki Sasaki exits Braves game after medical staff examines his pitching hand
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Dodgers watched Roki Sasaki get red-hot after the MLB All-Star break. The pitcher took to the mound against the Atlanta Braves courtesy of manager Dave Roberts. But he exited Wednesday’s game with an MLB Injury scare. Team trainers and fellow Dodger teammates attended to Sas
articles._body: The Los Angeles Dodgers watched Roki Sasaki get red-hot after the MLB All-Star break . The pitcher took to the mound against the Atlanta Braves courtesy of manager Dave Roberts. But he exited Wednesday’s game with an MLB Injury scare. Team trainers and fellow Dodger teammates attended to Sasaki at the hill. Sasaki sustained a blister on his right hand, his throwing hand. He wound up leaving in the fourth inning with LA up 3-2. Sasaki also left with runners on third and second base. Roki Sasaki is leaving the game with a trainer due to what appears to be a blister pic.twitter.com/23vhTFZFCB — SleeperDodgers (@SleeperDodgers) August 27, 2026 Sasaki ended his night pitching in 3.1 innings. He allowed six hits total, including one home run to Matt Olson, who pounded a 400-footer over to right field that put the Braves up early 1-0. But Sasaki made up for the costly homer by forcing a ground out and strikeout in the next two at-bats. Sasaki even turned to the rare forkball pitch twice, both hitting 87 and 89 miles per hour. But the right-hander came after the Braves with a concoction of different pitches. He trusted his four-seam fastball the most in firing off four pitches there. Sasaki turned to the splitter three times to close out the bottom of the first. He struck out two more batters while allowing four runs. Los Angeles and the National League East leader locked into a an offensive showcase especially after Sasaki left. Atlanta and LA exchanged leads and ultimately, entered the seventh inning tied up at 5-5. Tommy Edman powered one home run for the defending World Series champs. He, Shohei Ohtani and Freddie Freeman all powered two hits through seven innings. articles.summary: Jonathan Kuminga bet on flexibility when he chose the Minnesota Timberwolves. Gilbert Arenas believes the free agent may have sacrificed far too much to make that bet. Kuminga agreed to a two-year contract worth $12.4 million, with a player option for the second year. Minnesota presented him with
articles._body: Jonathan Kuminga bet on flexibility when he chose the Minnesota Timberwolves. Gilbert Arenas believes the free agent may have sacrificed far too much to make that bet. Kuminga agreed to a two-year contract worth $12.4 million, with a player option for the second year. Minnesota presented him with an opportunity to start beside Anthony Edwards, LaMelo Ball, Jaden McDaniels, and Rudy Gobert while competing in the Western Conference. That vision convinced Kuminga to reject interest from the Los Angeles Lakers, Chicago Bulls, and Portland Trail Blazers. The Lakers reportedly offered more than $12 million per season across three years through a potential sign-and-trade. Kuminga instead selected a shorter arrangement that could return him to free agency next summer. This man Just signed a podcast Deal Johnathan Kuminga i can make you a better offer (Dont sign) and u do GilsArena with me (Kuminga Arena) #soundsaboutright @playmaker Meet me at his house and bring the check book pic.twitter.com/s8e3ZZsFlz — Gilbert Arenas (@NoChillGilZero) August 27, 2026 Gilbert Arenas Questions Kuminga’s Contract Arenas could not understand why Kuminga accepted such a modest salary and mocked the agreement in a video posted to X. “This man Just signed a podcast Deal,” Arenas wrote before claiming he could present Kuminga with a better offer. The former NBA guard even proposed a “Kuminga Arena” partnership on his Gil’s Arena show and jokingly asked Playmaker to meet him at Kuminga’s home with its checkbook. Minnesota invested effort into landing the sixth-year wing. Edwards participated in the recruiting campaign, while team president Tim Connelly traveled to Miami for a four-hour meeting with Kuminga. The forward also spoke with coach Chris Finch as the Timberwolves offered their taxpayer midlevel exception and a role. The franchise must now create the necessary roster space. Minnesota can pursue a trade involving reserve wing Josh Green or waive and stretch his contract before Saturday’s deadline. Kuminga clearly prioritized opportunity and future control over long-term security. Arenas, however, sees a player accepting podcast money for an NBA starting job. Now he is fulfilling another dream: calling a game for the New York Mets. On Wednesday, Breen said to the SNY Mets crew that calling a game for them was
articles._body: Legendary sports broadcaster Mike Breen has done it all and seen it all. In June, Breen called the Knicks’ title run , fulfilling a dream. Now he is fulfilling another dream: calling a game for the New York Mets. On Wednesday, Breen said to the SNY Mets crew that calling a game for them was on his “bucket list,” per SNY Mets. “I love that booth,” Breen said. “It’s one of the great booths of all-time.” Mike Breen says it's a "bucket list" moment for him to be in the booth for part of tonight's Mets game: "I love that booth. It's one of the great booths of all-time." pic.twitter.com/PetadI0gR0 — SNY Mets (@SNY_Mets) August 26, 2026 Breen was in the booth calling a game at Citi Field in New York against the Milwaukee Brewers. Gary Cohen and Keith Hernandez joined him. During the broadcast, Breen said Hernandez intimidated him while doing radio broadcasts in 1986 for WNBC radio, per Andrew Battifarano of The New York Post. He referred to Hernandez as “Mr. Hernandez.” Currently, Breen is the play-by-play announcer for the NBA on ESPN. He has called NBA games for 30+ years for ESPN, NBC, ABC, and has called Knicks games. Breen has established his place amongst the greats with his signature line, “Bang!” after every big shot. He also did play-by-play for WNBA games on NBC from 1997 to 1999. Additionally, Breen has set a record for calling 21 NBA Finals. Meanwhile, the Mets’ organization has had its litany of broadcasters over the years. Lindsey Nelson was in the booth calling their miracle run to the World Series in 1969. Other names include Ralph Kiner, Bob Murphy, and Howie Rose. The current announcing team includes Gary Cohen, Keith Hernandez, and Ron Darling. They are the longest-running broadcast team in franchise history. Breen is a native New Yorker and grew up a huge Mets fan. The post Mike Breen shares heartfelt admission about joining booth appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles.title: Brewers’ Christian Yelich reveals why Pat Murphy actually benched Cooper Pratt
articles.summary: The Milwaukee Brewers made headlines on Tuesday night when rookie infielder Cooper Pratt was benched against the New York Mets. Pratt hit a pop fly to the outfield that eventually fell for a hit. He made it to first safely, but was pulled immediately after reaching base. Some have questioned why
articles._body: The Milwaukee Brewers made headlines on Tuesday night when rookie infielder Cooper Pratt was benched against the New York Mets . Pratt hit a pop fly to the outfield that eventually fell for a hit. He made it to first safely, but was pulled immediately after reaching base. Some have questioned why Pratt was pulled from the game. The rookie infielder appeared to run hard and ensure he made it to first. Some have theorized that manager Pat Murphy wanted him to end up on second. Veteran outfielder Christian Yelich believes this was more about culture and how Murphy coaches than anything else. “You couldn’t coach that way throughout the league. You really couldn’t. There’s a lot of players that wouldn’t accept that. It’s easier to get buy-in because of the amount of games we’ve won and how we’ve won,” the Brewers outfielder said, via MLB.com. For what it’s worth, Murphy did confirm that he felt Pratt should’ve tried for the extra base. But he also said that this play wasn’t the only thing that led to the rookie infielder’s benching against the Mets. “I think a ball that was up there that long, and hit [the ground] and kicked [away], you have to be on second. Then I was ticked about the bunt thing, and there’s a couple of other things that add to all of this that I don’t need to get into. But if you lived in the clubhouse, you would understand it,” Murphy said. The Brewers ended up falling to the Mets on Tuesday night. That loss marked their second straight defeat, and has Milwaukee looking for a way back in the win column. Let’s see how Pratt and his teammates respond against New York on Wednesday night. articles.title: Kansas football announces five team captains for 2026
articles.summary: Kansas football has selected five team captains for the 2026 season. The captains were chosen through a vote by their teammates.
articles._body: Kansas football has selected five team captains for the 2026 season. The captains were chosen through a vote by their teammates. It was announced tonight that Trey Lathan , Cole Ballard , Rino Monteforte , Calvin Clements and Blake Herold are the captains. Trey Lathan — Linebacker Lathan enters his second season at Kansas after transferring from West Virginia. The redshirt senior was one of the defensive standouts last year starting all 12 games and leading the Jayhawks with 86 tackles. He added seven tackles for loss, 1.5 sacks, five pass breakups, and an interception. He earned All-Big 12 honorable mention honors. Lathan was named to the Butkus Award preseason watch list this season. Cole Ballard — Quarterback Ballard, originally was a walk from Westfield, Indiana. He has played each of the last three seasons and as backup quarterback. He got his game action freshman in 2023 against Texas Tech and Kansas State. Ballard appeared in eight games in 2025, completing 10 passes for 108 yards and a touchdown. Rino Monteforte — Long Snapper Monteforte is in his first season at Kansas but brings experience from the Power Four level. The redshirt senior spent the 2025 season at California, where he was the long snapper and appeared in all 13 games. Before Cal, Monteforte spent three seasons at Notre Dame. He was the Fighting Irish’s primary long snapper in 2024, playing in all 16 games during their run to the national championship game against Ohio State. Calvin Clements — Offensive Line Clements is a Lawrence native and one the most experienced players on the KU offensive line. The 6-foot-7, 325-pound redshirt junior started all 12 games at left tackle in 2025 after appearing in all 12 games during the 2024 season. Clements played at Lawrence Free State and was rated among the top prospects in Kansas coming out of high school. Blake Herold — Defensive Tackle Herold is one of the veterans on the Kansas defensive line and is roommates with Clements. The Iowa native played in all 12 games in 2024. Last year he was sixth on the team with 43 tackles, including five tackles for loss and two sacks.

Bodycam footage of the scene shared by TMZ shows the 46-year-old York looking surprised after being approached by police while in his vehicle. The arrest was made after he arrived at the location where he and a fake prostitute agreed to meet up. Before that, York allegedly responded multiple times to a fictitious prostitution ad. York, who was wearing a Yankees shirt and basketball shorts during the arrest, was seemingly cooperative with police. He was placed in handcuffs and taken to the police car. Body cam of Jed York's arrest shows stunned 49ers owner. https://t.co/rjSYBSbrgF : East Palestine Police Dept pic.twitter.com/PZr8EXnk91 — TMZ (@TMZ) August 26, 2026 Asked what he was doing in the area, York simply answered: “just driving.” Police also found cash in York’s vehicle. He’s got a s**t ton of cash,” an officer was heard in the footage saying. “It’s crazy the people that do this,” another said. “They could do whatever they want. They could do other things. The 49ers released a brief statement on York’s arrest , acknowledging what happened and saying they will review the incident under the personal conduct policy. articles.title: Jed York Absent From NFL Owners’ Meeting
articles.summary: Sergio Estrada-Imagn Images
articles._body: ATLANTA — 49ers principal owner Jed York, who was arrested last weekend in a prostitution-related case in Ohio, did not attend Wednesday’s NFL owners’ meeting at an airport hotel in Atlanta. York was not spotted at the meeting, and his absence was confirmed to Front Office Sports by a source familiar with the matter. Al Guido, the CEO of the 49ers, attended the meeting, which isn’t unusual for him. However, he was the 49ers’ primary representative because of York’s absence. York was not the only primary owner of an NFL team missing from Wednesday’s meeting. But his absence was particularly noticeable because he faces possible disciplinary action by the NFL under its personal conduct policy. “It’s being reviewed under the personal conduct policy,” NFL commissioner Roger Goodell said of his arrest following the meeting. “And we’ll do that. And when there’s something to be reported, we’ll [comment further].” Several owners declined to discuss the situation as they left the meeting. “We’ll leave that to the league to handle,” one owner told FOS . The 2026 version of the personal conduct policy for league and non-player club employees says: “Ownership and club or league management have traditionally been held to a higher standard and will be subject to more significant discipline when violations of the Policy occur.” One source familiar with the NFL’s inner workings told FOS this week that York could spend some time away from the 49ers. York, 46, posted a $5,000 bond and was released on his own recognizance after pleading no contest to charges of disorderly conduct and possessing criminal tools, according to Columbiana County, Ohio, court records. York spent one day in jail and was fined $1,150, plus additional court fees. An initial filing said that York was arraigned for “engaging in prostitution.” The East Palestine, Ohio, police made the arrest, along with the Mahoning Valley Human Trafficking Task Force. The post Jed York Absent From NFL Owners’ Meeting appeared first on Front Office Sports .

articles._body: The pursuit of Jonathan Kuminga has finally come to an end , with the Minnesota Timberwolves getting their guy in free agency. Teams like the Cleveland Cavaliers, Los Angeles Lakers, and LA Clippers were all rumored to be interested in Kuminga, but the Timberwolves ultimately came out on top. Kuminga is expected to sign a two-year, $13 million with the Timberwolves. He did, however, have a multiple year offer from the Lakers. According to ESPN , Kuminga had a three-year, $12 million deal on the table from the Lakers. Kuminga chose the Timberwolves over offers from the Lakers, Bulls and Trail Blazers — bypassing a similar starting role and $12M-plus annually over three years in L.A. to land in Minnesota for a shorter-term deal and an ability to have more control of his future, sources said. Jonathan Kuminga was traded to the Atlanta Hawks from the Golden State Warriors last year at the February 2026 trade deadline. He played 16 games for Atlanta, averaging 12.3 points, 5.3 rebounds, 2.1 assists, and 0.9 steals per game. Kuminga’s best year of his career came during the 2023-24 season, where he averaged 16.1 points, 4.8 rebounds, and 2.2 assists. Now on the Timberwolves, Kuminga is expected to immediately slot into a starting role with Donte DiVincenzo out due to a torn Achilles tendon. Kuminga will slot into the frontcourt alongside Anthony Edwards, LaMelo Ball, Jaden McDaniels, and Rudy Gobert. Kuminga’s two-year deal is structured to have a player option for next offseason so he can test free agency in the event he has the career year he’s hoping to have. articles.title: Why Jonathan Kuminga makes Timberwolves a legit NBA Finals contender
articles.summary: The Minnesota Timberwolves were already poised to be championship contenders in the West, but they got a little bit better on Wednesday. They signed Kuminga to a two-year, $13 million contract with a second-year player option. This adds to an offseason of transition for the Timberwolves, as they
articles._body: The Minnesota Timberwolves were already poised to be championship contenders in the West, but they got a little bit better on Wednesday. They signed Kuminga to a two-year, $13 million contract with a second-year player option. This adds to an offseason of transition for the Timberwolves, as they made major acquisitions, including their blockbuster trade for All-Star point guard LaMelo Ball early in the offseason. In the NBA, the name of the game is always depth. You look to build a team that can withstand the grind of an 82-game schedule, but also deploy enough talented players to contend against the best teams in the NBA. Gone are the days of top-heavy teams or a squad led by only one star. The Timberwolves, led by general manager Matt Lloyd and team president Tim Connolly, built the perfect roster around the ascendant talent of Anthony Edwards. With LaMelo Ball, he can now play his natural position of shooting guard, as Ball inherits main playmaking responsibilities. With Ball as the Timberwolves’ point guard and his success in a fast-paced offensive system with the Hornets, it would only be wise for Minnesota to add athletic forwards and bigs who can benefit from Ball’s passing. That’s why Kuminga joining the team fortifies their contending chances. Kuminga found himself in limbo following a tumultuous future with the Golden State Warriors. Although he was immensely talented, he often found himself out of the lineup for the Dubs. This led many to wonder about his future in the NBA before the Atlanta Hawks acquired him at the trade deadline in February. There, he showed his potential for a playoff-contending team, averaging 12.3 points, 5.3 rebounds, and 2.1 assists while shooting 47% from the field, 37.6% from the three-point range, and 34.6% from three-point range. Questions then arose about his future as he hit free agency once again. He sat on the market until late August, hoping for not only a huge payday but an organization where he could contribute effectively. The question was never his game, but the circumstances around it. With the Timberwolves, just like with the Hawks, he has the opportunity to change the narrative. Kuminga brings not only athleticism but championship experience. In his rookie season with the Warriors, he contributed to the team winning the 2022 NBA Championship over the Boston Celtics, becoming the second-youngest player to win an NBA Championship, only to former Detroit Pistons big man Darko Miličić. Even at 23, he’s seen a lot of good basketball and, in organizations such as the Warriors, has built a winning culture. He’s also used to the bright lights and the big moments, which the Timberwolves can certainly use on their roster as they look to break through and make the NBA Finals this season. There’s nowhere to go but up for the Minnesota Timberwolves as Edwards enters the prime of his career. They did everything that they were supposed to following their playoff run this spring, and they built a better roster that can survive a tough Western Conference dominated by the San Antonio Spurs and the Oklahoma City Thunder. Barring injury, the Timberwolves will certainly be one of the top six teams in the West and could find themselves in the Western Conference Finals once again for the third time in four years. Kuminga can only add to that potential. The post Why Jonathan Kuminga makes Timberwolves a legit NBA Finals contender appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles.title: Everything South Carolina STC Matthew Smiley said in his first press conference of 2026 season
articles.summary: South Carolina special teams coordinator Matthew Smiley spoke with the media for the first time this preseason on Wednesday.
articles._body: South Carolina special teams coordinator Matthew Smiley spoke with the media for the first time this preseason on Wednesday. Here’s everything he had to say. How is the kicking competition going? “It’s going good. All those guys are working their butts off, and we’re getting up a bunch of reps. So it’s been good to watch all of them compete and grow. It’s been a good competition up to this point.” How would you assess how things went with the kickers in game-like situations when you guys are out there scrimmaging? “We try to put them in as many game-like situations as we can. There are periods where we’re just field goal versus field goal block, and you’re getting just rep after rep after rep. But coach (Shane Beamer) has been great, whether it’s a two-minute drive, different situations where they have to be up and ready. We’ll even sneak them reps between periods when it’s just snapper, holder, kicker run out, just in an effort to get them in front of the team as much as possible and to get them as much of those types of reps as possible. And they’ve been doing a good job with those.” Who are some of the main guys that will factor in on kick return? “We actually did kick return today. Got a lot of good work, and we got a few guys back there catching it, and all those guys looked good today. I checked the film out real quick before I came in here. Got to dive back into that, but there’s three or four guys that are that were back there getting work and look comfortable catching the ball.” Questions about this story? Jack Veltri is discussing it with subscribers on The Insiders Forum. When do you want to have a leader for the kicking competition, or has one already emerged? “I don’t think there’s a timeline. I think kickers are different than if you were figuring out a starting quarterback. We haven’t established, and in talking to coach, there haven’t been conversations of, ‘Hey, this is the date, this is the guy.’ We’re letting those guys compete and really letting it unfold in front of us. And as guys start to say, ‘Hey, this is my job,’ and move ahead, letting that happen naturally.” You mentioned kind of the next step for Vicari Swain was being comfortable catching every ball. Is that something that you’ve seen progress from him so far? “Yeah, he’s doing a great job. Yesterday, we did — we call it ‘sky’ — it’s the short punt situation. So the returners got a lot of that work just with gunners and just him working his decision-making back there, his catching, his all the other stuff we’re talking about, the decoy stuff when I’m fair catching it, he did a great job yesterday. He continues to be real good back there and real comfortable, which is nice. He’s working hard.” Have you in your career experienced something where you guys had multiple kickers that you were trying out using maybe some of the reps of the kicks in season to try to determine who ends up being the one relied upon in a tight game? “Have I ever been involved in a kicker competition? Yes, I have been. Usually in the NFL, it’s two guys; it’s not three guys that are getting some reps, just because your roster is not as big. But definitely been involved with that. You would really not like to use game reps because that means that whoever you sent out there didn’t stay out there. But we’re all about scoring points, so I think, and I’m sure Coach (Shane Beamer) would echo this. At any position, it’s not like, ‘Hey, there’s your starting fill in the blank, and the backup is never going to see the field the whole year.’ So it doesn’t matter who goes out there for the first extra point. The rest of the guys are working their butt off to compete because we’ve got to keep scoring points.” How are things going with the long snapper battle? “Long snappers, short snappers, they’ve been doing a great job. Without getting into too many details about what they got going on in punt, they’ve really embraced both the accuracy of short snapping and long snapping and the coverage aspects in punt, that kind of thing. So those guys have been doing a real good job. And that’s nice to see with those long snappers because sometimes it’s tough when you have a kicker battle if your long snappers are not pulling their weight, because those kickers are on the edge of their seats for every rep. The snappers have done a great job. Mason Love is the holder. They’ve been serving up good snap holds to those kickers as those kickers compete to fight for that spot.” Overall, with the kicking competition, do you feel like things have progressed the way you would have wanted them to when you came into the preseason? “For me, it’s here’s the situation, here’s today. Let’s see how today works out, and then let’s make good decisions for tomorrow. So it sounds a little bit like a cop-out answer, but that’s the truth.” If you had to, would it be a possibility to have one kicker for shorter field goals and one kicker for longer field goals? Would you entertain that? “Definitely entertain it. Now, when you’re talking about, let’s call them, 56-57, end of half, end of game, now potentially that could be a specialty guy, and then you get into the conversation where what’s the percentage of your specialty guy, let’s call it 59 yards, as opposed to is a Hail Mary as an offensive play better? articles.title: NFL Eliminates Pro Bowl Game, Adds Player-Accountability System
articles.summary: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images
articles._body: ATLANTA — The NFL and its players collaborated on two significant developments unveiled Wednesday. The league eliminated its Pro Bowl game and implemented a player-accountability system that will result in an automatic one-game suspension for any player who violates specified safety rules three times this season. The NFL scrapped the Pro Bowl after years of searching for ways to make the game more competitive and more appealing to fans. Most recently, the league converted the event to a flag football game, accompanied by skills competitions. “I think we’ve been focused on the game,” NFL commissioner Roger Goodell said at the completion of a one-day owners’ meeting at an airport hotel in Atlanta. “You’ve heard me say it for many years about the quality of the game in the Pro Bowl: I don’t think it’s up to NFL standards.” The league will continue to select and honor Pro Bowl players. It said it will choose 88 Pro Bowlers annually, without having to name replacements as it did in previous years when players withdrew from game participation. This season’s Pro Bowl players will be honored next year with a celebration in Los Angeles, the NFL said. “I think this is something that we talked to our players about, the Pro Bowl players in particular,” Goodell said. “We had conference calls the last couple years: ‘What’s working? What’s not? What would you like to see?’ And the number one thing that came out… is: ‘We want to be honored and celebrated as a Pro Bowl player.’… It just opened my eyes. I never really thought about it in the context of that. It’s not honoring the replacement players. It’s honoring the guys who are selected by the fans, by the players, by the coaches.” Players were adamant that they could not play in a competitive all-star game following the completion of the season, according to Troy Vincent, the NFL’s executive vice president of football operations. “They made that extremely clear on our calls and our discussions: ‘When our playoff run is over, our season ends. I don’t want to compete anymore,’ ” Vincent said. The NFL said it remains committed to supporting flag football, although that format no longer will be on display in the Pro Bowl. “That was really the core of it, is: How do we do this in the right way?” Goodell said. “And our players, you know, they did what they normally do. They had great recommendations on how to do that.” Player Accountability The NFL and the NFL Players Association also announced their new accountability system in a joint statement. Under it, a player who violates player-safety rules three times this season will automatically be suspended for one game. Players will have the right to appeal any fines for infractions to hearing officers jointly appointed by the NFL and NFLPA. Under the new system, any player who commits only one violation this season will have half his fine from that infraction refunded at season’s end. The player-safety violations covered by the new system include hip-drop tackles; horse-collar tackles; launching; illegal hits on players considered defenseless, such as a quarterback throwing a pass or a receiver in the process of making a catch; and illegal blindside blocks. “The accountability is really the discipline process,” Goodell said. “We’re not looking to fine [players]…. We want to change behavior to make the game safer and have players using the proper techniques. And when they don’t, we need to address that.” The league and union said in their joint statement that they’d worked on the new system for “the last several months.” Team-by-team player representatives for the NFLPA were briefed and voted to approve the new system Tuesday. Owners were told about it during Wednesday’s meeting. “We also wanted to get the union’s perspective: How can we do this the right way?” Goodell said. “Plus we’re obligated and feel it’s the best way to do it, within the context of collective bargaining. So it was a really healthy process. Listen, I think probably both sides would probably say, ‘This might work better or this.’ But we made an agreement that let’s try this. Let’s learn from it. And we’ll sit down and look at it at the end of the year.” The system is designed to punish repeat offenders and help one-time offenders. According to a source on the players’ side, an average of about $1.7 million would have been returned annually to players if this system had been in effect in recent seasons. About 250 players would have qualified for a refund annually, based on the last two seasons. One player would have been suspended in each of the past two seasons under this system. The system is in effect for this season only and then will be reevaluated. “Just to see if it works,” Vincent said. The post NFL Eliminates Pro Bowl Game, Adds Player-Accountability System appeared first on Front Office Sports .

articles.title: Cardinals’ Michael Wilson gets brutally honest about Keisean Nixon beef
articles.summary: Arizona Cardinals wide receiver Michael Wilson has never really seemed like the type of player who craves the spotlight. He generally keeps a low profile, choosing to stay out of the social-media frenzy that surrounds professional athletes. For that reason, Wilson’s apparent feud with Green
articles._body: Arizona Cardinals wide receiver Michael Wilson has never really seemed like the type of player who craves the spotlight. He generally keeps a low profile, choosing to stay out of the social-media frenzy that surrounds professional athletes. For that reason, Wilson’s apparent feud with Green Bay Packers cornerback Keisean Nixon is all the more interesting. The two players seemingly don’t see eye to eye, and their dislike for one another appears to go beyond the usual on-field competition. That was really hard to miss during Wednesday’s joint practice at Ray Nitschke Field. After Wilson made a first-down catch, Nixon held on while finishing what amounted to a practice tackle. The two exchanged words, leading to players from the sidelines to move toward the confrontation. The session featured several other scrums and extended exchanges between the Cardinals and Packers. When asked about his relationship with Nixon, Wilson didn’t hold back. “Me and him got a little bit of beef going back to my second year in the league. Every time I see him – I’m not going to say it’s smoke – but not too fond of him and I don’t think he’s too fond of me. I’ll just leave it at that,” he said following Wednesday’s practice per Arizona Sports’ Tyler Drake. That apparent history traces back to Arizona’s 34-13 loss to Green Bay at Lambeau Field in Week 6 of the 2024 season. Wilson caught two passes for 21 yards and a touchdown, while Nixon recorded three tackles and a pass breakup. The latest confrontation comes as both players enter important stages of their careers. Wilson is heading into his fourth NFL season after producing the best campaign of his career in 2025, when he logged 78 receptions for 1,006 yards and seven touchdowns. He is expected to have an expanded role under new head coach Mike LaFleur. Nixon, meanwhile, finished with 72 tackles, 17 passes defensed and one interception this past season. The veteran has developed from an All-Pro return specialist into a regular defensive contributor since joining the Packers in 2022 and is competing to retain his starting position. The Cardinals and Packers will meet again Friday at Lambeau Field in the preseason finale. The post Cardinals’ Michael Wilson gets brutally honest about Keisean Nixon beef appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles.title: 10 Days to Go: Kentucky gives fans another inside look at Fall Camp
articles.summary: Celebrate Kentucky Football being 10 days away with another behind-the-scenes video from fall camp.
articles._body: We are just 10 days away from Kentucky Football’s season opener. I’ve got the perfect way to celebrate: more behind-the-scenes footage of fall camp. Kentucky just released the All-Access video from the third week of camp. In it, we get to see Stein talk to the team on three different occasions, highlights from practice and the second scrimmage, and interviews with Brandon Roberts, UK’s Director of Football Sports Performance, and Devin Harris, Director of Football Performance Nutrition. Freshman wide receiver Prince Jean also shares his takeaways after a practice, raving about the “explosive plays” and “great team ball.” It’s hard to take much from the very short clips of action other than we’re beyond ready for the season to begin — especially after hearing Stein’s pep talks. “There are only so many opportunities in this game to play this game,” Stein says at a practice. “And when it’s over, fellas, it’s over. You ain’t putting the pads on anymore once it’s done. So, remember that. What would young you think about you playing at UK? You’d probably be pretty freaking fired up.” In the film room later on, Stein thanked the team for responding to his criticism of their first scrimmage, even mentioning redshirt freshman Nic Smith, who died in June , as a reminder to seize the moment. “Nothing is guaranteed. Take the field with a certain energy and enthusiasm, passion, love of just life. That’s real. That’s real. Nic was on my mind, Big Happ, and I want you guys to know nothing has been guaranteed. “Talk about reflection. We talked about that the other day. I’m very proud of this group based on the reflection we had as a team after scrimmage one. I straight up told you guys that was not good enough, and the way you guys attacked this week was elite. We had a great Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday. We had a great one. We had an elite Friday yesterday. You guys are rolling. Take that energy into today. articles.title: Sonny Gray’s strong season draws ‘savant’ admission
articles.summary: The Boston Red Sox took a chance on Sonny Gray last offseason, acquiring the veteran in a trade with the St. Louis Cardinals. Boston believed there was still some juice in his arm. And to this point, he has proven the Red Sox front office correct at every turn. Red Sox pitching coach Andrew Baile
articles._body: The Boston Red Sox took a chance on Sonny Gray last offseason, acquiring the veteran in a trade with the St. Louis Cardinals . Boston believed there was still some juice in his arm. And to this point, he has proven the Red Sox front office correct at every turn. Red Sox pitching coach Andrew Bailey appeared on MLB Network Radio on Wednesday when Gray was brought up. Bailey, a former MLB pitcher in his own right, had massive praise for his veteran hurler as he navigates an incredible season. “The communication between innings… He’s a savant. He retains information very well. And he knows exactly what pitch he threw to each guy in the first, second, and third at bat. He can just tap into that at any point in time,” Bailey said on Wednesday. It’s certainly hard to argue with the results. Gray has a record of 16-3 with a 2.79 ERA on the year this season. He has earned the win in three of his last four starts, as well. The veteran doesn’t strike out many hitters, fanning just 123 batters to this point. But he limits runs and gives his offense a chance to take control of the game. The Red Sox have benefited from his performance in a big way. Boston entered play on Wednesday with a record of 73-59. They own the second Wild Card spot in the American League. And they have the best run differential in the AL with a plus-105 margin. Gray has played a pivotal role in getting Boston into playoff contention. If can continue this into October, the Red Sox could be a very tough team to beat. articles._body: The Cleveland Guardians were seemingly on the verge of falling out of postseason contention a few weeks ago. However, Cleveland has now earned seven consecutive victories following its 4-3 win against the Los Angeles Angels in Anaheim on Wednesday. Steven Kwan has been one of the best hitters in baseball recently, as he had five hits in Tuesday’s 8-6 victory and added a clutch RBI double on Wednesday. “Saying that out loud feels pretty good,” Kwan said of the Guardians sweeping their road trip (Cleveland went 6-0 on its road trip in Colorado and Anaheim), via GuardsTV. “Just got some good momentum right now. We got to keep that rolling.” The American League is weak and the Guardians are heating up . This Cleveland ball club may have an opportunity to make a deep postseason push . The pitching has been respectable for the most part this season, but the offense has been the question mark. With that being said, the lineup has figured something out in August. The Guardians are beginning to not just get runners on base, but they are finally driving those runners in. As mentioned, Kwan had a clutch RBI double with runners on first and second base on Wednesday. His big hit occurred in the 9th inning with Cleveland trailing 4-3. Kwan tied the game, but he may have ended up with the go-ahead RBI as well had the ball not bounced over the right field fence for a ground-rule double. We're so back. #GuardsBall pic.twitter.com/sLjsrnPbcB — Cleveland Guardians (@CleGuardians) August 26, 2026 Kwan’s “Beaver brother” Travis Bazzana (Kwan and Bazzana both played their college baseball at Oregon State) followed Kwan’s double with the go-ahead sacrifice fly and the Guards did not look back. “I mean, I gotta look out for my Beaver Brother right there, right,” Kwan said. The Guardians are playing quality baseball right now. They will look to keep things going back in Cleveland on Friday night against the Kansas City Royals. articles.title: Big 12 joins SEC, Big Ten in banning pro players from returning to school
articles.summary: Following the trend of former pro players returning to college, the Big 12 has joined other Power Five conferences in banning the move. The conference issued a statement outlining its new rule on Wednesday evening. Official statement from the Big 12 Conference. pic.twitter.com/QWiHdvoZ4N —
articles._body: Following the trend of former pro players returning to college, the Big 12 has joined other Power Five conferences in banning the move. The conference issued a statement outlining its new rule on Wednesday evening. Official statement from the Big 12 Conference. pic.twitter.com/QWiHdvoZ4N — Big 12 Conference (@Big12Conference) August 26, 2026 “ The Big 12 has unanimously adopted a conference rule barring Big 12 member institutions from fielding professional athletes in any conference-sponsored sport. No member institution may roster an athlete who has, at any time: Declared for the draft or supplemental draft of a professional sports league and did not timely withdraw before the draft; Been listed on the roster of a professional sports league; or Signed a contract with any professional sports league to provide athletics services. This rule will apply independently of the status of NCAA eligibility determinations.” A court order granting a fifth year of eligibility to athletes from the 2022 class has thrown the NCAA into chaos, and two names now sit at the center of it: Dae’Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris. Both players left NFL training camps, Wright with the Cleveland Browns and Harris with the New Orleans Saints, to re-enter the NCAA transfer portal with intentions of joining Lane Kiffin’s roster at LSU, reuniting with their former coach, who they played for at Ole Miss. The ruling stems from a broader eligibility dispute. Athletes from the 2022 class, including Wright, played out four college seasons and turned pro under the assumption their eligibility was exhausted. That changed when the NCAA rolled out a new age-based model in June, allowing athletes up to five years of eligibility within a five-year window, a policy that left the 2022-23 class out of its coverage and set the stage for the current legal battle. articles.summary: "She's coming to Nashville and I'm going to go see her," the Oscar-winning actress says of the pop singer's current Red Bottoms Tour.
articles._body: Nicole Kidman may have needed a second to place the name, but once a fan mentioned Adéla ‘s upcoming song titled after her, the Oscar-winning actress was all in. At the London premiere of Practical Magic 2 on Wednesday (Aug. 26), Kidman was asked by a fan whether she knew Adéla, the Slovak singer/songwriter whose rapidly rising pop career is about to get an especially Kidman-esque addition. Related Adéla On Supporting KATSEYE From the Start, What She’s Learned From Beyoncé & More | Spotify Best New Artist Party 2026 Nicole Kidman Is 100% ‘That Girl’ in Ultra Glam Video For Troye Sivan’s ‘She’s the Best’ Single Nicole Kidman Didn’t Make It to That Bonkers Playoff Game, But She Sure Loved Este Haim’s Custom ‘Knickole Kidman’ Knicks T-shirt “Do you know who Adéla is?” the fan asked in a video. “No!” Kidman initially replied. After the fan explained that Adéla is a singer with a song called “Nicole Kidman,” however, Kidman’s memory quickly kicked in. “Oh, yes! She is! I do know!” Kidman exclaimed. “I think she’s Slovakian, right?” When the fan confirmed that the singer was “amazing,” Kidman doubled down on her fandom and revealed she may soon be seeing Adéla herself in concert. “I absolutely know who she is and she’s coming to Nashville and I’m going to go see her,” Kidman said. The timing couldn’t be better for the ascending, pink-haired pop star. Adéla is set to release her debut album, PRIMA , on Sept. 4, and the newly revealed 11-song track list includes “Nicole Kidman” as its second track. The project will also feature her breakout single “Ain’t in LA,” which became her first entry on the Billboard Hot 100 , debuting at No. 85. Adéla is currently bringing the PRIMA era to fans on her Red Bottoms Tour, which stops off in Nashville on Sept. 21 at The Basement East. According to Adéla Instagram fan site @adeladiary, the pop singer reacted to Kidman’s kind words later Wednesday, commenting: “WOW OH MY GOD NICOLE WOW OH MY GOD HOLY SH– WOW.” As for whether the actress has heard the song that bears her name? That’s a question the fan didn’t get to ask. But with PRIMA on the horizon, maybe Kidman will soon be able to report back. Watch the full video below.
