articles.title: Who are the players leaving Valkyries for FIBA World Cup?
articles.summary: With the FIBA World Cup break less than a week away, Golden State Valkyries coach Natalie Nakase revealed when the players committed to their national teams will head overseas to Germany in preparation for the international tournament. “They will be with us till New York,” Nakase said
articles._body: With the FIBA World Cup break less than a week away, Golden State Valkyries coach Natalie Nakase revealed when the players committed to their national teams will head overseas to Germany in preparation for the international tournament. “They will be with us till New York,” Nakase said before the front end of the Valkyries’ back-to-back with the Connecticut Sun and New York Liberty. As a result, the Valkyries will be without All-Star Gabby Williams, Cecilia Zandalasini and Sixth Player of the Year frontrunner Janelle Salaun for their Aug. 30 game against the Portland Fire, their final game before the break. Williams and Salaun will represent France on the French national team, while Zandalasini will represent Italy on the Italian national team. Nakase, who will head overseas as one of Team USA’s assistant coaches under Kara Lawson, will maintain her coaching duties right up to the break. It’s awkward timing for the Valkyries and the rest of the league, given that the WNBA will only have a handful of regular season games left to play before the postseason starts after coming back. But Nakase does not seem worried that the break may potentially disrupt their momentum and rhythm, pointing to how the Valkyries have planned for this eventuality. “It’s only going to interrupt it if you allow it to,” Nakase said earlier this week. “We planned it. I’ve been through it with the Olympics when I was with Vegas. I can’t remember exactly the amount of games that came after, but it’s only going to be interrupted if you don’t plan for it. So our leadership plan for it, and we do a good job communicating if there are any hiccups.” Justine Willard-Imagn Images Opportunities for the end of the bench While the Valkyries will only be missing their international players for just one game (presuming they return right after the break), they’ll still be without a combined average of 63.5 minutes and 36.0 points. That makes for ample opportunity for the end of the Valkyries’ bench, namely rookie Juste Jocyte. The fifth overall pick in the 2025 WNBA Draft hasn’t been able to crack Nakase’s rotation yet, appearing in only 11 games this season, mostly in garbage time. Nakase has emphasized that while Jocyte continues to do well in the “stay ready” scrimmages the reserves at the end of the bench participate in, the Valkyries coach said the 20-year-old is still growing and that her development “won’t happen overnight.” Jocyte, who was the subject of several trade rumors in a potential package for Kelsey Plum around the trade deadline, has maintained a day-by-day approach to the lack of playing time. “You start asking yourself questions, doubting yourself even a little bit,” Jocyte told the SF Chronicle. “But for me, it’s just having the right people around me to lead me in the right direction and just comforting me when I need to. So I’ve been dealing, of course, with some thoughts and everything, but just trying to go day-by-day.” With the postseason on the horizon and the Valkyries still chasing a top-three seed, the Fire game may be the last time Jocyte plays meaningful minutes this season. Developmental players Miela Sowah and Ashten Prechtel are also positioned to see some more playing time, as the two are expected to be activated for every game for the rest of the season. articles.title: Kylian Mbappe records hat trick for Real Madrid vs. Real Sociedad
articles.summary: Real Madrid forward Kylian Mbappe scored a hat trick to lead Los Blancos to a 4-1 win over Real Sociedad at the Santiago Bernabeu on Wednesday, giving new manager Jose Mourinho two victories from his first two matches back in charge of the Spanish club. Mbappe, who had not scored in Madrid’
articles._body: Real Madrid forward Kylian Mbappe scored a hat trick to lead Los Blancos to a 4-1 win over Real Sociedad at the Santiago Bernabeu on Wednesday, giving new manager Jose Mourinho two victories from his first two matches back in charge of the Spanish club . Mbappe, who had not scored in Madrid’s 2-1 win over Espanyol last weekend, opened his account for the season five minutes before halftime. Federico Valverde supplied the pass, with the French forward evading his marker before curling a beautiful left-footed finish into the top corner. However, Real Sociedad responded just three minutes later, with Luka Sucic restoring parity before the interval after Job Ochieng’s lackluster effort was blocked, leaving the rebound at his feet. Real Madrid regained control after the break. Jude Bellingham, who provided two assists, combined with Valverde before setting up Mbappe for his second goal. The striker then completed his hat trick in the 80th minute after Vinicius Junior supplied a perfectly weighted pass, with Mbappe lifting the ball over goalkeeper Alex Remiro. A HAT TRICK FOR KYLIAN MBAPPE, ASSISTED BY VINI JR. pic.twitter.com/jmrNGInJIs — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) August 26, 2026 Mbappe’s three goals came in the 40th, 60th and 80th minutes, producing an unusual pattern of one goal every 20 minutes. Vinicius also found the net as Madrid added a third goal before Mbappe completed his treble. A determined Bellingham won the ball back inside Real Sociedad’s penalty area after his initial effort was blocked, before calmly teeing up Vinícius for a simple tap-in. The result moved Real Madrid to two wins from two under Mourinho, whose return to the Bernabeu had been closely watched. His previous spell as Madrid coach lasted from 2010 to 2013. The hat trick added to Mbappe’s impressive LaLiga scoring record. He finished as the league’s top scorer with 31 goals during his debut campaign in Spain and followed that with 25 goals last season. He also entered the match as the 2026 World Cup’s leading scorer after recording 10 goals in the tournament, including a hat trick in the third-place match. Up next, Madrid will face Malaga on Sunday at the Bernabeu. The post Kylian Mbappe records hat trick for Real Madrid vs. Real Sociedad appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles.title: Astros share huge Carlos Correa injury return update
articles.summary: It’s been a while since Houston Astros fans saw Carlos Correa take the field. He suffered an injury back in May that has kept him sidelined for nearly four months. However, there is a chance the veteran infielder is back on the field sometime soon. Astros manager Joe Espada was asked about
articles._body: It’s been a while since Houston Astros fans saw Carlos Correa take the field . He suffered an injury back in May that has kept him sidelined for nearly four months. However, there is a chance the veteran infielder is back on the field sometime soon. Astros manager Joe Espada was asked about Correa’s injury status on Wednesday. He expressed optimism about his progress in rehabbing the injury. In fact, he went so far as to say that he could return next month if things continue on this track. “Carlos Correa’s attempt at a comeback is progressing so seamlessly that Houston Astros manager Joe Espada said on Wednesday he expects Correa ‘to be ready to go at some point in September,'” The Athletic’s Chandler Rome reported on Wednesday. Correa was initially thought to be lost for the entire 2026 season . He underwent surgery in May shortly after tearing peroneus brevis tendon in his left ankle. However, the veteran infielder has made a heroic attempt to stage a comeback late in this season. His comeback attempt couldn’t come at a better time, either. The Astros are fighting tooth and nail for a playoff spot this October. They are in a tense battle with the Texas Rangers for first place in the American League West. The teams are separated by just half a game. The Seattle Mariners are also in the conversation, sitting three games back of Houston for first place. The Astros could use all the help they can get down the stretch. Houston is treading water well enough, but they will eventually need to create some separation. Perhaps Correa’s return is the spark they need to truly establish themselves as the best in the AL West. articles.title: Gov. Landry: SEC ‘Creating a Legal Mess’ Over Athlete Eligibility
articles.summary: Dale Zanine-Imagn Images
articles._body: As a potential legal battle between LSU and the SEC looms , Louisiana Gov. Jeff Landry has issued a statement in LSU’s defense. “This whole thing is ridiculous. Don’t hate the player, hate the game,” Landry said in a statement to Front Office Sports on Wednesday afternoon. It’s hardly the first time the governor has involved himself in a controversy surrounding the Tigers athletic department. But it is the first time he has publicly commented on the SEC’s subsequent attempt to block LSU from signing two football players who participated in NFL preseason activities. “I’ve been saying for a year that college sports need to be fixed. The NCAA could have done it. Congress could have done it. Neither did,” Landry said. “Now the SEC is creating a legal mess over athletes it told were out of eligibility, only to change the rules afterward. The SEC accepted the courts’ decisions on Diego Pavia and Trinidad Chambliss. Why is this different? You can’t tell athletes their college careers are over, watch them move on, change the rules later, and then punish them for not predicting the future.” The situation Landry was referring to began this summer, when the NCAA implemented a new age-based eligibility policy offering players five seasons of eligibility—but excluding players who entered college in 2022 and had already completed four years. Many of these players sued for a fifth year. In one case last week, a Louisiana judge ruled that several of these players could return to college football despite having signed NFL contracts, appeared on NFL rosters, and participated in preseason activities. LSU has since said it would sign two of those players—Dae’Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris. But on Tuesday, the SEC attempted to block LSU from doing so by implementing a policy preventing professional athletes from returning to SEC schools. Despite the announcement, Wright’s representative, Darren Heitner, told FOS Wright’s camp still believes LSU intends to sign him. Meanwhile, attorneys leading the lawsuit were planning to take additional action to ensure the temporary restraining order would apply to the SEC as well as the NCAA. (LSU has not yet commented.) I asked Louisiana Gov. Jeff Landry’s office for his perspective on the pending battle between LSU and the SEC. His full statement: “This whole thing is ridiculous. Don’t hate the player, hate the game. I’ve been saying for a year that college sports need to be fixed. The NCAA… — Amanda Christovich (@achristovichh) August 26, 2026 Landry, for his part, has taken an interest in the success of LSU football. Last fall, Landry hosted a meeting that resulted in the firing of former LSU football coach Brian Kelly. He then effectively forced out former athletic director Scott Woodward and gave his blessing to Lane Kiffin and his $91 million contract when the Tigers landed the former Ole Miss coach. Landry also hand-picked current LSU president Wade Rousse, who reportedly voted Tuesday night in favor of the SEC’s new policy but abstained from voting Wednesday on the harsh penalties the conference suggested. In his statement, Landry did not address whether he had advised Rousse directly on this matter. Landry’s comments come as the college sports world waits on LSU’s next move—and as other conferences have begun to discuss and pass similar policies, most recently the Big 12. A spokesperson for the SEC did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The post Gov. Landry: SEC ‘Creating a Legal Mess’ Over Athlete Eligibility appeared first on Front Office Sports .

articles.title: DeWanna Bonner joins Angel Reese, Atlanta after Mercury buyout
articles.summary: The Atlanta Dream have added a veteran forward to help their playoff push. Per a report by ESPN’s Alexa Philippou, DeWanna Bonner has signed with the Dream on a prorated max, which Philippou says comes to about $116,000. The move coincides with Bonner’s desire to compete for a champio
articles._body: The Atlanta Dream have added a veteran forward to help their playoff push. Per a report by ESPN’s Alexa Philippou, DeWanna Bonner has signed with the Dream on a prorated max, which Philippou says comes to about $116,000. The move coincides with Bonner’s desire to compete for a championship as her career nears its end. “At this stage of my career, I don’t know what the future holds, but I’m grateful to the Mercury for giving me the opportunity to play in what could be one of my final postseason opportunities,” Bonner said in a quote obtained by The Athletic. “The fans, this community and the Mercury organization have embraced me throughout my career, and I’ll always be grateful for that. Being part of this franchise has given me so many incredible memories, and Phoenix will always be a special part of my career.” Bonner’s career has spanned three franchises and two decades, beginning when Phoenix took her fifth overall in the 2009 draft. Her decade with the Mercury produced two championships, in 2009 and 2014, along with three All-Star selections and three Sixth Player of the Year honors. A sign-and-trade sent her to Connecticut in 2020, where she spent five seasons adding three more All-Star appearances and guiding the Sun to four semifinal runs and a 2022 Finals berth that ended in a loss to Las Vegas. Indiana signed her to a one-year deal after that stretch, though she was waived just nine games in. Bonner found her way back to Phoenix from there, closing out last season as part of the Mercury’s trip to the 2025 WNBA Finals , where the Aces swept them to claim the title. Now, as the Mercury are out of playoff contention, Bonner looks to contribute her veteran experience to an Atlanta Dream team that had a strong regular season and aims to build on that success in the upcoming postseason. articles.title: Dodgers’ Dave Roberts sets ‘trending’ date for Shohei Ohtani’s pitching return
articles.summary: It appears that Los Angeles Dodgers two-way superstar Shohei Ohtani is close to making his return to the mound in the big leagues. Ohtani is said to be on schedule to have a bullpen session before a potential start in the upcoming series against the Detroit Tigers (h/t Jack Harris of the Californ
articles._body: It appears that Los Angeles Dodgers two-way superstar Shohei Ohtani is close to making his return to the mound in the big leagues. Ohtani is said to be on schedule to have a bullpen session before a potential start in the upcoming series against the Detroit Tigers (h/t Jack Harris of the California Post). “Shohei Ohtani update: Dave Roberts said he will actually throw his bullpen on Friday, in anticipation of a possible start Sunday (Ohtani usually throws his bullpens two days before starts),” Harris shared via a social media post on X (formerly Twitter) on Tuesday. “They’ll see how his ‘pen goes, but he’s definitely trending toward starting Sunday.” It has been nearly two months since the last time Ohtani had toed the rubber for the Dodgers. His most recent MLB mound appearance was during a start versus the San Diego Padres at Dodger Stadium on July 4. He pitched for six innings in that contest, allowing three earned runs on seven hits with nine strikeouts in a 4-3 victory. Ohtani hasn’t been cleared to pitch since that Padres start as he’s dealt with knee and biceps issues. In the event that Ohtani will not be able to give it a go on Sunday against the Tigers at Comerica Park in Detroit, Tyler Glasnow, who has also just recently returned, is going to take the starting duties , according to Harris. Otherwise, Glasnow will be pitching in relief of Ohtani, who will only be given an inning to pitch. On the season, the 32-year-old Ohtani has an 8-2 record with a 1.79 ERA through 14 starts. articles.title: Jay Wheeler’s ‘De Lejitos’ Gets Up Close With No. 1 on Latin Airplay: ‘Fills Me With Great Pride’
articles.summary: Plus, Banda El Recodo scores big with a cover of a 1958 classic by Antonio Aguilar.
articles._body: Jay Wheeler ’s “De Lejitos” is no longer distant from the No. 1 spot, as the song jumps 2-1 on Billboard ’s Latin Airplay chart (dated Aug. 29). The new chart-topper arrives just five months after the Puerto Rican led the overall Latin radio ranking in March. “’De Lejitos’ is a special song for me,” Wheeler shares with Billboard . “Today it’s a success because it went from being my daughter Aiunii’s favorite to becoming a favorite among all my fans, long before my team and I decided to officially release it. Every time I release music, I do it with the intention of getting everyone to dance, sing, and be happy listening to my songs, and reaching No. 1 on Billboard simply fills me with great pride. Related Becky G Returns to Top Latin Pop Albums Chart With ‘Baraja Bendita’ Karol G, Judeline & Rusowsky Take ‘BbY WOW’ To No. 1: ‘So Thankful’ Xavi Is First to Lead These 3 Latin Airplay Charts Simultaneously in 2026 “De Lejitos” lands at the summit on Latin Airplay with 6.7 million audience impressions earned in the United States during the Aug. 14-20 tracking week, according to Luminate; that’s a 4% growth from the week prior. “De Lejitos” began its chart journey with a top 20 debut on the Hot Latin Songs chart in April, holding in the top 10 for nearly 11 straight weeks. Its only detour from the upper region came during Karol G’s blockbuster debut week (dated Aug. 12), when songs from her album No Me Arrepiento de Sentir Tanto flooded the multi-metric tally , sending the song from No. 7 to No. 18, and back to the top 10 on this week’s chart, at No. 8, from streaming gain. On Latin Airplay , “De Lejitos” spent three weeks in the top 20 before landing at No. 2 last week. With its new ruling result, Wheeler ups his chart-topping count to four No. 1s. It follows “Viendo El Techo,” “Dos Tragos,” and its latest “Si Te Vas,” with Jay Balvin, all one-week champs between 2021-26. Band El Recodo Revives Antonio Aguilar’s 1958 ‘La Cama De Piedra’ For No. 1: Elsewhere on the Latin charts, Banda El Recodo de Cruz de Lizárraga picks up its 21st No. 1 on Regional Mexican Airplay with “La Cama de Piedra.” The new reworked version of Antonio Aguilar’s hit, released in 1958, was produced by his son Pepe Aguilar and Alfonso ‘Poncho’ Lizárraga, band leader. “La Cama de Piedra” rises after a 10% gain in impressions, to 5.9 million, earned during the tracking week. The song trades places with Xavi’s “Dosis” which leaves the top spot after an equal 10% decline, to 5.6 million. With its 21st Regional Mexican Airplay No. 1, Banda El Recodo now claims seven leaders in the ‘20s —the most that it has earned in any decade, following two in the 1990s and six each in the 2000s and ‘10s. The group also ties with Intocable for the fourth-most champs since the chart began in 1994. Here’s the list of champs: No. 1s, Artist 29, Calibre 50 22, Banda MS de Sergio Lizárraga 22, La Arrolladora Banda el Limón de René Camacho 21, Banda El Recodo de Cruz Lizárraga 21, Intocable 18, Los Tigres del Norte 17, Christian Nodal 17, Grupo Frontera

articles._body: On Wednesday, the Minnesota Timberwolves signed Jonathan Kuminga to a two-year $13 million contract. As a result, the team added a big name to their traveling circus. Many are expecting the Timberwolves to make waves in a competitive Western Conference, which includes the Spurs and Thunder. With the addition of Kuminga, Timberwolves’ Muse projected the starting lineup to look as such : Lamelo Ball, Anthony Edwards, Jaden McDaniels, Kuminga, and Rudy Gobert. The likes of Ayo Dosunmu, Joan Beringer, Jaylen Clark, Bones Hyland, and Josh Green are expected to come off the bench. Meanwhile, Donte DiVincenzo is expected to miss the season due to an Achilles injury. Timberwolves 2026 lineup: Lamelo | Ant | Jaden | Kuminga | Rudy Ayo | TJ | Joan | Clark | Lyles | Bones | Green Donte DiVincenzo will return later in the year — Timberwolves Muse (@Wolvesmuse) August 26, 2026 Now, Kuminga has the free agency headache behind him. He is coming off a season in which he played for both the Golden State Warriors and Atlanta Hawks. Altogether, Kuminga averaged 12.2 points and 5.6 rebounds per game. He also shot 46.3% from the field. Kuminga, 23, was one of the last remaining top players in free agency before signing with Minnesota. As far as the starting lineup goes, you can’t go wrong with it. First off, the combination of LaMelo Ball and Anthony Edwards in the backcourt is as explosively dynamic as all get up. They can push the tempo with the help of Gobert hitting the boards on the defensive end. Meanwhile, Kuminga can provide additional spacing and can run the floor in transition, finishing by attacking the rim. McDaniels adds a dimension of defensive versatility while locking it down at the four spot. Overall, the Timberwolves will be hard to catch up with. articles.title: Why Yankees will upset Rays in AL East standings
articles.summary: The New York Yankees may be 3.5 games behind the American League East-leading Tampa Bay Rays through the first 131 games of their season, but it is fully possible that they will be able to end the campaign at the top of the standings. Tampa Bay has led the division for the vast majority of [̷
articles._body: The New York Yankees may be 3.5 games behind the American League East-leading Tampa Bay Rays through the first 131 games of their season, but it is fully possible that they will be able to end the campaign at the top of the standings. Tampa Bay has led the division for the vast majority of the year, and has played exceptional baseball that’s included solid team hitting and strong starting pitching. Despite experiencing numerous injuries and losing skids, their overall health may be improving at the right time. Further, the Rays’ challenging September schedule may allow New York to sneak ahead just before the conclusion of a grueling 162-game slate. Such a turn of events could land the Yankees not only a division crown, but also the top seed in a rather weak AL. The Yankees’ health could improve before the end of the season © Vincent Carchietta-Imagn Images All-Star outfielder Cody Bellinger recently made his way back into New York’s lineup after suffering a left hamstring strain in July. The slugger has already hit a home run since his return and figures to add length and production to a lineup that needed a boost. Prior to his injury, the 31-year-old had slashed .259/.350/.420 with 21 doubles, 11 home runs and 53 RBIs in 102 games. Further, his defense has consistently been a key part of his game and will certainly be an asset down the stretch. According to Baseball Savant, he presently ranks in the 90th percentile in terms of Fielding Run Value and the 92nd percentile in terms of Outs Above Average. “He’s a guy that helps us tremendously on both sides of the ball,” Yankees manager Aaron Boone told Bryan Hoch of MLB.com. “To get one of our core guys back is big.” Beyond Bellinger’s return, the Yankees could also still receive a monumental reinforcement before the end of September. Reigning AL MVP Aaron Judge has progressed towards both hitting and throwing after being sidelined with a right rib stress fracture. “He’s got a calendar of what they’re doing, but you make adjustments to that as you go,” Boone said. “They’re definitely mapping things out, but as you go, you check some boxes and move on. Sometimes that progress speeds up a little bit. Sometimes you take a step back.” Featuring Judge in the lineup once again would be a critical help, especially since Giancarlo Stanton may be out for the remainder of the season. The eight-time All-Star can carry an offensive attack, and while he won’t necessarily have to be the only source of electricity, his presence alone has the ability to grant others more freedom to be aggressive. The Yankees’ rotation may also become stronger as the final weeks approach. Max Fried could be back sooner than some speculated he would be, and Ryan Weathers. These additions would join a contingent that already includes Gerrit Cole, Carlos Rodon, and Cam Schlittler. The Yankees’ remaining schedule can help them overtake the Rays According to some metrics, New York’s remaining schedule is kinder than Tampa Bay’s. The Rays will have to play the Atlanta Braves, Philadelphia Phillies, and Boston Red Sox among others, and could easily find themselves facing squads that are fighting for their postseason lives. The Yankees will face the Red Sox and San Diego Padres in the near future, but will also have series against the Los Angeles Angels and New York Mets. Additionally, the Bombers will host a four-game set against their division foe during the second-to-last week of September. If New York could pull within two or three games before that important matchup, they could place themselves in a perfect position to take advantage. It remains to be seen how the AL East standings will shake out, but it’s not time to count out the Yankees just yet. articles.title: TIGER TALK REVIEW: It’s Week Zero!
articles.summary: WRITER’S NOTE: “Tiger Talk” is the weekly radio show that features football coach Alex Golesh during football season. Back when Tommy Tuberville was the Tigers’ head coach, I would do tongue-in-cheek reviews of these shows because the shows were funny and questions from the p
articles._body: WRITER’S NOTE: “Tiger Talk” is the weekly radio show that features football coach Alex Golesh during football season. Back when Tommy Tuberville was the Tigers’ head coach, I would do tongue-in-cheek reviews of these shows because the shows were funny and questions from the phone (or in person) made it entertaining. It’s generally less entertaining now, but the show nonetheless gives Golesh — a remarkably forthcoming guy — a platform to pass along some different kinds of insights. So this is a general review of Golesh’s run on Tiger Talk this week. ps: Andy Burcham and Brad Law are the show’s hosts. Many years ago, I beefed with Brad and referred to him as “Not Andy” in these synopses. We got that all squared away. When that happened, I told Brad that I’d start referring to him as “Brad” in this space. He said he preferred “Not Andy.” So that’s what I call him. THE FIRST SEGMENT ANDY asks if it’s good to get away from football.  “It’s been a fun camp and it was cool to turn the page and get working on somebody else. In Year One, you just want to get to Game One. I’m excited to just see it.” NOT ANDY asks if AG is more intense now. “Are you saying I wasn’t intense before?” ( GUFFAWS ALL AROUND ) AG says he was filibustering with the Monday press conference because he just wants to get back into the film room. “My mind is in a lot of different places.” ANDY asks about the Fall Camp At The Hotel thing. Why was that important? “The camp piece very much is an NFL model. We’re trying to get there guys (to the NFL). So many things are not like the NFL in our game. One thing that is … they’re more spread out now. In that guys, guys actually have families and they’re grown-ups. We talk so much about process. What does elite, high-level process day to say look like? We talk about it, we teach it, we talk about it, we teach it. Here’s a two-week period where we can pull them out of their normal day-to-day and teach them, first hand, what that looks like.” “At the end of the day, it reconnects them and re-centers them.” “They thought it was really cool. It brought us closer together.” Photo by Auburn Athletics THE SECOND SEGMENT HERB is in the house. He wants to know how many players here are totally new to Auburn.  “We’ve got right around 40 that transferred in and about 14 that were freshmen. So right over 50 that are now to Auburn. We’ve got close to 70 that were here. That seem to really, really love it.” “Everybody that we get on campus … Bruce Pearl told me this — that we’ve got to get kids on campus. This town gives off a very welcoming vibe.” NOT ANDY thinks AG does some of the things that Bruce did when he started 10+ year ago. Is that true, big dog? “I actually enjoy people. So far, people have enjoyed me, I think, because we’ve been really successful … we haven’t played a game yet. We’ll see how this journey continues. You are a part of the community. The football program is part of the community. You drive around this community and it’s all Auburn flags. (His kids) are my life. For me to be able to let them enjoy living life like a normal person … we’ve chosen to live like normal people.” “The first question everybody asks you is: Do you love Auburn? Has Auburn been good to you? That is really, really unique. Auburn people want you to love Auburn as much as they do. That’s different. That is unique.” TEDDY/TEDDYE is in the house. She wants to know about AG’s family. “They’ve been in a really good spot. My little guy Bear is in sixth grade. He played in his first tackle football game last night. I haven’t had time to watch the film yet, but we’ll evaluate it.” (GUFFAWS ALL AROUND) “He’s having a blast. My daughter is cheering. They got lightning’d out right before halftime. For my wife, being back in the South is really important to her.” Photo by Jake Crandall/IMAGN THE THIRD SEGMENT BUSTER is in the house. He says he’s ready to be at the game in Atlanta , likes that Auburn has an experienced QB. He wants to talk about the 5-for-5 stuff and the NFL guys trying to come back to NCAA. What does AG think? “Which part. Was there a question?” (GUFFAWS ALL AROUND) “The 5-for-5 deal is only going to help, I think, how you’re able to manage the younger guys in your program. The ability to let guys that are young play in whatever role it is … it allows you to help those guys develop. Playing in actual games is the (best) way to actually develop. It allows you to play more guys.” “We’ve kinda take it day-by-day as it’s come up. We’re working through … does it actually make sense to potentially add somebody or not. If you’re ever going to add somebody this late … man, it better be somebody who’s familiar with your program and your kids. For us, that would be really, really hard to do.” NOT ANDY asks about players buying in and how players improve based on what coaches want.  “In this modern-day college football, we’ve … had to change as coaches. The one thing that hasn’t changed that young people crave relationships, they crave accountability, young people crave to be told the truth … and they crave to be loved. That hasn’t changed and I don’t know that it will. That’s why it’s not the NFL.” “We’ve hired people who care about young people, who are in it for the right reasons.” “We haven’t faced adversity in the sense of (facing) another team. That will be the true test of where we are. There is a level of trust th

articles._body: After navigating fall camp over the past month without any major injuries surfacing to the top, NC State is relatively healthy heading into its season-opening clash at Virginia on Saturday afternoon (3:30 p.m., ESPN). The Wolfpack designated seven players as “out” for the Week 0 tilt in its initial ACC availability report released Wednesday night. Virginia, meanwhile, will be without 16 players with two more listed as questionable going into the season. NC State’s report is headlined by freshman wideout Tyreek Copper not being available for the season opener. He received praise from wide receivers coach Joker Phillips, who noted that he “has a chance to play” this season after posting 105 catches for 2,242 yards and 33 touchdowns as a senior at Kinston (N.C.) High. Additionally, the Wolfpack’s nose guard depth is slightly affected with freshman Carmelo McKenzie not available against the Cavaliers. Sophomore tight end Gus Ritchey will be out until mid-October, which will make him a common appearance on this report until he is back healthy, while sophomore wideout Teddy Hoffmann is suspended by the NCAA due to testing positive for a performance-enhancing substance. On Virginia’s side, UCLA transfer wide receiver Rico Flores Jr. will not be available against NC State. Star linebacker Kam Robinson , meanwhile, is listed as questionable after being cleared for contact last week in his return from an ACL injury. articles.title: 49ers get major Mike Evans injury update on Week 1 availability vs. Rams
articles.summary: Wide receiver Mike Evans is easily one of the top players to watch out for in the coming 2026 NFL season over the side of the San Francisco 49ers. This is the first time that the former Texas A&M Aggies star wideout is suiting up for a different team other than the Tampa Bay Buccaneers [̷
articles._body: Wide receiver Mike Evans is easily one of the top players to watch out for in the coming 2026 NFL season over the side of the San Francisco 49ers. This is the first time that the former Texas A&M Aggies star wideout is suiting up for a different team other than the Tampa Bay Buccaneers since entering the league over a decade ago, so it will be interesting to see what kind of impact he will have on the field for the NFC West franchise. But first, he will have to be healthy . That has been a major issue in the offseason and in training camp for 33-year-old Evans, who missed Tuesday’s practice and also left a 49ers joint practice with the Los Angeles Chargers early last week . Concerns have since grown over whether the veteran will be able to make his 49ers debut in the season opener on Sept. 10 against the Los Angeles Rams. However, it appears that the six-time Pro Bowler will be ready just in time for that matchup against San Francisco’s division rivals. “49ers wide receiver Mike Evans plans to play Week 1 despite dealing with injuries this camp, per source. His latest, a groin issue, is considered minor barring a change,” Jeremy Fowler of ESPN shared via a social media post on X (formerly Twitter) on Wednesday. For now, the 49ers do not have to rush Evans into action, with weeks left before the Rams game, though, it should be noted that San Francisco will fly to Australia next week. Signed by the 49ers to a three-year, $42.4 million contract in March, Evans played in only eight games in 2025 and racked up 368 receiving yards and three touchdowns on 30 receptions and 62 targets. articles.summary:
I am excited to share WhisperBar with fellow developers or anyone who reads & writes a ton of text when interacting with their AI agent.

For the writing part, WhisperBar does what all other Whisper* apps do but a bit faster and more consistent, with a nice, stable, native macOS and iOS app.

B
articles._body: I am excited to share WhisperBar with fellow developers or anyone who reads & writes a ton of text when interacting with their AI agent. For the writing part, WhisperBar does what all other Whisper* apps do but a bit faster and more consistent, with a nice, stable, native macOS and iOS app. But where it really shines is in solving a problem that I'm sure you have encountered too: because of AI, we now have to read and comprehend so much more than before. Text to voice systems are not available everywhere, but even when they are, they sound so mechanical, and listening to the entire output is even more time consuming. What Gemini did by turning your research/response into a podcast was genius, and ChatGPT's new voice chat system is also much better (it allows you to have a conversation with the response). However, these two are not available everywhere that I interact with AI (specially with Claude Code and Codex) With WhisperBar, I can select a piece of text (anywhere, in any app) and press my keyboard shortcut to quickly listen to a short, ~20-second explanation. It does not matter how long the text I have copied is. This allows me to copy the entire response and then hear a summary, or select a section to zoom in on an explanation of that section of the document. Again, the point is that it is not text to voice, rather, it processes the text and comes up with a natural sounding short explanation. Oh, and another thing we don't store any data and only use providers with zero-data-retention policies. It is still a work in progress, and we have about 20 customers right now. It is available on the App Store for both iOS and macOS, with a 7-day free trial at only $4/month (plus Family Sharing). FYI, the WhisperBar iOS app is a bit different (it can record in the background for meetings, etc.). articles.title: Jeremy Jarmon Explains Why You Should Be Fired Up for Will Stein’s Changes at Kentucky
articles.summary: Will Stein has changed the Kentucky scheme and altered practices. Jeremy Jarmon articulates for BBN why they're so exciting.
articles._body: Jeremy Jarmon has not put on a Kentucky football helmet since 2008. Even though it’s been nearly two decades since he created havoc in the SEC trenches, he was ready to put the pads on after watching Will Stein operate in practice. “There’s not a lot of times since I’ve been done playing where I’ve gone out to a practice, and we get to the end of practice, and I’m like, ‘Man, it would have been fun to be out on that field today.’ I experienced that this past Wednesday,” Jarmon shared with 11 Personnel . Throughout the spring, there were plenty of practice observers who were blown away by the energy from Stein’s young coaching staff. That doesn’t quite articulate just what it’s like inside a Kentucky football practice. Times have changed since Jarmon was on the field. There is still a time and place for that authoritarian style of leadership, but that isn’t always the most effective way to reach kids of this generation. “There’s a lot of research going on in the country of how to make tough tasks fun and enjoyable. Football’s supposed to be a game, right? A kids’ game. What I see from Will, he understands that in the SEC, what they’re asking these guys to do it’s insane. I mean, they’re modern-day gladiators. But the way that he facilitates these practices, the way he starts them, they’re fun. The way that he ends them, it’s fun. “He’s gamifying a game, and I’ve been a player before. I’ve been on the field at practice, and after a while, it just feels like work. Until Saturday, that’s really all that it is. But now he’s making it very game-like every single snap, every day, every week, and it’s exciting, man. It is exciting.” It’s not just in the structure of the practices. Stein is on the microphone, providing positive reinforcement throughout practice. That instant feedback keeps the players pushing, no matter how hard it may be. If the practices are fun, there’s a much better chance this Kentucky football team is having fun on Saturdays this fall. How Kentucky Can Unlock Pass-Rushers We’ve been told that Jay Bateman will play a more aggressive style of defense that should open up more opportunities for the pass-rushers. So what exactly does that mean and how does it look? It’s best explained by someone who’s all over the UK record book. “That means that there’s going to be situations where they tell ( Mi’Quise) Humphrey-Grace that you get to the quarterback, and the linebacker or the safety is going to make you right,” said Jarmon. “At some point on this pass rush, or when you’re making your move, you declare. Declare either inside or outside. Don’t be lukewarm. Don’t be half pregnant, and stay butted up, face to face on somebody. Declare, and then somebody’s going to replace. When you got a guy with his skill set, and you’re giving him that green light, you’re just making him a like a havoc guy up front.” After earning Missouri Valley Conference Defensive Player of the Year honors in 2024, Humphrey-Grace had a solid debut for Kentucky, tallying 7.0 TFLs and 3.5 sacks. He’s built for success in the SEC. All of the tools are there. Now he’s playing in a scheme that will let him show off all of those tools. “He’s got a high football IQ. He’s obviously got a high motor. He’s a strong guy. He can do anything he wants,” said Jarmon. “He can come back inside with a power move. He can stutter bull (rush), knock a guy back. He can work the edge. And when you can do those things, why limit it in a system where you just got to stay outside? Let this guy show that he’s got a high skill set, and let him figure it out. I’m excited for him to be in a system where he’s going to potentially be rewarded with that type of green light.” If that doesn’t get you fired up for Kentucky football, this entire 30-minute conversation certainly will.

articles.title: Jeremiah Smith predicts Heisman Trophy for Ohio State freshman RB Legend Bey
articles.summary: Jeremiah Smith is gunning for his own Heisman Trophy in 2026. But if the Ohio State wide receiver cannot get the job done, he has a prediction for who might have the next best chance. Smith could not be higher on true freshman Legend Bey, predicting the running back to come home with college footbal
articles._body: Jeremiah Smith is gunning for his own Heisman Trophy in 2026. But if the Ohio State wide receiver cannot get the job done, he has a prediction for who might have the next best chance. Smith could not be higher on true freshman Legend Bey , predicting the running back to come home with college football’s most prestigious individual award at some point. “I think I said this back in spring,” Smith said via Chase Brown of 11 Warriors . “I said to Luke Montgomery, I said, ‘Before Legend Bey leave Ohio State, he’ll be a Heisman finalist or he’ll end up winning it.’ The things he’s been doing in practice has been pretty special.” [ $19.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage ] Bey winning the Heisman Trophy this season would be incredibly spectacular. Especially when somebody like Bo Jackson is leading the running back room. Consistent playing time at the top of the rotation is not considered to be available at the moment. He has three years to make Smith’s prediction come to life, though. Two of Ohio State’s first three games are against lesser opponents. Ball State is the opener, followed by Kent State in Week 3. That might be a spot where the Buckeyes get Bey some early playing time to wet his feet in the college game. More information on Legend Bey, early days at Ohio State Bey played high school football at Forney (TX) North Forney , where he was a four-star prospect. He was the No. 131 overall recruit in the 2026 cycle , according to the Rivals Industry Ranking , a weighted average that utilizes all three major recruiting media companies. There was some drama regarding Bey’s recruitment. Tennessee had his original commitment before Ohio State pulled off a flip. Late in the cycle, a few in-state schools — SMU , Texas , and Texas A&M — attempted to make a push. But when National Signing Day came around, Bey changed course again and signed with Josh Heupel and the Vols. A few days later, Bey was released from his National Letter of Intent and landed in Columbus. Head coach Ryan Day has to be quite thankful. If Smith’s endorsement was not enough, Ohio State likes the way Bey is progressing. On Tuesday, he became the latest player to lose his black stripe. On3 | Rivals’ Lettermen Row reported as such, also providing intel on what’s happening behind the scenes .

articles._body: The Milwaukee Brewers and New York Mets are playing a game on Wednesday night. However, an injury scare surfaced after just one pitch, as a line drive off Mets outfielder AJ Ewing’s bat that was recorded at 106 MPH hit the throwing shoulder of Brewers starter Dustin May. Milwaukee somehow recorded an out on the play, as the ball bounced to the third baseman who threw Ewing out at first. However, all of the focus immediately shifted to May after the out was recorded. Video via Foul Territory: Dustin May took a 106 mph line drive off the bat of A.J Ewing on the first pitch of the game to the shoulder. He seemed to be in severe discomfort and was removed from the game after throwing warmup pitches. We wish him a speedy recovery pic.twitter.com/AsuQouSzUb — Foul Territory (@FoulTerritoryTV) August 26, 2026 May was clearly in pain and he ultimately left the game after some warm-up pitches. Robert Gasser entered the contest to replace the Brewers starter. Milwaukee will need its bullpen to step up after May’s early exit due to injury. May was acquired by the Brewers from the St. Louis Cardinals before this season’s trade deadline. The Brewers believe he can play a crucial role for them down the stretch of the season. Now, Milwaukee is simply hoping May avoided a serious injury. The right-handed hurler holds a 4.57 ERA across 24 total starts this season between the Cardinals and the Brewers, three of which have come with Milwaukee (Wednesday was his fourth start with the Brewers). He entered the contest on Wednesday having surrendered 10 earned runs across 15 innings of work with Milwaukee. We will continue to monitor and provide updates on Dustin May’s injury status following his scare against the Mets. As for the game itself, Milwaukee currently holds a 4-0 lead in the 2nd inning. articles.title: NFLPA announces new penalty guidelines for 2026 season
articles.summary: The NFL and NFL Players Association have finalized a new on-field accountability system for the 2026 season, placing greater emphasis on five player-safety violations and introducing new consequences for repeated offenses. Under the updated system, a player who commits three violations in any of
articles._body: The NFL and NFL Players Association have finalized a new on-field accountability system for the 2026 season, placing greater emphasis on five player-safety violations and introducing new consequences for repeated offenses. Under the updated system, a player who commits three violations in any of five designated categories during a season will receive a one-game suspension. The five areas receiving increased attention are hip-drop tackles, horse-collar tackles, launching, hits on defenseless players and blindside blocks. The system was presented to teams during the league’s annual meeting in Atlanta on Wednesday. The changes were approved on a one-year basis, allowing the NFL and NFLPA to evaluate their impact over the course of the 2026 season. The revised system is designed to distinguish between isolated mistakes and repeated actions that could jeopardize player safety. Players will begin the 2026 season with a clean slate, although violations in the five identified categories will carry over into subsequent seasons. The new guidelines also provide financial incentives for players who avoid repeated violations. A player who receives a fine for one of the five outlined offenses will be eligible to receive 50% of that fine back at the end of the season if there are no additional fines for the same violation during that season. For a single violation in other eligible player-safety categories, the player can receive the full fine amount back if there is no repeat fine for the same foul during the season. The NFL and NFLPA did not specify which additional categories qualify for the full refund. Players who approach the three-violation suspension threshold will also be required to attend meetings with the NFL alongside their coaches. Teams that accumulate excessive health and safety violations will face increased financial penalties. Former NFL head coach and nine-year linebacker Ron Rivera will also join the group of former players responsible for overseeing appeals hearings involving on-field player discipline. That also includes team trainers. In the bottom of the 3rd inning, Mariners catcher Jhonny Pereda hit a foul ball to the P
articles._body: The Philadelphia Phillies defeated the Seattle Mariners 6-0 on Wednesday. All the while, the Phillies are making a playoff push . Therefore, everyone needs to be in one piece. That also includes team trainers. In the bottom of the 3rd inning, Mariners catcher Jhonny Pereda hit a foul ball to the Phillies’ dugout, where the coaches and trainers were. The ball bounced right into the trainers’ sunglasses and shattered them , per Jomboy Media. However, he was lucky they took the blow instead of his eyes. Phillies athletic trainer lost his sunglasses but they saved him from a black eye pic.twitter.com/6S1oHod4Je — Jomboy Media (@JomboyMedia) August 26, 2026 The trainer appeared to be Christian Bermúdez. Bermúdez has been an assistant trainer for Philadelphia since 2021. He had arrived via Triple-A Lehigh Valley and had worked as a medical operations liaison. Meanwhile, Philadelphia finishes the three-game series against Seattle, losing two games and winning one. On Friday, they will begin a three-game road series against the Los Angeles Angels. With the victory, Philadelphia is now 74-60 and is trailing the Atlanta Braves by four games in the National League East Division. Additionally, Philadelphia is trailing the Chicago Cubs by 2.5 games in the National League Wild Card standings. The Phillies turned a corner after a 9-19 start to the season. Then, after hiring Don Mattingly as manager , they surged their way back before the All-Star break. Since then, they have cooled off in the second half of the season and are trying to secure a playoff spot. Last year, Philadelphia won the NL East Division and lost to the Los Angeles Dodgers in four games in the NLDS. articles.title: Coinkite’s Coldcard Bug Exposed Single-Sig Risk. Multi-Vendor Multisig Is the New Bitcoin Custody Baseline
articles.summary: Bitcoin Magazine
articles._body: Bitcoin Magazine Coinkite’s Coldcard Bug Exposed Single-Sig Risk. Multi-Vendor Multisig Is the New Bitcoin Custody Baseline In the wake of Coldcard’s catastrophic entropy bug , self-custody advocates and experts have begun recommending a new standard, multi-vendor multisignature wallets, an approach that looks to minimize —among other threats— dependency on any single hardware wallet manufacturer. The Coldcard entropy bug that went undiscovered since at least 2021 has taught a hard lesson to the Bitcoin self-custody advocates and users. No matter how legitimate or competent a wallet provider might seem, how well recommended and reputable, a major bug may be possible. As a result, Bitcoiners are questioning old recommendations and assumptions, including many declaring the ‘death of single sig’ the popular self-custody method of trusting the private key pair generation to one wallet alone. The Threat Model Self-custody by any measure is an advanced practice in Bitcoin. Advocates recommend it as a way to protect user funds from exchange malfeasance like that seen in the cases of FTX and MtGox, among many others. But recent events have driven a revaluation of custody practices, with many bitcoin owners moving coins to exchanges — at least temporarily — while others upgrading or changing their self-custody setups altogether. Nick Neuman, CEO of Casa, claimed that 233k bitcoins moved to safety in reaction to the Coldcard hack. To understand when self-custody makes sense and for whom, it is essential to understand your personal threat model. A threat model is the careful analysis of threats to an individual, for the purpose of designing security practices and structures ahead of time. A simple threat model practice can be to take a step back and think about all the possible things that worry you about self-custody, and add them to a list. Then think about all the things that advocates caution users about, and append them to that same list. Next, sort or rate items on that list based on which are most likely to happen to you, and which are most likely to happen in general. Finally, you can rank each item in the list by how catastrophic it would be if it occurred; can your current setup and plans survive the realization of that threat? Two of the most likely causes of loss of funds in Bitcoin self-custody are user error related to backups or forgotten passwords, and of course theft. Many of the wallets believed to be lost bitcoins that have not moved come from bad backups of private keys in the early days, resulting in data loss after a computer failed. Others simply used passwords too difficult to brute force, and then forgot them, encrypting their private keys forever. On the theft dimension, bad entropy attacks likely rank among the most successful attacks on self-custody to date, with Coldcard joining a significant list of other wallets that have suffered bugs of the sort, intentional or otherwise, such as Trust Wallet, and many lesser-known and possibly malicious mobile wallets. In some cases, fake wallets like the iOS Sparrow Wallets simply stole user funds by keeping a copy of the user-generated private keys and sweeping the funds once deposited. In all of these examples, more thoughtful user behavior before trusting random software with your life savings is the solution. Once users have a clear threat model in place and a good enough understanding of the technology, designing security practices becomes more a science than an art. And while every individual has specific circumstances they need to take into account, some structures have emerged as the most resilient to most threats. One such practice becoming widely recommended and adopted among long-term self-custody Bitcoin holders is a carefully formed multisig setup. Multi-vendor Multisig The term “Multi-vendor Multisig” is relatively new in the self-custody niche. The term “multisig” has nevertheless gone viral in 2026, clearly triggered by the Coldcard hack that saw the loss of over 100 million dollars worth of bitcoin, mostly from single seed wallets. Most single-seed Coldcard users appear to have generated their private keys on the device without adding an extra passphrase, extra words that add custom entropy to the private keys, nor without extra dice rolls, which do the same in a different format. The weak entropy from the Coldcard firmware — which users had no reason to distrust, given the company’s strong brand — in turn made guessing the related private keys easy, with a bit of custom work, which hackers eventually figured out.  The resulting viral interest in multisig is warranted. Multisig Bitcoin wallets protect users from such hardware manufacturer errors by letting users construct a Bitcoin address that requires signing from multiple private keys and thus multiple devices, in what is known as a Bitcoin script. Bitcoin scripts are contracts of sorts that set spending conditions for a bitcoin wallet. All Bitcoin wallets can be thought of as having some kind of script involved, with the simplest and most popular being that anyone who can sign a valid transaction can spend all or any funds therein. Multisig scripts instead require a threshold of valid signatures from different keypairs to result in a valid withdrawal. These scripts are enforced by the Bitcoin consensus rules. Multi-vendor multisig theory posits that users should make sure every keypair used to construct a Bitcoin multisig is generated from a different wallet vendor. One example that is likely popular today might be the use of a Trezor Safe 7 hardware wallet with one key, a second key generated by a Ledger Nano , and a third key generated by a multisig wallet provider, considered a recovery key. A script of this sort would require any 2 valid signatures out of the three possible signatures in the setup. articles._body: The Edmonton Oilers signed goaltender Frederik Andersen in NHL free agency this summer. Fresh off winning a Stanley Cup with the Carolina Hurricanes , Andersen hopes to have the same success with the Oilers. However, his debut with his new team may be delayed. Andersen is going to miss the beginning of training camp, Edmonton announced on Wednesday . He is not alone in this, either. He is one of four players who will not be at camp with the Oilers when it begins next month. Andersen and forward Matt Savoie suffered injuries over the offseason that require time away from the ice. Meanwhile, forward Mattias Janmark and defenseman Alec Regula are still recovering from previously sustained injuries. Andersen is certainly the most notable name here for hockey fans. The veteran netminder, as previously mentioned, won the Stanley Cup this summer with the Hurricanes. He was dominant for most of the run, as well. Carolina went unbeaten in its first eight playoff games. And they lost just three games the entire postseason. The veteran netminder spent the last five seasons with Carolina. In that time, he ranked top 10 in the NHL for Goals Saved Above Expected, according to HockeyStats.com. He helped the Hurricanes make three appearances in the Eastern Conference Finals in addition to the Cup win in 2026. The Oilers are hoping Andersen can bring that sort of success to their team. Unfortunately, Edmonton is going to need to wait a bit before they see him on the ice. Hopefully, the injury is nothing major, and the veteran netminder can return sooner rather than later. articles.title: Kelvin Green has options to deploy new-look defensive tackles group for Purdue
articles.summary: If you need some humbling, go stand next to Purdue's defensive tackles. The behemoths up front for the Boilermakers will make even normal sized humans feel tiny.
articles._body: If you need some humbling, go stand next to Purdue’s defensive tackles. The behemoths up front for the Boilermakers will make even normal-sized humans feel tiny. That cast of defensive tackles includes transfer newcomers Wisdom Simms , Rodney Lora and Curt Neal , as well as the returning Ian Jeffries and TJ Lindsey . All five of whom tip the scales north of 300 pounds. When asked about Simms and Lora in particular, Purdue defensive tackles coach Kelvin Green spoke to the transfer tandem’s size as key attributes they bring to the defensive front. “The size, the mass, the being able to still attack and play violent, and they’re using their hands, and they’re picking up on how we do things and how we need things to be done in order to be really good players in the Big Ten. They just got to keep pushing. So they have brought the willingness to learn, and then they have the size and the mass, and they want to play in the backfield,” Green said. Simms transferred in from North Carolina Central, while Lora comes to West Lafayette after stops at North Carolina and UCF. The third portal addition of the off-season came via a well-traveled lineman from the Big Ten ranks. Curt Neal began his career at Wisconsin, where he spent three years and started 12 games as a sophomore before a one-year stint at Illinois last fall, starting eight games for the Illini. That experience and leadership have been invaluable for the Boilermakers already. “Old veteran. He gets how to play the game. He has played in this league, from Wisconsin to Illinois, and now being here. He understands what it takes day in and day out to play at this level, and he brings it every day. So it’s been a great addition to the room, and plus his leadership, he leads the right way. He speaks life into the boys, and he’s not a negative guy. He’s a positive guy. He wants guys to all succeed. So it’s great having him here,” Green said. That trio replaced departed starting defensive tackles Jamarrion Harkless (Kentucky) and Demeco Kennedy (Louisville), who left via the transfer portal this off-season. The Boilermakers did bring back a pair of rising linemen who could be poised for jumps heading into their second years with the program, TJ Lindsey and Ian Jeffries. Lindsey was set to be a big part of the defense a year ago, but is now coming off a torn ACL that he suffered in the USC game last year, and Green shared that he expects Lindsey to be a “vital piece,” but he needs to keep building as he returns from the injury. Jeffries emerged as a starter across the last six games of 2025 and was a key retention for the Boilermaker staff. Having a full off-season in West Lafayette could benefit him greatly. “It’s good to see his growth. When we got in, he was one of the guys that came in the summer, went through fall camp. He didn’t get a spring, so for him to get a spring and summer and the fall and to get with Coach Ro and his staff and get stronger, get bigger, he’s moving better. It’s just been a plus. Then you add Curt Neal and Rodney (Lora) and guys around him who can talk life into him, it’s just been good for him, and he’s progressing,” Green said. Purdue also has a pair of exciting true freshmen in former four-star prospect Josiah Hope and in-state product Kobe Cherry waiting in the wings for an opportunity. Elijah St. John and Drake Carlson round out the group, after serving in deep reserve roles a year ago. That’s a lot of names thrown at you, and Purdue has a limited number of spots. Kelvin Green will have ample options as he divvies up snaps for a number of defensive tackles this fall. As the season opener approaches, there is still competition to be had. “There’s a good bit, and I’m loving it every single time. I love going out there and competing. Coach also has us mixing and matching different guys, so it’s not a crazy competition. He knows that we’re all comfortable with each other, so it’s going to be fun to see who goes out there,” Lora said. “I can’t have a set number. We have guys that can go in, they can play, and that’s why you see me mix and match and trying to make sure guys get comfortable playing with anyone on the field. We have a number of guys that can go in there and do it,” Green said. Looking back to last season, the distribution was largely even, with Kennedy getting 37 snaps per game, followed by Jeffries at 36 per game and Harkless at 35 per game. TJ Lindsey, in his two full games, earned 61 total snaps as well. The snap counts and how Purdue chooses to deploy its new-look defensive tackles unit will be a key storyline with how aggressive new defensive coordinator Kevin Kane wants his defensive front to be this fall. “I’ve never had a coach tell me to just keep going straight. That’s the best way to describe it. We are fully blowing up gaps. We’re filling gaps. It doesn’t matter the job, as long as we get in that backfield. That’s that’s the main job. We’re not reading or reacting, we’re not sitting there waiting patiently, we’re going,” Lora said.

Next up: Who Purdue doesn’t play. • Toughest non-conference game: Notre Dame, Sept. 26 • Toughest conference: at Indiana, Nov. 28 • Who they don’t play: Michigan, Ohio State, Rutgers, USC, Oregon, Northwestern, Nebraska, Michigan State • Easiest game: Indiana State, Sept. 4 • Best chance to be upset: • Best chance to pull an upset : • Toughest stretch: The logic:  Indiana State will make the 87-mile drive from Terre Haute looking to stun the Boilermakers, who are riding a 10-game losing streak. Purdue never has lost a game vs. a FCS foe, going 15-0 all-time. The history: For the second time in three years, Purdue will open at home vs. FCS Indiana State. The last time was 2024, with the Boilermakers posting a dominating 49-0 victory. Purdue proceeded to lose its next 11 games, as Ryan Walters was fired. The Boilers are 7-0 all-time vs. ISU. The bottom line: Curt Mallory, son of iconic IU coach Bill, is back for his 10th season leading the Sycamores. In that span, he has one winning season–and that came in 2018 (7-4). articles.title: Selena Gomez Fights ‘Absurd’ Fraud Claims in Wondermind Investor Lawsuit
articles.summary: Lawyers say the pop star and actress “should never have been dragged into” a legal fight over the mental health startup.
articles._body: Selena Gomez is hitting back hard against claims that she was involved in fraud at the mental health startup Wondermind, saying she had nothing to do with the situation and calling the lawsuit “egregiously improper and legally deficient.” Gomez’s lawyers filed a motion on Wednesday (Aug. 26), obtained by Billboard , to dismiss the pop star and actress from a lawsuit brought two weeks ago by five Wondermind investors. These investors allege they were duped into investing $1.2 million in the struggling company led by Gomez’s mother, Mandy Teefey . “The notion that Ms. Gomez engaged in any form of ‘fraud’ is absurd,” writes a team of lawyers led by Mathew Rosengart , who’s best known for helping Britney Spears end her conservatorship. “She should never have been dragged into this action, and we respectfully submit she must be dismissed.” The lawsuit centers on claims that Teefey and her former co-CEO, Daniella Pierson , misrepresented the company’s structure and finances to investors Brent Saunders , Marc Roberts , EJ Solimine , Andrew Resnick and Mark Peikin . One allegation is that Teefey and Pierson falsely said Gomez would be heavily involved as Wondermind’s head of marketing, when in reality the star worked to “actively distance” herself from the company. According to Gomez’s lawyers, this claim demonstrates in and of itself that she should not be involved in the lawsuit. The attorneys say that since Gomez had no role in Wondermind’s fundraising or management, she “could not possibly have engaged in any ‘fraud.’” The lawsuit tries to plead around this issue by suggesting that Gomez had access to Wondermind’s financial numbers, and thus she must have known that company investors were being lied to. But Gomez’s lawyers say this is faulty too. “The mere fact that Ms. Gomez — who is literally one of the world’s busiest women — might have had the ability to request information by virtue of being a co-founder/consultant is not enough,” reads the motion to dismiss. “The lack of a single allegation that Ms. Gomez ever said anything about Wondermind’s operational state or financial condition — or any allegations stating that Ms. Gomez was privy to the other Defendants’ communications with Plaintiffs — requires dismissal of the fraud claims against Ms. Gomez.” In a statement sent to Billboard , Rosengart says their motion demonstrates that “the claims against her are completely meritless, if not frivolous.” “In addition to filing our motion, we are exploring other avenues of relief for Ms. Gomez, including sanctions against Plaintiffs for improperly including her,” adds Rosengart. The investors’ attorneys did not immediately return a request for comment on Wednesday. Wondermind launched in 2021 with plans for a suite of mental health media initiatives, including a digital magazine, mobile app and podcast. The company was thrust into the spotlight last year, when the Cut published a bombshell article reporting that the company’s finances were in dire condition due in part to Teefey’s alleged substance abuse issues and erratic behavior. In the Cut article, Teefey denied allegations of company mismanagement and said Wondermind remained viable: “I started Wondermind because I wanted to help people with mental illness,” she said in a statement to the magazine. “It’s unfortunate that a few disgruntled employees with an ax to grind can spread lies about me and distort the truth. Even more disappointing that the media is willing to amplify their lies.”

articles.title: NBA insider’s optimistic take on 2026-27 Celtics after Jaylen Brown trade to 76ers
articles.summary: As the shock from the Boston Celtics’ Jaylen Brown trade with the Philadelphia 76ers wears off, there are plenty of reasons for fans in Boston to be excited about the 2026-27 season. While some Celtics fans are talking themselves into Paul George delivering a stellar campaign in his first s
articles._body: As the shock from the Boston Celtics’ Jaylen Brown trade with the Philadelphia 76ers wears off, there are plenty of reasons for fans in Boston to be excited about the 2026-27 season. While some Celtics fans are talking themselves into Paul George delivering a stellar campaign in his first season with Jayson Tatum, others are pointing to the underrated free-agent signings of Mike Conley Jr. and Mitchell Robinson. How Tatum’s body responds in his first full season since rupturing his Achilles tendon is another significant factor for the Celtics’ upcoming season. However, the front office must have liked what it saw in Tatum’s six-week sample size after returning in March before missing Game 7 of their first-round 3-1 collapse against the 76ers. Either way, putting the Celtics’ offseason into perspective helps fans understand why Boston parted ways with Brown, as The Ringer’s Michael Pina noted, per CLNS Media’s Celtics Daily Podcast w/Bobby Manning. “To me, it begins with finances. I go back to the press conference that Bill Chisholm and Brad Stevens had, and I do think that finances were a major part of the decision to move on from Jaylen,” Pina said. “When you look back at when they did win the championship a few years ago, Tatum and Brown were the third-and fourth-highest-paid players on the team, and certainly not making 35 percent of the cap apiece on their contracts. “You just look across the league with regards to how teams are operating in the apron era, and Boston is not unique in how it has kind of deconstructed a championship-winning team. Getting optionality and all that stuff is really important, and I understand that.” Many NBA teams had to part ways with a handful of players to stay below the dreaded second apron, which comes with tax penalties that restrict teams from making various moves to improve their rosters. The Denver Nuggets are the only team in the second apron ahead of the upcoming season. The Celtics went through a similar process last summer, parting ways with key members of the 2024 championship team, including trading Jrue Holiday and Kristaps Porzingis, while Al Horford left via free agency to sign with the Golden State Warriors. While fans were quick to criticize the Celtics’ return for an aging George, who turned 36 in May, Pina reminded them of the other assets that came in return for Jaylen Brown, including the nine-time All-Star, his expiring contract, and draft capital. “So, getting two picks, one or maybe both, will be great, and be viewed highly around the league in trade talks, or maybe they end up using one of them, and end up drafting the next cornerstone, who knows,” Pina added. “But I think getting those two picks and getting a player in Paul George, who I think is, at this point, pretty underrated in what he’s capable of doing, and I think possibly more complementary to the pieces you already have. “Not to mention just his contract and the fact that it’s one year, and then a player option. With a player option, you can just do so much more stuff than with what Jaylen’s contract was, which was not loved or admired around the NBA, clearly, because no one wanted to do a trade with the Celtics for it.” The Celtics received a protected 2028 first-round pick (via LA Clippers), an unprotected 2031 first-round pick, and two second-round picks (2028, 2030) from the Sixers after signing Robinson to a three-year, $47.3 million contract, and Conley Jr. to a one-year deal, worth $3.8 million. “Getting what they got back for it, they’re able to still, realistically, aim for a championship, I think, and play for one,” Pina said. “I think there’s a lot of teams that are going to be shooting for a title this season. At the end of the day, when you look at who has won a title the last few years, so much about it is health in the playoffs.” While some NBA fans remain bullish on the Celtics’ chances of competing for a title this season, their offseason moves could reenter the title conversation for the foreseeable future. The optimistic prediction after Celtics’ Jaylen Brown trade Rob Gray-Imagn Images Despite how many feel about the complexion of the 2026-27 Celtics, Jayson Tatum will be leading a playoff team next season. While players like Payton Pritchard and Derrick White will take on increased roles to fill the void left by Celtics All-Star Jaylen Brown’s trade to the 76ers, Paul George’s playoff performance in 2026 is promising ahead of next season. Plus, the Celtics’ offseason additions of Mitchell Robinson, coming off a championship run with the Knicks, bolster the frontcourt. While Mike Conley Jr. gives the Celtics a veteran facilitator and defender in the backcourt, as The Ringer’s Michael Pina pointed out. “I like the makeup of the team, and I like the almost machine-like efficiency that they’re able to deploy with their playing style, which I’m also interested to see if that shifts at all, or if that doubles down,” Pina said. “If they double down on how Joe Mazzulla wants to play, which I think they probably will this season, and I think it’ll be very successful. I think they’re deep. I think they’re athletic. “I think that they’re young. I think a lot of their pieces should be better than they were last season. They have 3-point shooting, they have defensive versatility, and they’re super talented. I just like this team a lot.” For the first time in his career, Tatum won’t be sharing the floor with Brown. The 10-year era came to an end this summer, as Tatum leads the franchise to a new chapter. With head coach Joe Mazzulla at the helm, the Celtics should remain competitive. articles.title: How Pelicans can salvage former champion’s trade value after Bennedict Mathurin signing
articles.summary: After months of waiting, Big Easy basketball fans have some free agency news that might help fill Smoothie King Center seats. With apologies to DeAndre Jordan, the New Orleans Pelicans made their first significant signing of the 2026 offseason, agreeing to a two-year, $16 million deal with high-s
articles._body: After months of waiting, Big Easy basketball fans have some free agency news that might help fill Smoothie King Center seats. With apologies to DeAndre Jordan, the New Orleans Pelicans made their first significant signing of the 2026 offseason, agreeing to a two-year, $16 million deal with high-scoring wing Bennedict Mathurin . On the surface, it makes Jordan Poole all but expendable going into training camp. EVP Joe Dumars and head coach Jamahl Mosley need to instead focus on churning up some kind of trade value for the former champion before the holidays. Poole is entering the final season of an approximately $34 million contract. That expiring money will become increasingly useful as the trade deadline approaches, but salary relief alone will not force opposing executives to surrender anything meaningful. Dumars needs the rest of the NBA to see a player worth putting on the floor once the paperwork is complete. The trade-and-buyout options will be very limited this season. Even though the Pelicans are trying to change the toughness narrative , Mosley needs to show some early flexibility with the rotations. The goal is not to hide Poole defensively, but to put him in lineups that mask weaknesses while amplifying what he does best. Poole has shown he can produce at a high level with the ball (career-high 20.4 points, 4.5 assists, 3.0 rebounds in his final Wizards season) and as a movement shooter and finisher (Golden State Warriors pre-Draymond Green punch). Being able to operate in both roles should expand the market as the season unfolds. Pelicans playing odds Kamil Krzaczynski-Imagn Images Poole’s trade market value has tanked lower than a meme coin since leaving the Warriors. Showing a renewed sense of focus and purpose in training camp alone could alleviate some of the ‘seriousness’ concerns. No contender is going to take a chance on someone not committed to the cause, and, like the negative narratives, that’s not a switch Poole can easily flip. Show up to camp ready to compete for minutes against Mathurin, Herb Jones, Jeremiah Fears, and Saddiq Bey. Word will get out. Can the Pelicans trust Poole to be the scoring punch with defensive anchors Herb Jones, Saddiq Bey, Yves Missi, and a bulked-up Trey Murphy III? Will the Derik Queen and Point Zion Williamson experiment work with Poole cutting off the ball? In the first example, Poole must be willing to pass while acting as a featured scorer. In the second, Poole must be willing to continue moving even when someone else is getting the buckets. Poole’s first season in New Orleans could hardly have done more damage to his market. He was limited to 39 games and eight starts, averaging 13.4 points and 3.1 assists while shooting 37.2% from the field and 33.3% from 3-point range. Those numbers were a dramatic step backward and helped lead to this somewhat stagnated career situation. If it all clicks under a defensive-minded Mosley, the Pelicans will be able to rehabilitate Poole’s value without actually depending on him in 2027. Jordan Poole’s best punch A unit featuring Poole, Herb Jones, Trey Murphy III, Saddiq Bey and Yves Missi gives Mosley length at four positions while allowing Poole to initiate offense against second units. Jones can take the opposing team’s best perimeter threat. Murphy provides size and shooting. Bey gives the group another physical wing. Missi supplies pick-and-roll screening and a rim presence. Besides Jones, Poole’s other important partner should be Dejounte Murray. The Pelicans will have plenty of incentive to stagger Murray’s minutes with Jeremiah Fears and Bennedict Mathurin. Doing so would also allow Mosley to occasionally use Poole without forcing him to organize every possession. Murray can initiate the offense and defend the more dangerous opposing guard. Poole can run secondary pick-and-rolls, attack scrambled defenses, and hunt three-pointers. Given a chance to show a change in approach and form, a contender might become interested in Poole as a secondary creator capable of swinging a playoff game. A few lottery-bound teams might need to avoid the relegation zone as well. That matters this season and the Pelicans need to take full advantage. Teams shopping near the deadline will not evaluate Poole based solely on whether he can produce 20 points every night next to Zion Williamson. They will ask whether they can put him beside an established star, survive defensively, and steal eight minutes of a crucial game. Mosley needs to provide an answer. The new depth helps because no one will be asked or allowed to shoot their way out of a bad night. Mathurin’s presence makes the process easier because New Orleans no longer has to force Poole into every scoring situation. The Pelicans have enough firepower that Poole’s minutes can become more intentional, and intentional minutes may produce better numbers than the inconsistent reserve role he endured last season. Gauging good value Trevor Ruszkowski-USA TODAY Sports If Poole gets back into the neighborhood of 13-16 points per game while shooting 37% or better from beyond the arc, the trade value conversation changes. Then Poole stops looking like an expensive dead-end reclamation project and starts looking like an expiring contract attached to a legitimate bench weapon. There is a rental market for that player, and Joe Dumars will go from crickets to hearing a few calls. The objective should not necessarily be extracting a first-round pick for Poole in a vacuum. Turning his contract from something the Pelicans would have to pay to move or let expire for nothing into something another team actually wants included in a deal would already represent a significant recovery. Essentially, Dumars needs a team to believe Poole can help win a few games while simultaneously providing useful salary mechanics in a larger transaction.
