As far as today’s chat … PLEASE include your NAME and HOMETOWN along with your question(s). Here are the rules: Eric Hansen: The No Drinking and No Gambling edicts have been dropped for good behavior. Off we go … Dave from Columbus : Hi Eric, this team has lost a lot of explosive plays with Jeremiah Love,  Jadarian Price, and Malachi Fields moving on to the NFL. My understanding is that Jonas Walton and Bubba Frazier have had a good camp as far as freshmen go. And they appear to be two of the few players on the roster who have a third gear. Do you think the staff will find a way to get that speed on the field on certain plays, like jet sweeps, bubble screens, etc.? Eric Hansen : There are a few questions in the queue today regarding these two freshmen, and they’ve been on my mind as well. But both of the Georgia high school products just have been too impressive to put on the back burner. They both bring the speed. They’re both super intelligent. The next step for both is more consistency. They have a shared history as well — in track and field. As high school juniors in the spring of 2025, Walton finished second (10.66 seconds) and Frazier third (10.72) in the Georgia Class 4A track and field finals. Walton also finished 10th in the shot put. They did not run in this spring’s state track meet, as seniors, because they were already enrolled at Notre Dame as mid-year enrollees. Frazier has likely pushed his way into the Irish WR rotation, that will likely go 7 deep. Walton is No. 4 in a three-man running back rotation, and yet he and fellow freshman Javian Osborne will get their opportunities. And the more well-rounded Walton can be with all aspects of being a running back, the more of a chance he’ll get. This was offensive coordinator Mike Denbrock on Walton and Osborne in Tuesday’s post-practice interviews: “When you hand those guys the ball, it’s reminiscent of what we’ve watched the last couple of years. And I’m not comparing them to those two guys [ Jeremiyah Love and Jadarian Price ], but I’m saying they have something else about them that is really, really cool. And they’re home run hitters. And you get them in open grass, and they’re going to make people pay. “So, how do you balance that when that time comes? When do you get those guys in? Because in protection right now, they’re a disaster. And they have no idea where this is or that is. Quarterback’s pointing over here, ‘Hey, you’ve got him, and this guy, that guy.’ So anyway, there’s that part. “But if you hand it to them, there’s some special traits there and ability there that can help us be more explosive offensively. articles.title: NFL will no longer play Pro Bowl game after 75 years
articles.summary: In shocking news, the NFL has decided to cancel the Pro Bowl game. The game that celebrates the best players in the NFL has been played since 1951. However, the game itself has gone from a showcase of talent to a clear burden on players in recent years. Not only do players frequently decline invi
articles._body: In shocking news, the NFL has decided to cancel the Pro Bowl game . The game that celebrates the best players in the NFL has been played since 1951. However, the game itself has gone from a showcase of talent to a clear burden on players in recent years. Not only do players frequently decline invites, leading to role players and bench contributors earning the accolade of Pro Bowler, but the game itself has been a low-effort affair. Players have prioritized their health over actually giving effort on the gridiron recently. The game has even been played in flag football form in recent years. Jonathan Jones was the first to report the jaw-dropping news. The drastic decision comes after years of the NFL trying to improve the Pro Bowl weekend, along with the viewership of the game. Last year, the Pro Bowl was integrated with Super Bowl festivities. Before then, different formats were tested out, and the league even added skills competitions. Regardless of what changed/was added, it became clear that the Pro Bowl was a dying game. The decision to cancel the Pro Bowl game comes directly after the 75th anniversary of the game. The “American Conference” beat the National Conference 28-27 back in 1951. While the game itself is no more, the accolade of being a Pro Bowler still remains. In fact, being named to the Pro Bowl team will be even more prestigious going forward because the league won’t need to fill out the roster with alternates. The NFL has tweaked the Pro Bowl so much in recent years that it wouldn’t be a surprise if they eventually brought the game back, but for now, and during the 2026 season, it is a thing of the past. The post NFL will no longer play Pro Bowl game after 75 years appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles.title: Za’Darius Smith reveals heartbreaking reason why he retired abruptly in 2025
articles.summary: Za’Darius Smith shocked many in the football world when he announced his retirement last year. Now he’s opening up about his reasoning. In a recent news conference, Smith said that the reason he chose to retire during his time with the Philadelphia Eagles last season was because of hi
articles._body: Za’Darius Smith shocked many in the football world when he announced his retirement last year. Now he’s opening up about his reasoning. In a recent news conference, Smith said that the reason he chose to retire during his time with the Philadelphia Eagles last season was because of his family. Per Smith, he received a call from his mother’s doctors saying that she didn’t have much longer to live, and he opted to retire from the Eagles. His mother passed away last October following his retirement, as well as his father and grandfather. “I was in a dark place,” Smith recalls. After entertaining a return to the Cleveland Browns , he ultimately decided to sign with the Atlanta Falcons following James Pearce Jr.’s suspension and Jalon Walker’s season-ending ACL injury. Smith details the fit as perfect for several reasons, but specifically for one sentimental reason. “My mom — rest her soul, man — she always wanted me to be in Atlanta with the Falcons.” Selected 122nd overall by the Baltimore Ravens in 2015, Smith has carved out a career as one of the league’s premier defenders. He’s compiled 343 total tackles, 70.5 sacks, 16 pass deflections, 10 forced fumbles and two fumble recoveries over that span. Last week, during a media availability, Kevin Stefanski spoke about reuniting with Smith . “Za’Darius brings physicality, obviously. He’s somebody that I’ve been with, so I have a comfort level with Za’Darius the person. Za’Darius the player certainly brings an element of a veteran pass rusher, but a guy who can play on all downs.” He added, “I think we were together ’23, ’24. Then [they] traded him, in the middle maybe of ’24. But yeah, big personality, huge personality. You’re gonna hear him before you see him. But heavy hands, good against the run, was an excellent teammate for us.” The post Za’Darius Smith reveals heartbreaking reason why he retired abruptly in 2025 appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles.title: Dolly Parton Hit Billboard’s Dance Charts, Too, And Even Earned a No. 1 Hit
articles.summary: The icon first reached a dance ranking in 1978 and led in 2019 with her Galantis collaboration “Faith.”
articles._body: Dolly Parton built an unparalleled career in country music, charting more than 100 hits on Billboard ’s Hot Country Songs ranking and earning 25 No. 1s — the most among women all-time. But Parton, who died Tuesday in Nashville at age 80, also ventured into other genres, even finding success on Billboard ’s dance charts. Parton’s first foray into dance music came in 1978, when she released the disco-influenced country album Heartbreaker . The set reached No. 5 on the Top Country Albums chart (though it long predated the 2001 launch of Billboard ’s Top Dance Albums chart). Related Miley Cyrus Mourns Her Godmother Dolly Parton: ‘I Have an Angel by My Side’ Taylor Swift Remembers Dolly Parton as ‘True Grace & True Grit, All in One Dazzling Person’ Fearless, Fabulous Dolly Parton and What We Can All Learn From Her: A Remembrance Heartbreaker generated Parton’s first dance hit in the double-sided single “Baby I’m Burnin’”/“I Wanna Fall in Love,” which peaked at No. 15 in early 1979 on the (now-inactive) Dance Club Songs chart. Parton returned to Dance Club Songs in 1981 with another paired entry, “9 to 5”/“House of the Rising Sun.” The former served as the famed theme to the film of the same name, in which Parton co-starred, while the latter was her take on the traditional folk ballad., She made three more appearances on Dance Club Songs: with “Potential New Boyfriend” in 1983, bolstered by a nearly six-minute extended dance mix; her 1997 cover of Cat Stevens’ “Peace Train,” which received several dance remixes, including one featuring Ladysmith Black Mambazo; and, following a two-decade-plus absence, “Faith,” with Galantis and featuring Mr. Probz, in 2020. “Faith,” a dance reworking of John Hiatt’s 1987 song “Have a Little Faith in Me,” gave Parton a No. 1 on a dance chart at last, as it topped Dance Airplay in 2019. It also reached No. 10 on Hot Dance/Electronic Songs . When Parton announced “Faith” at the Grand Ole Opry in Nashville in 2019, she noted that she was prioritizing the release of positive, uplifting music. “This world is just so dark and ugly and awful … so I’m going to make it my business to try to do songs that are more uplifting, not all Christian-based songs, but songs about better things,” she said . “Do better, and have a little more love, a little more light and don’t be so dark and dirty.” During her lifetime, Parton topped five of Billboard ’s currently published radio charts: Adult Contemporary, Country Airplay, Christian Airplay, Christian AC Airplay and Dance Airplay. Parton’s genre-spanning exploration continued through her most recent studio album, Rockstar , in 2023. The set, her 49th studio release, earned the icon her first No. 1 on a Billboard rock chart when it spent a week atop the Top Rock Albums list. It also became her highest-charted entry on the Billboard 200 when it debuted and peaked at No. 3. The collection includes covers of rock classics and collaborations with many of the genre’s biggest names, including Lynyrd Skynyrd on “Free Bird,” Joan Jett on “I Hate Myself for Loving You” and Paul McCartney and Ringo Starr on “Let It Be.”

articles.title: 2027 NFL Draft QB rankings: Where do Arch Manning, Dante Moore rank before Week 0?
articles.summary: The last couple of quarterback classes in the NFL Draft have been somewhat underwhelming for one reason or another, but the same sentiment has remained: “Just wait for 2027.” Now, the 2026 college football season is here and it’s finally time to five into the 2027 draft class. A
articles._body: The last couple of quarterback classes in the NFL Draft have been somewhat underwhelming for one reason or another, but the same sentiment has remained: “Just wait for 2027.” Now, the 2026 college football season is here and it’s finally time to five into the 2027 draft class. As promised, there are a ton of big names and elite prospects at multiple premium positions, including quarterback. The popular names will get plenty of attention coming into the season, and rightfully so. Dante Moore of Oregon and Arch Manning of Texas are the consensus top two quarterbacks on the board coming into the season, and that is the case in our rankings as well. However, a number of players are behind them and will have a chance to make a statement and get into that conversation at the top of the draft. Without further ado, let’s get into the top 10 quarterbacks in the 2027 NFL Draft class before the season gets going. 1. Dante Moore, Oregon Jeffrey Becker-Imagn Images Moore very likely would have been the No. 2 overall pick if he had declared for the 2026 NFL Draft, and he is our early favorite to be the No. 1 pick in the 2027 draft coming into the season. The Oregon signal-caller has a great arm and elite accuracy, with the athleticism and playmaking ability to make things happen when the play breaks down. He has an elite group of skill players coming back to Eugene with him, which should only help him improve his draft stock. There are still a few concerns with Moore. First of all, Oregon has a new offensive coordinator after the departure of Will Stein and some questions on the offensive line that the second-year starter will have to overcome. On top of that, Moore has a thin frame (by all indications he has added weight over the summer) and has struggled at times when forced to play under pressure. If that improves, he has all the makings of a No. 1 pick. 2. Arch Manning, Texas Scott Wachter-Imagn Images Manning is still a bit more of a projection than Moore at this point, but it feels like he has a higher ceiling than the Oregon QB does. The former five-star recruit is a truly elite athlete who adds a ton in the running game with his size and speed. That size also gives him a commanding presence in the pocket, which improved during the 2025 season despite playing under duress constantly. He had accuracy issues early in the season, but those improved as the year went on and he became more comfortable and confident. Manning also showed some rare traits late in the season, both with pocket movement and anticipation, that some much more experienced quarterbacks do not have. Texas improved its skill group in 2026, and given Manning’s rate of improvement over the 2025 campaign, it would be no surprise if he’s at the top of this list before too long. 3. Darian Mensah, Miami (FL) David Butler II-Imagn Images This is a bit higher than most lists have Mensah, but it’s very easy to see where the Duke transfer could have a Cam Ward-style glow up after transferring to a very talented Miami squad. Mensah isn’t the most impressive quarterback physically, but he does a lot of things incredibly well at the position. He attacks the middle of the field with anticipation and accuracy, has an NFL-ready release and showed the ability to make plays outside of structure last season. Mensah led a Duke team that didn’t have a ton of talent to an ACC Championship last season. Now, playing with other NFL talent around him in Miami, the sky is truly the limit for our preseason Heisman Trophy pick in 2026. 4. CJ Carr, Notre Dame Sam Navarro-Imagn Images Carr came into the 2025 season as a bit of an unknown, but he proved throughout the season that he should be on the NFL radar coming into 2026. Carr has great intangibles for the position; he keeps the offense on schedule, finds the right place to go with the football and has the requisite physical tools to get it just about anywhere on the field. He is an excellent passer with a strong arm and good accuracy. If you’re poking holes in Carr’s game, it’s that he doesn’t necessarily possess the rare physical traits that a usual No. 1 pick-level of prospect has (though it is far from a weakness). Can he improve on that and add that “wow” factor to his game? That remains to be seen. Notre Dame also lost two running backs who were drafted in the first round of the NFL Draft a year ago, which means Carr will be carrying much more of a burden this season. That can be both a blessing and a curse, but it shouldn’t be a big issue here. 5. Drew Mestemaker, Oklahoma State Danny Wild-Imagn Images Mestemaker is a fascinating prospect for a few reasons. He lit it up at North Texas in 2025, and now he is following head coach Eric Morris to Stillwater along with many of his top weapons. He is a true gunslinger with a live arm, willing to make tight window throws all over the field. There isn’t a throw in between the white lines that he can’t access. He is also a fluid athlete at 6-foot-4, which opens a lot of things up for an offense But the drawback for Mestemaker is massive. He didn’t start at quarterback in high school, instead serving as a safety while being the backup QB. He walked on at North Texas and started just one game in 2024. That means he has just one year of experience as a starting quarterback since he was in middle school. Is two years, provided he starts all year in 2026, enough to make a bet on Mestemaker as an NFL signal-caller? It will be a massive jump mentally for him to get to the pros next season, especially if a team is taking a gamble on him as a first-round pick. A jump up in competition in the Big 12 this season will make him a fascinating watch in 2026. 6. articles.title: Report: NFL plans to eliminate annual Pro Bowl game, will honor players with celebration
articles.summary: The NFL has held its annual Pro Bowl all-star game in one version or another since 1951. Well, that tradition will end with the 2026 Pro Bowl after the league opted to finally do away with the non-competitive game traditionally held the Sunday before the Super Bowl, according to The Athletic‘s
articles._body: The NFL has held its annual Pro Bowl all-star game in one version or another since 1951. Well, that tradition will end with the 2026 Pro Bowl after the league opted to finally do away with the non-competitive game traditionally held the Sunday before the Super Bowl, according to The Athletic ‘s Jonathan Jones . Instead of holding a traditional game — or a series of all-star events as has been the case the past few years — the NFL will honor 88 total players during an annual in-person celebration in Los Angeles in February, according to Jones. The process for selecting Pro Bowl players will remain the same, through a combination of equally weighted votes cast by fans, players and coaches, per Jones. “All-star games, I think, for all leagues have been fraught for a long time, and they haven’t necessarily represented the very best premium of that sport for those players,” NFL executive vice president of club business, international and league events Peter O’Reilly told The Athletic . “I think all leagues have struggled with that. We made the switch four years ago from the ‘tackle’ Pro Bowl to the flag game, and that was more strategic for us. In many ways, we saw a decrease in the replacement players. “But ultimately, the Pro Bowl, at its core, is about honoring the best of the best in that season, on the field, in real games. And the shift here is about shifting the focus from the game — which is ultimately where people’s attention goes, especially the replacement players tied to it — to the honor.” This report will be updated.

articles.title: Jalen Brewster, the nation’s top recruit, locks in commitment to Texas Tech despite heavy pursuit
articles.summary: Five-star DL Jalen Brewster will stick with Texas Tech and enroll right away in Lubbock. Rivals has the latest on the big development for Joey McGuire and the Red Raiders.
articles._body: Five-star defensive lineman Jalen Brewster will honor his long-standing commitment to Texas Tech, his family tells Rivals. Rivals No. 1 recruit in the 2027 class was even considering enrolling early and playing this fall in Lubbock but will instead play his senior season at Buford (Ga.) High. Brewster ultimately chose to play for head coach Joey McGuire and the Red Raiders over LSU. Other schools he strongly considered throughout his process included Florida, Indiana, Ohio State, SMU and Texas. “Culture, family, atmosphere, everybody playing together,” Brewster has said of what stands out. He also talked about his process on his YouTube channel here. “The way they feed into their players. The words, the practices, practice like games. Culture for sure. “The way they run their program, how they were underdogs and nobody thought they would make it this far. It was me looking for a program where I can be a better self and have a great circle around me and make it to the next level.” Brewster’s family has always spoken highly of Texas Tech. His father Robert played offensive line in the NFL. “It’s a family atmosphere,” the elder Brewster said. “With a lot of these coaches it’s all about ball, that’s it. With (Joey) McGuire and Tech, especially McGuire, you can tell he cares about family and cares about the players and that’s the main thing I’m looking for in a school for my son. “Texas Tech from day one everything has been the same. They’ve never changed, never switched, that’s the one thing we love about them so much.” Rivals Director of Scouting Charles Power compares Brewster’s game to Jalen Carter. “Uber-athletic defensive line prospect with true game-wrecking ability. Measured in at around 6-foot-3, 300 pounds prior to his junior season. Carries his weight exceptionally well with a dense build. Tests as an elite athlete in the combine setting, easily cracking 5.0 seconds in the 40-yard dash. Carries that athleticism over to the field where he has consistent flashes of dominance on Friday nights. Lines up all over the defensive line for Cedar Hill (Texas) High while facing top competition. A dangerous pass rusher from any spot. Combines explosive get-off with the movement skills of a much smaller player, carrying elite testing numbers directly onto the field. Consistently collapses pockets and disrupts plays before they develop.  “Has legitimate game-wrecking moments on film. The quickness to dart into the backfield and the speed to hunt down ball carriers is eye-popping. Was tabbed as the Rivals MVP at the Under Armour All-America Game after his junior season. Showcased high-end functional power on top of his elite movement skills in the all-star setting. May not possess premier length. Father was a third-round pick by the Dallas Cowboys. Tracking as the top defensive line prospect in the 2027 cycle and projects to have high odds to ultimately become a 1st round NFL Draft pick.” Brewster is the jewel of a Texas Tech recruiting class that Rivals ranks No. 9 nationally. The Red Raiders also boast the No. 1 ranked class in the Big 12.

articles.title: Oklahoma State flips OL Odaefe Oruru away from Arkansas: ‘This staff is building something special in Stillwater’
articles.summary: Behind the scenes as the Cowboys secure their biggest flip of the 2027 cycle
articles._body: Oklahoma State is still days away from kicking off the 2026 season and its first game under new head coach Eric Morris — just as the Cowboys close out the offseason with some fireworks. Three-star Jenks (Okla.) High School interior offensive line prospect Odaefe Oruru has flipped his commitment from Arkansas to Oklahoma State, he tells Rivals. It’s a decision that has been brewing since the spring, when he committed to the Razorbacks. Morris, position coach Cody Crill , and the entire Oklahoma State coaching staff have been working feverishly to change his mind ever since. “I took some time to speak with my family and my team about what would put me in the best position moving forward,” Oruru told Rivals. “At the end of the day, I wanted the opportunity to represent my home state.” The Razorbacks and Cowboys were jockeying for position at the top of Oruru’s recruitment dating back to the spring — even before he declared for the Hogs. The Rivals Industry Ranking No. 36 interior OL logged both of his official visits in the spring. Oklahoma State kept its foot on the gas with the touted in-state target throughout the summer and finally pulled ahead as Oruru prepared to kick off his junior season at Jenks in a few days. “I’m most excited about coming in and making an early impact, and being able to do what I’ve always wanted to do…play football at the highest level,” he detailed. “My ties to Oklahoma. I’ve lived here my whole life, and this is home for me. The staff is building something special in Stillwater, and I want to be a part of it. I just thought, why not keep it going at the next level and represent the state I grew up in?” Oruru ranks as the No. 496 overall prospect in the 2027 class and the No. 12 player regardless of position inside the state of Oklahoma for the cycle.

articles.title: Ryan Waldschmidt clubs another walk-off home run
articles.summary: The former Bat Cat is Mr. Clutch.
articles._body: The push for October is ongoing in Major League Baseball. Teams are jockeying for playoff position right now. The Arizona Diamondbacks are making a push for one of the wild card spots in the National League. Former Kentucky outfielder Ryan Waldschmidt keeps impacting winning. This former Bat Cat is quietly becoming Mr. Clutch. Waldschmidt hit his second career walk-off home run to erase a deficit against the Chicago Cubs on Tuesday night just a couple of weeks after walking it off against the Los Angeles Dodgers . WALK-OFF HOME RUN Down to the @Dbacks last out, Ryan Waldschmidt flips the script! pic.twitter.com/5tq5ojZiN8 — MLB (@MLB) August 26, 2026 The Bradenton (Fla.) Braden River product started his college baseball career at Charleston Southern where he hit nine home runs and 43 RBI as a freshman. Waldschmidt then entered the transfer portal and landed at Kentucky in 2023. Waldschmidt hit .290 with 20 extra-base hits in his first year at UK on a super regional team. The outfielder then suffered a torn ACL while playing summer baseball but that did not stop him from making a big splash as a junior in 2024. Waldschmidt slashed .333/.469/.610 with 17 doubles and 14 home runs on a College World Series team. That ultimately led to a big opportunity in professional baseball. The Arizona Diamondbacks selected Waldschmidt with the No. 31 overall pick in the 2024 MLB Draft. After a strong 2025 run in Double-A where Waldschmidt hit .309 across 300 plate appearances with 14 doubles and nine home runs at Amarillo, Waldschmidt began this season in Triple-A and slashed .287/.400/.477 with nine doubles, three triples, and three home runs. That ultimately led to his first big break in May. It’s starting to look like the outfielder has staying power in the big leauges. This Kentucky product is slashing .276/.339/.400 with 15 doubles, one triple, three home runs, 21 RBI, and seven stolen bases across 236 plate appearances. Two of those dingers have been walk-off bombs to win the game. Arizona (70-63) is one game back of he Philadelphia Phillies for the final wild card spot in the National League with 29 games left to play. Ryan Waldschmidt will continue to play a role as this team continues its playoff push. The Kentucky product is helping the D-backs play winning baseball.

articles.title: Tim Curry’s 5 Best Musical Moments, From ‘Rocky Horror’ to ‘Muppet Treasure Island’
articles.summary: The legendary performer died at the age of 80 on Aug. 25.
articles._body: The world lost one of its most versatile, captivating performers when Tim Curry died on Wednesday (Aug. 25). The English singer-actor passed away at the age of 80 in his Los Angeles home, about 14 years after he suffered a major stroke that resulted in his use of a wheelchair for the rest of his life. His longtime manager, Marcia Hurwitz, confirmed the news to Billboard in a statement praising his “curious, expansive mind and generous, gentle heart, both of which remained open and filled with anticipation until his final breath.” But while Curry is no longer with us, fans will always have his illustrious resumé of iconic roles in film and theater to remember him by — many of which feature memorable musical numbers performed with a combination of charisma, comedic timing and booming baritone vibrato that was entirely his own. The three-time Tony nominee also enjoyed recording music independent of his acting projects, releasing three studio albums of both cover songs and originals. His most successful LP, Fearless , reached No. 53 on the Billboard 200 in 1979, and he even scored an entry on the Billboard Hot 100 back in the day — but more on that later. So, in honor of a truly irreplaceable figure in entertainment, Billboard is looking back at Curry’s best musical moments. From his performances in The Rocky Horror Picture Show to Muppet Treasure Island , his own recorded music and more, keep reading to see our favorite of the legendary star’s numerous forays into music below.

articles._body: Rockstar Games has taken a lot of heat over the last week, as leaks of their upcoming game — Grand Theft Auto VI — have been surfacing on social media by a frustrated gamer. Gameplay and story leaks have been among the primary things that have been posted online. On Wednesday, about a week after this all started, Rockstar Games has broken their silence and released a statement. Dear all, We know that many of you have been waiting to hear from us regarding the events of the past week. It would be an understatement to say that having videos of Grand Theft Auto VI gameplay leak in this way has been heartbreaking for our team, and this is obviously not how we intended for you to see the game after all this time. We are very sorry that everything has taken as long as it has – from getting the game finished (nearly there!) to sharing more details and official gameplay, and providing the community with everything you want to know. We are very excited for everyone to see the extended look tomorrow. It has taken longer than we wanted to get it ready, but as with everything we do, we know we need to exceed your expectations, and we are determined to deliver at the level you expect and deserve. While it is unfortunate that the intended game experience may now be impacted by some spoilers, we hope that everyone will wait a bit longer to experience the game for themselves on November 19. We want to thank everyone in the community who has reached out with messages of support this past week – your words have meant more to this team than you can imagine. Ultimately, we are making this game for you, and without you, we would not have the privilege of making games. We look forward to sharing more with you soon. Sincerely, Rockstar Games Some new features expected to be in the game include an in-game social media system that you can scroll through and see existing characters blow up through viral posts as well as the bodies of the main characters physically changing if you eat too much or work out. articles.title: Billions Pour Into Bitcoin ETFs as Rally Rolls On
articles.summary: Bitcoin Magazine
articles._body: Bitcoin Magazine Billions Pour Into Bitcoin ETFs as Rally Rolls On Bitcoin exchange-traded funds have continued their winning streak, attracting billions of dollars in new investment over the past week.  U.S. investors have thrown $2.56 billion since last Monday, according to Farside Investors data, helping push the leading cryptocurrency’s price higher.  And this week alone, nearly $652 million in fresh cash has hit the products managed by the likes of BlackRock, Morgan Stanley, and Fidelity.  Bitcoin was recently trading for $78,302 after jumping nearly 25% over a seven-day period. The coin touched as high as $81,160 on Monday.  JUST IN: U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs have taken in $2.08 billion over the past 5 trading sessions pic.twitter.com/GskNy0yPfc — Bitcoin Magazine (@BitcoinMagazine) August 26, 2026 Bitcoin’s rise comes after a sluggish June and July when it mostly traded below $65,000.  The cryptocurrency has benefited from news that the Treasury would at least double the size of its liquidity-support buyback operations. The announcement last week hurt the dollar but non-yielding assets like Bitcoin and gold have benefited.   Bloomberg Intelligence ETF Analyst Eric Balchunas wrote on X Wednesday that the debasement trade was back. “Gold and Bitcoin ETFs have combined for +$7b in flows in past week, by far a record for a 5-day period as debasement trade steals spotlight from AI,” he said.  The debasement trade is when investors buy an asset to hedge against a currency losing value. Investments like Bitcoin and precious metals have done well as part of the trade as they cannot be endlessly printed.   Last year, the investment strategy was much talked about but then went quiet as investors focused more on buying artificial intelligence-related equities. Investors now are fretting over U.S. borrowing, a weak dollar and efforts to contain long-term yields. Bitcoin ETFs had their best week since October last week, with nearly $2 billion in inflows.  Positive regulatory coming out of the White House has also spurred the flurry of trading activity. President Donald Trump held a meeting with crypto executives earlier last week before urging lawmakers to get the long-awaited crypto Clarity Act over the line. This post Billions Pour Into Bitcoin ETFs as Rally Rolls On first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Mathew Di Salvo .

articles._body: The Detroit Tigers are doing everything they can to avoid falling out of the postseason race. The Tigers initially found success after trading Tarik Skubal , but the team is now just 2-8 over its past 10 games. Riley Greene landed on the injured list with a hamstring injury on August 12, and the Tigers have been especially bad during his absence. So, will Greene return from the injury concern soon? According to MLB.com, Greene is expected to return at some point in early September and “ could begin rehab assignment soon .” Greene is already a three-time All-Star at just 25 years old. He is one of the better outfielders in the game and the Tigers clearly need him on the field. Updates on his injury status will continue to be monitored and provided as they are made available. Detroit is now 62-71 and in fourth place in the American League Central standings. The ball club is 7.5 games back of first place at the moment. Additionally, the Tigers are 5.0 games back of an AL Wild Card spot. The postseason remains within reach, but the Tigers’ recent slump has them on the verge of falling out of postseason contention. They need to turn things around as soon as possible with the season winding down. There is still plenty of baseball left to be played, but the Tigers must find a way to get back on track soon. Perhaps Riley Greene’s return from injury will help the Tigers figure things out. It remains to be seen when he will return from the hamstring injury, though. articles.title: Will Ella Langley’s ‘Choosin’ Texas’ Pass Mariah Carey’s ‘Christmas’ for the All-Time Hot 100 Record for Weeks at No. 1 — And Then Just Keep Going?
articles.summary: Langley's country-pop smash is already up to 19 weeks atop the Hot 100 — leaving it just three shy of the record Carey has set with her holiday perennial.
articles._body: This week, Ella Langley ‘s country-pop smash “Choosin’ Texas” hits another historic chart benchmark, spending a 19th week at No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 (dated Aug. 29). That ties the song with Lil Nas X’s Billy Ray Cyrus-featuring “Old Town Road” and Shaboozey’s “A Bar Song (Tipsy)” for the second-longest reign in the chart’s history — as well as the longest stay for a song during a single Hot 100 run. Related Ella Langley’s ‘Choosin’ Texas’ Ties for Longest Hot 100 Rule Among Non-Holiday Hits With 19th Week at No. 1 How Ella Langley Navigated The Whirlwind Success Of ‘Choosin’ Texas’ — And Why She Thinks ‘Women Are About To Take Over’ Ella Langley, Morgan Wallen & More: Inside Country Music’s Historic Decade and What’s To Expect Next But for the overall all-time record for the most weeks spent atop the Hot 100, there’s still one song to beat: “All I Want for Christmas Is You,” the 1994 Mariah Carey holiday perennial that first topped the chart in 2019, and has ruled for multiple weeks in every year since — not counting the rest of 2026, though it already did notch week on top this year in early January. That week was its 22nd at No. 1, putting it three frames ahead of any other No. 1 hit in Hot 100 history. Perhaps not for long, however. With no major current-day stars releasing new music on Friday (Aug. 21) and nothing below “Choosin’ Texas” on the Hot 100 particularly zooming up in performance this week, it seems a strong bet that “Texas” will become just the second song to ever spend 20 weeks at No. 1. And from there, it might not be long until it overtakes “Christmas” to become the lone record-holder for the longest-running chart-topper in Hot 100 history. Consider that despite having spent 44 weeks on the Hot 100 already — close to half of them at No. 1 at this point — “Texas” not only still sits atop the chart, it does so with a 1.54-to-1 lead in Hot 100 points over the current No. 2 song, Stella Lefty’s own country-pop crossover hit “Boston.” For some context of how sizable a lead that is, the points advantage that “Boston” currently has over the Hot 100’s No. 3 song this week, Taylor Swift’s “I Knew It, I Knew You” is just 1.09-to-1. (Those numbers reflect the blend of songs’ streaming, radio airplay and sales data that determines Hot 100 ranks each week.) What’s more, Langley’s lead is also “Texas”-sized when compared to the 19th week at No. 1 enjoyed by the song’s two predecessors. When “Old Town Road” was in its 19th week at No. 1 back in 2019, it held just a 1.16-to-1 advantage over that week’s No. 2 song (Billie Eilish’s “Bad Guy,” which took over the following week). When “A Bar Song (Tipsy)” reigned for a 19th frame, its total was practically equal to that of the No. 2 finisher (Lady Gaga and Bruno Mars’ “Die With a Smile”) — though both songs were passed the next week by Kendrick Lamar’s then-debuting “Squabble Up.” Finally, perhaps the most-impressive thing about Langley’s points lead is that it has essentially held steady for months. In the song’s 15th week at No. 1 (on the chart dated Aug. 5), her lead was 1.56-to-1. In the song’s 10th week at No. 1 (on the chart dated May 23), her lead over No. 2 was 1.55-to-1. Incredibly, that span of weeks also includes a five-week interruption where the song was deposed from No. 1 by a trio of generational superstars: Drake (“Janice STFU,” two weeks), Ariana Grande (“Hate That I Made You Love Me,” one week) and Taylor Swift (“I Knew It, I Knew You,” two weeks). But while those songs receded from clear-cut No. 1 contention shortly after their predictably resounding debuts, “Choosin’ Texas” has remained consistently strong. Looking to the future, it is hard to spot a new release — either out already or imminently due — that seems likely to be an aggressive challenger to “Texas” on the Hot 100 in the near future. New hits by Steve Lacy (“Oh Yeah?”) and Tame Impala (“Loser”) have surged up the chart recently, spurred by their synch placements in the new blockbuster Spider-Man: Brand New Day . But as that movie’s box office returns have naturally begun to slow (though are still  dominant ), so have the songs’ chart ascents: “Loser” bounds 22-18 this week and “Oh Yeah?” climbs 18-17, but both will likely need additional boosts to get within range of “Texas.” Meanwhile, the upcoming release schedule for the next month contains big names like Rod Wave, JENNIE, Luke Bryan, Tinashe and Riley Green, but no one who has a history of topping the Hot 100 (outside of Carly Rae Jepsen, who did so back in 2012, but has not visited the top five again since). Surprise releases or one-off singles may materialize in the interim — and certainly if you’re a fan of Drake or Taylor Swift , you may have your own theories as to what those reliable chart-toppers have in store for the upcoming months. But in terms of album releases currently on the calendar for the next month, it’s hard to see one posing a real immediate threat to Langley’s supremacy. So might it be up to Stella Lefty and “Boston,” then? If you’re a Lamb hoping that Carey is able to protect her all-time mark, that might be your best bet: Lefty’s breakout hit has steadily climbed the Hot 100 for most of the past 20 weeks, finally landing in the runner-up spot for the first time this week. articles.title: USC football’s 2027 NFL Draft prospect outlook before Week 0 opener
articles.summary: USC football pumped out its sixth NFL Draft first rounder since the 2020 class in Makai Lemon. The rookie Philadelphia Eagles wide receiver now leaves quarterback Jayden Maiava with a new WR1 to find before facing San Jose State in Week 0. But that also hands Maiava a strong chance to elevate his
articles._body: USC football pumped out its sixth NFL Draft first rounder since the 2020 class in Makai Lemon. The rookie Philadelphia Eagles wide receiver now leaves quarterback Jayden Maiava with a new WR1 to find before facing San Jose State in Week 0. But that also hands Maiava a strong chance to elevate his own draft stock ahead of Saturday. The nation’s No. 14 ranked team will help open the college football season up inside the Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum. And will more than likely draw NFL scouts in as the Spartans come to town. So that leads into the 2027 draft prospect look in the land of troy. Quarterback Jayden Maiava Troy Wayrynen-Imagn Images He’s hands down USC’s next best draft prospect from coach Lincoln Riley. Except Maiava can join history at both USC and under Riley. Maiava can become the ninth Heisman Trophy winner at USC with a breakout 2026. Plus rise as Riley’s fourth Heisman winner and join a fraternity that features Baker Mayfield, Kyler Murray and Caleb Williams, the latter representing Riley’s lone USC victor for the coveted award. SJSU doesn’t come off as a fierce challenge for Maiava. Especially after fielding the nation’s 121st overall defensive unit from 2025 and are undergoing a rebuild there. So signs point to a fast start for Maiava. But his draft stock elevates if he shreds these two future home opponents: No. 2 Oregon on Sept. 26, then top-ranked Ohio State on Halloween night. He’ll ignite Heisman conversations too in surpassing both heavyweights. Wide receiver Terrell Anderson Charles LeClaire-Imagn Images Tanook Hines enters this season anticipated to surface as Maiava’s new go-to target. But he’s only a sophomore, while the North Carolina State transfer Anderson presents his own intriguing skill set ahead of his junior season. Anderson arrives as the proverbial deep threat here, plus adds return value as a special teamer. Exploding in Riley’s offense in season one will catapult his name into league conversations. Anderson could join Jordan Addison as past transfers who rose as future first rounders after playing for USC. Center/Guard Tobias Raymond Raymond surfaces as a major X-Factor for USC. He’s sliding down to center amid Kilian O’Connor losing his 2026 season with a broken leg injury. Yet O’Connor’s absence presents this golden chance for Raymond: Showcasing his versatility and strength. The Ventura, California native Raymond can show the nation he’s both a road grader and Maiava’s top pass protector. Especially in handling blitzes up the middle as Raymond likely will get tested a lot among the five starting linemen. A dominating junior campaign can lift his own draft stock. Defensive Tackle Jide Abasiri This junior faces his own “step to the plate” moment. Abasiri’s heralded sophomore teammate Jahkeem Stewart won’t line up next to him amid his foot injury. So the muscular 6-foot-5, 280-pounder rises as the long-armed pass rusher inside for the Week 0 matchup. Abasiri can pile the sack count facing a pass-heavy SJSU team. He’s fresh off delivering 17 solo tackles with 3.5 sacks. Cornerback Jontez Williams Time for one more College Football Transfer Portal addition who can emerge as a draft selection here. Williams picked off four passes and swatted five more in 2024 with Iowa State. He heads to USC with quieter 2025 numbers (two PBUs and one pick) in tow. But new defensive coordinator Gary Patterson can re-unlock Williams especially in press man coverage. Plus Patterson’s mix-and-match ability can throw off quarterbacks and lead to errant throws, which can re-establish Williams as a ball hawk and possibly, become Patterson’s new “Jason Verrett” here as the latest high CB draft pick from him. articles.title: Countdown to kickoff prediction series: South Carolina will return to elite kick coverage performances
articles.summary: Continuing the countdown to kickoff prediction series: South Carolina will return to elite kick coverage performances
articles._body: In May, when the calendar revealed that it was 100 days until South Carolina kicked off the season, I posted a story on GamecockCentral entitled “100 predictions for the 2026 Gamecocks.” Now, that countdown is down to just 10 days. The prediction paired with day 10 read, “South Carolina’s kickoff coverage will mirror the beginning of the 2025 season, when it was borderline-elite, not the end of the 2025 campaign, when it was below-average.” Let’s break down that prognostication. Have a question for the GamecockCentral staff? Ask it now on The Insiders Forum. Fixing a problem For most of the Shane Beamer era, South Carolina has had a good kickoff return unit. In fact, the Gamecocks have never allowed a kick return touchdown during his five years at the helm of the program. 2025 started with USC continuing the trend of strong coverage play. But somewhere along the way, things fell apart a bit. That likely coincided with the season going sideways. Against Ole Miss, in particular, the Gamecocks surrendered a 42-yard and a 27-yard return. 42 yards is always too long, and so is 27 when one considers South Carolina’s emphasis on “touchbacks or pin ’em deep” kicks. Several other returns were just one broken tackle away from breaking. The kickoffs themselves weren’t always great, either. Max Kelley put multiple balls out of bounds as a freshman in 2025. He also had another kick that would have bounced out of bounds had a return man not made an ill-advised decision to pick up a shanked kick. There were definitely good moments defending kickoffs, but the combined efforts of Kelley and William Joyce at kickoffs and the other 10 Gamecocks in coverage weren’t consistent enough. In the end, South Carolina ranked as a top 30 national kickoff coverage team. That isn’t bad, but it isn’t up to the standard Shane Beamer holds for his special teams units. Beamer and new special teams coordinator Matthew Smiley will fight hard to return the coverage team to its previously elite status. What does this mean for the Gamecocks? Fellow subscribers are discussing it now on The Insiders Forum. Personnel Kickoffs start, of course, with a kicker. Max Kelley returns after an up-and-down freshman year. He is competing for the starting job again in 2026, along with transfer portal additions Upton Bellenfant and Malik Orsan. It is unclear at this time whether punter Mason Love is a major factor in the position battle, but he could handle duties if needed. The Gamecocks will need one of those players to step up and own the job this fall. Beyond the man who actually puts toe to leather, kickoff coverage has as much to do with the other 10 players on the field. Names like Maurice Brown, David Bucey, and Gerald Kilgore have had great moments on coverage units and return in 2026. Others like Justin Okoronkwo, Peyton Williams, Kendall Daniels, Donovan Darden, and Kelvin Hunter are among the other returners who have played in the past. Okoronkwo won South Carolina’s Special Teams Player of the Spring. Special teams units typically aren’t unveiled until the season officially begins. Because of that, knowing exactly who will play in the game’s third phase is impossible at this point. However, several of those names likely will reprise their roles. Based on the past (and this spring’s award), Brown, Bucey, Kilgore, and Okoronkwo appear very likely to contribute. Fans can also look to see several freshmen cut their teeth on special teams this fall. What’s your prediction? Share it with fellow subscribers on The Insiders Forum.

articles.title: Dolly Parton’s Manager Details the Business Ventures ‘She Had Yet to Fulfill’
articles.summary: Parton's team offered updates on projects including Dolly Parton's SongTeller Hotel and her Broadway musical.
articles._body: Music and entertainment legend Dolly Parton died on Aug. 25 at age 80, but the boundless creativity and tenacious work ethic that marked her life and career also mean that the slate of projects Parton and her team were working on at the time of her passing are still continuing on. Parton’s longtime manager Danny Nozell said in a statement, “Dolly worked up until the day she died. She loved seeing her dreams come to life, and loved knowing her work brought people joy. Ever the planner, Dolly worked with the team that she handpicked, for the past several years to build a project road map that will guide us for decades to come.” Related Dolly Parton Dead at 80: Music Executives Remember the Country Icon Dale Morris, Nashville Manager Who Guided Careers of Alabama & Kenny Chesney, Dies at 89 HYBE Pledges Over $300k for Colombia Earthquake Recovery Nozell continued, “As the leader of the team responsible for overseeing her legacy, we will ensure the many dreams she had yet to fulfill are brought to life. Many projects were in various stages of development, and we want to be transparent with her fans about this fact. If you see unreleased music, products, books, experiences, and campaigns launched through official Dolly Parton channels, you can have confidence in knowing that she placed her personal stamp on it.” The statement also offered updates on several business projects Parton and her team had been working on. In June, Parton opened Dolly’s Tennessean Travel Stops in Cornersville, Tenn., south of Nashville. The Parton-themed truck stop will take part in celebrating National Truck Driver Appreciation Week starting Sept. 13, 2026. Parton was also in the midst of opening the Dolly Parton’s SongTeller Hotel in downtown Nashville. The hotel will be open for stays beginning Sept. 14, with a grand opening planned for Sept. 29, 2026. Dolly’s Life of Many Colors Museum, which is housed in the hotel, is slated to have its grand opening on Sept. 29 as well. Parton has several other business products rolling out in September. A line of Dolly Dolls is set to launch online on Sept. 15. Dolly’s Cup of Ambition Coffee, created in partnership with Community Coffee, will launch online on Sept. 29, followed by a retail launch in spring 2027. The coffee will be available in light, medium and dark roasts, and is also sold at Dolly’s Tennessean Travel Stop. The singer’s musical about her life and career, Dolly: A True Original Musical , will begin Broadway previews on Dec. 7, with an opening night on Jan. 19, which would have been Parton’s 81st birthday. Parton and her team previewed the musical earlier this year at Nashville’s Belmont University. Additionally, a holiday project, Dolly On The Holly, is set to launch later this year, while the Kendra Scott x Dolly-The 9 to 5 collection of jewelry is slated to launch in January 2027. The jewelry collection includes rings and necklaces in Parton’s classic butterfly design, as well as earrings, necklaces and other jewelry in the designs of hearts and multicolored jewelry inspired by Parton’s song “Coat Of Many Colors.” Next year will also see the launch of Dolly’s Dog Treats line, as well as the Dolly Bedding & Home Decor line set for late 2027. Other projects in the pipeline include a Dolly avatar show, a Dolly musical documentary, an animated series based on her Billy The Kid children’s book series, as well as a Dolly-inspired biopic, docuseries and scripted series. On Aug. 25, representatives for Parton’s beloved Dollywood theme park also noted that the theme park would be open on Wednesday, Aug. 26, writing on Instagram, “In her spirit, Dollywood will be open Wednesday as Dolly wanted, always reminding everyone with her signature sparkle — ‘the show must go on.’ Together, we honor her by carrying forward her message of love, perseverance, and hope.” Parton passed away at Vanderbilt-Ingram Cancer Center in Nashville on Aug. 25, following a brief battle with cancer.

articles.title: David Pollack calls out ‘red flags’ for Texas ahead of 2026 season: ‘Where there’s smoke, there’s fire’
articles.summary: This has turned into one of the more anticipated seasons at Texas in recent times. Steve Sarkisian built a roster many believe is capable of winning the College Football Playoff. Sure, the schedule is tough but the Longhorns will have an advantage in most, if not all, of their games. And still, some
articles._body: This has turned into one of the more anticipated seasons at Texas in recent times. Steve Sarkisian built a roster many believe is capable of winning the College Football Playoff . Sure, the schedule is tough but the Longhorns will have an advantage in most, if not all, of their games. And still, some off-the-field incidents have led David Pollack to call out “red flags” for Texas. “There’s some angst in Austin,” Pollack said via See Ball Get Ball . “I think it’s been, ‘Okay, wait a minute.’ Worried about Arch… But Ty’Anthony Smith was dismissed last week from the team. Big-time contributor. Conduct detrimental to the team is what Sark said. He said he was dismissed, didn’t give a lot of detail. He wasn’t going to go into the details but he’s a really good player. You talk about depth. It’s unfortunate right now at this point of the season… “If you’re talking about somebody getting kicked off the team, so be it. But then you also have guys that are freshmen, their parents going on social media and blasting Texas and saying, ‘I’m going to unveil what’s going on.’ Where there’s smoke, there’s fire. There’s a lot of smoke in Austin. That’s not good, man. This is not how you want to start your season.” Smith was set to play an important role for Texas at linebacker. The third-year player recorded 60 tackles, 5.5 tackles for a loss, and 2.5 sacks in 2025. New defensive coordinator Will Muschamp did a couple of players in via the NCAA transfer portal , highlighted by Rasheem Biles . That kind of returning production is always welcome, though. Unfortunately, Smith will not wear burnt orange this season. As for the parent on social media, Pollack is referencing a tweet from the father of Hayward Howard Jr. It’s since been deleted but Howard Sr. said there’s “a lot of bull****” going on and he was willing to “expose” it all. Pollack admitted he did not expect Sarkisian to address this specific situation. Texas kicks things off on Sept. 5 at 2:30 p.m. CT, hosting Texas State. Everyone has the following week, welcoming the Ohio State Buckeyes to Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium for a massive nonconference showdown. Plenty of analysts and fans expect Sarkisian’s club to be playing a lot longer than the Nov. 28 finale against Texas A&M . However, Pollack is sensing some red flags coming out of the 40 Acres, saying there might be some fires to deal with.

They’ve already talked about the moment, and Mike was recently asked ho
articles._body: The Arizona Cardinals will be taking part in joint practices against the Green Bay Packers, and it should make for an exciting moment as brother Mike and Matt LaFleur will be going up against each other as head coaches. They’ve already talked about the moment, and Mike was recently asked how often they talk. Leave it up to the younger brother to throw in a joke here or there. “We talk a lot. Him and I talk ne less time than we talk to our wives …get than on camera,” Mike said via ESPN’s Rob Demovsky. Mike LaFleur on how much he and Matt talk: “One less time than we talk to our wives …get than on camera.” pic.twitter.com/VfUiG6Fn8y — Rob Demovsky (@RobDemovsky) August 26, 2026 There’s no doubt that the brothers are close, and Mike seems excited to be able to take part in something like this wit his brother. “It’s a cool place. They got the bikes with the kids and stuff like that, and that’s for a cool cause for the locals. And so we’ll do that too, just like a lot of the other teams do when they joint [practice]. And then there’s a ton of fans there. I mean, it’s Green Bay. What else you gonna do?” Mike said. The LaFleurs coached together with the Atlanta Falcons in 2015 and 2016, and went their separate ways afterwards. Though they were together at one point, it doesn’t hide the fact that they’re still pretty competitive, and Matt showed that when asked about joint practice with his brother. “If there’s an issue, I’m going to tell the guys, ‘Hey, you come tag me in. They can tag in my brother. And we’ll throw down on the 50,’” Matt said. “I think it’s going to be pretty special, but at the end of the day, we’re just looking to try to get good work on both sides. Certainly, always going to prioritize the Green Bay Packers but if there is another team in the National Football League that I’ll be rooting for, it will be the Arizona Cardinals.” The post Cardinals’ Mike LaFleur makes quip about his, Matt LaFleur’s wives he wants ‘on camera’ appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles.title: Everything Alabama DC Kane Wommack said after 17th preseason practice
articles.summary: Alabama defensive coordinator Kane Wommack spoke to reporters after the Crimson Tide's 17th preseason practice. Here is everything he said.
articles._body: TUSCALOOSA, Ala. — Alabama held its 17th preseason practice on Wednesday morning, and after the August 26 workout, third-year defensive coordinator Kane Wommack spoke to reporters inside the Hank Crisp Indoor Practice Facility. Below is everything Wommack said after Practice 17. Wommack on who is Alabama’s second-best pass rusher… That’s a good question. I think we’ve got a number of guys that I’m excited about. Obviously, Yhonzae [Pierre] is kind of the most experienced guy in the room, and, I think he’s taking his game to another level, so I’m excited to see that in real time on game day. But I think, Devan Thompkins does a really good job. I think Desmond Zulu brings a lot to the table there. Excited about a young guy in Xavier Griffin, and what he brings to the table, similar to, we used Jihaad [Campbell] in a number of different ways, and I think he kind of has that similar skill set in outside linebacker background with being able to play the inside linebacker position as well. And thenthere’s a couple of guys in Kevonte Henry, and Justin Hill, that bring different varieties to the table. So, I mean, you kind of got to see, who’s the hot hand, right? Who’s the guy that, when the bullets are flying, are gonna step up? But certainly, if you look at Devan’s career, you look at Des Zulu, and, and then, obviously, Yhonzae, those guys are the most experienced to this point.” Wommack on his message to Jeremiah Beaman after tearing his ACL… “Those are hard. Sometimes you just gotta sit with somebody in some really hard stuff. And that’s, he worked so hard to get himself ready to go and put himself in a really good position, was taking strides in the right direction. And then to have this injury again about the same time he did last year, it’s a hard thing to go with. And so, sometimes, it’s not what you say, it’s just sitting with somebody in that moment.” Wommack on which knee Beaman injured… “I believe it’s the same knee.” Wommack on Jah-Marien Latham… “Zebbo’s just, he’s a great football player. And so he’s kind of always been our Swiss army knife. He can do multiple things for us. I think you guys will see him at our boundary Wolf position at the field, Bandit position. He used to play three technique for us as well in a pinch, and even on some of the third down pass rush situations, he can do that. Good football players just find their way on the field. And Zebbo is just a really good football player.” Wommack on the message to the D-line room after Beaman’s injury… “Those guys know the drill. I mean, that happens. You’re gonna sustain injuries on the defensive line. It’s a very physical position. We typically carry more bodies on roster. We carry more bodies into the game plan. And so that’s a pretty natural, nobody likes to see a guy hurt, right? But they just kind of operate in that next man up mentality. And so I think our guys are ready to step in where they need to. The thing that we’ve tried to do in the off season is create more depth in our defense by position versatility, right? And so most of our guys on the interior can play multiple positions. We have some guys that are playing the bandit position that can also move inside and play the three technique for us as well. And so I think we’ve generated a little bit more depth by position versatility than maybe where we were in the past.” Wommack on what grade he would give Keelon Russell vs. his defense… “I think Keelon — I don’t watch it like that from that standpoint of being able to say what grade I could give on him. He, when you go against him, you feel like there’s a lot of variables you have to defend, right? And so I look at it from a standpoint of, what do I have to defend, to be able to take this guy away? And there’s things that he can certainly do with his feet both in the run game, scrambling ability, but the decisions he makes, there’s just guys, and you see these type of guys over the years, that can see the field naturally, right? They just have a natural, instinctive vision for the field, and they can work through a progression very quickly and find an open man. Keelon has it. And so that allows him, right — there’s a higher ceiling for guys like that, that have that type of field vision. And so when I think about, OK, how am I going to defend him in a game, there’s just a lot of variables to have to defend that I would prefer not to have to defend as a defensive coordinator.” Wommack on if there is a set guy next to Caleb Woodson at linebacker… “Yeah, I mean, Luke Metz is really our other starter right now, but those other guys have done a really good job. I’m pleased with that room. Chuck Morrell has done a fantastic job with the development in that room. You’re gonna see a number of guys in there, but certainly, Luke and Caleb would be the first two out.” Wommack on Dre Kirkpatrick Jr…. “Dre’s another one, you talk about just a good football player, and when he gets on the field, he just makes plays, and he usually makes plays in big moments. Scrimmages, he always seems to step up. Team, move the ball periods, right? He always seems to step up. So, uh, he’s another guy that there’s a lot of position versatility and things that we feel like we can do with them. His ability to make plays on the ball, I told our guys before, the way you’re gonna get on the field is to do your job to a consistent level that we trust you and create value by playmaking ability, right? And I think Dre is trending in the right direction there.” Wommack on if Alabama has a healthy Husky rotation… “Yeah, I think so. I think that Husky position, there’s a lot we a

articles.title: Check Out the Daily Schedule For BillboardTV
articles.summary: The team-up with Samsung TV Plus brings a 24/7 streaming destination for music culture, news and live events.
articles._body: BillboardTV , a collaboration between Billboard and Samsung TV Plus, features a variety of shows focused on some of Billboard ‘s most exciting editorial franchises, including Chart History, Takes Us Out, On the Record and In Conversation. The exclusive free streaming channel available now on Samsung TV Plus and Amazon’s Fire TV is packed with nonstop updates from Billboard News, as well as never-before-seen interviews, red carpet coverage, live concert specials and deep-dive documentary-style profiles of artists through their own eyes. Among the series fans can tune into now in two-hour blocks is On the Record, a weekly show featuring unfiltered conversations with executives, artists and innovators shaping the music industry hosted by Billboard Senior Correspondent Kristin Robinson. Previous episodes have included chats with John Summit, FINNEAS and Charlie Puth, in conversations where they break down the pipeline from boardroom decisions to the music that fans stream, buy and listen to live. Chart History takes a look at the artists behind the Hot 100 chart’s biggest hits, with acts including Snoop Dogg, Ciara and Mariah Carey breaking down the songs and videos that defined their careers in candid conversations featuring never-before-heard stories, memories and behind-the-scenes moments chronicling the chart-topping records that made music history. The popular Takes Us Out series invites viewers along as artists such as KATSEYE, Yungblud and Addison Rae grab a meal and chat about their music and life in a super-relaxed setting, while the Billboard News Interview serves up newsworthy chats with the biggest artists on the charts and Billboard journalists in a fast-paced, fun setting. You can also check out the more in-depth, premium Billboard Cover Interview series, a visual companion to the magazine’s cover stories, with verité, structured sit-downs and cinematic portraits shot on set with acts including Mick Jagger and Keith Richards, Riley Green and Kehlani. Other series now available include In Conversation, in which music’s biggest stars sit down with Billboard ‘s editorial team for candid chats about the defining moments in their careers; and Billboard Presents, an Emmy-nominated docu-style profile of artists through their own eyes, in which stars such as A$AP Rocky, Cardi B and Fuerza Regida pull back the curtain on their music and lives in a never-before-seen fashion. The daily schedule is as follows: 8 a.m. PT: Billboard On the Record 10 a.m. PT: Billboard Chart History 12 p.m. PT: Takes Us Out 2 p.m. PT: Billboard News Interview 4 p.m. PT: Billboard Cover Interview 6 p.m. PT: In Conversation 8 p.m. PT: Billboard Presents

articles.summary: The Atlanta Falcons are now a Kevin Stefanski operation. Atlanta’s new head coach should bring plenty of changes to the organization, particularly when it comes to the X’s and O’s. He will also look to get the most of Atlanta’s core players from the previous regime. Now th
articles._body: The Atlanta Falcons are now a Kevin Stefanski operation . Atlanta’s new head coach should bring plenty of changes to the organization, particularly when it comes to the X’s and O’s. He will also look to get the most of Atlanta’s core players from the previous regime. Now that training camp is practically over, the next task for Atlanta is cutting down to a 53-man roster. Will Falcons fans be surprised by any of the players let go before the regular season? Here is one version of what Atlanta’s final 53-man roster could look like after the deadline on August 30th. Quarterbacks (2) Michael Penix Jr., Tua Tagovailoa How could this be any other way? The Falcons have arguably the most variance in their quarterback room of any team in the league. Both Penix and Tagovailoa are streaky players who have struggled to stay healthy throughout their careers. It could be great, but the most likely outcome is disaster. So why would Atlanta choose to only keep two quarterbacks? The NFL’s emergency third-quarterback rule allows teams to dress an emergency QB without them counting towards the 53-man roster limit. As such, the Falcons will probably keep Cooper Rush or Jack Strand on the practice squad for that exact purpose. Running backs (3) Bijan Robinson, Brian Robinson Jr., Tyler Goodson The Falcons now have two B. Robinson’s in their backfield. Bijan is the heart and soul of Atlanta’s offense. The superstar running back just got a massive extension and should receive plenty of touches in 2026. Brian Robinson figures to take over the Tyler Allgeier role, which could involve a lot of touches compared to the average backup. That leaves only Goodson as a reserve player. On paper, it is risky to only keep three running backs given how much volume they’re expected to receive. Staying healthy will be paramount for Atlanta at this position. Wide receivers (6) Drake London, Jahan Dotson, Olamide Zaccheaus, Zachariah Branch, Chris Blair, Dylan Drummond Atlanta’s receiver room is full of promise, but it has few established stars behind London on the depth chart. Dotson will look to revive his career in Atlanta , and he may be given plenty of opportunities to do just that. The rookie Branch is the biggest unknown and could play a surprisingly big role if he can adapt to the NFL quickly. It was extremely difficult choosing between Blair and Drummond for a fifth roster spot. In this scenario, Atlanta splits the difference and keeps both players as depth pieces and special teams contributors. Tight ends (3) Kyle Pitts Sr., Austin Hooper, Charlie Woerner No real surprises here. Pitts will be expected to play a huge role as a receiver in 2026. This is especially true after looking at the wide receiver depth chart. In fact, it would not be surprising to see Atlanta deploy formations with multiple tight ends, allowing Pitts to motion into the slot or out wide. That feels destined to happen in part because of Atlanta’s personnel. Hooper is an all-around solid tight end who can do it all, But Woerner is at his best when blocking. Those skills sets match perfectly with using Pitts primarily as a receiver from multiple tight end looks. It will be exciting to see how O’Connell and OC Tommy Rees deploy Pitts throughout the season. Offensive linemen (9) Jake Matthews, Matthew Bergeron, Ryan Neuzil, Chris Lindstrom, Jawaan Taylor, Wanya Morris, Michael Jerrell, Kyle Hinton, Corey Levin Atlanta is able to keep all five starters as well as excellent depth at all key positions. The Falcons may like to keep a bit more depth at guard, but Bergeron and Lindstrom are both rock solid. In fact, Lindstrom has only missed one regular-season games since the 2020 season. One key position to watch is right tackle with Taylor coming over from Kansas City. He needs to play well early, at least as a run blocker, for Atlanta to retain their offensive identity. Defensive linemen (6) Brandon Dorlus, Da’Shawn Hand, Zach Harrison, Maason Smith, Chris Williams, LaCale London Atlanta’s d-line has a solid mixture of veteran talent and up-and-coming players. Dorlus and Harrison can both create pressure from the interior, and the Falcons may need that more than ever this year. If either of them goes down with an injury, Atlanta’s defense could struggle mightily to get after the quarterback. But overall, no difficult decisions for Atlanta to make at this position. Edge rushers (6) Za’Darius Smith, Samson Ebukam, Azeez Ojulari, Bralen Trice, Cameron Sample, Cameron Thomas The Falcons looks surprisingly good on the edge given how many players they will be down to start the season. James Pearce Jr. will not play until the middle of the season due to his eight-game suspension for violating the league’s personal conduct policy. Remember, suspended players do not count against a team’s 53-man roster limit. Pearce will become a major part of Atlanta’s defense once he returns, but he doesn’t count towards the final 53 for this exercise. Meanwhile, Jalon Walker will miss the entire season following his ACL injury. Atlanta will lean heavily on Smith, Ebukam, Ojulari, and Trice to hold down the fort while Pearce serves his suspension. Linebackers (5) Divine Deablo, Christian Harris, Harold Perkins Jr., JD Bertrand, Kendal Daniels This feels like the thinnest position on the entire defense. Deablo and Harris are both solid starters. However, it feels like Atlanta is missing a reliable third off-ball linebacker who can share reps with the other two starters. Perkins, Bertrand, and Daniels all provide value in their own ways. But none of them would be an average NFL starter if pressed into service. It will be interesting to see if opposing teams consistently attack the middle of Atlanta’s defense this fall. articles._body: The Atlanta Braves claimed right-handed pitcher Ricky Vanasco off waivers from the Detroit Tigers, the team announced Wednesday. “ The #Braves today claimed RHP Ricky Vanasco off waivers from the Detroit Tigers and optioned him to Triple-A Gwinnett,” the Braves announced on X, formerly Twitter. While the move itself won’t make or break Atlanta’s season, it does provide the Braves with additional pitching depth. The Braves have pitching question marks as they deal with multiple injuries , so adding Vanasco is certainly an understandable decision. Vanasco, 27, has pitched in a total of nine MLB games in his career. The right-hander most recently made a big league appearance with the Tigers in 2026. He has struggled at the MLB level, but Vanasco has impressed in the minor leagues. Vanasco turned in a strong 2.53 ERA across 35 outings (two starts) at Triple-A this season. He holds a career minor league ERA of 3.32 across 170 total appearances (43 starts). While he has some starting experience, it seems as if Vanasco is a reliever at this point in his career. It will be interesting to see if he impacts the big league ball club in 2026. Braves currently playing Dodgers The Braves most recently defeated the Dodgers by a final score 4-3 in Atlanta on Tuesday night. The contest represented the first of a three-game series between the National League ball clubs. Atlanta and Los Angeles lead their divisions at the moment. This series is a potential postseason preview. The Braves would certainly love to send a message by earning a series win. Wednesday night’s game is scheduled for 7:15 PM ET. articles.title: Carlos Vallarino, Fabian, Yele & More Emerging Latin Artists on Our Radar
articles.summary: Here are the rising stars we've discovered in August who should be on your radar.
articles._body: Every month,  Billboard   Latin  and  Billboard Español  editors spotlight a group of rising artists whose music we love. Think “diamantes en bruto,” or “diamonds in the rough.” These are newcomers who have yet to impact the mainstream — but whose music excites us, and who we believe our readers should make a point to discover. Our latest edition of  On the Radar  Latin includes a wave of emerging artists, who we discovered by scrolling on social media, networking, or coming across their music at a showcase, for example. See our August 2026 recommendations below. Artist: Carlos Vallarino Country: Panamá Why They Should Be on Your Radar: I met Carlos Vallarino last year during the second edition of CAMM 2025 in Costa Rica; he closed the second night of showcases, leaving the audience completely in love with his way of living and feeling music. That unique aura led him to sign a contract with Sony Music Publishing Colombia after they held a songwriting camp and discovered his great talent as an artist and songwriter. Always accompanied by a guitar, Vallarino has a very natural way of connecting and conveying both his joy and his sadness in every song, adding powerful quotes in each of his lyrics. His raspy but sweet voice connects with every verse and every person. He recently released his second album, Rumba Para La Tristeza , which reflects his purest way of feeling life. In the set, he mixes contemporary modern flamenco rhythms with fusions of boleros, reggae, and merengue with a very special swing and fully shows what a true artist can inspire. — INGRID FAJARDO Song for Your Playlist: “Se siente cabrón” Artist: Don Pablo Mures Country: Panamá Why They Should Be on Your Radar: I first clocked Panamanian artist Don Pablo Mures through “Deja La Envidia Pelao,” his new link-up with Los Rakas. The track runs on a smooth, unhurried groove, letting the Oakland duo bring their seasoned, party-starting Panamanian swagger while Mures slides in with a nimble delivery rooted in the streetwise sound of his native Panama City. Hailing from Santa Ana and trained as a trumpeter, he has built a catalog that folds urban music’s hard edges into musicianship and local texture — moving through songs like “99” with Aley La Nueve and Yemil, “Plata Llama Plata” with Akim and El Americano 4KT, and “Caldero Panameño” alongside Boza and Andiex. That range is what makes the collaboration land: another sharp connection with Raka Rich and Raka Dun that keeps Mures’ Panama sound in motion. — ISABELA RAYGOZA Song for Your Playlist: “Deja La Envidia Pelao” with Los Rakas Artist: FABIAN Country: Peru / United States Why They Should Be on Your Radar: As the son of renowned singer-songwriter Gian Marco — and brother of singer-songwriter Nic — Fabian Zignago follows in the family’s footsteps, having grown up surrounded by musical instruments and recording studios. Yet, at 23, the Peruvian-American singer-songwriter is forging his own path with a sweet voice and a refreshing style, evident in releases such as “Golpe,” “Pared,” and “Líneas Paralelas” with ROBI Last month, the artist had the opportunity to showcase his talent live at New York’s iconic SOB’s as part of the LAMC’s BMI Acoustic Lounge, and more recently he gave his first performance in Miami during the Creative Monday: Jam Session at Tripping Animals Brewing. — SIGAL RATNER-ARIAS Song for Your Playlist: “Líneas Paralelas” with ROBI Artist: Infloresencia Country: El Salvador Why They Should Be on Your Radar: Playing “The Dance of the Flowers,” the band Inflorescencia arrived at CAMM 2026 with a fresh and different performance. Its six members, each dressed in a mix of bright colors and pastel tones, brought their cumbia sound mixed with alternative rock, accompanied by yellow flowers symbolizing growth and transformation — a perfect introduction to their universe, where the sounds of the past meet the present. They seem like old souls who have returned to leave their mark in 2026, as if the ’60s and ’70s had reincarnated in a new generation that found its space in a corner of El Salvador. What impressed me most about this band, made up of Andrés Villalobos (drums), Naomy Díaz (vocals and minor percussion), Ricardo Bendek (vocals and guitar), Erick Chicas (guitar), Claribel Dimas (vocals), and Diego Chacón (bass), is the way they defend their music and their own style. Just as they integrate powerful sounds of alternative rock and indie pop, they also keep a cumbia that defines Central American culture with its expressions and words. — I.F. Song for Your Playlist: “Otro Día en la Colonia” Artist: LucasKG Country: Mexico Why They Should Be on Your Radar: A new generation of música mexicana stars are in the making, and LucasKG is hopping on the bandwagon. The Mexican newcomer kicked off his career in 2025, first releasing reggaetón and afrobeats songs, but quickly finding his sound and color in corridos. With his raspy and raw vocals, the young talent sings about his real-life experiences in search of an organic connection with his community. A promising star in the making, I discovered LucasKG at the 2026 Latino Music Conference in Miami, where I was speaker at a Billboard Q&A panel, and he was part of an artist showcase. — JESSICA ROIZ Song for Your Playlist: “No Que Muy Acá” Artist: Marco Montero Country: Costa Rica Why They Should Be on Your Radar: As a speaker at CAMM Panama in 2026, I had the chance to chat with Marco Montero at the roundtables, where several artists presented their projects.
