articles.title: Depth at RB is Improving According to Mark Atuaia
articles.summary: The running back depth behind Wayshawn Parker has made some big time strides during fall camp according to Mark Atuaia.
articles._body: In this new offensive system under Kevin McGiven , the Utah running backs will be asked to take on a bigger role in the passing game. With the season a week away, RB coach Mark Atuaia believes his group has done what it needs to do so they can be featured this fall. “I think we’ve all done a great job in acclimating to what Kevin McGiven wants us to do in the offense, and with all the strengths that they have, and piecemealing that into what McGiven wants us to do, we’ve done a pretty good job of that during fall camp,” Atuaia said earlier this week. “There’s only five skilled guys that can play on the field at a time, and being able to insert ourselves into those positions and seeing where we can help out the team, I think that’s the biggest thing that we’ve done this fall, in discovering what those things are and then honing in on those skills.” While Wayshawn Parker has locked down the RB1 spot this season, Atuaia has a growing confidence in the rest of the members of his room. He called Daniel Bray “a continuous bright spot” for the team and shared eagerness for the nation to see what the sophomore can do. Mateaki Helu is also on the rise after a strong fall camp. The former linebacker will have a role in this offense, according to Atuaia, and will also see time on special teams again this year. “He’s already huge in what we do on special teams, and then now being able to assert himself into what we’re doing on offense, it really does help our room, especially with the physicality part, and he catches pretty well for a guy that’s just transitioning over from the defensive side,” Atuaia said. The second-year coach called out Helu’s big frame at 6’1″ and 224 pounds. Historically, Atuaia has had success with guys of that size during his coaching career. “He fits that mold. He’s a strong kid. The part that we had to work on with him was obviously working with the ball. All the stuff without the ball, man, he’s phenomenal in that regard,” he said. San Jose State transfer Steve Chavez-Soto’s mindset has changed since the start of camp as well, leading to his time on the field increasing as well. “He’s done a phenomenal job in taking coaching, and then with the different aspects that we ask him to do in offense, particularly in playing without the ball, like blocking and being physical, and just understanding how it is to block in the perimeter, as it is blocking in the box, you know, he’s been doing a really good job at that. And the more he buys into that mindset, he’ll continue to rise, and I see a good future for him,” Atuaia said. articles.title: When Eagles will induct owner Jeffrey Lurie into Hall of Fame
articles.summary: The Philadelphia Eagles are just weeks away from kicking off their 2026 season, currently wrapping up their participation in training camp. The pressure is on for the Eagles to bounce back this year after an ugly Wild Card exit this past season. Now, the team has announced when franchise owner Je
articles._body: The Philadelphia Eagles are just weeks away from kicking off their 2026 season, currently wrapping up their participation in training camp . The pressure is on for the Eagles to bounce back this year after an ugly Wild Card exit this past season. Now, the team has announced when franchise owner Jeffrey Lurie will be inducting himself into the team’s Hall of Fame. “Congratulations to Chairman and CEO Jeffrey Lurie, this year’s inductee into the Eagles Hall of Fame! He will be honored at halftime of our game on Monday, October 26,” reported the team on X, formerly Twitter. Fans in the comment section were quick to point out that team owners ultimately decide who ends up getting inducted into team Halls of Fame or Rings of Honor, so Lurie ended up deciding to make this move for himself, but he is far from the first NFL owner to follow such a tradition. Lurie bought the Eagles over three decades ago and has helped turn them into one of the most well-run organizations in the NFL since then, with the team having won two Super Bowls in the last decade and consistently being among the most competitive squads in the league, with very few dry spells throughout his tenure. This offseason, the Eagles have made some big changes, headlined by the trade of AJ Brown to the New England Patriots and the hiring of offensive coordinator Sean Mannion to replace Kevin Patullo, among others. The moves have come as the Eagles look to put their agitated fanbase at ease on the heels of a frustrating 2025 season. The Eagles’ new campaign is set to get underway on September 13 against the Washington Commanders. articles.title: Mark Walter’s company releases defiant statement on potential Dodgers sale
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Dodgers have been the subject of some sale speculation in recent weeks amid the FBI’s probe into team owner Mark Walter’s business dealings. Walter recently gave the sports world a jolt when he sold the Los Angeles Lakers to Josh Kushner and Bob Iger less than one year
articles._body: The Los Angeles Dodgers have been the subject of some sale speculation in recent weeks amid the FBI’s probe into team owner Mark Walter’s business dealings. Walter recently gave the sports world a jolt when he sold the Los Angeles Lakers to Josh Kushner and Bob Iger less than one year after purchasing them from the Buss family. Recently, Walter’s company, TWG Global, has released a statement hitting back at the media circus surrounding his endeavors in the sports world. “Over the past several weeks, multipronged attacks against TWG have been advanced by unnamed sources with self-serving interests that have been reported in the media,” read the statement in part, per Jack Harris of the New York Post. About the Dodgers, the statement read, “To be clear, the team is not being sold and no sale process has been initiated.” The statement also addressed Walter’s line of thinking as it pertained to the shocking sale of the Lakers. “Mr. Walter and his partners continuously get interest from prospective buyers and co-investors in their sports assets and, as responsible owners and investors, they consider all legitimate offers when they are received,” the statement said. The Dodgers are currently looking to add a third straight World Series trophy to their collection this season, with the MLB playoffs just over a month away. The statement should help at least temporarily halt some of the negative press and rumors surrounding the team at the most important part of the season. In any case, the Dodgers are set to continue their regular season on Wednesday with a road game against the Atlanta Braves. articles.title: Katy Perry, Kesha, Pitbull and Jon Batiste Pay Tribute to Dolly Parton on Stage, in Song: ‘She Was Kind to Everyone’
articles.summary: The impact of the country icon's death on Tuesday (Aug. 25) at 80 could be felt around the world in shout-outs from London to New York and Mexico.
articles._body: It’s a testament to the wide and deep impact that Dolly Parton had on the hearts and minds of her musical peers that just hours after news broke about the country legend’s death at 80 on Tuesday night (Aug. 25), artists ranging from Katy Perry to Pitbull , Jack White and Kesha and Jon Batiste took time out to tip their hats to the “Jolene” hitmaker from the stage and studio. Related A Timeline of Dolly Parton’s Good Deeds Dolly Parton Remembered by Reba McEntire, Paul McCartney, George Strait & More: ‘We Will Always Love You’ Jay-Z 30 Pop-Up Experience to Open In London Ahead of Historic Tottenham Hotspur Stadium Shows At Perry’s show in San Luis Potosí, Mexico, the singer acknowledged Parton’s passing on stage, telling her fans, “ Dolly Parton was an icon … who defied the odds , ‘cause she had both big boobs, big brains and a big voice in one body. And on top of that, the biggest thing that she did was that she was constantly kind. She was kind to everyone. And it’s not always easy after you’re in the spotlight for decades, and decades, and decades. So I just wanna send a little love to Miss Dolly Parton.” Perry then went on to encourage her fans to discover, or rediscover, Parton’s impressive catalog of hits , emphasizing that she was, at heart, one of the most accomplished songwriters of all time. “It’s where all songwriters — we learn how to write music is through a songwriter like her,” Perry said before cueing one of the first song she ever wrote herself in her 20s, the 2008 One of the Boys song “Thinking of You.” Pianist Jon Batiste posted an emotional tribute to one of Parton’s most iconic hits, “I Will Always Love You,” performing the classic ballad on piano while wearing a black cowboy hat and blue jean overalls. Pitbull took time out from his show at Northwell Health at Jones Beach Theater in Wantagh, N.Y. on Tuesday night, telling the crowd that while they were having fun he wanted to shout out someone that was, “ very special to me and showed me love and believed in me when a lot of folks didn’t and gave me an opportunity.” When he mentioned Parton, the audience went wild as Pit added, “She lived an amazing life, a hard-working woman … intelligent, sophisticated, funny, powerful, intimidating, but more than anything a good human being with a good heart.” After taking a swig from a Champagne bottle and toasting Parton, Mr. Worldwide shimmied along with his dancers to her iconic hit “9 to 5” as the screen behind him filled with a giant image of the unlikely musical duo smiling for a picture. Parton teamed up with Pitbull in 2024 to record new vocals and a rap verse on his song “Powerful Women,” which sampled “9 to 5.” Kesha had a personal connection to Parton through her mom, Pebe Sebert, also a songwriter. During her show at Pavilion Star Lake in Pittsburgh on Tuesday, Kesha performed Parton’s 1980 hit “Old Flames (Can’t Hold a Candle To You),” a country tune co-written by Sebert and Hugh Moffat. The song was a country chart hit for Joe Sun in 1978 and then again in 1980 on Parton’s Dolly, Dolly, Dolly album, with that version hitting No. 1 on the Billboard Hot Country Songs chart. “I just want to say thank you for bringing me so much joy today, because earlier today, I’m sure many of y’all know that we lost Ms. Dolly Parton,” Kesha told the crowd as seen in a fan video . “We literally lost an angel. But through her art and through her kindness and through her love, she will live forever. And I want to talk about her a little bit. For those of you who don’t know, I come from a long lineage of songwriters and before I was born, my mom actually wrote a song for Dolly Parton. And that song bought us a house, like a roof. That song put me through school.” The connection came full circle in 2017, when Kesha recorded a duet with Parton on “Old Flames” for her Rainbow album in the midst of the singer’s long-running court battle with former producer/label boss Dr. Luke. She reminded the crowd that she recorded that album “in the middle of a very scary litigation, and I was in the #MeToo movement, and having such a legendary woman do this song with me and stand beside me, it made me really feel like God was on my side,” she said. “And that’s how it feels working with Dolly Parton. So in honor of her incredible legacy and her beautiful life, I’d like to sing the song that my mom wrote for her.” In addition, Jack White played a ferocious version of the oft-covered “Jolene” at London’s Eventim Apollo just hours after the news of her death broke. The Detroit rocker now based in Nashville posted a snippet of the performance on his Instagram after the show, beginning with the apt lyric: “Your beauty is beyond compare.” Earlier in the day, White shared a tribute to Parton via a 1965 photo of the legend with her classic towering beehive hairstyle and the two-word caption: “Instant Sainthood.” Parton had mostly been out of the public eye for more than a year due to a series of unspecified health issues and died on Tuesday in Nashville at 80 following a “brief battle with cancer.”

The 6-foot-1 rising senior out of Masters Academy International (MA) included the Jayhawks in his final eight schools in late July, along with Boston C
articles._body: Four-star Antonio Pemberton , one of the top point guards in the 2027 class, is set to take an official visit to Kansas this weekend, he told Rivals. The 6-foot-1 rising senior out of Masters Academy International (MA) included the Jayhawks in his final eight schools in late July, along with Boston College, Creighton, Marquette, Michigan State, Ohio State, Tennessee, and UCLA. Pemberton is coming off an official visit to Tennessee last weekend and previously took an official visit to Marquette, along with an unofficial visit to Boston College earlier this summer. He’s scheduled to officially visit each of his remaining finalists in the coming weeks and months. [ $19.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage ] Pemberton is ranked as the No. 26 overall recruit in the 2027 class and the No. 8 ranked point guard, according to the Rivals Industry Ranking , an average of all three major recruiting media companies (Rivals, ESPN, 247Sports). Pemberton on Kansas In a recent interview with Rivals, Antonio Pemberton discussed the Kansas program. Kansas: “My thoughts on them, they’re a winning school, so that’s what we talk about every time. They think I can go there and help them win. And talking to them, getting to know Coach Bill Self and Coach (Joe) Dooley is definitely a blessing. Bill Self is another legendary coach, and us talking about anything really. We talk about their dorms, their campus, eating stuff like that outside of the campus. Just getting to know them more means a lot.” More on Pemberton This summer on the adidas 3SSB Circuit, Antonio Pemberton averaged 19.8 points, 2.6 rebounds, and 3.3 assists per game while shooting nearly 38% from the field for Mass Rivals. Pemberton was the second-leading scorer at the  NBPA Top-100 Camp  in June, averaging 19.0 points per game while shooting 54.9% from the field and 64% from three. To no surprise, the Lawrence, Massachusetts native was one of the top performers at the event, prompting Rivals national recruiting analyst Jamie Shaw to write the following about him: “Antonio Pemberton is a scoring lead guard, and one who plays with a lot of confidence. The 6-foot-1 four-star gets to his spots, and he plays with excellent balance. He has a quick release and the range extends well beyond the three-point arc. Pemberton does a good job playing off the threat of his jump shot and is comfortable in the mid range with two and three-dribble pull-ups. In Pemberton’s second game on Thursday, he erupted for 27 points, going 7-9 from three. This is the type of performance that we have come to expect from him. “He has deep shooting range, which opens up a lot for the rest of his attack….He is a score-first lead guard and has the ability to get clean looks often.”

articles.title: Devon Jackson calls 2026 do or die, and Oregon’s defense is counting on it
articles.summary: Devon Jackson has been touted as a freak athlete since he arrived in Eugene, and he plans on getting everything he can out of himself and the Oregon defense in 2026.
articles._body: Oregon enters the 2026 season with one of the most experienced defenses in college football. Much of that stars up front with four returning starters along the defensive line, but everyone knows a great defense needs great linebackers directing traffic in the middle. Fifth-year senior Devon Jackson is hoping to be that for the Ducks this year as he closes in on what could he says be his last first game with no additional opportunities promised. Dan Lanning himself foresees Jackson’s play being a key component in the Oregon defense reaching its full potential, but praise from the head coach is only more fuel to his fire. “If I can be the player that I know I can be and the coaches believe I can be, then we can do something special. But you still gotta work for it,” Jackson said after Tuesday’s practice. “No one’s handed that to me in the five years I’ve been here. You gotta work at it every day. Rent’s due every day.” Following a blowout loss to Indiana in the Peach Bowl, Jackson and the Ducks are working tirelessly to take the next step as a program and make an even deeper run in the College Football Playoff. “We’ve been kind of right there the last handful of years,” the veteran defender said. “But to really just get over the hump, it takes one day at a time.” It feels like we’re always hearing that Oregon has an abundance of talent on paper. Jackson knows that as well as anyone. He also knows that it’s not what wins games. “I think the sky’s the limit honestly, for this defense,” he added. “There’s a lot of talent on paper, for sure. But it’s not about what’s on paper; it’s about what we do on a daily basis and how we show up every day.” Jackson echoed his belief in teammates like A’Mauri Washington and Bear Alexander along the defensive line and could see them being even better than recent Ducks that are now in the NFL. “You also had guys like Derrick Harmon and Ja’Maree Caldwell . It’s a first-round pick and it’s a third-round pick. Those guys can do the same, if not better,” Jackson said. “But again, it’s not about what you do on a piece of paper. It’s about how you show up every day.” Experience runs up and down the entire defense, not just the starters, and Jackson sees the value in that. Oregon’s defense is also communicating and finding its stride heading into Boise State week. “I feel like this is the most dialed we’ve been,” he said. “Look at our whole front. A’mauri’s in his fourth year. Bear’s in his fifth year of school. Obviously, second year here. Teitum (Tuioti) in his fourth year here. Matayo’s fourth year here. Jerry’s (Mixon) fourth year here. So a lot of people have been here. “Guys also in our linebacker room, Dylan Williams , third year here. Like, guys have been here. They might not get as much love as they might want, but people have been here and they’ve been working…Coach Lanning says all the time, if you’re on the field, you’re a starter because that means your teammates and the coaches have full faith in you.” Jackson acknowledged the gravity of what’s on the line this season, not just for the Ducks, but also for himself. And he’s bringing all the fire and intense he has. “I’m ready to just show it every play because this is it. This is the only guaranteed opportunity that I have for myself,” he said. “I wasn’t a Dante (Moore) or Stew ( Evan Stewart ) or Poncho ( Iapani Laloulu ) or all those other guys that could have went to the league. This is do or die for me, and so I have to bring it every day. There is no other option. There was no choice. It’s do or die now, and we’re gonna do it together to get where we want to go for sure.”

articles.title: Teddy Swims’ ‘Lose Control’ Leads Top TV Songs Chart Via ‘Ransom Canyon’ Synch
articles.summary: The former Hot 100 No. 1 leads a trio of songs from the Netflix series on the July 2026 chart.
articles._body: Music from the second season of Netflix’s Ransom Canyon occupies three of the top four positions on Billboard ’s Top TV Songs chart, powered by Tunefind (a Songtradr company), for July 2026, led by Teddy Swims ’ “Lose Control” at No. 1. Rankings for the Top TV Songs chart are based on song and show data provided by Tunefind and ranked using a formula blending that data with sales and streaming information tracked by Luminate during the corresponding period of July 2026. “Lose Control,” a one-week No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 in 2024 (and a song that currently holds the record for most cumulative weeks on the Hot 100 at 112), was heard in the fifth episode of Ransom Canyon ’s second season, which premiered in full on July 23. In July 2026, the song earned 58.2 million streams and sold 4,000 downloads in the United States, according to Luminate. Ransom Canyon also reaches Top TV Songs at Nos. 3 ( Thomas Rhett ’s “Ain’t a Bad Life,” featuring Jordan Davis ) and 4 (Davis’ own “Bar None”). The former peaked at No. 14 on Hot Country Songs earlier this year, while the latter reached No. 6 in 2025. The Cranberries ’ “Dreams” splits the three songs at No. 2 on Top TV Songs following its synch in Peacock’s The Five-Star Weekend , which aired its entire freshman season on July 9. The 1994 No. 42 Hot 100 hit racked up 11.8 million streams and 3,000 downloads in July 2026. The Five-Star Weekend is also responsible for two other Top TV Songs entries: Maggie Rogers ’ “Light On” at No. 5 and Leon Bridges ’ “River” at No. 8. articles.title: Show HN: Rudder – Red-Green TDD Workflow for Verifiably Comprehensive Specs
articles.summary: Rudder is a local Codex/Claude Code plugin that captures your specs and your coding agent session history to force your agent to rewrite unit tests exclusively from your expressed intent. This turns unit test coverage into a proxy for what percent of the code actually comes from decisions you've
articles._body: Rudder is a local Codex/Claude Code plugin that captures your specs and your coding agent session history to force your agent to rewrite unit tests exclusively from your expressed intent. This turns unit test coverage into a proxy for what percent of the code actually comes from decisions you've made and lets you see how much of your agent's generated code is uncovered by your spec. After showing you an initial coverage percentage, Rudder prompts you with targeted questions to increase coverage to your goal target and runs a red-green test driven development flow to get you up to your goal. Hitting coverage is the equivalent of saying "My decisions in chat conversation cover X% of the code here." It's fully open source and free to use, made for spec driven developers and vibecoders alike. Let me know what you guys think! Front Office Sports reports that MJ is not expected to return for the 2026-27 season on NBC. During his lone season with the network, his only
articles._body: After just one season with the NBA on NBC as a “special on-air contributor,” basketball icon Michael Jordan appears to be done at the network. Front Office Sports reports that MJ is not expected to return for the 2026-27 season on NBC. During his lone season with the network, his only contribution was a sit-down interview with Mike Tirico, which was spliced and released throughout the season . As Front Office Sports notes, the interview was “fascinating,” but it didn’t really focus on current events in the league. Ultimately, the likely hefty price tag that comes along with hiring Jordan is likely not worth bringing him back for another year. NBC declined to comment on Front Office Sports’ report. It remains to be seen whether or not the network will officially announce its intentions with Jordan for the upcoming season. NBA on NBC was revived during the 2025-26 season. The new deal between the league and NBCUniversal meant NBC and Peacock would cover games. NBCSN also broadcast certain games. NBC exec recently talked about NBA legend Michael Jordan’s future with network Paul Childs-Reuters via Imagn Images. Earlier in the year, NBC Sports president Rick Cordella reflected fondly on Jordan’s first year with the network. He claimed to be hoping for “more in the future,” even saying they’ve had “plenty of ongoing discussions.” However, he did note that “we’ll see what happens.” It appears Jordan is out for the upcoming season. The collaboration was initially intriguing, considering how little MJ has spoken about basketball since The Last Dance aired on Netflix in 2020. He is best known for his time with the Chicago Bulls. MJ and the Bulls won six championships during his career; he was named MVP of all six NBA Finals series. Additionally, he was a five-time NBA MVP and a 14-time All-Star. His accolades speak for themselves, and Jordan is still regarded as one of the greatest of all time. The post Michael Jordan 1-and-done with NBA on NBC coverage appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles.title: Report: ESPN removing BottomLine ticker during college football games in 2026
articles.summary: A popular but sometimes controversial feature offered on ESPN’s live broadcasts will be no more on college football games this fall. According to a report from Front Office Sports, the ESPN BottomLine ticker is going away. The organization reports that ESPN will no longer show the BottomLine t
articles._body: A popular but sometimes controversial feature offered on ESPN’s live broadcasts will be no more on college football games this fall. According to a report from Front Office Sports , the ESPN BottomLine ticker is going away. The organization reports that ESPN will no longer show the BottomLine ticker on regular-season games that air on ABC, ACC Network, ESPN, ESPN2, ESPNU, ESPNews, and SEC Network. The SEC confirmed that will affect all league inventory on ABC, ESPN and the SEC Network. [ $19.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage ] “We’re always looking for ways to better serve sports fans. By removing the BottomLine during live action, we’re creating a cleaner presentation that keeps the focus where it belongs—on the field,” an ESPN spokesperson told FOS. FOS notes that there “will still be score alerts during games at specific times during each quarter.” Updates will also pop up warning viewers of schedule changes that may occur as games get shifted from channel to channel. While proponents of the change note that updates provided on the BottomLine can always be found on a phone or tablet, others who liked the feature will likely miss the readily available info on broadcasts. In any case, it’ll be interesting to see how fans respond as the changes take place during the 2026 college football season. FOS does note that ESPN has already piloted the changes on College Football Playoff games and other big events like the NBA and NHL playoff games. So it’s not a completely out-of-the-blue change by the Worldwide Leader. First two College GameDay locations set With the start of the 2026 college football season comes the anticipation for one of the sport’s greatest offerings: ESPN’s College GameDay . And the signature pregame show has already decided its first two locations for this season. The first campus the show will visit is in Baton Rouge. LSU is set to host Clemson in Week 1, and College GameDay will be on hand to take it in. It’ll be Lane Kiffin ‘s debut for the Tigers, while Dabo Swinney is looking to quiet the noise in the system. While that one will be big, the Week 2 showdown promises to be even bigger. College GameDay will be staying in the SEC , heading to Texas for Ohio State ‘s arrival in a rematch of last year’s closely contested game. Julian Sayin vs. Arch Manning . Who says no? And now we know fans will be able to take in that contest without the BottomLine ticker at the bottom of the screen. We’ll find out quickly whether the move from ESPN proves a success.

articles.title: What does the SEC’s new eligibility policy mean for Kentucky WBB’s Ajša Sivka?
articles.summary: Kentucky women’s basketball player Ajša Sivka was once a WNBA Draft pick. Will the SEC’s new eligibility policy impact her status for the 2026-27 season? Let’s set the scene real quick. This week, the Big Ten and SEC announced a ban on professional athletes returning to college ath
articles._body: Kentucky women’s basketball player Ajša Sivka was once a WNBA Draft pick. Will the SEC’s new eligibility policy impact her status for the 2026-27 season? Let’s set the scene real quick. This week, the Big Ten and SEC announced a ban on professional athletes returning to college athletics. The SEC’s new policy states that member schools are not allowed to add any athletes to their rosters who have met the criteria of at least one of the following three bullet points. Previously declared for the NFL, NBA, or WNBA Draft, and did not appropriately withdraw. Signed a contract with an NFL (or other professional football league), NBA/G-League, or WNBA (or affiliate) team. Been listed on an NFL (or other professional football league), NBA/G-League, or WNBA (or affiliate) roster. These new rules are still somewhat vague. It remains to be seen how the policy will impact someone like new Kentucky men’s basketball commit Mark Mitchell , who played in the NBA Summer League with the Denver Nuggets but did not officially sign his Exhibit 10 contract. Mitchell had exhausted his four years of college eligibility following the 2025-26 season, automatically making him eligible for the NBA Draft — all of this happening before the advent of the 5-in-5 rule, which he is now fighting to join. Mitchell’s situation is still murky as of Wednesday morning. He (along with other college athletes) has been cleared to play by the courts for a fifth year, which the NCAA continues to fight, but the SEC has not clarified where former Summer League players like Mitchell fall within the new policies. Now let’s get back to Sivka. Her situation is unique. Born and raised in Slovenia, the 6-foot-4 guard was drafted by the Chicago Sky with the 10th overall pick in the 2025 WNBA Draft. As an international prospect, she was automatically ruled eligible for the WNBA Draft since she turned 20 years old during the same year of the draft. But instead of signing with the Sky, which still retains her rights, Sivka returned home to Slovenia to complete high school. That also means she did not appear on an official WNBA roster. Circling back to the SEC’s new policy, Sivka clears the second and third bullet points. As for the first bullet point, since Sivka was automatically eligible for the WNBA Draft as a 20-year-old, there was no formal process for her to withdraw, a source close to the situation tells KSR — even though she was drafted. In short, Sivka cannot withdraw from a draft she never technically declared for. She did not sign a contract with a WNBA team, was never listed on an official WNBA roster, and has not played in college athletics before. All of that would seem to be positive news for Sivka’s eligibility next season at Kentucky.

articles.title: Xbox’s new disc-to-digital program gives physical games a digital future
articles.summary: "Most" Xbox One and Series X games are compatible; discs will still work after being claimed.
articles._body: For decades, console owners have faced a choice between the convenience of digital downloads and the permanence of physical game discs. Soon, Xbox owners will be able to get the best of both worlds for thousands of supported titles as part of a newly announced disc-to-digital program. The program— announced today ahead of testing for Xbox Insiders starting August 31—will let players claim a "digital entitlement" for "most Xbox One and Xbox Series X disc-based games" simply by inserting the disc into a console and launching it. That game will then be playable completely digitally, without the need to ever insert the disc, as long as you (or a member of your family account) is logged in. The digital entitlement will also allow access to features like Xbox Play Anywhere (for play on PC) and Xbox Cloud Gaming, for supported titles. Microsoft says that your physical disc will "continue to work exactly as it always has" after the digital entitlement is claimed. But before you get any ideas, the fine print on the announcement mentions that there is only "one revokable license per game disc," so if you resell that disc or loan it to a friend, that digital entitlement could be transferred to a new account when someone else puts it into their console. articles.title: Aaron Judge’s rib and 4 Yankees’ injuries that will shape 2026 World Series outlook
articles.summary: The New York Yankees currently lead the American League Wild Card and are in second place in the American League East division. They will not have any trouble reaching the postseason. Reaching the World Series is realistic as well given how weak the AL is at the moment — although there are
articles._body: The New York Yankees currently lead the American League Wild Card and are in second place in the American League East division. They will not have any trouble reaching the postseason. Reaching the World Series is realistic as well given how weak the AL is at the moment — although there are some sneaky contenders who could make things interesting . Winning the World Series will be especially difficult given how many talented National League teams there are right now, however. Whichever ball club emerges from the NL will have a tremendous opportunity to win the Fall Classic. Many teams around the MLB world are dealing with injuries, and the Yankees are no different. Aaron Judge’s rib injury could ultimately determine just how far New York can go in the postseason. However, there are plenty of other injury situations to monitor on this ball club. Let’s take a look at five Yankees’ injuries that may shape the team’s 2026 World Series outlook. Aaron Judge (rib) Judge is working his way back from a rib injury. He has a stress fracture of his first rib on his right side — an injury that has kept him out since early June. The good news is that the Yankees are still expecting Judge to return before the end of the regular season. Judge should have at least some time to get some MLB games in before entering the postseason. Judge is the Yankees most important player and they will need him to play up to his expectations if they want to win their first World Series since the 2009 season. Max Fried (elbow) Fried is trending in the right direction and a recent report even suggested he could return as soon as the Yankees’ upcoming weekend series against the Boston Red Sox. The southpaw is battling back from a left elbow bone bruise. Of course, anytime the words “elbow injury” and “pitcher” are used in the same sentence, teams automatically proceed with extreme caution. Barring any setbacks, however, it seems as if Fried should be alright. The Yankees’ pitching has been their strength this season. They will need that to continue in the postseason. Carlos Rodon, Gerrit Cole and Cam Schlittler are quality hurlers, but having Fried available would only make the rotation stronger. Giancarlo Stanton (calf) The first two injury updates we mentioned in this story were optimistic for the most part. Fried is expected to return soon and Judge could return before the playoffs. Stanton’s calf injury situation, however, is trending in a different direction. Stanton was previously recovering from a right calf strain but recently suffered a left calf strain while running the bases. Stanton could miss the rest of the season — although nothing is official. Stanton may not be the player he once was, but the Yankees’ lineup has had ups and downs this season. They would benefit from Stanton’s power in the lineup. He will be missed if his calf injury does indeed keep him out for the rest of the year. Ryan McMahon (thumb) McMahon is not a star with the Yankees but he’s still an impactful player. He is currently dealing with a sprained left thumb. It seems as if McMahon could return in September. The infielder provides the Yankees with some left-handed power to go along with defensive versatility. He is known as a third baseman but McMahon can play second and first base as well. Having him available in the postseason would give the Yankees a boost. It seems as if he will indeed be ready for October baseball assuming no setbacks occur. Clarke Schmidt (Tommy John surgery recovery) Schmidt could realistically be the X-factor in the postseason. Everyone knows who the Yankees’ best pitchers are. MLB fans also know that starting pitchers do not always last as long in playoff games at times. Schmidt is likely going to serve as a reliever once he returns from his Tommy John surgery — with his return potentially coming in September. Schmidt could potentially enter games in the middle innings during the playoffs and give the Yankees multiple innings. Of course, it remains to be seen how effective he will be after returning from Tommy John surgery. If Schmidt can perform well, he would give the Yankees a crucial boost. articles.title: Rutgers Football Top 10 Countdown: J’Dan Burnett
articles.summary: The Knight Report counts down the days until Rutgers Football kicks off by breaking down the Top 10 Players for the Scarlet Knights in 2026.
articles._body: The Knight Report counts down the days until kickoff by breaking down the Top 10 Players for Rutgers Football in 2026, revealing one each day until the start of the season. Defensive lineman J’Dan Burnett becomes the second transfer acquisition to join the list, coming in at #9. Honorable Mentions (Just missed the cut): Kaj Sanders, Jourdin Houston, Moshood Giwa Profile The next player to appear on the list comes along the crowded Scarlet Knights defensive line. Burnett transferred to Rutgers following a one-season stop at Tulsa in 2025. BREAKING: Tulsa EDGE transfer J’Dan Burnett commits to Rutgers Football! He had 28 tackles, 9.5 TFLs, and 6.5 sacks, while earning All-AAC second team in 2025. https://t.co/Yn0riNhWj4 pic.twitter.com/xLVbRRbDoX — Rutgers Scarlet Knights | The Knight Report (@RutgersOn3) January 19, 2026 The Fort Worth, Texas native was the 941st ranked recruit in the 2021 class coming out of Nolan Catholic. The edge rusher wound up committing to play for Louisiana Tech. Burnett spent four seasons with the Bulldogs, biding his time before consistently carving out a role along the defensive line. He appeared in just one game as a freshman, and would start seven games over the following three seasons. Burnett opened the 2023 season with three consecutive starts before a lower-leg injury unfortunately ended his season. He was extremely successful in his role amongst a platoon of defensive lineman. As a redshirt freshman in 2022, Burnett recorded 21 tackles, 13 pressures, one sack, and two forced fumbles in 280 snaps. He got off to a hot start in 2023, racking up 11 tackles, 12 pressures, and two sacks in just three games prior to his injury. In his last season with Louisiana Tech, Burnett notched a then, career-high in snaps. He managed 19 tackles, 19 pressures, and two sacks in his first season post-injury. Burnett would find a change of scenery in 2025, joining the Tulsa Golden Hurricane. A fresh start boded well for him, as he dominated the front half of the schedule. In his first seven games, he racked up 15 tackles, 20 pressures, seven sacks – with one coming in each game, and a forced fumble. Interestingly, Burnett’s play dropped off once he was officially named a starter, as he registered just seven tackles and six pressures over the final five contests. The now, sixth-year senior joins a revamped Rutgers front with by far the most pass rushing production of the group. Burnett is more than accustomed to specialized usage throughout his career, and it is fair to assume he will be deployed similarly again in passing situations. Run Defense The Rutgers defense allowed an egregiously bad 6.8 yards per rush last season. Burnett will not come in and immediately be an anchor in that department, but he can be solid. This past season in the American Conference, he played on 274 rushing downs and came up with 20 tackles, not missing a single one. His average depth of tackle was just 1.4 yards, which would be an exceptional mark for interior players, let alone a defensive end. One of the most impressive parts of Burnett’s game is that he simply does not miss tackles. He missed all but one last season, and he has missed just three tackles in his entire career, which accounts for over 1,300 snaps. That is an absurd missed tackle rate of 3.9%, which would be 99th percentile for any defensive position. A big area of contention for Burnett and many defensive lineman alike is size, but nowadays there is not much correlation between size and ability, especially at the college level. Eric O’Neill, who many labeled as undersized, is notably bigger than Burnett. He enjoyed a decorated collegiate career, but still had a missed tackle rate of 20.1%, including nine just last season. Now that is not to say that tackle rate correlates directly to one’s ability in run defense, because it does not. That said, tackling is an ability that certainly helps in making a run defense effective. Whether Burnett finds himself in a one on one with a back on the edge, or en route to the quarterback you can count on him finish the play. Pass Rush This is the area where he can particularly excel. Seven sacks in seven games is impressive at any level of football, and Burnett did put together his best season in 2025 at the highest level of football he has played. That said, the jump to the Big Ten is not to be understated. At any level, he is undersized, but the difference in the Big Ten is that offensive lineman, while probably bigger as well, are simply more equipped to combat different types of bodies. Looking back at Burnett’s 2025 season, it was truly a tale of two halves. In the first seven games across 154 pass rushing opportunities, he forced 20 pressures and came away with seven sacks. In the final five games he produced just six pressures with no sacks in 97 pass rushing snaps. For the season is his pass rush win percentage leveled out at 14.8%, which is about an average mark. On true pass sets, which are passing plays that do not include screens, play-action, or rollouts he was effective. In 80 pass rush opportunities he accumulated 12 pressures and a pair of sacks, with a pass rush win percentage of 25.7%. The vast majority of players will produce more effectively against true pass sets, as they can tee off after the quarterback without having to account for forms of “deception”. The Scarlet Knights could not stop a nosebleed last season, and that is largely because of the down-to-down situations they often left themselves in. There is so much the offense can do when they are constantly operating from second-and-two, and largely avoiding third downs entirely. While he can assist, Burnett will not single-handedly improve the run defense, but where he can excel is as a pass rusher. articles.title: Doja Cat Says Ella Langley Has a ‘Very Pretty Voice’ But She Doesn’t Like ‘Choosin’ Texas’: ‘This Is Not My Vibe’
articles.summary: Doja went viral over the weekend for not knowing who the country singer was.
articles._body: Nineteen weeks at No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 wasn’t enough to get on Doja Cat’s radar, as she appeared to have no idea who Ella Langley was during a Sundae Conversation interview over the weekend. The Grammy winner did her homework on the country breakout star during a livestream on Tuesday night (Aug. 25), which saw Doja give an unfiltered review of Langley and “Choosin’ Texas.” “I really don’t just give a f–k about country music and I don’t understand what’s so hard to believe about that. I never cared. I like that one Keith Urban song from 2004,” she said. “I wouldn’t say that I like her music; she’s probably a fine lady. I don’t care for that type of s–t at all. It doesn’t inspire me, it doesn’t make me feel good.” Doja Cat gave “Choosin’ Texas” a listen for the first time during the livestream and she didn’t hold back with her opinion. “This is not my vibe, but she has a very pretty voice,” she added. “If this is No. 1 on the charts, I’m sure it’s on the radio. I could see them playing this s–t on the radio. I don’t like it, but that’s fine. It’s very earwormy it sounds like, it’s like catchy melody. I get it, and she’s pretty.” Doja didn’t end up making it through the entire song. “The song’s not bad, it’s literally not bad. The music’s not bad, I just don’t f–king like it,” she continued. “Just ’cause I don’t like something doesn’t make it bad. I’m sorry, I can’t do more than a minute and 17 seconds of that. I’m not gonna play the whole song.” While Doja hasn’t been up on Langley, millions of others have been fueling her “Choosin’ Texas” anthem, which notched a 19th week atop the Hot 100 on the chart dated Aug. 29. Doja Cat has topped the Hot 100 twice: with “Say So” featuring Nicki Minaj in 2020 and “Paint the Town Red” in 2023. Langley’s run at the summit ties her for the longest non-holiday No. 1 stretch ever, alongside Lil Nas X and Billy Ray Cyrus’ “Old Town Road” and Shaboozey’s “A Bar Song (Tipsy).” Doja Cat’s Tour Ma Vie World Tour kicks off in Detroit on Oct. 1. The Ravens have had an eventful offseason, including signing wide receiver Zay Flowers to one of the richest contracts in the position’s history. On Wednesday, the Ravens got an update on Flowers&#
articles._body: The Baltimore Ravens have just over two weeks left until they kick off their 2026 NFL season. The Ravens have had an eventful offseason, including signing wide receiver Zay Flowers to one of the richest contracts in the position’s history. On Wednesday, the Ravens got an update on Flowers’ status for practice. “Ravens WR Zay Flowers didn’t practice in the joint practice because he’s dealing with something minor, per Jesse Minter,” reported Jamison Hensley of ESPN on X, formerly Twitter. The Ravens are currently taking part in a joint practice with the Washington Commanders ahead of the preseason game between the two teams later in the week. Although the exact nature of Flowers’ ailment has not been specific, thankfully, it doesn’t appear to be anything too severe. Some fans were puzzled when the Ravens inked Flowers to a deal that pays him like one of the very best receivers in the NFL landscape, but he has become an integral part of Baltimore’s offensive attack over the last few years, using his elite speed and route-running ability to torch opposing defenses and give quarterback Lamar Jackson a reliable target downfield. The pressure is on for the Ravens to bounce back this year after missing the playoffs altogether in 2025, which caused the team to fire head coach John Harbaugh and bring in Jesse Minter to replace him. In any case, the Ravens are slated to kick off their regular season on September 13 with a road game against the Indianapolis Colts at 1:00 pm ET. articles.title: LSU, Players Gearing Up for Potential Battle With SEC Over Eligibility
articles.summary: Nathan Ray Seebeck-Imagn Images
articles._body: Last week, a Louisiana judge granted a temporary restraining order allowing players who had signed NFL contracts to go back to college programs. LSU has secured deals with two of them: Dae’Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris. But on Tuesday, SEC presidents tried to block these players from returning to college—the conference voted to sanction teams that roster former professional football or basketball players. The events have put LSU, as well as its future players, on a collision course with the SEC. As of Tuesday night, LSU was still planning to sign Wright. Players’ lawyers are gearing up for a legal battle with the conference. LSU, which has repeatedly supported players on this issue, will likely do the same. The ramifications go far beyond the SEC, however. The situation could test whether conferences have the legal authority to set and enforce rules the NCAA can’t. The entire college sports world is watching the powder keg in Baton Rouge with bated breath. If conferences can’t enforce their own rules, one power conference school source said: “It would take us from light speed to ludicrous speed—‘spaceballs.’” The Louisiana lawsuit wasn’t about getting former NFL players eligibility. Instead, it’s one of many cases arguing players who started college in 2022 and exhausted four years of eligibility should get a fifth year by being grandfathered into the NCAA’s new “age-based” eligibility policy. Plaintiffs included Wright, who played preseason games for the Browns, and Harris, who signed with the Saints but was waived on Aug. 8 before preseason began. Last Wednesday, the judge granted a temporary restraining order not only allowing them to return to college, but also preventing the NCAA from blocking them from playing on account of their professional experience—so long as they terminated their pro contracts and repaid any wages. The ruling didn’t open the floodgates—it only applied to the 16 football players who had signed onto the lawsuit. It was considered a one-off because the situation only arose from a challenge over the handling of the freshman class of 2022, rather than a challenge over professional eligibility rules. But it made waves across college football, especially after Wright was waived Sunday and his agent announced he had a deal with LSU—setting him up to be the first player in college football history to go from NFL preseason games to college football games. Other sports are affected by the SEC’s stance. On Monday night, in a completely separate case unrelated to the class of 2022 eligibility fight, former St. John’s standout men’s basketball player RJ Luis Jr. secured an injunction to play men’s college basketball this season despite signing NBA contracts (though he never appeared in a regular season game). Luis also has a deal to play at LSU. On Tuesday afternoon, the Big Ten announced it had voted unanimously to allow the conference to enforce a league-wide prohibition on players who signed NFL contracts. The SEC followed hours later, adding that it had empowered commissioner Greg Sankey to enforce “penalties” on schools that allowed players who signed with NBA, G-League, WNBA (or team affiliates), or pro football teams. The SEC vote was reportedly unanimous, including LSU president Wade Rousse; a university spokesperson did not confirm to FOS whether Rousse was at this meeting, or whether he voted yes. LSU athletics declined to comment on the SEC’s ruling Tuesday. Attorney Darren Heitner, who works with Wright’s representation, told FOS on Tuesday night he still expected LSU to sign Wright, despite the SEC’s threats. According to the Louisiana injunction, Wright “is not only allowed to play, but must be allowed to play,” Heitner said. “Our understanding is that’s the intention of LSU right now as well. But if the SEC takes some sort of action to intervene, then we need to reassess, and determine what the next step is.” As of Wednesday morning, Wright’s representation had not received indication that that position had changed. Also Wednesday, the SEC presidents voted on a set of steep penalties for schools who violate the rule—the vote was reportedly 15-0, with LSU president Wade Rousse abstaining. Wright and his lawyers could file a motion in Louisiana asking the judge to clarify that the temporary restraining order also prevents the SEC from sanctioning them. Then, on Monday, a hearing is set to consider whether to turn the temporary restraining order into a preliminary injunction. That injunction would be valid until trial, which likely wouldn’t take place until after the end of college football season. An attorney for Luis did not respond to a request for comment sent Tuesday night, but he could similarly fight for his injunction to apply to the SEC. In addition to the ongoing litigation, more lawsuits could follow. LSU could prepare litigation against the SEC if it is penalized for playing Wright, Harris, or Luis. Meanwhile, the SEC could take the route the Big 12 took in the Brendan Sorsby debacle by filing a lawsuit asking a judge to affirm that it has the right to enforce rules, regardless of any ruling impacting the NCAA. In the meantime, players who have participated in NFL preseason activities—and who fall into that class of 2022 freshmen category—are still considering filing lawsuits. These lawsuits may include conferences as defendants. Other conferences, including at the Group of 6 level, are discussing NFL player bans of their own, sources said. The post LSU, Players Gearing Up for Potential Battle With SEC Over Eligibility appeared first on Front Office Sports .

articles.title: Packers GM Brian Gutekunst reveals Josh Jacobs backup plan in case of suspension
articles.summary: Josh Jacobs was arrested in May on potential domestic abuse charges. While charges have not been formally made, Jacobs could still be punished by the NFL. Now, Packers GM Brian Gutekunst is revealing the plan in case of a suspension, per Rob Demovsky of ESPN. Gutekunst was asked if the Packers wo
articles._body: Josh Jacobs was arrested in May on potential domestic abuse charges. While charges have not been formally made, Jacobs could still be punished by the NFL . Now, Packers GM Brian Gutekunst is revealing the plan in case of a suspension , per Rob Demovsky of ESPN. Gutekunst was asked if the Packers would be keeping an extra running back in case of a suspension. “We could. You usually keep 3 or 4 running backs, and I think we have enough to do that,” Gutekunst said. He also noted that it is easy to elevate a running back off the practice squad if need be as well. Regardless, it will be difficult to replace Jacobs. He ran for 929 yards and 13 touchdowns last year. MarShawn Lloyd is currently the backup, but he has just six carries for 15 yards in his career, coming back in 2024. Lloyd has dealt with some injury issues, but the team is becoming more confident in him . “We’re starting to feel a lot more confident that he’s going to be fine. But you still have to be cautious. As much as you want to just jump in and just keep feeding him and keep feeding him, I think that part of it is still a work in process,” Packers running backs coach Ben Sirmans said. Chris Brooks and Pierre Strong Jr. are also on the roster and could both be kept if Jacobs is going to be suspended. Beyond the threat of suspension, Jacobs is also dealing with a groin injury. He is expected to go through some limited team work in practice this week, but may not play in the final preseason game. The Packers face the Cardinals on Friday night. articles.summary:
The San Diego Padres are hoping that Casey Mize will be just fine by the time he walks back to the mound next. He is lined up to pitch on Friday against the Tampa Bay Rays at Tropicana Field. That start is in doubt after tripping on the dugout steps during his last start on […]

The p
articles._body: The San Diego Padres are hoping that Casey Mize will be just fine by the time he walks back to the mound next. He is lined up to pitch on Friday against the Tampa Bay Rays at Tropicana Field. That start is in doubt after tripping on the dugout steps during his last start on Saturday night. “It’s a little swollen, tender, but woke up pretty encouraged with how I’m feeling. We’re just going to treat it a ton, do a lot of exercises, and then reevaluate — I think probably daily. But a little bit encouraged on how I’m waking up feeling today,” Mize said on Sunday. Mize will throw a bullpen session Wednesday after playing catch the last few days. If the bullpen session goes well, he may not need to miss a start because the Friars have a day off Thursday. If the Padres do want to move Mize back one day to Saturday, they have the depth in the pen to open the series against the Rays with a bullpen game. Mize has struggled for the most part since joining the Padres at the deadline from the Detroit Tigers. In four starts, he has seen his ERA rise to 3.97, and it’s at 7.00 with the Padres. He’s allowed five home runs and 14 runs total. This is definitely not what the Padres had imagined when they traded for him, but they are hoping that he will settle down soon and be a solid factor in their playoff run. The good news is that Joe Musgrove and Nick Pivetta are expected to start a game at some point in September. If those two are healthy down the stretch, that is a massive upgrade for the Padres. The injury occurred with less than three weeks to go until the Bengals are set to kick off their 2026 regular season. On Wednesday, the Beng
articles._body: On Tuesday afternoon, the Cincinnati Bengals got a scare when star wide receiver Ja’Marr Chase went down with an apparent leg injury at training camp. The injury occurred with less than three weeks to go until the Bengals are set to kick off their 2026 regular season. On Wednesday, the Bengals got a key update on Chase’s status moving forward in training camp. “Ja’Marr Chase is not practicing today, following his hyperextension during yesterday’s practice. Not surprising. It’s a light practice for the Bengals. No pads,” reported Caleb Noe of WCPO on X, formerly Twitter. Noe also reported that “WR Dohnte Meyers is getting reps with the first-team offense in the absence of Ja’Marr Chase.” The last thing Bengals fans want to see is their star wide receiver going down with injury prior to the season, after watching multiple years derailed, including 2025, by injury absences to quarterback Joe Burrow. However, thankfully, Chase’s injury doesn’t appear to be anything too severe. Kelsey Conway of the Cincinnati Enquirer also reported on X that “Bengals update: The starters won’t play against the Eagles in the final preseason game. And as far as an update on Ja’Marr Chase after yesterday’s injury and him not practicing, Zac Taylor is deferring to Ja’Marr’s comments yesterday.” Chase had previously downplayed the injury’s severity. Chase is arguably the best wide receiver in the NFL today, and forms one of the league’s most lethal duos alongside Tee Higgins, virtually guaranteeing that the Bengals will have an elite offense anytime those two and Burrow are on the field together. The big question mark is whether or not the Bengals defense has improved this offseason enough to make the team respectable again on that side of the ball and return them to contender status in the AFC. articles.title: Carly Pearce & More Will Honor Dolly Parton This Weekend at the Grand Ole Opry
articles.summary: The Country Music Hall of Famer died on Aug. 25 at age 80.
articles._body: As millions mourn the passing of music icon Dolly Parton , the Grand Ole Opry will dedicate its Saturday (Aug. 29) night show to honor the legend. The evening’s performer lineup will include Grammy winner Carly Pearce , who launched her career at Dollywood, Parton’s theme park in Pigeon Forge, Tenn. Parton surprised Pearce with an invitation to become a Grand Ole Opry member in 2021. Others on the Opry’s Saturday night lineup include Channing Wilson, Belle Frantz, Kathy Mattea, Molly Tuttle, Dan Tyminski, T. Graham Brown, and the Opry Square Dancers. The Saturday night Opry show will air on the Opry’s flagship station, WSM-AM and online at wsmonline.com, opry.com, and on SiriusXM channel 58. Parton died on Aug. 25 at Nashville’s Vanderbilt-Ingram Cancer Center, following a brief, private battle with cancer. The afternoon of Aug. 25, the Grand Ole Opry’s marquee also lit up with a message honoring the country music icon, and the marquee will show that message through the weekend. Parton was inducted as a member of the Grand Ole Opry in 1969 and has been an Opry member for more than five decades. In January, Parton shared an excerpt from her book Star of the Show: My Life Onstage on Instagram, writing about being an Opry member. “In January of 1969, I was inducted into the Grand Ole Opry,” she wrote. “I had always wanted to be a member. Back home and in country music, the epitome of success was to be on the Grand Ole Opry. To become a member was a big deal. I thought back to how I’d perform on my porch at my Tennessee mountain home, imagining that one day I was going to be on the Grand Ole Opry. By becoming an official member, I would forever be associated with the Opry. It was a dream come true. And it still is.” “Every member of the Grand Ole Opry family has a Dolly story, as does everyone around the world who was ever in her orbit,” Dan Rogers, senior vp and exec. producer of the Grand Ole Opry, said in a statement. “That’s just one of the things that made her so special. For more than 50 years as an Opry member, she used her talent and success to bring sheer joy to millions. To every artist, she provided inspiration beyond measure. To every fan, she connected in a way that made each of us feel like the most important person in the room. Her impact will live on forever as we all carry forward the kindness, compassion and generosity she shared throughout her life. Dolly always knew exactly what to say. I’m afraid the best I have on this terribly sad day is a genuine, heartfelt, ‘Thank you for everything, Dolly. We sure do love you.’” “Our beloved Dolly Parton spent her life and career bringing joy, laughter, hope and integrity into everything she touched,” read a statement , which was signed from Team Dolly. “Her unmatched generosity reached the lives of countless people whom she would never meet, yet she was always there to offer a helping hand. Whether it be the hundreds of millions of books donated through her invaluable Imagination Library or funding research that helped create a lifesaving vaccine used around the world, Dolly’s unconditional love for all people was the guiding force for her lasting impact. After bravely facing a brief battle with cancer, Dolly departed her Earthly life today at the Vanderbilt-Ingram Cancer Center surrounded by loved ones.”

articles.title: Show HN: Build your own theme park
articles.summary:

articles._body: I built an agent that helps you build Rollercoaster Tycoon-influenced theme parks. You can prompt something like “Build me a cool theme park” and it’ll build a cohesive theme park with multiple worlds and connected with paths and rides. The weird part is that I built it using the same ideas we use to make AI-generated websites follow a company’s design system. I work as an engineer at Magic Patterns, focused on building our Design System Agent, aimed to use your existing brand, components, and conventions instead of producing something that looks like generic AI-generated UI. By default, models tend to converge on similar-looking designs. This is part of that “vibe coded slop” feeling: the same typography treatments, shadows, cards, icons, animations, etc… My job is to figure out the right context and guardrails so that when you prompt “Build me a dashboard,” the result actually looks like your existing product. At some point I realized those same ideas could be applied to RCT. While in web, you might have rules about which typography, colors, spacing, and components should be used together. In a theme park, you need rules like: rollercoasters need complete tracks, rides need entrances connected to paths, paths need to connect different areas of the park, and a pirate-themed world should actually use pirate-themed scenery. It was interesting seeing how closely the problem of building a coherent theme park resembled the problem of building a coherent product UI. Similarly with web design, simply giving the model the right components wasn't enough. I ended up building an eval loop where Magic Patterns would generate a park, another agent would grade it against a rubric, and then the agent would update its rules and skill files before trying again. The rubric checked things like whether rollercoasters formed valid tracks with at least one drop, whether rides were accessible by paths, whether each world used the appropriate themed scenery, and whether the park worked as a whole. After a lot of iterations, you can now prompt something as simple as “Build me a cool theme park.” and you should get back a fully functioning park with guests, rides, paths, rollercoasters, and themed worlds. Best yet, you can also follow the guests, listen to their thoughts, and watch them ride the rides in RCT fashion. Happy to answer any questions, but would love to see the parks you all create! articles.title: Vikings player on roster bubble with most at stake in 2026 NFL preseason finale
articles.summary: The Minnesota Vikings came to the conclusion very quickly that they had made a key error at this time last season. They had been convinced that untested quarterback J.J. McCarthy was the right man to line up under center and help the team win the NFC North title and advance deep into the playoffs
articles._body: The Minnesota Vikings came to the conclusion very quickly that they had made a key error at this time last season. They had been convinced that untested quarterback J.J. McCarthy was the right man to line up under center and help the team win the NFC North title and advance deep into the playoffs. The Vikings pulled out a win in their Week 1 Monday night game against the Chicago Bears. While McCarthy had led the team to a fourth quarter comeback that helped secure a road victory, there were some problems that cropped up through the first three quarters that shook Vikings head coach Kevin O’Connell and the rest of the coaching staff. Despite their belief in McCarthy, the Vikings saw their quarterback miss open receivers at multiple points in the game. When Justin Jefferson is open in the secondary, getting the ball to him means there is a chance to score. McCarthy missed him and both the receiver and his coaches looked perplexed. This was an issue that would repeated at multiple points during the season. McCarthy had a few moments, but the lack of accuracy was not something that he was able to overcome. He also had a series of nagging injuries, and this was all on top of his empty 2024 season that was ruined by a torn meniscus in his first preseason game. The Vikings did not have a quarterback they could turn to if McCarthy was not up to the hype. That is not the case a year later. The Vikings acquired Kyler Murray from the Cardinals early in the offseason and the stated plan was that McCarthy would have to compete with Murray for the starting job in training camp. McCarthy was fighting from behind, and he is now at risk Mandatory Credit: Matt Krohn-Imagn Images That may not have been the case. The decision on Murray becoming the team’s starter was made before the first preseason game. If O’Connell and new Vikings general manager Nolan Teasley had truly wanted an open competition, no announcement would have been made until the team had played two preseason games. That was not about to happen. O’Connell did not want to risk injuries to either man, and he was impressed with Murray’s track record and spectacular athleticism. McCarthy may have been drafted because of his potential and intangibles — he led Michigan to a college national championship — but a lack of accuracy was going to be his underlying issue. So, with one preseason game to play before the Vikings finalize their roster and start preparing for the first game of the regular season against the Green Bay Packers, the Vikings have to figure out what to do with McCarthy. The Vikings have a starter in Murray and they have a veteran backup in Carson Wentz. He joined the Vikings in the middle of last season and now has the full understanding of the team’s offensive game plan. If he had to play because of injury, O’Connell has confidence that Wentz could do a competent job. McCarthy’s status is something of a mystery. He is technically listed as the No. 2 quarterback on the depth chart , but Wentz has done a better job during the preseason than McCarthy. It doesn’t seem that McCarthy has a real future with the Vikings. It may not have been fair to give the starting position to Murray before either one had played a preseason game, but that’s where Minnesota is at right now. Ideal move would be a trade shortly after roster cut down All NFL teams must cut their rosters down to 53 players by Sunday at 6 p.m. ET. However, that does not mean moves won’t be made before the first week of the season. Teams may find themselves in need of a young backup quarterback with a starter’s potential after rosters are pared, and Teasley may be getting calls inquiring about McCarthy. That would be the ideal scenario for Minnesota. The Vikings made McCarthy the No. 10 overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft. That class was heavy in top QB prospects with Chicago’s Caleb Williams and New England’s Drake Maye at the head of the class. The Vikings shouted that McCarthy was as good as the top QBs in the class, but they may not have believed it. They now understand that they overestimated his value. If the Vikings can trade McCarthy and get a second- or third-round selection, it would be an acceptable conclusion at this point. If McCarthy is going to build some kind of trade value, a strong showing in the team’s final preseason game against the Denver Broncos would be advisable. McCarthy took several hits against the Baltimore Ravens in last week’s preseason game, but he is likely to play at least one full quarter against the Broncos and possibly more. If he has a strong showing, the Vikings could get a legitimate trade offer for him and possibly move him. If not, they could possibly hold onto him with the hope that a trade offer will come before the Nov. 10 NFL trade deadline. They could also decide to send him packing, but that would be admitting to a punishing mistake — and that’s a very unpleasant scenario.   The post Vikings player on roster bubble with most at stake in 2026 NFL preseason finale appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles.title: Harry Potter star Rupert Grint to return as Ron Weasley on Broadway
articles.summary: Following in fellow co-star Tom Felton’s footsteps, Harry Potter Ron Weasley actor Rupert Grint will be reprising the role in the Broadway play, The Cursed Child, for a limited time. The show announced that Grint will return as Ron in the show for a limited engagement for 17 weeks from Feb.
articles._body: Following in fellow co-star Tom Felton’s footsteps, Harry Potter Ron Weasley actor Rupert Grint will be reprising the role in the Broadway play, The Cursed Child, for a limited time. The show announced that Grint will return as Ron in the show for a limited engagement for 17 weeks from Feb. 2, 2027, to May 30, 2027. This marks the first time playing Ron since the last Harry Potter movie, Deathly Hallows Part 2, which came out in 2011. Alastair Stout will assume the role in HBO’s upcoming series , which premieres on Dec. 25, 2026. How to get tickets for Rupert Grint’s Ron Weasley return in Harry Potter Broadway show Fans can sign up for access to the pre-sale to the performances with Grint as Ron. However, they only have a limited time to sign up, as the waitlist will close at 5:59 pm EST on Aug. 31. Those who sign up will receive an email with a pre-sale ticket link by 9 am EST on Sep. 1. The waiting room for the pre-sale will then open at 10:30 am EST on Sep. 1. Those who signed up for access can access the pre-sale via a link in the email. Then, at 11 am EST, people will be placed in line. Placement in line will be “randomly assigned.” According to the show’s website, “everyone who remains in line will have a chance to purchase tickets.” Harry Potter and the Cursed Child originally opened on the West End in June 2016. It was written by Jack Thorne and takes place after the events of the Deathly Hallows. J.K. Rowling received a story credit along with John Tiffany and Thorne. The Broadway production subsequently opened in April 2018 at the Lyric Theatre. It has remained there since it opened over eight years ago. Paul Thornley originally played Ron in the West End production before transferring to the Broadway show. He reprised the role in 2018 and 2020 as well. articles.title: Bob Myers walks through 76ers making Jaylen Brown trade with Brad Stevens’ Celtics
articles.summary: The Philadelphia 76ers have had one of their most transformative offseasons in franchise history this summer, first trading for Jaylen Brown of the Boston Celtics and then signing LeBron James in free agency. While the James signing has hogged most of the attention over the last month, the Brown
articles._body: The Philadelphia 76ers have had one of their most transformative offseasons in franchise history this summer, first trading for Jaylen Brown of the Boston Celtics and then signing LeBron James in free agency. While the James signing has hogged most of the attention over the last month, the Brown deal was the move that got the ball rolling. Now, Bob Myers, who has effectively been in charge of the 76ers’ front office this summer, broke down what went into that shocking trade with Brad Stevens and the Celtics. “You start hearing there was a possibility and the job then became is this a real thing with Jaylen Brown? … When Brad Stevens responded with, ‘What are you offering?’ Then you knew that there was a shot,” he said, per Cousins with Vince Carter & Tracy McGrady on X, formerly Twitter. Prior to the trade, there had been heavy rumblings that Brown’s time with the Celtics could be coming to an end, but few if any could have predicted that the 2024 NBA Finals MVP would be dealt to a divisional rival, and one that had just eliminated Boston from the playoffs after rallying from a 3-1 deficit at that. Even if the 76ers hadn’t signed James, fans would still have had plenty of reason to be excited about the upcoming season with Brown in the mix, and now that the former four-time league MVP is also on the squad, Philadelphia fancies itself a legit title contender for the first time since the days of Allen Iverson. Of course, there are still plenty of questions about the roster and how these pieces will fit together, but there’s no denying that the 76ers have certainly made themselves more intriguing this summer, if nothing else. articles.summary: Southern Land Co. has secured $165.9 million in financing for a mixed-use development underway in Houston’s Upper Kirby area. The Houston Business Journal reports that Bank OZK issued the loan to support th
articles._body: Southern Land Co. has secured $165.9 million in financing for a mixed-use development underway in Houston’s Upper Kirby area. The Houston Business Journal reports that Bank OZK issued the loan to support the construction of the 2811 Kirby development. The project broke ground in April. The 2-acre, 953,000-square-foot development at 2811 Kirby Drive, near the intersection of Kirby Drive and Kipling Street, will include two towers — one for offices and one for apartments — and approximately 15,000 square feet of ground-level restaurant space. The 38-story Lily River Oaks luxury multifamily building will have 331 apartments, including 18 penthouses. A separate 10-story commercial tower will offer Class AA office space totaling approximately 107,000 square feet. Stream Realty Partners is leading leasing efforts for the office component. Southern Land Co. expects to deliver the project in 2028. The development team includes Andres Construction as general contractor and Solomon Cordwell Buenz as architect and interior designer. articles.title: Will Serena, Venus Williams be teaming up for US Open doubles action?
articles.summary: The world has been wanting to see Serena and Venus Williams in action together at the US Open, and their wishes are soon to be granted. The sisters plan on playing doubles in the tournament, as they received a wild card, according to ESPN’s D’Arcy Maine. They played together last week
articles._body: The world has been wanting to see Serena and Venus Williams in action together at the US Open, and their wishes are soon to be granted. The sisters plan on playing doubles in the tournament, as they received a wild card , according to ESPN’s D’Arcy Maine. They played together last week at the Cincinnati Open after four years but lost in the first round. The Williams sisters won the 1999 and 2009 US Open doubles titles and, in their nine appearances, are 27-7. The last time they played was in 2022, which was Serena’s last match in Flushing Meadows. Serena is only set to play doubles at the US Open. She made it all the way to the quarterfinals in mixed doubles with Carlos Alcaraz earlier in the week before they were defeated by Belinda Bencic and Flavio Cobolli. Alcaraz noted how he was nervous playing alongside Serena, but she helped him settle down throughout the matches. “You know, full crowd. I was out for four months and a half, almost five months,” Alcaraz said. “I just, almost forget how I, how I feel, you know, stepping on the court once again. But it was just a couple of games. Then, you know, she made it easy for me. You know just try to enjoy to go for it every time. And, obviously the people, you know, like the week before the tournament began, being super electric helped me a lot. So I just, enjoy so much.” Now, everyone will have their eyes on the sister as they look to win their third tournament. articles.title: NBA rumors: Why Bulls lost out on Bennedict Mathurin to Pelicans
articles.summary: On Wednesday, it was reported by ESPN NBA insider Shams Charania that free agent wing Bennedict Mathurin had signed with the New Orleans Pelicans on a two-year, $16 million deal. The move ended the Chicago Bulls‘ pursuit of Mathurin, of which there had been rumors dating back to last season
articles._body: On Wednesday, it was reported by ESPN NBA insider Shams Charania that free agent wing Bennedict Mathurin had signed with the New Orleans Pelicans on a two-year, $16 million deal. The move ended the Chicago Bulls ‘ pursuit of Mathurin, of which there had been rumors dating back to last season. Now, ClutchPoints NBA insider Brett Siegel has broken down why Chicago ultimately missed out on their target. “Sources say the Bulls were among the most aggressive of several teams interested in a Bennedict Mathurin sign-and-trade this offseason, but signing with the Pelicans offered him a spot where he’s coveted long-term and can get to UFA quicker. The Year 2 player option also adds a layer of insurance for Mathurin,” reported Siegel on X, formerly Twitter. Acquiring Mathurin in a sign-and-trade scenario would have required a three-year deal from the Bulls, one less than he ultimately ended up signing for with the Pelicans. The move allows Mathurin to hit unrestricted free agency a year sooner, as he will now look to prove his worth to the league with his new situation in New Orleans. Meanwhile, the Bulls have had an eventful offseason, headlined by the additions of Norman Powell in free agency and Nic Claxton via trade. Chicago is hoping to defy expectations this season in a season in which many expect them to be among the worst teams in the Eastern Conference once again. Having Mathurin could have helped, but there are still other targets, specifically Jonathan Kuminga, on the market who could fill a similar role. The Bulls’ regular season is slated to get underway on October 21 with a road game against the Toronto Raptors.
