articles.title: Astros owner Jim Crane breaks silence on Joe Espada exit rumors after firing GM
articles.summary: The Houston Astros currently lead the AL West, but it has been a slight struggle this year. This has led Astros owner Jim Crane to move on from GM Dana Brown. The removal of the GM has led to questions of if Astros manager Joe Espada’s job was in jeopardy. Now, Crane is speaking out […
articles._body: The Houston Astros currently lead the AL West, but it has been a slight struggle this year. This has led Astros owner Jim Crane to move on from GM Dana Brown. The removal of the GM has led to questions of if Astros manager Joe Espada’s job was in jeopardy . Now, Crane is speaking out about the decision to move on from Brown and the future of Espada, per Chandler Rome of The Athletic. “There’s no good time for any of that, when you let someone go. I think just out of respect for Dana, we thought that was a time to give him a little space and regroup. He’s a great talent. He’s been in the business a long time. (It) gives him a little more time to get settled and get back to work somewhere else,” Crane said of the decision to move on from Brown. He was then asked if Espada would stay in his job for the rest of the season. “Oh, yes. Yes. I don’t know where that got mixed up, but that’s the same answer I’ve given since the first of the year,” Crane said. While Espada is safe for the rest of the year, his long-term future has not been decided. “Not yet. I told him we’d deal with that at the end of the season. We’ve never changed that answer all year long,” Crane said on if a decision has been made about Espada’s future. The Astros are now 66-66 on the year , which places them in first place in the AL West. They are a half-game ahead of the Texas Rangers in the division, and 2.5 games in front of the Seattle Mariners. The Astros continue their series with the New York Yankees on Wednesday night. articles.title: Dolly Parton Cited by Judge as He Strikes Down Texas Drag Law as Unconstitutional
articles.summary: The judge said the law was so broad that it might have even been turned against Parton for her "flamboyant clothes and breast exposure."
articles._body: On the same day Dolly Parton died, a federal judge cited the legendary singer as he struck down a 2023 Texas law restricting drag shows — ruling the “sweeping” statute was so broad that even the late star might have faced criminal penalties for how she dressed. In a decision on Tuesday (Aug. 26), Judge David Hittner ruled that the statute, known as Texas Senate Bill 12, was unconstitutional because it violated the First Amendment by infringing the freedom of speech. Related Dolly Parton Dead at 80: Music Executives Remember the Country Icon Dale Morris, Nashville Manager Who Guided Careers of Alabama & Kenny Chesney, Dies at 89 HYBE Pledges Over $300k for Colombia Earthquake Recovery The law is so vague that even “a single moment of eroticism could condemn an entire performance to criminal or civil penalties,” the judge said, before invoking Parton — who famously wore bright colors and low-necklines. “Just as many people… chastised Dolly Parton as a voluptuous sex symbol because of her big hair, flamboyant clothes and breast exposure,” the judge wrote, “there are ‘erotic’ elements in countless popular performances that could be subject to both civil and criminal penalties under S.B. 12.” Parton passed away earlier on Tuesday at the age of 80, sparking mass mourning for a legendary country singer and songwriter who spent half a century in the public eye. Hittner’s reference appears to be coincidental; it doesn’t reference her death and was likely written before the news was reported. But it was just one of several mentions of Parton in the ruling. The drag performer who challenged the law sometimes performed as Parton on stage, the judge wrote. And he said the law, which banned performances that are “in some sense erotic,” is so broad that it could criminalize “a Dolly Parton impersonator who uses a breast plate while dancing and making gestures.” The judge also cited other famous examples of musical artists who might have been subject to the Texas law, including Elvis and his “signature hip gyrations” and Miley Cyrus for “twerking on stage during a live performance at the 2013 MTV Video Music Awards.” “These are just a handful of traditionally constitutionally protected performances that S.B. 12 would prohibit,” Judge Hittner wrote. “This court need not list additional hypotheticals to which S.B. 12 would apply because the potential applications are limitless.” Enacted in 2023, S.B. 12 banned sexual gestures that use “accessories or prosthetics that exaggerate male or female sexual characteristics.” Violators can face up to a year in jail, and businesses hosting events can be fined $10,000 for each violation. An earlier version of the bill included explicit references to drag shows, but they were removed prior to passage in response to criticism. The law was part of a slew of such statutes passed by Republican-controlled legislatures in 2022 and 2023. A similar law in Florida was struck down in court on similar free speech grounds, but one in Tennessee was allowed to go into effect after the Supreme Court refused to hear the case. The judge, who previously issued an injunction refusing to allow the law to go into effect, concluded his ruling with a bit of plain-spoken advice: “For those who find such activities as described in this case offensive, the solution is relatively simple… just don’t go.” The decision can and likely will be appealed to a federal appeals court and then if necessary to the U.S. Supreme Court. A spokesperson for the Texas attorney general’s office did not immediately return a request for comment.

articles.title: SEC deals major blow to LSU coach Lane Kiffin’s NFL plot
articles.summary: Lane Kiffin and LSU have been collecting recently released NFL talent. Tight end Dae’Wuan Wright, who was cut by the Cleveland Browns, is set to join LSU. Meanwhile, Zxavian Harris is also looking to join Kiffin and LSU. Now, the rules for former pros attempting to return to the college ran
articles._body: Lane Kiffin and LSU have been collecting recently released NFL talent. Tight end Dae’Wuan Wright, who was cut by the Cleveland Browns, is set to join LSU . Meanwhile, Zxavian Harris is also looking to join Kiffin and LSU. Now, the rules for former pros attempting to return to the college ranks have been made clear, as has the punishment , per Daniel Hager of On3. The presidents, chancellors, and athletic directors of the SEC met and unanimously decided on the rules. “Following meetings with the presidents, chancellors, and athletics directors of the Southeastern Conference, the SEC will enforce the following policy: An SEC institution is NOT permitted to have an athlete on its roster who has: Previously declared for the NFL, NBA, or WNBA DRAFT, and did not appropriately withdraw, Signed a contract with an NFL (or other professional football league), NBA/G-League, or WNBA (or affiliate) team, or Been listed on an NFL (or other professional football league), NBA/G-League, or WNBA (or affiliate roster),” the ruling read. Both Wright and Harris have been listed on an NFL roster, meaning they are not permitted to play. If Kiffin and LSU decide to play the players, the SEC has already determined the punishment. It will be a half-season suspension for the head coach, in this case, Kiffin. SEC voting privileges will be revoked on business matters for the school that violates the rule. The SEC will also impose a fine of 50% of the sport’s annual operating budget. Further, the league is reserving the right to impose other penalties as seen fit. The SEC joins the Big Ten and Notre Dame in setting up punishments for teams that roster players who were formerly on a professional roster. articles.title: Michael Jordan Not Expected to Return to NBC’s NBA Coverage
articles.summary: NBC
articles._body: Michael Jordan is not expected to return to NBC Sports’s NBA coverage, Front Office Sports has learned. NBC scored a major coup when it landed His Airness as a “special on-air contributor” before the 2025–26 season. It was the first time Air Jordan really talked basketball on TV since 2020’s The Last Dance documentary, which focused on his Bulls dynasty. NBC aired all six of Jordan’s NBA titles during the network’s golden era of 1990s basketball coverage. Last year, Jordan’s contributions to NBC’s coverage consisted of one sit-down interview with Mike Tirico, which was spliced into multiple segments that aired throughout the season. Although his conversation with Tirico was fascinating, his appearances were ultimately few and far between, and they didn’t focus on the NBA’s current events. Jordan’s segments with Tirico were dubbed “MJ: Insights to Excellence.” Over five taped segments lasting about three to four minutes apiece, His Airness shared his thoughts on load management, playing at Madison Square Garden, and his Olympic experiences. During one segment, Jordan said load management shouldn’t be needed, noting stars have an obligation to the fans to suit up and play if they’re healthy. “I never wanted to miss a game,” he said. Michael Jordan made his NBC debut as a special contributor with the first edition of “MJ: Insights To Excellence” (via @NBAonNBC ) pic.twitter.com/AMvuanl7yJ — Yahoo Sports (@YahooSports) October 22, 2025 Despite the polarizing reaction to the Jordan segments, NBC earned critical raves for its “new-stolgic” return to NBA coverage , which included the return of John Tesh’s classic “Roundball Rock” anthem and appearances by legendary sportscasters such as Bob Costas. NBC will tip off the new 2026-2027 NBA season on Tuesday, Oct. 20, with a triple-header featuring Celtics-Pistons at 3 p.m. ET; Knicks-76ers at 7 p.m.; and Spurs-Thunder at 9:30. The NBA champion Knicks will get their rings and raise their first championship banner in 53 years during a pregame Opening Night ceremony. As always, the mercurial Jordan could change his mind. But right now, sources say NBC viewers likely won’t see or hear from basketball’s most famous face during the upcoming campaign. NBC declined comment. articles.title: Tim Curry, Star of ‘The Rocky Horror Picture Show,’ Dies at 80
articles.summary: The acclaimed British actor, author, comedian and singer was best known for playing cross-dressing Dr. Frank-N-Furter in the iconic late night movie classic.
articles._body: Tim Curry, the classically trained British actor and singer best known for playing the flamboyant Dr. Frank-N-Furter in the legendary midnight movie classic The Rocky Horror Picture Show has died at 80. According to TMZ , the Emmy-winning star of stage and screen (who suffered a major stroke in 2012) died on Tuesday night (Aug. 25) at his Los Angeles home, with no known cause of death at press time. Curry’s passing was confirmed to Billboard by Grand Central Publishing, which published his memoir, Vagabond: A Memoir , in 2025. Related It’s Astounding, Time Is Fleeting: 50 Years of ‘Rocky Horror’ Coverage In Our Back Pages Jay-Z 30 Pop-Up Experience to Open In London Ahead of Historic Tottenham Hotspur Stadium Shows Camilo's 'Vida de Rico' Enters YouTube's Billion Views Club After gaining notice as part of the original cast of the British production of the musical Hair in 1968, Curry rose to international stardom in the role that would come to define his half-century career as the lascivious, lingerie-wearing Frank-N-Furter in the original stage production of The Rocky Horror Show , a b-movie send-up that chronicles the misadventures of a naive couple who take refuge from a storm in the home of mad scientist Furter. Billboard ‘s April, 13, 1974 review of The Rocky Horror Show stage production touted the show for its “outrageously decadent humor” and recognized Tim Curry as “a major talent discovery” for his campy portrayal of the gender-bending mad scientist: “How many male performers could go through an entire play costumed in a Marlene Dietrich chorus girl outfit and still come across with Mick Jagger macho?,” the review asked. Though he would go on to perform in dozens of other plays and movies, it was his role in Rocky Horror that made Curry an international star, with audiences transfixed by his show-stopping, bump-and-grind introductory number, “Sweet Transvestite,” as well as the cabaret-like “I Can Make You a Man” and the emotional ballad “I’m Going Home,” among others. He famously reprised the role in the musical film adaptation in 1975, with that movie becoming a staple of interactive midnight screenings in which fans dressed up as his character (and others), and came armed with props mimicking the action on screen. Timothy James Curry was born on April 19, 1946 in Grappenhall, Cheshire England and showed musical talent early on, graduating with a degree in English and drama from the University of Birmingham in 1968. Following his breakout role in the Rocky Horror stage musical, Curry appeared in a string of stage plays and TV projects, including a lauded performance as William Shakespeare in the six-part 1978 British Will Shakespeare mini-series. HIs film career also took off, landing him roles in another cult classic, Times Square , as well as a scene-stealing turn as “Rooster” in the 1982 film adaptation of Annie . He scored another classic role in 1985 in the Ridley Scott fantasy film Legend as the Lord of Darkness, and another that year as Wadsworth the butler in the film adaptation of the board game Clue . Curry earned a Best Lead Actor Tony nomination in 1980 for his titular role in Amadeus and spent much of the next two decades bouncing between Broadway and London’s West End in a series of starring roles in The Threepenny Opera , The Art of Success , My Favorite Year (for which he earned his second Tony nomination) and as Scrooge in the 2001 musical A Christmas Carol . Audiences ate up his role as the hauty, suspicious Plaza Hotel concierge Mr. Hector in Home Alone 2 , which allowed the classically trained actor to indulge his silly, prat-fall-heavy, face-pulling less serious side. His range was proven via his horrifying role as the murderous Mr. Jigsaw in the horror parody Loaded Weapon 1 , as well as his droll turn as Gomez Addams in Addams Family Reunion in 1998. After moving the U.S., Curry began a run of television roles, including his Emmy-nominated portrayal of Winston Newquay in the triple role on the 1983 anthology series Tales From the Crypt , as well as a return to horror as Pennywise the Clown in the 1990 miniseries Stephen King’s It . In addition to his long list of stage, screen and television roles, Curry appeared on the Rocky Horror soundtrack — which reached No. 49 on the Billboard 200 album chart in 1978 — and released his debut album, a collection of mostly covers, on A&M Records in 1978, Read My Lips . His second LP, 1979’s more rocking collection of originals, Fearless , reached No. 53 on the Billboard 200 and spawned the minor hit “I Do The Rock,” which topped out at No. 96 on the Billboard Hot 100. Curry’s third album, 1981’s Simplicity , peaked at No. 112 on the Billboard 200. Curry was nominated for a Grammy Award in 2002 for Best Spoken Word Album for Children for his reading of A Series of Unfortunate Events: The Bad Beginning . Curry suffered a stroke in 2012 and spent the rest of his life in a wheelchair. He released his memoir, Vagabond , in 2025.

articles.title: Sky–Fever Game With Freedom Ejection Was WNBA’s Most Watched in Years
articles.summary: Patrick Gorski-Imagn Images
articles._body: The WNBA hit another viewership record, although this one came on a night the league would rather forget. Sunday’s Chicago Sky–Indiana Fever game drew 3.31 million viewers on NBC and Peacock, according to Nielsen Big Data + Panel and digital data from Adobe Analytics, the network announced Wednesday. It’s the most-watched WNBA regular-season game since the league’s opening weekend in 1997, NBC said in a statement. Last year’s Finals averaged 1.5 million viewers over four games on ESPN networks. NBC is broadcasting WNBA games this season for the first time since 2002 as a part of the league’s new media rights deal worth more than $3 billion . The Fever won the game, 113–90, with Caitlin Clark and Kelsey Mitchell combining for 67 points. But Sunday’s game was notable for an incident that did not involve Clark. Late in the third quarter, former NBA player Enes Kanter Freedom was ejected from Wintrust Arena after a verbal altercation with Sky guard Natasha Cloud. Freedom, who last played in the NBA in 2022, has been trolling the league for weeks and saying he wants to enter the 2027 draft as a woman.. The announcement comes a week after ESPN announced 2.6 million viewers for the Aug. 16 game between Fever–Atlanta Dream, the league’s most-watched regular-season WNBA game on cable . Fever–Sky games have consistently driven the highest WNBA viewership since 2024, when Clark and Angel Reese entered the league. (Reese was traded to the Dream in April.) League sources told Front Office Sports on Monday that Freedom, as well as former NBA player Royce White, who has also declared his intentions for the WNBA draft, are not eligible to play in the league based on its current eligibility rules. On Tuesday, Sky owner Michael Alter told media on a conference call that security rightfully removed Freedom from the arena after he “turned himself into a threat” for standing up and taking a step towards Cloud. Chicago has placed an indefinite ban on Freedom for attending Sky home games. But Freedom is not banned from attending other WNBA games as a fan, a league source told Front Office Sports . articles.summary: With Bennedict Mathurin agreeing to a deal with the New Orleans Pelicans, nearly all notable players in NBA free agency have signed new deals. There are a couple of good players left on the open market, though, including Jonathan Kuminga, who is pretty clearly the best remaining free agent beside
articles._body: With Bennedict Mathurin agreeing to a deal with the New Orleans Pelicans , nearly all notable players in NBA free agency have signed new deals. There are a couple of good players left on the open market, though, including Jonathan Kuminga, who is pretty clearly the best remaining free agent besides Jalen Duren. In recent weeks, the Los Angeles Lakers and Minnesota Timberwolves have emerged as the frontrunners to land the G-League Ignite product. The Lakers have revamped the roster this offseason, but they still need power forward help after moving on from LeBron James and Rui Hachimura. The Timberwolves have also been active all offseason long, but likewise, they need help at the four. Minnesota traded away Naz Reid and Julius Randle this offseason. While those teams seemingly remain the leaders to land the player who most recently suited up for the Atlanta Hawks, the Chicago Bulls have also emerged as contenders to land Kuminga, according to Jake Fischer. Chicago has been considered a potential fit for Kuminga for quite some time now, even dating back to trade rumors during his Golden State Warriors days. However, there wouldn’t be near the opportunity for Kuminga as there would be in Minnesota or Los Angeles, both from a contention standpoint and when it comes to playing time. The Bulls just drafted Caleb Wilson to be their star player, and their lottery pick one year prior, Noa Essengue, also plays the power forward position. Even so, Chicago does have a roster spot open, and they’ve got more money to spend than almost any other team in the league. Chicago is one of just three teams with cap space , and they are over $43 million away from the first apron . So, where will Kuminga play next? articles.title: How Warriors will honor Don Nelson this season
articles.summary: The Golden State Warriors will honor the late Hall of Fame head coach Don Nelson with a commemorative band on their uniforms in 2026-27. Nelson coached the Warriors for 11 seasons over two stints from 1988 to 1995, and 2006 to 2010, when he instilled a small-ball approach on offense, known as 
articles._body: The Golden State Warriors will honor the late Hall of Fame head coach Don Nelson with a commemorative band on their uniforms in 2026-27. Nelson coached the Warriors for 11 seasons over two stints from 1988 to 1995, and 2006 to 2010, when he instilled a small-ball approach on offense, known as “Nellie Ball,” which stuck throughout the 2010s, and led to Golden State’s four championships. The Warriors will wear a band that reads “Nellie” stitched onto their jerseys , which was Nelson’s nickname, according to NBA insider Marc Stein. The Warriors just announced that they will have a Don Nelson band affixed to their jerseys this coming season in tribute to their two-time head coach. Portland and Sacramento recently announced they would do the same in honor of Nelson’s fellow Hall of Famer Rick Adelman. pic.twitter.com/EalG8A4Thf — Marc Stein (@TheSteinLine) August 26, 2026 Nelson, a five-time champion with the Boston Celtics as a player, was inducted into the Naismith Basketball Hall of Fame as a coach in 2012. He also named head coach and general manager of the Dallas Mavericks from 1997 to 2005, before returning to the Warriors as head coach in 2006. Warriors’ Steve Kerr, Stephen Curry pay respect to Don Nelson Upon the news of his passing on August 9, Warriors’ Steve Kerr and Stephen Curry paid their respects to Don Nelson by speaking on his legacy as a head coach. The Warriors’ posted Kerr and Curry’s kind words on their X, formerly Twitter. “Don Nelson was a true innovator whose influence on the game of basketball is still felt today,” Kerr said. “He consistently challenged conventional thinking, experimented with different lineups and styles of play, and saw possibilities in the game that others often did not.” “One of the biggest reasons I was drafted by the Warriors was because of Don Nelson,” Curry added. “The story is he never liked rookies, but from Day 1 he challenged me and gave me an opportunity to be my best self on the court.” Nelson is the second all-time leader in wins as head coach (1,335). articles.title: Juan Gabriel’s 20 Best Songs of All Time, Ranked (Staff Picks)
articles.summary: A decade after his death, Billboard celebrates Gabriel's greatest hits of all time. From heartbreak anthems to pop gems and mariachi classics, see which song takes the No. 1 spot.
articles._body: A decade after his death, Juan Gabriel’s light still feels impossible to dim. The Mexican singer-songwriter, born Alberto Aguilera Valadez and forever known as the Divo de Juárez, was a once-in-a-generation artist whose work was as emotionally direct as it was grandly theatrical. He could turn a hushed confession into a full-scale melodrama, then punctuate it with a mariachi crescendo, a soaring vocal run or a defiant hip shake that brought an arena to its feet. In his rhinestone-studded jackets, glittering suits and flowing shirts, Juan Gabriel did not simply command a stage — he transformed it into a place where heartbreak, liberation, joy and spectacle could all coexist. His impact, of course, stretches far beyond his own extraordinary recordings. A prolific composer who wrote an expansive catalog of songs, Juanga supplied classics to some of the most celebrated voices in Spanish-language music, including Rocío Dúrcal, Isabel Pantoja, Lucha Villa and Ana Gabriel. His songs made room for the complicated dimensions of love: devotion and betrayal, loneliness and desire, tenderness and fury. Whether delivered with intimate restraint or a todo pulmón , his writing made emotional excess feel not only validated but transcendent. That gift made him both a chart force and a permanent pop-cultural reference point. “Te Sigo Amando” and “Abrázame Muy Fuerte” each reached No. 1 on Billboard ’s Hot Latin Songs chart, while hits such as “Hasta Que Te Conocí,” “Querida” and “Amor Eterno” have endured as essential standards in Latin music. His legacy continues to surface everywhere — from social-media trends and soccer celebrations (including the viral resurgence of “Así Fue” ahead of the 2026 FIFA World Cup) to the voices of new generations of artists embracing his genre-fluid songwriting, unabashed sentimentality and fearless self-expression. To mark the 10th anniversary of his death on Aug. 28, Billboard Latin and Billboard Español staff revisits the tracks that best illuminate Juan Gabriel’s towering genius. From devastating ballads to mariachi-fueled anthems and irresistible pop gems, these are El Divo de Juárez’s 20 Best Songs of All Time, ranked.

articles.title: John Cena pays silent tribute to Dolly Parton after death
articles.summary: After the shocking news of Dolly Parton’s death, WWE legend John Cena paid homage with a silent tribute after the country music icon passed away. Cena posted a picture of Parton doing what she did best: performing. However, the post did not feature a caption, but clearly, the 17-time world
articles._body: After the shocking news of Dolly Parton’s death , WWE legend John Cena paid homage with a silent tribute after the country music icon passed away. Cena posted a picture of Parton doing what she did best: performing. However, the post did not feature a caption , but clearly, the 17-time world champion had her on his mind. View this post on Instagram The post garnered several comments and reposts on Instagram. Not writing a caption is no shade to Parton, though, as very few of his posts have them. Dolly Parton’s cause of death revealed Scott Utterback/Courier Journal / USA TODAY NETWORK. After Parton’s death was first reported, her team confirmed to People that she passed away after a “brief battle with cancer.” However, the type of cancer was not disclosed. She died at the Vanderbilt-Ingram Cancer Center “surrounded by loved ones,” as the statement to People read. Parton passed away at 80 years old. The news was shared on her social media accounts in a video with her nephew, Bryan Seaver. He was asked to do the video years before Parton’s passing. He happily indulged. “My name is Bryan Seaver, son of Cassie Parton, and I’m representing the Parton and Owens family today announcing the passing of my aunt, Dolly Rebecca Parton Dean, Sister, Sis, and Granny to one generation and Gigi to the next,” Parton’s nephew began. “This video announcement is something Dolly asked of me years ago, before I fully absorbed it as a future reality. “As her head of security for more than two decades, a role my father Larry held before me, I have imagined the heaviness of this moment but haven’t truly felt it until now,” he continued. Parton is one of the most iconic country music singers of all time. She released countless albums throughout her career. Her last, Rockstar, was released in November 2023. It featured collaborations with icons like Paul McCartney, Elton John, Miley Cyrus, and Stevie Nicks. articles.title: Launch HN: Risklytics (YC S26) – Insurance brokerage for frontier tech companies
articles.summary: Hi HN, we're Sam and Alex, founders of Risklytics (https://risklytics.ai). We're both on leave from Harvard, and we run an insurance brokerage for companies building robots, drones, autonomous systems and satellites. You describe your machine, we find the insur
articles._body: Hi HN, we're Sam and Alex, founders of Risklytics ( https://risklytics.ai ). We're both on leave from Harvard, and we run an insurance brokerage for companies building robots, drones, autonomous systems and satellites. You describe your machine, we find the insurance companies willing to cover it, and we read everything before you sign. Buying insurance for any frontier tech goes like this: - your first customer or pilot requires coverage before your machine can work on their site - a broker hands you an application written for ordinary businesses, and often will deny you on baseless "risks" (one of our clients got denied for using CAD software in their workflow) - you get filed under something close or outright denied, the person at the insurance company often can't tell what they're looking at, and the safe answer is no - if a quote does come back, the AI risk is often quietly removed by an add-on clause that prevents you from truly being covered Those clauses surprised us. Insurance companies mostly don't write their own policies from scratch. They license standard forms from an industry body called ISO and attach add-on clauses to adjust them, and in January ISO published clauses that void coverage for losses arising out of AI in any part of a process. Each insurer decides whether to adopt them, account by account, and there's no public record of who has and to what capacity. There's an open question in the wording too. It defines generative AI as systems trained on data that produce text, images, audio, video or code. Whether a robot's control model, which produces motor commands, falls under that is unsettled. We've asked underwriters, the people at insurance companies who make these calls, and gotten different answers across the board. We didn't initially plan to be brokers. We came into YC to work in insurance and spent the first half of the batch on a wildfire risk model we wanted to sell to insurance companies. They liked it and wanted to build their own, which is the polite way to say no. While that was dying, a batchmate who launches satellites mentioned he couldn't get insured, and once we started asking around we kept hearing the same story from hardware companies. So we got licensed in a week and now can place coverage. What we've built so far: - a six-step application that asks about what you're building and drafts the structured version insurance companies like, omitting anything you didn't say - a map of which insurers add the AI clauses, which will remove them, and which cover frontier companies on purpose - when an insurer says no, you see their reason and what would change it, full transparency all the time - a hands off process for companies trying to get fully covered Here's a demo of the whole process: https://youtu.be/gVqCamTNH5E On money: the insurance company pays us a commission when you get covered, usually 10-20% of what you are charged, and we charge you nothing on top (that's right, no brokerage fees). Also, if you're a software company with ordinary needs, we'll still handle the whole process for you and get you the best policy we can find. In the past week alone we have helped three companies get covered that were denied elsewhere. The companies include a robotics wholesaler and rental store, who had trouble getting covered earlier because some of their property uses AI (even though they never use it themselves), a bridge collision system that was getting denied because they use CAD software, and a tele-operating robotics service that needed coverage within a week for their first pilot. If you're looking for insurance in any capacity feel free to reach out to me at alex@risklytics.ai or fill out an application at https://risklytics.ai . And if you work on the carrier side and think you'd wanna partner with us let us know. Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49451495 Points: 43 # Comments: 17

articles.title: Mark Walter’s Company Says There’s No Fraud, No Victim, and No Fire Sale
articles.summary: REUTERS/Jonathan Ernst
articles._body: Mark Walter’s TWG Global came out firing Wednesday, saying it has committed no fraud, rejecting the idea that Walter’s Lakers exit was part of a “fire sale” to raise money amid federal investigations, and insisting the Dodgers are not for sale. The press release marks the most substantial public statement since news broke that Walter’s companies are under parallel investigations by the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission and federal prosecutors in the Southern District of New York. “Over the past several weeks, multipronged attacks against TWG have been advanced by unnamed sources with self-serving interests that have been reported in the media,” the statement says. “It is important to set the record straight. TWG stands firmly behind the integrity of its business and remains focused on continuing to deliver value to its stakeholders.” Investigators are looking into at least two of Walter’s companies: Delaware Life and Clear Spring Life & Annuity. The probes center on inaccurate disclosures by the life insurers tied to what are known as “affiliated investments”; the amount originally disclosed was billions of dollars lower than what the company has since reported in restated disclosures. TWG’s statement says “there has been no fraud” and notes “there is no victim here. No one has been harmed, and no one has claimed they were harmed.” It also says TWG is “committed to working with” the DOJ and SEC to “resolve their inquiries,” and that it has “presented a plan to address any regulatory concerns.” A representative for the SEC declined to comment, and representatives for the DOJ and SDNY did not immediately respond to requests for comment. The idea that no one was harmed will not necessarily get Walter out of hot water, according to former DOJ trial attorney Michael Weinstein, who now works at law firm Cole Schotz. However, showing prosecutors that his companies have enough cash to restore the assets under investigation can give his attorneys a card to try and play to lessen any potential punishment. Weinstein compares it to someone who robs a bank and then returns the money. That person can “still be criminally prosecuted for robbing the bank,” he says. “He could be prosecuted if he intentionally misled investors, the insurance commissioner, or regulators, or committed some type of fraud,” he tells Front Office Sports . “That wouldn’t be wiped out by virtue of him having all the money now.” The issues at hand mirror claims made in a 2014 lawsuit —that money one of the plaintiffs paid into her life insurance policy was used to fund a $35 million loan that was connected to the purchase of the Dodgers. Although that suit was dropped one day after it was filed, the forensic accountant who helped build the case recently told FOS “my clients seemed pleased, that’s all I can say.” Weinstein tells FOS the 2014 suit is something prosecutors will likely take into account as they investigate. “Prosecutors look for patterns,” he says. “They look to see whether or not the accused individuals or companies have been doing this same type of thing for many years. They want to discern whether or not the most recent activity was inadvertent, or if there were law changes that caused them to conclude they could do it this way.” In Wednesday’s statement, TWG says “the allegation that the Los Angeles Dodgers were acquired or have been funded improperly is false and not supported by the facts.” It also notes the 2012 deal was “subject to significant scrutiny and complied with all rules and regulations that govern the purchase of Major League Baseball teams.” Further, it says the Dodgers “have the highest revenue in baseball,” and that the team’s revenue “significantly exceeds” its payroll obligations. A representative for MLB declined to comment. The idea that Walter could look to sell the Dodgers to raise funds amid what sources have called a “cash crunch” and “liquidity crunch” did not come out of thin air. Walter stunningly sold the Lakers to Joshua Kushner and Bob Iger at a $12.5 billion valuation earlier this month, and is in talks to sell his stake in Premier League soccer team Chelsea. However, TWG says it is “not looking to sell its sports assets at ‘fire sale’ prices to raise capital for its insurance operations. “TWG, Mr. Walter, and his partners continuously get interest from prospective buyers and co-investors in their sports assets, and, as responsible owners and investors, they consider legitimate offers when they are received,” the statement says. In addition to denying the Dodgers are up for grabs, TWG says Walter’s stake in the Cadillac Formula One team is not for sale. Walter also owns the WNBA’s Sparks and is the sole owner of the Professional Women’s Hockey League, which were not mentioned in the statement. Representatives for Walter and TWG did not immediately respond to questions about the Sparks and PWHL. The post Mark Walter’s Company Says There’s No Fraud, No Victim, and No Fire Sale appeared first on Front Office Sports .

articles.title: Walmart Closes on Celina Property, 2nd Store on Way
articles.summary: A second Walmart is coming to Celina. The company bought 41 acres at the southeast corner of FM 455 and the Dallas North Tollway, adjacent to Legacy Hills in Celina, a substantial master-planned communit
articles._body: A second Walmart is coming to Celina. The company bought 41 acres at the southeast corner of FM 455 and the Dallas North Tollway, adjacent to Legacy Hills in Celina, a substantial master-planned community in Celina. The town is America’s fastest-growing town. Celina City Council approved an economic development agreement with Wal-Mart in July. Walmart is set to receive up to $5.1 million in incentives. The planned store will be at least 150,000 square feet and requires a minimum $25 million investment from Walmart, not including the cost of the land, according to the agreement. Once the store is built, Walmart has to maintain at least 120 full-time employees for the duration of the agreement. The city of Celina and the Celina Economic Development Corp. will each give Walmart a 50% sales tax reimbursement grant for 10 years, It’s the town’s second Walmart. The city’s first Walmart opened off Preston Road in April (shown). The post Walmart Closes on Celina Property, 2nd Store on Way appeared first on Connect CRE .

articles.title: Court blocks Trump FCC order that could flood broadcast TV with more election ads
articles.summary: Republicans demanded that parties and fundraising committees be given lowest ad rates.
articles._body: A federal appeals court yesterday blocked a Trump administration decision that could have resulted in even more political advertisements appearing on broadcast television during the upcoming elections. The Federal Communications Commission recently ordered broadcasters to offer the lowest advertising rates to political parties and joint fundraising committees. Four Democratic candidates challenged the decision in court, saying that only individual candidates are entitled under US law to receive what is called the "lowest unit charge," or LUC. In a 2-1 vote, a judges' panel at the US Court of Appeals for the 4th Circuit agreed with the candidates and set aside the FCC decision that was scheduled to take effect on September 4. That's the start date of the 60-day period before the election in which broadcasters must offer the lowest ad rates to qualified candidates. Read full article Comments

articles.title: ESPN Removing BottomLine Ticker on College Football Games
articles.summary: ESPN
articles._body: ESPN is getting rid of its BottomLine ticker during college football games, the network confirmed to Front Office Sports . As it has already done away with for the College Football Playoff games and other big events like NBA and NHL postseason contests, ESPN will not feature the ticker for regular-season games that air on ABC, ACC Network, ESPN, ESPN2, ESPNU, ESPNews, and SEC Network. “We’re always looking for ways to better serve sports fans. By removing the BottomLine during live action, we’re creating a cleaner presentation that keeps the focus where it belongs—on the field,” an ESPN spokesperson said in the statement. There will still be score alerts during games at specific times during each quarter, one source said. There will also be updates in places like above the score bug or on the top right of the screen to help viewers navigate various schedule changes that occur, such as if the present game is running late and a new game is starting on a different channel or platform. The changes should provide a less cluttered viewing experience that better showcases the action on the field, and makes sense as a vast majority of fans can just check the scores of other games on their phones or tablets. The post ESPN Removing BottomLine Ticker on College Football Games appeared first on Front Office Sports .

articles.title: Golf Galaxy, Dick’s Pull Good Good Merchandise Amid Ad Controversy
articles.summary: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect
articles._body: Golf Galaxy and its parent company, Dick’s Sporting Goods, pulled Good Good Golf merchandise from in-person and online shelves Tuesday. It’s the latest consequence for the YouTube-channel-turned-major brand, which has been embroiled in controversy after posting a promotional video last Friday for a new driver—created in partnership with Callaway—that depicted Good Good cofounder Garrett Clark shoving a woman to the ground. Dick’s has yet to respond to repeated requests for comment from Front Office Sports about the status of its retail partnership with Good Good, but a search for the brand on Dick’s website currently yields a “ no matches found ” result. Good Good products are also no longer listed on Golf Galaxy’s website. FOS reached roughly a dozen Dick’s and Golf Galaxy locations across the country Wednesday morning; while some noted they still had Good Good merch on-site, all said the brand had been removed from their floors and its products were not available for sale. Several East Coast and Midwest locations of PGA Tour Superstore—Golf Galaxy’s biggest competitor—also said they had pulled Good Good merchandise when reached by phone Wednesday morning. One New Jersey store manager told FOS the move was a result of the backlash to the ad. “The video does not reflect our values or our commitment to making golf welcoming for everyone,” a PGA Tour Superstore spokesperson told FOS in a statement. Golf Channel announced late Tuesday it was postponing the premiere of a new show with the YouTube group, Big Break x Good Good , by a week to “allow for necessary production updates following a request from one of the show’s sponsors to remove its branding from the series.” Previous network communications about the show used the verbiage “Big Break x Good Good presented by Golf Galaxy,” suggesting Golf Galaxy is the dropout. (Golf Channel did not respond to a question asking about the sponsor.) Also on Tuesday, Callaway admitted involvement in the ad with a statement attributed to its CEO, Chip Brewer, who said the company “sincerely apologize[s],” is “conducting both internal and external investigations,” and has “already made changes to [its] approval processes aimed at ensuring this will never happen again.” Calls for the PGA Tour to drop Good Good as the title sponsor of its Fall Series event taking place Nov. 12–15 in Austin, Texas, are growing amid backlash to the ad. Asked about this Tuesday at a Tour Championship press conference, Tour CEO Brian Rolapp indicated a change wasn’t on the table—for now: “It’s a bit of a fluid situation. … It sounds like in the last 24 hours they’ve made some progress. We’ll continue to monitor the situation and see how it develops.” The fast-moving fallout represents a stunning turn of events for a brand that was otherwise red-hot. In an interview last month, Good Good’s VP of brand and marketing, Jeffrey Lefkovits , told FOS the company went from “roughly 800 to 4,000 retail doors in just the last year alone,” and claimed “a majority” of the top 10 best-selling hats at both Dick’s and Golf Galaxy in 2025. Dick’s, in contrast, had its worst day on record Tuesday. The retailer’s stock price dropped about 30% after reporting weak second-quarter earnings and slashing its full-year profit outlook. In addition to its almost 800 eponymous stores, Dick’s operates more than 70 Golf Galaxy locations across the United States. Extreme Backlash? Some onlookers have begun to wonder whether the reactions have gone too far. “Alright, the commercial was bad but what’re we doing,” Nate Geary, a Buffalo sports-radio host, wrote on X/Twitter Tuesday in response to a post about Golf Galaxy employees being ordered to pull Good Good merch. “My goodness this overreaction is getting out of control,” commented another user on the same post. “It was an ad made in poor taste…. they ended up pulling it & apologized.” Good Good, which has more than 2 million subscribers on its YouTube channel, has issued only one official statement on the situation so far. “We posted a video to our channels that ultimately depicted actions that are not aligned with our values as a brand,” the company wrote in a post on its X/Twitter account Saturday. “We have since taken that content down, and sincerely apologize. Good Good has always stood for making the game of golf more inclusive to all, and we will continue to ensure that is our mission moving forward.” However, its CEO, Matt Kendrick , spoke with The Wall Street Journal on Monday. “We fully own that we did make a mistake. … As the CEO of the company, the buck stops with me and we should have had better processes in place,” he told WSJ . “Obviously the execution missed the mark and didn’t come across the way that we wanted to, and in no way were we trying to make light of or support violence. But it came across that way, and that’s our fault.” Kendrick added that the full 60-second video was meant to spoof the horror movie Obsession , released earlier this summer. FOS obtained a copy of a memo Kendrick sent to all Good Good staff on Monday. In the email subject-lined “Owning Our Mistake,” he said the company plans to donate all proceeds of the driver campaign to an “organization supporting women in [its] local community.” Elsewhere, competitor brands are starting to pounce. Golf apparel and equipment provider Parsons Xtreme Golf (PXG) shared a video of women golfers using its drivers on Tuesday evening. It was captioned, “Our drivers play nice with everyone. #SheGolfs.” The post Golf Galaxy, Dick’s Pull Good Good Merchandise Amid Ad Controversy appeared first on Front Office Sports .

articles.title: SEC Sends Proposal to White House To Modernize Crypto Custody
articles.summary: Bitcoin Magazine
articles._body: Bitcoin Magazine SEC Sends Proposal to White House To Modernize Crypto Custody The Securities and Exchange Commission has sent a proposal to the White House aiming to “clarify the framework for the custody of crypto assets” for investment advisers and companies.  In a rule change sent Tuesday, the regulator said it wanted to “improve and modernize the regulations” surrounding custody for the crypto space. The proposal comes after a vote was delayed on the long-awaited Clarity Act. Despite the delay, regulators like the SEC and Commodity Futures Trading Commission have said they will still proceed with trying to shape crypto policy.  JUST IN: SEC has sent a new proposal to the White House concerning "amendments to the custody rules" to "clarify the framework for the custody of crypto assets" pic.twitter.com/c45BK1tlok — Bitcoin Magazine (@BitcoinMagazine) August 26, 2026 “This rulemaking would clarify the framework for the custody of crypto assets for investment adviser and investment companies, as well as make other modernizations needed to remove burdens from certain outdated provisions that are no longer needed to provide investor protection given the evolution in the markets and security trading and holding practices,” the proposal read.  Pro-crypto lawmakers had hoped to pass the Clarity Act before Congress broke for August recess, but the vote slipped to September after Democrats balked at the latest draft.  Some Republican senators — like Senator Cynthia Lummis — accused some of deliberately holding it back.  Still, pro-crypto regulators want to press ahead. CFTC Chairman Michael Selig has said he will proceed with rulemaking whether or not the Clarity Act is enacted, aiming to finalise rules before the administration’s term is out. And earlier this month, the SEC proposed its own framework to allow token issuers to raise money in the U.S. without falling foul of securities laws. President Donald Trump campaigned on a ticket to help the crypto industry and received major backing from Silicon Valley entrepreneurs. Since taking office, regulators have taken a remarkably different approach to watchdogging the digital asset space.  The president last week urged lawmakers to get the Clarity Act over the line. SEC Chair Paul Atkins has said he is “committed to supporting Congress in advancing” the bill.  This post SEC Sends Proposal to White House To Modernize Crypto Custody first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Mathew Di Salvo .

articles.title: Show HN: I built a tool that finds people asking for what you sell
articles.summary: I do cybersecurity consulting, so I do outreach every single day, and as you probably know, cold LinkedIn outreach usually has a very low response rate. I've also started launching SaaS products, and I know people running Etsy shops and e-commerce stores and getting users, even for free SaaS, is
articles._body: I do cybersecurity consulting, so I do outreach every single day, and as you probably know, cold LinkedIn outreach usually has a very low response rate. I've also started launching SaaS products, and I know people running Etsy shops and e-commerce stores and getting users, even for free SaaS, is hard. Meanwhile, people publicly ask for products and services every day on social media. That's why I launched ReachFast: 1. You enter your SaaS website, Etsy shop, App Store /Google Play page, Fiverr profile, even a Skool community link 2.No settings, no keywords, no linking your social accounts, ReachFast reads your website, understands what you sell and builds a detailed profile of your target customer 3. Then it looks for Reddit, X, LinkedIn and Facebook public posts that could be a customer asking for your product or service 4. Finally an AI judging round keeps only the warm leads likely to convert. Out of 4,000+ posts read, that can mean 350+ for a consumer product, or just 15 for a niche SaaS, but each one is someone actually asking 5. Initial scan is on the past 15 days but it also runs daily scans (on the past 24 hours posts) to find new fresh leads There is no automatic outreach, on purpose. The focus is to find quality leads, you decide how to reach them, usually by replying in the thread as yourself or DMs. From there you can also manage your pipeline by moving your posts into dead, reached or closed. For v2 I'm planning to work on a learning loop, once there's enough pipeline data, so the algorithm could learn which kinds of posts actually convert for each product and adjust what it keeps. Also, currently, niche B2B services, like my own pentesting firm, produce few leads but that's the nature of the business I guess, fewer asks, worth more each. Coverage is also uneven based on the nature of the product/service but again it makes sense. Cost is also variable based on the website (currently up to 8$ per initial scan on some Etsy shops) but again, focus is quality of leads, I will try to optimise later! Happy to answer anything and get your feedback! Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49450777 Points: 1 # Comments: 0

articles._body: After New Orleans Pelicans executive vice president Joe Dumars defended his relatively dormant offseason , one insider believes he could be on the cusp of landing LA Clippers restricted free agent Bennedict Mathurin. The Pelicans signed back-up forward Trendon Watford to a one-year, $2.9 million contract last week, and are now reportedly focused on making another move. The post
articles._body: It has been a horrible season for the New York Mets. The team is in last place in the NL East and has been dealing with a rash of injuries. Juan Soto has been on the IL since the end of July , while Jorge Polanco, Mark Vientos, and Devin Williams have also been out. Now, there are some updates on the status of both Soto and Williams, per MLB.com. “Restarted a running program in mid-August but has been on a deliberate progression. Has vowed to return before the season ends and should have more than enough time to do so,” the update said about Soto. Soto has been out with a calf injury and has not played since July 24 against the Los Angeles Dodgers. He has played just 84 games this year, hitting .283. He has 21 home runs and 52 RBIs this year as well. He is expected to return at some point in September. “Began feeling arm fatigue early in August but did not receive an MRI until after an Aug. 7 outing. That test revealed a strain. Expects to return at some point in September but was not close as of a late August update,” the update on Williams said. Williams has been out since August 7. He has pitched in 42 games this year, going 3-2 with a 4.66 ERA. He also has 16 saves and just three blown saves. He is also expected to return in September. The Mets are 60-72 on the year , which places them last in the NL East and 17 games behind the Atlanta Braves. They are also 10.5 games out of a wild card spot. articles.title: Why NC State women’s soccer is off to its best start to season since 2013
articles.summary: NC State women’s soccer coach Gary Higgins sat in his office earlier this week with a smile on his face. Donning a black Wolfpack-branded hooded long-sleeve shirt and an Adidas hat, the second-year man in charge of rebuilding the program smiled as he compared the beginning of each season in Raleigh.
articles._body: NC State women’s soccer coach Gary Higgins sat in his office earlier this week with a smile on his face. Donning a black Wolfpack-branded hooded long-sleeve shirt and an Adidas hat, the second-year man in charge of rebuilding the program smiled as he compared the beginning of each season in Raleigh. “It’s a lot better than last year,” Higgins quipped in his native Scottish accent. “I can assure you.” Last fall, just seven months after being hired, it took the Pack eight games to record its first win after two draws and five losses. But this time around, there’s a different vibe around the team, one that has led to an unblemished 4-0 start for the first time since 2013.  Where has this hot start come from? Like anything, it takes a little bit of time for a new coach to install everything they’re looking for within the program. In Higgins’ case, it was a combination of working through growing pains last year, getting the team to believe it can win at a high level and most importantly, playing with confidence in the offensive third of the pitch.  The first two traits were things the Wolfpack worked through as last fall went along, eventually closing the season with four wins and two ties across the last nine games to build momentum for this season. But the offensive attack wasn’t exactly where he wanted it a year ago, which has since changed this fall. “That usually takes the longest,” Higgins said. “They understand our system of play and what we’re looking for offensively a lot more now. When you have that, you’re able to impose yourself onto teams a little bit more.” NC State has seen the fruits of its labor when it comes to putting pressure on opposing backlines this fall. The Wolfpack, which deploys a high-pressing attack, has outshot its opponents 90-37 with a plus-10 goal differential during the four-game winning streak with victories over James Madison, VCU, Charlotte and Elon.  Senior forward Jade Bordeleau , who emerged as the program’s star goal scorer with 10 last fall, has picked up right where she left off with four tallies on eight shots on frame this season. She’s playing with a sense of confidence that seemed to delight Higgins, who worked with her and the rest of the team on self-belief upon his arrival on campus a year and a half ago. But the biggest reason why Bordeleau has scored 20 percent of her career goals in the first four games of this season is because she doesn’t have the feeling that she has to do everything herself, Higgins believed.  “I think Jade would also be the first to tell you that she’s got some support acts that are teeing her up and taking some of that weight off her shoulders,” Higgins said. “When that happens, she has a bit more time, a bit more space and a bit more confidence in front of goal because she knows it doesn’t always have to come from her.” Senior forward Erica Roberts has been a key part of that as she’s hit her stride alongside Bordeleau, scoring two goals so far this season, after finding stability with the Wolfpack. Roberts previously played at Florida and East Carolina, while also dealing with injuries, but she’s now healthy and making a key impact on the offense. Freshmen Katie Richter and Madison Casteen have also provided a jolt to the forward group with one goal apiece to this point of their debut campaigns. In addition to the forwards around Bordeleau, NC State’s midfield has also several players that have taken the pressure off the top group with Mana Nakata , Fien Leijdekker and Daisy Duda all creating quality chances with a combined four assists. Higgins, who already installed a stubborn and suffocating defense last season, believes the new progress on the other end of the field has created a drive that can carry over into ACC play in the coming months. “I think if we continue that and understand the offensive principles more and more, then that’s a good recipe for success,” Higgins said. “I’d definitely say the biggest improvement and most-drastic change is the offensive principles and understanding what we’re looking for with our high press and trying to create as many chances as we can.” While the offensive style of play has improved, the Wolfpack has also taken a positive step when it comes to responding to adversity. Higgins had an early look at his team’s resiliency in the season opener at JMU, where NC State conceded a goal just 22 seconds after taking the lead on the Dukes’ home field after a mental lapse. Higgins, at the time, wasn’t sure how his squad would respond. Would they panic and let one error snowball into more than just one goal? Or would they hold steady and look to find the back of the net once again? Well, he was pleasantly surprised at what he saw in what turned into a 3-1 win over the same JMU squad that blanked NC State 3-0 in the season opener last fall. “Nothing changed. The people that were involved in the mistake kept on going and kept playing well, we kept creating chances, which we eventually took and won the game,” Higgins said. “That was a big moment for me in terms of, ‘OK, we’re on the right trajectory from a mindset standpoint.’” NC State has shown immense growth in the early stages of Higgins’ second season in Raleigh. There’s still plenty of season left to be played, including an entire ACC slate, but the Wolfpack is trending in the right direction with just one fewer win than it had all of last season. Higgins has been pleased with his team’s overall performance in each match so far this fall. The quality of play has been what he’s looked for, and though there’s still plenty to clean up moving forward, the second-year coach is looking to use the early-season success as a spark for the rest of the campaign. “Proud of the performances, it’s a good habit to get into and winning, but the thing you’re always worried about is complacency,” Higgins said. “We’re just making sure that it doesn’t creep in and try and take over this momentum that we’ve got.” After a

articles._body: Demarcus Deroche had to sit and watch from the sidelines for most of the offseason. The four-star Miami tight end commit suffered a leg injury early in the spring and showed up to his UM visits on crutches. Instead of taking part in camps and 7-on-7 events, Deroche was forced to go through a rigorous rehab process. “I hated it so much,” Deroche said. “I want to go as hard as I could, but my leg just wasn’t strong enough. Mentally, I had to get prepared.” Eventually, that rehab process got better. Deroche started moving around and doing light workouts before quickly accelerating into more advanced drills. The hard work during the process paid off. Deroche’s recovery timeline was quickly expedited, and he even got to take part in Under Armour’s S7VNS event in July. While Deroche still looked a bit limited at that showcase, he’s now fully healthy heading into his senior season with Fort Lauderdale (Fla.) Cardinal Gibbons. “I’m back after attacking rehab hard,” Deroche said. “I’m healing a lot faster than I should be. I’m good to play. I’m able to jump higher and run faster. Everything is really coming together. I’m ready to play.” Deroche competed in the Rivals Miami Camp in the winter before the injury and was considered a Top 300 prospect nationally. However, Deroche has fallen in the rankings across the board through the rehab process and is now a three-star recruit on Rivals. While most would feel they have something to prove, Deroche isn’t letting the rankings talk bother him. “I don’t really care about the rankings,” Deroche said. “I feel like I’ve improved a lot, and I’m ready to go to Miami.” Deroche has been committed to Miami for more than a year. He picked the Hurricanes last August over offers from Auburn, Florida, Texas and others. Some of those SEC schools continued to recruit Deroche, but he recently shut down his recruitment after his official visit this summer. “Miami is everything you could ever want,” Deroche said. “I’ll leave it at that.” A two-way standout, Deroche makes plays at the high school level at both tight end and EDGE. At 6-foot-6, 200 pounds, Deroche is an intriguing athlete with a basketball background. Miami prefers to have his skillset on the offensive side of the ball — and so does Deroche. “I feel like tight end is the best fit for me,” Deroche said. “I’m able to outjump safeties and run past linebackers. I don’t mind playing EDGE, but I’m committed to Miami as a tight end. That’s where I think I fit best. I like having the ball in my hands and making plays.” Deroche and Cardinal Gibbons opened the season with a 14-7 win over Miramar (Fla.) High. He finished the contest with three receptions for 47 yards. Deroche is looking to have an even better performance this week. After all, bragging rights will be on the line as Cardinal Gibbons takes on Hollywood (Fla.) McArthur, which is home to a pair of fellow Miami commits in defensive backs Jaylyn Jones and Sherrod Gourdine. “I’m excited to play them,” Deroche said. “That’s all we’ve been talking about. Those are my boys, but we’re in different jerseys. They’re family, but I have to treat them like the opponent. My prediction is a lot to a little. Of course, I’m going to score on them (laughs).”

articles.title: Researchers get two genetic codes to work at the same time
articles.summary: Messing with the genetic code might have gotten a bit easier to do.
articles._body: The genetic code is what life everywhere uses to convert the information contained in DNA into specific protein sequences. With minor variations, the same genetic code is used by every living thing on Earth, suggesting it was already present in the last common ancestor of all of them. It's not an easy thing to change, because so many things in every cell depend on it. Nevertheless, some preliminary steps have been taken. Researchers have managed to add some new amino acids to a bacterial cell and were able to make proteins that were one amino acid less than usual. But it's a slog; for some of this work, people have had to re-engineer every single gene in a bacterial genome. Now, researchers have found a way to operate two separate genetic codes simultaneously, avoiding the need to do any work to compensate for altering the code that every protein in a cell relies on. They didn't test it in an actual cell, and it might cause some problems there. But it's a creative solution that should accelerate some synthetic biology work. Read full article Comments

articles.title: A former SEC star has committed to play for St. John’s, Rick Pitino
articles.summary: Auburn star transfer Keyshawn Hall has committed to play for St. John's next season, but he's going to need some help to be ruled eligible.
articles._body: Auburn star transfer Keyshawn Hall has reportedly committed to play for St. John’s next season, but he’s going to need some help to be ruled eligible. Hall, who earned All-SEC Third Team honors with the Tigers in 2025-26, was originally granted a fifth year of college eligibility through an injunction in the Ohio lawsuit. However, the NCAA was recently granted a stay in that injunction, which now has Hall deemed ineligible. He and his team will continue working through legal options (much like the rest of these fifth-year players with eligibility concerns are doing) as he fights for another college season. If Hall ends up being granted a fifth year with St. John’s, he’ll be a massive addition for head coach Rick Pitino . The 6-foot-7 forward averaged 19.3 points, 7.1 rebounds, and 2.6 assists per outing at Auburn last season. He would fill the hole left in the wake of Donnie Freeman , who recently suffered a torn Achilles. Kentucky was reportedly in the mix for Hall before landing Missouri transfer Mark Mitchell . NEWS: Auburn transfer forward Keyshawn Hall has committed to St. John’s, he told @On3 . The 6-7 senior averaged 19.3 PTS, 7.1 REB, and 2.6 AST this past season, earning Third Team All-SEC honors. Hall played NBA Summer League with the Miami Heat. https://t.co/tHMG2OkH08 https://t.co/ZPM1dNyXHZ pic.twitter.com/QwRMYdROT7 — Joe Tipton (@JoeTipton) August 25, 2026 Hall’s situation isn’t too far different than that of Mitchell’s, although Mitchell was part of the Louisville court case that granted him an extra year. Hall has not joined one of those lawsuits at this time. Like Mitchell, Hall played in this year’s NBA Summer League, but did not officially sign his Exhibit 10 contract . The SEC is trying to complicate Mitchell’s situation even further , but Hall could have a cleaner path in the Big East (which has yet to bar professional athletes from returning to college) if he’s able to join one of these eligibility lawsuits. St. John’s will be Hall’s fifth school in as many years if he’s deemed eligible. He began his career at UNLV before stopping at George Mason, UCF, and then Auburn. He was named All-A-10 at George Mason and All-Big 12 at UCF.

articles.summary: The Houston Texans have talent all over their roster and loads of potential. The team has arguably the best defense in the NFL, headlined by a pass-rushing duo of Will Anderson and Danielle Hunter, along with one of the best cornerbacks in the league, Derek Stingley. All three players have a case
articles._body: The Houston Texans have talent all over their roster and loads of potential. The team has arguably the best defense in the NFL, headlined by a pass-rushing duo of Will Anderson and Danielle Hunter, along with one of the best cornerbacks in the league, Derek Stingley. All three players have a case as one of the 50 best players in the NFL . Houston also has C.J. Stroud leading the offense, a recent number two overall pick who was responsible for one of the greatest rookie seasons ever not that long ago. Unfortunately, a few things have held Houston back. For starters, they just can’t seem to buck the injury bug. Furthermore, the offensive line has stood out as a weak spot. Both of those factors look even worse now, as offseason addition Braden Smith was just carted off the field during a joint practice with the Carolina Panthers. The former Indianapolis Colts player signed for two years and $20 million, and he was slated to start at right tackle this season. Now, his immediate future is in doubt. Amazingly, during the same play, Ali Gaye also suffered a lower leg injury and was carted off with Smith, according to James Palmer. Houston’s bad injury luck continued just days after news broke that Jayden Higgins tore his ACL and will miss the entire season. The receiver from Iowa State was primed for a breakout sophomore season as a big-bodied target for Stroud. As of now, it is unclear what the extent of Smith and Gaye’s injuries are, but Texans’ fans will be holding their breath that an already unfortunate training camp won’t get too much worse. articles.title: Europe Set to Drop FIFA Boycott Ahead of Women’s U-20 World Cup
articles.summary: REUTERS/Zorana Jevtic
articles._body: UEFA is set to drop its boycott of all FIFA tournaments triggered by Gianni Infantino’s short-lived plan to sell stakes in the World Cup. Europe’s continental body first threatened to pull out of tournaments in the days following Infantino’s FIFA Forward Enterprise Proposal. But after Infantino called off the plan on July 31, UEFA said on Aug. 6 that it would still uphold the boycott because it had not received “assurances” that “such attempts to disfigure the game in this way will never be made again.” The Times and Sky Sports first reported Wednesday that UEFA will tell its member associations at a meeting in Monaco on Thursday that it received the promises it needed in order to call off the boycott. UEFA did not immediately respond to a Front Office Sports request for comment. The boycott wouldn’t have just applied to senior World Cups, but also youth tournaments. The first tournament caught in the crossfire was set to be the Women’s U-20 World Cup kicking off in Poland on Sept. 5. FIFA said in a statement that it is “pleased that all qualifying teams” will play in the Women’s U-20 tournament. “FIFA strongly believes that football has the power to unite, even in challenging circumstances,” a governing body spokesperson said. Even without the boycott, UEFA is still pushing hard for Infantino to step down. In an episode of The Rest is Politics podcast released Sunday , president Aleksander Ceferin said either Infantino steps down, or the opposition raises a candidate against him in the upcoming FIFA presidential elections next spring. “The governance at FIFA on paper is clear: FIFA Council decides the main things,” Ceferin said. “FIFA Congress decides, and things like that. The president cannot decide by himself. But you know, we have bad experience with this organization for 100 years already. All the time, there are some problems, some controversies. There are some people who feel like kings.” Ceferin and the presidents of the North American and Asian confederations published a joint letter condemning Infantino earlier this month, while individual national federations are increasingly making statements to reaffirm or withdraw their previous endorsement of Infantino. FIFA has a Nov. 18 deadline to submit a challenger against Infantino in March’s election. Ceferin said on The Rest is Politics that he doesn’t know who that person would be. CONCACAF president Victor Montagliani’s name has repeatedly come up, but he has not formally announced his candidacy. articles.title: Browns trade up with Dolphins for new QB at No. 1 in ESPN’s new 2027 mock draft
articles.summary: The Cleveland Browns face a crossroads before the 2026 season. Cleveland’s Deshaun Watson experiment is almost over, creating hope for the future of the organization. Many analysts expect the Browns will pick a new franchise quarterback during the 2027 NFL Draft. ESPN’s Jordan Reid pu
articles._body: The Cleveland Browns face a crossroads before the 2026 season. Cleveland’s Deshaun Watson experiment is almost over , creating hope for the future of the organization. Many analysts expect the Browns will pick a new franchise quarterback during the 2027 NFL Draft. ESPN’s Jordan Reid published a new 2027 mock draft on Wednesday with the 2026 NFL regular season just weeks away. Reid’s mock draft included a shocking trade involving the Browns. Cleveland trades up with Miami, surrendering pick No. 4 and No. 32 for the No. 1 overall selection. The Browns also cough up a 2027 fourth-round pick and a 2028 second-round pick to get the deal done. As a result, the Browns select Oregon’s Dante Moore as their next franchise quarterback . “I had the Dolphins trade out because they recently invested in Malik Willis. While a lot depends on Willis’ performance this season, Miami does already have a promising young quarterback,” Reid argued. “Unless Shedeur Sanders makes a massive leap in Year 2 (which seems unlikely), the Browns do not. Deshaun Watson’s contract ends after this season, as well, making this a perfect time for Cleveland to take another swing at that elusive franchise QB to join the young talent it has accumulated in the past couple drafts.” Browns fans might prefer Texas QB Arch Manning in this scenario, who goes off the board at No. 2 to the Cardinals. Meanwhile, the Dolphins scoop up Ohio State star Jeremiah Smith at No. 4. Still, Moore is a talented quarterback prospect who would be a big upgrade for Cleveland. “Moore has squeaky-clean mechanics, and his accuracy shined in his first year as a starter,” Reid added. “This would be a good situation for him, with young players he can grow alongside. If he brings his stellar college play to the NFL, the Browns could turn things around quickly.” Cleveland already had some young talent with Quinshon Judkins and Harold Fannin Jr. entering the offseason. But the Browns doubled down and added even more talent in the 2026 NFL Draft. It is exciting to think about what the future could hold for Cleveland. But it is still far too early to fall in love with a specific quarterback prospect. In the meantime, the Browns must prepare for their preseason finale against the Patriots on August 27th. articles._body: Luka Doncic and Austin Reaves went face-to-face during the latest gym reaction challenge that is making the rounds on social media. The Los Angeles Lakers superstar point guard was locked in against Reaves for a fun ‘hip, knees, head, feet’ challenge. The challenge was to grab the basketball elevated on cylindrical foam as soon as “hoop” was called from the background. While both of them had fast hand movements, Doncic proved to be the fastest and grabbed the ball just in time when the call was made . Luka vs. Reaves – who's got the faster reactions? (via: Luka Dončić/IG) pic.twitter.com/yDbwLwjwr9 — NBA (@NBA) August 25, 2026 The clip was also shared on Instagram, where Reaves hilariously commented that the video was AI-generated . However, this comes amid the Lakers having a great time building chemistry around new players. The whole team was in Slovenia for a four-day trip hosted by Doncic. The overseas outing included golfing, going kayaking, and meeting a local pediatric clinic. The Lakers headed back home with memories and a new understanding of player dynamics. The franchise will be building a new structure after LeBron James’ departure to the Philadelphia 76ers. Playing for eight seasons in LA, James helped the team win one NBA championship in 2020. Now that responsibility falls on Doncic to help the team win a ring. He is also seen as the next franchise cornerstone. During the 2025-26 NBA season, the Slovenian superstar averaged 33.5 points , 7.7 rebounds, and 8.3 assists in the 64 games he played, per Basketball Reference. He has gone through another transformation phase, as recent social media posts have had NBA fans reeling over the change in his physical appearance . With the 2026-27 season kicking off October 20th, LA fans will have many reasons to pack Crypto.com Arena.
