articles.title: Show HN: I built a tool showing how AI providers (should) throttle their models
articles.summary:
OP here: this project was born out of the frustration/paranoia that AI providers are throttling their models when their server load is too high. So, I set out to model and study the problem mathematically to understand what was happening, what I found was quite surprising.

The idea seems natur
articles._body: OP here: this project was born out of the frustration/paranoia that AI providers are throttling their models when their server load is too high. So, I set out to model and study the problem mathematically to understand what was happening, what I found was quite surprising. The idea seems natural: as the data center demand increases momentarily through the day, throttling their models (either using a quantized version, reducing the context window or lowering the tier of the model to a smaller one) seems appealing as the model in principle uses less electricity. The problem is that this can cause in fact the opposite effect: as users are trying to solve a question, if the AI gives a bad answer, the user is likely to keep re-asking. On the AI provider side this looks paradoxical: throttling to a lower model creates in fact more demand for their data center. This problem is even worse for agentic workflows, as these are more likely to create a re-ask storm, and maybe explains the outages and anecdotal experiences of users that feel the models are degraded. The model: I used mainly queueing theory arguments solving the optimal scheduling serving for an AI fleet with heterogeneous users. Insights: The industry standard practice of throttling once the number of users in system is in fact what’s causing the problem, the optimal rule implies separating users that won’t feel degradation as much with users that are very sensitive to it. Limitations: The visualization and paper examples are a toy example to illustrate the problem, only the providers have enough data to properly calibrate these instances. Technical Details: The visualization is around 100 lines of flask plus js frontend (LLM assisted with ground truth based on the original numerical example of the paper). Paper with proofs/theory: https://throttle.staffinganalytics.io/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49448480 Points: 1 # Comments: 0

articles._body: Former Duke basketball star Kyle Singler has recently taken social media by storm with a series of videos he has been posting on his Instagram account. In one of his videos, the former Detroit Pistons small forward made serious accusations against his former coach, Mike Krzyzewski. In his recent posts , Singler accused Coach K of mistreating him and “setting him up.” “I need this message to go out (to) as many people as possible,” Singler said. “Man, Coach K has set me up. I have no power, and I have no house. I’ve reached out to coach, and everyone has turned the other way. I’ve reached out to coach, and he has fully dismissed my message.” Can somebody please check on Kyler Singler? @okcthunder hopefully somebody can reach out and get him some help. pic.twitter.com/gLiJt3FBZd — Drew (Toxic I Guess) (@ThunderHusky17) August 26, 2026 Additionally, in his lengthy social media video, the former Duke star also detailed the struggles he has been going through in his daily life. He also accused people of breaking into his house and stealing some money. “You guys are cutting my power off, breaking into my house, stealing money, ruining my life. Reached out to Coach K, and all he did was sit me on the bench. Thanks, man, so this is what we’re doing at school- send people down, teaching them up.” “Well, I have more to say, and I (just) need this message to go out. Coach, where you at? Help ‘em brother out. Thought we were on the same team, man,” he later said in his plea for help. Singler played four seasons under Coach K from 2007 to 2011, where he helped the team win the 2010 NCAA championship. He also won the Final Four Most Outstanding Player award. After his phenomenal years coming out of Duke. He was drafted 33rd overall by the Pistons in the 2011 NBA Draft. However, this was not the first time Singler shared concerning videos through his social media account. Back in 2024, he also shared a series of posts detailing about fearing for his life . “I have been mistreated and abused, neglected, made into a mental example. And I fear for my life every day. And people in my community make me look out as if I’m going to be someone that’s going to be a problem and make things difficult for people when I’m only trying to be helpful,” he said via ABC11. A couple of NBA players, including Kevin Love , Isaiah Thomas, Chandler Parsons, and Andre Drummond, did reach out to him at that time. Love even tweeted about Singler and asked the basketball community to show him love . articles.title: Show HN: fake-bpy-module – Blender/UPBGE Python autocompletion for external IDEs
articles.summary: I wanted to share fake-bpy-module, a collection of fake Blender Python API stubs designed to enable code auto-completion and type hinting in external IDEs like VSCode. I have been maintaining this open-source project for over 8 years, tracking Blender's active ecosystem from Blender version 2.78
articles._body: I wanted to share fake-bpy-module, a collection of fake Blender Python API stubs designed to enable code auto-completion and type hinting in external IDEs like VSCode. I have been maintaining this open-source project for over 8 years, tracking Blender's active ecosystem from Blender version 2.78 to 5.2+. -- The Pain Point for Development in Blender Python -- Blender does not expose its Python API (bpy) as standard Python files outside of its built-in text editor. This makes add-on development in external IDEs tedious and prone to type errors. -- Solution & How it Works -- Instead of relying on the starndard inspect module which often fails to handle edge cases in Blender's dynamic environment. fake-bpy-module parses the official Blender Python API documentation to generate .pyi stub files. Of course, documentation parsing comes with its own challenges. Some APIs are undocumented, and others cannot be used as-is (such as the bpy_prop_collection class). To address this, the generator internally transforms and patches the types during the stub generation phase to ensure strict compatibility. -- Availability & Daily CI/CD -- The stubs are available via PyPI (ex. pip install fake-bpy-module-5.2) and support a wide range of Blender versions. The latest stubs based on the latest Blender code are also available (pip install fake-bpy-module). To realize this, our custom CI/CD system builds the Blender binary daily from the latest source code. -- Sub-project: fake-bge-module -- UPBGE is an open-source game engine fork based on Blender. I have also created a dedicated sub-project fake-bge-module, for the UPBGE Python API (bge). https://github.com/nutti/fake-bge-module I would love to hear your feedback on these tools! articles._body: Texas Tech’s second scrimmage of fall camp provided plenty of positives for head coach Joey McGuire and the Red Raiders as they continue preparing for the season opener against Abilene Christian. From an offensive line that took a significant step forward against a deep and talented defensive front to standout performances from Bryson Jones , Quinten Joyner , and AJ Holmes and the kicking game, McGuire saw encouraging signs throughout the roster. There are still areas Texas Tech needs to clean up, particularly with pre-snap penalties and overall game-day operations, but McGuire likes where his team stands as the Red Raiders move closer to Week 1. I thought in the scrimmage it was our best that we’ve looked in the offensive line,” McGuire said. “I thought we strained. I always stand back there by the quarterback, and so I can really feel the pocket, if it’s clean or he’s getting a little pressure or he’s going to get hit. And I thought that was, for the most part, really clean. “We gave up two sacks, one with the ones and I think one with the twos. But the one with the ones, I mean, it was long. We’ve got to get open. It was more that than the offensive line not picking up anything. So I think that was the biggest thing. You could really feel the offensive line take a big step against this defensive line.” Hunter Zambrano currently leading left guard competition One of the biggest position battles throughout fall camp has come at left guard between Hunter Zambrano and D’Anthis Upshaw . Both have continued to receive opportunities with the first-team offensive line throughout camp, but McGuire provided some clarity Tuesday on where the competition currently stands. “Yeah, I think if we played today, then it would be Hunter Zambrano,” McGuire said. “But they’re both – like all the reps today, Hunter and D’Ant took reps with the ones. But if we were playing today, right now, I would throw Hunter out there with the ones.” That doesn’t mean the competition is over. Upshaw continues to work with the first team and has put together a strong offseason after receiving praise from the coaching staff for his performance during spring practice and carrying that momentum into fall camp. With the season opener approaching, left guard remains one of the few starting positions along Texas Tech’s offense that is still being decided. McGuire pleased with Texas Tech’s effort and competitiveness Beyond individual performances, one of McGuire’s biggest takeaways from Saturday’s scrimmage was the overall effort and competitiveness of his team. Texas Tech is still primarily focused on itself as fall camp winds down, but preparation for Abilene Christian will begin to ramp up as the season opener approaches. The Red Raiders will also have the benefit of watching ACU open its season against Lamar this Saturday , giving the coaching staff a full game of film to evaluate before putting together its plan for the Wildcats in Week 1. For now, McGuire likes the effort he is seeing and remains particularly encouraged by the depth in the running back, tight end and defensive line rooms. “One, I love where we’re at,” McGuire said. “I think our guys are playing extremely hard. We’re not 100% and we’re not game planning. We’re playing against each other, so we’re not game planning for a team.” “We’re still working on ourselves, and so I thought the effort was high. Our guys are playing extremely hard. We’ve got a bunch of pleasers on this team, so they’re really trying to do their job. Again, I’m excited about the running back room, the tight end room, the defensive line room.” McGuire has also been pleased with Texas Tech’s kicking game, where Stone Harrington and Will Karoll have emerged as valuable weapons. “We’ve got a weapon in Stone, and we’ve got a weapon in Will Karoll,” McGuire said. “Nobody wants to see Will Karoll except holding. His mom wants to see him punt, but we don’t want to see him punt. But those guys, man, they really are weapons.” McGuire wants penalties cleaned up before Week 1 While McGuire came away pleased with much of what he saw Saturday, the Red Raiders weren’t as clean from a penalty standpoint as he would have liked. Texas Tech had Big 12 officials working both of its fall camp scrimmages, with McGuire asking the crews to officiate them as they would a conference game. After committing only three penalties in the first scrimmage, the Red Raiders saw that number increase Saturday. articles._body: Reports have recently surfaced suggesting The Rock vs. Roman Reigns isn’t happening at WWE WrestleMania 43 in 2027 , but they may share the ring sooner than that. On Tuesday, Aug. 25, 2026, WWE announced a new tryout in Honolulu, Hawaii, that will be held on Oct. 16 and 17. The poster features current Superstars and Bloodline members Reigns and The Usos (Jey and Jimmy). It also features The Rock in the middle of them. Do you have what it takes? We are searching for our next Superstar in Hawaii! LEARN MORE https://t.co/Gnmqw0D55M pic.twitter.com/aX46gJMLJB — WWE (@WWE) August 25, 2026 Of course, The Rock, whose real name is Dwayne Johnson, is on the board of directors of TKO Group Holdings — UFC and WWE’s parent company. Perhaps he wants to be hands-on with the tryouts as part of the board. Additionally, like the other Bloodline members that will be there, he is part of the legendary Anoa’i family. Is there a chance Reigns and The Rock cross paths and set up a WrestleMania 43 dream match? It’s possible, but it remains to be seen if the “Final Boss” or Dwayne Johnson is showing up to the tryout. Will WWE dream match The Rock vs. Roman Reigns finally happen? Joe Camporeale-Imagn Images. For years, WWE has been teasing a dream match between The Rock and Reigns. It is perhaps the final dream match both men have yet to work. However, the stars have never aligned. It appeared The Rock was going to challenge Reigns for the Undisputed WWE Championship at WrestleMania 40 in 2024. He was set to leapfrog Cody Rhodes, who won the Royal Rumble, to face the “Tribal Chief.” This caused a revolt among fans. Instead, The Rock turned heel and joined the Bloodline, creating the “Final Boss” persona. The “Final Boss” and the “Tribal Chief” joined forces to take on Rhodes and Seth Rollins in the main event of Night 1 of WrestleMania 40. The following night, The Rock reemerged to try to help Reigns retain his championship against the “American Nightmare.” His efforts were for naught, as the “Tribal Chief’s” 1,316-day reign was ended by Rhodes. articles.title: Taylor Momsen Joining Soundgarden For Halftime Show at Seattle Seahawks Season Opener
articles.summary: The band will perform at for the Super Bowl champs' home game against the New England Patriots at Lumen Field on Sept. 9.
articles._body: Soundgarden will take the stage for their hometown team the Seattle Seahawks’ NFC West season home opener next month with a very special guest vocalist. The group will be joined by Pretty Reckless singer Taylor Momsen for a halftime show performance during a rematch with their vanquished Super Bowl LX foes the New England Patriots on Sept. 9. The reigning NFL champs will be saluted by the “Black Hole Sun” icons, who will also perform at Lumen Field with one of their grunge compatriots, Pearl Jam guitarist Mike McCready, who will play the National Anthem before the game on behalf of the Washington Innocence Project . It’s a return engagement for Momsen, who has played with the band a number of times since the death of singer Chris Cornell in May 2017 at age 52. In November of last year, Momsen subbed in for Cornell at Soundgarden’s Rock & Roll Hall of Fame induction, performing their hits “Rusty Cage” and “Black Hole Sun.” She previously sat in with them at the “ I Am the Highway: A Tribute to Chris Cornell ” benefit in January 2019 at the Forum in Los Angeles. A promo picture (see below) announcing the halftime show featured guitarist Kim Thayil, drummer Matt Cameron and bassist Ben Shepherd posing alongside Momsen and McCready. In addition to the all-star hometown rock tribute, the Seahawks announced a pregame Salute 250 Kickoff Concert featuring Luke Bryan, which will take place at 2:30 p.m. PT, three hours before kick-off. Soundgarden recently revealed that they are mixing an album featuring the final group of songs recorded with Cornell . Drummer Cameron said the surviving members are in the process of mixing tracks recorded with producer Terry Date for what is planned as an eight-track LP. He said the songs are based on demos the group’s members began working on in 2013 and 2014 and then again in 2015 and 2016 before what would be their final tour with Cornell in 2017. articles.title: Giants’ Calvin Austin III done for season with his ‘serious knee injury’
articles.summary: Calvin Austin III’s first season with the New York Giants has ended before it even started after suffering a knee injury in training camp on Tuesday. Austin was carted off the field after sustaining the non-contact injury during a one-on-one drill with Deonte Banks. On Wednesday, ESPN’
articles._body: Calvin Austin III’s first season with the New York Giants has ended before it even started after suffering a knee injury in training camp on Tuesday. Austin was carted off the field after sustaining the non-contact injury during a one-on-one drill with Deonte Banks. On Wednesday, ESPN’s Jordan Raanan reported that the fifth-year wide receiver is out for the season . “Calvin Austin’s ‘serious knee injury’ will keep him out for the season, per source. An unfortunate blow for the Giants slot receiver. He was going to play a significant role this season,” wrote Raanan on X. Austin signed with the Giants in March on a one-year contract worth $4.5 million after spending his first four seasons with the Pittsburgh Steelers. The 27-year-old Austin suited up in New York’s victory over the Miami Dolphins, 26-3, in the preseason at Hard Rock Stadium on Saturday, tallying two receptions for 24 yards. He did not play in their loss to the Minnesota Vikings, 13-10, at MetLife Stadium last week. It is the second time Austin will sit out an entire campaign after being sidelined by a foot injury in his rookie year. He was drafted by the Steelers in the fourth round in 2022. Austin was expected to start for the Giants alongside Malik Nabers and Darius Slayton. With his season-ending injury, his spot will likely go to Odell Beckham Jr. , who returned to New York in June after his one-year stop with the Miami Dolphins. Last season, Austin logged 31 receptions for 372 yards and three touchdowns in 14 games. articles.summary: After several months of rumors and speculation, Tyson Fury vs. Anthony Joshua has finally signed the contract for their fight. The two heavyweights are set to clash head-to-head in arguably one of the biggest fights in British boxing history later this year. However, months before their rumored f
articles._body: After several months of rumors and speculation, Tyson Fury vs. Anthony Joshua has finally signed the contract for their fight. The two heavyweights are set to clash head-to-head in arguably one of the biggest fights in British boxing history later this year. However, months before their rumored fight in Nov. 2026, boxing legend Mike Tyson addressed the bout and claimed that he could miss out on it . Previously reported by the Daily Mail, Joshua and Fury are said to have signed contracts to fight on Nov. 20, 2026, in New York City. But the news that the fight wouldn’t take place in Britain sparked a strong reaction. Recently, Fury announced in an explosive rant that the fight “doesn’t look like it’s going to happen,” criticizing his rival and accusing Joshua’s ‘money-thirsty’ promoter, Eddie Hearn. However, it did not sit well with boxing legend Mike Tyson, who believes the fight should take place in the UK. ‘It’s going to be a great fight, it’s going to be great for boxing… even though I can’t go – I’m barred from London – I think London should get the fight,’ said Tyson to the Daily Mail. Unfortunately, Tyson is blocked from visiting the UK due to his criminal history. “They’re both English and if they come here, all the English people are going to come anyway. So you’re home already, let’s do it there! Everybody that [wants] to be there, they’re going to come to the United States – it’s going to be full of English people. It’s just going to be just like it is over there. There ain’t going to be many Americans there because they’ll sell it out. All the English – very few Americans – sold it out when I fought Frank Bruno [twice in Las Vegas],” Tyson said. “Iron” Mike Tyson was jailed for rape in 1992 and has also been convicted of assault, cocaine possession and driving under the influence. articles.title: The Download: the Kids issue arrives, and Bill Gates reveals his AI fears
articles.summary: This is today’s edition of The Download, our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology. Introducing: the Kids issue If the desire to limit kids’ use of technology was once a subcurrent, it has become a raging flood. Countries around
articles._body: This is today’s edition of The Download , our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology. Introducing: the Kids issue If the desire to limit kids’ use of technology was once a subcurrent, it has become a raging flood. Countries around the world are banning children from social media. Schools across the US are ditching iPads and Chromebooks for actual books. Kids themselves seem to be embracing this tech skepticism too: the hottest gadget for Gen Alpha is a vintage Sony Walkman. A surprising—maybe troubling—number of people who work in big tech also keep their kids at arm’s distance from technology. They lock down their phones, if they have phones at all, and keep them off social media. Hell, even Mark Zuckerberg doesn’t publicly post his children’s faces on Facebook or Instagram. Yet there is no hiding from technology. It permeates nearly everything, everywhere. We have to prepare our children to live in the actual world we have actually created, not the one we wish we had. How can we help kids survive and thrive in what we have wrought? That’s what the new Kids issue of MIT Technology Review is all about. With the help of the editors of Anyway , a fantastic magazine for teens and tweens, we explore how young people really feel about AI , the support networks helping kids through the polycrisis , and what happens when a child’s robot best friend dies . We also ask why kids outlearn AI , whether monitoring apps are really keeping children safe online , how schools can encourage smarter AI use , and what happens when technology begins to reshape childhood itself, courtesy of exclusive new fiction from author and AI ethicist Jenny Williams. Together, these stories examine how childhood is changing in an age of AI—and how we can help kids navigate the world we’ve made. Subscribe now to read the print issue in full. Bill Gates says we’ve passed AI’s danger thresholds. Now what? —Mat Honan It’s a glorious day in Kirkland, Washington, an affluent Seattle suburb on the eastern shore of Lake Washington. The temperature is in the mid-80s, the sky is incapable of being any more blue, and the view is gorgeous. And vaguely terrifying. Because if the scene is placid, the messenger is not. Seated across from me at a conference room table, Bill Gates is rocking back and forth in his chair. And the more he has to say—about the threats of terror or economic collapse or just losing control of our AI systems—the more agitated I find myself becoming, too. The philanthropist and former Microsoft CEO says he has been growing increasingly alarmed by the rate at which AI technology is advancing, especially since guardrails are not keeping pace. “We’ve crossed the threshold in terms of [AI’s] bio-capabilities, cyber-capabilities, psychosocial capabilities, job-market-destruction capabilities, and even the lack of control,” he said. “I’m just stunned at the lack of concern and discussion outside of the industry.” Read the full interview with Bill Gates about the AI risks he says we’ve already crossed—and what we should do now . The must-reads I’ve combed the internet to find you today’s most fun/important/scary/fascinating stories about technology. 1 Trump’s EPA aims to exempt data centers from disclosing air pollution The EPA would also remove requirements for public input. ( NYT $) + The move is likely intended to curb criticism and oversight. ( Guardian ) + Texas’s attorney general has joined the data-center backlash. ( WP $) + We did the math on AI’s energy footprint. ( MIT Technology Review ) 2 SpaceX plans $100 billion launch site in Louisiana—its largest yet Construction of the “Starbase, Louisiana” project is due to start next year. ( BBC ) + It would be SpaceX’s second private launch site, after the original Starbase. ( NYT $) + The company said it will “support thousands of launches” annually. ( CNBC ) + But it’s cutting launches from Florida until Starship arrives. ( Ars Technica ) 3 China’s Z.AI has confirmed it’s behind the mystery AI model Ox Alpha The model has surged to the top of online usage charts. ( Bloomberg $) + China’s Moonshot is discussing a landmark deal with US hyperscalers. ( Reuters $) + Here’s what’s next for Chinese open-source AI. ( MIT Technology Review ) 4 Meta is discussing a settlement in its landmark teen-addiction trial The case involves 29 states seeking penalties and changes. ( Reuters $) + A loss at trial could saddle Meta with $1.4 trillion in penalties. ( Bloomberg $) 5 Huawei wants to build data centers in Egypt The US is alarmed and is preparing a counteroffer. ( Bloomberg $) + HP has signed a licensing deal for Huawei WiFi tech. ( CNBC ) 6 Trump is upping the price of Big Tech’s favorite visa He’s implementing a fee of over $103,000 on H-1B visas . ( Verge ) + His immigration policies are hurting young researchers. ( MIT Technology Review ) 7 Beijing fears that AI companions are replacing human intimacy New rules aim to limit emotional dependence on chatbots. ( Guardian ) + It’s surprisingly easy to fall for a chatbot. ( MIT Technology Review ) 8 Israel is running a synthetic think tank to influence AI search results It’s using AI-generated content to shape chatbot responses. ( 404 Media ) 9 Physicists are closing in on a way to test string theory A proposed dark dimension could be detectable within five years. ( Economist $) 10 AI music has been barred from the Australian charts, thanks to Madonna An AI-assisted cover of “Like a Prayer” helped prompt the ban. ( Reuters $) Quote of the day “ It is such an Orwellian technology being utilized by such comic book villain forces of evil trying to do dastardly things.”  —Anthony Ralphs, an events producer who dressed up as Darth Vader to ironically praise Flock at a San Diego City Council meeting, tells 404 Media why he sees parallels between the Dark Lord and the surveillance firm. articles.title: Taylor Swift pens emotional tribute to Dolly Parton after tragic death
articles.summary: The news of Dolly Parton’s death shocked the world on Aug. 25, 2026, and singer-songwriter Taylor Swift, who started her career in the country music genre, paid tribute to the late icon after she passed away. She issued a statement to People in the wake of Parton’s passing. Swift said
articles._body: The news of Dolly Parton’s death shocked the world on Aug. 25, 2026, and singer-songwriter Taylor Swift , who started her career in the country music genre, paid tribute to the late icon after she passed away. She issued a statement to People in the wake of Parton’s passing. Swift said that “a world without Dolly doesn’t feel possible, real, or right.” She then discussed the legacy Parton leaves behind. “But because of the eternally generous way she spent her time on this earth and the countless lives she changed for the better, her legacy will be an everlasting one,” she wrote. “Dolly gave us someone to look up to while encouraging us to be who we are as individuals.” Swift continued by praising how Parton “managed to give the world the ultimate mystery and fantasy in some corners of her life, but to give full transparency in the ways that counted. Somehow she was true grace and true grit, all in one dazzling person. She possessed the softest heart when it came to the struggles of others, and a backbone of steel to defend her own self worth as an artist.” The “Cruel Summer” is a fan first, and she’s “grateful” for her fandom. Parton served as a beacon of hope for aspiring artists like Swift. Parton’s nephew, Bryan Seaver, announced her passing on Tuesday, Aug. 25. According to People, her reps confirmed that she died after a “brief battle with cancer.” “My name is Brin Seaver, son of Cassie Parton, and I’m representing the Parton and Owens family today announcing the passing of my aunt, Dolly Rebecca Parton Dean, Sister, Sis, and Granny to one generation and Gigi to the next,” her nephew said. “This video announcement is something Dolly asked of me years ago, before I fully absorbed it as a future reality. “As her head of security for more than two decades, a role my father Larry held before me, I have imagined the heaviness of this moment but haven’t truly felt it until now,” he continued. articles.title: ‘She Might Be The Last American That Everyone Liked’: Jelly Roll Pays Tribute to Dolly Parton
articles.summary: “She was infinitely talented. She was relentlessly funny and adored by all. She might be the last American that everyone liked."
articles._body: Dolly Parton had it all. Talent, humor, an entrepreneurial spirit. A great, pounding heart. And she represented her homeland quite like no one else. For his second night hosting ABC’s Jimmy Kimmel Live , Jelly Roll had the difficult task of paying tribute to the legendary singer, songwriter and entertainer, and touching on those many things that made her unique. And completing his task without bursting into tears. “We lost a legend today, the great Dolly Parton,” he said at the top, during the monologue, staring down the barrel of the camera. “She was such an inspiration to so many, myself included. We’re both from Tennessee and she meant a lot to my family, y’all.” Parton’s influence on a young Jelly Roll (real name: Jason DeFord) was profound. “We used to sit around the kitchen table and listen to her music together as a family. I’ll never forget it,” he recalled. “I learned so much from Dolly over the years, about songwriting, how to handle this crazy business, and how to support your community.” Dolly was a one-off, and someone we could all be proud of. “She was infinitely talented. She was relentlessly funny and adored by all. She might be the last American that everyone liked,” he recalled. “We will miss her dearly. Rest in peace, Dolly. We will always love you.” Parton died Tuesday at age 80 following “a brief battle with cancer,” according to a statement released by her team. Parton died at Vanderbilt-Ingram Cancer Center in Nashville. With a career spanning more than 60 years, Parton has been one of country music’s leading lights, one of the genre’s most revered and prolific songwriters. She’s a member of both the Country Music Hall of Fame and Rock And Roll Hall of Fame, she wrote more than 3,000 and  placed 113 tunes on  Billboard ’s Hot Country Songs  chart starting in 1967. Cumulatively, those hits spent more than 28 years on the chart. Watch Jelly Roll’s tribute to Dolly Parton below.

articles.title: Unrivaled Valued at $650M After Latest Funding Round, Players Own 30%
articles.summary: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images
articles._body: Unrivaled, the 3-on-3 women’s basketball league that launched in 2025, announced a Series C funding round Tuesday, securing more than $100 million in funding that values the league at $650 million. The league has nearly doubled its valuation in a year; it was valued at $340 million in September after closing a series B funding round. The fundraising around was led by Ten Pillars Sports Fund, backed by UC Investments, and also included reinvestments from notable sports figures Carmelo Anthony, Geno Auriemma, Trae Young, Alex Morgan, and Trybe Ventures. In comparison, the Connecticut Sun, the most recent WNBA franchise sold, was purchased for $300 million earlier this year . The Golden State Valkyries are the highest-valued WNBA team at $1 billion, according to CNBC projects released in May. “I think this is a testament to how quickly the space is evolving and growing, but also to the incredible foundation that we’ve built,” Unrivaled co-founder Alex Bazzell told Front Office Sports . Bazzell co-founded the league with WNBA stars Breanna Stewart and Napheesa Collier, who is also his wife. Unrivaled also announced that the portion of the company owned by players is valued at nearly $200 million, about 30% of the company. The league says the player equity pool has increased 550% since it was launched. Unrivaled has been positioned as a player-driven league since its launch , guaranteeing six-figure salaries for all players (when the WNBA minimum was under $70,000) and offering equity stakes in the league. Bazzell did not share the precise number of players with equity in the league, but said that all 36 players who signed in the first season received an ownership stake, and that “at least 95% of our players are a part of this in at least some way, shape, or form.” He said every player was offered equity, and those that don’t currently have a stake chose to be paid more instead. “Some still value cash a little bit more than equity—there’s always that exchange between agents,” Bazzell said. “But I’m really proud of the fact that these players get to learn what it means to be an owner and inevitably make money during their sleep and when they’re in their offseason, or when they’re with the WNBA.” The terms of players’ equity stake is similar to that of traditional startups. Bazzell said all players’ stake has a four-year vesting period, and those who left the league before the four years (like Sabrina Ionescu, who only played in Unrivaled’s inaugural season) can choose what to do with the amount of equity earned. “If they didn’t stay for a certain time period, they wouldn’t vest the remaining amount, but they’ve still earned you know one year’s worth or two years’ worth of that equity,” Bazzell said. “And then for us, we have the optionality if we want to buy them out or if we want to continue to let them grow with the value of the business.” After a successful first season, Unrivaled saw its TV ratings dip in its second year. But the league, which plays most of its games at the 1,000-seat Sephora Arena in Miami, saw growth from two soldout tour stops at NBA arenas in Brooklyn and Philadelphia. It’s planning around eight tour stops in 2027. Bazzell also said Unrivaled will move out of Sephora Arena by 2028, saying they’ve “outgrown” the venue and will make more announcements in the coming months on their plans. He guaranteed that they will move to a larger venue, but said they want to continue providing an “intimate” experience for the fans. He said Unrivaled will not aim for an NBA-size arena as its home, instead looking for an venue that can fit 2,500 to 4,000 fans. “We’ll always have a one-singular arena for us, call it home arena, for us, while still integrating our tour model,” Bazzell said. Unrivaled will not be the only professional women’s basketball league with WNBA stars playing this coming winter as Project B, a new global basketball league co-founded by former WNBA star Alana Beard, is planning to launch in January. The league is scheduled to run around the same time period as Unrivaled, and has signed WNBA stars like Nneka Ogwumike and Jonquel Jones, as well as former Unrivaled players Kelsey Mitchell and Alana Smith. Bazzell said he doesn’t “put a lot of focus” into Project B, despite acknowledging that they have signed a “few solid players,” because Unrivaled has already signed most of its roster for the next two to three seasons. The league says they have signed more than 90% of their players for the 2027 season, including recent announcements Olivia Miles and Gabby Williams . He also said that Project B is focused on international play while Unrivaled’s competition is domestic. “I don’t think we’re at the point of maybe jockeying for positions as much as people would think,” Bazzell said. The post Unrivaled Valued at $650M After Latest Funding Round, Players Own 30% appeared first on Front Office Sports .

articles.title: Exclusive: Jamie Hayter believes AEW Women’s wrestling has evolved but it’s not enough
articles.summary: With just days left for AEW All In 2026 in London, British wrestling sensation and former Women’s World Champion Jamie Hayter appeared for an exclusive interview with Clutchpoints. All geared up for her tag title match against Megan Bayne and Lena Kross, Hayter is now hopeful to bring it ho
articles._body: With just days left for AEW All In 2026 in London, British wrestling sensation and former Women’s World Champion Jamie Hayter appeared for an exclusive interview with Clutchpoints. All geared up for her tag title match against Megan Bayne and Lena Kross, Hayter is now hopeful to bring it home with Alex Windsor. While England failed to win the FIFA World Cup this year and bring it home, Hayter is positive about Windsor, Will Ospreay, and her efforts. “ Of course, absolutely. This is the year it’s coming home. This is the year it’s coming home, and we’re gonna be the ones to facilitate that for everybody else. Of course. I hope so, anyway. I’m manifesting it,’ Hayter claimed, although she began the answer by first booing the English team. While Hayter and Windsor pursue the Tag titles, Mercedes Moné will be chasing Willow Nightingale’s AEW Women’s World title. Featuring a card of nine matches, where only two matches have been dedicated to the women, Hayter was asked about the evolution of AEW’s women’s division. When Hayter began her journey her All Elite journey, the roster was mostly Britt Baker, Hikaru Shida, Riho, Emi Sakura, and more. However, over the years, the roster has expanded and now boasts the likes of Moné, Nightingale, Toni Storm, Kris Statlander, and many more. “I think there definitely has been an evolution to the division. I think it’s been an incredibly slow process, though. I think it’s only really been the last few years. Well, I don’t know; it’s just been up and down. It’s hard to compare it to before because before there ‌were some positive things about when it first started and some negative things, and you can really say the same about now. Like, I’m always gonna be a champion for women having more time, women getting more opportunities, main eventing, this, that, and the other. “Like, I’m always gonna champion that, and it’s certainly happened; more of that has happened, but it’s never enough. So I think, like, and that’s like across the board in like women’s wrestling, women’s sport as a whole. There are definitely changes, but improvements, but they’re not good enough for me to be like, ‘It’s amazing. It’s really, really good.’ It’s okay. And that’s not just AEW specific. Again, it’s just very much how my thoughts and feelings towards women in sport in general and from my own experiences as well,” Hayter shared. Jamie Hayter feels proud of her good working relationship with her AEW boss, Tony Khan Doug Engle/Florida Times-Union Not everyone can say that they share a good working relationship with their boss , but Jamie Hayter can. “ It’s great. ‌I haven’t worked too closely with Tony [Khan] on so much stuff. But I really enjoy his passion, and everyone says it, and it’s just true. There’s really no other way to describe him as passionate as he is. And he just loves wrestling. He really cares about the talent. “I’ve always had such good conversations with Tony. I like him as a person, which, how many people can say that about their boss? That they, like, really like them, you know? And they think they’re overall, like, a great person. And they just‌ want the best for everyone. They want everyone to succeed, and that’s what it is,” Hayter further added. “So it’s‌ been really good. Like, I mean, I couldn’t really ask for anyone better to work under, to be honest with you. And that, that’s just from my experiences. I couldn’t really say enough positive things about that and about my experiences with him. So yeah, it’s been really good. Really, really good,” she finished. Sharing a positive rapport with Tony Khan, Hayter signed with the promotion in 2021 after first wrestling there in 2019. When asked what motivated her actions, she said, ”Honestly, from the two experiences that‌ I had in 2019, I just really liked it. I liked the people there. I liked the atmosphere. When I was backstage, everyone was very friendly, very supportive, and that was kind of ‌the case even when I left for a while, and you know, obviously the pandemic happened. “You didn’t really do that much travel. But I still stayed in contact with them, like, throughout, and you know, AEW was still interested in me at that time as well. So I just knew I wanted to go there. I was holding out hope that the pandemic wouldn’t last forever because, yeah, I don’t really think I could have seen myself really go anywhere else at that point. “I loved what I was doing in Japan, of course, but I wanted to try something else, and I had a really good relationship. I honestly wouldn’t‌ have done it any other way. I’m glad how it all happened, how it panned out, and what’s kind of come from that,” she finished. Jamie Hayter believes AEW has the best women’s division Jerome Miron-Imagn Images Sharing a positive mentality about different wrestling promotions, Hayter claimed that while most of the other promotions have a good women’s division, AEW has the best one. “Oh, that’s so hard but the best, obviously. Number one. If I didn’t say number one, I wouldn’t be a good representative of the girls. I really think we have a great division. Of course, like‌ all the other divisions, there are so many fantastic women’s wrestlers within them. “I think it’s so hard. Of course you want, you want your team to be the best. But I just think in general there’s, across all, across the board in every way you just said, so much talent. And it’s‌ good that it’s a nice spread of talent across every single company. So you can really just watch good women’s wrestling wherever you wanna check it out,” she finished.

articles.title: Show HN: DBLift – database migration management for Python teams
articles.summary:
I’ve been working for a while on DBLift, an open-source database migration toolkit for Python teams. DBLift follows the same model flyway does with the same main commands and the same history table structure making it easy to switch from one to the other with the import_flyway command.

By defau
articles._body: I’ve been working for a while on DBLift, an open-source database migration toolkit for Python teams. DBLift follows the same model flyway does with the same main commands and the same history table structure making it easy to switch from one to the other with the import_flyway command. By default DBLift is out of order meaning that any unapplied migration is eligible to be applied contrary to flyway which refuse to apply any migration with a lower version until you force it. You can still apply the original flyway model you can still opt-in with the —strict flag. https://docs.dblift.com/migrations-versioning The main difference is the runtime, No JVM. If you already work in python DBLift integrates with your existing tooling: pip, sqlalchemy, Django, Flask… Honest feedback welcome — especially if you're currently using Flyway on a Python project and it works fine, I'd like to understand what I'm missing. GitHub: https://github.com/dblift/dblift Docs: https://docs.dblift.com Move from Flyway: https://docs.dblift.com/move-from-flyway Supported databases: https://docs.dblift.com/supported-databases Ordering: https://docs.dblift.com/migrations-versioning Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49447202 Points: 2 # Comments: 0

articles.title: Show HN: Typebase – A single-folder back end you write in TypeScript
articles.summary:
Hey HN!

I built Typebase, a library that gives you Convex's DX with Supabase's openness.

After trying Supabase I liked how fast it is to spin up a DB and auth, but really didn't like using RLS and SQL for authorization. With Convex I loved how your server "lives" in your code, but disliked th
articles._body: Hey HN! I built Typebase, a library that gives you Convex's DX with Supabase's openness. After trying Supabase I liked how fast it is to spin up a DB and auth, but really didn't like using RLS and SQL for authorization. With Convex I loved how your server "lives" in your code, but disliked the DB model and the realtime-first defaults. With Typebase you just write TS files inside a typebase/ folder in your existing repo. You can define your DB tables inside a schema.ts file and export server functions that your frontend calls like local functions, fully typed. Auth is built in. Then one CLI command uploads your server to any of the available providers (Vercel, Cloudflare Workers or Deno Deploy for the servera and Neon for the DB), or generates the code so you can deploy it wherever you want. Built on top of oRPC, Drizzle, and better-auth. Happy to answer any questions or feedback! Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49447178 Points: 1 # Comments: 0

articles.title: Xtracycle's Swoop ASM e-bike brings an automatic transmission to cargo bikes
articles.summary: A steel frame cargo bike with a unique twist: You can let it choose your gear.
articles._body: The Velotric Discover M e-bike we reviewed earlier this year had a feature I found somewhat annoying: It would sporadically block much of the display with an alert telling me I should be in a different gear. While the implementation bugged me, the concept made a certain degree of sense; most e-bikes now know your cadence, how much torque you're generating, and how that power is being translated into speed. That's everything you need to know to determine an optimal gear. Somewhere in the back of my mind, I thought, "If you're so smart, why don't you just shift for me?" I was completely unaware that Shimano had already developed a system that did exactly that. And for the past few weeks, I've been using it on a $4,500 cargo bike from Xtracycle called the Swoop ASM that let me see what it's like to hand control of my gears to an electronic brain. articles.title: Deshaun Watson Has Done the Impossible: Unite Browns Fans
articles.summary: Scott Galvin-USA TODAY Sports
articles._body: CLEVELAND — Anthony Lima knows better than most that consensus among Browns fans is rare. A longtime radio host and media personality in his native northeast Ohio, the cohost of The Ken Carman Show with Anthony Lima has spent the last 15 years starting and fighting in arguments focused on a litany of Cleveland football figures. Typically, these debates follow the same format. A portion of the fan base champions the player/coach/executive du jour, while the other side is ready to move on. The exercise is tailor made for a quarterback-starved city like Cleveland: Brandon Weeden, Brian Hoyer, DeShone Kizer, and Baker Mayfield have all received such treatment during Lima’s time at 92.3 The Fan. Even Johnny Manziel had his share of supporters. The reaction to Monday’s announcement that the Browns have named Deshaun Watson as their starting quarterback less than 48 hours after he publicly clashed with fans who booed him during the team’s preseason loss to the Bills, however, has been different. For once, Cleveland fans appear to be aligned: They don’t want Watson as their starting quarterback. “I can’t remember anything like this,” Lima told Front Office Sports on Monday morning. “Like, yeah, fans were against Dwayne Bowe and Kenny Britt towards the end, but that’s normal stuff. Every NFL team has a villain that they can’t believe they’re paying. But this is insanity. “I said today, they were like Toledo —they were a test market for all the crazy stuff that could possibly happen in the NFL. And I did not think when I got up on Saturday morning, we were gonna have another shining example of things that have gone wrong for the Cleveland Browns organization.” Lima’s sentiments were echoed on social media throughout Monday, as several NFL media personalities weighed in with their own negative reactions to the Browns’ announcement. ESPN’s Dan Orlovsky called for a boycott of the team . Mina Kimes noted the moral dilemma the franchise has placed its fan base in for the past half-decade . Kyle Brandt tried to make sense of Browns owner Jimmy Haslam calling the trade for Watson a “big swing-and-miss” 17 months before he was once again named the team’s starting quarterback. “Browns fans I don’t know how you do it,” Brandt posted . Brandt’s statement appeared to be rhetorical. But if he’s looking for an answer, it appears to be “with a lot of frustration.” ‘It takes a lot to have the entire Browns fandom against you’ Outside Huntington Bank Field on Tuesday morning somebody taped multiple signs to a statue of Jim Brown denouncing Watson . The act of amateur vandalism may have been carried out by just one person. But it also fit right in alongside the overwhelming reaction on social media, as well as several fans FOS spoke with Monday. Chris McNeil, who runs the popular REFLOG18 social media account, told FOS that it was the angriest Browns fans had been since Art Modell moved the team to Baltimore in 1996. “It’s back to the ‘ Jump Art ’ days, where people are now galvanized against Deshaun Watson,” McNeil said. “It takes a lot to have the entire Browns fandom against you. But Deshaun Watson’s played himself into that unique position.” People taking to the streets in Cleveland pic.twitter.com/I8kk97e7j6 — McNeil (@REFLOG18) August 25, 2026 This isn’t the first time that Browns fans have clashed with their favorite team, especially since Haslam bought the team in 2012. In January 2018, McNeil famously organized a parody “Perfect Season Parade” that was attended by a few thousand fans, making good on his promise to do so if the team ever went winless for a whole season, as it managed to do in 2017. Ken Blaze-Imagn Images This being the Browns, even their losing was the subject of explosive allegations. Hue Jackson, who went 1–31 as Browns coach over 2016 and 2017, alleged in 2022 that Haslam offered him millions of dollars in bonuses in order to lose games and improve the team’s draft position. Haslam called Jackson’s account an “absolute falsehood.” Browns Baggage By this point, Cleveland fans’ frustration with losing seasons, missed draft picks, and a revolving door of head coaches has been well documented . But there’s something about the entire Watson situation that seems nastier than usual. “I’ve put up with bad football before this, but it never felt malicious. It just felt like they were too dumb to get out of their own way,” Ethan Moses, whose family recently canceled their four-pack of season tickets, told FOS . “This feels like they don’t give a shit about any of the fans.” A big part of that appears to be tied to the circumstances in which the Browns first acquired Watson, who was facing more than 20 civil lawsuits accusing him of sexual misconduct when Cleveland traded three first-round picks to the Texans and gave him a fully guaranteed $230 million contract in March 2022. The nature of the allegations against Watson—who has since settled more than two dozen lawsuits and started his Browns career by serving an 11-game suspension and paying a $5 million fine—led some fans to denounce their fandom and left many others with mixed feelings. “That trade for Deshaun really bugged me and mostly, there were people who had season tickets alongside us and our family who dropped their season tickets over it because everybody was very concerned about the off-the-field issues,” McNeil said. “That was really the first time in my Browns fandom that I had that in my circle and certainly I had my own reservations about it, too.” Watson, however, still had his share of supporters at the start of his Cleveland tenure. “It started out rough because he never showed remorse, and there were still people who were like, ‘I don’t really care. Football players do bad things,’” Lima recalled of the fan reaction at the time. “We have to watch Ben Roethlisberger and Ray Lewis in our division for years,” he said. articles.title: Newsstand: Notre Dame joins SEC, Big Ten in opposing NFL players returning to CFB
articles.summary: NFL players are being cut from training camp and immediately joining collegiate rosters. Notre Dame joined the SEC and Big Ten in opposing the idea.
articles._body: In the latest college football calamity, NFL players are being cut from training camp and immediately joining collegiate rosters. The SEC and Big Ten are implementing rules that they hope, pending inevitable legal challenges, will prevent those players from actually suiting up this season. According to Yahoo Sports’ Ross Dellenger , Notre Dame is also opposed to the idea. Dellenger reported that Fighting Irish officials “have communicated to both the SEC and Big Ten that the school is aligned with the prohibition on signing players who have been part of professional organizations.” It’s a significant development, because Notre Dame athletics director Pete Bevacqua often wields the power and influence of a conference commissioner in situations such as these. Whatever happens in 2026, it’s important to note that the “trend” of NFL players rejoining college teams is temporary. The players trying to do this are members of the class of 2022, who believed they were out of eligibility when they entered the 2026 NFL Draft. This will not be an issue moving forward, with age-based eligibility (otherwise known as “five-for-five”) serving as the law of the land. Former Notre Dame defensive end Junior Tuihalamaka is one of those class of 2022 players attempting to return to college football, committing to LSU on Friday. He did not sign with an NFL team or even participate in a rookie minicamp, so it’s possible he can still play for the Tigers even if the power conferences get their way. The Irish considered bringing Tuihalamaka back, but they ultimately decided against it. “For us right here at Notre Dame, it’s just too late in the graduate admissions process,” head coach Marcus Freeman said Friday. “And I don’t think it would put a person in a good situation this late — school starts on Monday — to have success in the classroom and on the field, so that’s kind of been our stance on it.” Notre Dame Tweets of the day Offensive line news… Today at Notre Dame football practice, we saw presumed swing tackle Styles Prescod take reps with the ones at right guard. Mike Denbrock said the right guard competition remains open, and Prescod is one of the players getting a serious look. — Jack Soble (@jacksoble56) August 25, 2026 Practice for Week 1: The power to leap was inside them all along… The only thing missing was the uniform. #GoIrish pic.twitter.com/3DQaDDOiKe — Notre Dame Football (@NDFootball) August 25, 2026 True freshmen to watch: Here are several Notre Dame true freshmen to watch this season pic.twitter.com/bnMBG1zWDw — Mike Singer (@MikeTSinger) August 25, 2026 Quote of the day “We’ve got a number of guys we’re taking a look at in there. Styles [Prescod] is one of those guys. We put him in there in the scrimmage last Friday, and saw some really natural things happen from him in there. And so, we’re going to keep trying to figure out what the best combination is up front. But Styles is definitely in the mix to become one of the five that goes out there.” — Notre Dame offensive coordinator Mike Denbrock on the right guard competition Headlines of the day Observations from Notre Dame football practice: Another offensive line surprise? articles.title: Dale Earnhardt Jr. breaks down Josh Berry, Bubba Wallace drama at New Hampshire
articles.summary: Dale Earnhardt Jr. hilariously breaks down the Josh Berry-Bubba Wallace drama and explains why he believes Berry immediately regretted the contact.
articles._body: Dale Earnhardt Jr. is unapologetically a Josh Berry fan.  The soon-to-be-free agent driver is racing for his career.  It didn’t stop Earnhardt Jr. from being highly entertained by a late-race incident with Bubba Wallace in the Dollar Tree 301.  With 80 laps to go at New Hampshire, some great racing and drama unfolded between Berry and Wallace.  Dale Jr. was highly amused and entertained.  The beginning of the Berry-Wallace incident You can watch the entire sequence below, but Earnhardt Jr. was fired up over the whole thing.  By fired up, we’re talking about excited about the hilarity of the entire scenario.  2nd to 1st to 3rd… pic.twitter.com/FkckVk8i5l — Team 21 (@21_WoodBrothers) August 23, 2026 “The Josh Berry, Bubba Wallace deal,” started Earnhardt Jr. on his podcast this week . “So I’m going to be honest, man. Bubba never ran like the same lap or line twice during this scenario. “So Josh is trying to pass Bubba, the 21 and the 12. They could get in the corner ridiculously deep. And Bubba was making a lot of adjustments on his entries. “The line he was running like a couple of laps before this, Josh just about ran in the back of him. Getting into turn one or something so close. And I think when they go down into turn three and four, Josh drives down in the corner and buries it down in there. “I don’t think that Josh meant to hit him. So Josh has buried it into the corner. And I think if Josh gets on the brakes harder to try not to hit the 23, he risks spinning himself out.  The car tips over on the right front and the left rear spins out. And so Josh is like, ‘Oh sh*t, I’m going to hit him. “He knows he’s going to hit him and he knocks the f*cking sh*t out of Bubba Wallace. And I think Josh in that moment goes, ‘Oh f*ck, I didn’t mean to do that.’  “And if you watch Josh, the line that he runs into Turn 1 is a, ‘Please don’t f*cking hit me. Please don’t hit me. Please don’t hit me.’  Dale Jr. doesn’t feel there was intent by Berry Earnhardt Jr. had so much fun breaking the whole series of events down.  His play-by-play of it all was the highlight of the Dale Jr. Download this week.  “He’s like, ‘I didn’t f*cking mean to do that. And he’s taking this sort of super defensive line so that the 23 Bubba, if he was really, really mad, doesn’t destroy him. And cause Josh is sitting there going, ‘I’ve got to run top 10 today. I’ve got to do it. I’ve got to keep this sort of narrative going that I belong here. I need to keep the conversation around me. ‘I’ve got to run good. I can’t f*ck this up.’  “And he got down in the corner, made a mistake. He dove into turn three, Bubba committed to the same line. And Josh is like, ‘F*ck it,’ and smashes him. “Cause Bubba’s sitting there going, you don’t know. Bubba might be sitting there saying, ‘What the f*ck was that?’ “Bubba, right here, could’ve wrecked him and he doesn’t. So I liked it.” ‘It’s good racing, but it was so funny’ In the end, Earnhardt Jr. chalked it up to good racing. And it was a great result for both Wallace and Berry, who finished P2 and P3 respectively . Not to mention, it was Berry’s fourth consecutive top ten finish, a first for Wood Brothers since 1994 when Morgan Shepherd did the same. “It’s good racing, but it was so funny. I was kind of laughing when you see the ultra-defensive line that Josh runs down into turn one. It’s a line of man, ‘I’m going to blow this corner. I’m going to run the worst line I could possibly run through this corner in an attempt to not get crashed.’ “I mean, I don’t know, man, Bubba might’ve hit him just as hard back, and maybe Josh doesn’t save his car.  I think it’s an eye for an eye out there. You hit me hard. I want to give it back to you right away. And I think all drivers are similar. I thought that was a funny series of events.”

articles.title: 100 Days of Georgia’s Greatest Plays—Day 10
articles.summary: On Day 10, we look back at Stetson Bennett’s 10-yard touchdown pass that completed Georgia’s thrilling comeback victory over Ohio State in the 2022 Peach Bowl.
articles._body: UGASports continues its 100-day countdown to the Bulldogs’ 2026 season opener with the “100 Days of Georgia’s Greatest Plays” series. Today, on Day 10 , we revisit one of the greatest plays in Georgia football history involving the number 10. On Day 10, we look back at Stetson Bennett’s 10-yard touchdown pass that completed Georgia’s thrilling comeback victory over Ohio State in the 2022 Peach Bowl. The Game: No. 1 Georgia (13-0 record off a win over LSU in the SEC title game) vs. No. 4 Ohio State (11-1 record off a loss to Michigan in the final regular-season game) at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta for the CFP Semifinal at the Peach Bowl on December 31, 2022. The winner was set to face No. 3 TCU, which had defeated No. 2 Michigan earlier that day in the Fiesta Bowl, for the CFP National Championship. The Bulldogs were established as 6-point favorites over the Buckeyes. “Get the Picture”: After Ohio State took a 41-35 lead on a 48-yard field goal by Noah Ruggles with 2:43 remaining in the game, Georgia took over at its own 28-yard line. Senior quarterback Stetson Bennett completed four passes for 57 yards, while the Buckeyes committed a 5-yard offsides penalty, moving the Bulldogs to the opposing 10-yard line. There, Georgia faced second-and-5 with less than a minute remaining and desperately needing a touchdown. The Play From the Ohio State 10, Bennett took the shotgun snap, dropped back and, with pressure closing in, lofted a pass toward the left corner of the end zone. Sophomore wideout AD Mitchell leaped over Ohio State cornerback Denzel Burke to make the 10-yard touchdown catch, tying the game at 41 with just 54 seconds remaining. Jack Podlesny’s ensuing extra point gave Georgia its first lead since the second quarter, 42-41. Trailing by a single point, Ohio State quickly moved into Georgia territory. However, a 50-yard game-winning field-goal attempt by Ruggles with eight seconds remaining sailed wide left, sending the Bulldogs to the CFP National Championship Game for the second consecutive year and third time in six seasons. Bennett, the 25-year-old, sixth-year senior and former walk-on, who had recently finished fourth in the Heisman Trophy voting, completed 23 of 34 passes for a career-high 398 yards and three touchdowns with one interception, while also rushing for a score. After rallying Georgia from a two-touchdown fourth-quarter deficit, Bennett was named the Peach Bowl’s Offensive MVP. In four CFP games during the 2021 and 2022 seasons—all Georgia victories—Bennett completed 78 of 115 passes (67.8%) for 1,239 yards, 12 touchdowns and just one interception, while rushing for three more scores. Fittingly, Bennett was named the offensive player of the game or MVP in each of his four CFP appearances.

At one point, as she was holding Paige by the head, her pants were being pulled down . it’s been 8 years. stop disrespecting nikki bella with the 'cena' chants… pic.twitter.com/wQP3wN3Dam — ☆ Z ☆ (@ItsaNewError) August 25, 2026 Luckily, she had shorts on underneath the pants, which led to some speculation that she was promoting a new product in this moment. Paige pulled down Nikki Bella's pants to help her promote the new shorts “Nikki Bella Fearless Boy Shorts” are now available on WWE Shop. pic.twitter.com/VMrNmN9yPW — 𝓢𝒕𝒂𝒓𝒔 𝓐𝒃𝒐𝒗𝒆 (@starspv_) August 25, 2026 One fan on X, formerly Twitter, believed that Bella was promoting her new boy shorts, which are available to purchase on WWE’s online shop. Luckily, she did have shorts on underneath her pants, and they were a WWE product. Perhaps they will keep it in for the product placement. They lost the Women’s Tag Team Championship to Fatal Influence (Fallon Henley and Jainey Red). At SummerSlam, the Bella Twins and Paige would face all three members of Fatal Influence. They lost, and afterward, the Bellas turned on Paige. However, Brie Bella suffered an injury in the match, so she won’t likely be a part of her sister’s feud with Paige, at least in the immediate future. articles.title: CaneSport to unveil memories of 2001 season with “The Vault”
articles.summary: Twenty-five years ago this fall, the most talented college football team ever assembled walked out of the Orange Bowl tunnel and into history. Twelve games. Twelve wins. Seventeen first round draft picks. Thirty-eight draft picks overall. A perfect season that ended with a 37-14 victory over Nebrask
articles._body: Twenty-five years ago this fall, the most talented college football team ever assembled walked out of the Orange Bowl tunnel and into history. Twelve games. Twelve wins. Seventeen first round draft picks. Thirty-eight draft picks overall. A perfect season that ended with a 37-14 victory over Nebraska in the Rose Bowl on January 3, 2002. The Hurricanes had an offense that averaged 43 points per game. And a defense that only allowed 9.8 points. The two-deep was so absurd that many of the backups — a safety named Sean Taylor, a nose tackle named Vince Wilfork, a cornerback named Antrel Rolle, an offensive lineman named Vernon Carey, a freshman tight end named Kellen Winslow, and running backs named Willis McGahee and Frank Gore—became first-round picks and Pro Bowlers themselves. The Vault recaptures memories from the 2001 National Championship season It was the most amazing assembly of talent in the history of college football. This fall, CaneSport is opening what we are calling “The Vault” of memories from that historic season for a season-long journey back with that team — told the way only we can tell it, because we were there for every snap. Part of that coverage will involve the launch of a new weekly show, The Vault with Bryant McKinnie , featuring the former Miami All-American, Outland Trophy winning and national and Super Bowl championship winning offensive tackle and look back at the team, the season and the people who made it unforgettable. The show debuts Thursday at 7 pm on the CaneSport You Tube channel. Friday we will visit with former Coach Butch Davis, who built the 2001 team and then left Miami eight months before the historic season played out. The Vault is one of the most ambitious projects in CaneSport history — a full season of premium long-form storytelling both in print and video, that replays the 2001 season in real time, 25 years to the day. We will go unit by unit through that roster — Ken Dorsey and the quarterbacks, the four-deep running back room of Clinton Portis, Willis McGahee, Frank Gore and Najeh Davenport, the receivers, Jeremy Shockey and the tight ends, the lines, the linebackers, and the greatest secondary ever. Every step of the way we will ask the question – Was this the greatest college football team of all time? We will remember the big games, 25 years to each day. We will take you back inside Beaver Stadium for the 33-7 statement that opened the season on September 1. On October 13, we will take you back inside Doak Campbell Stadium for the 49-27 dismantling of Florida State. On November 10, we will revisit Chestnut Hill — and The Play, when Ed Reed snatched the ball from defensive lineman Matt Walters’ hands and saved the perfect season. On December 1, we will revisit the survival test in Blacksburg. And on January 3, 2027 — 25 years to the day — we will remember the Rose Bowl victory over Nebraska and perfection. McKinnie won’t simply be just another person talking about the 2001 Hurricanes. He was there protecting Ken Dorsey’s blind side, not allowing a single sack. He won the Outland Trophy as the nation’s best lineman and went on to a decade-plus NFL career and a Super Bowl ring. He was in the locker room and in the huddle. He practiced every day against a roster loaded with future NFL stars. He experienced the personalities, competition, expectations and pressure from inside a program operating at a level college football has rarely seen. CaneSport.com Publisher Gary Ferman and Bruce “The Truth Teller” Warner will join McKinnie on the weekly show as the conversations revisit the championship season and explore the stories surrounding it. Throughout the season, members of the 2001 Hurricanes will join The Vault, giving former teammates an opportunity to reconnect, reminisce and tell stories that haven’t necessarily been heard before. What was that locker room really like? How competitive were the practices? Who were the funniest players on the team? When did the players realize how special they could be? What do they remember now that they didn’t fully appreciate then? And what was it really like being part of a team filled with so many players who believed they were destined for greatness? CaneSport has covered the Miami program continuously since before that team’s stars were in high school. We were in the room for the coaching change nobody wanted, on the sideline in Tallahassee and in Pasadena when the confetti fell. Back then we thought every Miami season was going to evolve like that. Little did we know how quickly it all could get away, that Miami would go 24 years between national title game appearances. The Vault will turn the clock back on the story of the greatest team ever. It begins tomorrow with a look at the 2000 season that set the stage for what 2001 would be, including the departure of Butch Davis and the hiring of Larry Coker and the debut of our new show, The Vault with Bryant McKinnie. There are moments in sports that become more fascinating with time rather than less. The 2001 Miami Hurricanes is one of them. Stories keep history alive. That is what The Vault is about. Twenty-five years later, we’re opening the door. The Vault is open. The stories will finally be told.

articles.title: Miami QB Dereon Coleman Adds 26 Pounds, Learning From Darian Mensah With an Eye on His Future
articles.summary: Miami quarterback Dereon Coleman is focused on 2026, but his development could shape the Hurricanes’ plans for 2027. After adding 26 pounds of muscle, the strong-armed passer is learning from Darian Mensah, refining his quick release and trying to prove Miami’s next starting quarterback is already o
articles._body: Cam Ward. Carson Beck. Darian Mensah. TBD. That’s the line of succession to the Miami Hurricanes QB throne, with the most recent trio massive home run additions. Why are we already talking about that 2027 “TBD”? Well, as anyone who knows Mario Cristobal well will tell you, his eye isn’t simply on this year. So that “TBD” is going to be evaluated all season as Luke Nickel , Dereon Coleman and Judd Anderson try to prove enough in practices throughout the fall to state their case for why UM doesn’t need to chase a portal QB next year. Fans will be watching Mensah and the offense thrive. Coaches will be drawing up game plans … and also evaluating the backups all season. The future of QB U probably isn’t something fans are thinking a lot about right now with the cusp of the season here. But it’s worth keeping in mind. Nickel and Coleman stood out in spurts this fall, and it’s Nickel that is expected to be QB2 this season with Coleman looking to pad his small frame. Anderson continues to be spotty with accuracy, although he’s much improved from a year ago. A reason coaches hope one of these guys emerges as a guy that can break out? Well, that will save millions that can be spread to other positions as the program continues in its phase of competing for national titles year after year. No one that’s not named Mensah or Malachi Toney have completed a meaningful college pass on this roster. Barring something happening to Mensah, that will remain the case. With that in mind, today we’re taking a closer look at Coleman. He’s an intriguing playmaker with one of the quickest releases you’ll find, and a strong, accurate arm. “Growing up, I always had a quick release,” Coleman told CaneSport. “I don’t know how it came, but it just always stuck with me. And I just had to add power into my hips, and that’s what I’ve been doing.” Judd Anderson (L), Darian Mensah and Dereon Coleman / Photo courtesy of Neil Gershman Photography-Zooba Images He’s more than mobile enough with a 1.62-second 10-yard split in summer testing, but the issue for him is he arrived this spring at 150 pounds. Yes, Miami offensive linemen could have stacked three Dereon’s on top of each other and benched him. Not so much anymore. Coleman says he’s put on 26 pounds since then, up to 176. He is targeting 200, which at 6-1 would be trending in the right direction. “That 26 pounds is pure muscle, no fat,” Coleman says. “Miami’s got a really good nutrition program and a strength and conditioning program, so I’ve just been working very, very hard in both of those. I try my hardest to do everything I can — eat, drink protein shakes, hydrate. I just go hard at what we do.” He’s also going hard at soaking up all the knowledge he can from Mensah. “Being with Darian a lot, on and off the field, he’s just been pouring into me so much, and I’ve just been taking in everything,” Coleman said. “He always gives me a lot of advice, even during practice. You know, he pulls me to the side, or when I’m coming off the field, we’ll talk about every play. Then after practice, we’ll go upstairs and watch film with each other and he’ll pour into me.” Film that Coleman checks out on his own time? That’s of NFL QBs Bryce Young and Jayden Daniels. “Bryce Young, I really look at how he’s doing everything, and he’s my size,” Coleman said. “So once I watch him, when people talk about my size I don’t really care. Because he won the Heisman, he went to the natty, you know, he’s in the NFL doing what he’s doing. So size doesn’t really affect me.” The big man on campus perhaps doesn’t have to be the biggest guy on campus, right? While Coleman strives to be that guy, it would be understandable if he cast an eye every now and then to what could be a year from now. But that’s not the Hurricane way. He’s brought into the program and Mario Cristobal’s 1-0 mentality “Next year, that’s not my goal right now,” Coleman said. “I’m just focused on this year.”

articles.title: A new Texas law declaws neighborhood groups that oppose housing projects
articles.summary: Lawmakers gutted an old state law that required a city council supermajority to approve a new housing development if neighbors petitioned the proposal.
articles._body: When a shrinking church proposed to turn its property in a wealthy South Austin neighborhood into homes for lower-income families, neighboring homeowners revolted — petitioning the Austin City Council to halt the project. Neighbors complained the 64-unit development — nestled in a desirable neighborhood just a block from the South Congress shopping district — would be out of character with surrounding single-family homes. The complex, they told city officials, would be too tall. The combination of new homes and a preschool planned for the site would jam up neighborhood streets with traffic, they argued. “Just because there is a developer willing to cram an absurdly out-of-scale project onto this site does not mean it’s the correct or best project for this property,” one resident wrote to city officials. In years past, their petition formally opposing the development — which had 29 property owners who signed it — would have made it difficult if not impossible for the city council to approve the project. Instead, the proposed development sailed through. One key reason: a new state law that makes it more difficult for neighbors to stop new housing. Among a suite of bills that passed last year to rein in the state’s housing costs, House Bill 24 effectively gutted a Jim Crow-era law that gave nearby property owners considerable leverage to prevent new homes from going up near them. Texas faces a considerable shortage of homes, which has kept the state’s home prices and rents elevated as households compete for too few homes and apartments. Lawmakers largely sought to tackle the housing crunch by loosening local regulations and allowing more homes to be built. HB 24 stands out among the suite of legislation because it’s aimed squarely at defanging “not-in-my-backyard” resistance from existing homeowners who often put pressure on local officials to prevent new homes from being built nearby. HB 24 “takes down some of the barriers to development,” said Jamee Jolly, CEO of The Real Estate Council, an industry group that represents developers in North Texas. Under the old law, if enough neighboring property owners formally petitioned against a project, the city council could only approve it by a supermajority — a high bar to clear. Even the idea of the petition triggering such a vote on the city council was enough to deter builders from pursuing much-needed housing. “It became an implicit threat,” said Salim Furth, a senior research fellow who studies housing production at the Mercatus Center, a libertarian think tank based at George Mason University. Sometimes, homeowners successfully petitioned against new housing. Two years ago, a proposed affordable housing development in San Antonio touted by Gov. Greg Abbott failed to get enough votes on the City Council to move forward after neighbors used the law. Now, under HB 24, those efforts only need a simple majority to pass, no matter how many neighbors oppose it. So far, it’s not clear how many developments have benefited from the law. But housing advocates, researchers and developers said it gives city councils more political leeway to approve individual developments or adopt broader, citywide zoning changes to combat the state’s deep shortage of homes. ‘Blood, sweat and tears’ South Austin Christian Church sits on a little less than an acre in Austin’s eclectic Travis Heights, a historic neighborhood with a funky mix of homes a short walk from South Congress. Its congregation had dwindled for decades, said Robin Stallings, the church’s treasurer, and had long been priced out of the neighborhood as South Congress transformed into a high-end shopping district. The typical home now goes for around $700,000, according to Zillow data. “Historically our members came from the neighborhood,” Stallings said. “But gradually, the neighborhood got more and more expensive and we had fewer and fewer people actually from the neighborhood.” Keeping the church open no longer made sense, Stallings said, so church leaders decided on a plan for the property they felt aligned with the church’s mission: sell the land to an affordable housing developer. The church aims to sell its property to developer O-SDA, which plans some 64 apartments on the site, with a range of units from studios to three-bedrooms. The development will be 100% income-restricted with each unit set aside for households making less than the area median income. More than half of those units will be geared toward households who make 50% of the area median income or less, which for a family of four is $67,200. O-SDA is also planning an onsite preschool to serve 25 to 40 children. City officials like the proposed development, dubbed Rowen Vale. For the past several years, the City Council has pushed for newer, infill development for lower-income families in Austin’s urban core, where housing costs have grown inordinately expensive in the past two decades. Rowen Vale’s proximity to South Congress potentially means housing options for workers in shops and restaurants there they may not have had otherwise. The property’s also within walking or biking distance of an H-E-B, Stallings noted. What’s more is the property is close to a stop on Austin’s planned light rail line. “We want people of all backgrounds and all income levels to be able to have the same Austin experiences,” said City Council Member Zohaib “Zo” Qadri, who represents the area where Rowen Vale’s slated to go. “If you want to live in Austin and you give your blood, sweat, and tears to the city, and you want your kids to be able to live in Austin and go to schools in Austin, you should be able to do that.” Neighbors pushed back, unleashing a litany of complaints typically lodged against new housing: Parking from the development would spill over into neighborhood streets, the new homes and preschool would generate too much traffic and the development would be too tall for a single-family neighborhood and encroach on nearby homes.
