The Lead The Vault Is Open: Reliving Miami’s Greatest Team 25 Years Later Twenty-five years ago, Miami unleashed a team that still looks ridiculous on paper. Twelve games. Twelve wins. Seventeen eventual first-round picks. Thirty-eight players drafted. The 2001 Hurricanes didn’t just win the national championship—they produced a roster so loaded that Sean Taylor, Vince Wilfork, Antrel Rolle, Willis McGahee and Frank Gore were among the guys waiting their turn. The players who lived it will take fans inside the locker room, practices and moments that turned a ridiculously talented roster into an undefeated champion. We’ll revisit everything from the opening demolition of Penn State to Ed Reed’s season-saving play at Boston College, the survival test at Virginia Tech and the Rose Bowl beatdown of Nebraska. Along the way, we’ll tackle the question that still sparks debate: Was this the greatest college football team ever assembled? Miami spent 24 years waiting to return to a national championship game. Now, as another Hurricanes team chases the ultimate prize, CaneSport is reopening the story of the group that actually reached perfection. The Vault is open. The Board Canes Chatter Gone Wild: Message Board Post of the Day Every morning Gary Ferman forces Matt Shodell to wake up extra early to identify the best recent fan  CaneSport Message Board  post. articles.title: Jay-Z 30 Pop-Up Experience to Open In London Ahead of Historic Tottenham Hotspur Stadium Shows
articles.summary: Fans can shop limited edition merchandise created exclusively for the concerts.
articles._body: A Jay-Z 30 pop-up experience is set to land at London’s UMusic Shop Camden this week, giving fans a chance to celebrate the rapper’s upcoming shows at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium . Located at The Stables Market, the pop-up will be open daily from 11 a.m. to 7 p.m. between Aug. 27 and Sept. 2, ahead of Jay-Z’s only U.K. performances of the year on Sept. 4 and 5. The Brooklyn-born rapper last toured the U.K. in 2018 as part of his On The Run II trek with Beyoncé, visiting stadiums in Cardiff, Manchester, Glasgow and London. Fans can shop a curated selection of limited edition merchandise created exclusively for the London concerts. The experience will also feature a series of DJ sets, with the likes of DJ Target, DJ Manny Norté, DJ Semtex and DJ Esi taking over the decks from 5 p.m. to 7 p.m. each day. The London double-header follows Jay-Z’s three-night run at Yankee Stadium in New York City, which took place in July. Across the shows, the rapper was joined by a star-studded line-up of guests that included Beyoncé, Alicia Keys, Usher, Eminem, Nas, Pharrell Williams, Rihanna, Slick Rick and more. The shows are billed as a celebration of the 30th anniversary of debut LP Reasonable Doubt , which kicked off the 56-year-old’s illustrious career in 1996. Reporting from night two of the Yankee Stadium residency, Billboard ’s Angel Diaz described the show as “a masterclass show.” She continued: “Jay went through each song at what felt like a feverish pace, giving fans little time to rest. And they didn’t mind – they just kept getting louder. It was impressive to see in person, especially when the surprise guests hit the stage.” Beyond London, Jay-Z is scheduled to bring the 30th-anniversary celebration to Paris’ Stade de France on Sept. 10, followed by two Los Angeles shows at SoFi Stadium on Oct. 23 and 24. He kicked off his run of comeback live shows by headlining Philadelphia’s Roots Picnic in March , which marked his first solo show in over six years. The performance spawned the “Roots Picnic Freestyle,” which, in June, Billboard crowned the best rap song of 2026 so far . Jay-Z has reigned as one of the biggest names in hip-hop for the past 30 years, and counting. Reasonable Doubt peaked at No. 23 on the Billboard 200 upon release in 1996. Jay-Z’s breakthrough LP The Blueprint was released five years later in 2001, debuting at No. 1 on the all-genres albums chart. Over time, Jay-Z has amassed 14 No. 1 albums on the Billboard 200, holding the all-time record among solo male artists. He has also scored four No. 1 hits on the Billboard Hot 100 .

articles.title: Nene Royal Rocks Into ‘AGT’ Final With Cover of Soundgarden’s ‘Black Hole Sun’: Watch
articles.summary: Royal cranked it up yet again with a performance of Soundgarden’s signature song, “Black Hole Sun.”
articles._body: Nene Royal didn’t enter America’s Got Talent to dilly-dally about. She came to rock. Hailing the Phuket, Thailand, the teenager made the long-haul to the United States to compete in the current, 21st season of AGT , getting it done with an electric guitar and a knack for cast-iron metal. From the top, Royal caught the attention of millions when she auditioned with The Cranberries ’ mid-‘90s protest anthem “Zombie.” If you weren’t already paying attention, the penny dropped when she covered “Hysteria” by Muse,” laid out on a bed of licks, squeals and technical tricks that Hendrix would’ve approved of. For Tuesday night’s (Aug. 25) Quarterfinals, Royal cranked it up yet again with a performance of Soundgarden ’s signature song, “Black Hole Sun,” a grunge-era classic which was released in 1994 on the band’s album Superunknown . Royal literally lit up the stage, for a heavy, and fiery, moment. The roar from the crowd told you all you needed to know. “I know I’m not supposed to say this. NBC, give her the million right now,” Howie Mandel enthused. “Nene I think you could really win this competition,” remarked Sofía Vergara. “Because you can sing and you can play that guitar. I mean, insanely. The way you look. No wonder everybody in the street asks me about you. I think you can win.” Mel B met the youngster and other contestants backstage. “You are just like the most quietest, humblest, sweet-like young lady. And then you’ve come out on this stage and it’s a different vibe,” she said. The Spice Girl, like her fellow judges, struggled to be heard over the raucous audience. “I have to say that I love really good vocals. I’m a ‘90s girl. I’m into pop music. That kind of music is not my vibe. But, your vocals are on point, your guitar is on point, your look, your energy, your vibe. How could I not do this.” And with that, Mel B dramatically activated the Golden Buzzer. Cue golden glitter, and tears of joy, hugs. Royal is now fast-tracked to the Finals. Her fellow Quarterfinalists will learn their fate during Wednesday night’s results show. America votes, and three more acts progress to the semifinals. Also on the night, Season 20 standout country singer Steve Ray Ladson returns to the stage alongside Grammy-nominated act The War and Treaty. Watch Nene Royal’s Golden Buzzer-winning performance below.

articles.title: Raised on AI
articles.summary: When my oldest child was born, I immediately set up Gmail and Twitter accounts in her name. I broadly announced her birth online and proceeded to plaster her photo across all sorts of platforms. In short, I began creating her digital footprint long before she could stand on her own two feet.  F
articles._body: When my oldest child was born, I immediately set up Gmail and Twitter accounts in her name. I broadly announced her birth online and proceeded to plaster her photo across all sorts of platforms. In short, I began creating her digital footprint long before she could stand on her own two feet.  Fast-forward a couple of years to when my second kid came, and I had essentially the opposite reaction. I wanted to make sure I preserved her privacy. I didn’t want her birthday to be a matter of public record or her face to feed the algorithms. In time, I would go back and scrub much of the early footprint I had created for my first child as well.  What happened? I watched the promise of the early internet give way to the reality of its potential for abuse. I myself was already fully in the throes of smartphone and social media obsession. My wife, a pediatric nurse, grew increasingly alarmed at the number of children admitted to her hospital struggling with the effects of things like body dysmorphia or cyberbullying as a result of interactions on social media. We became those parents. The ones whose kids carry flip phones and aren’t on TikTok.  We are not alone in this. A surprising—maybe troubling—number of people I know who work at big tech companies also keep their kids at arm’s distance from technology. They lock down their phones, if they have phones at all, and keep them off social media. Hell, even Mark Zuckerberg doesn’t publicly post his children’s faces on Facebook or Instagram.   If the desire to limit kids’ use of technology was once a subcurrent, it has become a raging flood. Jonathan Haidt’s best-selling 2024 book The Anxious Generation helped propel the issue into the mainstream (despite criticisms of his conclusions from some developmental psychologists). Last year, Australia became the first country to enact a social media ban for children under 16. Other nations, from Austria to Indonesia, have followed suit, announcing similar bans. The US Supreme Court recently upheld an age verification law in Texas, which acts as a de facto ban, and several states have flirted with their own measures. School districts all over the country are banning educational devices like iPads and Chromebooks in favor of actual books. Kids themselves seem to be embracing this tech skepticism too: The hottest gadget among the Gen Alpha set is a vintage Sony Walkman. We have to prepare our children to live in the actual world we have actually created, not the one we wish we had. Yet there is no hiding from technology. It permeates nearly everything, everywhere. And so we have to prepare our children to live in the actual world we have actually created, not the one we wish we had. How can we help kids survive and thrive in what we have wrought?  It’s a question that feels all the more urgent in the era of AI. To help answer it, we brought in the editors of Anyway —an utterly fantastic magazine for teens and tweens that is so good in large part because it meets them where they are. (If there is a teen in your life, I highly recommend it.) They helped us with the stories you’ll see in this issue, and they asked kids to share in their own words how they are feeling about AI and what’s to come. What those young people told Anyway was complex, fascinating, and, to an incredible extent, thoughtful and sophisticated.  Meanwhile, I’ve loosened the digital tether—just a bit. I still don’t post many photos of my kids online, and I remain abundantly concerned about the perils of social media and AI.  But when my older daughter started high school, we retired the flip phone in favor of an iPhone. And my younger one now sports an Apple Watch. These devices have opened up the world to them in all sorts of ways. They help forge new friendships, building relationships that move seamlessly between digital and physical spaces. They allow my kids to roam free—or at least more freely—beyond the known spaces of our neighborhood and across the city.  Along the way, they’re learning and testing boundaries, just the way they’re supposed to. I guess you could say I am too.

articles.title: AI models flub these intelligence tests. Can you fare any better?
articles.summary: Puzzles and games have been central to AI development since the very beginning. Just as we humans like to test our smarts with crosswords or logic puzzles, developers can test how far models have advanced with a gaming gauntlet. The term “machine learning” was popularized in a 1959 article by the IB
articles._body: Puzzles and games have been central to AI development since the very beginning. Just as we humans like to test our smarts with crosswords or logic puzzles, developers can test how far models have advanced with a gaming gauntlet. The term “machine learning” was popularized in a 1959 article by the IBM computer scientist Arthur Samuel about an algorithm that learned to play checkers. Chess and the Chinese board game Go are famous AI test beds too.  Judged purely on its puzzling skills, AI is improving a lot—and quickly. In late 2024, a team of scientists from Columbia University showed that even the best models could figure out only 18% of the infamous New York Times Connections puzzles; by early 2025, some models could solve them near perfectly every time.  But puzzles do more than just highlight the inexorable advance of AI capabilities. Seeing where models succeed and fail—and where we humans still beat them—can provide a useful window into the technology’s strengths and weaknesses. Despite advances, today’s models still fumble: Subtle changes in classic riddles often trip them up, and visual puzzles are a particular weak spot.  Here you’ll have the chance to test your wits on puzzles that have stumped models at one time or another. Some might be as tricky for you as they were for the AI; others are so simple that they’ll have you doubting whether AI is really intelligent at all. Each one highlights at least one way in which machine and human cognition differ. If you ace the test, you’ll have proved that you can out-puzzle an AI—at least for now.  Spatial Reasoning Let’s start with a domain where humans have a huge advantage: spatial reasoning. If you’ve ever taken an IQ test, you may have done a mental rotation problem. These puzzles ask you to determine whether different images represent the same objects from different angles. Though today’s language models typically have the ability to analyze visual inputs, they still fail abysmally at these puzzles. For all the talk of how world models can help AI understand physical environments, LLMs still don’t seem to be able to manipulate 3D objects the way spatial thinkers like architects and mechanical engineers can. Mental Rotation Instructions : Choose the answer that shows the object in the prompt, but from a different angle. In each case, there’s only one correct answer! Memory & Adaptability Frontier LLMs have extraordinary memories; they were exposed to a monstrous volume of facts during training and can recite many of them faithfully. That’s an asset for outcompeting humans at trivia, but it can also be a liability. When a puzzle closely resembles one a model saw during training, the model may whiz by key differences and respond with what it memorized.  This held true in a 2024 study in which researchers from Google and the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign trained and tested models on slight variations of a classic type of puzzle called Knights and Knaves. In these problems, some characters always tell the truth and others always lie, and you have to figure out who’s who. The same principle may be at work in a test called SimpleBench. These questions resemble more complicated problems that models likely encountered in training. Humans spot the trick, but even top-tier models trip. Knights and Knaves Instructions : The only thing you need to know to solve these puzzles is that knights always tell the truth and knaves always lie. Determine who’s what on the basis of what each character says. SimpleBench Instructions : Read these SimpleBench problems carefully, and you should be able to figure out the answers in no time. Abstract & Visual Reasoning AI doesn’t just bungle visual problems in 3D—two dimensions can trip it up as well. That’s a major factor in how well models do on the most famous ­puzzle-based benchmark, ARC-AGI. These problems require you to infer abstract, general rules from a set of examples. Models do better on ARC puzzles when they receive each grid not as an image but as a string of numbers that encodes the color of each cell.  Research suggests that even when models answer ARC-AGI questions correctly, they often do so using byzantine and non-­generalizable rules, whereas humans draw on simple visual concepts. Despite these disadvantages, models have gotten quite good at ARC-AGI over the past year, but some puzzles—such as the one printed here—still stump them. ARC-AGI Instruction s: Study the three pairs of grids shown below to figure out the rule that dictates how the ones on the left transform into the ones on the right. Then get out your markers or colored pencils and fill in the fourth grid using that rule. (The solution is the same no matter which way the grids are oriented.) Intuition It’s not just AI models that fall into traps. We humans have our own cognitive foibles, many of which AI does not share. Psychologists have designed problem suites that invert the SimpleBench phenomenon: For these questions, humans often give knee-jerk answers, whereas models will respond deliberatively. Some of the problems exploit errors in the ways that we intuitively do math; others are phrased so as to suggest obvious answers that fall apart if the question is read carefully.  Lightning Round Instructions : Answer the questions below as quickly as you can. Increasing Complexity In some cases, whether an LLM can complete a puzzle is a matter of scale. One study from researchers at Apple found that LLMs can ace simple versions of the Tower of Hanoi problem, which involves moving a stack of disks one at a time without ever putting a larger disk atop a smaller one, and river-crossing puzzles, in which a group of people must traverse a river according to certain rules. But only up to a point: As the number of disks or people hits six and higher, the models began to falter. articles.title: Camilo’s ‘Vida de Rico’ Enters YouTube’s Billion Views Club
articles.summary: The Colombian singer and songwriter passes one billion streams on YouTube with his feel-good 2020 single “Vida de Rico.”
articles._body: Welcome to the club, Camilo . That is, YouTube’s Billion Views Club. The Colombian singer and songwriter passes one billion streams on YouTube with his feel-good tune from 2020, “Vida de Rico.” Directed by Camilo’s wife Evaluna Montaner, the music video for “Vida de Rico” is his second to reach the 1 billion view mark, following his breakthrough collaboration with Mau y Ricky and Manuel Turizo, “Desconocidos,” which dropped in 2018. Following its release, “Vida de Rico” climbed to No. 1 on the Latin Airplay chart (dated Jan. 30, 2021), doing so in its 16 th week, and notched multiple weeks atop the Latin Pop Airplay tally. He also performed the number during Billboard ‘s virtual Latin Music Week in 2020, presented during the pandemic, and the following year during the 22nd annual Latin Grammy Awards. The Latin star is currently on the road with his Camilo Worldwide Tour , which continues in Mexico with 14 dates, starting in the capital, Mexico City, on Aug. 28, and ending Sept. 20 in Acapulco, before heading to San Juan and Santo Domingo, and returning to the United States in October. The trek will visit almost 40 cities across more than 15 countries in Europe and the Americas, coming to an end in his homeland, with a concert Dec. 11 at Bogotá’s Movistar Arena. “The best motivation while I finish my next album is that we already have the first dates to see each other,” Camilo said in a statement ahead of his tour, which began June in Spain. The six-time Latin Grammy winner is currently working on what will be his fifth studio album, the followup to his fourth album, cuatro , which arrived in May 2024. “When it comes to writing my songs, I’m systematically opposed to being a perfectionist. For me, perfectionism is a burden, a mask of cowardice,” he told Billboard’s 2025 Latin Alternative Music Conference . “We’re going to perceive excellence and it’s measured in the final product. It’s measured in the totality. I have the philosophy of ‘good enough.’ If I feel the song is good enough, that’s it — we’ll move on to the next one. When your creative brain is burned out, that’s when you start creating, and you ask yourself, ‘Is it good enough?’ Yes, next! Whatever is closest to the first creative seed is almost always the best.” Watch “Vida de Rico” below.

articles.title: Capitals sign former Wild goalie to professional tryout agreement
articles.summary: The Washington Capitals on Tuesday added goaltender Cal Petersen to their training camp roster, signing the 31-year-old to a professional tryout agreement. Petersen will participate in Washington’s training camp and preseason while attempting to earn a contract for the 2026-27 season. Peter
articles._body: The Washington Capitals on Tuesday added goaltender Cal Petersen to their training camp roster, signing the 31-year-old to a professional tryout agreement . Petersen will participate in Washington’s training camp and preseason while attempting to earn a contract for the 2026-27 season. Petersen, who was originally selected by the Buffalo Sabres in the fifth round, 129th overall, of the 2013 NHL Draft, spent the 2025-26 campaign in the Minnesota Wild organization after signing a one-year, $775,000 deal with the team in July 2025. He did not appear in an NHL game for the Wild but was recalled from the Iowa Wild several times during the season. With Iowa, Petersen played 33 AHL games and finished with a 13-16-2 record, a 2.73 goals-against average and a .896 save percentage. The Iowa season was Petersen’s seventh year playing in the AHL. He has appeared in 248 career AHL contests, while his recent AHL experience also includes 59 games with the Lehigh Valley Phantoms across two seasons, during which he recorded a .894 save percentage. Petersen brings 106 NHL appearances, including 98 starts, to the Capitals. His NHL career has included 101 games with the Los Angeles Kings and five with the Philadelphia Flyers. He owns a 46-44-10 career record, a 2.96 goals-against average and a .903 save percentage. His most recent NHL action came with the Flyers during the 2023-24 season. Petersen appeared in five games, making four starts, and recorded a 2-2-0 record with a 3.90 GAA and .864 save percentage. His best NHL season came with the Kings in 2020-21, when he played 35 games and registered a .911 save percentage. In 2021-22, he posted a 20-14-2 record in 37 appearances and had a 2.89 GAA. Washington already has Logan Thompson under contract through 2031 and Charlie Lindgren signed through 2028. Clay Stevenson is expected to handle the starting job for the AHL’s Hershey Bears after logging 18 wins and a .912 save percentage in 37 games last season. Petersen will therefore compete for organizational depth alongside Mitchell Gibson, who spent part of 2025-26 in the ECHL. The Capitals preseason begin September 20 against the Boston Bruins. articles.summary: Quinn Hughes has had a hectic seven months. articles._body: Quinn Hughes has had a hectic seven months. He navigated a trade from the Vancouver Canucks to the Minnesota Wild, scored the game-winning goal versus Sweden en route to helping the United States win its first men’s ice hockey Olympics gold medal since 1980, and he then played a massive role in the Wild’s first playoff series victory in 11 years. Now, as the 2024 James Norris Memorial Trophy winner approaches the final season of his contract, he is firmly in the rumor mill. Because Minnesota may have to commit a record-breaking deal to extend Hughes, there is speculation that the organization could trade him for a haul. His brother Jack’s team has been named as a possible destination. But people may not want to entertain such chatter . “As the Minnesota Wild continue extension talks with Quinn Hughes, league sources emphatically shot down reports that the Wild have engaged the New Jersey Devils — or any team — in trade talks regarding the superstar defenseman,” Michael Russo of The Athletic writes. “One source, speaking on the condition of anonymity to discuss negotiations that aren’t public, went as far as to tell The Athletic on Tuesday that the rumors are ‘bulls—,’ ‘made up” and ‘invented BS by bloggers.’” Considering what Hughes has already done for the franchise in the short amount of time he has been in Minnesota, it makes perfect sense for the Wild to lock him up. It will be expensive, though. NHL insider Elliotte Friedman is predicting that Hughes inks a three-year contract that carries an average annual value of $18 million. The Devils and others squads will surely be ready to pounce if talks break down, but it sounds like Wild fans have no reason to panic right now. articles.title: North Carolina transfer getting another QB1 shot with Wake Forest after failed stint under Bill Belichick
articles.summary: On Tuesday, Wake Forest football named Gio Lopez its starting quarterback for the 2026 season, according to On3’s Pete Nakos. The redshirt junior transfer enters the season as the most experienced quarterback on the Demon Deacons’ roster. Lopez spent the 2023 and 2024 seasons at South
articles._body: On Tuesday, Wake Forest football named Gio Lopez its starting quarterback for the 2026 season, according to On3’s Pete Nakos. The redshirt junior transfer enters the season as the most experienced quarterback on the Demon Deacons’ roster. Lopez spent the 2023 and 2024 seasons at South Alabama before transferring to North Carolina in 2025. He won the Tar Heels’ starting job but had a rocky campaign, completing 170 of 261 passes for 1,747 yards, 10 touchdowns and five interceptions. He completed 65.1% of his attempts while also producing 133 rushing yards and three rushing touchdowns. North Carolina finished 4-7 with Lopez as its starter. Lopez’s season at UNC came as the program underwent a major quarterback transition under Bill Belichick. After the 2025 campaign, Lopez transferred out of the Tar Heels, joining Wake Forest for the 2026 season. UNC also saw Max Johnson, Bryce Baker and Lopez leave the program. With the Demon Deacons, Lopez competed with redshirt freshman Steele Pizzella for the starting role during the spring and fall. Pizzella was Wake Forest’s third-string quarterback as a true freshman and did not complete his only pass attempt before redshirting. He originally committed to Washington State as a three-star recruit before joining the Demon Deacons. Lopez ultimately secured the position because of his starting experience and his familiarity with Wake Forest offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach Rob Ezell. Ezell previously served as South Alabama’s offensive coordinator in 2024, giving Lopez prior experience in his system. The decision gives Lopez another QB1 opportunity after his one season at North Carolina. For his college career, he has thrown for 4,781 yards and 32 touchdowns while adding 12 rushing touchdowns. The Demon Deacons will open their regular season against Akron at Allegacy Federal Credit Union Stadium next week. Wake Forest is replacing Robby Ashford, who started all 11 games during his only season with the program and finished with a 7-4 record. However, one analyst believes national championship contenders might be flying under the radar out in Los Angeles. FOX Sports college football analyst RJ Young recently identified USC football as his top sleeper pick to win the national championship this season. Young urged fans and analysts alike to stop sleeping on head coach Lincoln Riley’s squad. “I think we should paying attention to USC,” Young emphasized. “Very much so… USC was the #1 offense in the Big Ten last year.” “I think we should paying attention to USC. Very much so… USC was the #1 offense in the Big Ten last year.” @RJ_Young shares his sleeper pick to win the title this year | @CFBONFOX pic.twitter.com/xDPhiPOg1x — First Things First (@FTFonFS1) August 25, 2026 Young’s high praise rests on a solid statistical foundation. During their 2025 campaign, the Trojans posted a 9-4 record while fielding a dominant offensive unit. USC averaged a conference-leading 465.5 total yards per game, including a lethal passing attack that churned out 296.0 yards per contest. Quarterback Jayden Maiava engineered that explosive unit, amassing 3,711 passing yards and 24 touchdowns through the air while adding six rushing scores on the ground. The Trojans capped off their offensive showcase season in the Alamo Bowl, putting up 27 points against TCU, despite losing. With 15 returning starters back in Southern California for 2026 , including nine starter-caliber returners across the offensive unit, the Trojans boast the continuity needed to make noise. Riley’s offense now pairs experienced leadership along the offensive line with dangerous playmakers like wide receiver Tanook Hines and running back Waymond Jordan. If the defense takes an incremental step forward under the physical addition of transfers like defensive lineman Alex VanSumeren, Young’s bold prediction could easily become reality. Thompson is out to prove to everyone that he can still be a key contributor despite being slowed down by knee injuries. Thompson got his wish, joining a legitimate contender. He is expected to play significant minutes, joining Giannis Antetokounmpo, Bam Adebayo, Andrew Wiggins, Davion Mitchell, Bobby Portis, Tim Hardaway Jr., and Pelle Larsson in the core rotation. The 36-year-old Thompson is chasing his fifth ring. Many have compared his move to the Heat to Ray Allen’s move in 2012. Both were in the late stage of their careers, hoping to win another championship with a loaded squad. When asked about it, Thompson got excited . “Of course I like those comparisons. I love Ray Allen. Are you kidding me? He and Reggie (Miller) were the blueprint for my whole off-ball formula. I still do the drills, I still watch their footage all the time, how they got open and how much they moved without the ball,” said the four-time champion on “Theoretically Speaking.” “It gives me chills that I’m even in the same sentence as Ray because if you told me this my rookie season, I would’ve never believed you. Ray has one of the greatest shots, obviously, in NBA history, and I still practice that back pedal drill he did in Game 6 of 2013 (NBA Finals).” Klay Thompson says he LOVES the 2013 Ray Allen comparison: “Of course I like those comparisons. I love Ray Allen. Are you kidding me? Him and Reggie were the blueprint for my whole off ball formula. — it gives me chills I’m even in the same sentence as Ray because if you told me… https://t.co/OajD9DaKpx pic.twitter.com/u6Cb1EYvr0 — Heat Central (@TheHeatCentral) August 26, 2026 While Thompson has more championships than Allen, who won two rings with the Heat and the Boston Celtics, he maintained that he will never claim that he was better than the legendary shooter. “To be in the same breath as him is surreal, and it’s an honor,” added the five-time All-Star. Thompson, who owns the single-game record for most three-pointers with 14, is No. 4 in the all-time three-pointers list, just one spot below Allen. Thompson has a good chance to surpass Allen, who is ahead by 74 three-pointers, this season. Last season, Thompson drained 202 three-pointers in 69 games with the Dallas Mavericks. articles.title: Bill Gates says we’ve passed AI’s danger thresholds. Now what?
articles.summary: It’s a glorious day in Kirkland, Washington, an affluent Seattle suburb on the eastern shore of Lake Washington. The temperature is in the mid-80s, and the sky is incapable of being any more blue. The view from the Gates Ventures conference room overlooks the Carillon Point Marina, where a flotilla
articles._body: It’s a glorious day in Kirkland, Washington, an affluent Seattle suburb on the eastern shore of Lake Washington. The temperature is in the mid-80s, and the sky is incapable of being any more blue. The view from the Gates Ventures conference room overlooks the Carillon Point Marina, where a flotilla of expensive boats bob in the water, and across the lake to the Olympic Mountains that define the horizon. It’s gorgeous. And vaguely terrifying.  Because if the scene is placid, the messenger is not. Seated across from me at a conference room table, Bill Gates is rocking back and forth in his chair, totally animated. And the more he has to say—about the threats of terror or economic collapse or just losing control of our AI systems—the more agitated I find myself becoming, too.  The philanthropist and former Microsoft CEO says he has been growing increasingly alarmed by the rate of change at which AI technology is advancing, especially since guardrails are not keeping pace. In a new essay published today , Gates argues that we have passed the points where multiple potential dangers should have been checked. “We’ve crossed the threshold in terms of [AI’s] bio-capabilities, cyber-capabilities, psychosocial capabilities, job-market-destruction capabilities, and even the lack of control,” he said in an interview with MIT Technology Review about his new memo . “I’m just stunned at the lack of concern and discussion outside of the industry.” In an effort to wake the world up to what he sees as a rapidly growing societal disrupter, the 70-year-old tech titan has begun sounding the alarm as a “shrill voice,” both publicly with his new essay (the first of multiple he plans on the topic) and in meetings with the press, and privately in conversations with industry, government, and civil society leaders.  And while Gates is calling attention to a number of issues, his warnings about the bio-capabilities of the current frontier models are especially chilling. “Any model that can make novel molecules should be monitored,” he says. “I view bioterrorism risk, versus a natural pandemic, as about 50 times more scary, more likely than a natural pandemic risk.” In addition to the cautionary notes, he also advances some novel ideas for moving society forward. Among them are the concepts of human-reserved jobs, and taxes on robots and tokens. (A robot tax is a longtime notion of his.) The former would preserve some societally agreed-upon jobs for human beings, which he notes may vary from one nation to another. The latter is a tax that sets aside money earned from AI usage that replaces human work.  And to be sure, there is also a hint of optimism. Gates is bullish on the ways AI will continue to transform agriculture and health care and education, for example, or the ways in which it can help us navigate bureaucracy. And, he argues, eventually we do get to abundance. But first? Turbulence. And lots of it.  MIT Technology Review sat down with the billionaire philanthropist to talk about the road that lies ahead, its dangers, and how it could someday take us to a better place.  The following interview has been edited for length and to improve clarity and readability. Mat Honan / MIT Technology Review: Thanks for doing this. I don’t know if you had something you wanted to open with, or I can just jump in.  Bill Gates: You know, one good question I’ve had is: Why am I speaking out now? MIT Technology Review: Literally, my first question! Bill Gates: It’s really two things. One is that we’ve crossed the thresholds in terms of the bio-capabilities, cyber-capabilities, psychosocial capabilities, job-market-destruction capabilities, and even the lack of control; we’re seeing signs of difficulties there. And all these years, people have said, “Okay, when we get close to these thresholds, we’ll really figure out how to let only good people use it, or how to not let it do these things, and maybe that’s when we won’t let people copy models.” And I’m in a state of shock that we’ve crossed these thresholds.  So the fact that we’ve gotten past these is one reason, and the second is that I’m just stunned at the lack of concern and discussion outside of the industry. Within the industry, it’s complicated because the industry doesn’t like criticizing itself, or players like criticizing each other. Some companies are hiring fewer entry-level workers, which you’d have to call a pretty modest signal. But it’s going to happen, and not in any long time frame—because the things that hold people back in terms of capabilities and reliability, all those things are being solved. And so for a substantial part of the white-collar market, you have very low-cost substitution. And then you can have an opinion on how quickly robotics come along. We’re not there yet, but it is stunning the progress being made there—a little bit more in China than in the US, but somewhat in both. MIT Technology Review: You talked about all of this happening so much faster than the internet revolution did, than some of these previous technological revolutions did. What type of timescale are you talking about? You pointed to the thresholds that we’ve crossed. In your view, have we already passed some sort of tipping point where there’s going to be this inevitable change?  Bill Gates: The past definitely is very misleading on this, and a lot of people lean on that. “Hey, no previous technology resulted in a net jobs reduction,” and they’re right. And I’ve given that speech.  But with any credibility that I have, this time is different. When you can replace human cognition for an extremely high percentage of jobs across every industry in the same time frame at modest cost, relative to human labor costs, and your error rates … will probably be lower than human rates. The past is just very misleading. The current economic statistics are very misleading. “ If you’re worried about AI, going to a data center prote

articles.title: Bengals player on roster bubble with most at stake in 2026 NFL preseason finale
articles.summary: For the first time in what feels like ages, the Cincinnati Bengals have depth at multiple positions on their roster. Their wide receiver room was always a tad bit crowded, but this year, mutliple position groups have a handful of players contending for a spot on the main roster. Because of that,
articles._body: For the first time in what feels like ages, the Cincinnati Bengals have depth at multiple positions on their roster. Their wide receiver room was always a tad bit crowded, but this year, mutliple position groups have a handful of players contending for a spot on the main roster. Because of that, there are a few players currently on the bubble ahead of the final roster cut deadline. Which among these players have the most at stake coming into the final game of the preseason for the Bengals? Cornerback depth opens up potential spot for Josh Newton As usual, the Bengals’ wide receiver room is a tad bit crowded this preseason. Ja’Marr Chase, Tee Higgins, and Andrei Iosivas have locked up a spot on the starting 11, but after that, things got a little interesting in the preseason. UDFA Colbie Young broke out as one of the big standouts in preseason, and he’s more than earned his spot on the team. Dohnte Meyers has also been impressive in training camp, and after taking first-team reps in practice, figures to be part of the WR room. This should open up a competition between Mitchell Tinsley and long-time special teams ace Charlie Jones, but given Meyers’ experience as a returner in college, that final WR spot likely goes to Tinsley and should be his to lose. The offensive line would have likely been an interesting conversation a few days ago, particularly at the swing tackle position. After the Bengals dropped Cody Ford , though, Jalen Rivers likely has that spot on lock for the 2026 season. On the other side of the defensive line, rookie DT Landon Robinson stole the headlines with his play, and has locked up one of these spots. While there are some serious candidates outside of the top-53, the projected 11-man defensive line room seems to be mostly intact. Other position groups have their groups on lock, as well. The Bengals’ rurnning back room will be mostly solid with Chase Brown, Samaje Perine, and Tahj Brooks. Tight end isn’t an issue with Drew Sample, Mike Gesicki, Erick All and Tanner Hudson. The last spot on the team is likely going to go to Jack Endries if Cincy decides to invest in depth at that position. On the other side of the ball, the linebacker and safety positions seem to be mostly settled, with no player really challenging for the final spots in that area. That leaves the cornerback room, where there’s two former Bengals draftees battling for what could very well be the final piece of the puzzle. DJ Turner and Dax Hill have the starting positions on lock, while Tacario Davis, Ja’Sir Taylor, and Jalen Davis are the next three up. That leaves Josh Newton (2024 5th-rounder) and DJ Ivey (2023 7th-rounder) as the two competitors. Ivey currently has the edge over Newton, thanks in large part to the former’s better performance over the last few years. However, Newton is slowly but surely creeping up on Ivey’s position in the depth chart. He’s gotten an interception in three of their past practices, and has been slowly getting better over the course of this year’s training camp. He’s definitely making things interesting for the Bengals’ front office heading into the final roster cuts. Will Newton’s late-preseason push be enough to get him off the practice squad to start 2026? It’s hard to tell, but a great performance in the final preseason game against the Philadelphia Eagles should help him on that end. If he doesn’t perform well there, though, or gets outplayed by Ivey… well, he’s likely starting the season on the outside looking in. articles.title: Giants’ Matt Nagy teases exciting change on offense
articles.summary: Matt Nagy is not ready to hand over the blueprint just yet, but the New York Giants’ new offensive coordinator wants fans to know something different is coming. Asked this week what supporters should notice about the offense in 2026, Nagy leaned into the intrigue rather than the specifics.
articles._body: Matt Nagy is not ready to hand over the blueprint just yet, but the New York Giants’ new offensive coordinator wants fans to know something different is coming . Asked this week what supporters should notice about the offense in 2026, Nagy leaned into the intrigue rather than the specifics. “I would just say, you know, wait and see,” he told reporters . “I’m not going to get into a whole lot of the scheme part of it, but I think it’s going to be exciting. I think it’s going to be fun.” Matt Nagy was asked what he hopes Giants fans notice about the offense this season "I would just say wait and see. I think it's gonna be exciting, I think it's gonna be fun. We need to be able to be complementary. We're very optimistic on how this thing is gonna go" pic.twitter.com/0fgylUknrq — SNY Giants (@SNYGiants) August 25, 2026 Nagy stopped short of detailing any of the schematic wrinkles, but his message was one of confidence. He pointed to a strong offseason as the foundation, noting how the work carried over from OTAs into a productive training camp. “We’re very optimistic on how this thing’s going to go,” he said, before adding the necessary caveat that the group still has to prove it when the games count. The optimism is easy to trace. Nagy arrived in February as part of new head coach John Harbaugh’s staff, taking over a unit that finished 13th in total yards and tied for 17th in scoring during a 4-13 season. He inherits a young core with real upside, headlined by second-year quarterback Jaxson Dart , who flashed as a rookie with 15 touchdown passes and nine rushing scores despite an offense in transition around him. Dart will have more help this fall. Star receiver Malik Nabers is working his way back from the knee injury that cut short his 2025, and bruising back Cam Skattebo has returned from an ankle injury that ended his rookie season early. Tight end Isaiah Likely, who followed Harbaugh over from Baltimore, has already emerged as one of Dart’s most trusted targets in camp . Nagy also stressed the idea of complementary football, a nod to the offense working in concert with a retooled defense rather than carrying the load alone. It is a philosophy Harbaugh has preached for years, and one Nagy absorbed during four seasons alongside Andy Reid in Kansas City. For now, the specifics stay behind the curtain. But with Week 1 approaching, Nagy is betting the wait will be worth it. The post Giants’ Matt Nagy teases exciting change on offense appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles.title: Show HN: Hostflip – a macOS /etc/hosts switcher that detects external edits
articles.summary:
Hi HN — I built hostflip, a native macOS menu bar app for switching /etc/hosts profiles. It is free and open source under the MIT license.

The problem I wanted to solve was not just editing hosts entries. It was sharing /etc/hosts with Docker Desktop, VPN clients, scripts, and manual edits with
articles._body: Hi HN — I built hostflip, a native macOS menu bar app for switching /etc/hosts profiles. It is free and open source under the MIT license. The problem I wanted to solve was not just editing hosts entries. It was sharing /etc/hosts with Docker Desktop, VPN clients, scripts, and manual edits without one writer silently erasing another's changes. On first run, hostflip captures a read-only baseline (called Base Hosts) from the existing file and keeps the untouched original as hosts.orig. Active profiles are appended after the baseline in a clearly marked block. Writes are still atomic whole-file replacements under the hood. Before each write, the daemon hashes the live file and compares it with the expected hash. If they differ, it refuses the write; the app shows a diff and asks the user to reconcile the change first. A few other details: - Profiles can live in groups. At most one profile per group is active, while active profiles from different groups and standalone profiles stack together. - After a one-time approval in System Settings, subsequent switches no longer prompt for a password. The root helper is registered through SMAppService and exposes a single XPC operation: atomically replace the hosts file with merged content. The app and daemon verify each other's signing identity. - The bundled CLI shares the same workspace as the app and supports structured JSON output. hostflip doctor dev.example.com traces a hostname from profiles through the merged output and the live /etc/hosts file to the system resolver. - Remote profiles can refresh from HTTPS sources on a schedule. There is also an importer for existing SwitchHosts configurations. - The editor has cross-profile hostname/IP search, comment toggling, basic validation for malformed hosts lines, and stays responsive with large remote profiles. The app is built with Swift and SwiftUI, distributed through Homebrew or a signed and notarized DMG, and currently requires macOS 14 or later on Apple silicon. Intel, Windows, and Linux are not supported. I would especially like feedback on the conservative drift behavior: if another process changes /etc/hosts, hostflip blocks further writes to the system file until the user reviews the diff. How do you handle multiple writers to the hosts file, and would you expect a different reconciliation model? Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49444897 Points: 1 # Comments: 1

That t
articles._body: The WNBA had high expectations for its product after securing a historic collective bargaining agreement in the spring, and while there have been a plethora of notable achievements from both a team and individual perspective, media coverage continues to revolve around non-game story lines. That trend continued during Tuesday night’s battle between the Phoenix Mercury and Washington Mystics. A fan dampened the excitement surrounding Kelsey Plum’s home debut in the Mortgage Matchup Center. Once again, a sex toy was hurled onto the court during a WNBA game. This latest incident occurred in the final few minutes of the first half, forcing the action into a brief pause. Boos echoed the arena. The object was quickly removed from the area, and so was the perpetrator, per Eliav Gabay of Sports360AZ. Obscure object thrown on the court at #Mercury vs #Mystics in Phoenix. The object was quickly covered & the person who allegedly threw it was removed. @Sports360AZ pic.twitter.com/Tocd6MYAK5 — Eliav Gabay (@eliavgabay) August 26, 2026 The Chicago Sky experienced the same migraine in Friday night’s home game versus the Golden State Valkyrie. Players and coaches have had enough . Safety is always a concern when items are thrown, but it is also about the message that is being sent. Simply put, these women are being disrespected. Although Phoenix (13-25) did its best to flip the headlines back to basketball, the struggling squad could not overpower the visiting Mystics (23-15). Alyssa Thomas posted a double-double with three steals, Natasha Mack totaled 19 points, eight rebounds, three blocks and three steals of her own and Kahleah Copper added 19 points, but the Mercury still suffered a 94-84 loss in The Desert. Plum scored 10 points on just 4-of-12 shooting. Foul trouble limited her to 17 minutes of game time. Needless to say, it was not the first impression she wanted to make in Phoenix. The Mystics trio of Sonia Citron, Kiki Iriafen and Shakira Austin efficiently combined for 53 points in the victory. Ultimately, a significant amount of focus will be placed on the sex toy disruption. The WNBA should be running out of patience. articles.title: ‘It’s Hard to Imagine The World Without Her’: Australia’s Prime Minister Anthony Albanese Reflects on Dolly Parton
articles.summary: “Dolly Parton made our world a better place in so many ways," recounts Australia's leader.
articles._body: Dolly Parton isn’t a national icon. She’s an international icon. As fans from the music and entertainment communities share their memories of the late country music superstar, Australia’s prime minister Anthony Albanese has paid tribute to the “Jolene” singer and songwriter. “Dolly Parton made our world a better place in so many ways, it’s hard to imagine the world without her. A singer and songwriter of rare power and talent, she also shone brightly as an actor, author and philanthropist,” he writes in a social post, which is accompanied by a picture of the pair enjoying a laugh. “And the big, radiant heart of the Dolly universe was a personality as strong as it was compassionate, a vivacious woman of great humour and a sense of humanity sustained in no small part by the humble strength of her roots.” Parton made a rare trip to Australia for her Better Day tour of 2011. Michael Chugg was the promoter of that trek, her first of these parts in decades. Red tape, however, threatened to unravel the 12-show national trek, as Parton’s tour bus was found to flout the regulations. The vehicle was deemed to be too long, too wide for Australian roads. With the intervention of Albanese, who was federal transport minister at the time, in the Julia Gillard government, the shows went ahead. “One of the joys of my time in Government was when I was able to help Dolly overcome a bit of red tape and get her tour bus on to Australian roads in 2011. It was a magical experience meeting her, but what was even better was seeing her among her legions of local fans,” Albanese recounts. View this post on Instagram “There are a lot of broken hearts in Australia and across the world today. Wherever you are, turn your stereo or your phone to Dolly then turn the volume up. And may the great Dolly Parton rest in peace.” Parton returned to Australia in 2014 for six dates, part of her Blue Smoke World Tour . The “Islands In The Stream” artist had a special connection with Australia, and, particularly, the city of Melbourne, for which she was handed the keys to the city in 1987. The symbolic gesture “was the least we could do,” reads a social post from the City of Melbourne . “Dolly’s values of creativity and community are ones Melbourne shares. We are a city known for our love of music, and we embrace the songwriting legacy she leaves behind. As a UNESCO City of Literature, we’ll keep spreading the joy and importance of reading to the next generation. And as the inventors of the 8-hour day, we’ll be Workin’ 9 to 5 in your honor,” a nod to the 1980 comedy film, in which she starred, and its hit title track, which she performed. The state of Victoria’s peak body representing trade unions and hundreds of thousands of workers, the Victorian Trades Hall Council , also saluted Parton for her integrity and the choices she made to help countless others. “Dolly Parton could have been a billionaire. But instead, she chose to lift the rest of the world up,” reads a statement from the organization. “She created thousands of good jobs in the community she grew up in. She made sure that millions of children around the world have access to books in those vital early years. She donated millions to medical research. And she was a proud union member for over 50 years. Vale comrade Dolly.” Parton died in Nashville on Tuesday (Aug. 25) at the age of 80, leaving a legacy that will be cherished for as long as people listen to music. Named Billboard’s top country artist of all time in 2024, Dolly was a cultural and commercial force. She landed 49 albums in the top 10 on Billboard’s Top Country Albums chart, the most of any woman, and she landed more No. 1s on the Hot Country Songs chart for a woman artist, with 25. In 1999, she was inducted into the Country Music Hall of Fame, and in 2022, elevated into the Rock And Roll Hall of Fame.

articles._body: Collin Gillespie had a breakout campaign with the Phoenix Suns last season after struggling to carve out a role in his first years in the NBA. Some even considered him a candidate for Most Improved Player after putting up career-best numbers. In his third season, he averaged 12.7 points, 4.1 rebounds, 4.6 assists, and 1.2 steals in 80 games, including 58 starts. He shot 40.1% from long range. He was a perfect complement to Devin Booker , who continued to be the go-to guy for the Suns. A podcast, however, belittled Booker’s impact on the team. “Book affects one part of the game very strongly: Scoring. He doesn’t do that in defense. He doesn’t do that in playmaking to the level that it takes to take your team all the way. He can affect one phase of the game, not all three,” claimed the podcast. Gillespie did not approve . He shared it on X and wrote “Bad take” in the caption. bad take https://t.co/XbAOxRMI9F — Collin Gillespie (@Colling1021) August 26, 2026 Booker had another stellar season, putting up 26.1 points, 3.9 rebounds, and 6.0 assists in 64 games. He remained the driving force of the Suns with his two-way acumen. Perhaps more importantly, his selflessness helped improve the numbers of Gillespie, Dillon Brooks, Royce O’Neale, and Jordan Goodwin, all of whom averaged career-highs in scoring. With Booker leading the charge, the Suns had a 45-37 record and returned to the playoffs after a one-year absence. They, however, were swept in the first round by the Oklahoma City Thunder. Phoenix will enter the new season with a retooled roster, adding Miles Bridges, Luke Kennard, and Koa Peat. articles._body: Golden State Warriors veteran Draymond Green knows a thing or two about elite talent, and he recognizes a special aura when he sees it. Speaking on the broadcast panel during Shaquille O’Neal’s inaugural Dunkman World Championship event, Green got real about legendary dunker Mac McClung. “Mac McClung has IT,” Green said during the event coverage. “Like he’s a guy who, when the stage is big, he’s just got it. Some people has it, it’s that thing you can’t explain.” "Mac McClung has IT." @Money23Green believes Mac McClung has the “it” factor pic.twitter.com/NagXA2GTHA — TNT Sports U.S. (@TNTSportsUS) August 26, 2026 Coming from a four-time NBA champion known for his high basketball IQ, high praise like that carries serious weight. McClung has carved out an iconic reputation as one of the greatest showmen of this generation, previously becoming the first player to win three consecutive NBA Slam Dunk Contests. Even when facing high-stakes adversity, the 6-foot-2 guard continues to leave audiences speechless. Entering the Dunkman event as the top seed in Atlanta, McClung ended up suffering a shocking early-round exit at the hands of Dengxing Chen. However, before his elimination, McClung delivered the viral highlight of the night by launching himself over a car packed with three people stacked inside to throw down an absurd finish. While he didn’t secure the $500,000 grand prize, McClung’s flair for the dramatic proved Green’s point once again. For McClung, who spent part of the 2025–26 NBA regular season with the Chicago Bulls , highlighted by a 13-point outing in 18 minutes of action during a 149-128 loss to the Dallas Mavericks, the showmanship remains unmatched. Yan entered the ninth inning with runners on second and third and one out after Milwaukee had tied the game. He st
articles._body: New York Mets shortstop Francisco Lindor backed rookie reliever Jefry Yan’s animated celebrations Tuesday following a 3-2, 10-inning victory over the Milwaukee Brewers at Citi Field. Yan entered the ninth inning with runners on second and third and one out after Milwaukee had tied the game. He struck out Garrett Mitchell and then walked Joey Ortiz, loading the bases with two outs. David Hamilton then lined Yan’s sinker toward left field, but Lindor made a diving backhand catch to end the threat. Yan responded by pounding the turf in celebration. SNY Mets shared Lindor’s comments through its official account on X, formerly Twitter, after the narrow win by New York. “Vibes are contagious. He should continue to jump, he should continue to be himself. At the end of the day, Jefry got here for a reason and he continues to be himself. He shouldn’t tame it because people are saying it should be tamed.” "Vibes are contagious. He should continue to jump, he should continue to be himself. At the end of the day, Jefry got here for a reason and he continues to be himself. He shouldn't tame it because people are saying it should be tamed." – Francisco Lindor on Jefry Yan pic.twitter.com/rvxSZPuNUR — SNY Mets (@SNY_Mets) August 26, 2026 Lindor’s endorsement followed the southpaw’s tough outing Friday against the Chicago White Sox. Yan began celebrating what he believed was strike three against Colson Montgomery, but the pitch was called a ball. Montgomery eventually walked, and Jake Rogers hit a two-run walk-off homer that gave Chicago a 6-4 victory. Yan acknowledged afterward that he needed to wait until the play was complete before celebrating. Lindor’s comments supported the rookie’s personality while leaving room for him to learn from the mistake. Yan spent four years outside professional baseball following a serious elbow injury. He worked in roofing and home delivery while training to resume his career, eventually returning to professional baseball and making his major league debut on August 5. New York won Tuesday when the Mets infielder scored from second as the automatic runner in the 10th. Hamilton’s throw home on Christopher Morel’s grounder sailed wide, helping the club to improve to 60-72. Lindor’s defense, winning run, and support for Yan paired his performance with a message about preserving individuality while learning from mistakes. However, Ball ran into seemingly nonstop knee issues whi
articles._body: Lonzo Ball’s NBA career is quickly turning into a what-if story. Ball had been emerging as a winning player to start the 2020s, and he played a huge role in leading the Chicago Bulls back to the playoffs during the 2021-22 NBA season. However, Ball ran into seemingly nonstop knee issues which kept him out of action for two full seasons, and his career was never the same. In fact, Ball looked washed during the 2025-26 season, suiting up in just 35 games (three starts) for the Cleveland Cavaliers before the Cavs pulled the plug on the Ball experiment. With the Cavs, Ball shot a ghastly 30.1 percent from the field, and upon arriving with the Utah Jazz in a salary dump prior to the 2025 NBA trade deadline, he was waived. He hasn’t been on an NBA team since. Now that Ball is staring at the legitimate possibility that his NBA career is over, he looked back at some of the regrets he has for how the start of his career went, when his father, LaVar, was the driving force behind all of his decisions behind the scenes. “I had no structure, bro. I literally was just hooping and following my pops, listening to my pops. We had the (Big Baller Brand) going. … I never went to any Nike deal, no Adidas deal. I never heard no offers or nothing. I was not part of that s**t. I was just doing what I was told really. I guess that would be my one regret, like taking control of my career earlier,” Ball said in an appearance on Michael Porter Jr.’s “Curious Mike” podcast. Ball was indeed rocking BBB shoes to support the family brand, and he wanted to honor his father when he did that. However, if granted a chance to do it all over again, he would do things differently. “If I can go back, I would obviously do it different. I will actually get an agent, be in the meetings myself, do what I want to do,” Ball added. The post Lonzo Ball reveals regret about career involving dad LaVar appeared first on ClutchPoints .

After 35K+ users and 7M+ workflows, we spent the last few months attacking the cost of every agent step: - switching to DeepSeek Flash - Code Mode to one shot complex workflows - optimizing for 80%+ token cache hits So that now just an ad impression covers the entire cost of the agent (LLM inference included), so we can now offer the entire agent for free! More important than an agent that can scale with users, is an agent that gets better with every workflow. Retriever now continuously: → learns global skills for every website, so no mistake repeats twice → writes learnings from user tasks as personalized skills Curious to hear how others are tackling consumer agents and excited for the new era of free agentic apps! articles._body: Many are expecting Jordan Love to have a breakout campaign for the Green Bay Packers in the upcoming season. After an impressive stint last year, all signs point to the seventh-year quarterback earning his first appearance in the Pro Bowl or even his first nod to the All-Pro Team. Last month, Micah Parsons grabbed attention for his blunt reaction to Love being ranked No. 72 on the NFL’s top 100 list. On X, Parsons said: “Seventy-one players in the NFL aren’t better than Jordan Love!” Last season, Love threw for 3,381 yards, 23 touchdowns, and six interceptions. He tallied a 101.2 passer rating and was among the leaders in advanced statistics, a testament to Love’s improved efficiency . On “The Edge,” Parsons doubled down on his stance on Love. “I think Jordan is gonna be a top-five quarterback this year. I think he’s gonna show the world how great he really can be,” said the veteran enforcer. “When we go through our top 100 as players, fans, they’re like, ‘Oh, so-and-so is an All-Pro’ or ‘So-and-so was not an All-Pro,’ that’s not what we’re talking about. We’re talking about when I’m playing you on the field.” Micah sounds off after Jordan Love was ranked No. 72 on the NFL Top 100 Season Premiere of The Edge: https://t.co/R8pUD9t95M https://t.co/bpm2jInEf5 pic.twitter.com/rIdUoTjN59 — Bleacher Report (@BleacherReport) August 25, 2026 When asked to compare Love to other signal-callers ranked above him, including Trevor Lawrence of the Jacksonville Jaguars, Bo Nix of the Denver Broncos, Drake Maye of the New England Patriots, and Jared Goff of the Detroit Lions, Parsons continued to tout his teammate. “We swept the Detroit Lions last year. Jordan Love put up 30-plus (points) against one of the top defenses in the NFL. Come on, bro,” added the five-time Pro Bowler. Clearly, Parsons was deeply impressed with Love in his first stint with the Packers. He was traded to Green Bay by the Dallas Cowboys last season in exchange for Kenny Clark and two first-round picks. He is still recovering from an ACL injury. After reaching base on a high popup to right field that one would think would land on a Mets fielder’s glove, young shortstop Cooper Pratt rece
articles._body: A bit of controversy arose for the Milwaukee Brewers in the early goings of what would eventually be a 3-2 loss to the New York Mets in 11 innings. After reaching base on a high popup to right field that one would think would land on a Mets fielder’s glove, young shortstop Cooper Pratt received some tough love from manager Pat Murphy, as the Brewers pinch ran David Hamilton for the 22-year-old. The Brewers coaching staff felt as though Pratt did not hustle enough out of the batter’s box, and they expected him to be on second base after the ball landed fair on the aforementioned popup. Moreover, Pratt did not execute on the coaching staff’s instructions during his first at-bat, as he failed to lay down a bunt with runners on second and first with just one out in the inning. But at the end of the day, the Brewers shortstop took his benching on the chin and accepted the manager’s decision graciously, vowing that what he did on Tuesday will never happen again. “Our goal is to win. My job is to help the team win. I didn’t do that today. They hold you accountable, which is good. I need that. It will never happen again,” Pratt told reporters after the game, via Lily Zhao of FOX6 News. Cooper Pratt knows the standards are high with the #Brewers : "It will never happen again." pic.twitter.com/xDzGjhzTPE — Lily Zhao (@LilySZhao) August 26, 2026 Some Brewers fans believe that the manager was harsh on Pratt and he was simply using the 22-year-old to make an example out of to keep them focused with the final month of the regular season approaching. Whatever the case may be, this benching appears to have lit a fire underneath Pratt, who has been solid for the Brewers during his brief time in the big leagues thus far. His defense at shortstop has been solid, and his presence may have prevented Milwaukee from losing the way they did — with Hamilton, the man who pinch ran for Pratt, being guilty of the game-losing errant throw to home plate. articles.title: Brewers manager Pat Murphy explains why he benched Cooper Pratt in loss to Mets
articles.summary: Milwaukee Brewers manager Pat Murphy benched rookie shortstop Cooper Pratt during Tuesday night’s 3-2, 10-inning loss to the New York Mets after two mistakes in the game left Murphy wanting a better display of focus and effort. Pratt’s first issue came in the third inning against Mets
articles._body: Milwaukee Brewers manager Pat Murphy benched rookie shortstop Cooper Pratt during Tuesday night’s 3-2, 10-inning loss to the New York Mets after two mistakes in the game left Murphy wanting a better display of focus and effort. Pratt’s first issue came in the third inning against Mets starter Zac Thornton. After Garrett Mitchell and Joey Ortiz opened the inning with singles, Murphy asked Pratt to lay down a bunt with two runners aboard and nobody out. Pratt fouled off the first bunt attempt, then pulled the bat back on a fastball over the middle for strike two. He later fouled off two more pitches before hitting a comebacker to Thornton, who threw to third to force Mitchell. Thornton then retired Jackson Chourio and Brice Turang to end the threat. Two innings later, Murphy made the decision to remove Pratt after a shallow fly ball to right field. The ball dropped between three New York defenders and got past right fielder Carson Benge. Although the play resulted in a single, Pratt did not immediately run hard out of the batter’s box and was held to first base. Murphy believed Pratt could have reached second. “He’s a young player,” the two-time defending National League Manager of the Year said . “We asked him to get a bunt down and he pulled back on a strike. That happens, maybe, with one strike trying to get the guy to second and third for Chourio in a game where we weren’t swinging it too good to that point. We get first and second and ask him to bunt. [The] first one was a good attempt. Second one he pulled back on a strike right down the middle.. “I know who this kid is. He’s a great kid. It’s not laziness. You gotta have your head in the game. These games, like today, come down to Lindor’s great catch, an errant throw, whatever it may be, you’ve got to be locked in if you’re going to play at this level. So it was hopefully a good learning experience,” Murphy added. Murphy also made clear that Pratt is not expected to rely on home-run power at this stage of his career and therefore must consistently handle the smaller aspects of the game. “I love the kid and I believe in the kid immensely,” Murphy said. “But he’s got to be a player who does those [little] things. He’s not going to hit 30 homers at this point in his career. He’s a great defender and a really capable offensive player, and he can’t have that. It’s just not tolerated by anybody and it sends a message to everybody else, too, of, ‘You got to run.'” David Hamilton replaced Pratt as the pinch-runner and remained at third base, with Joey Ortiz moving to shortstop. Hamilton later became involved in the game’s fateful moment. In the 10th inning, with the bases loaded and one out, Christopher Morel hit a grounder to Hamilton’s left. Hamilton stopped the ball but rushed his throw home, sending it into the backstop and allowing the winning run to score. Pratt, who turned 22 last week, accepted responsibility afterward. He said the mistakes were inexcusable and repeatedly stated that they would not happen again. The rookie is batting .259 with two home runs, 18 RBIs and 10 stolen bases in 49 games for Milwaukee. The Brewers signed him to an eight-year, $50.75 million contract around two and a half months after selecting him in the sixth round of the 2023 amateur draft, and he made his major-league debut on June 16. The post Brewers manager Pat Murphy explains why he benched Cooper Pratt in loss to Mets appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles._body: The New York Giants are ushering in a brand-new era , and young quarterback Jaxson Dart is already buying into the leadership at the top. As the Giants navigate training camp and prepare for the upcoming campaign, Dart opened up about what has impressed him most regarding new head coach John Harbaugh . While Harbaugh brings a proven championship track record and intense detail to East Rutherford, the young signal-caller pointed to something much more personal as his standout trait. “The biggest thing that stands out with him is his relationships with his players,” Dart said when reflecting on Harbaugh’s impact on the locker room. "The biggest thing that stands out with him is his relationships with his players." @Giants QB Jaxson Dart discussed what HC John Harbaugh has brought to New York. https://t.co/dbQUay20PB #NYGiants | @BobPapa_NFL | @SimmsComplete pic.twitter.com/n39IqjvXWt — SiriusXM NFL Radio (@SiriusXMNFL) August 25, 2026 That player-first dynamic has already paid off during on-field adversity this preseason. In the Giants’ 13-10 preseason clash against the Minnesota Vikings, Dart got a firsthand taste of Harbaugh’s protective leadership. After taking a brutal unblocked hit from blitzing safety Jay Ward that sent the quarterback to the medical tent to be evaluated, Harbaugh did not mince words postgame. While Dart cleared evaluation and quickly returned to bounce back in style, completing 3 of 4 passes for 26 yards, capped off by a 15-yard touchdown strike to rookie wide receiver Malachi Fields, Harbaugh immediately focused on protecting his young passer. “We just keep playing football, and we’ll just try to do a better job of protecting him,” Harbaugh said firmly. “And there’s no way he should have been hit there.” That unwavering backing speaks volumes to a developing quarterback. For a franchise aiming to build a winning culture, Harbaugh’s mix of high accountability and genuine connection is already establishing a strong foundation with Dart leading the charge under center. articles.title: Chiefs’ most agonizing roster decision looming on 2026 cutdown day
articles.summary: Kansas City has spent the 2026 offseason trying to rebuild the margins around Patrick Mahomes. However, their final roster decisions may prove more painful than the biggest personnel moves. One of the most intriguing battles is for a place behind Mahomes and Justin Fields. Garrett Nussmeier has p
articles._body: Kansas City has spent the 2026 offseason trying to rebuild the margins around Patrick Mahomes. However, their final roster decisions may prove more painful than the biggest personnel moves. One of the most intriguing battles is for a place behind Mahomes and Justin Fields. Garrett Nussmeier has performed well enough throughout camp to make keeping three quarterbacks a genuinely tempting proposition. That said, doing so would consume one of the precious 53 roster spots that Kansas City could otherwise use to protect another promising contributor. Roster crunch Denny Medley-Imagn Images The urgency of this impending deadline has been amplified by everything that unfolded throughout the 2026 preseason campaign. Kansas City utilized the summer exhibition slate as an aggressive laboratory under returning offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy. With Patrick Mahomes intentionally held out of live contact drills, backup signal-callers Justin Fields, Garrett Nussmeier, and Chris Oladokun absorbed heavy live reps. Meanwhile, newly acquired feature back Kenneth Walker III established a dynamic backfield presence alongside Emari Demercado and Brashard Smith. Steve Spagnuolo’s defense also generated relentless pressure and physical perimeter play. With clear starting hierarchies solidified across the core units, the preseason film has forced the front office into a brutal roster bottleneck. That is precisely why Nussmeier has become such a fascinating problem. The Chiefs know that Mahomes is the franchise. They also know Fields gives them a dynamic alternative. Nussmeier, though, has made himself impossible to ignore. Quarterback dilemma Do the Chiefs keep three quarterbacks on the active 53-man roster to protect Nussmeier? Carrying three signal-callers is a luxury that modern NFL contenders rarely afford. A third quarterback is unlikely to play on a normal Sunday. That means that spot could instead belong to another offensive lineman, defensive back, pass rusher or special-teams contributor. Ordinarily, that would make the decision straightforward. Nussmeier has changed the equation. Throughout training camp and exhibition action, he has intriguing poise and arm talent. More importantly, he has shown an ability to process the offense quickly rather than merely surviving with simplified responsibilities. At this point, Nussmeier represents developmental insurance with legitimate long-term potential. The Chiefs therefore have to decide whether that potential is worth sacrificing a roster spot elsewhere. Perilous gamble If Kansas City attempts to sneak Nussmeier through waivers and onto the practice squad, there is a very real possibility another organization claims him. Quarterbacks with developmental upside are difficult to find. Quarterback-needy teams are not. They are constantly searching for inexpensive alternatives. A franchise willing to invest in Nussmeier’s development could claim him and immediately place him on its active roster. That would leave Kansas City with no opportunity to reclaim him anymore. That is the nightmare scenario. The Chiefs could save a roster spot today only to watch Nussmeier become valuable elsewhere tomorrow. The alternative is equally uncomfortable. Keeping Nussmeier means cutting another player who may eventually become a contributor. Kansas City would effectively be accepting short-term roster inefficiency in exchange for protecting a potentially valuable quarterback asset. Of course, QB development is difficult. The Chiefs understand better than most organizations how quickly a young passer can become enormously valuable. Losing a promising quarterback for nothing because of a numbers crunch could haunt the front office if injuries eventually expose the depth chart. Collateral damage Now, keeping Nussmeier on the active roster results in collateral damage elsewhere. Kansas City could be forced to make a difficult decision involving the secondary. Proven veterans such as Kristian Fulton and Kaiir Elam are already competing with promising depth pieces such as Jadon Canady. Losing a capable corner because of roster mathematics could leave Spagnuolo with less flexibility during a long season. The same dilemma exists along the offensive line. Swing tackles such as Esa Pole or Ethan Driskell could become vulnerable if the Chiefs need to maximize depth at other positions . Behind starters Josh Simmons and Kahlil Benson, maintaining enough versatility to survive injuries is critical. That is what makes the quarterback decision so consequential. It is never really just about the quarterback. Defining cutdown decision Denny Medley-Imagn Images Ultimately, Kansas City must determine how much it values immediate roster flexibility versus long-term quarterback security. The conservative approach would be to keep only Mahomes and Fields active. They would then move Nussmeier through waivers and use the extra roster spot elsewhere. On the other hand, the aggressive approach may be the smarter one. Kansas City is not building for tomorrow. It is all about winning now while simultaneously protecting the future. If Nussmeier has genuinely demonstrated enough developmental promise to attract interest around the league, sacrificing one roster spot to keep him may be a price worth paying. The post Chiefs’ most agonizing roster decision looming on 2026 cutdown day appeared first on ClutchPoints .
