articles.title: 1 Saints position group that could step up after Jordyn Tyson’s injury
articles.summary: The New Orleans Saints received a major gut punch to their passing attack before the regular season even kicked off. Rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson, selected eighth overall in the 2026 NFL Draft out of Arizona State, is expected to miss roughly two months after suffering a severe right hamstri
articles._body: The New Orleans Saints received a major gut punch to their passing attack before the regular season even kicked off. Rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson, selected eighth overall in the 2026 NFL Draft out of Arizona State, is expected to miss roughly two months after suffering a severe right hamstring injury during training camp. Losing a dynamic first-round playmaker leaves a massive void out wide, especially after the offense struggled to find rhythm in their 34-0 preseason loss to the Los Angeles Rams. However, New Orleans might not need to look far for a quick offensive pivot. On NFL Network’s “The Insiders,” league insider Mike Garafolo highlighted how head coach Kellen Moore and the coaching staff can shift their tactical focus toward the tight end room. “The Saints felt good about Delp, he’s currently dealing with a hamstring injury, doesn’t sound like a big deal,” Garafolo reported. “That’s really interesting information for you to say, okay cool, we’re banged up at the receiver position, we can lean on our tight ends.” From The Insiders on @nflnetwork following @wyche89 talking about the #Saints leaning on their TEs, especially with Jordyn Tyson shelved with a hamstring injury. Rookie Oscar Delp has one of his own but it doesn’t sound like it’s too significant. pic.twitter.com/FSrDtNjes0 — Mike Garafolo (@MikeGarafolo) August 26, 2026 Rookie tight end Oscar Delp brings the size and soft hands needed to clear up space across the middle of the field. While Delp is nursing a minor hamstring tweak of his own, his expected quick return makes him a logical focal point alongside veteran Juwan Johnson. Leaning heavily into multi-tight end sets allows New Orleans to shield its thinned-out wide receiver room, give quarterback Tyler Shough reliable safety valves, and stay physical in the intermediate passing game. The Saints still have work to do before Week 1, but recalibrating around their tight ends offers a clear blueprint to keep the offense moving until Tyson returns. articles.title: Taylor Swift Remembers Dolly Parton as ‘True Grace & True Grit, All in One Dazzling Person’
articles.summary: The legendary Parton died Tuesday after a battle with cancer.
articles._body: Dolly Parton and Taylor Swift never recorded a song together, but openly shared a mutual admiration. Now, Swift is sharing her heartfelt appreciation for Parton, who died Tuesday (Aug. 25) at age 80, thanking her for “the melodies and lyrics she wrote that thawed even the coldest hearts.” Swift praised Parton for her songwriting and also for her philanthropy and just general Dolly-ness. Related Dolly Parton Cause of Death Revealed Watch Jack White Cover ‘Jolene’ in London Hours After Dolly Parton’s Death: ‘Instant Sainthood’ Dolly Parton Chose Her Funeral Song More Than a Decade Ago & Left an Unreleased Song to Be Heard in 2046 “A world without Dolly doesn’t feel possible, real, or right,” Swift wrote in a statement provided to Billboard . “But because of the eternally generous way she spent her time on this earth and the countless lives she changed for the better, her legacy will be an everlasting one.” She lauded Parton for knowing her own value as a creator, something the two artists shared: “She possessed the softest heart when it came to the struggles of others, and a backbone of steel to defend her own self worth as an artist,” Swift said. Just last month, Parton took to social media to thank Swift and her then-fiancé Travis Kelce for their $2 million donation to Parton’s Imagination Library as part of their $26 million in charitable giving prior to the pair’s July 3 wedding. Parton even jokingly asked, “Hey, when you have your first born can I have it? Because that is going to be one special baby.” Parton often praised Swift, telling E! News last year , “I’m just crazy about Taylor. I just admire her so much for what she’s done with her life. Her career. Such a great artist and songwriter.” Swift’s statement in full is below. Like so many tributes to the icon, Swift even managed to fit in a reference to Parton’s most famous and enduring song, “I Will Always Love You”: “A world without Dolly doesn’t feel possible, real, or right. But because of the eternally generous way she spent her time on this earth and the countless lives she changed for the better, her legacy will be an everlasting one. She was truly the gift that kept on giving. Dolly gave us someone to look up to while encouraging us to be who we are as individuals. Somehow, she was able to give us her lessons about the world gently and honestly, simultaneously, and oftentimes hilariously. She managed to give the world the ultimate mystery and fantasy in some corners of her life, but to give full transparency in the ways that counted. Somehow, she was true grace and true grit, all in one dazzling person. She possessed the softest heart when it came to the struggles of others, and a backbone of steel to defend her own self worth as an artist. Along with her other fans, I am so grateful for all of it. For the melodies and lyrics she wrote that thawed even the coldest hearts. For the millions of books she provided children all over the world so that they might fall in love with stories the way she did. For the tightropes she walked so that young girls like me could grow up dreaming of joining the circus too. Dolly, I’ll think of you each step of the way.”

articles._body: Hello HN, After seeing all of the pushback and negative sentiment regarding GitHub and its poor reliability and everyone trying to move off of it, I decided to build this to make the transition easier. articles.summary: Mississippi State added depth on the defensive line with the addition of West Virginia transfer Eddie Kelly Jr. on Tuesday.
articles._body: Mississippi State head coach Jeff Lebby and defensive coordinator Zach Arnett have a new weapon on the defensive line in an unorthodox time of the season. The Bulldogs added Eddie Kelly Jr. through the transfer portal on Tuesday, per Pete Nakos, making Starkville the fifth FBS stop in the player’s career. Kelly entered the transfer portal earlier in the day on Tuesday and it wasn’t long before he picked his new home. BREAKING: Former West Virginia DL Eddie Kelly Jr. has signed with Mississippi State, @PeteNakos reports https://t.co/kSYG7dYADj https://t.co/utZ0h2s3uL pic.twitter.com/QysNDo1hPG — Transfer Portal (@TransferPortal) August 26, 2026 Kelley joined West Virginia for the 2025 season and played in all 12 games for the Mountaineers. He made four starts on the defensive line with 394 snaps on defense and special teams, and finished the campaign with 26 tackles, 1.5 tackles for loss, 0.5 sack and three pass breakups. According to WV Sports , Kelly sought an extra year of eligibility in July by filing for a temporary restraining order and preliminary injunction. He was reportedly still in game shape after training for action in the UFL, but did not reach the professional ranks. Kelly played for a season each at Missouri, Georgia Tech and USF before he made his way to Morgantown.

articles.title: Marshall Faulk gives update on return of star Southern player after court order
articles.summary: Marshall Faulk and Southern University could see the return of one of their best players from last season, former Southern University defensive star Ckelby Givens. Givens appeared to have played his last game for Southern University in last year’s Bayou Classic, but per Faulk, he is eligibl
articles._body: Marshall Faulk and Southern University could see the return of one of their best players from last season, former Southern University defensive star Ckelby Givens. Givens appeared to have played his last game for Southern University in last year’s Bayou Classic, but per Faulk, he is eligible to return for a fifth season and could be playing on Saturday when the team faces off against Alabama State. Here is Marshall Faulk's full answer on Ckelby Givens' eligibility. Faulk added that it would be nice to get 5-10 plays out of Givens for now. https://t.co/obP8wAZzxY pic.twitter.com/vyAXM3AabF — Kevin Batiste (@KBatisteJr) August 25, 2026 “My understanding is Ckelby is in with that group of guys that vowed to stay in the state of Louisiana and I believe with that, as that stay is, it allows him to play until something else is said. We’re looking for guidance from the NCAA or the lawmakers to tell us by Friday what we are to do and [I’m going to] follow the law. The law says that he can play and we’re happy to have him.” When he was asked if Givens will play, Faulk answered simply, “To my knowledge, he’s playing.” Givens was a pivotal player for Southern University the past four years and appeared to have an immediate NFL future. After four years at the institution, he finished last season with 41 total tackles, 23 solo tackles, 9.5 sacks for 81 yards lost, 2 forced fumbles, 1 fumble recovery, 5 quarterback hits, and 2 pass breakups. He then declared for the 2026 NFL Draft but went unselected and was ultimately invited to the Buffalo Bills’ rookie minicamp on a tryout basis, but he was not signed to the roster. Givens’ eligibility is part of the wider legal fight surrounding the NCAA’s new five-year eligibility model. On July 31, a federal judge in Colorado issued a class-wide preliminary injunction in Wisne v. NCAA. The injunction protected Division I athletes who began competing during the 2022-23 academic year, completed four seasons of eligibility by the end of the 2025-26 academic year, and were excluded from the NCAA’s new five-year eligibility rule. Last Friday, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the 10th Circuit granted the NCAA’s request to stay that preliminary injunction while the appeal proceeds. The decision temporarily removed the blanket federal protection that could have allowed thousands of athletes an additional season of eligibility, but it did not issue a final ruling on the lawsuit. Givens, however, has obtained a separate temporary restraining order that currently prevents the NCAA from barring him from competing. That order, rather than the now-stayed class-wide injunction in Wisne, is the immediate legal basis for Southern’s expectation that Givens can play on Saturday. Because the restraining order is temporary, his eligibility could still be affected by further court action. The Wisne lawsuit was filed on behalf of athletes such as Givens who began playing college sports during the 2022-23 academic year, completed four seasons by the end of the 2025-26 season, and were not included in the NCAA’s new five-year eligibility model. In the SWAC Coaches Call on Monday, Faulk said there was no clarity on Givens’ situation. “None right now,” Faulk said when asked about Givens’ eligibility. “We understand the situation that we’re in. You know, it’s the ebbs and flows.” The post Marshall Faulk gives update on return of star Southern player after court order appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles.title: Braves’ Spencer Strider still among starters who are unlikely to return this season
articles.summary: The past three seasons have been rough on the injury front for Atlanta Braves starter Spencer Strider. Strider made just two starts in 2024 before undergoing Tommy John surgery, which then kept him out for the majority of 2024 and rendered him relatively ineffective in 2025. There was hope that S
articles._body: The past three seasons have been rough on the injury front for Atlanta Braves starter Spencer Strider. Strider made just two starts in 2024 before undergoing Tommy John surgery, which then kept him out for the majority of 2024 and rendered him relatively ineffective in 2025. There was hope that Strider was going to start pitching at a level more reminiscent of his pre-Tommy John self as he distanced himself even further from that injury, but he’s remained stricken by injury woes in 2026. It was back in June when Strider was placed on the injured list due to right elbow inflammation. He only made eight starts this year before succumbing to another serious injury, and with September fast approaching, the 27-year-old remains on the sidelines. However, the deeper the Braves go into the regular season, the more unlikely it gets for Strider to return to the mound this year. As per Mark Bowman of MLB.com, there are no updates regarding the throwing program of Strider; while the Braves haven’t ruled out a potential return for their former ace, it would take a miraculous recovery and an equally as divine of a rehab process for him to make it back to the big-league team this year. Along with Strider, Spencer Schwellenbach and Hurston Waldrep are also among those the Braves did not have updates for. Schwellenbach is currently on the 60-day injured list along with Strider, as he is also dealing with an elbow injury. Meanwhile, Waldrep exited a start in Triple-A back in July due to right arm discomfort, and he hasn’t returned to action since. Strider, in eight starts this year, recorded an ERA of 5.30 across 39.0 innings of work. His lack of command remains concerning, and he is yet to even come close to his pre-injury level of play. The Braves will be cautious in bringing him back, as they must be hopeful still of getting the version of Strider who was putting up an argument for being the best pitcher in MLB. articles._body: With Paige Bueckers leading the charge, the Dallas Wings secured the final ticket to the playoffs on Tuesday after blowing out the Portland Fire, 96-78, at College Park Center. The Wings notched their third straight win and improved to 23-16, including 13-6 at home. The Fire, on the other hand, suffered their third consecutive loss and dropped to 15-23. Bueckers had 22 points, four rebounds, 11 assists, and two steals in an all-around performance in 33 minutes. According to ESPN Insights, the Wings’ 23 wins are their most since 2007, when the franchise was still known as the Detroit Shock. It also noted that Bueckers achieved another milestone . “Paige Bueckers recorded her 2nd game with 20 points and 10 assists this season, tied for the most in a season in Wings history,” said the post on X. The Wings clinch a playoff spot as they got their 23rd win of the season, their most in any season since 2007 when the franchise was known as the Detroit Shock. Paige Bueckers recorded her 2nd game with 20 points and 10 assists this season, tied for the most in a season in… pic.twitter.com/oocSEVbM19 — ESPN Insights (@ESPNInsights) August 26, 2026 The 24-year-old Bueckers, who was coming off a 32-point explosion against the Seattle Storm on Sunday, has had to carry a heavier load after the season-ending injury to Azzi Fudd. But she is used to being the go-to gal, even during her days at Connecticut , so embracing a bigger role is not a problem. She had plenty of help against the Fire, as her fellow starters all scored in double digits. Jessica Sheppard had 21 points, nine rebounds, six assists, and two steals, while Awak Kuier added 12 points, 12 rebounds, three steals, and five blocks. Arike Ogunbowale and Alanna Smith combined for 27 points, six rebounds, six assists, and three steals. Dallas shot 55% from the field, including 11-of-24 from long range, and led by as much as 26 points. The Wings will face the Connecticut Sun on Sunday. articles.title: Bills’ most agonizing roster decision looming on 2026 cutdown day
articles.summary: The Buffalo Bills certainly have enough talent to make difficult decisions, and now that depth is becoming their biggest headache. A so far undefeated summer has left Sean McDermott’s staff with an enviable problem as the roster deadline approaches. Nowhere is the squeeze more painful than
articles._body: The Buffalo Bills certainly have enough talent to make difficult decisions, and now that depth is becoming their biggest headache. A so far undefeated summer has left Sean McDermott’s staff with an enviable problem as the roster deadline approaches. Nowhere is the squeeze more painful than in the backfield. That’s where Frank Gore Jr and Ian Wheeler have turned a seemingly minor depth battle into one of the most compelling competitions on the entire roster. With James Cook III entrenched atop the depth chart and Ray Davis and Ty Johnson providing proven complementary options, Buffalo may have room for only one more traditional running back. Overwhelming organizational depth Scott Galvin-Imagn Images The Bills launched their exhibition slate by inaugurating their state-of-the-art venue with a commanding 29-14 triumph over the Carolina Panthers. When the coaching staff rested nearly the entire starting lineup for a road showdown against the Cleveland Browns, the reserve units delivered a masterclass. They pulled away for an emphatic 31-7 rout. Meanwhile, the defense’s new Base 3-4 scheme has smothered opposing offenses, allowing an average of fewer than 200 total yards per contest. Now, the front office faces the daunting reality that several legitimate NFL-caliber contributors simply cannot fit onto the active roster. Crowded backfield When evaluating the entire depth chart, the most agonizing decision facing Buffalo resides directly in the running back room. Gore has become a fan favorite, but his place on the final roster is threatened by the explosive Wheeler. Again, Cook remains the clear centerpiece after his spectacular production atop the league’s rushing hierarchy. Davis and Johnson provide established complementary options. Add fullback Ben VanSumeren to the equation, however, and the roster math becomes increasingly unforgiving. Keeping four traditional tailbacks alongside a dedicated fullback is a luxury in the NFL. Doing so would mean sacrificing depth somewhere else. That makes the Gore-Wheeler competition a philosophical decision about what Buffalo wants from its final offensive roster spot. Does the team prioritize the dependable runner who understands the offense? Do they chase the explosive athletic ceiling? Vision against explosion Gore and Wheeler represent two completely different interpretations of what a reserve running back should provide. Gore’s appeal begins with his running style. He is a decisive, north-south runner who consistently searches for the correct crease. His low center of gravity allows him to absorb contact. Meanwhile, his vision gives him an ability to salvage yardage when blocking breaks down. Gore’s understanding of pass protection also gives Buffalo a reliable option on obvious passing downs. His situational awareness allows offensive coaches to keep the playbook intact. A reserve back who knows where to be can be more valuable than a more explosive player who occasionally creates assignment problems. Wheeler, however, presents an entirely different proposition. His track-level speed can transform an ordinary handoff into an explosive play. Give him a crease on the perimeter, and the defense can suddenly be defending 60 yards of grass rather than 10. That kind of acceleration is difficult to manufacture through scheme alone. More importantly, Wheeler’s athletic profile gives him a legitimate avenue to contribute on special teams. At the bottom of a roster, those third-phase contributions can become decisive. Gore gives Buffalo certainty. Wheeler gives Buffalo possibility. Now, the Bills have to determine which one is more valuable. Waiver wire gamble The most painful part of the equation is the possibility that Buffalo cannot simply move the losing candidate to its practice squad. Both backs have generated enough preseason attention to make waiver-wire exposure dangerous. A team searching for inexpensive backfield depth could easily identify either player as a worthwhile claim. That means Buffalo risks losing a legitimate contributor without receiving anything in return. That is the type of roster decision that can linger long after September. Choose the right philosophy Nathan Ray Seebeck-Imagn Images General manager Brandon Beane and head coach Joe Brady have repeatedly emphasized competition and versatility. However, cutdown day strips away all sentimentality. The Bills just cannot keep everyone. The roster spot occupied by Gore or Wheeler could instead go to another offensive lineman, defensive contributor, or special-teams specialist. There is a compelling argument for Gore because Buffalo knows exactly what it will receive. He can keep the offense on schedule and handle difficult situations without requiring a specialized package. Yet Wheeler may ultimately possess the more difficult trait to replace. Speed changes defensive behavior. It forces safeties to respect the perimeter and gives offensive coordinators access to explosive plays. If Buffalo believes Wheeler can develop into a reliable all-around contributor, keeping him may represent the smarter long-term investment. The post Bills’ most agonizing roster decision looming on 2026 cutdown day appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles.title: Broncos OC Davis Webb makes Jaylen Waddle promise that fantasy football managers will love
articles.summary: The Denver Broncos are looking to level up next season. It will be hard to top, or even match, the previous season: they made it all the way to the AFC Championship Game and were just one touchdown away from reaching the Super Bowl. However, they have added some pieces to the team that should [&#
articles._body: The Denver Broncos are looking to level up next season. It will be hard to top, or even match, the previous season: they made it all the way to the AFC Championship Game and were just one touchdown away from reaching the Super Bowl. However, they have added some pieces to the team that should improve their chances. The crowning jewel of their offseason is acquiring ex-Miami Dolphins wide receiver Jaylen Waddle. Waddle immediately slots in as the Broncos’ WR1 for the 2026 season. However, fans are wondering how the star wide receiver will be used in this offense. Well, offensive coordinator Davis Webb gave an encouraging answer on that front that should excite fans AND fantasy football managers. “He’s going to play everywhere,” Davis said, per Zac Stevens on X. “He’s really really good. He’s going to play everywhere. Except offensive line.” Waddle should be featured prominently in the Broncos’ offense due to his versatility. While he functioned primarily as the WR2 in Miami, Waddle shined by donning many hats in the Dolphins’ offense. He worked as an outside receiver most of the time, but was also placed in the slot and as a motion man in Mike McDaniel’s trademark exit/cheat motion. With the increased prevalence of wide receivers working out of the backfield, Broncos fans can reasonably expect Waddle to do the same thing in Denver. The Broncos’ offense last season was already pretty good, finishing top 10 in total yards per game and 11th in passing EPA. Bo Nix’s creativity in the pocket has made him the perfect skipper of Sean Payton’s offense, even though he could stand to slow down a little bit . Denver did all that without having a true WR1 option on paper. Now that they have that premier pass-catching option in Waddle, the team will be much, much better. articles.title: LeBron James borrowed $300 million for LLC tied to Mark Walter, Guggenheim
articles.summary: LeBron James borrowed $300 million in 2018 from Guggenheim Partners for his LLC before he put on the Los Angeles Lakers jersey. Guggenheim Partners’ CEO is the former Lakers owner, Mark Walter, who is currently under federal investigation for fraud. According to the New York Post, Walter is
articles._body: LeBron James borrowed $300 million in 2018 from Guggenheim Partners for his LLC before he put on the Los Angeles Lakers jersey. Guggenheim Partners’ CEO is the former Lakers owner, Mark Walter, who is currently under federal investigation for fraud. According to the New York Post, Walter is under investigation “over potential hidden, related-party transactions.” While James borrowed the $300 million from Midwestern Life Insurers, which is under Guggenheim Partners, there is nothing that indicates he has anything connected to do with the ongoing federal investigation. The bond was set to give James a stream of future revenue tied to his non-NBA earnings, like his lifetime Nike deal, according to Bloomberg reports. Following the 2018 loan, the same Midwestern insurers gave him cash in 2022 after signing a $97 million contract extension with the Lakers. The outlet reports that they bought almost $60 million of 34-year bonds with a 5.75% interest rate. “The 2018 and 2022 transactions were a securitization done by Mr. James with his personal, non-NBA salary, assets and income which is a very common financial structure for an individual with this level of earnings and assets,” a rep for James told Fox Business. “Both transactions were fully approved by NBA. Mr. James has no affiliation with Guggenheim, Sammons Financial, North American Life or Midland National beyond their participation in these transactions.” The NBA superstar’s bond is not due until 2049. Walter’s making headlines follows the sale of the Lakers earlier this month to businessmen Josh Kushner and Bob Iger for $12.5 billion. He began his ownership of the Lakers with a minority stake in 2021 and later acquired a majority controlling stake in 2025. Following the sale of the Lakers, Walter said in a statement: “Owning the Los Angeles Lakers has been one of the great honors of my life — an extraordinary investment, but what I will carry with me is the community, the fans, and a city that treats this team as family,” Walter said in a statement. “I am grateful to Jeanie Buss, the Buss family, the players, and the staff for welcoming me into this chapter. The Lakers belong to Los Angeles, and I have every confidence the best is still ahead.” The post LeBron James borrowed $300 million for LLC tied to Mark Walter, Guggenheim appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles._body: Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver Roman Wilson is in his third season , and he is aiming to have a breakout campaign after not getting ample opportunities in his first two years due to the team’s stacked rotation. The Steelers will face the Buffalo Bills in a preseason clash on Friday, and Wilson has another chance to prove his worth. He only logged a combined total of three receptions for 23 yards in their previous assignments against the Green Bay Packers and the New York Jets. The learning curve is high for the 25-year-old pass-catcher, whom the Steelers drafted in the third round in 2024. On “Not Just Football,” he revealed that he studies the game of former star Antonio Brown. “A big one for me is AB. I have a whole (video) cut-up. It’s literally all his targets since he’s been in the league. I watch that s*** all the time,” said Wilson. Who are the Steeler WR's studying? Roman Wilson AB Germie Bernard Ja'Marr Chase/CeeDee Lamb Michael Pittman Brandon Marshall, Larry Fitzgerald, JSN pic.twitter.com/d2vzDLnIAV — Not Just Football (@NotJustFootball) August 25, 2026 Brown was a top-tier wide receiver during his prime. He was a five-time All-Pro, seven-time Pro Bowler, two-time receptions leader, two-time receiving yards leader, and a one-time receiving touchdowns leader. Later in his career, he helped the Tampa Bay Buccaneers win the Super Bowl in 2021. Sadly, he has been embroiled in legal issues and numerous controversies following his retirement. Still, Wilson has learned a lot by watching Brown’s highlights. It is up to him to translate it on the field with the Steelers , who are looking to improve their passing game. Last season, he was targeted 21 times, leading to 12 receptions for 166 yards and one touchdown. articles._body: A’ja Wilson is, of course, featured in the latest edition of NBA 2K, but she’s seen repping Alpha Kappa Alpha in a brand-new way. Wilson appears in the game not only as a playable character on her team, the Las Vegas Aces, but also on the main menu . There, Wilson showcases some Alpha Kappa Alpha stroll moves. A’ja Wilson & AKA representation in NBA 2K27 pic.twitter.com/McWZL8RMHJ — naeohmii aka Female MP (@naeohmii_2k) August 25, 2026 Wilson is not shy in showcasing her affiliation with the oldest historically Black sorority in the nation. In a quote obtained by ESPNW and Andscape, Wilson spoke about the sorority’s impact on her life. “I am so grateful for the sisterhood that I formed in college through AKA. It allowed me to be a woman. As I’ve gotten older and become a leader, I have to credit AKA and our sisterhood when it comes to that.” She’s also shown love for the sorority via her Nike A’One and A’Two branded shoes . She recently revealed the Nike A2 pinkies up colorway, a new edition of the signature sneaker with the pink and green colors popularized by the sorority. Alpha Kappa Alpha was established at Howard University in 1908 by nine collegiate women and has since grown into one of the largest Black Greek-letter organizations in the world, with a membership exceeding 355,000 across 12 countries. Wilson joined the sorority’s Theta Gamma Chapter in 2017 while a student at the University of South Carolina, becoming part of a sisterhood whose ranks include prominent figures across politics, business, entertainment, and sports. If the Mets are to pull off an upset series win over Milwaukee, which has the best record overall in the big leagues, they will need [&#
articles._body: The New York Mets are in a tough series at home, with the Milwaukee Brewers visiting Citi Field in Queens for a three-game series that started on Tuesday night. If the Mets are to pull off an upset series win over Milwaukee, which has the best record overall in the big leagues, they will need Francisco Lindor to step up in any way he can. Lindor showed exactly that on offense and defense. He hit a solo home run that went 400 feet deep in the fifth inning to level the score at 1-1. Then, in the ninth inning, with the Brewers loading up the bases and with two outs, Lindor flashed his glove and made a leaping catch to end the inning and save the day for New York and keep the score tied at 2-2. The FULL EXTENSION from Francisco Lindor to keep Mets-Brewers tied in the 9th pic.twitter.com/jG9cMcutRL — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) August 26, 2026 Fans clearly appreciated the effort shown by the two-time Gold Glove Award winner. “People really wanted to trade this guy Still a top 5 SS in the mlb,” a fan said . “And still there are people that want to trade him for pennies on the dollar.,” a social media user on X shared . “Francisco Lindor will return in Avengers Doomsday,” another one commented . “Lindor flashes some leather!!” a different fan said . “That play by Lindor was incredible, just gotta tip your cap!” another comment read. As it turned out, Lindor’s heroics did not go to waste, as New York stunned the Brewers in a walk-off manner for a 3-2 victory, with him scoring the game-winning run off a throwing error by Milwaukee in the bottom of the 10th inning. The Mets are unlikely to make the playoffs , but they will always have this memorable win over a World Series contender. articles.title: Eagles’ Saquon Barkley reveals which 2026 addition is a massive ‘steal’
articles.summary: While there’s plenty of continuity on the Philadelphia Eagles offense heading into 2026, one major change involves the X wide receiver spot, with Green Bay Packers draftee Dontayvion Wicks taking over for AJ Brown after a June 1 trade. On paper, going from arguably the most prolific wide re
articles._body: While there’s plenty of continuity on the Philadelphia Eagles offense heading into 2026, one major change involves the X wide receiver spot, with Green Bay Packers draftee Dontayvion Wicks taking over for AJ Brown after a June 1 trade. On paper, going from arguably the most prolific wide receiver in franchise history over a four-year period to a 25-year-old who has never recorded 600 yards in a single season is a tough pill to swallow. But in the opinion of franchise running back Saquon Barkley , the Eagles might not have taken as large a step back as some might have thought, as he might just turn out to be the steal of the summer . “There’s a route that I want to be really good at this year, which I will not say. I watched him run it, and I think he does at a high level. Tay is a steal. I love everything that he’s about. Shout out to Howie again. I don’t know how we got him for whatever round we traded for,” Barkley declared. “He just brings like a different type of energy for the wide receiver group. He’s a violent rock runner, and he’s violent catching the ball, but he also put his face in there and blocks at a high level. So I’m excited to have him as a teammate this year.” Has Wicks recorded fewer yards over his entire NFL career than Brown recorded in 2022 and in 2023? Yes, but that doesn’t necessarily mean he can’t step up and become a certified starter next to DeVonta Smith and summer breakout star Darius Cooper . If the Wicks hype train continues to chug along into the regular season, the Eagles might really have something. articles.title: Browns’ most agonizing roster decision looming on 2026 cutdown day
articles.summary: For the Cleveland Browns’ 2026 roster, no roster decision will be more painful than what they must do at quarterback. The top of the room appears firmly defined with Deshaun Watson starting — at least for now. And yet, the battle for the final developmental spot has created a fascinat
articles._body: For the Cleveland Browns’ 2026 roster, no roster decision will be more painful than what they must do at quarterback. The top of the room appears firmly defined with Deshaun Watson starting — at least for now. And yet, the battle for the final developmental spot has created a fascinating collision between certainty and upside. Turbulence and transformation Cleveland’s ongoing preseason campaign has delivered a turbulent glimpse into a franchise undergoing a fundamental identity shift. Todd Monken has installed an aggressive, tempo-driven offensive scheme. As such, live exhibition snaps have produced sharp contrasts and dramatic momentum swings across the depth chart . The summer slate reached a critical fever pitch during a weather-delayed matchup against the Buffalo Bills. Dynamic playmaking sparked scoring momentum while pocket indecision and turnovers led to visible frustration from the home faithful. Along the line of scrimmage, rebuilt trenches have endured baptism by fire. Those exhibitions have provided Cleveland’s coaching staff with the unfiltered evidence necessary to make increasingly difficult personnel decisions. And no position has produced a more consequential decision than quarterback. Cleveland’s biggest headache When examining the entirety of Cleveland’s depth chart, no dilemma is more agonizing or structurally consequential than the quarterback spots. Carrying four quarterbacks on an active 53-man roster is generally difficult to justify. They already did it before, and it basically went nowhere. For Cleveland, the first two positions appear secure. Watson’s massive guaranteed contract makes him extremely difficult to move. Shedeur Sanders has asserted himself as an electric catalyst. That leaves Gabriel and Green fighting for what could be the lone developmental spot. The decision is therefore about what the Browns value more: immediate operational security or potentially transformational upside. Gabriel offers safer path Gabrielis straightforward: he looks like the quarterback who can be trusted to execute. His quick release, pocket composure, and experience give him a polished feel. Gabriel can deliver the football on time and keep the offense moving. That matters enormously for a team attempting to establish a new offensive identity. If Watson were unavailable or Sanders needed additional time to develop, Gabriel would offer a relatively clean transition. There is also value in predictability. NFL teams spend enormous resources creating systems that depend on timing, communication, and precision. Gabriel’s profile suggests he can step into that structure without creating unnecessary disruption. Of course, reliability does not necessarily equal scarcity. If the Browns believe Gabriel’s ceiling is that of a competent backup, they must ask whether that profile is worth protecting at the expense of Green’s considerably more intriguing athletic upside. Swing-for-the-fences option Green’s case is built almost entirely around what he could become. His combination of size, mobility, and arm talent gives him tremendous physical tools. Green can threaten the edge on designed runs and escape pressure when protection breaks down. He can also create explosive plays when things break down. Monken has an opportunity to construct an offense around dynamic movement and quarterback versatility. Green provides precisely the kind of raw physical ingredient that could eventually unlock another dimension. Choosing Green, however, requires patience and high risk-tolerance. The Browns would be betting that their coaching infrastructure can refine his processing, accuracy, and decision-making without sacrificing the traits that make him special. That is a substantially different proposition from simply keeping the more polished player. Waiver wire risk The most agonizing element of this situation may be what happens after the roster decision. If Cleveland chooses Gabriel and attempts to send Green through waivers, the Browns could be inviting another organization to acquire one of the more intriguing developmental quarterbacks available. A player with Green’s physical profile would have obvious appeal to quarterback-needy teams. That makes the practice squad route dangerous. The Browns could theoretically attempt to keep both players by placing one outside the initial 53 and hoping he clears waivers. Still, hoping is not a roster strategy. Conversely, choosing Green means accepting the possibility that Gabriel’s polished profile could disappear. A quarterback with his experience and efficiency could immediately attract teams looking for dependable depth. Cleveland therefore faces a genuine lose-lose scenario. Upside or insurance Kirby Lee-Imagn Images For GM Andrew Berry, this is precisely the kind of roster decision that can cause migraines. The easy answer would be to keep everyone. The NFL roster, however, does not permit easy answers. Keeping four quarterbacks just has not and would not work for Cleveland. It will surely create vulnerabilities at positions where injuries are considerably more common. Keeping three means one of Gabriel or Green is exposed to the waiver process. Keeping only two would be an even more aggressive gamble. The most logical solution may ultimately be to keep the player Cleveland believes has the greatest chance of becoming a long-term asset. That gives Green a compelling edge. Gabriel is the cleaner quarterback today. That said, Green’s athletic ceiling could make him much harder to replace tomorrow. If Cleveland genuinely believes Monken can develop him, allowing another team to claim him would be a difficult mistake to reverse. articles._body: I had to develop a course related to quantum chemistry and unfortunately, Claude just kept writing it in its own very annoying claude-speak. It actually cost our team a lot of time and tokens to wrestle it to just speak like a normal human. We used skills, as well as initial prompts and subagents to make sure that all of the tics were gone, but there was one too many times where it just wouldn't fix itself despite telling it in the prior prompt! I made speak-english based off of https://github.com/gvzdv/claudish-to-english/commits/main/ and it runs a qwen model on my gcp servers. It can convert documents or respond in-line in sessions with claude and I anticipate building a solution for prime-agent. articles.title: Here’s Everything Morgan Scalley Said After Practice
articles.summary: Here's everything Utah HC Morgan Scalley said after practice on Tuesday.
articles._body: The focus has fully turned to game prep for Utah head coach Morgan Scalley and members of his inaugural squad. With just a little bit over a week until the Utes host Idaho, the pressure and excitement are ramping up. Below is everything Morgan Scalley said after practice on Tuesday: What are your biggest takeaways now that fall camp has wrapped up? Scalley: Injury-free for the most part. We got some bumps and bruises, guys that still need to get some rehab in, but we’ll be ready to go for game one and feel very good about where we’re at in terms of depth chart and stuff like that. Stuff I won’t talk to you guys about. You are about one week out from the start of the season. Just what is the biggest thing left to do on the checklist? Scalley: Odds and ends with some situational stuff, and obviously now it turns from our behavior, our culture, now to studying opponent film, and with Idaho you’re looking at Iowa State on the defensive side of the ball. You’re looking at Grand Valley on the offensive side of the ball. You’re trying to get any sort of information you can get from where these coaches are coming from. The good news is they’ll be playing on Friday, so we’ll get a really good peek at that, but just making sure your guys understand how to study film the right way. There is a process to going about it, and you really have to teach them, okay, so on a control down day, first and second down, this is what you’re looking at. These are the cutups that you need to look at, and just schooling them up on that. So much more opponent work right now. Did you accomplish what you wanted to accomplish in fall camp? Scalley: Yes, 100%. We got depth figured out. We stayed for the most part injury-free, and we established our leadership. Has it been announced? Oh, fantastic. Yeah, you can see it’s a big one, right? You got a big leadership council, and I think you’ve got a lot of guys getting a lot of votes. That’s a good thing. That’s a good thing. There’s not one guy in that group, whether from the captain group or the leadership council group, that I’m sitting there going like, I don’t know. Those guys are compelling. They’re bringing others with them. It’s a really solid group. How do you feel about the deep defensive line depth? Scalley: Really good, really good. And you may not know why. It’s good to have Karson [Kaufusi] back the past couple of days, and you’ve had a couple guys that were dinged up, and we’ve had to rotate and do some stuff. But really like the progress of those guys, and there may be a couple others that show up. You talked about wanting to improve red zone efficiency during camp at one point. How has that been now that camp is over? Scalley: I’m glad I said that because maybe they got butt hurt or something, because it’s been fantastic since then. So maybe they thought I was calling them out. Man, really good the next couple of days. That was fantastic. So McGiven is a competitor, and maybe he heard that and was like, okay. No, that was good. We cleaned some stuff up for sure. Have you noticed a different energy yesterday and today? Now that it’s not fall camp and it’s more into that game mindset. Scalley: Yeah, well, and school starts, so you get school starting and you got an academic schedule and guys are going to school. We were practicing more in the morning during fall camp than practicing in the afternoon, so it’s just making sure those guys bring the same energy, regardless of what time of day you’re practicing. And I thought, for the most part, today was our more physical practice kind of plan for the first day of school, being something that you gotta, okay, let’s get started with some opponent work, nothing too taxing, but today was a grinder for them. It was really good, What does Semi Taulanga bring to this team? Scalley: Oh man. Well, you talk about the safeties being versatile. This is a guy that can play smash-mouth football. He can block on the edge. He can run routes. He can catch the ball. Obviously, in high school, he was a defensive tackle. So there’s a lot that this guy can do. The guy I don’t want everyone to sleep on is Sione Motuapuaka . That guy is just as valuable as Semi is, and for the exact same reasons- just the versatility of what we’re able to do with him- and so I can’t say enough about those guys. Plus the fact that they’re team guys, they’re guys that were recruited at one position, asked now to play a different position, and didn’t bat an eye doing it. I love those guys. Love that because I didn’t do that. I was asked to move to safety, and I was like, “What? No.” Wish I had thought about that sooner. How would you assess the team in the tackling category after fall camp? Scalley: We got more tackling in spring ball than we ever have. Fall camp was tackling early on, but you’re trying to mix it in and trying to get to the party healthy. There are some guys that we certainly trust, and then other guys that, if we feel like they need continued tackling work, that’s going to be more in a controlled setting with scout team players, but you’ve got to do it. You got to do it. We don’t go out there on Saturdays and play tag. articles.title: Blaze Berlowitz beats out five-star prospect Jared Curtis in Vanderbilt QB battle
articles.summary: A prized five-star recruit will not be starting for Vanderbilt in Week 1.
articles._body: Fall camps are wrapping up across college football. That means quarterback competitions are coming to an end. The one at Vanderbilt might officially be over yet but we know who will run out on the turf in the West End first in the opener against Austin Peay. The Commodores have named veteran Blaze Berlowitz the new QB1 — for now. NEW: Vanderbilt has named Blaze Berlowitz its starting QB, @PeteNakos reports https://t.co/xxUJED1cHY pic.twitter.com/fLH5PpXC7m — On3 (@On3) August 25, 2026 This former New Mexico State transfer followed offensive coordinator Tim Beck and senior offensive advisor Jerry Kill to Nashville and sat behind Diego Pavia . After not appearing in a game in 2024, Berlowitz completed 9-of-17 passes for 131 yards in backup action. Now the fourth-year player out of Cushing (Okla.) High will get an extended look this fall. Holding onto this job won’t be easy because of what happened this offseason. Vanderbilt shocked the college football world on the way to a 10-2 regular season when five-star recruit Jared Curtis flipped from Georgia to Vandy. The Nashville native was the No. 3 overall recruit in the 2026 high school cycle. Keeping the Nashville native home was not cheap. Curtis has a big-time arm and the athleticism to break the pocket and make plays out of structure. The is No. 1 overall pick potential with the five-star recruit. The young phenom will play eventually. Expect to see both quarterbacks on the field in the first two weeks when Vanderbilt hosts Austin Peay and Delaware to start the season before NC State rolls into town on Week 3. A road trip to Auburn will take place in Week 4 before consecutive SEC games against Georgia and Ole Miss. Vandy will head to Kroger Field in Week 8. Odds are high that this quarterback battle is settled by then. Berlowitz will get the first opportunity, but holding off Curtis could be a difficult task. By taking a deep dive look at all of Kentucky’s opponents before Labor Day weekend arrives. This marks my ninth year providing in-depth football breakdowns for KSR. The scouting report series is one of my favorite things to write all year. This is the start of that exercise. We simply cannot do those during the season without the research. This is the pre-work. Not familiar with these? They are jam-packed features that drop every week during the season. The scouting reports include advanced stats, program history, betting nuggets, film cut ups, and matchup analysis. The summer series is an abbreviated deep dive to help you know more about the opponent. Early Scouting Report: Vanderbilt Commodores Lock in for a pivotal Kentucky football season with KSR Plus! articles.title: Braves get big Robert Suarez injury update during Dodgers series
articles.summary: The Atlanta Braves (76-55) cannot simply look ahead to October, as they are still trying to hold off the Philadelphia Phillies in the National League East and jump the Los Angeles Dodgers for a first-round bye, but they need a healthy pitching staff more than anything. Injuries seriously hindered
articles._body: The Atlanta Braves (76-55) cannot simply look ahead to October, as they are still trying to hold off the Philadelphia Phillies in the National League East and jump the Los Angeles Dodgers for a first-round bye, but they need a healthy pitching staff more than anything. Injuries seriously hindered the club during its last postseason trip in 2024, so management will likely do everything possible to preserve its most important arms for the final stretch of the year. Robert Suarez is certainly included in that group. The right-handed reliever has not pitched in more than two months due to elbow inflammation, but he is slowly making his way back to the mound. Suarez is now throwing from 100 feet and building up his arm strength , positioning him to begin bullpen sessions soon, per Grant McAuley of 92.9 The Game. If he advances past that step, manager Walt Weiss says a rehab assignment will be the next and final checkpoint to clear. Braves fans have been patient, for they understand how valuable Suarez can be at full strength. The two-time All-Star, who racked up 76 saves combined in the previous two years with the San Diego Padres, owns a sensational 0.56 ERA in 32 innings pitched for Atlanta in 2026. Dylan Lee, Didier Fuentes and Dylan Dodd have boosted the Braves’ bullpen toward the top of MLB, and Raisel Iglesias remains reliable overall despite a recent skid. Robert Suarez is the X-factor, however. Atlanta signed the Venezuelan hurler to a $45 million contract for that very reason. He intends to pay the franchise back for that generous investment in the near future. The post Braves get big Robert Suarez injury update during Dodgers series appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles.title: Kelsey Plum promises to be ‘shot out of cannon’ in Mercury home debut
articles.summary: PHOENIX– Kelsey Plum feels as ready as ever to play her first game in front of the Phoenix Mercury fans. After spending years playing against the fanbase, she now gets to have their support for the remainder of the season. Originally, the past two weeks were thought to be Plum’s retur
articles._body: PHOENIX– Kelsey Plum feels as ready as ever to play her first game in front of the Phoenix Mercury fans. After spending years playing against the fanbase, she now gets to have their support for the remainder of the season. Originally, the past two weeks were thought to be Plum’s return from injury, but that never happened. And once the team was nearing the end of playoff contention, keeping her healthy was a priority. Not to mention, she was dealing with a lingering calf issue that cost her substantial time when she was with the Los Angeles Sparks. Fast forward to when Plum made her Mercury debut ; that same week she was injured again. Is the injury truly that concerning? For someone of her skill set, it can be. Her game is about getting downhill and to the rim, while being an extremely effective off-the-dribble shooter and playmaker. That extra burst can be the ultimate difference-maker. Regardless, Plum doesn’t have any worries and actually feels the antithesis of any doubt. “I feel extremely prepared; I’m as strong as I’ve ever been,” she explained during Tuesday’s shootaround. “I’ve never gone out there and played with any fear. If I had any fear, I probably wouldn’t be playing tonight. “For me, I’ll play like I always played: getting shot out of a cannon. Hopefully you don’t notice any difference because I won’t.” Kelsey Plum on if she has any concerns about aggravating her calf ahead of her first Mercury home game tonight: "I feel extremely prepared. I'm as strong as I've ever been. I've never gone out there and played with any fear. If I had any fear, I probably wouldn't be playing… pic.twitter.com/S4XqnBfQwL — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) August 26, 2026 Kelsey Plum’s confidence is unmatched There’s a fearlessness Plum plays with that the rest of the team can use. She consistently gets into the paint, as judging by the 56.3% of her points coming from that area, in addition to the 20.5% from the charity stripe. However, she didn’t have another dynamic scorer like Kahleah Copper. The duo plays similar, yet extremely different. Plum has had to create a majority of her offense off the dribble and in the half court. But on-court things aside, it doesn’t make the preparation any less difficult. Luckily, she’s been around the Phoenix practice facility for the past couple of weeks, which she said makes her feel more comfortable to play. She’s had that mindset no matter what, as head coach Nate Tibbetts alluded to in weeks prior. Physical preparation is one thing, but the mental is a completely different ball game. “I’ve never been in a situation like this before,” she explained. “2020 was kind of an anomaly, but I think for me, I’ve learned a lot this year, and through it all I feel like it’s going to fare me well moving forward. Through it all, it’s brought me here, so I’m super grateful for that. “At the end of the day, I know God’s always directed my steps, and this is no different, and so I’m just grateful to be able to come out tonight and play… sometimes you get the short end of the stick, and you’ve got to make the best of it.” Mercury fans will be ecstatic for Kelsey Plum The season hasn’t been what anyone anticipated, but there is a clear vision for the future. Despite Plum being set to become a free agent at the end of the season, the Mercury might be her No. 1 choice . The extended time recovering, finally playing in front of the home crowd, as well as the FIBA World Cup, can mark the end of what would have been a tumultuous season and into a promising 2027. articles.title: Dolly Parton Chose Her Funeral Song More Than a Decade Ago & Left an Unreleased Song to Be Heard in 2046
articles.summary: "I'm sure they'll be playing 'I Will Always Love You' when I die, just like they did with Whitney Houston," she said in a 2015 interview -- but she had a different pick.
articles._body: Dolly Parton spent her life turning her own experiences, memories and emotions into music. Even after death, her songs will continue to tell her story — including two that show just how thoughtfully she considered her musical legacy. The country music icon, who died Tuesday (Aug. 25) at age 80 after a brief battle with cancer, had already decided what song she wanted played at her funeral more than a decade before her death. And, in true Dolly fashion, she also left behind another song that she specifically instructed would not be heard until her 100th birthday in 2046. Related Dolly Parton, One of Country Music’s Biggest & Brightest Icons, Dies at 80 Dolly Parton’s 25 Best Songs: Critics’ Picks Dolly Parton’s Top Billboard Hot Country Songs Hits In a 2014 interview with Entertainment Weekly , Parton was asked what song she would want played at her funeral. While many might have expected “I Will Always Love You” — the song she famously wrote and recorded and then later watched become an even bigger hit through Whitney Houston ‘s rendition — Parton had something more personal in mind. “I’m sure they’ll be playing ‘I Will Always Love You’ when I die, just like they did with Whitney Houston,” she told the outlet at the time. But when it came to the song she actually wanted for her own funeral, she chose “If We Never Meet Again,” an old country-gospel hymn with a particularly meaningful connection to her family. The song had been her father’s favorite, and it was performed at his funeral. Parton said she hoped the same song would one day be sung at hers. The choice is fitting, given the song’s message about separation and the hope of being reunited in the afterlife. Her funeral plans were indeed something Parton had considered in advance. Her representatives confirmed Tuesday that she requested a small, private service for immediate family. Her nephew and head of security, Bryan Seaver, also shared that Parton wanted to be laid to rest in a “beautiful bed of plush cotton.” But Parton’s planning for the music that would remain until after her death went beyond her funeral. At Dollywood’s DreamMore Resort in Pigeon Forge, Tennessee, sits a locked chestnut box containing a recording of an unreleased Parton song called “My Place in History.” The song was written in 2015 , the same year the resort opened, and Parton specifically arranged for it to be unveiled on what would have been her 100th birthday: Jan. 19, 2046. Inside the box is a CD containing the recording, along with a CD player so that future generations will be able to hear it, outwardly a Dolly time capsule. The country legend even acknowledged the uncertainty of leaving technology from 2015 to be opened decades later. “There’s no telling what music is going to be by then,” she wrote in her 2020 book, Dolly Parton, Songteller: My Life in Lyrics . “Hopefully, it will play and the whole thing ain’t rotted.” Parton also joked that she hoped she would live long enough to hear the song herself when the box eventually opened. She was 69 when she wrote and recorded “My Place In History.”

Early in the third quarter, she hit a transition 3-pointer to get her 16 points on the night, which ultimately resulted in her joining the Indiana Fever’s Caitlin Clark and the Phoenix Mercury’s Kelsey Plum as the sole players in WNBA history to reach 750+ points and 200+ assists in a single season. With this bucket, Paige Bueckers joins Caitlin Clark and Kelsey Plum as the ONLY players in WNBA history to reach 750+ pts and 200+ assists in a single season! https://t.co/74csQhn7p7 — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) August 26, 2026 Bueckers’ new historic milestone adds a crescendo to her already impressive season. The Dallas Wings guard has played 36 games this season and is averaging 20.6 points, 5.8 assists, and 4.1 rebounds while shooting 50.6% from the floor and 39.6% from three. Her elevated level of play has allowed the Dallas Wings to stay in playoff contention at 22 and 16. Bueckers’ new historic milestone adds a crescendo to her already impressive season. Bueckers has shown immense focus during her team’s playoff push, which she highlighted in comments after Sunday evening’s game against the Seattle Storm. In post-game remarks, she talked about how the team has approached games this season. “Honestly, we want to have the same approach every single game, and play every game like it’s a playoff game and play every game like it’s the most important one ahead of us. So, obviously that’s the next one on the schedule. But we can’t play like we’re trying to make the playoffs. She added, “We’ve got to play to our identity and to what we want to build on and to what we’ve been this entire season. Obviously, the stakes are higher, but once you focus on that, you kind of lose sight of where you are in the present.” The post Paige Bueckers joins Caitlin Clark, Kelsey Plum in WNBA history amid historic season appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles.title: Players’ attorney calls out ‘cartel-like conduct’ of SEC, Big Ten
articles.summary: In recent years, the NCAA has been embroiled in a complicated saga over its eligibility rules. There have been lawsuits, court rulings, and injunctions, and it looks like the whole circus will not end anytime soon. On Tuesday, the SEC and the Big Ten announced their revised policies, essentially
articles._body: In recent years, the NCAA has been embroiled in a complicated saga over its eligibility rules. There have been lawsuits, court rulings, and injunctions, and it looks like the whole circus will not end anytime soon. On Tuesday, the SEC and the Big Ten announced their revised policies , essentially barring athletes who have been drafted or appeared on a professional roster from returning to play college sports. The two conferences want to prevent schools from becoming landing spots for players who already have professional experience, ensuring competitive fairness. Atty. Ryan Downtown, who represents athletes in legal battles against the NCAA, slammed the SEC and the Big Ten in a statement , as reported by ESPN’s Pete Thamel. “The SEC’s actions put the NCAA in contempt of multiple court orders. It is cartel-like conduct when NCAA conferences attempt to create their own spur-of-the-moment rules in response to courts enjoining those same rules at the NCAA level,” said Downtown. He also said the NCAA should be held “in contempt of court for permitting conferences under its purview to blatantly violate court orders,” as quoted by Yahoo! Sports’ Rose Dellenger. Downtown added that he is planning to file a motion or an “appropriate legal response” to halt the SEC and the Big Ten from imposing their revised policies. Some athletes who were allowed by court rulings to play despite having professional experience include LSU’s RJ Luis Jr. and Kentucky’s Mark Mitchell Jr. in basketball and LSU’s Dae’Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris in football. The SEC and the Big Ten are part of the so-called “Power Four” in the NCAA, which holds the highest financial resources, athletic dominance, and political control in college sports. articles.title: Sky’s Courtney Vandersloot hits incredible 3,000-assist milestone during loss to Sun
articles.summary: Courtney Vandersloot etched her name deeper into the WNBA record books on Tuesday night, becoming just the second player in league history to reach 3,000 career assists. The Chicago Sky legend hit the milestone during an 87-81 road loss to the Connecticut Sun, but the setback did little to dimini
articles._body: Courtney Vandersloot etched her name deeper into the WNBA record books on Tuesday night, becoming just the second player in league history to reach 3,000 career assists. The Chicago Sky legend hit the milestone during an 87-81 road loss to the Connecticut Sun, but the setback did little to diminish the historic nature of the achievement. With the dime, Vandersloot joined Sue Bird as the only players ever to cross the 3,000-assist threshold. The all-time list underscores just how rarefied the company is: Bird sits atop the leaderboard at 3,234 assists, followed by Vandersloot at 3,000 and counting. Ticha Penicheiro ranks third with 2,599, Diana Taurasi fourth at 2,394, and Lindsay Whalen fifth with 2,345. The milestone is all the more remarkable given the road Vandersloot traveled to reach it. The 37-year-old missed most of the 2025 season after suffering a torn ACL just seven games in , spending a grueling year in rehabilitation before returning to the floor in June 2026. She has embraced a shared point guard role this season alongside veteran Natasha Cloud, sacrificing some of her own numbers for the good of the team. Even in a diminished offensive role, Vandersloot’s brilliance as a facilitator never faded . The 37-year-old has long been regarded as one of the greatest passers the women’s game has ever seen, a five-time All-Star who once averaged a league-record 10 assists per game in 2020. Her resume also includes two WNBA championships, both of which were the first titles in the respective histories of her teams. The accomplishment adds another chapter to a career defined by generosity on the court. Vandersloot has always credited her teammates for her assist totals, pointing to the scorers who finished the plays she created. That selflessness has been the throughline of a Hall of Fame-caliber tenure, most of it spent in a Sky uniform, where she is also the franchise’s all-time leading scorer. For a Chicago team well out of playoff contention at 15-24, nights like these offer something to celebrate beyond the standings. Vandersloot’s pursuit of Bird’s all-time record now becomes must-see viewing down the stretch. articles.title: Why Bears must make Gervon Dexter trade with Cardinals before Week 1
articles.summary:
As the Chicago Bears finalize their 2026 roster, defensive tackle Gervon Dexter has emerged as a potential trade candidate. If the Bears are to pull off a trade, they must do so with a clear goal in mind. Dexter is set to be a free agent after the season. The fact his name is even […]

<
articles._body: As the Chicago Bears finalize their 2026 roster, defensive tackle Gervon Dexter has emerged as a potential trade candidate . If the Bears are to pull off a trade, they must do so with a clear goal in mind. Dexter is set to be a free agent after the season. The fact his name is even in trade rumors could be a sign that Chicago doesn’t plan on extending him. But trading him for solely draft capital – even if a mid-round pick – would be counterintuitive. The Bears’ defensive line has been their biggest red flag all offseason. While the focus has been on Chicago’s pass rush, their interior defensive line needs work as well. It’s why they signed Neville Gallimore and Kentavius Street in free agency before drafting Jordan van den Berg in the sixth-round. That depth is nice, and van den Berg has been getting plenty of hype specifically . But none of them offer the experience playing on Chicago’s defensive line that Dexter does. Furthermore, he is coming off of a six-sack campaign, with his 72.7 pass rush grade from Pro Football Focus ranking 20/134 defensive linemen. Dexter did earn an overall mark of 57.7, which may be why the Bears are potentially souring on him long-term. But the defensive tackle has been a valuable resource on defense over the past two seasons. Chicago is entering 2026 with real Super Bowl aspirations. Trading Dexter before free agency ensures they’d get some extra draft capital. But with their current defensive tackle standing, they’re a better team with him on the roster. Instead, the Bears should focus on the now. If Dexter is going to be traded, it should be a larger deal for a more impactful player rather than future draft picks. In that case, Arizona Cardinals pass rusher Josh Sweat would be an ideal target. Bears should use Gervon Dexter in Josh Sweat trade Mandatory Credit: Joe Camporeale-Imagn Images Dexter is only 24-years-old and is coming off a season in which he started all 17 games. The Cardinals are looking to find consistent playmakers across their roster. While they’d have to sign him to a new contract, Dexter could be a key piece of a new look defensive front in Arizona. If Sweat is in a deal, the Bears will have to trade away some draft capital as well. But including Dexter in the trade could help lessen that blow. There are a lot of moving pieces, and Arizona may not even have Dexter on their radar. But at least on paper, the Cardinals are building for the future and Dexter could play a key role in it. As for Sweat, he remains a top flight pass rusher, recording 12 sacks in 2025. However, he signed with the Cardinals when Jonathan Gannon was the head coach. Seeing Arizona go 3-14 and then the rest of the NFC West get better didn’t sit right with the pass catcher. He has been away from the team for most of the offseason, just recently being activated from the PUP list . The Cardinals have clearly been reluctant to trade Sweat, especially with how often his name has bene thrown in trade rumors. But there’s a chance Arizona has no choice. If Sweat truly voices his displeasure and the Cardinals get a deal they can’t refuse, a trade becomes much more likely. Trading away Dexter before his free agency season makes sense, get something rather than him walking for free. But the Bears are trying to win, and the defensive tackle helps get them closer to that goal. Unless Chicago is getting an impactful player, ideally Sweat, in a trade back, they must be cautious about dealing away the 24-year-old. articles._body: The official start of the 2026 college football season is just days away, beginning with Saturday’s noon ET kickoff between North Carolina and TCU from Dublin, Ireland. Of course, those aren’t the only Power Four programs to open the 2026 season with Week 0 action. In fact, 14th-ranked USC will kick off what is shaping up to be a promising 2026 season later Saturday with a 3 pm ET kickoff against in-state foe San Jose State inside Los Angeles Memorial Stadium. Ahead of that game, On3’s Crain & Cone crew released their team-by-team regular-season record predictions for all 18 of the Big Ten programs as the conference seeks a fourth consecutive national championship. [ $19.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage ] With that in mind, let’s dive into the Big Ten team-by-team records as predicted by Jake Crain , David Cone , and Blain Crain during Tuesday’s Crain & Cone show with Week 0 coming up this weekend: Illinois Fighting Illini The Crain & Cone crew are split on Bret Bielema’s Fighting Illini, but all three expect a similar result to a year ago, when Illinois went 5-4 in Big Ten play before finishing with a 9-4 record overall. David Cone is a little more confident in Illinois than the Crain brothers, predicting a 9-3 regular-season finish, while his co-hosts both expect four conference losses. Jake Crain: 8-4 (5-4) David Cone: 9-3 (6-3) Blain Crain: 8-4 (5-4) No. 6 Indiana Hoosiers Blain Crain expects the Curt Cignetti train to keep rolling right along and will direct the reigning national champions to a second consecutive undefeated regular season with a perfect 12-0 record in 2026. Jake Crain and David Cone are far less confident Cignetti and the Hoosiers will come away unscathed during the regular season, and will finish a distant third in the final Big Ten standings. Jake Crain: 10-2 (7-2) David Cone: 10-2 (7-2) Blain Crain: 12-0 (9-0) No. 22 Iowa Hawkeyes The entire Crain & Cone crew were in total agreement regarding the Hawkeyes, projecting a slight one-game regression from a year ago. Iowa has been notoriously consistent over the past several years, with Kirk Ferentz ‘s squad finishing the last five seasons with at least four losses. That’s why Jake Crain called their Iowa predictions the “easiest” pick on the board in the Big Ten. Jake Crain: 8-4 (5-4) David Cone: 8-4 (5-4) Blain Crain: 8-4 (5-4) Maryland Terrapins Based on their projections, the entire Crain & Cone crew expects the Terrapins could be in line for a coaching change this offseason if head coach Mike Locksley extends Maryland’s bowl drought for a third consecutive season. And after back-to-back 4-8 (1-8) seasons under Locksley, all three co-hosts project a slight one- to two-win improvement in 2026. Whether it’s enough to save his job is yet to be seen. Jake Crain: 5-7 (3-6) David Cone: 5-7 (3-6) Blain Crain: 4-8 (2-7) No. 16 Michigan Wolverines David Cone, a former Wolverines quarterback, predicts his alma mater will bounce back with a 9-3 record, including home victories over Penn State and Indiana before closing the regular season with road losses at Oregon and Ohio State. Jake Crain was in complete agreement. Meanwhile, Blain Crain is less confident, projecting the Wolverines will lose to all three Big Ten powers: Indiana, Ohio State and Oregon. Jake Crain: 9-3 (7-2) David Cone: 9-3 (7-2) Blain Crain: 8-4 (6-3) Michigan State Spartans While the entire Crain & Cone crew doesn’t have high hopes for the first season under former Northwestern coach Pat Fitzgerald , David Cone is far more confident than his fellow co-hosts and expects the Spartans to at least challenge for a bowl berth with a win over Washington. Meanwhile, Blain and Jake Crain are on the same page with Michigan State going a dismal 1-8 in Big Ten play this season. Jake Crain: 3-9 (1-8) David Cone: 5-7 (3-6) Blain Crain: 3-9 (1-8) Minnesota Golden Gophers While there were some wildly different projections from the Crain & Cone crew, Jake Crain and David Cone are confident the Gophers will catch a couple of Big Ten programs sleeping and eke out a bowl berth in 2026. At the same time, Blain Crain went the other direction and predicts Minnesota will backtrack and suffer through its worst season in 10 years under head coach P.J. Fleck . Jake Crain: 7-5 (4-5) David Cone: 6-6 (3-6) Blain Crain: 4-8 (2-7) Nebraska Cornhuskers All three members of the Crain & Cone crew have wildly different projections for the Cornhuskers, with Blain Crain the most confident in Matt Rhule ‘s rebuilt Nebraska roster featuring new dual-threat QB Anthony Colandrea . Meanwhile, Jake Crain envisions a fourth conference loss for Nebraska, while David Cone expects the Huskers will be fighting just to secure bowl eligibility for a second straight season. Jake Crain: 8-4 (5-4) David Cone: 7-5 (4-5) Blain Crain: 9-3 (6-3) Northwestern Wildcats All three Crain & Cone co-hosts have little faith in Year 2 under David Braun , with all three projecting a three-game regression after the Wildcats went 7-6 overall and 4-5 in Big Ten play in 2025. Not helping matters is a difficult conference slate that includes road games at Indiana, Oregon, and Ohio State, as well as home games against Penn State, Iowa, and Illinois. Tough sledding for the Wildcats. Jake Crain: 4-8 (1-8) David Cone: 4-8 (1-8) Blain Crain: 4-8 (1-8) No. 1 Ohio State Buckeyes Both Jake Crain and David Cone expect the Buckeyes will come up short in its non-conference road game at Texas before dropping just one of their conference games — a road game at USC. Meanwhile, Blain Crain projects Ohio State beats Texas before losing to both Indiana and Oregon in conference. Jake Crain has the Buckeyes winning the Big Ten title with a championship game victory over Oregon in Indianapolis. articles.title: Watch Jack White Cover ‘Jolene’ in London Hours After Dolly Parton’s Death: ‘Instant Sainthood’
articles.summary: The Whites Stripes released their "Jolene" cover as a B-side in 2000 & a live single in 2004.
articles._body: Hours after news of Dolly Parton ‘s death broke on Tuesday (Aug. 25), Jack White paid live tribute to the late country icon by covering her song “Jolene” at London’s Eventim Apollo. Related Dolly Parton Cause of Death Revealed Fearless, Fabulous Dolly Parton and What We Can All Learn From Her: A Remembrance Dolly Parton Forever: See Pictures From Her Billboard Photo Shoots Over the Years The rock singer posted a snippet of the performance on his Instagram account after the show, beginning with the fitting lyric: “Your beauty is beyond compare.” White also shared a tribute to Parton earlier Tuesday, posting a 1965 photo of the legend with her classic beehive hairstyle with the two-word caption: “Instant Sainthood.” View this post on Instagram This is hardly the first time White has covered Parton’s legendary 1973 song begging another woman not to steal her man. The White Stripes — White’s rock duo with drummer Meg White — released a studio version of the song as a B-side to “Hello Operator” in 2000 and also dropped a live single in 2004. Their cover never charted in the U.S., but it did top the UK Indie chart and peaked at No. 16 on the UK Singles chart in 2004. Parton’s original version peaked at No. 60 on the Billboard Hot 100 and topped the Hot Country Songs chart in 1974. It also spawned many covers beyond The White Stripes’ as well, including Beyoncé ‘s interpolation from her country album Cowboy Carter , which featured some new lyrics and peaked at No. 7 on the Hot 100 in 2024. Parton herself was also featured on a Pentatonix cover, which reached No. 18 on Hot Country Songs in 2016. Following “a brief battle with cancer,” according to her team, Parton died Tuesday at age 80 in Nashville. Her nephew, Bryan Seaver, shared the news through a video message on Parton’s socials. articles.title: Max Muncy reveals the Dodgers’ message in 2026, and it’s not to ‘three-peat’
articles.summary: The second Freddie Freeman caught a perfectly placed double-play ball to take down the Toronto Blue Jays in the 11th inning of the 2025 World Series, the pressure began to mount for the proverbial three-peat. One of the most elusive feats in all of sports, which hasn’t been accomplished sin
articles._body: The second Freddie Freeman caught a perfectly placed double-play ball to take down the Toronto Blue Jays in the 11th inning of the 2025 World Series , the pressure began to mount for the proverbial three-peat . One of the most elusive feats in all of sports, which hasn’t been accomplished since the New York Yankees over 25 years ago, the Dodgers have a chance to cement this current run into the annals of sporting history in a way few have matched with another win this October. But is that the focus for the Dodgers in 2026, a history-making third-straight win? Discussing the prospects of a three-peat heading into the fall with Jimmy Rollins, Max Muncy let it be known that the Dodgers aren’t focused on the three-peat , as simply winning a single World Series is enough of a challenge for the team to focus on. “Well, I mean, you know, to me, the message has been the same all year long. And it’s something that I’ve tried to preach, you know, yes, we are trying to three-peat, but that’s not, you know, our mindset going in. Our mindset is just to win the World Series. Winning the World Series is already hard enough as it is. There’s enough pressure on you. And it’s already a daunting enough task to just to do that,” Muncy explained. “If you start talking about three-peat, repeat or back-to-back or, you know, any of the stuff that goes along with what we’ve accomplished, then you’re adding more pressure that just doesn’t need to be there. And so for us, it’s always been just we’re focused on winning the World Series for this year; we don’t care about the last two years, the last several years, it doesn’t matter. We’re just trying to focus on what we have right now in front of us. And, you know, that’s that’s worked out for us the last couple of years. And, you know, we’re going to try to keep it going this year.” As the Dodgers learned all too well last season during the World Series, the prospect of winning the big one is easier said than done, as a play or two going the other way could have resulted in a parade in Toronto, instead of Los Angeles. With that in mind, maybe the Dodgers’ mindset is on the money, even if the prospect of blocking out the three-peat might be easier said than done.
