articles._body: The Miami Dolphins are entering the final stretch of the 2026 preseason with more questions than answers. That may be exactly what new head coach Jeff Hafley needs. After two ugly exhibition losses, Miami’s new regime has been forced to evaluate every corner of its roster. What matters now is which players have demonstrated enough physicality, consistency and schematic discipline to survive the final cutdown. With one exhibition remaining against Atlanta, the Dolphins face a fascinating roster puzzle in which several positions appear settled while others could come down to the final handful of reps. Miami’s growing pains Sam Navarro-Imagn Images The Dolphins’ 2026 preseason has prioritized scheme installation, physical trench identity, and deep roster evaluation. Miami opened with a 20-7 road loss against Washington before suffering a 26-3 defeat at Hard Rock Stadium against the New York Giants. Those results have highlighted the growing pains of a systemic rebuild. Individual performances, though, have offered encouraging glimpses. Malik Willis has received limited opportunities with the starting unit. Miami has given extended looks at Quinn Ewers and Cam Miller, which have exposed the need for greater consistency. Defensively, aggressive play along the front seven and timely situational stops have shown promise. Still, turnovers and breakdowns from depth units have repeatedly stalled momentum. One final tune-up against Atlanta now stands between Miami and the 53-man roster deadline. Offensive Playmakers Quarterbacks (2): Malik Willis, Quinn Ewers Willis enters the season as the starter offering the mobility necessary to operate Slowik’s play-action-oriented system. His ability to threaten defenses with his legs can create opportunities for Miami’s rushing attack and simplify certain throwing windows. Ewers provides a different profile as the primary backup. He gives the Dolphins another option if the offense needs a more traditional pocket distributor. Running Back (3): De’Von Achane, Jaylen Wright, Ollie Gordon II Achane is the obvious main back here because few others can match his combination of acceleration and explosiveness. Slowik’s offense should create opportunities for him in space. Wright provides complementary speed, while Gordon offers a more physical presence between the tackles. Wide Receiver (6): Malik Washington, Jalen Tolbert, Caleb Douglas, Chris Bell, Kevin Coleman Jr, Jalen Reagor Washington projects as a primary target. Tolbert offers experience and outside versatility. Douglas gives the group another receiving option capable of handling meaningful snaps. Bell and Coleman add competition and developmental upside. Reagor’s experience and return ability strengthen his case for the final spot. Tight End (4): Greg Dulcich, Will Kacmarek, Ben Sims, DJ Herman Dulcich offers the most obvious receiving upside. Kacmarek and Sims provide additional versatility. Herman’s H-back/fullback capabilities are particularly useful in an offense that wants to manipulate defensive personnel. The decision to keep four players at the position reflects the importance of flexible formations. Offensive Line Offensive Line (9); Patrick Paul, Austin Jackson, Charlie Heck, Caedan Wallace, Kadyn Proctor, Jonah Savaiinaea, Josh Priebe, Aaron Brewer, Andrew Meyer Brewer provides the central piece at center. Paul and Jackson give the Dolphins established tackle options. Heck and Wallace add depth at tackle. Proctor, Savaiinaea, and Priebe will compete for interior responsibilities. Meyer provides additional center depth. That’s an important consideration given how quickly offensive-line injuries can derail a season. Defense Interior Defensive Line (5): Zach Sieler, Kenneth Grant, Jordan Phillips, Zeek Biggers, Matthew Butler Sieler provides veteran stability. Grant gives Miami an imposing presence in the middle. Phillips brings experience and rotational strength. Biggers and Butler will supply additional depth . EDGE (5): Chop Robinson, Josh Uche, Clelin Ferrell, Robert Beal Jr, Max Llewellyn Robinson provides the explosive pass-rushing element Miami needs. Uche offers another speed threat. Ferrell’s experience and Beal’s rotational ability help round out the group. Several injured players, including Trey Moore, David Ojabo and Cameron Goode, could complicate the final decisions depending on their roster designations. Linebacker (6): Jordyn Brooks, Tyrel Dodson, Jacob Rodriguez, Ronnie Harrison Jr, Kyle Louis, Jackson Woodard Brooks and Dodson are projected to handle the starting workload. Rodriguez and Harrison offer valuable depth. Louis and Woodard could earn their places through special-teams contributions as much as defensive snaps. Cornerback (6): JuJu Brents, Chris Johnson, Jason Marshall Jr, Ethan Bonner, Alex Austin, AJ Green III The group lacks the established star power of some AFC competitors. That places enormous importance on communication and consistency. Brents and Johnson could see significant responsibility. Marshall provides additional boundary depth. Austin, Bonner and Green must prove they can contribute on special teams and survive matchup-specific defensive assignments. Safety (4): Dante Trader Jr, Michael Taaffe, Zayne Anderson, Lonnie Johnson Jr Trader and Taaffe project as the core options, with Anderson and Johnson supplying experience and versatility. The limited number of safeties means Miami will need contributions from its corners and linebackers in hybrid packages. That could become a defining characteristic of Hafley’s defense. He has projected four SEC teams, four Big Ten teams, one Big 12 team, one Pac-12 team, and one Independent ( Notre Dame ) to make up the field. College Football Playoff First Round No. 9 USC at No. 8 Alabama At long last, USC is projected to make the College Football Playoff for the first time in program history by Pate. It’s projected opponent? The Alabama Crimson Tide, playing in the First Round of the CFP for the second consecutive season. This would mark the first matchup between the teams since the 2016 season opener, which saw Alabama come away with a dominant 52-6 win. Pate is projecting Alabama to win a First Round CFP game for the second consecutive season, this time in Tuscaloosa. Winner: No. 8 Alabama “This is presumably, what the internet was trying to tell me, Lincoln (Riley) was trying to avoid,” Pate said. “Playing on the road in the SEC. That’s why they tell me he didn’t go to LSU . But of course, we don’t believe that. But be that as it may, that’s what the streets will say.” No. 12 Boise State at No. 5 Indiana Neither of these opponents would be new to playing in the College Football Playoff. This would mark Indiana ‘s third consecutive CFP appearance, while also being Boise State ‘s second in the past three seasons. The Hoosiers would be opening, what they hope would be, their march back to a second consecutive National Championship in Bloomington. Pate is going with Curt Cignetti ‘s team to avoid the First Round upset and advance to the Quarterfinals. Winner: No. 5 Indiana “I should play the Jeopardy music before I tell you that Indiana bodybags Boise (State) ,” Pate said while predicting the Hoosiers would advance to the quarterfinals once again in 2026 by taking down the Broncos. No. 10 Texas Tech at No. 7 Texas After comments were made by Texas Tech head coach Joey McGuire about ‘ spotting the ball ‘ with the Longhorns this offseason, this would surely make for the most anticipated First Round matchup. Longtime rivals Texas and Texas Tech haven’t met since the 2023 season, which was Texas ‘ last as a member of the Big 12 Conference. The Red Raiders are looking to bounce back from being blanked in last year’s CFP, while the Longhorns are looking to advance to (at least) the Quarterfinals for the third time in the past four seasons. Pate is rocking with Steve Sarkisian ‘s team to get the win in Austin. Winner: No. 7 Texas “Memory spans are that of a fruitfly these days, so people have already stopped talking about this little dust-up between Joey McGuire and Steve Sarkisian back in the spring,” Pate said. “But, I remember. And, everyone will remember when we have a week or so to build up to this game. Texas Tech at Texas . I’ve got to go Texas .” No. 11 Oklahoma at No. 6 Oregon An appearance in this year’s College Football Playoff would mark the third consecutive for Oregon , which is still seeking its first ever National Championship. This would also mark a second strait appearance for the Sooners, as they look to bounce back from blowing a 17-0 lead in the First Round of last year’s CFP. These two programs haven’t met since the 2021 Alamo Bowl, in which Oklahoma came out on top 47-32. Pate sees this game going differently, however. He is going with the Ducks to down the Sooners and advance to the Quarterfinals. Winner: No. 6 Oregon “I will take Oregon over Oklahoma ,” Pate said. “However, let’s just remember, a lot of the vibe around Dan Lanning at Oregon right now is that ‘they can’t win big games’. Cannot does not equal have not.” CFP Quarterfinals No. 1 Notre Dame vs. No. 8 Alabama After being the First Team Out of last season’s College Football Playoff, Pate has projected Notre Dame to go undefeated and earn the No. 1 seed this season. The Fighting Irish’s Quarterfinal matchup would come against the Alabama Crimson Tide. Last season, the Tide were walloped by eventual National Champions, Indiana , 38-3 in the Quarterfinal (Rose Bowl). Those fortunes won’t be reversed this year, as Pate is going with Notre Dame to knock off Alabama for the first time since 1987 to advance to the Semis. Last season, Fernando Mendoza and the Hoosiers downed the Hurricanes 27-21 in the national title game. This season, however, Pate is going with Mario Cristobal ‘s program to get its revenge in a massive way. This victory would send Miami to the Semifinals for the second consecutive season. articles.title: USC Football: DL Jahkeem Stewart injury update via Lincoln Riley
articles.summary: USC football defensive lineman and returning freshman All-American Jahkeem Stewart will miss time with injury.
articles._body: USC football will be without sophomore defensive tackle Jahkeem Stewart for several weeks with a foot injury. CBSSports.com’s Matt Zenitz first reported the news, which WeAreSC.com can confirm. The former blue-chip prospect is expected to be a national breakout this season. USC head coach Lincoln Riley commented on the injury during his Tuesday presser, calling the injury “minor.” Riley said Stewart would miss the opener but was optimistic he could return after. “Plan is to probably hold him and then I think he’ll be available from that point forward,” he said. “It’s certainly not long term. A little precautionary right now.” WeAreSC.com sources initially mentioned that Stewart would be out at least three weeks, but Riley sounded optimistic it would be one game. WeAreSC.com first noted the injury on Friday afternoon . Given the nature of the injury, Riley said it was something they would need to monitor moving forward. This injury echoes 2025 where Stewart was injured leading into the season opener, a broken foot that nagged him all year. Sources indicate this current injury is on the same foot and described as a stress fracture. BECOME A WEARESC MEMBER TODAY! Right now you can subscribe for 75% off the regular annual membership price for the best coverage of USC football! Stewart missed Week 1 but went on to play in the next 11 games. Stewart racked up 7.5 tackles for a loss, second on the team, with a pick and forced fumble despite the injury. He earned FWAA All-American honors. Stewart was the first FWAA defensive line All-American for USC since Leonard Williams in 2012. He did not play in the Alamo Bowl, opting for surgery to be healthy for 2026. Stewart is the second notable injury in the buildup to the season along with center Kilian O’Connor . O’Connor suffered a season-ending lower body injury during the first full week of camp and underwent surgery. Stewart is a former four-star prospect as the No. 33 overall recruit and the No. 5 defensive lineman in 2025. Stewart was one of the gems of the class as USC beat out Oregon, LSU and Ohio State. Defensive Room Outlook without Jahkeem Stewart The loss of Jahkeem Stewart is a blow for USC football’s defensive line room. Yet, there is enough talent and depth to overcome for the first stretch of the season. The Trojans are clear favorites in the first three games against San Jose State, Fresno State and Louisiana. Stewart’s absence will allow more reps for fellow sophomore Floyd Boucard and potentially five-star freshman Jaimeon Winfield . Stewart’s overall healthy and leadership were two huge points of emphasis this offseason. “The main thing for Jahkeem going forward is just to stay healthy,” said defensive tackle coach Skyler Jones in spring. “He’s another one that that has to take a leadership role in becoming a vocal, positive leader because they look up to him. A lot of the young guys in that room, they came here because of Jahkeem. And so, you have guys that are going to follow you.” The 6-foot-5, 305-pound Stewart was recently named WeAreSC.com’s No. 3 Most Important Trojan for 2026. articles.title: Everything Shane Beamer said in media availability with season opener looming
articles.summary: South Carolina football head coach Shane Beamer spoke with the media on Tuesday afternoon during training camp.
articles._body: South Carolina football head coach Shane Beamer spoke with the media on Tuesday afternoon during training camp. The Gamecocks have less than two weeks until the season kicks off at Williams-Brice Stadium against Kent State on Sept. 5. Here’s everything he had to say. Opening Statement “Hope everybody had a good weekend, (and) is having a great week. Great to be here today. Getting closer to playing a game and game week, and thank God. Obviously, can’t wait to play a game, but also tired of talking season, as Coach (Steve) Spurrier used to call it, and tired of talking about the injury situation of two players. Tired of talking about the color of the shirt that I wear up here with the backdrop behind me. Tired of talking about our quarterbacks’ class schedule. I can’t wait till next week when we can actually talk about football and playing games, but on those things, color shirts, color schemes, I got nothing to do with, so I ain’t getting into all that. “One, I think it’s absolutely ridiculous (of) any kind of criticism that LaNorris Sellers took last week about an internship in his last semester of college. The same people out there that are criticizing that failed to report that he’s been on the dean’s list four times as a student here at (South) Carolina, primarily taking in-person classes. (They) failed to report that he has a chance to be an academic All-American, not academic All-Conference, academic all-American, and that he’s about to graduate from South Carolina, so they failed to talk about another previous internship that he took or that he did with contract construction and Greg Hughes last summer, and was involved with the stadium project. So hate to see any player on our team criticized. I’m going to defend our players at all times, and that’s a joke that anybody would criticize his class schedule and what he’s taken in his final semester of college when he needs one class to graduate. So, I hope he goes and has a hell of a time at the driving range and hits 1000 balls and does a good job over there because he’s earned it. Second of all, with (Jacarrius) Peak and (Dylan)Stewart, I know that was some big headline last week because a national reporter was here, and I told him that it’s probably unrealistic for them to play game one. I don’t think that’s earth-shattering, like breaking news. You guys have been out at practice, and if they’re not actually practicing, there’s a process in order to get ready to play. (I) did not rule it out. They can very easily be cleared before the Kent State game, and then I have to make a decision if they’re going to be able to play or we should play them. If they just got cleared tomorrow, I probably wouldn’t. They have futures…they’re human beings first and foremost that I care about, and they have futures in football beyond Carolina. So we’ll have them out there when they’re ready, and they’re getting closer and closer every single day to being cleared. I’ve been nothing but honest with you guys and anyone else in the national media since they got hurt with the information that I have available at the time. Anybody that has these conspiracy theories out there about their whereabouts or their status or anything is not accurate. They’re gonna play, and they’re gonna play very, very, very soon. And they’re ahead of progress in regards to benchmarks that they have to hit to one be cleared, and then it’s not like we just say the Friday before the Kent State game, ‘Okay, they’re cleared. All right, run your butts out there and let’s go play 70 plays.’ Like it doesn’t happen that way, guys. So they’re ahead of progress. They’re going to play very, very soon. They’re not there yet. Not ruled out that they’re not playing against Kent State, but it’s probably unrealistic at this point. But Towson, who knows? Mississippi State, we’ll see. But that’s where we are right now on that one. “Last week with our players, let’s talk some football, last week with our players, I thought was a really good week. Really proud of our guys on how they handled the…I don’t want to say distraction, but the schedule being different with classes starting here. So they got out of camp mode, but we told them even though you’re taking classes, we were still in camp mode, and really was pleased with the way they handled their business last week. Got off to a good start academically in the classroom, and then along those lines too, let’s digress back to academics. Nobody wants to report that, I think the four highest grade point averages in the history of the football program at the University of South Carolina are in the last four semesters with what our guys are doing well academically. So it’s not just LaNorris that bothers me that got criticized. When you criticize one guy, you’re criticizing all of our players and what they’re doing, what they’re doing from an academic standpoint, and our guys are doing a great job. Justin Light, who heads up our academics for our football players, is doing a great job, and our guys are killing it academically, and our true student-athletes. “Back to football. Impressed with the way that our players handled last week. Got a lot of situational work in. We went in the stadium on Saturday, 12:45 kickoff, just like the Kent State game is going to be. So we simulated everything, the game day is going to be like at Carolina, pregame warmups because we got a lot of coaches and players that are going through that for the first time. So we wanted to make sure we were all on the same page with how we do things in pregame warmups, how we do things when we come off the field after pregame warmups, how we do things during the

articles.title: Stanford Men’s Basketball lands 4-star transfer Nick Townsend from Yale
articles.summary: On Tuesday, Stanford men’s basketball landed a commitment from 4-star transfer Nick Townsend.
articles._body: Credit: Tipton Edits/USA TODAY Sports On Tuesday, Stanford men’s basketball landed a commitment from 4-star transfer Nick Townsend , who played four years at Yale before playing in NBA Summer League with the Philadelphia 76ers. On3’s Joe Tipton first reported the news. Townsend projects to be a starter for the Cardinal this coming season, giving head coach Kyle Smith a versatile, 6’7”, 250 pound player that can play both out on the wing and in the post. Townsend was Ivy League Player of the Year last season, averaging 16.3 points, 7.4 rebounds, 4.3 assists, and 1.1 steals per game in 30 games played (33.3 minutes per game). He shot 51.1% from the field, 46.3% from 3-point range, and 75.3% from the foul line. In two NBA Summer League games with the 76ers , Townsend averaged 7.5 points, 3.0 rebounds, 0.5 assists, and 0.5 steals per game. He has shown an ability to shoot the ball at an elite clip scoring all 15 of his Summer League points in one game. Sports-Reference: Nick Townsend VIDEO: CourtVision-Nick Townsend Summer League Highlights In this new era of guys being allowed to return to college after brief stints in the NBA, this is the first time Stanford has benefited from this change in policy. Now, it should be noted that Townsend went undrafted and only played in two NBA Summer League games, but still. Getting a guy who made a Summer League roster and scored 15 points in one of those games is a huge get. If I could make a comparison to a recent Stanford player, Townsend reminds me of Spencer Jones , who is now with the Denver Nuggets. They have similar size and abilities. Just in terms of being guys with length that can defend in the post, rebound, and shoot from the perimeter. The one thing that Townsend does do better than Jones is facilitate. Townsend’s 4.3 assists per game more than doubles the 2.0 assists per game Jones averaged his final year on The Farm. Given Kyle Smith’s track record in player development, Townsend should leave Stanford even better prepared for a chance to make an NBA roster. Overall, Nick Townsend is a fantastic pickup for Stanford. He’s a for sure starter and a guy who the Cardinal should be able to rely on in crunch time. As Stanford looks to get back to the NCAA tournament for the first time since the 2013-14 Sweet Sixteen run, Townsend projects to be a major piece in helping them accomplish that goal. articles.title: Cutter Boley produces his ‘best day’ of preseason practices, Dillingham still mum on starting QB
articles.summary: For most of Arizona State’s football roster, Tuesday was just another day. It was another morning practice in the lead-up to Week 1, one of the last before the preparation for Morgan State begins. For third-year quarterback Cutter Boley, Tuesday was something more: his 21st birthday. Head coach Kenn
articles._body: <a href="https://www.on3.com/sites/asu-devils/join/?utm_source=publisher&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=subscriber_referral&ref=1035347"> <img src="https://on3static.com/cdn-cgi/image/quality=95,format=jpg/uploads/dev/assets/cms/2026/08/04213143/Devils-Digest-FC26.png"> </a> <a href="https://www.SanTanFord.com"> <img src="https://on3static.com/cdn-cgi/image/quality=95,format=jpg/uploads/dev/assets/cms/2025/07/25180034/2024-San-Tan-Ford-Banner-3.jpg"> </a> For most of Arizona State’s football roster, Tuesday was just another day. It was another morning practice in the lead-up to Week 1, one of the last before the preparation for Morgan State begins. For third-year quarterback Cutter Boley, Tuesday was something more: his 21st birthday. Head coach Kenny Dillingham could’ve helped make Boley’s birthday unforgettable if he announced him as the team’s starting quarterback; however, he indicated that ASU’s quarterback competition is still ongoing despite Boley’s “best day” of the fall. Dillingham told the media on Tuesday that he’ll name a starting quarterback “in the next week or so,” after stating that he would “hopefully have an answer” to the QB1 question in the days following Saturday’s scrimmage. Thus, until the “week or so” is up, Boley and sixth-year quarterback Mikey Keene will continue to duke it out.  And while Dillingham didn’t name a starter, he did share what made Boley’s day so good.  “Today was a really good day with how we structured practice and allowed the quarterbacks to really get a good beat on what we’re going to see. Almost more game plan-y,” Dillingham explained. “(Boley) brings joy every day; he’s super consistent, and he knows the things. So, happy Birthday.” Boley completed passes at a high rate on Tuesday and worked with his receivers to create big plays. Boley connected with fourth-year wide receiver Reed Harris down the left sideline for a touchdown of over 30 yards — the longest pass over the air on Tuesday — during one of the team’s 11-on-11 segments in the Verde Dickey Dome.  “We hit an awesome home run post for a touchdown,” Dillingham remarked. “We hit a few intermediate passes for big plays today. … I thought it was one of his best days, if not his best day, which is a blessing.”  It’s important for Boley, Keene and the rest of the offense to continue to produce good days as the season opener nears. For Boley and Keene in particular, it’s critical for each of their chances to be named QB1 to not take steps in the other direction.  Dillingham is paying attention to which of his QBs is taking care of the football the best and scoring the most, but he’s taking note of the smaller slip-ups that can cost teams games. Over the next few practices, it’s imperative for Boley and Keene to be as close to flawless as they can possibly be.  “(The) goal is to not make the same mistake twice,” Dillingham expressed. “You’re not going to be perfect, but you should be closer to perfect in terms of where your eyes are, what decision you make post-snap. Then you hope that the identity of not taking negative plays starts to be embedded in guys.”  *** Dillingham had one major roster announcement to make following Tuesday’s practice, revealing that sixth-year linebacker Zyrus Fiaseu will be out for the year with a lower-body injury. Fiaseu was granted an extra year of eligibility for the 2026 campaign after a separate injury cut his 2025 season short after just four games. Now, he won’t suit up for a single snap in his final year.  Fiaseu — who recorded an interception, three pass deflections, two pass breakups and 34 tackles in 2024, his last full season and only full season as a Sun Devil — will be missed on the field, but his leadership impact, evident by his inclusion on the Pat Tillman Leadership Council, isn’t going anywhere.  “My heart felt heavy for him,” third-year linebacker Martell Hughes said. “All the work he’s put in, being able to come back, getting that extra year, and then just see him go down. I know the whole group felt that, but I know that we’re going to be playing for him.  “Zyrus was here this morning, still pushing us, getting us ready for practice.” Fiaseu’s impact can be felt on every linebacker in the room, from Hughes, who he’s been teammates with for two seasons, to third-year player Owen Long, who he met in the spring.  Long recalled that Fiaseu was one of the first Sun Devils to offer him help, remembering one night in particular when Fiaseu came back to the building at 10:00 p.m. to let him in since his own phone wasn’t working. “That’s just the type of guy he is,” Long explained. “He’s looking out for everyone.” While Fiaseu might be irreplaceable off the field, someone will need to step into his on-field role. Long and Hughes both mentioned fellow third-year player Ramere Davis, as well as second-year guys Tristan Bacon, Isaiah Iosefa, and Lee “Puka” Fuimaono, as linebackers who have progressed in recent months. Long, while balancing improving on the field, is looking to lead the aforementioned young players in the right direction. “Guys got to step up,” Long expressed. “Between me and (Martell), we got to take it upon us to step it up a level. I look at myself as a leader; I always try to give to other people what I can, and that’s not going to change.” Long and Hughes are likely to be ASU’s starting linebacker duo this season. Long proved himself a season ago at Colorado State, recording an FBS-leading 151 tackles, but now, at the Power Four level, he’s ready to prove he’s grown even more.  “I feel like I’ve grown tremendously,” Long said. “Learning the system, getting to a point where now it’s all about just playing fast, there’s no thinking going on. It’s just playing football at the end of the day, playing ball how I like to play ball, which is go run and hit.” *** The job of replacing Fiaseu on the field migh

articles._body: A year ago, Elijah Thomas wasn't ready to contribute at wide receiver for OU. The Checotah High School product certainly had the athletic talent to play. No one questioned his physical traits, even as a freshman. But mentally, Thomas had a lot of growing up to do. Understanding the playbook, learning how to run proper routes and just knowing where he's supposed to be on offense were things he struggled with as a true freshman. "Massive maturation," Thomas said on Tuesday when asked about the biggest difference in his game this year. "A lot of maturation in my process. I changed my process up. My mindset is all different. I’m coming for it."

articles._body: KPop Demon Hunters has slayed on Billboard ’s Top Soundtracks chart, having led the list for 57 weeks – just five weeks shy of the record. This chart was introduced a little more than 25 years ago – on June 30, 2001 – which means it doesn’t include blockbuster soundtracks of previous eras, such as West Side Story, The Sound of Music, Doctor Zhivago, Saturday Night Fever and Purple Rain . Actually, it does include one – The Vince Guaraldi Trio ’s 1965 TV soundtrack, A Charlie Brown Christmas – but only because of its chart success since 2001. KPop Demon Hunters has been No. 1 for all but four of its 61 weeks on Top Soundtracks, having yielded for one week each to Wicked: For Good , the holiday perennial A Charlie Brown Christmas , Charli xcx ’s Wuthering Heights and the soundtrack to this year’s most-talked about TV miniseries, Heated Rivalry . Related ‘Golden’ From ‘KPop Demon Hunters’ Wins Best Original Song at 2026 Oscars, But Speech Is Cut Short With KPop Demon Hunters likely to set a new record for the most weeks at No. 1 on Top Soundtracks, we thought it would be a good time to look at the 12 soundtracks that have led the chart for 25 weeks or more. The list includes two TV soundtracks and 10 film soundtracks. Notably, the five soundtracks with the most weeks at No. 1 are all from animated films. Here are the 12 soundtracks that have logged the most weeks at No. 1 on Billboard ’s Top Soundtracks chart since the chart was introduced on June 30, 2001. The number in each header is the number of weeks the album has spent at No. 1. They are listed in ascending order.

articles.title: Dolly Parton Cause of Death Revealed
articles.summary: The icon died Tuesday after "a brief battle with cancer," her team shares.
articles._body: Dolly Parton, who died today at age 80 , went through “a brief battle with cancer,” according to a statement released Tuesday evening (Aug. 25) by her team. Parton died at Vanderbilt-Ingram Cancer Center in Nashville. “Our beloved Dolly Parton spent her life and career bringing joy, laughter, hope and integrity into everything she touched,” read the statement simply signed Team Dolly. “Her unmatched generosity reached the lives of countless people whom she would never meet, yet she was always there to offer a helping hand. Whether it be the hundreds of millions of books donated through her invaluable Imagination Library or funding research that helped create a lifesaving vaccine used around the world, Dolly’s unconditional love for all people was the guiding force for her lasting impact. After bravely facing a brief battle with cancer, Dolly departed her Earthly life today at the Vanderbilt-Ingram Cancer Center surrounded by loved ones.” Related A Timeline of Dolly Parton’s Good Deeds Fearless, Fabulous Dolly Parton and What We Can All Learn From Her: A Remembrance Dolly Parton, One of Country Music’s Biggest & Brightest Icons, Dies at 80 For more than 60 years, Parton has been one of country music’s leading lights and one of music’s most revered songwriters. Beloved around the world for not only her music — including such songs as “Jolene,” “I Will Always Love You” and “Coat of Many Colors” — she also left a life filled with service , giving back in myriad ways. Parton, a member of both the Country Music Hall of Fame and Rock & Roll Hall of Fame, placed 113 tunes on Billboard ’s Hot Country Songs chart starting in 1967. Cumulatively, those songs spent more than 28 years on the chart. Her death, initially announced by her nephew, Bryan Seaver, Tuesday morning without a cause, came almost a year and a half after the death of her husband of nearly 60 years, Carl Dean, who died in March 2025. “Dolly has lived in the light and is in the arms of Jesus, surely met by Carl, her parents and countless others who had watched her and longed for her to meet them in the heavens,” Seaver said. “She never saw a door she couldn’t open and the doors she opened made and changed history.” Even in death, Parton displayed her trademark wit. Seavers added, “Dolly called me and said she wants to rest in a beautiful bed of plush cotton because after a life wearing heavy rhinestones she finally deserves to be comfortable.”

articles.title: 3 players who must save Phillies amid Zack Wheeler’s sudden collapse
articles.summary: The Philadelphia Phillies enter Tuesday night’s second game of their three-game road series vs. the Seattle Mariners at 73-59, just 3.5 games behind the Atlanta Braves. However, Zack Wheeler’s sudden regression has created an urgent postseason problem. He entered the All-Star break at
articles._body: The Philadelphia Phillies enter Tuesday night’s second game of their three-game road series vs. the Seattle Mariners at 73-59, just 3.5 games behind the Atlanta Braves. However, Zack Wheeler’s sudden regression has created an urgent postseason problem. He entered the All-Star break at 10-1 with a 2.13 ERA before going 0-4 with a 7.18 ERA across his first seven second-half starts. Wheeler allowed eight earned runs, nine hits, five walks, and four home runs over four-plus innings Monday. The eight earned runs matched his career high. His velocity has largely remained intact, and he said he feels healthy, but his diminished command has weakened the Phillies’ greatest postseason advantage . The Phillies’ starting rotation can still spearhead a potential World Series run. However, Philadelphia needs its other three established starters to redefine their roles before October rather than wait for Wheeler to rediscover his command. Cristopher Sanchez must become the Phillies’ unquestioned ace Cristopher Sanchez can no longer function merely as Wheeler’s co-ace . He must become the unquestioned leader of the Phillies’ postseason rotation and their Game 1 choice if Wheeler’s command issues continue. Sanchez is 16-4 with a 2.62 ERA, 1.22 WHIP, and 194 strikeouts across 168 1/3 innings. Before allowing four runs Sunday against the St. Louis Cardinals, the 29-year-old pitcher had gone 6-0 with a 2.18 ERA over his last seven starts. Philadelphia now needs him to work deep into games and limit the pressure on its vulnerable middle relief corps. Excellent production is no longer enough. Sanchez must give the Phillies a true ace. Jesus Luzardo must preserve Philadelphia’s rotation Jesus Luzardo must provide the second frontline option that keeps Philadelphia’s rotation formidable. His 11-5 record, 3.35 ERA, 1.15 WHIP, and 194 strikeouts show he can control games without relying heavily on defense or run support. The Phillies especially need the dominant pitcher who emerged after June 10. Entering his start last Friday, Luzardo had recorded a 1.98 ERA and an MLB-high 105 strikeouts across 12 outings. His occasional home-run lapses carry greater consequences while Wheeler struggles. Allowing two homers against St. Louis offered a reminder of that risk. Luzardo must sustain his swing-and-miss dominance and prevent one mistake from becoming a crooked inning. Aaron Nola must make his August turnaround permanent Aaron Nola offers Philadelphia the greatest uncertainty and clearest opportunity. His 5-9 record, 5.12 ERA, and 1.42 WHIP across 137 innings reflect a difficult season. His recent improvement suggests he can still restore balance to the rotation. Nola has posted a 2.51 ERA with 34 strikeouts over his last five starts. He also held the Miami Marlins to just one run across seven innings, striking out eight without issuing a walk. Now, he must prove that sharper command can withstand better lineups. Tuesday’s matchup against George Kirby provides an immediate test. Sanchez and Luzardo already look like postseason starters. Nola must turn an encouraging August into dependable October-level form. Wheeler still has five or six starts to fix his command, while his intact velocity provides legitimate optimism. Yet the Phillies cannot make their World Series hopes dependent upon that recovery. Sanchez must lead, Luzardo must dominate, and Nola must make his resurgence last. articles.title: Sabrina Carpenter Remembers Dolly Parton: ‘How Lucky Are We All to Have Experienced Your Singular Magic’
articles.summary: "The only thing I could say after we first met was, 'She really is an angel walking the earth,'" the pop singer writes.
articles._body: Sabrina Carpenter is remembering Dolly Parton following the country music legend’s death at 80. Parton died Tuesday (Aug. 25) , with the news shared by her nephew, Bryan Seaver, via Instagram. The singer/songwriter, actress, entrepreneur and philanthropist leaves behind a six-decade legacy that includes some of country music’s most famous songs, including “Jolene,” “9 to 5” and “I Will Always Love You.” Related Dolly Parton, One of Country Music’s Biggest & Brightest Icons, Dies at 80 Fearless, Fabulous Dolly Parton and What We Can All Learn From Her: A Remembrance Dolly Parton Forever: See Pictures From Her Billboard Photo Shoots Over the Years Carpenter posted a poignant Instagram carousel of photos of herself and Parton on the set of the “Please Please Please” music video, along with a heartwarming caption reflecting on the time they spent together. “Oh Dolly,” Carpenter began with a broken heart emoji. “The only thing I could say after we first met was, ‘She really is an angel walking the earth’ and ‘we look like we could be sisters!'” Carpenter continued by remembering the conversations and laughter she shared with Parton, writing that she would carry the country icon’s “wisdom, your playful outlook on life, and perfect sense of humor” with her. “There will never be another you and how lucky are we all to have experienced your singular magic as well as your once in a lifetime voice, songs, and heart,” she wrote. “Your light will be something the world will search forever to find again.” “I will always love you,” Carpenter concluded, adding three butterfly emojis. Carpenter and Parton famously joined forces earlier this year for a new version of Carpenter’s “Please Please Please,” released on the deluxe edition of her 2024 album Short n’ Sweet . The pair also starred together in the song’s music video, which finds them singing in a pickup truck and embarking on a Thelma & Louise -inspired adventure. Carpenter has cited Parton as one of her musical heroes for quite some time, so the collaboration was seemingly a dream come true for her. When announcing the Short n’ Sweet deluxe edition , Carpenter captioned the news with, “And yes that does say featuring Miss Dolly Parton…. she wouldn’t want me to swear but holy sh–!!!!!” The original “Please Please Please” was also a major career milestone for Carpenter, considering the song became her first No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 in June 2024. articles.title: Aaron Judge’s latest step toward injury return will catch fans’ attention
articles.summary: The New York Yankees are seeing day-by-day progress with Aaron Judge. As the playoff race continues to heat up, every little bit of progress helps. On Tuesday, manager Aaron Boone provided an update on Judge that will include a perplexing maneuver, per Bryan Hoch of MLB.com. Essentially, Judge wi
articles._body: The New York Yankees are seeing day-by-day progress with Aaron Judge . As the playoff race continues to heat up, every little bit of progress helps. On Tuesday, manager Aaron Boone provided an update on Judge that will include a perplexing maneuver, per Bryan Hoch of MLB.com. Essentially, Judge will likely transition to right field, but it is not certain whether he would be the DH. “I’m not saying there won’t be a DH day in there, but my plan is to have him play in the field,” Boone said. Additionally, Boone has noted that Judge has been progressing after throwing balls from 100 feet in right field at Yankee Stadium. He was also seen running in the outfield. “He looks good,” Boone said. “He’s been shagging [fly balls] just to kind of get the body used to being out there in the field and stuff, so he’s doing pretty well”. Judge has been nursing a fractured rib since April 26. Since then, Judge has missed at least 85 games since his last appearance on May 31. Meanwhile, the Yankees are leading the American League Wild Card standings at 74-59. The Boston Red Sox are coming from behind at 72-59. As for Judge, he is looking to transition into live batting practice. From there, he could experience a minor league rehab assignment. “He’s got a calendar of what they’re doing, but you make adjustments to that as you go,” Boone said. “They’re definitely mapping things out, but as you go, you check some boxes and move on. Sometimes that progress speeds up a little bit. Sometimes you take a step back.” Judge is batting .248 with 53 hits, 17 home runs, and 38 RBIs. articles.summary: The original intention was just to introduce a time dimension to solve the blockchain trilemma. Now it has turned into 312 Rust crates and 2.8 million lines of Rust code (about 2 million lines in production, about 400,000 lines in standalone test directories, and about 600,000 lines in in‑src tes
articles._body: The original intention was just to introduce a time dimension to solve the blockchain trilemma. Now it has turned into 312 Rust crates and 2.8 million lines of Rust code (about 2 million lines in production, about 400,000 lines in standalone test directories, and about 600,000 lines in in‑src test modules). Perhaps it’s just a huge ball of mud. The whitepaper that matches this ball of mud is also a huge ball of mud: https://www.niumeta.com/en/developers/architecture This doesn’t seem to be a public chain, nor a consortium chain—but it is definitely secure, decentralized, and its performance is up to standard. I gave it a name: Zero-Trust Network. Also a huge ball of mud. 6 seconds per block is actually quite slow—how can this support high‑frequency order‑book trading? In reality, high‑frequency order placement and cancellation still happen on centralized servers; only the final settlement is settled on the decentralized system at a 6‑second tick. That seems workable, because you don’t need to open an account with a broker, you don’t need to pay broker trading fees, and you can trade 24/7. That said, the code is written, but we don’t have enough hardware and network resources to test and optimize it properly. articles.title: Notre Dame joins Big Ten, SEC in ban on professional players returning to college
articles.summary: The Big Ten and SEC issued policies on Tuesday banning professional players from returning to the collegiate level. With the Notre Dame Fighting Irish being an independent program, the school had the choice to either allow it or not. Reports indicate that Notre Dame is joining the Big Ten and SEC
articles._body: The Big Ten and SEC issued policies on Tuesday banning professional players from returning to the collegiate level. With the Notre Dame Fighting Irish being an independent program, the school had the choice to either allow it or not. Reports indicate that Notre Dame is joining the Big Ten and SEC in the policy bans , according to Ross Dellenger of Yahoo! Sports. The Irish are on the board with preventing NFL, NBA, WNBA, and G League players from going back to college to play sports. “Notre Dame officials have communicated to both the SEC and Big Ten that the school is aligned with the prohibition on signing players who have been part of professional organizations, sources tell Yahoo! Sports,” Dellenger reported. “The Irish are adamantly opposed to adding pro players.” Dellenger also claimed that the ACC and Big 12 are expected to adopt similar policies . If that is the case, each of the major programs, along with Notre Dame, is on the same page. Nothing has been said about the minor programs. Not yet, at least. “ACC leaders meet later this week to consider a similar policy and Big 12 administrators are expected to also take up the matter,” Dellenger said. “The power leagues and Notre Dame seem aligned: Professional athletes do not belong in college sports.” The decision comes right before the start of the 2026-27 campaign. Timing is everything, as Chris Vanini of The Athletic reported that NFL final cuts are set for Sunday , August 30. It appears college football programs were expecting multiple pro players to attempt to return to college sports and have promptly put a stop to it. “Important note about the timing of these conference bans: NFL final cuts come Sunday, and CFB teams must lock in their rosters the day before their first game,” Vanini reported. “A flood was coming.” One of the only major programs potentially upset with the new policies is the LSU Tigers. Lane Kiffin was in line to sign not one, but two players who were previously cut from the NFL. However, that will no longer come to fruition. articles.title: Britney Spears’ Son Jayden James Lands MAC Cosmetics Campaign & Says He’ll Release Music ‘When He’s Ready’
articles.summary: The 19-year-old is adding another fashion credit to his career after walking the Vetements runway at Paris Men's Fashion Week.
articles._body: Jayden James, the 19-year-old son of Britney Spears and Kevin Federline , is the latest face of MAC Cosmetics’ relaunched digital publication MACzine , which revealed his cover on Tuesday (Aug. 25). In the cover image, James is seen holding the brand’s Fix+ Setting Spray as he looks directly into the camera, while the cover poses a cheeky question: “Who the f— is Jayden James?” Related Writer Liz Meriwether Has Been Listening to Britney Spears ‘A Lot’ While Writing Script For ‘The Woman in Me’ Biopic Britney Spears Says Beyoncé Is ‘All I Listen To’ Lately, Especially Her ‘Naughty’ Album Here’s Why Cardi B Calls Herself ‘Hip-Hop’s Britney Spears’ The answer, at least for right now, is model, musician and emerging creative. In his MACzine interview, James opened up about his approach to skincare, giving most of the credit to his girlfriend. “Hydration always, but my girlfriend does my whole routine for me, so she’s really the expert,” he said. MAC global creative director Nicola Formichetti also pointed to James’ creative instincts as a reason for bringing him into the MAC world. “At MAC, we celebrate emerging talent and love following their creative journeys,” Formichetti said in a statement. “Jayden’s unique sensibility makes him the perfect MACzine cover star. He’s also an incredible pianist, and I’m so excited to see what he does next.” The cover gives James another fashion triumph to celebrate after he and his older brother, Sean Preston, 20, made their runway debuts during Paris Men’s Fashion Week in June. The brothers walked in Vetements’ Spring/Summer 2027 menswear show, making it their first major runway appearance. James subsequently told Vogue that he was interested in doing more modeling, while acknowledging that his first trip down the runway left him wanting to sharpen his skills. “I could master my walk better — I was definitely stiff because I was nervous,” he said. “But Preston and I are trying to do music and other things.” Music remains an important part of the brothers’ creative lives. Sean Preston once described music as his “foundation,” while James has said that the two have been making music together for years. James also told MACzine that he is continuing to work on his own music, although he plans to share it publicly “when he’s ready,” the story notes. For now, fashion is giving him plenty to work with. Earlier this month, James attended MAC Cosmetics’ House of Glass event in Los Angeles, where he joined guests including JT , Gabbriette, Ashtin Earle and Landon Barker .

articles.title: Mark Mitchell did not sign Exhibit 10 contract
articles.summary: Will Mark Mitchell play at Kentucky? A positive step was taken on Wednesday. Another big step remains.
articles._body: Will Mark Mitchell play for Kentucky in the 2026-27? That’s what everyone is trying to figure out. Some more clarity was found on Wednesday but the road is not completely clear yet. The wildest August in college athletics history is not slowing down. Shortly after the Big Ten voted and approved a policy that banned NFL players from playing college football again, the SEC followed suit. The newest major eligibility policy in college athletics has a bigger reach. That makes things more complicated in college basketball. CBS Sports’ Jon Rothstein reported after the SEC’s announcement that any player that signed an Exhibit 10 contract will not be eligible to play . Luckily, that should not affect Mitchell. KSR’s Jack Pilgrim reports that the former Missouri star and current Kentucky commit did not sign an Exhibit 10 contract despite playing in NBA Summer League with the Denver Nuggets. Kentucky commit Mark Mitchell did not sign an Exhibit 10 contract with the Denver Nuggets, source tells KSR https://t.co/6rBkhCNcOn — Jack Pilgrim (@JackPilgrimKSR) August 25, 2026 SEC bans former pros, gives Greg Sankey authority to suspend schools that violate the rule Kentucky seems to have avoided one major conflict with its prized transfer portal recruiting win in August, but the coast is not clear yet. Is playing in NBA Summer League allowed? We won’t know until the league office released the official language of this new eligibility policy. There is also another roadblock to get through. Since Mitchell did not enter the portal during the April window, SEC rules state that he is not allowed to transfer from one league school to another. Will this rule be enforced? That’s what we’re about to find out. SEC commissioner Greg Sankey was just awarded full authority to enforce penalties for eligibility violations. Does that authority include the transfer rule? The commissioner has been a stickler for this rule and could attempt to make a hard stance after a crazy month with multiple league members attempting to add players to rosters via lawsuits. The Cats got some good news on Wednesday night but the fight to get Mark Mitchell on the floor at Rupp Arena is not over yet. But he cannot build on momentum if he is not in the lineup . Adames has a moderate UCL sprain in his non-throwing arm, per NBC Sports Bay Area’s Alex Pavlovic. The soon-to-be 31-year-old Dominican plans to get a second opinion before proceeding forward. Given the Giants’ ugly 53-78 record, there may be no point in bringing him back for the remainder of the 2026 MLB campaign. Though, the organization could find value in a strong finish to his individual season. Whether it is to grow his confidence for 2027 or increase his stock for a potential offseason trade, San Francisco can benefit greatly from an active Adames. Pushing through an elbow issue can be brutal, however. Who is to say the veteran right-handed hitter can even be productive in such condition? An injury-hampered Matt Chapman does the Giants no good, and the same logic applies to No. 2. A healthy Willy Adames is the best outcome president of baseball operations Buster Posey can ask for heading into the new year. If surgery is required, he will end the campaign with a .230 batting average, .289 on-base percentage, .424 slugging percentage, .713 OPS, 21 homers, 51 RBIs and 25 doubles in 121 games played. Giants fans should get a clear answer about Adames’ immediate future soon. The post Giants’ Willy Adames gets elbow injury update before Reds game appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles.title: Another HBCU inks national campaign with renowned clothing brand
articles.summary: Southern University’s Human Jukebox is bringing HBCU culture and style to one of fashion’s most recognizable brands. The iconic marching band has partnered with Gap for the brand’s new “Denim on Your Own” campaign, spotlighting the individuality, creativity, and unmistakable energy of the Human J
articles._body: Southern University’s Human Jukebox is bringing HBCU culture and style to one of fashion’s most recognizable brands. The iconic marching band has partnered with Gap for the brand’s new “Denim on Your Own” campaign, spotlighting the individuality, creativity, and unmistakable energy of the Human Jukebox. The collaboration pairs Gap’s signature denim with the sound, movement, and tradition that have made Southern University’s band a staple of HBCU culture. Known for its precision, powerful arrangements, and high-energy performances, the Human Jukebox has built a legacy that extends far beyond the football field. Now, the Baton Rouge-based band is bringing that influence into the fashion world. Leaning into what the brand does best, Gap styled members of the Human Jukebox in Canadian tuxedos — but with a Southern University twist. Throughout the campaign, band members can be seen wearing dark denim jackets and matching jeans, complete with Southern University branding across the backs and sleeves of the jackets. The customized pieces blend Gap’s classic denim aesthetic with the school pride and personality that have long defined the HBCU experience. Those familiar with HBCU culture know these institutions have always been breeding grounds for creativity and self-expression, especially through fashion. From Homecoming looks and everyday campus style to marching band uniforms, students have long used clothing to showcase their individuality and school pride. While much of that influence was once celebrated primarily within HBCU communities, mainstream fashion has increasingly begun recognizing the creativity that has existed on these campuses for generations. Southern University isn’t the only HBCU receiving a larger fashion spotlight. Earlier this month, Grambling State University’s World-Famed Tiger Marching Band appeared in Urban Outfitters’ “All Together Now” campaign. The campaign featured 76 students representing 10 universities, with Grambling serving as the only HBCU included. Texas Southern University’s Ocean of Soul Marching Band also received a major fashion moment when it was featured in Vogue in June. Released on Juneteenth, the special summer edition highlighted the people, places, and communities that have helped shape modern Texas while giving the Ocean of Soul an opportunity to showcase HBCU band culture on a national stage. articles.title: R&B legend makes surprise pop-up on HBCU band
articles.summary: Southern University’s Human Jukebox got an unexpected visit from R&B royalty during a recent band practice. Grammy Award-winning singer Bobby Brown surprised members of the Human Jukebox last week, stopping by as the iconic marching band prepared for another season of bringing its signature s
articles._body: Southern University’s Human Jukebox got an unexpected visit from R&B royalty during a recent band practice. Grammy Award-winning singer Bobby Brown surprised members of the Human Jukebox last week, stopping by as the iconic marching band prepared for another season of bringing its signature sound to the field. The surprise gave students a chance to meet the New Edition member and solo star whose career has helped shape R&B and pop music for decades. Known for hits including “My Prerogative” and “Every Little Step,” Brown rose to fame as a member of New Edition before launching a successful solo career in the 1980s. His visit brought together two influential pieces of Black music culture, as the legendary performer spent time with one of the most celebrated marching bands in the HBCU community. For members of the Human Jukebox, what started as another day of practice quickly turned into a memorable moment with a music legend. Although his visit to the band was a surprise, Brown was already scheduled to be on Southern University’s campus. The singer was set to headline the Southern Jaguars Athletics Gala the following night, an annual event that raises money to support the university’s student-athletes and athletic programs. During his visit, Brown listened as the Human Jukebox rehearsed before taking a moment to praise the students for their sound. “I just want to say you guys sound amazing, and I’m glad I was able to bear witness to it,” Brown told the students. With a career spanning nearly five decades, Brown has made a lasting impact not only on R&B but also on Black music and culture as a whole. Many of his solo hits, including “My Prerogative” and “Every Little Step,” along with songs from his time with New Edition, have become popular arrangements for HBCU marching bands across the country. That connection made Brown’s visit to the Human Jukebox even more fitting. HBCU bands have long taken songs from influential Black artists and transformed them into powerful arrangements that introduce the music to new generations. Brown getting the opportunity to hear one of the culture’s most celebrated bands up close brought that relationship full circle. articles.title: Youth Music Awards Heads to Liverpool for 2026 Ceremony: See Full List of Nominations
articles.summary: The judging panel features artists Myles Smith, Bicep & ALT BLK ERA.
articles._body: The Youth Music Awards are hitting the road. Nominations for the 2026 ceremony have been unveiled, with this year’s event moving from London to Liverpool for the first time since its launch in 2019. Taking place at St George’s Hall on Oct. 28, the event shines a spotlight on the emerging artists and community projects helping shape the future of British music. The 2026 shortlist spans 11 categories, recognising talent both onstage and behind the scenes, as well as the young leaders working to make the U.K. music industry more accessible. More than 60 judges from across the sector will select this year’s winners, representing companies including Apple, Meta, Sony Music, Spotify, Universal Music Group and YouTube. Artist judges include BRIT Award winner Myles Smith, DJ duo Bicep, heavy rockers ALT BLK ERA, Faithless’ Sister Bliss and BBC Radio 1Xtra and BBC Introducing presenters Snoochie Shy and Jess Izsatt. Among this year’s nominees are several Liverpudlian acts, spanning singer-songwriters Livvy K, Bethane and Astles to rapper KOJ, giving the host city a strong presence across the shortlist. The rising star award (artist) features bilingual rapper Hulton, Livvy K, Marz Fay, Righteous Reck and Roukaya B. The lyricist award shortlist includes Astles, KOJ, M. Yesekaon, and Sunkissed Child, while the music video award features Dayzy, Hillarynx and Simon A. As per a press release, the event’s relocation to Liverpool will create 23 paid opportunities for young people in the city and across the North West region, with roles including photographers, PR assistants, content creators and event runners. The Youth Music Awards Access Fund, funded by Sony Music, will also support nominees with travel costs to and from the event. Three recent Mercury Prize winners have been previously supported by Youth Music-backed projects: Sam Fender (2025) received early funding through the Newcastle-based organisation Generator, English Teacher (2024) won the Youth Music Awards’ rising star award in 2022. Ezra Collective (2023) developed through London youth groups Tomorrow’s Warriors and Kinetika Bloco. In a statement, Carol Reid , interim co-CEO at Youth Music said: “We’re so excited to announce this year’s Youth Music Awards nominees. It’s an inspiring snapshot of what a more diverse and creative music industry could look like, if we support grassroots music. These are the future changemakers of our industry.” See the full list of nominees below. articles.title: Beyoncé Pays Tribute to Dolly Parton for Her ‘Profound Impact on the World’
articles.summary: "I'm honored that I had the privilege to work with you. I will treasure that forever," Bey wrote to the late country singer.
articles._body: Beyoncé is remembering Dolly Parton following the country music legend’s death at 80. On Tuesday (Aug. 25), Beyoncé shared an emotional tribute to Parton on her official website, recalling the impact the country star had on her and countless other artists. Related Beyoncé Drops ‘Morning Dew (Donk)’ Remix Pack Featuring Jay-Z Fearless, Fabulous Dolly Parton and What We Can All Learn From Her: A Remembrance Dolly Parton’s Half-Century Hot 100 Legacy: ‘9 to 5,’ ‘Islands in the Stream’ & More “Dolly, you were the barometer. The North Star. Bold and brilliant. Talented and tenacious,” Beyoncé wrote. “You taught so many lessons on how to be uniquely oneself.” The superstar went on to thank Parton for her artistry and influence, writing that she was “grateful for your art, your heart, your generosity, your humor, your entrepreneurship.” “I’m honored that I had the privilege to work with you. I will treasure that forever,” Beyoncé continued. “Thank you for your profound impact on the world.” Beyoncé concluded her message by describing Parton as “an angel who has made this world a happier place because of your joyful art,” adding, “You are truly one of one. Rest peacefully.” Parton was featured on Beyoncé’s 2024 country-inspired album Cowboy Carter , lending her voice to the album’s “Dolly P” interlude before introducing Beyoncé’s reimagining of Parton’s 1973 classic “Jolene.” Parton’s voicemail on “Dolly P” directly set up Beyoncé’s version of the song, which featured newly written lyrics and a more confrontational take on its narrator’s warning to Jolene. Beyoncé’s reinvention landed on the Billboard Hot 100 at No. 7, surpassing the original version’s peak at No. 60 back in 1974. Their collaboration came as Beyoncé began to shift and experiment with country music and the genre’s Black roots and broader history on Cowboy Carter . The album featured a number of country legends and collaborators, with Parton’s presence serving as a meaningful bridge between Beyoncé’s contemporary interpretation and one of country music’s eternal voices. Parton died Tuesday in Nashville at age 80, her family announced. Her nephew, Bryan Seaver, shared the news in an Instagram video , describing her as having “lived in the light.” Across a career spanning more than six decades, Parton became one of music’s most influential singer/songwriters, with classics including “Jolene,” “9 to 5” and “I Will Always Love You.” Her influence extended well beyond country music through her work as an actress, entrepreneur, and philanthropist. Read the full message Beyoncé wrote to Parton below. Beyoncé pays tribute to the legendary Miss Dolly Parton. ❤️ https://t.co/NysKafJI1N pic.twitter.com/zYv4UeHs6y — BEYONCÉ LEGION (@BeyLegion) August 25, 2026

articles.title: Eagles’ Lane Johnson injury scare brings dark cloud before preseason finale
articles.summary: With seemingly the entire City of Brotherly Love packed into Lincoln Financial Field for the Philadelphia Eagles’ open practice before their preseason finale against the Cincinnati Bengals, clouds formed over South Philly when Lane Johnson exited the field early with trainers and moved to t
articles._body: With seemingly the entire City of Brotherly Love packed into Lincoln Financial Field for the Philadelphia Eagles’ open practice before their preseason finale against the Cincinnati Bengals , clouds formed over South Philly when Lane Johnson exited the field early with trainers and moved to the sidelines during individual drills. Taking to social media to break down what happened, ESPN’s Tim McManus revealed what he saw early and how it impacted the rest of Johnson’s practice. “Eagles RT Lane Johnson is not currently participating in team drills after walking off the field earlier in practice with a trainer,” McManus wrote. “Johnson remains on the sideline in uniform, helmet in hand.” While it is unclear how this assumed injury will impact Johnson for the rest of the month, as it’s not like he was expected to see snaps in the final preseason game of the summer, any missed time will hurt even more because there simply isn’t much left. The Eagles’ first-round pick in 2013, Johnson announced earlier in the summer that he will most likely be calling it a career when the 2026 NFL season comes to an end, opting to focus on his family over another campaign with his Hall of Fame spot more or less locked up. Even if Markel Bell looks like the future of the position, and Johnson himself has handed the 6-foot-9 supersized Miami Hurricane his endorsement , No. 65 remains arguably the best right tackle in football and will be paramount in establishing Chris Kuper’s system after well over a decade with Jeff Stoutland running the show. He has been dealing with neck inflammation, but it seems as if Smith could return when rosters expand in September. Dodgers manager Dave Roberts believes that may indeed be the case. “I was talking to Brandon McDaniel actu
articles._body: Will Los Angeles Dodgers catcher Will Smith return from injury soon ? He has been dealing with neck inflammation, but it seems as if Smith could return when rosters expand in September . Dodgers manager Dave Roberts believes that may indeed be the case . “I was talking to Brandon McDaniel actually, who does kind of a lot of different things in our organization,” Roberts said Tuesday, via AM 570 LA Sports. “B-Mac said that he’s (Smith) gonna catch five innings today and the outlook is he will be active on September 1. With that, he will probably be every other day, but getting him back September 1 would be fantastic.” Smith has been limited to 52 games played this season due to injury. He was hitting .249/.338/.382 across 201 plate appearances before suffering the injury. The Dodgers would love to have Smith return on September 1 so he has time to prepare for the postseason with the big league ball club. Returning on September 1 would allow Roberts and the Dodgers to ease Smith back into the lineup. As Roberts said, the catcher may initially play “every other day” once he first returns. With expanded rosters, Los Angeles can realistically keep catchers Ben Rortvedt and Hunter Feduccia on the roster even once Smith makes his return from injury. It is worth remembering that catcher Dalton Rushing is also working his way back from injury. He may return as only a hitter and not a catcher before the playoffs this season, however. The Dodgers are currently playing the Braves in Atlanta. The post Dodgers’ Dave Roberts reveals Will Smith’s potential injury return date appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles.title: Eminem Shares Heartfelt Letter Dolly Parton Sent Him About an ‘Unexplained Connection’ Between Them
articles.summary: The country legend died at 80 years old on Tuesday (Aug. 25).
articles._body: Eminem and Dolly Parton never met, but they shared a mutual admiration for each other’s craft. Following Parton’s death on Tuesday (Aug. 25), Slim Shady shared a heartfelt note that the country icon sent him after he was inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame in 2022. “I’m sorry we never got a chance to meet, but getting this note from Dolly really had a an impact on me,” Em captioned the post on social media. “She definitely didn’t have to take the time to do it. Even for a kid who mostly listened to rap music, she was an icon. A superstar in every sense. Rest easy Dolly. And thank you for the kind words.” Related Dolly Parton, One of Country Music’s Biggest & Brightest Icons, Dies at 80 Fearless, Fabulous Dolly Parton and What We Can All Learn From Her: A Remembrance Dolly Parton Forever: See Pictures From Her Billboard Photo Shoots Over the Years In her letter, Parton revealed how, while she wasn’t very knowledgeable when it comes to hip-hop, she’s long felt an “unexplained connection” to Eminem. “Congratulations on your induction into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame,” she wrote. “Your performance was amazing and everybody said so. Even though I don’t know a lot about rap music, I’ve come to know that you are the very best at it. Aside from that I hope what I have to say will not seem weird or strange to you but I have always felt some unexplained connection to you like I know you somehow.” The versatile singer/songwriter continued: “I had hoped to meet you at the show but you know how nuts those things are, personally I hate ’em and I missed my chance but maybe someday we’ll meet. In the meantime, keep doing what you’re doing because you do it so well and no matter how complex your world may be just know you are very special and touch people in ways you don’t even know.” Parton left an indelible mark on country and pop music with a career that spanned more than half a century. Parton died Tuesday in Nashville at 80 years old. She spent the last year dealing with unspecified health issues, which led to her canceling numerous public appearances, including her 2025 Las Vegas residency. On Tuesday, her reps revealed that Parton died “after bravely facing a brief battle with cancer.” Paul McCartney, Billy Ray Cyrus, George Strait and Elton John were among the outpouring of moving tributes to the “9 to 5” singer spanning music and all facets of entertainment since Parton’s death became public knowledge. articles.title: Wisconsin WR Eugene Hilton Ready to Make Noise in 2026
articles.summary: Sophomore wide receiver Eugene Hilton could help Wisconsin balance out its offense in 2026 and provide some consistency with the passing attack.
articles._body: MADISON, Wis. — Wisconsin quarterbacks coach Kenny Guiton teaches his players ‘KYP’ or know your personnel. When it comes to Eugene Hilton , Guiton says, trust that if you put it in his area, the sophomore wide receiver has the tools to come down with it. “I think he’s really taking a stride around here that everyone is loving to see,” Guiton told Badger Blitz. Prior to the question being posed, Guiton jokingly gave a little hush signal to not let the cat out of the bag with Hilton. The former four-star wide receiver has shown flashes of beginning to blossom during fall camp. In one practice, Hilton had a total of four touchdowns, including one rushing score on an end-around. “It’s been awesome,” said junior quarterback Colton Joseph . “He’s been making plays. He’s been getting open. That’s helped me gain confidence in him down the field.” As a true freshman, Hilton caught eight passes for 91 yards. Hilton had a career-high two receptions in Wisconsin’s upset win over No. 21 Illinois and a career-long 42-yard catch that set up a touchdown at sixth-ranked Oregon. Playing behind the likes of Vinny Anthony and Jayden Ballard , Hilton’s opportunities in the pass game were few and far between. Add in the fact that just shy of 50 percent of his snaps came on running plays, and the Badgers were constantly rotating quarterbacks due to injuries, Hilton wasn’t able to aid a UW passing attack that ranked among the worst in the country in 2025. Even though he’s moved to arguably the top of the totem pole in terms of pass catching threats, Hilton still doesn’t want to set the bar too high. “The mindset stays the same,” Hilton told Badger Blitz. “We’ve got a lot of depth, so sometimes you might get the ball five times. Sometimes you might get it once. You might get it eight times. Just making the most of the opportunities when you get the ball.” Hilton Enters the Portal, Returns to Wisconsin In the off-season, Hilton entered the transfer portal. He heard from the likes of Indiana, LSU, Florida, and Michigan State, but opted to return to Wisconsin for his sophomore season. Expressing concerns over the direction of the offense, Hilton was swayed by head coach Luke Fickell and former wide receivers coach Jordan Reid . “I didn’t want to waste another year,” Hilton told reporters in the spring. “I wanted to make sure that we were going to do things right here — We were going to make big plays, we were going to have the right guys. Not saying we didn’t last year, but I just think we needed to make bigger strides.” The Badger Blitz Fall Camp Sale is still live! Nobody gets you closer to your favorite team and now you can become a VIP annual subscriber for 75% off! That’s right. For just $29.99, you’ll get exclusive insight, analysis, and coverage of Wisconsin football, basketball, and recruiting for the next year! Speaking exclusively with Badger Blitz in January, Hilton said the additions in the portal from Joseph, running back Abu Sama , running back Bryan Jackson , wide receiver Jaylon Domingeaux , and wide receiver Shamar Rigby reinstilled his belief in the Badger offense. Along with that, UW believes Hilton could be their go-to receiver in year two. “They believe I’m a guy who can really help them in the future. I’m looking to be the number one guy next year,” Hilton added about his decision to return to UW. “It wasn’t necessarily that. They always valued me, and I believed it. It was just outside things and other factors that led to the decision to enter the transfer portal. “It never had anything to do with Wisconsin, the program, or the coaches.” Is Hilton WR1? If you ask Hilton today, he’ll give you a different answer about being the No. 1 receiving option. Wisconsin appears to be deeper than expected at the position. Like Hilton, Rigby also had a breakout camp. The Badgers returned valued seniors Chris Brooks and Tyrell Henry as well. When asked if he’s the ‘3rd and 8, gotta have it receiver,’ Hilton won’t shy away from the pressure, but won’t be demanding the football either. “I would hope the coaches think of me as that, but we also have a lot of other guys who are a good option for that,” said Hilton. “It’s just everybody being ready for that situation. That comes with having an attacking mindset. Regardless if it’s me or someone else, I know we’re all going to do our 1/11th and go get our job done.” Hilton certainly has the right bloodline for the job. The son of former NFL All-Pro wide receiver T.Y. Hilton , Eugene has advantages most don’t. Hilton said that when he gets extended breaks during fall camp, he’ll reach out to his father, who accumulated nearly 10,000 receiving yards and 53 touchdowns at the highest level. “He’s been my support system since I was a kid. He’s always been there for me,” said Hilton. “Him instilling how are you reading the defense? How are you getting open? Just helping me with the smaller details that I think a lot of people overlook — the releases, the top of the routes, and things like that.” Hilton is also growing as a run blocker. Challenged by offensive coordinator Jeff Grimes in the off-season, Hilton has taken that role to heart. “I’ve grown a lot,” said Hilton. “Just getting myself stronger and building up muscle, but blocking is just a want-to. It’s an effort thing. Last year, I obviously wanted to block, but coming in from high school, you know, it’s a little different. You’re the guy, and you’re not really worried about blocking. articles.title: Former Miami WR Cam Vaughn files lawsuit against school seeking to enter NCAA transfer portal
articles.summary: Former Miami receiver Cam Vaughn has filed a lawsuit against the school and the NCAA in an effort to officially enter the transfer portal, Vaughn’s representatives told On3’s Pete Nakos. Vaughn was dismissed from the Hurricanes football program earlier this month after joining the progra
articles._body: Former Miami receiver Cam Vaughn has filed a lawsuit against the school and the NCAA in an effort to officially enter the transfer portal, Vaughn’s representatives told On3’s Pete Nakos . Vaughn was dismissed from the Hurricanes football program earlier this month after joining the program in January. Miami head coach Mario Cristobal confirmed Vaughn’s dismissal during a Monday morning radio hit on WQAM last week, ending the former West Virginia and Jacksonville State transfer’s time in Coral Gables before ever playing a snap with the Hurricanes. Now, Vaughn is taking Miami to court for an opportunity to hit the transfer portal for the fourth time in the last three years. [ $19.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage ] “Today we filed suit in Miami-Dade County against the University of Miami and the NCAA on behalf of Cameron Vaughn, an accomplished Division I wide receiver who committed to Miami based on its promises of a multi-year scholarship and revenue-sharing and NIL compensation,” Vaughn’s representative, Blake Sercye , said in a statement to On3. “On August 17, 2026, Miami dismissed Cam and cancelled his scholarship with no written explanation, no identified rule violation, and no hearing. Miami then refused to submit the waiver request the NCAA requires so that he can enter the transfer portal — leaving Cam without the ability to pursue his education or a team to play for. We are asking the court to hold Miami and the NCAA responsible for their failures to Cam, and grant him the relief he needs so that he can continue his education and career.” Vaughn signed with the Hurricanes in January following a transfer from West Virginia , where he hauled in 35 receptions for 541 yards and four touchdowns for the Mountaineers in 2025. He previously spent the 2024 season at Jacksonville State , where he caught 803 yards and five touchdowns as a redshirt freshman. After entering the transfer portal, Vaughn became the No. 201 overall player in the  On3 Industry Transfer Rankings . He was also the No. 36-ranked wide receiver to hit the open market during the 2026 portal cycle. Vaughn played high school football at  Temple  (Ga.) before joining Jacksonville State in 2023. He committed to West Virginia as the No. 439 overall player and No. 73-ranked wide receiver to enter the transfer portal from the 2025 cycle, according to the  On3 Industry Transfer Portal Rankings . Vaughn was one of 13 players to commit to Miami out of the transfer portal this past cycle. That group includes former  Duke  receiver  Cooper Barkate , who was one of Miami’s marquee transfer additions along with fellow Blue Devils teammate  Darian Mensah after last year’s run to the national championship game. — On3’s Nick Schultz contributed to this report.
