articles.title: Show HN: CaptureAgent – find, price, draft, grade, run and fund federal work
articles.summary:
I’m a 2x defense founder and aerospace engineer.

I initially built CaptureAgent for my own company, but now I want to share it with other founders. While running my defense startup, I lost days deciding which federal opportunities to pursue and weeks assembling teams, researching competitors, p
articles._body: I’m a 2x defense founder and aerospace engineer. I initially built CaptureAgent for my own company, but now I want to share it with other founders. While running my defense startup, I lost days deciding which federal opportunities to pursue and weeks assembling teams, researching competitors, pricing work, checking compliance, negotiating with subcontractors, and writing proposals. I see startups and the small-business industrial base as one of America’s secret weapons, but small business win rate for federal funding is between 17-22% annually and competing for funding can push founders away from the companies they set out to build. To keep my company afloat, I sometimes pursued tangential tech areas instead of staying focused on our original vision. Pursuing poor-fit opportunities, or being disqualified over technicalities, consumed runway and pulled me away from engineering. The software, consultants, and proposal shops I engaged or worked with were expensive and still left much of the work to me. Independent capture and proposal consultants can charge roughly $150–$300 an hour. SBIR advisory firms typically charge $3,000–$7,500 monthly plus 3-7% of an award ($7,500–$17,500 on a $250,000 win). CaptureAgent was conceived to help hack into this inefficient system and cut through the red tape. It streamlines and automates the federal contracting lifecycle for small government contractors. Users provide their own SAM.gov, Anthropic, and OpenAI API keys; they are envelope-encrypted per organization. Admins get to set fine-grained read/write permissions for users, and External agents can also get MCP access through the same permissions to automate up to 90% of the workflow. One company profile supports searches across several public procurement sites, fit and eligibility scoring; competitive analysis; and proposal drafting and evaluation. After an award, CaptureAgent uses the proposal info to seed a project-management workspace and create an integrated master schedule with earned-value metrics and CDRL tracking. The same profile and contract-performance data can be reused for fundraising. Users can search 1,391 U.S. investors and 30 accelerators and prepare SAFEs, pitch decks, financial models, and applications. The platform also provides AI-guided readiness tracking for compliance certifications, including DD2345, FCL, ATO, CMMC, and FedRAMP, and CMMC (with a computed SPRS score). Compliance alone costs small businesses hundreds of thousands $$$,$$$. Capture, delivery, compliance, and fundraising reuse the same company and opportunity data instead of rebuilding it across fragmented tools and teams. I’d value feedback from anyone who has managed federal bids or delivered government contracts. YC defense founders, feel free to contact me for free test access. articles.title: Fearless, Fabulous Dolly Parton and What We Can All Learn From Her: A Remembrance
articles.summary: Parton died Aug. 25 at the age of 80, leaving far more than just her incredible career in music behind.
articles._body: When the news broke today that Dolly Parton had died, everyone in the Billboard newsroom from the most seasoned veteran to the college intern shed a tear — because it felt like, as one person said, “an angel had just died.” The world already feels like a colder place without her in it. Everyone loved Dolly Parton because Dolly Parton honestly loved everyone. (Which is very different from liking everyone.) Parton felt like the one person on earth that everyone could agree was nothing but a universal good. Groups who were famously at odds, such as conservative Christians and the LGBTQIA community, agreed on their love for Dolly. Today she’s even being mourned by The Muppets . Parton generally declined to talk politics or politically charged issues, but she very clearly made her strong opinions known, and the thread always led back to treating people with love and kindness. She constantly stressed that she wasn’t here to judge; she’d leave that up to God. But that doesn’t mean she played it safe. Not in her words or in her music. People weren’t writing songs about dying by suicide because they were pregnant in 1968 (or really now, 60 years later), but Parton was. In “The Bridge,” a women jumped off a bridge where she and her lover had first kissed after he abandoned her when she became pregnant. Even more heartbreaking is 1969’s “Down From Dover,” about a pregnant teen whose parents send her away and her baby dies while being born — because, the protagonist reckons, the baby knew the father was never coming back. That one got banned from the radio. (By the today’s far right definition, she was “woke” — but not even the far right was ever going to cancel Dolly.) She had a unique blend of savvy and sensitivity, knowing when the right thing for her business was also just the right thing in general. In 2018, she renamed her Dixie Stampede dinner attraction Dolly Parton’s Stampede because she became aware the word “Dixie” and its associations with the Confederacy could be hurtful to some. “When they said ‘Dixie’ was an offensive word, I thought, ‘Well, I don’t want to offend anybody,” she told Billboard in a 2020 cover interview . “This is a business. We’ll just call it The Stampede.’ As soon as you realize that [something] is a problem, you should fix it. Don’t be a dumbass. That’s where my heart is. I would never dream of hurting anybody on purpose.” In that same interview, she was ready when asked about the Black Lives Matter movement and was unequivocal in her support of peaceful protests: “I understand people having to make themselves known and felt and seen,” she said. “And of course Black lives matter. Do we think our little white asses are the only ones that matter? No!” In my more than 30 years as a journalist, I have never had a line from a story picked up as much as her “little white asses” comment, though Billboard deliberately didn’t lead with it or put it in the headline. Other artists may have backed down or said they were misquoted, but not Dolly. So many artists, especially young ones, could learn from Parton about professionalism. Parton’s publicists never asked for questions in advance or said any topics were off limits — because Parton knew how to handle herself, and though petite, was hardly delicate. She was also freakishly punctual. One time I had a 6:00 a.m. interview with Parton. I commented about it being so early, and she chided me for thinking that 6:00 a.m. was early, since she normally got up by 4:00 a.m. We had exactly 10 minutes. She was still answering a question when we rounded the 10-minute mark. She finished around 10 minutes and 15 seconds in, and immediately told me we had run over and she had to go. I still got enough from that 10-minute interview to write two pieces with no overlap at all. Parton leaves behind more than 3,000 songs — one of which, “Jolene,” Billboard editors picked as the Best Country Song of All Time . (Which was just one year after the editors chose Parton as the Greatest Country Artist of All Time .) But her legacy is so much more than even that. Her Imagination Library provided free monthly books to children from birth to age five for more than 30 years, serving more than 3 million kids. She gave $1 million to Vanderbilt University to help develop the COVID-19 vaccine. Here’s how trusted she was to do the right thing: In 2022, Jeff Bezos and his wife, through their Bezos Courage and Civility Award, gave Dolly Parton $100 million to donate to the non-profits and charities she chose. In my office, I have a painting of Dolly with the initials WWDD, short for What Would Dolly Do? Now that she’s gone, those are words to live by now more than ever.

articles.title: Yankees’ Aaron Boone gets 100% real on George Lombard Jr.’s defensive woes
articles.summary: New York Yankees shortstop George Lombard Jr. has made a significant impact since being promoted to the big leagues, but the infielder has struggled from a defensive standpoint in recent action. Lombard has made four errors across his last four games, which is something manager Aaron Boone addres
articles._body: New York Yankees shortstop George Lombard Jr. has made a significant impact since being promoted to the big leagues, but the infielder has struggled from a defensive standpoint in recent action. Lombard has made four errors across his last four games, which is something manager Aaron Boone addressed before Tuesday night’s contest against the Houston Astros, via Bryan Hoch of MLB.com. “I feel like over time he’ll be really good at the routine [plays]. So I think that’s just a little bump in the road,” Boone said. The Yankees believe in Lombard . The defensive woes are not ideal, but it is important to remember that he is only 21 years old and has only appeared in 17 big league games heading into Tuesday’s matchup. Additionally, he has swung the bat well. Lombard is currently hitting .288/.348/.407 across 66 plate appearances. He has two home runs during that span as well. He can become a better defender, and the offensive production is already speaking for itself. Lombard could certainly become a star at the MLB level down the road. Tuesday night’s contest represents the first of a three-game series between the Yankees and Astros in New York. The Yankees are in second place in the American League East but they do lead the AL Wild Card. New York is only 3.5 games behind the Tampa Bay Rays in the AL East standings, so the ball club could still win the division. At the moment, the Yankees’ focus is on Tuesday night’s ball game against the Astros. articles.title: Countdown to kickoff prediction series: South Carolina will have three kickers and punters play major role
articles.summary: Continuing the countdown to kickoff prediction series: South Carolina will have at least three kickers and punters play a major role in 2026
articles._body: In May, when the calendar revealed that it was 100 days until South Carolina kicked off the season, I posted a story on GamecockCentral entitled “100 predictions for the 2026 Gamecocks.” Now, that countdown is down to just 11 days. The prediction paired with day 11 read, “At least three kickers and punters will play a major role again in 2026.” Let’s break down that prognostication. Have a question for the GamecockCentral staff? Ask it now on The Insiders Forum. Three starters in 2025 Following the 2024 season, South Carolina had to replace both Alex Herrera and Kai Kroeger. Because of that, the Gamecocks were without a starter to handle punting, placekicking, or kickoff duties. Redshirt freshman Mason Love wound up being the easy choice to replace Kroeger. The Missouri native had a Freshman All-SEC season for the Gamecocks, averaging over 45 yards per attempt. Fellow freshman Max Kelley handled the majority of the team’s kickoffs last fall. He was solid but somewhat inconsistent. At placekicker, redshirt senior walk-on William Joyce was the primary option. He was fine but didn’t have much range, going 5-for-8 from beyond 40 yards and not attempting a 50-yarder. Joyce subbed in for Kelley on seven kickoffs, as well. Love tried the only long field goal attempt of the year, a miss against LSU from 53 yards out. He also made a PAT. It seems likely that South Carolina will have at least three kickers and punters playing big roles in 2026, as well. What does this mean for the Gamecocks? Fellow subscribers are discussing it now on The Insiders Forum. South Carolina’s legs in 2026 With Joyce graduated, there will be at least one kicking job handled by a different player this fall. Mason Love is pretty clearly the starter at punter again. There has been virtually no controversy in that regard. However, South Carolina headman Shane Beamer has repeatedly said that Love likely will not have opportunities to win the team’s placekicking job. Kickoff duties have yet to be determined, but with Max Kelley returning as the incumbent, he could have a leg up for that job. The Gamecocks have had a long and public placekicking battle this offseason. USC brought in former Texas Tech, Buffalo, and Alabama kicker Upton Bellenfant via the transfer portal to compete with Kelley for the first-team PAT/field goal job. When neither player separated themselves as the clear leader to start, the Gamecocks added another transfer in Southeast Missouri State’s Malik Orsan. With still no clear position battle winner announced, it would make sense for South Carolina to split the kickoff and field goal jobs. Having one less responsibility could help a new kicker maintain confidence and focus on putting kicks through the uprights. Plus, there is the very real possibility that more than one player handles the placekicking role this season. The close competition could extend into the season. South Carolina fans saw that happen in 2017, as Alexander Woznick beat out Parker White before White overtook him during the season. White, of course, went on to become one of the best kickers in program history. Three (or more) kickers and punters could be significant pieces of the 2026 South Carolina football puzzle. What’s your prediction? Share it with fellow subscribers on The Insiders Forum.

articles.title: Huff leaning one way in QB competition, no final decision made yet

articles._body: Memphis football plays its first game at UNLV in four days, and according to Charles Huff , no one knows who the starting quarterback will be. Huff said earlier this month that both West Florida transfer Marcus Stokes and South Carolina transfer Air Noland would be informed which of the two would start on Sunday, Aug. 23 . However, that plan changed due to power outages that affected the Billy J. Murphy Athletic Complex. “We haven’t informed the team because we were supposed to do it in the midst of the storm,” Huff said. This does not mean the quarterbacks are unaware of what might happen. Huff and the staff did meet with both Stokes and Noland and told them which way they were leaning. “Met with the two guys, we let them know, this is what we’re looking at. This is what we’re leaning toward,” Huff said. While Memphis’ staff is leaning a certain direction towards either Stokes or Noland , Huff still wants to see how they would respond after being told they are either the starter or backup. “We’re going to continue to evaluate because I wanted to see how either one would change.”

articles.title: Paul Finebaum can’t wait for Bill Belichick tenure with North Carolina to crash and burn
articles.summary: Paul Finebaum is known to give his opinion and doesn’t care if it comes off as cruel. The longtime college football analyst delivered a brutal assessment of Belichick’s short tenure with the Tar Heels, criticizing both his personality and his ability to adjust to the college game. “I’m not
articles._body: Paul Finebaum is known to give his opinion and doesn’t care if it comes off as cruel. The longtime college football analyst delivered a brutal assessment of Belichick’s short tenure with the Tar Heels, criticizing both his personality and his ability to adjust to the college game. “I’m not pulling for Bill Belichick,” Finebaum said. “He’s a grouch. He’s a bully, and his career in college is about to go down in flames.” “He’s one of the worst college football coaches in a short period of time I have ever seen,” Finebaum concluded. “And I see no way this is going to be a successful landing or ending for Belichick.” North Carolina takes on TCU this Saturday for a Week 0 matchup. Regardless of what happens in Ireland for that game, Finebaum doesn’t believe Belichick will last the entire season . Belichick arrived in Chapel Hill with six Super Bowl championships and a reputation as one of the greatest coaches in NFL history. That résumé created enormous expectations, but college football requires much more than drawing up schemes and preparing for games. It’s still shocking that North Carolina was even willing to go this route. “He couldn’t accept that nobody in the NFL wanted him anymore,” Finebaum later said. Recruiting, transfer-portal management and connecting with younger players are all major parts of the job. Finebaum clearly believes Belichick has failed to make that transition. It’s been a short example, but Belichick must start producing results before North Carolina’s ambitious experiment turns into an expensive failure. articles._body: Tom Brady has spent most of his public life succeeding in places built around precision, preparation, and pressure. Now, the seven-time Super Bowl champion has accepted a challenge with no playbook: modeling for Gucci. Brady made his runway debut during Demna’s first Gucci cruise show in Times Square, per GQ. He will also appear in a fall-winter 2026 campaign photographed by Michal Chelbin alongside Alex Consani, EsDeeKid, and Shawn Mendes. The opportunity initially caught him off guard, but its unfamiliarity ultimately drew him in. “I always say the only place for growth is outside your comfort zone,” Brady told GQ. He called the experience a chance to try something entirely new on a major stage. EXCLUSIVE: Tom Brady on his new Gucci campaign—and becoming a leather pants guy at 49 https://t.co/uvDl318agg pic.twitter.com/4Zsx8tasuv — GQ Magazine (@GQMagazine) August 25, 2026 Leather Becomes Brady’s New Uniform Demna dressed Brady in leather from top to bottom for the runway. Brady compared the structured outfit to his old football uniform, but the biggest surprise came from the pants. He found them comfortable enough to earn space in his closet, giving his wardrobe an unlikely post-retirement addition. Brady also wore a shirtless suit in the campaign, though viewers should not expect him to recreate that look during Fox broadcasts. Since he often removes his jacket while covering games, he joked that the experiment could quickly go wrong. The campaign introduced Brady to Demna’s detailed creative process and a side of fashion he had never explored professionally. Brady said he entered without fixed expectations and trusted the designer’s direction. After conquering football, his latest uniform shows that even an established icon can still find room to stretch. articles.title: UCLA releases statement on JMU transfer’s status after attending NFL minicamps
articles.summary: Trent Hendrick is eligible to see action for the UCLA Bruins after all. Amid the Big Ten’s new ruling banning players’ eligibility under certain conditions, Hendrick appears to have gotten the green light to play for UCLA football in 2026. Under the conference’s new rule, player
articles._body: Trent Hendrick is eligible to see action for the UCLA Bruins after all. Amid the Big Ten’s new ruling banning players’ eligibility under certain conditions, Hendrick appears to have gotten the green light to play for UCLA football in 2026. Under the conference’s new rule, players who declared for the NFL draft and did not withdraw, those who appeared on an NFL roster, or those who signed a professional contract are not allowed to be part of a Big Ten roster. Apparently, none of those categories deem Hendrick ineligible, paving the way for his successful transfer from the James Madison Dukes to UCLA football . “We support the Big Ten’s adoption of the new professional football players rule and understand the importance of having clear and consistent eligibility standards across the conference,” UCLA athletic director Martin Jarmond said in a statement (h/t Ben Bolch of the New York Post). “We have been in communication with the Big Ten throughout this process, and our student-athletes are eligible under the guidelines adopted today. We are excited to turn our full attention to the upcoming season and our opener vs. California on Sept. 5.” Hendrick would be a big addition to UCLA football’s stop unit. He played four seasons in James Madison colors, seeing action in 49 games and racking up 209 combined tackles to go along with 19.0 tackles for loss, 6.0 sacks and five passes defended. He was named Sun Belt Defensive Player of the Year last season. The Bruins won just three games in the 2025 season and is now under a new head coach in Bob Chesney. articles.title: Report: Big 12 ADs in unanimous support of ban on professional athletes returning
articles.summary: Big 12 ADs met earlier Tuesday and are in unanimous support of a ban on professional players returning to compete in the conference, Yahoo Sports’ Ross Dellenger reported. The Big 12 has joined the SEC and Notre Dame in taking this stance. The Big Ten unveiled a ban on NFL players returning to
articles._body: Big 12 ADs met earlier Tuesday and are in unanimous support of a ban on professional players returning to compete in the conference, Yahoo Sports’ Ross Dellenger reported . The Big 12 has joined the SEC and Notre Dame in taking this stance. The Big Ten unveiled a ban on NFL players returning to compete in the conference, but has not yet addressed sports other than football. The Big Ten , SEC and Notre Dame have all gone public with their stance against professional athletes returning to college sports. The Big Ten and SEC both adopted rules against it. Now, the Big 12 followed shortly thereafter. The league is expected to finalize the policy within the next 24-36 hours. $19.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage These rules come after a Louisiana court ruled that the 16 players, some of whom were competing in NFL training camps, could return to college with eligibility for the 2026 season. That gave them a a fifth year in light of the five-for-five ruling earlier this year. The SEC released a statement on this matter on Monday, although the conference did not directly take action. Instead, they called upon Congress for the Protect College Sports Act and whatever solutions it might bring. To be fair, the SEC pushed back on pro athletes returning to college. “College athletes, not former professional athletes, have been at the heart of the Southeastern Conference,”  the statement reads.  “Individuals who choose to leave college athletics, sign professional playing contracts, and compete professional should not then be permitted to return to college competition. Allowing that to occur will blur the line between college and professional sports, create significant competitive equity concerns, and reduce opportunities for high school and current college athletes. “College sports are for college athletes. The current confusion around national eligibility standards emphasizes the need to advance the Protect College Sports Act.” Big 12 latest conference to ban pro players from returning to college football Per the signed order, the 16 college football players were allowed to enter the transfer portal. The NCAA’s rule of restitution and the ghost transfer rule were also enjoined. Now with the Big 12 aboard, options are running out for these specific players. In the aftermath of the TRO, former  Ole Miss  stars TE  Dae’Quan Wright  and DL  Xzavian Harris  have already committed to  LSU  out of the portal. Harris was signed by the New Orleans Saints as an UDFA this offseason, and Wright appeared in multiple preseason games for the Cleveland Browns. Other players, such as former Seattle Seahawks running backs  Anthony Hankerson  and  TJ Harden , remain in the portal. “College football has officially plunged into the abyss,” ESPN’s  Paul Finebaum  said on Monday morning’s episode of  Get Up . “We have never been at a place like this before. There have been scandals far more serious, but this is a new low in terms of the machinations of the legal system, the NCAA, and all these things. “It’s just incomprehensible to think that someone was on an NFL roster the other day and he very well could be playing for  LSU  a week from this Saturday, but it’s the way things are right now.”

articles.title: Royals’ Tony Gonsolin takes step toward making MLB comeback
articles.summary: Former Los Angeles Dodgers legend Tony Gonsolin is trying to work his way back from serious elbow surgery. Now a member of the Kansas City Royals, the right-hander is one step closer to making his MLB comeback. Gonsolin is set to begin a rehab assignment on Wednesday with Triple-A Omaha, the team
articles._body: Former Los Angeles Dodgers legend Tony Gonsolin is trying to work his way back from serious elbow surgery. Now a member of the Kansas City Royals , the right-hander is one step closer to making his MLB comeback. Gonsolin is set to begin a rehab assignment on Wednesday with Triple-A Omaha, the team announced. There’s no word on exactly how many starts he’ll have to make before returning to the majors. Still, the Royals will take a cautious approach with Gonsolin. For starters, his elbow injury came after he already had to miss time with a previous Tommy John surgery. Kansas City doesn’t want to rush him back and risk a setback. Especially based on their 58-74 record. Sitting 10.5 games back of the AL Central lead and eight games back of a Wild Card spot, it’s not like Kansas City is making an earnest playoff push. Gonsolin will be able to take the time necessary to make a proper return. When he does, the one-time All-Star and World Series champion will be looking to regain his old form. Over his six years with the Dodgers, Gonsolin held a 3.34 ERA and a 387/149 K/BB ratio. The righty may not be the pitcher he once was, especially after his injuries. But he wouldn’t be trying to make a comeback if he didn’t think he had gas left in the tank. Gonsolin’s deal with the Royals contains a club option for the 2027 season. If he comes back healthy and productive, perhaps he can become a true factor in Kansas City’s pitching rotation then. For now though, Gonsolin is just trying to get back into the bigs. articles.title: New SEC policy means no Dae’Quan Wright, Zxavian Harris signings for LSU, Lane Kiffin
articles.summary: The LSU Tigers’ football team hit the news cycle once again after reports indicated that Lane Kiffin and the program were going to sign former NFL players Dae’Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris. However, not long after the Big Ten announced punishments for programs for signing pro players
articles._body: The LSU Tigers’ football team hit the news cycle once again after reports indicated that Lane Kiffin and the program were going to sign former NFL players Dae’Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris. However, not long after the Big Ten announced punishments for programs for signing pro players, the SEC made an announcement of its own. On Tuesday afternoon, the SEC announced that it is banning NFL players, along with NBA and G League players, from returning to the collegiate level, according to Nicole Auerbach of NBC Sports. “NEWS: The SEC has banned not just NFL players but also NBA/G League players from returning to play in college,” Auerbach reported. SEC Commissioner Greg Sankey was granted by the SEC presidents unlimited authority to suspend a school if it signs a former pro player, per Ross Dellenger of Yahoo Sports! Sankey can also deem which players are eligible or not, and can also suspend coaches and administrators. “SEC presidents granted Greg Sankey ‘full and unlimited authority,’ which includes suspending a school from competition, sources tell Yahoo Sports!” Dellenger reported. In addition to that, league bylaws grant the commissioner powers to deem a player ineligible, suspend coaches/administrators, etc.” The SEC shared on X its official policy. It reveals the exact wording that grants Sankey the power to prevent former NFL, NBA, WNBA, and G League players from returning to the college level within the conference. Following meetings with the Presidents, Chancellors, and Athletics Directors of the Southeastern Conference, the SEC will enforce the following policy: pic.twitter.com/LohWnb7G1J — Southeastern Conference (@SEC) August 25, 2026 With this new policy in place, the LSU Tigers will not be able to sign either Dae’Quan Wright or Zxavian Harris. Wright was cut by the Cleveland Browns during training camp shortly after he was cut by the Philadelphia Eagles. Harris was cut by the New Orleans Saints. Both were undrafted free agents from the 2026 NFL Draft class. The SEC made the change on the same day Lane Kiffin argued that he, his program, Wright, and Harris did nothing wrong whatsoever. But now, with the policies in place, LSU will not benefit from adding two players who had previously declared for the NFL Draft. articles.title: Brewers’ Jake Bauers dealing with foot injury concern after Williamsport series vs. Braves
articles.summary: Milwaukee Brewers first baseman and outfielder Jake Bauers is dealing with a swollen foot after fouling a ball off it during Sunday’s Little League Classic against the Atlanta Braves, but the 30-year-old reassured he is healthy enough to play. Bauers was left out of Milwaukee’s lineup
articles._body: Milwaukee Brewers first baseman and outfielder Jake Bauers is dealing with a swollen foot after fouling a ball off it during Sunday’s Little League Classic against the Atlanta Braves, but the 30-year-old reassured he is healthy enough to play. Bauers was left out of Milwaukee’s lineup for Tuesday’s series opener against the New York Mets, with Andrew Vaughn starting at first base and Jackson Chourio, Garrett Mitchell and Luis Lara covering the outfield. Bauers indicated that his absence was not because of a serious injury . In his seventh major-league season, Bauers is producing career-best numbers. Through 118 appearances, he is hitting .273 with a .382 on-base percentage and .884 OPS. He has also recorded 23 home runs and 75 RBIs. Bauers has also given manager Pat Murphy flexibility because he can play first base and multiple outfield positions. His availability is particularly important with the Brewers competing for the top position in the National League and home-field advantage throughout the playoffs. Bauers has performed against left-handed pitching this season, but he has been more effective when holding the platoon advantage against right-handers. With his foot still swollen but not preventing him from playing, he could remain available off the bench if needed. His next opportunity to return to the starting lineup is Wednesday. Milwaukee entered Tuesday at 81-50, having won three of its last four games, including two victories against Atlanta. The Brewers have a 30-game magic number to clinch the No. 1 position in the National League and is currently ahead of the Los Angeles Dodgers, Braves and Chicago Cubs in that race. Milwaukee has been particularly successful against teams above .500 , going 43-22 in those games. The Brewers have already secured the season series against the Dodgers and currently hold an advantage over the Cubs, although seven games remain between Milwaukee and Chicago. articles.title: Tigers pay tribute to Dolly Parton with ‘Jolene’ batting practice soundtrack
articles.summary: A familiar Dolly Parton song created a quiet moment at Comerica Park on Tuesday as the Detroit Tigers prepared to face the Tampa Bay Rays. “Jolene” played during early batting practice, adding significance to the routine pregame soundtrack in light of Parton’s death. Parton passed away peacefully
articles._body: A familiar Dolly Parton song created a quiet moment at Comerica Park on Tuesday as the Detroit Tigers prepared to face the Tampa Bay Rays. “Jolene” played during early batting practice, adding significance to the routine pregame soundtrack in light of Parton’s death. Parton passed away peacefully Tuesday in Nashville, Tennessee, at age 80, her publicist said. The country music icon built a career spanning nearly six decades as a songwriter, performer, actor, businesswoman, and philanthropist. News of her death prompted tributes from fans throughout the afternoon. MLive Media Group’s Evan Woodbery noted the song selection Tuesday on X, formerly Twitter, before the Tigers took on the Rays in the second game of the series. “They’re playing “Jolene” during early batting practice at Comerica Park.” The Tigers did not publicly explain whether the selection was intended as a tribute. Its timing, however, connected an ordinary part of Detroit’s preparation with the widespread remembrance of one of country music’s most influential artists. Parton wrote and recorded “Jolene” in 1973. The song became one of her defining works and country music’s most recognizable recordings. Parton said she drew inspiration from a bank teller who appeared interested in her husband, Carl Dean. Numerous artists later recorded their versions, extending the song’s reach across generations and musical genres. Music remains central to the atmosphere surrounding baseball, from player-selected walk-up songs to ballpark playlists between innings. Before fans filled Comerica Park on Tuesday, Parton’s unmistakable recording carried meaning beyond entertainment. The moment offered another example of how her music continues to resonate in unexpected settings. At Comerica Park, “Jolene” served as a simple soundtrack while the sports and entertainment worlds reflected on the legendary country music artist’s enduring influence. articles.title: Lil Nas X Says Fans Are Being ‘OD Nice’ to Him Since He Got Out of Rehab
articles.summary: The "Old Town Road" rapper/singer seems to be in positive spirits since finding himself in legal trouble last summer.
articles._body: Lil Nas X is trying to keep a positive attitude since getting out of rehab. The rapper and singer posted an Instagram Reel telling fans that everyone has been treating him very well since he came from a recent rehab stint. “Ever since I got out of rehab, like, everybody’s, like, OD nice to me,” he said jokingly. “I can be like, ‘Hey!’ Everybody’s gonna be like, ‘Oh my God, you’re so brave.’ I can try to post a thirst trap on my Instagram Story, and then it’s gonna be somebody like, ‘Keep fighting, King.'” In keeping with his newfound positivity, he posted an Instagram Story holding a cake to celebrate his 10,000th day on planet Earth and poked fun at the people that may not make it to day 10,000. “So, tomorrow is my 10,000th day alive and I made it,” he said. “A lot of you won’t make it, but I made it.” Back in June, Nas posted an IG Reel to give his fans and followers an update of where he’s been. “I’ve been in rehab for a few months,” he said. “Since then I’ve been back home, whether its in Atlanta with my family or in Los Angeles with myself, friends, and what not. And trying to ground myself down to Earth and get out of my head. I have a therapist now and a psychiatrist which is really helpful.” He added that he originally was in denial about being bipolar. “When I got my bipolar disorder diagnosis,” he began. “I feel like I had known for like the past few year but I didn’t want to admit to it ’cause I didn’t want to have to take medication and I don’t know, have people think different of me. I mean, I’m already Black and gay, like damn, God, come on. Black. gay, bipolar, I’mm like living life on like extreme hard mode.” Lil Nas X found himself in legal trouble when he was charged with four felonies after allegedly attacking police while walking the streets of L.A. naked. According to Variety , he’ll have his charges dismissed if he continues mental health treatment.

articles.title: Lauren London to Play Snoop Dogg’s Mother in Biopic, Plus 2Pac Casting News
articles.summary: Panic actor Camron Jones is slated to play Snoop's Death Row running mate.
articles._body: Lauren London is set to play Snoop Dogg’s mother, Beverly Tate, in the upcoming Snoop biopic, according to Deadline . The Universal Pictures film is coming to U.S. theaters on Aug. 6, 2027. It wouldn’t be Snoop Dogg’s complete rap story without 2Pac , and The Hollywood Reporter revealed on Tuesday (Aug. 25) that Panic actor Camron Jones is slated to play Snoop’s Death Row running mate. Hustle & Flow ‘s Craig Brewer is directing the biopic, which has cast Outerbanks star Jonathan Daviss as Snoop Dogg and BMF ‘s Myle Bullock Be in the role of Dr. Dre. Beverly Tate had a profound impact on Snoop’s career. In addition to being his mother, she worked as a director in the local church choir and began calling her son Snoopy, based on the dog from the TV show Peanuts . Snoop Dogg and 2Pac’s careers crossed paths while dominating rap as superstars leading Suge Knight’s Death Row Records in the mid-’90s. They teamed up for hits like “2 of Amerikaz Most Wanted.” Snoop also had the honor of inducting Pac into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2017. Lauren London and Snoop have history as well, as the West Coast rap legend previously enlisted the ATL actress to appear in his and Pharrell’s “Drop It Like It’s Hot” music video, which topped the Billboard Hot 100 in 2004. London’s partner, the late Nipsey Hussle, was actually offered to play Snoop Dogg in 2015’s N.W.A. biopic, but Hussle ultimately turned Straight Outta Compton down and the role went to LaKeith Stanfield. As far as her recent work, Lauren London starred in You People in 2023 and made an appearance in Tyler, The Creator’s “Darling, I” music video last year. articles.title: Why White Sox are in serious trouble in AL Central amid Guardians’ surge
articles.summary: The Chicago White Sox have been one of baseball’s best stories this season, but their surprising run to the top of the AL Central is about to face its toughest test. Cleveland is coming. The Guardians have won five consecutive games and seven of their last 10, transforming what appeared to be Chi
articles._body: The Chicago White Sox have been one of baseball’s best stories this season, but their surprising run to the top of the AL Central is about to face its toughest test. Cleveland is coming. The Guardians have won five consecutive games and seven of their last 10, transforming what appeared to be Chicago’s division to lose into a legitimate race. With roughly 30 games remaining, the White Sox hold a lead of only 2.5 games over Cleveland. That margin can disappear in a matter of days. Cleveland represents the immediate threat because it combines its current momentum with the experience needed to handle a tense September race. However, the Minnesota Twins and Detroit Tigers are in the race as of now. With these current rosters, the Guardians have been here before. The White Sox have not. Cleveland creates another challenge for a young White Sox roster attempting to complete an unexpected rise from a rebuilding club to division champion. White Sox must prove their young core is ready for the moment Matt Marton-Imagn Images Chicago remains in the best position to capture the AL Central. The White Sox have led the division for a reason, and their young players have continued to exceed expectations throughout the season. Miguel Vargas has become one of baseball’s most improved hitters since the Los Angeles Dodgers traded him to Chicago. Once viewed as a player without an obvious long-term role, Vargas has developed into a central piece of the White Sox lineup. Colson Montgomery and Munetaka Murakami provide the type of power capable of changing a game with one swing. Chase Meidroth, meanwhile, is developing into one of the league’s most productive second basemen. Chicago’s rise has not been built around one superstar carrying the entire offense. Several young hitters have arrived or taken significant steps forward at the same time, giving manager Will Venable a lineup capable of competing beyond this season. The question is whether those hitters can maintain their production as the pressure rises. Every loss will feel more significant in September. Every Cleveland victory will place additional pressure on a White Sox team learning how to protect a division lead for the first time. That is where the Guardians’ experience could matter most. Chicago’s pitching could determine the AL Central race The White Sox have also received respectable pitching throughout the season. Sean Burke, Anthony Kay, and Davis Martin have delivered exceptional performances, giving Chicago the stability it needed to become a playoff contender. Martin’s current stint on the injured list creates another concern, however. Chicago needs him healthy for the final stretch, especially if Cleveland continues applying pressure. A young offense can overcome an occasional quiet night during the summer, but the margin for error shrinks in a pennant race. If the rotation begins struggling or the bullpen becomes overworked, Chicago’s division advantage could vanish quickly. Venable’s responsibility is to keep the train moving while making sure his young roster does not begin playing cautiously. The White Sox reached this position by trusting their emerging core. Changing that approach now would be a mistake. Chicago must continue playing aggressively while relying on the same players who built the lead. Guardians-White Sox series could decide the division The AL Central race could ultimately come down to one final head-to-head meeting. Chicago and Cleveland will meet for a three-game series in Cleveland during the middle of September. If the standings remain this close, those games will carry enormous weight. The White Sox will have an opportunity to create separation and quiet the Guardians’ push. Cleveland will have a chance to erase the gap without relying on another team to beat Chicago. For the White Sox, simply reaching that series with the division lead would be significant. Winning it could place them in control entering the final weeks. Losing it could force their young roster to chase a Guardians team that already knows how to finish a playoff race. Chicago should still win the AL Central. Its young lineup has produced all season, its pitching has been better than expected, and it controls its own path. Cleveland’s winning streak has turned the final month into a test of Chicago’s readiness. The White Sox have proven they are talented enough to lead the division. Now they must prove they are composed enough to finish the job. The post Why White Sox are in serious trouble in AL Central amid Guardians’ surge appeared first on ClutchPoints .

The 22-year-old quarterback hit the transfer portal again and stepped in as the starter for the Florida State Seminoles last season. While he’s flashed potential as a dual-threat quarterback, the 2025-26 campaign was nothing to gloat about. Castellanos finished the year with 2,760 passing yards, 557 rushing yards, and 24 total touchdowns (15 passing, 9 rushing) while completing 58.3% of his pass attempts. He also threw nine interceptions, but did lead the ACC passing yards per attempt with 8.9. As of now, Thomas Castellanos is not with a football program. He was recently granted a fifth year of eligibility after winning a legal temporary injunction. Whether it’s Texas Tech or another school in the nation that signs him, Castellanos will be available to play in the 2026-27 campaign. Assuming he is given the starting job. articles._body: Los Angeles Dodgers star Shohei Ohtani hasn’t been on the mound since July 3 as he battles through knee and biceps injuries. However, his return could be coming sooner rather than later. While manager Dave Roberts didn’t confirm anything, he said Ohtani pitching on Sunday against the Detroit Tigers remains, “a possibility,” via Fabian Ardaya of the Athletic. If he is back in pitching action, that would be a massive boon for Los Angeles. Still, the Dodgers are going to be cautious. They have their eyes set solely on winning their third-straight World Series title. Having Ohtani on the mound and batter’s box only helps those chances. Because of that, they want him to be as healthy as possible come playoff time. But if Ohtani is cleared from all injury issues, Roberts plans to throw him. And if everything checks out Sunday, it wouldn’t be shocking to see the reigning MVP finally make his mound return. Over his 14 starts in 2026, Ohtani holds a 1.79 ERA and a 95/26 K/BB ratio. Those numbers are impressive on their own before you consider his effort at the plate. Ohtani has still been serving as designated hitter despite his injuries, hitting .288 with 30 home runs and 80 RBIs. If Ohtani wants to make up ground against Chicago Cubs superstar Pete Crow-Armstrong in the MVP race, a successful return to the mound would certainly help. Starting on Sunday would give the right-hander more opportunities to make an impact down the stretch. Still, the Dodgers’ biggest prerogative remains winning a title, and keeping Ohtani healthy. Roberts will make his decision on Sunday, and moving forward with those two things in mind. articles.title: What’s Next for Jed York After Prostitution Arrest?
articles.summary: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images
articles._body: Jed York, the 49ers, and the NFL now must deal with the fallout from York’s arrest last weekend in a prostitution-related case. York, the 49ers principal owner, faces potential discipline by the NFL under its personal conduct policy. And while some in and around the league tell Front Office Sports they don’t expect the incident to prompt York’s family to sell the 49ers or threaten his ability to remain as primary owner, they believe York could be pushed to take time away from the franchise. “There will be something in addition to the embarrassment,” one source familiar with the NFL’s inner workings tells FOS . The personal conduct policy applies to owners and would allow commissioner Roger Goodell and the league to fine or suspend York if they determine that’s warranted. “It is a privilege to be part of the National Football League,” the 2026 version of the policy for league and non-player club employees reads. “Everyone who is part of the league must refrain from conduct detrimental to the integrity of, or public confidence in, the NFL. This includes owners, coaches, players, other team employees, game officials, and employees of the league office, NFL Films, NFL Network, or any other NFL business.” That version of the policy is separate from the version for NFL players. “Ownership and club or league management have traditionally been held to a higher standard and will be subject to more significant discipline when violations of the Policy occur,” it says. The conduct policy for non-players also says: “Conduct that is illegal, violent, dangerous, or irresponsible puts innocent victims at risk, damages the reputation of others associated with the game, and undercuts public respect and support for the NFL. We must endeavor at all times to be people of high character; we must show respect for others inside and outside our workplace; and we must conduct ourselves in ways that favorably reflect on ourselves, our teams, the communities we represent, and the NFL.” York, 46, posted a $5,000 bond and was released on his own recognizance after pleading no contest to charges of disorderly conduct and possessing criminal tools, according to Columbiana County, Ohio, court records. York spent one day in jail and was fined $1,150, plus additional court fees. An initial filing said that York was arraigned for “engaging in prostitution.” The East Palestine, Ohio, police made the arrest, along with the Mahoning Valley Human Trafficking Task Force. “We are aware of the matter, which will be reviewed under the personal conduct policy,” NFL spokesman Brian McCarthy said Monday. The NFL Players Association declined to comment Tuesday about the potential application of the personal conduct policy to an owner, rather than a player, in this case. Late Colts owner Jim Irsay was suspended for six games and fined $500,000 by the NFL in 2014 under the policy after he pleaded guilty to one misdemeanor count of operating a vehicle while intoxicated. His toxicology report showed that he had the painkillers oxycodone and hydrocodone in his system when he was arrested after a traffic stop near his home in the Indianapolis suburb of Carmel, Indiana. Jerry Richardson, the late owner of the Panthers, was fined $2.75 million by the NFL in 2018, a month after owners ratified his $2.275 billion sale of the team to David Tepper. The fine followed an investigation into allegations of workplace misconduct. Richardson put the Panthers up for sale after Sports Illustrated reported in late 2017 that he made sexually suggestive comments to women and on at least one occasion directed a racial slur at a scout for the team. In 2023, the same day owners approved outgoing Commanders owner Daniel Snyder’s sale of the franchise for $6.05 billion to a group led by private equity investor Josh Harris, the NFL said Snyder would make a $60 million payment to the league. The NFL said an investigation conducted by attorney Mary Jo White concluded the Commanders withheld revenue that should have been shared with other franchises and that Snyder sexually harassed a former team employee. But the NFL has not acted in every case involving allegations of misconduct by an owner. Patriots owner Robert Kraft faced no known disciplinary action by the league after he pleaded not guilty to two misdemeanor counts of solicitation in a 2019 prostitution case involving a Florida massage parlor. Prosecutors dropped the charges after losing a key court decision regarding video recordings. In February, the NFL said it would review communications between Steve Tisch, then the Giants co-owner, and Jeffrey Epstein, the convicted sex offender who took his own life in 2019. “I would say that absolutely we are going to look at all the facts,” Goodell said in San Jose, Calif., at his annual news conference during Super Bowl week. “We’re going to look at the context of them and try to understand that. And we’ll look at how that falls under the policy. But I think you take one step at a time, and let’s get the facts first.” Tisch’s name reportedly appeared at least 440 times in more than three million documents released by the Justice Department the week before Goodell’s comments. Epstein connected Tisch with several women, according to email exchanges. Goodell was asked in February whether he was concerned the Tisch matter reflected poorly on the league. “Sure,” Goodell said. “But that’s why we have a personal conduct policy, and that’s why we’ll look into the facts.” Tisch is not known to have been fined or suspended under the policy. In March, the NFL told teams via a memo that Tisch and his siblings, Laurie Tisch and Jonathan Tisch, were transferring their remaining ownership stakes in the Giants to trusts for their children. The transactions meant that Steve, Laurie, and Jonathan Tisch would “no longer own any interest in the Club,” the league’s March memo said. articles._body: I'm happy to say that https://use-fs.com 2.0 has been released with brand new OPFS support. If you're building browser-based apps that heavily interact with the file-system this package is a must to have in your package.json! A React hook that watches a directory and re-renders when a file is added, changed, or deleted. Point it at a folder the user picked and you're reading and writing their real files — no uploads, no endless file dialogs New in 2.0: it watches the origin private file system too. No picker, no permission prompt, no user gesture — and, unlike File System API, it works in Safari and Firefox What's OPFS? A file store the browser gives each origin — real directories and files, but readable only by your own site through the File System API, never by the user's file manager or other apps. articles.title: SEC plans to enforce rules around professional athletes returning to college sports
articles.summary: The SEC is taking action amid the latest eligibility controversy in college football. The conference is set to pass a rule prohibiting players who have moved on to the NFL from returning to play college football at an SEC school.  The move comes as lawsuits around the country have opened the do
articles._body: The SEC is taking action amid the latest eligibility controversy in college football. The conference is set to pass a rule prohibiting players who have moved on to the NFL from returning to play college football at an SEC school.  The move comes as lawsuits around the country have opened the door for players who previously exhausted their eligibility to receive another season at the collegiate level. Some of those players have already spent time on NFL rosters during training camp before being released. Now, the SEC is drawing a line regarding who can return to the college game. $19.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage The decision comes one day after the conference released a strong statement regarding professional athletes returning to college: “College athletes, not former professional athletes, have been at the heart of the Southeastern Conference,” the SEC’s statement read . “Individuals who choose to leave college athletics, sign professional playing contracts, and compete professionally should not then be permitted to return to college competition.” The SEC also argued that allowing former professional players to return could create competitive equity issues while taking opportunities away from high school recruits and current college athletes. “College sports are for college athletes,” the conference added . “The current confusion around national eligibility standards emphasizes the need to advance the Protect College Sports Act.” Alas, the SEC’s decision follows a similar move from the Big Ten . ESPN’s Pete Thamel reported Tuesday that the Big Ten is set to pass a rule preventing players from returning from the NFL to play for one of its schools. Under the Big Ten’s rule, any player who declared for the NFL Draft and did not withdraw, appeared on an NFL roster or signed a contract with a professional league would be prohibited from joining a Big Ten roster. The issue became increasingly complicated after a Louisiana court ruled that 16 players could return to college with eligibility for the 2026 season. Some of those players had already participated in NFL training camps before being released. The ruling allowed those players to enter the transfer portal. The NCAA’s rule of restitution and ghost transfer rule were also enjoined as part of the order. Of all teams, LSU has been directly involved in two of the most notable cases. Lane Kiffin and the Tigers recently landed former Ole Miss tight end Dae’Quan Wright after he spent training camp with the Cleveland Browns before being released. Meanwhile, LSU basketball coach Will Wade and the Tigers secured a preliminary injunction allowing former St. John’s standout RJ Luis to play college basketball after spending time with the Utah Jazz and Boston Celtics as an undrafted free agent in 2025. The SEC had already made its stance clear Monday. Now, the conference is putting that position into action by preventing players who have moved on to professional football from returning to an SEC roster.

Hall was recently granted a fifth year of eligibility through an injunction in t
articles._body: Auburn transfer forward Keyshawn Hall has committed to St. John’s , he told On3.  The 6-foot-7 senior averaged 19.3 points, 7.1 rebounds, and 2.6 assists per game this past season, earning Third Team All-SEC honors. Hall was recently granted a fifth year of eligibility through an injunction in the Ohio lawsuit , challenging the NCAA’s new age-based eligibility rules . However, the NCAA has since been granted a motion to stay the injunction, temporarily pausing the court’s decision. Therefore, Hall is currently ineligible, but he and his attorney are working through legal options in hopes of allowing him to play for the Johnnies this upcoming season. Assuming he regains eligibility, Hall will help fill the void left by St. John’s forward Donnie Freeman , a transfer from Syracuse, who will miss the entire 2026-27 season after suffering an Achilles injury. Hall, one of the top available players in the transfer portal, joins forces with another major addition for St. John’s in former Baylor small forward Tounde Yessoufou , who averaged 17.8 points per game last season. [ $19.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage ] In addition to St. John’s , Hall drew interest from Kentucky, USC, Houston, SMU, Gonzaga, and several other programs. Prior to considering a fifth year of college basketball, he played NBA Summer League with the Miami Heat. Keyshawn Hall arrived at Auburn last offseason via the transfer portal from  UCF , where he earned All-Big 12 Second Team honors after averaging 18.8 points, 7.1 rebounds, and 2.4 assists per game for the Knights. Prior to UCF, Hall played his sophomore season at  George Mason (16.6 PPG) and his freshman season at  UNLV (5.4 PPG).

articles._body: Odell Beckham Jr. delivered a vintage moment Tuesday, making a one-handed catch as he continued his push for a roster spot. Beckham, now a 33-year-old veteran , opened one of his strongest practices with the leaping grab in East Rutherford, New Jersey. He recorded four receptions during live drills, reinforcing his case before Sunday’s final cuts. ClutchPoints shared a video of the catch Tuesday on X, formerly Twitter, crediting The Trentonians’ Greg Johnson with capturing the play . Beckham reached behind himself, elevated, and secured the football with one hand. “Odell Beckham Jr makes the one handed catch look TOO EASY in Giants practice (via @gregp_j)” Odell Beckham Jr makes the one handed catch look TOO EASY in Giants practice (via @gregp_j ) pic.twitter.com/XJks5WlcZa — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) August 25, 2026 The play recalled Beckham’s famous three-fingered touchdown catch against the Dallas Cowboys in 2014, which accelerated his rise to stardom during his rookie season with New York. His performance arrived amid uncertainty in the Giants’ receiving corps. Calvin Austin III sustained what ESPN reported was a serious right knee injury Tuesday and left practice on a cart. Austin had appeared positioned for a significant role, while Beckham worked primarily with the second team throughout camp. Beckham entered Tuesday’s practice on the roster bubble. He caught two passes for 17 yards in Saturday’s preseason game vs. the Miami Dolphins but dropped a potential touchdown. His limited special-teams value also complicates New York’s evaluation of the veteran receiver. Still, Tuesday’s practice showed that Beckham’s signature ball skills remain. He did not play in 2025 after receiving a six-game suspension for violating the NFL’s performance-enhancing drugs policy. The Giants signed him to a one-year contract in June, bringing him back to the organization that selected him 12th overall in the 2014 NFL Draft. Beckham now awaits the Giants’ final roster decision as he looks to carry his reunion into the regular season. articles.title: Show HN: Game to see if you're over-/under-confident in your own knowledge
articles.summary:
I wrote a simple "trivia" game to get a sense about how well calibrated you are in terms of how well you know things: https://est.alejo.ch

You get ten simple "what happened first" questions and give a confidence level (for each answer). The game
articles._body: I wrote a simple "trivia" game to get a sense about how well calibrated you are in terms of how well you know things: https://est.alejo.ch You get ten simple "what happened first" questions and give a confidence level (for each answer). The game tracks your success rates per confidence level and gives you a calibration graph/table (e.g., "you consistently over-estimate your success rate"). You can play multiple times to see aggregated statistics. After 60 games (480 questions), I found out that I am relatively well-calibrated, though I should ~never bet under 60% (for this specific type of binary questions): https://alejo.ch/3mk The game is open source (GPLv3 at https://github.com/alefore/estimate ) and it's just static files. There's no server-side logic: the game log/stats are stored in your browser (local storage API). It's pure TypeScript, no framework. You can read more about it on https://alejo.ch/3m9 Just figured I'd share in case others find it useful and/or have suggestions to improve it. I'd also be curious to see the calibration stats of other people. Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49441660 Points: 2 # Comments: 0

articles._body: Tuesday is a special night for the Los Angeles Dodgers as it marks the return of one of their key assets after a long absence. Tyler Glasnow, who last toed the rubber on May 6 against the Houston Astros at Daikin Park in Houston, is set for a return to action in Tuesday’s series opener against the Atlanta Braves. The game, which will be at Truist Park in Atlanta, has Dodgers fans excited. Dodgers manager Dave Roberts, meanwhile, revealed what he expects from Glasnow in his first MLB appearance in a while. “Seeing him getting into the 6th inning is our hope, our goal… Tyler’s anxious to get back,” Roberts told reporters before the game (h/t SportsNet LA). The reigning World Series champions finally activated Glasnow from the 60-day injured list ahead of the Braves series, paving the way for him to make his first start since that meeting with the Astros. Glasnow landed on the IL with back issues and made multiple rehab starts . In four starts in the minors, he gave up just two earned runs through 13 2/3 innings of work. In what was his final rehab start, he lasted 5 1/3 frames and threw a total of 77 pitches. Glasnow rejoins the Dodgers amid the team’s hot stretch, and he will look to do his part in sustaining Los Angeles’ form. The Dodgers enter the Atlanta series on a six-game winning streak and an 80-51 record. Before he was placed on the IL, the 33-year-old Glasnow went 3-0 with a 2.72 ERA in three starts in the 2026 MLB season. articles.title: Sean McVay reveals Rams’ plan for Ty Simpson, Stetson Bennett amid heated QB2 battle
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Rams were the biggest winners of the offseason. After trading for Myles Garrett and Trent McDuffie, the team should now have one of the best defenses in the entire league. Of course, Matthew Stafford, Puka Nacua, and Davante Adams help form one of the best offenses in the league,
articles._body: The Los Angeles Rams were the biggest winners of the offseason. After trading for Myles Garrett and Trent McDuffie, the team should now have one of the best defenses in the entire league. Of course, Matthew Stafford, Puka Nacua, and Davante Adams help form one of the best offenses in the league, too. Stafford is fresh off an MVP win , and Nacua and Adams’ status as the best receiver duo in the NFL is safe. Clearly, the team is all in on winning the Super Bowl now. However, if they made one move that surprised fans, it was their first-round selection of Ty Simpson. The Rams needed a quarterback of the future, but drafting Stafford’s backup during a window of contention was a questionable decision to many. Even so, the team has high hopes for the signal caller from Alabama. On top of the former MVP and the recent first-rounder, the Rams also really like what they have in Stetson Bennett, a former fourth-round pick who won two national titles in college. This stacked quarterback room means that the Rams will roster three quarterbacks on their 53-man roster. Stu Jackson reported that Sean McVay confirmed as much. Stafford’s job as the starter is obviously safe, but Bennett and Simpson have been competing for the right to back him up. The Rams will play their Week 1 matchup against the San Francisco 49ers in Australia, and it is unclear as of now which reserve will be QB2. Los Angeles’ final preseason game of the year is against the Los Angeles Chargers on Aug. 27, so perhaps the quarterback competition will be solved then. articles.title: Rich Rodriguez press conference summary: 8-25
articles.summary: West Virginia head coach Rich Rodriguez addressed the media following a preseason practice and WVSports.com provides a summary of what was said.
articles._body: New to WVSports.com? For a limited time, get your first year of premium coverage for just $30 during our biggest sale of the year. Click here to learn more and join. West Virginia head coach Rich Rodriguez addressed the media following a preseason practice and WVSports.com provides a summary of what was said. –Rodriguez said that because of the lack of a preseason game, you don’t ever truly know but for as long as he’s done it, he’s got a good feel. His team needs a hot day to practice next week. They’ve identified a lot of the guys that can help win but they need more. –West Virginia does a mock game eight days before, Friday, and will start the Coastal Carolina stuff this week and after Friday it will go to game week. –Anytime there are new starters, there is some unknown and some anxiety on how they’re going to play and you put them in pressure situations in practice. They are doing it now to find out who is truly ready. –Because of the unknown, rarely in this age do you have a team with 14 or 15 starters coming back so you have to adapt a little bit. You have to have a plan for it. –Rodriguez said offensively in general it takes a little longer to get rhythm because you’re not going full speed all the time. They’ll do the best they can and adapt. He doesn’t want his team playing slower because they are thinking too much but by Monday of next week he wants to know exactly what the plan is so they won’t screw up in all three phases. –You want quarterbacks that run the offense but have explosive ability so there’s less you have to put in because your quarterback can be dynamic in the throw or run game. What he has tried to stress to the quarterbacks is avoiding the bad plays. –Rodriguez said he has played true freshmen before in big stadiums at quarterback but he is more nervous than they usually are but part of the methodology is to create intense situations in practice. They’ve got some guys that have started games and will find out in the first game. No matter who you open up with in college football, you’re probably a little more anxious because you have no idea. –To manage the unknowns, you go back to what they’ve done in practice in situational stuff. His pet peeve with his team is to pay attention. They don’t run a team period or skelly without down and distance and play clock. –Rodriguez said they had 12-15 guys come out for the walk-on tryouts and they only have one spot. He said it has to com from the student body, they’re on hold right now. –Biggest difference in this camp is it was two weeks before school started and you still have enough time to get ready. If he looks back at 28 or 29 previous years, they are right on track with the rest of them. The quicker you have to get ready for the game, the better you are because coaches try to do too much at times. He is kind of treating this like an open date. –Rodriguez said that it’s been less physical but some of that in the NCAA governance on full pads and when you can be in helmets and when you can hit. You’d like to dictate that if you had a soft practice and want to get physical to teach them something. — Josh Sapp has experience and great ball skills at tight end. He’s learning how to be a physical blocker and has taken a lot of reps due to the other injuries and has gotten better. Sapp is around 240-pounds and he can run. He’s got a little bit of a feel and you can tell he has played some hig- level college football. –Rodriguez sees how you can address a need with an NFL player coming back to college but it’s sort of crazy. You have to take control conference by conference. He doesn’t know the legality but he thinks all the conferences should not allow it. It’s crazy to be adding guys that were playing in the NFL that could be playing college football in a week. –The weekend scrimmage was light and they treated it like an exhibition game. The second group did about 35 plays and the young guys did 40-45 plays live. He wanted to get a long hard look at some of those younger guys that could play. –The intensity has never been bad and has been pretty even throughout. It’s not like guys are messing around on the sidelines but the level of intensity he wants to see out of them all the time is always going to be a work in progress. Every day they’ll find a loaf or two but they’ve worked pretty hard but it’s not as hard now to be a college football player as it used to be. –Rodriguez said you knew the guy was coming back in the past so you didn’t have to evaluate them as hard. –Medical staffs now are enormous, and the nutritionists and the way they eat is different. They have a GPS on them to track how far and how intense they were running. The players should be physically monitored better than in the past. Now, you are a little bit conscious that not only is a player a starter but he’s taking a big salary so you want to make it through the games. Rodriguez said he has cut some things out because you want your players to get through a season but they have to be ready to play, too. –There is more intentional players coming to America in football now than ever before and you’re getting some big, tall and athletic players that might be a little raw. West Virginia will go anywhere to recruit. Wondering what other WVU fans are saying? articles.title: WNBA’s Sky Ban Kanter Freedom From Arena Indefinitely
articles.summary: Patrick Gorski-Imagn Images
articles._body: Enes Kanter Freedom is banned from Chicago Sky games at Wintrust Arena. In a rare interview with Chicago-based media members, Chicago Sky owner Michael Alter denounced the actions of former NBA player Enes Kanter Freedom, who attended Sunday’s game at Wintrust Arena between the Sky and Indiana Fever. “It was pretty clear to us that his purpose of coming here was trying to be provocative and just see how much attention he could get,” Alter told reporters. Freedom was removed from the third quarter of Sunday’s game after an altercation with Sky guard Natasha Cloud . Weeks before Sunday’s game, Freedom, an 11-year NBA veteran who last played in 2022, declared for the 2027 WNBA draft, claiming he identifies as a woman. Alter said Freedom is not allowed back into Wintrust Arena “unless sometime in the future, he’s able to prove to us that he’s able to abide by our rules without being a potential threat.” A Sky spokesperson confirmed Freedom is banned indefinitely from the team’s home games. A league source with knowledge of the situation told Front Office Sports that the WNBA does not intend to impose a league-wide ban on Freedom. Chicago Sky owner Michael Alter is meeting with local Chicago Sky beat writers and local Chicago media. — Colin Salao (@colincsalao) August 25, 2026 “He Made Himself Into a Threat” Alter said multiple people seated close to Freedom told him the former NBA player started talking to Cloud during the game. “I’ve had both of these people, separately, confirm that the dialogue, the engagement, whatever you want or however you want to characterize it, between Cloud and Freedom Kanter, started with Kanter.” (One fan, Trista Smith, told reporters after the game, including FOS, that Freedom did not say anything to initiate the altercation.) Alter said he was told Freedom began to chirp at Cloud some time in the third quarter. “I would characterize it as trash talking, nothing personal, basketball-related, but enough to get her attention and to engage her, and, in my opinion, try to provoke her,” Alter said. After Cloud made a layup in the third quarter, she began to say something toward Freedom, who proceeded to stand up, raise his arms, and step forward. Freedom was immediately restrained by security and escorted out. Freedom did not pass the baseline, but Alter said he had “turned himself into a threat” by standing up and approaching a player. Alter said arena security, NBA security, Chicago Sky security, Indiana Fever security, and the Chicago Police Department all agreed that Freedom’s actions were worth removing him from the arena. “The security people’s job is not to wait until a threat intensifies. … We had five different security authorities all agree very quickly that there was no alternative but to throw him out because he made himself into a threat,” Alter said. No Relationship Alter also rejected Freedom’s claim that the team welcomed him. Freedom said Monday on Fox News that he texted Sky GM Jeff Pagliocca before the game to inform him he would come. Freedom claimed Pagliocca told him to “just enjoy the game.” Freedom was once a client of Pagliocca, a former basketball trainer. But Alter said their partnership ended in “2018 or 2019” and that the two have not spoken in years. On Tuesday, Alter read the text exchange between Hank Fetic, Freedom’s manager, and Pagliocca. “I got a new number. You’ve always been fair to me so I figured you deserved a heads up in advance. Enes and I will be at the Sky game tonight. Hope you are all well,” Fetic’s text read, according to Alter. It was around 2:30 p.m. CT when the Sky first heard Freedom was coming to the game at 6 p.m. CT. Pagliocca’s response about an hour later was “appreciate the text.” Alter said that by Freedom’s manager needing to provide a heads-up about their presence, it suggested they weren’t just coming to be regular fans: “There wouldn’t need to be a heads-up for that.” A Sky spokesperson reiterated Pagliocca did not invite nor speak to Freedom during or after the game. “It goes without saying that Jeff does not endorse Enes Kanter,” the spokesperson said. Freedom did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The Sky owner said they were not aware where Freedom would be seated until he arrived at the game. An unidentified third party purchased the ticket and gave it to Freedom, and the team allowed Freedom to attend the game as a fan. “We don’t censor people or prevent people from coming based upon anything other than their conduct. … He’s got the right to be here as long as he behaves, and we’ll keep an eye on to make sure that’s what’s going on,” Alter said. He added his “one regret” was not informing the players before the game that Freedom was expected to arrive. “I felt that it was too close to tip-off time, and that I just didn’t want it to become a distraction. … I don’t know that anything would have changed, but that’s my one regret,” Alter said. Cloud has yet to speak to reporters about the incident. A Sky spokesperson said Sunday that she spoke to team and league security after the game. She has posted on Threads over the last two days, including one Tuesday : “Your beliefs shouldn’t affect [others’] lives. You don’t have to agree or live your life like that. But you can stfu & mind your business, home, beds, and bodies.” The post WNBA’s Sky Ban Kanter Freedom From Arena Indefinitely appeared first on Front Office Sports .

articles.title: Texans sign standout UFL defender
articles.summary: The Houston Texans on Tuesday signed defensive end Derek Parish to their 90-man roster, according to ESPN’s Adam Schefter. The move comes after Houston lost defensive end Dylan Horton for the 2026 season with a torn Achilles. The Texans also placed Horton and linebacker Marte Mapu on injure
articles._body: The Houston Texans on Tuesday signed defensive end Derek Parish to their 90-man roster, according to ESPN’s Adam Schefter. The move comes after Houston lost defensive end Dylan Horton for the 2026 season with a torn Achilles. The Texans also placed Horton and linebacker Marte Mapu on injured reserve, per the NFL’s daily transaction report. The team has also been dealing with injuries to Jadeveon Clowney and Dominique Robinson, with Clowney nursing a lower-leg injury and Robinson recovering from a calf injury suffered after Houston’s preseason game against the Las Vegas Raiders. Parish brings a different path to the Texans. The 27-year-old defensive end was selected by the Jacksonville Jaguars with the 240th overall pick in the seventh round of the 2023 NFL Draft. He spent part of the 2023 season on Jacksonville’s practice squad but never appeared in an NFL game. The Jaguars listed him as a tight end. Before entering the professional ranks, Parish spent five years at the University of Houston from 2017 through 2022. He played both fullback and edge rusher during his college career. He also attended Pearland High School in Pearland, Texas, making his return to Houston a homecoming of sorts. After his time with Jacksonville, Parish played for the Toronto Argonauts in the CFL before joining the UFL’s DC Defenders. During the 2026 UFL season, he appeared in 10 games and produced 23 total tackles, four tackles for loss and three sacks. He also recorded a forced fumble. Parish logged three tackles across two postseason appearances. The Texans defensive-end depth has become a concern with several players unavailable, creating an opportunity for Parish. Houston is scheduled to face the Carolina Panthers in its third and final preseason game Friday, giving him a limited window to make an impression before the roster is reduced to 53 players Sunday. A solid preseason showing could give Parish a chance to remain with the Texans beyond the roster cuts, including potentially earning a practice squad spot. articles.summary: The New England Patriots and Christian Gonzalez have been in contract talks throughout the offseason. Nothing has come to fruition, despite the Week 1 opener against the Seattle Seahawks being just a few weeks away. On Tuesday, Gonzalez fielded some questions about his situation, but didn’t
articles._body: The New England Patriots and Christian Gonzalez have been in contract talks throughout the offseason. Nothing has come to fruition, despite the Week 1 opener against the Seattle Seahawks being just a few weeks away. On Tuesday, Gonzalez fielded some questions about his situation, but didn’t offer too much insight. When asked if he’s optimistic a deal will be finalized before the start of the regular season, the 24-year-old cornerback claimed he is simply focusing on Week 1 , according to Doug Kyed of the Boston Herald. Gonzalez did not provide any details about his contract dispute with the Patriots. “I mean, I’m focused on Week 1 at this point,” Gonzalez said. “I mean, it’s been all offseason, so like I said, I feel like the line of today is, it is what it is. So focused on Week 1 and doing what I gotta do.” In a follow-up question from Kyed asking him if he is prepared to play in the season opener even if a contract extension is not reached, the former first-round pick continued to beat the drum that he is simply focused on preparing for the first game of the campaign. “I’m focused on today, on this practice, and see where we go from here,” Gonzalez claimed. After an injury derailed his rookie season, Gonzalez has bounced back as one of the league’s premiere cornerbacks. The 2025-26 campaign was arguably the best of his career, despite the fact he failed to record an interception. The former Oregon Duck ended last season with 69 combined tackles (54 solo) and 10 pass deflections.
