articles.title: Peyton Watson pens heartfelt goodbye to Nuggets after Cavs trade
articles.summary: The Denver Nuggets recently shook things up when they sent Peyton Watson to the Cleveland Cavaliers as part of a big trade. The Nuggets have since pivoted by signing veteran guard DeMar DeRozan, as there are now fewer than two months to go until the upcoming season. Now, Watson has taken to his a
articles._body: The Denver Nuggets recently shook things up when they sent Peyton Watson to the Cleveland Cavaliers as part of a big trade. The Nuggets have since pivoted by signing veteran guard DeMar DeRozan , as there are now fewer than two months to go until the upcoming season. Now, Watson has taken to his account on Instagram to pen a heartfelt goodbye to the city of Denver. “Thank you for having me for the first four years of my career. As a young NBA player, who was a bit naive and hadn’t seen much of the real world, you guys took care of me better than I could have ever imagined,” read Watson’s statement in part. “… thank you to the fans. Playing in front of you has been a dream come true. I’ll see you all soon,” he added. Watson had a breakout year last season for the Nuggets, taking full advantage of his increased playing time during Nikola Jokic’s injury absence and turning into a legit two-way force for Denver, showing an increased perimeter jump-shooting ability, as well as no hesitation to create his own offense on occasion. The Nuggets are seemingly in dire need of players just like Watson, who provide size and athleticism on the wing, both of which the team was missing in their first-round playoff loss to the Minnesota Timberwolves, which Watson missed due to injury. However, the Nuggets’ sketchy financial situation ultimately led the team to trade Watson, and now they will hope that DeRozan’s veteran scoring ability and leadership will make up the difference. In any case, the Nuggets are set to kick off their new season on October 22 against the Oklahoma City Thunder. articles.title: The world's busiest spaceport is about to get a lot quieter, at least for now
articles.summary: SpaceX aims to launch Starship from Florida by the end of the year. 2027 seems more likely.
articles._body: SpaceX made Florida's Space Coast home to the world's busiest spaceport for a decade, but that will change this year. The company is significantly cutting the number of launches from Florida until Starship arrives, a senior SpaceX official confirmed Tuesday. The Falcon 9 rocket has been SpaceX's workhorse, routinely launching batches of satellites for the company's Starlink network, primarily from launch pads at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station and NASA's Kennedy Space Center in Florida. There were 165 Falcon 9 launches last year—about three flights per week—and about 75 percent of them carried Starlink satellites. This year is different. SpaceX has launched more missions from its West Coast launch pad at Vandenberg Space Force Base in California since January, and this trend will amplify for the rest of the year. articles.title: Vance Joseph rips Denver’s ‘lazy’ approach to start of Packers preseason game
articles.summary: Denver Broncos defensive coordinator Vance Joseph wasn’t pleased with how the defensive unit handled Friday’s matchup against the Green Bay Packers. the Broncos lost 33-13 in the home preseason opener and in a performance that Sean Payton immediately decried. Broncos defensive coordinator Vance J
articles._body: Denver Broncos defensive coordinator Vance Joseph wasn’t pleased with how the defensive unit handled Friday’s matchup against the Green Bay Packers. the Broncos lost 33-13 in the home preseason opener and in a performance that Sean Payton immediately decried. Broncos defensive coordinator Vance Joseph was extremely displeased and didn't mince words regarding how his defense approached its first series last Friday night. "Our approach — in my opinion — was was unengaged and a little bit lazy," he said. pic.twitter.com/Yn0bB7CsNs — Andrew Mason (@MaseDenver) August 25, 2026 “We can’t just say, ‘Hey, this is preseason [game] two,'” Payton said following the game. “Each phase saw their share of what ended up being the final score. So, tomorrow we’ve got to be able to come in — coaches the same way — and look closely at what we’re doing and get the corrections made. You can’t not pay attention to these games, these scrimmages, these important steps towards the start of the regular season.” Vance weighed in with his thoughts in a Tuesday media availability. “I think that first drive was kind of twofold for me. I didn’t think our approach, in my opinion, was engaged and a little bit lazy. It wasn’t the right approach even in pregame so I felt that. That was the first lesson. The second lesson is I think, in the two games we’ve played here, we’ve seen how offenses see us. He added, “Lots of boots, lots of misdirection, outside runs more often than not, match protection, passes, quick game. Teams don’t want to lose first down because if they do lose first down, our rush kind of comes alive.” Vance then spoke about how he believes that though it is a preseason game, it’s a precursor for what’s to come from their opponents. “I think that game was an example of what is coming in the future: how teams see us run game-wise, pass game-wise, winning first down with quick game boots, outside runs more often than inside runs. To me it was a great lesson on both ends: when we play it’s a standard and I want to see it all the time. Obviously how teams see us, and in two weeks we’ve seen that kind of trend that way.” The Broncos had a phenomenal season in 2025, making the AFC Championship before ultimately losing to the New England Patriots . Both Payton and Vance look to improve from the preseason shortcomings to return to form at the start of the new season The post Vance Joseph rips Denver’s ‘lazy’ approach to start of Packers preseason game appeared first on ClutchPoints .

On Tuesday, Monken cleared the air, saying that Kiffin didn’t actually call him . “First off, I should not … one of our staff had said, that’s why I said ‘us’ and not ‘me’ … one of our staff had said they had gotten a text,” Monken said (h/t Mark Heim of AL.com). “I should’ve followed through with it. Maybe they meant someone from (LSU’s) staff. That’s on me. Should not throw someone’s name on there without following through on it. “I was just making light of it. I was really not trying to make a big thing of it. I was just like, ‘man, what this world has come to.’ It was almost silliness and goofiness. It’s really not a big deal other than I probably shouldn’t have (said that) without following through.” In any case, the Wright situation is a much bigger and more intriguing subject than Monken’s clarificatory statement on a supposed call he got from Kiffin.4 Wright is among the players given a temporary restraining order by a Louisiana court that paved the way for them to hit the transfer portal. Even though he could play in the NFL and was on the Browns’ roster for a preseason game , Wright has a chance to see action for a college football team in 2026. That team is expected to be LSU, with Wright clearing waivers on Tuesday . articles.title: South Carolina women’s basketball alum A’ja Wilson approaches another all-time WNBA record, wins Player of the Week honor
articles.summary: South Carolina women's basketball legend A'ja Wilson has won yet another Western Conference Player of the Week award.
articles._body: South Carolina women’s basketball legend A’ja Wilson has done it again. For the 32nd time in her professional career, Wilson has earned the WNBA Western Conference Player of the Week award. No other player has ever won that many. When considering instances of winning either the Eastern or Western Conference Player of the Week honor, Wilson only trails Tina Charles’ 33 total award wins. This was also Wilson’s fourth POTW award of the 2026 season. She has earned at least four such honors every year since 2022. En route to this week’s selection, Wilson averaged 25.7 points, 8.0 rebounds, 4.7 assists, 1.7 blocks and 1.3 steals per game. She also shot 50% from the field and 87% from the free throw line across three games. Wilson’s efforts included a 27-point, 14-rebound double-double against the Atlanta Dream, three outings with at least 20 points, and three games with at least three assists. Oh, and she helped her Las Vegas Aces squad to clinch a playoff berth. Questions about this story? Kevin Miller and Chris Wellbaum are discussing it with subscribers on the Women’s Basketball forum. Incredibly, Wilson’s Player of the Week numbers are merely in line with her full-season averages. So far in 2026, the MVP frontrunner is averaging 26.0 points, 9.5 rebounds, 3.2 assists, 2.0 blocks, and 1.4 steals. She is shooting 50.1% from the field, 37.6% from the 3-point line, and 85.8% on free throw attempts. Per the Polymarket prediction markets, Wilson is the odds-on favorite to win her fifth WNBA MVP award. She is currently second (behind Gabby Williams of the Golden State Valkyrie) in the odds to win her fourth WNBA Defensive Player of the Year award. The Aces also have the third-best odds (behind the Minnesota Lynx and Indiana Fever) to win the 2026 WNBA Finals. Want to talk South Carolina women’s basketball? Join the discussion on the Women’s Basketball forum.

articles.title: Dolly Parton Forever: See Pictures From Her Billboard Photo Shoots Over the Years
articles.summary: The incomparable legend died at the age of 80 on Aug. 25, 2026.
articles._body: On a list of accolades that includes 10 Grammys, 22 Billboard Hot 100 hits and inductions into both the Country Music and Rock & Roll Halls of Fame, Dolly Parton was also a Billboard cover star. The legendary musician and cultural icon — whose death at age 80 on Tuesday (Aug. 25) has made for an indescribable loss — was on the cover of Billboard in 2020 , a historically difficult year for many during which Parton’s infallible optimism and kindness were needed more than ever. She spoke to executive editor Melinda Newman about keeping her groundbreaking Dollywood enterprise on its feet in the face of the devastating COVID-19 pandemic at the time, as well as her industry savvy and endurance over the course of her six-decade career. Above everything, though, she emphasized her commitment to generosity. “As the scripture says, ‘To whom much is given, much is required,’” Parton said in the piece, which also served as 2020’s Billboard Country Power Players issue. “So I look at my life with that every day and think that God expects it of me. I expect it of myself, and I think people expect it of me. If I can be an inspiration, then I want to be that. That makes me feel good.” Parton was also featured six years prior in a 2014 issue of Billboard , answering questions about everything from her long marriage to late husband Carl Dean to her love for her LGBTQ fanbase and position as a role model with her signature sparkling wit. “I’ve lived a lot and I’ve done a lot,” she said at the time. “I’ve been around so long that I think people just kind of feel like I’m a member of their family — like a favorite aunt or an older sister. People relate to me because I grew up poor and in a big family. They know I understand all the hardships.” In honor of the irreplaceable superstar, take a look at the photos from Parton’s unforgettable shoots with Billboard in 2020 and 2014 below.

articles.title: Heat’s Klay Thompson compares Giannis Antetokounmpo impact to Stephen Curry
articles.summary: With Klay Thompson making the move to sign with the Miami Heat, he will be looking to add a fifth championship to his accomplished resume, though it will be without long-time teammate Stephen Curry. As Thompson joins Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo on the Heat, the star three-point shooter
articles._body: With Klay Thompson making the move to sign with the Miami Heat , he will be looking to add a fifth championship to his accomplished resume, though it will be without long-time teammate Stephen Curry. As Thompson joins Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo on the Heat, the star three-point shooter would compare one of his new teammates to Curry. Miami’s biggest acquisition this season was no doubt Antetokounmpo, who has a championship to his name to go along with two Most Valuable Player (MVP) awards. To Thompson, he sees a similarity in how the two impact the game, boasting that Antetokounmpo will be another MVP that he’s played with, which he claims to be “rare.” “They both have similar impact on the game,” Thompson said Tuesday in his introductory press conference to Miami. “I play with, I think Giannis can be the third MVP I’ve been able to play with now, which is really cool. His interior scoring is one of the best ever, and his jump shot is greatly improved now. You can’t sag off him like you used to. He will punish you, and he’s just an incredible talent who has a great will to win.” “And I love being around guys like that who leave it all on the floor to really care about the craft, and that’s what attracts me too. So I don’t take this role I have lightly,” Thompson continued. “I’m just…not just happy to be here, but I’m just thrilled to have a defined role in this team to try and help guys with my experience and help guide the team through a rollercoaster of a season because it’s never easy when you’re trying to chase what we’re trying to do.” Klay Thompson on the impacts a player like Giannis Antetokounmpo and Stephen Curry share. “They both have similar impact on the game…I don’t take this role I have lightly, whatever it is, I’m just happy to be here, thrilled to have a defined role in this team…” #Heat pic.twitter.com/yRcr19vHn0 — Zachary Weinberger (@ZachWeinberger) August 25, 2026 Klay Thompson speaks on his fit with the Heat Thompson would continue speaking about the prospects of playing with Antetokounmpo, even calling the former Milwaukee Bucks star “one of the best players of all time.” The 36-year-old emphasizes not only helping each other, but aiding the rest of the team with their experience winning the highest honor. Thompson’s fit with Miami is an easy one to picture, as with Antetokounmpo and Adebayo commanding the paint, he’ll have lots of three-point opportunities to capitalize on, as he echoes the same sentiment. “I mean, just freeing them up for lanes to drive, for space to operate, and for myself, I’m going to get so many great looks playing off him and Bam and Wiggs and the rest of the guys because they create so much pressure going to the basket, and it’s going to be fun just figuring out how we all fit together, what our actions work well, and we can all screen for each other. It’s going to be great, and we’re all very versatile on both sides of the floor,” Thompson said. “You know, being able to guard one through five, being able to lead the fast break,” Thompson continued. “So it’s almost like limitless what we could do, and I can’t wait to get the whole squad together and see what works well, and define our rules. It’s really, really exciting, and it’s like coming in this building just gave me a whole new jolt of energy to be myself again.” Klay Thompson on now having Giannis Antetokounmpo as a teammate: “Giannis is one of the best players of all time…I think we can both just help each other, not just him, but the whole team…” Full response: #Heat pic.twitter.com/2fsIJ31fSg — Zachary Weinberger (@ZachWeinberger) August 25, 2026 At any rate, Thompson will prepare for his 14th season in the NBA with Miami, hoping to raise another banner in South Beach. articles.title: Show HN: TeXbrain, a LaTeX editor that runs pdfTeX in the browser via WASM
articles.summary: I'm a master's engineering student and a big fan of LaTeX, which I used for my thesis and research articles. I have used Overleaf and that was fine until I wanted to git sync, which unfortunately sits behind a paywall. Since I didn't want to pay subscriptions for things that should simply just wo
articles._body: I'm a master's engineering student and a big fan of LaTeX, which I used for my thesis and research articles. I have used Overleaf and that was fine until I wanted to git sync, which unfortunately sits behind a paywall. Since I didn't want to pay subscriptions for things that should simply just work, I built the editor I wanted in my free time, where you open a tab, write LaTeX, get your PDF and the files stay all in one folder on my disk. TeXbrain is a static site with no backend. pdfTeX is compiled to WebAssembly (SwiftLaTeX) and runs in your browser. The editor can read and write your project folder through the File System Access API, so you can use git, any local TeX install, local AI Agents, or any other editor on the same files. Git is built in through isomorphic-git for anyone who would rather not touch a terminal and clone, branch, commit, push or pull via commands. No account is needed, no analytics, and everything works offline after the first load. Try it out: https://tex.swimmingbrain.dev/ (Chromium browsers get direct folder access, while Firefox or Safari fall back to a virtual filesystem) Or for self-hosting/contributing: https://github.com/swimmingbrain/texbrain (MIT, the pdfTeX engine is EPL 2.0 / GPL 2.0 and is listed in the THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES file). The part I'm most proud of getting to work is the package loading. The engine itself is only 1.8 MB. When it asks for a file it doesn't have, then a service worker intercepts the request and resolves it through Cache Storage first, then a small bundled subset, then a TeX Live tree mirrored on jsDelivr, then a SwiftLaTeX style server as a last resort. Every file is fetched once at most and after the first successful compilation, the core subset is prefetched in the background so that the offline story actually holds. Only file names go over the network, never any document content. So far, it only supports pdfTeX (no XeTeX or LuaTeX), so fontspec or polyglossia won't work, packages are pinned to the TeX Live 2020 era to stay coherent with the engine's format file and there is no bibtex or biber in the engine yet, which is maybe the roughest edge. This is should be a good solution for people on a work laptop, a Chromebook, or a university lab PC where installing TeX Live isn't always an option, and people who don't want to maintain a TeX install at all. If you already have a local setup you like, keep it. This isn't necessarily thought as a replacement for that. Some people have already used it for their thesis in the past months and their bug reports (which I would never have hit on my own) were then most of the summer's work. The first outside PR also landed recently, so if something doesn't compile for you, an issue with the package name or the bug itself is the most useful thing you can send me! articles._body: Meghan Trainor signed with United Talent Agency (UTA) for global representation in live touring, brand partnerships, filmed entertainment, digital media and theatre, the agency announced. Trainor released her seventh studio album, Toy With Me , in April. The record saw Trainor address online comments. Sitting down with Billboard back in April, she shared the inspiration for her latest album’s name came from playing toys with her kids, stating, “I want my music to take me back to childhood when everything was easier and better and lighter.” Trainor’s 2015 album Title hit No. 1 on the Billboard 200, while 2016’s Thank You peaked at No. 3. In 2025, Trainor received the Hitmaker Award at the Billboard Women in Music event. When she spoke to Billboard ahead of receiving the honor, she said she considered a hit song something her at the time “three-year-old would know,” noting that she believes the biggest hits to be cross-generational. In 2014, her single “All About That Bass” spent eight weeks atop the Billboard Hot 100 and a total of 47 weeks on the chart. Her 2016 single, “No,” peaked at No. 3. Her song “Criminals” was the theme song for Netflix’s The Perfect Couple , which helped the song land on the Hot 100. In 2016, Trainor won the Grammy Award for Best New Artist. She has also made appearances as a judge, coach and mentor on The Voice , The Voice UK , The Four and Australian Idol . Trainor is managed by Bond Artist Management’s Nikola Barisic and represented by Myman Greenspan Fox’s Aaron Rosenberg . See more artist signings below.

articles.title: President Trump Orders U.S. Flags Lowered to Half-Staff for 1 Week to Mourn Dolly Parton: ‘The World Loves You’
articles.summary: The country music icon died Tuesday (Aug. 25) at age 80.
articles._body: As the world mourns the death of Dolly Parton , President Donald Trump announced Tuesday (Aug. 25) that flags around the country will be lowered to half-staff beginning at 6 p.m. in honor of the late country icon. In a post on Truth Social, Trump wrote , “Very sad to report that Dolly Parton, one of the greatest country singers, and far beyond, ever, has just passed away. This is a true loss for millions of people. There has never been anyone like her, and never will. In her honor, I am lowering the American flag throughout the United States for a one week period beginning tonight at 6 p.m. Rest in peace, Dolly! The world loves you. President Donald J. Trump.” Related Dolly Parton, One of Country Music’s Biggest & Brightest Icons, Dies at 80 Dolly Parton’s 25 Best Songs: Critics’ Picks Dolly Parton Remembered by Reba McEntire, Paul McCartney, George Strait & More: ‘We Will Always Love You’ Tennessee native Parton died Tuesday in Nashville, at age 80. Parton’s nephew and head of security Bryan Seaver announced Parton’s death in a video on social media. During her career, Parton often avoided delving into politics. She previously revealed during a Today show interview in 2021 that she was twice offered the Presidential Medal of Freedom during the Trump administration, and turned it down both times. “I couldn’t accept it because my husband was ill and then they asked me again about it and I wouldn’t travel because of the COVID,” Parton told Today at the time, and noting she had heard from President Joe Biden at the time about accepting the honor as well. “Now I feel like if I take it, I’ll be doing politics, so I’m not sure.” Parton dedicated her life and career to bettering the world in so many ways , from her Dollywood theme park to her Imagination Library, which has promoted childhood literacy through delivering millions of books to children. She launched the Dollywood Foundation in 1988, and in 2000, she launched the Dolly Parton Scholarship to help college-bound students in her home area of Sevier County, Tennessee. She made donations to help people in East Tennessee following devastating wildfires, and donated $1 million to the Monroe Carell Jr. Children’s Hospital at Vanderbilt University Medical Center in 2017. As a singer, artist, songwriter, entertainer, author, businesswoman and philanthropist, Parton built a multifaceted career that included multitudes of accolades. She was a member of both the Country Music Hall of Fame and Rock and Roll Hall of Fame, and earned 25 No. 1 hits on Billboard ‘s Hot Country Songs chart. She also earned 10 Grammy wins from 55 nominations. An official statement regarding Parton’s death on Aug. 25 reads: “A rhinestone life that shone bright enough for the world to see, Dolly will forever stand as an inspiration not only through her timeless music and prolific songwriting, but also her wit, warmth, and kindness that made us all feel like family. Dolly Parton’s legacy is one of love, compassion, and resilience. With a seven-decade career, she inspired multiple generations of artists and fans with her music and an unwavering commitment to making the world a better place. Her songs will continue to resonate with people of all ages, and her philanthropic work will have a lasting impact.”

articles.summary: DeMar DeRozan has six All-Star nods to his name, 26,711 career points, and a case as one of the best shooting guards in NBA history. The USC product has been getting NBA buckets in the mid-range since 2009, and he just agreed to a contract to join a Denver Nuggets team in dire need of […]</
articles._body: DeMar DeRozan has six All-Star nods to his name, 26,711 career points, and a case as one of the best shooting guards in NBA history. The USC product has been getting NBA buckets in the mid-range since 2009, and he just agreed to a contract to join a Denver Nuggets team in dire need of depth. Of course, though, DeRozan isn’t the caliber of player he once was, and it took the Sacramento Kings waiving him for the shooting guard to hit the open market. Michael Scotto just reported that Sacramento will stretch the remaining $10 million that was left on DeRozan’s contract, meaning the Kings will pay their former player $3.33 million over each of the next three seasons, just not play for somebody else. DeRozan is entering his 18th season in the NBA. Last season, which was his second with the Kings, was his first since 2012-13 in which he didn’t surpass the 20-point-per-game threshold. DeRozan seemingly still has something left in the tank, at least when it comes to scoring. He averaged a respectable 18.4 points per game last season and is expected to play a big role on Denver’s bench. The Nuggets lost Tim Hardaway Jr. to the Miami Heat in the offseason. He was their spark plug sixth man who played the two-guard position. Financial issues for the Nuggets to trade Peyton Watson away, too. The newest Cleveland Cavaliers was an up-and-coming player, especially as an isolation scorer. DeRozan’s defense, playmaking, and 3-point shooting leave a lot to be desired, which is why the Kings moved on, even at the cost of stretching his contract. Even so, it will be interesting to see his role on a Nikola Jokic-led team this year. articles.title: Vikings make eye-opening backup QB practice decision
articles.summary: J.J. McCarthy’s fall down the Minnesota Vikings’ quarterback depth chart may not be over yet. ESPN’s Kevin Seifert reported that McCarthy and veteran Carson Wentz split second-team reps during a relatively brief 80-minute Vikings practice. One practice does not determine Minnesota’s backup quarte
articles._body: J.J. McCarthy’s fall down the Minnesota Vikings’ quarterback depth chart may not be over yet. ESPN’s Kevin Seifert reported that McCarthy and veteran Carson Wentz split second-team reps during a relatively brief 80-minute Vikings practice. One practice does not determine Minnesota’s backup quarterback, but the distribution of reps is an interesting development for McCarthy. The former Michigan star entered the NFL as a first-round pick with hopes of becoming Minnesota’s long-term answer at quarterback. Two years later, his career appears to be trending in the wrong direction. McCarthy has already lost the starting job to Kyler Murray. Now, instead of receiving the majority of the second-team work, he is sharing those opportunities with Wentz. This does not necessarily mean Wentz has officially passed McCarthy on the depth chart. Minnesota could simply be evaluating both quarterbacks or helping Wentz become more comfortable in the offense. It would be unfair to draw a firm conclusion from one abbreviated practice in August. Still, the Vikings’ decision is worth monitoring. If McCarthy were firmly established as Murray’s primary backup, there would seemingly be little reason to divide the second-team work evenly. Giving Wentz those snaps suggests the veteran has at least entered the competition for the No. 2 role. McCarthy does have an undisclosed injury from last week’s preseason game, where he did not play well. Wentz’s experience could give him an advantage if the Vikings need someone to replace Murray during the regular season. He has started 94 NFL games and would likely be viewed as the safer short-term option if Minnesota believes it can contend immediately. McCarthy still has time to change the conversation, but his margin for error is shrinking. Losing the QB1 job was already a major setback. Falling behind Wentz would leave the former first-round pick entering the season as Minnesota’s third quarterback. One practice is not enough to declare that competition over. It may, however, be the first real sign that McCarthy’s place on the depth chart is less secure than expected. articles._body: New York Yankees starting pitcher Max Fried is battling back from an elbow injury . Elbow injuries always sound frightening for pitchers, but Fried has been making quality progress . In fact, Fried may even end up returning this weekend during the Yankees’ series against the Boston Red Sox. “Max Fried threw four innings of live BP yesterday. Could potentially put him in play to be activated this weekend against the Red Sox (doubleheader on Saturday),” Greg Joyce reported Tuesday. Fried, 32, has been effective while on the mound this season. He has only appeared in 15 games due to injury, but the southpaw has recorded a 2.81 ERA during that span. He has 79 strikeouts in 86.1 innings of work as well. The Yankees would have obviously loved to have Fried available on a more consistent basis this season. With that being said, he has played a role in their success. Having him available for the stretch run and postseason will be of the utmost importance. The Yankees hold the top American League Wild Card spot at the moment. In the AL East division, New York trails the first place Tampa Bay Rays by 3.5 games. The Yankees could still win the division, but they should be able to at least reach the playoffs as an AL Wild Card ball club. It remains to be seen if Max Fried will indeed return this weekend against the Red Sox. However, it is seemingly a legitimate possibility. articles.summary: Superstar edge rusher Nick Bosa is currently working his way back from surgery that repaired a torn ACL in his right knee. While a return to action by Week 1 of the new season is not likely, San Francisco 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan provided some news that fans can still get excited about. Rep
articles._body: Superstar edge rusher Nick Bosa is currently working his way back from surgery that repaired a torn ACL in his right knee. While a return to action by Week 1 of the new season is not likely, San Francisco 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan provided some news that fans can still get excited about. Reports indicate that the club is hoping Bosa will finally return to practice shortly after Thursday’s preseason finale against the Las Vegas Raiders, according to David Lombardi of the San Francisco Standard. Nothing appears to be guaranteed, but Bosa seems to be making progress in his recovery. “Kyle Shanahan says Nick Bosa ‘is doing good’ and the 49ers hope that he’ll be back in practice next week,” Lombardi reported. While the eight-year veteran continues his recovery process, the 49ers have been utilizing Sam Okuayinonu, rookie Romello Height, and Ogbo Okoronkwo in Bosa’s place. Mykel Williams is also dealing with an injury of his own, so the other side of the defensive line consists of Keion White, Quinton Bell, Victor Dimukeje, and Viliami Fehoko Jr. When healthy, Nick Bosa is one of the league’s most dominant pass rushers . The 49ers missed him dearly last season after he suffered the injury in the first three games of the 2025-26 campaign. With seven years in the NFL under his belt, the five-time Pro Bowler has accumulated 278 combined tackles (192 solo), 64.5 sacks, 13 forced fumbles, five fumble recoveries, and two interceptions. The 49ers will provide more injury updates for Bosa throughout the next few weeks. Until then, the club will focus its attention on Thursday’s preseason game against the Raiders before taking on the Los Angeles Rams in Week 1 of the regular season. One of the biggest is who will be starting at right guard. Jackson Powers-Johnson and Caleb Rogers have been battling for the opportunity all training camp. The Raiders p
articles._body: Head coach Klint Kubiak will have plenty of decisions to make when crafting his first final roster with the Las Vegas Raiders. One of the biggest is who will be starting at right guard . Jackson Powers-Johnson and Caleb Rogers have been battling for the opportunity all training camp. The Raiders preseason finale against the San Francisco 49ers will play a major role in Kubiak’s ultimate decision, via Sam Warren of the Athletic. “It continues. This game will be really important for that battle,’ Kubiak said. “I know both of those guys are gonna play this year. We’re counting on both of them, as well as a lot of other guys.” Powers-Johnson appeared in eight games during the 2025 campaign, starting seven at right guard before suffering a season-ending ankle injury. He earned a 63.8 overall grade from Pro Football Focus, ranking 37/81 guards. Furthermore, Powers-Johnson’s 66.6 run blocking mark ranked 31st. The guard has appeared in 23 games over his two years with the franchise, starting 21 of them. Rogers filled in for Powers-Johnson after his injury, starting six games as a rookie. As a third-round pick, the Raiders have high hopes for his future. Still, it’s clear there is some development to be had, as Rodgers earned a 59.6 grade from PFF. However, the 2026 season is a completely different beast. Kubiak is now installing his brand of offense. Either player must prove to be a strong fit, especially playing next to new offensive line building block Tyler Linderbaum. One game won’t decide the starter alone, but it could be the determining factor. If Powers-Johnson and Rogers are truly neck-and-neck, the preseason finale will be extremely pivotal for both guards. articles.title: Taylor Swift’s ‘I Knew It, I Knew You’ Hits No. 1 on Billboard’s Radio Songs Chart
articles.summary: The Toy Story single is her ninth all-format airplay leader.
articles._body: Taylor Swift claims the No. 1 spot on Billboard ’s all-format Radio Songs chart as “I Knew It, I Knew You” rises a rung on the Aug. 29-dated ranking. The song drew 64.7 million airplay audience impressions Aug. 14-20. (The chart measures songs’ weekly reach, as tabulated by Mediabase and provided to Billboard by Luminate, on more than 1,100 U.S. radio stations.) Related Taylor Swift Surprises ‘Toy Story 5’ Premiere With Rare Performance & We Were Inside to Tell the Full Story Inside ‘Toy Story 5’ World Premiere: Taylor Swift & Randy Newman’s Friendly Duet & More Magical Moments Rock on the Rise, Pop Drops: Five-Year Trends on Billboard’s Radio Songs Chart “I Knew It, I Knew You” becomes Swift’s ninth career Radio Songs No. 1 Here’s a recap of her leaders. Title, Weeks at No. 1, Year(s): “I Knew It, I Knew You,” one (to date), 2026 “Cruel Summer,” 12, 2023-24 “Anti-Hero,” five, 2022-23 “Wildest Dreams,” two, 2015 “Bad Blood,” five, 2015 “Blank Space,” six, 2014-15 “Shake It Off,” four, 2014 “I Knew You Were Trouble.,” four, 2013 “You Belong With Me,” two, 2009 “I Knew It, I Knew You” is from Toy Story 5 , inspired by the film’s cowgirl heroine, Jessie . In June, the song launched as Swift’s 15th No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 . It became just the third leader on the list ever from an animated Disney movie, and the first from its Pixar studio. Meanwhile, the track is the second Radio Songs No. 1 this year from a soundtrack — HUNTR/X’s “Golden,” from KPop Demon Hunters , led for a week in January. On its way to its Radio Songs reign, “I Knew It, I Knew You” has claimed milestones on individual-format airplay charts. On Adult Pop Airplay, it became Swift’s 16th No. 1, lifting her past Maroon 5 for the most leaders , dating to the chart’s debut in Billboard in March 1996. On Country Airplay, the song became the first by a woman ever to debut in the top 10 . It has since reached No. 7. It has also become her 29th top 10 on Pop Airplay and her 23rd on Adult Contemporary. Notably, Swift made history when “You Belong With Me” became her first Radio Songs No. 1, marking the first country crossover leader since the chart began in December 1990. It surpassed three such No. 2 hits to that point: Shania Twain’s “You’re Still the One” (1998), Faith Hill’s “Breathe” (2000) and Swift’s “Love Story” (earlier in 2009).

articles.title: Why Braves are in serious trouble in NL East amid Phillies’ push
articles.summary: What appeared to be a secure division lead for the Atlanta Braves has suddenly become anything but comfortable. The Philadelphia Phillies have stormed back from a miserable first half and emerged as one of the hottest teams in baseball. They recently rattled off nine consecutive victories before
articles._body: What appeared to be a secure division lead for the Atlanta Braves has suddenly become anything but comfortable. The Philadelphia Phillies have stormed back from a miserable first half and emerged as one of the hottest teams in baseball. They recently rattled off nine consecutive victories before the Seattle Mariners ended the streak Monday, but that loss should not distract from how quickly Philadelphia has transformed the NL East race. The Phillies have won nine of their last 10 games and collected 16 victories in August. Even after Monday’s defeat, they sit only 3.5 games behind Atlanta. Before that game, the gap was down to three. That is far too close for a Braves team heading in the opposite direction. Atlanta remains talented enough to win the division and make a deep postseason run, but its recent play has opened the door. The Braves are just 3-7 over their last 10 games, allowing the Phillies to erase much of a deficit that appeared daunting only a few weeks ago. Philadelphia is no longer simply chasing. It is applying real pressure. Braves need more than Ronald Acuña Jr.’s return to hold off Phillies Jordan Godfree-Imagn Images Ronald Acuña Jr. is healthy again, but his return has not translated into enough victories. One superstar cannot solve every problem, particularly when Atlanta’s rotation no longer resembles the dominant unit the organization expected to deploy. Losing Spencer Strider was a significant blow. Chris Sale and Bryce Elder have provided consistency, but the Braves need more behind them. Grant Holmes and Martín Pérez must pitch well during the final month if Atlanta hopes to maintain its lead. Tyler Mahle could become an important addition for the stretch run and postseason, but the Braves cannot afford to wait for everything to fall perfectly into place. Their starting pitching must improve immediately. The bullpen gives Atlanta some reason for confidence, but relying heavily on relievers becomes dangerous when starters consistently fail to work deep into games. That formula can exhaust even a quality bullpen before October arrives. Atlanta’s offense also needs more consistent production. Drake Baldwin played at an MVP-caliber level early in the season. Although he continues to perform well, expecting a young catcher to carry the offense for an entire season was always unrealistic. Austin Riley has not provided the same power production that defined the beginning of his career. Meanwhile, Matt Olson and Michael Harris II have been forced to shoulder much of the offensive responsibility. A roster containing Acuña, Riley, Olson and Harris should not have to scratch its way through the final month. Atlanta needs its stars producing together instead of waiting for one or two players to rescue the lineup every night. Phillies-Braves September showdowns could decide NL East The Braves will begin a three-game home series against the Los Angeles Dodgers before facing the Colorado Rockies and San Francisco Giants. Those final two matchups are highly winnable, making this a crucial opportunity for Atlanta to regain control. Anything less could allow Philadelphia to close the gap — or erase it entirely. The Phillies may have the more difficult remaining schedule, but their momentum cannot be ignored. Their lineup is clicking, their confidence is rising, and they can see the Braves directly ahead of them. Most importantly, Philadelphia will have two chances to take control without needing help from anyone else. The rivals begin a four-game series in Philadelphia on Sept. 4. With roughly 20 games remaining afterward, a decisive series victory could determine which team enters the final stretch with the advantage. They will meet the following weekend again for three games in Atlanta. Seven head-to-head matchups across two weekends will give both teams a chance to settle the race themselves. With approximately 30 games remaining, the Phillies look like the better bet to win the division. They are playing their best baseball at the right time, while the Braves are watching their once-comfortable advantage disappear. Atlanta still controls its own fate, but that control will not last much longer without a complete turnaround. If Philadelphia wins both September series, the Phillies will not merely make the NL East race interesting. They will take the division from the Braves. articles.title: Arkansas lands 2023 All-American safety in transfer portal
articles.summary: Arkansas signed former Liberty safety Brylan Green to the roster Tuesday, giving the Razorbacks another experienced option in the secondary ahead of the 2026 season. Green became eligible for a fifth college season after a temporary restraining order in Louisiana granted additional eligibility to
articles._body: Arkansas signed former Liberty safety Brylan Green to the roster Tuesday, giving the Razorbacks another experienced option in the secondary ahead of the 2026 season. Green became eligible for a fifth college season after a temporary restraining order in Louisiana granted additional eligibility to him and 15 other players. He subsequently entered the transfer portal and committed to Arkansas. The Lafayette, Louisiana, native spent all four of his previous collegiate seasons with the Flames. He played as a true freshman in 2022 and faced the the Razorbacks that year, recording four tackles in a game the Liberty won in Fayetteville. Green developed into a productive defensive back during his Flames career. Across four seasons, he accumulated 141 tackles, one sack, one forced fumble and six interceptions. His best season statistically came in 2023, when he intercepted five passes, the sixth-most in the country, and earned Conference USA All-Conference First-Team recognition. He was also named to the FWAA All-American Second Team that season. During the 2025 campaign, Green finished with 39 tackles, one tackle for loss, one fumble recovery and five pass breakups. Pro Football Focus gave him a 78.6 overall grade across 493 snaps, including a 79.5 coverage grade, 74.7 rush-defense grade and 54.6 pass-rush grade. PFF ranked him No. 116 among FBS safeties last season. Green also contributed on special teams at Liberty, returning 19 punts for 186 yards. His longest punt return covered 45 yards in 2024. His arrival adds further depth to an Arkansas secondary that underwent numerous changes during the offseason. The Razorbacks have 22 secondary transfers, four incoming freshmen and one returning player from the Sam Pittman era. Arkansas also added Caleb Wooden and Sean Williams through court-related eligibility rulings, although an Aug. 21 ruling from the 10th Circuit Court of Appeals made both players ineligible. The Razorbacks secondary has a lot of room for improvement after ranking No. 101 nationally in passing yards allowed, No. 102 in interceptions, 13th in the SEC in passing defense and last in the conference in scoring defense. Christian Harrison and Miguel Mitchell are expected to handle the starting safety roles, while Green provides another veteran option behind them. The remaining depth includes JUCO transfers Kyeaure Magloire and Nsongbeh Ginyui, true freshman Tay Lockett and Iowa State transfer LaMarcus Hicks, who has appeared in three games. Green’s addition comes after Arkansas allowed several explosive plays during two fall-camp scrimmages, including touchdown receptions of 96, 34 and 66 yards. articles.title: Heat’s Erik Spoelstra shuts down Klay Thompson-Ray Allen comparison with ‘special’ declaration
articles.summary: MIAMI – With Klay Thompson joining Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo on the Miami Heat, there is one player that fans have been comparing the signing to who could have championship gold on their mind. As Thompson makes the move to the Heat with the prospect of competing for a title, hea
articles._body: MIAMI – With Klay Thompson joining Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo on the Miami Heat , there is one player that fans have been comparing the signing to who could have championship gold on their mind. As Thompson makes the move to the Heat with the prospect of competing for a title, head coach Erik Spoelstra gives his thoughts on the comparisons being made between Thompson and legendary player Ray Allen. Why the comparison excites Miami fans is that Allen was a key part of the franchise’s championship legacy, hitting the famous three-point shot in Game 6 of the 2013 NBA Finals that tied the game, leading to the victory and ultimately the championship. Plus, the age matches up, as both Thompson and Allen, aside from being two of the greatest three-point shooters in NBA history, were both 36 years old when signing with the Heat. Spoelstra was the head coach during both signings, as he said to ClutchPoints that he “ can see where people would make that comparison,” as it’s one “born out of respect.” However, he wants this team to have a “new history.” “Yeah, I haven’t given a lot of thought. I can see where people would make that comparison, and I mean, that’s one born out of great respect. They’re two of the best and the greatest that have done it like that. But what I would say to that is, let’s let this team have its own journey and its own identity, its own story. That’s in the past. So that’s a great part of our history,” Spoelstra said Tuesday. Asked Erik Spoelstra about the comparison lof Klay Thompson coming to the #Heat at this point of his career to that of Ray Allen: “I can see where people would make that comparison, that’s born out of great respect….let’s let this team have its own journey and own identity…” pic.twitter.com/AzUVQ2p33Y — Zachary Weinberger (@ZachWeinberger) August 25, 2026 Heat’s Erik Spoelstra excited for upcoming season Spoelstra would continue by saying that the Heat are enthusiastic about the team that has been crafted this offseason, which, besides signing the four-time NBA champion with the Golden State Warriors, a blockbuster trade dominated the headlines. Joining the Miami captain in Adebayo is Antetokounmpo, and with the main priority being three-point shooting, the team ended up acquiring one of the most accomplished shooters in history, ranking fourth all-time in shots made from that range (2,899). “We’re putting together this team for a new history, and we think we have, you know, the makings of something special,” Spoelstra continued. “We’ll get into the season and all the things that happen during the course of a long 82-game season to get ready for the playoffs. But we’re just excited about the group that we have. And five weeks from now, we’re going to get to work at camp and create our own story. And hopefully, it ends with something spectacular.” Heat’s Klay Thompson on Erik Spoelstra Tuesday saw the Heat introduce Thompson in his first press conference, where he was asked about Spoelstra and if there had been a prior relationship. While there really hasn’t been one, he had heard nothing but great things from Golden State head coach Steve Kerr and others, as both also share a connection, as Thompson’s brother, Mychel, went to the same high school as Spoelstra in Oregon. “To be honest, not really. But I know Coach Spo’s story. I know the respect he commands in the world of basketball is very high, and I mean, we’re from the same city, so I heard great things. You know, he went to Jesuit just like my brother did, and they got a lot of family friends who have known him for a long time, and nothing but great things have been said.” “And I know him and Steve Kerr worked together for a couple stands with Team USA, and Steve had nothing but great things to say,” Thompson continued. “And so do my friends who have played for the Miami Heat, and I know it’s a demanding atmosphere, and it’s one that’s really competitive, and that’s what attracted me to being here. So that’s something that I think reflects my mindset to a T. So that was an easy choice for me.” Klay Thompson on being on the #Heat and if he had a relationship with Erik Spoelstra before: “I know him and Steve Kerr worked together with Team USA and Steve had nothing but great things…I know it’s a demanding atmosphere and that’s what attracted me…” pic.twitter.com/GznrNeudFf — Zachary Weinberger (@ZachWeinberger) August 25, 2026 At any rate, it remains to be seen if Thompson has the same impact Allen did with the Heat, as there’s no doubt that he’ll get three-point opportunities with Antetokounmpo and Adebayo commanding the paint. articles.title: NFL players going back to college has Rams HC Sean McVay questioning reality

In 2026, at least for members of the
articles._body: Normally, when it doesn’t look like a rookie is going to make their team’s 53-man roster coming out of training camp, their agent will reach out to other teams like the Los Angeles Rams to see if they would like to sign them after clearing waivers. In 2026, at least for members of the 2022 recruiting class, the question has instead been: should they return to college for a fifth season of eligibility after the US Tenth Circuit Court of Appeals granted an injunction allowing a fifth year of eligibility, which has left Rams head coach Sean McVay in a bit of a, shall we say, head fog. Discussing the prospects of professional athletes going back to college for another season Old School style, McVay kept it brief but left the definitive piece of criticism on the subject, noting that the entire process has him feeling a certain type of way . “I feel like I took a freakin’ gummy,” McVay declared via LA Times’ Gary Klein. Now does the prospects of a player like, say Jack Pyburn, who had two sacks in his preseason debut for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, playing for a college program this fall instead of an NFL organization make about as much sense as buying blizzard insurance in Long Beach? Yes. Does having professional athletes who have already cashed NFL checks returning to college create enough additional questions to make Cheech and Chong’s heads spin? You betcha, but for the time being, that is the reality as both the NCAA and NFL seasons approach. Needless to say, how both leagues will handle this injunction will be fascinating. articles.title: Dolly Parton Was All Smiles & Jokes at Final Public Appearance, 2 Months Before She Died
articles.summary: The country star made a surprise appearance at the grand opening of Dolly's Tennessean Travel Stop in Cornersville, Tennessee.
articles._body: Dolly Parton ‘s final public appearance came just two months before her death at age 80. The country music icon, who died Tuesday (Aug. 25), was last seen publicly on June 24, when she made a surprise appearance at the grand opening of Dolly’s Tennessean Travel Stop in Cornersville, Tennessee. Related Dolly Parton’s Half-Century Hot 100 Legacy: ‘9 to 5,’ ‘Islands in the Stream’ & More Dolly Parton’s Life in Photos: From Smoky Mountain Girl to Queen of Country Music A Timeline of Dolly Parton’s Good Deeds Parton arrived at the new travel center in a whimsical blue-and-pink fringed outfit and took part in the ribbon-cutting ceremony, greeting the crowd gathered for the occasion. The appearance was a rare one for the superstar, who was staying out of the public eye during ongoing health complications. The June event also showcased the admirable sense of humor that had long been synonymous with Parton. While welcoming guests to the travel stop, she joked about competing chain Buc-ee’s, whose mascot is a beaver. “I couldn’t leave it to beavers,” she quipped. View this post on Instagram Parton’s appearance was exciting due to the uncertainty surrounding her health and professional plans. She announced in September 2025 that she was postponing her Las Vegas residency because of health issues. She eventually did cancel the full run in May 2026, explaining that she still had lots of healing to do before returning to the spotlight. She did, however, continue to work on the projects that had kept her busy throughout her career. In the days before her death, Parton spoke about her health while announcing plans surrounding her upcoming Broadway musical, Dolly: A True Original Musical , as well as a new museum in Nashville. She said at a time that she was still healing but remained determined to see her projects through. “I’m still workin’!” Parton said in an Aug. 21 statement to People , adding that she had “so many things” she still wanted to accomplish. Her June appearance at the Tennessee travel stop wasn’t her only public-facing moment of the year. Earlier in March, she attended the opening-day ceremony at Dollywood in Pigeon Forge, Tennessee, and she continued to connect with fans through videos and other appearances when she was unable to attend events in person. Parton’s health challenges followed an unfortunate and difficult period in her life, as her husband of nearly 60 years, Carl Dean, died in March 2025. Parton later acknowledged that she had neglected her own health while taking care of him. Despite those struggles, she continued to pursue music, business and other entertainment endeavors until the end of her life. Parton’s death was announced Tuesday by her newphew Bryan Seaver, who shared the news in an Instagram video . Seaver said the announcement was something Parton had asked him to make years earlier.

articles.title: Notebook: Chiles formally named QB1, OL still in flux, team names six captains
articles.summary: Head coach David Braun formally named Aidan Chiles as Northwestern's 2026 starting quarterback, named the team's six captains and addressed other fall camp developments as the Sept. 5 opener vs. South Dakota State draws nearer.
articles._body: EVANSTON-Head coach David Braun officially announced what was made public online yesterday when he named transfer Aidan Chiles his starting quarterback for the Sept. 5 season opener against South Dakota State. Chiles’ coronation marks the eighth straight season a transfer has gotten the nod at quarterback for the season opener. The last homegrown Wildcat to start the first game of the season was Clayton Thorson in 2018. Chiles had by far the best resume of Northwestern’s quarterbacks, room with more than 30 games played and more than 4,000 career passing yards after a season at Oregon State and the most recent two at Michigan State. While the decision came as no surprise, Braun and his staff still wanted to see a little bit more this fall before they gave Chiles the starting mantle. “You’re looking for a level of assertiveness, command and leadership,” Braun said. “I think Aidan did a remarkable job of relationship building when he first got here. It says it right up here on the wall, one of our core values is competition. We wanted there to be quarterback competition and whoever earned that position, we wanted to know it was competed for and earned. … “The thing that shows up in practice right now and on tape is his consistency. I think a lot of that comes from his comfort level as he’s gotten more ingrained into the system. Specifically over the last week, you’ve really seen things just start to click for him and there is a level of confidence when he steps in the huddle, like, ‘Hey, I’m the one driving this ship,’ and that’s what you need out of a quarterback.” For Chiles, this is confirmation of the work he has put in since he arrived in Evanston in the spring, and he is eager to move forward into the 2026 season in earnest. “It feels good to have it solidified and be ready to go,” Chiles said. “I’m no longer thinking about anything else but competing.” Linebacker Braydon Brus complimented Chiles. The fifth-year grad student is eager to finish the fall camp, where they’re competing against each other, and get to the part where they’re competing together. “Aidan is a stud both throwing the football and with his legs,” Brus said. “It’s really good, I think, to get a different look of having a really athletic quarterback and getting to go up against him, knowing that we’re going to be playing a lot of athletic quarterbacks this fall. “It’s been great and I think he’s really pushed our defense.” Offensive line is still under construction Even with a quarterback named, there is work still left to be done on the depth chart. Namely, the offensive line. Braun said that he is still tinkering with the unit with a little more than a week to go until the Wildcats take on the Jackrabbits at Martin Stadium. “I would say there’s still element of evaluation and competition, but that’s a good thing,” Braun said. He highlighted center Jackson Carsello , left guard Ezomo Oratokhai , and transfer tackle Grant Seagren as standouts, remarking that they had all played a lot of college football — though Seagren played his at Oklahoma State. Carsello and Oratokhai are sure bets to occupy the starting spots they did last season, but after that it gets murkier. Seagren played all 12 games last season at right tackle for the Cowboys, and also played 21 snaps of left tackle for Nebraska in 2024. Braun confirmed Seagren has been swinging back and forth throughout camp. “Grant certainly has the ability to play both, and he has played both,” Braun added. Those three names are all but guaranteed to fit into the starting lineup. Then Braun added another three names into the mix: graduate swing lineman Deuce McGuire , redshirt sophomore tackle Dennis Rahouski and redshirt sophomore guard Idrys Cotton . McGuire started two games at right tackle last season, playing 229 snaps on the season per PFF. Rahouski and Cotton have barely played: Rahouski got into two games last season, while Cotton appeared in just one. But both have battled their way into the mix this fall. Seagren will be one of the tackles, but on which side? Will Northwestern go to Rahouski at the other tackle spot and move McGuire back inside to guard? Will they keep McGuire at right tackle, flip Seagren to left and insert Cotton at guard? Or eschew the experienced McGuire and give both of the youngsters the green light? Braun plans to figure out their five by the end of this week. “That offensive line, that starting five, is something we plan on having solidified going into next week on Sunday,” he said. Mandatory Credit: Patrick Gorski-Imagn Images Northwestern brought in a couple of experienced transfers into their secondary with Montae Pate from Weber State and Brenden Deasfernandes from Central Michigan. However, based on Braun’s remarks, they seem to project as vital depth pieces, as Josh Fussell and Ore Adeyi return as the lead corners. “I would say that based on the level of experience in this system that Josh and Ore are the guys that we’re really going to lean on,” Braun said. “Montae Pate has done an incredible job. articles.title: Indie Latin Labels & Publishers Win $1.2 Million Court Judgment Over Illicit Catalog Distribution
articles.summary: A man was found liable for signing a distribution deal with Warner's ADA Latin for music he did not own.
articles._body: A group of independent Latin record labels and music publishers have been awarded $1.2 million in a lawsuit over the unauthorized distribution of their catalogs. An Aug. 16 judgment from Miami federal court, obtained by Billboard , finds musician Luigui Bleand (real name Luis Alfredo Silverio) and his companies liable for infringing 40 works owned by J&N Music Group, 829Music Mundial and Mayimba Music. These include tracks by the Dominican artists Ramón Torres, Grupo Aguakate and El Chaval de la Bachata. Related Bad Bunny Won’t Get $500K Legal Bill Repaid After Failed Lawsuit: ‘Would Send the Wrong Message’ Dale Morris, Nashville Manager Who Guided Careers of Alabama & Kenny Chesney, Dies at 89 HYBE Pledges Over $300k for Colombia Earthquake Recovery The labels and publishers sued Bleand in 2024, alleging he had falsely claimed to own their catalogs and entered a distribution agreement with Warner Music Group’s ADA Latin three years earlier. Relying on Bleand’s claims, ADA allegedly distributed the tracks to streamers including Spotify, Amazon and YouTube. ADA ultimately terminated Bleand’s distribution agreement upon learning he did not actually own the rights to this music. The Warner subsidiary was initially named as a defendant in the lawsuit brought by J&N, 829Music and Mayimba, but it quickly reached a confidential settlement and exited the case. Meanwhile, Bleand and his companies initially denied wrongdoing and hired lawyers to defend the claims. They reached a tentative settlement with the labels and publishers in 2025, but it later fell apart. Their attorneys then quit, and Bleand stopped responding to the litigation. This led Judge Darrin P. Gayles to issue the Aug. 16 judgment finding Bleand and his companies liable for copyright infringement. The judge awarded $30,000 in damages for each of the 40 infringed works for a total of $1.2 million. He also said Bleand should be on the hook for legal fees incurred by J&N, 829Music and Mayimba. “The undisputed facts establish that Silverio knew of Plaintiffs’ ownership interests when defendants began exploiting the works, knew that neither he nor the [companies] possessed a license or other authorization to distribute them, and nevertheless provided the works for distribution,” wrote Judge Gayles. In a joint statement on the decision, representatives for J&N, 829Music and Mayimba said, “Through this action and the court’s determination, Plaintiffs send a message to those in our industry who are gaming the system — indies or not, we will protect our rights to the fullest extent of the law.” Bleand and a representative for Warner Music Group did not immediately return requests for comment.

articles.title: Russell Simmons Recovers Celsius Drink Stock After Legal Battle Tied to Malaysian Bond Fraud
articles.summary: The Def Jam founder previously agreed he would use at least $8.6 million from the lucrative stock holdings to pay past-due settlements.
articles._body: Russell Simmons is getting access to valuable stock in the energy drink brand Celsius after a stranger-than-fiction legal saga that pitted the Def Jam founder against his ex-wife, her now-incarcerated second husband and the Department of Justice. Court papers docketed on Monday (Aug. 24) and first reported by Billboard say Simmons can recover some of the nearly 10 million Celius shares that are in DOJ possession as part of the federal prosecution of Tim Leissner , a former Goldman Sachs banker and the second husband of Simmons’ ex-wife, Kimora Lee Simmons . It’s not disclosed what percentage Simmons is receiving from these shares, which are currently worth more than $350 million in total. Related Chris Brown’s Ex-Housekeeper Can Take Cut of Tour Profits to Pay $13M Dog Attack Verdict, Judge Says Dale Morris, Nashville Manager Who Guided Careers of Alabama & Kenny Chesney, Dies at 89 HYBE Pledges Over $300k for Colombia Earthquake Recovery The filing says Simmons has promised to first use the Celsius stock to “pay certain of his creditors” before doing anything else with the money. Court records obtained by Billboard show that as of 2025, the record executive owed more than $11 million in past-due settlements to six women, some of whom have publicly accused him of sexual assault. He previously agreed to spend at least $8.6 million of the recovered Celsius shares satisfying these debts. The legal saga dates back to 2015, when Simmons, Lee Simmons and Leissner went in together on 3.3 million Celsius shares for a total of $3 million. The investment turned out to be quite shrewd; a Celsius stock split in 2023 tripled the amount of shares, and they’ve soared in value over the last decade. When the markets closed on Tuesday (Aug. 25), Celsius was trading at $35.40 per share. The trouble arose when Leissner was arrested on federal criminal charges in 2018 for helping orchestrate a massive Malaysian bond fraud known as the 1MDB scandal. He put the lucrative Celsius stock up for bail and ultimately forfeited the shares to pay off his financial penalties upon pleading guilty. This set off years of litigation between Simmons, Lee Simmons, Leissner, and the DOJ over the fate of the sum. Simmons alleged his ex-wife and her new husband had conspired to steal his 49% portion of the Celsius stock, claims they deny. Lee Simmons, meanwhile, said she remained entitled to nearly 900,000 Celsius shares she’d funded with money from her modeling career and fashion line. Meanwhile, Simmons became embroiled in his own controversy when numerous women accused him of sexual misconduct in a 2017 New York Times investigation and the 2020 HBO documentary On the Record . Simmons denies all wrongdoing, while many of these women have since hired attorneys to bring legal claims. Though Simmons is currently fighting some allegations in court, he largely avoided a litigation onslaught by signing numerous settlements in late 2023 and early 2024. He agreed to pay a total of $10.5 million to four women who publicly accused him of raping them in the 1980s and 1990s: Tonie Sallie, Tina Klein-Baker, Sheri Abernathy and Sil Lai Abrams, according to court filings. Court records also show that around the same time, Simmons agreed to pay two other women, Alexia Jones and Wendy Franco, a combined $800,000 in settlements for undisclosed claims. But the Def Jam founder never delivered the bulk of the promised payments; according to the filings, in 2025 he still owed more than $11 million in total to those six women. Last fall, as Simmons was hammering out a deal with the DOJ to recover a slice of the Celsius shares, he signed a series of new agreements with some of the claimants vowing to carve out a portion of the stock recovery to satisfy their debts. Specifically, four October agreements docketed in court allocated $5.7 million from the Celsius shares to Klein-Baker, $512,000 to Franco, and $1.2 million each to Abernathy and Abrams. It’s not clear whether Simmons signed similar follow-up agreements with Sallie or Jones. Reps for Simmons and the six claimants all either declined to comment or did not return inquiries as to whether or how much these women will now be paid. As for the rest of the Celsius shares not recovered by Simmons, Lee Simmons is also getting back an undisclosed amount of the stock per Monday’s DOJ filing. A longtime friend and investment partner of Leissner’s is getting another slice of shares, and the federal government will keep the rest as criminal forfeiture proceeds. Leissner, who is now serving a two-year prison sentence and in the midst of divorcing Lee Simmons, gets nothing.

articles.title: Show HN: Ecdeos – P2P Web/Native Distributed OS on Entity Core Protocol
articles.summary:
Hello, I wanted to share an update of the current progress of the Entity System.

https://ecdeos.org is one domain in a constellation of peers/sites that is the main project of the Entity System, a Tauri Rust/WASM browser engine and Rust backend bu
articles._body: Hello, I wanted to share an update of the current progress of the Entity System. https://ecdeos.org is one domain in a constellation of peers/sites that is the main project of the Entity System, a Tauri Rust/WASM browser engine and Rust backend built on the Entity Core Protocol. It's primarily a research prototype of a P2P distributed cross-platform userspace operating system. The long-term goal is functional P2P management of devices and applications, scaling from individual use (managing personal devices, apps and servers) to multi-user organizations with internal services/application stacks all the way to internet-scale public or federated P2P networks. Its closest parallels are Plan9, Erlang/BEAM, IPFS, ATProto, Nostr, as well as many other antecedent technologies including Git, HTTP, and other internet protocols. The particular combination of features and focus on "everything is an entity", content-addressed data, full decentralization, and its capability security model gives it a unique position in the landscape, most of it coming from the Entity Core Protocol itself. Each web deployment also ships with 30+ Entity-Apps including games, music (forgive me if the audio misbehaves, it's fully synthesized running on the main thread), art and basic tools. Entity-Apps have a basic contract with the host and run in isolated iframe sandboxes; they're currently written in Javascript using a custom engine. Also included are a few Entity-Native compute apps running as Rust WASM Entity Core peers in an iframe that show the transferable Entity System compute language running live on a cross platform generic system host interface the engine manages. The compute code is compiled/tested on a separate workbench Go project which operates a parallel implementation of the application conventions, generic system host interface and the Entity Core Protocol. The Tauri native backend peer includes support for SQLite storage, TCP and WebSockets, while the browser environment supports WebSockets and WebRTC P2P chat, file and entity transfer - with plans to add more storage, networking and application conventions. Sites and a registry example are hosted at https://entitychurchregistry.org . All the Ecdeos-based domains are running with peers in "coral reef" mode (no live peer required) and can pull the CDN hosted registry names and fetch the signed hosted sites from any other domain/peer in the network; they are cached locally in each peer's local storage afterwards. Peers can sign/host their data publicly on standard commodity hosting services and both the registry and sites are available to any application that understands the Entity Core Protocol and system extension standards. For the other example domains with peers hosted on static sites as well as more background information, see https://entitychurchfoundation.org , https://entitycoreprotocol.org , or https://billslab.com . Bills Lab is the research arm that is currently exploring the background technology from different perspectives. Almost all of the code and content is AI generated, but we do our best to make it some of the best slop available on the internet. The overall project is still early and needs to get stress tested but the design is holding up well so far. Let me know if you have any feedback. -Bill Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49440805 Points: 2 # Comments: 0

articles.title: UMusic Unveils Plans for Austin Hotel & Residential Community Built Around Live Music
articles.summary: The 71-acre project is slated to open in 2029 with 150 hotel rooms, 600 residences & a 10,000-seat amphitheater.
articles._body: All products and services featured are independently chosen by editors. However, Billboard may receive a commission on orders placed through its retail links, and the retailer may receive certain auditable data for accounting purposes. Austin has long been a city where music spills out of every corner, from legendary venues to neighborhood bars and local stages. Now, a new development aims to bring that culture into the foundation of a new hospitality and residential destination. UMusic Hospitality & Lifestyle has unveiled plans for UMusic Hotel & Private Residences Austin, a 71-acre property that will combine luxury accommodations, residences and live entertainment at the intersection of Southwest Parkway and Highway 71. The project will mark the second UMusic Hotel location, following the 2022 opening of the brand’s first property in Madrid, Spain. Unlike the Madrid location, the Austin development will introduce private residences alongside its hotel and entertainment offerings. The project’s centerpiece will be White Rocks Amphitheater , a 10,000-seat outdoor venue designed to host concerts and cultural events. The development will also include 150 hotel rooms, 600 private residences, recording and content creation studios, an indoor event venue with a capacity of 1,500, a comedy club, dining options, wellness and longevity facilities and entertainment spaces. Construction is expected to begin in the first quarter of 2027, with the first phase projected for delivery in early 2029 and additional phases continuing through 2032. Residences are currently available, with The Preserve I starting at ~$760,000 and Private Residences starting from approximately $1.6M. “Our vision is to create places where culture is made, shared, and celebrated. Launching UMusic Hotel & Private Residences Austin through storytelling rather than convention is a natural extension of that philosophy, “said Jordi Solé, President of UMusic Hospitality & Lifestyle.“ This property combines performance, wellness, nature, and community into a single living ecosystem, reflecting Austin’s creative spirit on a global stage.” Beyond music, the property will feature two fine dining restaurants, three bars, an on-site distillery and tasting room, a private members club, underground comedy club, resort-style pools and spa services, and a large Las Vegas-style beach club. The development was introduced at an exclusive launch event on April 23, 2026, featuring performances from Lyle Lovett and Asleep at the Wheel. Developers say the project will also support the local creative community through artist programming, partnerships and funding initiatives. This ongoing commitment is further solidified by a newly announced endowment, a first-of-its-kind funding model designed to provide permanent support for Austin’s arts and nonprofit organizations. The project also recently announced the White Rocks Collab, an artist development and performance venue which will be a permanent downtown addition to the main White Rocks project. The Collab will provide artists creative and career development support and a live performance space.
