articles.title: 49ers’ Jed York did not pay his court fees, so who did?
articles.summary: The San Francisco 49ers have generated some headlines for all the wrong reasons this week when team owner Jed York was arrested in Ohio for engaging in prostitution. York has since pleaded no contest and has been sentenced to two days in jail, in addition to owing thousands in court fees. Recentl
articles._body: The San Francisco 49ers have generated some headlines for all the wrong reasons this week when team owner Jed York was arrested in Ohio for engaging in prostitution. York has since pleaded no contest and has been sentenced to two days in jail, in addition to owing thousands in court fees. Recently, it was revealed by TMZ that “…it looks like the San Francisco 49ers’ Chief Security Officer paid his boss’ court fees. According to online records, someone named “D Cory” paid Jed’s fees after he pleaded no contest to a couple of misdemeanors in Ohio.” The publication also noted that “‘D Cory’ appears to be Dan Cory … the CEO of Nickel Group, a security and risk management firm that protects San Francisco 49ers executives and team members.” It’s certainly been a bizarre turn of events for the 49ers and an unwanted distraction with less than three weeks to go until the new season gets underway. York isn’t the first NFL owner to have been accused of engaging in such behavior, as New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft was arrested in 2019 for soliciting a prostitute, although that case ended up being dismissed after evidence was thrown out. At this point, it remains to be seen what kind of discipline the NFL might bring down on York, in addition to the punishments he has dealt with in the legal system. York himself has yet to speak on the matter. In any case, the 49ers will look to keep their attention on the football field as the team gears up to kick off its regular season on September 10 with a game against the divisional rival Los Angeles Rams in Australia. articles.title: Dolly Parton’s Top Billboard Hot Country Songs Hits
articles.summary: The icon's biggest Billboard Hot Country Songs hits, from enduring solo songs to collaborations with artists including Kenny Rogers.
articles._body: Dolly Parton , a member of both the Country Music Hall of Fame and the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame, crafted hits for more than six decades, starting with her 1959 debut single, “Puppy Love.” When the country icon died at the age of 80 on Tuesday (Aug. 25), she left behind one of the most substantial, beloved and influential catalogs in music history. Over the years, her recordings have lit up Billboard ‘s charts in a variety of genres — namely country, naturally, but also bluegrass, CCM and rock. And of course, it was the East Tennessee native who brought to life “I Will Always Love You,” which she had a country hit with as a solo artist (twice — once solo and once and as a duet with Vince Gill), while Whitney Houston’s soaring, soul-stirring version became an enduring pop classic. As a recording artist, Parton lobbed tender ballads and jaunty uptempo tracks to the top of the charts, with solo performances as well as enduring collaborations with artists including Kenny Rogers, Billy Ray Cyrus and both Linda Ronstadt and Emmylou Harris (via her work on the acclaimed Trio albums). In 2023, following her induction into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame, she turned her love of music toward rock classics with her album Rockstar , working with legends including Paul McCartney and Elton John. Through the decades, Parton always made country music her musical heartbeat and homebase. Below, we count down Parton’s biggest Billboard hits on the Hot Country Songs chart. Dolly Parton’s Biggest Billboard Hits chart is based on actual performance on the weekly Hot Country Songs chart through Aug. 29, 2026. Songs are ranked based on an inverse point system, with weeks at No. 1 earning the greatest value and weeks at lower ranks earning less. Due to changes in chart methodology over the years, eras are weighted to account for different chart turnover rates over various periods.

articles.title: Google's anti-nausea Motion Assist dots finally rolling out on Android
articles.summary: It's currently only appearing on Pixels running Android 17.
articles._body: Some people are cursed with motion sickness, which can make it impossible to read or use a phone in a moving vehicle without suffering waves of nausea. There's a surprisingly simple trick that can make smartphones usable in such situations. Apple deployed it on the iPhone a couple of years ago, and now Google's own version is finally coming (slowly) to Android. Motion sickness is caused by a disagreement between what your inner ear senses and what your eyes see. If you're looking at a book or a screen while in a car, the sensory mismatch can lead to a pretty unpleasant time. As part of iOS 18 in 2024, Apple released a feature called Motion Cues that places a network of moving dots on the screen to alleviate motion sickness, and it seems to work surprisingly well. Google's version is similar, but it's called Motion Assist. Google began testing Motion Assist back in 2024, but it never expanded beyond an internal test until now. Android Authority reports Motion Assist is appearing on Pixel phones running Android 17, but there's no app or update you can install to get the feature—it's being delivered by Play Services as part of a staged rollout. articles.title: Bryce Underwood in Friday’s scrimmage: ‘It was clean … efficient football’
articles.summary: Michigan quarterback Bryce Underwood continues to improve ...
articles._body: By all accounts, Michigan sophomore quarterback Bryce Underwood played well last week, especially Wednesday in practice and then in Friday’s scrimmage. Quarterbacks coach Koy Detmer challenged him in May to put in the time, and Underwood responded — and then some. Our spotters said the sophomore had a 60-yard strike to Andrew Marsh along with a few other nice completions to his classmate, along with several other good throws. “It was clean,” Detmer shared Tuesday. “That’s always what I ask of our guys is just staying on schedule, playing efficient football, being clean with the football. He was able to start off with a really nice drive there [of 16 plays for a touchdown]. “We go punch it in, and we converted on a couple of third downs, critical downs where we’re going to need to be good this year to help ourselves, move the ball and score points. It was good to see that … him being able to stand in the pocket, deliver the ball to our receivers, and make some real big plays on third and fourth down. ” Back in spring, Detmer continued, everyone knew there were more ups and downs than they would have preferred from day to day. Offensive coordinator Jason Beck said recently the work Underwood put in during the offseason showed, noting he’d had “13 good practices” after No. 13. “Over summer, just to really put in the extra work, both with his footwork, pocket presence, and different things of that nature … to his credit, man, he hit it,” Detmer said. “He hit it head on and worked his tail off, got a lot of really good work in May, really good work in the summer, and was able to carry that into camp. “I’d say the biggest thing that I’ve noticed, over these last couple of weeks is just his comfortability. In the pocket, in the system … it was a new system, and we threw everything at him. To his credit, he took all that knowledge in at a really fast pace and did a really good job with it.” It looked slower for him and he was much more comfortable with his feet and pocket presence, Detmer added, noting, “I feel like he is in a really good spot and has done a good job. It’s been a challenge for the cornerbacks, too, assistant Jernaro Gilford said. His group has been charged with trying to slow a rapidly improving talent. “Night and day from spring to now, man,” Gilford said of Underwood. “Starting in fall camp, he’s made so many amazing throws … wild throws that had us in awe.  He’s doing stuff like that. “He’s going to be all right. Knowing what our defense does to opposing quarterbacks, to see him make certain throws against us makes us pretty, pretty confident in that young man. ”

articles.summary: Vanderbilt football has been holding a quarterback competition in an effort to find a replacement for Diego Pavia. Vanderbilt landed on Blaze Berlowitz as their starting quarterback for Week 1 against Austin Peay, as he beat out 5-star recruit Jared Curtis for the job. Berlowitz sat behind Pavia
articles._body: Vanderbilt football has been holding a quarterback competition in an effort to find a replacement for Diego Pavia. Vanderbilt landed on Blaze Berlowitz as their starting quarterback for Week 1 against Austin Peay , as he beat out 5-star recruit Jared Curtis for the job. Berlowitz sat behind Pavia for three years, one at New Mexico State and two at Vanderbilt. Now, Pavia is praising the decision to roll with his understudy to start the 2026 campaign, posting on social media. “WELL EARNED- been watching this king from the start of time at NM STATE when he took over in the championship game at 18 years old and BALLED- yall better stand down this man the truth!” Pavia posted on X, formerly Twitter. Berlowitz committed to New Mexico State out of Oklahoma to continue his football career. He used his redshirt season that year, but did play in one game. He started the Conference-USA Championship game against Liberty in place of an injured Pavia. While Pavia said he “balled,” he was not amazing in the contest. Berlowitz completed ten of 19 passes for 134 yards with a touchdown and an interception. He also ran four times for 36 yards. The relationship between Berlowitz, the coaching staff, and Pavia was clearly strong, though. After the 2023 season, Jerry Kill, the New Mexico State head coach, took a consultant role with Vanderbilt. Tim Beck, the offensive coordinator, then took a job as the OC at Vanderbilt. Both Pavia and Berlowitz would join them. Berlowitz sat the entire 2024 season behind Pavia, not seeing any action. He would see action in 2025, appearing in six games, mostly in mop-up duty. He completed nine of 17 passes for 131 yards with a touchdown. The quarterback also ran for 81 yards and another score. Vanderbilt opens their season on September 5 against Austin Peay. The conference features everything from established stars and Heisman Trophy contenders to highly touted newcomers preparing for their first opportunities as starters. With that in mind, Athlo
articles._body: Quarterback play could ultimately determine whether the SEC returns to the top of college football in 2026. The conference features everything from established stars and Heisman Trophy contenders to highly touted newcomers preparing for their first opportunities as starters. With that in mind, Athlon Sports’ Steve Lassan ranked all 16 starting quarterback situations in the SEC ahead of the new season, factoring in talent, their supporting cast, previous production and projections for 2026. Players like Texas’ Arch Manning and Ole Miss’ Trinidad Chambliss are strong contenders in a loaded group after last season. Elsewhere, Georgia , LSU and South Carolina also have proven options, while Alabama is betting on the enormous upside of Keelon Russell . articles.title: Astros manager Joe Espada’s job security is ‘in trouble,’ but he’s not guaranteed to be fired
articles.summary: The Houston Astros and general manager Dana Brown recently agreed to part ways. A recent report suggested that manager Joe Espada could also end up out of the organization following the season. However, that is reportedly not guaranteed to occur. “Not from what our reporter Chandler Rome un
articles._body: The Houston Astros and general manager Dana Brown recently agreed to part ways . A recent report suggested that manager Joe Espada could also end up out of the organization following the season. However, that is reportedly not guaranteed to occur. “Not from what our reporter Chandler Rome understands,” Ken Rosenthal of The Athletic said during an appearance on Foul Territory in reference to the aforementioned report about Espada. “The Astros vehemently denied that, it was a report from Bob Nightengale yesterday. Joe Espada, if he was in that position, he certainly has not acknowledged it. I don’t want to dump on anybody’s report, but this was denied.” However, Espada’s job security with the Astros is indeed in a difficult position. “Now, is Joe Espada in trouble? By definition he is in trouble,” Rosenthal continued. “One, because he’s in the last year of his contract. Two, because the guy who hired him just got fired. So, put those two things together and the fact that this team, I don’t know if it’s fair to say that they have underachieved because a lot of what Dana Brown did did not work out… That’s on the GM, not the manager. “Perhaps that’s why the GM was fired when he was. But Joe Espada, at the very least, will have to deal with a new GM above him, and that always is perilous for a manager.” The Astros have not performed especially well but they are still near the top of the American League West standings. Espada can potentially help his job security by leading Houston to the postseason. articles.title: Dolly Parton’s 25 Best Songs: Critics’ Picks
articles.summary: The Queen of Country's best solo songs, from "9 to 5" to "Jolene."
articles._body: Following the release of her 1967 debut solo album, Hello, I’m Dolly , Dolly Parton spent nearly 60 years changing the face of the entertainment industry. Kicking down doors for female performers in both country and pop music, she soared in the worlds of books, television, philanthropy and movies — and pretty much whatever else she tackled. Sadly, Parton died at age 80 on Tuesday (Aug. 25), bringing the nation to a near-standstill as tributes to the beloved artist and entertainer poured in from all across the worlds of music, film, culture and beyond. Parton’s expansive roster of hits — including two No. 1s on the Billboard Hot 100 and a whopping 25 on Billboard ‘s Hot Country Songs chart — reads like a “best of” list of the 1970s and 1980s, and it remains one of the strongest song catalogs of any singer-songwriter in any genre. As a writer, she has penned everything from poignant, detailed ballads about life in the Great Smoky Mountains, where she grew up, to some of the most defining love songs of all time. Her prowess as a songwriter and performer is so great, it earned her a historic induction into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame in 2022 — an accomplishment she almost didn’t accept, telling Billboard at the time that she didn’t feel like she “measured up” to past inductees. A legacy like hers, however, deserves the title of “rock star” no matter what style of music she makes, and the world agreed. She went on to become the second female country artist (after Brenda Lee) to be inducted in both the Rock & Roll and Country Music Halls of Fame. (Parton has also been inducted into the Songwriters Hall of Fame.) “People usually [say] ‘Dolly rocks’ or ‘you rock’ or ‘you’re a rock star,’” she said. “I thought they just meant that I was cool, and I took that as a great compliment. But now I’m going to have to take it literally!” In choosing our favorite Dolly Parton songs, we settled on these 25. Many of them came from her own pen, and all of them will “Always” have staying power. To be fair, we could do a list of our favorite Dolly duets, too, but wanted to keep this one solo-focused. Keep reading to see the best songs from Dolly Parton’s beyond-legendary six-decade career below. [Ed. note: A shorter version of this list was published prior to Billboard writer Chuck Dauphin’s passing in 2019.]

articles.title: Lil Durk Murder Trial, ‘KPop Demon Hunters’ Lawsuit, Bad Bunny Ruling & More Top Music Law News
articles.summary: In this week's Legal Beat newsletter, Lil Durk's day in court, a "Demon Hunters" trademark fight, Bad Bunny's big legal bill and much more.
articles._body: THE BIG STORY: Two years after he was indicted on murder-for-hire charges, Lil Durk finally went to trial in a Los Angeles federal courtroom — where prosecutors told jurors that the rapper put out a hit on rival Quando Rondo after becoming “consumed with revenge.” The once-rising Chicago drill rapper stands accused of ordering members of his Only the Family (OTF) label crew to kill rival Rondo in retaliation for the 2020 killing of his close friend and collaborator King Von . Rondo was shot at a Los Angeles gas station in 2022 and survived, but another man known as Lul Pab was killed in the crossfire. Related Lil Durk Is Going to Trial on Murder-for-Hire Charges. Here’s What to Know About the Case Dale Morris, Nashville Manager Who Guided Careers of Alabama & Kenny Chesney, Dies at 89 HYBE Pledges Over $300k for Colombia Earthquake Recovery In opening statements, Durk’s defense strategy quickly emerged: To pin the murder on co-defendant Kavon “Vonnie” Grant. They said Grant had access to Durk’s credit cards and had framed him once he was caught: “He thought, ‘Oh man, I’ve got an insurance policy,’” Durk’s attorney told the jury. “I’ve got a big fish I can give them.” For more, go read Billboard ’s explainer on the case and full coverage of the first day — which also featured argument over prosecutor’s controversial decision to use Durk’s rap lyrics as evidence. And stick with Billboard for updates as the trial moves ahead. You’re reading The Legal Beat , a weekly newsletter about music law from Billboard Pro , offering you a one-stop cheat sheet of big new cases, important rulings and all the fun stuff in between. To get the newsletter in your inbox every Tuesday, subscribe here . Other top stories this week… -Netflix was hit with a trademark lawsuit over the massively successful KPop Demon Hunters , filed by a Christian metal band that’s used the name Demon Hunter for decades. – Bad Bunny won’t be repaid the $500,000 he spent beating a copyright lawsuit over a sample on Un Verano Sin Ti after a judge ruled that such a penalty was unwarranted and “would send the wrong message.” -A settlement was reached in a lawsuit filed over Rihanna ’s Smurfs movie song, a case that claimed Paramount never paid a songwriter for writing it because it was “mad” at the star for budget overruns. -A California appeals court ruled that a woman who was scammed out of more than $300,000 by a Kenny Chesney impersonator can’t sue the country superstar . – Ariana Grande won a court order allowing her to subpoena online platforms so that she can unmask the identities of hackers who she says have leaked her unreleased content. -Sony Music filed a copyright case against Kroger claiming it illegally used songs by Harry Styles , SZA and other stars in TikTok and Instagram posts — the latest in a flood of such cases. -A judge ruled Chris Brown must fork over money from his R&B Tour concerts with Usher to an ex-housekeeper who won a $13 million verdict after she was mauled by the singer’s dog. -Robert Clivillés, one of the co-founders of C+C Music Factory, sued rapper Freedom Williams over control of the 1990s dance group’s name. -The first week of the Tupac Shakur murder trial wrapped up after heated testimony and infamous recordings in which defendant Duane “Keffe D” Davis candidly discussed the shooting. – Lady Gaga won a court ruling dismissing a lawsuit that claimed her Mayhem album infringed the trademarks of a surf company that sells a brand of Mayhem surfboards. – FKA Twigs defeated trademark infringement claims over her stage name, with a judge ruling that an indie band named The Twigs forfeited its right to sue due to years of inaction. -A judge refused to dismiss a copyright lawsuit filed against T.I. by hip-hop producer Sir Jinx over his work on the 2016 Dr. Dre collaboration “Dope.” – Elton John and other celebs were ordered to repay a £9.54 million ($13 million) legal bill following the loss of their U.K. hacking lawsuit against the Daily Mail. -A California appeals court seemed inclined to affirm the dismissal of Jay-Z ’s extortion and defamation lawsuit against personal injury attorney Tony Buzbee. – Los Lobos reached a settlement with Sony Music to end a lawsuit royalties for “Canción del Mariachi,” the band’s collaboration with Antonio Banderas from the 1995 Western Desperado .

articles.title: Raleigh Music Publishing Forms Joint Venture With ICM Crescendo Music Royalty Fund
articles.summary: The new venture will see Raleigh administering catalogs acquired by ICM Crescendo Music Royalty Fund.
articles._body: Raleigh Music Publishing and ICM Crescendo Music Royalty Fund have formed a joint venture to acquire music publishing catalogs. Under the terms of the joint venture, ICM Crescendo will commit dedicated acquisition capital to music publishing catalogs sourced and administered by Raleigh. As part of the deal, Raleigh Music Publishing will gain an equity stake in the acquisitions through its catalog administration role in the joint venture. Related The 13 Biggest Music Business Deals of 2026 So Far Dale Morris, Nashville Manager Who Guided Careers of Alabama & Kenny Chesney, Dies at 89 HYBE Pledges Over $300k for Colombia Earthquake Recovery The two companies first joined forces when acquiring the Kal Mann catalog, which included hits such as Chubby Checkers’ “Let’s Twist Again” and a sample share in House of Pain’s “Jump Around.” According to the announcement, the partnership combines “Raleigh Music’s deep operational expertise and long-standing relations with ICM Crescendo’s music copyright expertise, investment infrastructure and deep pockets.” The companies say they expect to announce multiple transactions in the near term, drawing on a pipeline of opportunities developed by Raleigh through its relationships with catalog owners, artist estates and music rights holders.   Raleigh Music is led by co-president Peter Raleigh , who previously led the copyright teams at Cherry Lane and Imagem Music Publishing U.S.; and co-president Steven Storch , who spent 21 years at Sony Music Publishing and had been the company’s CFO before moving onto Imagem. Raleigh Music’s holdings already include the published works of Elvis Presley — among them “Can’t Help Falling in Love,” “All Shook Up,” “A Little Less Conversation” and “Don’t Be Cruel” — as well as the George Gershwin catalog including “Summertime” and “Rhapsody in Blue”; the Alan J. Lerner catalog, encompassing standards from “My Fair Lady,” “Brigadoon” and “Gigi”; and the Tokens’ “The Lion Sleeps Tonight” and Tony Bennett’s “Blue Velvet.” “The American Songbook and the great songs of the 1950s and 1960s represent some of the most enduring creative achievement in our culture,” Raleigh said in a statement. “At Raleigh, we see ourselves first and foremost as stewards of that legacy. The families and heirs who entrust their songs to us do so because they know we genuinely love this music and will protect its copyrights, its integrity and its place in the world for generations to come. This partnership with ICM Crescendo allows us to extend that commitment to more of these extraordinary catalogs and to ensure that the songs that shaped American music continue to be heard, valued and cared for.” ICM Crescendo Music Royalty Fund already owns 6,500 songs across more than 50 catalogs representing over 500 artists and is managed by ICM Asset Management, which describes itself as a Canadian alternative investment manager with more than $2 billion in assets. ICM Crescendo Music Royalty Fund’s website says its holdings include songs performed by Taylor Swift; the ownership of a catalogue of songs by Anuel AA, including “Sola (Remix)”; and “Nachos Pa Morir”; and the copyright and royalty interests in Lauren Daigle’s Grammy-award-winning, platinum-certified album, Look Up Child . Past announcements by the company include the acquisition of Adrian Belew’s publishing and PRO rights; and the Rebel Made publishing catalog, which includes A$AP Rocky’s “L$D,” Kelly Rowland’s “Motivation” and Usher’s “There Goes My Baby.” “At ICM, we seek to partner with experienced operators who bring deep industry expertise and access to differentiated opportunities,” ICM Asset Management president and portfolio manager David Vankka said in a statement. “Raleigh has built an impressive track record of sourcing, acquiring and managing high-quality catalogs, making them a natural partner as we continue to grow our presence in the music royalties asset class. We look forward to building our existing relationship and pursuing additional opportunities together.” Storch said, “We are extremely excited to partner with David Vankka and the ICM team who, like Raleigh, understand and appreciate classic song catalogs. Partnering with ICM Crescendo gives us the capital to move decisively when… opportunities arise.”Partnering with ICM Crescendo gives us the capital to move decisively when… opportunities arise.”

articles.title: Lane Kiffin defends LSU football signing ex-NFL players with wild spin
articles.summary: Recently, the LSU football program has been at the center of attention when Dae’Quan Wright opted to return to the program despite having been a member of multiple NFL teams during training camp. The move has reignited debate about how strict college eligibility requirements should or shoul
articles._body: Recently, the LSU football program has been at the center of attention when Dae’Quan Wright opted to return to the program despite having been a member of multiple NFL teams during training camp. The move has reignited debate about how strict college eligibility requirements should or shouldn’t be as the lines between ameteur and professional continue to blur. Recently, newly minted LSU football head coach Lane Kiffin stopped by ESPN’s The Pat McAfee Show to give his two cents on the debate. “I don’t think professionals should come back to college sports and college football particularly.. This isn’t professionals who have gone and played seasons or just randomly filed an injunction in a state to become eligible,” said Kiffin, per Pat McAfee on X, formerly Twitter. As Kiffin referenced, Wright, and other players who have followed a similar path, have not actually played games at the NFL level, but some fans still feel that the fact that they were on training camp rosters and competing in professional practices should be enough to disqualify them from returning to school. With NIL money and the transfer portal both becoming major hot topics in the college football world in recent years, it was seemingly only a matter of time until this kind of story started to emerge, and the Tigers are more than happy to be the beneficiaries of Wright’s return to school. Kiffin is looking to justify his controversial decision to leave Ole Miss for LSU last season when he and the Tigers take the field in 2026, beginning on September 5 with a marquee home game against the Clemson Tigers. articles.title: Tonopah Valley (Ariz.) football program’s 2026 season suspended
articles.summary: According to an announcement by Saddle Mountain USD Superintendent Dr. Mike Winters on Tuesday, Tonopah Valley High School (Ariz.) will not be playing football until further notice. Winters announced that the upcoming varsity matchup pitting the Phoenix versus Scottsdale Christian Academy (Ariz.) is
articles._body: According to an announcement by Saddle Mountain USD Superintendent Dr. Mike Winters on Tuesday, Tonopah Valley High School (Ariz.) will not be playing football until further notice. Winters announced that the upcoming varsity matchup pitting the Phoenix versus Scottsdale Christian Academy (Ariz.) is canceled and the 2026 season is currently suspended. [ $19.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage ] In the letter penned to parents and families of the Saddle Mountain USD, Winters said a “potentially serious incident involving faculty members and members of the high school football team,” which led to the decision to pause the Tonopah Valley football program, varsity and JV, until the investigation concludes. There is no timeline on when the investigation will end, per the letter. ‘The safety and well-being of every student remain the highest priorities of the Saddle Mountain Unified School District. Late Friday afternoon, the District received a report concerning a potentially serious incident involving faculty members and members of the high school football team. Given the seriousness of the allegations, I immediately canceled Friday’s Varsity game and initiated a thorough investigation to ensure all facts were carefully reviewed. The JV game was subsequently canceled earlier today. Over the weekend, I consulted with the Governing Board and continued gathering information regarding the matter. As a result, certain faculty members have been placed on administrative leave pending further investigation. The District also initiated contact with local law enforcement and is cooperating fully with its investigation. We understand that cancelling a football game affects our students, families, coaches, and community. However, the safety and protection of our students must always come before athletics or any other consideration; therefore, Varsity and JV football is suspended until further notice. Because this matter involves an active investigation and concerns students and personnel, there are limits to what the District can share at this time. Nevertheless, we remain committed to transparency and will provide additional information as circumstances allow and as it is appropriate to do so. We appreciate the patience and understanding of our students, families, staff, and community as this process continues. If you have questions or would like to discuss this matter, please contact me directly. Thank you Our commitment is clear: the safety, well-being, and protection of our students will always come first.’ Tonopah Valley is coming off a 2025 season where the Phoenix went 2-5 and entered this fall as the state’s No. 161st ranked team, according to the Arizona 2026 High School Football Massey Rankings. More about Tonopah Valley High School “Tonopah Valley High School, located in Tonopah, AZ, is committed to providing a rigorous and well-rounded education to its students. The school offers a variety of academic and extracurricular opportunities, with a strong focus on community involvement, athletics, and personal growth. With dedicated faculty and a supportive environment, Tonopah Valley helps students prepare for success beyond high school. The Phoenix mascot symbolizes resilience and transformation, embodying the spirit of the school.”

articles.title: Data Center Developer Increases Land Holdings at Briscoe County Site
articles.summary: Soluna Holdings, a developer of green data centers for intensive computing applications, including AI and Bitcoin mining, closed the purchase of 397 acres in Briscoe County, Texas. The land will host Pr
articles._body: Soluna Holdings, a developer of green data centers for intensive computing applications, including AI and Bitcoin mining, closed the purchase of 397 acres in Briscoe County, Texas. The land will host Project Dorothy 3, Soluna’s planned renewable-first AI computing campus with a potential capacity of up to 300 MW. Briscoe County is between Amarillo and Lubbock. The parcel sits adjacent to Projects Dorothy 1 and 2 and to the 150 MW Briscoe Wind Farm, which Soluna acquired in April. The Briscoe Wind Farm’s Substation sits directly across from the acquired property, positioning Dorothy 3 for direct, behind-the-meter access to generation the Company owns outright.  The 397 acres exceed the 300 acres Soluna originally identified for the campus. The additional land gives the Company room to add data halls should further generation or storage capacity become available at the site.  Project Dorothy 3 is part of Soluna’s development pipeline of approximately 6.3 GW across multiple sites. Soluna currently operates approximately 192 MW of energized capacity.  The post Data Center Developer Increases Land Holdings at Briscoe County Site appeared first on Connect CRE .

articles.title: Packers’ O-line ranking on RotoWire a cause for concern for 2026 season
articles.summary: The Green Bay Packers have been up and down so far during training camp and the preseason, giving fans things to be both excited and discouraged by as the new season approaches. One area of concern for the Packers heading into the 2026 campaign is the offensive line, which the team didn’t d
articles._body: The Green Bay Packers have been up and down so far during training camp and the preseason , giving fans things to be both excited and discouraged by as the new season approaches. One area of concern for the Packers heading into the 2026 campaign is the offensive line, which the team didn’t do much to upgrade over the course of this offseason. Now, Ian Hartitz of Rotowire has revealed on X, formerly Twitter, that the Packers have the 30th, or third-to-last, ranked offensive line unit in the league this year according to the publication, with only the Cleveland Browns and Tennessee Titans being worse. Directly ahead of the Packers are the Carolina Panthers and the Jacksonville Jaguars. The Packers will certainly want the offensive line to perform better than that ranking would indicate this year in order to help keep star quarterback Jordan Love upright this season. Love has dealt with numerous injury absences throughout the course of his career, and now that he no longer has the reliable Malik Willis backing him up, it will be even more important for the offensive line to give him time in the pocket and keep him on his feet. The good news for the Packers is that they are among the most talented teams in the NFL in various other positional departments. Green Bay is looking to bounce back after two straight ugly Wild Card exits over the last couple of seasons, with the pressure threatening to heat up on head coach Matt LaFleur if the team can’t scrape together a better result this time around. The Packers are slated to kick off their regular season on September 13 with a divisional road game against the Minnesota Vikings. The announcement was made by her family on Instagram on Tuesday, Aug. 25. It was clearly emotional, as her nephew, Brin Seaver, shared the tragic news. He called it an “honor” to make the announcement. He had been the country music star’s head of security for years before her death. View this post on Instagram “My name is Brin Seaver, son of Cassie Parton, and I’m representing the Parton and Owens family today announcing the passing of my aunt, Dolly Rebecca Parton Dean, Sister, Sis, and Granny to one generation and Gigi to the next,” he said. “This video announcement is something Dolly asked of me years ago, before I fully absorbed it as a future reality. “As her head of security for more than two decades, a role my father Larry held before me, I have imagined the heaviness of this moment but haven’t truly felt it until now,” he continued. Dolly Parton’s iconic career before her death Scott Utterback/Courier Journal / USA TODAY NETWORK. Before her tragic passing, Parton was a country music icon. From Dallas Cowboys halftime shows to hit albums, she did it all throughout her career. She started performing at a young age, and she released her debut studio album, Hello, I’m Dolly, in 1967. Parton released countless albums throughout her career and won 10 Grammys out of 55 nominations. Her last album, Rockstar, was released in 2023. The album consisted of various rock covers with collaborations with the likes of Paul McCartney, Ringo Starr, Peter Frampton, Mick Fleetwood, Stevie Nicks, Elton John, Miley Cyrus, John Fogerty, and more. In addition to her music career, she acted in several projects. Parton starred in the likes of 9 to 5, Rhinestone, Straight Talk, Gnomeo & Juliet, and Joyful Noise. articles._body: As the new season approaches, the pass-rushing arms race is heating up. After several teams added veteran sack artists to their roster as Week 1 nears, there are now rumors that Haason Reddick could be the next edge rusher to find a home ahead of the 2026 season. “Sources: 2x Pro Bowl OLB Haason Reddick has become the latest veteran pass-rusher drawing interest from teams after recent signings, including Von Miller to Dallas, Za’Darius Smith to Atlanta, and Derek Barnett to Cleveland,” NFL insider Jordan Schult reported Tuesday. “The 31-year-old Reddick has 61.5 career sacks and spent last season in Tampa Bay.” Reddick was last a Pro Bowl player in 2023, and over the course of the last two seasons, he’s produced just 3.5 sacks. However, he is younger than Miller (38) and Smith (34 in Week 1), so he may have more gas left in the tank as a situational pass-rush specialist. As for the most likely Haason Reddick landing spot for the 2026 season, that’s hard to say, and the self-proclaimed “insider” Schultz stopped short of actually naming any teams that may be interested. The Philadlephia Eagles remain the most likely choice , and Jonathan Greenard is dealing with injuries, and Reddick is a familiar face. The pass-rusher played for The Birds in 2022 and 2023, posting the best seasons of his career. He had 27.0 sacks there and had made his two Pro Bowls while in Philly. If Schultz’s “sources” are right, and there are multiple teams interested, it may be with franchises like the New England Patriots, Minnesota Vikings, or Atlanta Falcons. articles.title: Dolly Parton, One of Country Music’s Biggest & Brightest Icons, Dies at 80
articles.summary: Parton was one of the most influential songwriters to hit Nashville -- or the world
articles._body: Dolly Parton , the extraordinarily versatile singer and songwriter who built up her artistic credibility and commercial fortunes in both country and pop music over more than half a century, died in Nashville on Tuesday (Aug. 25) at the age of 80. Parton had been mostly out of the public eye for the past year following a struggle with unspecified health issues that forced the “9 to 5” singer/songwriter to curtail public appearances and postpone, then cancel her planned 2025 Las Vegas residency. Her death came 17 months after the passing of her husband of nearly 60 years, Carl Dean, who died on March 3, 2025 at age 82. “At Dolly’s request, a small, private service will be held for immediate family,” read a press release announcing the awful news. “Dolly’s fans and friends from around the world are encouraged to pay tribute to Dolly on social media by tagging @DollyParton or by leaving a message at www.dollyparton.com. In lieu of flowers the family asks for donations to be made to Dolly Parton’s Imagination Library at www.imaginationlibrary.com.” Her nephew, Bryan Seaver, shared a message on Instagram after her passing. View this post on Instagram “The magic with me,” Parton liked to say, “is that I look completely false when I’m completely real.” She was famous for her wall of self-conscious artifice — she modeled her done-to-the-nines appearance on a prostitute in her hometown, and she always had a self-teasing quip at the ready. But she was also a magnificent singer, with an aching soprano trill that never left her, and a virtuosic songwriter whose work was adopted by artists from Whitney Houston (“I Will Always Love You”) to the White Stripes (“Jolene”). Parton, who Billboard editors named the top country artist of all time in 2024,  was a cultural and commercial force. She landed 49 albums in the top 10 on Billboard’s Top Country Albums chart, the most of any woman. She also scored more No. 1s on the Hot Country Songs chart for a woman artist at 25.  Born January 19, 1946, to a poor family in Sevier County, Tenn., Parton started recording at an early age: her first single, “Puppy Love,” appeared when she was 13. At 18, she moved to Nashville, where she became a professional country songwriter, while also recording a few minor pop singles. In 1966, she married Dean, who kept a famously low profile for the rest of her career; her childhood friend Judy Ogle, meanwhile, remained inseparable from her. “Those two people actually have been the rock,” she told The Guardian in 2014. Parton found her groove as a country performer in 1967, replacing Norma Jean as Porter Wagoner ‘s co-host and duet partner on his weekly TV show. (Wagoner and Parton would go on to place 20 duets on the country charts.) After her first Hot Country Songs charting hit, “Dumb Blonde,” in 1966, she had a number of songs that reached the 40s and 50s, until her breakthrough as a solo artist, a 1970 cover of Jimmie Rodgers ‘ “Mule Skinner Blues,” which reached No. 3). Over the next few years, her string of hits — many of which she wrote, including “Coat of Many Colors” and “My Tennessee Mountain Home” — established her persona: a passionate sentimentalist, shaped by the rural poverty of her childhood. (She went on to release at least one Top Ten Country single every year through 1985.) 1973’s heartbreaking true-live tale of romantic jealousy, “Jolene,” which would become her most-covered song, crossed over to the Hot 100, and gave her a taste of broader pop stardom. In 1974, she wrote and recorded a magnificent farewell to Wagoner, whose organization she was leaving: “I Will Always Love You” was first a No. 1 country single for her in 1974, and again when she re-recorded it for the soundtrack of The Best Little Whorehouse in Texas in 1982. (Then, of course, there was Houston’s monumental 1992 cover — followed by Parton’s third country-hit recording of the song, as a duet with Vince Gill in 1995.) She famously turned down Elvis Presley’s request to record the song because Col. Tom Parker insisted on Parton giving up half of her publishing royalties.  “That was one of the hardest things I ever had to do because I loved Elvis,” Parton told Billboard in a 2020 cover story .  “I Will Always Love You” was also the closing theme of Dolly! , the syndicated variety show she hosted in 1976 and 1977. The series was a springboard for her concerted efforts to expand her audience: she had her first top 10 Billboard Hot 100 in 1978 with “Here You Come Again,” and even hit the disco chart with 1978’s “Baby I’m Burning.” Her 1981 theme song from the movie 9 to 5 (in which she also starred) reached No. 1 on the Hot 100, Hot Country Songs and Adult Contemporary chart, a feat she repeated with 1983’s Kenny Rogers duet “Islands in the Stream,” written for them by the Bee Gees . In total, she topped the Hot 100 twice and topped the Hot Country Songs chart 25 times. As her songwriting output slowed (and the sound of country music passed her by) in the mid-’80s, Parton branched out. In 1986, she took over the Pigeon Forge, Tenn., theme park Silver Dollar City, and reopened it as Dollywood (with a replica of her childhood home). Trio , her 1987 collaboration with Linda Ronstadt and Emmylou Harris , was a neo-traditionalist setting for the three singers’ exquisite harmonies, and a platinum hit. After her appearance in the 1989 film Steel Magnolias , Parton returned her focus to recording country music, and rarely performed live for most of the ’90s; the appearance of her 1994 memoir, Dolly: My Life and Other Unfinished Business , signaled a move toward trading on her reputation. articles.title: Jason McCourty reveals when Shedeur Sanders could replace Deshaun Watson as Browns’ QB1
articles.summary: Recently, the Cleveland Browns caused a stir when head coach Todd Monken revealed that Deshaun Watson will get the starting quarterback job over Shedeur Sanders to begin the new season. The announcement comes less than three weeks before the Browns are slated to kick off their 2026 season, one th
articles._body: Recently, the Cleveland Browns caused a stir when head coach Todd Monken revealed that Deshaun Watson will get the starting quarterback job over Shedeur Sanders to begin the new season. The announcement comes less than three weeks before the Browns are slated to kick off their 2026 season, one that is not exactly filled with high expectations. Still, despite losing out on the starting job for now, that doesn’t mean Sanders won’t ever get a chance to get under center again, and recently, former NFL player and current ESPN analyst Jason McCourty broke down the opportunity that the former Colorado standout still has in front of him. “If he doesn’t perform well in those first two games… I think it’s very possible that we see Shedeur Sanders in week 3… The leash is that short when it comes to Deshaun Watson,” said McCourty, per First Take on X, formerly Twitter. Both Watson and Sanders have been up and down so far during their appearances at joint practices and in preseason games so far during training camp. Many have speculated that the much higher salary figure that the Browns have tied to Watson may have prompted ownership to pine for Monken to give him the starting role in order to save face. Still, if Watson’s previous starts for the Browns were any indication, it might not be long before the team is looking elsewhere at quarterback, and if Sanders does indeed get another opportunity, it will be up to him to take full advantage and show Cleveland, and other teams around the league, for that matter, that he can be a starter at the NFL level. articles.summary: Do fine art and high tech ever converge? At Sotheby’s they do, thanks to Kelly Shen ’17. Shen works in the growing field of art intelligence for the New York auction house. Shen builds algorithms to predict prices, using factors like buying trends and artists’ popularity. She has also worked on such
articles._body: Do fine art and high tech ever converge? At Sotheby’s they do, thanks to Kelly Shen ’17. Shen works in the growing field of art intelligence for the New York auction house. Shen builds algorithms to predict prices, using factors like buying trends and artists’ popularity. She has also worked on such efforts as cataloguing and ensuring that real-time systems can handle thousands of potential bidders visiting the house’s website. At the same time, she serves MIT as a class officer, vice president of the Association of MIT Alumnae, and a volunteer for the MIT Club of New York. A double major in computer science and math, Shen credits lessons from MIT—along with a lifelong passion for drawing—with shaping her career. Her favorite class was Project Laboratory in Mathematics, where students present creative answers to intricate math puzzles. “The class helped me talk about what I do with different audiences,” she says.  Though she appreciates elegant algorithms, she understands when they’re impractical: “You can build a super-sophisticated algorithm, but if it doesn’t bring more audience engagement, it doesn’t really matter.” Read more at www.technologyreview.com/alumni-profiles .

articles.title: Cheer Up: The Music Industry Is in Good Shape, Despite What You May Have Heard (Guest Column)
articles.summary: Today’s industry has its share of problems, but overall, it’s a healthier (and less centralized) business than ever before.
articles._body: Back in 2013, as the recorded music business grappled with an historic collapse in revenues, a hapless reporter asked two artist managers their thoughts on the plight of the industry. The response was bemused laughter. Their No. 1 client was a certain One Direction . Amid the wholesale collapse of the wider industry, they and their clients were having their best time yet. Related Live Nation Lost Its Monopoly Trial. What’s Next — and Could Ticketmaster Really Be Sold?  Dale Morris, Nashville Manager Who Guided Careers of Alabama & Kenny Chesney, Dies at 89 HYBE Pledges Over $300k for Colombia Earthquake Recovery It’s a potent reminder that in neither good times nor bad is success or good fortune equally distributed in music. At the lowest points, someone somewhere is having a great old time; even in boom times, someone is miserable. Which brings us to summer 2026 and the mood of an industry which seems, well, muted at best. Scene One: a computer screen displaying a plunging music-company share price. Camera pulls back to reveal a trader staring aghast at the numbers. Scene Two: a cocktail party in the Hamptons. A slightly grizzled but certainly well-to-do musician bemoans his lot, fragments of dialogue emerging over the hubbub: “Everything’s too difficult… There’s no money in it… AI will put us all out of work…” Having taken an unfamiliar “break” from the business these past couple of years, noses far from the grindstone, deep in garden leave — you should see the dahlias — may we be allowed to share a little perspective. The music industry is in remarkably good shape. Related AI Is Scaling Biases That the Music Industry Has Already Built (Guest Column) For the best part of 15 years, during the rise of what deliberately set out to be a different kind of music company, we argued that the most significant impact of streaming would not simply be its desperately needed effect on revenues — and don’t forget those have doubled since 2013 — but the long-overdue structural changes it would unleash. We were right. For artists and songwriters, digital platforms have driven an unprecedented democratization of creation, distribution and marketing. Just look around: More artists have meaningful access to a global market, and more routes to earning money from recorded music than ever before. Social media has made marketing reach more accessible than ever. Streaming has led to significantly higher artist royalty rates based on a simplified business model. Songwriters collectively receive a materially greater share of recorded music revenues than in the pre-digital world. Independent artists and businesses command a greater share of the market than they have for decades. The impact on the business has been just as decisive. The economics created by streaming have helped enable artists and songwriters to sell catalogues for millions or even hundreds of millions of dollars; led billions of dollars of new capital to enter music, funding not just catalogues but artists, entrepreneurs and technology companies; and created a landscape in which an increasing share of rights and revenues sit outside the traditional major-label system. For everyone who abhorred the waste, executive egos and dismissive or exploitative attitude towards “talent” that characterised the worst of the old world, this should be a time of celebration. Artists and entrepreneurs have more options, more potential partners and more agency than ever before. Naturally, that doesn’t mean everything is wonderful. Far from it. The economics of touring are brutally difficult for many artists. Breaking new acts in a world of almost infinite choice is harder than ever. Growth in mature streaming markets is slowing. The sheer volume of music being released creates unprecedented competition for attention. And AI raises profound questions about authorship, rights and how value will be distributed. Those concerns are real, but they are not evidence of the business dying. They are symptoms of an industry undergoing another structural transformation. Related Artist & Label Services Consultants Are Multiplying Rapidly. How Do You Know They’re Legit? (Guest Column) Part of the problem is that we continue to judge the health of music through an increasingly outdated lens. For understandable historical reasons, the fortunes of a handful of large record companies have traditionally served as shorthand for the fortunes of the entire recorded music sector. The major record companies remain powerful, successful and important businesses. But their interests are not synonymous with those of the music industry as a whole, and their share price woes are a critique of their business model, not of the prospects for music itself. The verdict from investors has been brutal. At the time of writing, Warner Music Group has lost nearly a quarter of its value in a year and Universal Music Group nearly 40%. The fact is, streaming and the forces surrounding it have steadily undermined many of the assumptions on which the traditional bundled record company model was built. Take the idea that major record companies are uniquely essential to discovering talent. That was never really true. Imagine the industry without Muddy Waters (Chess), U2 and Bob Marley (Island), Taylor Swift (Big Machine), Marvin Gaye (Motown), Depeche Mode (Mute), Guns N’ Roses (Geffen), John Lee Hooker (Modern Records), The Police (A&M), Adele (XL), Blondie (Chrysalis), Oasis (Creation) or Bad Bunny (Rimas Entertainment). Today, the argument is less relevant still. Much of the discovery, audience-building and proof of demand that once happened after an artist entered the record-company system now happens before they even get there. Meanwhile, the cost-benefit equation of a bundled major-label contract is less compelling when many of its component services can be sourced separately, often at lower cost. articles.title: Chiefs’ Patrick Mahomes drops preseason truth bomb amid injury recovery
articles.summary: The Kansas City Chiefs have one final preseason game remaining, on Friday against the reigning Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks. Patrick Mahomes hasn’t played in the preseason, and his status still hasn’t been made official for Week 1 as he recovers from the torn ACL he suffered t
articles._body: The Kansas City Chiefs have one final preseason game remaining, on Friday against the reigning Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks. Patrick Mahomes hasn’t played in the preseason, and his status still hasn’t been made official for Week 1 as he recovers from the torn ACL he suffered toward the end of last season. Recently, Mahomes spoke on his approach to training camp as practices increase in intensity for the upcoming season. “The more we practice, the better I feel,” said Mahomes, per Nate Taylor of ESPN on X, formerly Twitter. Mahomes also spoke about the fact that he hasn’t missed a single day of work since training camp began, despite dealing with the injury recovery process. “It’s been awesome for me to be able to do that. I haven’t had to miss anything, other than the preseason games. I’ve done every single [practice] rep,” he said. The Chiefs are surely hoping that Mahomes looks like the prime version of himself sooner rather than later, although it wouldn’t be a surprise if there was some rust to shake off following the injury rehab process. Mahomes had a solid year for the Chiefs last season, but the team largely fell apart around him, with the team’s lack of a running game, combined with a big step back from its defense, ultimately spelling Kansas City’s downfall and causing them to miss the playoffs for the first time since Mahomes arrived in town. This offseason, the Chiefs made some big moves on both sides of the ball, including signing reigning Super Bowl MVP running back Kenneth Walker III from the Seahawks, as well as trading up to draft cornerback Mansoor Delane in the first round. Kansas City will get its regular season underway on September 14. The post Chiefs’ Patrick Mahomes drops preseason truth bomb amid injury recovery appeared first on ClutchPoints .

He accepted the money to help cover travel costs to a pre-draft facility. Ultimately, Carter had repaid the money to the agent. On Tuesday,
articles._body: In July, Tennessee LB Arion Carter received a two-game suspension from the NCAA after accepting a $427 flight from a sports agent before the 2026 NFL Draft. He accepted the money to help cover travel costs to a pre-draft facility. Ultimately, Carter had repaid the money to the agent. On Tuesday, Carter’s suspension was limited to one game, per Austin Price of On3Sports.com. Meaning that Carter will be eligible to play for Tennessee’s game against Georgia Tech on Sept. 12. Carter had declared for the draft in December 2025. During the season, he suffered a foot injury in which he ruptured the MTP joint and plantar plate. In January, he reaggravated the injury and had to undergo surgery. That month, Carter withdrew from the draft . He finished the season with 28 solo tackles and averaged 1.5 sacks. In the meantime, Tennessee finished the season at 8-5 and 4-4 in the SEC. They reached the 2025 Music City Bowl in Nashville. Ultimately, T ennessee would lose to Illinois 30-28 . The NCAA has rules that prohibit college players from accepting payments and signing with agents to maintain amateurism. After the decision, Tennessee athletics director Danny White issued a statement , per ESPN. “While I strongly agree with Josh Heupel’s comment about how ridiculous this is in our current environment, 1 game is better than 2,” Whtie said “If players around the country are allowed to leave NFL camps and play college football, the NCAA should do the right thing and drop it all altogether. “This is yet another example of applying archaic rules from another era, without evolving and, most importantly, putting student-athletes’ experiences above bureaucracy. Arion doesn’t deserve this unnecessary distraction.” The Volunteers kick off the season on Sept 5. against Furman. articles._body: Olivia Rodrigo is taking Daisy Chain Fields to the airwaves. As announced Tuesday (Aug. 25), the pop star is teaming up with iHeartRadio for two different specials centered around her inaugural charity festival’s lineup, mission and performances during the last weekend of August. Related Olivia Rodrigo Announces Her Own All-Women Festival With Chappell Roan, KATSEYE & More on Lineup Olivia Rodrigo Visits Planned Parenthood’s Offices to Talk Reproductive Rights: ‘Women & Girls Matter to Me’ Olivia Rodrigo’s ‘Handmaid’s Tale’-Inspired Song ‘Serena Joy’ Is Now on Streaming After Record Store Release The first of the Rodrigo-led programming will broadcast on Friday (Aug. 28) starting at 9 p.m. ET. It will involve the Grammy winner serving as guest host of iHeartRadio’s weekly She Is the Voice show to highlight the all-women Daisy Chain Fields bill that she personally curated as well as her Billboard 200 -topping third album, You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love . The hourlong special will be available to listen to on both iHeartRadio ALT stations nationwide and two of the company’s digital stations, Alt Radio and She Rocks Radio. It’ll also replay nightly at 7 p.m. ET on She Rocks Radio from Aug. 28 to Sept. 4. Then, on Monday (Aug. 31), the company will devote 30 minutes to “iHeartRadio Presents: Olivia Rodrigo: Songs from Daisy Chain Fields,” which will showcase exclusive recordings of Rodrigo’s set at the festival. Fans can tune in at 7 p.m. local time on CHR and Hot AC stations, or they can listen via iHeartRadio’s digital station Hit Nation starting at 7 p.m. ET. Daisy Chain Fields is slated to take place in Irvine, Calif., on Saturday (Aug. 29), with artists such as Chappell Roan, Doechii, KATSEYE and more on the lineup. Rodrigo will close out the daylong event with a headlining set that night, featuring special guests Stevie Nicks, Sarah McLachlan and Karen O. All of the proceeds from the festival will go to charities supporting women and girls, including Planned Parenthood, Center for Reproductive Rights, National Domestic Workers Alliance and more. “I’ve had a dream of doing this festival for years and i am so ecstatic it’s finally coming true!!” Rodrigo stated when she first announced Daisy Chain Fields. “By bringing together women in music and organizations helping shape a better future for women and girls, I hope we can build a community that inspires hope and positive change.” Leading up to the festival, Rodrigo has also visited the offices of Planned Parenthood and Center for Reproductive Rights to discuss the most pressing issues in women’s rights and healthcare access, a cause that she’s long been outspoken about and has made one of the main focuses of the Daisy Chain Fields fund. Plus, the vocalist recently surprise-dropped standalone single “Serena Joy” — poignantly named after a character in The Handmaid’s Tale — on streaming services after a limited record store CD release. A portion of the net proceeds from the song will be funneled into the causes that are already benefiting from the festival.

articles.summary: The Detroit Lions are hungry to get to the Super Bowl during the 2026 season. Detroit has a sense of urgency around the entire organization after last season’s disappointing 9-8 finish. The Lions are doing their due diligence on one veteran player just weeks before the regular season. The L
articles._body: The Detroit Lions are hungry to get to the Super Bowl during the 2026 season. Detroit has a sense of urgency around the entire organization after last season’s disappointing 9-8 finish. The Lions are doing their due diligence on one veteran player just weeks before the regular season. The Lions hosted veteran running back Kareem Hunt for a visit on Tuesday, per ESPN’s Adam Schefter. Hunt did not immediately sign with Detroit after his visit. Still, this potential addition is something for Lions fans to keep their eyes on ahead of the regular season. This visit comes one day after the Lions signed free agent running back Roydell Williams to a contract. Detroit seems determined to add depth at running back ahead of the regular season. It is a stark change of strategy after Dan Campbell praised the team’s depth following Detroit’s preseason win against Washington. If the Lions did signed Hunt, they would reunite him with former Chiefs teammate Isiah Pacheco. In fact, that would give Detroit both of Kansas City’s leading rushers from the 2025 season. The Lions plan to feature superstar Jahmyr Gibbs in 2026 after giving him a monster contract extension. Pacheco should provide some power running on the side, with Jacob Saylors and Sione Vaki also in reserve alongside Williams. As for Hunt, he appears to still have some juice after an underrated 2025 season. He logged 163 carries for 611 rushing yards and eight touchdowns last year. Hunt also added 18 receptions for 143 receiving yards and a touchdown through the air. Ultimately, Hunt looks like a better depth player than any other options currently on the roster. It is easy to understand why Detroit wanted to kick the tires on Hunt. It will be fascinating to see if Hunt decides to join Detroit ahead of a crucial 2026 season for the organization. Next up for the Lions is their preseason finale against the Colts on August 29th. The post Kareem Hunt makes intriguing Lions move appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles._body: The Arizona Cardinals are locking up one of their most consistent offensive linemen for the next few years. It’s a move that maintains a solid contributor to serve as a building block for the club’s continued rebuild. Reports indicate that Hjalte Froholdt, a native of Denmark, has agreed to sign a two-year, $20 million contract extension with the Cardinals, according to Ian Rapoport of the NFL Network. Froholdt will now remain with the franchise through the 2028-29 season. “ Sources: The Cardinals and C Hjalte Froholdt have agreed to terms on a 2-year, $20M contract extension, keeping him in the fold through the 2028 season,” Rapoport reported. “One of their most consistent [performers] and anchors of their O-line gets rewarded.” Froholdt is entering his seventh year in the NFL, and his fourth with the Cardinals . Since joining Arizona in 2023, the 30-year-old center has not missed a single game. After beginning his career as a backup with the New England Patriots, along with two years with the Cleveland Browns, Foholdt has become a reliable starter in the NFL. While the contract extension is a great signing for Hjalte Froholdt and the Cardinals, Froholdt is not being paid as a top tier center in the league. His $10 million a year average puts him well below the top earners in the position. Tyler Linderbaum is making an average of $27 million a year in his deal with the Las Vegas Raiders. Meanwhile, Creed Humphrey has the second-highest contract with the Kansas City Chiefs, making $18 million per year. With the center position set for the next few years, the Cardinals will shift their attention to the upcoming campaign. Arizona will begin the 2026-27 season with a Week 1 matchup against the Los Angeles Chargers on the road on September 13. articles.title: Michael Porter Jr. reveals move that was ‘beginning of downfall’ for Nuggets
articles.summary: The Denver Nuggets have had a painfully quiet offseason, recently signing DeMar DeRozan as a consolation prize after trading Peyton Watson to the Cleveland Cavaliers. The Nuggets look poised to bring back mostly the same roster that exited in the first round last year in embarrassing fashion agai
articles._body: The Denver Nuggets have had a painfully quiet offseason, recently signing DeMar DeRozan as a consolation prize after trading Peyton Watson to the Cleveland Cavaliers. The Nuggets look poised to bring back mostly the same roster that exited in the first round last year in embarrassing fashion against the Minnesota Timberwolves. Recently, former Nuggets wing Michael Porter Jr. broke down where he thinks things started to go wrong for Denver. “I don’t know why they let (Kentavious Caldwell-Pope) go. That was the beginning of our downfall,” said Porter Jr., per Curious Mike, via Hoopshype. Indeed, the Nuggets let KCP walk in free agency following their 2024 loss to the Timberwolves, as the two-time champion ended up signing with the Orlando Magic. In fairness to the Nuggets’ front office, Caldwell-Pope’s play has largely fallen off a cliff in the two years since then, so signing him to a big contract might have been an even worse decision. Still, there are plenty of other moves that fans can criticize, including the trade of Porter Jr. himself to the Brooklyn Nets, which brought back Cam Johnson, who went on to have a rough first season overall with the Nuggets. Denver still has arguably the game’s best player in Nikola Jokic, but the team’s lack of size and athleticism was sorely exposed in the latest loss to Minnesota, as was the team’s lack of reliable perimeter scoring options when Jamal Murray doesn’t have it going. While the Nuggets will always have the 2023 championship to hold onto, the prospects of reaching those heights again in the current era are looking fainter by the day. articles.title: Karol G, Judeline & Rusowsky Take ‘BbY WOW’ To No. 1: ‘So Thankful’
articles.summary: "I’m so thankful to Karol for giving me this opportunity," says Judeline on their first No. 1.
articles._body: Judeline and Rusowsky score their first Billboard No. 1, as “BbY WOW,” with Karol G , rockets from No. 5 to the top of the Hot Latin Songs chart (dated Aug. 29). “BbY WOW” lands at No. 1 on Hot Latin Songs — which blends streams, airplay and sales — off a streaming-fueled surge. The collab registered 6.1 million official on-demand streams in the United States during the Aug. 14-20 tracking week, according to Luminate. The sum takes the song to a No. 34 start on the overall Streaming Songs chart and to an equal 5-1 trek on the Latin Streaming Songs list. “It’s honestly hard to believe that a song we recorded just last month is already topping the charts — and in the U.S. of all places,” Judeline shared with Billboard . “Everything around ‘BbY WOW’ has happened so fast that I’m still processing it. I’m so thankful to Karol for giving me this opportunity, and to everyone who has embraced the song. Seeing how far it has traveled in such a short time is something I never could have imagined.” Related Xavi Is First to Lead These 3 Latin Airplay Charts Simultaneously in 2026 Karol G Floods Hot Latin Songs Chart With ‘No Me Arrepiento de Sentir Tanto’ No Regrets, Just No. 1s: Karol G’s ‘No Me Arrepiento De Sentir Tanto’ Debuts Atop Top Latin Albums Chart “BbY WOW” gives Karol G her 11th No. 1 on Hot Latin Songs—and makes her the first artist in nearly two years to replace herself at the summit. Her Drake collaboration “Ahí” falls 1-4 after a 30% streaming dip, with 4.2 million U.S. clicks. The chart mixes streaming data, radio airplay and digital sales into its formula. The last artist to pull off the feat was Bad Bunny, whose “Nuevayol” handed the crown to “DtMF” in January 2025. Among female acts, Karol last did it in September 2023, when “Qlona,” with Peso Pluma, replaced “Mi Ex Tenía Razón.” In addition to their Hot Latin Songs win, Spanish artists Judeline and Rusowsky race to their first No. 1 on the Hot Latin Rhythm Songs chart, where “BbY WOW” climbs 5-1. Meanwhile, it soars 73-38 on the all-genre Billboard Hot 100 — Karol’s highest ranking in two years, after the No. 32-peaking “Si Antes Te Hubiera Conocido” (August 2024). On the global front, “BbY WOW” surges 171-37 on the Billboard Global 200 chart, with 17.9 million streams in the U.S. Plus, it debuts at No. 41 on the Global Excl. U.S. tally with 11.9 million clicks registered outside the country. All charts dated Aug. 29, 2026, will update on Billboard.com on Aug. 25. articles.summary: The San Francisco 49ers are currently gearing up for their preseason finale on Thursday against the Las Vegas Raiders. The 49ers are desperately hoping for a somewhat healthy season this year after their last couple of campaigns have been derailed by injuries. Recently, newly signed wide receiver
articles._body: The San Francisco 49ers are currently gearing up for their preseason finale on Thursday against the Las Vegas Raiders . The 49ers are desperately hoping for a somewhat healthy season this year after their last couple of campaigns have been derailed by injuries. Recently, newly signed wide receiver Mike Evans has been dealing with a quad issue, and on Tuesday, the team got the latest update on his status ahead of that day’s practice. “#49ers WR Mike Evans working on the side as team begins practice Tuesday,” reported Nick Wagoner of ESPN on X, formerly Twitter. The 49ers signed Evans in free agency this year after he spent the first decade-plus of his Hall of Fame career with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, where he remained remarkably durable, although he did miss time with a broken collarbone this past season. Evans will be particularly counted upon this year due to the fact that Ricky Pearsall has already been ruled out for the season, and with George Kittle seemingly needing some time to round fully back into form after an Achilles injury he suffered last year during the NFL playoffs. If Evans can stay on the field, he figures to provide Brock Purdy and the offense with a key downfield threat who can still rise up over smaller cornerbacks and win contested catches at the summit, which is something that San Francisco has been sorely missing over the last few years. In any case, the 49ers are set to get their regular season underway on September 10 in Australia for a key divisional game aainst the new-look Los Angeles Rams. articles.title: Bill Barnwell’s Greatest Show on Turf Rams comp is a warning to Patriots
articles.summary: The New England Patriots might have an MVP-caliber quarterback, an upgraded offense, and legitimate expectations entering the 2026 season. But ESPN’s Bill Barnwell believes there is one obstacle that could derail the hype before it ever translates into another dominant campaign. Their schedule. B
articles._body: The New England Patriots might have an MVP-caliber quarterback, an upgraded offense, and legitimate expectations entering the 2026 season. But ESPN’s Bill Barnwell believes there is one obstacle that could derail the hype before it ever translates into another dominant campaign. Their schedule. Barnwell compared New England’s situation to the Rams following their remarkable turnaround in 1999. After going 4-12 in 1998, St. Louis exploded onto the scene with a 13-3 record and a Super Bowl title the following season. But repeating that success proved difficult when the schedule became less forgiving. The 2000 Rams still featured one of the most dangerous offenses in football, but their record fell to 10-6. That is the type of regression Barnwell believes New England could experience. “One obvious comparable would be the 1999 Rams, who stunningly jumped from 4-12 to 13-3 despite losing starting quarterback Trent Green just before the season. Kurt Warner came off the bench and wildly exceeded every possible expectation at quarterback, and that Rams team had added guys like Marshall Faulk to the mix … but they also faced an incredibly easy schedule. Those Rams faced one team all regular season with a winning record: the 13-3 Titans, whom they would then beat in the Super Bowl. “The following year, those same Rams went 10-6 and finished second in the NFC West … a tougher slate of opponents made life more difficult the following year.” His research found that teams with the 30 easiest schedules since 1990 averaged 9.3 wins during those favorable seasons, adjusted for a 17-game schedule. The following year, their average dropped to 8.0 wins as their opponents became significantly tougher. Barnwell expects the addition of A.J. Brown will help with some of the concerns. But he specifically warned that New England appears vulnerable to injuries and a tougher slate, suggesting the Patriots have a lower floor than their offseason optimism might indicate. If the Patriots are going to prove last season was sustainable, they will need to show they can win when the schedule stops doing them favors. The post Bill Barnwell’s Greatest Show on Turf Rams comp is a warning to Patriots appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles.title: Two unvaccinated people die from measles in Pennsylvania, officials confirm
articles.summary: "[P]eople are not familiar with this disease and don’t fully understand the potential severity."
articles._body: Two unvaccinated people have died from measles in Pennsylvania, state health officials confirmed Tuesday . They are the first measles deaths reported in Pennsylvania in 35 years and the first deaths reported in the US in 2026. Last year, the US saw three measles deaths : two in otherwise-healthy but unvaccinated school-age children in Texas and one in an unvaccinated adult in New Mexico. Prior to those deaths, the US had not seen a measles death since 2015 , when a woman with underlying conditions became severely ill. Citing privacy, health officials in Pennsylvania are not providing information on the people who died beyond that they were unvaccinated and were residents of Lancaster County. Officials noted that the deaths are among 393 confirmed cases reported this year across 28 counties in the state. Read full article Comments

articles.summary: "This will be a project like no other."
articles._body: Louisiana Gov. Jeff Landry said Tuesday that SpaceX will commit $100 billion to develop Starship factories and launch pads in the state's coastal areas. In doing so, the company seeks to replicate the Starbase facility it has built over the last decade in southern Texas on a larger scale. The announcement capped months of speculation about SpaceX's interest in a sprawling parcel of land along the Gulf coast of Louisiana, which offers room to build multiple launch towers and offers access to the methane propellant that fuels the Starship rocket. Gwynne Shotwell, the president and chief operating officer of SpaceX, said the "Starbase Louisiana" facility would become a self-sustaining spaceport with propellant production, power generation, deep-water shipping capabilities, vehicle processing facilities, and an airport on site.
