articles.title: US Opens a New Front Against Iran’s Crypto Economy
articles.summary: Bitcoin Magazine
articles._body: Bitcoin Magazine US Opens a New Front Against Iran’s Crypto Economy The U.S. this week closed in on Iran, further targeting its crypto-related methods of dodging sanctions in a new economic campaign against the country.  In a Monday announcement, the U.S. Department of the Treasury said it had placed Iran’s digital asset sector under the same sanctions authority it has long used against the country’s oil, banking and metals industries.  . @SecScottBessent : "This is a sustained campaign to collapse every last option for Iran. Let there be no ambiguity as to the position of the United States: an economic engagement of any kind with this murderous regime will expose those responsible to the full reach of American… pic.twitter.com/tlx2gcNs1d — Treasury Department (@USTreasury) August 24, 2026 The move, as part of Operation Economic Outcast, a campaign against the Islamic Republic dubbed “economic D-Day,” is a first, and a significant escalation in exposure for crypto businesses worldwide. With the new action, the Office of Foreign Assets Control can sanction any person, regardless of where they are located.  “The Iranian regime increasingly turns to cryptocurrency as a tool of choice for sanctions evasion, supporting transactions linked to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps and Iranian regime insiders,” OFAC said in a statement.  Foreign exchanges, OTC desks, payment processors and infrastructure providers that knowingly facilitate transactions supporting Iran’s digital asset sector are now exposed to designation themselves, along with the loss of access to the U.S. financial system that typically follows. OFAC also designated members of a group within the Ministry of Intelligence and Security accused of hacking U.S. critical infrastructure on the regime’s behalf and published their wallets. Group co-leader Behzad Mesri and members Keyvan Fayyaz Ghareh Blagh and Arman Kahzadian each had bitcoin, and other crypto addresses added to the Treasury’s sanctioned list. The three belong to a larger MOIS contingent that has pursued U.S. targets through data theft and intrusions against corporations and government offices. Bloomberg first reported in May that Iran had started a bitcoin-backed insurance service for Iranian shipping companies. The U.S. in July said that it had frozen crypto linked to the Iranian regime, mostly in the form of the Tether stablecoin.  Stablecoins like Tether’s USDT can be frozen by the company that issues the asset but bitcoin, being decentralized and having no single issuer, cannot.  This post US Opens a New Front Against Iran’s Crypto Economy first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Mathew Di Salvo .

articles.title: ESPN Using RedZone Branding for US Open Coverage
articles.summary: Aaron Doster-Imagn Images
articles._body: ESPN’s first usage of its ability to deploy the RedZone IP as part of the NFL Network acquisition might not have been on anyone’s bingo card. For the first six days of the US Open—beginning Aug. 30— RedZone coverage will stream on the ESPN Unlimited platform from 11 a.m. through 6 p.m. ET. “We’re going to be using each day a few commentators across our roster, many names you’re familiar with, to both host as the traffic cop but also to actually call the points that the viewer is seeing on the screen,” ESPN senior director of programming and acquisitions John Suchenski told Front Office Sports . “So it is not a set host and commentator roster each day. It’s really going to rotate, and we like that because it’s going to give everyone a chance to contribute and be fanned here from a lot of different voices, including many of our notable talent—John McEnroe, Patrick McEnroe, Andy Roddick, Caroline Wozniacki, etc.” Suchenski declined to specify who the traffic-cop hosts for the tennis version of RedZone will be. Nevertheless, Scott Hanson—the popular NFL RedZone host—will not be one of them, as he remained an NFL Media employee in the swap. NFL still retains production and digital distribution of RedZone , while ESPN and its parent company Disney have the linear TV distribution rights. Suchenski said the tennis RedZone “is intended to be fast-paced whiparound coverage, similar to what fans have become accustomed to with the NFL RedZone .” He said that ESPN has utilized whiparound coverage in the past with tennis, but in a more “methodical” manner. The new offering promises to be a much more frenetic pace. Suchenski said it will be “potentially point-to-point, not necessarily game-to-game or match-to-match.” Asked by FOS about which other sports, including college football, ESPN might apply the RedZone branding to in the future, Suchenski said it is “to be determined.” The post ESPN Using RedZone Branding for US Open Coverage appeared first on Front Office Sports .

articles._body: Alexander Grene Development broke ground on the $78 million mixed-use business park Lilac Field in League City. The development is seeking its first industrial and retail tenants. Located between League City Parkway and SH 146, Lilac Field will span 24.5 acres and include 70,000 square feet of retail and restaurant space and 220,000 square feet of flexible warehouse space. Community Impact reports once complete, Lilac Field will include 16 small warehouse units and seven retail and restaurant buildings, with warehouse tenants expected to include entertainment venues, gyms, childcare providers and breweries. The development’s first two industrial buildings are expected to be completed by early 2027. The developer is seeking industrial clients, such as aerospace and aviation suppliers, marine service groups, technology firms, energy service companies, advanced manufacturing users and specialty distributors to rent its warehouse space. articles.title: Ben Johnson called Bears the ‘No. 1 regression candidate’ – ESPN reveals why he’s right
articles.summary: Chicago Bears head coach Ben Johnson expressed his frustration after joint practice sessions with the Cincinnati Bengals, pointing out three procedural errors during the first seven snaps. While he praised his defense for competing against high-level opponents, Johnson noted that starting slowly
articles._body: Chicago Bears head coach Ben Johnson expressed his frustration after joint practice sessions with the Cincinnati Bengals, pointing out three procedural errors during the first seven snaps. While he praised his defense for competing against high-level opponents, Johnson noted that starting slowly cost the team valuable opportunities. He views the upcoming road schedule as essential for addressing these mistakes before the regular season begins. This sense of urgency is reflected in Johnson’s candid public assessment that Chicago is the NFL’s top candidate for regression heading into 2026. A detailed analysis by ESPN supports Johnson’s concerns, indicating that his projection is statistically justified . After an 11-6 season in 2025, which included a modest +26 point differential and a 7-4 record in one-score games, advanced metrics suggest the Bears benefited from an unsustainable level of luck. They achieved a remarkable +22 turnover differential, having forced 33 turnovers while only committing 11, the fewest in the league. Historical data shows that 20 of the last 21 teams that posted a +20 turnover margin since 1990 experienced a decline in wins the following year, with their turnover margins dropping by an average of 19 takeaways. Additionally, the Bears recovered 66.7% of all fumbles during their games, a rate that no team in modern NFL history has maintained in consecutive seasons. Adding to these statistical concerns, the Bears faced significant defensive issues last season. They ranked 27th in points allowed per drive on non-turnover possessions and 29th in pressure rate. Despite having young offensive talent around quarterback Caleb Williams, issues with execution were evident during a 27-9 preseason loss to Cincinnati. In an interview with the Chicago Tribune, Johnson expressed deep disappointment with the team’s 11 penalties and lackluster performance, emphasizing that losing by multiple scores is unacceptable, regardless of the game’s exhibition status. The post Ben Johnson called Bears the ‘No. 1 regression candidate’ – ESPN reveals why he’s right appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles.title: Jets end major competition after loser’s ‘dreadful day’
articles.summary: The New York Jets have just a few weeks remaining until they kick off their 2026 season with a game against the Tennessee Titans. The Jets have several roster competitions still ongoing during training camp, but one of those reportedly came to an end on Tuesday. “STC Chris Banjo says Jason
articles._body: The New York Jets have just a few weeks remaining until they kick off their 2026 season with a game against the Tennessee Titans. The Jets have several roster competitions still ongoing during training camp, but one of those reportedly came to an end on Tuesday. “STC Chris Banjo says Jason Sanders ‘has won the job’ at placekicker. Cade York has been waived. Banjo says he feels ‘really, really good about where Jason is.’ Cites his experience in the AFC East as a positive,” reported Rich Cimini of ESPN on X, formerly Twitter. Cimini also pointed out that “York has a stronger leg than Sanders, but York had a dreadful practice yesterday. Sanders wasn’t all that great, either, yesterday.” Sanders has spent the majority of his NFL career with the Miami Dolphins and now will handle the reps, at least to start out, for the Jets. Meanwhile, York has bounced around the league since being selected in the fourth round of the draft a few years ago in a surprising move, and will now look to find a roster spot elsewhere as training camps around the NFL wind down. Kicking is one of many areas where the Jets were not up to par last year, with the team ending up as the last winless squad in the NFL at one point before finally stringing together a couple of victories down the stretch of the season. Some fans were surprised when head coach Aaron Glenn was brought back for another year despite the losing, but it’s safe to say that some marked improvement must be in order for him to be able to keep the job over the long haul. articles.title: Kalshi Lands 5 MLB Teams as Prediction-Market Boom Continues
articles.summary: Bob DeChiara-Imagn Images
articles._body: Less than six months since Polymarket became the exclusive prediction-market partner of Major League Baseball, seven individual teams now have prediction-market agreements of their own—including five with Kalshi. Kalshi came out swinging on Tuesday, unveiling exclusive, multiyear “brand partnerships” with the Braves, Red Sox, Dodgers, Padres, and Giants. That means Kalshi now has commercial relationships with one-sixth of the 30 MLB clubs. Under the deals, Kalshi will be featured on in-stadium signage, in social media posts, and more. As part of the deal with the Dodgers, the Gold Glove Bar at Dodger Stadium is being renamed the Kalshi 435 Club. Kalshi says baseball-related trading volume on its platform is 36 times higher than it was a year ago. “The idea is that fans are already engaging with their favorite teams on Kalshi, so it only makes sense to extend that fandom to some of the most beloved baseball teams in America,” Kalshi’s head of sports partnerships, Adam Barrick, said in the press release . The Red Sox, Dodgers, and Giants have since issued their own press releases confirming the agreements. “Our shared commitment to innovation and excellence makes this partnership a natural fit, while creating new opportunities to engage Red Sox fans across Fenway Park and through our digital and broadcast channels,” said Red Sox EVP and chief marketing and partnerships officer Troup Parkinson. “The Dodgers are always looking for innovative ways to connect with our fans, and Kalshi represents an exciting new category,” said Lorenzo Sciarrino, SVP of global partnerships for the Dodgers. “Creating unmatched experiences for our fans is a top priority, and we’re excited to work with Kalshi to deliver on that commitment,” said Giants SVP of partnerships Steve Tseng. The Braves and Padres did not respond to requests for comment. Tuesday’s flurry comes about three weeks after the Yankees signed a deal with Polymarket through the rest of this season. That announcement came roughly one week after the Mets became the first MLB team to sign a prediction-market partnership—through an exclusive, multiyear agreement with Novig. Although seven teams now have team-level deals with prediction markets—or nearly one-quarter of MLB clubs—not every franchise is ready to join the party. Front Office Sports reached out to every MLB team to ask about prediction-market plans. Many did not respond, although representatives for the Guardians, Nationals, Phillies, and Rockies said those teams don’t have any prediction-market partnerships. Sports-event contracts from Kalshi and other prediction-market platforms are the subject of numerous lawsuits winding through the U.S. court system; several states argue they should be treated like traditional sports betting, which is regulated by individual states. The Red Sox, Dodgers, and Braves began rolling out their activations, including through signage at games and sponsored emails, ahead of the announcements . The moves led to online speculation that teams were reaching deals quietly with platforms to avoid public ridicule. MLB received a lot of backlash to the Polymarket deal; Sen. Richard Blumenthal (D., Conn.) told FOS , “It is astonishing and appalling that Major League Baseball would, in effect, be complicit in this.” However, sources tell FOS that teams are not intentionally hiding these partnerships to avoid public pushback. “If teams were worried about fan sentiment, they wouldn’t do the deals,” says one source who has worked on commercial partnerships like this for teams in one of the big four North American sports leagues. A source familiar with the matter tells FOS the premature Red Sox rollout was “just a wonky timing thing.” The post Kalshi Lands 5 MLB Teams as Prediction-Market Boom Continues appeared first on Front Office Sports .

articles.title: Breaking down the top WR classes in the 2027 cycle so far
articles.summary: Recruiting wide receivers can often be adventurous as the position is always full of boisterous and talented blue-chippers. It’s become rare that a cycle doesn’t feature a big flip or two from one of the nation’s top pass-catchers. If a school wishes to add another elite receiver t
articles._body: Recruiting wide receivers can often be adventurous as the position is always full of boisterous and talented blue-chippers. It’s become rare that a cycle doesn’t feature a big flip or two from one of the nation’s top pass-catchers. If a school wishes to add another elite receiver to their class, it will indeed have to be a flip, as all 54 of the blue-chip prospects at the position — according to the Rivals Industry Ranking — are currently committed, as of Aug. 25. $19.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage Those 54 commitments have dispersed among 37 college programs. Fourteen schools have multiple blue-chip WR commits this cycle. There’s a quintet of five-star pass-catchers this cycle and they are each headed to powerhouses. Rivals breaks down the top receiver classes nationwide coming out of the summer: Oregon 5-star Dakota Guerrant (No. 21 NATL., No. 5 WR) 4-star Xavier Sabb (No. 36 NATL., No. 7 WR) 3-star Malachi Garlington (No. 947 NATL., No. 129 WR) Oregon continues to target and land elite talent from all over the country. Its trio of wide receiver pledges is a great example of that. Guerrant is the No. 1 senior prospect in Michigan, while Sabb checks in as the No. 2 recruit out of New Jersey. The former received his fifth star in the latest Rivals300 update and reminds Rivals’ Scouting and Rankings Team of Emeka Egbuka . Guerrant had over 1,000 receiving yards and 17 touchdowns as a junior last fall. He chose the Ducks over Michigan and a slew of other high-profile contenders. The latter has been a five-star at points throughout the cycle and remains on that bubble heading into his senior season. Sabb has caught 30 touchdowns during an illustrious prep career and is just as dynamic on the defensive side of the ball. Then there’s Garlington, the No. 3 recruit in Oregon who’s set to stay in-state. Also note that this doesn’t even include four-star athlete commit Tae Walden Jr. , another top-100 overall prospect who could line up at receiver or defensive back at the next level. Position coach Ross Douglas has a legit group headed his way. Texas A&M 4-star Eric McFarland (No. 34 NATL., No. 6 WR) 4-star Jaden Upshaw (No. 57 NATL., No. 9 WR) 3-star Damani Warren (No. 429 NATL., No. 59 WR) 3-star Trey Haddad (No. 1,320 NATL., No. 178 WR) Along with Oregon, Texas A&M is the only other program to tote a pair of top-10 receiver commitments this cycle. The Aggies have a firm grip on the nation’s No. 1 class. McFarland and Upshaw are two of Mike Elko’s 11 pledges that rank as top-100 prospects. McFarland hails from Las Vegas but stars on a loaded IMG Academy (Fla.) squad. He caught 11 touchdowns in nine games last season and possesses elite speed that helps him dominate in the slot. He committed at the end of June. Upshaw was a big win for the Aggies back in April. One of four blue-chippers from Georgia to commit to the SEC program this cycle, he ranks as the No. 5 senior in the Peach State and reminds Rivals of Michael Gallup . Warren is another Las Vegas product who’s still in Sin City this fall. He’s the No. 4 senior recruit in Nevada and was another June pledge alongside Haddad, a nifty playmaker out of Ohio who’ll look to bolster his stock this fall. Cal 4-star Charles Davis (No. 84 NATL., No. 15 WR) 4-star Demare Dezeurn (No. 201 NATL., No. 30 WR) 4-star Zion White (No. 214 NATL., No. 33 WR) 3-star Blake Gunter (No. 1,070 NATL., No. 149 WR) New head coach Tosh Lupoi is working to revitalize his alma mater, and if his work on the recruiting trail is any indication, he’s well on his way. Cal is one of three programs to hold commitments from three blue-chip receivers this cycle. The Bears currently have the nation’s No. 21 class and the trio of receiver commits sit atop the pledge list. Davis is the headliner for position coach Ike Hilliard , checking in as the lone top-100 prospect in the class. He committed on April 10 and his stock has continued to rise heading into his senior season. Dezeurn and White both committed during the busy month of June. The former is a one-time Oklahoma pledge who ultimately decided to stay in the Golden State at the next level. The latter is now in Hawaii for his senior year but is ready to make his way to Berkeley in 2027. Cal beat North Carolina and Washington for White’s pledge. Florida 4-star Elias Pearl (No. 91 NATL., No. 17 WR) 4-star Tramond Collins (No. 138 NATL., No. 23 WR) 4-star Anthony Jennings (No. 308 NATL., No. 45 WR) Another program that’s hit the recruiting trail running under a first-year staff is Florida. New head coach Jon Sumrall has the Gator faithful excited by the SEC program’s class that currently checks in at No. 8 in the Rivals Industry Team Recruiting Rankings. There’s no shortage of blue-chip commits on the offensive side of the ball and that includes three in-state four-star receivers. UF’s biggest win came in May as it beat out Georgia for Pearl, the No. 11 player in the Sunshine State. He’s also a top-10 receiver in the updated Rivals300 rankings. Collins had already committed to Florida under Billy Napier . He then re-opened his process but proceeded to choose the Gators again in March. Previously listed as an “athlete,” Collins is a dynamic two-way playmaker who’ll likely line up as a receiver at the next level for position coach Marcus Davis . Jennings joined the fold in April, choosing UF over Miami. He’s another top-30 player in Florida that’s headed to The Swamp. It was eye-opening and we need to go back and watch the tape.” Bucs QB Baker Mayfield said Jacksonville was playing with “their hair on fire” and said had it been a game today; his team would not have been on the winning side. pic.twitter.com/GRpGpnEWTO — Rick Stroud (@NFLSTROUD) August 25, 2026 While Mayfield is happy with how the team has developed and learned during training camp, at the end of the day, football is a physical sport, and that was lacking against Jacksonville. “I feel like we are in a good spot with the understanding of the system, the checks, what we are trying to get done, and now it is just strictly about execution and physicality,” Mayfield said. “That’s the part today that we were lacking. I don’t think that anybody is too far behind when it comes to the knowledge of what we are trying to get done, which is great; that is what you want at this point in camp, but also, when you have that down, the execution needs to be there.” Video: Baker Mayfield says players understand the new offense well but need to bring a physicality that was lacking in today’s practice with the Jaguars. pic.twitter.com/xHRsICmIlf — Greg Auman (@gregauman) August 25, 2026 The good news is that the Buccaneers aren’t known as a soft team. Mayfield, in particular, always plays with a chip on his shoulder and is perhaps more willing to play with physicality than any other quarterback in the NFL. That is especially true with the QB playing for a new contract this year, and he will surely set the tone after this eye-opening practice against the Jaguars. The post Buccaneers’ Baker Mayfield calls out Tampa Bay after sloppy Jaguars joint practice appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles.title: Gabz Landman Named Executive VP of A&R at Warner Chappell Music
articles.summary: Landman's signings include Laufey, Madison Beer, The Chainsmokers and Diplo.
articles._body: Gabz Landman has been promoted to executive vp at Warner Chappell Music, the company announced this week. Since joining the publishing outfit in 2022, Landman has facilitated several key signings including those of Laufey , Madison Beer , The Chainsmokers and Diplo . Landman will continue to be based out of the company’s Los Angeles office, where she reports to Ryan Press , president of A&R, North America. Related Publishing Briefs: Laufey Renews Deal With Warner Chappell Music, Plus Claudia Brant & More Dale Morris, Nashville Manager Who Guided Careers of Alabama & Kenny Chesney, Dies at 89 HYBE Pledges Over $300k for Colombia Earthquake Recovery “Gabz has a natural instinct for spotting and developing talent ahead of the curve, and she brings a 24/7 hustle to everything she does that’s rare to fine,” Press said in a statement. “Having built some of the strongest relationships in this business, she’s a real advocate for artists and songwriters, and a true leader helping drive Warner Chappell’s growth, both on the charts and culturally. She’s earned this, and I couldn’t be prouder to see this next step.” Landman has also worked extensively with songwriter Amy Allen , who won pop music songwriter of the year at the 2026 ASCAP Pop Music Awards and was the first woman to win the Grammy Award for songwriter of the year when she took home the honor in 2025; Allen has collaborated with Olivia Rodrigo , Tate McRae , Sabrina Carpenter and Olivia Dean , among many others. Landman has also worked with Cal Shapiro , who has collaborated with Alex Warren and Cameron Whitcomb . Landman had most recently held the title of senior vp of A&R at Warner Chappell. Prior to joining the company, she served as creative director at TAP Management and as vp of A&R at Warner Records. At the start of her career, Landman was an intern at Billboard . Related Amy Allen On Modern Songwriting and Her Creative Chemistry With Sabrina Carpenter, Harry Styles “I’m incredibly grateful to Ryan and the entire team at Warner Chappell for this opportunity,” Landman said in a statement. “Since joining the company, I’ve had the privilege of working alongside some of the most talented songwriters and artists in the industry, and I’m endlessly inspired by their creativity and drive. Discovering and developing talent is my greatest passion, and I’m excited to keep building on that work in this new role.” In April, Laufey renewed her publishing deal with Warner Chappell Music. Her album, A Matter of Time , hit No. 4 on the Billboard 200 following its release and a Grammy for best traditional pop vocal album. Landman appeared on Billboard ’s 40 Under 40 list in 2025 and was also named to Billboard ’s Women in Music .

articles.summary: The Jacksonville Jaguars are currently gearing up for their preseason finale on Friday against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. The Jaguars are looking to build off the success of last year, when they made the playoffs under first-year head coach Liam Coen and blew away expectations. On Tuesday, the tea
articles._body: The Jacksonville Jaguars are currently gearing up for their preseason finale on Friday against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. The Jaguars are looking to build off the success of last year, when they made the playoffs under first-year head coach Liam Coen and blew away expectations. On Tuesday, the team got a scare on the injury front regarding a key member of their wide receiver room, with NFL insider Michael DiRocco of ESPN reporting that wideout Brian Thomas Jr. “(hurt) his left shoulder and then (sat) out the rest of today’s practice.” However, Coen didn’t appear to be overly concerned about the issue after practice. “I think it’s alright. Just came down on his shoulder. Holding him out was smart, keep him out and then get him go for Cleveland,” said Coen, per DiRocco on X, formerly Twitter. This would entail sitting out Thomas for this week’s final preseason game against the Buccaneers. Thomas Jr. has been a standout for the Jaguars since being drafted in the first round back in 2024, making the Pro Bowl in his rookie season and providing a reliable downfield target for quarterback Trevor Lawrence. It’s certainly understandable that the team would want to make sure he is fully healthy before letting him go back out on the field again in training camp or the preseason. Meanwhile, the Jaguars are hoping to prove that last year’s success was no fluke. They will get their regular season on September 13 with a home game against the Cleveland Browns at 1:00 pm ET. articles.title: Lady Gaga’s Fiancé Michael Polansky Has a Biotech Startup Involving AI & Living Skin
articles.summary: Outer Biosciences is also using AI to predict the next gen of skin-disease treatments by sourcing skin that would typically be discarded after surgery.
articles._body: Lady Gaga has a thriving skincare line in Haus Labs, the cosmetics brand she built from her kitchen floor to worldwide prominence. Now, fiancé Michael Polansky says the engaged couple are mixing up Polanksy’s background in applied mathematics, computer science and the cutting-edge world of Silicon Valley tech and investment with the singer’s global brand and business acumen in search of skincare for, and of, the future. In an interview with Tech Crunch , Polansky revealed that Gaga sits on the board of the startup Outer Biosciences , which was co-founded by Polansky in 2022 out of frustration that “the pace of innovation in biology and chemistry has never matched software, in large part because there’s no ethical way to run experiments directly on people,” according to technology news site. Polansky and his team were reportedly not satisfied with the traditional stand-ins used by scientists, such as animal models and lab-grown organoids that mimic the structure and development of real human organs in order to better understand how real human organs behave. So, instead of engineering a synthetic organ, the company says it ethically sourced real human skin that would typically be tossed after surgery — mostly plastic surgery — usually within hours of surgery while it is still “alive.” The samples, which are “de-identified” to protect the donor and supply organizations’ privacy, are then fed nutrients and stripped of metabolic waste to extend the sample’s viability “well past the industry norm.” Rather than the typical window of a few days to test such skin, Outer Biosciences has reportedly figured out a way to keep the tissue alive for up to four weeks. The material, referred as Yuna, an “ex vivo human-skin platform that keeps full-thickness skin alive for four weeks,” reportedly has the ability to make 30-day-old tissue look almost identical to day-one tissue. So, what are their plans for this typically discarded biological material? Using an AI model, the team said it can predict which untested chemicals might have a “beneficial effect on a specific skin function,” and, after being run through the living-tissue system, see if their prediction was right and improve it during the next round. For now, the actual product is not a skincare ingredient, but the ability to find one faster. The company’s goal, according to Polansky, 42, is to discover cosmetic ingredients, not drugs, in order to avoid a lengthy, potentially costly FDA approval process and then partner with a licensee who can bring that innovation to the commercial market in the form of serums or creams. Polansky said that four of Outer Bioscience’s six current leads are likely to reach commercialization. At press time a spokesperson for Gaga had not returned Billboard’s request for additional details on when Gaga joined the Outer Biosciences board and what, if any, role she has in the firm’s business. While they await those end results, the company — which has reportedly raised $23 million in funding to date — is also generating revenue via collaborative research partnerships, including one studying why certain cancer drugs cause severe skin rashes. At press time it was unclear what, if any, role Gaga plays in the firm’s work, though the “Disease” singer has said in the past that she’s very heavily involved in product development, brand strategy and the creative vision for her Haus Labs brand. In addition to reportedly sitting on the board of Outer Biosciences, Gaga, 40, promoted the work of the company on X earlier this week, writing, “Meet @outerbio and YUNA. We are building the future of skin health. Welcome from Michael, Me and the entire team at Outer Bio,” including a link to the company’s website.

articles.title: How Tekno Found Solace Again in Music After Almost Quitting the Industry
articles.summary: After facing health challenges that led to vocal cord surgery, the Nigerian singer-songwriter has fallen back in love with music with his release Where Did Love Go?
articles._body: Tekno is in a season of peace.  After residing in Nigeria and the United States, the 33-year-old musician has called Paris home for four months by the time of his Zoom call with Billboard . “I feel like spending this amount of time in Europe is very amazing for me mentally, it’s really helped me,” Tekno says. Reaching the state of serenity isn’t just by happenstance, but the aftermath of resilience. In April 2017, Tekno publicly announced that he suffered from severe acid reflux, which caused his vocal cords to become inflamed. The diagnosis followed his slew of hits including the global smash “Pana,” penning and producing Davido’s genre-defining “If,” and receiving co-signs from the likes of Drake and Billie Eilish . The hitmaker transitioned from being one of the biggest stars to come from the continent to him considering quitting music. “Why is it the same moment I’m with Drake in the studio and I can’t sing?” the Nigerian singer-songwriter recounts to Billboard . “[Or] I’m supposed to be recording this record for Billie Eilish, Travis Scott and I’m here I can’t even sing for them. All that boiled into anger and dissatisfaction, I was sad. I don’t like using the word ‘depressed,’ but I was cooked.” Tekno’s ongoing battle with acid reflux resulted in a severe episode, where he was unable to speak for nine months, and was forced to cancel shows that totaled a loss of millions. The mental and financial turmoil pushed Tekno to search for a resolution. After numerous doctor’s visits, Tekno made the decision to get vocal cord surgery in New York in 2019. While the procedure was successful and he fully regained his voice a year later, his passion for music didn’t return with it. “I actually hated listening to music,” he admits of his post-surgery malaise. “If I heard a new artist it used to piss me off. For a while, I thought it was because I lost my voice and I couldn’t sing. But even after I got my voice back and I could sing, I was still mad…To be a good artist, you have to listen to music. Not being able to listen to music was such a dark [period].” His aversion towards music became exacerbated around the releases for his debut album Old Romance in 2020 and The More The Better in 2023. Tekno explains that the projects, especially the latter, didn’t come out of a positive place, but rather one of urgency. The More The Better was pushed out to earn his release from his contractual obligations to SoundCloud. “We were just going through label wars,” Tekno explains. “[Those projects] weren’t released from a place of happiness or excitement. It was more like, ‘Let me drop this so I can move on about my business.’ So it didn’t allow me to love the project.”  After experiencing all-consuming anger, Tekno decided he desperately needed to change his perspective and find himself again. He credits reading as one of the major keys for pulling him out of the darkness. The mindset shift led him to create his third studio album, Where Did Love Go?, released in July 2026 via Mr Eazi’s emPawa Africa. He says the project took him back to his days of being unapologetic and free-spirited in the music industry. “I didn’t care about [anything],” Tekno recalls. “I just wanted to make music. I didn’t care if the label told me ‘We like this record’ or ‘We don’t like this record.’ I’m putting it out. [They weren’t] telling me nothing.” When reflecting on the era of “Pana” that propelled his career before health challenges caused him to pause, Tekno says he has “zero mixed feelings.” Although he admits one of his few regrets is not releasing his debut album around when he was dropping hit after hit, he says he “just didn’t know any better” and had no guidance at the time. “I’m one of the opportune,” Tekno says. “At that time, it wasn’t about no algorithm. I didn’t have this huge label that put millions on my material. It was just pure love from the fans. To be among one of the few [artists] that could make a record in your bedroom and have people in Nigeria, East Africa, West Africa, Turkey, London love it. It’s such a privilege to experience that. That’s such a beautiful time in my life.” As for receiving credit for the impact he made on the rising Afrobeats scene in the 2010s, Tekno doesn’t entertain the narrative.  “For me, receiving the flowers, it’s almost like I’m doing this for you guys to tell me how amazing I am,” he emphasizes. “That’s not why I do it. I do it because I love it. And I’m among the few that is opportune to do what he loves and get to travel the world for that. I would never say I wasn’t appreciated enough and I haven’t been given my flowers. I feel like that’s just a trend that started. They give you your flowers when you’re in the grave… So while I’m alive, thriving and making history, keep them flowers, man. I’m good.” While the 2010s was a prime era for Afrobeats, Tekno believes the global genre is currently “in the best place it could possibly be.” He shares with Billboard that several of his favorite Afrobeats artists today include Burna Boy, Asake, Rema, Tems (who he calls “spiritual”), Victony, and FOLA (“Oh my God, some wild melodies, man”). Where Did Love Go? is only the beginning of Tekno’s official return to music. He confirms to Billboard that the album was just the “warm-up” and he is set to drop his next project in September 2026. As for performing, he is set to tour the UK and Australia this year including a stop in London on October 4 to celebrate Nigerian Independence Day. In addition, he has hopes to tour across Africa and the U.S. in the near future.  Tekno says he is excited to be back where it all started with his true love for the game and he’s made it clear that he’s “chasing no position with nobody in the business.” “I think when you start to only chase

articles.title: It sure seems like Falcons players want Michael Penix Jr. to start over Tua Tagovailoa
articles.summary: During a recent appearance on The Pat McAfee Show, ESPN’s Adam Schefter explained that Tua Tagovailoa did not secure the Week 1 starting role during a challenging summer in Flowery Branch. With Michael Penix being officially cleared for 11-on-11 team drills after recovering from left knee surgery
articles._body: During a recent appearance on The Pat McAfee Show, ESPN’s Adam Schefter explained that Tua Tagovailoa did not secure the Week 1 starting role during a challenging summer in Flowery Branch. With Michael Penix being officially cleared for 11-on-11 team drills after recovering from left knee surgery, the Falcons now find themselves in a genuine quarterback competition as the regular season approaches. Beyond the logistical aspects of the depth chart, the atmosphere inside the Falcons’ facility noticeably changed once Penix returned to the field. Offensive coordinator Tommy Rees spoke to reporters about the emotional boost in the locker room. According to Falcons.com digital editor Tori McElhaney, Rees highlighted , “There was a lot of joy with Michael Penix out on the field,” emphasizing that his teammates were genuinely excited to have him leading drills again. ESPN’s Marc Raimondi also reported that Rees observed: “a lot of joy for Penix to be out there yesterday, and a lot of joy from his teammates.” Additionally, Falcons team writer Will McFadden mentioned that Rees stated, “I could not be more pleased with the work that he’s put in and where he’s at mentally.” When asked by The Atlanta Journal-Constitution’s D. Orlando Ledbetter whether Penix would play in the preseason finale , Rees noted, “Really not a question for me to answer.” The overwhelming excitement from teammates aligns with evaluations from national insiders. NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport pointed out that while Atlanta initially preferred to gradually ease Penix back into action , nine months after his ACL tear, Tagovailoa’s noticeable struggles during preseason games and team practices have made a cautious approach almost impossible. If Penix demonstrates full physical readiness, it seems the locker room and coaching staff are ready to allow him to lead the offense. articles.title: Forever No. 1: Shelley Fabares, ‘Johnny Angel’
articles.summary: When she dethroned Connie Francis, it marked the first time female singers had back-to-back No. 1s on the Hot 100.
articles._body: Forever No. 1 is a Billboard series that pays special tribute to the recently deceased artists who achieved the highest honor our charts have to offer — a Billboard Hot 100 No. 1 single — by taking an extended look back at the chart-topping songs that made them part of this exclusive club. Here, we honor the late TV star Shelley Fabares, whose “Johnny Angel” reached No. 1 in April 1962. “Johnny Angel” is so innocent, so chaste, that it immediately conjures a simpler time. It has that in common with such other defining hits of the era as The Chordettes’ “Mr. Sandman” (1954) and The Teddy Bears’ “To Know Him, Is To Love Him” (1958). “Johnny Angel” is a classic “crush” song, in which the singer pines about a boy who is utterly oblivious:”Johnny Angel, how I love him/ He’s got something that I can’t resist/ But he doesn’t even know that I exist.” Related Gone But Not Forgotten: Musicians We Lost in 2026 Forever No. 1: Connie Francis, ‘My Heart Has a Mind of Its Own’ Forever No. 1: Connie Francis’ ‘Everybody’s Somebody’s Fool’ Singer and actress Shelley Fabares , who died on Sunday (Aug. 23) in Los Angeles at age 82, recorded the song in September 1961 when she was just 17. She performed it in her role as daughter Mary Stone on The Donna Reed Show in the episode (“Donna’s Prima Donna”) that aired on Feb. 1, 1962 (by which time she had turned 18). The song topped the Billboard Hot 100 two months later. Lyn Duddy and Lee Pockriss wrote “Johnny Angel,” which is distinguished by a lilting and lovely pre-chorus: “I’m in heaven, I get carried away/ I dream of him and me/ And how it’s gonna be/ Other fellas call me up for a date/ But I just sit and wait/ I’d rather concentrate/ On Johnny Angel.” The song also has a nice line in the chorus: “And I pray that someday he’ll love me/ And together we will see/ How lovely Heaven will be.” Darlene Love and her group, the Blossoms, sang backup vocals on the track. (They also sang, uncredited, on The Crystals ’ far earthier “He’s a Rebel,” which likewise topped the Hot 100 later in 1962.) Musicians who played on “Johnny Angel” include Hal Blaine on drums, Carol Kaye on bass and Glen Campbell on guitar – legends all. It wasn’t Fabares’ idea to make records. The decision was forced on her. Reed’s husband, Tony Owen, produced The Donna Reed Show , which ran for eight seasons (1958-66). During the 1961-62 season, Owen decided to follow the lead of another long-running family series, The Adventures of Ozzie and Harriet (1952-1966), which saw its ratings jump when younger son Ricky Nelson performed his pop hits on the series. During the run of the show, two of Nelson’s hits, “Poor Little Fool” (1958) and “Travelin’ Man” (1961), reached No. 1 on the Hot 100. Owen told Fabares and Paul Petersen, who played her younger brother Jeff on the series, that they would record pop tunes to perform on the series. Note that he didn’t ask them if they’d like to do this. Petersen jumped at the chance. “I was friends with Ricky Nelson,” he told Susan King in a 2011 interview in The Los Angeles Times . “He was having fun. The girls were screaming. He drove a fast car. I was like, give me some of that…” Fabares wasn’t nearly as sure that this was the right move for her. “I remember saying, ‘Mr. Owen, Paul can do it,” she told King. “He can do anything.’ Maybe a month later, he came up to me one day and said, ‘Hey, kid. Do you like being on the show? Do you want to be on next year?’ Not seeing the train heading directly toward me, I said, ‘Oh, yes, Mr. Owen. I do.’ Then he said, ‘Sing.’” Both young performers signed contracts with Colpix Records, which was the record arm of Screen Gems, which produced the TV show. Both singers’ debut singles entered the Hot 100 in the week ending March 3, 1962: Fabares’ “Johnny Angel” at No. 81 and Petersen’s “She Can’t Find Her Keys” not far behind at No. 90. Fabares’ hit quickly surged ahead. It shot to No. 50 in its second week and No. 28 in its third. “Johnny Angel” reached No. 1 for the week ending April 7, 1962, in just its sixth week on the chart. When it dislodged Connie Francis ’ “Don’t Break the Heart That Loves You” from the top spot, it marked the first time since the Hot 100 launched in 1958 that female artists appeared at No. 1 back-to-back. (Francis, the top female singer of that era, died in July 2025 at age 87.) “Johnny Angel” remained No. 1 for two weeks before ceding the top spot to Elvis Presley ’s “Good Luck Charm.” Fun Fact: Fabares went on to co-star alongside Presley in three films: Girl Happy (1965), Spinout (1966) and Clambake (1967). Fabares’ recording was also heard in a later episode of the Reed show that aired on May 17, 1962. It soundtracked a scene where the boys are in the malt shop. (It really was a more innocent time.) Fabares lip-synched her hit on  American Bandstand  during a June 19, 1962 appearance. Fabares wasn’t much of a singer, but her lack of training may have worked in her favor on “Johnny Angel.” There’s an innocence and guilelessness in her vocal that made it more relatable and accessible. Lee Pockriss, who co-wrote “Johnny Angel,” had a hand in writing numerous hits from the 1950s to the 1970s, including Perry Como’s “Catch a Falling Star” (which hit No. 1 on a pre-Hot 100 songs chart in Billboard in 1958), Brian Hyland’s “Itsy Bitsy Teenie Weenie Yellow Polkadot Bikini” (No. 1 on the Hot 100 in 1960), Anita Bryant’s “In My Little Corner of the World,” The Cuff Links’ “Tracy” and Clint Holmes’ “Playground in My Mind” (No. 2 in 1973). Stu Phillips produced and arranged Fabares’ recording. Phillips had a long career, producing hits for James Darren, Nina Simone, The Skyliners and The Monkees, in addition to Fabares. He later segued into composing theme songs for TV series including McCloud, Battlestar Galactica and Knight Rider . In 2002, Phillips published his autobiography, Stu Who?: Forty Year

articles.title: Mike McCarthy’s 6-QB bar on Steelers’ 53-man roster drama
articles.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers are currently gearing up for their preseason finale, which will take place on Thursday against the Buffalo Bills. The Steelers are coming off an ugly home loss to the New York Jets, in a game in which quarterback Will Howard struggled mightily to get anything going. The St
articles._body: The Pittsburgh Steelers are currently gearing up for their preseason finale, which will take place on Thursday against the Buffalo Bills. The Steelers are coming off an ugly home loss to the New York Jets, in a game in which quarterback Will Howard struggled mightily to get anything going. The Steelers are still trying to figure out what their final QB depth chart will look like heading into the season, and recently, head coach Mike McCarthy weighed in on the debate. “I’d keep six QBs in the building if it worked,” said McCarthy, per Mike DeFabo of The Athletic on X, formerly Twitter. The quote comes amid speculation that the Steelers could have four quarterbacks on their final 53-man roster this year, including Howard, rookie Drew Allar, veteran Mason Rudolph, and starter Aaron Rodgers. Rudolph is expected to earn the primary backup role behind Rodgers this year, with both Howard and Allar vying for the third spot on the roster. Keeping four quarterbacks on the roster is a rarity in today’s NFL, but if the Steelers see enough to like about both Howard and Allar, they could opt to keep both around as opposed to letting them potentially be scooped up by another team in free agency. Meanwhile, Steelers fans are hoping that the backup quarterback debate is an afterthought this year, assuming Rodgers can stay healthy and productive in his age-42 season. Rodgers and McCarthy are hoping to rekindle the magic of their days together with the Green Bay Packers this year. The Steelers’ regular season is slated to kick off on September 13 vs the Atlanta Falcons at home. The post Mike McCarthy’s 6-QB bar on Steelers’ 53-man roster drama appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles.title: The ‘most important challenge’ Mike Babcock faces to get Oilers over Stanley Cup hump
articles.summary: The Edmonton Oilers have had a lot of success in recent years, but the club still searches for an elusive Stanley Cup title. Mike Babcock is taking over head coaching duties for the team. A new report argues he faces a tough challenge as he looks to end the team’s Stanley Cup drought. ̶
articles._body: The Edmonton Oilers have had a lot of success in recent years, but the club still searches for an elusive Stanley Cup title. Mike Babcock is taking over head coaching duties for the team. A new report argues he faces a tough challenge as he looks to end the team’s Stanley Cup drought. “Reshaping the Oilers’ defensive identity is easily the single most important on-ice challenge Babcock faces. He has already made his desire for a cohesive, five-man defensive system clear, which will require more buy-in from the forward group. Centres, including McDavid and Draisaitl, will likely be expected to track lower in the defensive zone and break out as a single unit,” The Athletic reported. Babcock could end up adjusting his lineups for the upcoming campaign. “We also know from Babcock’s time in Toronto how much he likes a lefty-righty configuration for his defence pairs. This wasn’t a hard-and-fast rule, but he made his displeasure for same-handedness pairs well known. The complementary setup is intended to prevent defenders from being handcuffed and improve the success rate of their outlet passes,” the outlet added. Babcock has had success in the NHL, but he has also caused some controversy. He briefly had the job as head coach of the Columbus Blue Jackets a few years ago, but stepped down after questions were raised about how he treated players. The Oilers made the Stanley Cup Playoffs during the 2025-26 season. Edmonton lost to the Anaheim Ducks in a playoff series. Edmonton also reached the Stanley Cup Final in 2024 and 2025. Babcock replaced Kris Knoblauch as the Oilers head coach . Knoblauch was fired by the team, after their 2025-26 season ended. Edmonton last won the Stanley Cup in 1990. The franchise has five Stanley Cup titles. The post The ‘most important challenge’ Mike Babcock faces to get Oilers over Stanley Cup hump appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles._body: The Chicago Cubs dominated the Arizona Diamondbacks on Monday night. There were some tense moments in the game, as the Diamondbacks thought Cubs third base coach Quintin Berry was trying to look into Merrill Kelly’s glove . Kelly was clear after the game; he believed the Cubs were doing something nefarious , per Matt Ehalt of the New York Post. “Stealing signs is as old as baseball. I think it’s a little bulls–t when it comes from a coach,” Kelly said. ““If it’s a guy on second base and they see a grip in your glove or if the hitters can see something you’re doing with your glove, I think that’s fair game. I think guys have been doing that since the beginning of baseball. I think it’s a little bush league when it comes from outside that. I think inside the lines is one thing, I think the guys that are standing outside the lines I think it’s a little bush league.” Kelly went five and two-thirds innings in the game, giving up five hits, three walks, and three runs in the loss. “That was probably the most egregious I’ve seen from coaches,” Kelly added. “Everyone in this game is trying to get an edge wherever they can. Definitely not the first time a coach has relayed signs, but I think in that situation I think it should stay between the players.” After the game and Kelly’s tirade, fans went after Kelly. articles.title: Tiger Woods’ immediate reaction to radical postseason, PGA Tour Championship overhaul
articles.summary: Tiger Woods has already made his feelings clear about the PGA Tour’s dramatic postseason changes. Beginning in 2028, the Tour Championship will feature a 32-player field competing in head-to-head match play across two weeks and two different courses. The overhaul represents a significant departur
articles._body: Tiger Woods has already made his feelings clear about the PGA Tour’s dramatic postseason changes. Beginning in 2028, the Tour Championship will feature a 32-player field competing in head-to-head match play across two weeks and two different courses. The overhaul represents a significant departure from the traditional season-ending format. 32 players. Two weeks. Head-to-head. Match play returns to the @PGATOUR at the 2028 TOUR Championship. pic.twitter.com/1zZbnjPuO6 — TOUR Championship (@TOURChamp) August 25, 2026 Woods welcomed the announcement and emphasized that the PGA Tour’s finale should match the significance of the regular season. “The conclusion of the season should be worthy of the journey it takes to get there. Today’s announcement is a result of the hard work and passion of our players. Excited to usher in a new era of match play on the PGA Tour.” Woods also credited the players who helped develop the new format and expressed excitement about bringing match play back into the PGA Tour spotlight. The changes should create a different kind of postseason drama. Instead of players spending four rounds chasing a position on the leaderboard, the new format will place competitors directly against one another. That structure could produce compelling matchups between golf’s biggest stars while making each round feel more consequential. Extending the event across two weeks and multiple courses should also give the season finale a larger stage. By this time, LIV players could be back on Tour . Not everyone will embrace the change. Some fans will question whether match play appropriately rewards players who excel throughout the season, while others may prefer the familiarity of a traditional tournament. The new format will not debut until 2028, but the message is already clear: The PGA Tour wants its season finale to feel bigger, bolder and more unpredictable. Tiger Woods is ready for it. articles._body: Fans may have to keep waiting to see The Rock vs. Roman Reigns , as the filming of Fast Forever may affect its WWE WrestleMania 43 status . It was recently announced that Fast Forever will begin filming in December 2026. Fast Forever is the 11th and last installment in the Fast & Furious saga. That means The Rock and other actors will likely be busy for months making the movie. Dave Meltzer of the Wrestling Observer reports that the dream match happening in 2027 is “very unlikely.” “Because that movie is gonna take months to film, if he is in it, which he is scheduled to be in it, that him doing a match at WrestleMania would be out the window,” Meltzer said. “I mean, could he fly to Saudi Arabia and show up? Of course. Of course he could, and he could always do that.” Money talks, and it was reported that Saudi Arabia was set to offer the “Final Boss” a massive payday to wrestle at WrestleMania 43. Meltzer knows that a big offer could change things, but he’s unsure if he would have the time to train while making Fast Forever. And The Rock isn’t likely going to compete without training. “He has too much pride, if that’s the right word, to go out there and half-a*s it,” he explained. “I mean, the one thing that you could say is every time he came back, he trained his a*s off.” Will The Rock vs. Roman Reigns finally happen at WWE WrestleMania 43 in Saudi Arabia? Joe Camporeale-Imagn Images. Ultimately, Meltzer doesn’t envision him doing the long-awaited dream match. However, he did concede that he could see The Rock “showing up for an appearance. However, it wouldn’t be to face Reigns. The Rock has made some sporadic appearances since his last match at WrestleMania 40. He played a role in John Cena’s heel turn last year. A match against Reigns has been teased for over a decade. If WWE were ever going to do it, WrestleMania 43 feels like one of the last chances to make it happen. articles.title: NHL Moving Closer to Expansion in Thriving Sun Belt Market
articles.summary: David Kirouac-Imagn Images
articles._body: Even without a broad, formalized process in place, the prospect of NHL expansion is heating up across multiple markets. As the league approaches the start of its 2026–27 regular season, several developments are emerging to push the NHL closer to its 33rd team, and a possible 34th one eventually. Among the recent events: The NHL is aiming to debut a second Texas team for the 2029–30 season to join the existing Stars, who are moving to Plano . The league in June reached an agreement with billionaire Dan Friedkin to explore expansion to either Houston or Austin. Houston remains the more likely choice, NHL deputy commissioner Bill Daly said last week during a European media tour: “We hope to have definitive agreements in place that would commit the franchise as early as December this year.” The Alpharetta, Georgia, city council voted 4–3 Monday night to rezone the Atlanta suburb’s North Point Mall to allow a mixed-use development that would support a NHL franchise. The vote doesn’t guarantee the league will place a franchise in the market, but it was a necessary step to allow an arena project to occur there. Like many sports-oriented developments, the Alpharetta project is inspired in part by The Battery created by the neighboring MLB Braves. “I absolutely believe the NHL is coming to Atlanta,” said Alpharetta city councilman John Hipes, one of the “yes” votes. The metro Phoenix area, a market left behind when the then-Coyotes franchise moved to Utah and ultimately became the Mammoth , is still part of ongoing deliberations by the league—though without the ownership-level or local political developments seen thus far in Texas or metro Atlanta. The Atlanta situation, however, is still somewhat muddled. Beyond the Alpharetta effort, there is a competing proposal in nearby Forsyth County that already has an approved local plan . These developments also continue to burnish the league’s already powerful presence across the U.S. Sun Belt . Teams from that region have claimed the past four Stanley Cup titles, and six of the past seven, including the Hurricanes this past season . It is not critical that the NHL bring in expansion clubs in even pairs. There was a four-year gap between the 2017 arrival of the Golden Knights, the league’s 31st team, and the Kraken’s 2021 beginning as the 32nd franchise. articles._body: Canaster is a canvas based visual workspace (think high performance hierarchical miro board). I had a particular vision for workspace I wanted where I can put my documents including pdfs/markdowns/tables/checklists in a visual hierarichal workspace. I started with a DOM based approach but that quickly hit its limits of responsiveness in terms on interaction, so i built this one with webgl and my main priority was a consistent 120+ fps rendering (you can see the fps number by clicking the (i) icon in the bottom right, the other buttons there are for refit/rearrange panels). You can drop pdfs/markdown files as it is organize them. Each 'panel' can the canvas can be maximised to interact with it and can inline edit with double clicking. You can also embed other websites (the ones which allow it) Workbooks can be private or public. Here are a bunch of documents I have created as a demo https://canaster.in/d/naruto-casefiles/how-come-these-three-... https://canaster.in/d/admin/thirty-six-views-one-mountain--0... (ps, documents have original images which can be large and depending on your location might be slow to load since its running on a single server in 1 location) there are more things I am adding like email to a workbook (each account gets their own email account @canaster.in) and can connect panes to each other (have not created a good demo for it yet) you can switch dark/light theme, and can set image for the panel/canvas background as well (cmd/ctrl + k to bring up the command menu). canaster is optimized for usage on mobile as well. https://x.com/phparth/status/2077397341674627470 (a screen recording from past when it was in dev) Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49436551 Points: 2 # Comments: 0

He’s a bully, and his career in college is about to go down in flames.” Finebaum pointed toward the turnover surrounding Belichick’s program as a major reason for his pessimism. General manager Michael Lombardi is no longer with North Carolina, while Belichick’s son, Steve, also departed the Tar Heels after serving as defensive coordinator. “It is mass chaos in Chapel Hill, and I don’t believe they’ll win this game in Ireland, and I don’t think Bill Belichick is going to survive until the end of the season,” Finebaum added, regarding their showdown with TCU on Saturday. Of course, Belichick’s legacy in football is already secure. He won six Super Bowls as head coach of the New England Patriots, building one of the greatest dynasties in professional sports history alongside Tom Brady. Still, Finebaum believes Belichick’s decision to enter the college ranks has damaged the final chapter of his coaching career. He argued the 74-year-old only landed at North Carolina because another NFL opportunity never materialized. “He couldn’t accept that nobody in the NFL wanted him anymore,” Finebaum pointed out. “And because he is Bill Belichick, and he knows more than anybody, even though we all now know that it was Tom Brady who led him to all those Super Bowl championships. Brady proved that the second he got out of there.” Alas, Finebaum believes Belichick went to North Carolina intending to prove he could dominate another level of football. Instead, he believes the experiment has become a disaster. “He’s one of the worst college football coaches in a short period of time I have ever seen,” Finebaum concluded. “And I see no way this is going to be a successful landing or ending for Belichick.” It’s hardly the first time Finebaum has questioned Belichick’s future. Back in July , Finebaum said Belichick’s “college future” was at stake during the 2026 campaign. North Carolina entered the season facing modest expectations, with ESPN projecting the Tar Heels to finish 15th in the ACC. At the time, Finebaum stopped short of predicting Belichick would be fired, instead suggesting retirement might be the best option. One month later, his outlook has become even more pessimistic. North Carolina’s season has yet to begin, but Finebaum is already predicting Belichick won’t be around to see how it ends. Whether that becomes the case remains to be seen, but there’s a ton riding on this season for the iconic head coach.

articles.title: Show HN: Searching for optimal strategies in a puzzle game with chance (Drop7)
articles.summary: Sixteen years ago, I wrote a Java program which tried to pick the ideal move in a puzzle game called Drop7. On each turn, the player only has seven choices for their next move, but there is also an element of chance which turns this simple game into a surprisingly difficult problem involving sear
articles._body: Sixteen years ago, I wrote a Java program which tried to pick the ideal move in a puzzle game called Drop7. On each turn, the player only has seven choices for their next move, but there is also an element of chance which turns this simple game into a surprisingly difficult problem involving search, hidden information, long-term planning, and chance. I renewed my investigation this weekend, into whether there is an autonomous strategy that averages more than one million points per game. An experienced human player can score a million points with long-term strategic thinking, but the best automated strategies I could come up with are currently averaging around 300k-400k points. One of the easiest ways to contribute to advancing this research is to compete on the global leaderboard and submit your human strategy - https://drop7.dev/compete . This project has also been an enlightening experiment into using agents as research collaborators and evidence collectors. Repository: https://github.com/keshavsaharia/drop7-bench I’d especially appreciate feedback from people who are knowledgeable in game theory, stochastic planning, learned value functions, or heavy-tailed evaluation. How would you approach long-horizon action ranking here? I’d also love to hear whether the research makes sense to someone encountering the project for the first time. articles.title: Lab supply companies have been selling antibodies using manipulated images
articles.summary: Image changes that would get a paper retracted are widespread among suppliers.
articles._body: Antibodies play a central role in your body's immune defense. But they're also nearly ubiquitous in biological research, being essential for several widely used lab techniques. While some researchers need to go through the process of producing their own antibodies, antibodies to many key proteins are commercially available and can be ordered for overnight delivery. In May, however, Reese Richardson, a post-doc at Northwestern University, discovered that some of the images used to demonstrate how these antibodies performed in lab experiments had been subject to image manipulation —the sorts of changes that would get a paper retracted if they had appeared in the academic literature. The manipulations ranged from removing background noise to copying and pasting data to fabricate results. Now, he has done a more exhaustive search and found problematic manipulations in images used to market over 17,000 commercial antibodies. Antibodies are useful in the lab because the immune system generates them to recognize specific proteins. While those proteins typically appear on the surface of pathogens, the immune system doesn't know where a given protein it encounters comes from. So, if you inject an animal with your protein of interest, it will typically generate antibodies to recognize that. Read full article Comments

articles._body: The Alabama Crimson Tide received bad news on Monday after five-star freshman Jireh Edwards suffered an arm injury during practice. He was forced to undergo surgery on his right arm. While the news is less than ideal, Tuesday’s reports provide a silver lining for the situation. Edwards, who is a Maryland native, was informed that despite undergoing surgery, there is a belief that he will return well before the end of the 2026-27 campaign , according to Matt Zenitz of CBS Sports. Alabama is optimistic and hopes he can return early in the season. “Good news on Alabama five-star freshman defensive back Jireh Edwards, who suffered an arm injury in practice yesterday,” Zenitz said. “Despite needing to undergo surgery to repair the injury, there’s optimism he’ll end up being able to return early in the season, sources tell CBS Sports.” Jireh Edwards is a 6-foot-2, 218 lbs safety who committed to Alabama in July 2025. The Crimson Tide has a loaded secondary, and now, due to the injury, Edwards may not see much playing time at all in his first year in college. Head coach Kalen DeBoer has two safety’s in the starting positions who are both seniors: Bray Hubbard and Keon Sabb. While Edwards may not play a whole lot in Year 1 at Alabama, he brings strong depth to a deep roster. Additionally, if he can heal from the surgery sooner rather than later, he can jump back into training as a safety, furthering his development for future years. While Jireh Edwards works his way back from injury, Alabama will focus on the upcoming season . The Crimson Tide are scheduled to kickoff the new campaign with a Week 1 home opener against the East Carolina Pirates. Throughout training camp and preseason games, Joe Milton III and veteran free-agent
articles._body: The Dallas Cowboys enter the 2026 season with their core starting players firmly in place, but a captivating competition remains unresolved for the backup quarterback position behind franchise player Dak Prescott. Throughout training camp and preseason games, Joe Milton III and veteran free-agent signing Sam Howell have competed intensely for the role. According to ESPN’s Todd Archer, Milton has distinguished himself on the field by showcasing remarkable arm talent , sharp poise, and command. He has accumulated 286 passing yards, three passing touchdowns, and a rushing touchdown in two turnover-free appearances. This impressive performance has garnered national attention, with FOX Sports highlighting Milton as their “favorite watch of the preseason” and suggesting that his sudden rise should make the decision on Dallas’ QB2 role straightforward. While head coach Brian Schottenheimer stated on DallasCowboys.com that he is not in a hurry to finalize the depth chart before Friday’s exhibition finale against the New Orleans Saints, he openly praised Milton’s refined nuance and ball placement. Schottenheimer pointed out that Milton has evolved well beyond just having a strong arm, emphasizing his touch on a double-move touchdown pass to Jonathan Mingo, a scramble throw to Camden Brown, and a delicate flip pass to Malik Davis, which demonstrated veteran restraint instead of relying on overpowering velocity. This steady maturation signifies a significant transformation in Milton’s reputation. Speaking with beat reporter Clarence Hill Jr. on X, Schottenheimer remarked that Milton has shed his previous label as a one-dimensional , raw passer: “He was once known as a strong-arm QB who could throw it a long distance: ‘Go to the fair, win a teddy bear.’ It takes much more to play quarterback. Milton is demonstrating that now.” With Milton combining exceptional physical tools with newfound pocket discipline, Dallas may already have its definitive backup plan secured. articles.title: NFL Will Continue Strict Taunting Crackdown in 2026
articles.summary: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect
articles._body: The NFL will continue to stress strict enforcement of its sportsmanship-related rules by its on-field officials this season. That means the officials will be expected to keep a close eye on players violating the league’s rules prohibiting taunting opponents, illegal celebrations and fighting, at the behest of the NFL’s competition committee. The approach was confirmed to Front Office Sports by a source familiar with the views of the NFL and competition committee. The league also cited that stance last week when it fined the Cowboys and Saints $500,000 each for their actions during a fight-marred joint practice. “The Competition Committee has made sportsmanship–including at joint practices–a point of emphasis over the past several years,” the NFL said in a written statement announcing the Cowboys and Saints fines. “All clubs were reminded by memo prior to training camp of their responsibility in preventing unsportsmanlike behavior at joint practices that has the potential to result in injury.” There were 28 taunting penalties called league-wide last season. That was up from 21 such penalties in the 2024 season; 18 in 2023; and 22 in 2022, though players were warned about the taunting rules before the 2025 season started. The recent high came with 61 taunting penalties called in the 2021 season. Taunting violations and illegal celebrations are 15-yard penalties. NFL team owners approved a proposal by the competition committee this offseason to allow instant replay officials at the league’s game-day officiating center in New York to intervene to eject a player for a flagrant football or non-football act not spotted by the on-field officials. The NFL is slated to give teams an update on competition committee and officiating matters during Wednesday afternoon’s special league meeting in Atlanta, at which the owners are expected to ratify the $9.612 billion sale of the Seahawks . The focus on sportsmanship as a point of emphasis for the officials is not new this season. The NFL said last August that it would be a point of emphasis in 2025. “It’s just one of those areas that the league wants to work actively on,” Walt Anderson, the NFL’s officiating rules analyst, said then during a video news conference. “There are plenty of ways for players to be able to celebrate. And they come up with some very unique and often entertaining ways. So we want them to focus on those and not the inappropriate areas.” Troy Vincent, the NFL’s executive vice president of football operations, addressed the issue in a video sent to teams ahead of last season. “The sportsmanship is a point of emphasis and clarification for the players and the clubs this year,” Anderson said last August. “I know Troy addressed this in the annual video that all of the clubs see during training camp from the standpoint of our taunting was up [in 2024]…. Unsportsmanlike gestures, whether they were either simulating either shooting a gun or brandishing of a gun or inappropriate gestures like a throat-slash or unfortunate sexual gestures that were made, those were up almost 133 percent.… The officials have made it a point of emphasis to all of the clubs.” The NFL once was derided by some as the “No Fun League” for cracking down on player celebrations. It has attempted to strike a balance between allowing players to celebrate but issuing 15-yard penalties for demonstrations aimed at opponents or containing violent or offensive gestures. “At this level of competition emotions will run high, but no amount of emotion should give way to demeaning and offensive words, taunting, or other non-football acts,” the league wrote in a memo to teams just ahead of the playoffs to conclude the 2024 season. “No one wants a penalty, or a player ejection, to determine the outcome of a game.” The post NFL Will Continue Strict Taunting Crackdown in 2026 appeared first on Front Office Sports .

articles.title: PGA Tour Not Offering Another Lifeline to LIV Players Just Yet
articles.summary: Kyle Terada-Imagn Images
articles._body: ATLANTA — With LIV Golf’s future in limbo following the conclusion of its 2026 season, there remains no clear-cut path for any of the league’s players to potentially return to the PGA Tour. “Rules matter,” PGA Tour CEO Brian Rolapp said Tuesday at his pre-tournament press conference ahead of this week’s Tour Championship. And “rules only matter if they’re enforced,” Rolapp added during his address to media and tour stakeholders inside the clubhouse at East Lake Golf Club. LIV players have been banned from the PGA Tour since the league launched in 2022, with most facing at least a one-year suspension dating back to the most recent LIV event they played in. Five-time major champion Brooks Koepka bucked that trend when he re-joined the PGA Tour in January—just five months after completing his fourth LIV season—as the first and so far only member of the PGA Tour’s Returning Member Program , which Rolapp at the time described as a “one-time, defined window” with “no promise” it would be available again. “Currently there’s no current plans for a Returning Member Program like you saw earlier this year,” Rolapp said. Koepka was one of four LIV players eligible for that, alongside Jon Rahm, Bryson DeChambeau, and Cam Smith. DeChambeau and Smith are among the most pro-LIV players, while Rahm is widely seen as being ready to leave the league. “I don’t know the future of LIV,” Rolapp said. “It sounds like they’re working really hard to come up with the next iteration of it. We’ve been consistent. Anyone who’s interested in coming to the PGA Tour needs to demonstrate that they are relieved of their contractual commitments or any tail obligations they might have in that legacy model. Brooks certainly did that, and until then, we weren’t really able to consider anything seriously. I would say the same thing here.” Rahm has multiple years remaining on his LIV contract, but could come to terms on a buyout offer this fall. DeChambeau’s contract with LIV expired after the 2026 season. Earning It on the Course While Rolapp acknowledged that fans “want to see the best golfers competing week in and week out,” he said meritocracy will be key for shaping the PGA Tour moving forward, with or without any former LIV members. “Every player, whether they’re already here or they’re trying to be here, they’re going to earn a place based on their performance and on their success,” Rolapp said. The PGA Tour is moving to a two-track model in 2028 with a top-tier Championship Series with $20 million-plus purse events and a second-tier Challenger Series with prize money no less than $4 million per tournament. The 2027 PGA Tour season will be key in shaping who lands on which circuit the following year. Playing on the DP World Tour in 2027 and earning potential promotion to the PGA Tour in 2028 could be a potential option for some former LIV players, if they end their affiliation with the league. articles.title: Former Pitt Baseball Standout Jim Negrych Returns to Program
articles.summary: Pitt baseball head coach Mike Bell is bringing a former Panther standout back to the program. The Pitt baseball program announced on Tuesday that former Forever Panther Jim Negrych has been hired as an assistant coach and the teams new recruiting coordinator. Negrych will be working with Panther&#82
articles._body: Pitt baseball head coach Mike Bell is bringing a former Panther standout back to the program. The Pitt baseball program announced on Tuesday that former Forever Panther Jim Negrych has been hired as an assistant coach and the teams new recruiting coordinator. Negrych will be working with Panther’s hitters and infielders in addition to his recruiting duties. Prior to this hiring, Negrych was working as a Northeast Area Scout for the St. Louis Cardinals. “My family and I could not be more excited to be back at Pitt,” said Negrych. “This university and program mean so much to us. I’m looking forward to bringing a championship caliber team to Pitt.” “As we like to say – Once a Panther, Always a Panther, Bell said. “Jimmy’s historical track record as a player in the collegiate and professional ranks speaks for itself, but what he has accomplished as a scout over the last nine years gives him a unique skill st that is very beneficial in today’s world of college athletics. We are extremely excited to welcome Jimmy and his family back to the Steel City.” During his playing career at Pitt (2004-06), Negrych was a three-time All-American, three-time All-Big East selection and the 2004 Big East Rookie of the Year. He was a First team All-American and First Team All-Big East player in both 2005 and 2006. In his career at Pitt, Negrych batted .374 with 213 hits, 48 doubles, 34 home runs and 164 RBIs. In terms of ranking within the Panther program, Negrych ranks second all-time in RBIs, third in home runs and total bases, fifth in doubles and sixth in batting average. After entering the 2006 MLB Draft, Negrych was drafted by the Pittsburgh Pirates in the sixth round. He went on to be named their Minor League Player of the Year, a High-A All-Star and the Tops Carolina League Player of the Year in 2008. Following his time with the Pirates, Negrych played in the Florida, Washington and Toronto organizations. A career highlight was being named to the Triple-A All-Star teams in both 2012 and 2013. In eight seasons of minor league baseball, Negrych batted .296 with 811 hits, 417 runs scored, 353 RBIs, 158 doubles and 32 home runs in 796 career games. After retiring from minor league baseball, Negrych returned to Pitt for two seasons as a volunteer assistant coach in 2016 and 2017.
