articles.title: Show HN: CanvasForMusic – I made a free Spotify Canvas maker that doesn't suck
articles.summary:
Hello I know most of you are devs, but if you also make music, this is for you.

I've been on a hunt lately of finding tools for artists centred around promoting and posting music and rebuilding them with more intention. If it helps me promote my own music easier, it will surely help others too.
articles._body: Hello I know most of you are devs, but if you also make music, this is for you. I've been on a hunt lately of finding tools for artists centred around promoting and posting music and rebuilding them with more intention. If it helps me promote my own music easier, it will surely help others too. Recently, I was having a look around at the top search ranking Spotify Canvas Maker tools for artists and found that they all sucked. They produced generic looking canvas videos using stock images or stock videos and didn't really have any options that actually looked decent to add to your song on Spotify. It's a small detail but you may as well just leave the static cover art on the song rather than have a corny looking canvas on Spotify. I'm a big fan of getting more quality out into the world, easier. Not just more quantity. There was already too much slop and low effort tools in the creative world, well before AI entered the picture. The idea was to make it as low friction as possible for the artist and let them use assets they already have for the release. The user will add their artwork for the release, then they can choose between a Vinyl rotating preset or a crop & zoom preset that makes their artwork a bit more interesting by bouncing around the image. I might add another but for now these are a good starting point. I built it in under a day, mainly because I was able to leverage what I had already built with BeatVisualiser (a music visualiser product of mine) and brought over the vinyl animation and in browser rendering process. This was an easy choice for me as I just needed to take something I've already built on my app and repurpose it and it lets an artist get a Canvas video per Spotify's required specs quick and easy, no strings attached, no faffing about in After Effects or video editors and it also doubles as a natural upsell into my music visualiser app. I made sure to get looping figured out on the Vinyl preset by locking the variable speeds to only be loop friendly for the 8 second limit. Certain rotating speeds left a visible break in the animation which looked ugly. Completely free to use, no sign up or anything. Cheers! All 32 of the five-star recruits in the 2027 cycle — according to the Rivals Industry Ranking — have made their college commitments and remain off the board, as of Aug. 25. Last month, we saw Five-Star Plus+ cornerback John Meredith reclassify up to the 2026 cycle and join Texas early, while five-star CB A’mir Sears reclassified up to 2027 and made his commitment to Miami . Rivals takes a look at the 32 five-star prospects in the cycle, as of Aug. 25, with football season officially here. The Rivals Industry Ranking is a proprietary algorithm that compiles ratings and rankings from all three primary recruiting media services. The Rivals Industry Ranking is the industry’s most advanced, complete, and unbiased measurement. It equally weights the primary recruiting media services as follows: Rivals (33%), 247Sports (33%), and ESPN (33%). 1. DL  Jalen Brewster  — Texas Tech Rivals300 Ranking: No. 1 247Sports: No. 5 ESPN: No. 1 School: Buford (Ga.) Scouting Summary : “Uber-athletic defensive line prospect with true game-wrecking ability. Measured in at around 6-foot-3, 300 pounds prior to his junior season. Tests as an elite athlete in the combine setting, easily cracking 5.0 seconds in the 40-yard dash. Carries that athleticism over to the field where he has flashes of dominance on Friday nights. Dangerous pass rusher from any spot. Combines explosive get-off with the movement skills of a much smaller player, carrying elite testing numbers directly onto the field. …Consistently collapses pockets and disrupts plays before they develop. Has legitimate game-wrecking moments on film. The quickness to dart into the backfield and the speed to hunt down ball carriers is eye-popping. May not possess premier length. Father was a third-round pick by the Dallas Cowboys. Tracking as the top defensive line prospect early on in the 2027 cycle with the upside to be an early NFL Draft pick.” 2. IOL Maxwell Hiller — Florida Rivals300 Ranking: No. 6 247Sports: No. 2 ESPN: No. 3 School: Coatesville (Pa.) Scouting Summary : “Elite interior offensive line prospect with ready-to-play size, athleticism, and physicality. Measured in at around 6-foot-5, 305 pounds as a junior. Arm length checks in at 32 inches or a shade under. Registers as a plus athlete in the combine setting. A dominant run blocker on Friday nights. A fluid, reactive mover at the second level. Locks on defenders and imposes his will. Not uncommon to see him drive defensive linemen to the sideline. Plays with an innate edge and level of physicality. Has the movement skills to project as a high-level pass protector. …High level of coordination leads to a natural technical acuity with advanced hand placement and usage. Has the movement skills to play some tackle at the college level, but lack of arm length will ultimately force him inside. Also plays basketball. His younger brother, Colton Hiller, is a five-star basketball prospect in the 2028 cycle. Has a strong case as the most ready-to-play interior offensive line prospect in the 2027 cycle and could be primed for an instant impact at the college level.” 3. EDGE David Jacobs — Ohio State Rivals300 Ranking: No. 12 247Sports: No. 1 ESPN: No. 2 School: Blessed Trinity Catholic (Ga.) Possesses the play strength and athleticism to develop into a dominant three-down defender at the next level that can stand up or play with his hand in the dirt along the defensive front.” 4. articles.title: New bootloader lets you take the "Meta" out of the original Meta Quest
articles.summary: Privilege escalation attack grants "full control" and freedom from Meta's servers/apps.
articles._body: Remember the original Quest headset that Meta (then Oculus) trumpeted back in 2019 ? Meta seems to hope you don't, since the company officially stopped supporting the wireless VR headset in 2023 to focus on the more popular Quests 2 and 3 . However, tinkerers haven't abandoned the hardware and recently released a new root-access exploit and bootloader that gives "developers and enthusiasts full control over Quest 1 hardware." The QuestStack project integrates previously known vulnerabilities in the Quest's Android fastboot process into a privilege escalation chain that leads easily to full root access on the device. The bootloading process is now streamlined enough that it can be completed without any downloads through a web interface after connecting the headset to a PC. With this exploit, the original Quest hardware can now be officially divorced from any reliance on Meta's servers or services to be useful. That means enterprising Quest owners should be able to sideload apps without needing to register for a Meta Developer account and activating Developer Mode through Meta's mobile app . It also means users should be able to go through the initial setup and login steps for a fresh Quest headset even if and when Meta decides to shut down the servers that currently support this process. articles.title: Paul Finebaum, Booger McFarland question if Deion Sanders can have success at Colorado in current era
articles.summary: ESPN’s Paul Finebaum and Booger McFarland questioned if Deion Sanders could have additional success at Colorado in this era of college football. Going into Year 4 in Boulder, Sanders has certainly moved the needle and had a breakthrough 2024 season. But sandwiched in between that 9-4 season were sea
articles._body: ESPN’s Paul Finebaum and Booger McFarland questioned if Deion Sanders could have additional success at Colorado in this era of college football. Going into Year 4 in Boulder, Sanders has certainly moved the needle and had a breakthrough 2024 season. But sandwiched in between that 9-4 season were seasons of four and three wins. While Sanders was immensely successful at Jackson State , he set the expectations high when he arrived at Colorado and despite the national conversation, the buzz about them has certainly fizzled compared to Years 1 and 2. $19.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage McFarland chalked it up to Sanders being in the wrong era as a college football coach. If this were the old school, actual amateur era, perhaps Sanders could have Colorado running the Big 12. “Deion has been a phenomenal coach going back to high school, he was brought from Jackson State to Colorado to reinvigorate a program to make Colorado more notable,” McFarland said on First Take . “He’s done that, but now can he go to the next level? Can he take Colorado and have them competing in the Big 12? I think it’s going to be really tough. This is a new era, and this new era isn’t about who’s coaching; it’s about how much money you’re spending. If this were 15 years ago, when the college players were more connected to who primetime Deion Sanders was, I think Deion could recruit on the level of Nick Saban.” Finebaum added that’s why Saban ultimately left college football: he foresaw the drastic changes coming to the sport. Sanders’ window to be highly successful at Colorado is certainly not closed, but it’s still a difficult path. “Deion in the right circumstance could work,” Finebaum said. “Unfortunately, Booger is correct. He won’t put up with all this stuff, and that’s why he’s struggling. And that’s why Saban left, and that’s why other coaches are going to flee.” Deion Sanders up against it at Colorado? McFarland added on that the new era has been the exact opposite of what can aid Sanders in recruiting and coaching. Simply being a fundraiser is not what makes Sanders unique and great as a coach. “I think his cachet, his persona, everything he stands for, if this were 10 or 15 years ago, he could have recruited five-star after five-star the way that Nick Saban did,” McFarland said. “The fact that this is a new era and Saban is gone because it’s a new era, and now it’s about your school, how much money you have, and how much you’re willing to spend. Deion has been on record about paying players and about how much he’s not willing to do it, and about who he’s willing to do it with.  “And so I think this is a critical season because I think Deion is old school, and if my son were a football player, I would want him to play for somebody like Deion because of what he stands for. The problem is this: how many players is he going to be able to get in the future based on that? How many games is he going to win based on this new era of college football? I think that’s the ultimate test.” Sanders is 16-21 at Colorado but 43-27 overall as a head coach. He went 27-6 at Jackson State, winning th Southwestern Athletic Conference in 2021 and ‘22. His impact on Colorado and the community at large can’t be understated. But more wins have to follow eventually. “I don’t think Deion is going to win enough games this season, and then it comes down to the administration: Are you willing to continue with the experiment and get more than you thought you were going to get,” McFarland said. “Because he’s made Colorado more notable. He’s put Colorado back on the map. We talk about Colorado on national television now. Do you think he can take you to the next level? I can’t answer that question. That’s going to be up to the administration.”

articles.title: Big Ten, SEC Ban NFL Players From Returning, Other Conferences Mull Options
articles.summary: Petre Thomas-Imagn Images
articles._body: Last week, a Louisiana state judge granted a temporary restraining order allowing a group of players who participated in NFL training camp and preseason to return to college. As a result, conferences are working to prevent that scenario from becoming a reality. On Tuesday, the Big Ten became the first conference to vote to implement a rule banning NFL players from returning to college, the conference confirmed in a statement. The votes were unanimous. The rule will “prohibit football players who have signed a professional contract, were on a professional roster at any point, or declared for the NFL Draft as an underclassman without withdrawing, from maintaining eligibility for athletic competition at a conference institution,” the Big Ten said. On Tuesday night, the SEC announced it would enforce a similar policy , as well as prohibiting men’s and women’s basketball players from going from the WNBA or NBA back to college. The ACC and Big 12 are reportedly having similar conversations . In addition, the American is considering a similar conference-wide ban on NFL players, a source confirmed to FOS. The original Louisiana lawsuit itself didn’t challenge the NCAA’s ban on professional athletes returning to college. Instead, it was one of many that have been filed to challenge the implementation of the NCAA’s new “age based” eligibility policy , which would give players five years to complete five seasons (up from four) starting when they enter college or on their 19th birthday, whichever comes first. The NCAA declined to grandfather in players who joined college in 2022 and have already completed four years of eligibility—so players from that group have decided to sue in both state and federal court. The Louisiana lawsuit challenged that implementation policy, and argued additionally that players never would have participated in NFL activities if they knew they would have a fifth year of eligibility. The judge ruled in their favor, granting the TRO that will extend until a hearing on Aug. 31, but said these players would have to terminate their NFL contracts and pay back any NFL money they made in order to return to college. Most notably, Browns tight end Dae’Quan Wright has secured a deal to play for LSU this fall after being waived this weekend. Wright will be the first player to go from participating in preseason games to college. His old teammate at Ole Miss, Zxavian Harris, also a plaintiff in the lawsuit, was signed by the Saints this summer but was injured and never participated in preseason games; he was waived on Aug. 8. He’s now signed with LSU as well. (As part of a separate lawsuit, Texas’s Cole Hutson was able to secure a return to the Longhorns despite participating in NFL training camps, but not being signed with a team.) At this point, only players involved in this lawsuit (or who file their own separate state lawsuit) are eligible to go from NFL preseason back to college. And while other players are considering filing cases of their own, the situation is broadly considered to be a one-off given that it’s specifically about the freshman class of 2022, as FOS previously reported . The Big Ten’s new rule attempts to prevent any player who had an NFL contract or who willingly participated in the NFL draft process. But there are a few caveats. First, the rule’s NFL Draft language only prohibits players who declared for the draft before exhausting all years of eligibility. Players who completed four years and whose names were entered into the draft through the automatic entry process—and not drafted—are still eligible. Players in this scenario who then participated only in rookie mini-camp tryouts, held in the first two weekends after the NFL Draft, but didn’t ultimately sign with a team, are also still eligible. Under this policy, UCLA transfer Trent Hendrick, who was part of the Louisiana lawsuit, would be eligible. UCLA released a statement effectively confirming as much shortly after the Big Ten’s policy announcement. The Big Ten also said it was considering implementing similar rules for other sports. The SEC’s rules, meanwhile, stipulate that teams are not allowed to include players who “did not appropriately withdraw” from the NFL, NBA, or WNBA Drafts. Players who signed contracts with the NFL or other pro football leagues, the NBA, WNBA, G-League or WNBA affiliates are banned as well, as are any players listed at any point on the rosters of any of these teams. The statement said the SEC could assign “penalties against member institutions” for signing these players. Under these rules, Wright and Harris would be ineligible to play at LSU. So would former St. John’s standout men’s basketball player RJ Luis, who won an injunction to play basketball at LSU despite signing NBA contracts. LSU did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The road will likely be bumpy, however. Players may end up suing conferences in addition to the NCAA in future lawsuits in order to prevent them from enforcing these types of bans as well. Attorney Darren Heitner, part of Wright’s representation team, told FOS Tuesday night that he “is not only allowed to play, but must be allowed to play,” based on the Louisiana court order. “Our understanding is that’s the intention of LSU right now as well,” Heitner said. “But if the SEC takes some sort of action to intervene, then we need to reassess, and determine what the next step is.” An attorney representing Luis did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The post Big Ten, SEC Ban NFL Players From Returning, Other Conferences Mull Options appeared first on Front Office Sports .

articles.title: Oregon’s freshmen linemen are enormous, hungry and already earning Iapani Laloulu’s respect
articles.summary: Oregon's starting center loves what he's seen from the new faces along the offensive line as players like Tommy Tofi and Immanuel Iheanacho work to meet the standard in Eugene.
articles._body: Oregon’s offensive line continues to be one of the top storylines in Eugene as the Ducks work through fall camp and aim to uphold a standard that’s pumped out NFL players and produced one of the best fronts in college football each year. Veteran center Iapani ‘Poncho’ Laloulu returns as the cornerstone of A’lique Terry ‘s group and spoke very highly about some of the new faces in the room, as well as returners that are fighting for larger roles this fall. True freshmen Tommy Tofi and Immanuel Iheanacho have fans excited as the two mammoth linemen could get on the field early. “It’s been good. Obviously, those dudes are huge,” Laloulu said following Monday’s practice. “They come and walk up to me and just tap me on my back. Man, you ain’t gotta slap me that hard. Two massive kids, but the thing I like about those two guys, they always have joy. Always willing to learn, asking questions, and just not sitting in the back.” Their hunger for growth is an encouraging sign for the Oregon offensive line staff and Laloulu likes the strides he’s seen from each of the newcomers. “Just seeing the way they develop, Tommy been here longer, so just being able to see how Tommy transitioned from when he first came in as a high schooler to where he is at now is a huge step,” the center said. “And also with Manny too, just coming in the summer and doing workouts and just seeing how when coach talks about certain scheme and stuff, he’s quick to answer. That’s just a testament to Coach Terry and the Law Firm coaches and what they do.” Tofi has been moving around the line in fall camp, spending time at left tackle in Oregon’s scrimmage this past weekend. That versatility should make him a reliable option this season. “Tommy does a great job. He played all four besides center right now,” Laloulu said. “The coaches are kind of throwing him in the fire right now, and I think it’s good because if God forbid anything happens, Tommy’s one of those guys that can step up and play. And Tommy, he does a great job at it. There’s still some things you need to work on, and transitioning-wise from his playing style from high school to now in college. And Tommy’s been taking it as opportunity, and just going and just running with it.” Ziyare Addison and Gernorris Wilson are two other names to watch up front for the Ducks this fall. Wilson had carved out a role before an injury sidelined him and Addison is ready to assert himself after appearing in two games as a freshman. “G Baby (Wilson) had something that kind of nicked him towards the end of the season last year. Just seeing the way he attacks it. Like I said, I see all those guys in the treatment room, in the weight room, the way they attack, and the energy that they bring,” Laloulu said. “And also for Ziyare being a young dude, just seeing the fire that he has every day, and also kind of the brains he has. From where he first came freshman year, like that’s a dude I would want on my team because he’s in the treatment, he’s also in the film room. Like every time we finish meeting, Ziyare is already over here, and that’s what I like to see when I see younger dudes taking that initiative to take time out of their life and to come and watch film and stuff.” Yale transfer Michael Bennett was the only transfer Terry brought in this offseason and he’s been quick to earn the veteran’s respect in the Oregon offensive line room. “Man, he got the brains. He picked up things kind of quick. I’m not gonna lie,” Laloulu added. “Just seeing the way he comes and attacks it every single day, and the questions he has. After probably every rack or whatever, he come up and ask me a question. And I like that because that means he’s into it. He wants to learn. He wants to understand our scheme better. So just being able to have those conversations is pretty huge.”

articles.title: At least 1 Raiders insider demands for Fernando Mendoza to start immediately over Kirk Cousins
articles.summary: As the Las Vegas Raiders prepare to close out the preseason against the San Francisco 49ers on Thursday at 5 p.m. PT, FOX NFL writer Steven Ruiz believes the organization should abandon its apparent plan to sit rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza behind Kirk Cousins. Ruiz made the case for the No
articles._body: As the Las Vegas Raiders prepare to close out the preseason against the San Francisco 49ers on Thursday at 5 p.m. PT, FOX NFL writer Steven Ruiz believes the organization should abandon its apparent plan to sit rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza behind Kirk Cousins. Ruiz made the case for the No. 1 overall selection in the 2026 NFL Draft to start immediately in his latest QB Notebook, arguing that Mendoza has already displayed traits that suggest he is ready for NFL action. “The Raiders plan to subject us to a full season of Kirk Cousins as part of Fernando Mendoza’s developmental plan,” Ruiz wrote. “While that’s disappointing, the reasoning is easy to understand. We’ve seen bad supporting casts stunt a young quarterback’s development.” Despite concerns surrounding Las Vegas’ offensive supporting cast, Ruiz believes Mendoza’s first two preseason appearances have separated him from a typical rookie quarterback. “After watching Mendoza’s first two preseason games, though, the Las Vegas brain trust, led by Tom Brady, should feel confident that Mendoza isn’t like most rookies,” Ruiz wrote. “He’s already showing the polish and refinement coaches want to see from developing quarterbacks before handing them the keys to the offense.” Fernando Mendoza showing NFL-ready traits for Raiders David Brytus-Imagn Images Ruiz highlighted Mendoza’s ability to process coverages and make the correct reads as one of the strongest arguments for starting him. He also noted that first-year Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak has already challenged Mendoza with difficult dropback concepts rather than relying heavily on screens and run-pass options. “I’ve been most impressed with Mendoza’s eyes,” Ruiz wrote. “They always seem to go to the right spots based on the coverage.” Ruiz pointed to multiple throws against the Arizona Cardinals in Las Vegas’ preseason opener as examples of Mendoza manipulating defenders and progressing through his reads. He also highlighted Mendoza successfully connecting on a backside drift route, a concept prevalent in Kubiak’s offense and influenced by San Francisco 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan’s system. Mendoza still experienced some rookie struggles in the Raiders’ 22-20 victory over the Houston Texans last Thursday. He completed 8 of 15 passes for 86 yards with an interception and finished with a 42.6 quarterback rating. Still, Ruiz argued those imperfections are another reason Las Vegas should give Mendoza regular-season experience rather than keeping him behind Cousins. “Mendoza already has the mental acuity to play NFL quarterback,” Ruiz wrote. “He just needs to get comfortable executing against a live defense. That won’t happen on the bench.” With one preseason game remaining, Las Vegas faces a significant decision over how quickly Mendoza should take control of the offense as his rookie season approaches. articles._body: The New York Knicks are looking to repeat as NBA champions. At the same time, Josh Hart is eligible for a new contract extension . He became eligible for a four-year, $132 million deal on Aug. 10. However, reports say he will receive a smaller deal worth up to $62 million over three years. But no matter what, Hart intends to stay in the Big Apple for the remainder of his career, per Caroline Fenton of Yahoo Sports. “I’ve always said NY is a home for me and has given me some of the best years of my career,” Hart said. “Of course I want to stay here and retire here.” "I've always said NY is a home for me and has given me some of the best years of my career. Of course I want to stay here and retire here." -Josh Hart via @carolinefenton1 , @YahooSports pic.twitter.com/Y50CnDrxj4 — Knicks Fan TV (@KnicksFanTv) August 25, 2026 In 2023, Hart was traded to the Knicks via the Portland Trail Blazers. Since then, he has become a secondary playmaking force along with being a terrific rebounder and defender. All the while being a focal point in a tight-knit core that includes Jalen Brunson, Karl-Anthony Towns, OG Anunoby, and Mikal Bridges. Along the way, New York made significant inroads in the postseason. He, Brunson, and Bridges played at Villanova and won a national championship in 2016. All three hold the distinct honor of winning both an NCAA and NBA title as part of the same team. Hart’s best season was 2024-25, when he averaged 13.6 points, 9.6 rebounds, and 5.9 assists per game. Last season, he averaged 12.0 points, 7.4 rebounds, and 4.8 assists. In the playoffs, Hart averaged 10.4 points, 8.9 rebounds, and 4.6 assists. He achieved a career-high 26 points and 7 assists in Game 2 of the Eastern Conference Finals against the Cleveland Cavaliers. The Knicks begin the preseason on Oct. 5 against the Philadelphia 76ers. articles.title: The Human Rights Foundation Announces Support for 16 Projects Worldwide
articles.summary: Bitcoin Magazine
articles._body: Bitcoin Magazine The Human Rights Foundation Announces Support for 16 Projects Worldwide The Human Rights Foundation has announced support for more projects around the globe, this time giving over 500 million satoshis — worth $396,854 at today’s prices — in grants to 16 projects based in Africa, Asia, and Latin America. Coming from the HRF’s Bitcoin Development Fund, the grants will help projects that want to strengthen the Bitcoin protocol, expand practical Bitcoin access and facilitate secure messaging and community infrastructure for dissidents, among other things, according to the NGO.  The grants are the second round of funding to come in 2026, after the NGO announced it had supported 26 projects in April. HRF said the funding works to reinforce Bitcoin’s role as a tool for financial freedom, enabling journalists, nonprofit organizations, and activists to more securely communicate, organize, and receive support globally through Bitcoin. Bitcoin Payments BitSpenda Across Africa, cross-border money transfers are often slow, costly and rely on intermediaries. BitSpenda , a mobile money-to-bitcoin bridge, offers a non-custodial, account-free tool that lets people in Nigeria, Kenya, Cameroon, Uganda, and Ghana send bitcoin from a Lightning wallet directly to a mobile money account, where it is received in local currency. With HRF’s support, BitSpenda plans to expand its payment tools to make cross-border payments faster, cheaper, and more accessible in the region. Project Island Resilience In parts of the Caribbean, power outages and authoritarian repression can cut people off from both communication and access to money. Project Island Resilience builds on Flash, a Bitcoin and Lightning wallet created by Jamaican developer Dread. After Hurricane Melissa devastated Jamaica in late 2025, the app raised and distributed more than $10,000 in bitcoin within 72 hours. Now, the project plans to add offline payments to Flash using Bluetooth, near-field communication (NFC), and ecash, creating a model for how Bitcoin can continue working in adversarial conditions. HRF’s grant will support this next phase, helping build practical Bitcoin infrastructure that can be used during protests and internet shutdowns. Bitzed In Zambia, mobile money is commonly used, but buying bitcoin still usually requires banks or centralized exchanges that maintain identity records and control individuals’ assets. Bitzed , created by Bitcoin educator Humphrey, is an account-free platform that connects mobile money networks directly to Bitcoin in Zambia. Users can buy bitcoin using existing mobile money accounts and receive it straight to their own Lightning wallet. HRF’s funding will help expand this self-custodial path into Bitcoin for Zambians excluded from traditional banking and subject to financial repression. Bitcoin Development Libbitcoinkernel Many Bitcoin applications have to rebuild the protocol’s most complex security rules from scratch, which increases the risk of catastrophic errors. Libbitcoinkernel is a software project pulling the core security and transaction rules directly from Bitcoin’s original code and turning them into reusable software modules. This will allow freedom tech developers to build more secure and independent wallets, services, and infrastructure without having to duplicate Bitcoin’s critical code. Support from HRF will help developer yuvicc continue this foundational work, strengthening the foundations of Bitcoin tools on which people under financial repression rely. A Node in Every Wallet: Utreexo Wallet Integrations Most Bitcoin wallets still rely on centralized servers to access balance and transaction history, compromising user privacy. Floresta is a lightweight version of a Bitcoin node that embeds directly into wallet apps, reducing the storage needed to verify Bitcoin transactions, so wallets can then check data locally and privately. This grant will support developer Luis Schwab in ensuring that wallets cut out the middlemen and interface directly with the Bitcoin network.  BDK-Dart In many authoritarian countries, mobile wallets are the most practical way to access Bitcoin. But building apps that give users full control of their funds without relying on a central authority remains a challenge. BDK-Dart is a toolkit that gives developers pre-built Bitcoin wallet-building blocks for Flutter, a popular framework to build apps for any device. The toolkit allows developers to more easily build secure, custodial Bitcoin wallets using a single, shared codebase across platforms. Supported by HRF, software developer John Osezele will make a major release of this software and a reference wallet, lowering barriers for developers to build self-custodial Bitcoin apps worldwide. WalletScrutiny Most Bitcoin users have no way to check whether a wallet app actually matches the open-source code it claims to run. WalletScrutiny is a project that audits Bitcoin wallets for transparency and verifies that the distributed software matches its source code. Funding will support expanded review of wallet dependencies and third-party frameworks, helping activists, journalists, and changemakers choose trustworthy Bitcoin applications in authoritarian contexts. HRF has supported WalletScrutiny before, and this grant continues that work as the recent Coldcard hack underscores the importance that the software running on a Bitcoin wallet is actually the software users expect. Nostr Vector Privacy: Privacy by Principle In high-risk environments, private messaging requires more than just encryption; it also means avoiding account creation, metadata trails, and censorship. Vector is an open-source messenger built on Nostr (a decentralized communications protocol) that is permissionless and uses end-to-end encryption. articles.title: Is Digi-Pop the Newest Hyperpop Wave?
articles.summary: How Pupsies' debut chart hit "Misery" could be leading the charge.
articles._body: What’s initially most striking about Pupsies’ “Misery” is the song’s sonics: a buzzing, blaring, synth-bass hum matched with a lo-fi melody that could soundtrack an 8-bit video game. While Pupsies’ favorite part kicks in later — a dramatic, crunchy guitar hook from co-producer Goetia that accompanies her wailing vocal climax — it’s this early, beatless section that helped the song take off on TikTok. Cindy Kamgaing, the 19-year-old from North Carolina better known as Pupsies, has been building an internet following since 2023 for her kinetic, therapeutically revealing digi-pop jams, but had yet to really unlock a mainstream crossover until “Misery.” Following its March release, the emotionally overflowing (but “cute”-­sounding, as Kamgaing proudly puts it) single went viral, taking off with animation edits (like a Steven Universe one that Kamgaing found particularly delightful), and with users jokingly referring to it as a “LARP” song (an abbreviation that traditionally means live action role playing but has come to refer to anyone seen as playing a specific part). “I think people started saying it because the song is kind of like, ‘I’m depressed, I’m a girl,’” Kamgaing says. So far, the song about a no-good relationship has reached a No. 50 high on the Billboard Hot 100 — and is one of the first true chart hits of a movement that started almost a decade ago: hyperpop. Since emerging, the subgenre has undergone countless permutations but has retained the same frenetic energy, unguarded emotion, lo-fi production and DIY aesthetic of its musical precursors, while producing streaming hits of various degrees by Penelope Scott (“Rat”), C–tsniffer (“Meant to Be”) and Laydownrot (“Perfect Face”), among others. But with “Misery,” hyperpop could enter its next phase this fall. “I think, especially post-COVID, more people are more online,” Kamgaing says of why hyperpop is finally starting to bubble over. “People used to say, ‘It’s just the internet,’ but I think now we’ve come to a position in society where the internet is so intertwined with the real world, and it’s sort of got this symbiotic relationship. So I think it is possible that something that was very niche becomes more mainstream.” And while “Misery” is helping the latest flavor of hyperpop continue its mainstream ascent, Kamgaing admits that “I don’t listen to the genre of music I make.” She says she’s more interested in mixing a variety of music styles into her digital-sounding productions: “I want to show people that you can do whatever you want to, you can express yourself however you want to.” This story appears in the Aug. 22, 2026, issue of Billboard.

articles.title: Cardi B, Meek Mill, Lil Uzi Vert & More Fuel the Atlantic’s Hustle & Grit: See the Movement Mix
articles.summary: From New York swagger to Philly determination, Billboard and Planet Fitness soundtrack the Atlantic region’s drive with a mix informed by Luminate listening data
articles._body: Along the Atlantic, movement has its own rhythm—from New York’s relentless pace and Philadelphia’s determination to New Jersey’s energy and Virginia’s musical innovation. It’s a region where hustle and grit aren’t just ideas; they’re embedded in the culture and the music that comes from it.  That spirit drives the  Atlantic Flow Movement Mix , part of the Planet Fitness Movement Mixes exploring the music that keeps people moving. Curated by Billboard’s editorial team and informed by Luminate streaming and consumption data from the region’s top 200 tracks from January 2026 to present, the playlist pairs what Atlantic listeners are playing now with songs that reflect the region’s musical DNA.  The result moves across hip-hop, pop and dance—from Cardi B and Pop Smoke’s New York energy to Meek Mill and Lil Uzi Vert’s Philly drive and Missy Elliott’s Virginia-born innovation. Different sounds and generations, connected by the same thing: music that makes you want to move, push harder and keep going.  From the first warm-up to the final push, consider the Atlantic Hustle & Grit Movement Mix (listen HERE ) a soundtrack for wherever your own momentum takes you and sign up at your local Planet Fitness with code ATLANTICFMF to keep moving. Code ATLANTICFMF will give you your first month of Planet Fitness membership for FREE and is applicable to either membership (Black Card or Classic Card). This offer expires December 31, 2026. The Spins — Mac Miller , Empire of the Sun “The Spins” captures Mac Miller at his most youthful and freewheeling, pairing a bright, instantly infectious sample with an easygoing flow. The production feels light on its feet, while Mac’s delivery brings an effortless confidence that keeps the track moving. More than a decade later, that combination still gives the record its feel-good lift. Public Service Announcement (Interlude) — JAY-Z Few records communicate confidence as efficiently as “Public Service Announcement.” Just Blaze builds the track around a dramatic, soul-driven beat that feels larger with every bar, while JAY-Z delivers with measured precision. There’s no rush to the performance—its power comes from control, creating the feeling of someone completely certain of his place in the room. AH HA — Cardi B Cardi B attacks “AH HA” with the sharp delivery, humor and bravado that have become signatures of her sound. The production gives her plenty of room to punch through, with a hard-edged rhythm that keeps the record tense and propulsive. Cardi’s personality does the rest, turning every bar into an extension of the track’s confrontational energy. Beauty and a Beat — Justin Bieber featuring Nicki Minaj “Beauty and a Beat” is pure pop maximalism. Bright synths, electronic drums and an enormous chorus give the track its rush, while Justin Bieber’s melodic delivery keeps it light and buoyant. Nicki Minaj arrives with a playful verse that adds another jolt of personality before the song launches back into its dance-floor pulse. Dreams and Nightmares (Intro) — Meek Mill “Dreams and Nightmares (Intro)” is defined by transformation. Meek Mill begins over a sparse, reflective piano progression before the production abruptly shifts and his delivery erupts with it. That transition—from measured reflection to full-throttle release—is what gives the record its lasting power, turning mounting tension into pure adrenaline. Plain Jane — A$AP Ferg “Plain Jane” thrives on minimalism. Its hypnotic production leaves space for A$AP Ferg’s clipped, rhythmic delivery to become part of the beat itself. Repetition creates momentum rather than slowing it down, giving the record a steady, almost mechanical drive that makes it easy to lock into. Promiscuous — Nelly Furtado featuring Timbaland “Promiscuous” is built around chemistry and rhythm. Timbaland’s production is sparse but deeply percussive, allowing the back-and-forth between him and Nelly Furtado to function almost like another instrument. Playful, flirtatious and constantly in motion, the track proves how much energy can come from groove alone. Just Wanna Rock — Lil Uzi Vert “Just Wanna Rock” wastes little time getting to the point. Built around the rapid pulse of Jersey club, the track favors repetition, percussion and physical energy over a traditional verse-chorus structure. Lil Uzi Vert floats in and out of the beat, allowing the rhythm to do much of the work and creating a record that feels almost impossible to experience sitting still. Dior — Pop Smoke “Dior” moves with weight. Sliding bass, sharp percussion and dark production create a menacing backdrop for Pop Smoke’s unmistakably deep voice, which lands as another rhythmic element within the track. The contrast between his controlled delivery and the restless beat gives the record its particular intensity. Lose Control — Missy Elliott featuring Ciara & Fatman Scoop “Lose Control” turns controlled chaos into a dance record. Frenetic percussion and electronic production move at a relentless pace while Fatman Scoop’s booming commands raise the intensity even further. Missy Elliott and Ciara glide through the commotion, creating a track whose entire structure seems designed around the physical act of movement. articles.title: Titans’ Brian Daboll knows Cam Ward isn’t only problem with Tennessee’s putrid passing game
articles.summary: Things didn’t go well for the Tennessee Titans against the Seahawks. That’s especially true of Cam Ward and the offense. However, Brian Daboll knows Cam Ward isn’t the only problem with the Titans’ putrid passing game, according to a post on X by Turron Davenport. It’s about the middle-range stuf
articles._body: Things didn’t go well for the Tennessee Titans against the Seahawks . That’s especially true of Cam Ward and the offense . However, Brian Daboll knows Cam Ward isn’t the only problem with the Titans’ putrid passing game, according to a post on X by Turron Davenport. It’s about the middle-range stuff, the Titans’ offensive coordinator said. “The intermediate chunk plays,” Daboll said. “Whether that’s layered throws, man-to-man throws. I mean, that’s encompassing everybody. It’s incumbent upon the receiver to take proper angles. It’s incumbent on the protection. And then ultimately, Cam hitting plays.” Titans need offense to take strides Ward holds the key. There’s no sugarcoating that. But Daboll made it clear that Ward isn’t getting the help he needs to make the unit function efficiently. “(It’s) just not on Cam,” Daboll said. “Certainly not on Cam — all of it. It’s a combination of things. We’ve been working on it. We’ll continue to work on it. That’s part of the execution stuff we’re going to continue to grind away at. That’s an element of our offense we’ve got to improve.” Ward acknowledged his own issues against the Seahawks, according to NFL.com. “I think just missed opportunities on some plays, particularly our passing game,” Ward said after the tilt, via the team’s official transcript. “I think it was improvement from last week, but just got to be better down the field as a whole.” Head coach Robert Saleh provided a positive spin. “Thought Cam, again, was good with the ball, good decision-making,” Saleh said. “We just couldn’t connect on a couple of deep throws. But overall, it’s got to be better, guys. I’m not trying to sugarcoat it. It does (have) to be better. But at the same time, there’s always going to be things that we can take from.” Ward said he’s learning the new system. “Everything slowed down,” Ward said. “We’re finally at the point where we’re not going to be installing too much stuff. It’s going to be nice to really show what we really are about when the time comes.” The post Titans’ Brian Daboll knows Cam Ward isn’t only problem with Tennessee’s putrid passing game appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles.summary: The St. Louis Cardinals are reportedly placing shortstop Masyn Winn on the injured list and promoting former star prospect Nolan Gorman to the big league team, according to Jeff Jones of bnd.com. According to Derrick Goold of the St. Louis Dispatch, rookie JJ Wetherholt will handle shortstop duti
articles._body: The St. Louis Cardinals are reportedly placing shortstop Masyn Winn on the injured list and promoting former star prospect Nolan Gorman to the big league team, according to Jeff Jones of bnd.com. According to Derrick Goold of the St. Louis Dispatch, rookie JJ Wetherholt will handle shortstop duties during Winn’s injury absence. Winn has been dealing with a thumb injury. It is uncertain how much time he will miss. Winn also dealt with a knee injury earlier in the year. Still, he has appeared in 122 games, hitting .238 to go along with a .641 OPS during that span. Updates on Winn’s injury status will continue to be monitored and provided as they are made available. The Cardinals optioned Gorman — who is a former star prospect — in June following his abysmal start to the season. The 26-year-old infielder was hitting just .194 with a .598 OPS when he was optioned. He has continued to struggle at Triple-A, hitting .182 overall. However, he does have a .758 OPS and 13 home runs across 46 games played, so power hasn’t been a problem for him in the minor leagues. Still, the team would obviously love more overall offensive consistency. Gorman can help this Cardinals ball club down the stretch. He offers some defensive versatility, as he can play second or third base. His power from the left side of the plate could also be valuable as the Cardinals attempt to sneak into the postseason. St. Louis is currently five games back of a National League Wild Card spot. Reaching the postseason will be a challenge, but it is not out of the question. articles._body: The San Diego Padres are currently in a position to make the playoffs in 2026. The Padres added pitchers at the MLB trade deadline, adding Casey Mize and Robbie Ray. There is also hope that Joe Musgrove could be returning to the Padres soon . Now, another update on the progress of Musgrove has been given, per MLB.com. “Threw a bullpen at Petco Park on Aug. 22. Will make fourth rehab start with Triple-A El Paso on Aug. 27. Could rejoin the rotation after that,” the update read. Musgrove underwent Tommy John surgery in October 2024. He was solid that year, going 6-5 with a 3.88 ERA and a 1.17 WHIP. He then pitched 3.2 innings in the playoffs against the Atlanta Braves, giving up just one run, before leaving with an injury. Musgrove has started three games in the minor leagues, pitching 10.2 innings. He has a 5.91 ERA in the three starts and has an 0-1 record. He also has a 1.875 WHIP so far in the three starts between El Paso and Lake Elsinore. Musgrove is still striking out batters at a solid rate, striking out ten batters in the 10.2 innings of work. The Padres could use more reinforcements in the bullpen or the starting rotation. Recently, Mize has also had an injury scare , but may not miss a start. The Padres are 71-61 on the year, which places them in second in the NL West. They currently hold the last wild card spot in the National League, with a two-game lead over the Arizona Diamondbacks. The Padres continue their series with the Pittsburgh Pirates on Tuesday night. The post Padres pitcher Joe Musgrove’s injury return timeline gets huge update appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles._body: The NFL has taken a page out of the NBA’s book with NFL Rivalry uniforms. The alternate jerseys worn in much-anticipated divisional matchups are reminiscent of the NBA’s City Edition jerseys, and the Indianapolis Colts were the most recent team to announce their new and colorful threads. Legends in the state of Indiana, Tyrese Haliburton, Pat McAfee, and Kelsey Mitchell, teamed up with Colts quarterback Daniel Jones to unveil the new jerseys, which have been coined “The Anvil Strike.” The new jerseys are dark grey with blue and white accents, and McAfee pointed out that fans have long awaited blue helmets. “The blue helmet, people have been asking for this for a long time,” McAfee informed Haliburton. “The Colts are blue; the mascot’s name is ‘Blue.’ They are tough, too.” BREAKING Me, @Hali , and WNBA record holder @Kelz_Hoop had the incredible opportunity to see the @Colts brand new “Rivalries” uniforms first SAY HELLO TO “THE ANVIL STRIKE” ERA pic.twitter.com/DMZt6bRO0H — Pat McAfee (@PatMcAfeeShow) August 25, 2026 In addition to the helmets being blue, this will be the first time that the horseshoe logo is on the jersey. However, not everyone is stoked on the new uniforms. Some fans have compared the jerseys to the Buffalo Bills’ new alternate uniforms, which were not well received . The Colts took more creative liberties than the Bills did, though, not only adding a much-anticipated new helmet color but also a unique jersey color as well. Despite some criticism, the Colts will fit the moniker of look good, play good. Our approach was to use an infinite canvas desktop app for the TUIs we already know and love, mainly
articles._body: Hi HN, I’m Michael, I built AgentGrid with my friend Souren because we were tired of losing our coding sessions and couldn't keep track of what was actually being built across our many projects. Our approach was to use an infinite canvas desktop app for the TUIs we already know and love, mainly claude + codex. We drew inspiration from Figma and Railway. Overtime we added image nodes, notes, terminals, coding editors, source control, etc. I wasn't sure about it at first. It took me a month to give the first version Souren built a real try. What got me was an Apple System Update I've been ignoring for weeks to avoid losing my +20 open claude code tabs in warp. In the course of using it and contributing, I broke it a few times and had to go back to the way we were doing things. It was miserable. It's been a few months now and I can't imagine going back. Most of you are builders and this tool should be really helpful. So I'd love for you to give it a spin. I would love your honest opinion. For the rest of the discussion, I would love to focus on the question of what is the right UI for agentic engineering? I would argue IDE is too much in the way, TUI is a terrible DX with a lot of hacks just for basic features. Finally, a GUI chat interface is far better but lacks the dimension of seeing the connection between items and is a poor collaboration surface. Now infinite canvas has a sprawl problem too, What do you think? Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49436219 Points: 1 # Comments: 0

articles.title: Ye’s Russia Shows Canceled After Venue Says No Rental Agreement Has Been Signed
articles.summary: Yeezy was slated to perform a pair of shows at Gazprom Arena in October.
articles._body: Ye’s (formerly Kanye West ) pair of Russia shows slated for October have reportedly been canceled by the venue. Saint Petersburg’s Gazprom Arena posted on social media on Monday (Aug. 24) that the 80,000-capacity stadium “did not sign any contracts for the stadium rent for the event.” “There is no such agreement,” the post continued. “Accordingly, the concert cannot take place on our site.” However, since the shows were announced, Gazprom Arena has been singing a different tune, hyping up hosting Ye on social media. The Russian shows were set for Oct. 10 and Oct. 11 and promoters are now scrambling to find a new venue, according to BBC . “We learned about [it] at the same time as you did, through the media,” the concert’s promoter Say Agency reportedly wrote on Telegram. “As of now, the Ye concert has not been canceled. We are trying to contact the venue to find out the reason for the post and resolve the issue. We will keep you updated.” If he took the Gazprom Arena stage, West would have been the first rap superstar to perform in Russia since the country invaded Ukraine in 2022. The Ukrainian Institute called for Ukraine allies to suspend cultural cooperation with Russia. Billboard has reached out to Ye’s reps and Say Agency for comment. Publicly, Ye has remained mostly quiet in 2026 while touring with spot dates across the globe. Overseas, he’s performed in Turkey, the Netherlands, Georgia, Albania, Portugal, Spain and Kazakhstan this year. In the U.S., the Grammy-winning rapper returned in April with a pair of SoFi Stadium shows in Los Angeles and has made stops in Tampa Bay and San Antonio. Ye’s performing in New Orleans on Friday (Aug. 28) and then has a pair of homecoming concerts in Chicago at Soldier Field on Sept. 3-4. West is still feeling the backlash from his years of antisemitic remarks and embrace of Nazi symbolism , which began in 2022. He’s had shows in France, Poland, Czech Republic and a headlining set at London’s Wireless Fest canceled this year, while dates in Italy and India cited “security concerns.” On the music front, Ye released his Bully album in March, which debuted at No. 2 on the Billboard 200.

articles.title: Callaway CEO Apologizes for Good Good Ad
articles.summary: John Dufour-Imagn Images
articles._body: Callaway admitted it had the final say on a controversial, since-deleted ad for its new co-branded driver with Good Good Golf, the YouTube channel-turned-major golf brand. In a statement addressed, in part, to “golfers everywhere,” Callaway CEO Chip Brewer said the promotional video—which depicted Good Good co-founder Garrett Clark running and shoving fellow Good Good talent Alexis Miestowski to the ground as she reached for the club out of his bag—was “approved by Callaway prior to posting.” The message was shared at 1a.m. ET Tuesday morning to Callaway’s X/Twitter and Instagram accounts. Brewer also said the company “sincerely apologize[s],” is “conducting both internal and external investigations,” and has “already made changes to [its] approval processes aimed at ensuring this will never happen again.” The video sparked online outrage almost immediately after Good Good posted it early Friday morning. And amid the controversy, Golf Channel is postponing the premiere of its new Big Break x Good Good show. Many users, including several high-profile golf media personalities, described the content as confusing , scary , and endorsing violence against women. Good Good removed it from all platforms by Friday evening. Both companies issued initial statements on Saturday. In a post to its X/Twitter account, Good Good apologized and said it decided to take the video down because it “ultimately depicted actions that are not aligned with our values as a brand.” A Callaway spokesperson, meanwhile, told Front Office Sports the company was “disappointed by the content” and appreciated Good Good’s addressing of the situation. Good Good’s statement was widely perceived as lackluster , including by PGA Tour CEO Brian Rolapp. At a press conference on Tuesday ahead of the Tour Championship this weekend, he described the company’s initial response as “a bit defensive and late.” Calls for the Tour to drop Good Good as the title sponsor of its Fall Series event taking place Nov. 12–15 in Austin, Texas, are growing amid backlash to the ad. Asked about this Tuesday, Rolapp indicated that a change wasn’t on the table—for now: “It’s a bit of a fluid situation … It sounds like in the last 24 hours they’ve made some progress. We’ll continue to monitor the situation and see how it develops.” Good Good, which has more than 2 million subscribers on its YouTube channel, has not released an official follow-up statement, but its CEO Matt Kendrick spoke with The Wall Street Journal on Monday. “We fully own that we did make a mistake…As the CEO of the company, the buck stops with me and we should have had better processes in place,” he told WSJ . “Obviously the execution missed the mark and didn’t come across the way that we wanted to, and in no way were we trying to make light of or support violence. But it came across that way, and that’s our fault.” Kendrick added that the full 60-second video was meant to spoof the horror movie “Obsession,” released earlier this summer. FOS obtained a copy of a memo Kendrick sent to all Good Good staff on Monday. In the email subject-lined “Owning Our Mistake,” he said the company plans to donate all proceeds of the driver campaign to an “organization supporting women in [its] local community.” (Good Good is based in Frisco, Texas.) Internal creative process reviews are also underway, and Kendrick will be personally approving content released through Good Good’s content and marketing teams “for the foreseeable future,” per the memo. Callaway did not immediately respond to a request for comment about the long-term future of its partnership with Good Good, which began in 2023. In addition to special-edition clubs, the companies have released co-branded balls, gloves, and shoes over the years. Good Good Golf Channel Show The controversy has also resulted in Golf Channel postponing the premiere of a new show with the YouTube group, Big Break x Good Good . The revamp of the network’s competition reality TV series that last aired in 2015 was scheduled to debut Tuesday night. “Golf Channel is postponing tonight’s premiere of Big Break x Good Good to next Tuesday September 1,” Golf Channel said in a statement posted on X late Tuesday afternoon. “This will allow for necessary production updates following a request from one of the show’s sponsors to remove its branding from the series.” Previous announcements used the verbiage “Big Break x Good Good presented by Golf Galaxy” when referring to the official show title. (Golf Channel did not immediately respond to a question asking about the sponsor.) The new edition of Big Break is a collaboration with Good Good, and was filmed earlier this year. The show’s winner will earn an exemption into the Good Good Championship PGA Tour event in November. Good Good’s Brad Dalke and Sean Walsh are two of the show’s 12 competitors, while fellow members Garrett Clark—who shoved the woman in the driver ad—and Bubbie Broders are non-playing team captains. The post Callaway CEO Apologizes for Good Good Ad appeared first on Front Office Sports .

articles.title: Shakira & Burna Boy’s ‘Dai Dai’ Continues Its Global Charts Reign: Here’s How the Song Took Over
articles.summary: Sony Music U.S. Latin’s GM Esteban Geller talks about the song’s continued success, even one month after the end of the World Cup.
articles._body: More than a month after the World Cup came to an end, its official FIFA anthem, “Dai Dai,” helmed by Shakira and Burna Boy, continues on its global domination streak. The infectious track — released in May, just two months before the month-long soccer tournament kicked off — laces Afrobeats with dance-pop, world beats and reggaetón, bridging the musical worlds of the Nigerian star and Colombian sensation. Lyrically, it keeps true to the sport’s spirit, sending motivational messages. Additionally, 100 percent of the song’s royalties are donated to the FIFA Global Citizen Education Fund, which provides education and soccer resources to children around the world. Related Shakira & Burna Boy’s ‘Dai Dai’ Rolls On at No. 1 on Billboard Global Charts, More Than a Month After the End of the World Cup 5 Ways Shakira & Burna Boy’s ‘Dai Dai’ Has Made World Cup History How Shakira & Burna Boy’s ‘Dai Dai’ Turned World Cup Buzz Into Global Chart Domination But beyond its musical and philanthropic impact, “Dai Dai” became a force to be reckoned with, making history as the first-ever World Cup song to reach No. 1 on the Billboard Global Excl. U.S. chart dated July 4, and later reached the top of the Billboard Global 200. Currently — more than one month after Spain was crowned the 2026 World Cup champs — ”Dai Dai” holds its crown as the biggest song in the world, leading the Billboard Global 200 chart for a sixth week and Billboard Global Excl. U.S. for a ninth frame. “Ultimately, people connected with the song,” Esteban Geller, Sony Music U.S. Latin’s general manager, tells Billboard exclusively. “The [FIFA] World Cup gave it an extraordinary platform, but the audience is what turned that opportunity into a global success.” Below, Geller elaborates on the song’s creation and its continued global domination, as well as talks about the new Spanish version of the song:  When did actual conversations begin between FIFA and Sony Music Latin? The FIFA World Cup was something we had been thinking about well in advance, particularly given Shakira’s history with the tournament and the unique global platform it represents. There was also a natural connection through Shakira’s longstanding relationship with Global Citizen and her commitment to education. As the opportunity developed, it became clear that there was potential to bring those different worlds together: music, football and social impact. What ultimately made “Dai Dai” particularly special was that it wasn’t simply about creating a song for a sporting event. It became an opportunity to connect a global cultural moment with a cause that could have a lasting impact beyond the tournament. How did you work with FIFA to amplify the success of “Dai Dai”?  The collaboration with FIFA was essential because the World Cup is one of the few cultural events capable of bringing audiences around the world together at the same time. Our focus was on making “Dai Dai” feel like a natural part of that experience. Working alongside FIFA, Global Citizen, Shakira’s team and Sony Music teams globally, we created opportunities for the song to live across different aspects of the tournament, from the music and performances to digital, social and fan experiences. The scale of FIFA’s platform, combined with Shakira’s global reach, allowed the song to connect with audiences far beyond traditional music audiences. Ultimately, the goal was to make “Dai Dai” feel like part of the cultural fabric of the World Cup, rather than simply a song released in connection with it. Shakira and Burna Boy perform at the halftime show at the FIFA World Cup Final match between Spain and Argentina on July 19, 2026, at New York New Jersey Stadium in East Rutherford, N.J. Bob Kupbens/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images “Dai Dai” peaked at No. 1 on the Billboard Global charts in July — two months after its release and in the midst of the World Cup — what do you think truly sparked its global success? There wasn’t one single factor. It was the combination of the song, Shakira’s global appeal and the extraordinary cultural moment surrounding the World Cup. Shakira has a unique history with this event, and audiences already have a strong emotional connection to her music in that context. At the same time, “Dai Dai” introduced her to a new generation of fans and brought together different musical and cultural audiences. The official video also helped tell that story visually, bringing together major football stars alongside Shakira, Burna Boy and the Ghetto Kids. It created a connection between music, football and younger audiences while also reinforcing the message behind the Education Fund. Ultimately, people connected with the song. The World Cup gave it an extraordinary platform, but the audience is what turned that opportunity into a global success. “Dai Dai” is the first official World Cup anthem to reach No. 1 on Billboard: What was the core strategy behind sustaining momentum even a month after the World Cup finished? We always saw the World Cup as the beginning of a longer journey for the song, rather than its endpoint. Once the tournament ended, we continued to give audiences new ways to engage with “Dai Dai” through additional versions, creative content and performances. The connection to the Education Fund also gave the song a purpose that extended beyond the competition. There’s also a powerful legacy associated with Shakira’s World Cup music. Songs like “Waka Waka” and “La La La” remain part of the cultural memory of those tournaments, and “Dai Dai” now has the opportunity to become part of that same tradition. articles.title: Tony-Winning ‘Hadestown’ Musical Arrives on Digital Ahead of Blu-ray & DVD Release
articles.summary: Anaïs Mitchell’s acclaimed musical, which won eight Tony Awards, including Best Musical, is making its way from the stage to the home screen.
articles._body: All products and services featured are independently chosen by editors. However, Billboard may receive a commission on orders placed through its retail links, and the retailer may receive certain auditable data for accounting purposes. Hadestown has already conquered Broadway , the West End and, apparently, the box office. Now, the Tony-winning musical is heading home. As of today (Aug. 25), Hadestown: The Musical is now available to purchase or rent digitally, with Blu-ray and DVD editions due out on Oct. 20. Both physical versions are currently available for preorder. The filmed stage production had an impressive run in theaters after opening across North America on July 24. In its first weekend, it earned $10.2 million, beating the $10.1 million opening weekend of Hamilton ’s theatrical stage capture in 2025. The result made Hadestown the biggest opening for a live theater capture at the North American box office. And audiences weren’t exactly ready to say goodbye. The film brought in another $8 million in its second week, pushing its domestic total to $18.2 million. For anyone who didn’t make it to the theater, there’s an easier way to see what all the fuss is about. Starting today, the filmed musical is available for digital purchase and rental through services including Amazon Prime Video and Apple TV. On both platforms, the purchase price is $24.99, while a 48-hour rental is listed at $19.99. And if you’d rather own a copy, the Blu-ray and DVD editions are already available for preorder on Amazon ahead of their October release. OFFICIAL DIGITAL RELEASE Watch 'Hadestown: The Musical' on Prime Video $24.99 Rent/Buy on prime video The digital purchase is expected to be $24.99, while rentals will cost around $19.99 for 48 hours. The filmed version of Hadestown is now available on Prime Video, following its theatrical release. The musical centers on Orpheus and Eurydice as they navigate the underworld, alongside the story of Hades and Persephone. AVAILABLE IN 4K Watch 'Hadestown: The Musical' on Apple TV $24.99 Rent/buy On Apple TV The Tony-winning musical is also available for purchase at $24.99, and rented for $19.99 (at a two-day period). articles.summary:
I have spent 15 years in DevSecOps, platform engineering and offensive security. Over the last year I did most of the things HN says not to do. I wrote a lot of code alone in a vacuum and built this thing far past an MVP.

It started as a way to automate my bug bounty hobby and to try to find an
articles._body: I have spent 15 years in DevSecOps, platform engineering and offensive security. Over the last year I did most of the things HN says not to do. I wrote a lot of code alone in a vacuum and built this thing far past an MVP. It started as a way to automate my bug bounty hobby and to try to find an edge so I could get more findings (scale, automation etc). I wanted agents that could run recon, triage what they found, keep a record etc etc. Then I noticed the same patterns at every client I had worked with, (mainly banks and gov teams) and pivoted. What it is now: an all-in-one solution to getting your agents into prod. You keep your framework, or build from scratch with gibson. A named person grants each agent read, write or execute on specific things, and the grant cannot exceed what that person holds. Every model call and tool call goes through the runtime first, and a call outside the grant never executes. Untrusted work runs in its own Firecracker microVM. Every action lands in an append-only record you can replay to any moment. Everything an agent finds goes into a knowledge graph (on going memory for all agents), so the next run starts from it. It runs in Kubernetes, hosted or in your own cluster, can be air-gapped. This could also have been an Ask HN. I am trying to figure out how to go to market. Im not sure if I should open source it, do a true platform or move back entirely and go deep into what I truly like doing which is red team/hacking and re-release it as an offsec focused tool and try to innovate there with the framework. Any advice/suggestions would be awesome. Thanks! Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49435908 Points: 1 # Comments: 0

articles.title: Show HN: See if bloated 'skills' are degrading your coding agent's performance
articles.summary: I read the 'Skills: Attention is all you have' paper from earlier this month and it struck a chord with me. They researched 50k agent skills and found that a ton of them have all these instructions to try to force invocation, as a result of which they all compete for attention and degrade the per
articles._body: I read the 'Skills: Attention is all you have' paper from earlier this month and it struck a chord with me. They researched 50k agent skills and found that a ton of them have all these instructions to try to force invocation, as a result of which they all compete for attention and degrade the performance and usefulness. It's kind of a tragedy of the commons situation because if you develop a skill, of course you want to tell the agent to "BE SURE TO INVOKE THIS WHEN USER MENTIONS X" or whatever, but then all the skills add the same language and the agent doesn't know what to do. I built a skill grader to grade Agent skills based on the paper's methodology. Paste Github repo and see score. My own skill got a C, by the way, so I'm improving it by reducing keywords and description bloat, etc. I hope we can get to a place where users all reject the bloated skill trend... it just never made sense intuitively to have thousands of words of context loaded to do simple things.. cough G stack... articles.title: Bitcoin Tops $81,000 — Is the Debasement Trade Back?
articles.summary: Bitcoin Magazine
articles._body: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Tops $81,000 — Is the Debasement Trade Back? Bitcoin soared past $81,000 for the first time since January on Monday before dropping slightly. The recent moves have market observers asking if the debasement trade is back.  The biggest cryptocurrency was recently trading for $79,098 on Tuesday morning in New York after hitting $81,160 the evening before. Over a 24-hour period, the coin now sits unmoved. But zoom out seven days and it has jumped by 23%.  Bitcoin has benefited from news that the Treasury would at least double the size of its liquidity-support buyback operations. The announcement last week hurt the dollar but non-yielding assets have benefited.  JUST IN: $80,834 Bitcoin! pic.twitter.com/1Ouoi92RmA — Bitcoin Magazine (@BitcoinMagazine) August 25, 2026 This has some asking whether 2025’s much talked about debasement trade is back. The strategy — when investors buy an asset as a way to hedge against a currency losing value — has in the past benefited Bitcoin along with precious metals because such assets cannot be endlessly printed.  Analysts frequently touted the trade last year but following Bitcoin’s decline since October, it became less talked about as traders turned their attention to stocks related to artificial intelligence.  Though since the dollar has become increasingly weaker, Bitcoin could be attracting longer-term and “smart money” investors, market observers have said .  U.S. investors last week piled back into Bitcoin exchange-traded funds; the investment vehicles had their best week since October, with nearly $2 billion in inflows.  Bitcoin notched a new record of $126,080 in October before the biggest liquidation event in crypto history hurt its price. It continued to dip in 2026 on negative macroeconomic headwinds and fears that the Federal Reserve would not lower interest rates.  Still, it has become increasingly less volatile and so far has suffered from its shallowest bear market, according to analysts.  This post Bitcoin Tops $81,000 — Is the Debasement Trade Back? first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Mathew Di Salvo .

articles.title: AI won’t replace radiologists, but it will dramatically change their jobs
articles.summary: A pioneering AI scientist once predicted computers would replace human radiologists. They haven't.
articles._body: In 2016 Geoffrey Hinton, the Nobel-winning “godfather of AI,” predicted that radiologists—the physicians who read X-rays, ultrasounds, and other images to help make medical diagnoses—would find themselves replaced by computers within five years. Today the field can retort by quoting Mark Twain’s famous quip: The report of my death was an exaggeration . Radiology’s ranks are in fact growing steadily, with the number of practitioners expected to expand by 26 percent or more over the next three decades . But what Hinton may have missed about the dynamics of the job market should not obscure his prescience: He was correct that human physicians now have a silicon-based colleague in the room that matches or exceeds their performance. In fact, radiology is far and away medicine’s hot spot for AI, making it a bellwether for the adoption of expert decision-making systems across healthcare and perhaps in other fields. As of early 2026, about three-quarters of the 1,400 AI-enabled medical devices cleared by the Food and Drug Administration were for radiology. Some make physicians more efficient by drafting reports or alerting them to the images that urgently need attention. But other AI tools have the potential to improve on human performance by identifying abnormalities that may not be visible to the human eye, or interpreting images as well as—and sometimes better than—trained radiologists. For example, an analysis of 43 clinical trials concluded that AI-assisted colonoscopies reveal more polyps than conventional ones. Read full article Comments

articles.title: Show HN: A hash-chained ledger for AI reasoning you can verify yourself
articles.summary: SDI protocol defines a reasoning computer for AI. The computer runs an LLM one turn at a time, guiding it through a reasoning grammar; the grammar, which is both natural language and algebraic, allows it to be checked at a compile gate. The gate validates safety, a workfloor, and alignment with t
articles._body: SDI protocol defines a reasoning computer for AI. The computer runs an LLM one turn at a time, guiding it through a reasoning grammar; the grammar, which is both natural language and algebraic, allows it to be checked at a compile gate. The gate validates safety, a workfloor, and alignment with the grammar before it commits. What commits is a hash-chain ledger of the agent's reasoning, forming a longitudinal data set that becomes the agent's functional memory/system state. Chromite, the protocol's public agent, has been reasoning on one continuous hash chain since springtime this year and has used multiple models through three frontier providers to do so. What makes it more than a log of its reasoning is an argumentation graph. The graph is the memory and is retrieved and fed to the agent during its call sequence. The agent can hold or defeat prior acts, keeping the memory calibrated and the context window under control. Anyone can pull an act and recompute the seals for Chromite; it exists to be examined; that is what this post is requesting. No account, no SDK, curl and Python. I spent 20+ years as a Marine working in command and control, learning decision doctrine and intelligence gathering. I have been working on this system for roughly three years and its a solo build. I have a lineage page on the site to show the computing and reasoning traditions this system uses, but that was all discovered along the way or after the build. This system really comes from taking decision doctrine and turning it into a computable syntax and taking intelligence-gathering techniques for evidence handling. Ten seconds, if you just want to see the gate work: curl -s https://www.sdi-protocol.org/_functions/der | python3 -c "import json,sys; print(json.dumps(json.load(sys.stdin)['golden_example']))" > example.json curl -s -X POST https://www.sdi-protocol.org/_functions/compile -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d @example.json Returns PASS. What you just submitted is a complete reasoning record, with every required block, which is why it passes. Delete one field and resubmit; the error names the specific failure. To examine system liveness, pull Chromite's last 5 reasoning acts. You will see the full reasoning act. The grammar, cited sources, and reasoned positions. curl -s "https://api.sdi-protocol.org/ledger/recent/SDI-5AA8C82A2537?n=5" | python3 -m json.tool Fifteen minutes, if you want to verify the chain: sdi-protocol.org/verify walks through pulling a live record and recomputing its hashes, work score, and admissibility index from scratch. The repo has the same scripts, check summed, plus a committed record you can test them against offline first: github.com/StructuredDecisionIntelligence/Structured_Decision_Intelligence Three ethical floors at the gate. DECLARATION_INTEGRITY has fired. The two conjunction-based safety guards, PRIMUM and Absolute Value Guard, that admit no human attestation by permanent design have not fired yet. No act has ever declared the conditions to trip them. Refusal path is a separate hash chain ledger, and the DECLARATION_INTEGRITY check is inspectable. Schema Eras: The reasoning metrics that work at the gate have evolved, the chain remains unbroken, and sealed records permanently carry their eras formulas; sealed records can't be rewritten. The verify script detects each entry's era and applies the right math. The sdi-protocol.org exists to provide transparency over the reasoning protocol that produces transparent AI reasoning. The idea is that both must be transparent to trust either. Disclosure: This will be a commercial product at sdireckoner.com, commissioning a private Reckoner in late fall 2026, but everything in this post is about the free open protocol layer; nothing requires a paid side to verify anything. Chromite exists to be examined by the public as part of the transparency of the protocol itself. Feedback welcome at support@sdi-protocol.org.
