articles.title: Chicago Stars Will Return to Northwestern Lakeside Stadium Next Year
articles.summary: David Banks-Imagn Images
articles._body: The Chicago Stars are extending their stay at Northwestern’s 12,000-seat lakeside college football stadium. The NWSL team played its first match at Martin Stadium last September, drawing more than 10,000 fans, before officially moving in this season. The team is last in the NWSL with a 5-15-1 record. The Stars are set to announce their plans to stay by the lake and open up season ticket deposits for next year later Tuesday. The announcement also means Northwestern will not yet tear down the revamped Martin Stadium, which it upgraded in 2024 . The school had long described the stadium as a temporary solution during construction on its new $875 million football stadium roughly one mile away. The Stars originally wanted to follow the football team into the new Ryan Field, which will hold 35,000 people, but scrapped those plans this spring after resistance from local residents wary of private events at the stadium. Northwestern football is scheduled to play its first game in the new venue against Penn State on Oct. 2. Since 2016, the Stars had played at SeatGeek Stadium in the southwestern suburb of Bridgeview, Ill., which is difficult to reach by public transit. The move to Evanston was initially celebrated by fans for being more accessible, but as the team struggled on the pitch this season, attendance has stayed down. The Stars are so far averaging 4,316 fans per match at home this year, according to the team, the lowest figure in the league. A Wednesday night match in late March drew fewer than 2,000 people. Season ticket sales, however, are up 31% from last year, the team says. The Stars did not share financial details of the deal, and a representative for Northwestern did not respond to a request for comment. But a person familiar with the matter tells FOS that the Stars will pay more to use Northwestern’s facilities in 2027 than they did in 2026, with the reasoning being that they become Martin Stadium’s “primary tenant” after Northwestern football moves. (Northwestern’s defending national champion women’s lacrosse team and soccer teams also play at Martin Stadium.) Earlier this month, the Stars fired coach Martin Sjögren, elevating assistant Karina Báez for the rest of the season. Báez said on Sunday that she views windy conditions by the lake as part of the team’s home field advantage. “It’s a beautiful view, you can see the lake, it’s a beautiful environment, but yes, [the wind is] part of our home,” Báez said in response to a question from FOS . Stalled Plan at New Ryan Field Northwestern added more seats to Martin Stadium, its venue for soccer and lacrosse, ahead of the 2024 college football season as the nearly century-old Ryan Field was demolished. At the time, the school told FOS football revenues would be higher at the lakeside structure than they were at the old 47,000-seat Ryan Field thanks to increased premium seat offerings. While Martin Stadium sits within Northwestern’s campus, the school has long fought with residents in Evanston and neighboring Wilmette over its other athletic facilities located about a mile away. Residents have long complained about noise and traffic from sports and future concerts, and cited Northwestern’s property tax exemption in battles with the private university. Local residents opposed the Stars’ request for special approval from Evanston to move into the new Ryan Field, with one local group saying it “would wreak havoc” on their communities by bringing more private events to the stadium. The Stars said in March they would halt the effort and play all 2026 home games by the lake, citing a local “call for more dialogue and understanding” as well as Northwestern’s “desire to open the new Ryan Field in a phased approach out of consideration for its neighbors.” While the Stars said they weren’t moving forward with their application for the Ryan Field permit “at this time,” the team said it would be “continuing to connect with the community through additional conversations, town halls, and civic engagement.” The next month, the team got Evanston’s approval to play the 2027 season at Martin Stadium, an easier process than obtaining the up to five-year Ryan Field permit. The team’s goal is to eventually move into Ryan Field, the source says, but the Stars aren’t planning to begin that process again until after the new stadium opens in October. Kansas City is currently the only NWSL team with its own stadium, although 2026 expansion team Denver is building its own venue to open in 2028. (Fellow debutant Boston is also renovating its own stadium for public-private use, and last week won a Massachusetts Supreme Court case over local opponents.) The Stars are building their own training facility in the Chicago suburb of Bannockburn, slated to open next year, and have also talked about wanting to one day build their own stadium , too. Many NWSL teams share a venue with an MLS team. In New York, Gotham FC recently announced plans to move from New Jersey into NYCFC’s new Etihad Stadium in Queens. The Stars formerly shared SeatGeek with the Chicago Fire, who are building their own $750 million privately funded stadium in the city’s South Loop, scheduled to open in 2028. The Fire’s current agreement with city officials for McDonald’s Park allows for 45 major events per year, excluding the playoffs, according to the team. That figure will include 17 regular-season home matches, concerts, and other community events, and the stadium doesn’t have restrictions on whether other teams can play there. The NWSL currently has 15 home games per regular season, raising the possibility that the Stars could become tenants at the Fire’s new stadium. The post Chicago Stars Will Return to Northwestern Lakeside Stadium Next Year appeared first on Front Office Sports .

articles.title: Cross Ocean, Fuller Picks Up Massive Houston Office Campus

articles._body: Cross Ocean Partners and Fuller Realty have acquired Eldridge Place, a three-building, 828,784-square-foot office campus in Houston’s Energy Corridor. Commercial Search reports the last time the asset traded hands, in 2019, Granite Properties paid $78.4 million to the seller, TIER REIT. Eldridge Place consists of the 245,315-square-foot One Eldridge Place, the 275,283-square-foot Two Eldridge Place, and the 308,186-square-foot Three Eldridge Place. One and Two were developed in 1986, while Three came online in 2008. Located at 737, 757 and 777 N. Eldridge Parkway, the buildings were 94 percent leased all together at the time of sale. articles.title: Padres Will ‘Live Within Our Means,’ New Owners Say
articles.summary: Denis Poroy-Imagn Images
articles._body: One of MLB’s most aggressive spenders this decade is suggesting that a financial belt tightening could soon arrive, something likely to have large-scale impacts across the league. José E. Feliciano and Kwanza Jones, the new Padres owners, were formally introduced late Monday, heralding their arrival after recently completing a $3.9 billion acquisition that shattered the league record for a valuation in a control transfer . Operating in one of MLB’s smallest and more geographically isolated markets, the Padres often conducted themselves like a high-revenue club under the club’s prior owner, the late Peter Seidler. Prior to Seidler’s death in November 2023, the Padres frequently had a top-10 luxury tax payroll, and even ranked No. 2 behind only the Dodgers in 2021. Even after some more recent retooling, the Padres still rank seventh in the league with a 2026 outlay of $263.8 million. While Feliciano and Jones promised a vigorous pursuit of the club’s first World Series title, something that eluded the Padres since their 1969 formation, they also signaled a more disciplined financial approach. “We are going to live within our means, and that could mean different things in different years,” Feliciano said. “But again, we want to win, and we’re going to continue supporting that goal in many different ways, and that means at some moments, we’re going to be aggressive, but we’re always going to do it with the long-term health of the team in mind.” Financial Matters The Seidler era, extended to somewhat more measured degree by his family and estate after his death, included four Padres playoff berths between 2020 and 2025, and the club is currently in position for another return to the postseason this year. It also was marked by signing the seventh, ninth, and 18th largest contracts in MLB history with Manny Machado, Fernando Tatis Jr., and Xander Bogaerts, respectively, which helped elevate salaries across the league. But the team also generated undisclosed operating losses under Seidler estimated to be well into eight figures. In early 2023, the Padres were the first MLB club to lose its local media rights tie with Main Street Sports Group, now not broadcasting, and San Diego remains part of the league’s in-house program for local game production and distribution. The Padres’ willingness to spend aggressively in pursuit of championship glory has been repeatedly cited by the MLB Players Association as a model for others around the league—but also is an approach under threat as the union and league are engaged in a fractious labor fight that includes a management proposal for a hard salary cap . “San Diego is a small-market team. They went out, decided to compete, signed a lot of players, turned around their franchise,” MLBPA interim executive director Bruce Meyer said in June regarding the Padres. “They’ve grown attendance. They’ve grown interest, and we’ve all seen the exploding in their franchise value. They went under our revenue-sharing system from a revenue-sharing recipient to a revenue-sharing payor because they went out and tried to compete.” The husband-and-wife team of Feliciano and Jones, meanwhile, pledged to continue the robust attendance patterns of their ownership predecessors. The Padres set a franchise attendance record of 3.4 million at Petco Park last season, and now solidly rank as the game’s second-best draw behind the rival Dodgers. “We have been blessed with a team in a city that is supporting us in a way that is allowing us to invest back in the team, in the stadium, and in the city,” Feliciano said. The Padres’ new owners remain on the hook to Machado, Bogaerts, and Tatis Jr. well into the 2030s, and by 2029, that trio alone will be owed more than $100 million annually. Feliciano, the cofounder of private investment firm Clearlake Capital, is also a part-owner of the Premier League’s Chelsea F.C., and is joined in that franchise with Dodgers owners Mark Walter and Todd Boehly. The post Padres Will ‘Live Within Our Means,’ New Owners Say appeared first on Front Office Sports .

articles.title: Seahawks’ 53-man roster prediction for 2026 NFL season
articles.summary: The Seattle Seahawks have difficult roster decisions almost everywhere. Mike Macdonald’s team has spent August balancing Super Bowl expectations with the brutal reality of assembling a 53-man roster. The result is a fascinating mix of proven veterans, ascending contributors, and hungry dept
articles._body: The Seattle Seahawks have difficult roster decisions almost everywhere. Mike Macdonald’s team has spent August balancing Super Bowl expectations with the brutal reality of assembling a 53-man roster. The result is a fascinating mix of proven veterans, ascending contributors, and hungry depth pieces. Now, with Week 1 approaching, Seattle must decide which combination gives it the best chance to defend its title and which promising players simply cannot fit within the numbers. Final preseason test © Darren Yamashita-Imagn Images The Seahawks’ 2026 preseason has been an intense audition under the glare of HBO’s Hard Knocks cameras. Sure, established starters such as Sam Darnold, Jaxon Smith-Njigba and newly extended cornerstone cornerback Devon Witherspoon were largely preserved for the regular season. However, Macdonald used exhibition matchups against Dallas and Tennessee to stress-test their depth. Underdog wide receiver Montorie Foster Jr seized the spotlight with dynamic perimeter play. The offensive backfield adapted seamlessly through heavy workloads for Jadarian Price and George Holani. The blockbuster signing of veteran cornerback Trevon Diggs and the return of safety Nick Emmanwori from injury further strengthened Seattle’s championship-caliber roster. Offensive Playmakers Quarterback (3): Sam Darnold, Drew Lock, Jalen Milroe Darnold remains the unquestioned starter after establishing stability. Lock offers valuable experience as the primary insurance option. Milroe earns the third spot because of his developmental upside and athletic ability. Running Back (4): Jadarian Price, George Holani, Emanuel Wilson, Brady Russell Charbonnet will begin the season on the reserve list. Price has been one of the more important beneficiaries of Charbonnet’s absence. He has shown that he can handle significant responsibility. Holani has similarly capitalized on expanded opportunities. He gives Seattle another dependable runner capable of absorbing carries. Wilson adds additional depth, while Russell’s fullback versatility makes him valuable in heavier personnel packages. Wide Receiver (6): Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Cooper Kupp, Rashid Shaheed, Tory Horton, Montorie Foster Jr, Emmanuel Henderson Jr Smith-Njigba is the centerpiece , but the supporting cast gives Darnold a fascinating collection of complementary weapons. Kupp brings veteran route-running intelligence and reliability. Shaheed supplies explosive speed capable of changing defensive geometry. Horton provides another perimeter option. Foster’s preseason emergence has transformed him from an under-the-radar candidate into a legitimate contributor. Henderson rounds out a group that offers Seattle speed, experience and versatility. Tight End (3): AJ Barner, Elijah Arroyo, Nick Vannett Barner gives the offense blocking flexibility and a dependable option underneath. Arroyo provides athleticism against linebackers and safeties. Vannett’s experience could ultimately prove decisive in the final roster calculation. Offensive Line Offensive Tackle (3): Charles Cross, Abraham Lucas, Josh Jones Cross starts at left tackle, with Lucas at right tackle. Jones serves as the swing option. Cross and Lucas provide the foundational pieces, while Jones’ versatility is essential because a nine-man offensive-line configuration leaves little room for redundancy. Interior Offensive Line (6): Grey Zabel, Jalen Sundell, Anthony Bradford, Beau Stephens, Christian Haynes, Olu Oluwatimi The interior group is where Seattle’s depth could become particularly important. Sundell’s presence at center, Bradford’s experience at guard and the flexibility of Haynes and Oluwatimi give Seattle multiple ways to handle injuries or matchup-specific adjustments. Defense Defensive Tackle (5): Leonard Williams, Byron Murphy II, Jarran Reed, Rylie Mills, Brandon Pili Williams remains the veteran centerpiece. Murphy provides disruptive athleticism from the interior. Reed’s experience adds stability, particularly in early-down situations. Mills and Pili round out a group designed to keep the defensive front fresh. EDGE (5): DeMarcus Lawrence, Uchenna Nwosu, Derick Hall, Dante Fowler Jr, Jared Ivey Lawrence brings veteran pedigree and power. Nwosu provides speed and versatility. Fowler adds another experienced pass-rushing presence. Hall and Ivey offering rotational energy. Macdonald’s defensive philosophy demands relentless pressure and multiplicity. That makes five edge players a logical allocation. Cornerback (6): Devon Witherspoon, Trevon Diggs, Josh Jobe, Julian Neal, Nehemiah Pritchett, Noah Igbinoghene Witherspoon remains the emotional and competitive fulcrum of the secondary. Diggs gives Seattle another experienced outside defender. The combination allows Macdonald to deploy more aggressive coverage concepts without leaving the defense completely dependent on safety help. Safety (5): Julian Love, Ty Okada, Nick Emmanwori, Bud Clark, Rodney Thomas II Love provides veteran leadership. Emmanwori’s return from injury is particularly significant. The Seahawks now have enough versatility on the back end to disguise coverages and move defenders around before the snap. Special Teams Kicker: Jason Myers Punter: Michael Dickson Long Snapper: Chris Stoll Myers provides reliability at kicker. Dickson remains one of Seattle’s most trusted field-position weapons. Stoll handles long-snapping duties. Unlike several position groups undergoing transition, the specialists offer the Seahawks continuity heading into their title defense. Repeat championship ambitions Steven Bisig-Imagn Images The most striking feature of this projected roster is its balance. Seattle has veteran stars capable of carrying enormous responsibility. articles.summary: Colorado football is coming off a disaster of a season, going just 3-9 in 2025. Deion Sanders has worked heavily in the transfer portal in order to attempt to reshape the roster once again. Sanders was aggressive this offseason to be competitive this year. Regardless, Sanders is just 16-21 at Col
articles._body: Colorado football is coming off a disaster of a season, going just 3-9 in 2025. Deion Sanders has worked heavily in the transfer portal in order to attempt to reshape the roster once again. Sanders was aggressive this offseason to be competitive this year. Regardless, Sanders is just 16-21 at Colorado, with just one bowl game. This is leading to the question of job security around Sanders, according to Ross Dellenger of Yahoo Sports. “That shine in hiring one of the biggest sports celebrities in the industry took a hit last year as the Buffaloes finished 3-9. Sanders has battled serious health issues, spends much of his offseason outside of Boulder and won just three games in 2025 — the second losing season in his three years. The nine-win campaign in 2024, led by Heisman winner Travis Hunter, seems like a distant memory,” Dellenger wrote. “Sanders overturned the roster again with more than 50 new players. With a new AD on board, Fernando Lovo, the Buffs need to show marked improvement if Sanders plans to stick around long term. They kick off the season at Georgia Tech on Sept. 3 in a game that’ll tell us plenty.” While Sanders is not in any immediate danger, with a $26-$28 million buyout, he could be with another bad season. Sanders was great at Jackson State, going 27-6 in three years and winning the SWAC twice. He brought with him his son, Sheduer Sanders, and future Heisman winner Travis Hunter to Colorado. They went 4-8 in their first year before going 9-4 with an Alamo Bowl loss in 2025. Still, they went 3-9 in 2025. Colorado opens their season on the road against Georgia Tech. They also have games agaisnt Texas Tech, Utah, and Houston this year, which could lead to a disaster of a season for the Buffaloes. articles._body: It’s no secret that LeBron James loves his hometown of Akron, Ohio, and the NBA legend will partner with the PGA Tour for a special golf event. They will be teaming up to launch the LeBron James Family Foundation Invitational, which will be held from July 6-7, 2027, at the South Course at Firestone Country Club. The event will feature amateur and pro players from the PGA Tour’s Pathway to Progression Pro-Bound Five program. “Golf has become a passion of mine, and I’ve seen firsthand how the game can open doors, build relationships and create opportunities that many kids don’t even know exist,” James said in a statement (via ESPN). “This partnership with the PGA Tour gives my foundation a chance to introduce my I Promise students and more people to the game at a young age, support talented athletes chasing their dreams, and continue investing in the city of Akron that means everything to me.” The golf outing will connect students in the LeBron James Family Foundation’s I Promise program with pro golfers. The I Promise program is for students and their families in the Akron area. It provides programs, support, and resources to assist the students in school. NBA star LeBron James’ love of golf Bill Streicher-Imagn Images James is known for his love of golf. He launched a YouTube channel devoted to golf earlier in August 2026. He held a golf trip with some of his former Cleveland Cavaliers teammates, including Kevin Love. J.R. Smith, Richard Jefferson, and Tristan Thompson. LeBron is heading into his first year with the Philadelphia 76ers. He decided to sign with the Sixers in free agency after leaving the Los Angeles Lakers. He had spent the last eight seasons in the City of Angels. Now, he joins a team that made it to the Eastern Conference Semifinals last year. The 76ers were swept by the New York Knicks in the series. However, they have added the likes of James and Jaylen Brown during the offseason. articles.title: Lakers get almost zero love from ESPN experts for West supremacy as Thunder, Spurs dominate

The Lakers want to have a head start in preparing for the new season, especially since they practically have a new roster. With the departure of LeBron James, Doncic and Austin Reaves wil
articles._body: The Los Angeles Lakers are in Slovenia for a mini-training camp and team-building trip hosted by Luka Doncic . The Lakers want to have a head start in preparing for the new season, especially since they practically have a new roster. With the departure of LeBron James, Doncic and Austin Reaves will have to take on even bigger responsibilities for the Purple and Gold. They have proven that they can mesh well despite being both high-usage players. Doncic and Austin will likely be joined by Walker Kessler, Jake LaRavia, and Quentin Grimes in the starting lineup. While the Lakers are no pushovers, ESPN analysts believe the team is not among the top contenders in the Western Conference. Los Angeles only earned two votes in the poll for the possible winner of the Western Conference. The Oklahoma City Thunder and the San Antonio Spurs dominated with 88 votes and 74 votes, respectively. “It will be surprising if there isn’t a rematch of last season’s West Finals, a seven-game battle won by the Spurs that seemed like the first chapter of the NBA’s next epic rivalry. The Thunder (60.5) and Spurs (59.5) have by far the conference’s highest over/unders for projected wins, according to DraftKings,” wrote ESPN’s Tim MacMahon. The Thunder and the Spurs each retained their core, with the former drafting Aday Mara and the latter adding Tobias Harris. MacMahon also gave honorable mention to the Minnesota Timberwolves , who received nine votes. He lauded the addition of LaMelo Ball, with the Timberwolves forming “arguably the league’s most talented backcourt” with Anthony Edwards. The Lakers had a 53-29 record last season, their most wins since the 2010-2011 season. They had an inspired effort in the first round of the playoffs, beating the Houston Rockets despite missing Doncic due to a hamstring injury. They, however, got swept by the Thunder in the second round. The Lakers have not ruled the Western Conference since winning the title in the 2019-2020 season. articles.title: Cubs’ Kevin Gausman getting World Series itch again after self-admitted 2nd-best start of season
articles.summary: The Chicago Cubs’ 7-0 win over the Arizona Diamondbacks on Monday gave Kevin Gausman another reason to believe his new team has the pieces to make a postseason run. Gausman allowed three hits and one walk while striking out six across seven scoreless innings, needing 94 pitches to complete
articles._body: The Chicago Cubs’ 7-0 win over the Arizona Diamondbacks on Monday gave Kevin Gausman another reason to believe his new team has the pieces to make a postseason run. Gausman allowed three hits and one walk while striking out six across seven scoreless innings, needing 94 pitches to complete his strongest outing since the Cubs acquired him from the Toronto Blue Jays at the trade deadline. The right-hander stopped short of calling it his best start of the season, giving that distinction to his seven-inning, one-hit performance against the New York Yankees in June. “Hey, anytime you can beat the Yankees,” Gausman was quoted as saying , per Bob Nightengale of USA Today. Arizona anticipated Gausman’s split-fingered fastball, but he countered by relying on his four-seam fastball to work through the Diamondbacks’ lineup. The outing improved Gausman to 2-1 with Chicago and provided another look at what he could bring to the Cubs’ rotation in the postseason. “The sky’s the limit,” Gausman said. “This defense, this offense, the pitchers that we have here, it’s a really great team. Not many weaknesses. When you play good, clean baseball, you’re going to put your team in a good spot to win every night.” Chicago also received production throughout its lineup despite Pete Crow-Armstrong going hitless in five at-bats and Alex Bregman recording one hit. Pedro Ramírez, Michael Conforto and Carson Kelly combined to go 6-for-10 with two home runs, a triple, a double, four RBIs and four runs. Conforto and Kelly hit consecutive home runs in the sixth inning to help break open the game. Conforto reached base four times, while Ramírez added two hits. “I mean, they’re just relentless, from one through nine,” Gausman said. “There’s no gaps in this lineup.” The win moved Chicago within 5 1/2 games of Milwaukee for the NL Central lead. Information from a report by David Brandt of The Associated Press contributed to this article. articles._body: Last year in Dec. 2025, Jake Paul stepped into the boxing ring with Anthony Joshua. In a fight between different weight classes, Paul fell short and was dominated and defeated by Joshua. However, not only was Paul defeated, but he also suffered a severe broken jaw that required two surgeries. Still out of action and healing from the injury, Paul’s decision to fight Anthony Joshua was recently praised by UFC President Dana White. Although White and Paul have rarely agreed, it was unusual to see White compliment Paul. “I literally didn’t think that was going to happen,” White said on the Plan Bri Uncut show. “And I said — when you go in there and box a guy like AJ, this isn’t a joke. This isn’t a game. That could kill him. And look, he literally broke his face. … It was a ballsy move getting in there with Anthony Joshua.” However, despite his rare praise, White is not fond of bringing Paul to Zuffa Boxing or promoting him whatsoever. “No. That’s not what I do,” White said when asked about bringing Paul to Zuffa Boxing. “There’s obviously a market for that, but that’s not what I do. I put the best fighters in the world against each other. From the minute that they get into the sport, all the way up to world champion, the best fight the best. There’s always going to be a place for the Paul brother type fights, but that’s not what I do. The best. I’m looking for the best fighters in the world.” Paul is currently recovering from the injury and is now interested in pursuing a career in the NFL or participating in MMA fights. articles.summary: The New York Knicks are the defending NBA champions. Two months later, and it is still something to savor. With the 2026-27 NBA season around the corner, New York will be counted on to repeat. However, ESPN experts have the Knicks winning the Eastern Conference, but not the title. Instead, the ex
articles._body: The New York Knicks are the defending NBA champions . Two months later, and it is still something to savor. With the 2026-27 NBA season around the corner, New York will be counted on to repeat . However, ESPN experts have the Knicks winning the Eastern Conference, but not the title . Instead, the experts have the Spurs, whom the Knicks defeated in the Finals , as title favorites along with the Oklahoma City Thunder. The Thunder led the way with 84 points and the Spurs with 74 points. The Thunder also won the Western Conference with 88 points. The Spurs came in second with 74 points. Meanwhile, New York is expected to win the Eastern Conference with 68 points. The Philadelphia 76ers come in second with 51 points. According to ESPN NBA insider Tim MacMahon, the Thunder and Spurs hold the edge because of talent. “Few forecasted New York to go on a title run last season, but Jalen Brunson led the Knicks on a dominant march to the franchise’s first championship in more than five decades, losing only three games in the playoffs. Nevertheless, the Knicks come in a distant third among title favorites, according to our panel, trailing the two West powers that are loaded with ascending talent.” For the Spurs, they obviously have Defensive Player of the Year Victor Wembanyama. They have an emerging core with De’Aaron Fox, Dylan Harper, and Stephon Castle. Meanwhile, the Thunder still have the top-notch Shai Gilgeous-Alexander. They also have depth in Chet Holmgren, Ajay Mitchell, and Jalen Williams. Combine that with LeBron James and Jaylen Brown on the 76ers, and the Knicks have their work cut out for them. articles.title: Bengals rumors: Insider brushes off Joe Burrow trade firestorm after ‘now or never’ comments
articles.summary: The Cincinnati Bengals have incredibly high expectations for the 2026 season. Joe Burrow wants to win a Super Bowl and hasn’t been shy about talking about that goal. But his recent comments have created a firestorm of speculation about a potential trade. Bengals insider Paul Dehner Jr. push
articles._body: The Cincinnati Bengals have incredibly high expectations for the 2026 season. Joe Burrow wants to win a Super Bowl and hasn’t been shy about talking about that goal. But his recent comments have created a firestorm of speculation about a potential trade. Bengals insider Paul Dehner Jr. pushed back on the idea of a Burrow trade after his recent “now or never” comments. “I think the now or never thing has gotten a little too much run,” Dehner Jr. said on Tuesday via The Ross Tucker Podcast. “I mean this is a guy that a couple of months ago, a month ago, right before the end of mandatory minicamp was saying this front office has taken too much heat. They have done an incredible job, they have set us up. It is up to us and the players now.” Burrow was recently asked if 2026 is a “now or never” year for Cincinnati to win a Super Bowl. He simply replied “that’s how I’m treating it.” Dehner Jr. believes that the media is taking this idea and running too far with it. Especially when assuming Burrow would want out of Cincinnati if the 2026 season doesn’t go as planned. “I think people want to turn some of the stuff that he’s said into like oh they win now or he’s out, he’s done with this,” Dehner Jr. continued. “Like no, he’s just trying to instill urgency inside that locker room. He is trying to keep his foot on the pedal every day for every player, for every coach. … This is about Joe Burrow really leaning into the urgency because he said it very clearly multiple times, he just thinks they’re really good. He thinks this team can win a Super Bowl and he’s not afraid to say it.” Meanwhile, the optimism around Cincinnati is quite understandable after upgrading their defense this offseason. Hopefully the Bengals can finally make a deep playoff run again in 2026. Next up for the Bengals is their preseason finale against the Eagles on August 28th. articles.title: Bears’ 53-man roster prediction for 2026 NFL season
articles.summary: The Chicago Bears are planning to show their competition in the NFC North that the 2025 season was just a starting point for the franchise and not just a fluky, first-place finish. The Bears responded brilliantly to the coaching of Ben Johnson and his staff and played their best football during t
articles._body: The Chicago Bears are planning to show their competition in the NFC North that the 2025 season was just a starting point for the franchise and not just a fluky, first-place finish. The Bears responded brilliantly to the coaching of Ben Johnson and his staff and played their best football during the most crucial moments of late-season games to win the division title and gain a postseason victory over the archrival Green Bay Packers. Caleb Williams improved dramatically from his lukewarm rookie season in 2024 and looked like an elite quarterback. The Bears should have the ability to light up the scoreboard this season and Williams has a pair of game-changing players in WR Rome Odunze and TE Colston Loveland. However, there are questions about the crucial left tackle position. If the Bears can’t protect Williams’ back side, Johnson may not be able to develop the strategy that is needed for the offense to reach its potential. The Bears defense has multiple issues because they ranked 29th in yards allowed last year and were dependent on taking the ball away from their opponents. Kevin Byard, Nahshon Wright and Tremaine Edmunds combined for 16 interceptions last year, and all three are no longer with the team. Here’s our projection as to what that 53-man roster will look like at 6 p.m. ET Sunday. Quarterbacks (3) Caleb Williams, Tyson Bagent, Case Keenum If the Bears are going to build off of what they accomplished last year, it’s all about Williams continuing to make plays when the game is on the line. He has brilliant escapability and that allowed him to buy enough time for his receivers to get open and make big plays. He needs to be more accurate with his short- and medium-range throws this season. The Bears love Bagent as their backup quarterback because he plays with confidence and surprising leadership. Keenum has a solid track record when asked to take over under center. Running Backs (3) D’Andre Swift, Kyle Monangai, Salvon Ahmed The running game is one of the most underrated aspects of the Bears’ offense and Swift ran for 1,087 yards and averaged nearly 5.0 yards per carry. He should be able to match or exceed those numbers in 2026. Monangai is tough to bring down and finishes his runs with authority. Ahmed will edge out Roschon Johnson for the last RB spot. Wide Receivers (6) Rome Odunze, Luther Burden III, Kalif Raymond, Jahdae Walker, Zavion Thomas, Scotty Miller There is a huge change from last season as veteran D.J. Moore has moved on to the Buffalo Bills and that means that Odunze is the team’s go-to guy. Burden has the guts to go over the middle and make by big plays. Raymond is expected to make a solid contribution and get the job done on key third-down plays. Miller will earn the final WR spot over Kaden Thomas because he can make the tough catch and absorb the hit. Tight Ends (3) Mandatory Credit: Matt Marton-Imagn Images Colston Loveland, Cole Kmet, Sam Roush Johnson loves using multiple-TE formations and he will be tempted go with four tight ends on the roster. However, he will end up with three tight ends, and that’s bad news for Stephen Carlson. Loveland should be one of the best tight ends in the league and Kmet is not far behind. Offensive Line (9) Braxton Jones, Joe Thuney, Garrett Bradbury, Jonah Jackson, Darnell Wright, Ozzy Trapilo, Theo Benedet, Logan Jones, Jordan McFadden This is the area that Williams is most dependent on for his success, and while the group looks solid, the left tackle position is somewhat shaky. When Jones is healthy, he is competent and can get the job done, but he had a minor knee injury in training camp. He should be ready to start in Week 1 against the Carolina Panthers, but depth at that position is clearly an issue. Thuney is one of the best interior blockers in the league. Bradbury is a veteran center who has played with the Vikings and Patriots. He has plenty of know-how, but bigger, stronger interior pass rushers give him problems. Center Drew Dalman’s retirement is an issue for this group. Defensive Line (10) Montez Sweat, Grady Jarrett, Gervon Dexter Sr., Dayo Odeyingbo, Austin Booker, Daniel Hardy, Neville Gallimore, Kentavius Street, Marcus Davenport, Jamree Kromah The Bears need Sweat to play with consistency from Week 1 through Week 18 and once again put double-digit sacks on the board. Odeyingbo is coming back from a ruptured Achilles and he will be an every-down player. Dexter needs to continue to grow in his position. Kromah will make the final roster because of his hustle and excellent work in training camp. Linebackers (6) Mandatory Credit: Bob Kupbens-Imagn Images T.J. Edwards, Devin Bush, D’Marco Jackson, Jack Sanborn, Noah Sewell, Ruben Hyppolite II The loss of Tremaine Edmunds could be a big problem for defensive coordinator Dennis Allen. Bush will be an excellent addition because of his speed and instincts. Sanborn is an excellent fit and he is also an eye-catching special-teams player. There may be a chance that 5th-round pick Keyshaun Elliott takes the last LB spot and sends Hyppolite to the practice squad. Cornerbacks (6) Jaylon Johnson, Tyrique Stevenson, Malik Muhammad, Josh Blackwell, Jaylon Jones, Dontae Manning The absence of Kyler Gordon from the roster means he will be on the Reserve/PUP list. Ben Johnson seems annoyed that Gordon has not participated during training camp after playing just 3 games last year. Jaylon Johnson is the best cover man of the group and Stevenson must pick up his game this season or the Bears will be vulnerable in coverage. Safeties (4) Cam Lewis, Dillon Thieneman, Xavier Woods, Skyler Thomas This area could be disastrous for the Bears. Not only did they lose Byard, the league’s leader in interceptions last year, the season-ending injury suffered by Coby Bryant leaves this group in a vulnerable situation. The Bears need rookie Thieneman to step in and play like a veteran from the start. Special Teams (3) Cairo Santos

articles.title: JOL’s Countdown to Kickoff: No. 9
articles.summary: JOL continues its countdown to kickoff with a look at historical Jacket Joshua Nesbitt, current Jackets Amontrae Bradford and Grady Adamson.
articles._body: The countdown is on until “Toe Meets Leather” on Sept. 3 when Georgia Tech hosts Colorado in the 2026 season opener on The Flats. Over the next several days JOL will look at at least one current Jacket and/or a historical Jacket of the corresponding number to the days until kickoff, continuing today with No. 9. Historical Jacket: Joshua Nesbitt Joshua Nesbitt was the first quarterback to run Paul Johnson’s option attack after he took the head coaching job at Georgia Tech in 2008, and Nesbitt set the bar very high for all the QBs to come in the future with his control of the offense, physical running style and ability to hurt the defense with his arm as well. Nesbitt was a highly-rated recruit in the class of 2007 thanks to in incredible high school career at Greene County High (Ga.) in Greensboro where he was a two-time First-Team All-State pick and the Class AA Offensive Player of the Year as a junior, throwing for more than 5,000 yards and 63 touchdowns and running for than 1,700 yards in his final two prep seasons. Despite being recruited by multiple other premier programs, Nesbitt decided to stay close to home and sign with Georgia Tech as part of former head coach Chan Gailey’s impressive 2007 recruiting class. After serving as the backup quarterback in 2007 behind Taylor Bennett and being used on special packages while running for 339 yards and passing for one touchdown, Nesbitt got his first real chance once Johnson took over the program in 2008 and inserted him as the starter to lead his option offense. As a sophomore, Nesbitt went on to rush for 693 yards and seven touchdowns and throw for another 808 and two touchdowns during Johnson’s first season, which included a share of the ACC Coastal Division title, a win over rival Georgia and a berth in the Chick-fil-A Bowl. Nesbitt and the Jackets really hit their stride offensively in 2009 as the quarterback had a huge season, running for 1,073 yards yards on 279 carries with 18 touchdowns and throwing for 1,701 yards and 10 touchdowns to lead the way to Tech’s 11-3 campaign that included an ACC Championship Game win over Clemson and an Orange Bowl berth. He was named First-Team All-ACC along with six other teammates. Nesbitt finished off his career on The Flats with a strong senior season in 2010 before a late-season arm injury at Virginia Tech cost him the final few games. He still ran for 737 yards and 10 touchdowns and threw for 674 yards and seven touchdowns in nine games. Nesbitt ranks first in Georgia Tech program history in career rushing yards by a quarterback with 2,806 while also being seventh in career rushing yards overall. He’s third all-time in career rushing touchdowns with 35 and has the third-highest single-season rushing touchdown total with his 18 in 2009. Nesbitt signed with the Buffalo Bills as an undrafted free agent in 2011 and eventually was elevated to the 53-man roster late in that season before being waived the following preseason in 2012. Nesbitt was inducted into the Georgia Tech Sports Hall of Fame in 2022 and the Georgia High School Football Hall of Fame in 2025. Georgia Tech’s Amontrae Bradford works through drills at a recent fall camp practice. (Photo by Kelly Quinlan/JOL) Current Jackets: Amontrae Bradford and Grady Adamson Wearing the No. 9 this season are a pair of Jackets, junior defensive end Amontrae Bradford and redshirt-freshman quarterback Grady Adamson . Bradford came to Tech as part of the 2024 recruiting class out of Statesboro where he was ranked as a 3-star prospect by Rivals. He played in 10 games as a freshman on The Flats, mostly on special teams, and recorded two tackles. Bradford took a big jump in playing time and production in 2025 as he saw action in 13 games and started seven while compiling 20 tackles (10 solo), 5.5 tackles-for-loss, 2.5 sacks, four QB hurries and one pass breakup. Bradford is majoring in architecture at Georgia Tech. Adamson was part of the 2025 signing class for Tech after being rated as a 3-star quarterback and No. 25-ranked player at his position in the class by Rivals out of Deer Creek (Okla.). He didn’t see game action in his first year on The Flats and redshirted. Adamson, who is now well known for his efforts in the weight room including a 600-plus pound squat max this past summer, is majoring in business administration at Georgia Tech. Georgia Tech’s Grady Adamson makes a throw during a drill at a recent fall camp practice. (Photo by Kelly Quinlan/JOL)

articles.title: Big Ten will not allow NFL players return to college football
articles.summary: The Big Ten has made a stand. Will the SEC follow suit?
articles._body: LSU has recently taken two commitments from NFL players involved in training camps. Kentucky is recruiting former UCLA and SMU running back TJ Harden . The former three-star recruit was just released by the Seattle Seahawks. Pure chaos is going on in college athletics right now. Some in college football have seen enough. The Big Ten decided to make a stand on Tuesday. Tony Petitti’s league will not allow NFL players to return to college football and play for a conference member . “Sources: The Big Ten is set to pass a rule today that doesn’t allow players to return from the NFL and play for a Big Ten school,” ESPN’s Pete Thamel wrote on social media. “Anyone who has declared for the NFL Draft and did not withdraw, appeared on an NFL roster or signed a contract with a pro league cannot be on a Big Ten roster.” On3’s Pete Nakos reports that the ACC is considering a similar rule and that the SEC will discuss a similar rule on Tuesday during meetings in Birmingham with commissioner Greg Sankey and university presidents. Expectation is that the SEC will talk over a similar rule at today's meetings in Birmingham. Big Ten has meeting later today. https://t.co/TsfYBP5ePV — Pete Nakos (@PeteNakos) August 25, 2026 If the same rule that the Big Ten is using applies to the SEC, then Alex Afari Jr. would be consdiered ineligible by the conference after he entered the 2026 NFL Draft and went undrafted before signing a rookie camp deal with the Green Bay Packers. What does it mean for Mark Mitchell ? That is to be determined after the new Kentucky commit signed an Exhibit 10 deal to play with the Denver Nuggets in NBA Summer League. The action to enforce this potential rule has already started in the SEC. Yahoo’s Ross Dellenger reports that SEC presidents are expected to direct ADs against accepting pro players . In the age of non-stop eligibility lawsuits, can this conference ruling hold up in court? That should become known soon. Conference leaders are attempting to stop the roster anarchy. Is self-governance at the conference level a feasible solution for college athletics? We’re about to find out. articles._body: UNLV needed a new quarterback for the 2026 season. UNLV lost quarterback Anthony Colandrea to the transfer porta l, leading to the need for a new QB1. The team brought in former Oklahoma and Auburn quarterback Jackson Arnold to compete with Alex Orji for the starting job. Now, UNLV coach Dan Mullen has made a decision , per Pete Nakos of On3. “UNLV head coach Dan Mullen plans to play both Jackson Arnold and Alex Orji on Saturday night against Memphis, he announced,” Nakos posted on X, formerly Twitter. While Mullen noted that both will play, he did not say who will get the first snaps. Arnold is attempting to resurrect his career . Arnold was a four-star recruit out of high school, while being named Gatorade Football Player of the Year in 2022. He chose to attend Oklahoma. He played in seven games with one start in his freshman season. He was named the starter for the 2024 season, but after struggling was benched in favor of freshman Michael Hawkins Jr. This led to Arnold transferring to Auburn, where he passed for 1,309 yards and six touchdowns. With a new coaching staff coming in, Arnold transferred again to UNLV. Meanwhile, Alex Orji began his career at Michigan, primarily as a backup in 2022 and 2023. He would start three games while playing 11 in 2024 for the Wolverines, primarily being used in running situations. He then decided to transfer, moving to UNLV. Last year, he played in three games with one start for UNLV. In that time, he was three for three for 37 yards while running for 42 yards and a touchdown. articles.title: Billboard Affirms Commitment to Transparency Around AI-Generated Music
articles.summary: Billboard is optimistic about new tools that will tag and identify AI-created songs, including Luminate's proprietary AI detection program.
articles._body: On Tuesday (Aug. 25), Billboard announced its commitment to creating greater transparency around the use of artificial intelligence in music, including identifying songs on its charts and in its editorial coverage that use AI. Billboard remains committed to accurately reflecting how audiences around the world consume music. For nearly a century, the Billboard charts have served as the industry’s most trusted record of the music fans embrace, evolving alongside new forms of artistic expression and technological innovation. Related Luminate to Add Labels to AI Music Later This Year The Recorded Music Industry Wants Labels on AI Music. How Could That Work? (FAQ) Record Companies Want to Regulate AI Tracks. How Do Their Proposals for Charts and Streaming Services Compare? A combination of committed content creator/artist transparency and reliable tools to identify AI-generated music is essential to making well-informed decisions when categorizing AI-generated content. This shared commitment to responsibly reporting AI use is critical to the wider industry and will help ensure that the charts continue to reflect music consumption accurately and responsibly. “Ensuring transparency around AI-generated music requires collaboration across the entire industry from artists and labels to DSPs, technology companies and industry organizations,” said Silvio Pietroluongo, EVP, Charts & Data Partnerships, Billboard . “We’re encouraged by the development of new identification tools and will continue testing and leveraging solutions across the ecosystem, to ensure our charts continue to accurately and responsibly reflect music consumption.” “ Billboard will always champion artists, celebrate music and promote editorial transparency,” said Leila Cobo, Co-Chief Content Officer, Billboard . “In this moment of evolution, it is critical that creators leveraging AI identify use so that we can be transparent and accurate in our editorial coverage and in our charts.” Billboard remains dedicated to an open, collaborative dialogue with industry stakeholders, including artist communities, label groups, DSPs, AI music companies and organizations advancing this conversation and promoting transparency in AI tagging, as the industry works diligently to navigate these complexities and develop solutions. “Although the ways in which AI informs and interacts with modern music are changing on a daily basis, we are committed to working alongside all industry parties allowing us to make clear, well-informed decisions across our platforms, now and moving forward,” said Jason Lipshutz, Co-Chief Content Officer, Billboard . Billboard is optimistic about the development of new and first-to-market tools and initiatives that will tag and identify AI-created songs — including the recent announcement from Luminate regarding its proprietary AI detection program — as well as commitments by industry bodies and DSPs to identify and tag AI-generated songs across various platforms. Billboard will continue to collaborate broadly across the industry, testing available tools, leveraging its editorial and data analytics expertise, and developing best practices to achieve these goals.

articles.title: New York Times reveals scary study showing at least 25% of NFL players get CTE, and it may be higher
articles.summary: Over the last 20 years, CTE and the NFL have been a hot topic, as hundreds of former players have been posthumously diagnosed with it, and a new study uncovered by the New York Times showed how many athletes get it. According to new data from the New York Times, at least one in four […]
articles._body: Over the last 20 years, CTE and the NFL have been a hot topic, as hundreds of former players have been posthumously diagnosed with it , and a new study uncovered by the New York Times showed how many athletes get it. According to new data from the New York Times, at least one in four NFL players get CTE. The study was of hundreds of cases over a recent six-year period (2016 to 2021). The study considered all 878 former NFL players who died in that time frame. “Some” passed away in their 20s, while “some” were in their 80s. However, “most” of the players were “in between” those ages. 215 of the 878 former players, which is 24.5%, had CTE. Unfortunately, the prevalence of the disease may be higher, as the study didn’t consider the 643 brains that weren’t examined. There is a chance that most of those players also had it. Some players aren’t surprised by this figure. In fact, former Tampa Bay Buccaneers center Randy Grims, 66, said that he imagines “the real number is a lot bigger.” CTE is caused by repeated impacts to the head. As of now, it can only be diagnosed posthumously. According to the New York Times, the rate of CTE in those who haven’t sustained repeated impacts to the head is “nearly zero.” The disease was first discovered almost a century ago in boxers. Initially, it was called “dementia pugilistica.” Some of the symptoms include memory loss, confusion, and uncharacteristic mood swings. Additionally, decreases in executive function and increases in erratic and impulsive behavior (which includes addiction) are also potential symptoms. Football is the sport most associated with CTE, due to the physicality of the sport. However, it is found in other athletes in sports like hockey, rugby, and soccer. Wrestlers and bobsledders have also been diagnosed with it. Military veterans who work with artillery may also be susceptible to CTE. The new data comes after former NFL quarterback Matt Hasselbeck announced his participation in scans and tests to try to find a living diagnosis of CTE. articles._body: First came the Carolina Panthers hype for Bryce Young . Then the quarterback stumbled a bit . But there’s no doubt about his standing on the team. That’s not the case with other players, and here is the prediction for the Panthers’ 53-man roster for the 2026 NFL season. It could be a tough season for the Panthers if Young takes a step back instead of moving forward. Making the right roster decisions would help him. Quarterbacks (3) Bryce Young, Kenny Pickett, Haynes King Young is QB1, and Pickett is QB2. So does King fit into the 53-man equation? It’s a tough call, but he looked good in the Hall of Fame contest. It doesn’t help King’s cause that he suffered a hamstring injury in the contest. For now, it looks like the Panthers will roll with three QBs. But if things get really tight this week at another position, King might join Kyle Trask on the outs. Running backs (4) Chuba Hubbard, Jonathon Brooks, Trevor Etienne, AJ Dillon This is actually an interesting backfield mix. It’s potentially strong and deep. Keeping Dillon cuts out Anthony Tyus III. But that looks like the right call. Regardless, the Panthers seem to want a committee approach , according to a post on X by Joe Person. “Canales: If Chuba is good to go, it will be RB by committee (w/ Brooks) in Week 1.” Wide receiver (6) Tetairoa McMillan, Jalen Coker, Xavier Legette, Jimmy Horn Jr., Brycen Tremayne, Ja’seem Reed There are a couple of tough cuts here. But that’s a good sign of a strong receiver room, especially since the Panthers lost a potential star to injury in rookie Chris Brazzell II. Out are David Moore and John Metchie. The latter particularly hurts because he has NFL ability, for sure. But Reed has earned trust , according to panthers.com. “He’s consistently where I need him to be,” backup quarterback Kenny Pickett said. “We have great conversations on the field, off the field. I have full faith he’s going to be where I need him to be, and he just keeps showing up. So there’s no surprise.” Young also had praise for Reed. “Same thing he’s been doing all camp, being consistent, doing a great job of winning, great job of understanding leverage, understanding route timing, and for us, I think someone that we can trust,” Young said. “We feel like that with all of our guys. But when you go out there, and you just see him continue to put it on film … We all trust him in the room, so it’s no surprise he’s been having the success of that.” Tight ends (4) Tommy Tremble, Mitchell Evans, Ja’Tavion Sanders, Feleipe Franks This is a tough call. The Panthers signed Darren Waller last week. But he’s old and injury-prone. Does he get a roster spot ? No, says ESPN. “The addition of Darren Waller raised eyebrows,” Mike Kaye wrote. “But the lack of interest in him before his signing and his lack of workload before cuts could make him more of a practice-squad option, barring a trade of an incumbent tight end. Waller isn’t subject to waivers, so the Panthers can be strategic with the vested veteran’s inclusion in and around the cut-down deadline.” Franks’ special teams value keeps him on board. Offensive line (8) Rasheed Walker, Damien Lewis, Luke Fortner, Robert Hunt, Monroe Freeling, Brady Christensen, Sam Hecht, Stone Forsythe The call between Forsythe and Jake Curhan is razor-thin close. The Panthers could be OK either way. But overall, this line could struggle , according to Pro Football Focus. “Carolina has quietly built an above-average offensive line in recent seasons,” Bradley Locker wrote. “But injuries and exits have already taken a toll — and are casting real doubt about how strong the unit will be in 2026. “Ikem Ekwonu is expected to miss the majority of the season after suffering a ruptured patellar tendon in the playoffs, while Taylor Moton will be sidelined into the starting slate due to blood clots in his lung.” The Panthers plugged gaps with Freeling, a first-round pick. But the unit will have three new starters. Defensive line (5) Derrick Brown, Bobby Brown III, Cam Jackson, Lee Hunter, Elijah Garcia This would leave Aaron Hall out in the cold. However, Garcia has earned a place with a standout camp. The four-year veteran has bounced around to four teams already. And he has experienced very limited game action. Perhaps Garcia only sticks around until Tershawn Wharton gets off the PUP list. But at least he would have a shot. Outside linebacker/Edge (5) Jaelan Phillips, Patrick Jones II, Princely Umanmielen, Thomas Incoom, Trevis Gipson There’s quite a battle for the final spot of this group. It’s between Trevis Gipson, Cam Gill, and Jeremiah Moon. Incoom is safe because of his special teams prowess. Of course, Nic Scourton’s season-ending preseason injury opened up a spot that otherwise wouldn’t have been there. Inside linebacker (5) Devin Lloyd, Trevin Wallace, Claudin Cherelus, Bam Martin-Scott, Jackson Kuwatch There aren’t any current cut candidates. However, the Panthers may tinker with this position. “The Panthers might be looking for an upgrade opposite Lloyd over the next few days,” Kaye wrote. “Wallace and Cherelus are still competing for the other starting job this summer, and neither option has run away with the gig. Martin-Scott is a promising 2025 holdover who has been a productive special teams player. Kuwatch, the team’s 2026 seventh-round pick, is a long-term development keeper.” Cornerback (5) Jaycee Horn, Mike Jackson, Chau Smith-Wade, Will Lee III, Akayleb Evans The Panthers are rock solid in the starting lineup with Horn and Jackson. articles.title: Big Ten responds to Lane Kiffin’s NFL shenanigans with rule that SEC, ACC, Big 12 will mimic
articles.summary: The NCAA football landscape is changing drastically this offseason. Following news that LSU football was going to bring in a former NFL player to the 2026 roster, college athletics conferences are scrambling to respond to that. The Big Ten is one of those conferences. “Sources: The Big Ten
articles._body: The NCAA football landscape is changing drastically this offseason. Following news that LSU football was going to bring in a former NFL player to the 2026 roster, college athletics conferences are scrambling to respond to that. The Big Ten is one of those conferences . “Sources: The Big Ten is set to pass a rule today that doesn’t allow players to return from the NFL and play for a Big Ten school. Anyone who has declared for the NFL Draft and did not withdraw, appeared on an NFL roster or signed a contract with a pro league cannot be on a Big Ten roster,” ESPN’s Pete Thamel posted to X, formerly Twitter. The ACC is expected to follow suit , per Yahoo Sports reporter Ross Dellenger. Dellenger then posted soon after that the Big 12 is also set to address the issue. “The Big 12 is also considering a league-wide policy banning pro players returning to the conference, meaning that all four power leagues are set to consider such a rule,” Dellenger wrote. Kiffin is set to start his first season at LSU, in just days. News broke recently that former Ole Miss tight end Dae’Quan Wright would be leaving the NFL and joining LSU. Wright was playing this summer for the Cleveland Browns. That move was met with a firestorm of criticism from college football analysts. Kiffin defended the decision . “They’re available to recruit. So, ourselves, like many places around the country, are recruiting them,” Kiffin said, per the Associated Press. It isn’t clear how this will all play out. The SEC was also looking into the situation , as it appears LSU adding Wright may be against SEC rules. Kiffin is no stranger to controversy. He left the Ole Miss football program during the 2025 season, while the team was getting ready for a College Football Playoff appearance. LSU kicks off their 2026 season with a game against Clemson. That contest is scheduled for September 5. The post Big Ten responds to Lane Kiffin’s NFL shenanigans with rule that SEC, ACC, Big 12 will mimic appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles.summary: After being called out for staying put in the offseason, the Golden State Warriors made an under-the-radar move on Monday by signing a promising guard. The Warriors added more depth in the backcourt after acquiring Brandon Williams on a short-term deal. Williams spent the last three years with th
articles._body: After being called out for staying put in the offseason, the Golden State Warriors made an under-the-radar move on Monday by signing a promising guard. The Warriors added more depth in the backcourt after acquiring Brandon Williams on a short-term deal. Williams spent the last three years with the Dallas Mavericks. ESPN’s Shams Charania revealed the savvy move by Golden State. “Free agent guard Brandon Williams has agreed to a one-year, $2.6 million deal to sign with the Golden State Warriors, agents Derek Lafayette and Curtis Lawrence told ESPN. Williams averaged 13 points, 3.9 assists, and 22.2 minutes per night across 66 games for Dallas last season,” wrote Charania on X. The 26-year-old Williams had a breakout campaign last season , displaying his speed and athleticism. His ability to go downhill and create plays off the dribble should help the Warriors, especially with their aging core. Last month, ClutchPoints’ Brett Siegel reported that Golden State was eyeing Williams . “Sources say Kelly Olynyk, Brandon Williams, Gabe Vincent, and Gary Payton II are all players in consideration for a minimum deal from the Warriors, along with current two-way guard LJ Cryer,” said Siegel. Williams will likely come off the bench, joining Payton, Cryer, De’Anthony Melton, Moses Moody, and Will Richard in the backcourt rotation in the second unit. Williams, who went undrafted in 2021, took advantage of the opportunities given to him in Dallas last season, with Kyrie Irving out with an ACL injury. While he was erratic at times, he showed he can contribute on both ends of the floor. The post Warriors add ex-Mavericks guard who scored 13 PPG last season appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles.title: Dexter and the Moonrocks Want ‘to Set the Tone of What Rock Music Is Going to Be’
articles.summary: How the fast-rising grunge band is shaping what “a new rock star is.”
articles._body: “We’re four dumbasses from West Texas — like us or hate us, this is who we are,” drummer Ryan Fox (commonly referred to as just Fox) says matter-of-­factly of a band that has both helped to resurrect the sound of ’90s grunge and bring them back to the Billboard charts. The four members of Dexter and the Moonrocks started out exploring red-dirt country but have surged to the forefront of the current rock revival with songs that marry country’s confessional lyrics (“I’m a bad guy” stories, as guitarist Ryan Anderson puts it) with grunge’s heavy guitars, acoustic introspection and affinity for strong melody. The resulting sound — they’ve dubbed it “Western space grunge,” the name of their July 2024 debut EP — is powered by singer James Tuffs’ ­magnetic, raw vocals and can evoke everything from Alice in Chains to Weezer. After getting together outside Abilene and releasing its debut single in 2021, the band began a still-relentless live schedule, getting signed by Severance Records in a joint venture with Big Loud Rock in 2023 and making its alternative radio breakthrough the following year. But it wasn’t until earlier this year that Dexter and the Moonrocks became a true commercial force, when its smash, “Freakin’ Out,” spent five weeks at No. 1 on Alternative Airplay , broke onto Pop Airplay and became the band’s Billboard Hot 100 debut, reaching No. 33. It will be on the debut full-length, Friends That I Don’t Like (out Oct. 2), from the four guys who all still live within two hours of each other in northwest Texas. As Anderson vows, “We’re never, ever moving to Nashville.” Related Dexter and the Moonrocks Land Second Alternative Airplay No. 1 With ‘Freakin’ Out’ How Rising Rock Bands Edgehill & Dexter and the Moonrocks Landed Their Biggest Chart Hits to Date Chartbreaker: Could Rising Rock Band Edgehill Top Alternative Airplay Twice? Why ‘Love To Go’ Is Climbing Fast Why did “Freakin’ Out” feel like the right breakout moment for you? Ryan Anderson: I was always under the impression we were going to do this organic growth thing, where three albums later [we] finally blow up. I didn’t think we were going to have a pop moment. But credit to James and Fox; in the studio when we were still working on it, they both were saying, “This is the one.” Ryan Fox: And then you don’t understand what that actually means, and it’s like, oh, this is a way different beast. I think back to like “Ritalin” and “Sad in Carolina” and all those moments where I’m like, “God, these are such good songs, I wish these did bigger.” But there isn’t a universe where I think “Freakin’ Out” isn’t the best moment for this band to accelerate. We finally became professionals touring, we understood our sound and who we wanted to be.  Thank God we had our massive hit when we also had a robust discography, a base of diehard fans and we had done the grinding of touring. We established who we are.   Since “Freakin’ Out” took off, have you seen the effects of your success at radio? Fox: We’ve always been the weird “I don’t know what to do with you, so I’m not going to do anything with you” kind of band. And so the radio success didn’t feel like it was moving my personal needle as much as seeing more and more guys in cowboy hats standing next to goth chicks, and dudes wearing all black going on a date with, like, the most “do-a-dollop-o’-Daisy” girl you’ve ever seen in your life at our concerts. That’s awesome. How did being the “weird band” benefit you? Fox: We had some success and there were people whispering in our ears like, “You need to market yourself this way. You need to appeal to this audience.” There was about a year of that and then we all looked at each other like, “This sucks. Let’s go back to making stuff that we enjoy, that feels like the full amalgamation of our upbringing as musicians.” Anderson: And that’s what got us attention. We said, “We know what got us here, and we appreciate any advice, but we want to trust ourselves.” Fox: Our [2025 EP] Donkey Flats we recorded ourselves out of a double-wide trailer. We kind of hit reset, changed our team, and also, got more of a “f–k you” behind us. And then “Freakin’ Out” came out, and it was finally like, oh, man, we get to set the tone of what this culture is going to be, what rock music is going to be, for the next three to five years. Your music is often heavy — both sonically and lyrically — but you also have a knack for melody. What is the band’s writing process? Anderson: Melody always comes first — not just in [process] order, but I think that’s what we prioritize the most. Fox: We each inherently have our own different styles, and those styles mesh to be us. That’s why we’ve realized we can’t do cowrites — sitting in a room and doing the whole Nashville thing. The only people that really know how to write a Dexter and the Moonrocks song are Dexter and the Moonrocks. How do you guys now characterize the country influence on you?   Anderson: I think originally the country thing kind of bled in because that’s what we were listening to when we started the band, and that’s kind of what we thought we were going to do — not like, boot scootin’ fiddles and steel guitars, but the more Texas-y red dirt thing. And that went away immediately, and the rock thing took over pretty naturally. The confessional side of the lyrics and the “it’s my fault” kind of thing in our songs… that’s where the country comes in these days.   Fox: I’ve always been a big believer that grunge and country talk about the exact same things — loss and addiction and being angry at the government and all of that. For me at least, our sense of country is from a sense of place and identity. We are so proudly Texan. articles.title: Duetti Opens Office in Nashville’s Music Row
articles.summary: The company is closing in on having 100 employees since it first began four years ago, Duetti's CEO Lior Tibon says.
articles._body: Catalog investment firm Duetti has opened a new Music City office, located in Nashville’s Music Row area at 1604 16th Ave. S, Billboard can reveal. The move brings the company’s A&R, publishing and marketing teams under one roof to deepen the company’s partnerships with Nashville-based writers and artists, in order to serve Nashville’s music community, spanning genres including country, Americana, pop, R&B, Gospel, hip-hop and more. Related How Duetti Finds Big Value in Small Catalogs: ‘It’s Not About Aggregating Rights… It’s About Taking Care of Them’ Ella Langley Co-Writer JoyBeth Taylor On ‘Choosin’ Texas’ and ‘I Can’t Love You Anymore’: ‘My Whole Career Changed When I Found My Crew’ Ryan Beuschel Promoted to Co-Head of The Neal Agency Duetti already works with Nashville-based artists and writers including Spencer Crandall, Parson James, Molly Grace, Dave Fenley, Jessie Villa, and Ryder Johnson, and has partnered with more than 50 Nashville artists and songwriters to date. Approximately 30% of those deals have been country music writers and/or artists, 29% being in the pop genre and 12% each in the folk/Americana and rap spaces. “We are a four-year-old company and growing very fast,” Duetti CEO Lior Tibon told Billboard . “We’re going to pretty soon be at 100 full-time employees worldwide and we keep increasing the platform. So we are always thinking where we should expand our footprint. We are following where we see a lot of interest and activity. Since we started, we’ve done deals with over 50 artists and songwriters that are based in Nashville. It’s just a very clear indication that there is a lot of activity and the market here is very receptive to the concept that Duetti is leading.” Duetti, which was founded in 2022 by Tibon and COO Christopher Nolte , partners with indie artists and songwriters to buy, manage and market their catalogs and offers marketing, publishing and A&R support. The company allows artists to monetize a portion of their music rights, while retaining a working partner for creative and marketing. “Before we came into operation, I would say any catalog that is younger than the five-to-seven year mark was considered almost non-financeable at the time, because there were all these restrictions by the banks and other providers,” Tibon said. “We said there’s really no reason for that, and with all the data and information that’s out there, we can definitely go earlier on. Back in June, we announced even taking the threshold lower on the master side, to just six months for us to at least start engaging and thinking about what a deal could look like. It’s not for everyone, but I think especially for younger creators or artists earlier in their career, that’s particularly relevant as just another option.” Since launching, the company has partnered with over 1,100 creators. Beyond catalog investments, Duetti has earned over 5 million playlist followers spanning its user-generated playlist network on Spotify, and has secured sync placements on Netflix, Showtime, SEGA, Apple TV+ and more. They worked with artist Fenley to also offer marketing support for his new album (which is outside of his deal with Duetti), including offering a TikTok campaign and a Spotify Marquee campaign. Fenley said in a statement, “In this industry you encounter so many companies that are simply transactional. Duetti has proven to be anything but that. They’ve invested in my career, celebrated my wins, and have given me a peace of mind that’s very hard to find in the music business.” Duetti also celebrated the opening of the new Nashville office with a launch dinner for artists, managers and other industry friends at Geist.

articles.title: Luminate to Add Labels to AI Music Later This Year
articles.summary: The move follows several announcements by streaming services and the record business to pursue labels for AI content earlier this summer.
articles._body: On Tuesday (Aug. 25), entertainment data company Luminate announced a new framework for AI music. This includes the addition of labels for AI-generated content on its platform, starting later this year, which will be visible to its customers and partners. The move comes just weeks after Apple Music and Spotify announced plans for their own versions of labeling for AI music by the end of 2026. Luminate’s system will rely on a combination of its proprietary identification technology and collaborations with major streaming services and AI music companies to determine which songs should be labeled. A label stating “AI Generated” will be added to any song or artist profile identified through their system, and, in the case of false positives, artists and labels can go through a “dedicated review process” to have the labels reconsidered. Related Billboard Affirms Commitment to Transparency Around AI-Generated Music Dale Morris, Nashville Manager Who Guided Careers of Alabama & Kenny Chesney, Dies at 89 HYBE Pledges Over $300k for Colombia Earthquake Recovery In its framework, Luminate’s CEO Rob Jonas states that “this is a starting point. No single organization can address this challenge alone,” and details a three-pronged approach to labeling: Proprietary Identification System: Luminate’s technology continuously analyzes streaming data and metadata, in addition to leveraging audio identification tools to track AI-generated music in CONNECT. Streaming Data: As DSPs roll out their own capabilities for identifying AI-generated music, Luminate will support ingestion of this data through its existing partnerships. Attribution at the Source: To capture AI-generated music before a song or artist reaches a DSP, Luminate is in discussion with AI music companies to source attribution data directly as content is generated. Dating back to early 2025, online music platforms have been toying with the concept of clear labels to disclose AI music to the public. First, in January of last year, Deezer added tags to 100% AI-generated tracks, and this year several others have followed suit. Spotify is now tagging what it calls “AI Personas” rather than tracks, and Apple Music is going to add AI labels based on self-disclosed AI use later this year. Many members of the recorded music industry, which provides songs to the streaming services, have also weighed in on the debate, signaling their support for AI label measures in July. Related The Recorded Music Industry Wants Labels on AI Music. How Could That Work? (FAQ) Still, even though this has become a popular way to regulate the flood of AI music, some music listening platforms have taken other approaches. Bandcamp and iHeartRadio , for example, have both issued bans for largely AI-generated music. “The rapid growth of AI-generated music has outpaced the industry’s ability to consistently identify it and measure its impact,” Jonas said of the new Luminate framework. “Greater visibility is critical to understanding broader trends, assessing the risk of fraud and making informed decisions. Luminate has always been the entertainment business’s source of truth, and tracking AI-generated music with the same rigor we apply to every other category is core to our mission.”

articles._body: Vanderbilt knew going into the season that they would need to replace Diego Pavia as QB1. It has been a fight between Jared Curtis and Blaze Berlowtiz for the first start of the season . Now, a decision has been made on QB1, but with a twist, according to Pete Thamel of ESPN. “Vanderbilt senior Blaze Berlowitz will be the starting quarterback to open the season for the Commodores. He’ll make his first career start against Austin Peay on Sept. 5. Five-star true freshman Jared Curtis will also play in that game, marking his first career snaps,” Thamel posted on X, formerly Twitter. Berlowitz is entering his senior season at Vanderbilt. He initially was a backup to quarterback Diego Pavia at New Mexico State, but saw little action. He attempted just 19 passes in 2023, completing ten of them for 134 yards with a touchdown and an interception. He followed his head coach, Jerry Kill, and Pavia to Vanderbilt in 2024. Berlowitz did not see action in 2024, but attempted 17 passes in 2025. He completed nine of the passes for 131 yards and a touchdown. Now, Berlowitz will get his first start. Meanwhile, Curtis was a five-star recruit in the 2026 recruiting cycle. He was initially committed to Georgia, but decided to flip his commitment to Vanderbilt, becoming the highest-ranked recruit to ever sign for Vandy. Whoever ultimately ends up with the QB1 job has some big shoes to fill. Pavia passed for 3,539 yards and 29 touchdowns. He also ran for 862 yards and ten touchdowns last season. With Dwayne “The Rock” Johnson, John Cena, and Dave Bautista being some of the biggest names in the industry, former WWE World Champion Drew McIntyre could be doing something similar. Although he has been involved in other projects with WWE, including a lead acting role. While there has been no update regarding his return timeline, as of this writing, McIntyre is still listed as an active member of WWE’s SmackDown roster. Previously, reports emerged about McIntyre potentially returning at WWE SummerSlam 2026. However, the reports were later dismissed by PWInsider, who claimed that the rumors about his SummerSlam 2026 return were inaccurate due to there being “nothing on the table” for “The Scottish Warrior” creatively in WWE.
