articles.title: Mavericks rumors: Kyrie Irving trade speculation lives after coach leaves Dallas to reunite with LeBron James on 76ers
articles.summary: Many are eager to see the tandem of Kyrie Irving and Cooper Flagg lead the charge for the Dallas Mavericks in the upcoming season. They have yet to play together, as Irving was sidelined with an ACL injury during Flagg’s rookie campaign. Despite the incessant chatter about a possible trade,
articles._body: Many are eager to see the tandem of Kyrie Irving and Cooper Flagg lead the charge for the Dallas Mavericks in the upcoming season. They have yet to play together, as Irving was sidelined with an ACL injury during Flagg’s rookie campaign. Despite the incessant chatter about a possible trade, the Mavericks maintained that they are keen on keeping Irving . Fans, however, have continued to theorize, and the recent exit of Phil Handy as assistant coach of the Mavericks will only give them more fuel. Handy has agreed to join the Philadelphia 76ers to reunite with LeBron James, whom he has won three titles with. The Stein Line’s Marc Stein described Handy’s departure as a “lesser but also notable factor” in the trade speculation surrounding Irving. “Once Irving began to flourish as a Maverick after arriving via the February 2023 trade deadline, his strong relationships with (Jason) Kidd and then-Mavericks assistant coach God Shammgod were frequently cited as key factors in a highly successful transition from Brooklyn,” wrote Stein on his Substack. “When Shammgod left Dallas for Orlando after the 2024-25 season, Handy was hired to fill the vacancy and immediately began working closely with Irving.” Irving and Handy won a ring together on the Cleveland Cavaliers in 2016. The nine-time All-Star has often credited Handy for helping his career and refining his all-around game. The 55-year-old Handy, who also won a championship with the Toronto Raptors and the Los Angeles Lakers, was hired by the Mavericks in 2025 and was assigned to develop Flagg, Brandon Williams, and Ryan Nembhard, among others. His stint in Dallas, however, proved to be short. “When August began, Handy and Josh Broghamer—who worked closer with Flagg than anyone on Kidd’s staff—were the lone holdovers from Kidd’s bench to be retained by new Mavericks coach Dusty May. Yet both also wound up departing the franchise this month. Broghamer (as I reported on August 7) was the first to exit to join Sean Sweeney’s maiden staff in Orlando,” noted Stein. Irving has been linked to the Minnesota Timberwolves, the Detroit Pistons, the Houston Rockets, and the Miami Heat. articles.summary: After his controversial appearance at the Chicago Sky-Indiana Fever game and ineligibility ruling for the WNBA Draft, Enes Kanter Freedom has insisted that he’s a woman. Appearing on Fox News, Kanter Freedom was adamant that he is a “woman,” meaning that he “should be allo
articles._body: After his controversial appearance at the Chicago Sky-Indiana Fever game and ineligibility ruling for the WNBA Draft, Enes Kanter Freedom has insisted that he’s a woman. Appearing on Fox News, Kanter Freedom was adamant that he is a “woman,” meaning that he “should be allowed to play” in the WNBA. “Article 13 Section 1 says if you identify as a woman, then you are [allowed] to play,” he reasoned. “I identify as a woman, sure, yes, so I can play.” Enes Kanter Freedom responds to reports that he’s ineligible to play in the WNBA: “I am a woman. I should be allowed to play.” “Article 13 Section 1 says if you identify as a woman, then you are allowed to play. I identify as a woman, so yes I can play” pic.twitter.com/cR6v7l3SXk — BrickCenter (@BrickCenter_) August 24, 2026 He then said that he is “just following the rules” that are in place. Kanter Freedom claimed that he would be willing to “respect” the WNBA if they change the rules, but as of now, he feels he “should be allowed to play.” Enes Kanter Freedom’s recent WNBA controversies Credit: Patrick Gorski-Imagn Images On Aug. 7, 2026, Kanter Freedom declared for the 2027 WNBA Draft. He was challenging the support of transgender women in the league, claiming he met the eligibility guidelines through self-identification. Royce White would follow suit and also announce his candidacy to play women’s basketball. A few weeks later, Kanter Freedom attended the Sky and Fever game on Aug. 23. He wore a shirt that featured the definition of a woman. He would be removed from the game following a verbal exchange with the Sky’s Natasha Cloud. It appears he is not done yet, after his appearance on Fox News. The WNBA reportedly will not allow him and White to be eligible for the 2027 Draft, which will be held in April. Kanter Freedom was the third overall pick in the 2011 NBA Draft. During his NBA career, he played for the Utah Jazz, the Oklahoma City Thunder, the New York Knicks, the Portland Trail Blazers, and the Boston Celtics. In addition to his basketball career, he has been an outspoken human rights activist. articles._body: Hi all. I'm working on GitBiased platform. Basically the idea is to let you or your team (manager) know what is happening at the moment in your development life. articles.title: Show HN: Wirespan, a daily power grid optimization puzzle I made for my son
articles.summary: This was a lot of fun to build! I have an autistic son who is extremely interested in power lines, electrical transmission towers, and how the grid works. I decided to build a little game for him. When I finally showed it to him with bated breath, he rolled his eyes and said, “Is it 3D? I’ll only
articles._body: This was a lot of fun to build! I have an autistic son who is extremely interested in power lines, electrical transmission towers, and how the grid works. I decided to build a little game for him. When I finally showed it to him with bated breath, he rolled his eyes and said, “Is it 3D? I’ll only like it if it’s 3D!” So, I decided to polish it up and release it to the world! You get a 9x9 map with one power plant, three houses, and terrain obstacles, and the goal is to connect the power plant to the houses with an optimal path. Beneath the coat of paint, it’s a graph theory optimization puzzle, very nearly a Steiner-tree puzzle. Any two nodes within Chebyshev distance 2 are wired together automatically. But the wires travel in Euclidian space, so reach is measured on a square and wire on a circle. The skill is balancing that asymmetry to find the shortest route to light up the whole map. Because the original goal of this project was to provide joy to my son, I’ve done my best to make it accessible to everyone. It’s localized into 18 languages so far, has a high-contrast mode meeting AAA standards, reduced motion mode, etc. I do collect usage telemetry to help me improve the game, but I’ve done my very best to take privacy very seriously, collecting anonymous stats about the gameplay itself, with a random id the game generates rather than anything about the player or device. I also generate the privacy policy directly from the analytics code, as a contract to ensure nothing is ever collected without being fully disclosed. I had a really great time with this project, and hope to continue to improve it! I’d love any feedback I can get! Please let me know if you have any questions, and I’ll stick around to answer them! (Reposting because my first attempt landed during a super quiet hour and didn't really get seen) Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49433314 Points: 6 # Comments: 6

articles.title: Paul Finebaum: Lane Kiffin ‘missed the boat’ on comments regarding Dae’Quan Wright
articles.summary: Lane Kiffin tried to explain and defend the Dae’Quan Wright situation based on the current setup of college athletics. But, he missed the boat according to ESPN’s Paul Finebaum. Wright intends to play for LSU via the transfer portal despite being cut by the Cleveland Browns. Wright previ
articles._body: Lane Kiffin tried to explain and defend the Dae’Quan Wright situation based on the current setup of college athletics. But, he missed the boat according to ESPN’s Paul Finebaum. Wright intends to play for LSU via the transfer portal despite being cut by the Cleveland Browns. Wright previously played for Virginia Tech and Ole Miss before going undrafted this spring. Wright was officially waived Monday by the Browns. He entered the transfer portal last week, and if he clears waivers, he intends to play for LSU, reuniting with his old coach. Wright was one of 16 football players who filed a lawsuit against the NCAA in Baton Rouge, Louisiana. $19.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage “At the end of the day, because of these rulings, they’re either going to play for you or they’re going to play somewhere else around the country,” Kiffin said in part Monday. “We made a decision to recruit them, like probably most people are.” So with that, Finebaum took his shot at Kiffin. What else is new right? But it wasn’t overly critical towards Kiffin, but rather what the LSU coach should’ve said if he wanted to be brutally honest about the situation regarding Wright and other players. “I think he missed the boat, Greeny,” Finebaum said on Get Up . “I mean, Kiffin’s smart. He’s crafty, but he should have said something that all college football fans will understand: Nobody wants to play for the Cleveland Browns, and everyone wants to play for the LSU Tigers. That would have worked. Instead, he tried to (look at) his notes, something that the legal staff had written for him, and he wildly missed. But there is no easy way to explain it. But that would have done the job.” Paul Finebaum wishes Lane Kiffin were more honest about Dae’Quan Wright Dae’Quan Wright played four seasons of college football, two at Virginia Tech and the latter two at Ole Miss. He broke out under Kiffin in 2025 while in Oxford, Mississippi, as he finished with 39 catches for 635 yards, five touchdowns and 16.3 yards per catch. Overall, Wright totaled 113 catches for 1,603 yards, nine touchdowns and 14.2 yards per catch over the course of 47 games. There is some question, though, as to whether intraconference transfers will be allowed in the SEC. Wright suited up for Ole Miss last season. To transfer to LSU, he’d have to get around a current SEC rule that prevents transfers within the conference that are not “within their sport’s regular NCAA transfer window immediately following the sport’s championship segment.” It’s unclear if that rule applies to someone coming from the NFL. SEC commissioner Greg Sankey recently provided guidance to league schools on that front, cautioning them to proceed carefully when dealing with players who may have gained eligibility through court proceedings. Kiffin declined to comment Monday when asked why he believed Wright playing for LSU would not break the league rule.

articles.title: Timberwolves rumors: What bombshell ownership change means for crucial Tim Connelly contract talks
articles.summary: Last week, a big change happened to the Minnesota Timberwolves after it was reported that co-owner Marc Lore sold his majority stake in the team and the Minnesota Lynx to Marc Stad for $4.5 billion. Now, the question is what will happen to Tim Connelly, the Timberwolves’ president of basket
articles._body: Last week, a big change happened to the Minnesota Timberwolves after it was reported that co-owner Marc Lore sold his majority stake in the team and the Minnesota Lynx to Marc Stad for $4.5 billion. Now, the question is what will happen to Tim Connelly, the Timberwolves’ president of basketball operations? While Lore will stay as a minority owner, the arrival of Stad could have a huge impact on Connelly, who will enter the final year of his contract. The Dallas Mavericks tried to hire Connelly a few months ago to fill the vacancy after the firing of Nico Harrison. Their pursuit, however, did not prosper. The Mavericks eventually went with Masai Ujiri. According to The Stein Line’s Marc Stein, it appears that Connelly will remain in his post with the Timberwolves even after the ownership change. “Timberwolves lead roster decision-maker Tim Connelly is said to have a strong relationship with Stad. This figures to be key given that Connelly—after Dallas ultimately conceded in the spring that it would not be granted permission to pursue Connelly for its front office vacancy as the Mavericks had initially hoped—is entering the final year of his current contract in 2026-27 and needs a new deal,” wrote Stein on his Substack. “The Wolves have won five separate playoff series over the past three seasons with star swingman Anthony Edwards, coach Chris Finch, and Connelly as their leading trio of influence.” Stein noted that the NBA’s approval process that will officially install Stad, who has a net worth of $5 billion, as the Timberwolves’ majority owner might take until January. It is too early to tell how hands-on Stad will be. But in the meantime, Connelly can stay focused on his job instead of looking over his shoulder and worrying about a new contract. He was hired by Minnesota in 2022. The Timberwolves had a busy offseason, adding LaMelo Ball and letting go of Julius Randle and Naz Reid, in an effort to build a roster more suited for Edwards to maximize his prime years. articles.title: How one of Taylor Swift’s biggest songs evolved from ‘sad’ origins
articles.summary: One of the biggest songs from Taylor Swift’s discography is “I Knew You Were Trouble,” which was initially a “sad piano ballad.” Luckily, it was changed for the better. During her Grammy Museum conversation, Swift revealed that the hit song from her Red album was ori
articles._body: One of the biggest songs from Taylor Swift’s discography is “I Knew You Were Trouble,” which was initially a “sad piano ballad.” Luckily, it was changed for the better. During her Grammy Museum conversation, Swift revealed that the hit song from her Red album was originally a “sad piano ballad” before producers Max Martin and Shellback made a helpful suggestion . “I was really excited to bring it in,” she recalled, “and I played them this really, really sad ballad, and I was like, ‘I think just no drums,’ and they’re like, ‘What if it’s dubstep?'” #TaylorSwift reveals that “I Knew You Were Trouble” started as a “sad piano ballad” until Max Martin and Shellback suggested, “What if it’s dubstep?” Swift adds that it ended up being “the best thing” that could have happened to the song. Watch the full Grammy Museum… pic.twitter.com/q3fhTLODw9 — Variety (@Variety) August 24, 2026 She initially had some hesitation, but it worked out. The producers didn’t want to have any piano in the arrangement, and she eventually gave in. “It ended up being the best thing for it, and I think that as a collaborator, my favorite people to be in the room with are ‘yes, and’ people,” Swift said. “I Knew You Were Trouble” was the first single issued after Red’s release. The album was preceded by two singles: “We Are Never Ever Getting Back Together” and “Begin Again.” The song was co-written by Swift, Martin, and Shellback, and the latter two co-produced it. A music video was released that featured Swift and Reeve Carney as her love interest. Of course, nearly a decade later, Red (Taylor’s Version) was released. This was the second re-recorded album in the (Taylor’s Version) series after Fearless. Among the re-recorded songs was “I Knew You Were Trouble,” which was produced by Swift, Christopher Rowe, and Shellback this time around. In the years since its release, “I Knew You Were Trouble” has remained one of Swift’s biggest songs. It is the sixth most-played song in her discography, having been performed 350 times, including at every show on the blockbuster Eras Tour . It is between “We Are Never Ever Getting Back Together,” which has been performed 368 times, and “Shake It Off,” which has been performed 341 times. One of the top Superstars on the WWE roster, Belair has been suffering from a finger injury for over a year now, making her ineligible for an in-ring return. A couple of months ago, Belair shared an update on social media, where she noted that her finger injury was getting better due to her pregnancy absence. However, in a now- seemingly deleted Instagram story, Belair shared a concerning update. Belair provided an update on her finger injury via her Instagram stories (via Fightful), stating that she has carpal tunnel. Unfortunately, the original social media story has now been deleted from her social media. However, some sharp-eyed fans noticed it and began sharing the news. “No one ever talks about this stuff… currently carpal tunnel in both hands… fingers completely numb, no feeling in surgery finger whatsoever, no grip strength, and now also Mom thumb…wtf lol,” Belair seemingly shared on her social media. “Carpal tunnel syndrome is one of the most common hand conditions. It is caused by pressure on the median nerve in the carpal tunnel. The carpal tunnel is a narrow passageway in the wrist. It is on the palm side of the hand,” according to information available on Mayo Clinic’s website. Unfortunately, the actual source of the news is now nowhere to be found as Belair seemingly deleted it. However, the news has now been spreading like wildfire on social media, with several reputed pro-wrestling websites covering it. Belair has not yet officially commented on it. While “The EST” continued making sporadic television appearances following the injury, she did not wrestle a single match after that. articles.title: KSR Today: The SEC takes on eligibility, football talks defense, and more
articles.summary: A new KSR Today covers the SEC’s eligibility stance and meetings in Birmingham, Kentucky Football practice, an upcoming Happy Hour, and more.
articles._body: Hey there, friend. Welcome back to KentuckySportsRadio.com. We appreciate you checking in from time to time. It’s an honor to be part of your internet routine. In this Tuesday, August 25 edition of KSR Today, we’re talking about the Southeastern Conference with our morning coffee. The SEC made a big splash yesterday ahead of two days of meetings starting today. Then, in Lexington, we have more football practice, a bad rivalry loss, and more to address. The SEC doesn’t want former pros returning to college sports The presidents and chancellors of the Southeastern Conference met by videoconference Monday evening, then released a statement drawing a line in the sand on the growing eligibility debate. The conference said athletes who leave college, sign professional contracts and compete professionally “should not then be permitted to return to college competition.” This comes as college football teams have turned to NFL training camps for last-minute roster additions. The SEC argues that allowing former pros back into college sports would create competitive-equity concerns and take opportunities away from high school and current college athletes. The statement comes amid court challenges to NCAA eligibility rules and ends by calling on Congress to advance the Protect College Sports Act. SEC presidents and ADs meeting in Birmingham today As the uncertainty continues, the league’s presidents and athletic directors are in Birmingham for the next couple of days. The SEC’s two-day league meetings begin today with a long list of issues to discuss. Yahoo!’s Ross Dellenger says “an exploration into a conference-only governance model” is at the top of the list. SEC presidents and ADs will convene in Birmingham on Tuesday for a 2-day meeting – scheduled weeks ago – centering on an exploration into a conference-only governance model, sources tell @YahooSports . The focus, for now, is on self-governance and not a competitive breakaway. — Ross Dellenger (@RossDellenger) August 24, 2026 A trip to Alabama wasn’t in KSR’s August budget, but we’ll pass along any news that leaks from today and tomorrow’s meetings. J Batt and Will Stein were in Louisville for lunch Before he left for Birmingham, J Batt spent part of his Monday with Will Stein at Kentucky’s Louisville Kickoff Luncheon. Hosted at Churchill Downs, this year’s luncheon offered scenery and an opportunity for the new AD and head coach to impress fans and the donor base in Louisville. They shared their first impressions in Lexington as they take on brand-new challenges and start a new era for Kentucky Football . There wasn’t any big news (except this ) from Stein’s final public speaking event of the offseason. Still, KSR was there because Nick Roush lives at Churchill Downs: Stein, Batt Rally Kentucky Football Fans at Louisville Kickoff Luncheon . We’ll hear from the defense after today’s practice In Lexington, preseason training camp continues in its final stretch before game prep and the weekly routine begin next week. Today, we’ll hear from the defense as cornerbacks coach Allen Brown and stars coach James Gibson are scheduled to answer questions, along with post-practice conversations with several defensive players. Check back here or over on KSR’s YouTube channel after lunch for their comments. UK Men’s Soccer blew a 2-0 lead in home rivalry loss to the Cards The men’s soccer version of the Battle of the Bluegrass went red last night, as Kentucky lost to its rival on home soil in Lexington. The way it went down made the rivalry loss even worse. The Wildcats led 2-0 at halftime, but gave up three second-half goals, including the game-winner with only eight seconds left in the match—a brutal way to suffer the first loss of the season. Something about the Battle of the Bluegrass and the final minute #GoCards pic.twitter.com/JVap7mvXvC — Louisville Men's Soccer (@LouisvilleMSOC) August 25, 2026 Find KSR’s Happy Hour at PARLOUR Pizza + Pints in Lexington Need something to do in Lexington later this week? Maybe a reason to drive to Lexington? On Thursday, we’re taking our KSR Happy Hour live stream to PARLOUR Pizza + Pints for our first remote Happy Hour show. The hourlong Thursday afternoon YouTube series runs from 4-5 p.m., and this week’s episode will be our first in-person. Come out for pizza, a pint, and a new Happy Hour, or watch live online if you can’t make it. KSR’s morning show is back in studio today Tune in at 10 a.m. today and every day for KSR’s live morning radio show. Today, we’re back in the downtown iHeart studio after a fun Monday at KSR’s golf scramble in Louisville. On the agenda: more discussions about eligibility, football, and whatever else comes up. Go Cats.

articles.title: Where NC State falls in preseason bowl projections going into 2026 campaign
articles.summary: NC State, like every other program around the country, is confident coming out of fall camp ahead of its season opener. The Wolfpack has high hopes for the year, even as it flies under the radar with a bevy of newcomers on the roster this fall. How might the season go? The program’s win total [&#823
articles._body: NC State , like every other program around the country, is confident coming out of fall camp ahead of its season opener. The Wolfpack has high hopes for the year, even as it flies under the radar with a bevy of newcomers on the roster this fall. How might the season go? The program’s win total sits at 7.5 at this stage of the preseason, just four days ahead of NC State’s Week 0 clash at Virginia in Charlottesville on Saturday afternoon (3:30 p.m., ESPN).  If that number rings true (or is exceeded), the Pack would make a bowl game for the 12th time in Dave Doeren’s 14 seasons by the end of this campaign. Since experts around the country like to predict the future, let’s take a look at where NC State is projected to land after its 12 regular season games this year. On3’s Brett McMurphy and CBS Sports both predict the Wolfpack to play in the Sun Bowl on Dec. 31 in El Paso, Texas. McMurphy has Utah as the opponent, while CBS Sports has Arizona on the other sideline. Doeren has a win in this postseason contest after he led the Pack over Arizona State in the 2017 iteration of the event.  Athlon Sports and ESPN’s Mark Schlabach believe that NC State will make its way to the Fenway Bowl on Dec. 26 in Boston. The former’s projection has Army as the opponent, while the latter has Navy battling against the Wolfpack inside the oldest active MLB stadium.  Rounding out the major predictions, Jerry Palm placed NC State in the Military Bowl against Navy on Dec. 28 in Annapolis, Md., inside the Midshipmen’s home stadium. ESPN’s Kyle Bonagura, meanwhile, did not project the Wolfpack to make the postseason, thus meaning he believes the program will fall short of the six-win mark in 2026. In the event NC State were to not make a bowl game, it would be the first time the Wolfpack missed the postseason since it went 4-8 in 2019. In all, the Pack has appeared in 10 bowl games (qualified for 11, but the 2021 Holiday Bowl was canceled due to positive COVID-19 tests within UCLA’s program) under Doeren’s guidance. NC State has played in the Belk, Duke’s Mayo, Gator, Gasparilla, Holiday, Independence, Pop-Tarts, Military, St. Petersburg and Sun Bowls over that span.

articles.title: Valkyries’ ‘huge leap’ on defense helped finally defeat Lynx
articles.summary: Tenth time’s the charm. The Golden State Valkyries can exhale after finally taking down the Minnesota Lynx for 80-66 Monday night on the road, after entering the Target Center 0-9 against the Lynx all-time over the course of the last two seasons. But maybe more important than finally accomp
articles._body: Tenth time’s the charm. The Golden State Valkyries can exhale after finally taking down the Minnesota Lynx for 80-66 Monday night on the road, after entering the Target Center 0-9 against the Lynx all-time over the course of the last two seasons. But maybe more important than finally accomplishing what’s alluded the otherwise historically successful expansion franchise is the fact they accomplished one of the goals coach Natalie Nakase has stressed over the last month– playing four full quarters of high-intensity, high-energy basketball. And in Minneapolis, in a game they needed, against a team that has haunted them, they finally did so, according to the second-year head coach. “Yes, tonight definitely was [four full quarters of basketball],” Nakase said, describing how the team took an “emptying the tank” approach to the game. “It was about us. Just focusing on the attention to detail. We talked about bringing a different game plan. So just credit to our coaches. Landon [Tatum], it was his scout, but more importantly, the girls executed it. So just attention to detail. We did it all four quarters. This is a huge leap for us. Again, [we’re] trying to prepare to be at our best for the playoffs. And then keeping that team to 66 [points]. That’s a very, very talented team. They’re number one for a reason. Really proud to keep them to 66.” Veronica Burton finished with 14 points, nine assists, and five steals; Gabby Williams added 15 points and five rebounds to shake off a rough patch of shooting over the past couple of games; and Cecilia Zandalasini caught fire for 18 points, including eight in the fourth quarter. Additionally, the bench combination of Tiffany Hayes and Janelle Salaun gave Golden State the juice they needed to spark timely runs, finishing with 14 points and 12 points, respectively. Valkyries’ defense on Minnesota’s stars The Lynx’s 66 points were their season low as the Valkyries’ league-best defense swarmed them on all levels. Olivia Miles, Napheesa Collier, and Kayla McBride, who combined for 58 points in their win in Golden State last week, were held to just 29 total points on a combined 7-of-33 from the field. For Collier specifically, Nakase cited the efforts of center Kiah Stokes for taking the lion’s share of guarding the Lynx star in the post. “Kiah Stokes just did a phenomenal job,” Nakase said. “I know she’s had a lot of reps in terms of guarding her, but Kiah’s length– she moves her feet really well, so she doesn’t give up, usually, any angles. And then, more importantly, defending without fouling. Then she did an amazing job boarding. Credit to Kia, just being a one-man protection down there for us, because [Collier is] an incredible scorer; she can score at all three levels.” Along with Stokes as the primary defender, the Valkyries made a concerted effort to jam up the Lynx in the midpost with their low-man defense, cutting off the actions Minnesota likes to generate along the baseline. They also junked up Miles’ pick-and-roll game with Burton and Williams, game-wrecking what Minnesota tried to develop. And then they got out on the break. As Nakase so often likes to say, the defense flows into the offense, and with the Valkyries generating 12 steals on the night, they were able to find easy baskets in transition to unclog a cold start offensively. Washing away the two-game skid With all the questions about effort, urgency, and energy in the last couple of games, it’s a win the Valkyries can use to wash away the angst and anxiety of a very dramatic two-game losing streak in which the Lynx humbled them and the Chicago Sky’s Sydney Taylor walked them down with a game-winner in the clutch. Before the game, Nakase told reporters that the conversations she said she was going to have in the wake of the Sky loss were productive, saying she let the team meet with themselves before engaging them. And when she did engage them, Nakase said she took special care to do more “listening” in order to understand the “why.” And her takeaway was straightforward. “That everyone sees things, whether it’s the game plan or the offensive game plan, they see a little bit differently,” Nakase said. “And so that’s when I was like, ‘Oh, okay, here’s a lot of the holes of maybe the rough starts,’ and so I just got to make sure I put everyone on the same page. That’s the biggest thing.” A big part of those important conversations over the weekend was Burton. And in this important win against the Lynx, her leadership was on full display from Nakase’s inside perspective. “No letdown at all today with V,” Nakase said. “That’s been something our staff has kind of been on her of like, whether you make a mistake, it doesn’t matter; keep going, keep leading whatever the team needs. Do they need a harsh, quick conversation? Do they need support? V was elite tonight. On top of that, she made all the calls. [I] didn’t really look over too much, and we just kind of let V run the show.” For Burton, while it’s a good win, the Valkyries’ floor general isn’t getting ahead of herself as the team prepares for the rigors of the postseason. “It feels good. Getting any win on the road, at this point in the season, feels good,” Burton said. “Just trying to gear up for playoff basketball. The way we did it and the way we made adjustments, obviously, just seeing them less than a week ago, so it feels good. But a lot to build off on this one.” The post Valkyries’ ‘huge leap’ on defense helped finally defeat Lynx appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles.title: How Sam Fender & Olivia Dean’s ‘Rein Me In’ Became the U.K.’s Longest-Running No. 1 Single Ever
articles.summary: The song now holds the all-time record for the longest-running U.K. No. 1 single.
articles._body: Sam Fender ’s show at the London Stadium in June 2025 remains momentous for many reasons. It was the midway point of the rollout of his Mercury Prize-winning LP People Watching , and also his largest ever headline show. But perhaps the most consequential moment from it came midway through the set, album deep cut “Rein Me In” got an airing, with the show’s support act Olivia Dean , then a rising star, joining on vocals for a new verse. Now their careers — and that song — appear unstoppable. “Rein Me In” is in record-breaking territory on the U.K.’s Official Singles Chart. The track has earned 22 weeks at No. 1, and became the longest-running No. 1 single of the 21st century after 16, surpassing Drake’s “Hotline Bling.” It has now pulled clear of Frankie Laine’s “I Believe” in the all time rankings, which notched 18 weeks at the summit back in 1953, to become the longest-running U.K. No. 1 single ever. In February, it earned the BRIT Awards’ publicly voted song of the year prize, with Dean and Fender on hand to collect the prize in Manchester. Amid chart dominance in early May, Dean returned the favor by inviting Fender to give the song a rare live outing at her headline performances at London’s O2 Arena . Both are now leading the way for British acts on the global stage, capping off a remarkable turnaround for the scene. This is the story of how a fan favorite became the biggest U.K. chart success of all time.

articles._body: This is today’s edition of The Download , our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology. How to encourage smarter AI use in the classroom Chatbots took schools by surprise. Suddenly, students carried an app in their phones that could magically answer almost any homework question or spin up an essay in seconds. Organizations ranging from OpenAI to UNESCO encourage AI use in the classroom, but many teachers aren’t sure how to handle it. Yet some promising approaches are emerging. At Cheshire Academy, for example, teachers are trained on general techniques for using AI rather than prescribed tools. They use generative AI to prepare class materials, and one teacher has developed a traffic light system that tells students when they can use AI for assignments. The school has also explored specialized tools including an AI platform for educators. Here’s how it works—and how other teachers can apply it . —Peter Hall This article is from Making AI Work , our limited-run newsletter examining how to apply LLMs across industries. To receive it in your inbox, sign up here . I spent a day at a robot “carnival” in Shanghai. Here’s what I saw. —You Xiaoying Applause rings out from the main tent of a robot “carnival” on the outskirts of Shanghai. There, a humanoid wearing a blinged-out top is showing off a martial arts style known as drunken boxing as a fellow humanoid performs a front flip to woo the crowd. The audience can’t get enough. They chant: “More, more, more.”  Humanoid robots are having a moment in China. The popular machines are part of the country’s strategy to bring AI into daily life. Nearly 90% of the more than 13,000 two-armed, two-legged robots delivered globally last year were made in China.     Showcases like this event are important because they invite the public to experience robots up close. And exposure matters, as elsewhere, humanoids’ progress has been slow, Take a tour of the robot carnival to see what it reveals about China’s humanoid ambitions . articles.title: Writer Liz Meriwether Has Been Listening to Britney Spears ‘A Lot’ While Writing Script For ‘The Woman in Me’ Biopic
articles.summary: Since you asked, her favorite songs at the moment are deep cuts "Perfume" (from 2013's Britney Jean) and "If I'm Dancing" (from 2016's Glory).
articles._body: New Girl and Furious screenwriter Liz Meriwether has been doing all the things one does when preparing for a biopic on one of the world’s most famous pop icons. She’s listening to the Michelle Williams-read audiobook of Britney Spears ‘ 2023 The Woman in Me memoir, and, in news that should warm the hearts of the Britney Army, she is seemingly doing a deep dive into Brit’s music, at least as evidenced by which tracks she told The Hollywood Reporter are her current favorites from the singer’s nine-LP catalog. Meriwether spoke to the magazine about the task of adapting the tell-all into a film and though details of what the movie will look, and sound like are scarce, she did delve into her prep for the project that will team her with the creative hive mind behind the pair of hit Wicked films, director Jon M. Chu and producer Marc Platt; Universal has not yet confirmed any details about the adaptation. Meriwether told THR that it’s still early in the process, but she’s spoken to Chu and Platt “so much” already and found them to be very collaborative. “I’m so used to being the final word on everything,” she said of her frequent dual roles in the past as writer and showrunner. “But it feels really relaxing at the moment because I’m writing something and I don’t have to be the one to figure this out … I get to just be a writer and that’s fun.” She noted that she’s both read the hard copy and listened to The Woman in Me audiobook “multiple times,” praising her former Dying For Sex collaborator Michelle Williams for just crushing the audiobook read. “Michelle is unbelievable. It’s like a monologue. I told her that her performance of the audiobook broke my heart in so many ways,” she said. “She’s being true to Britney and also telling a story in the way she’s reading it. Another spoiler: Michelle’s a really good actor. Maybe I’ll turn a script in to Mark and Jon that’s just Michelle on a stage, reading. I wonder what will happen.” Spears’ plainspoken memoir traces her career from her humble beginnings in Louisiana to her rise to pop superstardom in the late 1990s and early 2000s. It tackles her often contentious relationship with her family head-on, as well as her tabloid catnip romance with then-*NSYNC superstar Justin Timberlake and the public mental health struggles that led a 13-year stint in a tightly controlled conservatorship she fought for years. The book was a bestseller and the Williams-read audiobook became the fastest-selling in publisher Simon & Schuster’s history. Meriwether said she’s also been listening to Spears’ music “a lot,” as well as the other music that was released during the years Spears was making albums; since getting out of the restrictive 13-year conservatorship in Nov. 2021, Spears has vowed not to return to the music business and has not released any new songs since her July 2023 one-off with Will.i.am “Mind Your Business.” “I want to just get the feeling that moment in time or just remind myself,” said Meriwether of her musical deep-dive. “I’m exactly Britney’s age, so a lot of that music just takes me, like, immediately back.” And, in a detail that should make Spears’ legion of fans happy, Meriwether has also been doing a serious excavation into Brit’s catalog to get into the mood. While making playlists of her favorites, she couldn’t point to a single song, but nodded to two deep tracks from late-period Britney as her current go-tos. She’s said she’s been loving the emotionally turbulent love triangle tale “Perfume” (from 2013’s Britney Jean ), as well as the fan-favorite electropop banger “If I’m Dancing,” which appeared on the singer’s most recent, and possibly final album, 2016’s Glory . “She’s made a lot of albums,” Meriwether said. “Her hits have been such big hits that I think there are a lot of songs that people don’t think of.”

articles.title: Steelers’ rookie finds hilarious way to poke fun at Aaron Rodgers’ age
articles.summary: While playing for more than two decades in the NFL, Pittsburgh Steelers’ Aaron Rodgers has always been a little strict with the rookies. Though it’s hard to imagine playing your first football season alongside the future Hall of Famer, rookie wide receiver Germie Bernard found a hilarious w
articles._body: While playing for more than two decades in the NFL, Pittsburgh Steelers’ Aaron Rodgers has always been a little strict with the rookies. Though it’s hard to imagine playing your first football season alongside the future Hall of Famer, rookie wide receiver Germie Bernard found a hilarious way to troll him. During his recent appearance on Not Just Football with Cam Heyward, Bernard compared Rodgers to his mother. “I’m 22. He’s been playing for that long. I think he might be older than my mom,” Bernard said. "I think he might be older than my mom" Rookie WR Germie Bernard is learning a lot from Aaron Rodgers pic.twitter.com/EmyqStQFqF — Not Just Football (@NotJustFootball) August 24, 2026 However, the rookie WR’s hilarious reference did not come out of nowhere. He was initially commending Rodgers’ long years of experience and how he pushes everybody to their limits. “I ain’t lying, I be having low-key a little bit of anxiety when I’m out there with him just because it’s like I don’t really want to mess up cuz then I feel like damn, he finna chew my a** out,” he earlier said. “I enjoy being there with him and being under him because he’s just teaching me the game; he’s given me all the knowledge he knows about the game.” Born on December 2, 2003, he was drafted 47th overall in the second round of the 2026 NFL Draft. He had a strong preseason debut during the Steelers 28-9 win over the Green Bay Packers. Entering his rookie year, being predicted to make the Steelers’ 53-man roster for the 2026 NFL season , Bernard has a long way to go. The Alabama alum even won praise from Rodgers for his physical traits. “Germie just needs to learn the offense inside and out. When he does that, he has a lot of great physical traits…I think he’s got a really bright future because of his attitude (and) his approach,” Rodgers said. articles.title: Joe Rogan issues warning to Conor McGregor using Mike Tyson example
articles.summary: After a wait of five years, Conor McGregor returned to MMA at UFC 329, where he lost to Max Holloway within a few seconds. Suffering an ACL injury, McGregor ruled himself out of the fight and later underwent surgery to repair it. However, since the surgery, McGregor has maintained an extremely ac
articles._body: After a wait of five years, Conor McGregor returned to MMA at UFC 329, where he lost to Max Holloway within a few seconds. Suffering an ACL injury , McGregor ruled himself out of the fight and later underwent surgery to repair it. However, since the surgery, McGregor has maintained an extremely active presence on social media, talking about his healing process and comeback fight in 2027. Despite the hype on social media, UFC commentator Joe Rogan remains doubtful of McGregor’s health. Rogan believes that fighters like McGregor can never get their prime back. During The Joe Rogan Experience #2544 (via EssentiallySports), Chris Williamson and Rogan opened up on McGregor’s situation by using boxing legend Mike Tyson as an example. “You can only maintain that level of RPMs for so long before you just go crazy. Because it’s too hard,” Rogan said. “It’s everything about you. It’s not a sustainable thing. The peak performance of the elite athlete, Mike Tyson when he was 20 years old, Roy Jones Jr. in his prime- you can’t keep that up. It’s too hard. You keep it up for a little while, but eventually your body’s going to fall apart. Your knees are going to give out. You’re going to have back problems. You’re going to break your hands. Something’s going to go, and then you’re going to be compromised.” “And a lot of these guys, they look the same. They get out there, and they’re ripped. They’ve got six-packs. They’re bouncing around, but they know there’s something wrong. They know their elbow sucks. They know their neck is f—d up. They know they probably need a back operation.” Despite McGregor’s pre-fight intense workout sessions and commendable physical shape, he suffered an early injury in the fight, which aligns well with Rogan’s comments. While no return opponent for McGregor has been fixed, he wishes to come back and have his last fight in 2027. Jury Convicts Las Vegas Man of $24M AI Crypto Mining Ponzi Scheme
articles.summary: Brent Kovar told at least 400 investors a supercomputer was mining crypto for them, and that their money was insured by the FDIC.
articles._body: In brief - A federal jury has convicted Brent Kovar of defrauding at least 400 investors of $24 million through his company Profit Connect. - He promised fixed returns of 15% to 30% a year, a full money-back guarantee, and reserves of hundreds of millions of dollars in crypto. - The SEC shut the company down in 2021, when it put the losses at half that figure. A federal jury in Las Vegas has convicted a business owner of running a $24 million cryptocurrency Ponzi scheme that took money from at least 400 investors, the Justice Department said on Monday. Brent C. Kovar owned Profit Connect, a Las Vegas company that from late 2017 until July 2021 claimed to run artificial intelligence software on a supercomputer that mined cryptocurrency and verified transactions on other networks. Investors were promised a fixed return of 15% to 30% a year and a full money-back guarantee, and told the company was backed by hundreds of millions of dollars in crypto reserves. Prosecutors said Kovar knew Profit Connect was not profitable, held no reserves, could not pay the returns it advertised, and had no way of honoring the guarantee. Money from investors went on running the company, buying gifts for employees and buying Kovar a house, with some of it recycled to earlier investors as though it were mining proceeds. Kovar also told investors their money was insured by the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation, according to Ryan Korner, the special agent in charge at the FDIC's Office of Inspector General, whose office investigated the case alongside the FBI and IRS Criminal Investigation. Kovar was convicted after a nine-day trial on 11 counts of wire fraud, two of mail fraud and two of money laundering. He is due to be sentenced on November 30 and faces a statutory maximum of 280 years, though the actual term will be set by the judge under federal sentencing guidelines. A scheme first halted in 2021 The SEC shut Profit Connect down five years ago, obtaining a restraining order and asset freeze in July 2021 and putting the losses at up to $12 million from at least 277 investors, half what prosecutors have now established. More than 90% of the company's income came from investors, the regulator said, and none of it was used to trade crypto. Kovar ran the business with his mother Joy, then 86. The SEC said $1.2 million went into her personal account in ten equal transfers over less than two months, with a further $1.7 million taken out through cash withdrawals, credit card payments and the purchase of a car. Monday's announcement names only Brent Kovar. The regulator had dealt with him before, filing a civil injunction against him and his father Glenn in 2009 over a pump-and-dump scheme run through a company called Skyway Global, which also cost investors $12 million. Investment fraud remains the largest single category of crypto crime reported to the FBI, which logged $11.37 billion in losses for 2025, up 22% on the year before. The Consumer Federation of America scaled that to $80.7 billion using a multiplier for unreported fraud, with Americans over 60 accounting for $4.4 billion of the reported total. articles._body: Three years ago on Aug. 24, 2026, the wrestling world lost one of its gems, Bray Wyatt. After staying out of action for several months, Wyatt passed away due to a heart attack in his sleep at his home in Brooksville, Florida, at the age of 36. An extremely beloved figure across the industry , Wyatt’s passing left many shocked. Still not forgotten , WWE and several Superstars continue to respect and honor Wyatt’s legacy, while his influence lives on. Recently, Wyatt’s former wife, Joseann Offerman, aka, JoJo Offerman, penned an emotional note on social media on the 3rd anniversary of Wyatt’s tragic death while reflecting on their relationship. “Never would I have imagined during any of these moments that one day you wouldn’t be here anymore. It’s been 3 years without you Windham. 3 years since I last hugged you, or kissed your lips. 3 years since I last heard your laugh or you telling me that you love me. The pain remains the same, even if the days are a bit easier to handle. “But nothing’s ever easy, it’s so hard without you. The kids and I miss you so much, and they never stop talking about their daddy! I just know you’re proud but there are so many moments I wish you were still here for. I hope you feel how celebrated and loved you are each day. Thank you for giving us a love we will always carry with us. We love you more than anything and I’ll always be grateful for you, my forever love. Don’t forget to visit me in my dreams,” Offerman wrote. Offerman was a part of WWE from 2013 until 2021. She later joined AEW in 2025 and has been a part of the promotion since then. articles.title: 49ers owner Jed York filed for divorce months before arrest involving prostitution
articles.summary: It turns out that a few months before San Francisco 49ers owner Jed York was arrested after allegedly paying a woman $140 for sexual activity, he had filed for divorce from his wife, Danielle. The California Post (via the New York Post) reports that York filed for divorce in Santa Clara County on
articles._body: It turns out that a few months before San Francisco 49ers owner Jed York was arrested after allegedly paying a woman $140 for sexual activity , he had filed for divorce from his wife, Danielle. The California Post (via the New York Post) reports that York filed for divorce in Santa Clara County on May 11, citing “irreconcilable differences” as his reason for the filing . Their two minor sons (who are 13 and 10) were listed as parties in the case. According to the report, the divorce hasn’t been resolved yet. York’s filing stated that they got married on June 24, 2011. However, the date of separation was “TBD.” The 49ers owner wants joint legal and physical custody of their sons. According to the filing, they entered a premarital agreement in July 2011, the month after they got married. Why was 49ers owner Jed York’s arrested? Joe Nicholson-Imagn Images Over the weekend on Sunday, Aug. 23, 2026, York was arrested in Ohio and subsequently received a jail sentence after entering a plea in municipal court. He was arrested on suspicion of engaging in prostitution. York allegedly arranged to engage in sexual activity with a woman for $140. Upon arriving at the agreed-upon location, he was taken into custody. He would post a $5,000 bond before appearing in court on Monday, Aug. 24. York pleaded no contest to two misdemeanor charges. The first was for disorderly conduct and the second was possession of criminal tools. He was sentenced to two days in Columbiana County Jail, which he would serve concurrently, though he was given credit for one of the days already being served. Additionally, the Niners owner was ordered to pay $1,150 in fines. He also forfeited $160 that was seized to the Mahoning Valley Human Trafficking Task Force. York has been working for the 49ers for years. His parents, John and Denise DeBartolo York, brought him into the family business. In 2008, he became the team’s CEO. articles.title: Jelly Roll Jabs Trump Over Weight While Guest-Hosting ‘Jimmy Kimmel Live’
articles.summary: "Well, Mr. President, from one fat pig to another, take it from me that physical fitness is very important," Jelly Roll said.
articles._body: Jelly Roll took several jabs at President Donald Trump during his opening monologue as guest host of Jimmy Kimmel Live on Monday (Aug. 24), turning his fill-in stint into a pointed political set. The country star, who is guest-hosting the ABC late-night show for four nights while Jimmy Kimmel is away, opened by noting it was the first time he’d “worn a suit and a tie ever.” “I didn’t wear one to the Grammys. I didn’t wear one to court. I didn’t wear one to my father’s funeral,” he said. “But I look alright, don’t I?” Referencing a Washington Post report on the president’s recent weight gain, Jelly Roll noted that he has dropped around 300 pounds himself in recent years — “that means I’ve lost an entire Donald Trump,” he said, before tacking on a jab at the president’s approval numbers. He also mocked Trump’s appearance at a Washington, D.C. IndyCar race over the weekend, and ran a montage of the president mocking other people’s appearances after wryly insisting the audience shouldn’t stoop to weight jokes. “Well Mr. President, from one fat pig to another, take it from me that physical fitness is very important,” Jelly Roll concluded. Back for his second consecutive summer filling in for Jimmy Kimmel, Jelly Roll is hosting for four nights, with guests including podcast host Jay Shetty and actor Glen Powell — who revealed that Jelly Roll has a small role in his upcoming film The Comeback King — and Stevie Nicks booked as a musical guest later in the run. The guest hosting spot comes at a career high point for the country star, born Jason DeFord, who has become one of the most successful crossover artists in country music. Earlier this year, he won the Grammy for Best Contemporary Country Album for Beautifully Broken , the 2024 release that became his first No. 1 on the Billboard 200. Its single “I Am Not Okay” reached No. 14 on the Hot 100 and became one of six career No. 1s on the Country Airplay chart, alongside “Son of a Sinner,” “Need a Favor,” “Save Me” (with Lainey Wilson) and “Halfway to Hell.”

100 Days of Georgia’s Greatest Plays—Day 11
articles.summary: On Day 11, we look back at Matthew Stafford escaping pressure and finding a leaping A.J. Green for an 11-yard game-winning touchdown at Kentucky in 2008.
articles._body: UGASports continues its 100-day countdown to the Bulldogs’ 2026 season opener with the “100 Days of Georgia’s Greatest Plays” series. Today, on Day 11 , we revisit one of the greatest plays in Georgia football history involving the number 11. On Day 11, we look back at Matthew Stafford escaping pressure and finding a leaping A.J. Green for an 11-yard game-winning touchdown at Kentucky in 2008. The Game:  No. 14 Georgia (7-2 record coming off a 49-10 loss to No. 5 Florida) vs. Kentucky (6-3 record coming off a one-point win at Miss. State to become bowl eligible) at Commonwealth Stadium in Lexington, Kentucky, on November 8, 2008.   Preseason ranked No. 1 in the nation, Georgia entered the game coming off its second conference loss, a setback that had all but eliminated the Bulldogs from SEC East contention. Two years earlier, on Georgia’s previous trip to Lexington, Kentucky had upset the Bulldogs 24-20. This time, Georgia was regarded by oddsmakers as a 13-point favorite. “Get the Picture”: With Georgia surprisingly trailing Kentucky 38-35 late in the fourth quarter, the Bulldogs’ struggling defense forced the Wildcats to punt. Taking over at its own 15-yard line with 3:55 remaining, Georgia struck immediately when junior quarterback Matthew Stafford connected with senior wideout Mohamed Massaquoi for a 78-yard gain to the Kentucky 7-yard line. However, the Bulldogs lost four yards on the next two plays. With 2:05 remaining, Georgia faced third-and-goal from the 11-yard line, still trailing by three and in need of a touchdown. The Play On third down from the 11, Stafford took the snap from center, dropped back and immediately faced pressure as the pocket collapsed. Georgia’s junior quarterback escaped to his right with Kentucky defenders in pursuit. Near the sideline, Stafford dodged a defender, pump-faked and was nearly sacked by linebacker Micah Johnson before lofting a pass toward the far back-right corner of the end zone. Meanwhile, wide receiver A.J. Green had worked his way across the back of the end zone. Stafford put the ball high enough for the 6-foot-4 freshman to go get it, and Green leaped above the surrounding Kentucky defenders to make the catch. As he came down, Green was hit by defensive backs Randall Burden and Ashton Cobb , but held on for the 11-yard touchdown. The spectacular play gave Georgia a 42-38 lead with 1:54 remaining. Kentucky responded by driving to the Bulldogs’ 13-yard line, but defensive end Demarcus Dobbs sealed the victory with a game-saving interception. “I figured if [Green] didn’t catch it, no one would,” Stafford said afterward of his game-winning touchdown pass. Georgia head coach Mark Richt had instructed Stafford beforehand to throw the ball away if his protection broke down and his receivers were covered, preserving an opportunity for a game-tying field goal. Instead, Stafford kept the play alive and went for the victory. “I was not real happy there, initially,” Richt said afterward. “But when I saw the results, I thought the kid (Stafford) was a genius.” In Georgia’s 42-38 comeback victory over Kentucky, Stafford completed 17 of 27 passes for a then-career-high 376 yards, three touchdowns and no interceptions. His 216.6 passer-efficiency rating versus the Wildcats was the highest of his 39 career games at Georgia.

articles.summary: West Hill (Calif.) Chaminade offensive lineman and Notre Dame class of 2027 commit Jackson Hill will miss the rest of the season.
articles._body: West Hill (Calif.) Chaminade offensive lineman and Notre Dame class of 2027 commit  Jackson Hill will miss the rest of the season, according to a report in Southern California. “Chaminade has lost standout offensive tackle Jackson Hill for the season after knee surgery,” Los Angeles Times’ reporter Eric Sondheimer shared on Sunday Night. This is obviously a bummer on several fronts. Hill misses an entire season of development as he looked to play a big part in helping turn things around for Chaminade after a difficult season. After a strong offseason, Hill earned his Notre Dame offer, and the feeling was that he was a potential rankings riser with a strong senior campaign. While that is less important than other aspects of the injury, it is still worth noting. Rivals lists Hill as a three-star prospect and the No. 46 offensive tackle in America. Hill originally committed to UCLA on April 4, picking the Bruins over Oregon State, Colorado State, UNLV, Nevada, San Diego State and a few Ivy League schools. He added an offer from Stanford on May 5, but a few days later, he privately committed to Notre Dame after a few weeks of a quiet recruiting process with the Irish staff. “The education at Notre Dame is an opportunity you can’t pass up,” Hill previously told Blue & Gold. “The alumni network is top-notch, and the football is incredibly good. It’s not that UCLA had negatives, it’s just that Notre Dame had so many positives. “I fit the best at Notre Dame. During my visit, I was able to eat wings with the offensive linemen, and I felt like I was so similar to those guys.” Hill is among five Notre Dame offensive line commits, with the others being Jersey City (N.J.) articles.title: Busta Rhymes Releases J Dilla-Produced ‘Dillagence II’ Project Featuring D’Angelo, Lil Wayne, Ludacris & Big Sean: Stream It Now
articles.summary: A sequel to Busta and Dilla's 2007 mixtape is here.
articles._body: Nearly 20 years after the original, Busta Rhymes has posthumously collaborated with the late J Dilla to release their joint Dillagence II project. The anticipated sequel arrived on streaming services on Tuesday (Aug. 25). The project boasts 19 tracks and is loaded with a range of features, including Dilla’s mother, Ma Dukes, R&B legend D’Angelo, Big Sean, Ludacris, Lil Wayne, Common, Talib Kweli, Anderson .Paak and upstarts like La Reezy and Honey Bxby. D’Angelo, who passed away from pancreatic cancer in 2025, appears on “This Woman” and Busta revealed that the track came from an unfinished collab between the Voodoo singer and J Dilla over 20 years ago. “I was gifted with something that they did that they didn’t finish when the word started to spread about this project. I didn’t know that it existed because it was done 20-something years ago,” Busta told New York Times’ Popcast . “They started something and it just never got finished. I love both of them, so I wanted to do whatever justice I could do and continue to uphold the legacies of these brothers.” Busta also teased a music video for “This Woman” on social media directed by Hype Williams, who has an extensive history working with both the New York rapper and D’Angelo. Bus-a-Bus has been sitting on nearly 300 J Dilla beats, a portion of which he polished to make up Dillagence II . “In my experience with Dilla, he was a man of few words. I heard him talk more when he was rhyming than in actual conversation,” the 54-year-old explained on Popcast . Dilla and Busta originally joined forces for Dillagence in 2007, which came just over a year after J Dilla’s death in February 2006. Even at 54, Busta Rhymes has stayed in the studio. Busta’s Dragon Season… Equinox project arrived last year and he released his BLOCKBUSTA album in 2023. Stream Dillagence II below.

articles.title: What to know about state takeovers as Texas wrestles with the future of Austin public schools
articles.summary: More districts across Texas are at risk of intervention by the state’s education commissioner. Here’s what that means for public schools.
articles._body: Chronic academic underperformance at two Austin public schools has the district in jeopardy of severe state sanctions. Now, Texas Education Commissioner Mike Morath will decide what intervention looks like for the school district of nearly 70,000 students. Morath must either close the struggling schools or replace the locally elected school trustees and superintendent with leaders of his choosing. The state is leading the country in its use of such takeovers. While this kind of intervention has historically been a last-resort measure, Texas leaders have used it in recent years as a tool they say will improve student learning. In many cases, it is carried out amid protest from parents. Since 2023, seven districts — including Fort Worth and Houston — have had Morath replace their leaders. What is a state takeover? This intervention into public schools happens when the Texas Education Agency commissioner temporarily removes democratically elected local school trustees and replaces them with a board of managers he appoints. It is seen as the most severe formal state sanction for schools. The managers assume school board duties, which includes approving budgets and tax rates as well as setting district policies on a range of issues from safety to instruction, according to state and federal law. School boards hire superintendents to manage the daily operations of a district. The state education chief can — and often does — swap out a superintendent during a takeover. Even though Fort Worth superintendent Karen Molinar changed up lesson plans that parents said drove academic gains, Morath ousted her, signaling the state wanted a hard reset for the district. Why do takeovers happen? Agency officials can step in due to persistent academic struggles, financial mismanagement or systemic corruption. A 2015 law made it easier for TEA officials to intervene when campuses fail state academic standards. Texas grades public schools on how they are educating students, largely based on how students do on the state standardized tests. Five consecutive Fs at a single campus triggers state action. At that point, the education commissioner must either close the school or replace the district’s elected school board with an appointed board of managers. The campuses that trigger a districtwide takeover have predominantly served Black, Latino or low-income students. State Rep. Harold Dutton grew up in Houston and was a student at Wheatley High School, the school that triggered the takeover in HISD. The Democrat has said he wrote the 2015 law to force districts and the state to reckon with long-struggling schools. The ratings that are the basis of recent takeovers largely come from the widely unpopular STAAR, which is being phased in response to concerns that it creates too much stress for students and takes up too much teaching time. It will be replaced with new assessments. A district can be taken over multiple times. For example, TEA appointed managers in Beaumont ISD in 2014 because of financial mismanagement. It again seized control about a decade later over academic underperformance. Before 2015, a commissioner already had the power to appoint a conservator to oversee a district or campus, while the district’s locally elected school board and superintendent remain in place. The commissioner can then appoint a board of managers in a district that has been under a conservator for two years. Who is on the board of managers during a takeover? A board of managers must be primarily made up of local residents, according to state law. Voters who live within the district’s boundaries can apply. In past job descriptions, agency officials have stressed that the ideal candidates have experience in parent or neighborhood advocacy, social work, psychology, business, finance or law. The essential job duties of managers include evaluating the superintendent and preparing the locally elected trustees to eventually assume their responsibilities again. The managers are required to hold public meetings under the Texas Open Meetings Act. Meanwhile, the trustees can serve in an advisory capacity without decision-making power, like other community members. Local school board elections continue as normal, according to the TEA. Once the commissioner ends a state takeover, the most recently elected school board members will be phased back into governing the district. How long do takeovers last? Commissioner-appointed managers are typically in place for two to six years, TEA spokesperson Jake Kobersky has previously told the Tribune. The length of a takeover depends on how fast a district can meet the academic and exit goals set by the state commissioner. After two years with managers, state law allows the TEA commissioner to restore local control if the failing campus gets passing grades on accountability ratings for two consecutive years. The commissioner can also extend the takeover. Once it is determined that the campus or district has met standards, the commissioner can plan for a transition. The Marlin school district, east of Waco, was under state control for seven years before TEA officials began to relinquish control to the elected school board in February 2024. What can districts do to avoid a takeover? In a rare case, the Wichita Falls school district met the bar of five Fs at a middle school for a takeover — but the commissioner allowed the district to keep its elected school board. While Wichita Falls was facing pressure to improve academic performance, the district adopted state-produced math materials and outsourced operations at the struggling campus to Third Future Schools, a charter network that focuses on turning around schools. To get a break from harsh penalties and buy time before they are at risk of a takeover, school districts can hand over the management of underperforming campuses to charter schools or nonprofits. That’s because of a 2017 law that also gives the school extra dollars for the partnerships. Austi

articles.title: Penn State great Allen Robinson retires after 11 NFL seasons
articles.summary: Penn State news, notes, and updates for Aug. 25 include a former Nittany Lion retiring from the NFL, headlines of the day, and more.
articles._body: Penn State news, notes, and updates for Aug. 25 include a former Nittany Lion retiring from the NFL, headlines of the day, and more. Allen Robinson II is officially calling it a career after 11 seasons in the pros. He did not suit up for a team on game day in 2025. One of the Lions’ best receivers of all-time, the Michigan native finishes his time in the NFL with 565 catches for 7,058 yards and 43 touchdowns. “As I reflect on another year of life, I find myself especially grateful; not just for where I am, but for the journey that brought me here. This birthday feels a little different. It marks not only another year, but the beginning of a new chapter,” Robinson wrote on Instagram, per The Athletic . “To every love story, there comes a final chapter. Football gave me more than I ever could’ve imagined. It challenged me, shaped me, humbled me, and rewarded me in ways I’ll carry for the rest of my life. “I came, I saw, I conquered and I leave with nothing but gratitude.” Robinson was a second-round draft pick of the Jacksonville Jaguars after leaving Penn State following the 2013 season. His best year in the pros came in 2015, when he caught 80 passes for 1,400 yards and 14 touchdowns. He topped 100 receptions once, netting 102 with the Chicago Bears in 2020. Besides those two teams, Robinson also played for the Los Angeles Rams, Pittsburgh Steelers, and Detroit Lions. The rest of today’s newsstand is below. It just goes off the field and what the people that I trust in the treatment room and the strength staff are saying to me, what the numbers are saying and things like that. There’s so much that goes into it. I think it’s just so important that I go out there feeling good about it.” PSU TE Gabe Burkle to BWI on his injury recovery ahead of the 2026 season.

articles.title: THE PULSE: Miami Is Built to Win It All
articles.summary: Good Morning CaneSport! We have all your Miami Hurricanes daily news right here with the staff breaking it all down, from football to basketball, baseball, recruiting and more.
articles._body: SUBSCRIBE TO CANESPORT NOW  /  SIGN UP FOR THE CANESPORT NEWSLETTER CaneSport Front And Center August 25, 2026 Miami is back in the national championship hunt, and the foundation is once again being built in its own backyard. Mario Cristobal has rebuilt the State of Miami pipeline, with South Florida stars like Malachi Toney, Mark Fletcher and Xavier Lucas forming the core of a loaded roster. But one major question remains: can a rebuilt offensive line replacing four starters hold up? Cristobal and Alex Mirabal have conquered that challenge before. Plus, CaneSport breaks down Miami’s biggest keys to finishing the job this season, while five-star Nick Lennear and the Hurricanes’ future stars continue making noise on the recruiting trail. The Lead The State of Miami Is Back — And So Are the Hurricanes Miami can spend big in the portal. It can win NIL battles. But the foundation of Mario Cristobal’s rebuild is sitting right in his backyard. After two decades of watching South Florida stars bolt for Alabama, Ohio State, Florida State and everywhere else, the Hurricanes are finally rebuilding the wall around the State of Miami. Look at the core of this championship contender. Mark Fletcher, Malachi Toney, Josh Moore, Ahmad Moten, Armondo Blount, Bryce Fitzgerald, Xavier Lucas, Damari Brown and OJ Frederique all grew up within roughly 60 miles of campus. Fletcher returned instead of jumping to the NFL. Toney became one of college football’s most dangerous players while he should have still been in high school. And another wave of local stars is already committed for 2027. That local foundation matters even more in the portal era. Transfers can transform a roster, but homegrown players provide continuity—and make Miami a more attractive destination for stars like Darian Mensah and Cooper Barkate. Cristobal hasn’t abandoned national recruiting or the portal. He’s built something underneath them. The wall around South Florida isn’t finished. But Miami is competing for championships again with Miami players at its core. One elite roster can be bought. Sustained success requires a pipeline. And for the Hurricanes, that pipeline will always run through The Crib. The Board Canes Chatter Gone Wild: Message Board Post of the Day Every morning Gary Ferman forces Matt Shodell to wake up extra early to identify the best recent fan  CaneSport Message Board  post. It could be a question, a statement, conjecture, even a food recipe (orange and green macaroni & cheese anyone)? Today’s winner (or loser, depending on your perspective): Only one question for me … Posted by  Chasmish :  It all comes down to Shannon Dawson. Will he run no huddle and run 80 to 90 plays and destroy opponents defenses or will he huddle up and let other teams stay in the game because of slowing up every thing? Dawson is the key to the season, as we saw last year. CaneSport’s Response : This is a great question, and it’s always going to be a balance that coaches like to call “complementary football.” I personally agree that Miami should score as many points as possible using its best attribute, which I do believe is going to be throwing the ball all over the field at a quick pace to keep defenses off balance. But on the flip side a lot will hinge on Miami’s defensive depth. Because if there is a big drop-off from the first team to the second team, I would not take as much issue with Miami perhaps slowing things down for periods of time to keep the game rep count manageable. As you point out, running 80 or 90 plays could destroy and opposing defense. But you also could actually wind up keeping other teams in it by wearing down your own defense when the opponent runs its own 80 or 90 plays. So there’s definitely going to be balance needed … depending on how good Miami’s depth is on defense. If it’s good, then throw it, run hurry-up, and blowout after blowout should be in store. Everything Else That Matters Alex Mirabal – Photo by Neil Gershman / Zooba Images Miami’s Biggest Question Mark? Cristobal and Mirabal Have Been Here Before Why It Matters: Miami’s rebuilt offensive line remains the biggest variable in an otherwise loaded offense, with four starters gone and freshmen potentially filling major roles. But Mario Cristobal and Alex Mirabal have successfully navigated massive OL turnover before, and early returns on Samson Okunlola, Matthew McCoy and the young interior options are encouraging. If this group quickly develops chemistry, Miami’s championship-level offense should have everything it needs up front. Miami’s Biggest Keys to a Title Run Miami enters 2026 with national-title expectations, but CaneSport’s staff sees consistency, leadership, defense and dominant trench play as the keys to getting back to the championship game. Gary Ferman says avoiding the costly ACC slip-ups that plagued the past two seasons is paramount. Matt Shodell points to new leaders emerging around Darian Mensah and Mark Fletcher while Miami’s defense remains elite despite major departures. Luke Chaney focuses on rebuilding the offensive and defensive lines after losing stars on both fronts. The consensus is clear: Miami has championship talent, but turning preseason hype into hardware requires showing up every single week. Miami Commits Take Center Stage Miami’s future was on display across the high school football landscape this weekend. Five-star WR commit Nick Lennear continued making spectacular plays while establishing himself as the centerpiece of a dangerous Carol City team. QB commit Knox Annis earned bragging rights by leading Mandarin past a McArthur defense featuring fellow Cane commits Jaylyn Jones and Sherrod Gourdine. Meanwhile, Miami’s momentum with elite 2028 safety Casey “Superman” Barner continues to grow. The nation’s No. 1 safety is becoming a fan favorite after another highlight-filled performance and will visit Miami for the Florida State game af

articles.title: Welcome to the spiderverse, a world measured through webs
articles.summary: Counting the creatures in the world around us is critical for a raft of conservation efforts. It helps scientists gauge biodiversity, track migration, and spot invasive species. That census-taking, though, often requires humans to tabulate what they see, trap, or otherwise sense—a potentially labori
articles._body: Counting the creatures in the world around us is critical for a raft of conservation efforts. It helps scientists gauge biodiversity, track migration, and spot invasive species. That census-taking, though, often requires humans to tabulate what they see, trap, or otherwise sense—a potentially laborious, costly process that can still leave gaps. But developments over the last decade have revolutionized eco-surveillance. Biologists have tapped into sequencing technology to analyze environmental DNA, or eDNA—genetic material shed by living things. Samples collected from scat, soil, water, and air have opened up a new avenue scientists can use to monitor endangered species and detect invasive ones before anyone can even lay eyes on them. More recently, they’ve uncovered an eDNA gold mine: spiderwebs. The naturally sticky stuff traps material from its arachnid creators, crumbs from their suppers, and, crucially, bio-detritus like saliva and pollen from nearby plants and animals. Every living thing, it seems, sheds copious DNA all over the place, including into the air, and webs then easily ensnare it. “It’s probably one of the best substrates we’ve used and tried to date,” says Joshua Newton, a molecular ecologist at Curtin University in Perth, Australia, who’s sampled flowers, streams, hollows of dead trees, and even filters on moving cars to study vertebrate populations. Newton recently compared the biological diversity in spider­webs with that found in other sources—including vegetation swabs, water, soil, and a fan outfitted with a filter—near a zoo and wildlife sanctuary outside Perth. Each had its obvious strengths: The vegetation swabs revealed more forest mammals, and the water samples identified more fish. But no passive tool matched spiderwebs’ ability to ID vertebrates, echoing results from a similar study conducted in France. Here’s where things get sticky: To gather meaningful data, they had to destroy about 40 webs. “It kind of goes against everything that we’re trying to do if we’re collecting the home of an organism,” Newton says.  Fortunately, his research caught the attention of Angela McGaughran, a genomicist at New Zealand’s University of Waikato. She bought a bag of faux webs from her local Halloween store, wrapped a few coat hangers, and hung them outside. The synthetic material snagged eDNA from nearby cows and sheep, as well as from exotic birds at a nearby aviary. It also detected fungal spores better than real webs—a boon for plant pathologists watching for agricultural threats. Her group is now developing larger experiments to see whether artificial webs can unlock a cheap and ruthlessly efficient way to mimic spiderwebs’ DNA-snagging superpowers anywhere and everywhere. Stephen Ornes is a science writer based in Nashville.
