articles.summary: Humanoid robots are having a moment in China. The popular machines are part of the country’s strategy to bring artificial intelligence into daily life. Embedding the technology into physical systems—an idea called embodied AI—was a key facet of China’s latest five-year plan, and companies here are a
articles._body: __________________________ THE PLACE Shanghai, China Humanoid robots are having a moment in China. The popular machines are part of the country’s strategy to bring artificial intelligence into daily life. Embedding the technology into physical systems—an idea called embodied AI—was a key facet of China’s latest five-year plan , and companies here are already world leaders in humanoids. Nearly 90% of the more than 13,000 two-armed, two-legged robots delivered globally last year were made in China.     “Look, it is trying to do a handstand!” an 11-year-old boy shouts excitedly while watching his new mini robotic dog attempt a series of stunts. The toy pet is a gift his mom just bought him at a robot “carnival” held by an R&D center on the outskirts of Shanghai, and he can’t stop showing it off to passersby. It’s a public holiday, and curious families are pouring in to the event to see what’s on display.  This busy hub houses more than 100 companies that research, develop, manufacture, and market robotic technologies and equipment. Many build specialized bots of all shapes that can do practical tasks, such as transporting heavy loads or inspecting sewage pipes.  Today, however, things are mostly for show. Meters away from where parents and children are queued up to buy the robotic dog, two staffers teach youngsters how to make a quadrupedal robot walk up a flight of stairs. Farther along, a tense battle breaks out between two remote-controlled robots firing water beads at each other, as boys and girls cheer them on from around a temporary ring. (A staffer declares the duel a draw.) Showcases like this are important, because they invite the public to experience robots up close. Some of China’s most prominent robotics companies are building humanoids. These machines “can free people from physical work and mundane chores,” says Yang Duan, a product manager at DexForce, which is at the carnival exhibiting a model that can make coffee. A few booths down, a pair of robotic arms attempts to fold a basket of T-shirts.  INTELLIGENT MANUFACTURING & ROBOTICS GLOBAL CO-INNOVATION CENTER INTELLIGENT MANUFACTURING & ROBOTICS GLOBAL CO-INNOVATION CENTER Robots in many forms—including humanoid ones—entertained the public and demonstrated their skills. Exposure matters, because elsewhere humanoids’ progress has been slow, marred by safety challenges due to their heft and need to balance on two legs . High prices and short battery life have also limited their appeal. Plenty of roboticists are skeptical that a human form is the best shape for a robot to take. But Chinese firms are pushing forward and showing off their latest models. As this carnival takes place in Shanghai, shopping malls and tourist attractions in several other Chinese cities host humanoids that perform for crowds. In Beijing, bipedal robots are running half-marathons. The PR campaign seems to be winning over hearts and minds—at least on this particular weekend in Shanghai. Applause rings out from the festival’s main tent. There, a humanoid wearing a blinged-out top is showing off a martial arts style known as drunken boxing as a fellow humanoid performs a front flip to woo the crowd. Alongside the stage, a squad of small robotic lions are lined up waiting to perform.  The audience can’t get enough. They chant: “More, more, more.”  You Xiaoying is a London-based freelance journalist focusing on China.

articles._body: Agent work is safe today mostly because agents work alone. With one agent, one session and one person working on a task. It's essentially single-player. This changes when a platform has multiple people, each working with multiple agents, all acting on shared tasks and shared data, (multiplayer). Ablo is the infrastructure that enables agents and the people working alongside them to read and write on the same state. Traditional sync engines make sure everyone sees the same state, Ablo does that too but the difference is that Ablo also governs who gets to act on it. articles._body: Hey HN, I routinely run out of RAM, CPU or GPU resources and wanted to know when it happens and what app was causing it. But, I didn't want my menu bar to turn into a row of numbers. articles.title: Show HN: I built an AI music generator with some harnesses
articles.summary:
I’m a developer, and also a music producer. When I work on commercial music, especially songs for ads, I’ve gotten pretty used to using AI music tools as part of the creative process.

But I noticed that some people around me — e.g. my girlfriend — also want to create music as a way to express t
articles._body: I’m a developer, and also a music producer. When I work on commercial music, especially songs for ads, I’ve gotten pretty used to using AI music tools as part of the creative process. But I noticed that some people around me — e.g. my girlfriend — also want to create music as a way to express themselves, but often run into a few problems when using AI music tools: 1. They don’t have a music background, so it’s hard for them to clearly describe the sound they want. 2. Sometimes they just want a song in the style of a certain artist, and the easiest way for them to express that is by naming the artist. But an artist’s name isn’t necessarily a useful description of the actual musical characteristics they’re looking for. 3. A lot of interfaces contain professional terms and parameters, like “weirdness,” that aren’t really designed from a normal user’s perspective and can be confusing. So I built onlymusic.ai and added some harnesses around the underlying models. (Okay, I know “harness” has become a pretty popular word lately.) In practice, it’s mostly prompt preprocessing, a rule system, and model orchestration. For prompt-to-song generation, when someone enters something very simple, we transform it in the background using some good prompt patterns we’ve collected. The goal is to preserve what the user actually meant, while translating it into language that the music model can understand better, hopefully improving the generation results. We also added one-click optimization for styles and lyrics. For styles, if someone mentions an artist, we translate that into musical characteristics — things like era, instrumentation, rhythm, vocal texture, and production style. For lyrics, we try to preserve things like the original rhyme, imagery, and intent, while rewriting parts that may not work well for generation. On the UI side, I’ve also tried to use simple, everyday language wherever possible, remove unnecessary options, and keep only the elements that actually matter, so the interface is cleaner and easier to use. Finally, a big thanks to open-source models like ACE. We deploy some of the models ourselves, which keeps the cost manageable, so we’re able to offer a pretty generous free tier with no signup required. In Fast mode, you can generate up to 5 songs without an account. After signing in, you can generate up to 20 songs per day. (That’s for Fast mode — if you use the more capable models, you’ll get fewer generations.) The credits refresh every day. We’ll keep an eye on the costs. If they become too much, we may have to reduce the free quota a little in the future There are still a lot of features under development. Feedback is very welcome, and I’d love for you to try it! I’m also working on a non-form-based lyrics generator right now. Once it’s ready, I’ll share that with you guys too. articles.title: Vince Staples Announces 2027 Australian Headline Tour
articles.summary: The shows mark his first solo Australian dates in nearly a decade.
articles._body: Vince Staples is heading back to Australia. The “Norf Norf” rapper has announced a run of headline shows for January 2027 in support of his latest album Cry Baby , marking his first solo Australian dates in nearly a decade. Presented by Untitled Group and Beyond the Valley , the Cry Baby Tour will take in Perth, Brisbane, Sydney and Melbourne, wrapping around Staples’ set at Beyond the Valley, the sold-out Victorian festival where he is among the headliners. The run marks his first headline shows in the country since 2018. The tour supports Cry Baby , Staples’ seventh studio album, released in June via Section Eight Arthouse, Loma Vista and Concord. A departure from the introspective, hometown-focused work of 2022’s Ramona Park Broke My Heart and 2024’s Dark Times , the album is a more outward-facing piece of social commentary built around live instrumentation, and was trailed by videos for “Blackberry Marmalade,” “White Flag” and “Cotton.” Staples has been performing the material with a live band, a shift he first showcased at his sold-out Los Angeles album-release show. The Long Beach, California, native broke through with his 2015 debut Summertime ’06 and its platinum single “ Norf Norf. ” His 2017 sophomore album Big Fish Theory debuted at No. 16 on the Billboard 200 — his highest-charting album to date — and he has continued to chart with each subsequent release, including his 2021 self-titled album, which reached No. 21. Beyond music, Staples has expanded into television, creating and starring in the Netflix comedy The Vince Staples Show , which premiered in 2024. Tickets go on general sale Tuesday, Sept. 1 at 3 p.m. AEST, following an Untitled presale from Aug. 31. articles.title: Trey Benson lets frustration out with powerful post after getting cut by Cardinals
articles.summary: Trey Benson is going through a rough period after getting cut by the Arizona Cardinals on Monday, just a few days before the announcement of the 53-man roster. He has not seen action since Week 4 of last season due to a knee injury. While Benson participated in training camp, the lingering issue
articles._body: Trey Benson is going through a rough period after getting cut by the Arizona Cardinals on Monday, just a few days before the announcement of the 53-man roster. He has not seen action since Week 4 of last season due to a knee injury. While Benson participated in training camp , the lingering issue has continued to bother him. The 24-year-old running back could be an interesting piece for some teams because of his youth and potential. In four games last year, he rushed for 160 yards and tallied 13 receptions for 64 yards. In the meantime, Benson will have to lick his wounds and pick himself up. He shared on his Instagram Story a powerful message , as captured by Sports Illustrated’s Donnie Druin. “Remember, you can’t control storms, but you can control how you respond to them. It doesn’t matter what adversity comes your way. It doesn’t matter who said you can’t do it, who said no, or who hopes that you fail,” read the post. “What you experience in the present is only a partial portrait of what God is painting for your future. So, what are you missing? NOTHING! What you need, you already have. Remember, faith is the substance of things hoped for and the evidence of things not seen.” Trey Benson posted this on his Instagram story after being waived by the #AZCardinals today. Hope he lands somewhere and can hit his potential. Rooting for him and everybody else cut this weekend. pic.twitter.com/raFjuuSrCy — Donnie Druin (@DonnieDruin) August 25, 2026   The Cardinals drafted Benson with the No. 66 pick in 2024 after a standout career at Florida State. He, however, did not get a lot of opportunities in his rookie year. He was having a more productive stint in his second year when his knee injury derailed him. Now, he is looking for a second chance to prove himself. While it might not be an easy stretch, Benson can always lean on his self-belief. As they say, faith comes when reason ends. The post Trey Benson lets frustration out with powerful post after getting cut by Cardinals appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles.title: Dream’s Angel Reese has perfect explanation for historic rebounding feat
articles.summary: The day Angel Reese does not get a single rebound is the day the Milky Way burns to smithereens. Reese had a historic performance for the Atlanta Dream on Monday, grabbing a career-high 26 rebounds, including eight off the offensive glass, against the Los Angeles Sparks at Crypto.com Arena to set
articles._body: The day Angel Reese does not get a single rebound is the day the Milky Way burns to smithereens. Reese had a historic performance for the Atlanta Dream on Monday, grabbing a career-high 26 rebounds, including eight off the offensive glass, against the Los Angeles Sparks at Crypto.com Arena to set a new league record for most rebounds in a game and most rebounds in a single season. The Dream beat the Sparks, 78-71, for their fourth straight victory. They improved to 25-13. In an interview with NBC after the game, Reese was asked by Tina Charles about her mindset. The 24-year-old forward did not hesitate with a six-word declaration , while also saluting the WNBA legend. “Anything that goes up is mine,” said Reese. “You just got to have that mindset, you know. Even when I watch you and play against you, you go up there, you’re so aggressive, and you’re consistent every single night. That makes you one of the greatest players in this league, and I want to be one of those when I walk away from the game.” "ANYTHING THAT GOES UP IS MINE." Angel Reese talked with Tina Charles about her rebounding mindset after a career night on the boards. pic.twitter.com/tMUU9spouB — WNBA on NBC and Peacock (@WNBAonNBC) August 25, 2026 Safe to say, Charles knows a thing or two about getting rebounds. She owns the all-time record with 4,262 rebounds. She was also a four-time rebounding leader and had two games with 23 rebounds. So she definitely understood what Reese said. Reese, who shared a special moment with Nneka Ogwumike after beating the Sparks, is on track to lead the WNBA in rebounds for the second straight season, averaging a league-best 12.2 boards per game. Her arrival has helped the Dream become one of the toughest contenders. She will play in the playoffs for the first time. The Dream will return to action on Friday against the Portland Fire. articles.title: Rams’ 53-man roster prediction for 2026 NFL season
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Rams enter the 2026 season with a roster capable of making another deep postseason run. Matthew Stafford leads an offense featuring Puka Nacua, Davante Adams, and Kyren Williams, while Myles Garrett joins Byron Young, Kobie Turner, and Braden Fiske on a talented defensive front. M
articles._body: The Los Angeles Rams enter the 2026 season with a roster capable of making another deep postseason run. Matthew Stafford leads an offense featuring Puka Nacua, Davante Adams, and Kyren Williams, while Myles Garrett joins Byron Young, Kobie Turner, and Braden Fiske on a talented defensive front. Most starting positions are settled, but the Rams’ unofficial depth chart leaves several competitions unresolved. Los Angeles must settle the backup quarterback order, reserve running back roles, final receiver spots, offensive-line depth, defensive reserves, and return assignments. The Rams are 2-0 in the preseason after beating the Kansas City Chiefs 20-12 and New Orleans Saints 34-0. Ty Simpson and Dean Connors connected for two touchdowns in the victory over the Chiefs. Stetson Bennett IV, Wesley Bailey, and Alex Cook then strengthened their cases vs. the Saints. The Rams conclude the 2026 NFL preseason against the Los Angeles Chargers on Thursday before opening the regular season against the San Francisco 49ers in Melbourne on September 10. The NFL roster-reduction deadline is Sunday before 6 p.m. ET, when teams must reach the 53-player limit. Here is our projection for what the Rams’ initial 53-man roster will look like when the deadline arrives on Sunday. Quarterbacks (3) Matthew Stafford, Stetson Bennett IV, Ty Simpson Stafford remains the unquestioned starter , but Sean McVay has not selected his backup. Simpson’s 21-of-25 performance for 190 yards and two touchdowns against Kansas City reinforced the first-round pick’s developmental value. Bennett’s experience in the offense and two rushing touchdowns against New Orleans earn him third place. Thursday could determine their order behind Stafford . Matthew Caldwell projects to the practice squad. Running Backs (4) Kyren Williams, Blake Corum, Ronnie Rivers, Jarquez Hunter Williams and Corum lead the backfield. Rivers stays because of his experience on special teams and ability to contribute in the return game. Hunter earns the final spot based on the Rams’ 2025 fourth-round investment and his 12-yard touchdown against New Orleans. Connors is the most difficult cut after catching both of Simpson’s touchdowns vs. Kansas City. The projection here places Connors and Jordan Waters on the practice-squad radar. Wide Receivers (5) Puka Nacua, Davante Adams, Jordan Whittington, Konata Mumpfield, Xavier Smith Nacua and Adams headline the group, with Whittington positioned for an expanded role. Mumpfield provides experienced depth in the offense. Smith’s receiving ability and value as the projected punt returner secure the final place after his 40-yard return against Kansas City. Sixth-round pick CJ Daniels is the notable cut, but the Rams could attempt to develop him on the practice squad alongside Brennan Presley or Tyler Scott. Tight Ends (5) Tyler Higbee, Colby Parkinson, Davis Allen, Terrance Ferguson, Max Klare Los Angeles’ extensive use of multiple-tight-end formations makes keeping five reasonable. Higbee, Parkinson, Allen, and Ferguson all contributed last season, while second-round pick Klare caught seven passes in his preseason debut. Allen also returned to individual drills Monday following a quadriceps injury. Klare’s draft status and receiving potential eliminate any realistic bubble concerns. Mark Redman remains a strong practice-squad candidate. Offensive Line (9) Alaric Jackson, Steve Avila, Coleman Shelton, Kevin Dotson, Warren McClendon Jr., David Quessenberry, Beaux Limmer, Justin Dedich, Keagen Trost Jackson, Avila, Shelton, Dotson, and McClendon form the projected starting line. Quessenberry supplies veteran tackle depth, while Limmer and Dedich provide interior versatility. Although the live roster still displays Dedich under Reserve/NFI, the Rams’ newer injury update says he passed his physical and practiced Monday. The projection therefore counts him on the 53. Los Angeles remains hopeful Trost can return from his hamstring injury before Week 1. Austin Blaske, Blake Hance, and Dylan McMahon are the leading alternatives. Defensive Line (5) Kobie Turner, Braden Fiske, Poona Ford, Tyler Davis, Ty Hamilton Turner, Fiske, and Ford anchor the interior, with Davis serving as an experienced rotational option. Hamilton earns the final spot after appearing in 14 games last season and providing additional size against the run. The Rams can afford to carry five because Desjuan Johnson offers flexibility between the defensive line and edge. Larrell Murchison is the notable veteran cut, while seventh-round pick Tim Keenan III could land on the practice squad. Outside Linebackers/Edge Rushers (5) Myles Garrett, Byron Young, Josaiah Stewart, Desjuan Johnson, Wesley Bailey Garrett and Young give Los Angeles two established perimeter rushers. Stewart’s growth into a more versatile defender makes him the primary reserve, while Johnson can move between alignments. Bailey claims the final spot after producing five tackles, one sack, three quarterback hits, and a forced fumble against New Orleans. Tomon Fox and Darryl Peterson III remain in contention, making Thursday especially important for the reserve edge group. Inside Linebackers (4) Omar Speights, Nate Landman, Shaun Dolac, Grant Stuard Landman and Speights return as the starting tandem after combining for 217 tackles last season. Dolac provides defensive depth and strengthened his case with an interception late in training camp. Stuard makes the roster because of his special-teams experience and two-year contract. Elias Neal, Nikhai Hill-Green, and Monty Rice are fighting for practice-squad opportunities. Cornerbacks (5) Trent McDuffie, Jaylen Watson, Emmanuel Forbes Jr., Josh Wallace, Cam Lampkin McDuffie and Watson are the projected starters, with Forbes positioned to handle a significant role in subpackages. Wallace’s experience in the system makes him a valuable fourth option. Lampkin earns the final spot after spending last season on the practice squad and producing a fourth-down pass

articles.title: Giants pull pitcher early from start vs. Reds amid injury concerns
articles.summary: The San Francisco Giants have not been having a good season this year. Sitting at 53 wins and 78 losses this year, it’s all but guaranteed that the team will miss the postseason again. This will be the fifth consecutive year the Giants will miss the postseason since they were eliminated by
articles._body: The San Francisco Giants have not been having a good season this year. Sitting at 53 wins and 78 losses this year, it’s all but guaranteed that the team will miss the postseason again. This will be the fifth consecutive year the Giants will miss the postseason since they were eliminated by the Los Angeles Dodgers in the NLDS in 2021. Unfortunately, the misfortunes just continue to pile up for San Francisco, even though things are going well for them. The Giants got off to a 5-0 start against the Cincinnati Reds, going on the verge of upsetting a team with a better record than them. Carson Whisenhunt, who started the game, had held Cincinnati to just two hits through two and two-thirds innings. However, while facing the third hitter in the third inning, Whisenhunt seemingly felt some discomfort. A few minutes later, the pitcher was taken out of the game. Carson Whisenhunt was removed from the game after appearing to sustain an injury pic.twitter.com/HC1lU46CAL — SF Giants on NBCS (@NBCSGiants) August 25, 2026 The Giants announced later on that Whisenhunt exited the game with left elbow discomfort. Whisenhunt was having a rare good start after struggling for most of the season. The Giants’ sophomore pitcher has started in seven games this year, collecting a disastrous 7.03 ERA in 32 innings pitched and a 3-4 record. It’s a far cry from his rookie year, when he was solid in short spurts (5.01 ERA through five games). The Giants ended up winning the game 5-0, shutting out the Reds completely. Rafael Devers hit a three-run homer in the second inning to extend the lead to five after the team scored two runs in the first inning. While the team did not score another run in the game after the second inning, the pitching staff made a collective effort to hold down the fort in Whisenhunt’s absence. The Giants’ win snapped a four-game losing streak for the team. San Francisco was swept by the Boston Red Sox previously, a losing streak that s parked a flurry of roster moves . Among those moves were the decision to place Willy Adames on the 10-day IL and optioning former Little League standout Matt “Tugboat” Wilkinson. articles.title: Diamondbacks’ Merrill Kelly alleges Cubs coach was relaying signs
articles.summary: The start of the work week wasn’t very kind to the Arizona Diamondbacks. They were on the receiving end of a 7-0 demolition at the hands of the Chicago Cubs, and considering that the Diamondbacks are chasing a postseason spot, losses like this do not help. However, starting pitcher Merrill
articles._body: The start of the work week wasn’t very kind to the Arizona Diamondbacks. They were on the receiving end of a 7-0 demolition at the hands of the Chicago Cubs, and considering that the Diamondbacks are chasing a postseason spot, losses like this do not help. However, starting pitcher Merrill Kelly believes that the Cubs crossed a line on Monday, which helped them grab a convincing victory over the Diamondbacks. Kelly, who allowed three earned runs on five hits and three walks before being pulled with two outs in the sixth inning, alleged that the Cubs’ third base coach was relaying signs . It got to a point where Kelly and Cubs third base coach Quintin Berry were chirping at one another. “We just thought that he was relaying signs. We thought he had something on my changeup. We thought he was giving, especially to lefties, every time I was throwing a changeup,” Kelly said, via Cameron Cox of 12 News. “Stealing signs is as old as baseball. I think it’s a little bulls**t when it comes from a coach.” “If it’s a guy on second base and they see the grip in your glove. Or if the hitters can see something that you’re doing with your glove. I think that’s fair game. Guys have been doing that since the beginning of baseball. I think it’s a little bush league when it comes from outside that.” POSTGAME: #Dbacks pitcher Merrill Kelly says they thought #Cubs third-base coach was relaying signs and believes that part of the game should stay between the players. "I think it's a little BS when it comes from a coach." (video courtesy https://t.co/Zd1ZFEYu7y ) pic.twitter.com/gZTJJlIxdF — Cameron Cox (@CamCox12) August 25, 2026 But at the end of the day, the Diamondbacks veteran acknowledged that he has to be better at hiding his intentions on the mound, knowing that if the Cubs picked up on it, others would too. “I got to take a look at what I’m doing because clearly he had something. Obviously, if he has it, then other people would probably pick up on it as well. I got to figure out and do better on my part to not give it away,” Kelly added. articles._body: Hey HN! I just released Cookwing. This is an AI app that solves the biggest problem I had when I was cooking with ChatGPT : The quantities are often hallucinated. I was curious, so I even built my own cooking quantity benchmark while development, and here are the results. We're using my system, which is anchoring tables that are searched in the original country of the recipe. articles.summary: The Los Angeles Sparks suffered their seventh loss in eight games after bowing to the Atlanta Dream, 78-71, at Crypto.com Arena on Monday. Angel Reese delivered a historic performance for the Dream, tallying 11 points, a league-record 26 rebounds, three assists, and three steals. They won their f
articles._body: The Los Angeles Sparks suffered their seventh loss in eight games after bowing to the Atlanta Dream, 78-71, at Crypto.com Arena on Monday. Angel Reese delivered a historic performance for the Dream, tallying 11 points, a league-record 26 rebounds, three assists, and three steals. They won their fourth straight game and improved to 25-13. The Sparks, on the other hand, fell to 13-25. After the game, Nneka Ogwumike shared a special moment with Reese. They hugged at center court and chatted for a few minutes, with Ogwumike appearing to give advice . It remains unclear what the veteran star said to the third-year forward, but it was obvious that Reese was intently agreeing. A beautiful moment between Nneka Ogwumike and Angel Reese following tonight's Dream-Sparks matchup pic.twitter.com/eVClykPOMt — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) August 25, 2026 Fans were all for Ogwumike’s classy gesture. “Greatness recognizing greatness ,” said @rustynailyourBM. “Good advice to stop letting the non-calls get in her head,” claimed @DaHonorable49er. “Nneka teaching her baby ,” wrote @uncleFEEL_. “Nneka telling her game. Respect to the vets,” added @Its_QueenAR10. “I miss Nneka already! ,” commented @Portia82907199. The 36-year-old Ogwumike recently revealed that she will retire at the end of the season, capping off a legendary career that saw her become a champion, an MVP, a Rookie of the Year, an eight-time All-WNBA, a seven-time All-Defense, an 11-time All-Star, and a four-time winner of the Sportsmanship Award. Reese penned a heartfelt message to Ogwumike following the announcement. “Since I came into the league, you’ve shown me nothing but love and treated me like I was one of your own. My first vet. One of my GOATS. Thank you for always pouring into me, believing in me, and having my back,” said the three-time All-Star, as quoted in a report from Athlon Sports’ Chris Phelps. Reese has often expressed her admiration for Ogwumike, particularly for her leadership of the WNBA Players Association. He took to the mound against the Seattle Mariners on Monday, but his fortunes remained the same. The Mariners tagged Wheel
articles._body: The Philadelphia Phillies have played fantastic baseball as of late. Unfortunately, one player who has struggled mightily in this recent stretch is star pitcher Zack Wheeler . He took to the mound against the Seattle Mariners on Monday, but his fortunes remained the same. The Mariners tagged Wheeler for five runs in the first inning. He finished the game having tossed just four innings, allowing nine hits and eight runs. He also threw an unbelievable 103 pitches in those four innings. Wheeler’s ERA in his last five starts ballooned to 9.27. The veteran starter was asked about his health after Monday’s loss, with concerns that an injury could be causing issues on the mound. However, he says everything is good , which has only added to his frustration. “I feel perfectly fine,” Wheeler said, via NBC Sports Philadelphia. “Healthy, strong. Everything’s there. Just got to zone back in and figure it out. It’s been a while. I haven’t had a stretch like this in a while. That’s why I’m so frustrated.” The Phillies’ bullpen did well to limit the damage after Wheeler exited the game. They allowed just one run in the final six innings. However, Cal Raleigh’s three home run game led the charge toward a 9-2 Seattle win. Philadelphia had won nine games in a row to this point. They are chasing a playoff spot and a potential NL East division title. The Phillies are 3.5 games back of the Atlanta Braves for first in the NL East. Of course, Philadelphia’s true ambitions go beyond simply getting into October. This franchise believes it has a chance to win the World Series right now. To do that, though, they will need to figure out what is causing Wheeler’s recent struggles. articles._body: San Antonio Spurs center Victor Wembanyama has been raising the temperature in the 2027 FIBA World Cup European Qualifiers. While he’s taking care of business for the French national team , his teammates found a new way to troll him for his comical shoe size at the camp. In a recently surfaced video on X, formerly Twitter, Wembanyama’s France teammates Nadir Hifi and Matthew Strazel were seen geeking out at his Nike shoes, size 21. Team France poking fun at Wembanyama #nba #porvida #sanantonio pic.twitter.com/XRWiYrNLyP — JeffGSpursZone (@JeffGSpursZone) August 24, 2026 The two guards were hilariously imitating Wemby’s shooting rhythm while pretending to use the 7’4” center/forward’s footwear as a phone. However, the latest fun moment comes after an otherwise intense stretch for the Frenchmen. They had back-to-back exhibition games against Nikola Jokic’s Serbian team. While France lost 90-87 the first time they met, they edged out Serbia 91-90 on Sunday. Wemby had an impressive stat line during his 24 minutes of play on Sunday. The two-time NBA All-Star scored 18 points and recorded five blocks, while also shooting 5-of-11 from the field. As for Serbia, Jokic had a comparatively better performance with 34 points, 13 rebounds, and five assists. Irrespective of how the two games ended, the two NBA superstars made sure to show respect for each other. Answering a reporter’s question about learning something new from The Joker, the Spurs superstar had the most honest response . “Of course you always learn when you play against Jokic. You always catch some stuff and smarter moves on the court in those duels with him,” he said. Similarly, Jokic gave his thoughts on the Spurs phenom becoming one of the best the league has ever seen. “He has the opportunity to be the most unique basketball player we’ve ever seen. It only depends on him how well he’s gonna fit, how well he’s gonna work hard, how well he’s gonna get to his spots, and treat his body well. He definitely has the opportunity to be the best ever,” he said after their first clash. articles.title: Jets’ 53-man roster prediction for 2026 NFL season
articles.summary: The New York Jets actually look like they have some genuine momentum. After dropping their preseason opener to Tampa Bay, Aaron Glenn’s team responded with a statement performance in Pittsburgh. Suddenly, the competition for roster spots feels considerably more consequential. Geno Smith has
articles._body: The New York Jets actually look like they have some genuine momentum. After dropping their preseason opener to Tampa Bay, Aaron Glenn’s team responded with a statement performance in Pittsburgh. Suddenly, the competition for roster spots feels considerably more consequential. Geno Smith has already demonstrated that the offense can operate efficiently under Frank Reich . There defense has generated pressure and turnovers. With one preseason game remaining against the Giants, the Jets must separate legitimate contributors from temporary summer standouts. This will determine which 53 players give them the best chance to compete when the games finally count. Jets gaining momentum Mandatory Credit: John Jones-Imagn Images The Jets sit at 1-1 through two preseason games. They recovered from a 24-16 home defeat against Tampa Bay with a dominant 17-0 shutout of Pittsburgh at Acrisure Stadium. The encouraging response has given Glenn’s revamped squad some much-needed confidence. Smith was particularly impressive in his preseason debut. He completed all seven of his passes on a touchdown drive while operating Reich’s offense with efficiency and rhythm. Meanwhile, the defense overwhelmed Pittsburgh with four sacks and two takeaways. That offered a glimpse of the aggressive identity Glenn wants to establish. The Giants now provide the final measuring stick before New York must finalize its 53-man roster. Offensive Playmakers Quarterback (2): Geno Smith, Cade Klubnik Smith has the experience and accuracy to serve as the unquestioned starter. His early preseason performance reinforced why the Jets believe he can provide stability. Reich’s system should allow Smith to operate from structure while taking advantage of his ability to make quick decisions. Klubnik earns the backup spot. He gives New York a developmental option with enough mobility to expand the offense when necessary. The Jets ultimately cannot afford to devote a third roster spot to the position. Running Back (5): Breece Hall, Braelon Allen, Isaiah Davis, Kene Nwangwu, Andrew Beck Hall remains the centerpiece because of his home-run potential. The Jets have every reason to maximize his touches. Allen provides physicality and complementary early-down work. Davis gives the team another capable runner. Nwangwu’s value extends beyond the backfield because of his special-teams ability. Beck’s fullback versatility makes him particularly useful in short-yardage packages. It is an unusually deep group, but every member offers a distinct role. Wide Receiver (6): Garrett Wilson, Adonai Mitchell, Omar Cooper Jr, Tim Patrick, Arian Smith, Isaiah Williams Wilson should remain the primary target in Reich’s passing attack. His ability to win at multiple levels gives Smith a reliable option. Mitchell brings size and vertical ability. Patrick supplies veteran experience and contested-catch reliability. Cooper and Arian Smith add explosiveness. Williams provides versatility from multiple alignments. Tight End (3): Mason Taylor, Kenyon Sadiq, Jelani Woods Taylor projects as an important receiving component. Sadiq adds athleticism and the ability to threaten defenses vertically. Woods provides a massive target and a useful option in the red zone. Offensive Line Offensive Line (9): Olu Fashanu, Dylan Parham, Josh Myers, Joe Tippmann, Armand Membou, Max Mitchell, Chukwuma Okorafor, Xavier Newman, Anez Cooper Fashanu anchors the left side. Membou handles the right tackle position. Myers gives the interior a veteran presence at center. Parham and Tippmann complete the projected starting configuration. The depth is arguably just as important. Mitchell’s ability to play multiple positions, Okorafor’s tackle experience, and Newman’s interior versatility provide insurance against potential injuries. Defense Defensive line (5): T’Vondre Sweat, Harrison Phillips, David Onyemata, Jowon Briggs, Darrell Jackson Jr Sweat and Phillips provide substantial size and power. Onyemata adds veteran savvy and pass-rushing experience. Briggs offers rotational flexibility, with Jackson providing additional depth. The objective is clear: force opposing offenses to account for the interior before they can attack the Jets’ edge rushers. EDGE (5): David Bailey, Will McDonald IV, Joseph Ossai, Kingsley Enagbare, Nate Lynn McDonald is the explosive pass-rushing threat capable of changing games. Bailey and Ossai provide additional pressure packages. Enagbare brings versatility and experience, and Lynn rounds out the rotation. Linebacker (4): Demario Davis, Jamien Sherwood, Francisco “Kiko” Mauigoa, Marcelino McCrary-Ball Davis supplies the veteran leadership and football intelligence. Sherwood complements him with athleticism and range. Mauigoa and McCrary-Ball provide younger rotational options. The Jets do not need this group to dominate statistically if the defensive line and secondary can consistently create favorable situations. Cornerback (6): Brandon Stephens, Nahshon Wright, Jarvis Brownlee Jr, Azareye’h Thomas, D’Angelo Ponds, Qwan’tez Stiggers Stephens provides experience on the perimeter. Wright adds another lengthy coverage option. Brownlee and Thomas give the Jets additional physicality. Ponds and Stiggers provide depth and developmental upside. Safety (5): Minkah Fitzpatrick, Andre Cisco, Dane Belton, Malachi Moore, Samuel Womack III Fitzpatrick gives Glenn the freedom to move him around the formation. Cisco brings playmaking ability. Belton, Moore, and Womack provide rotational and special-teams value. Special Teams Kicker: Jason Sanders Punter: Austin McNamara Long Snapper: Thomas Hennessy. Sanders gives the Jets a proven option at kicker. McNamara handles punting and holding duties. Hennessy provides continuity at long snapper. With the rest of the roster undergoing significant transition, maintaining stability here is particularly valuable. Final 53 John Jones-Imagn Imag

articles.title: Dodgers’ Blake Snell gets new company in extremely exclusive Rays club
articles.summary: Blake Snell has been quite brilliant for the Los Angeles Dodgers ever since he came off the injured list. He’s allowed just two earned runs in 18.0 innings pitched since, lowering his ERA to 2.57 on the season. Snell continues to be one of the best pitchers in MLB, as he has been since the
articles._body: Blake Snell has been quite brilliant for the Los Angeles Dodgers ever since he came off the injured list. He’s allowed just two earned runs in 18.0 innings pitched since, lowering his ERA to 2.57 on the season. Snell continues to be one of the best pitchers in MLB, as he has been since the start of his big-league career with the Tampa Bay Rays. The Rays traded Snell back in 2020, with Tampa Bay selling high on him even though he was still under contract until the end of the 2023 season. This is Tampa Bay’s standard operating procedure; they keep the line moving to avoid running into payroll problems as a small-market club. Since then, the Rays have developed quite a few quality starting pitchers. In 2026, one of their best starters has been Drew Rasmussen, who pitched another quality start for Tampa Bay in a 4-1 win over the Detroit Tigers on Monday. Rasmussen earned the win after he allowed just one earned run on three hits in six innings of work, striking out five while walking none. With that latest win for Rasmussen, he became just the second pitcher in Rays history to earn a win in at least seven consecutive starts, joining Blake Snell in that exclusive club, according to MLB Stats on X. Snell accomplished the feat in 2018, when he earned a win in nine consecutive starts for the Rays. During that nine-game stretch, Snell pitched 52.2 innings and allowed just six earned runs, which was good for an ERA of 1.03. He ended that season with a win-loss record of 21-5. Even though the Rays finished 2018 with a 90-72 record, they missed the postseason after finishing third in the stacked AL East. In 2026, the Rays have led the AL East for much of the season and are currently on top of the division with a 78-53 record. Rasmussen has a 14-5 record this year with an ERA of 2.95 across 140.1 innings (25 starts). articles._body: Angel Reese had herself a night on Monday, leading the Atlanta Dream past the Los Angeles Sparks , 78-71, at Crypto.com Arena with a historic performance. Reese finished with 11 points, a career-high 26 rebounds, three assists, and three steals. She set the league record for most rebounds in a game and most rebounds in a single season. Reese surpassed Chamique Holdsclaw and A’ja Wilson , respectively, for the impressive feats. She leads the WNBA in rebounds this season with 12.4 per game. She has 458 rebounds and counting. She was the rebounding queen last season with 12.6 boards per game. RECORD-BREAKING NIGHT FOR ANGEL REESE A new WNBA record for rebounds in a game pic.twitter.com/AxZ1PqZ6XT — ESPN (@espn) August 25, 2026 Fans gave the 24-year-old forward her flowers for her latest milestone. “26 rebounds in a single game is purely historic! Angel Reese owns the glass,” said @lucky_voller. “All that backlash on her. She’s really showing us what she can do,” added @jackson_da55761. “She’s just getting warmed up. The girl got a motor on her,” wrote @trapmamba318. “I feel like she’s working towards (being the) best rebounder of all time,” posted @zaireoneal. “26 REBOUNDS! ANGEL REESE, YOU’RE UNREAL. History right there!” commented @RebeccaJoy211. The three-time All-Star grabbed at least 20 rebounds in a game for the fifth time since entering the WNBA in 2024. Her tenacity and competitiveness have made her a menace on the glass. Even at LSU, the 6-foot-3 Reese was almost impossible to keep off the paint. She tallied her 27th double-double of the season, the most by any player. The Dream outrebounded the Sparks, 48-32, including 15-7 on the offensive glass. Reese had eight offensive rebounds. Atlanta notched its fourth straight win and improved to 25-13. The post Dream fans give Angel Reese her flowers for historic performance vs. Sparks appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles._body: The shape of the Indianapolis Colts’ 53-man roster is beginning to emerge from the chaos. At 0-1-1, Indianapolis has not exactly overwhelmed opponents in the preseason. Still, the exhibition slate has provided Shane Steichen with valuable information about his revamped depth chart. Daniel Jones is settling again into the starting role . That makes the preseason finale against Detroit even more important. Questions to answer Eric Canha-Imagn Images Indianapolis has navigated a turbulent, evaluation-heavy preseason. They had a 13-13 tie against New England and the 34-6 home loss to Atlanta. The latter result was particularly revealing because the Colts were outgained 461-164. Their reserves struggled to sustain drives against Atlanta’s depth. That said, the preseason should be judged primarily through individual evaluations. Steichen used the extended training-camp stay at Grand Park and joint practices with Atlanta to continue integrating Jones and assess the depth behind him . The Colts also made a significant commitment to Taylor. They signed their star running back to a two-year extension. With Detroit next, Indianapolis has one final opportunity to settle the roster battles that remain. It also allows Indianapolis to retain multiple pathways if injuries or performance force another adjustment. Running Back (3): Jonathan Taylor, Seth McGowan, DJ Giddens Taylor’s new extension reinforces that their offense is at its best when the explosive veteran runner is the foundation. His ability to create explosive gains gives Steichen a reliable offensive centerpiece. McGowan and Giddens provide contrasting depth. Ulysses Bentley IV and Anderson Castle are projected toward the practice squad. Downs provides the quick separation and underneath creativity. Indianapolis signed Allen to a one-year deal in August after trading away Michael Pittman Jr. That makes his veteran presence particularly important. Dulin and Westbrook-Ikhine offer complementary experience. Owen earns the final spot through his versatility. Tight End (4): Tyler Warren, Mo Alie-Cox, Drew Ogletree, Will Mallory Warren provides the most dynamic all-around option. Alie-Cox remains a formidable inline presence. Ogletree and Mallory provide additional depth for an offense capable of using multiple tight-end formations. Pharaoh Brown is projected toward injured reserve. Offensive Line Offensive Line (9): Bernhard Raimann, Quenton Nelson, Tanor Bortolini, Matt Goncalves, Jalen Travis, Blake Freeland, Luke Tenuta, Jalen Farmer and Dalton Tucker Nelson remains the veteran anchor. Raimann provides stability at left tackle. Bortolini’s versatility is especially useful in the interior. Goncalves and Travis provide additional flexibility. The depth pieces are critical because Indianapolis cannot afford another season in which injuries completely destabilize its offensive operation. Josh Sills, Jimmy Morrissey, Geno VanDeMark, and Josh Kreutz are projected to miss the initial 53. Defense Defensive Line (10): Laiatu Latu, DeForest Buckner, Grover Stewart, Arden Key, Jaylahn Tuimoloau, Micheal Clemons, Colby Wooden, Adetomiwa Adebawore, Derrick Nnadi, George Gumbs Jr Buckner and Stewart provide the veteran interior foundation. Latu and Key bring pass-rushing ability from the edge. Tuimoloau adds another disruptive dimension. Adebawore’s positional flexibility makes him particularly valuable. The depth battle is fierce. Jerry Tillery, Caden Curry, Tim Smith, Cameron Ball, and Mitchell Melton projected outside the roster. Linebacker (5): CJ Allen, Akeem Davis-Gaither, Bryce Boettcher, Jaylon Carlies, Austin Ajiake. Allen should take the middle linebacker role. Davis-Gaither gives the group athleticism and coverage versatility. Carlies and Ajiake provide useful depth and special-teams value. The lack of overwhelming depth here could ultimately force Indianapolis to monitor the waiver wire once cuts begin. Ward supplies veteran experience. Walley, Blackmon, and the younger corners give the Colts multiple options to rotate behind them. Cam Taylor-Britt’s one-game suspension for Week 1 adds an additional layer to the equation. Indianapolis must carry enough depth to survive his absence without compromising its defensive structure. Safety (4): Camryn Bynum, AJ Haulcy, Hunter Wohler, Jonathan Owens Bynum provides the veteran stability, while Haulcy’s physical style gives the unit an intriguing complement. articles.title: Dream’s Angel Reese gets ‘a talent’ praise from Allisha Gray
articles.summary: Angel Reese may not be a perfect basketball player by any means, but one thing that everyone is always guaranteed to see out of her is that she’s never going to stop putting in effort in every second she spends on the hardwood. On Monday, the Atlanta Dream forward made history during a 78-7
articles._body: Angel Reese may not be a perfect basketball player by any means, but one thing that everyone is always guaranteed to see out of her is that she’s never going to stop putting in effort in every second she spends on the hardwood. On Monday, the Atlanta Dream forward made history during a 78-71 victory over the Los Angeles Sparks, as she set the all-time single-game record for rebounds in a WNBA game, with 26. The previous single-game record for rebounds in the WNBA is 24, which Chamique Holdslaw set all the way back in 2003. It should go without saying now that Reese is one of the greatest rebounders in the history of the association even this early in her career. Her detractors can’t even chalk up her record-setting rebound night to her merely rebounding her own misses, as she hauled in 18 defensive boards compared to eight on the offensive glass. Even her Dream teammate, Allisha Gray, who led the team in scoring on Monday with 20 points on 7-11 shooting, couldn’t believe the game she had on the boards. “I was looking at the stat thing, and I’m like, ‘Dang, 20 something rebounds?’ How many rebounds she had? I don’t think in my life I got more than 10 rebounds. I think she’s a talent. I’m just watching her rebound, like, that’s a talent,” Gray said of Reese in her postgame interview, via Women’s Hoops Network on X. Allisha Gray on Angel Reese breaking the WNBA single-game rebounds record with 26 REBOUNDS (!!!) : pic.twitter.com/I5pxo66fmY — Women’s Hoops Network (@WomensHoops_USA) August 25, 2026 Effort requires talent, and Reese has that in spades. It takes so much energy to command the glass the way she does, and the most important thing on defense is securing the ball — and no one does that better in today’s WNBA than the Dream forward. Never mind that she went 4-14 from the field and she has her troubles at times to put the ball through the hoop. Reese is proving herself to be a winning player by committing herself to doing all the dirty work for her team every time she’s on the court. articles.title: Dream’s Angel Reese sets new single-game WNBA record with insane effort vs. Sparks
articles.summary: Angel Reese made history for the ages as she crashed the glass in the Atlanta Dream’s 78-71 win over the Los Angeles Sparks on Monday night. Reese is going through the third season of her WNBA career, her first with the Dream. She is enjoying her best campaign to date, finally getting to ex
articles._body: Angel Reese made history for the ages as she crashed the glass in the Atlanta Dream’s 78-71 win over the Los Angeles Sparks on Monday night. Reese is going through the third season of her WNBA career, her first with the Dream. She is enjoying her best campaign to date, finally getting to experience the first playoff berth after Atlanta recently punched its ticket. Reese stands out as one of the best rebounders in the entire league, often boxing out opponents to gain possession of the ball and create second chances. The spotlight shined on her once again, seeing her make history in 38 minutes of action. Reese finished with a stat line of 11 points, 26 rebounds, three assists, and three steals. She shot 4-of-14 from the field and 3-of-4 from the free-throw line. Her efforts ended up setting a new WNBA record , per reporter David Mendez-Yapkowitz. Angel Reese was DOMINANT in tonight's win over the Sparks 11 points 26 rebounds 3 assists 3 steals 4-of-14 FG 3-of-4 FT She made history tonight by breaking the single-game and single-season rebounding records. pic.twitter.com/xvJQm5FqPx — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) August 25, 2026 How Angel Reese, Dream played against Sparks Angel Reese dominated the glass as the Sparks couldn’t match her inside the paint. This resulted in the Dream securing a quality win on the road. Four players scored in double-digits for Atlanta in the win, including Reese. Allisha Gray led the team with 20 points, six assists and three rebounds. She shot 7-of-11 overall including 2-of-6 from beyond the arc, and 4-of-5 from the charity stripe. Rhyne Howard came next with 18 points and six rebounds, Naz Hillmon had 12 points and seven rebounds, while Jordin Canada provided nine points and four assists. Atlanta improved to a 25-13 record on the season, sitting at first place in the Eastern Conference standings. They are above the Indiana Fever and the New York Liberty at the moment. Rolling with four consecutive wins, the Dream will look forward to their next matchup. They are at home when they host the Portland Fire as tip-off commences on Aug. 28 at 7:30 p.m. ET. articles._body: The high school football season officially kicks off this week in Missouri. Ahead of that, Blue Springs South (Mo.) enters the upcoming season as the number one team in Missouri high school football, according to Rivals Preseason Missouri Top 25 Rankings . Kicking off their season, the Blue Springs South Jaguars take on Lee’s Summit (Mo.) in a clash between two of the top teams in the state. When the two schools met in 2025, the Jaguars came out on top in a surprisingly one-sided clash, with Rivals predicting that Blue Springs South will come out on top once again in 2026. With both sides meeting as two of the top teams in Missouri high school football, Lee’s Summit sits at No. 8 in the Massey Ratings, putting together a 9-4 record. Going into the upcoming season, the Tigers will be without two of their biggest offensive weapons from 2025, with three-star running back Preston Hatfield and three-star wide receiver Karsten Fiene enrolling at Missouri. However, they do return a significant amount of talent on the defensive side of the ball. With three-star defensive line prospect Zayre Thomas going into his junior year, three-star linebacker Drew Banassi also returns for his senior year, after putting up 139 tackles, 19 for loss, 5 sacks, two fumble recoveries, and an interception in 2025. They are also backed by Rivals’ Missouri high school football coach of the year, Todd Miller. Meanwhile, Blue Springs South returns the top prospect in Missouri high school football, with four-star linebacker Prince Goldsby , the number eight linebacker in the class of 2027 according to Rivals Industry Rankings. “As a junior, the Blue Springs South edge rusher was one of the most dangerous players on the line in 2025, recording 13.5 sacks and 22.5 tackles for loss. articles.title: Devils’ glaring roster flaw that must be fixed before 2026-27 NHL season
articles.summary: The New Jersey Devils have a new general manager at the helm heading into 2026-27. Sunny Mehta returns to the franchise after spending time as an assistant general manager with the Florida Panthers. Mehta, having won two Stanley Cups to his name, returns to the franchise that gave him his start i
articles._body: The New Jersey Devils have a new general manager at the helm heading into 2026-27. Sunny Mehta returns to the franchise after spending time as an assistant general manager with the Florida Panthers . Mehta, having won two Stanley Cups to his name, returns to the franchise that gave him his start in the NHL. He returns at a time when New Jersey truly needs it. This franchise has come close to being a Stanley Cup contender in the past. On paper, this is a team that should be able to contend with some of the Eastern Conference heavyweights. However, they have managed to fall short throughout the 2020s. This past season was a prime example. The Devils failed to make the Stanley Cup Playoffs after making it in 2025. In fact, New Jersey was the second-worst team in the Metropolitan Division. Only the New York Rangers finished with fewer points in the Metro. Mehta’s first offseason at the helm has been an interesting one, to say the least. The Devils traded Jacob Markstrom to the Panthers , adding Evan Rodrigues as part of the return. They also acquired Declan Chisholm and Amadeus Lombardi in separate trades. The Devils also traded defenseman Simon Nemec to the Calgary Flames. NHL Free Agency was a quiet affair for the new general manager. David Rittch signed to add goaltending depth to this organization. And veteran winger Anthony Mantha joined on a two-year contract. With New Jersey’s offseason unofficially over, let’s take a look at what the team’s biggest roster flaw is heading into the 2026-27 NHL season. Who will be the Devils’ starting goaltender? Ed Mulholland-Imagn Images The Devils have a deep goaltending room with three realistic options to play NHL games. Rittich has experience and a solid enough track record as a backup goaltender. Nico Daws has shown some flashes and has youth on his side at just 25 years old. Then there’s veteran Jake Allen, who many would consider the favorite to be the primary starter. Allen has had a very solid career in his own right. And his time in New Jersey has certainly gone well for him personally. He has recorded a .900 save percentage each year in the parts of three seasons he has played for the Devils. The question for New Jersey, though, is how this unit will perform. Allen is a solid goaltender, but he is not getting any younger. Daws could be a long-term option, but can he make a significant impact right now? Rittich, like Allen, is getting up there in age. And he has also been inconsistent throughout his career. New Jersey is trying to win games right now. They will need these three goaltenders to perform at their best if they want to make the Stanley Cup Playoffs. It’s certainly easier said than done to acquire a top-tier goaltender. A trade for Winnipeg Jets star Connor Hellebuyck would be a fantastic option for the Devils. However, it’s hard to imagine the Jets moving him at this point in the offseason. It’s also a question of whether the Devils have the assets to make that deal in the first place. New Jersey has high hopes for this upcoming season. They want to compete with the best in the East and play for a chance at a Stanley Cup next summer. Shoring up their goaltending could give them that little extra push toward Cup contention in 2027. articles._body: Mitchell Robinson has been doing individual training ahead of his first training camp with the Boston Celtics. Robinson signed with the Celtics on a three-year, $47.4 million contract in July, and he wants to prove he is worth every cent. It has been quite the transition for Robinson. He moved to Boston just a few weeks after he won a title with the New York Knicks. He did not want to leave New York , but the team could not afford him anymore due to its financial constraints. The Celtics were happy to take him in. While the 28-year-old pivot is putting in the work, he is enjoying it as well. On Instagram, he shared a video of himself making back-to-back free throws to take on a fan’s challenge . “Okay, can you get off my now? Please and thank you. #TakeThatForData ,” wrote Robinson in the caption. View this post on Instagram His post quickly attracted various reactions. “Now, do three,” said @hunterphay. “This is AI,” added @reflectmebaby. “LMFAO,” wrote @owdawgin16. “Aye, Mitch, I’m proud of you, but try not to shoot like that against the Knicks. ,” pleaded @itaddy. “They got you Shaqtin’ up out here,” claimed @koby_steed. “ you, Big Mitch. Keep shining ,” stated @classcteacher. Many commented with laughing emojis, including Andre Drummond, who essentially replaced Robinson on the Knicks. “ Don’t change, bro,” said Drummond. Robinson and Drummond have become notorious for being terrible at free throws, joining other big men like Wilt Chamberlain, Shaquille O’Neal, Ben Wallace, and DeAndre Jordan, among others. Last season, Robinson shot a career-worst 40.8% from the charity stripe. He averaged 5.7 points, 8.8 rebounds, and 1.2 blocks in 19.6 minutes off the bench. They have outscored their opponents 64-29 and have swept three different teams during that span. And while fan morale has reached
articles._body: The Philadelphia Phillies entered play on Monday against the Seattle Mariners having won nine consecutive games to keep cementing their place in an NL Wild Card spot. They have outscored their opponents 64-29 and have swept three different teams during that span. And while fan morale has reached a season-high for a Phillies team that’s battled against inconsistency for much of 2026, some fans are still hesitant to go all-in on this squad. In particular, Spike Eskin of WIP straight up said that he doesn’t trust the Phillies yet even amid this recent hot streak, as they need to show more consistency to earn stronger trust from the fanbase. “They have not earned your belief. They have not earned your trust. They have not earned your faith. You have to make them earn it,” Eskin said. “I’m not saying not to enjoy the Phillies. I am not believing they are real yet.” Spike Eskin isn't ready to fully believe in the Phillies just yet: “They have not earned your belief…You have to make them earn it.” pic.twitter.com/WIj8ba1hDX — SPORTSRADIO 94WIP (@SportsRadioWIP) August 24, 2026 Eskin then reminded fans of how the Phillies performed in 2024 when they looked to be in as good a position as any other team in competing for a World Series title. “Let me take you back. Phillies start off in 2024, 61-32. They swept the Dodgers. After sweeping the Dodgers, they lost 14 of their next 20. They lose meekly to the Mets in the NLDS,” Eskin explained. “In 2025, they have a nine-game winning streak in May. They start 34-18. After that nine-game winning streak, what do they do? They go 1-9.” “I am talking as a person who has been hurt by this team.” The Phillies’ nine-game winning streak ended on Monday in a 9-2 loss to the Seattle Mariners, with Zack Wheeler having one of the worst starts of his career. Could this be the beginning of another prolonged slump for Philly? Or have they finally learned their lesson from the past few years and start being a more trustworthy team in the eye of their weary fanbase? articles.title: Cubs, Diamondbacks engage in fiery exchange in tense moment
articles.summary: The Chicago Cubs and Arizona Diamondbacks exchanged words during a tense fifth inning Monday night at Chase Field, adding friction to a series between two National League playoff contenders. The dispute centered on Cubs third base coach Quintin Berry and Diamondbacks starting pitcher Merrill Kell
articles._body: The Chicago Cubs and Arizona Diamondbacks exchanged words during a tense fifth inning Monday night at Chase Field, adding friction to a series between two National League playoff contenders. The dispute centered on Cubs third base coach Quintin Berry and Diamondbacks starting pitcher Merrill Kelly. Arizona personnel appeared to believe Berry was trying to look into Kelly’s glove. The right-hander responded by staring toward the Cubs coach as Kelly faced Michael Busch, with the Cubs up 2-0. Members of Arizona’s dugout then shouted and gestured across the field. Chicago responded from the opposite side, but players remained in their respective dugouts. The confrontation did not become a benches-clearing incident or cause an extended interruption. Foul Territory TV shared footage of the confrontation Monday on X, formerly Twitter, capturing the tense exchange between the two dugouts. “The Cubs and Diamondbacks dugouts had some words for each other. ” The Cubs and Diamondbacks dugouts had some words for each other. pic.twitter.com/qleOIaAUZX — Foul Territory (@FoulTerritoryTV) August 25, 2026 The apparent concern that Berry was reading Kelly’s pitches made the situation particularly sensitive. Teams closely protect signs and pitcher tendencies, and even suspected gamesmanship can provoke an immediate response. In this instance, however, the disagreement remained verbal, and play continued without further escalation. The Cubs controlled the series opener before and after the confrontation. Pedro Ramirez opened the scoring with an RBI triple, and Seiya Suzuki added an RBI double. Michael Conforto and Carson Kelly later hit consecutive home runs during a three-run sixth inning as the Cubs extended their advantage. Kevin Gausman limited the Diamondbacks to three hits and one walk across seven scoreless innings while striking out six. Ryan Zeferjahn followed with a scoreless eighth before Chicago completed a 7-0 shutout, improving to 76-56. For the Diamondbacks, the exchange unfolded during a damaging home loss amid a crowded National League Wild Card race. The Cubs, meanwhile, paired their dugout response with a commanding performance. Monday’s confrontation added tension to the late-August series without producing another incident, while Chicago left Chase Field with a decisive victory. articles.title: Dream’s Angel Reese breaks A’ja Wilson’s WNBA record with stunning stat vs. Sparks
articles.summary: Angel Reese had a night to remember on Monday, with the Atlanta Dream star forward making WNBA history during a game against the Los Angeles Sparks at Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles. Reese entered the game with 432 total rebounds in the 2026 WNBA season, trailing just Las Vegas Aces star A’
articles._body: Angel Reese had a night to remember on Monday, with the Atlanta Dream star forward making WNBA history during a game against the Los Angeles Sparks at Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles. Reese entered the game with 432 total rebounds in the 2026 WNBA season, trailing just Las Vegas Aces star A’ja Wilson for most boards ever in a single campaign. Wilson set the record in 2024, when she pulled down a total of 451 rebounds. The former LSU Tigers women’s basketball star Reese made sure that record wouldn’t stand for long, finishing the Sparks game with an incredible 25 (!) rebounds. Of course, the Dream were not going to let that accomplishment go by without flexing it on social media . “YOU CAN’T STOP HER Angel Reese now holds the WNBA single-season record for total rebounds. Dominant in her game ,” Atlanta shared on X, formerly Twitter. Reese has always been known as a rebounding machine, and she surely lived up to that reputation against the Sparks. On top of her outrageous total on the glass, the 24-year-old Reese came away with 11 points, three assists and three steals in 38 minutes of action in the Dream’s 78-71 win. She shot just 4-for-14 from the field, but her tenacity on the glass gave Atlanta several extra possessions, as eight of her rebounds were off the offensive glass — as many as the difference between the Dream’s and the Sparks’ total shot attempts. The Dream have six more games left on their schedule in the regular season, giving Angel Reese several more chances to pad her single-season rebounding record . articles.title: From 2-star to Superstar: A look at the rise of Matt Rose
articles.summary: Looking ahead to 2026, one thing we know for certain is that veteran inside linebacker Matt Rose projects to be the centerpiece of the Stanford defense.
articles._body: Nov 22, 2025; Stanford, California, USA; Stanford Cardinal linebacker Matt Rose (35) celebrates after recovering a fumble by California Golden Bears quarterback Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele (3) during the fourth quarter at Stanford Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Sergio Estrada-Imagn Images Looking ahead to the 2026 Stanford football season, one thing we know for certain is that veteran inside linebacker Matt Rose projects to be the centerpiece of the Cardinal defense. Rose is coming off a season in which he played in all 12 games, totaling 106 tackles (49 solo), 8.0 tackles for loss, 3.0 sacks, three pass deflections, one forced fumble, and one fumble recovery. He did miss one half due to a targeting call, so his numbers could have been even higher. It was a major leap forward from his redshirt sophomore season in which he had 32 tackles (17 solo), 3.5 tackles for loss, and one pass deflection in 12 games played. Given the leap he took forward in his redshirt junior season, it’s honestly scary to think about what he’s going to be as a redshirt senior. Matt Rose joins running back Micah Ford and safety Jay Green on the Stanford billboard on El Camino. When Rose committed to Stanford as part of their 2022 class, Rivals rated him as a 2-star recruit. He was an afterthought and viewed as someone who might become a decent special teams guy or backup linebacker. The fact that that he’s become the heart of the Cardinal defense and their most valuable player is a testament to his work ethic, grit, and determination. At 6’2”, 230 pounds, Rose is now a guy who opposing offenses have to fear. He’s a tackling machine that also makes plays in the backfield. A budding force of nature in the center of the defense. “Yeah, I would say just kept developing,” Rose said of his growth. “Yeah, I think that’s the key. I just kept developing, you know. Studying the playbook and I just knew when my opportunity would come, I knew I would be ready for it and I would not, I just knew I would be ready for the opportunity…I don’t think I surprised myself. Like, I always, something I believed I could do when I got the opportunity to do it.” Looking ahead to his redshirt senior season, Rose should be looking to get a similar amount of tackles while tacking on a few more high impact plays. If he could jump to 110-115 total tackles while having 10-12 tackles for loss, 4-5 sacks, 2-3 forced fumbles, and 5-6 pass breakups, that would be fantastic. Of course, if he has a repeat of last year, that would be great, too. He really took a massive jump last season and now this year it’s going to be more about maintaining that consistency and making tweaks to improve his game. “I think his pass coverage is improving,” Stanford inside linebackers coach Andy Thompson said of Rose. “He plays the run really well, but he’s really put an emphasis on his pass coverage, so I think he’s doing a good job of that. I think he’s also doing a good job of leading every day. When you have some success you know, the rest of the team looks for you to see how you’re going to work and he’s been a tremendous worker, he’s a great person, and really excited to see him play his senior year.” What makes Rose special though is his impact goes beyond the numbers. He’s a guy who his teammates all respect and look up to. He works extremely hard, leads by example, approaches the game the right away, and also just has a love for playing a physical brand of football. It’ll be fun to see what he has in store for the Cardinal in 2026. Note: Cardinal Sports Report has you covered for all the latest news on Stanford as they begin the Tavita Pritchard era. articles.title: Mariners catcher Cal Raleigh’s personal Home Run Derby hits impressive mark vs. Phillies
articles.summary: Cal Raleigh’s level of production has fallen off a cliff, and the Seattle Mariners offense has gotten much worse amid his steep decline. The Mariners entered their Monday night clash against the Philadelphia Phillies tied for the fewest runs scored in MLB in 2026, and Raleigh’s .579 O
articles._body: Cal Raleigh’s level of production has fallen off a cliff , and the Seattle Mariners offense has gotten much worse amid his steep decline. The Mariners entered their Monday night clash against the Philadelphia Phillies tied for the fewest runs scored in MLB in 2026, and Raleigh’s .579 OPS on the year heading into the night has not helped matters whatsoever. However, Raleigh appears to be getting into a rhythm , if his play on Monday night against the Phillies is any indication. Raleigh homered twice off of Phillies veteran Zack Wheeler, and as the cherry on top of what has already been an incredible night for the 2025 AL MVP runner-up, he hit another long ball in the seventh inning, this time against reliever Chase Shugart. This seventh-inning dinger from Raleigh pushed the Mariners’ lead to 9-2 as they’re well on their way to taking a victory at home against the Phillies. CAL RALEIGH WITH A THREE-HOMER MASTERCLASS FOR THE MARINERS pic.twitter.com/bI54cduZjb — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) August 25, 2026 Raleigh has been able to turn on pitches on Monday, which may be a sign that the Mariners catcher is putting his injury woes in the rearview mirror. There’s no secret that an oblique injury slowed his roll considerably to begin the 2026 season, and he hasn’t been able to find his rhythm — perhaps until now. The Mariners catcher turned on a 95-mph four-seam fastball for his first home run of the night, sending it deep into the right-field bleachers. His second homer was almost identical to the first one, but this time, he punished a cutter from Wheeler right at the heart of the plate to send it close to where his first long ball landed. Cal Raleigh goes deep for the second time in this game https://t.co/lGEX1Ccf6s pic.twitter.com/YR1srNkvJm — MLB (@MLB) August 25, 2026 And then for his third dinger, Raleigh hit a cutter around the knees for a wall-scraper, which counts the same as a moonshot. Raleigh was in complete command of the strike zone for all three of those at-bats, and this is the version of him the Mariners need moving forward as they try to keep in step in the race for the AL West crown. articles.title: SEC releases statement on professional athletes returning to NCAA football
articles.summary: The Southeastern Conference has drawn a firm line in the sand. Following a Monday evening videoconference of the league’s presidents and chancellors, the SEC issued a pointed statement opposing the idea of former professional athletes returning to compete in college sports. The message left
articles._body: The Southeastern Conference has drawn a firm line in the sand. Following a Monday evening videoconference of the league’s presidents and chancellors, the SEC issued a pointed statement opposing the idea of former professional athletes returning to compete in college sports . The message left little room for interpretation. “Individuals who choose to leave college athletics, sign professional playing contracts, and compete professionally should not then be permitted to return to college competition,” the statement read. The conference’s leadership argued that permitting such returns would blur the line between college and professional sports, create competitive equity concerns, and reduce opportunities for high school and current college athletes. The SEC closed with a rallying cry and a legislative nod, declaring that college sports are for college athletes and pointing to the confusion around national eligibility standards as a reason to advance the proposed Protect College Sports Act. The statement didn’t emerge in a vacuum. It comes on the heels of a wave of court rulings that have upended eligibility norms, including a Louisiana judge’s temporary restraining order that allows double-digit football players to return to the sport in 2026, even barring the NCAA from enforcing rules that block players who signed pro contracts from coming back. That ruling has created some jarring scenarios . Players currently on NFL rosters, such as Tampa Bay Buccaneers edge rusher Jack Pyburn and Cleveland Browns tight end Dae’Quan Wright , both part of the lawsuit, are now eligible to return to college football. Wright has already made his move, transferring from the Browns to LSU, an SEC program. The league’s most prominent voice has been sounding this alarm for a while. Commissioner Greg Sankey filed an affidavit in an eligibility case, warning that permitting former professional athletes to return creates “a competitive disadvantage and fundamental unfairness” for current student-athletes who stayed committed to the collegiate model. With Week 0 kicking off the 2026 season in a matter of days, the SEC’s statement signals that the sport’s most powerful conference intends to fight the trend, even as the courts continue to reshape who is eligible to take the field.
