Haliburton has gone through rehab over the past year, having torn his Achilles in Game 7 of the 2025 NBA Finals against the O
articles._body: Tyrese Haliburton is nearing the finish line of his Achilles rehab as the Indiana Pacers star guard expressed an exciting message for fans ahead of the 2026-27 NBA season. Haliburton has gone through rehab over the past year, having torn his Achilles in Game 7 of the 2025 NBA Finals against the Oklahoma City Thunder. The injury ended up sidelining him for the entire 2025-26 campaign, giving him a full year of recovery. Haliburton has been making his rounds around the country, hosting events that allowed him to interact with fans. His latest activity was a softball charity event that had him collaborate with Indianapolis Colts star quarterback Daniel Jones in Indiana. Team Haliburton ended up coasting to a 28-6 win over Team Jones, giving fans plenty of entertaining moments. The biggest one was from Haliburton himself, making a declaration about his return to the court. “0 will be back this season, baby!!!” Haliburton said, per reporter Scott Agness. “0 will be back this season, baby!!!” pic.twitter.com/Ak13Civdtg — Scott Agness (@ScottAgness) August 25, 2026 What lies ahead for Tyrese Haliburton, Pacers this season Tyrese Haliburton nearly led the Pacers to the championship in 2025. Barring any setbacks, he looks to pick up where he left off and finally lead the franchise to the mountaintop or at least lead them to more deep playoff runs. The 2024-25 season was solid for Haliburton, earning All-NBA third team honors. He averaged 18.6 points, 9.2 assists, 3.5 rebounds, and 1.4 steals per game throughout 73 appearances in the regular season. In the playoffs, he produced 17.3 points, 8.6 assists, 5.3 rebounds, and 1.3 steals per contest. Indiana sorely missed Haliburton’s presence on the hardwood last season. They finished with the second-worst record in the Eastern Conference standings, ending the season at 19-63. They were above the Washington Wizards while being under the Brooklyn Nets and the Chicago Bulls. The Pacers’ regular season will get underway on the road against the Pelicans. That matchup commences on Oct. 21 as tip-off takes place at 8 p.m. ET. The post Pacers’ Tyrese Haliburton hypes up crowd at charity game with huge message on return appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles.title: Phillies’ Zack Wheeler gets shelled by Mariners in 1 of his worst starts ever
articles.summary: Zack Wheeler has been one of the most consistent starting pitchers in MLB throughout his whole career, and even now that he’s 36 years of age, he continues to be good ol’ reliable for the Philadelphia Phillies. However, even pitchers of his caliber have off nights — even when fa
articles._body: Zack Wheeler has been one of the most consistent starting pitchers in MLB throughout his whole career, and even now that he’s 36 years of age , he continues to be good ol’ reliable for the Philadelphia Phillies. However, even pitchers of his caliber have off nights — even when facing the most inept offense in MLB in the Seattle Mariners. The Mariners entered their Monday night clash against the Phillies tied with the Toronto Blue Jays for the fewest runs scored in MLB in 2026, with 521 in 132 games. Wheeler entered the night with a 2.92 ERA, and on paper, this was looking like a game in favor of the Phillies. Alas, the 36-year-old proceeded to allow eight earned runs on nine hits in just four innings of work, and they currently find themselves down 9-2 through seven innings. Zack Wheeler is getting hit around tonight. He has given up 8 runs, 9 hits, and has 5 walks. His ERA is now 3.40 His night is done after 4 innings ￼ pic.twitter.com/6tjHlLlE2o — John Clark (@JClarkNBCS) August 25, 2026 Wheeler’s ERA ballooned to 3.40 ERA with this horrible start, and this was just a terrible outing for the Phillies veteran all around. He even allowed more walks (five) than he had strikeouts (four), and that is not a stat any starting pitcher would want to have on any given night. Eight earned runs is tied for the most Wheeler has allowed in a single game in his big-league career. He allowed eight earned runs three different times previously in his career, most recently in 2024, when he allowed the Baltimore Orioles to score eight through 4.1 innings of work. This outing blows away Wheeler’s previous worst start of 2026. The most earned runs he’s allowed in a single game this year is five, which he did on July 27 in an 8-7 loss to the Miami Marlins. But of Wheeler’s 22 starts this year, he’s only allowed over three earned runs seven times, so this is nothing more than an outlier for the Phillies veteran . Even if the Phillies don’t mount a comeback on Monday against the Mariners, they should still end the night in an NL Wild Card spot. articles._body: Natasha Howard kept the big picture in full view despite Olivia Miles and the Minnesota Lynx’s 80-66 loss to the Golden State Valkyries on Monday night. Going into the matchup, Minnesota has been dominating opponents as one of the best teams in the entire league. Miles has played a pivotal role in their success, a firm favorite for the Rookie of the Year award. However, Golden State decided to crash the party on Minnesota’s momentum. The visitors’ defense was stout as the hosts were unable to spark a run, going through a poor shooting night. Miles had a rough performance in 28 minutes of action. She finished with eight points, five assists and four rebounds on 3-of-12 shooting from the field, including 1-of-5 from beyond the arc. Despite her struggles, Howard came to the rookie’s defense after the game. “Yeah I agree with Cheryl, absolutely because you don’t want to have these kind of losses come playoffs. Because you get one of these losses and the series is tied 2-2… right now it’s good for all of us, it’s a learning lesson for the whole group as well, is not only on Liv, it’s the whole team,” Howard said, per reporter Andrew Dukowitz. Natasha Howard on Cheryl Reeve’s insight that the loss to the Valkyries being a good thing for Olivia Miles and the Lynx. “Yeah I agree with Cheryl, absolutely because you don’t want to have these kind of losses come playoffs. Because you get one of these losses and the series… pic.twitter.com/vDTBKjmIZG — Andrew Dukowitz (@adukeMN) August 25, 2026 How Natasha Howard, Lynx played against Valkyries Natasha Howard, Olivia Miles and the Lynx won’t let their loss to the Valkyries stunt their growth as an elite squad. Two players scored in double-digits for Minnesota in the loss, including Howard. She finished with a stat line of 13 points, seven rebounds, one assist, one steal, and one block. Kayla McBride came next with 12 points and four rebounds, while Napheesa Collier and Maya Caldwell provided nine points each. Minnesota fell to a 31-8 record on the season but continue controlling the top spot in the Western Conference standings. They are above the Valkyries and the Las Vegas Aces at the moment. The Lynx will look to bounce back in their next matchup, being on the road. They take on the Atlanta Dream as tip-off takes place on Aug. 30 at 3 p.m. ET. articles.title: Australia’s Laneway Festival Confirms 2027 Dates
articles.summary: It follows confirmation earlier this month that Adelaide and Perth would miss out on the festival in 2027.
articles._body: Australia’s Laneway Festival has confirmed the dates for its scaled-back 2027 edition, with Sydney set to open the touring festival for the first time in its history. The four-date run begins at Sydney’s Centennial Park on Friday, Feb. 12, followed by Brisbane Showgrounds on Saturday, Feb. 13. The following weekend, the festival returns to its longtime Melbourne home at Flemington Park on Friday, Feb. 19, before wrapping across the Tasman at Auckland’s Western Springs on Sunday, Feb. 21. The route follows confirmation earlier this month that Adelaide and Perth would miss out on Laneway in 2027 as organizers reduce the festival’s footprint. At the time, the festival said the demands of staging multiple events across Australia and New Zealand within a short window had contributed to the decision. “Running so many shows, so close together, across so much ground is a logistical feat we’re proud of, but it also asks a lot of our lineup and crew,” organizers said, adding that a pause would allow them “to focus on making the festival the best it can be.” They stressed the omissions were not necessarily permanent. The 2027 route also marks Laneway’s return to the Brisbane Showgrounds after the Queensland leg moved to Southport Sharks on the Gold Coast for the 2026 edition. The lineup remains under wraps, with the first artist announcement expected in late September. The dates arrive during a period of transition for the festival, which last week saw festival director Jessie Parker announce her departure after 16 years. Laneway marked its 21st anniversary in 2026 with a lineup led by Chappell Roan, alongside Wolf Alice, Role Model, Wet Leg, PinkPantheress and Geese. LANEWAY FESTIVAL 2027 Feb. 12 — Sydney — Centennial Park Feb. 13 — Brisbane — Brisbane Showgrounds Feb. 19 — Melbourne — Flemington Park Feb. 21 — Auckland — Western Springs

articles.title: Rangers’ Joc Pederson gets tossed from White Sox game after heated exchange
articles.summary: The Texas Rangers may have taken an 11-2 victory over the Chicago White Sox on Monday to move to first place in the AL West standings with a 66-66 record, but that win of theirs did not come without its fair share of drama. In the top of the second inning, Joc Pederson found himself […]
articles._body: The Texas Rangers may have taken an 11-2 victory over the Chicago White Sox on Monday to move to first place in the AL West standings with a 66-66 record, but that win of theirs did not come without its fair share of drama. In the top of the second inning, Joc Pederson found himself in the center of a controversial strike three call for the second out of the inning. The Rangers were already leading 2-0 at the time of Pederson’s strikeout, so it’s not like Texas lost a lot of ground with that turn of events. Nonetheless, Pederson felt that the 1-2 pitch from Jose Urquidy was low, and the home plate umpire made the wrong call. He then tapped his helmet, signaling the use of an ABS Challenge. Home plate umpire Chris Guccione, however, did not grant Pederson the challenge. This infuriated Pederson, who continued chirping at the umpire all the way from the dugout. Fed up, Guccione tossed Pederson from the game as a result. Joc Pederson was not happy with the home plate umpire after he was not granted an ABS challenge as the umpire thought he challenged too late. Pederson checked the replay and started saying from the dugout that the pitch was low. He continued to argue and the umpire ejected him… pic.twitter.com/QmIyljxzbe — js9innings (@js9inningsmedia) August 25, 2026 Umpires are strict regarding the timing of ABS challenges, and Pederson seemed to hesitate for a split second. It is clear in the rules that the manager or coaches cannot request a challenge or assist players in requesting one. The Rangers may have given Pederson the green light to tap his helmet in the end, which led to Guccione’s decision not to grant the challenge. This was Pederson’s second plate appearance of the night. He drew a walk and later on scored in the first inning, and his strikeout in the second inning marked an early end to his outing. His ejection did not prove to be an issue for the Rangers in the end. They scored 11 runs on 14 hits and rose to the occasion to start a three-game series against a fellow division leader in the White Sox. articles.title: ARIA Sets AI Eligibility Rules for Its Charts, Barring Wholly AI-Generated Tracks
articles.summary: To qualify, a recording must be "substantially human-made" and raise "no stream or chart manipulation concerns."
articles._body: The Australian Recording Industry Association has become the first national chart body to implement eligibility rules for recordings made with generative AI, confirming that wholly AI-generated tracks will be barred from the ARIA Charts . Recordings that use AI in a supporting role remain eligible; tracks generated wholesale by AI do not. The changes take effect from the chart dated Monday, Aug. 31. To qualify, a recording must be “substantially human-made” and raise “no stream or chart manipulation concerns,” with ARIA applying the global music industry’s AI labelling standard, announced July 10, to tell AI-generated recordings from AI-assisted ones. The move implements the global principles set by the IFPI and the major labels earlier this year — ARIA being the first national chart body to adopt them with a firm date. “Artists already use AI tools in their work, the charts can and should evolve to keep room for that, but music generated wholesale by services built on artists’ recordings is a different matter,” ARIA CEO Annabelle Herd said. She added that “a chart that rewards unlicensed AI output would undercut the very basis of the recorded music we exist to represent,” and urged other decision-makers, “particularly radio,” to adopt similar codes. The rules carry teeth. ARIA can decline to survey an ineligible recording, remove it from the charts, adjust positions, withdraw accreditations, and revoke any ARIA No. 1 Award; ineligible tracks are also barred from the ARIA Awards. Artists can contest exclusions through an updated disputes process. The policy arrives as AI-generated music has begun testing the boundaries of chart systems worldwide. The AI country act Breaking Rust reached No. 1 on Billboard’s Country Digital Song Sales chart in 2025, and in April 2026 the AI act IngaRose topped iTunes charts in the U.S. and globally — cases that focused industry attention on the absence of any chart rules governing AI. Neither involved detected streaming fraud; both drew on real purchases or organic interest on narrower charts. ARIA said it will keep the code under review as AI policy and technology continue to develop.

articles.summary: There was a time when it was impossible to imagine Klay Thompson playing for any team other than the Golden State Warriors. Now, he is on his third squad after signing with the Miami Heat following his buyout from the Dallas Mavericks. After an empty two-year stint with the Mavericks, Thompson ma
articles._body: There was a time when it was impossible to imagine Klay Thompson playing for any team other than the Golden State Warriors. Now, he is on his third squad after signing with the Miami Heat following his buyout from the Dallas Mavericks. After an empty two-year stint with the Mavericks, Thompson made it known that he wanted to join a championship contender and chase a fifth ring. The Heat became an ideal destination, especially with the addition of Giannis Antetokounmpo. The 36-year-old Thompson gave up almost $10 million in his buyout with Dallas to sign a two-year, $13 million contract with Miami. On Monday, he was all smiles as he arrived in South Beach to begin the new chapter in his illustrious career. “My joints just feel good being out here with this climate,” said Thompson. “I can’t wait to meet the staff, my co-workers, the executives, try new cuisines, get some really good local food, and get to work. I was always here in passing, so it’s nice to be planted, just being able to experience a great place.” Drop a if you’re excited for him to meet his coworkers…Welcome to Miami, @KlayThompson ! pic.twitter.com/tDRVJJJ4bR — Miami HEAT (@MiamiHEAT) August 25, 2026 While leg injuries have slowed down the four-time champion, he is still a valuable weapon. He can still drop eight three-pointers on any given night. Plus, coach Erik Spoelstra has a knack for effectively utilizing outside shooters—Ray Allen, Duncan Robinson, and Max Strus easily come to mind—so Thompson should not have any trouble adjusting to the system. Being the fierce competitor that he is, Thompson is probably eager to bounce back after his dud last season, averaging career-lows of 11.7 points, 39.3% shooting, 2.1 rebounds, 1.4 assists, and 21.7 minutes off the bench. He has a chance to start on the Heat, along with Davion Mitchell, Andrew Wiggins, Giannis Antetokounmpo, and Bam Adebayo. articles.title: 49ers rookie receiver gets a ‘pro’ endorsement from Mike Evans
articles.summary: The San Francisco 49ers are getting an early look at how quickly rookie wide receiver De’Zhaun Stribling can contribute to a reshaped offense. Through two NFL preseason games, Stribling has caught 11 of 13 targets for 109 yards while pushing for a meaningful role in a receiver room led by veteran
articles._body: The San Francisco 49ers are getting an early look at how quickly rookie wide receiver De’Zhaun Stribling can contribute to a reshaped offense. Through two NFL preseason games, Stribling has caught 11 of 13 targets for 109 yards while pushing for a meaningful role in a receiver room led by veteran Mike Evans. Stribling, the No. 33 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, returned to practice Sunday in a noncontact jersey after sustaining a shoulder injury during Thursday’s win over the Los Angeles Chargers. His availability bears watching as San Francisco prepares for Thursday’s preseason finale at Las Vegas. Coach Yac, a popular 49ers account, posted a clip on X, formerly Twitter, Monday night that paired Evans’ assessment with footage of Stribling’s preseason work. “Strib gets the job done. He’s a rookie, but he’s a pro. He’s been a pro. The way he practices, the way he prepares, he’s gonna make a lot of plays for us this year.” “Strib gets the job done. He’s a rookie, but he’s a pro. He’s been a pro. The way he practices, the way he prepares, he’s gonna make a lot of plays for us this year.” — Mike Evans on De'Zhaun Stribling pic.twitter.com/58eFFzPgVM — Coach Yac (@Coach_Yac) August 25, 2026 Evans’ praise arrives as the 49ers search for dependable receiving options behind him. Ricky Pearsall is on injured reserve for the season after undergoing surgery on his PCL, while Christian Kirk has missed training camp time with a calf injury. The endorsement also carries weight because of Evans’ resume. He earned six Pro Bowl selections during 12 seasons with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and tied an NFL record by opening his career with 11 consecutive 1,000-yard receiving seasons before joining the 49ers in the offseason. San Francisco selected the 23-year-old receiver after his final college season at Ole Miss. His production during the 2026 NFL preseason has strengthened his case for immediate opportunities in Kyle Shanahan’s offense once the regular season begins. His return to limited practice is an encouraging sign, but the shoulder issue could still affect his status for Thursday’s third and final preseason game vs. the Las Vegas Raiders. The 49ers open the regular season against the Los Angeles Rams in Melbourne, Australia, on September 10. articles.title: Sparks’ Cameron Brink rejects Angel Reese twice, but did she foul?
articles.summary: Los Angeles Sparks forward Cameron Brink led the defensive charge against the Atlanta Dream on Monday and in a first-quarter sequence defending Angel Reese, a major call for a foul was raised among social media critics. In a recently shared video on X, formerly Twitter, Brink looked dedicated to
articles._body: Los Angeles Sparks forward Cameron Brink led the defensive charge against the Atlanta Dream on Monday and in a first-quarter sequence defending Angel Reese, a major call for a foul was raised among social media critics. In a recently shared video on X, formerly Twitter, Brink looked dedicated to blocking Reese in the paint while the Dream forward delivered elbow-to-rib blows. However, despite multiple attempts to go past the defensive play, Reese’s attempt ultimately ended in frustration. Soon after the video surfaced online , fans were divided on the definition of a foul. Cameron Brink rejects Angel Reese twice in a row, but Reese wanted a foul call following that play pic.twitter.com/agRLaHig6T — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) August 25, 2026 According to the WNBA’s Rule 12B, Section IV-a , “If contact committed against a player, with or without the ball, is interpreted to be unnecessary, a flagrant foul-penalty 1 will be assessed. A personal foul is charged to the offender, and a team foul is charged to the team.” However, looking closely at the sequence, the continuous attempt from Brink to block Reese looks like it should have been a foul, but it wasn’t. Even going by the rule, contact on the hand of the offensive player while that hand is in contact with the ball is generally legal. Amid the outcry, Reese has been continuously criticized for her shooting struggles near the basket. While her career field goal percentage remains 42.9%, she has shown impressive improvement during the 2026 WNBA season, averaging 44.1% from the field, per Basketball Reference. Recently, Reese had a career night against the Phoenix Mercury , scoring 31 points during the Dream’s 99-89 victory on Saturday. She also had her 26th double-double for the season. After the Washington Commanders star took action against his alma mater LSU over their use of his #5 jersey, Daniels has been clowned endlessly on social media. The current running joke around Daniels is mockingly not using the number five as a form of “respect” for the star. It’s interesting, then, that the College Football Playoff page on X seemingly made a reference to this meme… without overtly talking about Daniels. The CFP’s post asking their followers who the greatest player to wear #5 seems innocuous at first glance . Given the current meme landscape on social media, though, one might wonder if the page was hinting at the Commanders star’s current debacle. Daniels is currently being clowned on social media after his family threatened legal action against LSU. This issue stems from Lane Kiffin and the team’s decision to give the #5 jersey to sophomore cornerback DJ Pickett. According to the Daniels family, they were promised that the Commanders quarterback’s jersey will never be used after his Heisman-winning season. LSU has only one jersey number retired, Billy Cannon’s #20 jersey. Cannon is the first Tiger to win the Heisman. Because of this fiasco, the Commanders quarterback is now catchig a ton of heat from fans, who find this current sitaution to be ridiculous. Many are making jokes about the family by saying that they’re not using the number five as “respect” for Daniels. This has been an abject PR disaster for the Daniels family heading into the 2026 season. Daniels and the Commanders are looking to bounce back after a disappointing 2025 campaign. Coming off the heels of an NFC Championship game appearance in Daniels’ rookie year, the team completely missed the playoffs. One of the biggest factors in their 2025 campaign is their quarterback’s injuries: Daniels missed a significant chunk of the season after sustaining injuries throughout the year. articles.summary: The Boston Red Sox rained on star pitcher Sandy Alcantara’s parade during their matchup against the Miami Marlins on Monday night. Boston has emerged as one of the best performing squads throughout the second half of the 2026 season following a poor start. They look to be firm in the playof
articles._body: The Boston Red Sox rained on star pitcher Sandy Alcantara’s parade during their matchup against the Miami Marlins on Monday night. Boston has emerged as one of the best performing squads throughout the second half of the 2026 season following a poor start. They look to be firm in the playoff picture as the campaign winds down to the final months. Sweeping the San Francisco Giants this past weekend, Boston wanted to keep the momentum going against Miami. Alcantara did his best efforts to put a stop to their win streak, limiting them to one run during his seven innings on the mound. This ended up allowing him to take over first place in a certain statistic , per ESPN Insights. “Sandy Alcántara had his 8th start of at least 7 innings pitched allowing 1 run or fewer on Monday night, breaking a tie with 3 others for most such starts in MLB this season ,” the post read. How Red Sox played against Sandy Alcantara, Marlins The Red Sox had a tough time dealing with Sandy Alcantara on the mound. As soon as he checked out of the game, Boston went on to take down the Marlins 4-2 on the road. Miami had a 2-1 lead after Alcantara ended his service on the mound. The last two innings saw Boston strike back with the last three runs of the game. They tied the game with a pitching error in the eighth inning, then Anthony Seigler and Nick Sogard dealt the final blows in the final frame. Boston improved to a 72-59 record on the season, sitting at third place in the AL East Division standings. They are above the Toronto Blue Jays and the Baltimore Orioles while trailing the New York Yankees and the Tampa Bay Rays. Rolling with four consecutive wins, the Red Sox will look forward to Game 2 of their series against the Marlins. The upcoming matchup will happen on Aug. 25 at 6:40 p.m. ET. articles._body: Minnesota Lynx guard Olivia Miles reached another milestone in the first quarter against the Golden State Valkyries at Target Center on Monday. But that was the only positive note in her performance, as they lost to the Valkyries, 80-66. The Lynx saw their six-game winning streak get snapped, falling to 31-8, including 14-6 at home. Golden State, meanwhile, stopped a two-game losing skid and improved to 26-11, including 11-6 on the road. Miles had a forgettable showing. She was limited to eight points, the second-lowest in her rookie campaign, on 3-of-12 shooting from the field, including 1-of-5 from long range. She had four rebounds, five assists, and four turnovers in 28 minutes. In the postgame conference, Lynx coach Cheryl Reeve did not mince her words on Miles’ struggles against the Valkyries, although she remained even-keeled about the 23-year-old guard. “I want games like this for Liv as a rookie. We need games like this so that there’s learning that happens. There’s disappointment, maybe, that she’s feeling for sure. She needs that, and we need that. That’s the kind of stuff that makes us a better team,” said Reeve in the video posted by Lynx reporter Andrew Dukowitz. Cheryl Reeve on Olivia Miles ball movement struggles against the Valkyries “I want games like this for Liv as a rookie. We need games like this so that there’s learning that happens. Theres disappointment maybe, that she’s feeling for sure. She needs that, and we need that.… pic.twitter.com/e6YiByQp9l — Andrew Dukowitz (@adukeMN) August 25, 2026 Miles had been on an impressive stretch entering the game against Golden State, putting up 21.0 points, 3.6 rebounds, 8.1 assists, and 1.3 steals during their six-game winning streak. The Valkyries, however, pounced on her on defense, playing her physically and giving her different looks. They pried the ball away from her as quickly as possible, eliminating her every chance to make an impact. But it could be a blessing in disguise for the Lynx, who played without Courtney Williams , as it served as a preview of the level of challenge she will likely face in the playoffs. It could be a good thing that Miles experienced it early, allowing her to iron out the kinks in her game. articles.title: 2nd year Eagles defender earns props from likely fellow starter
articles.summary: After watching his rookie season end in tragedy when he was placed on IR with an ankle fracture in Week 12, Andrew Mukuba is back on the field for training camp with the Philadelphia Eagles, and he’s already turning heads among his fellow defensive backs. Discussing what he’s seen fro
articles._body: After watching his rookie season end in tragedy when he was placed on IR with an ankle fracture in Week 12 , Andrew Mukuba is back on the field for training camp with the Philadelphia Eagles, and he’s already turning heads among his fellow defensive backs. Discussing what he’s seen from Mukuba over their time together in Vic Fangio’s defense, Marcus Epps had nothing but nice things to say about the second-year pro out of Texas, noting that he’s maturing nicely along his NFL journey. “He’s made a lot of great steps, man. It’s been really good to see his progression over the past year, and especially this offseason. I think he’s doing a really good job of just honing in on the small details,” Epps said. “He’s a lot more urgent, so that’s a really good thing to see from a young guy. He’s trying to continue to learn and continue to grow his game, and you can tell things have slowed down a lot for him. So that’s been really good to see.” Marcus Epps said he’s noticed a big step from Drew Mukuba this summer, particularly when it comes to picking up on small details and finding a routine. #Eagles pic.twitter.com/yrdPyyVsZn — PHLY Eagles (@PHLY_Eagles) August 24, 2026 While it will be nice to see Mukuba take the field once more after putting some quality play on tape as a rookie, the man who will likely be starting next to him, Epps, has had his own journey back to the starting lineup after it looked like his career was almost over. Asked what it’s been like to have his spot on the 53-man roster more or less locked up after an ACL tear ended his run with the Las Vegas Raiders in 2024, Epps noted he’s enjoying his own journey as there have been some “ dark days ” along the way. “I mean, it’ll mean everything to me. I worked real hard to get back to where I’m at, man. There was a lot of dark days, but I still got work to do,” Epps noted. “I haven’t arrived by any means. It’s a long season, and we’re still here just in camp. So that’s where my focus is on camp, finishing out camp the right way, and just continuing to get better.” Initially joining the Eagles for the second time in late August of 2025 as a member of the practice squad, Epps benefited the most from Mukuba’s injury, starting four games down the stretch plus Philadelphia’s lone playoff game next to Reed Blankenship. With Blankenship gone, Mukuba and Epps are now likely going to start together to begin the 2026 NFL season as Fangio’s free and strong safety, with fellow 2025 addition Michael Carter II mixing in as a do-it-all defensive back both at safety and in the slot situationally. Eagles safety Marcus Epps was asked what it would mean to him to be a starter again after the journey he went through. pic.twitter.com/hP1I4K46FY — Dave Uram (@MrUram) August 24, 2026 The post 2nd year Eagles defender earns props from likely fellow starter appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles.title: Vikings’ 53-man roster prediction for 2026 NFL season
articles.summary: The Minnesota Vikings came to the conclusion last season that they did not have good enough play from the quarterback position. That’s why they lost 8 of their first 12 games and it was the primary reason they were out of playoff contention before Thanksgiving. The Vikings were not fooled i
articles._body: The Minnesota Vikings came to the conclusion last season that they did not have good enough play from the quarterback position. That’s why they lost 8 of their first 12 games and it was the primary reason they were out of playoff contention before Thanksgiving. The Vikings were not fooled into thinking their 5-game winning streak at the end of the season was significant. They knew they had to bring in an experienced quarterback in order to give the team a chance to win. They did that by acquiring Kyler Murray from the Arizona Cardinals and he is now the starting quarterback over former hot prospect J.J. McCarthy. If the Vikings are going to be a winning team and contend for the NFC North title, Murray will have to come through on a consistent basis, but there is much more to the team than just the play by the QB1. The Vikings will open the season Sept. 13 by hosting the archrival Green Bay Packers. They have one more preseason game before head coach Kevin O’Connell and his coaches have to finalize the roster. Here’s our projection as to what that 53-man roster will look like at 6 p.m. ET Sunday. Quarterbacks (3) Kyler Murray, Carson Wentz, J.J. McCarthy After O’Connell named Murray as the starting quarterback, the battle for the No. 2 quarterback was at hand between Wentz and McCarthy. The belief here is that Wentz will be the backup and McCarthy will be a very disappointing No. 3 quarterback. Max Brosmer will have a spot on the practice squad, but once other teams finalize their rosters, the Vikings could get a call to trade McCarthy because he could be a solid backup elsewhere. If that happens, that will remove some of the tension in the Vikings locker room and give Brosmer an opportunity as the No. 3 quarterback. Running Backs (5) Aaron Jones, Jordan Mason, Demond Claiborne, Zavier Scott, Max Bredeson (FB) Jones and Mason should give the Vikings an excellent 1-2 punch at the RB spot and they may come very close splitting the RB responsibilities on a 50-50 basis . Claiborne has explosive 4.37 speed and Scott’s time in Minnesota could be coming to a close even though he is fairly versatile. Bredeson will serve as an extra blocker in the backfield, but he will surprise opponents with an occasional carry. Wide Receivers (5) Mandatory Credit: Robert Deutsch-Imagn Images Justin Jefferson, Jordan Addison, Jauan Jennings, Myles Price, Tai Felton Jefferson is motivated to regain his status as the best receiver in the NFL, and he should have a chance to do that with Murray under center. Addison is an explosive No. 2 receiver, while Jennings looks like a perfect fit at the No. 3 receiver. Price may prove to be capable of providing game-changing plays late in the fourth quarter. Tight Ends (3) T.J. Hockenson, Josh Oliver, Gavin Bartholomew The Vikings are hoping for a big season from Hockenson, but that will require him staying off the Injured List. Oliver is a blocker who can make some surprising catches. Bartholemew (neck) was injured last year but he has looked good in camp. Offensive Line (10) Christian Darrisaw, Donovan Jackson, Blake Brandel, Will Fries, Brian O’Neill, Ryan Van Demark, Michael Jurgens, Joe Huber, Caleb Tiernan, Walter Rouse This may be the most critical area for the Vikings. The offensive line has regularly looked imposing at this point in the year, but weaknesses have always cropped up. Darrisaw and O’Neill are potential All-Pros at the OT spots if they can stay healthy. The big issue is interior blocking, and Jackson, Brandel and Fries have to come through. Depth appears to be better than it has been in the past, with Van Denmark looking solid at tackle while Huber can get the job done at guard. Defensive line (6) Jalen Redmond, Levi Drake Rodriguez, Caleb Banks, Domonique Orange, Tyrion Ingram-Dawkins, Elijah Williams This is a position that could be vulnerable for the Vikings since they are going with multiple inexperienced players. Defensive coordinator Brian Flores is counting on Redmond being the leader, but he also needs rookies Banks and Orange to make serious contributions Linebackers (7) Mandatory Credit: Robert Deutsch-Imagn Images Andrew Van Ginkel, Dallas Turner, Eric Wilson, Blake Cashman, Jake Golday, Bo Richter, Tyler Batty This is the position that must come through for the Vikings with big plays throughout the season. Van Ginkel excels at setting up opposing quarterbacks for interceptions and bringing them back a long way. Turner has an excellent chance to record double-digit sacks. Cashman is probably the surest tackler on the team. Ivan Pace Jr. has been a solid contributtor in the past, but he is likely to find himself on the outside looking in. Cornerbacks (5) Byron Murphy Jr., Isaiah Rodgers, James Pierre, Charles Demmings, Dwight McGlothern Jr. This has been a position that has been a problem area for the Vikings for multiple seasons. Murphy has a chance to become an All-Pro, while Rodgers is a dynamic cover man who can make big plays for Flores’ defense. However, consistency has been an issue. The Vikings may not have the depth that will allow them to shut down high-level receivers for 60 minutes. Safeties (6) Joshua Metellus, Jay Ward, Theo Jackson, Jakobe Thomas, Tavierre Thomas, Jacob Thomas Metellus has been an ideal player in Flores’ defense for multiple seasons, and his role will increase this year since the Vikings no longer have Harrison Smith in the secondary. The injury suffered by Jamal Adams means the Vikings will depend on rookies Jakobe Thomas and Jacob Thomas — with their near-identical names — to provide depth in this crucial area. Special teams (3) Will Reichard (K), Brett Thorson (P), Andrew DePaola (LS) Reichard is an All-Pro and may be the best placekicker in the league. Thorson had a tough assignment this summer as he battled veteran Johnny Hekker, but he comes away with the Vikings punting job.     The post Vikings’ 53-man roster prediction for 2

articles._body: The Pittsburgh Steelers stretched their Joey Porter Jr. contract standoff to the final full week of August 2026. Even All-Pro cornerback teammate Jalen Ramsey shared an opinion on it . But so has the father of Asante Samuel Jr. The elder Samuel dropped a blunt take on Porter’s situation. But he doesn’t take the cornerback’s side here. “I don’t think he’s handling the situation the best way. [Especially] by not going to practice,” Samuel said on his “Say What Needs to be Said” podcast Monday. “You’ve gotta know when to read the room and who you’re dealing with.” He added more context into what Porter is also doing. Which involves dealing with a fiery fanbase but also the organization. “These people seem like they really get offended over there in Pittsburgh. They really are in tune to what’s going on and their players and who their players are and paying their players,” Samuel said. “They do things a certain way, they don’t just like to break bread.” Head coach Mike McCarthy originally placed Porter on the PUP (Physically Unable to Perform) list during NFL Training Camp. However, speculation grew that Porter is really sitting out amid his contract debate. The summer already saw Seattle Seahawks star cornerback Devon Witherspoon reset the market. Witherspoon signed a $132 million extension for four years during August camp. So now the focus shifts over to how the Steelers handle Porter from here. However, Christian Gonzalez of the New England Patriots is one more CB who can change the market there too, as he’s up for his own new extension. articles.title: DeSean Jackson, Delaware State name new QB1 to start season
articles.summary: Ahead of the start of Delaware State’s football season on Thursday, DeSean Jackson has named Ui Ale QB 1. His decision ends a high-stakes quarterback battle featuring Coastal Carolina QB Samari Collier, returning QB Jayden Sauray, and former Delaware State quarterback Marqui Adams, who retu
articles._body: Ahead of the start of Delaware State’s football season on Thursday, DeSean Jackson has named Ui Ale QB 1. His decision ends a high-stakes quarterback battle featuring Coastal Carolina QB Samari Collier , returning QB Jayden Sauray, and former Delaware State quarterback Marqui Adams, who returned to the team after entering the transfer portal in 2025. Jackson announced the decision on Monday during the MEAC Coaches Call. “Ui has emerged as the starter right now,” Jackson said. “Over the past week and a half or two weeks, he’s emerged as the No. 1 starter…We feel very confident that he can come in and win us a game,” Jackson said. “Those guys have been taking command and taking the load off our offensive line.” Ale spent last season as Troy’s third-string quarterback, seeing limited action with a lone appearance at Buffalo, where he completed 5-of-10 passes for 54 yards and added three rushing yards on six carries. Before landing at Troy, he spent two seasons at Houston, where he saw the field in five total games across 2023 and 2024. His most productive stretch came during his redshirt sophomore year in 2024, when he completed 10-of-13 passes for 112 yards and a touchdown without throwing an interception, highlighted by a career-high seven completions for 74 yards and a score against UNLV. His path to Houston began at Golden West College, where he threw for 1,335 yards and 12 touchdowns as a freshman in 2023, connecting on 111-of-204 attempts. He turned in one of his best outings that season against Southwestern, throwing for 297 yards and three touchdowns, and found the end zone in seven of his final eight games. Ale honed his game at Carson High School, playing three seasons under his father, Arnold, including a sophomore campaign in which he threw for 1,331 yards and 12 touchdowns while also contributing 103 rushing yards. Now he prepares to lead the Hornets against Stony Brook and jump-start the second campaign for Jackson after a successful and historic 8-4 season. They were one game away from winning the MEAC championship and clinching a bid to the Cricket Celebration Bowl. articles.title: Hutchins making serious case for Patriots roster spot
articles.summary: With the biggest play of his football life on Friday night in the Patriots preseason game against the Eagles, Q Hutchins continues to make a real case to make the initial roster, or at least the practice squad.
articles._body: FOXBOROUGH – Moments before his game-sealing strip sack against the Eagles on Friday night, Quintayvious Hutchins wasn’t happy with himself. Hutchins had made a mistake on the kickoff team, but quickly made his loudest case yet for a roster or practice squad spot, sacking Cole Payton and stripping the ball, allowing Casey Rogers to fall on it and seal the win. With one week to go until roster cuts and one preseason game left on Thursday, the biggest moment of Hutchins’ football career came at the perfect time. “Yeah, definitely,” Hutchins said with a big smile in the locker room postgame. “It means a lot. It’s definitely the No. 1 play of my life would far. I was still stuck in my head from the previous kickoff return. I just had a simple thought of going and ending the game right there.” Hutchins had two tackles in the first preseason game and while he continues to look for more consistency on special teams, his speed off the outside the game-clinching play could open some eyes, especially with EDGE still lacking depth. “I feel like after the first preseason game, it was just like back in college,” Hutchins said speaking on how much more comfortable he’s gotten. “Get the call, line up and just execute the call.” Just how much he’s learned about being a pro in a short amount of time will be tested this week. Short weeks weren’t really a thing at BC unless there was the rare Friday night game. New England has practice Monday and Tuesday before flying to Cleveland Wednesday. Hutchins will most likely see quite a bit of time in the preseason finale on Thursday as he continues to fight for a role. “Recovery,” Hutchins quickly added when asked what he thinks the key to being ready for a quick turnaround will be. “Take care of your body. Take care of your mind. “It’s a shorter week, so the better you can prepare yourself mentally and physically, you’ll be ready for the week.” Hutchins followed that up with two ‘sacks’ in practice on Monday afternoon. With one more preseason game in Cleveland set for Thursday, a big performance could lock in the life long dream for Q.

articles._body: Even though the NFL and the NBA are still on break, the Indianapolis Colts and the Indiana Pacers have continued to make an impact in the community. On Monday, Colts quarterback Daniel Jones and Pacers guard Tyrese Haliburton starred in the return of the Charity Softball Classic at Victory Field. Haliburton had a big hand in pushing for the revival of the erstwhile annual event, with the help of the Pacers Foundation. It was held to help raise money and awareness to fight youth food insecurity in Indiana. Jones and Haliburton served as captains of the opposing teams. During the game, Colts owners Carlie-Irsay Gordon and Kalen Jackson vowed to donate $100,000 if Haliburton could reach base. Always the clutch performer, he delivered, as shown in the video posted by The Athletic’s James Boyd. #Colts owners Carlie-Irsay Gordon and Kalen Jackson just donated $100K since #Pacers star Tyrese Haliburton got on base. Super cool gesture. pic.twitter.com/d07UoAbwPG — James Boyd (@RomeovilleKid) August 25, 2026 It was also encouraging to see Haliburton moving well as he continues his recovery from his Achilles injury. He has formed a strong friendship with Jones , who also suffered an Achilles injury last season. They both underwent surgery at the Hospital for Special Surgery in New York. “We have the same surgeon, so we’ve talked a lot (throughout) the process. I was obviously ahead of him, so he has picked my brain a little bit, and I try to help as much as I can,” said Haliburton on “The Pat McAfee Show.” Their strong bond has led to the revival of the Charity Softball Classic, which was halted in 2018, and for sure, the Colts and the Pacers will continue to be a big part of the community. Earlier this month, the Colts, the Pacers, the Indiana Fever, and the Noblesville Bloom teamed up to donate $250,000 for flood relief in the state. articles._body: The Louisville Kickoff Luncheon is the final speaking engagement of the offseason for the Kentucky head coach. This year, the keynote speaker was a Louisville native, and he brought his new boss with him to his hometown. This is not a news-breaking event. It’s built to give the Kentucky head coach some face time with some of the more prominent fans in the state’s largest city. Approximately 650 tickets were sold for lunch at Churchill Downs’ First Turn. J Batt and Will Stein were comfortable on stage, engaging with many people who help financially support Kentucky football. J Batt Shows Fundraising Chops For some in the audience, this was their introduction to J Batt. You could see why he has developed a reputation as a fundraiser. The Champions Clue CEO opened by toasting Tom Leach to his 30th season as the Voice of the Wildcats. Then he turned his attention to the fans, praising BBN for their passion. “Coach Stein and I got a chance on an early Saturday morning, maybe two or three weeks ago, to drive around and visit tailgaters, a bunch of them who came from here, by the way, who were setting up and had tailgated to tailgate a month later,” said Batt. “ There’s nowhere else in college athletics that does that , and I think it’s just a small, small kind of indicator of just how much people care.” Batt only spoke for a little more than five minutes. As he praised BBN, he sprinkled in little hints here and there that did not go unnoticed. “We like to say that it’s the Kentucky athletics family. And what does family do for each other? They dig a little deeper, go a little further, give a little more, maybe,” said Batt. The Champions Blue CEO said that for the program to have success, it needs to be “well-capitalized.” He’s confident BBN can make that happen. “I’ve never been more certain, though, that we are well-positioned.” Levity from Will Stein Tom Leach posed questions to the Kentucky head coach for about 20 minutes. While you’ve heard him address many of the talking points about the team so far, he used the homecoming to highlight what’s made it so special for him. There have been many pinch-me moments. One of them was getting teamed up with Tim Couch at Jacob Tamme’s annual golf scramble. “He looks really good. I mean, that guy is jacked,” Stein said, drawing some laughter from the crowd. “That guy looks like a linebacker.” As you’re well aware by now, Stein spent his Saturdays as a child at Commonwealth Stadium. Tom Leach asked him what it feels like to be on the other side now. Before sharing that experience, Stein had to start with a different memory of his time in the stands. “I remember too, just being at Commonwealth and coming over the other sideline and just like cussing out the away players, and whatever hand signs I was giving them. I can remember that. If they threw up their wristbands, we’d just throw ’em right back. So I was that fan too.” That even got a laugh from Leach. The moments of levity reminded Kentucky fans that the new head coach is also one of them. That street goes two ways. The Kentucky football team can’t win without Big Blue Nation. “I think the people in this room are a part of our team. We are all on the same team. So, the louder you cheer, the longer you stay, the better opportunities we have to win,” Stein said. “Think about it like that. Don’t think about the scoreboard or the time left. Regardless, we are all-in together. We all have to go out there. We all have to perform, and so that’s what I’m asking these people in the room, and then your friends, your family, man, stand up, be loud. Somebody tells you to sit down. That you’re ruining their view. Tell them to stand up. Like, let’s get on our feet and make some noise.”

articles.title: Watch Jo Adell get a hero’s welcome in Angels’ return
articles.summary: Jo Adell received plenty of appreciation from Los Angeles Angels fans Monday night as the Cleveland Guardians outfielder returned to Angel Stadium for the first time since being traded. Adell acknowledged the applause by tipping his helmet before his first-inning plate appearance, marking his fir
articles._body: Jo Adell received plenty of appreciation from Los Angeles Angels fans Monday night as the Cleveland Guardians outfielder returned to Angel Stadium for the first time since being traded. Adell acknowledged the applause by tipping his helmet before his first-inning plate appearance, marking his first trip to the batter’s box in Anaheim as a visiting player. Foul Territory Network shared video of the reception on X, formerly Twitter, as Angels fans welcomed back their former outfielder. “Jo Adell received a warm welcome from Angels fans in his return to Angel Stadium. ” Jo Adell received a warm welcome from Angels fans in his return to Angel Stadium. pic.twitter.com/sd8cFSiHiY — Foul Territory (@FoulTerritoryTV) August 25, 2026 The reunion came three weeks after L.A. dealt Adell to the Guardians in exchange for minor-league catcher Jacob Cozart at the August 3 MLB trade deadline. The move ended the outfielder’s lengthy run with the only organization he had known since entering professional baseball. Los Angeles selected Adell with the No. 10 overall pick in the 2017 MLB Draft out of Ballard High School in Louisville, Kentucky. He rose through the system as one of baseball’s top prospects before developing into a regular power threat, culminating in a career-high 37 home runs during the 2025 season. The Guardians acquired the 27-year-old to add right-handed power while pursuing an American League wild-card berth. His return to Anaheim therefore arrived under considerably different circumstances, with Adell now trying to help the Guardians during the stretch of the 2026 MLB season. Adell struck out in his first plate appearance Monday, but the moment before the at-bat highlighted the connection he maintained with the Angels fan base following the trade. The reception also underscored the respect he built during his years in Anaheim before beginning a new chapter with Cleveland. articles.title: Sandro Mamukelashvili puts on a show in glimpse of what he can do for Lakers
articles.summary: Sandro Mamukelashvili is not wasting time getting back to action following a trip to Slovenia with his new Los Angeles Lakers teammates. Mamukelashvili recently hit the court and played for his country, Georgia, in an exhibition matchup against Israel at Otar Korkia and Nodar Jorjikia Tbilisi Spo
articles._body: Sandro Mamukelashvili is not wasting time getting back to action following a trip to Slovenia with his new Los Angeles Lakers teammates . Mamukelashvili recently hit the court and played for his country, Georgia, in an exhibition matchup against Israel at Otar Korkia and Nodar Jorjikia Tbilisi Sports Palace in Georgia on Sunday. The 27-year-old Mamukelashvili had quite a performance in the Israel game. Together with Orlando Magic big man Goga Bitadze, Mamukelashvili led the way for Georgia to a 101–90 victory. Mamukelashvili, who played college basketball for the Seton Hall Pirates, put up 20 points to go along with six rebounds, six assists and three steals. Here is a video of some of the highlights from Mamukelashvili and Georgia from that contest (h/t LakersMuse). Sandro Mamukelashvili highlights in the win against Israel: 20 PTS | 6 REB | 6 AST | 3 STL (Via: GioArena/YT) pic.twitter.com/fFCm8Nv03o — LakersMuse (@LALMuse) August 24, 2026 Mamukelashvili is not going to enjoy that many touches on the court once he starts playing games for the Lakers, as he is mostly going to be serving a supporting role behind the likes of Luka Doncic and Austin Reaves. But the meeting with Israel still shows a sneak peek of what he can bring to the table for Los Angeles, which went 53-29 in the 2025-26 NBA season, reached the second round of the playoffs, and got swept by the Oklahoma City Thunder. The Thunder, San Antonio Spurs and Minnesota Timberwolves are some of the teams expected to be chief contenders for the Western Conference title in the coming season, but the Lakers shouldn’t be slept on, with Doncic about to fully take over as the clear face of the franchise following LeBron James’ offseason departure. Still, guys like Mamukelashvili will be vital to the Lakers, who signed him to a four-year, $52 million contract in July. Mamukelashvili is coming off his best season yet in the NBA , as he averaged 11.2 points, 4.9 rebounds, and 1.9 assists while shooting 52.3 percent from the field in 80 games in the 2025-26 campaign with the Toronto Raptors. articles._body: I built a to-do list and calendar for tracking EVERYTHING we must worry about on one page. articles.title: Two Purdue defenders absent as Boilermakers enter final phase of camp
articles.summary: Two players who figure to play key roles for the Purdue defense in 2026 are out: defensive back Smiley Bradford and linebacker Anthony Speca.
articles._body: Two players who figure to play key roles for the Purdue defense in 2026 are out: defensive back Smiley Bradford and linebacker Anthony Speca . Bradford–a junior–emerged last year, playing in 12 games with a start. He made 30 tackles with seven PBUs, five TFLs and an interception in 2025. The East St. Louis (Ill.) native played in five games with four starts in 2024 as a true freshman. “Smiley stepped away from football activities dealing with a personal matter,” said Barry Odom after practice on Monday. No timetable on when–or if–to expect the return of Bradford, who primarily has been a nickel back. Purdue has some other veteran options in the secondary to pick up the slack, including Mister Clark , Jaden Mangham , John Slaughter , Justin Denson –among others. Does Odom expect Speca–thought to be dealing with injury–to be ready for the season, which starts Sept. 4. vs. Indiana State? “We are,” said Odom. Speca arrived at Purdue in the offseason from Penn State. He was challenging to start but at the least looks to provide valuable depth. Speca appeared in 16 games total the last two years at Penn State, making 14 tackles. Purdue’s top two linebackers are Charles Correa and Jojo Hayden . Winston Berglund and Hudson Miller are next up. articles.title: Marshall Faulk, Southern face tough test versus ascendant Alabama State
articles.summary: The start of the football season is upon us, and Marshall Faulk is already ready for his biggest test yet: a matchup against the ascendant Alabama State Hornets, led by coach Eddie Robinson Jr. and star quarterback Andrew Body. I circled this game the moment it was announced back in February, as
articles._body: The start of the football season is upon us, and Marshall Faulk is already ready for his biggest test yet: a matchup against the ascendant Alabama State Hornets, led by coach Eddie Robinson Jr. and star quarterback Andrew Body. I circled this game the moment it was announced back in February, as it’s a matchup sure to answer a lot of critical questions about Faulk and what will happen in his first season in the SWAC. Faulk landed in an ideal situation when he accepted the Southern University job. Southern is a proud HBCU football program with plenty of football accolades. From Pete Richardson, who led Southern University for 16 years, to Dawson Odum’s reign of success and even Southern’s appearances in the SWAC championship over the past few seasons. The Jaguars have proven that they can be a contender in any era of HBCU football. But still, there’s a lot that’s undefined about Faulk as he starts his tenure. We know he wants a fast and quick offense. Even though he made his Hall of Fame career as a running back and boasts one of the most explosive tailbacks in Trey Holly, he wants an active passing game. Is that really going to work? Especially when we know that heading into the season, Marshall Faulk didn’t know who was going to start at quarterback. And to be honest, do we know now? If we don’t know now, will we know before the huge matchup on Saturday? Well, here’s one thing I can predict: Andrew Body is going to be the best quarterback on that field, no matter who else is out there for Southern. I can guarantee that. And I’m so happy Andrew Body decided to come back. He could’ve gone to another institution. He stayed in the transfer portal long enough that there could’ve been FBS offers, places where he could’ve shown his talent to NFL scouts. But he came back to Alabama State, and he said he did it because he wants to show that HBCU football can produce players who make it. Andrew Body had a phenomenal year last year that was, unfortunately, cut short by injury. He’s had a lot of injury concerns throughout his career, and we’re hoping and praying he has a healthy final year at Alabama State, and that he becomes the first quarterback out of the HBCU ranks to really make it to the NFL. I think that return starts with this game. Alabama State is on a SWAC championship trajectory, and their road won’t be easy. They have to face tough matchups to start October against Bethune-Cookman and Florida A&M. They then have their final two games of the season against Jackson State, which could decide who makes the SWAC championship for the East, and then a matchup against the potential SWAC West champion in Prairie View A&M. Alabama State needs to start the season with fervor and beat Marshall Faulk in his first game, with all eyes on the matchup because of Faulk’s status as a Hall of Fame running back. Could be what’s needed. Body and Alabama State proved their competitiveness in their first game against the University of Alabama Birmingham last year. This could be another showcase of the possibilities of Alabama State’s potent offense with Body under center. Southern will have its own advantages, with Trey Holly still a playmaking running back Faulk could likely unlock. Their running back room will be incredibly strong, even with the loss of former Texas A&M standout Ronnie Crosby, but it’s unlikely that they will be able to contain Alabama State’s firepower if the Hornets play as they did in 2025. My prediction: Alabama State wins this game, perhaps by two or more touchdowns. The post Marshall Faulk, Southern face tough test versus ascendant Alabama State appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles.title: Luka Doncic makes Kobe Day surprise in heartwarming hospital visit
articles.summary: Every Aug. 24 holds special meaning for the Los Angeles Lakers. It is recognized as Kobe Bryant Day, honoring his numbers 8 and 24. It also falls on the day after Kobe’s official birthday of Aug. 23. Players, family, friends, and fans worldwide commemorate the occasion however they see fit,
articles._body: Every Aug. 24 holds special meaning for the Los Angeles Lakers. It is recognized as Kobe Bryant Day , honoring his numbers 8 and 24. It also falls on the day after Kobe’s official birthday of Aug. 23. Players, family, friends, and fans worldwide commemorate the occasion however they see fit, in keeping with Kobe’s legacy. The new face of the Lakers, Luka Doncic, did his part when paying a surprise visit to a hospital in his home country of Slovenia. He gave a bag of gifts to a mother who named her newborn son Luka. The sweetest Kobe Day surprise in Slovenia with Luka & @UCLAHealth pic.twitter.com/pSjOLSYRNO — Los Angeles Lakers (@Lakers) August 24, 2026 Over the weekend, Doncic organized a team trip to Slovenia as part of minicap. In total, 16 of 17 players were on the trip, with rookie Cam Carr the exception because of orientation. The team practiced at Stožice Arena in Ljubljana. In addition, Doncic took the team to a newly renovated basketball court where he played as a child. In Slovenia, Doncic is a beloved icon. Over the last several years, he helped put the nation on the basketball map. He led them to the gold medal at FIBA EuroBasket in 2017. In 2020, Doncic led Slovenia to their first Olympic appearance in Tokyo. His enormous popularity has earned him a position as an ambassador on the Slovenian Tourist Board, promoting Slovenia everywhere he goes. After LeBron James left for the Philadelphia 76ers , Doncic is now carrying the Lakers on his shoulders. One can only imagine what it would be like if Kobe were still with us and what he would have thought of Doncic’s Lakers. articles.title: Kentucky men’s soccer falls to Louisville in final minute
articles.summary: Well, this was going to be a fun article about beating the crap out of Louisville and why Kentucky owns the state, but the Cardinals ruined that for us. 31 minutes into the Wildcats’ rivalry matchup in Lexington, it was all blue. Michael Lee got the good guys on the board first at the 17:22 [&
articles._body: Well, this was going to be a fun article about beating the crap out of Louisville and why Kentucky owns the state, but the Cardinals ruined that for us. 31 minutes into the Wildcats’ rivalry matchup in Lexington, it was all blue. Michael Lee got the good guys on the board first at the 17:22 mark to take a 1-0 lead, followed by another by Yasha Schaerer at 30:56 to jump ahead 2-0 approaching halftime. They were both left-goal shots to take what felt like an insurmountable lead going into the second half, considering the momentum and home advantage at The Bell. Michael Lee strikes first. – https://t.co/tsx7dCL4Z0 – https://t.co/c2jK2gOddx pic.twitter.com/7op9pgWMTA — Kentucky Men’s Soccer (@UKMensSoccer) August 25, 2026 Yasha with class – https://t.co/tsx7dCL4Z0 – https://t.co/c2jK2gOddx pic.twitter.com/1CTsimy5tC — Kentucky Men’s Soccer (@UKMensSoccer) August 25, 2026 We even got some fisticuffs with pushing and shoving as tempers flared, including eight total yellow cards called between the two teams, with four apiece. With so much going for you early and into the second, you have to pull it off, right? No better rivalry in the country than the Cats and the Cards pic.twitter.com/hShTCYga7b — Blue Chips Media (@BlueChipsBBN) August 25, 2026 The Cards responded on a penalty kick to cut it to 2-1 at 56′ — not ideal, but no reason to panic at the time, especially considering the Cats held firm for the next 27 minutes to make the comeback window about as tight as possible for the rival from down 1-64W. And then Giacomo Zizza took things over himself with back-to-back goals in the final eight minutes, then eight freaking seconds. He pushed one through at the 82:08 mark, then did it again at 89:52 to take the 3-2 lead and ultimately close out the victory to extend Louisville’s unbeaten streak to four games against Kentucky. As you can imagine, the Cards lost their collective minds while the Cats stood around in absolute shock after choking away such a comfortable lead, captured well by LEX18’s Sierra Newton. END OF GAME: Louisville 3, Kentucky 2. Tied at 2 with just eight seconds left on the clock Louisville’s Zizza calls game. A tough one at the Bell. NEXT: @UKMensSoccer hits the road, Friday at Virginia Tech. 6:30 p.m. pic.twitter.com/Ugh7KPk8RW — Sierra Newton (@SoFlossieWrites) August 25, 2026 Kentucky and Louisville tied 2-2 last September — the result we thought we were going to have in the final minutes, only for Zizza to pull another one out of his hat. In 2024, the Cards left Lexington with a 1-0 win, and also protected their home field in 2023 with a 4-2 victory. The Cats’ last win came in 2022 with a 3-2 upset in Lexington, sending the top-10 opponent home pouting as the road favorite. This time around, it was trending toward a similar result, until it wasn’t. Kentucky must shake off the tough loss and prepare for its next test against Virginia Tech in Blacksburg. That one is scheduled for Friday, Aug. 28 at 6 p.m. ET. That one hurts, folks. So close, but so far.

articles.title: Lynx’s Napheesa Collier gets real about playing without Courtneyu Williams
articles.summary: The Minnesota Lynx were without one of their ace players in their marquee matchup with the Golden State Valkyries at Target Center on Monday, as Courtney Williams was sidelined by a foot injury. Losing Williams gave the Lynx a real handicap, especially in a battle between the top two teams in the
articles._body: The Minnesota Lynx were without one of their ace players in their marquee matchup with the Golden State Valkyries at Target Center on Monday, as Courtney Williams was sidelined by a foot injury . Losing Williams gave the Lynx a real handicap, especially in a battle between the top two teams in the league. The 32-year-old guard is averaging all-around numbers of 14.4 points, 5.1 rebounds, 4.3 assists, and 1.1 steals this season. She suffered the foot injury in their win over the Washington Mystics at CareFirst Arena on Friday. Before the game, Napheesa Collier was asked about not having Williams against the Valkyries. Collier was quite candid with her reply. “This is the first game she’s ever missed due to injury in 11 years. That’s incredible. That has to be a record. She was just out being suspended,” joked Collier in the video posted by Lynx reporter Andrew Dukowitz. “It will definitely be weird. I’ve never played a game without Courtney since she’s been here.” Napheesa Collier on playing her first game without Courtney Williams in three years “Yeah this is the first game she’s ever missed due to injury in eleven years… has to be a record(laughs), she was just out being suspended(laughs)… it’ll definitely be weird I’ve never played… pic.twitter.com/hxNLjBUVBZ — Andrew Dukowitz (@adukeMN) August 24, 2026 The five-time All-Star, however, turned serious when asked about Williams’ impact on the Lynx. “Her energy, her vibes, her passion for the game. Obviously, she’s a big voice on our team. She gets us going. She’s very passionate about the game, and that rubs off on us,” added Collier. Minnesota signed Williams in 2024. Before sitting out against Golden State, the three-time All-Star had not missed a game in four seasons. She has teamed up with Olivia Miles to form arguably the most prolific backcourt in the WNBA. Her return, however, is still unclear. As of this writing, the Lynx are trailing the Valkyries in the fourth quarter, putting their six-game winning streak in jeopardy. articles.title: Chiefs’ 53-man roster prediction for 2026 NFL season
articles.summary: The Kansas City Chiefs’ decisions are becoming very real. At 0-2 in the preseason, Kansas City has dropped consecutive one-score preseason contests. Of course, the results have mattered far less than the individual auditions taking place underneath them. Andy Reid is protecting Patrick Maho
articles._body: The Kansas City Chiefs’ decisions are becoming very real. At 0-2 in the preseason, Kansas City has dropped consecutive one-score preseason contests. Of course, the results have mattered far less than the individual auditions taking place underneath them. Andy Reid is protecting Patrick Mahomes as he works his way back from a knee issue. Elsewhere, Kenneth Walker III has begun settling into his new backfield role. Kahlil Benson has generated intriguing attention along the offensive line. A revamped secondary featuring L’Jarius Sneed, Mansoor Delane, Nohl Williams and Kader Kohou has offered plenty of reason for optimism. With the 53-man deadline looming , Kansas City now has one final opportunity to resolve the roster’s most difficult questions. Searching for answers Denny Medley-Imagn Images. The Chiefs have approached the 2026 NFL preseason with a clear emphasis on depth evaluation and roster trimming. They sit at 0-2 after tight exhibition losses to the Los Angeles Rams and Tampa Bay Buccaneers. With Mahomes held out of live game action, Justin Fields, Garrett Nussmeier and Chris Oladokun have piloted the offense. The preseason has also provided extended opportunities for Walker and several players competing for roster spots. Jalen Royals, for example, caught all six of his targets for 51 yards against Tampa Bay. Meanwhile, Felix Anudike-Uzomah recorded a sack in the narrow loss. The most pressing issue may be at right tackle. That’s where Benson’s development has created an intriguing competition but also exposed some growing pains. Offensive Playmakers Quarterback (3): Patrick Mahomes, Justin Fields, Garrett Nussmeier Mahomes obviously occupies the top spot. His absence from preseason games should not be interpreted as uncertainty about his position. The Chiefs are simply taking a cautious approach to his knee recovery. Fields gives Reid a fascinating backup option because of his mobility and experience. Nussmeier has done enough to justify keeping him as the developmental third quarterback. Running Back (4): Kenneth Walker III, Emari Demercado, Emmett Johnson, Brashard Smith Walker is the clear centerpiece after arriving in Kansas City with the explosiveness. His ability to create outside the tackles also fits an offense that wants to manufacture space for its backs. Demercado provides dependable complementary work. Johnson offers another dynamic runner. Smith’s versatility and return ability strengthen his case for the final spot. Wide Receiver (6): Rashee Rice, Xavier Worthy, Tyquan Thornton, Cyrus Allen, Jalen Royals, Nikko Remigio Six receivers give the offense flexibility. Rice and Worthy remain the most prominent pieces. Thornton gives the offense another vertical threat. Allen and Royals offer intriguing complementary skill sets. Remigio earns the final spot because of his return value. Tight End (3): Travis Kelce, Noah Gray, Jared Wiley Kelce remains the centerpiece at tight end, of course. Gray provides established complementary value. Wiley gets the third spot, although Jake Briningstool remains a legitimate bubble candidate. Offensive Line Offensive Tackle (4): Josh Simmons, Jaylon Moore, Kahlil Benson, Esa Pole Moore remains a significant option on the edge. Benson is perhaps the most fascinating developmental storyline. His physical profile has earned him meaningful opportunities. However, the Tampa Bay game illustrated why the right tackle battle remains unsettled. He played 35 snaps and allowed two pressures in 25 pass-blocking opportunities. Interior O-Line (5): Creed Humphrey, Trey Smith, Kingsley Suamataia, Mike Caliendo, Hunter Nourzad Humphrey and Smith provide the veteran foundation, while Suamataia gives Kansas City another important piece of interior versatility. Defense EDGE (5): George Karlaftis, Ashton Gillotte, Felix Anudike-Uzomah, R Mason Thomas, Emmanuel Ogbah The defensive front has star power. Karlaftis remains the established anchor. Anudike-Uzomah’s preseason sack against Tampa Bay was an encouraging sign. Thomas has also generated significant pressure during exhibition action. Defensive Tackle (4): Chris Jones, Khyiris Tonga, Peter Woods, Amari McNeill Inside, Chris Jones, Khyiris Tonga, Peter Woods and Amari McNeill make the projected group, with Omarr Norman-Lott currently on the PUP list. Jones remains the gravitational force that opposing offenses must account for. The challenge is developing enough complementary disruption to prevent offenses from simply concentrating protection toward him. Linebacker (5): Nick Bolton, Drue Tranquill, Cooper McDonald, Jeffrey Bassa, Cam Jones Linebacker depth looks settled. Bolton and Tranquill provide the experience and communication required to organize the defense. McDonald and Bassa offer athleticism and developmental upside. Cornerback (6): L’Jarius Sneed, Mansoor Delane, Nohl Williams, Kader Kohou, Jadon Canady, Christian Roland-Wallace The secondary is undergoing a transformation. Sneed provides the established veteran presence. The younger corners have created genuine competition. Delane and Williams have both flashed during the preseason. Kohou’s versatility gives Spagnuolo another useful chess piece. Safety (5); Alohi Gilman, Chamarri Conner, Jaden Hicks, Xavier Nwankpa, DeShon Singleton At safety, the projection is Alohi Gilman, Chamarri Conner, Jaden Hicks, Xavier Nwankpa and DeShon Singleton. The group gives Spagnuolo plenty of options for disguising coverage and rotating defenders late in the pre-snap process. Special teams Kicker: Harrison Butker Punter: Matt Araiza Long Snapper: James Winchester This is straightforward. Butker remains the established kicker. Araiza has the leg strength to provide a significant field-position advantage. Winchester’s reliability at long snapper makes him one of the safest roster decisions on the team. articles.title: Cypher Tank Returns to Lugano, Expanding Its Bet on Bitcoin Founders
articles.summary: Bitcoin Magazine
articles._body: Bitcoin Magazine Cypher Tank Returns to Lugano, Expanding Its Bet on Bitcoin Founders Cypher Tank is back.  Applications for 2026’s Bitcoin-focused pitch competition are now open after last year’s event drew over 4,000 participants from 64 countries.  Like 2025’s event, the format, promoted and funded by the Plan ₿ VC Fund and the Plan ₿ Foundation, pairs a “Shark Tank”-style negotiation format with a documentary-style production, filming real pitches, deals and judge deliberations for release as an online series.  This year’s edition expands the finalist field to 12 projects — eight for-profit and four nonprofit — up from last year’s eleven, with founders competing to negotiate direct investment from a panel of judges known as the “honey badgers” and to win one of three $100,000 prizes in incubation, acceleration, or relocation services. Finalists are chosen by committee against three criteria: alignment with the values of individual freedom, privacy, decentralization, and resilience; execution ability, sustainability, and market feasibility; and integration within the broader Plan ₿ ecosystem. The competition unfolds in four phases. Applications opened August 13 and close September 25, after which finalists are notified starting September 30. The finals themselves run October 25–27 at PoW Space Lugano, immediately following the Plan ₿ Forum — beginning with a coaching day where finalists rehearse pitches with communication experts, followed by two days of live pitching and negotiation split into batches on October 26 and 27. Winners are selected at the close of the second day. The recorded episodes then go into post-production through the end of the year, airing online in January 2027, with the winners’ incubation and acceleration support kicking off at the end of February once their NDAs lapse. The show’s first season launched in 2025 with similarly high stakes — over $850,000 in total prizes and a judging panel that included Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino, Blockstream’s Adam Back, Ten31’s Matt Odell, Lightning Ventures’ Mike Jarmuz, and Ego Death’s Preston Pysh.  It rode the momentum of a record-breaking Plan ₿ Forum, which drew more than 4,000 attendees from 64 countries and upward of 800,000 livestream viewers, before its episodes premiered at Plan ₿ Forum El Salvador in January 2026 and winners were formally honored in Lugano that March. With season two now underway, Cypher Tank is betting that a bigger finalist pool and a tighter four-phase structure can build on that first-season visibility — continuing its push to position Lugano as a global hub for Bitcoin and freedom-tech innovation. For more information and applications, founders can visit the application portal . This post Cypher Tank Returns to Lugano, Expanding Its Bet on Bitcoin Founders first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Mathew Di Salvo .
