articles.title: Senators’ glaring roster flaw that must be fixed before 2026-27 NHL season
articles.summary: The Ottawa Senators are coming off their second straight playoff appearance. Ottawa made the postseason following a bit of a slow start to the year. The Senators were unable to build on their 2025 playoff appearance, though. They were swept in the first round this past season by the eventual Stan
articles._body: The Ottawa Senators are coming off their second straight playoff appearance . Ottawa made the postseason following a bit of a slow start to the year. The Senators were unable to build on their 2025 playoff appearance, though. They were swept in the first round this past season by the eventual Stanley Cup champion, the Carolina Hurricanes. Ottawa certainly had some hope heading into the 2026-27 campaign, despite the sweep. Brady Tkachuk remained a top player, and the Senators have talented young players. Jake Sanderson and Tim Stutzle are two of the best young players in the NHL right now. It wasn’t out of the realm of possibility that improvements internally could have led to better playoff fortunes next year. Unfortunately, this feeling had a wrench thrown into it this offseason. Tkachuk, the Senators’ captain, requested a trade this summer. He got his trade before the 2026 NHL Draft. Ottawa sent him to the Florida Panthers , where he’s been reunited with his brother, Matthew. The Senators certainly still have a quality team without Tkachuk. But the team took a big hit by losing its captain and one of its best players. Ottawa had to find a way to improve its roster this summer and reach playoff contention again. Whether they successfully remained a playoff contender remains to be seen. For now, let’s take a closer look at this roster and detail one glaring flaw the Senators should try to address before the 2026-27 NHL season. Senators still need top-six forward after Brady Tkachuk trade James Guillory-Imagn Images There is a lot that can be said about Tkachuk and the trade with the Panthers. However, focusing on the Senators, the trade made an already glaring roster flaw even more apparent. Ottawa needs a top-six forward in the worst way. Ottawa did address their forward group this summer. In fact, they used part of the Tkachuk return to do so. The Senators flipped the ninth overall pick acquired in this trade to the San Jose Sharks in exchange for forward William Eklund and two prospects. Eklund is a fine player who has shown glimpses of brilliance in the past. He was one of San Jose’s leading forwards in the days before Macklin Celebrini. However, whether he can be a quality top-six forward on a team with playoff ambition remains to be seen. Outside of him, there are two returning players who are also question marks in the top six. Ridly Grieg did score 35 points last season, which is certainly nothing to sneeze at. But he will need to produce a lot more to truly be effective at the top of the lineup. Claude Giroux is back after pondering his future in the NHL. The 38-year-old scored 45 points last year and has loads of experience he can draw upon. However, as he continues to get up there in age, it’s fair to question how much longer he can be effective in the top-six. The Senators are largely set elsewhere. Stutzle and Dylan Cozens are a good top-six duo down the middle. And Drake Batherson is coming off a fantastic season in which he scored 33 goals and 71 points. As mentioned, Ottawa has those good, young players at the top of the lineup that can take this team far. With that said, though, there are clear question marks atop their lineup heading into 2026-27. articles.title: Mike McCarthy gets 100% real Steelers’ reported 4-QB plan
articles.summary: Mike McCarthy shut down the idea of having four quarterbacks on the Pittsburgh Steelers roster going into the 2026 NFL season. McCarthy is preparing for the first year of his head coaching stint with the Steelers. Following past destinations with the Green Bay Packers and the Dallas Cowboys, the
articles._body: Mike McCarthy shut down the idea of having four quarterbacks on the Pittsburgh Steelers roster going into the 2026 NFL season. McCarthy is preparing for the first year of his head coaching stint with the Steelers. Following past destinations with the Green Bay Packers and the Dallas Cowboys, the coach looks to get Pittsburgh back to serious playoff contention. Pittsburgh currently has four quarterbacks on the team, having Aaron Rodgers, Drew Allar, Will Howard, and Mason Rudolph. Teams typically cut that down to three for the regular season, indicating a possibility that one of the quarterbacks won’t be on the roster. However, there is a report that showed Pittsburgh will start the roster with four quarterbacks. McCarthy didn’t give any legitimacy to that article when the media asked him about it, via Steelers Depot. “I haven’t been a part of any conversations about the 53 that’s been decided already,” McCarthy said. Barry Reeger-Imagn Images What lies ahead for Mike McCarthy, Steelers this season Mike McCarthy has the experience for the Steelers to experience solid success. Aaron Rodgers has one more year before retiring, but McCarthy will look forward to the growth of Drew Allar and Will Howard. McCarthy has been a head coach in the NFL since 2006. He led the Green Bay Packers for 13 years, winning a Super Bowl title in 2010. The Cowboys were his next destination, coaching them for five years as he got them to the playoffs three times. The Steelers will attempt to improve on their 10–7 record of the past three seasons. They will also attempt to end their seven-game playoff game losing streak dating back to the 2016 season. Rodgers is the starting quarterback as he prepares for retirement from the NFL as a future Hall of Famer. Pittsburgh has one more preseason contest to deal with, facing the Buffalo Bills on Aug. 27 at 7 p.m. ET. Their regular-season opener commences at home against the Atlanta Falcons on Sept. 13 at 1 p.m. ET. articles.title: Jo Adell opens up about return to Angels after Guardians trade
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Angels welcomed a familiar face back to Angel Stadium on Monday, though this time Jo Adell arrived in the visiting clubhouse with the Cleveland Guardians. Adell’s return came exactly three weeks after the Angels traded him to the Guardians on the August 3rd MLB trade deadline for
articles._body: The Los Angeles Angels welcomed a familiar face back to Angel Stadium on Monday, though this time Jo Adell arrived in the visiting clubhouse with the Cleveland Guardians. Adell’s return came exactly three weeks after the Angels traded him to the Guardians on the August 3rd MLB trade deadline for Jacob Cozart. Los Angeles selected the outfielder No. 10 overall in the 2017 MLB Draft, and he debuted in 2020. Until the trade, Adell had spent his entire professional career in the Angels organization. After hitting 37 home runs in 2025, the 27-year-old outfielder was batting .239 with 16 homers and 62 RBIs at the time of the deal. Because the trade occurred on an off day, he did not have the opportunity for a traditional farewell before leaving Anaheim. Angels’ Erica Weston shared a graphic on X, formerly Twitter, Monday evening featuring Adell’s reflections on returning to the ballpark where his major league career began. “I was just alluding to it earlier, but really, just the fact that I kind of became a man, you know, in the game here in Anaheim, and the ups, the downs, the great moments—you know, everything started on this field. And every time that I come here, it’s that reminder of the player that I am today. It happened here at the stadium, so it’s really a really surreal moment, and just really proud of my time, you know, as an Angel and what I was able to bring to the table, and how much that group helped me grow as a player, and so just forever thankful for that. And you know, now being on the other side, we’re going to go try to take care of business.” Jo Adell reflecting on his time as an Angel, as he returns to Anaheim 3 weeks to the day after being traded to Cleveland: pic.twitter.com/LV2lSMmjxA — Erica Weston (@EricaLWeston) August 25, 2026 The return added a personal subplot to the series as the Guardians opened their series in Anaheim while pursuing an American League wild card berth during the closing stretch of the regular season, giving Adell an opportunity to return to familiar surroundings while competing against the organization that originally drafted and developed him. articles.title: Tennessee EDGE Jordan Norman compares teammate, QB Faizon Brandon, to Lamar Jackson
articles.summary: It was announced on Monday that incoming five-star freshman quarterback, Faizon Brandon, will open the 2026 season as Tennessee‘s starting quarterback. Brandon was the No. 3 ranked quarterback in the Class of 2026, and has earned the starting job heading into his first season of college footba
articles._body: It was announced on Monday that incoming five-star freshman quarterback, Faizon Brandon , will open the 2026 season as Tennessee ‘s starting quarterback. Brandon was the No. 3 ranked quarterback in the Class of 2026, and has earned the starting job heading into his first season of college football. Brandon will join Nico Iamaleava as the only true freshman quarterback to start a game for Tennessee in the Josh Heupel era. Iamaleava’s first career start came in Tennessee ‘s 2024 Citrus Bowl matchup against Iowa . He was named Citrus Bowl MVP following the Volunteers’ 35-0 victory. $19.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage Expectations are certainly high for the Greensboro, N.C. native, who will face off against FCS Furman in his first start. Tennessee EDGE rusher Jordan Norman , who transferred to the program from Tulane this offseason, added fuel to the fire of such expectations. He compared the freshman to Louisville football legend and two-time NFL MVP Lamar Jackson , winner of the 2016 Heisman Trophy. “I would say, honestly, it’s like trying to tackle Lamar Jackson ,” Norman said, via knoxnews.com . “Somebody who can run, shake you. I thought I had him. Next thing you know he was out of the pocket. That’s one of the plays that stuck out to me like, ‘Yeah, he can really do that.'” Brandon beat out sophomore quarterback, George MacIntyre , for the Tennessee starting job. MacIntyre, four-star recruit in the Class of 2025, appeared in two games for the ‘Vols last season. He completed 7/9 passes for 69 yards. Josh Heupel opens up about decision to name Faizon Brandon QB1 Shortly after Brandon was indeed revealed to open the season as Tennessee ‘s QB1, head coach Josh Heupel discussed the decision. The five-star freshman will join Joe Milton III (2021 and 2023), Hendon Hooker (2022), Nico Iamaleava (2024), and Joey Aguilar (2025) as Week 1 starters at Tennessee during the Heupel era. “We named him the starter because we believe in the work that he’s put in and how he’s continued to grow and play throughout training camp,” Heupel said . “The second week through the second scrimmage, he’s earned that right. But, just like every position, you can consistently evaluate. “I don’t think there’s just one thing (Brandon did to win the job). At times, people want to say, ‘is there one focal point that changed it?’ I think in all his control and command of what we’re doing offensively; that’s run game, RPO game, the drop back, play-action. Combine that with fundamentals, technique, and pocket awareness. You put all that together… decision-making, and taking care of the football while still allowing his playmakers to make plays down the field. You look at the total volume of work and he’s earned the right to start.” Tennessee is looking to bounce back from a turbulent end to its 2025 season, which saw the Volunteers lose four of their final seven games.

articles.title: Stephon Castle’s friends won’t let him play as Victor Wembanyama in NBA 2K27
articles.summary: LOS ANGELES — While Victor Wembanyama gets a lot of the love from fans, especially now as the cover athlete for NBA 2K27, the San Antonio Spurs also have one of the best, up-and-coming two-way guards in the NBA in Stephon Castle. With Castle and Wembanyama alongside one another, the Spurs have a
articles._body: LOS ANGELES — While Victor Wembanyama gets a lot of the love from fans, especially now as the cover athlete for NBA 2K27, the San Antonio Spurs also have one of the best, up-and-coming two-way guards in the NBA in Stephon Castle. With Castle and Wembanyama alongside one another, the Spurs have a bright future that also features Dylan Harper, who just finished his rookie season in the NBA, and De’Aaron Fox, and established and proven veteran in the league. In the past, teams like the Golden State Warriors with Kevin Durant have been off-limits due to their high ratings and star-power. This year, the Philadelphia 76ers are looking awfully familiar, boasting four players with a 91 overall rating or higher. But according to Stephon Castle’s friends, the San Antonio Spurs are also off limits. Castle recently tried to play as the Spurs against some friends in NBA 2K27, but they gave him a lot of grief, and sometimes don’t even let him. Castle, who spoke with ClutchPoints at NBA 2K27 Community Day, says his friends call it, “cheating.” “I’ll be playing my friends and they’ll be telling me I can’t get the Spurs,” Castle explained in disbelief. “They said we’re cheating. I don’t know [how that’s cheating]. Hopefully I’ll be able to get the Spurs this year if I let them get the Sixers or something.” During the interview with Stephon Castle , the Spurs guard also said he used to play with them back in NBA 2K14, along with the Kevin Durant-led Oklahoma City Thunder and the LeBron James-led Miami Heat. Stephon Castle: I thought the Spurs were really cheesy. I don’t know what made me use them back then. Because, I mean, it’s not like they had crazy just star athleticism, stuff like that. But, I mean, they were pretty good back then. I think the Thunder team was good before they gave up KD. And obviously the Heat were probably off limits when you play with somebody.” In just his second season in the NBA, Castle averaged 16.7 points, 5.3 rebounds, 7.4 assists, and 1.1 steals per game while shooting 47.1 percent from the field. He was even better during his first ever playoff run, averaging 18.2 points, 5.0 rebounds, 6.1 assists, and 0.9 steals per game in 23 appearances while shooting 46 percent from the field and being one of the leaders in the Spurs’ NBA Finals run. After falling short against the New York Knicks, San Antonio will surely have revenge on their mind heading into the 2026-27 season. articles.title: David Pollack dubs Alabama QB Keelon Russell a ‘carbon copy’ of Jayden Daniels
articles.summary: Alabama has a new starting quarterback, bringing a lot of excitement to Tuscaloosa. Keelon Russell beat out Austin Mack, a decision head coach Kalen DeBoer announced on Saturday. Russell is considered an immense talent, earning Five-Star Plus+ status out of Duncanville (TX). Now, Alabama is hoping t
articles._body: Alabama has a new starting quarterback, bringing a lot of excitement to Tuscaloosa. Keelon Russell beat out Austin Mack , a decision head coach Kalen DeBoer announced on Saturday. Russell is considered an immense talent, earning Five-Star Plus+ status out of Duncanville (TX). Now, Alabama is hoping to unlock the potential this season. Comparisons are always a great way to show how highly thought of somebody is. David Pollack put together quite a flattering one for Russell. Pollack likened the Alabama QB to a former Heisman Trophy-winning QB in Baton Rouge — LSU ‘s Jayden Daniels . “He reminds me of a very specific player,” Pollack said . “Release, size, shiftiness, running ability. Like, he’s a carbon copy for me… it’s Jayden Daniels. It’s exactly who it is. It’s tall, it’s skinny, it’s fast. His release is quick. I’m telling you. Y’all are going to watch this and just remember… He looks like Daniels.” Turns out, Pollack is not the only one to see a lot of Daniels in Russell. When scouting Russell out of high school, Rivals saw the same thing. Daniels was his main comparison, but CJ Stroud and Teddy Bridgewater got thrown in there too. “Keelon Russell’s frame, arm talent, accuracy and gaudy passing production remind us of Jayden Daniels,” the scouting report said. “Daniels was much more productive as a run threat, eclipsing 1,500 yards on the ground as a senior in high school. We also see some similarities between Russell and CJ Stroud and Teddy Bridgewater out of high school.” Daniels began his college career at Arizona State before spending two seasons at LSU. Both of those were under Brian Kelly , where the development showed in a big way. By the 2023 season, Daniels was one of the best quarterbacks in the country. As mentioned, he won the Heisman Trophy and was eventually the No. 2 overall pick of the Washington Commanders. Russell has at least two years of college remaining. DeBoer has a recent track record of putting quarterbacks in the first round, seeing Michael Penix get taken by the Atlanta Falcons and the Los Angeles Rams drafting Ty Simpson . If the comparison between Russell and Daniels plays out in front of our eyes, another one might be put on the board. There is still plenty of football to be played between now and then, though. Alabama opens the 2026 season with East Carolina on Sept. 5. Russell will be thrown into the fire one week later with an SEC road game vs. Kentucky .

And here is the Titans’ 53-man roster prediction for the 2026 NFL season. Coming off bad seasons, the Titans need to energize their fan base. Hiring Sal
articles._body: There are lots of Music City sour notes for the Tennessee Titans . And the defense didn’t even avoid Robert Saleh’s wrath . But cut day is coming. And here is the Titans’ 53-man roster prediction for the 2026 NFL season. Coming off bad seasons, the Titans need to energize their fan base. Hiring Saleh helped, but making the right roster decisions is a critical step if the team is going to be more competitive this season. Let’s see what the best path is. Quarterback (2) Cam Ward, Mitchell Trubisky It’s time for the Titans to move on from Will Levis. They selected him in the second round of the 2023 NFL Draft. But his career record of 5-16 speaks volumes. It’s becoming a consensus , with ESPN on board. “Carrying two quarterbacks will most likely signal the end for Will Levis’ time in Nashville,” Turron Davenport wrote. Running backs (4) Tony Pollard, Tyjae Spears, Nicholas Singleton, Julius Chestnut The first three spots are solid. Each of those guys has a specific place right now. However, who gets the No. 4 spot? Chestnut’s recent strong performance against the Seahawks gives him a leg up over Kalel Mullings for the slot. Chestnut carried eight times for 48 yards, including a 15-yard scamper. Also, he added three catches for 24 yards. It was impressive enough to put him in the driver’s seat. But Mullings still has a shot. This could come down to the wire. Wide receivers (6) Calvin Ridley, Wan’Dale Robinson, Carnell Tate, Elic Ayomanor, Chimere Dike, Bryce Oliver It’s not a great room. So, for KJ Osborn and Xavier Restrepo, missing out here doesn’t bode well for their NFL futures. Ayomanor has been a bright spot during camp. He said it’s partly a mindset thing , according to nashvillepost.com. “There were times when I just wasn’t being fully myself in terms of like aggression and attacking every [snap],” Ayomanor said. “So that’s something I’ve been working on a lot this offseason.” Tight ends (4) Gunnar Helm, Daniel Bellinger, David Martin-Robinson, Kylen Granson It’s possible the Titans will hold back and only keep three tight ends. If they do that, Granson probably hits the road. However, he and Martin-Robinson are both athletic enough. They’ve stayed in the mix. But it appears Martin-Robinson has the edge right now if a cut is needed. Offensive line (9) Dan Moore Jr., Peter Skoronski, Austin Schlottmann, Fernando Carmona Jr., JC Latham, Brandon Crenshaw-Dickson, Jackson Slater, Pat Coogan, Andre James Like the receiver room, the offensive line doesn’t have a list of stars. The Titans will do their best to hang in there with what they have. It’s hard to imagine late cuts like Cordell Volson or Austin Deculus finding anything other than a practice squad opportunity. James sticks because of his versatility. That’s always a plus for offensive linemen. Injuries will come, so being able to play more than one spot can help immensely when cut day comes. Overall, Saleh said the Titans have to get better on the line — and across the offense. They didn’t show enough against the Seahawks, according to NBC Sports. “I thought the first drive was good,” Saleh said. “We went out there and got some points. Thought Cam, again, was good with the ball, good decision-making. We just couldn’t connect on a couple of deep throws, but, overall, it’s got to be better. I’m not trying to sugarcoat it. It does got to be better, but at the same time, there’s always going to be things that we can take from.” Defensive line/Edge (10) Jeffery Simmons, John Franklin-Myers, Jermaine Johnson II, Jordan Elliott, Keldric Faulk, Femi Oladejo, Solomon Thomas, Jackie Marshall, Jacob Martin, Khalen Saunders Of all the positions, this is one of the stronger ones from top to bottom. ESPN went a step further. “The front line is the best unit on the team,” Davenport wrote. “Saleh wants a deep rotation along the line, so they keep 10 defensive linemen. Johnson and Martin lead a young group of outside pass rushers.” Linebackers (5) Cody Barton, Cedric Gray, Anthony Hill Jr., James Williams Sr., Mohamoud Diabate There’s a way where Dorian Mausi makes the 53-man unit and the Titans go with only nine players up front. And this is a close call. Cornerbacks (5) Alontae Taylor, Cor’Dale Flott, Marcus Harris, Joshua Williams, Micah Robinson This is another place where the Titans could add one while subtracting from somewhere else. That could bring Keydrain Calligan back into focus. Right now, he’s on the edge. Safety (5) Amani Hooker, Kevin Winston Jr., Tony Adams, Kendell Brooks, Erick Hallett II Saleh is going to demand toughness from his defense. Hallett can reach that requirement while also being versatile. And those are good enough reasons to get him onto the 53-man roster. Special teams (3) K — Joey Slye, P — Tommy Townsend, LS — Morgan Cox With a big leg, Slye has been able to maintain an NFL paycheck for seven seasons. That’s a consistent deal even though his employers have been the Commanders, Panthers, Patriots, Titans, Texans, and 49ers. Against the Seahawks, Slye solidified his spot by making all four of his field goal attempts. A 55-yard connection was included in the mix. articles.title: Lynx’s Olivia Miles passes WNBA legend for big milestone in game vs. Valkyries
articles.summary: The Minnesota Lynx put their six-game winning streak on the line as they hosted the Golden State Valkyries at Target Center on Monday. With Olivia Miles, Napheesa Collier, Natasha Howard, Courtney Williams, and Kayla McBride at the forefront, the league-leading Lynx have been on an absolute tear,
articles._body: The Minnesota Lynx put their six-game winning streak on the line as they hosted the Golden State Valkyries at Target Center on Monday. With Olivia Miles, Napheesa Collier, Natasha Howard, Courtney Williams, and Kayla McBride at the forefront, the league-leading Lynx have been on an absolute tear, going 16-1 in their last 17 assignments. In particular, Miles has been nothing but phenomenal . She has practically engraved her name on the trophy for Rookie of the Year with her all-around performances. In the first quarter against the Valkyries, the No. 2 pick set another milestone by passing Ticha Penicheiro for the second-most assists by a rookie in league history. OLIVIA MILES CONTINUES TO MAKE HISTORY. She passes Ticha Penicheiro for the second-most assists by a rookie in WNBA history Watch Golden State/Minnesota on USA Network! pic.twitter.com/tbJ4klDV3V — NBA (@NBA) August 25, 2026 Penicheiro, a one-time champion and three-time All-WNBA, tallied 224 assists in her rookie year with the Sacramento Monarchs in 1998. She was a seven-time assists leader. Caitlin Clark of the Indiana Fever crushed Penichiero’s record in 2024, totaling 337 assists. The 23-year-old Miles has been the perfect addition for the Lynx , showcasing her willingness to share the ball and set up her teammates. While she was a scoring machine for Notre Dame and TCU in college, she knew she had to adjust her game in the WNBA and give up her usual touches. She has been highly instrumental in Minnesota’s surge, as the team tries to advance to the WNBA Finals for the second time in three years. Miles is well on her way to becoming the sixth player in team history to be named Rookie of the Year, joining Betty Lennox (2000), Seimone Augustus (2006), Maya Moore (2011), Napheesa Collier (2019), and Crystal Dangerfield (2020). As of this writing, the Lynx are trailing the Valkyries in the third quarter. The post Lynx’s Olivia Miles passes WNBA legend for big milestone in game vs. Valkyries appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles.title: Raiders’ 53-man roster prediction for 2026 NFL season

The Raiders have invested heavily in reshaping the quarterback room and strengthening the offen
articles._body: The Las Vegas Raiders look dramatically different from the team that took the field a year ago. Klint Kubiak now faces the difficult task of squeezing an increasingly talented group into just 53 spots. The Raiders have invested heavily in reshaping the quarterback room and strengthening the offensive line. They have injected speed throughout the defense. Several previously overlooked players have also forced their way into serious roster consideration. The result is a fascinating mix of established veterans and ascending contributors. That makes for difficult cut decisions. Now, Las Vegas attempts to identify the group best equipped to support its new offensive identity and compete in a fiercely contested AFC West. Raiders’ finale David Brytus-Imagn Images Through the first two weeks of the 2026 NFL exhibition slate, the Las Vegas Raiders sit at an even 1-1 record. After dropping their preseason opener at Allegiant Stadium in a 27-14 loss to the Arizona Cardinals, Las Vegas rebounded with a gritty 22-20 road victory against the Houston Texans. The exhibition games have provided valuable extended reps for quarterback Fernando Mendoza. He showcased poise against Arizona and bounced back from early growing pains in Houston. Meanwhile, camp standouts such as wide receiver Malik Benson, defensive tackle Tonka Hemingway and running back Dylan Laube have translated their practice momentum into live-game production. That makes the preseason finale against San Francisco particularly important. The Raiders have enough established talent to feel confident about the top of the roster. Still, the bottom half remains filled with players fighting for their professional futures. Offensive Playmakers Quarterbacks (3): Kirk Cousins, Fernando Mendoza, Aidan O’Connell Cousins remains the established starter and provides the veteran command Kubiak wants. Mendoza represents an important long-term piece of the quarterback equation. O’Connell is the difficult luxury. Carrying three quarterbacks consumes a roster spot that could otherwise strengthen another position. Still, his experience makes him valuable insurance. Running Backs / Fullbacks (4): Ashton Jeanty, Mike Washington Jr, Dylan Laube, Connor Heyward Jeanty headlines a versatile backfield. He is the centerpiece, pending a return from injury . Meanwhile, Washington provides complementary early-down ability. Laube has done enough to earn continued consideration. Heyward’s versatility is particularly valuable in Kubiak’s system. The Raiders could theoretically save a roster spot by going lighter at the position. However, Heyward’s special-teams and schematic utility makes him difficult to remove. Wide Receivers (6): Tre Tucker, Jalen Nailor, Malik Benson, Jack Bech, Dont’e Thornton Jr, Dareke Young Benson’s breakout changes the receiver equation. He is the biggest development here. His dominant training camp has turned what initially looked like a depth battle into a clear roster case. His vertical acceleration and route precision give the Raiders another weapon capable of stretching defenses beyond the numbers. Tucker, Nailor, Bech and Thornton offer different dimensions. Young earns the final spot because of his special-teams value. Tight Ends (3): Brock Bowers, Michael Mayer, Ian Thomas Bowers and Mayer anchor the tight end room, for sure. Bowers is obviously the offensive centerpiece at the position. Mayer gives Kubiak a versatile second option capable of contributing as both a blocker and receiver. Thomas provides a more traditional inline presence. Offensive Line Offensive Line (9): Kolton Miller (LT), Spencer Burford (LG), Tyler Linderbaum (C), Jackson Powers-Johnson (RG), Delmar “DJ” Glaze (RT), Trey Zuhn III (Swing T/G), Charles Grant (OT), Caleb Rogers (OG), Jordan Meredith (IOL) This iteration of the offensive line reflects the team’s new investment. The starting five appears settled. Miller will be at left tackle, Burford at left guard, Linderbaum at center, Powers-Johnson at right guard, and Glaze at right tackle. The addition of Linderbaum gives the interior an immediate stabilizing presence. Zuhn, Grant, Rogers and Meredith provide the versatility needed to survive the attrition that inevitably comes along the offensive line. Defense Defensive Line / EDGE (4): Maxx Crosby, Kwity Paye, Malcolm Koonce, Keyron Crawford Four edge rushers headline the defense for the Raiders. Crosby remains the unquestioned defensive centerpiece, while Paye adds another explosive pass-rushing presence. Koonce provides valuable rotational juice, with Crawford rounding out the group. Defensive Tackles (6): Adam Butler, Jonah Laulu, Folorunso Fatukasi, Tonka Hemingway, Thomas Booker IV, Brandon Cleveland Hemingway earns his place inside. Hemingway has been one of the preseason’s biggest winners. His emergence gives the Raiders another disruptive interior option. Fatukasi provides the physical run-stopping presence needed in the AFC West. Butler, Laulu and Booker provide rotational versatility. Cleveland rounds out a group that should allow Kubiak’s defense to maintain fresh legs throughout games. Linebackers (4): Nakobe Dean, Quay Walker, Cody Lindenberg, Tommy Eichenberg Dean and Walker represent the headline additions. They should bring considerably more speed to the second level. Lindenberg and Eichenberg become especially valuable because of their special-teams contributions. Cornerbacks (6): Taron Johnson (Slot), Eric Stokes, Darien Porter, Decamerion Richardson, Hezekiah Masses, Jermod McCoy Six corners will provide flexibility for Las Vegas. Johnson gives them an established slot presence. Stokes and Porter provide the primary outside depth. Masses and McCoy have benefited from the increased opportunities created by Chigozie Anusiem’s move to injured reserve. articles.title: Dae’Quan Wright explains why he’s going from the NFL to an Ole Miss rival
articles.summary: Dae’Quan Wright finished Ole Miss’ College Football Playoff run without expecting to play another college game. The NFL was his only focus.
articles._body: Dae’Quan Wright finished Ole Miss’ College Football Playoff run without expecting to play another college game. The NFL was his only focus. A court ruling and an uncertain professional future changed the calculation. The Cleveland Browns waived Wright on Sunday, clearing a path for the former Ole Miss tight end to join LSU for an unprecedented fifth college season. Wright has an agreement with the Tigers if he clears NFL waivers and receives final clearance to play. “Honestly, after our college season was over, I really had no intention of playing another year,” Wright told 13WMAZ . “My focus was the NFL. “It wasn’t until a couple of weeks ago when they brought it back up and actually passed it that I started looking at the situation I was in. If I can go back another year, it would be helpful and beneficial to me.” Wright signed with the Philadelphia Eagles as an undrafted free agent after earning second-team All-SEC honors for Ole Miss last season. Philadelphia released him during training camp, and Cleveland claimed him off waivers. His agent, Drew Rosenhaus, said last week he didn’t expect Wright to make the Browns’ 53-man roster or be claimed again. Rosenhaus viewed another college season as an opportunity for Wright to return to the NFL Draft healthier and potentially improve his stock. Wright was among 33 athletes granted temporary protection from an NCAA rule prohibiting players who signed professional contracts from returning to college. Former Ole Miss defensive tackle Zxavian Harris and safety Wydett Williams Jr. joined him in the Louisiana lawsuit. Harris is headed to LSU, too, in what he deemed on social media a “business decision.”  Ole Miss had little interest in a reunion. Harris is apparently pushing 380 pounds and is dealing with the lingering effects of a foot injury that required surgery. The order created a route back to college football, but its timing left Wright making a career decision after participating in the NFL Combine, signing two professional contracts and spending nearly an entire training camp pursuing a roster spot. “A lot of people want to put the blame on us athletes, but it’s also bad timing by the people giving us the fifth year,” Wright said. “If they were going to pass this, they should have done it a long time ago. They should have done it earlier this year instead of letting people go to NFL teams. “Now it looks like you’re leaving a team and going back to college.” Wright said the unusual optics have not bothered him. “Never worry about the noise or what other people are saying,” he said. “Do what’s best for you.” LSU provides Wright with an immediate opportunity. The Tigers have concerns about their depth behind starting tight end Trey’Dez Green. Wright caught 39 passes for 635 yards last season and would bring two years of SEC experience to LSU’s offense. Head coach Lane Kiffin confirmed LSU has decided to recruit players made available by the recent court rulings. “At the end of the day, because of these rulings, they’re either going to play for you or they’re going to play somewhere else around the country,” Kiffin said. “We’ve made the decision to recruit them, like probably most people are.” Wright’s potential return remains subject to more than NFL waivers. The temporary restraining order is not a final decision, and questions remain about the application of SEC intraconference-transfer rules. “College athletes, not former professional athletes, have been at the heart of the Southeastern Conference,” the SEC said in a statement released Monday evening. “Individuals who choose to leave college athletics, sign professional playing contracts and compete professionally should not then be permitted to return to college competition. “College sports are for college athletes. The current confusion around national eligibility standards emphasizes the need to advance the Protect College Sports Act.” Ole Miss head coach Pete Golding indicated Monday the Rebels are evaluating late additions only at positions where injuries or depth create an identifiable need, specifically offensive line and cornerback. Ole Miss already has a crowded tight end room featuring Caleb Odom, Luke Hasz, Michael Smith, Brady Prieskorn and Hayden Bradley. Wright is focused on what another season could do for him beyond adding production. “I want to make the best of this opportunity because it really is a blessing,” Wright said. “Nobody knew this was going to happen. “I want to show how much I’ve grown, not just as an athlete, but as a person and a leader. I want to finish my career knowing I gave everything I had and have no regrets afterward.”

articles.title: How these 5 stats have shaped Valkyries’ impressive 2026 season
articles.summary: At this point in the season, we know what the Golden State Valkyries are all about– a vicious, defense-first team that relies on its depth, high-volume 3-point shooting, strength-in-numbers culture, and coaching to overwhelm opponents. That’s why they hold the second-best record in the league; it
articles._body: At this point in the season, we know what the Golden State Valkyries are all about – a vicious, defense-first team that relies on its depth, high-volume 3-point shooting, strength-in-numbers culture, and coaching to overwhelm opponents. That’s why they hold the second-best record in the league; it’s why they’ll be going to the playoffs once again in just their second season in the WNBA; and it’s why they are firmly in the title contender circle. But what story do the statistics and analytics tell about the Valkyries’ impressive 25-10 season thus far? How do they contextualize what makes Golden State so potent, and what makes them potentially vulnerable as the postseason quickly approaches? Here are five stats that have shaped the Valkyries’ season so far and what they may point to for how their season will finish. All statistics are accurate as of August 24. A closer look at the Valkyries’ shot selection, shot diet, and shot quality It’s pretty obvious that th e Valkyries are subscribers to the 3-point variance method of offense. They shoot a league-leading 30.6 3FGA per game, with 38.8% of their points coming from behind the 3-point line. And while they aren’t exactly the best at knocking them down, only seventh in the league in 3-point percentage (34.7%), they’re trying to take advantage of the math. The expected value of threes is more favorable than twos, and thus if you shoot a high volume of them, over time you’ll score more on average (at least in a statistical sense). However, if you dive into the Valkyries’ shot diet, they aren’t creating as big of an edge as you might think. According to The Shot Report, Golden State’s expected points per shot attempt, based on the types of shots they take, is 1.01 points per shot attempt, which ranks only seventh in the league. And while the margin between the Valkyries and the league-best Atlanta Dream is only four one-hundredths, Golden State’s total expected points from field goals per game ranks 10th in the W at only 68.8, which falls 5.7 behind the Dream, who rank first. There are two reasons for this. Firstly, the Valkyries don’t generate a lot of shot attempts. They generate a ton of 3s, but with their league-low 75.80 pace/40, they’re actually just below average when it comes to getting up shots and having more possessions. And secondly, the Valkyries don’t generate shots near and around the rim. Golden State averages only 17.6 shot attempts within five feet of the rim, the fewest in the league. Which by consequence, bogs down their “good look rate,” which The Shot Report identifies as the percentage of a team’s shot attempts that come from around the rim and from corner 3s, aka the highest-percentage looks on the court. The Valkyries only generate a 29.0% good look rate, third worst in the league. They do average 4.0 attempts from the two corners (tied for sixth), but because a lion’s share of their 3-point attempts comes from above the break (which are considered “neutral looks”), their 3-point volume isn’t quite giving them an advantage in expected value per shot attempt. What does this all mean? The Valkyries aren’t creating high-quality looks at the rim, and they’re making up for it by shooting a lot of 3s. As a result, the expected points edge you’d typically get from shooting a lot of threes is negated. Looking at a team like Atlanta, generating a 44.0% good-look rate on the season, they’re getting the best of both worlds. A league-best 32.2 FGAs at the rim and a fifth-best 26.6 3FGAs. Atlanta’s shot diet elevates their offense while the Valkyries’ barely keep them average. If the Valkyries can’t score, neither can their opponents. But while the Valkyries high-volume 3-point shot diet isn’t exactly creating an edge for them, their defense is dragging opponents into the mud with them. The Golden State defense does an excellent job of taking away opponents’ good looks and forcing them into “bad looks” (which The Shot Report classifies as midrange shots given the lower expected points value). Opponents’ midrange shot diet shifts by +2.0 pp while their high-value shots shift down by -7.5 pp, saving an average of 7.0 points compared to what each of their opponents is expected to score. The Valkyries allow only 14.8 FGAs at the rim , the lowest in the league, and 2.7 3FGAs from the corners, the second lowest in the league, taking away the highest-percentage looks on the floor . Add in the fact they allow the second fewest offensive rebounds (7.8) and the least amount of field goal attempts (62.4), and you can start to realize how they win games by essentially forcing teams to live and die by low-value looks on a limited number of possessions. That’s a credit to their scheme, coaching, scouting, and communication. Center Kiah Stokes in particular has been a linchpin to their defensive coverages , protecting the rim with her second-best 1.7 blocks a game and league-best 97.1 defensive rating among qualified players (more on her later). It’s also why coach Natalie Nakase emphasizes that everything runs through so much on the defensive end. Golden State actually ranks fourth-best in the league in transition points per play (1.12) but gets out on the break the least, with only 10.0% of their plays being transition opportunities (as of August 20). So when the defense is humming, it flows into the offense, allowing them to go on devastating runs. Neville E. Guard-Imagn Images The Valkyries’ shot difficulty is brutal The WNBA has finally begun tracking “shot difficulty ” this season, which uses tracking data to measure how difficult the shots a player is taking, quantified by expected field goal percentage (xFG%). The higher the xFG%, the easier, higher-quality, higher-percentage looks a player is consistently getting. Conversely, the lower the xFG%, the more difficult, low-quality, low-percentage looks a player gets. xFG% is not a field goal percentage; it’s a player’s baseline probability of making a shot based on the exac

articles.title: Greg McElroy: Alabama QB Keelon Russell ‘will be an All-SEC player’
articles.summary: Kalen DeBoer is putting the fate of Alabama’s 2026 season — and potentially his future in Tuscaloosa — in the hands of redshirt freshman Keelon Russell. The second-year player and former Five-Star Plus+ prospect was named the Crimson Tide’s starting quarterback for the team’s seaso
articles._body: Kalen DeBoer is putting the fate of Alabama’s 2026 season — and potentially his future in Tuscaloosa — in the hands of redshirt freshman Keelon Russell . The second-year player and former Five-Star Plus+ prospect was named the Crimson Tide’s starting quarterback for the team’s season opener over the weekend, beating out Washington transfer Austin Mack . The two were engaged in a competitive battle for the starting job, with DeBoer ultimately deciding that the high upside and pure ability of Russell was enough for him to win out. And despite being just a redshirt freshman, sky-high expectations are being put on Russell’s shoulders out of the gate. Alabama has College Football Playoff aspirations after being blown out by Indiana last year. And the only way for that to happen is for Russell to live up to the immense hype he has been receiving. That praise is coming from another former Alabama star now, too. On Monday night, ex-Crimson Tide quarterback and ESPN college football announcer Greg McElroy made a big statement about just how good he thinks Russell can be. “Austin Mack is a guy they have a ton of confidence faith in,” said McElroy. “I was told that he could be an All-SEC type of player. But Keelon Russell will be an All-SEC type of player. So they have two good quarterbacks there in Tuscaloosa, but the guy with the highest ceiling ended up winning it because of the wow plays he made throughout the entire fall camp. And especially since that first scrimmage, he has been on a moonshot over the last five or six practices, which resulted in him being named the starting quarterback.” Russell draws comparison to NFL star, former Heisman winner Russell, who has only attempted 11 career passes at the college level, now steps squarely into the spotlight in a critical year for DeBoer and the Crimson Tide program. Alabama returns a lot of talent on the offensive side of the ball, namely at receiver and tight end. However, they’ll be breaking in multiple new starters along the offensive line. And Russell’s ability to create plays with his feet could be a major asset as that group looks to gel together early in the season. On Monday night, former ESPN personality and NFL linebacker David Pollack draw parallels between Russell and ex-LSU quarterback and Heisman Trophy winner Jayden Daniels . Yet another big comparison. Russell, though, won’t shy away from it. The 6-foot-3, 181-pounder was the No. 2 overall prospect and No. 2 quarterback in the 2025 class. He won Elite 11 Finals MVP ahead of his senior season and rewrote the Texas high school state record books while throwing for 90 touchdowns across his final two seasons at the prep level.

articles.title: The Zay Flowers reason Torrey Smith doesn’t like No. 1 wide receiver label
articles.summary: Zay Flowers enters the 2026 season wealthier thanks to the Baltimore Ravens. Flowers now rakes in $140 million as the top wide receiver for Lamar Jackson. Yet former Raven Torrey Smith dropped a blunt take on the term “WR1.” Why? Because Smith isn’t fond of the term, stating the
articles._body: Zay Flowers enters the 2026 season wealthier thanks to the Baltimore Ravens. Flowers now rakes in $140 million as the top wide receiver for Lamar Jackson. Yet former Raven Torrey Smith dropped a blunt take on the term “WR1.” Why? Because Smith isn’t fond of the term, stating these reasons on Monday. “I hate the term No. 1 wide receiver. To me, it’s not about your numbers and your volume. It’s about what you add to your team,” Smith said on his podcast Level 82 TV. He later dipped into a deeper explanation on stating his case, including bringing up Cincinnati Bengals star Ja’Marr Chase. “You look at the league as a whole, you have some receivers who get over 1,000 yards with limited targets. And there are some receivers that may take one to 60 to get there,” Smith said. “Perfect example: Flowers had 118 targets last year and went over 1,200 yards. Yet Ja’Marr Chase who, most guys will say is the top dog in the league, had 1,400 yards but had 67 more targets. That is the equivalent of six or seven games for a No. 1 receiver.” Smith continued to back his claim about value rising as the most important factor. “So again, it’s not about numbers,” Smith said, “It’s about what value you add to your team.” Smith caught 319 total passes from 2011 to 2018. But grabbed 213 of those passes with the Ravens. He later lined up for the San Francisco 49ers, Philadelphia Eagles and Carolina Panthers. The past Maryland star won two Super Bowls in his career with the Ravens (2013 season) and Eagles (2017). articles.title: SEC pushes back on pros returning to college ahead of major Tuesday meeting
articles.summary: NFL players are being cut from training camp and entering the transfer portal. NBA players with signed two-way deals who were previously involved in trades are receiving injunctions to play college basketball. It’s a weird time to follow these sports we know and love — or thought we knew
articles._body: NFL players are being cut from training camp and entering the transfer portal. NBA players with signed two-way deals who were previously involved in trades are receiving injunctions to play college basketball. It’s a weird time to follow these sports we know and love — or thought we knew, at least. The SEC is taking a side in all of it ahead of a major meeting scheduled for Tuesday. “College athletes, not former professional athletes, have been at the heart of the Southeastern Conference. Individuals who choose to leave college athletics, sign professional playing contracts, and compete professionally should not then be permitted to return to college competition ,” the league announced in a statement following a Monday-evening videoconference of SEC presidents and chancellors. “Allowing that to occur will blur the line between college and professional sports, create significant competitive equity concerns, and reduce opportunities for high school and current college athletes. “ College sports are for college athletes. The current confusion around national eligibility standards emphasizes the need to advance the Protect College Sports Act.” The statement, which calls for action but doesn’t necessarily threaten it from the league, comes on the heels of two major pro-to-college moves in recent days — both involving LSU. Lane Kiffin and the football Tigers took a commitment from former Ole Miss tight end Dae’Quan Wright, who had been in training camp with the Cleveland Browns before he was cut. Will Wade and the basketball Tigers fought to get former St. John’s star RJ Luis eligible after he spent time with the Utah Jazz and Boston Celtics as an undrafted free agent in 2025, winning that court battle — for now, at least — with a ruling for a preliminary injunction to grant him immediate eligibility. Other cases are similar to varying degrees, including Mark Mitchell ‘s commitment to Kentucky after agreeing to an Exhibit-10 contract with Denver and suiting up for the Nuggets in the NBA Summer League, before a Louisville court issued a temporary restraining order allowing him to enter the transfer portal and join the Wildcats. It’s been an avalanche of lawsuits against the NCAA, mostly from high school class of 2022 student-athletes fighting for a fifth year, but not limited to that group, as Luis has shown. On3’s Pete Nakos reports that the call with SEC presidents and chancellors was “just for general discussion regarding the current eligibility situation in college sports” — but it set the tone for a massive in-person meeting in Birmingham on Tuesday. On3 contributor Ross Dellenger broke the news that SEC presidents and ADs will gather for the two-day meeting, which was scheduled weeks ago, “centering on an exploration into a conference-only governance model.” “Already seen as an unusual gathering, the meeting now takes on more significance as SEC leaders meet at a time of unrest,” he wrote, adding that the meeting’s original intent was to “create conference-only rules/enforcement” for transfers, eligibility and revenue-sharing “as a way to avoid the legal challenges.” Dellenger reports that substantial decisions are “unlikely” at this time, but considering the mass chaos and pushback — including a strong statement from the SEC tonight alone — who knows? It feels that was specifically in response to those LSU moves rather than Kentucky and Mitchell or some of these other fifth-years. After all, they are not “individuals who choose to leave college athletics,” but rather individuals whose eligibility was thought to be exhausted before courts decided the NCAA was in the wrong for leaving them out in 5-for-5. We know the SEC wants to hold firm on its intraconference transfer rules, specifically when it comes to entering the portal outside of a sport’s designated window , but does that apply to E-10 guys in basketball months before the season or NFL signees trying to play college football just days before games start? It’s all a mess, and the league hopes to get to the bottom of it in Birmingham over the next two days. We’ll see what that means exactly — and whether it impacts Mark Mitchell suiting up as a Wildcat.

articles.title: Injunction allows RJ Luis Jr. to play for LSU despite 2025 two-way NBA contract
articles.summary: LSU basketball has received a massive eligibility boost for the 2026-27 season after a Baton Rouge judge granted RJ Luis Jr. a preliminary injunction on Monday. The ruling temporarily prevents the NCAA from enforcing its eligibility ban and allows Luis to compete for the Tigers. Luis had challeng
articles._body: LSU basketball has received a massive eligibility boost for the 2026-27 season after a Baton Rouge judge granted RJ Luis Jr. a preliminary injunction on Monday. The ruling temporarily prevents the NCAA from enforcing its eligibility ban and allows Luis to compete for the Tigers. Luis had challenged the NCAA after being ruled ineligible because he signed a professional two-way contract with the Utah Jazz in 2025 . However, injuries prevented him from appearing in an NBA regular-season or G League game. The court also blocked the NCAA from imposing retroactive “restitution” penalties against LSU, allowing Luis to immediately join the Tigers and prepare for the upcoming season . The 2025 Big East Player of the Year began his college career at UMass after entering the 2022 high school class. He spent one season with the Minutemen before transferring to St. John’s, where he played two seasons. Luis entered the 2025 NBA Draft, went undrafted and subsequently signed with the Jazz. Luis did not participate in NBA Summer League because of an injury. Afterward, he was traded to the Boston Celtics and played in the preseason but never appeared in a regular-season or G League contest. The Celtics eventually waived him. During his first three college seasons, Luis appeared in 85 games, starting 52, while averaging 14.1 points, 5.6 rebounds, 1.5 assists and 1.3 steals per game on 43.9% shooting. In his final season with the Red Storm in 2024-25, he averaged 18.2 points per game. Luis now joins a LSU roster that also added former UCLA guard Donovan Dent, the 2025 Mountain West Player of the Year at New Mexico, along with transfers Divine Ugochukwu, Skyy Clark, Abdi Bashir Jr. and Mouhamed Dioubate. articles.title: Michael Jordan teammate preaches patience with Bulls’ young core
articles.summary: Horace Grant is one of the most beloved and passionate members of the Chicago Bulls family. Thirty-plus years after he wore red and black, Grant remains feverishly enthralled as he was then. That is especially true for this season. The Bulls will look different with new management, new coaching,
articles._body: Horace Grant is one of the most beloved and passionate members of the Chicago Bulls family. Thirty-plus years after he wore red and black, Grant remains feverishly enthralled as he was then. That is especially true for this season. The Bulls will look different with new management, new coaching, and a new desire to build for the future. They added rookie Caleb Wilson into the mix of Matas Buzelis, Josh Giddey, Norman Powell, and Nic Claxon. Fans naturally want instant gratification. However, Grant is using his experience to foster calm , especially since they haven’t tipped off yet, per Kyle Odegard of Action Network. He cited the time it took to build chemistry among the first three-peat teams (1991 to 1993). “To go back iconic like we did back in the day, it’s going to take some work,” Grant said. “It’s going to take some patience. But with the core they have now, staying healthy, and then I still think they need a little bit more leadership in that locker room. I played with some great leaders in Chicago. MJ, Pip, Bill Cartwright, you can throw John Paxson in there as well. Once Michael Jordan was surrounded by Scottie Pippen, Bill Cartwright, John Paxson, Grant and others, the results spoke for themselves. “The city is going to have to stay patient, because they are a very young crew,” Grant said. “I tell people this: when Scottie and I first got there in ‘87, we were getting our heads knocked in by the Detroit Pistons almost every year. It took patience. It took trust in each other, and then the rest is history.” Last season, team chemistry enabled the Bulls to a spectacular start to the year at 6-1. Let’s see if that comes again this October. The post Michael Jordan teammate preaches patience with Bulls’ young core appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles.title: 1 last-minute trade Raiders must make before Week 1 of 2026 NFL season
articles.summary: With the first regular-season game of new head coach Klint Kubiak’s tenure fast approaching, the Las Vegas Raiders are still working on finalizing their roster. GM John Spytek continues to tinker with the team, as a notable transaction on Monday went to the receiver room. Just eight days af
articles._body: With the first regular-season game of new head coach Klint Kubiak’s tenure fast approaching, the Las Vegas Raiders are still working on finalizing their roster. GM John Spytek continues to tinker with the team, as a notable transaction on Monday went to the receiver room. Just eight days after signing him, the Raiders released veteran receiver Noah Brown. The move leaves the Raiders very light in experience with their wide receiving group. Spytek signed former Minnesota Vikings wideout Jalen Nailor this offseason, yet most of the depth is a mixture of recent draft picks. Tre Turner and Jack Bech look like they’ll begin the season alongside Nailor as starters. Dont’e Thornton Jr. and Malik Brown, the latter a sixth-round pick in this past April’s NFL Draft, are also set to play featured roles in Kubiak’s attack. Despite all of the potential in the Raiders’ receiving room, the need for a true number one receiver is painfully obvious. While one of these young receivers could emerge into the role, Kubiak could use a top guy right now. With veteran Kirk Cousins holding down the fort at quarterback for now, there’s no need to rush 2026 No.1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza. While the league might be short of true number one receivers that could be had via trade, there are some wideouts out there with the potential to grow into the role quickly. One name should interest the Raiders in particular: Jacksonville Jaguars wide receiver Brian Thomas Jr. As the Jaguars look to make a postseason return once again in 2026, would they be willing to part ways with Thomas Jr. so close to the start of the regular season? Brian Thomas Jr. could give Fernando Mendoza a long-term top target Corey Perrine/Florida Times-Union / USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn Images The Jaguars’ 2024 first-round pick, Thomas Jr., had an electric rookie season. A stat line of 87 catches for 1,282 yards and ten touchdowns. Even though the Jaguars failed to make the playoffs, it was clear that Jacksonville had the pieces to help them get back. After head coach Liam Coen was hired last offseason, the hype around Thomas Jr. climbed. Many thought the ex-LSU star would have a monster sophomore season. Yet, injuries and ineffectiveness hamstrung Thomas Jr. in 2025. In 14 games, he caught 48 balls for 707 yards and two touchdowns. A severe drop-off across the board, especially disappointing considering the excellent rookie campaign in 2024. Now, as Thomas Jr. enters year three, trade rumors have swirled around him. The question of whether he’ll be able to succeed under Coen has been asked at least a few times by now. Would a new home entering his third NFL season help him put the disappointment of last fall behind him? In Las Vegas, Thomas Jr. would be given the room to get back towards that 2024 form. Kubiak got a career year out of another former first-rounder last year in Jaxon Smith-Njigba. While it’s unclear that Kubiak’s scheme could guarantee that type of jump for Thomas Jr., growing alongside Mendoza could be the start of a foundational partnership. Add in other offensive pieces, like running back Ashton Jeanty, tight end Brock Bowers, and center Tyler Linderbaum, and the Raiders could have some major core pieces on offense. It’s up to Kubiak and Mendoza to get everything to click. If Spytek can trade for Thomas Jr., or another potential top target, then the odds in Vegas may flip into the Raiders’ favor. The 10 Giants roster moves included three IL placements, one bereavement-list placement, one option, and five recalls from Triple-A Sacramento. In a Monday article, MLB Tra
articles._body: The San Francisco Giants announced 10 roster moves Monday after the Boston Red Sox completed a weekend sweep at Fenway Park. The 10 Giants roster moves included three IL placements, one bereavement-list placement, one option, and five recalls from Triple-A Sacramento. In a Monday article, MLB Trade Rumors’ Anthony Franco detailed the roster overhaul following Boston’s sweep. “San Francisco placed Willy Adames (left elbow sprain), JT Brubaker (bruised ribs) and Victor Bericoto (bone bruise in right knee) on the injured list,” Franco wrote. “Adames and Bericoto land on the 10-day IL, while Brubaker will miss a minimum of 15 days. San Francisco also placed Bryce Eldridge on the bereavement list and optioned rookie southpaw Tugboat Wilkinson.” The Red Sox sweep left the Giants at 52-78 and raised concern about Adames’ injury. Adames hurt his left elbow during an awkward slide in Sunday’s finale. Victor Bericoto sustained a right knee bone bruise, while JT Brubaker bruised his ribs diving for a foul ball. Matt “Tugboat” Wilkinson allowed four earned runs across 3 2/3 innings as the Red Sox pulled off a 5-4 comeback on Sunday. Franco also identified the five recalls from the organization’s minor league affiliate: “To fill those active roster spots, the Giants recalled five players from Triple-A Sacramento: Nate Furman, Grant McCray, Anthony Molina, Ryan Walker and Shay Whitcomb.” Each recalled player owns major league experience. Anthony Molina and Shay Whitcomb could make their Giants debuts if either appears. Meanwhile, Nate Furman, Grant McCray, and Ryan Walker have already played for San Francisco. Altogether, the transactions reshaped nearly 20% of the active roster. The Giants returned home Monday to open a series vs. the Cincinnati Reds with their reshuffled group. San Francisco stands fourth in the National League West and 27.5 games behind the Los Angeles Dodgers. Therefore, the remaining schedule gives the organization opportunities to evaluate its Sacramento depth. Ted Cruz (R-Texas), only to be opposed by conferences like the Big Ten and SEC. There are supporters, though, and one of the bigger names is Nick Saban . Monday was another example, as Saban explained that the PCSA is “certainly 100 times better than what we have now.” These comments are fresh off players who were in NFL training camps jumping back into college football. Saban says the bill passing would solve a lot of the problems at hand. [ $19.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage ] “I think a lot of the issues that we have right now could be resolved in this bill, if people would get on board with it,” Saban said . “But it’s not perfect. But the thing about it is, democracy is not perfect, but it’s better than everything else. Tell me something better. This bill is not perfect, but it’s better than everything else, and it’s certainly 100 times better than what we have now, and it probably solves 80% of the problems. We want to stay focused on 20% of the problems that it doesn’t solve. But if you just solve one transfer, control NIL to some degree in terms of a level playing field and five years of eligibility, you would answer your own question about the guy from the Cleveland Browns. Five years of eligibility.” Nick Saban explains why he does not get into politics Shortly before discussing the PCSA, Saban was asked if he would ever want to get into the political world. It’s something we have seen in the state of Alabama before, as Tommy Tuberville is the former Auburn head coach. Saban retired from coaching following the 2023 season before getting into the media world. SUBSCRIBE to the On3 NIL and Sports Business Newsletter Turns out, his work in the media is why politics is not of interest. Saban said he enjoys being on ESPN College GameDay, talking football with Rece Davis, Pat McAfee, Desmond Howard, and Kirk Herbstreit. It’s not something he wants to give up. “Why would I want to get thrown into that briarpatch? I like what I’m doing right now,” Saban said. “I mean, I speak, I’ve got businesses, I love being on ESPN. Got a great group of guys to be around every single Saturday. There’s no consequence — we never lose a game. So, why would I get involved in that?”

The former Washington Huskies star signal-caller has already
articles._body: The Atlanta Falcons still have an ongoing quarterback quandary , and the competition for the QB1 role is about to get more intense for the NFC South franchise with Michael Penix Jr. taking a big step in his progress from his ACL injury. The former Washington Huskies star signal-caller has already been cleared for full practice , the first time he’s been given such clearance after going under the knife in November 2025 to repair a left ACL injury. The Falcons have Tua Tagovailoa, who signed a one-year, $1.3 million contract with the team in the offseason, but he hasn’t been exactly impressing people in practices and in the preseason. Tagovailoa’s struggles in the offseason with the team have made it seemingly “impossible” for the Falcons to wait several weeks into the 2026 NFL season before they can start deploying Penix under center, according to insider Ian Rapoport of the NFL Network. “Remember, it’s still nine months or so from the ACL tear. Really, you’d like him to be inactive for the first several games and really just take his time and make sure he’s fully healthy. Tua’s play made that impossible, not just in the preseason game, which we’ve seen, but sounds like practice as well,” Rapoport said. “All of which is to say, this is Michael Penix’s job for the taking. If he comes out and plays as well as he can, it actually could create the best-case scenario for the Atlanta Falcons.” From The Insiders on @NFLNetwork : Michael Penix Jr now has a chance to win the starting job for the #Falcons , which would be great news for the organization. pic.twitter.com/rVvQHU1jLX — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) August 24, 2026 The Falcons have one more preseason game to play, which is a date with the Miami Dolphins on the road this coming Friday. It is possible that Atlanta will wait until the last few days of the offseason to announce its QB1 decision, but it is clear that Penix will get his chance to prove himself as the team’s long-term answer under center The post Falcons fans will love Ian Rapoport’s Michael Penix Jr. evaluation appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles.title: Veteran Nashville Music Journalist and Author Vernell Hackett Dies at 77
articles.summary: During her career, Hackett worked with artists including Chris LeDoux and Dale Ann Bradley.
articles._body: Veteran music journalist Vernell Hackett , a longtime chronicler of Nashville’s top music artists, died on Aug. 14 in Chicago, after suffering from cardiac arrest. Hackett was 77. Related Dale Morris, Nashville Manager Who Guided Careers of Alabama & Kenny Chesney, Dies at 89 Yung Miami Is Ready for Her Solo Debut Thanks to 'Spend Dat': 'People Are About to Eat Their Words' Capitol Christian Music Group Celebrates 50-Year Anniversary, Holds Annual Partner Summit in Nashville Born Vernell Dell Boswank, she grew up in the small Texas town of Riesel, and graduated from Sam Houston State University in Huntsville, Texas.  Though she initially had plans to pursue a career in crime reporting, her passion for music led her on a path to becoming a top music journalist. She and her husband Ken relocated to Buffalo, N. Y., to live closer to his family, before relocating to Nashville. Hackett worked for booking agent Tandy Rice at Top Billing International, where Rice represented artists including Dolly Parton , Jim Ed Brown , Jerry Clower , Porter Wagoner, Jeannie C. Riley, Tom T. Hall and others. Hackett was known for her heartfelt and vivid storytelling, her deep connections with artists and songwriters, and her passion for music and creativity. Hackett’s work in journalism included time as an editor of Country News , Country Rhythms and American Songwriter magazines. Hackett was a co-founder of American Songwriter magazine, and she served as the publication’s editor-in-chief for over a decade. She also freelanced for many publications, as well as radio syndicators. During her career, Hackett also worked in public relations, including time as part of the Country Music Association’s communications department. In the 1980s, Hackett worked with a young rodeo cowboy by the name of Chris LeDoux , who also dreamed of being a country music singer. LeDoux went on to earn the top 10 Billboard Country Airplay chart hit “Whatcha Gonna Do With A Cowboy” in 1992, while his song “Cadillac Ranch” reached the chart’s top 20 in 1993. LeDoux passed away in 2005, and Garth Brooks honored LeDoux’s memory with the song “Good Ride Cowboy.” Hackett also represented artists including bluegrass artist Dale Ann Bradley , Americana duo Jesse and Noah, nitty gritty dirt band founding member John McEuen , and singer-songwriters Ryan Murphey, Joni Harms and Randy Huston. She was also an author, writing books including a biography of Carrie Underwood . She also penned the book Ghosts, Gangsters and Gamblers of Las Vegas , with her longtime friends and colleagues Liz Cavanaugh and Michelle Honick . Beyond music, Hackett was a champion for animal rights, working with rescue shelters and supporting the Robyn’s Nest shelter. Many years ago, after Hackett asked that friends bring dog food in lieu of gifts to her birthday party, a longtime tradition was started, which ultimately resulted in thousands of pounds of pet food, as well as monetary donations, being made to Robyn’s Nest. “Vernell was my close personal friend for decades. Sometimes, we would talk two or three times a week,” The Oak Ridge Boys ’ Duane Allen said in a statement. “The last week of her life, she sent a beautiful poem that was suitable to hang on any wall. She was always positive. I sent her a funny video of a very small dog singing and a big dog hitting the small dog with flip-flops. Vernell and I had three things in common. She loved the Lord, her friends and animals. I look forward to seeing her in Heaven, rejoicing with our many mutual friends, and I can imagine that there will be many of our four-legged friends to keep us company.” Musician Michael Martin Murphey added in a statement, “Vernell Hackett was the kindest, most down-to-earth journalist and human being I’ve ever known. She had a sense of what the common, everyday country music fan is looking for in a story…Vernell went out of her way to support me on my journey.” “Very sad to hear about Vernell’s passing; she was always so very kind to us, and we feel privileged to have known her through the years,” said David Bellamy of The Bellamy Brothers said in a statement. “We send prayers and condolences to her family and loved ones.” Hackett is survived by her nephew Glen Boswank (Nashville, Tennessee) and niece Katy Prewitt (Kaufman, Texas).

articles._body: Just two games out of the final NL Wild Card spot, the Arizona Diamondbacks just finished off a three-game series win over the visiting Cincinnati Reds with a 5-3 win on Sunday. Now, the Diamondbacks will look to continue their climb up the standings with another series win over a visiting NL Central club, the Chicago Cubs. Following the Cubs series, Arizona will travel to San Francisco for a four-game set with their division rivals, the Giants. By this time next week, the Diamondbacks will be due a potential big boost to their lineup. According to MLB insider Francys Romero on X (formerly Twitter), second baseman Ketel Marte is tentatively expected to be activated next Tuesday ahead of a home series against the Philadelphia Phillies. “Ketel Marte is tentatively expected to be activated next Tuesday, when the D-backs open their series against the Phillies in Arizona,” reported Romero on Monday evening. “The infielder began his knee rehab last Friday in Arizona, putting him on track for a potential return.” Marte has been a source of consistent drama for the Diamondbacks over the last few days. The veteran second baseman, subject of numerous trade rumors over the last 12-18 months, left the team once they got to Boston to play the Red Sox. After a stint on the restricted list, Arizona transferred him to the IL after an MRI revealed left knee inflammation. The controversy surrounding Marte swelled late last week when the former All-Star was seen at a nearby casino while the Diamondbacks played a home game. Now, with Arizona pushing for a postseason return, the question is: will Marte be locked in for a potential October run? Reports indicate that many on the team are not happy with the star second baseman. With one of the most pivotal offseasons in MLB history approaching, Marte could go down a number of paths. If he returns and truly contributes to the Diamondbacks’ playoff push once again, then the futures of both parties could be a lot brighter. articles._body: Taylor Swift has made a name for herself as a singer/songwriter for the past two decades exploring different genres of music, including pop, indie, country and other styles. But she says her country roots have only become more meaningful to her over time. During a conversation at the Grammy Museum presented by the Recording Academy’s Songwriters & Composers Wing on Aug. 18 (which was just released in full on YouTube), Swift fondly reflected on the songwriter she was when she released her debut single, “Tim McGraw,” and the artist she has become nearly two decades later. When asked by Recording Academy CEO Harvey Mason jr. what has remained the same and what has changed between herself then and now, Swift pointed to the country foundation that assisted in the launching of her career. Related Adam Scott Reveals the Impression Taylor Swift & Travis Kelce’s Wedding Left on Him Who Should Win Video of the Year at the 2026 MTV Video Music Awards? Vote! Taylor Swift Breaks Record for Most Adult Pop Airplay No. 1s With ‘I Knew It, I Knew You’ “I’ve loved — and I think this can happen as you grow up — my country roots more and more,” Swift said. “The further along this path I get, I want to honor them more and more, and I feel more and more tied and more loyal to them — the people that shaped who I am as an artist and as a writer.” Those roots, Swift noted, trace back to Nashville, where she developed her identity as a songwriter. Earlier in the conversation, she recalled becoming fascinated with the city at around age 10 after learning that Faith Hill had been discovered at the Bluebird Cafe. Swift made it a personal goal to perform at the famed Nashville venue, while also teaching herself instruments and writing songs by studying the structures of the music she loved. That early immersion in country music did influence the picturesque storytelling that would become one of the distinctive and beloved attributes of Swift’s songwriting. Looking back at “Tim McGraw,” she pointed to elements of the song that seemingly foreshadowed the kind of writer she would eventually become, including character work, vivid detailing and the way the song moves through time. “I was 16 putting out an album in country music that was all about my life as a kid in high school,” Swift explained during the conversation, recalling how some people around her questioned whether a teenager writing about her own life would connect with country’s music presumed audience. She decided to trust her instincts rather than conforming to those expectations. Swift famously pushed far beyond the country genre once her debut album ignited. Audiences first saw her experimenting with her 2012 album Red , straying away from traditional collaborators and sounds before she made her official pop pivot with 2014’s 1989 , both of which debuted atop the Billboard 200 . Even as her music evolved, however, the songwriting principles she refined in Nashville remained part of her creative groundwork. She pointed to “Mean,” from 2010’s Speak Now , as one example of how her country background directly influenced her approach. At the time, one criticism she was hearing was that she wasn’t “country enough,” so she responded by leaning into the genre’s sonic characteristics, joking that she put “just as much banjo on this as we can possibly put.” That willingness to experiment did lead her to some of the more unexpected genre combinations of her career. Swift spoke about bringing the earworm hit “I Knew You Were Trouble.” to Max Martin and Shellback as a sad piano ballad, only for the producers to suggest turning it into somewhat of a dubstep-influenced track. She agreed to try it, and the result become the biggest turning point of her moving away from the country genre. Nearly 20 years after “Tim McGraw,” Swift seems to be looking back at her country beginnings with renewed appreciation. Watch the full conversation with The Recording Academy below. In addition to the Q&A with Mason, Swift also threw things back to her Eras Tour days by mashing up her Toy Story 5 song “I Knew It, I Knew You,” “August” and “All Too Well” on the very piano she brought out for the acoustic section of that show.
