articles.title: How Zion Williamson’s Pelicans can change ‘toughness’ conversation this season
articles.summary: Toughness is one of those NBA words that can mean almost anything until a team is forced to prove it. EVP Joe Dumars has said the word so often this offseason that it has become shorthand for everything the Zion Williamson-era New Orleans Pelicans are trying to fix. They have heard the outside no
articles._body: Toughness is one of those NBA words that can mean almost anything until a team is forced to prove it. EVP Joe Dumars has said the word so often this offseason that it has become shorthand for everything the Zion Williamson-era New Orleans Pelicans are trying to fix. They have heard the outside noise. Skepticism about their durability from a beleaguered fanbase, and about their ceiling with Dejounte Murray, Trey Murphy, and Herb Jones through the trade market has been noted, stored away for the summer’s workout fuel. However, it’s what Dumars has consistently said inside the building that stands out. Basically, it’s a question of heart over whether this collection of talent can ever translate assumed potential into sustained winning. Toughness might be the word that determines whether this season becomes another exercise in explaining away disappointment or the beginning of the turnaround the front office believes is much closer than the standings suggest. “We are going to build. We are going to win. We don’t believe we are that far away from winning. We had a tremendous amount of very close games that we should have won,” Dumars admitted in April. “I feel that we are close enough. But it takes some work. To the fans, I’d say I understand being discouraged. But I firmly believe we are going to win, and I don’t think this is some long rehaul process.” The Pelicans went just 10-24 in 34 clutch games. That is a lot of competitive basketball followed by a lot of empty trips back to the locker room. Woeful third quarters became a trend. Being so close yet fallen so far behind the NBA Play-In pack, it was hard not to conclude that there is one thing missing. “I would add more toughness to this team,” stressed Dumars. “We have to be able to compete every night. We cannot get banged around, pushed around. We have to be physical and compete every night. There were some nights we did it, but too many nights we didn’t compete at a high enough level for me. You can’t get past that in this league. We have talent. But if you think you’re just going to roll talent out on an NBA court and that’s all you need to do to win, that’s not going to happen.” It is going to take more than Jamahl Mosley taking over as coach and DeAndre Jordan in free agency to convince fans to fill the Smoothie King Center, though. Given the lack of moves this offseason, the Pelicans have bet that the locker room has a lot more to give than has been demonstrated. Every player must bring a bit more of an edge, a seriousness to the squad next season…or it’ll all fall apart before Christmas. Group project this may be, Williamson will get all of the blame if this blows up. Zion Williamson’s showing work Matthew Hinton-Imagn Images Williamson’s camp (mainly trainer Kris Chrisp) has been releasing more workout footage this offseason than in any previous summer. Fans should appreciate deliberate signals that the 26-year-old forward is attacking his preparation with a new level of professionalism. Dumars does. “To be great, you have to be obsessed with this,” Dumars explained. “You can’t casually become great in this league. What I’ve seen from him this summer is that he’s obsessed with the work he’s putting in. And that is really encouraging for me that he’s putting this type of work in.” There has never been much question about whether Williamson is physically strong enough for the NBA. The power/point forward might be one of the strongest players in professional sports. However, questions have always lingered about whether he could make that strength available often enough to matter. The habits in those videos need to survive road trips from Thanksgiving through Mardi Gras for the Pelicans to succeed . That conversation changed somewhat last season. Williamson appeared in 62 games, the second-highest total of his career, while averaging 21 points, 5.7 rebounds, and 3.2 assists. The Pelicans still lost; he took the blame. Clearing the 65-game All-NBA threshold has to be the goal moving forward. At least then New Orleans will not have to spend another spring wondering what its roster might have looked like had its best player actually been available. Winning back fans requires a bit more, well, toughness in conditioning, in running back on defense instead of complaining about a foul, in rebounding when the Pelicans go small, and accepting that being the most talented player on the roster also means setting the physical standard for everyone else. Do all of that, and nothing less, and the fans will come back around. If Williamson gets to around 70 games, is obsessive with the details, and plays with the physicality Dumars is preaching, the rest of the toughness equation gets much easier to solve. Doubting Dejounte Murray Matthew Hinton-Imagn Images Only a select, unfortunate few can even understand toughness quite like Dejounte Murray. His introduction to New Orleans became a nightmare almost immediately. Murray’s mother suffered a stroke shortly before his first regular-season game with the Pelicans. He then broke his left hand in that opener and missed 17 games. A cousin was killed. An uncle died from an overdose. His right Achilles tendon ruptured in January 2025. Murray later described that stretch as the worst three months of his professional career on and off the court. Basketball became secondary. Instead of shutting down completely, getting himself back became the challenge; those 14 games at the end of a lost season helped with the healing process. “I worked my tail off to even be in a position to play,” Murray shared. Navigating circumstances bigger than sports is something New Orleans does very well. Finding a way to channel pain back into a positive is at the very essence of the city’s history. articles.title: Rust, reset and a revamped Evan Stewart: Oregon’s offense rebounds after weekend scrimmage
articles.summary: Oregon offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer has refocused his side of the ball after the defense got the edge in the final scrimmage of fall camp.
articles._body: Oregon offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer met with the media on Monday afternoon following the second and final scrimmage of fall camp on Saturday. While the defense held the edge coming out of the tilt, the offense has regrouped to start the week. “I think our theme after that was reset, refocus, and those guys did that,” Mehringer said. “I thought we had a much better day today. The execution and detail and all the things that you’re looking for were a lot higher.” Mehringer and the offense are still sorting through their options behind Jamari Johnson at tight end heading into week 1 and he had some interesting insight on the pace at which players develop in his old room. “I think we’ve seen a lot of good things from all those guys. Coach (Jack) Smith has done a really good job in that room, helping me out there. And I think that the tight end position kind of grows a little bit slower than others, just because aside from throwing the football, they do pretty much everything else. So there’s a lot of skill and a lot of knowledge you gotta acquire, and so all three of those kids have done a really, really good job… I think it’s a really good room that will continue developing it better.” Both Gatlin Bair and Evan Stewart haven’t played a live game in over a year but Mehringer didn’t seem too concerned with where either player is at given the live competition they’re both facing in practice. “I think it’s been great. I do think that I’ve had three knee surgeries in my lifetime, we’re talking about Evan. I certainly didn’t haven’t taken a two-year mission like Gatlin, but I think that anytime you go through periods of time without playing, even if it’s just for our guys coming off of summer break for a week, there’s always going to be a little bit of rust, right? And both of those guys have had a great attitude and great intention on improving their game as fast as possible. So I’ve been really proud of both those kids.” Stewart’s growth from 2025 to 2026 has been a major talking point heading into the year and Mehringer has seen him continue to mature in how he carries himself. “Evan does not lack confidence at all. Evan’s grown so much in the sense that his cockiness doesn’t turn into arrogance at all. He has confidence in his ability to go do it, but he wants to be coached and he wants to get better and he wants to develop. He doesn’t want to walk off the practice field and nobody said anything to him about how he can improve his performance. He rarely has bad days. He’s got a big smile on his face. He dances and he sang all the lyrics to Party in the USA or something like that last night. He’s a stud. I love being around Evan.” The veteran wideout changing how he’s approached things and his work ethic have been two big tweaks that could lead to a big year on the field for the explosive wideout. “Evan changed almost all of his work habits, and he’s had an unbelievable camp for us,” the Oregon offensive coordinator said. “He’s an extremely hard worker, but he hasn’t changed who he is…he’s worked his tail off, playing a number of different positions for us right now. More than he did for us in 2024. So I’m really excited about the season that he’s going to have for us, and very proud of him for the way that he’s worked. So we’re pumped.”

articles.title: Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur reveals ‘cool’ plan ahead of Packers joint practice
articles.summary: The Arizona Cardinals have gone through three preseason games so far under first-year head coach Mike LaFleur. LaFleur was not happy with the Cardinals’ last performance against the Dallas Cowboys. Now, he is preparing for a week of joint practices with the Green Bay Packers, who are coache
articles._body: The Arizona Cardinals have gone through three preseason games so far under first-year head coach Mike LaFleur. LaFleur was not happy with the Cardinals’ last performance against the Dallas Cowboys . Now, he is preparing for a week of joint practices with the Green Bay Packers, who are coached by his brother Matt LaFleur. One Monday, the younger LaFleur revealed a fun plan for his Cardinals when they arrive at Packers camp , per Donnie Druin of On SI. “It’s a cool place. They got the bikes with the kids and stuff like that, and that’s for a cool cause for the locals. And so we’ll do that too, just like a lot of the other teams do when they joint [practice]. And then there’s a ton of fans there. I mean, it’s Green Bay. What else you gonna do?” LaFleur said. Matt and Mike have been close, but have coached together just once, as both were on the Atlanta Falcons staff in 2015 and 2016. The younger brother also noted that he does love Green Bay and his kids are excited to see their Aunt Bre to get all the snacks. Mike also took some playoff jabs at his brother , speaking to the media, per Rob Demovsky. “If there’s an issue, I’m going to tell the guys, ‘Hey, you come tag me in. They can tag in my brother. And we’ll throw down on the 50,'” Matt said. “I think it’s going to be pretty special, but at the end of the day, we’re just looking to try to get good work on both sides. Certainly, always going to prioritize the Green Bay Packers but if there is another team in the National Football League that I’ll be rooting for, it will be the Arizona Cardinals.” The Cardinals and Packers are set to face off on Friday night. articles.title: Bulls legend gushes over Caleb Wilson’s ‘killer’ quality
articles.summary: Almost everyone in Chicago is excited about Caleb Wilson. Undoubtedly, the No.4 draft pick by the Bulls is expected to do great things. One of those beaming with glee is Bulls legend Horace Grant. On Monday, Grant was thrilled that the Bulls got Wilson, per Kyle Odegard of Action Network. Mainly,
articles._body: Almost everyone in Chicago is excited about Caleb Wilson . Undoubtedly, the No.4 draft pick by the Bulls is expected to do great things. One of those beaming with glee is Bulls legend Horace Grant. On Monday, Grant was thrilled that the Bulls got Wilson, per Kyle Odegard of Action Network. Mainly, he admired Wilson’s “killer instincts. “Oh my goodness, man,” Grant said. “What a beast. What a freakin’ beast. He has all the intangibles, the skillset. But what I love about him is that he has the mindset of a killer. A dog. He goes out and gets it.” In the same breath, Grant said that this was the best move the franchise made in years involving a certain someone. Additionally, Grant didn’t go too far in saying Wilson was up to par with a few of his contemporaries. “It’s one of the best draft picks since Derrick Rose. I’m not going to put him with MJ and myself and Pip, but since Derrick Rose, one of the greatest choices the Bulls have made, in my humble opinion.” Grant played for the Bulls from 1987 to 1994 and won three titles. In 2008, Rose was selected as the No.1 draft pick. He would go on to solidify his place amongst the Bulls’ best . Meanwhile, Wilson is fresh off a standout NBA Summer League . He averaged 23.5 points, 7.3 rebounds, and 2.5 blocks per game. “When you showcase yourself like that, especially in the Summer League, it gives us Bulls fans hope that he will be one of those pieces along with Josh (Giddey) and (Matas) Buzelis,” Grant said. “There are more pieces that we need, but man, what I saw in Vegas, he’s the real deal.” In the end, Wilson was named to the NBA All-Summer League First Team. articles.title: Kyle Petty defends Wood Brothers’ Josh Berry decision with brutal assessment
articles.summary: Kyle Petty delivers a blunt assessment of Josh Berry and explains why he believes Wood Brothers made the right call choosing Jesse Love for 2027.
articles._body: Kyle Petty isn’t among those who feel the Wood Brothers are making a mistake by replacing Josh Berry after the 2026 season with Jesse Love.  The former NASCAR driver delivered what he feels is a truth bomb for fans, and even Berry.  On Inside the Race , Petty dropped a searing hot take on Berry. Essentially, it’s too little, too late for the 35-year-old soon-to-be free agent. Petty gives Josh Berry hot take Recency bias be damned, Petty doesn’t care that Berry has four consecutive top tens.  He doesn’t care that it’s the first time for Wood Brothers since Morgan Shepherd did it in 1994.  “I think Josh Berry is a good race car driver,” said Petty. “I don’t think Josh Berry is a great race car driver.  “He averaged like a 27th place finish in the first 21 races of the year and now he’s averaged fifth.” Ceiling over floor For Petty, Wood Brothers made the right decision because of future potential.  Petty pointed to not just Jesse Love, but also Connor Zilisch as the future of the sport vs. a 35-year-old Berry.  “I think the potential that a Jesse Love has, the potential that these younger drivers have, there’s a lot more blue sky for them than there is for Josh Berry.  “When you get to 29 or 30 now, if you’re not winning races, sorry. We’re not all Jeff Gordon. “We’re not all Jimmie Johnson who go to a place and stay your entire career.”  Not an audition Hard to agree with Petty on a lot of things, but this might be the hardest. He said that Berry is not auditioning for his next job. He’s been auditioning all along, and therefore, he is what he is. “You audition every time you set your butt in one of these things for what your next ride is going to be.” ‘Just watch the races’ After Sunday’s P3 finish at New Hampshire , Berry said that’s all it takes despite what Petty said. Just watch Josh Berry in these races if you question whether he belongs in the Cup Series. “You just watch the races,” said Berry to Dustin Albino . “I don’t know what else you can say. I’ve been pretty honest about my feelings with how this stuff works.  “It just boils down to finding someone that believes in me that I can do this. Unfortunately, most of the time, it comes down to how much money you have to find opportunities.  “Hopefully, something is out there for me.” And there’s a lot of NASCAR that are hoping the same thing for Berry.

articles.title: Skip Bayless calls for Browns to trade Shedeur Sanders to NFC team
articles.summary: Sports personality Skip Bayless was not happy with the Cleveland Browns’ decision involving quarterback Shedeur Sanders ahead of the 2026 NFL season. Sanders is preparing for the second season of his career with the Browns. He garnered some starts as a rookie, showing flashes of what he can
articles._body: Sports personality Skip Bayless was not happy with the Cleveland Browns’ decision involving quarterback Shedeur Sanders ahead of the 2026 NFL season. Sanders is preparing for the second season of his career with the Browns. He garnered some starts as a rookie, showing flashes of what he can bring to the table in the league. Sanders was competing with Deshaun Watson for the starting job throughout training camp and the preseason. Head coach Todd Monken named Watson the starting quarterback over Sanders going into Week 1, meaning a lot of eyes will be on the veteran to have his healthiest campaign in a Browns jersey. Bayless, an open fan of the Dallas Cowboys, was not happy to hear the news about Cleveland’s starting quarterback. He took to social media to demand Cleveland trade Sanders to a certain NFC team that would have excitement with having the young quarterback on the roster. “This sorry-ass franchise does not deserve to have Shedeur Sanders on its roster anymore. I wish there were some way that Jimmy Haslam and Todd Monken would decide, as we near the season, to get rid of Shedeur, to set him free, to trade him elsewhere,” Bayless said. “I’d love to see Shedeur in Atlanta. Do I think Shedeur Sanders this coming football season could win more games than Penix or Tua could win? You better believe that I do. Shedeur Sanders is better than either quarterback that the Atlanta Falcons have right now that they’re trying to decide between.” PLEASE TRADE SHEDEUR TO THE FALCONS! pic.twitter.com/VBkYbktick — Skip Bayless (@RealSkipBayless) August 24, 2026 What lies ahead for Shedeur Sanders, Browns this season Shedeur Sanders will be busy trying to make his case as the Browns’ starter in the future. If Deshaun Watson disappoints in the first set of games, Sanders may get his chance to shine then. Sanders finished the 2025 season with a 3–4 record in seven starts, a 56.6% completion percentage, 1,400 passing yards, seven passing touchdowns, 10 interceptions, and one rushing touchdown. The Browns will attempt to improve on their 5-12 record from 2025. They also intend to return to the playoffs after a two-year absence, and end their 33-season division title drought, last winning one in 1989. Cleveland will have the first two games of its 2026 campaign start on the road. They take on the Jacksonville Jaguars on Sept. 13 at 1 p.m. ET before facing the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sept. 20 at 1 p.m. ET. articles.title: Louisiana judge grants RJ Juis injuction, opens door to spend 2026-27 season at LSU
articles.summary: RJ Luis just took a major step forward in spending the 2026-27 season in Baton Rouge. On Monday, a Louisiana judge granted Luis an injunction, On3’s Pete Nakos has confirmed. Luis now has an avenue to play for Will Wade and the LSU Tigers with an additional year of eligibility. This is another
articles._body: RJ Luis just took a major step forward in spending the 2026-27 season in Baton Rouge. On Monday, a Louisiana judge granted Luis an injunction, On3’s Pete Nakos has confirmed. Luis now has an avenue to play for Will Wade and the LSU Tigers with an additional year of eligibility. This is another example of a member of the 2022 recruiting class using the legal system to get back into college athletics. Luis spent three seasons at two different schools, initially suiting up for UMass . But after a year there, he opted to play for Rick Pitino at St. John’s . Luis thought his college basketball career was over, entering the 2025 NBA Draft. He did not get selected but signed a two-way contract with the Utah Jazz. A stint out West did not last too long, as Luis was traded to the Boston Celtics in August. Unfortunately, just over two months later, he got waived. [ $19.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage ] The last time we saw Luis on the court, he was helping St. John’s win a Big East championship and earn a two seed in the NCAA Tournament. In 35 games played, 32 of them were starts. He averaged 18.2 points, 7.2 rebounds, and 2.0 assists per game. Plenty of awards followed due to his performances. Luis was named a second-team All-American by multiple outlets. Wade is hoping Luis can find that kind of form with LSU. Potentially a major get for the Tigers this late in the offseason. SEC Commissioner Greg Sankey files affidavit against RJ Luis SEC Commissioner Greg Sankey filed an affidavit in an eligibility case involving LSU and former St. John’s star RJ Luis. Sankey called Luis’ attempt to play for the Tigers “a competitive disadvantage and fundamental unfairness,” per ESPN’s Pete Thamel. “These rules are grounded in the principle that athletics are an integral part of the academic experience,” Sankey wrote. “The rules align the time permitted for college athletics with the pursuit of an undergraduate education and further the important purpose of preserving opportunities for future student-athletes to participate in college sports.” This is a move we have seen from Sankey before. Back when Alabama was going through the Charles Bediako situation, he opposed Nate Oats getting the big man on his roster. In the end, Bediako was ruled ineligible and his time in Tuscaloosa came to an end. On3’s Nick Kosko contributed to this report

articles.title: ALL’N Is Billboard’s K-Pop Up & Comer of the Month for August: Exclusive Photos
articles.summary: The meaning behind his stage name ALL’N — both a play on “all in,” meaning to give it your all, and “olin,” a shortened form of “violin” — are important clues to understanding his music.
articles._body: Classical violin and K-pop. At first glance, the two may seem like worlds apart, but ALL’N is carving out a new path between them in his own way. A classically trained musician who won international violin competitions and performed as both a concertmaster and soloist with orchestras, he eventually discovered another possibility—one that could not be fully expressed through the violin alone. Rather than putting the violin aside, however, that realization led him to expand the places the violin could go. For him, K-pop was not simply a new genre of music. It was a culture where performance, individuality, visuals, and fandom come together to draw people directly into the music. As ALL’N expanded his own skill set to include guitar, vocals, rap, dance, and production, he began to believe that the violin, too, did not have to remain confined to the boundaries of classical music. From that idea came what he describes as “violin-driven K-pop.” But in ALL’N’s music, the violin is more than simply a differentiating element. From his debut single “We Up,” he naturally weaves the violin into rap, vocals, and performance, treating classical music and K-pop not as two separate worlds, but as languages that can coexist within a single piece of music. In some songs, the violin takes center stage as a powerful main hook; in others, it supports the emotion of the vocals. Its role continues to shift according to what each song demands. The meaning behind his stage name, ALL’N—both a play on “all in,” meaning to give it your all, and “olin,” a shortened form of “violin”—are both important clues to understanding his music. It represents his determination to give his best to everything within his control and to pour everything he has into the path he has chosen, without regret. Rather than searching for answers within predetermined boundaries, his attitude of creating new possibilities for himself is reflected in the way he approaches music. ALL’N is starting from what he does best and, from there, building a musical language of his own. How far can music that began with the violin expand on the new stage of K-pop? Now, hear the story of ALL’N as he puts everything he has on the line and walks that path.

articles._body: Philadelphia Phillies rookie pitcher Andrew Painter traded baseballs for fish Monday during a visit to Pike Place Market. The rookie joined the fish toss before the Phillies began a three-game series vs. the Seattle Mariners at T-Mobile Park. The stop gave Painter and several teammates time to enjoy one of the city’s signature attractions. Workers at Pike Place Fish Market routinely throw seafood across the counter while calling orders. The 23-year-old pitcher joined the market workers for a toss as his teammates watched the lighthearted moment unfold. Painter enters Seattle after dominant start The outing followed Painter’s best major league performance . He held the St. Louis Cardinals to one earned run across a career-best seven innings on Saturday. The pitcher recorded eight strikeouts, allowed five hits, issued no walks, and threw 103 pitches. His fastball reached 99.6 mph on pitch No. 100. Crossing Broad’s Luke Arcaini took to X, formerly Twitter, on Monday to post a clip that Stubbs originally recorded for Instagram. He highlighted the unusual throwing assignment while several Philadelphia players watched Painter participate. “Andrew Painter did the fish throw at Pike Place Market out in Seattle with a bunch of Phillies in attendance : @GarrettStubbs on Instagram” Andrew Painter did the fish throw at Pike Place Market out in Seattle with a bunch of Phillies in attendance : @GarrettStubbs on Instagram pic.twitter.com/tVkQwUDJj9 — Luke Arcaini (@ArcainiLuke) August 24, 2026 Painter owns a 3.62 ERA across five starts since returning from Triple A. Philadelphia demoted him on June 18 after he posted a 7.06 ERA through 14 starts. However, his latest outing helped the club secure its eighth consecutive victory. The Phillies enter Monday’s action at 73-58 and on a nine-game winning streak. They sit just three games behind the Atlanta Braves in the National League East. Zack Wheeler is scheduled to face Logan Gilbert in Monday’s 9:40 p.m. ET series opener. The moment offered fans a relaxed look at the young pitcher amid a promising turnaround. Instead of preparing for another start, the highly regarded rookie tested his arm with flying fish. Meanwhile, the Phillies continue to build momentum during a stretch of their pursuit of the Braves atop the NL East. articles.title: Saints’ Kendre Miller sends strong message amid Alvin Kamara injury
articles.summary: The New Orleans Saints are hoping that the injury bug can take a hike. It’s been a brutal offseason regarding talent on both sides of the ball. However, running back Kendre Miller understands that Alvin Kamara’s injury creates a significant opportunity in the New Orleans Saints’ backfield.
articles._body: The New Orleans Saints are hoping that the injury bug can take a hike. It’s been a brutal offseason regarding talent on both sides of the ball. However, running back Kendre Miller understands that Alvin Kamara’s injury creates a significant opportunity in the New Orleans Saints’ backfield. While Miller expressed concern for his injured teammate, he made it clear that he intends to take advantage of his expanded role. Kendre Miller says he expects a bigger role with Alvin Kamara down: “I’m going to just take that and try to run with it.” pic.twitter.com/BiQWTMdFbc — NOF (@nofnetwork) August 24, 2026 “I gotta put whatever I can on tape,” Miller said. “I never want to see that — teammates get hurt. It’s always a next-man up mentality. I have a bigger role now that AK is down, so I’m going to just take that and try to run with it.” Injuries have been the story of Miller’s career, so this is something he is now on the other side of. He’s never played more than eight games in a season. The hope is that he can finally stay healthy and emerge as a star. The Saints are expected to rely on Travis Etienne Jr. as their starting running back while Kamara is sidelined. Miller should move into the backup role, positioning him to receive more opportunities than initially expected. Replacing Kamara’s production will not be easy. His versatility as a runner and receiver has made him an important part of New Orleans’ offense for the last decade, and his absence places additional responsibility on the rest of the backfield. Etienne figures to handle the largest workload, but Miller could provide valuable support by spelling the starter and contributing when the Saints need fresh legs. For Miller, he must consistently produce when his number is called. Reliable performances could help him secure a meaningful role even after Kamara returns. articles.title: SEC presidents, chancellors push back on athletes returning to college after starting pro careers
articles.summary: In a statement released Monday night, SEC Presidents and Chancellors have pushed back on athletes returning to college after starting professional careers. “College athletes, not former professional athletes, have been at the heart of the Southeastern Conference,” the statement reads. &#
articles._body: In a statement released Monday night, SEC Presidents and Chancellors have pushed back on athletes returning to college after starting professional careers. “College athletes, not former professional athletes, have been at the heart of the Southeastern Conference,” the statement reads. “Individuals who choose to leave college athletics, sign professional playing contracts, and compete professional should not then be permitted to return to college competition. “Allowing that to occur will blur the line between college and professional sports, create significant competitive equity concerns, and reduce opportunities for high school and current college athletes. “College sports are for college athletes. The current confusion around national eligibility standards emphasizes the need to advance the Protect College Sports Act.” $19.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage Per On3’s Pete Nakos , the SEC presidents’ call was just for general discussion regarding the current eligibility situation in college sports. No decisions were made ahead of tomorrow’s league meetings in Birmingham. 16 college football players were granted TRO for fifth-year of eligibility last week The statement comes after a Louisiana court ruled that the 16 players, some of whom were competing in NFL training camps, could return to college with eligibility for the 2026 season. That gave them a a fifth year in light of the five-for-five ruling earlier this year. Per the signed order, the 16 college football players were allowed to enter the transfer portal. The NCAA’s rule of restitution and the ghost transfer rule were also enjoined. In the aftermath of the TRO, former Ole Miss stars TE Dae’Quan Wright and DL Xzavian Harris have already committed to LSU out of the portal. Harris was signed by the New Orleans Saints as an UDFA this offseason, and Wright appeared in multiple preseason games for the Cleveland Browns. Other players, such as former Seattle Seahawks running backs Anthony Hankerson and TJ Harden , remain in the portal. “College football has officially plunged into the abyss,” ESPN’s Paul Finebaum said on Monday morning’s episode of Get Up . “We have never been at a place like this before. There have been scandals far more serious, but this is a new low in terms of the machinations of the legal system, the NCAA, and all these things. “It’s just incomprehensible to think that someone was on an NFL roster the other day and he very well could be playing for LSU a week from this Saturday, but it’s the way things are right now.”

articles._body: LSU forward Kate Koval has departed the women’s basketball program ahead of the 2026-27 season, head coach Kim Mulkey revealed Monday night. Koval averaged 8.3 points and 6.3 rebounds last season for the Tigers. “Kate came to see me on Sunday and told me that after much consideration, she will be leaving the program for personal reasons,” Mulkey said, via a release . “We will respect her privacy on her decision, but we had a long talk about it, and it was a hard decision for her. “I know it is hard because she loves LSU . Kate is a great person. She has to do what she feels is right for her, and we fully support her in that. We all wish her the best.” $19.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage The Kyiv, Ukraine native played in 35 games (17 starts) for LSU last season. She opened her career at Notre Dame , where she played in 32 games (10 starts) alongside WNBA rookie sensation Olivia Miles . Across her two-year collegiate career, the 6’5″ forward boasts averages of 6.9 points, 5.5 rebounds, and 1.5 blocks. LSU is coming off heartbreaking NCAA Tournament loss to Duke LSU is coming off a 29-6 (12-4) season, in which it advanced to the Sweet Sixteen of the NCAA Tournament. There, the No. 2 seeded Tigers fell to No. 3 seed Duke 87-85 after Blue Devil guard Ashton Jackson nailed a game-winning three-pointer at the buzzer. “I’ve been around a long time. I’ve seen endings like that. I’ve been a part of those endings. It takes a while to get over it, but you go in the locker room and you hug their necks and you tell them what a wonderful year we had,” Mulkey said following that loss. “And you put yourself in a position to win the game. You put yourself in a position to win the game and a crazy shot like that beats you. Mulkey is heading into her sixth season at the helm in Baton Rouge. Across that span, Mulkey has led LSU to a 151-26 (65-15) record and a National Championship in 2023. Following their loss to the Blue Devils, she seemed optimistic about the upcoming season. “Well, you’re looking at a team that is very talented, a team that — freshmen got lots of minutes this year. And you add a few to the mix and hope that we’re back in this position again. That’s what I hope,” Mulkey said.

articles.summary: Could we get a Kentucky vs. Louisville battle for one of the top point guards in the class of 2027? We’re one step closer to that possibility, as five-star Reese Alston has included the Wildcats and Cardinals in his most recent list of finalists, cut down to seven remaining contenders. The gro
articles._body: Could we get a Kentucky vs. Louisville battle for one of the top point guards in the class of 2027? We’re one step closer to that possibility, as five-star Reese Alston has included the Wildcats and Cardinals in his most recent list of finalists, cut down to seven remaining contenders. The group of seven? Houston , Kentucky , LSU , Louisville , Tennessee , Vanderbilt and Wichita State , he told Rivals’ Joe Tipton. Alston is ranked as the No. 8 overall recruit in the 2027 class and the No. 3 point guard, according to the Rivals Industry Ranking , an average of all three major recruiting media companies (Rivals, ESPN, 247Sports). He is the son of former NBA player Rafer “Skip to My Lou” Alston , who played with Mark Pope on the Milwaukee Bucks from 2000-02. His offer from the Wildcats came following an unofficial visit to Lexington for Big Blue Madness last October. Pope went out of his way to prioritize the prized target during the final live period of the summer, opening the crucial championship weekend of travel ball down in Texas for the Puma Pro16 circuit — not Nike EYBL or adidas 3SSB — alongside assistant coach Mikhail McLean. “My relationship with Kentucky is pretty good,” he told Rivals’ Jamie Shaw in July. “They have great coaching with Coach Pope, you know, we’ve been able to build a great relationship. We have a great relationship with Coach McLean, too. The history of Kentucky basketball really stands out to me. You know, just all the guards they have had, all the guards they have put in the league. And, you know, the great coaches who have been there. The history stood out to me.” Standing 6-foot-3 out of Second Baptist (TX), Alston averaged 22.2 points, 5.3 rebounds, 3.9 assists, and 2.7 steals per game during the 2025-26 high school season en route to MaxPreps Junior All-American First Team honors. He’s in the process of scheduling official visits, with Kentucky likely to get one ahead of a commitment before the early signing period in November. Louisville is also considered a top contender to earn his signature while LSU and Wichita State also remain firmly in the mix. We’ll see if Pope can hold off Pat Kelsey and the Cardinals for one of the nation’s best — or if anyone else swoops in late as his recruitment winds down.

articles.title: Countdown to kickoff prediction series: Maurice Brown and David Bucey will continue their special teams excellence in 2026
articles.summary: Continuing the countdown to kickoff prediction series: Maurice Brown and David Bucey will excel on special teams again
articles._body: In May, when the calendar revealed that it was 100 days until South Carolina kicked off the season, I posted a story on GamecockCentral entitled “100 predictions for the 2026 Gamecocks.” Now, that countdown is down to just 12 days. The prediction paired with day 12 read, “Even with increased roles on offense and defense, players like Maurice Brown and David Bucey will continue to excel on special teams. Brown will get at least one de-cleater by year’s end.” Let’s break down that prognostication. Have a question for the GamecockCentral staff? Ask it now on The Insiders Forum. Brown and Bucey in 2025 for South Carolina South Carolina’s 2025 season didn’t go like the Gamecocks wanted. However, among the list of positives from last season were the special teams efforts of Maurice Brown II and David Bucey. Brown, a junior tight end last year, was the most prominent coverage player on special teams. He had a couple of huge hits on kickoffs and was always near the ball. He also famously had a leaping blocked punt against LSU in 2024. Bucey, a sophomore defensive back in 2025, posted some special teams tackles, as well. He had two forced fumbles in the game’s third phase as a freshman in 2024. Brown and Bucey both have been credited at different times for the blocked punt that led to Vicari Swain’s third punt return touchdown. What does this mean for the Gamecocks? Fellow subscribers are discussing it now on The Insiders Forum. Bigger roles could limit special teams reps in 2026 Neither Brown nor Bucey held prominent roles away from special teams in 2025. That could change this fall. Brown is big, strong, and athletic, and depending on what new offensive coordinator Kendal Briles might need, the senior could play a role for the Gamecocks. He is not expected to start, but if Brown plays more under control, he has the profile of a player who could help as a blocker or receiver. For Bucey, a starting spot could be in the cards. Redshirt senior Peyton Williams is back at one safety spot. The other safety position battle has been ongoing, and Bucey has been at the center of it. He and freshman J’Zavien Currence might be the top contenders for that job. If either Brown or Bucey are called upon to have a high snap count, they might get moved from their prominent special teams roles. However, South Carolina has not been afraid to play important pieces on special teams if needed. Last year, Nyck Harbor was the team’s starting gunner, and several other starters saw extensive special teams work, too. If put to work by special teams coordinator Matthew Smiley, Brown and Bucey should resume their special teams excellence. What’s your prediction? Share it with fellow subscribers on The Insiders Forum.

articles.summary: Colt Emerson was selected in the first round of the 2023 MLB Draft by the Seattle Mariners. Before making his MLB debut, Emerson signed a record-breaking extension with the club. The expectation was that he was set to be a cornerstone of the franchise. It was a disappointing campaign for the rook
articles._body: Colt Emerson was selected in the first round of the 2023 MLB Draft by the Seattle Mariners. Before making his MLB debut, Emerson signed a record-breaking extension with the club . The expectation was that he was set to be a cornerstone of the franchise. It was a disappointing campaign for the rookie , and now the season has come to an end for Emerson, per Darragh McDonald. Emerson is going to have season-ending surgery on his left wrist. He was sent to the minors out of spring training, but still got the extension from the team. He was finally promoted in May, making his debut against the San Diego Padres on May 17. The season did not go as planned for Emerson. He hit just .190 with eight home runs and 23 RBIs. He struggled heavily in August, hitting .182 with a .206 on base percetnage. Emerson also was striking out on 34.4 percent of his plate appearances at the major league level. He also had just one home run and two RBIs during the month. The Mariners planned to demote Emerson back to Triple-A, but instead he was moved to the IL with wrist inflammation. The Mariners are 62-69 on the season , which places them in third place in the AL West. While the team is seven games under .500 on the year, they are just three games out of first place in the division, sitting behind the Houston Astros and Texas Rangers. The Rangers are also in control of the final wild card spot in the American League. The Mariners open a series against the Philadelphia Phillies on Monday night. articles.summary: The San Diego Padres made three roster moves Monday before their game against the Pittsburgh Pirates, adding outfielder Dustin Harris to the major league roster while sending infielder Sung-Mun Song to Triple-A El Paso. The team made the announcement Monday afternoon on X, formerly Twitter. San D
articles._body: The San Diego Padres made three roster moves Monday before their game against the Pittsburgh Pirates, adding outfielder Dustin Harris to the major league roster while sending infielder Sung-Mun Song to Triple-A El Paso. The team made the announcement Monday afternoon on X, formerly Twitter. San Diego selected Harris’ contract from El Paso and optioned Song in the corresponding active-roster move. The Padres also transferred right-hander Lucas Giolito to the 60-day injured list to clear a spot for Harris on the 40-man roster. Harris, ranked as the Padres’ No. 29 prospect per Darragh McDonald of MLB Trade Rumors, earned the promotion after a productive stretch with El Paso. In 29 games since joining the Triple-A club, Harris hit .350 with a .422 on-base percentage and .617 slugging percentage across 135 plate appearances. He also hit six home runs while posting a 10.4% walk rate and 8.9% strikeout rate. The 27-year-old has already spent time with multiple organizations this season. Harris began the year with the Chicago White Sox before being designated for assignment and claimed by the Houston Astros. After Houston also designated him for assignment, he returned to the White Sox before opting out of his minor league deal in July and signing with San Diego . Harris has a career .225/.307/.371 slash line across 102 major league plate appearances. His arrival gives the Padres another outfield option behind a starting group of Fernando Tatis Jr. in right field, Jackson Merrill in center and Luis Rengifo in left. Austin Hays and Jace Bowen are also available off the bench. Giolito’s move to the 60-day IL is procedural. He has been sidelined with elbow inflammation since June 22 and has already missed more than 60 days, meaning the transaction does not delay his eligibility to return. He has yet to begin a rehab assignment. The Padres face the Pirates at home Monday at 11:40 p.m. ET. The post Padres make flurry of roster moves before Pirates clash appeared first on ClutchPoints .

articles.title: Tracy McGrady reveals why MVPs matter more than winning a championship
articles.summary: For Hall of Fame forward Tracy McGrady, winning an MVP award is more valuable for a player than an NBA championship. Ahead of the 2026-27 season, McGrady has been very vocal about his opinions. From McGrady’s hot take on Allen Iverson’s legacy to how an NBA player values a championshi
articles._body: For Hall of Fame forward Tracy McGrady, winning an MVP award is more valuable for a player than an NBA championship. Ahead of the 2026-27 season, McGrady has been very vocal about his opinions . From McGrady’s hot take on Allen Iverson’s legacy to how an NBA player values a championship in comparison to a title, he doesn’t hold back on his takes. McGrady, alongside Hall of Fame forward Vince Carter, explained why an MVP award matters more , per the Cousins with Vince Carter & Tracy McGrady podcast. “The MVP of the regular season has more weight than a championship,” McGrady said. “Hell yeah, why wouldn’t it? Man, name the tenth or the eleventh player on the Chicago Bulls or the Los Angeles Lakers, or the Detroit Pistons, or the Boston Celtics. Who are they? Any of those teams, name me the eleventh or the twelfth guy.” In McGrady agreeing with Houston Rockets All-Star Kevin Durant’s MVP take, Carter couldn’t name the various players at the end of the bench of championship teams such as the 2024 Boston Celtics, the 2020 Los Angeles Lakers, the 2004 Detroit Pistons, or the 1998 Chicago Bulls. “You can’t even think of them. He got a ring, and he can’t even think of them,” McGrady added. “He has a ring, but does he have an MVP? Absolutely not. No. So, yes, the MVP of the regular season has more weight than a championship.” For Tracy McGrady, an NBA championship takes more of a group effort from the team and the organization’s vision, whereas an MVP winner honors one individual rather than multiple people. The lawsuit comes after CalMatters has spent the past year attempting to obtain information about how the universities pay its student athletes. The news organization first submitted records requests to 16 University of California and California State University campuses, seeking information about how they go about paying their Division I athletes. However, most schools contacted failed to report adequate data. $19.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage Per calmatters.org, ‘the lawsuit states that taxpayers are entitled to know the names of players who have received money and the teams they play on.’ “When public institutions distribute public resources, the public is entitled to know who receives those resources, in what amounts, and on what terms,” the lawsuit says. Stett Holbrook , a spokesperson for the UC Berkeley ( Cal ) system, said the UC will “respond appropriately in court” and that it takes the “California Public Records Act and student privacy obligations seriously.” UCLA and Cal ultimately reported paying student athletes around $20.5 million for 2025-26 Initially, UCLA and Cal both rejected CalMatters’ records request. Per the release, ‘they argued that sharing information about their payments to students would put their players at a competitive disadvantage or violate students’ right to privacy in education.’ Following a meeting with attorneys at Davis Wright Tremaine LLP (which represented CalMatters), the universities finally uncovered some records. Both universities reported paying their student athletes around $20.5 million for the 2025-26 academic year. That is the maximum amount allowed. UCLA claimed that it paid 229 athletes, while Cal claimed it paid just 147. The names of the players, or a breakdown of how much money went to the individual sports, were not given. “We’re simply asking these public institutions to follow the law and explain what’s being done with tens of millions of taxpayer dollars,” CalMatters CEO Neil Chase said. “But they still refused, so unfortunately we’ve had to take this next step with UCLA and are planning a similar action involving UC Berkeley .” Per calmatters.org, San Diego State and UC Riverside provided the most information about student payments. Private universities, such as Stanford and USC , are not subject to the state’s public records laws.

articles.title: Rick Ross Responds to 50 Cent’s Aging in Hip-Hop Comments: ‘F— What Your Age Is’
articles.summary: 50 recently told Apple Music that he doesn't release much music anymore because at his age, he doesn't want to be "in the way."
articles._body: Rick Ross predictably has a message for his fellow troll-in-arms 50 Cent . The Miami rapper took to social media to respond to 50’s recent comments about still putting out rap albums and wanting to be the hottest rapper after a certain age during an appearance on Apple Music’s Rap Life Review . “I saw Curtis Jackson say he ain’t doing no music and it makes sense for the music he make,” he said in a video posted to his Instagram Stories before bringing up Bun B , who’s still actively rapping in his early 50s. “But Bun B just hit the stage, the South won’t let Bun B stop rappin’. If Pimp C was alive we wouldn’t let Pimp C stop rappin’, they could put out albums til they’re 85 years old, n—a. That’s how it go. When the streets love you and the culture needs you and you bring something that can’t be duplicated. F— what your age is.” Last week, 50 gave Apple Music host Ebro the reason why he doesn’t release much music these days unless said music is attached to one of his film projects. “I’m not trying to be in the way,” the Queens rapper and filmmaker explained. “Hip-hop culture is connected to youth culture. You are not supposed to be the hottest in nothin’ at 60. F— that, man.” He then added that he still has love for music, but if it doesn’t make dollars, then it doesn’t make sense. “I still got love for music. I’m never going to lose that. I’ma always want to do something,” 50 continued. “And those are like entries. It’s me putting a little piece or tap something in there for them to hear that I still do it, that I still got it. If it doesn’t sell, you keep it to your motherf—king self. Motherf—ker’ll tell you, ‘This is a personal album. I made this for this and that.’ Then why do I hear it, b—h?” Both Ross and 50 have been busy in between trolling each other. Rozay dropped his 12th solo album Set in Stone last month and is currently on tour celebrating the 20th anniversary of his debut Port of Miami while 50 had a cameo during the Verzuz between Donnell Jones and Joe , and is in the live-action Street Fighter film that’s set to hit theaters in October.

articles._body: Seven years after Quincy Pondexter retired as an NBA player , he is returning to his former team as a coach. On Monday, the Chicago Bulls made it official that Pondexter will be the new head coach of the Windy City Bulls, per Gavin Dorsey of Roundtable Sports. Pondexter, 38, is replacing Billy Donovan III to take command of the G League affiliate for the Bulls, per K.C. Johnson of the Chicago Sports Network. He had played in the NBA for eight seasons from 2010 to 2019. Pondexter was drafted by the Oklahoma City Thunder of the University of Washington. Shortly thereafter, he was traded to the New Orleans Hornets. He played in New Orleans from 2010 to 2011 before joining the Memphis Grizzlies (2011 to 2015) and the New Orleans Pelicans (2015 to 2017). However, he missed both seasons due to knee injuries. In 2017, Pondexter suffered a life-threaning knee infection that required surgery. That same year, the Bulls traded for Pondexter . Ultimately, he missed the entirity of the preseason. Altogether, Pondexter played one season, averaging 2.0 points and 1.2 rebounds per game in 23 appearances. On February 1, 2018, the Bulls waived Pondexter. That August, he was picked up by the San Antonio Spurs and signed a one-year contract. However, he only played in five games and averaged 2.4 minutes. In 2021, Pondexter returned to the University of Washington to be an assistant coach under Mike Hopkins. After three years, Pondexter was then hired as an assistant coach for USC in 2024. The next year, he went back to Washington for one more season. Now, he is looking to charter a new course for the Windy City Bulls after a 15-21 campaign last year. articles._body: The San Diego Padres have a new ownership group after Jose E. Feliciano and his wife/business partner, Kwanza Jones, purchased the franchise for an MLB record high of $3.9 billion. With the sale finalized in mid-August, Jones was incredibly enthusiastic about the purchase and fully believes the team can win a World Series. While talking with media members on Monday, Jones was seemingly over the moon to be one of the new owners of the Padres. While she did not pick a specific year for San Diego to win a title, the goal is incredibly clear with the new owners: win a championship. “We gonna win,” Jones said. “We gonna win! Win it all!” New Padres owner Kwanza Jones' opening statement: "We are all in. It's not lip service." Her energy is through the roof! pic.twitter.com/LeBSs44899 — Talking Friars (@TalkingFriars) August 24, 2026 Overall, Jones appeared thankful for the opportunity to step in as an owner of the Padres. Not only did she give the team a shoutout, but she claimed the organization is in it together to lead the way to what they hope will be World Series wins. Kwanza Jones made history as the first black woman to become a majority owner of an MLB franchise. She is well known for being an American artist, investor, entrepreneur, and philanthropist. Meanwhile, Jose E. Feliciano is a billionaire investor and a co-founder of Clearlake Capital. This season, the Padres are right in the mix for the playoffs, as the club is sixth in the playoff rankings. That’s good enough for a spot in the Wild Card. The organization has made aggressive moves in the past, so it will be interesting to see how the new ownership group operates things moving forward. articles.title: Mystics take big first step toward WNBA championship contention with playoff-clinching win over Fire
articles.summary: After a regime change, parting ways with their general manager, and drafting six first-round players over the last two years, the Washington Mystics will make the playoffs this season for the first time since 2023. They guaranteed it with their 105-100 road win over the Portland Fire on Sunday, a
articles._body: After a regime change, parting ways with their general manager, and drafting six first-round players over the last two years, the Washington Mystics will make the playoffs this season for the first time since 2023. They guaranteed it with their 105-100 road win over the Portland Fire on Sunday, as they’re now seven games ahead of the ninth-place Fire with seven regular-season contests left. They own the head-to-head tiebreaker 2-1, and Portland is the only team outside of playoff position to not be eliminated yet. The Mystics partially won because of their 38-25 rebounding advantage, which has been a common theme this year. They lead the WNBA with 37.8 boards per game, led by center Shakira Austin (9.6) and power forward Kiki Iriafen (9.3). Those two rank third and fifth among all players, respectively. Additionally, Washington shot 32-of-44 (73%) from the free-throw line, while Portland shot 15-of-15 (100%). That’s been another pattern, as the Mystics lead the league with 25.4 free throws attempted per game. Finally, they outscored the Fire in the paint 48-42, another hallmark of their play style. They rank second in the WNBA with 42.8 points in the paint per game, 1.1 points behind the Atlanta Dream. Those data points signal Washington’s size and strength, which helps them dominate inside on both ends. For example, Austin is 6-foot-5, Iriafen is 6-foot-3, and backup center Lauren Betts is 6-foot-7. Minnesota Lynx superstar Olivia Miles complimented the Mystics’ physicality after her squad beat them 94-84 in the nation’s capital on Friday. Olivia Miles on what makes the Mystics hard to face: “They’re strong as hell. They are strong as hellll. I can’t say enough about how incredible [Natasha Howard] and [Nia Coffey] were in terms of dealing with that physicality. It was on [Courtney Williams], [Kayla McBride] and I… pic.twitter.com/IKdrFoZ9Le — Joshua Valdez (@joshvaldez100) August 22, 2026 “They’re strong as hell. They are strong as hellll,” the rookie said when asked what makes Washington hard to face. “The physicality that they bring…and they have a ‘not caring’ sense about them. They’re the youngest team in the league; they know that. They just go and hoop; they don’t care who’s in front of them. If you’re the best or the worst, it doesn’t matter. They exert their physicality and dominance on you. It’s something I respect, and also something really challenging to get through, and makes them hard to play against.” The Mystics outrebounded the Lynx 36-26 and outscored them 40-36 in the paint despite the loss, showing that they can bully even the league’s best team inside. Minnesota is 31-7, five games ahead of the Golden State Valkyries for the first seed. Plus, Washington is not only the WNBA’s youngest team with an average age of 24.06 years , but the youngest playoff squad in history, per Elias Sports Bureau. Although they’ve still got room for growth as the seventh seed, they’re ahead of more than half of the league despite being in the second year of a rebuild. Sonia Citron holds key to Mystics making deep playoff run in 2026 Soobum Im-Imagn Images Austin now leads Washington with 17 points per game on 48.5% shooting (35.4% 3-point), but guard Sonia Citron is still its biggest threat offensively. The two-time All-Star is averaging 16.9 points on 47.4% shooting (31.6% 3-point) and a team-high 4.2 assists. Citron is a three-level scorer despite her struggles from deep this season, as she converted 44.5% of her three-pointers on 4.1 average attempts as a rookie last year. The 22-year-old is averaging four attempts this season, but didn’t take any on Sunday and is 2-for-8 over the last three games. However, head coach Sydney Johnson is not worried . “You know, it’s just a matter of time,” he insisted after Washington beat the Los Angeles Sparks 80-70 at home on August 16. “She’s a lights-out shooter, shows it in our gym. She’s not immune to a little bit of a slump there shooting the ball, but she’s given us so much other stuff, and we know her three-point shot’s gonna come around. We’ve seen that the last few games.” Citron went 4-for-5 from downtown in that game, 5-for-6 in the Mystics’ 95-75 win over the Phoenix Mercury on August 9, and 2-for-3 in their 79-74 win over the Dream on August 7. Conversely, Citron’s also gone 1-for-4 from deep four times in August and went 1-for-6 in a 96-92 victory over the Dallas Wings on August 5. That’s not ideal on a team that’s 14th in the league with a 30.4% three-point clip, as forward Michaela Onyenwere is its only player shooting at least 35% on two-plus average attempts. Washington needs more from the team as a whole, but Citron has the best chance to improve immediately based on her talent and track record. If the Notre Dame alum finds her rookie three-point form over the coming weeks, it will make the Mystics even harder to stop offensively. Washington currently sits a half-game ahead of Dallas and a half-game behind the New York Liberty at 22-15. Up next are road matchups with the Mercury on Tuesday and Thursday, followed by another one with the Sparks on Friday to finish the month. articles.title: Ex-Kings star Anze Kopitar opens up about how retirement has treated him
articles.summary: For the first time since 2006, the Los Angeles Kings will play a season without Anze Kopitar on the roster. The now-former Kings captain has retired from the game of hockey. He left an incredible impact on this franchise and is now riding off into the sunset. Kopitar is likely to be a Hockey Hall
articles._body: For the first time since 2006, the Los Angeles Kings will play a season without Anze Kopitar on the roster. The now-former Kings captain has retired from the game of hockey. He left an incredible impact on this franchise and is now riding off into the sunset. Kopitar is likely to be a Hockey Hall of Famer once he’s eligible. The Kings legend won two Stanley Cups with Los Angeles, being the only captain in franchise history to win the Cup. Additionally, he scored more than 1300 points in his career. The 39-year-old has accomplished a lot in his career. Now that it’s over, he is content with what he did on the ice, and he’s enjoying his time off. “I am very happy,” Kopitar said about his retirement , via NHL.com. “It’s great. Obviously, I get to spend a lot more time with my family. I get to go (watch my) kids … my son’s hockey tournament, my daughter’s figure skating competition. So, there is still life in ice arenas, but I’m enjoying it very much.” The former Los Angeles captain spent his entire career with the franchise. He debuted in 2006-07, scoring 61 points in his rookie campaign. He’d go on to score at least 60 points in all but four seasons of his career. As mentioned, he won the Stanley Cup with Los Angeles twice, lifting it in 2012 and 2014. Los Angeles has not named a new captain. However, they are only just beginning to honor their former leader. The Kings are going to retire his number 11 on February 24, 2027. The post Ex-Kings star Anze Kopitar opens up about how retirement has treated him appeared first on ClutchPoints .

The top seven playoff spots have officially been claimed, leaving one left for two teams to battle over as the campaign comes to a close. This week’s rankings make it clear which sides see
articles._body: The final weeks of the 2026 WNBA season produced a useful snapshot of the current state of the league. The top seven playoff spots have officially been claimed, leaving one left for two teams to battle over as the campaign comes to a close. This week’s rankings make it clear which sides seem the most ready to tackle the postseason, which ones are just barely hanging on to their playoff hopes, and which are already looking forward to next year. WNBA STANDINGS UPDATE The @minnesotalynx continue to hold the No. 1 spot as they come in hot on a six game win streak. The @AtlantaDream are on a three game win streak, going 7-3 in their last 10 games. Both the @nyliberty and @WashMystics clinched a playoff berth… pic.twitter.com/ymsidF0NDq — WNBA (@WNBA) August 24, 2026 1. Minnesota Lynx Minnesota’s recent results reinforce an already dominant season. At 31-7, the Lynx have built the W’s best record and currently hold the longest active win streak with six victories in a row. What has carried Minnesota this far and separates from the pack its consistency. The kind of late-season volatility that can make a championship favorite seem vulnerable has been nonexistent for this team. The Lynx have combined winning with the ability to navigate the increasingly challenging schedule, as all of their recent wins have come against solidified playoff teams or hopefuls. Their steady position at the top of these rankings isn’t about one spectacular week – it’s about repeatedly producing the strongest overall level of basketball. 2. Atlanta Dream Atlanta climbs this high because its recent performances have been convincing and impressive. The Dream have won three straight and seven of their last 10 games, one of the best recent marks in the W. They look to finally be over their recent slump and are showing more of their early-season dominance at the perfect time. The Dream have entered the closing stretch with momentum rather than simply protecting an established position. Their consistency has also been rewarded with an official playoff berth, and at this point, Atlanta looks capable of making the postseason uncomfortable for a higher seed rather than simply participating. 3. Las Vegas Aces Las Vegas had an easier schedule this past week, beating the Toronto Tempo by 10 on Sunday behind 27 points from A’ja Wilson and the Connecticut Sun on Thursday by 23 behind Jackie Young’s 24 points. Before that was a chaotic 15-point loss to the surging Dream, though, which keeps the Aces from rising any higher in these rankings. The Aces’ 26-13 record puts them among the league’s elite, and they’re still a team that’s dangerous even when not operating at peak efficiency. But they’ve struggled to beat the W’s other top teams lately, and that could be a troubling sign this close to the playoffs. The most encouraging aspect of the week was Wilson and Young’s ability to generate offense without needing a perfect game from everyone around them. 4. Golden State Valkyries Golden State has firmly established itself as one of the season’s biggest success stories, but this week was probably the most it’s struggled throughout 2026. The Valkyries fell to the Lynx, which isn’t unexpected, but they also lost to the already eliminated Chicago Sky on Friday after blowing a major lead. It’s most likely just a misstep, but it’s also the worst time of year to make out-of-character mistakes. , joining Minnesota and Las Vegas among the Western Conference teams already assured of postseason basketball. The Valkyries’ recent 6-4 stretch is not quite as dominant as Minnesota’s, but they have also clinched a playoff berth, and their overall body of work is still exceptional. They’ve avoided the type of prolonged slump that could have erased the advantage it built earlier in the year, but with the postseason approaching, the Valkyries need to reestablish their position a legitimate contender. 5. Indiana Fever The Fever secured their playoff placement over the weekend, overwhelming Chicago 113-90. Caitlin Clark put up 37 points and 10 assists while Kelsey Mitchell scored 30, and that kind of offensive explosion is why Indiana is a dangerous postseason opponent. The Fever’s recent form has not been flawless – falling to the New York Liberty and Dallas Wings during the week prevents them from moving any higher in the rankings. But their ability to overwhelm an opponent when the backcourt gets rolling makes them one of the W’s hardest teams to ignore. 6. New York Liberty The Liberty’s recent output arguably makes them worthy of an even higher position, but they’ve had an easier slate of opponents lately, and the teams above them have stronger current momentum, stronger records, or both. Still, this is a team that’s proving it’s one that no one should want to face. New York has enough wins to establish a playoff-caliber floor while possessing the experience and talent needed to stay competitive in a postseason series. Especially after a hard-fought win over the Fever, the Liberty look to be building more confidence. 7. Washington Mystics Washington remains the season’s biggest surprise. The Mystics clinched their first playoff berth since 2023 after beating Portland 105-100 on Sunday, with Shakira Austin delivering a career-high 31 points as they bounced back from a 10-point loss to the league-best Lynx. The recent surge makes Washington more dangerous than its seventh-place position in these rankings suggests. The Mystics have paired youth with increasingly reliable execution, and their defensive performance has helped sustain the impressive turnaround. A team that was not even expected to be a factor in this year’s playoff picture has transformed into one of the W’s most compelling late-season stories. 8. Dallas Wings The Wings land in eighth because they just deliver

articles.title: Why the Nuggets give DeMar DeRozan his final chance to compete for a championship in 2026-27
articles.summary: The Denver Nuggets signed DeMar DeRozan to a one-year contract after trading Peyton Watson in a sign-and-trade, worth $88 million to the Cleveland Cavs in exchange for an unprotected 2031 first-round pick, a 2032 second-round pick, and Julian Reese. The multi-team deal saved the Nuggets roughly $
articles._body: The Denver Nuggets signed DeMar DeRozan to a one-year contract after trading Peyton Watson in a sign-and-trade, worth $88 million to the Cleveland Cavs in exchange for an unprotected 2031 first-round pick, a 2032 second-round pick, and Julian Reese. The multi-team deal saved the Nuggets roughly $18.06 million, as DeRozan agreed to a $3.9 million contract in exchange for the $20.4 million owed to Watson in 2026-27. The Nuggets are the only team in the NBA’s second apron. After the Oklahoma City Thunder signed restricted free agent Spencer Jones to a two-year, $12 million contract, the Nuggets were forced to match it, pushing them into the dreaded second tax apron. This led Denver to offload Watson, who’s coming off a breakout season. The Nuggets lost their standout 3-and-D wing. After averaging 14.6 points on 49.1/41.1/73.0 shooting splits, Watson emerged as a potential trade target for the Cavs, especially after LeBron James chose the Philadelphia 76ers over a reunion in Cleveland. In games where All-Star Nikola Jokic sat, Watson’s averages spiked to 23.1 points, 6.1 rebounds, 1.4 blocks, and 1.3 steals per game. At the same time, DeRozan is an ideal consolation prize for a team with championship aspirations. In his 17th NBA season, he averaged 18.4 points on 49.7% shooting, 4.1 assists, and 1.0 steals for the Sacramento Kings in 2025-26. But what stands out most for how the Nuggets could utilize the six-time All-Star is DeRozan’s mid-range shot. By mid-March, DeRozan’s 48.0% was tied for ninth-best in mid-range field-goal percentage for players with at least 100 field-goal attempts, per Stat Defender. Best Mid-Range FG% In The 2025-26 NBA Regular Season (Min. 100 Total FGA) : 1. Rui Hachimura — 56.0% 2. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander — 53.4% 3. TJ McConnell — 52.9% 4. Donovan Mitchell — 51.0% 5. Devin Vassell — 50.0% 6. Kevin… https://t.co/0G56Pr1QIH pic.twitter.com/zZa7KgmXIe — Stat Defender (@statdefender) March 17, 2026   By the end of the regular season, DeRozan made 52.7% of his field-goal attempts from inside the 3-point arc. While he won’t be the caliber of defender the Nuggets had in Watson last season, his offense helps keep Denver among the NBA’s best offenses. The Nuggets’ 122.6 offensive rating ranked first in 2025-26 and second-best in NBA history. In competing with the likes of Defensive Player of the Year Victor Wembanyama and the defending Western Conference champion San Antonio Spurs, and two-time MVP Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and the 2025 champion Oklahoma City Thunder, DeMar DeRozan keeps the Nuggets afloat offensively. Ahead of the upcoming season, this could be one of his last chances to win his first championship. For teams ranked in the bottom half of the NBA in defensive rating last season, the Nuggets’ 108.2 was the sixth-worst mark. Denver’s opponents averaged 116.9 points a game, the tenth-highest in 2025-26. But there’s still upside to the Nuggets signing DeRozan for a team looking to return to the Finals since winning it all in 2023. Will DeMar DeRozan’s signing bring Nuggets closer to title contention? Darren Yamashita-Imagn Images After his first nine seasons, including four All-Star appearances and two All-NBA selections, the Raptors traded DeMar DeRozan to the Spurs for Kawhi Leonard, which led to the Raptors’ first title in franchise history. DeRozan spent three seasons with the Spurs before he was traded to the Bulls, and after his past two seasons with the Kings, DeMar’s still chasing his first title. Amid a rebuild, the Kings waived DeRozan this summer, allowing him to sign with a contender like the Nuggets, who are undoubtedly a step in that direction, led by three-time MVP Nikola Jokic (2021, 2022, 2024). It’s a perfect situation for DeMar to prove himself in 2026-27, as the Nuggets will look to build off their 4-2 first-round playoff exit against the Timberwolves. DeRozan, who finished second for the Comeback Player of the Year award in 2023-24, posted averages of 24.0 points on 48.0% shooting, 5.3 assists, 4.3 rebounds, and 1.1 steals per game. His numbers aren’t far off from his days with the Bulls, including the last time he averaged 20+ points (22.2) in 2024-25 for the Kings. As for making up for DeRozan’s defensive limitations, Spencer Jones, alongside Christian Braun, will most likely fill the void left in Peyton Watson’s absence at the wing position. Aaron Gordon’s clean slate on the health front would also go a long way for the Nuggets. Hamstring strains and a left calf injury hampered his 2025-26 campaign, as he played in only 36 regular-season games and three of the Nuggets’ first-round, best-of-7 series, which his team lost 4-2 to the Timberwolves. Losing Gordon in Game 7 of the Nuggets’ second-round series, a 4-3 loss to the Thunder in 2025, is the closest they’ve come to returning to the Western Conference Finals since winning it all in 2023. Still, the Nuggets’ DeRozan signing is a low-cost/high reward kind of move for a veteran scorer with a high IQ. He’s 16th on the all-time scoring list (26,711 career points). Among active players, he’s fourth overall in total scoring, trailing 76ers forward LeBron James, Rockets’ Kevin Durant, and Cavs’ James Harden. However, unlike the aforementioned all-time active leading scorers, DeRozan hasn’t reached the playoffs since 2021-22. He watched the Raptors win a championship without him. The Spurs made their first NBA Finals appearance in 12 years, five years removed from DeRozan’s tenure with the team last season. Joining a team with one of the best players in the association, Jokic, will only motivate the veteran forward. Perhaps competing against a team projected to compete for a championship leads DeRozan to turn back the clock. At 37, this could be one of his last opportunities to win a title, and the Nuggets’ on

Now, the 11-year NFL veteran is callin
articles._body: Allen Robinson last appeared in an NFL game during the 2024 season with the Detroit Lions. The receiver attempted to find work in 2025, as Robinson offered his services to the Kansas City Chiefs . Nothing came of that offer, and Robinson did not play in 2025. Now, the 11-year NFL veteran is calling it a career, announcing his retirement on social media . View this post on Instagram “As I reflect on another year of life, I find myself especially grateful; not just for where I am, but for the journey that brought me here. This birthday feels a little different. It marks not only another year, but the beginning of a new chapter. To every love story, there comes a final chapter. Football gave me more than I ever could’ve imagined. It challenged me, shaped me, humbled me, and rewarded me in ways I’ll carry for the rest of my life,” the caption of his post read. “I came, I saw, I conquered and I leave with nothing but gratitude. The memories, the relationships, the victories, the lessons, they’ll stay with me forever! Thank you for every moment, every cheer, every lesson, and every opportunity. With love and gratitude, Allen Robinson.” Robinson was drafted in the second round of the 2014 NFL Draft by the Jacksonville Jaguars after playing his college ball at Penn State. His breakout season came in his second campaign in 2015. That year, he brought in 80 receptions for 1,400 yards with 14 touchdowns, leading the league in touchdown receptions. He was named a Pro Bowler that season. In 2017, he tore his ACL in the first game of the season and did not play for the Jaguars again. Robinson signed with the Chicago Bears ahead of the 2018 season and played five seasons in Chicago, including back-to-back years of over 1,110 yards. He would then sign as a free agent with the Los Angeles Rams ahead of the 2022 season, before being traded to the Pittsburgh Steelers for 2023. After being released by the Steelers, he signed with the New York Giants, but was cut prior to the season. Robinson then signed on with the Detroit Lions, initially on the practice squad, before being elevated to the main roster. He finishes his career with 565 receptions for 7,058 yards and 43 touchdowns. The post Allen Robinson announces retirement after 11 NFL seasons appeared first on ClutchPoints .

As the Jaguars get ready for the 2026 schedule , defensive end Josh Hines-Allen would speak about Lloyd’s absence and the one player who’s filling in his shoes. Came in and worked every single day to get better. When you lose a piece like that, somebody that was so inspirational to the team last year by the plays that he made, but you see the way that he worked every single day. You’re missing a piece like that; obviously, it hinders that mindset that you can have on a defense.” “But then, when you replace it with the guys that we have now, it’s people that can develop to be to the mindset that Devin was,” Hines-Allen continued. “But we have true ballers now. We got Ventrell [Miller]. I just told him today he’s going to lead the NFL in punchouts this year.” #Jaguars OLB Josh Hines-Allen tells me losing Devin Lloyd is a tough pill to swallow, but he has one bold prediction: LB Ventrell Miller – who is replacing Lloyd – will lead the NFL in punch-outs this season. “Catch the ball. articles.title: Marlins fire entire pro scouting department
articles.summary: The Miami Marlins have missed the playoffs each of the last two seasons, and the team is currently not set to make the playoffs in 2026. The Marlins also sold off at the MLB Trade Deadline, which further hampers their playoff chances. While the team attempts to make a run in the National League,
articles._body: The Miami Marlins have missed the playoffs each of the last two seasons, and the team is currently not set to make the playoffs in 2026. The Marlins also sold off at the MLB Trade Deadline , which further hampers their playoff chances. While the team attempts to make a run in the National League, they have made some major changes to the front office , per Bob Nightengale of USA Today. “The Miami Marlins make wholesale firings in their pro scouting department,” Nightengale posted on X, formerly Twitter. The entirety of the pro scouting department was let go today. According to Will Sammon and Ken Rosenthal of The Athletic, this was not an uncommon move . “Those familiar with the Marlins’ decision did not specify exactly how many scouts were being let go but said the move reflected the front office’s desire to use more video during the scouting process. Many clubs have cut from their various scouting departments in recent years because more video and information is available on players. For clubs like the Marlins, the scouting job has evolved, changing what they value,” Rosenthal and Sammon wrote. There could be a logical explanation, as the team is preparing for a potential lockout in 2027 as the collective bargaining agreement is set to expire. It could also be another cost-cutting measure. The Marlins are currently 67-64 on the year , which places them in third in the NL East, and nine games back of the Atlanta Braves in the division. They are also four games behind the San Diego Padres for the final wild card spot in the National League. The Marlins begin a series with the Boston Red Sox on Monday night.
