Entering his sixth season, it looked as if veteran Danny Pinter was the favorite for the role. However, Ravens head coach Jesse Minter conf
articles._body: Heading into last Wednesday’s joint practice with the Minnesota Vikings, the Baltimore Ravens had a three-way competition for the starting center role. Entering his sixth season, it looked as if veteran Danny Pinter was the favorite for the role. However, Ravens head coach Jesse Minter confirmed that Pinter’s right patellar tendon tear looked to be a season-ending injury. ESPN’s Jamison Hensley shared Minter’s take on the center competition via X, formerly Twitter. Now, Ethan Pocic and Jovaughn Gwyn will continue to compete for the role, according to Minter. Jesse Minter said Jovaughn Gwyn and Ethan Pocic will both get work with the first team this week. They’re competing for the starting center job. pic.twitter.com/xYvB6CZN8P — Jamison Hensley (@jamisonhensley) August 24, 2026 “Jesse Minter said Jovaughn Gwyn and Ethan Pocic will both get work with the first team this week,” shared Hensley. “They’re competing for the starting center job.” Pocic signed with Baltimore following four seasons with the Cleveland Browns. Before that, Pocic spent five seasons with the Seattle Seahawks after they drafted the ex-LSU standout in the second round of the 2017 draft. Meanwhile, Gwyn was a seventh-round pick with the Atlanta Falcons in 2023. He spent three years in Atlanta before joining the Ravens this offseason. Along with Pinter, the trio competed to replace former starter Tyler Linderbaum, a former first-round pick. Linderbaum left Baltimore for Las Vegas, signing a lucrative three-year deal with the Raiders. Now, the ex-Raven will help aid the development of number one overall pick Fernando Mendoza in the desert. Pinter’s likely season-ending injury comes after he joined Baltimore as well this offseason, following six years with the Indianapolis Colts. Ravens GM Eric DeCosta went with a few veterans in an attempt to find a diamond in the rough. With Pinter out, Baltimore could have lost one. Will Pocic or Gwyn stand out in his absence? Or will the pair struggle to connect with quarterback Lamar Jackson, putting the new system offensive coordinator Declan Doyle is installing at risk? articles.title: Reggie Watts Dropped From Podcast Intro & Comedy Festivals After Report Alleging Disturbing Behavior in Romantic Relationships
articles.summary: A recent piece brought to light several claims of "reckless" drug use, psychological abuse & more.
articles._body: The Comedy Bang! Bang! podcast and multiple festivals appear to be distancing themselves from Reggie Watts following a disturbing Rolling Stone report that detailed his allegedly toxic, controlling and at times abusive behavior toward ex-girlfriend Katherine McCollough, who died by suicide this spring after developing an addiction to drugs over the course of their relationship. The outlet reported Monday (Aug. 24) — four days after the initial investigation was published — that the Watts-composed Comedy Bang! Bang! theme song had been notably absent from the latest episode, despite serving as the intro music since 2011. Instead, Rolling Stone writes that the installment was preceded by “a generic British woman’s voice” that simply stated the episode’s number. Also in the aftermath of the publication’s shocking report on Watts, the 2026 lineups for Greenbelt Festival, Shambala Festival and Electric Picnic no longer display his name. As previously announced, Watts had been scheduled to perform at all three events over the course of the weekend of Aug. 27-30. Billboard has reached out to Watts’ reps for comment. The developments come after the musical comedian faced lengthy accusations from numerous people interviewed by Rolling Stone of him pressuring his former partner, McCollough, into using heavy amounts of dangerous substances such as ketamine in order to remain emotionally close with him throughout their romance, which lasted from approximately May 2024 to October 2025. A few months after their breakup, McCollough — a Cornell law student and eventual producer for some of Watts’ comedy endeavors — traveled to Peru to obtain a euthanasia agent and end her life. Watts’ lawyer, Andrew Brettler, vehemently denied all claims that the former Late Late Show With James Corden bandleader was ever “abusive” toward any of his romantic partners, adding that it’s “dangerously false” to link McCollough’s suicide to her relationship with Watts. “Ms. McCollough did not need any so-called ‘encouragement’ from him [to take drugs],” the attorney told Rolling Stone , calling McCollough an already “experienced” drug user prior to meeting Watts. Numerous people close to McCollough, however, told the publication that the South Carolina native had only previously taken drugs in small quantities before dating Watts, a vocal advocate of using ketamine as a means of spiritual enlightenment who would allegedly goad his then-girlfriend into taking drugs in large amounts. One source who remained anonymous claimed in the report that Watts is “incredibly reckless” with how he “administers” dosages of ketamine to other people, including but not limited to McCollough. “I’m confident if she never met Reggie, she’d be alive,” an anonymous former classmate of McCollough’s told Rolling Stone . Sources alleged plenty of other alarming behaviors exhibited by Watts, accusing him of withholding payment for McCollough’s part in producing and financing one of his comedy specials and his improv talk show Watch Watts Happen Live . Five other women who previously dated Watts told Rolling Stone that they, too, had experienced Watts being allegedly emotionally and psychologically abusive toward them during their relationships with him, which his attorney denied and called “false.” The attorney also denied one woman’s accusation that Watts had knowingly exposed her to an STD, while providing no response to a different claim that Watts had allegedly filmed a sexual encounter with a partner without her knowledge. If you or someone you know is currently struggling with depression, suicidal thoughts or substance abuse issues, call or text the  National Suicide Prevention Lifeline  by dialing   988 or contact the Substance Abuse & Mental Health Services Administration  at 1-800-662-4357.

articles.title: Beto y Sus Canarios Leader Edilberto Portillo ‘Is Alive’ After Armed Attack, His Family Says
articles.summary: “Don Beto,” as he's known, was shot before a performance at the Rodeo Texcoco in Mexico on Saturday (Aug. 22)
articles._body: Edilberto Portillo , founder and lead singer of the Tierra Caliente music group Beto y Sus Canarios , is alive after being shot on Saturday shortly before going onstage at Rodeo Texcoco in Chicoloapan, Estado de México, his family said Monday (August 24) in a press release shared on social media. “Given the news that has circulated in recent hours, the family of Edilberto Portillo, known as ‘Don Beto,’ founder of Beto y Sus Canarios, wishes to inform the public, friends, fans and the media that Don Beto is alive and currently receiving medical attention after being the victim of an armed attack,” reads the statement , published on the band’s official Facebook account. “Don Beto is under the care of medical professionals and receiving all necessary attention. Our absolute priority at this time is his life, his recovery, and his safety.” The family added that no other members of the band were injured during the incident. Portillo was shot by unknown individuals outside Rodeo Texcoco, where he was scheduled to perform Saturday night at the event “Los 4 Patrones de Tierra Caliente.” The lineup also included other groups from the genre, such as Los Player’s de Tuzantla, Súper Banda Los Pajaritos and La Dinastía de Tuzantla. The incident gained traction on social media, but no authorities, the venue or anyone from the group made any statements until Monday afternoon. The event organizers also did not address the incident and proceeded with their scheduled program. With over four decades career, Beto y Sus Canarios, originally from Huetamo, Michoacán, was founded in 1987 by Portillo and Gabino García, launching a genre that came to be known as Tierra Caliente music, named after the region. The musical movement gained momentum in the early 2000s with hits like “Está Llorando Mi Corazón” and “Noche Eterna,” and had chart presence on Billboard . Their 2005 LP Ardientes spent two weeks at No. 1 on Top Regional Mexican Albums, where the group placed a total of seven albums. On Regional Mexican Airplay, they charted 13 songs, with two reaching No. 1: “No Puedo Olvidarte,” which spent 16 weeks at the top that same year, and “Está Llorando Mi Corazón,” which led for 12 weeks in 2004. “We deeply appreciate the expressions of love, prayers and messages of support we have received,” the family added in their statement. “We respectfully ask the public and the media to avoid sharing unconfirmed information or speculation about what happened and to rely only on information shared through our official channels.”

He was traded to the Miami Dolphins ahead of the 2023 season, and then traded to the Steelers ahead of the 2025 campaign. Overall, Ramsey has played in 152 games, with 622 tackles, six sacks, 116 pass breakups and 15 interceptions. Ramsey is expected to be one of ten defensive backs the Steelers keep on the roster . articles.title: Fever’s Sophie Cunningham urges haters to ‘look at the stats’ in confident clapback
articles.summary: NEW YORK — The Indiana Fever’s road trip took them to Brooklyn on Saturday night, where the New York Liberty won 109-102. They, and a particularly charged home crowd, were ready for battle. Ahead of the game, competing protests took place outside of the Barclays Center in the wake of Fever
articles._body: NEW YORK — The Indiana Fever’s road trip took them to Brooklyn on Saturday night , where the New York Liberty won 109-102. They, and a particularly charged home crowd, were ready for battle. Ahead of the game, competing protests took place outside of the Barclays Center in the wake of Fever Sophie Cunningham’s comments about wanting to “protect young girls in a locker room, or young girls in sport, who shouldn’t have to go against biological men.” Those protesting any inclusion of transgender women in women’s sports used Cunningham’s name, image, and likeness on t-shirts and signs, ahead of Saturday’s matchup. The same happened outside of recent games in Chicago, Seattle, Portland, Las Vegas, Minnesota, and Dallas. Before facing off against New York, reporters asked Cunningham about the latest iteration of the continued protests. The 30-year-old said while “ it’s cool that people are using their freedom of speech and doing what they want to do,” she’s in her “own two feet” and solely focused on the Liberty. The Fever came to Brooklyn having won five of their last seven. Cunningham declared ahead of that stretch that she wanted “to get back to basketball.” Before the game, she also disagreed with the notion that anything had changed for her personally amid Indiana’s success. The wing asserted nothing had changed at all. “I think that if you look at my stats, from the very beginning of the year, that I’ve been shooting a really high percentage. I’m always one, two, or three [in the WNBA] with the 3-point percentage. And, so, I’ve been locked in. I don’t know why everyone thinks this is such a huge distraction. I’ve been locked in, look at the stats, look at our team stats, I’m really excited about where our team is at,” she said. Cunningham didn’t pick the best time to direct fans to her statistics . She had just missed all four of her shot attempts against the Dallas Wings en route to recording zero points, rebounds, and assists in 15 minutes. Her point about her efficiency, though, holds mostly true. The Missouri product ranks fourth in WNBA 3-point percentage through Sunday. She was in third before a 1-of-4 performance against the Chicago Sky. The Fever still won that game after dropping back-to-back contests to the Dallas Wings and Liberty. Cunningham says ‘America can get better’ at showing peace and love Patrick Gorski-Imagn Images Despite expressing an interest herself in getting “back to basketball,” Cunningham also implied on Saturday that efforts to silence her come from a country-wide issue with navigating disagreement. The wing was asked if stunts by former NBA players to capitalize on the topic were opportunities for WNBA unity. She responded by saying she’s going to continue to be herself, regardless of what anyone thinks, and offering thoughts on Americans needing to improve their approach to conflict. “I think it’s funny, because- I said this in the last game, people are like, ‘hey, you guys have a huge platform. Use it!’ Well, once you use it, ‘Hey, stick to basketball. You’re an athlete.’ Like, you can’t satisfy anyone,” Cunningham explained. “So you might as well be yourself, and beat to your own drum, and that’s what I do. I’m 100% okay, and happy, and at peace with who I am. You can always be better, but I do think that’s something America can get better at. Maybe not always agreeing with people, but also just showing peace and love.” In a vacuum, Cunningham is right. However, an initial lack of peace and love for the transgender community began this discussion. Simply put, there are no transgender women playing in the WNBA. NCAA President Charlie Baker testified in December 2024 that he knew of fewer than 10 transgender college student-athletes among over 510,000 in total. And the league’s only issues regarding the participation of transgender athletes, prior to Cunningham’s interview with ESPN, have been brought to WNBA arenas by disruptors like Enes Kanter Freedom . Kanter Freedom’s stunt is a low point for Sophie Cunningham, WNBA Patrick Gorski-Imagn Images The former NBA center attended a Chicago Sky game on Sunday under the guise of support for Cunningham. Arena security removed him after he stepped onto the court in an attempt to confront Sky guard Natasha Cloud. Ironically, the largest present danger to the WNBA seems to be Kanter Freedom himself. As a result, many believe agitators like Kanter Freedom and Royce White are acting in bad faith. Whether it’s to distract from issues that more directly affect Americans or to advance their own political agendas is unclear. The WNBA has certainly not benefited from the intrusion, which directly impacted a Fever game on Sunday. That’s what made Cunningham’s decision to pass on the opportunity to unite players against these stunts odd. It was even more odd that she portrayed herself as the victim of hypocrites. The pushback to her comments did not stem from her mere utilization of her platform, but rather her specific use of that platform to amplify what many believe is a political distraction. It’s tough to get an exact read on what exactly Cunningham wants those fans to discuss, instead. In some moments, she’s maintaining that she’s just being herself — guiding media and fans alike to focus on Fever basketball and her 3-point consistency. In others, she’s insisting on her apathy toward the subject while simultaneously calling out critics for trying to censor her. The only thing that seems clear at the moment is that this debate, and the resulting protests, will continue to follow the Fever. No matter how exhausting their road trips may be, fans are seemingly going to gather in front of arenas to support their side. Cunningham sees the prover

articles.title: Bryson DeChambeau shares cryptic Instagram post amid LIV’s future

articles._body: Bryson DeChambeau just gave golf fans another reason to question LIV Golf’s future. The two-time U.S. Open champion shared a cryptic message on Instagram that read, “It was a good run.” DeChambeau did not explain the post, leaving fans to wonder whether it referenced LIV, his future with the league, or something unrelated. However, the timing immediately fueled speculation amid ongoing questions about the circuit’s long-term outlook. His message also came shortly after he acknowledged the challenges LIV faces during its event in Indianapolis . DeChambeau admitted the league has “a lot against us” while stressing that employees, players, and organizers continue working to make the events successful. He also pointed to the economic impact LIV tournaments can have on the communities that host them. “You know, it’s tough. It’s not easy. We definitely have a lot against us. But, behind the scenes, we have a lot of people who are working hard to make this possible for not only all the players out here, but all the fans that come out to these events. The economical impact.” Those comments suggested DeChambeau remained hopeful despite the league’s uncertain position. Still, DeChambeau is one of the league’s most recognizable players. His major championship success and massive online following have made him central to LIV’s efforts to attract fans and maintain relevance. Any suggestion that his involvement could change is bound to draw attention. Until DeChambeau clarifies his message, speculation will continue. For now, four simple words have created another uncomfortable question about LIV Golf’s future. articles.title: Analyst ‘can’t see a world’ where Dodgers’ Shohei Ohtani just opens a playoff game
articles.summary: As Los Angeles Dodgers star Shohei Ohtani is making a push for another MVP award, he still has yet to return to the mound this season, though he is progressing ahead of the postseason. While Dodgers fans await the pitching return of Ohtani, this former player and analyst would question a certain
articles._body: As Los Angeles Dodgers star Shohei Ohtani is making a push for another MVP award, he still has yet to return to the mound this season, though he is progressing ahead of the postseason. While Dodgers fans await the pitching return of Ohtani , this former player and analyst would question a certain aspect of the sensation on the mound when the playoffs come around. Speaking on MLB Network, Mark DeRosa would express that he “can’t see a world” where Ohtani opens a playoff game, citing how the team has Blake Snell, Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Tarik Skubal, and a “rested” bullpen. “I don’t know how they roll out the first three games of the postseason, but these are the three guys,” DeRosa said. “And I saw Otani is getting ready to come back, and he’s thrown getting he’s thrown some live sims to Will Smith, and they’re going to start building him back up, maybe as early as the first week of September. And [Tyler] Glasnow is scheduled to pitch this week.” “No, there’s no way. And I can’t see a world where…are you going to start a postseason game with him just opening?” DeRosa continued. “These dudes are nasty, and your bullpen’s rested.” #MLBCentral on the Dodgers' rotation with the Postseason approaching: "They're starting to roll it out now… it's starting to take shape." pic.twitter.com/VXTHSjM5ch — MLB Network (@MLBNetwork) August 24, 2026 Ohtani hasn’t pitched since early July due to a knee issue, though it hasn’t stopped his offensive production, recording a .288 batting average with 30 home runs and 80 RBIs. When pitching this season in the 14 games he’s started, he had a 1.79 ERA with 95 strikeouts and an 8-2 record. At any rate, it remains to be seen when Ohtani returns to pitching for Los Angeles, as manager Dave Roberts said on Saturday that he threw 30 pitches and will need another live batting practice , via Fabian Ardaya. articles.title: Show HN: My friend built a Gleam server – let's try to take it down
articles.summary: Hi! My friend, who I'm mentoring, had some free time and was looking for something interesting to build. I suggested he take a look at Gleam, since I've been interested in the language myself, and build both the backend and frontend for a project that fits the spirit of the BEAM ecosystem well.
articles._body: Hi! My friend, who I'm mentoring, had some free time and was looking for something interesting to build. I suggested he take a look at Gleam, since I've been interested in the language myself, and build both the backend and frontend for a project that fits the spirit of the BEAM ecosystem well. The result is https://kms.andrewpavlov.org/ . Using the UI on the website, you can gradually increase the load and watch how the server's CPU and RAM usage respond in real time. Maybe the HN effect will do its job and take the server down. Although I have a feeling the BEAM might survive. :) For those hearing about Gleam for the first time: Gleam is a functional, statically typed programming language that compiles to both Erlang and JavaScript. This makes it possible to build backend and frontend code in the same language and, where appropriate, share code between the two targets. On the backend, Gleam runs on the Erlang VM (BEAM), giving it access to Erlang/OTP's lightweight concurrency, fault tolerance, and supervision model. Failures in individual processes can be isolated from other processes rather than necessarily bringing down the entire application. On the frontend, Gleam's type system catches many classes of errors at compile time, which can significantly reduce runtime bugs. The programming model is somewhat reminiscent of Elm, while still being part of the broader BEAM ecosystem. The project is open source, and the website itself is inspired by the Gleam website. I think Gleam is an interesting technology for building highly concurrent applications, especially real-time systems where Erlang and Elixir have already proven themselves at scale. WhatsApp and Discord are good examples of what the BEAM ecosystem is capable of. My friend built the project and will be answering questions in the comments. I'll be following along as well. Let's see if the HN effect can take it down. :) Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49426508 Points: 1 # Comments: 0

Sean Payton was not happy with the Broncos’ performance in the preseason affair. In the game, cornerback Riley Moss suffered a rib injury, but coach Payton is not concerned, per Chris Tom
articles._body: The Denver Broncos took a loss to the Green Bay Packers in their second preseason game on Friday night. Sean Payton was not happy with the Broncos’ performance in the preseason affair . In the game, cornerback Riley Moss suffered a rib injury , but coach Payton is not concerned, per Chris Tomasson of the Denver Gazette. “Broncos coach Sean Payton said Riley Moss injury is nothing serious and they are being smart by him not practicing,” Tomasson posted on X, formerly Twitter. Moss was a third-round pick of the 2023 NFL Draft by the Broncos after playing his college football at Iowa. He played in 14 games in his rookie season, coming away with six tackles. Moss broke out in 2024, making 14 starts and coming away with 86 tackles, eight pass breakups and an interception. He would improve in 2025, starting all 17 games for the Broncos. He came away with 80 tackles, 19 pass breakups, and an interception. Moss was on the sideline during the practice, along with Drew Sanders, Alex Forsyth, and Caleb Lohner. RJ Harvey was also on the side for the first part of practice. Meanwhile, Frank Crum was absent from practice after an injury he suffered in the preseason game. While Moss missing any time would be a major issue, the team still has 2024 NFL Defensive Player of the Year Pat Surtain II in the secondary. The Broncos also recently added Taylor Rapp to the elite defense . The Broncos have high expectations in 2026. They made it to the AFC Championship in 2025 and hope to take the next step this year. They open their season on September 14 on the road against the Kansas City Chiefs on Monday Night Football. articles.title: Colts assistant reveals coaching plan after suffering brutal knee injury during preseason game
articles.summary: Indianapolis Colts special teams coordinator Brian Mason does not expect his latest left knee injury to keep him away from the sideline when the regular season begins. Mason suffered multiple ligament damage during the final play of Indianapolis’ preseason opener against the New England Pat
articles._body: Indianapolis Colts special teams coordinator Brian Mason does not expect his latest left knee injury to keep him away from the sideline when the regular season begins. Mason suffered multiple ligament damage during the final play of Indianapolis’ preseason opener against the New England Patriots after two players rolled into him near the sideline . Despite the injury, Mason returned to the field for the Colts’ next practice and has not missed a day of work. He is coaching from the press box for the remainder of the preseason but plans to return to his normal sideline position when Indianapolis opens the regular season versus the Baltimore Ravens on Sept. 13. “Before New England, I was a coach with a really bad knee that will someday need a knee replacement,” Mason said on Monday. “After the New England game, I am a coach with a really bad knee that still someday needs a knee replacement.” Mason also does not plan to undergo surgery because of the latest injury. He described his knee as one that already needed a future replacement before the collision and said that remains the case after the latest setback. The injury is the seventh major issue Mason has experienced with his left knee. He tore the ACL twice while playing running back at Zionsville High School and suffered two more ACL tears during his college career at Denison. The second college injury ended his playing career after doctors determined he could no longer pass a physical. Mason later suffered another ACL tear in 2012 while playing basketball at Butler. In 2021, while working on landscaping, he sustained another serious injury to the same knee. He now avoids taking unnecessary risks with landscaping, but his coaching responsibilities require him to remain active on game days. During Colts games, Mason works closely with long snapper Luke Rhodes and punter Rigoberto Sanchez on punt decisions when Indianapolis is backed up. He also communicates with the personal protector about snap counts and works with the gunners on potential punt-return looks. When the Colts move the ball and reach kicking situations, Mason shifts his attention to the kickers. He also makes adjustments during kickoff and kick-return situations, making his sideline presence an important part of his responsibilities. Mason is entering his fourth season as Indianapolis’ special teams coordinator after joining Shane Steichen’s staff in 2023. Before that, he held the same position at Notre Dame in 2022 and Cincinnati from 2018-21. His coaching career began at Denison after his playing career ended because of his knee. articles.title: Keisean Nixon is finally taking Packers’ heated CB competition into his own hands
articles.summary: The Green Bay Packers have plenty of talent in the secondary, as the team has enough cornerbacks that there is a position battle going on in training camp. On Monday, Keisean Nixon seemed to have finally gained a big advantage with a strong practice. Reports indicate that Monday’s practice
articles._body: The Green Bay Packers have plenty of talent in the secondary, as the team has enough cornerbacks that there is a position battle going on in training camp. On Monday, Keisean Nixon seemed to have finally gained a big advantage with a strong practice. Reports indicate that Monday’s practice was easily Nixon’s best performance throughout training camp so far, according to Kyle Malzhan of WFRV Local 5 in Green Bay. The 29-year-old cornerback appears to be in line to win one of the starting jobs before Week 1 of the regular season. “This is by far Keisean Nixon’s best training camp practice of the summer,” Malzhan reported. It’s said that Nixon picked off quarterback Jordan Love to end a two-minute drill , per Andy Herman of Packer Report. In fact, the defense got the better of the offense through the entirety of the drill. Nixon’s interception was the icing on the cake of what was a strong showing from the defensive unit. “Love rolls out, heavy pressure. Picked by Keisean to end the drive,” Herman reported. “What a bounce-back day for Keisean Nixon so far.” Other cornerbacks in the mix for playing time on the outside include Carrington Valentine, Benjamin St-Juste, and 2026 rookie Brandon Cisse. Meanwhile, Javon Bullard and Kamal Hadden are competing for the nickelback position in the Packers’ defense. Keisean Nixon is entering his eighth season in the NFL, and his fifth in Green Bay. He’s been a major contributor for the Packers throughout his tenure, as he’s never missed a single contest in his first four years with the club. He finished last season with 72 combined tackles (58 solo), one interception, 17 pass deflections, and one fumble recovery. His efforts earned him the first Pro Bowl nod in his career. articles.summary: Big Ten football will be on your televisions Saturday afternoon. Week 0 provides a showdown between USC and San Jose State, before the rest of the conference joins the party Week 1. It’s been three straight seasons of national championships in the Big Ten, now looking to four-peat. Some teams
articles._body: Big Ten football will be on your televisions Saturday afternoon. Week 0 provides a showdown between USC and San Jose State , before the rest of the conference joins the party Week 1. It’s been three straight seasons of national championships in the Big Ten, now looking to four-peat. Some teams are receiving more hype than others, while some are not receiving enough. Everyone wants to know who is overrated at the moment and possibly even underrated. CBS Sports took a swing at the idea on Monday. [ $19.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage ] Eight different programs are involved, two of which are considered both overrated and underrated. Let’s check out the full list from CBS Sports below, starting with a potential College Football Playoff contender. USC Trojans – Overrated Beginning out West, the USC Trojans are the first overrated team to be mentioned. Per usual with head coach Lincoln Riley , defense is the main reason. Riley brought in former TCU nemesis Gary Patterson to run the show. CBS Sports’ John Talty is not buying into Patterson actually performing in Los Angeles. “If you want to buy into Lincoln Riley and USC, go for it,” Talty said. “I won’t be one of those people… I’m skeptical that turning to Gary Patterson, who last worked as an on-field coach in 2021, to run the defense proves to be some magical fix.” Washington Huskies – Underrated Of the Big Ten’s four recent expansion teams, Washington might get the least publicity. Jedd Fisch has spent the last two seasons in the Pacific Northwest building his program. Now, the Huskies feel like they have a roster worthy of contending, led by quarterback Demond Williams Jr . “A difficult November stretch (Penn State, Indiana, Oregon) will determine just how far the Huskies can go, but I expect them to be in the Big Ten mix when that slog begins,” Chris Hummer said. Michigan Wolverines – Overrated Michigan unexpectedly entered a new era after firing Sherrone Moore. An unusual coaching search led to Kyle Whittingham taking over after a lengthy stint at Utah. While many are excited to see what Whittingham can do in the Big Ten, that’s one of the reasons Hummer is skeptical of the Wolverines. Two other areas bring pause. First, he mentions the lack of weapons surrounding second-year quarterback Bryce Underwood. And then on the other side of the ball, just three defensive starters return. Not usually a recipe for success. Iowa Hawkeyes – Both Conflicting feelings are there when it comes to Iowa. Beginning with the case of them being overrated, the loss of Mark Gronowski is pointed to. Not because of his ability to throw the ball, but because of the quarterback’s threat of taking off in the red zone with his legs. “The Hawkeyes finished 11th in the country in points per red zone possession, due in part to Gronowski’s legs… For a team that wins on the margins, any regression in that area could cause problems,” Fornelli said. On the flip side, Talty argues that Iowa is always considered an underrated team entering a season. Preseason hype is not exactly what Kirk Ferentz is used to. Yet, the Hawkeyes find a way to perform on an annual basis. “The Hawkeyes seem to be perennially underrated,” Talty said. “They don’t play a sexy style of football and never get the preseason hype as some of their peers.” UCLA Bruins – Underrated “Contextually, Bob Chesney may have been the best hire on the coaching carousel,” Brandon Marcello said. ” … Grabbing a coach who can rebuild the roster overnight with a slew of transfers from a playoff team like James Madison is as good as it gets.” A James Madison coach taking some players with him to a new job and finding instant success? Sure does sound familiar. Maybe Chesney is looking to replicate the Curt Cignetti model. UCLA likely is not expecting a national championship but Marcello believes they will be a middle-of-the-pack Big Ten team. Maryland Terrapins – Underrated On paper, Maryland put together a poor 4-8 season after winning four straight to start the year. Three of those losses were by a combined 10 points. A lot of the same talent returns for head coach Mike Locksley , hoping to make a jump. “The Zahir Mathis injury stings for Maryland, but other than that, the Terps bring back so much of the top-end talent that was young from last year’s team,” Johnson said. ” … Don’t sleep on the Terps.” Penn State Nittany Lions – Both Similar to Iowa, Penn State and first-year head coach Matt Campbell are on both sides of the coin here. Brad Crawford made the case for underrated, explaining how Campbell brought over a lot of familiar faces from Iowa State. Continuity plus an easy schedule makes for a successful recipe. “Facing the most favorable slate among Big Ten teams ranked in the preseason… it’s a yellow brick road — of sorts — Year 1 setup for Matt Campbell, who brought the best of his two-deep from Iowa State with him to Happy Valley,” Crawford said. Richard Johnson is not buying the idea of an easy schedule being why Penn State is underrated, though. Maybe the results are positive ones for Campbell, but Johnson appears to be bumping the brakes to the team’s quality. “With Penn State, it feels like the upshot everybody’s pointing at is the schedule, which doesn’t necessarily mean you’re actually a good team,” Johnson said. “It just means you play an easy first five or six games.” Minnesota Golden Gophers – Underrated Minnesota is not going to produce a lot of glitz and glamour in the offseason. articles.title: AI is hitting entry-level jobs hardest, Stanford study finds
articles.summary: Young employment in AI-impacted fields down 19% compared to more AI-resistant occupations.
articles._body: For years , AI industry watchers of all stripes have been warning of a coming jobs apocalypse driven by ultra-intelligent AI systems that will be able to replicate most human tasks more cheaply. Now, newly updated research from Stanford University economists suggests AI seems to be causing significant entry-level job losses for younger workers in some fields, even as older workers appear largely unaffected so far. The August 2026 edition of "Canaries in the Coal Mine? Six Facts about the Recent Employment Effects of Artificial Intelligence" updates and revises a paper of the same name published last year with fresh data and refined statistics. In that update, the Stanford researchers find the employment trends they identified for entry-level workers last year are persisting and expanding. Specifically, employment levels for workers ages 22 to 25 in the most "AI-exposed" occupations are now 19 percent below those of their peers in fields less exposed to AI disruption. Last year, that gap measured just 13 percent. Read full article Comments

articles.title: 1 stat that proves Josh Sweat’s importance to Cardinals’ pass rush
articles.summary: The Arizona Cardinals received an important defensive boost Monday when edge rusher Josh Sweat was activated from the physically unable to perform list (PUP). One statistic explains exactly why his return matters. According to NFL Research, only six players have recorded more sacks than Sweat sin
articles._body: The Arizona Cardinals received an important defensive boost Monday when edge rusher Josh Sweat was activated from the physically unable to perform list (PUP). One statistic explains exactly why his return matters. According to NFL Research, only six players have recorded more sacks than Sweat since 2024, including the playoffs: Myles Garrett, Micah Parsons, Will Anderson Jr., Danielle Hunter, Nik Bonitto, and Brian Burns. That places Sweat among the NFL’s most productive pass rushers over that stretch and reinforces how much Arizona’s defense relies on his ability to disrupt opposing quarterbacks. Sweat recorded 12 sacks in 17 games last season after spending the first seven years of his career with the Philadelphia Eagles. His production gave the Cardinals the reliable edge presence they needed, and his return should immediately strengthen their defensive front. The Cardinals also removed running back Trey Benson from the roster in a corresponding move. For Arizona, having Sweat healthy is particularly important in a division featuring several dangerous offenses. A consistent pass rush can force hurried throws, create turnovers and reduce the pressure placed on the secondary. Sweat’s impact extends beyond his sack totals. Opposing offenses must account for him in protection, which can create opportunities for the rest of Arizona’s defensive line. Still, the sack statistic tells the story better than anything else. When only six players have been more productive at reaching the quarterback over the past two seasons, losing that player is not something a defense can easily overcome. The Cardinals need Sweat on the field. His activation suggests their most important pass rusher is moving closer to being ready when the games count. articles.title: Field Yates reveals the silver lining in naming Browns’ Deshaun Watson QB1
articles.summary: Deshaun Watson will be the starting quarterback for the Cleveland Browns in Week 1, and many fans aren’t feeling the best about it. Whether it was because of how he played over the past few weeks or how much money he’s making, the Browns ultimately believe that he gives them the best
articles._body: Deshaun Watson will be the starting quarterback for the Cleveland Browns in Week 1, and many fans aren’t feeling the best about it. Whether it was because of how he played over the past few weeks or how much money he’s making, the Browns ultimately believe that he gives them the best chance to win. ESPN’s Field Yates offered a different take for Browns fans, and though it may not excite them for this season, it could hold some weight at the end of the year. “Today was yet another, to me, message from the Cleveland Browns that the QB of their future is not on the roster right now. They have two first-round picks in the 2027 NFL Draft; that’s probably when they will acquire their quarterback of the future. I know Shedeur Sanders fans are a passionate bunch and probably feel he is or can be the answer for Cleveland. If the Browns felt that way, he’d be starting from the very beginning of the season because if you believe enough in a player to be your QB1 of the future, you’re going to believe enough in that player to start Week 1,” Yates said. "Today was yet another, to me, message from the Cleveland Browns that the QB of their future is not on the roster right now." — @FieldYates on Deshaun Watson being named the Week 1 starter pic.twitter.com/2f20Dy7H0H — NFL on ESPN (@ESPNNFL) August 24, 2026 Most people believed that Sanders was the answer at QB1 for the Browns, but apparently he didn’t do enough to secure the spot. He’s not out of the picture yet, as Watson can very much still be benched if he doesn’t perform to the Browns’ standard throughout the season. If that is the case, it’ll be interesting to see what the Browns do with Watson moving forward. Cutting him may be the worst idea ever because of the cap hit they’ll take, and nobody is going to trade for him at this point. For now, they can only hope that Watson proves to be the answer and leads the team to wins this season. articles.title: Confidence Building for Kevin McGiven and the Utah Offense
articles.summary: Utah OC Kevin McGiven has a growing confidence in his offense as the season inches closer.
articles._body: With just a little bit over a week to go until the 2026 football season kicks off, Utah offensive coordinator Kevin McGiven has growing confidence in his side of the ball. While it starts at the quarterback position, it trickles down to each and every room on the offense. “When the ball is distributed, you’re not really in a panic in terms of whose hands it’s going to fall in. I think we have an ability to mix and match personnel and formation to attack people some different ways,” McGiven said on Monday. “Guys have shown proficiency in being able to execute different things with our schemes and with our presentations. So I like the direction that’s headed. I like where we’re headed culturally, in terms of just the effort that they play with and the physicality that they play with. I think that’s come a long way as well, and a lot of things that I think they’re doing pretty well right now.” McGiven joked that he doesn’t have to be perfect as a play caller this fall because a quarterback like Devon Dampier can take a negative and turn it into a positive. “He just kind of makes things right when things break down. Obviously you want to put him in good situations, but that is one of the key components to the ball moving, and we’re able to see that in practices when he just kind of takes over or something kind of breaks down, and he’s still able to make something out of it. But his playmaking ability, coupled with the progress that he’s made as a leader, as a decision-maker, his processing within the offense- all those kinds of things- I’m really anxious to see it all come to fruition,” McGiven said Dampier has always been a leader for this Utah team, but the senior has taken a major step forward in that department over the last few months. “I think with him a big factor in all of it was just how comfortable he was with the offense. Sometimes hard to be a leader, and especially a vocal leader, when you’re out there, and you’re kind of swimming a little bit,” McGiven said. “But the more confident you get, the faster you’re playing. Then you can start to think about those other things, and getting other guys going because you’re not so worried about yourself and making sure that you know what’s going on and that you’re taking care of your role first.” The Utah wide receiver room also has continued to pick up speed over the last few weeks with Ricky Johnson and Creed Whittemore impressing the Utes’ first-year OC. “Creed probably has carved out more of a role than what he even had in the spring,” McGiven said. McGiven is also optimistic about his tight end room and the usage they will get this fall. It starts with Hunter Andrews and his ability to stretch the field, and it cascades through other members of the room. “I think they’ve all really, really developed as in-line guys in terms of blocking and with their ability to execute things in the pass game, and make some plays and contested catches, things like that. And so the biggest thing I see in that room is just a bunch of versatility and different guys that you can utilize in different ways in terms of your personnel packages,” McGiven said. The Utah offensive line remains the area where things are still up in the air, but McGiven has trust in whatever five players earn the starting nod come game week. “Still a little bit of mixing and matching going on, but I think as a as a total unit, there’s there’s enough chemistry there, regardless of who you put in there, where the communication is really good because those guys have been around each other and they’ve been in the in the system now for a little bit, and so I think there’s there’s a comfortability with those guys, regardless of who’s in there. There’s trust being developed, regardless of who’s in there at what spot, and still just trying to solidify things a little bit,” he said. articles.summary: The Los Angeles Sparks suffered one of their worst losses of the season last Thursday after falling to the Atlanta Dream, 124-88. With a rematch against the Dream on Monday, the Sparks could be short-handed as starting wing Rae Burrell popped up on the team’s injury report. Rae Burrell is officia
articles._body: The Los Angeles Sparks suffered one of their worst losses of the season last Thursday after falling to the Atlanta Dream, 124-88. With a rematch against the Dream on Monday, the Sparks could be short-handed as starting wing Rae Burrell popped up on the team’s injury report. Rae Burrell is officially listed as questionable on the Sparks’ injury report for their game against the Dream due to an illness. If Burrell is unable to play, the Sparks will be without one of their primary scoring options. The No. 9 overall pick in the 2022 WNBA Draft, Burrell has been one of the lone bright spots amid a roller coaster season that will see the Sparks miss the playoffs for the sixth consecutive year . Her role shuffled a bit during the beginning of the season, going from starting to coming off the bench, but she’s solidified herself as arguably the team’s most consistent player this year. Burrell has appeared in all 37 games to this point, including 29 starts, at just about 29 minutes per game. She’s been averaging a career-high 14.4 points, just about double her average from last season. She’s also putting up 2.3 rebounds and 2.5 assists with splits of 46.4 percent shooting from the field, 38.7 percent shooting from the 3-point line and 79.5 percent shooting from the free-throw line. She’s coming off one of her best games this season during the Sparks’ win against the Connecticut Sun last Saturday, finishing with a game-high 20 points to go along with two rebounds, two assists, three steals and three blocked shots. After that game, she explained how her comfort level with her teammates has contributed to her career year. “I think just being comfortable, honestly. It just makes it so much easier when you’re comfortable out there, when your teammates and your coaches, they got your back,” Burrell said, “Just being able to play with that confidence. So I think that’s just helped me play more freely.” The former Tennessee star returned to the Sparks this past offseason, re-signing on a one-year contract after being a reserved free agent in which the Sparks held exclusive negotiating rights. articles._body: The Arizona Cardinals got hit with the early NFL Injury bug. Quarterback Carson Beck and running back Jeremiyah Love aren’t anticipated to play in the NFL Preseason finale. But the Cards looks ready to lure back edge rusher Josh Sweat from the PUP (Physically Unable to Perform) list. Yet a corresponding move needed to be made in order to activate the veteran veteran. Through cutting former third round selection Trey Benson at running back, with ESPN NFL insider Adam Schefter confirming the Monday move . Benson appeared to become lost in the backfield shuffle anyway amid Love’s arrival. He played two seasons under former head coach Jonathan Gannon, tallying 451 rushing yards and scoring once. He also caught 19 passes out of the backfield for 123 yards. Benson first arrived as the 66th overall pick of the 2024 draft class out of Oregon. Plus he previously played at Florida State. But again, Love’s addition as the third overall selection this past April painted the picture that Benson’s usage was going to be diluted. He was already dealing with a late 2025 ailment too. He never touched the football in the 34-13 preseason loss to the Dallas Cowboys amid his 2025 knee injury. He’s endured a rather oft-injured career in the desert and officially won’t become a part of the Mike LaFleur regime moving forward. Meanwhile, LaFleur can certainly lean into Sweat’s past championship experience to rebuild the Cards. Sweat won Super Bowl 59 with the Philadelphia Eagles as part of a loaded defensive lineman room. He first joined Arizona to reunite with Gannon, who oversaw his 2021 Pro Bowl campaign. articles.title: Data centers become "killer application" for new power transformer tech
articles.summary: Solid-state transformers could also benefit EV charging and, someday, households.
articles._body: Data centers have become the largest driver of a surging electricity demand that is straining US power grids. But the AI data center boom has also accelerated investment in a technology that could provide a silver lining for everyone—solid-state power transformers that replace industrial-age technology with modern power electronics. Power grids currently rely on conventional transformer technology that is painstakingly assembled by hand and has a fundamental design dating back to the 1880s. Two copper wire coils manually wound around a steel core create electromagnetic fields that help step up voltage levels of alternating current electricity for long-distance transmission or step down voltage levels for the electricity use of homes and businesses. The largest power transformers cannot be mass-manufactured but are instead custom-built for each utility company’s electrical substations. Manufacturing constraints, coupled with the scramble to upgrade US power infrastructure, have meant utility companies and other customers must wait up to several years for delivery of new power transformers. That not only hinders power grid infrastructure expansion needed to support growing electricity demand, but also delays the process of replacing aging power transformers. Read full article Comments

articles.title: Five Takeaways from Billy Edwards Jr.  Ahead of Week 1 Start
articles.summary: Billy Edwards Jr. spoke to the media for the first time after being named the starting quarterback with the matchup against TCU in Ireland approaching.
articles._body: CHAPEL HILL, N.C. — Freshly named starting quarterback Billy Edwards Jr. spoke with the media for the first time on Monday ahead of the Tar Heels’ upcoming matchup with TCU in Ireland. The 23-year-old is entering his sixth season of college football after stops at Wake Forest, Maryland and Wisconsin. Edwards suffered a season-ending injury after starting two games last season with the Badgers. Still, his experience and leadership convinced Bill Belichick and new offensive coordinator Bobby Petrino that he positioned North Carolina best for Week 1 under center.  Here are Edwards’ most notable remarks from his press conference: Decision Making “The biggest thing I’ve learned throughout my time in college, whether it was at any of my three previous stops, is just being consistent as a quarterback and making the right decision. Sometimes that means throwing the ball away. Sometimes that means running out of bounds for a gain of one. Just trying to put the offense in the best situation and eliminate the negative plays. “One of the phrases I got taught as a younger player that kind of stuck with me is mitigating risk. Coach Belichick always says we can go forward, and the only way we can go forward is by not going backwards. “Whatever the defense gives us, we’re going to be able to take. In Coach Petrino’s system, there’s the ability to take more shots, but I think a shot called doesn’t always mean a shot taken.” Why North Carolina? “I’d been to a number of other stops, and really just looking forward to what opportunity could give me the best opportunity to grow, right? Coming here and working for a coach like Coach Petrino, and playing under a coach like Coach Belichick, those were obviously the two biggest factors for me. “The one thing that I’ve always tried to do is just seek opportunity. And you know, when you seek the opportunity, and you prepare the right way, and those two meet, you have a chance to be successful. “There are learning curves and growth in transferring. So really just trying to get myself outside my comfort zone, go to a new place, a new program, run a new scheme, and continue to become a better player.” Working With the WRs “The receiver room and quarterback room as a whole, it’s been great seeing all of us come together. This is how we envision that route being run at this depth, making sure we’re all on the same page. It’s been a lot of fun just seeing the guys make plays. “There’s a lot of characters in the room, too. So there’s never a dull moment when we’re all in there watching film. We’re all talking in the locker room. So it’s been a lot of fun. “We’ve seen everybody make tremendous strides in the offense dating back to January and even through spring ball. We had some good days in spring ball where we were explosive. We’ve had our days in fall camp where we’ve hit some deep shots.” Leadership Role “I’m not going to be the guy yelling all the time. That’s not really my personality. I like to keep a calm presence and have some poise out there. I think that is the biggest thing for me. It’s just remaining authentic, being true to myself, and then understanding that each situation, each opportunity to lead calls for something different.  “There’s going to be days where, yeah, I’m going to put my arm around a guy, but then there’s going to be days where I’m going to have to confront and demand, and maybe get on a little bit. But I think the relationship piece and knowing that it’s coming from a good place.” Learning Another Offensive System “Every year when I was at Maryland we had a new offense coordinator. It’s kind of humbling when you come in at the beginning, and you get new terminology and a new playbook. But I find it really fun. “In this last year alone, I’ve made like 1,000 flashcards, trying to write it all down. The guys in the quarterback room, we’re all different learners, and for me, I’m a rep guy. I need to write it down 1,000 times. I want to see it. I want to go walk through it by myself. I’ve always enjoyed that challenge of trying to learn a new system. “I have a little bit of type A personality. I like to be organized. I like to have my stuff in order, so I definitely have some of my mom in me. I think that’s where I get all the flashcards, and I go home and take a million of her office supplies to make sure I’ve got all the stuff I need to learn a new system.”

articles.title: Hilary Duff Reveals Why She Declared ‘I’m Going to Be a Pop Star’ After ‘Lizzie McGuire’
articles.summary: "I'm going to make music and I'm going to get a record deal and I'm going to be a pop star," the 38-year-old manifested.
articles._body: Hilary Duff didn’t just stumble into the world of pop stardom after becoming a Disney Channel star. She says she actively pursued music as a way to move beyond her beloved television persona. During a conversation with Drew Barrymore on The Drew Barrymore Show , Duff ruminated on the complicated experience of growing up in the public eye and being forever associated with Lizzie McGuire, the titular character she played on the Disney Channel series from 2001 to 2004. Related Hilary Duff Pays Tribute to Hayden Panettiere: ‘I So Deeply Wish This Wasn’t the End for You’ Hilary Duff Pays Tribute to Late Ex Aaron Carter During Lucky Me Tour Stop in Philadelphia Hilary Duff’s Madison Square Garden Show: 5 Best Moments Barrymore asked Duff whether she ever consciously tried to prove herself or others that she was no longer Lizzie McGuire, particularly as she began to grow up. “I think that was why I became — I wanted to be a pop star,” Duff said. “You know, the second I finished filming Lizzie, I was like, ‘Cool. I don’t want to be called that anymore.’ And I’m going to be — I’m going to make music and I’m going to get a record deal and I’m going to be a pop star.” “And you did,” Barrymore replied. “I did,” Duff said. Duff’s transition from Disney star to recording artist quickly became one of the defining chapters of her early career. Her 2003 album Metamorphosis peaked at No. 1 on the Billboard 200 , making Duff a chart-topping pop artist while she was still in her teens. Her 2005 compilation Most Wanted also reached No. 1, and to this day, she’s had seven songs hit the Billboard Hot 100 . Duff says the transition wasn’t necessarily as simple emotionally as it might have looked from the outside. During her conversation with Barrymore, she explained that it took her about a decade to make peace with the fact that Lizzy McGuire would remain frozen in time for audiences while she continued growing up. “It’s weird to play a character that people fall so in love with that doesn’t grow up,” Duff said. “She stays that age, and then I grew up.” Duff added that she eventually became “obsessed” with Lizzie and learned to appreciate the character alongside the fans, but said there was a period when it was difficult to change and evolve while constantly being identified with her Disney alter ego. Barrymore, who also grew up in the spotlight, connected Duff’s experience to her own childhood roles. The two discussed how audience can attach themselves to the younger versions of actors they grew up watching, even as those performers continue to age and establish identities of their own. For Duff, music became part of that evolution. She went on to release Metamorphosis in 2003, followed by albums including Hilary Duff , Dignity and Breathe In. Breathe Out. Her latest album, luck… or something , arrived in February 2026 after more than a decade between studio albums. Billboard previously reported that the 11-track project excitedly signaled Duff’s return to music through Atlantic Records . More than two decades after Lizzie McGuire premiered, Duff is starting to embrace both sides of her legacy. Her latest era incorporates her latest hits while introducing audiences to the adult artist she has become. In the Barrymore interview, she said performing now has allowed her to reconnect with the audience that grew up alongside her while also sharing new music that showcases their lives as adults. “It’s like I get to have these pillars of my old music, which feels so nostalgic and makes people find that kid in them again,” Duff said. “But then also [I can] share my new music, which is like, introducing all of us as adults.” Watch the full interview with Duff and Barrymore below.

articles.title: Adam Schefter’s ‘skeptical’ Deshaun Watson Browns take gives hope to Shedeur Sanders
articles.summary: The Cleveland Browns are moving forward with Deshaun Watson as their starting quarterback. But that doesn’t mean Shedeur Sanders won’t end up starting for Cleveland — and soon. Although the Browns named Watson as the starter today, ESPN NFL insider Adam Schefter said on the R
articles._body: The Cleveland Browns are moving forward with Deshaun Watson as their starting quarterback . But that doesn’t mean Shedeur Sanders won’t end up starting for Cleveland — and soon. Although the Browns named Watson as the starter today, ESPN NFL insider Adam Schefter said on the ‘Pat McAfee Show’ that he would not be surprised if Sanders ended up starting more games for the Browns in 2026 than Watson, who is coming off back-to-back Achilles tendon tears and, most recently, a disastrous press conference. “It has always felt like it was trending towards Deshaun Watson [starting] as a veteran with two games on the road to start the season at Jacksonville, Tampa,” Schefter said. “Now again, even with Saturday’s events, where Deshaun Watson did not play well, where he talked about how the fans were disrespectful, he didn’t appreciate the boos, and his postgame press conference, which obviously did not play over well anywhere. “You have a situation where basically, it always felt like it was trending towards the veteran. And when they named Deshaun Watson as the starting quarterback, they name him for now . I think that’s the key point to raise here. Is Deshaun Watson going to wind up starting more games than Shador Sanders this season? I’m skeptical of that. It’s up to him and how he performs in the first two games. If he plays well the first two weeks on the road, he’ll continue to be the quarterback. If not, I believe there’s a realistic chance that for their home opener, Shedeur Sanders is the starting quarterback for the Cleveland Browns.” "It has always felt like it was trending towards Deshaun Watson as a veteran starting the season for the Browns.. He's the starting quarterback for now.. Is he gonna start more games Shedeur Sanders this season.. I'm skeptical of that" @AdamSchefter #PMSLive https://t.co/SMWcqYtDHh pic.twitter.com/GNmauGbZPD — Pat McAfee (@PatMcAfeeShow) August 24, 2026 Watson, who has been a shell of himself since being accused of sexual misconduct by more than 20 women and subsequently being traded to the Browns and suspended by the NFL, went 5-for-12 for 35 yards and an interception in Cleveland’s second preseason game over the weekend. That, plus the boos he received from the home fans, preceded comments in which Watson, who has since apologized , claimed the negative reaction had “nothing to do about the performance” and was instead “personal” and “a disrespectful thing.” Watson has played far below expectations since being acquired by the Browns, with whom he has played 19 games in four seasons. Due to injuries and suspension, he has failed to play more than seven games in any given year since 2020. Sanders, a fifth-round draft pick from a year ago, played eight games and started seven as a rookie. He finished the season with 1,400 yards, 8 total touchdowns, and 10 interceptions. articles.title: What Happened to the Dallas Wings After the All-Star Break?
articles.summary: Not long ago, the Dallas Wings looked like one of the most dangerous up-and-coming teams in the WNBA. But now, they are searching for answers.  At a glance, it may seem as if the Wings have taken a sudden decline; however, rather than an abrupt downfall, their initial flaws are simply more appare
articles._body: Not long ago, the Dallas Wings looked like one of the most dangerous up-and-coming teams in the WNBA. But now, they are searching for answers. At a glance, it may seem as if the Wings have taken a sudden decline; however, rather than an abrupt downfall, their initial flaws are simply more apparent now, and much harder to overlook.   Dallas Had Enough Going Right to Cover the Rest Ever since the Wings drafted Azzi Fudd with the No. 1 pick in the 2026 WNBA Draft, more eyes have been on a franchise that has one of the most exciting, young rosters in the league. To start the season, the first few games were like a rollercoaster. One game, Dallas would take a close loss, and the other, a blowout victory. However, in just the seventh game of the season, the Wings found their groove as they went on a four-game winning streak. It was in this stretch of victories that Dallas would have a collection of individual success that ultimately came together as a full team effort in the end. Whether it was Paige Bueckers torching opposing defenses with her midrange jumpers or Jessica Shepard starting her historical season with her first triple-double, all other contributions from the Wings’ roster came into play beautifully. Such teamwork was seen when the Wings faced off against the Las Vegas Aces on May 28. Although they were serious underdogs taking on the defending champions, Dallas came together for a commanding 95-87 win thanks to an all-around performance from Bueckers, Fudd, and Shepard who each had at least 20 points in this game. Not only was this matchup a turning point for the Wings after beating the 2025 WNBA Champions, it also put on display their bright future as Shepard recorded her second career triple-double and Fudd arguably had her second breakout game of the season with 22 points of her own. Through this unified team effort, many considered the Wings as a threatening team early.   Two Stars, One Unsettled Offense Paige Bueckers’ Role Has Started to Shift Prior to the All-Star break, it was clear that Bueckers was the number one option for the Wings in terms of scoring. Because of this, we saw not just her individual success that would progress to averaging over 20 points per game, but the Wings had positive results as well. Bueckers’ success as Dallas’ “go-to” in the first half of the season was evident in the 10-game stretch she had just before All-Star weekend. In this run, Bueckers averaged 24.1 points, 4.7 rebounds, and 6.2 assists per game, a career-high in each category. In 8-of-10 of these games, the Wings were victorious. That said, no matter how successful Bueckers is, it takes a total team effort to take down the Las Vegas Aces and Minnesota Lynx, the two teams they lost to in that 10-game span. Since the second half of the season began, some shifts and changes have occurred in the Wings’ playstyle. Most noticeably in their three most recent matchups, Dallas has been exceedingly more reliant on Arike Ogunbowale to kickstart the offense rather than Bueckers. Though Bueckers has still been able to put up a respectable stat line, trusting her to score in crunch time or in the game in general have seemingly begun to fade. In close contests where the Wings took difficult losses such as in their matchup with the Atlanta Dream on July 29 or the Washington Mystics on August 5, Bueckers has noted in post-game press conferences that she had looked to get the ball back in hopes to get a good look for her team. Even so, she did not receive the ball in what were crucial final moments in those games. This leaves fans wondering what exactly head coach Jose Fernandez wants the future of Dallas’ offense and leadership to look like.   Return to Arike-Centered Offense Has Not Clicked Keeping in mind that the Wings’ offense has been redirected in a way that Bueckers appears to be not as large of a priority as she was, there is only one player that Dallas has turned back to: Arike Ogunbowale. Without a doubt, Ogunbowale is a great player and when she is hot, she is hot. That said, when Ogunbowale’s shots are not on the mark, it can be exceedingly difficult to find a rhythm individually and as a team. Now, Ogunbowale has been a part of the Wings for eight seasons, and in those seasons, she has been one of the top options for the franchise no matter the numerous changes in front office, coaching, and rosters. Since Bueckers landed on the Wings in 2025, it was assumed by many that Bueckers would take the lead as a generational talent with an incredibly high ceiling. In the 2025 season, this was true as Bueckers led the Wings in scoring with 19.2 points per game along with 3.9 rebounds, 5.9 assists, and 1.6 steals. Considering the fact that both Bueckers’ and Ogunbowale’s individual playstyles require the ball in their hands often, the dynamic of the two is rather complicated and difficult to balance. For these reasons, many had speculated that Dallas would trade Ogunbowale before the 2026 trade deadline to open the floor for Bueckers to lead. However, no trades were made by the Wings, leaving them with the same strange, awkward backcourt in Bueckers and Ogunbowale. Not only does this seem to create a clash within the way Bueckers plays as a scorer and facilitator and Ogunbowale as a volume scorer, but it also further proves why the Wings have struggled to win in the home stretch of the regular season.   Wings Cannot Win on Star Power Alone The Azzi Fudd Factor As important as stars like Bueckers and Ogunbowale are to the Wings’ success, a team cannot win with just two players. It takes a team to win games. Regardless of the many controversies around Dallas taking Fudd with the No. 1 pick in the 2026 WNBA Draft, Fudd is a lethal and established shooter that, if nothing else, spaces the floor for the Wings. articles.title: From Undrafted to Unstoppable: The Story of Sydney Taylor
articles.summary: Every season in the WNBA, there always seems to be a player who shocks the world with a breakout game and even a breakout season. This year, that player is an undrafted rookie: Sydney Taylor.  Not only has Sydney Taylor taken the league by storm by breaking rookie records and leading the Chicago
articles._body: Every season in the WNBA, there always seems to be a player who shocks the world with a breakout game and even a breakout season. This year, that player is an undrafted rookie: Sydney Taylor. Not only has Sydney Taylor taken the league by storm by breaking rookie records and leading the Chicago Sky in the midst of an injury-filled season, but she has also made a name for herself in the W, proving that she can compete and dominate with some of the best in the league despite going undrafted. Taylor’s Journey to the W Taylor’s story about her road to achieving such a crucial role for the Sky is one of the most unique and impressive progressions that the league has seen, and it is only her rookie season. From 2019-23, Taylor spent four seasons competing for UMass, but it is not even that simple. In her freshman season, Taylor would play an average of 6.1 minutes per game, averaging just 1.9 points, 0.9 rebounds, and 0.5 assists per game. However, Taylor would make a momentous leap from her freshman season to her sophomore campaign as her stats multiplied, showing her incredible growth. Such progression is evident in her stats, averaging 15.6 points, 3.8 rebounds, 1.3 assists, and 1.2 steals per game in the 2020-21 season over 34.5 minutes of play per outing. This notable leap in Taylor’s ability to contribute for the UMass Minutemen on both ends of the court was evident as she continued to average approximately 16 points and at least four rebounds per game in her final two seasons. Because of the NCAA’s COVID-19 eligibility waiver, Taylor was granted one final year of college eligibility, where she would take her talents to Louisville after entering the transfer portal. Although her stats were not as padded and full as they were at UMass, Taylor remained a key contributor for the Cardinals as she put up 10.8 points, 2.8 rebounds, and 2.2 assists per contest, starting nearly every matchup for the Cards. Following her final season of college basketball, Taylor went undrafted. That said, her hard work did not stop there, as she began her professional career playing overseas. In the 2024-25 EuroBasket season, Taylor competed for Lithuania. Although her stats during her time overseas are not publicly available, Taylor’s dedication to her craft was once again put on full display when she made the move to suit up for Poland in the 2025-26 EuroBasket season. It was in that season that Taylor would put the world on notice, recording 22.7 points, 3.8 rebounds, 4.1 assists, and 1.5 steals per game in just under 29 minutes. Not only was Taylor able to score on a high level, but also efficiently, as she shot 56.7 percent from the field, 40.8 percent from three, and 79.4 percent from the free-throw line. This tremendous development and progress from Taylor in just one season was crucial to the next chapter of her life as she continued to work towards making it into the WNBA.   One Opportunity, One Turning Point On April 13, 2026, the entire trajectory of Taylor’s career would change with one offer. It was on this day that the Sky offered Taylor a training camp contract, an opportunity to show not just her skill, but also her potential in hopes that she could make the final roster. In the Sky’s second preseason game, Taylor showed up and showed out, recording 23 points on 7-of-13 shooting from the field. It was through this standout performance, as well as her incredible work ethic, that Chicago would sign Taylor to the official roster, a pivotal moment in her career. Since then, Taylor’s mindset has not changed in that she still strives to put forth her best effort. And because of that, she was able to put herself in the starting lineup just over a month into the regular season.   Stepping Up in the Sky’s Time of Need Heading into the 2026 WNBA season, it was without a doubt that Chicago was in the midst of serious adversity, with injuries as well as a completely new roster as the franchise continues to rebuild. The Sky began the season on a difficult note with Rickea Jackson almost immediately ruled out for the season with a torn ACL, DiJonai Carrington dealing with a lingering ankle injury that required surgery, as well as a few other day-to-day and week-to-week absences from Azur á Stevens and Skylar Diggins. Despite the discouragement that comes with these injuries, this challenging time for Chicago was also a time in which a star was born — or rather introduced. In just the fifth game of the season, Taylor put up a monstrous 27-point clinic against the Toronto Tempo on June 27. Although this standout performance from Taylor was not enough to get the Sky the win, it was certainly a spark of excitement for their future. Taylor has already recorded at least twenty points in six more games this season, and in two of those games, Taylor recorded her first two thirty-point outings in the W, highlighted by a career-high of 31 points against the New York Liberty on July 22. Not only did she beat her previous career-high of 30 points, but she also did so shooting 52.9 percent from the field and 57.1 percent from beyond the arc. Even though Chicago’s record does not completely display Taylor’s individual success, her growth, production, and impact on the team go far beyond the box score and have proven her value as an emerging star in the WNBA.   Taylor’s Latest Statement Coming off a strong team win against the Connecticut Sun just two days before their matchup with the defending champions Las Vegas Aces, the Sky were looking to keep the momentum going. Regardless of the fact that the odds were stacked against the Sky as major underdogs in this contest with the Aces, they battled until the final buzzer, with Taylor delivering a defining moment. Throughout this matchup with Las Vegas, Taylor was firing on all cylinders with no signs of stopping.
